issues.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex App

### What feature would you like to see?

I would like Codex App to support displaying multiple independent, first-class chat threads simultaneously within the same window.

Each pane should contain a normal Codex conversation with its own context, composer, history, and agent execution.

This is specifically about multiple normal, persistent, independent conversations being visible at the same time — not `/side`, a subagent view, or simply tabs for switching between chats.

Ideally, users could:

- split the current workspace vertically or horizontally;
- open an existing or new chat in another pane;
- display 2, 3, or more chats simultaneously;
- resize individual panes;
- move chats between panes;
- maximize or close individual panes;
- preserve the layout per project/workspace.

This would be especially useful for parallel agent workflows, for example keeping one chat working on implementation, another discussing architecture, and another handling tests or debugging.

For example:
```text
┌────────────────────┬────────────────────┬────────────────────┐
│       Chat A       │       Chat B       │       Chat C       │
│                    │                    │                    │
│   implementation   │    architecture    │  tests / research  │
│                    │                    │                    │
└────────────────────┴────────────────────┴────────────────────┘

### Additional information

Codex already supports working with multiple tasks and conversations, but switching between them means losing visual context.

With larger or ultrawide monitors, being able to keep several independent chats visible at once would make Codex much more effective as an agentic development workspace.

Example workflow:

- Chat A: implements a feature
- Chat B: reviews architecture and design decisions
- Chat C: runs tests, investigates failures, or performs research

The important distinction is that these should all be regular, independent Codex threads.

This is related to existing requests for multi-pane workspaces, such as #33301, but the core request here is narrower: allowing multiple independent Codex chat threads themselves to occupy panes simultaneously, e.g. `chat + chat + chat`.

Tabbed chats improve switching between conversations; this feature would improve simultaneous monitoring and interaction with multiple conversations.

issues.title: Cross-device conversation sync becomes stale; stale client can hide newer mobile continuation

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: codex-web
labels.description: Issues related to Codex Web

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

issues.body:
## Summary

Cross-device conversation synchronization can become stale between the ChatGPT iPhone app and Windows/web.

In the failure state, the iPhone continues to receive and send new messages, while the same conversation on Windows/web remains frozen at an older revision. Refreshing the Windows/web client may eventually catch up, but sometimes only after repeated refreshes or a delay.

The more serious failure occurs when the user continues the conversation from the stale Windows/web state: the newer mobile continuation may disappear from the visible conversation, or the two clients can show divergent conversation histories.

This is not just a cosmetic refresh delay. It appears to be a stale-client / conversation-version conflict problem.

---

## Feedback reference

Feedback ID:

`no-active-thread-01a0dec2-9d2c-7350-be15-e34062f9bf82`

---

## Environment

- Account: same ChatGPT account on both devices
- Mobile client: ChatGPT iPhone app
- Desktop client: Windows/web
- Same conversation open on both devices
- Reproducible repeatedly
- Observed date: September 26, 2026

---

## Observed behavior

### 1. Mobile advances, desktop stays behind

The iPhone app continues to show newly sent messages and newly received assistant replies.

At the same time, Windows/web can remain on an older conversation state and does not automatically advance to the latest server-side history.

The stale desktop tab still appears usable, even though newer messages already exist on the same conversation from the mobile device.

### 2. Manual refresh is unreliable

Refreshing/reopening the desktop client sometimes causes the missing messages to appear, but:

- it is not immediate,
- it may take repeated refreshes,
- there is no visible indication that the client is stale,
- there is no explicit “refresh conversation from server” action.

This means the user cannot reliably tell whether the desktop is showing the latest authoritative conversation revision.

### 3. Stale desktop can continue from an old revision

If the user sends a new message from the stale Windows/web state before it catches up, the conversation can diverge.

The newer mobile continuation may then disappear from the visible conversation or become hidden by the continuation created from the stale desktop state.

This creates a data-integrity concern from the user's perspective: a valid conversation continuation appears to have been lost even though it had already existed on another client.

### 4. No conflict warning

The desktop client currently provides no warning similar to:

- “This conversation changed on another device.”
- “You are viewing an older revision.”
- “Refresh before continuing.”
- “Conversation conflict detected.”

The send box remains active, allowing a message to be sent from an outdated local state.

---

## Reproduction steps

1. Sign in to the same ChatGPT account on iPhone and Windows/web.
2. Open the exact same conversation on both devices.
3. Send a message from one device and continue the conversation on iPhone.
4. Confirm that iPhone shows the newest messages/replies.
5. Return to Windows/web.
6. Observe that Windows/web can remain frozen at an older message.
7. Wait or refresh.
8. In some cases, the newer messages still do not appear immediately.
9. Before desktop catches up, send another message from the stale Windows/web state.
10. Compare the conversation on both devices.
11. The newer mobile continuation may disappear from the visible history or the two clients may show inconsistent conversation states.

---

## Concrete test performed

During testing, short messages such as:

- `pc test`
- repeated `pc test` messages
- `SYNC-TEST-3`

were used specifically to make it obvious which client had received the latest server-side continuation.

The tests showed that one client could be visibly behind even while the other client had already advanced.

---

## Screenshot evidence already captured

The following screenshots were captured during the failure and show the problem from the user's side.

### Screenshot A — Windows/web stale conversation state

Shows the desktop/web conversation still sitting on the two “pc test” messages and corresponding assistant replies while cross-device testing was being performed.

What it demonstrates:

- the desktop UI can remain on an older visible revision,
- the conversation remains interactable,
- there is no warning that the view may be stale.

### Screenshot B — repeated sync failure after prior catch-up

Shows that even after the conversation temporarily synchronized, it later stopped updating again.

What it demonstrates:

- this is not a single one-off load failure,
- synchronization can regress after appearing to recover,
- reopening/refreshing is not a dependable permanent fix.

### Screenshot C — no available update / no obvious recovery control

Shows the client state while attempting to resolve the problem, with no clear client-side update or manual conversation-sync mechanism available.

What it demonstrates:

- the user has no direct recovery action specific to conversation synchronization,
- troubleshooting currently depends on refresh/reopen behavior.

### Screenshot D — explicit sync test across devices

Shows the conversation after cross-device test messages were sent.

What it demonstrates:

- different clients can temporarily expose different conversation revisions,
- the issue is visible at the conversation-history level rather than only delayed typing/rendering.

### Screenshot E — request for manual sync control

Shows the user explicitly requesting a manual “Sync conversation” action after repeated stale states.

What it demonstrates:

- automatic recovery is insufficient for this failure mode,
- a manual authoritative-server refresh would provide an immediate recovery path.

---

## Expected behavior

A conversation should have a clearly authoritative server-side revision.

Before a client sends a new message, it should verify that the local conversation revision is current.

If the server has a newer revision, the client should either:

1. automatically fetch and merge the latest state before sending, or
2. block the send and inform the user that the conversation changed on another device.

A stale client should never silently create a continuation that causes a newer continuation from another device to disappear from the visible history.

---

## Suggested implementation safeguards

### 1. Conversation revision / optimistic concurrency check

Each client should track a conversation revision/version identifier.

When sending a new message, include the revision the client believes it is continuing from.

If the server's current revision differs, return a conflict instead of silently accepting a continuation from stale state.

Conceptually:

`client_revision != server_revision -> refresh / conflict flow`

### 2. Manual “Sync conversation” action

Add an explicit UI action such as:

**Sync conversation**
or
**Refresh from server**

This should:

- discard stale local cache for that conversation,
- fetch the authoritative server history,
- refresh visible messages,
- re-establish streaming/subscription state.

### 3. Visible synchronization status

Show a lightweight state indicator:

- Synced
- Syncing
- Out of date
- Conflict detected

This would immediately tell the user whether it is safe to continue from the current client.

### 4. Preserve both branches on conflict

If two devices genuinely create separate continuations from the same earlier revision, preserve both branches.

Do not silently hide one.

The UI could present:

- “Conversation changed on another device”
- “Choose latest branch”
- or a branch/recovery view.

### 5. Server-authoritative refresh on focus/resume

When a conversation tab/app returns to foreground after being inactive, compare the local latest message/revision with the server before allowing continued interaction.

### 6. Realtime subscription health check

If the app relies on a realtime stream/subscription, detect when that subscription becomes stale or disconnected.

A client can otherwise look “online” while no longer receiving conversation updates.

---

## Why this matters

This bug is more serious than ordinary delayed synchronization because the stale client is still allowed to mutate the conversation.

The failure mode is effectively:

1. Device A advances conversation.
2. Device B does not receive that update.
3. Device B still accepts user input.
4. Device B creates a continuation from obsolete state.
5. One continuation may disappear from the user's visible history.

That creates a risk of apparent conversation loss and makes cross-device use unreliable for long-running work.

---

## Requested fix

Please consider implementing all three layers:

1. automatic server-side stale-revision detection,
2. a visible/manual **Sync conversation** control,
3. conflict-safe preservation of divergent continuations.

Even if realtime sync temporarily fails, these safeguards would prevent a stale client from silently continuing from an obsolete conversation state.

## Environment

- Windows connected computer, desktop package `OpenAI.Codex_26.930.3930.0_x64`
- Installed CLI: `codex-cli 0.160.0`
- Task created by a dot on the connected Windows computer

## Issue

A fresh dot-created task reports a different execution policy from the existing user-level Codex defaults. I could not identify a supported persistent setting that controls this launch route. This report is about fresh task creation/default inheritance, not changing permissions after launch or authorizing a particular repository action.

Existing user configuration:

```toml
approval_policy = "on-request"
approvals_reviewer = "user"
sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"
```

Reported policy in the newly created task:

- `sandbox_mode = workspace-write`
- `approvals_reviewer = auto_review`
- Managed, restricted filesystem profile; writes limited to task workspace and system temporary directories
- Restricted command networking; `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=1`
- The launch's effective `approval_policy` was not separately reported

## Reproduction / observed workflow

1. Have the above existing user-level configuration on a connected Windows computer.
2. Ask a dot to create a fresh task on that computer.
3. Inspect the new task's reported sandbox/reviewer/network policy before changing task permissions.
4. Observe the difference above.

Read-only diagnosis found no project configuration along this task's directory ancestry and no documented Windows system requirements or legacy managed-config file. Effective remotely supplied requirements and explicit launch fields remain unknown. Reading process launch flags was denied; a supported app-server diagnostic query failed before connection with `Could not find home directory`. No attempt was made to bypass either boundary.

## Expected behavior / requested clarification

Please identify which policy source controls dot-created local tasks and whether non-inheritance of user defaults is intentional. If an independent policy applies, expose/document a persistent user-visible launch control and accurately show its effective values. If inheritance is intended, investigate the mismatch.

I am not asking to bypass OS administrator permissions, organization-enforced requirements, or action-specific safeguards. Editing the same global sandbox default again has no demonstrated effect. The dot's exposed task-creation interface has no sandbox or approval override parameter.

## Related reports

- #50671 concerns task-selected Full access and delegated/resumed work
- #50701 includes a similar Windows configuration discrepancy but primarily concerns propagation of explicit authorization
- #50333 concerns dot SSH execution restrictions

These may share a cause, but that is not established. I found no verified Desktop/dot resolution in those discussions. Please consolidate if this fresh-launch/default-control case belongs in an existing issue.

No configuration changes, private repository details, credentials, session transcripts, or personal filesystem paths are included.

26.1007.2314.0 (MSIX OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0, process ChatGPT.exe)

TODO

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64  -  Windows 11 Home 26H2, zh-CN

### What issue are you seeing?

After the Codex App auto-updated today (2026-10-11), the maximized window is taller than the screen, so the bottom strip of the window - which contains the chat input/composer - is rendered below the bottom edge of the display and is unreachable.

Measured from a per-monitor-v2 DPI-aware process:
- Physical display: 1920 x 1080 (single monitor)
- Display scale: 150% (window DPI = 144)
- Accessibility text size: 150%
- Window rect: 1920 x 1350 at (0,0)  -> 270 px below the bottom edge
- Window is maximized (IsZoomed = true, showCmd = 3)
- Restored rect: 1047 x 672 at (74,0) - fits fine

Only the maximized geometry is wrong.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Windows 11, 1920x1080, display scaling 150%, Accessibility text size 150%.
2. Launch the Codex App (MSIX 26.1007.2314.0) and maximize the window.
3. Read the geometry from a per-monitor-DPI-aware process: GetWindowRect -> 1920x1350 at (0,0); GetWindowPlacement.showCmd -> 3; GetDpiForWindow -> 144.

The maximized window should be clamped to the monitor work area (~1920x1032 at 150%) so the whole window, especially the composer at the bottom, stays on screen.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

codex、gpt-6-luna

### What subscription do you have?

pro 200

### What platform is your computer?

windows

### What issue are you seeing?

Title: Why did 34 web-tool actions produce 15.9 million input tokens in a single turn?

I ran one continuous Codex session with five sequential turns, using gpt-6-luna.

Turn 1: Load background information
Web-tool actions: 0
Input tokens: 72,458

Turn 2: Web research
Web-tool actions: 32
Input tokens: 7,216,519

Turn 3: Web research
Web-tool actions: 54
Input tokens: 22,301,794

Turn 4: Web research
Web-tool actions: 34
Input tokens: 15,897,762

Turn 5: Consolidate findings into a final report
Web-tool actions: 0
Input tokens: 648,490

Total reported input tokens: 46,137,023.

These numbers came from thread/tokenUsage/updated. Each turn's usage was calculated by subtracting consecutive end-of-turn cumulative totals, not by repeatedly summing cumulative snapshots.

The counts represent web-tool actions, not unique webpages.

Why did Turn 4 accumulate nearly 16 million input tokens from 34 web-tool actions, while Turn 5, using the existing conversation to produce the final report, required only about 648,000?

Please explain:

1. How much comes from retrieved content versus repeatedly processing existing context?
2. Are unnecessary model/tool round trips amplifying usage, or is there a reporting issue?
3. How do these reported tokens translate into subscription-limit consumption?

The visible search results do not suggest a massive crawl or an enormous volume of retrieved material. Even assuming a few thousand tokens per webpage, that is nowhere near 15.9 million tokens of new content.

So how the hell does a modest web-research task produce this kind of token explosion?

If the explanation is that the same conversation gets counted repeatedly after each tool action, that still raises a serious efficiency and transparency problem. Calling it cumulative usage does not explain why so much repeated processing is necessary, or how much subscription allowance it consumes. A high cache-hit rate alone does not answer these questions either.

Please show the actual breakdown: newly retrieved content, repeated context, model requests, and the resulting quota impact.

Users should not have to reverse-engineer your accounting to understand why a relatively small research task produces tens of millions of reported input tokens.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The affected run used the following workflow:

1. Create a fresh Codex session using gpt-6-luna through the Codex SDK.
2. Turn 1: Provide approximately 102,446 characters of background information.
3. Turns 2–4: Send three successive web-research prompts in the same session. Let the model search and return its findings after each prompt.
4. Turn 5: Ask the model to consolidate the existing findings into a final report without further web searches.
5. Record thread/tokenUsage/updated notifications throughout the session.
6. Calculate each turn's input usage by subtracting the previous turn's final cumulative input total from the current turn's final cumulative input total.

Observed results:

Turn 1: 0 web-tool actions; 72,458 input tokens.
Turn 2: 32 web-tool actions; 7,216,519 input tokens.
Turn 3: 54 web-tool actions; 22,301,794 input tokens.
Turn 4: 34 web-tool actions; 15,897,762 input tokens.
Turn 5: 0 web-tool actions; 648,490 input tokens.

Total: 46,137,023 input tokens.

One context-compaction event was observed during Turn 3.

These are recorded results from one run, not guaranteed identical counts on every reproduction. Web-tool actions are not unique webpage counts. Cumulative snapshots were not repeatedly summed.

### What is the expected behavior?

I expect web research to avoid unnecessary repeated processing and to provide understandable, verifiable usage accounting.

I am not claiming that total input tokens must equal the text retrieved from webpages. However, tens of millions of reported input tokens for this workflow require a concrete explanation.

Please provide a per-request breakdown showing:

1. Newly retrieved content.
2. Existing context processed again.
3. The number of model requests and tool actions.
4. Any additional usage caused by compaction or retries.
5. How this reported usage affects subscription limits.

If unnecessary model/tool round trips are amplifying consumption, please fix them. If these totals are intended accounting, please document why this level of repeated processing is necessary and provide practical controls to reduce it.

A high cache-hit rate alone is not an adequate explanation.

### Additional information

_No response_

### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Installed Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0`, verified from the Windows package metadata. This is the package version, not an inferred CLI version.

The Cloudflare plugin bundle reported version `1.0.1` before its capabilities disappeared.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT account authentication, rather than API-key authentication. The exact subscription tier is not included in this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows, OS version `10.0.26300.0`.

### What issue are you seeing?

During a Codex Desktop task on **October 13, 2026, around 23:00 America/New_York (EDT / UTC-04:00)**, the Cloudflare plugin became unavailable again after successful OAuth and successful live MCP operations.

There appear to be inconsistent states across the plugin installation UI, dependency lookup, and callable tools. This report does not assume those surfaces share the same authentication state or that their errors establish the root cause.

Observed sequence:

1. The Cloudflare OAuth flow had previously been completed through all steps and displayed success.
2. After restarting Codex Desktop, the plugin UI showed the plugin as not installed.
3. Trying to connect/install again opened **three apparently identical authorization pages**. This is the user's observed browser behavior; duplicate authorization requests have not been verified with a network trace.
4. The native Cloudflare MCP route became available again. `whoami` and an R2 bucket-list request succeeded; a private bucket was created, and a small object PUT/GET succeeded. These successful operations demonstrate that this route was actually usable, rather than only showing an authorization-success screen.
5. Later in the same work session, the native Cloudflare tools disappeared from the available tool set again. The Cloudflare bundled skills also ceased to be listed.
6. A separate app-backed Cloudflare route reported `USER_NOT_LOGGED_IN` / not connected. Plugin dependency lookup returned `plugin_not_found`.

The Cloudflare website remained usable through an existing browser login, and the task was completed there. This is a fallback observation, not evidence that the plugin connection recovered.

No deliberate plugin uninstall or account disconnect was part of this workflow. No local plugin/configuration repair was applied during the subsequent investigation.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The sequence above was observed during normal use; I do not yet have a deterministic minimal reproduction. The behavior to investigate is:

1. Install/connect the OpenAI-curated Cloudflare plugin and complete OAuth.
2. Restart Codex Desktop and inspect whether the installation/connection is retained.
3. If it is shown as missing, attempt one connection flow and inspect whether multiple authorization pages open.
4. Once MCP tools are available, perform an authorized operation and continue working in the same session.
5. Compare the plugin UI/dependency state with actual tool availability if the plugin becomes unavailable again.

### What is the expected behavior?

- A successful installation and connection should persist unless explicitly disconnected or invalidated for a reported reason.
- Successful live MCP calls should not be followed by silent loss of the plugin/tools without an actionable error.
- Installation, dependency, authorization, and tool-availability surfaces should present consistent state, or clearly explain which separate connection is missing.
- A single connection attempt should present one understandable authorization flow rather than several indistinguishable pages.

### Additional information

Related reports were reviewed before filing:

- #34859, particularly the [September 1 Windows Desktop comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/34859#issuecomment-5493240661): installed/enabled Cloudflare metadata conflicts with a not-installed permission lookup and missing MCP tools. That report used plugin `0.1.2`; this observation involves bundle `1.0.1` and includes a transition from successful live calls to disappearance.
- #28703: other Windows plugins were reported removed after a successful UI installation and subsequent app restart. Those are different plugins, so this is only a related symptom.
- [cloudflare/mcp-server-cloudflare#446](https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp-server-cloudflare/issues/446): previous ChatGPT plugin/tool availability problems, with a maintainer response about an earlier fix. This does not establish the cause of this newer Desktop incident.

Could the team investigate whether remote plugin installation reconciliation, connection lookup, and active-session tool refresh are remaining consistent during this transition, and whether the reconnect UI can launch duplicate authorization flows?

Private account identifiers, authorization URLs, credentials, local paths, and task data are intentionally omitted. No raw logs or screenshots containing those details are attached.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.928.21956

### What subscription do you have?

sub Pro5.x

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Summary
The Codex desktop app cannot execute even basic read-only commands when the Agent environment is set to WSL.
Every attempt fails during process creation, before the command runs:
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"Failed to create unified exec process: No such file or directory (os error 2)\")" }
The same commands work when invoked directly through WSL from PowerShell. The standalone Codex CLI also works after repairing a separate npm installation issue.
Restarting the desktop app and creating a new chat in the same project did not resolve the desktop failure.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

````markdown
# [Windows][WSL2] Desktop execution tools fail to create processes while direct WSL commands and standalone Codex CLI work

## Summary

The Codex desktop app cannot execute basic read-only commands with **Agent environment set to WSL**.

Every execution attempt fails during process creation, before the command runs:

```text
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"Failed to create unified exec process: No such file or directory (os error 2)\")" }
```

Direct WSL commands launched from PowerShell work. The standalone Codex CLI also successfully executes read-only commands.

Fully restarting the desktop app and creating a new chat in the same project did not resolve the issue.

Personal and project-specific paths below have been replaced with placeholders.

## Environment

| Component | Version / configuration |
|---|---|
| Desktop Windows package | `OpenAI.Codex` |
| Package version reported by `Get-AppxPackage` | `26.928.2636.0` |
| Desktop update tool: `installedVersion` | `26.928.21956` |
| Desktop update tool: `installedBuildVersion` | `12404` |
| Desktop update tool: `installedReleaseChannel` | `prod` |
| Desktop update tool: status | `up_to_date` |
| Agent environment | WSL |
| Default WSL distribution | Ubuntu, running under WSL 2 |
| WSL version | `2.7.14.0` |
| Linux kernel | `6.18.33.2-2` |
| Windows version reported by WSL | `10.0.26200.9457` |
| Standalone Codex CLI | `0.159.3` |
| Node.js used by standalone CLI | `18.19.1` |
| npm used by standalone CLI | `9.2.0` |
| Project storage | Ubuntu Linux filesystem, under `/home/<user>/projects/<project>` |

The desktop version values come from different interfaces. I am reporting both without assuming that the difference indicates a fault.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an existing project stored in the Ubuntu Linux filesystem.
2. Set the desktop app’s **Agent environment** to **WSL**.
3. Fully exit and restart the desktop app.
4. Ask the desktop agent to execute:

   ```bash
   pwd
   id
   ```

5. Also ask it to read a known existing file in the project.
6. Observe that all attempts fail during process creation.
7. Create a new chat in the same project and repeat the checks.
8. Observe the same failure.

## Expected behavior

The desktop agent should start a process in the selected WSL environment and execute the read-only commands.

If a required executable, helper, or working directory cannot be resolved, the diagnostic should identify the missing component or path.

## Actual behavior

Each attempt fails with:

```text
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"Failed to create unified exec process: No such file or directory (os error 2)\")" }
```

No command output is produced.

The following variations were tested and failed:

- Explicit `/bin/bash`.
- Explicit `/bin/sh`.
- Default shell configuration.
- Project working directory.
- `/tmp` working directory.
- Existing chat.
- Newly created chat after restarting the desktop app.

The working directory passed to the tool is only an input parameter. It was not verified by a successful `pwd` inside the desktop execution tool.

## Additional tool error

The Node REPL tool also fails before reading a file:

```text
Mcp error: -32602: js: codex/sandbox-state-meta:
sandboxCwd is not a local file URI:
file:///home/<user>/projects/<project>
```

The path above is redacted.

I do not know whether this shares a root cause with the execution failure, but it may be relevant to Windows/WSL path handling.

## Successful checks outside the desktop tools

Direct execution through PowerShell works:

```powershell
wsl -d Ubuntu -- /bin/bash -lc 'whoami'
```

Additional direct WSL checks confirmed that:

- The project directory exists.
- The tested file exists.
- The directory and file are owned by the expected Linux user.
- The file permissions allow reading.

The standalone Codex CLI `0.159.3` also successfully:

- Read the project’s instruction file.
- Executed `pwd`.
- Executed `id`.

**The desktop execution tools still fail despite these successful checks.**

## Separate CLI installation issue — resolved

During diagnosis, the standalone npm-installed CLI initially reported:

```text
Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-linux-x64
```

The declared dependency was:

```json
{
  "@openai/codex-linux-x64": "npm:@openai/codex@0.159.3-linux-x64"
}
```

An installation attempt using the existing npm registry configuration returned `ETARGET`. An explicit query to the npm public registry confirmed that the platform version exists.

After repairing the installation using the public registry, the standalone CLI became functional.

**This did not fix the desktop failure.** I am not assuming that the desktop app uses the separately installed CLI.

## Additional observation

Direct WSL startup reports a warning that a localhost proxy configuration was detected but was not mirrored into WSL in NAT mode.

Local commands still execute successfully despite this warning. There is no confirmed evidence that it causes the desktop process-creation failure.

## Impact

The desktop agent cannot read project files, edit files, or run validation commands.

The standalone CLI is usable, but the desktop execution tools remain unavailable.

## Diagnostic assistance requested

Could you advise:

1. Which executable or helper might be failing to start?
2. Whether the `sandboxCwd` URI error is related to Windows/WSL path mapping?
3. Which targeted, sanitized diagnostics would help investigate this without deleting configuration, authentication data, or session history?

No sandbox bypass, project permission changes, or configuration-directory deletion has been used as a workaround.
````

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex app are you using?

Codex desktop for Windows, app release `codex@26.915.31945`, installed from the Microsoft Store (MSIX package `OpenAI.Codex` version `26.915.4065.0`).

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### Which model were you using?

A custom provider configured in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
model = "deepseek-flash"

[model_providers.deepseek]
base_url = "https://api.deepseek.com"
wire_api = "responses"
```

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 (build 10.0.26200), x64. Time zone Asia/Tokyo (UTC+9).

### What terminal are you using?

The Codex desktop app UI.

### What did you do?

I had been using this provider and model in this thread for days without problems. On 2026-09-21 at 19:48 JST I told the agent to keep working on its own until 10:00 the next morning, and left it running.

### What did you expect to see?

The agent keeps working as before.

### What did you see instead?

Every request in that thread is rejected before the model produces any output. The thread is now permanently unusable with this provider.

The error, taken verbatim from the thread's turn error records:

```
{"error":{"message":"Invalid schema for function 'codex_app::automation_update': schema must be a JSON Schema of 'type: \"object\"', got 'type: null'.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

Failed turns in that thread (JST):

| # | Turn started | Turn ended | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-09-21 19:48:20 | 2026-09-21 20:24:31 | failed |
| 2 | 2026-09-22 10:50:27 | 2026-09-22 10:50:30 | failed |
| 3 | 2026-09-22 10:52:28 | 2026-09-22 10:52:40 | failed |
| 4 | 2026-09-22 10:52:59 | 2026-09-22 10:53:01 | failed |
| 5 | 2026-09-22 10:54:14 | 2026-09-22 10:54:16 | failed |
| 6 | 2026-09-22 11:16:54 | — | failed |
| 7 | 2026-09-22 11:18:15 | — | failed |
| 8 | 2026-09-22 11:18:28 | — | failed |

### Additional information

- **It is specific to this thread, not to the provider or the model.** At the same time on the same machine, with the same provider and the same `deepseek-flash` model, other threads keep working normally — one of them was streaming tool calls at 2026-09-22 11:19 JST while this thread was failing.
- **Restarting the app does not clear it.** I restarted the app and the first attempt afterwards (11:16:54 JST) failed with the same error.
- The error names a tool from the `codex_app` namespace, `codex_app::automation_update`, and says its schema has `type: null` instead of `type: "object"`. That tool's `parameters` schema appears to be defined at top level with `properties` + `oneOf` + `$defs` and without a root `"type": "object"`, which a strict validator rejects. Because the rejection is at request level (`invalid_request_error`), the whole turn is lost rather than just that tool.
- **Leading hypothesis (inference, not proven):** the thread only started carrying this tool once it was put into "keep working on your own" / ongoing-goal mode. The first failing turn is exactly the message in which I asked it to continue autonomously, and the thread displays an ongoing goal in the UI. I cannot see the outgoing tool list from the client, so I am flagging this as a hypothesis rather than a conclusion. Before that message the same thread, same model, same provider worked normally for days.
- Impact: with any provider that validates function schemas strictly (this affects DeepSeek through the Responses wire API at minimum), a thread that carries this tool can never complete a turn again. The only workarounds I found are to switch that thread to a first-party model, or to stop using that thread.

### What I am asking for

1. Can you confirm whether `codex_app::automation_update` is being sent with a `parameters` schema that is missing a root `"type": "object"`?
2. Is there a supported way to exclude that toolset from a thread (or to make the schema valid) so third-party providers can keep working?
3. If the schema is generated per feature, is the automation/goal toolset supposed to be attached to every thread, or only when the goal feature is in use?

(Reference: I also reported a separate desktop crash issue as #46808.)

issues.body:
# Bug report: Local projects disappear from sidebar after Windows desktop update

## Summary

After updating the Codex/ChatGPT Windows desktop app, the **Projects** section shows **No projects**. Existing chats remain visible under **Recents**, and all source folders still exist on disk.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Installed Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.901.4073.0_x64`
- App-server client version observed in logs: `26.901.31953`
- Bundled Codex CLI: `codex-cli 0.153.1`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have multiple local Codex projects with chats assigned to them.
2. Update the Windows desktop app.
3. Launch Codex.
4. Inspect the left sidebar under **Projects**.

## Actual result

- Sidebar displays **No projects**.
- Clicking **Choose project** opens **Create project**, requiring projects to be recreated manually.
- Restarting the app and restarting Windows do not restore the projects.
- Closing the visible app window does not terminate all `ChatGPT.exe` background processes.

## Expected result

Existing local projects and their chat assignments should be migrated and remain visible after an update.

## Diagnostic evidence

The underlying data was checked locally:

- `state_5.sqlite` still contains 14 project records and 14 project roots.
- All 14 source folders still exist.
- 54 of 62 local threads have a non-null project assignment.
- The desktop global-state file is rewritten on startup with:
  - `local-projects: {}`
  - `thread-project-assignments: null`
  - migration state `projectsMigrated: true`
  - migration state `threadAssignmentsMigrated: false`
- Reconstructing the sidebar registry while the app is running is overwritten by the app's in-memory state when it closes.
- A recovery helper waiting for the app to exit timed out after 30 minutes because background `ChatGPT.exe` processes remained active after the window was closed.

This looks like a Windows desktop migration/regression where the durable SQLite project records survive, but the sidebar registry and thread-assignment migration do not load or complete.

## Data-loss impact

No source folders appear to be deleted, but project organization is effectively lost in the UI. Manually recreating the projects would also require users to remember which chats belonged to each project.

issues.body:
## Summary

When the TUI resumes a session whose latest turn is still in progress, the status indicator appears to restart its elapsed timer instead of reflecting the turn's original start time. The status can therefore show approximately `0s` even when the turn has been running much longer.

## Source trace

The replay path receives `started_at` for each turn, but the `TurnStatus::InProgress` branch calls `on_task_started()` without passing or restoring that timestamp. `on_task_started()` resets the status timer to zero. The live start notification and replay path therefore use different timing information.

## Expected behavior

For a replayed in-progress turn with a start timestamp, initialize the status timer from that timestamp so the elapsed indicator continues across reconnect/resume. Keep the zero-time behavior for a genuinely new live turn.

## Reproduction

1. Start a turn and leave it running long enough for the status indicator to show elapsed time.
2. Reopen or resume that thread in the TUI while the turn remains active.
3. Observe that the status timer starts near zero rather than showing the elapsed duration.

This is a TUI replay/status issue, separate from thread ownership or active-writer locking.

issues.title: <image_resize_notice> is written between tool outputs of the same batch, wedging threads on strict OpenAI-compatible providers

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.21159 (bundled codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2)

### What subscription do you have?

API - custom OpenAI-compatible provider (a self-hosted relay, `wire_api = "responses"`, which validates tool pairing strictly). Not the ChatGPT/OpenAI backend.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.6 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64 (Apple Silicon)

### What issue are you seeing?

A thread became permanently unusable. The first request after a batched tool call failed with:

```
{"error":{"code":null,"message":"An assistant message with 'tool_calls' must be followed by tool messages responding to each 'tool_call_id'. (insufficient tool messages following tool_calls message)","param":null,"status":400,"type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

Every later user turn in the same thread then failed with the same 400 within ~4 s.

Root cause, taken from the session rollout JSONL: in one assistant turn that contained **two parallel tool calls**, the client appended the image tool output, then a **developer `<image_resize_notice>` message**, then the second tool output:

```
09:01:10.383  function_call          js               call_00_sklbnyw...
09:01:10.384  function_call          exec_command     call_01_asvwdd...
09:01:11.838  function_call_output   call_00_sklbnyw...   (screenshot image, ~438 KB)
09:01:11.838  message (developer)    <image_resize_notice>
09:01:11.839  function_call_output   call_01_asvwdd...    (command output)
09:01:16.923  task_complete          error: the 400 above
```

The notice text is:

```
<image_resize_notice>
Image 1 of 1 in the preceding tool output was resized from 3024x1898 to 1989x1248 pixels.
</image_resize_notice>
```

So the assistant message with two `tool_calls` is **not** followed contiguously by its two tool messages: the developer notice splits the block. Strict OpenAI-compatible validators reject that shape (this is what produces `insufficient tool messages following tool_calls message`). Because the interleaved order is **persisted in the rollout**, the malformed block is replayed on every following request, and the thread can never make progress.

Session scan of the affected rollout (856 response items, 129 tool calls): every `function_call` has a matching `function_call_output`, and this was the **only** place where a non-tool item sits between two tool outputs of the same batch. Two later user turns (09:03:10 and 09:03:19 UTC) failed with the identical error in <4 s, without reaching the model.

How this differs from #44604 (inference): there, the wedge is attributed to the follow-up sampling request going out before the last tool output of the batch was appended (a race; gaps of 68 ms / ~30 s). Here the two tool outputs are 1 ms apart and the bad ordering is written into the rollout itself, so the stored history is invalid even with all outputs present; request gating alone would not correct the on-disk ordering.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use the Codex App against a custom OpenAI-compatible provider that validates tool-call/tool-output ordering strictly.
2. Have one assistant turn issue two parallel tool calls where the first one returns a screenshot image large enough to be resized (e.g. a computer-use/MCP tool returning a 3024x1898 image) and the second is any other tool (e.g. `exec_command`).
3. The app writes: tool output #1 -> `<image_resize_notice>` developer message -> tool output #2, in that order, into the rollout.
4. The next sampling request is rejected with the 400 above, and the thread stays wedged afterwards.

Affected session (truncated): `01a124e4-...-9c9dbc7b37ea`, 2026-10-10 09:01-09:03 UTC.

### What is the expected behavior?

1. Non-tool protocol items such as `<image_resize_notice>` must never be emitted between the `function_call_output` items of the same assistant batch - emit the notice after the batch's final tool output, or attach it to the image output it annotates.
2. Before sending, the client should verify that each assistant `tool_calls` message is followed contiguously by tool messages for all of its `call_id`s (fail closed: wait or synthesize an output instead of sending an invalid body).
3. This 400 should be recoverable: re-send once with a stand-in output for the offending `call_id` rather than ending the turn and wedging the thread.

### Additional information

Related: #44604 (same trigger - `<image_resize_notice>` after an image output; attributed to a request race), #38365 (notes a developer message between a tool call and its output breaking custom providers), #26865 and #25380 (same 400 / wedged-thread symptom).

Happy to attach a redacted excerpt of the rollout JSONL if that helps.

issues.title: Windows desktop freezes during automatic Git review when spawning a ~32K-character diff command

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
## Summary

The Windows desktop app becomes permanently unresponsive when its automatic Git review/changes summary launches a Git diff with a long list of path arguments. On this machine, one captured command line was 32,411 UTF-16 characters. The main window thread was blocked inside process creation, before Git started executing.

This is a confirmed trigger and a confirmed workaround on one affected machine. The precise Windows/kernel/driver cause of the process-creation stall has not been identified. The command is below the documented CreateProcessW limit, so this should not be described as an ordinary command-line-limit error or as proof of a Git executable defect.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Home, Chinese locale, x64, build 26200.
- Microsoft Store desktop package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0.
- Window/executable name: ChatGPT / ChatGPT.exe.
- Bundled Codex engine: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- Git for Windows: 2.44.0.windows.1.
- A Git-backed development project with hundreds of changed paths relative to an older review baseline.

A subsequent read-only audit established why the path list is large: the review baseline is an October 2 commit, whereas the current HEAD is from October 11. Comparing the baseline to HEAD produces 435 changed entries; the current uncommitted tracked changes relative to HEAD produce 80 entries; the cumulative baseline-to-working-tree diff produces 466 entries. These counts overlap and do not add directly. No paths under common bin/obj/node_modules/dist/build/.vs/target/packages directory names appeared among those tracked changes. This is mostly ordinary source/configuration change history, rather than a huge collection of generated build files. Committing the pending changes alone would not eliminate a diff against the old baseline.

## Desktop reproduction observed on the affected machine

1. Completely exit the desktop app and its child processes, including its bundled codex.exe backend.
2. Launch the desktop app normally with existing projects/history.
3. Select the affected Git-backed project or open its existing conversations. No new user request to run Git is needed.
4. The desktop's automatic changes/review summary starts a command of this shape:

```text
git -c diff.mnemonicPrefix=false -c diff.noprefix=false -c core.quotePath=false
    -c safe.bareRepository=explicit -c core.hooksPath=NUL -c core.fsmonitor=
    diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --color=never --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/
    <review-baseline-commit> --find-renames --raw --no-abbrev --numstat -z
    -- <hundreds of relative file paths>
```

5. The parent ChatGPT.exe window becomes unresponsive. Captured total command-line length: 32,411 characters. Another desktop run reached 32,469 characters and also froze.

Expected: the changes summary completes, fails with an actionable error, or can be cancelled without blocking the window.

Actual: the window stops responding indefinitely while the native process-creation call is blocked. The child Git process exists in an initialized state, with no execution/CPU progress.

## Native evidence

The main window thread's captured native stack, from the blocking leaf upward, included:

```text
ntdll!NtCreateUserProcess+0x14
KERNELBASE!CreateProcessInternalW
KERNELBASE!CreateProcessW
KERNEL32!CreateProcessW
chrome.dll!uv_spawn
```

The child's image was git.exe from the installed Git for Windows distribution. Its working directory was the affected project repository. Paths, repository names, commit IDs, account details, and conversation content are intentionally omitted from this public report.

## Isolation results

- A clean restart verified zero ChatGPT/Codex processes before launching the desktop. It froze again within about 15 seconds, before another IDE/CLI Codex backend was present during the observation. Leftover backends do not explain this reproduction.
- Isolating the most recently used conversation and its seven child conversations did not fix the freeze.
- Restoring that conversation family while Git discovery remained paused succeeded: eight session files, 25 turns, and 1,303 history items were readable again. The restarted desktop window remained responsive.
- SQLite integrity checks and session JSON validation passed. This trigger does not require treating the history as corrupt.
- The relevant freeze observations had zero ResizeObserver-loop messages. Historical layout-loop warnings alone do not explain this captured native stall.

## Independent process-creation probes

Short read-only Git commands completed normally, including git --version and a one-file diff. Replaying the long diff in an independent PowerShell/.NET Process.Start probe also blocked inside process creation.

Additional padding probes on the same machine:

| Probe | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Git --version with padding targeting approximately 32,000 total characters | Completed normally |
| Git --version with padding targeting 32,500 total characters; actual total about 32,492 | Process creation blocked |
| Git --version with padding targeting 32,700 total characters; actual total about 32,692 | Process creation blocked |
| cmd.exe with padding targeting approximately 32,500 characters | Process creation blocked |

This points to a long-command process-creation problem on the affected Windows environment, not uniquely to Git. These values are observations, not a universal cutoff. No vendor/security product has been established as the cause.

### A short alternative was verified

A read-only metadata diff with the same baseline and diff flags, but without the individual path arguments, used a command line of approximately 352 characters. It completed in 2.93 seconds and returned 466 changed entries (112,741 output bytes). This demonstrates that this repository can be compared without constructing a 32K-character command. Integrating this alternative into the desktop would still require filtering the result to the requested paths and preserving the intended rename semantics; it has not been installed as a desktop patch.

Microsoft documents a maximum CreateProcessW command-line size of 32,767 characters, including the terminating null: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessw

## Confirmed temporary workaround

Launch the desktop with a process-scoped GIT_DIR pointing to a deliberately nonexistent directory. Git then reports that the project is not a repository, and the automatic diff path is not reached.

This left the repositories and Windows global environment unchanged. After this launch, the main window remained responsive during two minutes of checks, and the user confirmed that project switching and opening conversations worked again. The conversation family was subsequently restored and the restarted window also stayed responsive.

This is a workaround: desktop Git functionality is unavailable, and child terminals/agent commands may inherit the GIT_DIR value. Removing GIT_DIR in a child shell allows normal Git use there. A regular launch without the workaround can retrigger the freeze.

## Bundled-code observation and possible fixes

Read-only inspection of this installed version's JavaScript bundle found the tracked review-summary command builder in .vite/build/worker.js. The minified function c4 constructs an argument array equivalent to:

```js
[...diffArgs, ...whitespaceOptions,
 '--find-renames', '--raw', '--no-abbrev', '--numstat', '-z',
 '--', ...paths]
```

That construction does not itself bound the accumulated path arguments. A separate untracked-file path already contains batching logic using a length budget and a file-count cap. A patch should audit both the summary path and other large multi-path diff calls, rather than assuming the untracked batching protects all Git launches.

Suggested maintainer fixes:

1. Bound the final Windows command length, accounting for executable name, flags, UTF-16 length, and Windows quoting/escaping. Use a generous margin below the OS maximum.
2. Avoid passing every changed path when a short whole-repository metadata diff followed by filtering is sufficient. Alternatively, batch paths while preserving correct rename detection and output semantics across boundaries. Do not assume git diff accepts the git add --pathspec-from-file flags.
3. Isolate native process creation in a separate utility/helper process so that a stuck CreateProcessW cannot block the main UI. A JavaScript timeout on the already blocked thread is insufficient.
4. Provide a supported option to pause automatic Git refresh while retaining normal project/chat use.

The installed app has not been patched. These are code-level findings and proposed fixes, not a claim that a permanent fix has been applied or that a specific driver is responsible.

## Related reports

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53697 describes an app-server-wide stall during an MCP server spawn. This report concerns the ChatGPT.exe window thread, automatic Git diff, and a long path-argument list, so the component and reproduction trigger differ. Both suggest that process-creation stalls should be isolated from critical threads; the precise underlying Windows cause is not assumed to be the same.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35776 describes a background Git loop and system resource exhaustion.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48666 describes accumulating Git processes and severe memory pressure.

They may share the automatic Git trigger, but this report adds a specifically captured long-command NtCreateUserProcess/uv_spawn stall with a process-scoped workaround. It is not claiming those reports have the identical root cause.

issues.title: Android Remote saves phone-started threads under `openai`, then hides them when the host's default provider is custom

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Codex Desktop 26.1007.30912 (build 20156), bundled app-server 0.162.0-alpha.17.2. Phone: ChatGPT for Android, current release on 2026-10-13. The host logs the phone as `client_name="codex_chatgpt_android_remote"`, `client_version="dev"`.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT (`planType: prolite`)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

On a host whose default provider is custom, every thread I start from ChatGPT Android Remote is saved under `openai`, but the phone's thread list only shows threads saved under the host's default provider. A thread started on the phone is visible while it runs, then drops out of the phone's list once it goes idle. Codex Desktop still lists it.

Host config, abbreviated:

```toml
model_provider = "custom"
openai_base_url = "<redacted>"   # the built-in openai provider is also routed, so both providers run turns normally

[model_providers.custom]
name = "Custom proxy"
base_url = "<redacted>"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = true
```

**Start and list disagree on the provider.** I matched every `thread/start` in the host log (`~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite`) on 2026-10-13 to the row it created in `~/.codex/state_5.sqlite`:

| Client that sent `thread/start` | Saved threads | Saved `model_provider` |
|---|---|---|
| `codex_chatgpt_android_remote` | 3 | `openai` (3 of 3) |
| `Codex Desktop` (user threads, automations, agent-created threads) | 9 | `custom` (9 of 9) |

The phone's list matches `thread/list` with `modelProviders` omitted, which the app-server resolves to the host default (#48358, #24648). Calling `thread/list` on the host with a `cwd` filter for one project:

| `modelProviders` | Threads returned |
|---|---|
| omitted | 2, both `custom`, the same 2 the phone shows |
| `[]` | 46 |
| `["openai"]` | 43 |

**What this looks like on the phone.** The newest thread in a project is often the missing one, because recent work started from the phone is saved under `openai`. Three projects on the same host:

- Project A shows its 2 `custom` threads. The other 44 are hidden, including one active the same evening as the visible ones.
- Project B hides its newest thread, which was started from the phone that afternoon, and shows 4 older `custom` threads.
- Project C shows the running thread plus 4 older `custom` threads, and hides two `openai` threads that were active earlier the same day. One of the two was started from the phone.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On a macOS host, set `model_provider` to a custom Responses provider (as above), stay signed in with ChatGPT, and enable Remote Control.
2. From ChatGPT for Android, open the host, start a new thread in any project, and let the turn finish.
3. On the host, check the saved provider: `sqlite3 ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite "select model_provider from threads order by created_at desc limit 1"` returns `openai`.
4. Close and reopen the thread list on the phone. The new thread is gone. Codex Desktop still shows it.
5. Optional: on the host, call `thread/list` with a `cwd` filter, once with `modelProviders` omitted and once with `modelProviders: []`. Only the second includes the phone-started thread.

### What is the expected behavior?

A thread started from the phone stays in the phone's list. Either change would do that:

- The Android Remote client sends `modelProviders: []` on `thread/list`, the spelling recommended in #48358, so the phone sees the same threads as Desktop.
- Remote `thread/start` saves the host's configured `model_provider`, so start and list agree.

The first also brings back Desktop threads that were saved under a non-default provider.

### Additional information

- **Thread cap and order within a project.** After the provider filter, the phone showed at most 4 idle threads per project, ordered by `updated_at` (last rollout write) instead of `recency_at` (last activity), which is how Desktop orders them. In two projects the phone's order matched `updated_at` descending exactly and the 5th thread was dropped. In one of them a thread sat at the top because its rollout file was written hours after its last turn, and in the other two threads appeared in the opposite order from their last activity. This pushes the most recently active thread out of view even among threads that pass the filter.
- **Related:** #24780 reports remote tasks disappearing on a custom-provider host where the phone-started task ran under the custom provider. Here the phone-started task is saved under `openai`, so the start/list mismatch hides it from the other direction. #48358 and #24648 cover the omitted-`modelProviders` default. #15494 covers provider switching hiding history. #22806 and #36454 cover project order on the phone.
- **Workarounds tried:** Switching the host default to `openai` only swaps which threads disappear. Rewriting the saved provider on existing threads would make the list complete but changes the provider used on resume, which #5658 was written to avoid.

4. The profile avatar continued to work normally on the external monitor.

No restart, logout/login, cache clearing, or authentication changes were required.

## Expected behavior

Clicking the profile avatar should open the profile/account menu regardless of which display the application window is on.

## Actual behavior

The avatar visually receives the click and shows the normal pressed animation, but the profile menu does not appear.

The issue is resolved by moving the application window to another display and then moving it back.

## Steps observed

1. Use ChatGPT/Codex with a MacBook built-in display and an external monitor.
2. Place the application window on the external monitor.
3. Click the profile avatar in the bottom-left corner.
4. The avatar shows a click animation, but the profile menu does not open.
5. `Cmd + ,` still opens Settings normally.
6. Move the application window to the MacBook built-in display.
7. The profile menu starts working again.
8. Move the window back to the external display.
9. The profile menu continues working.

I have not yet confirmed a fully deterministic reproduction sequence.

## Workaround

Move the application window from the external monitor to the built-in MacBook display, then move it back.

This immediately restored the profile menu for me.

## Environment

- ChatGPT/Codex App version: 154.0.8037.57
- Subscription: ChatGPT Plus
- Device: MacBook Pro 14-inch, 2021
- Chip: Apple M1 Pro
- Memory: 16 GB
- macOS: Tahoe 26.5
- Display configuration: MacBook built-in display + external monitor

## Additional observation

The avatar was visually receiving the click, so this does not appear to be a simple pointer-event failure.

Because moving the window between displays immediately fixes the problem, this may be related to display/window coordinate state, popup positioning, display scale factor changes, or stale UI state when the window is on an external display.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Connect the MacBook to an external monitor.
2. Open the ChatGPT/Codex desktop app.
3. Move the app window to the external monitor.
4. Click the profile avatar in the bottom-left corner.
5. The avatar shows the normal click/pressed animation, but the profile menu does not open.
6. `Cmd + ,` still opens Settings normally, and account/usage information can still be loaded.
7. Move the ChatGPT/Codex window from the external monitor to the MacBook's built-in display.
8. Click the profile avatar again. The profile menu now opens normally.
9. Move the window back to the external monitor.
10. The profile avatar continues to work normally.

I have not yet found a fully deterministic way to trigger the bug, but moving the window between displays reliably fixed it in my case.

No restart, logout/login, or cache clearing was required.

### What is the expected behavior?

Clicking the profile avatar should always open the profile/account menu, regardless of whether the ChatGPT/Codex window is on the MacBook's built-in display or an external monitor.

Moving the application window between displays should not be required to restore the profile menu.

### Additional information

The avatar visually receives the click and shows the normal pressed animation, but no menu appears. This suggests the button itself is receiving input, while the profile popup/menu may fail to render or may be positioned incorrectly when the window is on the external display.

issues.title: thread/list: omitted modelProviders filters to the server default provider, hiding other threads

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
## Problem

Codex app-server's `thread/list` treats an omitted `modelProviders` parameter as "filter to the server's configured default provider" rather than "all threads".

Observed on `codex app-server` 0.155.0-alpha.16 / 0.158.0-alpha.2 (Windows), driven over the WebSocket JSON-RPC API:

- Config: `model_provider = "custom"` + a `[model_providers.custom]` table
- Threads created earlier under the built-in `openai` provider (~5,200 rows)
- `thread/list` **without** `modelProviders` → returns only the threads tagged `custom` (1 item)
- `thread/list` with `modelProviders: []` → returns all threads

So omission and an explicit empty list behave differently, and omission silently hides most of the user's history.

## Impact

Clients that omit `modelProviders` — notably the ChatGPT mobile remote-control client — render an almost-empty thread list on any host whose default provider differs from the provider its existing threads were created with. Nothing in the host's data is lost; the threads are simply filtered out of the default view.

## Suggestion

Either:

- treat omitted `modelProviders` as "no provider filter" (same as `[]`), or
- document the default-provider semantics and have remote-control clients send the full configured provider list explicitly.

Repro steps: configure a second provider, set it as `model_provider`, keep older `openai`-tagged threads, then compare `thread/list` with and without `modelProviders`.

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Codex Desktop: `26.519.81530`  
Codex CLI: `0.133.0`

### What platform is your computer?

macOS `26.3.1 (a)` (`25D771280a`)

### What issue are you seeing?

When Codex Desktop on macOS is configured to use a custom OpenAI-compatible Responses API provider, Codex Mobile remote control can start a new task and the Mac host executes it successfully. However, after refreshing the Codex Mobile thread/task list, that task disappears from the mobile list.

The task is not deleted locally. It remains present in the Mac host's local Codex state (`~/.codex/state_5.sqlite`) and rollout JSONL under `~/.codex/sessions/...`.

This appears related to custom-provider thread list/history filtering, but the user-visible symptom is specifically in Codex Mobile remote control:

- Mobile can create/send the task to the Mac host.
- The Mac host executes the task using the custom provider.
- The live task is visible while it is running.
- After refreshing/reopening the mobile list, the task is no longer visible.
- Threads created with the normal `openai` provider are visible in the mobile history/list.
- Existing local `custom_responses_provider`/custom-provider Mac threads are not discoverable from the mobile history/list.

The custom provider is configured in `~/.codex/config.toml` similarly to:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.5"
model_provider = "custom_responses_provider"

[model_providers.custom_responses_provider]
name = "Custom Responses Provider"
base_url = "<redacted OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint>"
wire_api = "responses"
env_key = "CUSTOM_RESPONSES_API_KEY"
```

The Mac host is still logged in to the ChatGPT/OpenAI account for Codex Mobile remote control. Remote control enrollment is present and working: mobile remote control can reach the Mac and submit work.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Codex Desktop for macOS, configure a custom model provider in `~/.codex/config.toml`, for example `model_provider = "custom_responses_provider"` with `wire_api = "responses"`.
2. Keep Codex Desktop logged in to the ChatGPT/OpenAI account used by Codex Mobile.
3. Connect Codex Mobile to the Mac host through remote control.
4. From Codex Mobile, start a new task/thread on that Mac host.
5. Observe that the Mac host receives the task and executes it successfully through the custom provider.
6. Refresh or reopen the Codex Mobile task/thread list.
7. Observe that the newly created custom-provider task disappears from the mobile list.
8. Switch the Mac host back to the normal `openai` provider and create a task. That task appears in the mobile history/list as expected.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex Mobile should list and allow reopening/continuing local Mac-host threads created through remote control even when the host used a custom model provider.

More specifically:

1. A task created from Codex Mobile and executed on the Mac host with `model_provider != "openai"` should remain visible after mobile list refresh.
2. The mobile history/list should include local host threads across providers, or at least include threads for the currently connected host regardless of provider.
3. Opening a custom-provider thread from mobile should route continuation back to the same Mac host and preserve the thread's persisted model provider.

### What is the actual behavior?

1. The custom-provider task runs successfully on the Mac host.
2. It may appear temporarily while live/running.
3. After refreshing the Codex Mobile list, it disappears.
4. Local Mac state still contains the thread and rollout file.
5. Normal `openai` provider threads remain visible in the mobile history/list.

### Local evidence

On the affected machine, local SQLite state shows custom-provider threads are persisted and not archived:

```text
model_provider  source  thread_source  archived  n
--------------  ------  -------------  --------  --
custom_provider  cli     user           0         1
custom_provider  vscode  user           0         7
openai          cli                    0         17
openai          exec                   0         12
openai          vscode                 0         34
openai          vscode  user           0         8
```

Remote control enrollment exists locally, and the mobile-to-Mac execution path works:

```text
app_server_client_name  server_name               websocket_url_len
----------------------  ------------------------  -----------------
Codex Desktop           <local Mac host name>      56
```

The custom-provider threads also have rollout JSONL files under `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/`.

### Related issues

This seems related to existing custom-provider history/list issues, but this report is specifically about Codex Mobile remote-control visibility after refreshing the mobile list:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/20184
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/19088
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/20004
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/15494
- https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/19287

### Security notes

No API key or private provider URL is included here. Thread titles and message content are intentionally omitted.

issues.title: (app-server and Desktop) thread/list treats omitted modelProviders as current-provider filter instead of all providers

labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: custom-model
