prs.title: fix(core): let /ide enable reconnect after the IDE server restarts
prs.body:
## Summary

After VS Code's **Developer: Reload Window** (or an extension update/disable), the CLI running in the surviving integrated terminal reported `🔴 Disconnected: IDE connection error…`, and `/ide enable` kept failing with `Failed to connect to IDE companion extension…` until VS Code was fully closed and reopened.

#29674 fixed the server side of #28785 (`IdeServer.stop()` hanging and leaking its port file). This PR fixes the **client side**, which could not survive an IDE-server restart even with a fixed extension — and still cannot with the Marketplace extension (v0.20.0), which predates #29674 and leaks a port file on every reload.

Two defects in `IdeClient`:

1. **Discovery tried a single port file.** The reloaded extension host starts a new server (new port, new token, new port file), but the terminal's `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_SERVER_PORT` / `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_AUTH_TOKEN` stay frozen at the old values. `getConnectionConfigFromFile()` used that frozen port as the tie-breaker, so a leaked old file was selected deterministically, `connect()` never fell through to the live file, and the env fallback pointed at the same dead port.
2. **A superseded client kept driving the state.** `onerror`/`onclose` were bound to the `IdeClient`, not to the client that registered them, and `establish*Connection()` never closed the previous client. After a successful `/ide enable`, the old transport's SSE reconnection attempts against the dead port (1 s, 2.5 s) flipped the state back to `Disconnected` while the new connection was healthy.

Two source files in `packages/core`, no public API change, no new `eslint-disable`.

## Details

### `ide-connection-utils.ts`

- New `getConnectionConfigsFromFile(pid)` returns **every** workspace-valid candidate, best first: the file whose port matches `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_SERVER_PORT` (the window the terminal belongs to), then the rest in the existing `sortConnectionFiles()` order. When no file matches the workspace it still returns the single best-sorted entry so the detailed "Directory mismatch" error is preserved.
- `getConnectionConfigFromFile()` is now `candidates[0]` — the ranking of the preferred file is **unchanged** (all 46 pre-existing tests pass untouched). The three inline config types were replaced by an exported `IdeConnectionConfig` alias. The module is not re-exported from core's index.

### `ide-client.ts`

- `connect()` iterates the candidates, each with **its own** auth token, before the env fallbacks. Behaviour is identical whenever the first candidate answers — the only case that worked before.
- `registerClientHandlers()` captures the client it is registering for; `onerror`/`onclose` no-op once `this.client` has moved on.
- New `retireClient()`, called by both `establishHttpConnection()` and `establishStdioConnection()` before creating a new `Client`: detaches the handlers and `close()`s the superseded client (aborting its socket and retry timers); a rejected `close()` is debug-logged.

### Deliberately out of scope

- Deleting stale files from the client (unsafe when the CLI runs in a sandbox/remote where a port is legitimately unreachable); an extension-side GC of dead sibling files is a natural follow-up.
- Auto-reconnect on disconnect (policy change). Users still see one `IDE connection error… run /ide enable` line after a reload; this PR makes that documented recovery actually work.
- Carried over: a stale file whose port was reused by an unrelated process that accepts TCP but never answers would wait for the SDK's `initialize` timeout (same exposure as before, now per candidate).

## Related Issues

Related to #28785 — client-side follow-up to #29674 (which fixed `IdeServer.stop()`; the issue was closed by it, but the reload symptom it mentions remained).

## How to Validate

**Unit / integration tests**

```bash
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/ide/
# 7 files, 181 passed | 1 skipped
```

- `ide-connection-utils.test.ts` — +9 cases for `getConnectionConfigsFromFile` (legacy file, empty/error paths, workspace filtering and order, env-port promotion with fallbacks retained, no env match, mismatch → single entry, malformed files, singular returns the first candidate).
- `ide-client.test.ts` — +9 cases: candidate iteration (next candidate on failure with its own token, stop at first success, http → stdio candidate, env fallback after all candidates, disconnected when nothing answers) and reconnecting (superseded client closed and detached, its late error/close ignored, errors from the current client still reported, rejected `close()` tolerated). Also fixes the latent singleton reset in that file (`instancePromise`, not `instance`) so its tests are actually isolated.
- `ide-client.server-restart.test.ts` (new) — real `node:http` MCP servers and real port files in a private `TMPDIR`, no SDK mocks: (1) leaked file matching the frozen env port, (2) late errors from the superseded transport after a clean restart, (3) several leaked files with no env hint, (4) the env-matching window still wins when several servers are alive. (1) and (2) fail on `main` with exactly the user-facing messages above and pass with this change.

**End-to-end with the real `/ide` commands** (harness kept out of the tree): the real `ideCommand()` actions from `packages/cli`, the real `IdeClient`, and the real companion `IDEServer` (vscode API mocked), executed as stash-fix → rebuild → run → restore → rebuild → run:

| Step | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/ide status` | `🟢 Connected` | `🟢 Connected` |
| Reload Window (A: v0.20.0 leaks file · B: fixed extension) | — | — |
| `/ide status` ≈1 s later | `🔴 Disconnected: IDE connection error…` | same (by design, one notification) |
| `/ide enable` | A: `🔴 Disconnected: Failed to connect to IDE companion extension…` · B: `🟢 Connected` | A & B: `🟢 Connected` |
| `/ide status` 4.5 s later | B: `🔴 Disconnected: IDE connection error…` | A & B: `🟢 Connected`, `isDiffingEnabled() === true` |

**Manually in VS Code**

1. `rm -f /tmp/gemini/ide/gemini-ide-server-*.json` (macOS: `$TMPDIR/gemini/ide/`), open the repo, run `gemini` in the integrated terminal, `/ide status` → `🟢 Connected to VS Code`.
2. **Developer: Reload Window**; keep the terminal. Within ~1–2 s the CLI prints `IDE connection error… run /ide enable`.
3. `/ide enable` → **before:** `🔴 Disconnected: Failed to connect to IDE companion extension in VS Code…` (with the Marketplace extension; `ls /tmp/gemini/ide/` shows the leaked old file next to the new one) — **after:** `🟢 Connected to VS Code`, and `/ide status` stays connected; diffs work.

**CI parity (Linux, Node 20.20.2):** all `ci.yml` Lint-job steps (lockfile, eslint, actionlint, shellcheck, yamllint, build, typecheck, prettier, settings docs `--check`, sensitive keywords, actions pinning) and both Test (Linux) shards + `test:scripts` + bundle + bundle/npx smoke tests ran locally and passed; `npm run preflight` passed (cli 7327, core 8341, a2a 177, companion 62, scripts 202 tests).

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed) — not needed: docs already tell users to run `/ide enable` to reconnect and tell plugin authors to delete their discovery file on deactivation; this change makes that recovery work.
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any) — none
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
  - [x] Linux
    - [x] npm run
    - [x] npx
    - [ ] Docker

prs.title: fix(cli): handle a registry port in sandbox image name parsing
prs.body:
## Summary

`parseImageName()` splits an image reference on *every* colon, so a registry host that carries a port is misparsed: the port is taken as the tag, the real tag is lost, and a `/` survives into the result — which then gets handed to the container runtime as `--name`/`--hostname`, where `/` is not a legal character. A colon is now only treated as the tag separator when it comes after the last `/`.

## Details

```ts
parseImageName('localhost:5000/my-image:v1');
// before: 'localhost-5000/my-image'
// after:  'my-image-v1'
```

The old `const [fullName, tag] = image.split(':')` destructures positionally, so for a reference with a port `fullName` becomes `localhost` and `tag` becomes `5000/my-image`; the `split('/').at(-1)` fallback then leaves the host in the name. The reference grammar is `[registry[:port]/]name[:tag]`, so the tag separator is the last colon that comes after the last slash.

This is an untested hole rather than an unsupported configuration: `sandboxUtils.test.ts` already asserts `parseImageName('gcr.io/my-project/my-image:v1') === 'my-image-v1'` in `should handle registry path`, and `git blame` shows that test and the function were introduced by the same commit, so registry references are intended to work. The fix keeps that case byte-identical.

The two new tests are one for the return value and one for the invariant that broke along with it — that the result never contains a path separator — since that is the part a container runtime would reject.

Digest references (`img@sha256:…`) behave the same before and after; I did not add a test for them, to avoid pinning a behavior that is not currently specified either way.

## Related Issues

Closes #29572

## How to Validate

The results below are earlier implementation validation. The October 13 update only removes a tool co-author trailer: the source tree is identical to the previous head, and no tests were rerun for that history change.

1. `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/utils/sandboxUtils.test.ts` — 52 passed.

   Both new cases fail on the base commit `38700b4b3`:

   ```
   × should handle registry path with a port
     → expected 'localhost-5000/my-image' to be 'my-image-v1'
   × should never produce a name containing a path separator
     → expected 'localhost-5000/ns/my-image' not to contain '/'
   ```

2. `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/utils/` — 46 files, 773 passed.
3. `npx eslint packages/cli/src/utils/sandboxUtils.ts packages/cli/src/utils/sandboxUtils.test.ts` — clean.
4. `npx prettier --check` on both files — clean.

Manual check: with `GEMINI_SANDBOX_IMAGE=localhost:5000/my-image:v1`, the container name is now `my-image-v1`.

I did not run a container runtime, so I have not observed the `--name` rejection itself; the falsifiable claim here is the return value of `parseImageName`, which is what the tests pin.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [x] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [x] MacOS

    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
  - [ ] Linux
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker

Unit tests, ESLint and Prettier on macOS. The change is a pure string-parsing function with no platform-specific behavior, so I did not exercise the packaged `npx` path or the container sandboxes. The CLA checker already covers the author. Its previous failure came from an old tool co-author trailer, which has now been removed without changing the author or source tree.

prs.title: fix(core): keep line terminators when truncating
prs.body:
## Summary

`truncateString()` now keeps line terminators instead of silently deleting them, and counts them against `maxLength`. One character of change (the `s` flag on the grapheme-cluster regex) plus a regression test.

Fixes #29562.

## Details

`truncateString` walks the string with a hand-rolled grapheme-cluster regex:

```ts
const graphemeRegex = /(?:[\uD800-\uDBFF][\uDC00-\uDFFF]|.)\p{M}*/gu;
```

The `u` flag is there for the `\p{M}` property escape, but there was no `s` (dotAll) flag, so `.` cannot match a line terminator. `exec` still advances past the unmatched code units, so `\n`, `\r`, ` ` and ` ` were never emitted and cost nothing against the budget:

```ts
truncateString('aa\nbb\ncc', 4, ''); // before 'aabb'  → after 'aa\nb'
truncateString('a\nb\nc', 3, '');    // before 'abc'   → after 'a\nb'
truncateString('x\r\ny', 3, '');     // before 'xy'    → after 'x\r'
```

The second line is the budget half of the bug: a `maxLength` of 3 consumed five source characters, because the two terminators were free.

Each terminator is a single-code-unit grapheme cluster, exactly like the surrogate-pair branch in the same regex already handles, so nothing else in the loop needed to change.

This is the shared truncation helper, and the callers pass it content that is normally multi-line:

- `packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts:404` — `truncateString(output, 5000)` on background-command output
- `packages/core/src/tools/web-fetch.ts:700` and `:749` — fetched page content against `MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH`
- `packages/core/src/telemetry/trace.ts:60,68` and `packages/core/src/telemetry/semantic.ts:121`

The change is deliberately narrow: I did not touch *where* truncation splits, so a string without line terminators truncates exactly as before and no existing test in the file moves.

## Related Issues

- #29562 — the defect report, with the caller list and the root-cause analysis.

## How to Validate

Earlier implementation checks are below. October 13 changed only commit metadata; source trees are identical and tests were not rerun.

On the base commit, with only the new test applied:

```
FAIL src/utils/textUtils.test.ts > truncateString > should preserve newlines when truncating multi-line text
AssertionError: expected 'aabb' to be 'aa\nb'
 ❯ src/utils/textUtils.test.ts:131:49
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 9 passed | 41 skipped (51)
```

On this branch:

```

prs.title: fix(core): treat monthly spending cap as a terminal quota error
prs.body:
## Summary

A 429 whose `details` array is empty and whose message is a project spending cap was classified as retryable. The TUI then treated it as transient high demand and kept retrying. The same message is now a terminal quota error, and the dialog shows the API text.

## Details

`classifyGoogleError` fell through to `RetryableQuotaError` when a 429 had no structured details and did not match a capacity or "Please retry in" pattern. Account-level spending caps are not transient, so fallback reset the attempt counter and the notice looped. The classifier now returns `TerminalQuotaError` for HTTP 400/429/499 spending-cap messages before that fallback. The quota dialog keeps the API message instead of replacing it with "high demand" or a generic usage-limit line. Ordinary rate limits, 503s, and capacity exhaustion are unchanged.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29504

## How to Validate

1. `npx vitest run src/utils/googleQuotaErrors.test.ts` in `packages/core`.
   Expected: the monthly spending-cap case with empty `details` is a `TerminalQuotaError`, not a `RetryableQuotaError`.
2. `npx vitest run src/ui/hooks/useQuotaAndFallback.test.ts` in `packages/cli`.
   Expected: the spending-cap dialog text is the API message and does not say "high demand".

prs.body:
## Summary

Shell and internal git environments were overriding `core.sshCommand` with an empty string. Git then tried to exec a blank SSH binary and failed with `fatal: unable to fork` on SSH remotes. The override now points at `ssh`, which still blocks a repo-configured command while letting the system client run.

`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*=core.sshCommand` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*=` was injected in both the shell runner and `getSafeGitEnv`. An empty value is not the same as "unset": Git treats it as the SSH program name. Replacing it with `ssh` keeps the security override and matches the workaround reporters already use via `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`.

`tryParseGithubUrl` stripped `.git` with `String.replace('.git', '')`, which

prs.title: fix(core): ensure YOLO and AUTO_EDIT modes downgrade redirected shell commands (#29310)
prs.body:
Fixes #29310

 Description
In `PolicyEngine`, shell commands containing redirection (`>`, `<`, `2>&1`, heredocs, etc.) previously bypassed downgrade to `ASK_USER` in `ApprovalMode.YOLO` and `ApprovalMode.AUTO_EDIT` unless a rule with `argsPattern` was configured. Additionally:
- When no rules matched in YOLO mode, shell tool calls bypassed `checkShellCommand()`, leaving unconfigured shell commands uninspected for redirection.
- When shell command parsing encountered errors or syntax issues, `checkShellCommand()` early-returned `ALLOW` in YOLO mode before checking `shouldDowngradeForRedirection()`.

 Changes
1. Redirection Downgrade: Removed the early-return bypass for `YOLO` and `AUTO_EDIT` modes in `shouldDowngradeForRedirection()`. Redirection now always downgrades `ALLOW` to `ASK_USER` (or `DENY` in non-interactive mode) unless explicitly opted into via `allowRedirection: true`.
2. Parser Error Handling: Added `shouldDowngradeForRedirection()` check prior to the YOLO early-return when shell command parsing fails or has syntax errors. Commands with redirection fallback to `defaultDecision` (`ASK_USER` / `DENY`), while clean unparseable commands without redirection continue to be allowed in YOLO mode unless restricted by `argsPattern`.
3. Unmatched Tool Fallback: Ensured shell tool calls in YOLO mode without matching rules route through `checkShellCommand()` with a baseline decision of `PolicyDecision.ALLOW` so redirection checks are consistently applied.
4. Shell Utils Fallback: Added fallback regex validation in `hasRedirection()` for bash commands when syntax errors are present in the AST, matching the safety behavior of the PowerShell parser.
5. Tests: Added comprehensive test coverage for YOLO and AUTO_EDIT modes covering clean, redirected, and unparseable commands with and without explicit `allowRedirection` flags.

prs.title: fix(cli): prevent right-hand border bleed in scrollable tool containers
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes a UI rendering glitch where bordered tool output containers (such as expanded `WriteFile` and `Edit` views in compact mode and scrollable tool results in alternate buffer mode) intermittently break or bleed past the right-hand border when displaying both a nested vertical scrollbar and dynamically wrapped text.

## Details

    - **Root Cause:**
      - In `DenseToolMessage`, the outer bordered `<Box>` (with `borderStyle="round"` and `paddingX={1}`, consuming 4 columns of border/padding chrome) was capped at `PAYLOAD_MAX_WIDTH` (`124`), leaving `120` columns of inner width. However, `ScrollableList` was passed `Math.min(PAYLOAD_MAX_WIDTH, ...)` without subtracting `PAYLOAD_BORDER_CHROME_WIDTH`, allowing the inner list to span `124` columns on wide terminals (`terminalWidth >= 135`), overwriting the right- hand border `│` and pushing the scrollbar outside the container. On narrower terminals, subtracting `PAYLOAD_SCROLL_GUTTER = 4` from `ScrollableList`'s outer width left a 4-column gap before the right border. Additionally, `colorizeCode` and `renderDiffLines` received `terminalWidth - PAYLOAD_MARGIN_LEFT` instead of the safe inner content width.
      - In `ToolResultDisplay`, when `isAlternateBuffer` is enabled, content is wrapped in `<Scrollable width={childWidth}>` (which reserves 1 column via `paddingRight={1}` for the vertical scrollbar), but nested components with explicit width constraints (`MarkdownDisplay`, `DiffRenderer`, `SubagentProgressDisplay`, `AnsiOutputText`) were passed `childWidth` instead of `childWidth - 1`.
 
    - **Fix:**
      - Explicitly calculate `safeContentWidth = Math.max(0, totalContainerWidth - borderSpace - scrollbarBuffer)` in both `DenseToolMessage` and ToolResultDisplay`.
      - Apply `safeContentWidth` to nested `<Box>` and text-wrapping/diff/markdown containers so wrapped text and diff hunk separators never collide with the vertical scrollbar or overwrite the right-hand border.

## Related Issues

Fixes #24768

## How to Validate

   1. Run the unit and regression tests for `DenseToolMessage` and `ToolResultDisplay`:
       ```bash
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/components/messages/DenseToolMessage.test.tsx src/ui/components/messages/ToolResultDisplay.test.tsx

  2. Run typecheck and lint:
    npm run typecheck -w @google/gemini-cli
    npm run lint

  3. In the CLI with alternate buffer and compact tool output enabled (useAlternateBuffer: true, compactToolOutput: true), trigger a WriteFile or Edit tool call with >15 lines and long wrapped lines, expand the diff subview, and verify across narrow and wide terminal widths that the vertical scrollbar remains inside the box and the right-hand border (│) is intact on every row.

prs.title: fix(ui): implement synchronized output and isolate spinner rendering
prs.body:
## Summary

Implement terminal synchronized output around interactive UI frame writes and isolate spinner rendering state to eliminate screen flickering in terminal multiplexers such as `tmux`.

## Details

- **Synchronized Output Stream Wrapper (`packages/core/src/utils/stdio.ts`, `packages/cli/src/interactiveCli.tsx`):**
  - Added `wrapWithSynchronizedOutput` and `createSynchronizedStdout` (along with the `synchronizedOutput` option in `createWorkingStdio`) to bracket interactive UI frame writes with terminal synchronized output sequences:
    - Standard terminals: DEC Private Mode 2026 (`\x1b[?2026h` / `\x1b[?2026l`), which is buffered atomically by supporting terminals and silently ignored by non-supporting ANSI terminals.
    - `tmux` environments (`process.env.TMUX`): `tmux` DCS synchronized update sequences (`\x1bP=1s\x1b\\` / `\x1bP=2s\x1b\\`).
  - Preserved passthrough behavior for standalone terminal mode sequences and `dumb` terminals.
- **Spinner State Isolation & Tmux Throttling (`CliSpinner.tsx`, `GeminiSpinner.tsx`, `GeminiRespondingSpinner.tsx`, `LoadingIndicator.tsx`, `StatusRow.tsx`):**
  - Localized spinner tick intervals strictly within `CliSpinner` and `GeminiSpinner` and wrapped `CliSpinner`, `GeminiSpinner`, `GeminiRespondingSpinner`, `LoadingIndicator`, `StatusNode`, and `StatusRow` in `React.memo` so frame ticks do not trigger parent or sibling re-renders.
  - Adjusted the spinner frame and color gradient interval to `120ms` (`TMUX_SPINNER_INTERVAL_MS`) when `process.env.TMUX` is present to reduce PTY redraw overhead.

## Related Issues

Fixes #22004

## How to Validate

1. Build all packages and run type checks:
   ```bash
   npm run build
   npm run typecheck
   ```
2. Run unit tests for `stdio` synchronized output and spinner component isolation:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/stdio.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/components/CliSpinner.test.tsx src/ui/components/GeminiRespondingSpinner.test.tsx src/ui/components/LoadingIndicator.test.tsx src/ui/components/StatusRow.test.tsx src/ui/components/Composer.test.tsx
   ```
3. Launch `gemini-cli` inside a `tmux` session and trigger a model response to verify smooth spinner updates without screen flickering.

prs.title: fix(ui): fix debug console height calculation and terminalBuffer flickering
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes Debug Console (`F12`) height/layout calculation bugs and improves rendering stability in `terminalBuffer` mode by enabling incremental rendering and static history item memoization with safe cache invalidation.

## Details

- **Debug Console (`F12`) height calculation ([`Composer.tsx`](packages/cli/src/ui/components/Composer.tsx))**: Fixed `debugConsoleMaxHeight` calculation to use `terminalHeight` (`rows`) from `useTerminalSize()` instead of `terminalWidth` (`columns`), preventing the Debug Console from expanding to 20% of the terminal column count on wide terminals.
- **Debug Console inner list viewport height ([`DetailedMessagesDisplay.tsx`](packages/cli/src/ui/components/DetailedMessagesDisplay.tsx))**: Subtracted the outer box border and header height (`headerAndBorderHeight = 4`) when passing `height` and `containerHeight` to the inner `<Box>` and `<ScrollableList>`, preventing the bottom 4 lines of log messages from being clipped and fixing scroll bounds.
- **Prevent unconstrained height / static refresh flash on `OpenDebugConsole` ([`AppContainer.tsx`](packages/cli/src/ui/AppContainer.tsx))**: Removed `setConstrainHeight(false)` from `openDebugConsole` so auto-opening the Debug Console on error does not uncap UI heights or trigger a `refreshStatic()` (`clearTerminal`) flash on the next keystroke. Also updated `refreshStatic` to increment `historyRemountKey` in `terminalBuffer` mode (without writing `ansiEscapes.clearTerminal`) so theme and markdown toggles invalidate `<StaticRender>` caches cleanly without screen flashing.
- **Enable `incrementalRendering` for `terminalBuffer` mode ([`interactiveCli.tsx`](packages/cli/src/interactiveCli.tsx))**: Allowed `incrementalRendering` when `config.getUseTerminalBuffer()` is active (in addition to `useAlternateBuffer`), avoiding full-frame log-update erasures on each thinking/streaming tick when `useAlternateBuffer: false` and `terminalBuffer: true`.
- **Mark non-interactive history items as static with cache invalidation ([`MainContent.tsx`](packages/cli/src/ui/components/MainContent.tsx))**: Expanded `isStaticItem` in `MainContent` to return `true` for completed, non-interactive history items (`user`, `gemini`, `gemini_content`, `thinking`, `info`, `warning`, `error`, `hint`, etc.) while keeping interactive/mutable items (`tool_group`, `compression`, `pending`, and `header` while `updateInfo.isUpdating` is active) dynamic, and included header/markdown/remount state in `keyExtractor` so `<StaticRender>` invalidates when those states change.

## Related Issues

Fixes #10673

## How to Validate

1. Run targeted unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/components/Composer.test.tsx src/ui/components/DetailedMessagesDisplay.test.tsx src/ui/components/MainContent.test.tsx src/ui/AppContainer.test.tsx src/gemini.test.tsx
   ```
2. Run typecheck and linter:
   ```bash
   npm run typecheck && npm run lint
   ```
3. Manual verification:
   - Start Gemini CLI in a wide terminal (e.g., 200x40) and press `F12` to open the Debug Console; verify its height is constrained to 20% of terminal rows and all log lines scroll cleanly without bottom clipping.
   - Run with `"useAlternateBuffer": false, "incrementalRendering": true, "terminalBuffer": true` and verify smooth streaming updates without full-viewport flicker.

prs.title: fix(cli): prevent session poisoning on rapid Ctrl-C interruption
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes a session poisoning race condition when a user rapidly presses `Ctrl+C` twice during tool execution or streaming. Previously, pressing `Ctrl+C` invoked `void cancelOngoingRequest?.()` as an unawaited, detached operation, and the second `Ctrl+C` immediately triggered `/quit` before cancelled tool calls were recorded to the session log. This left dangling `model` `functionCall` turns in `session-*.jsonl` without matching `user` `functionResponse` turns, causing `gemini --resume` to fail with `HTTP 400 Requests ending with a model turn are not supported`.

## Details

- **Refactor `cancelOngoingRequest` to return `Promise<void>` (`useGeminiStream.ts` & `useAgentStream.ts`):**
  - Updated `cancelOngoingRequest` in both [`useGeminiStream.ts`](packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.ts) and [`useAgentStream.ts`](packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useAgentStream.ts) to return a `Promise<void>` that awaits `agent.abort()` or in-flight tool scheduling bounded by a 1-second `Promise.race()` timeout.

- **Harmonize cancellation with session logs (`recordCompletedToolCalls`):**
  - Added `createCancelledToolCall` to synthesize a cancelled `CompletedToolCall` containing a filler `functionResponse` (`[Operation Cancelled] Reason: User cancelled operation`).
  - Immediately upon aborting in both the default flow (`useGeminiStream`) and the experimental agent loop (`useAgentStream`), any active, scheduled, or unsubmitted model-initiated tool calls are recorded via `chat.recordCompletedToolCalls(currentModel, synthesizedCalls)` so `session-*.jsonl` maintains valid `Model (functionCall) -> User (functionResponse)` turn alternation on resume.

- **Await in-flight cancellation on rapid double `Ctrl+C` (`AppContainer.tsx`):**
  - Stored the active `cancelOngoingRequest?.()` promise in `cancelPromiseRef` on `Command.QUIT` (`Ctrl+C`) and awaited it (bounded by a 1-second `Promise. race()` timeout) in `handleExitRepeat` and `slashCommandActions.quit` before exiting.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29588

## How to Validate

    1. Run targeted unit tests:
       ```bash
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useAgentStream.test.tsx src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx src/ui/AppContainer.test.tsx
       ```
    2. Run typecheck and lint:
       ```bash
       npm run typecheck
       npm run lint
       ```
    3. Manual verification:
       - Start `gemini` and trigger a tool call (e.g., a long-running shell command).
       - Rapidly double-tap `Ctrl+C` while the tool call is active; verify the CLI exits cleanly within ~1.5 seconds.
       - Restart with `gemini --resume` and send a follow-up prompt; verify the session resumes without `HTTP 400 Requests ending with a model turn are not supported` and `session-*.jsonl` contains matching `functionResponse` entries for the cancelled tool call.

prs.title: refactor(core,cli): emit tool call groups from the scheduler and drop the UI lookahead
prs.body:
`useGeminiStream` decided on its own which finished tool calls belong together. For sub-agent calls it looked ahead through the live tool list and held a finished call back until every following consecutive agent call had finished too, and it merged consecutive agent calls into one history item by checking the tool kind. A `TODO` in that code asked for `packages/core` to provide those boundaries instead. This change does that: the scheduler marks each run of two or more consecutive sub-agent calls in a batch with a shared `groupId`, and the hook only holds back and merges calls that share a `groupId`. The lookahead and the `Kind.Agent` checks are gone from the hook. For parallel sub-agents the behavior is the same as before.

## Details

- **`ToolCallRequestInfo.groupId` (`packages/core/src/scheduler/types.ts`)**: new optional field. Calls with the same value are presented, and treated as finished, together. The calls of a group are adjacent in their batch. A call that is not part of a group leaves it unset.
- **`Scheduler` (`packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.ts`)**:
  - `_startBatch` assigns the groups once per batch, after the requests are ordered, with the new `getToolCallGroupIds` helper. A run of two or more adjacent calls to tools of kind `Kind.Agent` shares the call ID of the first call in the run. A lone agent call and every other call get no group. A tool that is not registered counts as not being an agent.
  - A tail call keeps the group of the call it replaces.
  - The ID is part of the call request, so it is included in every `TOOL_CALLS_UPDATE` snapshot and stays with the call through its status changes. No new event type is needed.
- **`useGeminiStream` (`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.ts`)**, in the effect that pushes finished tools to history:
  - A finished call that has a `groupId` waits until every call with the same `groupId` has finished (success, error or cancelled). Calls ahead of the group are still pushed in order.
  - Calls with the same `groupId` are pushed as one history item. Calls without a `groupId` are pushed one by one as soon as they finish, as before.
  - The lookahead and its `TODO(#22883)` comment are removed, and the hook no longer imports `Kind`.
- **Unchanged behavior**:
  - `ToolGroupMessage` still derives how it draws consecutive agent calls from the tool kind. That also covers restored sessions, which do not go through the scheduler. Moving it to `groupId` would be a follow-up.
  - Execution is untouched: which calls run in parallel is still decided by `isParallelizable`.
  - Sequential agent calls are still grouped, because a group follows the order of the requests in the batch and not how the calls are executed.
- **Tests**:
  - `packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler_parallel.test.ts`: contiguous agent calls share the ID of the first call; a lone agent call is not grouped; a new group starts after a call that is not an agent; agent calls separated by another call or by an unregistered tool are not grouped; groups are computed after topic updates move to the front.
  - `packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.test.ts`: a tail call keeps the group of the call it replaces.
  - `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx`: new `Grouped Tool Calls` tests. A group is held back until all of its calls have finished and is then pushed as one item; failed and cancelled calls count as finished; calls are grouped by `groupId` and not by tool kind; calls without a `groupId` are pushed individually; finished calls ahead of a group that is still running are pushed while the group waits. The old lookahead had no direct test coverage.
  - On the previous code, 4 of the 7 new core tests and 2 of the 5 new hook tests fail. The others pass before and after the change, because they pin behavior that is meant to stay the same.

## Related Issues

Fixes [#28258](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/28258)

## How to Validate

1. Run the targeted unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/scheduler/scheduler_parallel.test.ts src/scheduler/scheduler.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx
   ```
2. Run the full preflight:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```
3. Manual check. This is not easy to do by hand: the difference only shows while two or more sub-agents run in the same turn. That needs a real model session, and the model decides what to call and when each agent finishes. The unit tests above cover the logic, so treat this as an optional smoke test:
   1. Build and start the CLI from this branch:
      ```bash
      npm run build
      npm start
      ```
   2. Ask for two sub-agents in one turn. Any two enabled sub-agents work, for example:
      ```
      Run two codebase_investigator tasks in parallel: one on how the scheduler orders tool calls, and one on how finished tool calls are added to the history.
      ```
   3. Expected, and the same as before this change:
      - While the agents run, both stay together in the live tool area.
      - When the last agent finishes, both results move into the history together as one block. An agent that finished earlier is not printed on its own first.
   4. If the model does not call two agents in the same turn, the check does not apply. Try another prompt.

prs.body:
## Summary

Registers the Gemini 4 Argon model (`gemini-4-argon`) so it can be selected and used like any other model, instead of only through a custom model override.

- Adds `GEMINI_4_ARGON_MODEL` and includes it in `VALID_GEMINI_MODELS`.
- Adds the model config (chat alias extending `chat-base-3`) and its definition (`tier: pro`, `family: gemini-4`, thinking).
- Lists the model in the `/model` picker and in the ACP model list.
- Regenerates the settings schema, the configuration docs, and the resolved-aliases goldens.

Argon is served by Agent Platform (Vertex AI); a backend that does not carry it rejects the id with a clear "model not found" error, so it stays listed for every auth method.

## Details

- The definition mirrors the existing Gemini 3 Pro entries: `thinking: true`, `multimodalToolUse: true`, `isPreview: false` (Agent Platform reports `launchStage: GA`).
- The chat alias extends `chat-base-3`, i.e. `thinkingLevel: HIGH`.
- Capability-family plumbing (`getToolFamily`, `supportsModernFeatures`) is intentionally left untouched; `family: gemini-4` is recorded so it can be wired separately once the model's tool family is confirmed.
- Verified live against Agent Platform via ACP: the picker lists `gemini-4-argon` and a turn runs on it (`modelUsage: gemini-4-argon`, `stopReason: end_turn`). It is served from the `global` location; `us-central1` returns 404.
- Implemented with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

prs.title: fix(cli): restore debounced static UI refresh on terminal width changes
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->
Restores the debounced `refreshStatic()` effect on `terminalWidth` changes in `AppContainer.tsx` (using a 100ms debounce) so that horizontal terminal resize events in default inline rendering mode clear wrapped frame remnants (`ansiEscapes.clearTerminal`) and remount the `<Static>` history region at the updated column width.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->
- **`packages/cli/src/ui/AppContainer.tsx`**:
  - In default inline mode (`ui.useAlternateBuffer: false` and `ui.terminalBuffer: false`), narrowing the terminal width causes full-width lines in the dynamic `Composer` region (`────`, `▄▄▄▄`, `▀▀▀▀`) to soft-wrap across multiple physical terminal rows. Because Ink's `log-update` renderer erases `previousLineCount` logical lines rather than the wrapped physical row count, the top portion of the previous dynamic frame remains in scrollback during resize events.
  - Restores `isInitialMount` (`useRef(true)`) and a 100ms debounced `useEffect` watching `[terminalWidth, refreshStatic]` to clear the terminal and increment `historyRemountKey` once horizontal resizing settles.
  - Scopes the dependency array strictly to `terminalWidth` (excluding `terminalHeight`) so vertical-only terminal dimension changes (such as mobile virtual keyboard toggles) do not trigger `<Static>` remounts.
- **`packages/cli/src/ui/AppContainer.test.tsx`**:
  - Adds unit test coverage verifying that `AppContainer` skips `refreshStatic()` on initial mount and on height-only dimension changes, debounces rapid `terminalWidth` updates by 100ms, and writes `ansiEscapes.clearTerminal` while incrementing `historyRemountKey` in default inline mode.

## Related Issues

<!-- Use keywords to auto-close issues (Closes #123, Fixes #456). If this PR is
only related to an issue or is a partial fix, simply reference the issue number
without a keyword (Related to #123). -->

## How to Validate

expected results, and edge cases. -->

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/AppContainer.test.tsx

2. Manually start Gemini CLI in default inline mode, type a prompt into the input box, resize the terminal window horizontally, and verify that after 100ms the terminal clears any wrapped line remnants and re-renders cleanly at the new width.

prs.title: fix(core): treat whitespace-only UTF-16 and UTF-32 files as empty
prs.body:
`isEmpty()` removed the byte order mark and then always decoded the sampled bytes as UTF-8. In UTF-16 and UTF-32 a whitespace character is two or four bytes wide, so decoding it as UTF-8 leaves NUL characters behind, and `trim()` does not strip NUL. A file that held only whitespace was therefore reported as non-empty, and `validatePlanContent()` accepted a whitespace-only plan file saved as UTF-16 or UTF-32 with a BOM. This change decodes the sampled bytes according to the detected BOM, the same way `readFileWithEncoding()` already does.

## Details

- **`decodeBOMContent` (`packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.ts`)**: new helper that skips the BOM and decodes the remaining bytes according to the BOM's encoding (UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE, UTF-32 LE/BE). It is the switch that used to live inline at the end of `readFileWithEncoding()`.
- **`isEmpty`**: uses `decodeBOMContent` for files that start with a BOM. Files without a BOM are still decoded as UTF-8.
- **`readFileWithEncoding`**: calls the same helper, so reading a file and checking whether it is empty cannot drift apart again. Its behavior is unchanged.
- **`decodeUTF16BE`**: ignores an incomplete trailing code unit instead of throwing. `Buffer.swap16()` throws on an odd number of bytes. Because `isEmpty` now reaches this decoder, such a file would otherwise fall into the catch-all in `isEmpty` and be reported as empty even though it contains text. This matches how Node's UTF-16 LE decoder and `decodeUTF32` treat an incomplete trailing unit.
- **Unchanged behavior**:
  - Only the first 1 KB of the file is sampled.
  - A file that cannot be read is still treated as empty.
  - Files without a BOM, and UTF-8 files with a BOM, give the same results as before.
- **Tests**:
  - `packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.test.ts`: for UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE and UTF-32 LE/BE files, all with a BOM, a whitespace-only file is empty, a whitespace-only file larger than the 1 KB sample is empty, and a file with text is not empty. One more test covers a UTF-16 BE file with a trailing partial byte and text, which is not empty.
  - `packages/core/src/utils/planUtils.test.ts`: a whitespace-only UTF-16 LE plan returns the `Plan file is empty` error, and a UTF-16 LE plan with content passes validation.
  - The whitespace-only UTF-16 and UTF-32 cases, and the whitespace-only plan case, fail on the previous code.

## Related Issues

Fixes [#29142](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/29142)

## How to Validate

1. Run the targeted unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/fileUtils.test.ts src/utils/planUtils.test.ts
   ```
2. Run the full preflight:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```
3. Manual check with throwaway files (nothing in your settings or workspace is touched):
   1. Build, then create three files in a temporary directory. `FF FE` and `FE FF` are the UTF-16 LE and BE byte order marks. Two files contain only a space, a line feed and a tab; the third contains `# Plan`:
      ```bash
      npm run build
      dir="$(mktemp -d)"
      printf '\xff\xfe\x20\x00\x0a\x00\x09\x00' > "$dir/utf16le-whitespace.txt"
      printf '\xfe\xff\x00\x20\x00\x0a\x00\x09' > "$dir/utf16be-whitespace.txt"
      { printf '\xff\xfe'; printf '# Plan' | iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-16LE; } > "$dir/utf16le-text.txt"
      ```
   2. Run the plan validation on each file, from the repository root:
      ```bash
      node --input-type=module -e "import { validatePlanContent } from '@google/gemini-cli-core'; for (const f of process.argv.slice(1)) console.log(f.split('/').pop(), '=>', await validatePlanContent(f));" "$dir/utf16le-whitespace.txt" "$dir/utf16be-whitespace.txt" "$dir/utf16le-text.txt"
      ```
      - Expected:
        ```
        utf16le-whitespace.txt => Plan file is empty. You must write content to the plan file before requesting approval.
        utf16be-whitespace.txt => Plan file is empty. You must write content to the plan file before requesting approval.
        utf16le-text.txt => null
        ```
      - Before this change, the two whitespace-only files were accepted (`null`). This is what the new unit tests show on the previous code.
   3. Clean up:
      ```bash
      rm -rf "$dir"
      unset dir
      ```
   - The interactive plan mode flow writes UTF-8 plan files, so it does not produce these inputs on its own. The check above calls the same validation function directly.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [x] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker

prs.title: fix(cli): correct reverse search highlight index for expanding unicode characters
prs.body:
## Summary

Resolves an off-by-one UTF-16 substring highlight offset in reverse history search (`Ctrl+R`) when a command contains Unicode characters whose lowercase form expands in length (such as `İ` / `U+0130`, which maps to `i\u0307`).

## Details

Previously, `useReverseSearchCompletion` computed `matchedIndex` using `cmd.toLowerCase().indexOf(query)`. When characters in `cmd` expand to multiple UTF-16 code units under `.toLowerCase()`, the resulting index is shifted relative to the original-case `label` string rendered in the UI.

This change computes `matchedIndex` directly against the original-case `cmd` string using a Unicode case-insensitive regular expression (`new RegExp(escapeRegExp(query), 'iu')`) on the un-lowercased query, escaping special regex characters in `query` so literal characters and length-expanding Unicode characters are matched accurately.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29302

## How to Validate

1. Run the reverse search completion unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useReverseSearchCompletion.test.tsx
   ```
2. Verify that `matchedIndex` is `7` when searching for `'abc'` in `'echo \u0130 abc'`, `5` when searching for `'\u0130'` directly, and that queries containing special regex characters (e.g., `[a-z]`, `foo*`, `(unclosed[`) match literally without throwing syntax errors.

prs.title: fix(cli): use --userns=keep-id for rootless podman sandboxes
prs.body:
## Summary

Rootless Podman users hit `EACCES` when the sandbox runs as a non-root user, because the container's user namespace doesn't map the caller's UID to a valid user inside the container.

This PR appends `--userns=keep-id` to the sandbox args only when the container command is `podman` AND the daemon is running rootless, so the caller's UID is preserved inside the sandbox.

Fixes #29338

## Details

- Detect rootless Podman via `podman info --format '{{.Host.Security.Rootless}}'` (new `isRootlessPodman()` helper; any failure is treated as rootful so behavior is unchanged elsewhere).
- New `sandboxFlagsSetUserns(flags)` helper checks whether `SANDBOX_FLAGS` already sets `--userns` — if the user provides their own value, we never override it.
- `--userns=keep-id` is appended only when:
  - command is `podman` (Docker untouched),
  - rootless mode is detected,
  - the `shouldUseCurrentUserInSandbox()` branch is active (the same path that previously caused EACCES),
  - `SANDBOX_FLAGS` does not already set `--userns`.
- Rootful Podman and all Docker setups are unchanged.
- Added unit tests for the three new helpers (`sandboxUtils.test.ts`).

## Related Issues

- Fixes #29338

## How to Validate

On Linux with rootless Podman:

1. Clone this branch and `npm ci`
2. Set `GEMINI_SANDBOX=podman` and run any sandboxed command
3. Before: `EACCES` permission error
4. After: sandbox starts normally, sandbox container runs with `--userns=keep-id`

Unit tests:

```
npm run test --workspaces -- --run packages/cli/src/utils/sandboxUtils.test.ts
```

prs.title: fix(cli): load environment variables before resolving settings placeholders
prs.body:
## Summary

Resolves a load-order race condition in `_doLoadSettings` and `loadEnvironment` where settings files (`system`, `systemDefaults`, `user`, `workspace`) had environment variable placeholders expanded and validated *before* `.env` files were loaded into `process.env`. Because `.env` variables were not yet in `process.env`, settings referencing `.env`-defined secrets (such as `$GITHUB_MCP_PAT` in `mcpServers` headers or args) remained unexpanded as literal strings.

## Details

- **Decoupled Raw Parsing from Resolution & Validation (`_doLoadSettings`)**:
  - Updated `load` (and `loadSystemFile`) in `packages/cli/src/config/settings.ts` to read and parse raw JSON objects without prematurely expanding environment variables or recording Zod validation warnings.
  - Added a unified `resolveAndValidate(rawSettings, filePath?)` helper that expands environment variables via `resolveEnvVarsInObject` and validates/coerces types via `validateSettings` (only recording warnings to `settingsErrors` when `filePath` is provided on the final pass).
  - Pre-existing `process.env` variables in `initialTrustCheckSettings` and `tempMergedSettings` are still expanded and coerced before calling `isWorkspaceTrusted` and `loadEnvironment`, preventing unexpanded string placeholders (e.g., `"$ENABLE_FOLDER_TRUST"`) from being evaluated as truthy strings.
  - Once `loadEnvironment` populates `process.env` from `.env`, each scope (`system`, `systemDefaults`, `user`, `workspace`) is resolved and validated.
- **Cloud Shell Auth Type Expansion (`loadEnvironment`)**:
  - Populates `process.env` from `.env` before resolving `security.auth.selectedType` via `resolveEnvVarsInString` and invoking `setUpCloudShellEnvironment`, ensuring `.env`-backed auth type placeholders (`vertex-ai`) properly skip the Cloud Shell `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` override.

## Related Issues

Fixes #28684
Related to #28597

## How to Validate

1. Run the unit tests in `packages/cli/src/config/settings.test.ts`:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/settings.test.ts
   ```
   Verify all 125 tests pass, including:
   - `should resolve environment variables loaded from .env files`
   - `should resolve environment variables in security settings using pre-existing process.env before checking trust`
   - `should resolve placeholders in selected auth type during loadSettings and skip Cloud Shell override`
2. Run full preflight validation:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```

prs.title: fix(grep): prevent command-line option injection by passing search patterns with explicit -e delimiter
prs.body:
### Summary
This PR hardens the local grep execution module in `packages/core/src/tools/grep.ts` against Command-Line Option / Argument Injection (CWE-88) by enforcing strict argument separation using the explicit pattern terminator (`-e`) for both `git grep` and system `grep` pipelines.

### Problem / Vulnerability Addressed
When constructing search queries, both `git grep` and system `grep` previously appended user-supplied or workspace-derived search patterns directly as raw positional arguments:
- `gitArgs = ['grep', '--untracked', '-n', '-E', '--ignore-case', pattern]`
- `grepArgs.push(pattern)`

Because POSIX and GNU command-line parsers process arguments sequentially from left to right, any token beginning with a hyphen (`-` or `--`) is interpreted as a command-line flag or option rather than a literal search string. 

**Impact:**
1. **Command Behavior Alteration / Flag Injection:** Attackers or untrusted workspaces containing files or search inputs starting with hyphens (e.g., `-v`, `--max-count`) could force the underlying tool to misinterpret inputs as flags, altering search output or triggering inverted matches.
2. **Denial of Service (DoS):** Passing invalid flag structures (such as `--max-count` without a trailing integer value) caused the underlying subprocess to crash with fatal errors (`fatal: option '--max-count' requires a value`), disrupting the active CLI session.
3. **Defense-in-Depth Violation:** Failing to isolate positional match patterns from command option parsers violated secure subprocess spawning guidelines.

### Solution & Key Changes
1. **Explicit `-e` Delimiter Enforcement:**
   - Updated `git grep` command building to push `-e` immediately before the search `pattern`:
     ```ts
     gitArgs.push('-e', pattern);
     ```
   - Updated system `grep` command building to prepend `-e` before the `pattern`:
     ```ts
     grepArgs.push('-e', pattern);
     ```
2. **Comprehensive Unit Testing:**
   - Added robust unit test cases in `packages/core/src/tools/grep.test.ts` validating that leading-hyphen search patterns (e.g., `-v` and `--flag`) are safely preceded by the `-e` flag in spawned arguments.

### Test Verification
- Core grep test suite (`grep.test.ts`): **35 / 35 tests passed (100%)**
- Linter & Typecheck: **Clean (0 errors, 0 warnings)**

Relates to #29627

issues.title: Allow a credential command in providers.json and managed settings so BYOK providers work without a per-invocation launcher

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Since 1.0.84, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY_COMMAND` lets the CLI obtain a BYOK credential by running a command, so short-lived per-user tokens (OIDC/JWT from a gateway, Entra, STS, …) can rotate during a session. 

The gap is that it only exists as an environment variable. The file-based surfaces have no equivalent:

- `providers.json` entries accept only a static `apiKey` / `bearerToken`.
- Enterprise managed settings (MDM / `managed-settings.json`) have no BYOK provider keys at all.

So anything that wants a rotating credential must set the environment before Copilot starts: a wrapper script, a shell alias, or a launcher process. Consequences:

- Plain `copilot` (and anything else that spawns `copilot`, e.g. IDE integrations, scripts, `--acp`) is not routed; only the wrapped invocation is.
- Organizations cannot enforce "route through our gateway with your identity" via policy; the user has to remember to use the wrapper.
- Writing the rotating token into `providers.json` as `apiKey` would put a bearer credential on disk and defeat rotation.

Other coding agents already support this in their config files, which is why the same gateway integration is a static config drop for them but a launcher for Copilot CLI:

- Codex: `model_providers.<id>.auth = { command = "...", args = [...] }` in `config.toml` / managed config.
- Claude Code: `apiKeyHelper` in `settings.json` / managed settings.
- Prior art elsewhere: Git/Docker credential helpers, AWS `credential_process`, kubectl exec credential plugins.

### Proposed solution

Provider registry: accept a command-based credential in `providers.json` provider entries, with the same semantics as `COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY_COMMAND` (run to obtain the credential; cache; re-run near expiry and on 401, then retry once):

```json
{
  "providers": [
    {
      "name": "gateway",
      "type": "openai",
      "baseUrl": "https://gateway.example.com/v1",
      "wireApi": "responses",
      "apiKeyCommand": ["/usr/local/bin/agentdesktop", "credential", "--client-id", "copilot-cli"]
    }
  ],
  "models": [
    { "provider": "gateway", "id": "gpt-4.1", "modelId": "gpt-4.1", "wireModel": "gpt-4.1" }
  ]
}
```

(Field names other than `apiKeyCommand` should follow whatever the current `providers.json` schema uses. A `bearerTokenCommand` twin would mirror the existing `apiKey` / `bearerToken` pair.)

Prefer an argv array executed without a shell; optionally also accept a string executed like the env var does today.

Managed settings: allow the same provider definition (including the command) under enterprise managed settings, so an organization can pin the default provider and its credential source, and users cannot override it with a personal `providers.json` or env var.

Precedence: managed settings win when present; below that, keep env > providers.json > default, consistent with the flag > env > config ordering proposed in #2710. The env var keeps working as an override for ad-hoc use.

Security: never persist the command's output; redact it from logs, `/collect-debug-logs`, session state, and telemetry; run the command with a timeout and a bounded output size; treat non-zero exit as "no credential" rather than sending an empty bearer.

### Example prompts or workflows

```sh
# Dropped once by MDM or a fleet agent, no per-user setup:
#   ~/.copilot/providers.json   the provider entry above
#   ~/.copilot/settings.json    { "model": "gateway/gpt-4.1" }

copilot                            # interactive
copilot -p "summarize this repo"   # non-interactive
copilot --acp                      # spawned by an IDE or ACP client
```

All three route through the gateway with no wrapper or alias, and the token rotates for the life of the session.


### Additional context

Related: #3682 , #3282, https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/2710

issues.title: BYOK custom providers: CLI forces greedy sampling (temperature=0) causing reasoning-model degeneration and silent hangs on context overflow
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

For BYOK / custom OpenAI-compatible providers (e.g. a small thinking model such as qwen-27b served by vLLM), CLI 1.0.81 and later send `temperature: 0`, `top_p: 0.95`, `frequency_penalty: 0`, `presence_penalty: 0` in every chat-completion request. CLI 1.0.80 sends no sampling parameters at all, letting the server use its own defaults.

With `temperature: 0` (greedy decoding) forced on a thinking model, the model degenerates into long, repetitive, pure-reasoning outputs. Those oversized reasoning outputs (10.6k–25.5k tokens in a single call, verified in session logs) push the request past the provider's hard `max_prompt_tokens` limit (131,072), triggering compaction + truncation — after which the client either **hangs with no error and no further model call** (22 minutes until the user killed the process) or ends the turn with a **contentless reasoning-only `finish_reason: stop` response** and goes idle with no user-visible signal.

Secondary symptom observed in the same sessions: during compaction / auto-mode utility calls, the CLI sends the internal model id `gpt-5.4-nano` instead of the configured BYOK model name to the custom endpoint, producing a silent 404.

This is a CLI regression, not a model problem: the same model and the same server run fine on 1.0.80.

## Affected version

1.0.81 – 1.0.87 (regression introduced in 1.0.81; verified by wire capture of 1.0.80/1.0.81/1.0.82/1.0.86/1.0.87 — 1.0.80 is healthy)

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure a custom OpenAI-compatible provider (BYOK):
   ```
   COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai
   COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=<vLLM endpoint>/v1
   COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY=<any>
   COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS=131072
   COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8192
   COPILOT_MODEL=qwen-27b
   ```
2. Run a sustained multi-step task with CLI ≥ 1.0.81 (small tasks like "create fib.py with memoization, run it, verify output" complete fine — degeneration manifests under sustained load, i.e. over many hours / compactions).
3. Observe: repetitive pure-reasoning output; context crossing the 131,072 limit; then either a silent hang (no error, no further model call, for 22+ minutes) or a contentless reasoning-only turn ending the turn with no signal.

Minimal wire-level reproduction of the sampling regression (no long task needed): capture the request bodies of 1.0.80 vs 1.0.81 sent to the same endpoint for the same task. 1.0.80 sends no sampling parameters; 1.0.81 sends `temperature: 0, top_p: 0.95, frequency_penalty: 0, presence_penalty: 0`.

## Expected behavior

- Custom / BYOK providers are not pinned to sampling parameters (1.0.80 behavior: none sent, server defaults apply) — or sampling parameters are configurable via provider settings. `temperature: 0` is harmful for thinking models.
- Requests never exceed `max_prompt_tokens`: the compaction decision accounts for `max_output_tokens` headroom, so the CLI compacts *before* overflow rather than truncating *after*.
- After a truncation/compaction, the CLI issues the next model call or surfaces an error — it never sits silent.
- Contentless reasoning-only turns (large reasoning, 0 content, 0 tool calls, `finish_reason: stop`) are detected and surfaced or retried with adjusted parameters.
- Utility/compaction calls use the configured BYOK model name, not an internal id (no 404 for `gpt-5.4-nano`).

## Additional context

### Wire-level request diff (socket capture, identical task, identical model)

Task: "create fib.py with memoization, run it, verify output" — non-interactive mode, BYOK `qwen-27b` via an OpenAI-compatible vLLM endpoint.

**1.0.80 request body (top-level keys):**
```
model, messages, tools, stream, stream_options
```
No sampling parameters — server defaults apply.

**1.0.87 request body (top-level keys):**
```
model, messages, temperature: 0, top_p: 0.95, frequency_penalty: 0, presence_penalty: 0, tools, stream, stream_options
```

**Version pinning** — all five versions captured running the identical task against the identical endpoint:

| CLI version | Top-level request keys (sampling params) |
|---|---|
| 1.0.80 | `model, messages, tools, stream, stream_options` — **no sampling params** |
| 1.0.81 | `+ temperature: 0, top_p: 0.95, frequency_penalty: 0, presence_penalty: 0` (+ `snippy: {enabled: false}`) |
| 1.0.82 | same as 1.0.81 (incl. `snippy` stub) |
| 1.0.86 | same as 1.0.81 (no `snippy`) |
| 1.0.87 | same as 1.0.81 (no `snippy`) |

**The regression was introduced in 1.0.81** — the same release that added the interrupted-session restore mechanism (#4673).

Both versions replay assistant reasoning text into the message history (standard for thinking models; not the differentiator).

### Session log evidence (2026-09-22, all qwen-27b)

| Session | CLI | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| 26a9ef8c | 1.0.80 | 475 model calls over 22 h, 11 compactions (max 118.5k, never over limit), 0 truncations, 0 hangs. Work completed, PR merged. Max reasoning call 9,754 tokens — productive. |
| 8bdd58ac | 1.0.87 | User: "you are in a reasoning loop" (02:22) |
| dd3a60cd | 1.0.87 | User: "you stuck in a reasoning loop" (04:31); 6 compactions (up to 123.5k — near the 131k limit) |
| 8278f5c4 | 1.0.87 | User: "you are in a reasoning loop" (04:48). Compaction call 404'd once (`gpt-5.4-nano` does not exist — see below), then an **empty 10,662-token pure-reasoning turn** (`finish_reason: stop`, 0 content, 0 tool calls) at 04:58; client went silent for 25 min until user kill. |
| bf54a1ec | 1.0.87 | 25,510-token degenerate reasoning call (04:56–05:05) → context 131,805 (> 131,072 limit) → `compaction_start` + truncation 131,805→122,893 at 05:05:21 → **no compaction_complete, no further model call** → 22-minute silent hang until user kill (05:27). |

### Causal chain

1. Forced `temperature: 0` → greedy decoding → repetition collapse in the thinking model's reasoning trace.
2. Oversized reasoning outputs (and full reasoning replay in history) exceed the provider's hard prompt limit between compaction-threshold checks (threshold ≈ 113k, limit 131k; a single 25k-token call crosses it).
3. Context overflow → truncation. Client then either:
   - (a) hangs: compaction starts, truncation applied, but no compaction-complete and no next model call (bf54a1ec), or
   - (b) emits a contentless reasoning-only `finish_reason: stop` turn and goes idle with no user-visible signal (8278f5c4).

### Secondary bug: utility model calls 404 for BYOK

During compaction (and for auto-mode utility calls) the CLI sends the internal model id `gpt-5.4-nano` instead of the BYOK model name to the custom endpoint:

```
model.turn_failed
  model: gpt-5.4-nano   (modelInfo: {id: "gpt-5.4-nano", name: "qwen-27b"})
  error: 404 The model `gpt-5.4-nano` does not exist.
```

The turn silently recovers (falls back to truncation), but the failure is invisible to the user. Related: #4445 (auto mode picks unavailable models).

### Environment

- Operating system: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, x86_64, bash
- Model server: vLLM 0.28.0 (OpenAI-compatible), `max_model_len` 262144
- Related issues: #4673 (auto-restore mechanism from the same 1.0.81 release — fixed/disabled by default since 1.0.83), #4445 (auto mode model availability)

issues.title: Cloud agent: the built-in Playwright MCP session is already closed at the first tool call, and recovery reports it as browser OAuth required
issues.body:
### Describe the bug


Split out of #4378, which carries two faults. The registry policy 401 in that issue has a cause and a workaround. This one does not, and it survives that workaround.

## Summary

In a Copilot cloud agent session on a GHEC data residency tenant (`<tenant>.ghe.com`), every call to a `playwright/*` tool fails. The Playwright server is healthy for the whole session. The coordinator's MCP session to it is not. The second error message is wrong and sends a reader after a sign-in problem that does not exist.

The built-in Playwright MCP server is enabled by default and is documented as needing no setup. It is unusable here.

## Reproduction

Any session in any repository on the tenant. Serve any page on `localhost` and call `playwright/browser_navigate`. It needs no repository-specific state.

First call:

```
MCP server 'playwright': Tool call failed: Error: MCP request failed: Transport closed
```

Recovery attempt:

```
MCP server 'playwright': Tool call failed after session recovery:
MCPOAuthBrowserRequiredError: Browser-based OAuth required for http://localhost:3100/mcp
```

The second message is misleading. The server is on `localhost`, it is unauthenticated, and it needs no sign-in of any kind.

## The server is healthy throughout

- It runs from `/opt/copilot-runtime` on the runner image's own Node 24.
- It listens on port 3100 for the whole session.
- A direct MCP `initialize` answers HTTP 200 and reports Playwright MCP `0.0.40`.
- The coordinator retrieves all 21 of its tools at session start, and they appear in the agent's tool list.

By the time the agent calls a tool, the coordinator's MCP session to that server is already closed. The recovery request gets HTTP 404, because the session no longer exists. The client then enters OAuth handling for an unauthenticated localhost server.

## The coordinator does not talk to the Playwright server directly

The coordinator connects through a bridge process, not to port 3100:

```
/opt/hostedtoolcache/node/24.20.0/x64/bin/node \
  /opt/copilot-runtime/copilot-developer-action-main/dist-cca-v3/mcp-proxy-bridge.js \
  --proxy-url=http://127.0.0.1:2301 --server-name=playwright
```

The peer it initializes against names itself accordingly:

```
[INFO]  Created session: <redacted>
[ERROR] Using deferred connection for default Playwright server
[INFO]  [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client
  peer_info: Implementation { name: "mcp-proxy-bridge/playwright", version: "1.0.0" }
```

Three things follow.

- `Using deferred connection for default Playwright server` is logged at **ERROR** level, 216 milliseconds after the session is created, before the bridge initializes. It is the only error in the runtime lifecycle log.
- `127.0.0.1:2301` is the same internal MCP proxy named in #4378.
- The transport that closes is the coordinator's connection through that bridge. It is not a connection to Playwright.

## Session lifetime: the server is not the cause

I created an MCP session against port 3100 by hand and held it idle.

```
initialize                          HTTP/1.1 200 OK
                                    serverInfo: {"name":"Playwright","version":"0.0.40"}
notifications/initialized           HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
tools/list immediately              HTTP/1.1 200 OK   (21 tools)
tools/list after 120 seconds        HTTP/1.1 200 OK   (21 tools)
tools/list after 420 seconds        HTTP/1.1 200 OK   (21 tools)
GET /mcp opened then killed         (stream closed by the client)
tools/list after that close         HTTP/1.1 200 OK   (21 tools)
```

No 404 at any point. The Playwright server does not expire an idle session, and it does not drop a session when the client closes the SSE stream. Whatever closes the coordinator's transport is above the server.

## It is not a timing problem either

I called `playwright/browser_navigate` with `about:blank` as the **very first action of a session**, before reading a file and before any shell command. It failed with the same two errors. So the transport is not closed by the agent's own work, and calling the browser early is not a workaround.

## Ruled out, with evidence

- **The SDK token 401 of #4378.** The failure persists with the Agents variable `GH_HOST=<tenant>.ghe.com` set and no 401 anywhere in the runtime log.
- **The Node version the repository installs.** `actions/setup-node` puts Node 26 on `GITHUB_PATH` for the shell. The runtime starts its MCP servers on the image's own Node 24. The two never meet.
- **An environment variable holding a personal access token.** The first failing session carried none, and the failure survived renaming the secret.
- **The application under test.** The frontend served correctly on `http://localhost:4200` in the same session.
- **An egress proxy with no localhost exclusion.** The runtime process carries no `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` or `NO_PROXY` variable in any case.
- **The Playwright server expiring the session.** See the lifetime table above.
- **The agent taking too long before the first call.** See the first-action test above.

## What I could not find reported anywhere

There is no report of `MCP request failed: Transport closed` against the **built-in default** Playwright server, and no report of `Browser-based OAuth required for http://localhost:3100/mcp`. Every public `MCPOAuthBrowserRequiredError` I found is a genuine remote OAuth server.

## What I ask for

1. The cause of the transport closing. It is closed before the agent's first action, so it is not an idle timeout and not the agent's doing.
2. A correct error for a closed MCP session. The current message tells a customer to sign in to an unauthenticated localhost server, which is neither possible nor needed.
3. Whether this and #4378 share a root cause at `127.0.0.1:2301`. `GITHUB_COPILOT_3P_MCP_POLICY_ENABLED` is `true` in this session, and the only ERROR in the lifecycle log is the deferred connection line.
4. Whether `Using deferred connection for default Playwright server` is expected. It is logged at ERROR level. #1938 is an open request for deferred connection as a feature, which suggests it is not yet a settled behavior.
5. If the built-in Playwright server is not expected to work on a `.ghe.com` tenant, document it. The data residency feature overview lists no such limitation today.

## Impact

The built-in browser is the intended route for a Copilot cloud agent to look at a page it changed. On this tenant it never works. Session ids and full runtime logs are available on request.

issues.title: Support attaching PDFs to GitHub issues from Copilot CLI
issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Allow Copilot CLI to upload and attach PDF documents to GitHub issues, matching the attachment capability available in the GitHub browser issue editor.

This is about uploading a document to a GitHub issue, not attaching a PDF to a Copilot conversation for model analysis.

### Proposed solution

Provide a supported workflow for uploading PDFs when creating or updating GitHub issues and inserting the resulting attachment link into the issue body or a comment.

The reported current workflow relies on `gh issue ... --attach`, which accepts images/videos but rejects PDFs. If PDF support requires an upstream GitHub CLI change, track that dependency and update Copilot's attachment tooling/instructions when it becomes available. Until then, explain the limitation and browser workaround explicitly rather than implying that GitHub issues cannot accept PDFs.

Expected behavior: a user can ask Copilot to attach a local PDF to an issue without switching to the browser or hosting the document elsewhere. Respect GitHub's supported file types, size limits, authentication, and upload permissions.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. "Create an issue describing this bug and attach ./reproduction.pdf."
2. "Attach ./design-spec.pdf to issue #123 and reference it in the issue description."
3. "Add a comment to issue #123 with ./investigation-report.pdf attached."

### Additional context

A support-thread reproduction reported the following with GitHub CLI 2.100.0:

- `gh issue ... --attach` rejects `.pdf` locally, before any upload.
- Its supported-file list contains images and videos only.
- Dragging the same PDF into the browser issue editor succeeds and produces an attachment link that can subsequently be reused from the CLI.

These observations are reported from the supplied conversation; they have not been independently reproduced while filing this issue.

References:
- [GitHub CLI issue create manual](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_issue_create)
- [GitHub browser attachment documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/working-with-advanced-formatting/attaching-files)

Duplicate search covered open and closed issues involving PDFs, attachments, uploads, and the built-in media skill. #4583 concerns PDF input/analysis in Copilot conversations, not uploading PDFs to GitHub issues; #3375 concerns associating CLI sessions with issues, not document attachments. No matching issue was found.

issues.title: ACP: /rename reports success but doesn't rename the session

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp --stdio`), `/rename <name>` reports success but doesn't rename the session. Copilot advertises the command in `available_commands_update`, and sending it as a `session/prompt` ends `end_turn` in about 1 ms, with no model call, with the reply `Session renamed to: <name>`. But nothing is saved: the session's `workspace.yaml` keeps its old `name` and `user_named: false`, and `session/list` keeps returning the old `title`, from the same process and from a new one. `/session rename <name>` behaves the same.

ACP has no client method to set a session's title (titles are agent-owned and reported with `session_info_update`), so `/rename` is the only way for an ACP client to rename a Copilot session.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.95

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start `copilot --acp --stdio` and `initialize`.
2. `session/new` with a `cwd`, and send one ordinary prompt, so the session is saved and listed (its title is the first message).
3. Send a `session/prompt` with the text `/rename My new name`.
4. The reply is `Session renamed to: My new name`, with `stopReason: end_turn`.
5. Call `session/list` with that `cwd`, in the same process or a new one: the session's `title` is still the first message.
6. Open `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/workspace.yaml`: still the old `name`, and `user_named: false`. No `session_info_update` is sent with the new title.

### Expected behavior

`/rename <name>` over ACP renames the session as it does in the interactive CLI: it saves the name (`name`, `user_named: true`), `session/list` returns it, and Copilot sends a `session_info_update` with the new `title`, so the client can update its view.

### Additional context

- Windows 11, x86_64. Driven from a Node ACP client (`@agentclientprotocol/sdk`).
- Writing `name` and `user_named: true` into `workspace.yaml` by hand does change the title in `session/list`, so the listing side works. Only the command doesn't save.
- In the 1.0.95 bundle, one session implementation's `renameSession()` calls the native `session.name.set`, and another's is an empty stub (`async renameSession(t){}`, next to `getWorkspace(){return null}`). The ACP session seems to get the stub. The success message is printed either way.
- Related: #4244 (`/rename` in VS Code agent sessions), #2622 (a manual name overwritten by an automatic one).

issues.title: BYOK: populate the /model picker from the provider's /models endpoint
issues.body:
## Problem

When the CLI runs against a custom provider (`COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`), exactly one model can be configured (`COPILOT_MODEL` / `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID`). In-session, `/models` shows only that single configured model — there is no way to browse or switch models without quitting and relaunching with `--model` (which must be guessed, since nothing lists what the provider serves).

## Request

For `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai` (and `azure`), populate the model picker from the provider's standard OpenAI-compatible catalog endpoint:

```
GET {COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL}/models
```

- Fall back silently to today's single-model behavior when the endpoint 404s or errors.
- `data[].id` is enough for a useful picker; if present, `capabilities.limits` / `supported_endpoints` style metadata could fill the Context column the way the native picker does.

A lighter-weight alternative (or complement): a `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODELS` env var accepting a comma-separated id list, for providers whose catalog endpoint can't be reached at startup.

## Why it matters

Practically every OpenAI-compatible backend already serves `/models` — Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM, Azure, and enterprise LLM gateways. We operate such a gateway: it fronts the Copilot API itself (billing stays on the user's Copilot seat) and serves `GET /models` with exactly the models the seat's plan/org policy allows — but the CLI never asks, so enrolled users see a one-entry picker and file "the CLI is broken" reports, while the native CLI right next to it shows the full list.

Observed on v1.0.77 and v1.0.78 (linux-x64 and darwin-arm64).
