issues.title: Windows: runaway MCP OAuth initialization opens repeated browser sessions; Maximum update depth exceeded
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

Running `copilot` interactively on Windows causes repeated OAuth browser sessions during initialization. Browser sessions keep opening until the user terminates Copilot. This prevents normal startup and authentication.

Existing CLI logs confirm rapid repeated authentication initiation for the same MCP servers, and a "Maximum update depth exceeded" error during the same startup. No deliberate reproduction was attempted after the problem was reported, to avoid launching more browser sessions.

## Affected version

- Copilot CLI: 1.0.60 (recorded in startup logs)
- Node.js: v24.16.0 (recorded in startup logs)
- Windows NT 10.0.26200.0, x64
- Installed via the npm launcher
- Terminal emulator and shell used for the affected launches: not collected
- Observed October 13, 2026

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure multiple remote HTTP MCP servers, including Supabase staging/production, Expo, Linear, and Resend in a workspace-root `.mcp.json`.
2. Have authentication required for configured remote servers.
3. Run `copilot` in the workspace.
4. During initialization, repeated OAuth browser sessions open. The user must terminate Copilot to stop them.

Representative sanitized workspace configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "supabase-staging": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref=<staging-project-ref>"
    },
    "supabase-production": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref=<production-project-ref>"
    },
    "expo": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.expo.dev/mcp",
      "tools": ["*"]
    },
    "linear": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.linear.app/mcp",
      "tools": ["*"]
    },
    "resend": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.resend.com/mcp",
      "tools": ["*"]
    }
  }
}
```

Project references are redacted. Additional user-level MCP servers are configured, including Atlassian.

## Expected behavior

Deduplicate in-progress OAuth flows per server, avoid launching a new browser flow repeatedly during initialization, and allow cancellation. Authentication waiting/failure should not cause an unbounded UI update loop or prevent startup.

## Additional context

In one standalone CLI process log, from 18:15:57.838Z to 18:16:26.803Z (about 29 seconds), there are **488** messages matching `Server <name> requires authentication, initiating OAuth flow`:

| Server | OAuth initiation messages |
| --- | ---: |
| supabase-staging | 115 |
| supabase-production | 115 |
| expo | 115 |
| resend | 115 |
| linear | 27 |
| atlassian | 1 |

Examples of the same server being retried within milliseconds:

```text
2026-10-13T18:16:02.994Z [ERROR] Server supabase-staging requires authentication, initiating OAuth flow
2026-10-13T18:16:03.071Z [ERROR] Server supabase-staging requires authentication, initiating OAuth flow
2026-10-13T18:16:03.094Z [ERROR] Server supabase-staging requires authentication, initiating OAuth flow
2026-10-13T18:16:03.099Z [ERROR] Server supabase-staging requires authentication, initiating OAuth flow
```

During that startup:

```text
2026-10-13T18:16:11.958Z [ERROR] Maximum update depth exceeded. This can happen when a component calls setState inside useEffect, but useEffect either doesn't have a dependency array, or one of the dependencies changes on every render.
```

That log records three explicit `Opening browser for ... authentication` messages. The user observed many browser sessions; the 488 count measures authentication-initiation messages, not independently verified browser launches.

A separate earlier CLI process log shows similarly repeated Supabase OAuth initiations within milliseconds, so the repetition is present across multiple launches.

Related VS Code issue: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341353. In a Copilot SDK-backed VS Code Agent Host session on this machine, Authenticate instead does nothing and authorization-server metadata discovery fails. Terminal authentication was attempted as a workaround and encountered this browser-session storm. These may be distinct bugs; a shared root cause is not established.

Possible related CLI report: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4695 (OAuth token reuse across sessions). The distinguishing symptom here is rapid repeated initiation within a single startup, accompanied by the UI update-depth error.

Only sanitized excerpts are included. No credentials, project identifiers, private repository details, OAuth URLs with query tokens, or complete raw logs are attached.

issues.title: Content Exclusion Service fails closed (blocks all shell commands) after auth/token refresh — use-after-dispose (v1.0.61)

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
[Copilot speaking]

## Affected version
GitHub Copilot CLI **v1.0.61** (`pkg/win32-x64/1.0.61/app.js`). Identified by reverse‑engineering the shipped bundle and correlating multiple session logs.

## Summary
After a credential/token update during a session, the `ContentExclusionService` is disposed but a **dangling, unretained reference** to it remains in the cached shell tool's config. The disposed service **fails closed**, so every subsequent shell command in that session is blocked as "targeting an excluded path" — even when the org has **zero** exclusion rules, and even for non‑file tokens like `git`, `Set-Location`, or `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe`. The session never recovers.

## Observable symptoms
- Logs show `[ContentExclusionService] Loaded 0 exclusion rule(s)` (no rules configured), yet later:
  `[ContentExclusion] Blocked shell command targeting excluded path: <path>`
- The blocked "paths" are nonsensical — they're the first token of the command resolved against the cwd (e.g. `<cwd>\git`, `<cwd>\Set-Location`), including interpreters like `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe`.
- Blocking begins **mid‑session** and persists for the rest of the session (no recovery).
- Strong temporal correlation with auth instability / re‑auth (`/login`) prompts.

## Root cause (precise chain, with bundle anchors)

1. **Service is single‑owner, refcount‑based.** `kat` initializes `retainCount=1`; `dispose()` does `retainCount--; if(retainCount<=0) disposed=true`. The **only** `retain()` call in the bundle is inside `setContentExclusionService(e,r)` (`…&& !r && e.retain()`). The lazy creator calls `setContentExclusionService(_hn(...), /*skipRetain*/ true)`, so a freshly‑created service stays at **refcount 1** — the session manager's field is its sole owner.

2. **The shell tool captures the service without retaining it.** `getToolConfig()` builds the tool config with `contentExclusionService: this.contentExclusionService` — a plain **value snapshot, no `retain()`**. The shell tool (`Umt`) stores it as `this.config` and is **cached for the session** as `this.shellContext` (only rebuilt on an `enableScriptSafety` change, *not* on auth change).

3. **An auth change disposes the service out‑of‑band.** `updateOptions(e)` (the config‑delta handler) disposes + nulls the service whenever any of these change:
   - `authInfo`: `this.authInfo !== e.authInfo && this.setContentExclusionService(void 0, false)` — a **reference** comparison, so *any* new authInfo object (token refresh, `/login`, session reattach) triggers it.
   - the `CONTENT_EXCLUSION` feature flag toggles.
   - `additionalContentExclusionPolicies` changes.

   `updateOptions({authInfo})` is invoked externally by the **`setCredentials` RPC**: `setCredentials(e){ return t.updateOptions({authInfo:e.credentials}), {success:true} }`. This can fire **at any time, including mid‑turn**. Because the shell tool never retained the service, `setContentExclusionService(void 0,…)` drops refcount 1 → 0 → `disposed=true` **while the shell tool still references it**.

4. **The use site has no liveness guard.** `Umt.executeShellToolCallback` does:
   ```js
   let a = this.config.contentExclusionService;          // dangling, disposed instance
   if (a && s.possiblePaths.length > 0) {
     let u = await a.findFirstExcluded(possiblePaths…);   // no isUnavailable() check, no re-create
     if (u) /* log "Blocked shell command…"; block */
   }
   ```
   No `isUnavailable()` check, no re‑creation. The only re‑create guard lives in the per‑turn manager path and rebuilds **the manager's own field**, never the cached shell tool's snapshot.

5. **Disposed → fail closed.** On a disposed instance:
   ```js
   async findFirstExcluded(e){
     if (this.isUnavailable()) {
       let n = this.getUnavailableResult();  // {excluded:true, reason:"Content exclusion rules could not be fetched…"}
       return n.excluded && e.length>0 ? { path: e[0], result: n } : null;  // ← first token, unconditionally
     } … }
   ```
   Hence every command is blocked and the reported "excluded path" is just `possiblePaths[0]`.

**Net:** disposing the sole owner's reference on auth change, with (a) an unretained capture in the cached shell tool and (b) no liveness check at the use site, yields a use‑after‑dispose that fails closed for the remainder of the session.

## Why it correlates with re‑authentication
The disposal trigger is `this.authInfo !== e.authInfo` (reference inequality). Routine token refresh, `/login`, and session reattach all push a new `authInfo` object via `setCredentials`, disposing the service. Frequent re‑auth prompts and the spurious blocking are **two symptoms of the same credential churn** — causally linked, not coincidental.

## Evidence (anonymized)
Across the session logs reviewed, blocking appeared only in a small number of sessions; all the rest never blocked. The blocking sessions share a common signal:

| Session | Blocks | Token 401s | Service re‑inits |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 8 | many | 2 |
| B | 6 | 1 | 3 |
| C | 4 | 0 | 4 (two within ~1 s) |

- **No** non‑blocking session had any token 401s; the auth‑unstable sessions (A, B) were the ones that blocked.
- The blocking session with **no** 401 (C) instead showed the **highest service churn** (rapid re‑inits, two within ~1 s) — consistent with a non‑auth config update (flag/policy) or an `authInfo` object swap landing mid‑turn.
- In every blocking session there were **zero** service re‑inits after the first block → it never recovers in‑session.
- Representative timing: a token 401, then a service re‑init shortly after, then blocking begins ~1–2 minutes later and continues until the turn/session ends.

## Suggested fixes (any one breaks the chain; ideally all three)
1. **Retain on capture / use a live accessor.** Have the tool config `retain()` the service, or read it via a live getter (`getContentExclusionService()`) instead of a value snapshot, so the instance can't be disposed while in use.
2. **Guard the use site.** In `executeShellToolCallback`, treat `isUnavailable()` like "no service" (skip the check or lazily re‑create), rather than calling `findFirstExcluded` on a possibly‑disposed instance.
3. **Don't dispose on benign authInfo churn.** Compare auth identity by value (token/identity), not object reference, before disposing — and/or recreate the service atomically instead of disposing then waiting for the next turn.

Bonus: when failing closed, don't report `possiblePaths[0]` as an "excluded path" if it isn't an existing absolute file path — the current behavior is misleading and blocks shell builtins/interpreters.

## Workaround for users
Restart the CLI session when blocking begins — a fresh process re‑creates the service cleanly. Updating to a newer CLI build (if available) is advisable.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

I'm getting into a loop when CLI switches between shell and tool commands with certain MCP servers.  CLI seems to be unable to "find" the MCP call it is looking for and reverts back to shell and is unable to proceed. It keeps trying useless shell commands and eventually gives up without actually doing what it was asked.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.41-0

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Set up MCP server (either the Unity official one, or an open source Unity MCP, OR the official Atlassian MCP server (https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp)
2. Issue the following prompt: "can you try a test with a simple shell command followed a test Confluence request and then back to shell again? repeat this sequence exactly twice"
3. You may have to issue this prompt twice in a row to get the resulting behavior

Another repro is to attempt to use one of these MCP servers with a workflow where it naturally has to switch back and forth between MCP and shell commands.

### Expected behavior

For this prompt, it should issue a shell command (such as Write-Output), followed by a successful MCP call, followed by another similar shell command. It should do this consistently and without extra shell commands.

### Additional context

This:
1) Only seems to happen in Copilot CLI (not VSCode)
2) Only seems to happen with certain (kinds of?) MCP servers (I have tried several different Unity MCP servers as well as the official Atlassian server)
3) Only seems to be an issue when it switches back and forth between shell (aka Powerhsell) commands and unity MCP tool calls.

A possible clue is when it sometimes fails with "I couldn’t get the Unity console output in this turn because the Unity console tool isn’t visible in my callable tool schema right now, even though it appeared in the prior tools-changed notice."

I don't know what's different about certain servers, (maybe a latency thing?) but most of them do not seem to lead to this issue.

Possibly coincidentally, this seemed to start happening around the time of the change to use .mcp.json instead of mcp.json.

I can attach log files if that would be helpful.

## Description

When the CLI was shipped for public preview, it shipped with a _passable_, but sometimes incorrect, often overbearing, and lacking in configuration, experience.

## Public Issues

These are the issues that I could find relating to permissions in this repo. I intend to go through these and break them apart into themes.

- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/67
  - On Windows, built-in `findstr` uses args like `/i`
  - On PowerShell, built-in `-replace` syntax accepts regexes
- [ ] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/144
  - Either expand variables when `$HOME` (etc) is passed to `/add-dir`, or reject args that aren't dirs that exist
- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/145
  - Asking for an alias to `--allow-all-tools --allow-all-paths`
- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/159
  - With heredoc syntax (`cat << 'EOF' (some content) 'EOF'`), we look for paths inside `(some content)` but should not
  - Awk command parsing misses cases `awk '/^ir:/,/^sentinels:/{print NR": "$0}' xyz.yml | head -220` and `cd /workdir && awk '/CreateTable/,/name:/'
   Services/Migrations/20251001031252_InitialCreate.cs`
- [ ] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/162 (I think)
  - Asking for a permissions display/editor
- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/176
  - Another one about PowerShell `-replace` syntax
- [ ] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/179
  - Asking for more flexibility about global config defaults
- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/211
  - `2>&1` detected as path (already fixed?) and should allow redirection `> /dev/null`
- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/216
  - Should know that `gh api /repos/myuser/myrepo` refers to parts of a URL, not a file path
- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/219
  - PowerShell `Select-String -Pattern (regex?)` and `'string' -match (regex)` syntax
- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/247
  - Should know that `bazel test //foo/bar:baz` resolves `foo/bar` within the Bazel workspace
  - But I'm not sure we should be baking in knowledge of how Bazel locates its workspace root
  - Also, even if you approve it, it keeps asking. We should fix that part at least.
- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/261
  - When running under Cygwin, paths become weird (`/c:/Users/etc`) and we don't understand them
  - Not sure we should fix Cygwin-specific things unless we get more reports

  - Asking for more granular control over the file write tool (so it would do *more* permission requests)

  - Very small tweak to phrasing in file write confirmation prompt
- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/306
- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/307
  - Meta-issue (AI generated?) summarizing many of the other ones here
- [x] https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/342
  - Draft PR: https://github.com/github/sweagentd/pull/7608
- [ ] PowerShell `Measure-Object` should be approved by default

## Other things to think about

- when a user opts to approve a command for the rest of the session we could persist that into the session log such that when they later `--resume` they don't have to go through all the same approvals again

issues.title: SCP-style remote retains leading slash in GitHub repository owner

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
## Description

Copilot CLI retains the leading slash in an SCP-style GitHub remote when deriving the repository owner:

```text
Remote:                 git@github.com:/Azure/AgentBaker.git
Expected repository:    Azure/AgentBaker
Observed repository:    /Azure/AgentBaker
Observed API owner:     %2FAzure
```

This produces an invalid GitHub REST API request and repeated HTTP 404 errors for PR discovery. The repository in this report, `Azure/AgentBaker`, is public.

The same startup also reports an HTTP 400 while fetching MCP registry policy and blocks all three configured non-default MCP servers. **The repository parsing error is directly demonstrated by the logs; its causal connection to the MCP policy error is not yet confirmed.** The CLI does not log the policy request URL or response body, which makes that part difficult to diagnose.

## Affected version / environment

- GitHub Copilot CLI `1.0.90-6`
- Linux
- Terminal CLI, GitHub.com
- Public repository: https://github.com/Azure/AgentBaker
- Remote at the time of the failing startup: `git@github.com:/Azure/AgentBaker.git`

## Steps to reproduce

The following minimal recipe recreates the remote configuration from the affected checkout. The evidence below comes from that existing checkout, not a separately executed clean-clone reproduction.

1. Create a disposable checkout of the public repository:

   ```sh
   git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Azure/AgentBaker.git agentbaker-url-repro
   cd agentbaker-url-repro
   ```

2. Set an SCP-style remote with a slash immediately after the colon:

   ```sh
   git remote set-url origin git@github.com:/Azure/AgentBaker.git
   git remote get-url origin
   # git@github.com:/Azure/AgentBaker.git
   ```

3. With a GitHub-authenticated Copilot CLI, start a fresh process:

   ```sh
   copilot --log-level debug
   ```

4. Inspect the process log under `~/.copilot/logs/` for repository identification and PR lookup. In the affected session, the repository is identified as `/Azure/AgentBaker`, and the PR lookup uses `/repos/%2FAzure/AgentBaker/pulls`.

5. If non-default MCP servers are configured, also check whether the startup reports `MCP servers were blocked by policy` and `Failed to fetch MCP registry policy: 400 Bad Request`. This additional symptom was observed, but may have another cause or require additional conditions.

### Suggested A/B check

Change only the remote to the conventional form, then fully exit and start a new CLI process:

```sh
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:Azure/AgentBaker.git
copilot --log-level debug
```

The leading-slash form was observed during diagnosis; the remote has since been changed to the conventional form. A fresh-process A/B result has not yet been captured, so this is a proposed verification step, not a claim that the MCP failure is fixed.

## Expected behavior

Normalize the GitHub repository identity to `Azure/AgentBaker`, without a leading slash in the owner. PR discovery should use:

```text
https://api.github.com/repos/Azure/AgentBaker/pulls?head=Azure%3Amain&state=open&per_page=1
```

If this remote spelling is intentionally unsupported, report a clear remote-parsing error rather than silently constructing an invalid API owner.

A failure to retrieve MCP policy should remain distinct from an explicit policy denial in the user-facing message. Diagnostic logs should include a safely redacted endpoint and error response, without authentication material.

## Actual behavior and sanitized log evidence

These are excerpts from the affected process log. Timestamps and GitHub request IDs have been removed; no full logs are attached.

### Incorrect repository identity

```text
[INFO] Session indexing debug: SESSION_INDEXING=true, repository=/Azure/AgentBaker
```

### Invalid PR API request

```text
[ERROR] Request to GitHub API at https://api.github.com/repos/%2FAzure/AgentBaker/pulls?head=%2FAzure%3Amain&state=open&per_page=1 failed with status 404 (request ID: [REDACTED]), body: {"message":"Not Found","documentation_url":"https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#list-pull-requests","status":"404"}
[DEBUG] [branchPr] PR lookup failed for /Azure/AgentBaker: HttpError: Not Found - https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#list-pull-requests
```

The same malformed PR request appears repeatedly in the process log, not just once at startup.

### Concurrent MCP policy failure (causality unconfirmed)

```text
[WARNING] Failed to fetch MCP registry policy: Failed to fetch MCP registry policy: 400 Bad Request. Non-default MCP servers will be blocked until the policy can be fetched.
```

The startup warning listed three configured non-default MCP servers as blocked. Their names and endpoints are omitted because they are not needed to demonstrate the parsing failure.

The managed-settings resolution logged `source=none`, `bypassDisabled=false`, and `serverFetchFailed=false`. No local `/etc/github-copilot/managed-settings.json` was present.

During diagnosis, a separate authenticated request using `gh api /copilot/mcp_registry` returned HTTP 200, with both returned registry entries reporting `registry_access: "allow_all"`. Registry owner identities and configuration are intentionally omitted. This direct request is not an exact replay of the CLI request and does not prove why the latter returned HTTP 400.

## Additional context

- Related: github/copilot-cli#4374 reports an MCP registry-policy HTTP 400 tied to non-GitHub remote context; this report instead concerns a GitHub.com SCP-style remote and a visible leading-slash normalization error.
- Related: github/copilot-cli#4585 reports SSH remote recognition failures on GHE, but not this specific `%2F` owner encoding.
- Unlike github/copilot-cli#4957, the affected process log does not contain `blocked by enterprise customization lockdown`; the observed persistent MCP warning is the registry-policy HTTP 400.

Privacy: this report excludes local usernames and absolute checkout paths, account/enterprise identities, session IDs, request IDs, credentials, and private MCP server names/URLs. Only the public repository example and selected sanitized diagnostic text are included.

issues.title: Provide a system-wide Windows installer for enterprise deployment

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

In our environment, GitHub Copilot CLI installs into the user profile and also attempts to execute files from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\copilot`.  This conflicts with our corporate security requirements, which restrict execution from user-writable directories. Installing the main executable centrally is therefore insufficient if the CLI still extracts or runs supporting executables from the user profile.  We need a supported deployment option that works without weakening these restrictions.

### Proposed solution

Provide an official system-wide Windows installer, preferably MSI, with the following capabilities:

- **Machine-wide installation** into an administrator-controlled location such as `%ProgramFiles%\GitHub Copilot CLI`.
- **All bundled executables and runtime dependencies installed centrally**, without extracting or executing them from `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, `%APPDATA%`, or other user-writable locations.
- **Silent installation, upgrade, and uninstallation** for centralized software deployment.
- **Operation without local administrator privileges** after installation.
- **Administrator-controlled updates**, including an option to disable automatic updates and prevent per-user executable downloads.
- **Clear separation between application binaries and user data**. Configuration, authentication information, logs, and session history may remain in the user profile, but application executables should not.
- **Documentation of executable locations and update behavior** so administrators can configure application-control policies appropriately.

## Acceptance criteria

An administrator can deploy GitHub Copilot CLI once for all users. A standard user can then use it without the CLI installing, extracting, updating, or executing its own bundled binaries in user-writable directories.

This should work in an environment where execution from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\copilot` and other user-profile directories is blocked.

## Business value

This would make GitHub Copilot CLI deployable in managed corporate environments without requiring security-policy exceptions or unsupported packaging workarounds.

issues.title: SDK with BYOK providers: short model names aren't matched to the provider's models (custom agents fail; a short session model fails with a misleading "No GitHub OAuth token" error)

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug


When an SDK session configures BYOK `providers` and `models`, its models are only known as
provider-qualified ids such as `copilot/gpt-5.4-mini`. Any model given by its **short name** is not
matched to them, even when exactly one configured provider serves that model:

1. **Custom agents.** An agent whose `model` is a short name fails when the main agent starts it.
   The tool call returns
   `Model 'gpt-5.4-mini' is not available. Available models: copilot/gpt-5.6-sol, copilot/gpt-5.6-luna, copilot/gpt-5.4-mini, copilot/gpt-5.6-sol, copilot/gpt-5.6-luna, copilot/gpt-5.4-mini`.
   The list itself names the model, and also lists every model twice. This happens for agents
   passed as `customAgents` and for `.github/agents/*.agent.md` files loaded with
   `enableConfigDiscovery: true`.
2. **Session model.** `createSession` accepts a short `model` (`session.start` reports
   `selectedModel: "gpt-5.6-sol"`), but the first turn fails with
   `Execution failed: InvalidArg, No GitHub OAuth token or Copilot HMAC key provided`. The debug log
   shows the turn quietly switched to `claude-sonnet-4`, a model that isn't configured, on GitHub's
   own inference:

   ```text
   [WARNING] model resolution before the turn did not commit a new selection {"error":"No model available. Check policy enablement under GitHub Settings > Copilot"}
   [WARNING] turn model is in neither the picker nor the unfiltered catalog, ...; falling back to default capabilities and the chat-completions wire {"model":"claude-sonnet-4",...}
   ```

   The error points at authentication, not at the model name. When the user is also signed in to
   GitHub, the request would presumably go to GitHub's own inference instead of the configured
   provider, without any error.

**Why it matters.** Agent files are shared between Copilot CLI and SDK sessions. In CLI BYOK mode
the same `.agent.md` must use the short name, and a file can't know which provider name an SDK host
chose. With discovery on, the main agent sometimes recovers by retrying with the qualified name. That
costs a failed tool call, depends on the model noticing, and in our runs a retry sometimes picked a
different model instead. GitHub Agentic Workflows currently rewrites every agent's model to a
qualified name before creating the session; we'd rather not keep that workaround.

This short-name matching is probably also the SDK-mode cause of #5126 (built-in agents' default
models never match).


### Affected version

`@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.19 against `copilot --headless` from Copilot CLI 1.0.96. Also seen with SDK 1.0.16 and CLI 1.0.90.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior


Start `copilot --headless --port <port>` with no GitHub sign-in, and use one BYOK provider:

```json
{
  "providers": [{ "name": "copilot", "type": "openai", "wireApi": "responses",
                  "baseUrl": "https://api.githubcopilot.com", "bearerToken": "<token>",
                  "headers": { "Copilot-Integration-Id": "copilot-developer-cli" } }],
  "models": [{ "id": "gpt-5.6-sol", "provider": "copilot" },
             { "id": "gpt-5.6-luna", "provider": "copilot" },
             { "id": "gpt-5.4-mini", "provider": "copilot" }]
}
```

All models are on the same wire API, so #5103 doesn't apply.

1. **Custom agent with a short model:** session `model: "copilot/gpt-5.6-sol"`, plus
   `customAgents: [{ "name": "quick-checker", "description": "Finds where a function is defined", "prompt": "...", "model": "gpt-5.4-mini" }]`.
   Prompt: `Use the task tool with agent_type "quick-checker" to find which file defines add_numbers.`
   Observed: the first task call fails with `Model 'gpt-5.4-mini' is not available. Available models: ...copilot/gpt-5.4-mini...`.
2. **Same agent from a file:** no `customAgents`, `enableConfigDiscovery: true`, and
   `.github/agents/quick-checker.agent.md` with `model: gpt-5.4-mini` in its front matter. Observed:
   the same error.
3. **Control:** the same agent with `"model": "copilot/gpt-5.4-mini"` runs on mini
   (`modelSelectionSource: "agent_definition_default"`).
4. **Short session model:** `model: "gpt-5.6-sol"` and prompt `Reply with the single word OK.`
   Observed: `session.error` `Execution failed: InvalidArg, No GitHub OAuth token or Copilot HMAC key provided`,
   with the `claude-sonnet-4` warnings above in the debug log.

### Expected behavior


1. A short model name resolves to the configured provider model with that id when exactly one
   provider serves it: `gpt-5.4-mini` → `copilot/gpt-5.4-mini`. This applies to the session model,
   custom agents from `customAgents` or discovered files, and built-in agent defaults (#5126).
2. If several providers serve the id, pick deterministically (for example, the provider whose wire
   API the model supports), or report the ambiguity and list the qualified choices.
3. A session model that can't be resolved fails at `createSession` with an error that names the
   model and the available ids. It isn't silently replaced by another model, and the error doesn't
   point at authentication.

### Additional context

- Related: #5126 (built-in agents ignore their default models under BYOK) and #5103 (one wire
  API per BYOK session in CLI mode).
- Environment: Linux ARM64 (Ubuntu 24.04), Node 22. Also seen on GitHub Actions Linux x64 runners
  through GitHub Agentic Workflows' AWF API proxy as the BYOK provider.

issues.title: BYOK: built-in agents (explore, task, research) never use their default models and silently run on the session model

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug


Copilot CLI's built-in agents declare their own models in their definitions (unchanged from 1.0.90
to 1.0.96):

| Agent | Default models, in order | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| `explore` | `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.4-mini` | `low` |
| `task` | `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.4-mini`, `claude-haiku-4.5` | - |
| `research` | `claude-sonnet-5` | - |

In a normal signed-in session these models are used, so a quick `explore` search runs on a small
model. **In a BYOK session they are never used.** Every built-in agent runs on the session's
model, even when the BYOK provider serves the default model and the session lists it.

As far as we can tell, the cause is the check that a definition's model is "available" in the
session. Under BYOK it never passes:

- **CLI with provider environment variables** (`COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_*`,
  `COPILOT_MODEL`): the only available model is `COPILOT_MODEL`.
- **SDK with `providers` and `models`:** the session's models are provider-qualified
  (`copilot/gpt-5.6-luna`), while the definitions use short names (`gpt-5.6-luna`), so they never
  match. Issue #5127 describes the same short-name matching problem for models the user
  configures.

**The fallback is silent and misreported.** It isn't logged at the default log level, and the
`subagent.started` and `subagent.completed` events report
`"modelSelectionSource": "agent_definition_default"` with `model` set to the session model. That
reads as if the definition chose that model.

**Why it matters.** A BYOK session on an expensive model makes every built-in agent expensive too.
GitHub Agentic Workflows (`github/gh-aw`) runs Copilot through a proxy configured as a BYOK provider
and picks the session model per task. On runs on Claude Opus, `explore` and `research` used 49–58%
of the run's AI credits, all on Opus, although their definitions ask for Luna, mini and Sonnet.
`explore` is also slower on a large model.

**The provider does serve the default model.** As a diagnostic, setting
`subagents.agents.explore.model` in `~/.copilot/settings.json` makes `explore` run on Luna through
the same provider (`modelSelectionSource: "configured_preference"`). We don't want to rely on that
setting as a fix: it skips the cost guard (a Sol preference in a Luna session ran on Sol), so every
integrator would have to re-implement the runtime's model choice and cost rule.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.96, and `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.19 against `copilot --headless` 1.0.96. Also seen on 1.0.90 and 1.0.95.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior


**CLI mode** (BYOK straight to the Copilot API, no proxy):

```bash
mkdir demo && cd demo
printf 'def add_numbers(a, b):\n    return a + b\n' > math_utils.py
export COPILOT_OFFLINE=true \
  COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=https://api.githubcopilot.com \
  COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai \
  COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API=responses \
  COPILOT_PROVIDER_BEARER_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)" \
  COPILOT_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol
copilot --allow-all-tools --no-ask-user --log-level all --log-dir ./logs -p \
  'Use the task tool with agent_type "explore" to find which file defines add_numbers. Do not search yourself.'
```

Observed: the output shows `● Explore (model: gpt-5.6-sol)`, and the log's `subagent.started`
event has `"model":"gpt-5.6-sol","taskModelSource":"unset","modelSelectionSource":"agent_definition_default"`.

**SDK mode:** start `copilot --headless --port <port>` and create a session with these options:

```json
{
  "model": "copilot/gpt-5.6-sol",
  "providers": [{ "name": "copilot", "type": "openai", "wireApi": "responses",
                  "baseUrl": "https://api.githubcopilot.com", "bearerToken": "<token>",
                  "headers": { "Copilot-Integration-Id": "copilot-developer-cli" } }],
  "models": [{ "id": "gpt-5.6-sol", "provider": "copilot" },
             { "id": "gpt-5.6-luna", "provider": "copilot" },
             { "id": "gpt-5.4-mini", "provider": "copilot" }]
}
```

Send the same prompt.

Observed: `subagent.started` has `"model":"copilot/gpt-5.6-sol","modelSelectionSource":"agent_definition_default"`,
and every request goes to `gpt-5.6-sol`. This happens although `copilot/gpt-5.6-luna` is one of the
session's models.

**Control** (shows the provider serves Luna): add
`{"subagents":{"agents":{"explore":{"model":"gpt-5.6-luna"}}}}` to `~/.copilot/settings.json` and
rerun the CLI steps. `● Explore (model: gpt-5.6-luna)`, with
`"modelSelectionSource":"configured_preference"`.

### Expected behavior


1. Under BYOK, a built-in agent uses its definition's model when the session can serve it, just as
   in a signed-in session:
   - **SDK mode:** match the definition's short name to the session's provider-qualified model
     (`gpt-5.6-luna` → `copilot/gpt-5.6-luna`).
   - **CLI mode:** don't treat `COPILOT_MODEL` as the only available model. The session needs a way
     to know the provider's other models; #3795 (BYOK model discovery) would provide one.
2. The existing cost guard keeps applying, so a default that costs more than the session model
   (`research` → Sonnet under Luna) is still skipped. It should also work under BYOK, where pricing
   may have to come from the model id.
3. A default the session can't reach is skipped, not tried and failed. For example, in CLI mode a
   Claude default under a GPT session model is on the other wire API (#5103).
4. When the agent does fall back to the session model, the fallback is visible: logged at info or
   warning level, and reported in `subagent.started` with its own `modelSelectionSource` value or a
   fallback reason, not as `agent_definition_default`.

### Additional context

- Related: #5103 (one wire API per BYOK session) and #3795 (BYOK model discovery). This issue
  doesn't depend on #5103 for same-family defaults: `explore`'s defaults are GPT models, which a
  GPT session can reach today.
- `code-review` and `general-purpose` have no default model and inherit the session model, which is
  expected.
- GitHub Agentic Workflows confirmed the same behaviour on GitHub Actions (Linux x64, CLI 1.0.90 and
  1.0.95, CLI and SDK mode): all five built-in agents ran on the session model.

issues.title: `--agent <name>` selection is dropped ~1s after startup (race with sign-in / MCP reload)

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When starting the CLI with `--agent <name>`, the custom agent is selected and then silently deselected ~1 s later, before any user input. The banner shows `Selected custom agent: my-agent`, then `MCP Servers reloaded: 1 server connected`, and the agent disappears from the status bar; the session falls back to the default agent.

It looks like a race between the startup agent selection and the agent/MCP refresh after sign-in. `events.jsonl` of an affected session (no user input in between):
```
14:59:11.603 subagent.selected {"agentName":"my-agent"}
14:59:11.765 subagent.selected {"agentName":"my-agent"}
14:59:11.717 subagent.selected {"agentName":"my-agent"}   <- out of order, concurrent re-selection
14:59:12.400 subagent.deselected {}
```
The deselect follows `Signed in to https://github.com` and the MCP client re-init in the process log (`Service initialized as client` -> `task cancelled` -> `Service initialized as client`).

### Affected version

1.0.95

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Have a custom agent available (user-level `~/.copilot/agents/my-agent.md`, or plugin-provided).
2. Start interactively: `copilot --agent my-agent`
3. Don't type anything; watch the banner and status bar for ~2 s.
4. Agent is gone from the status bar; `events.jsonl` shows `subagent.deselected`.

### Expected behavior

The agent passed via `--agent` stays selected for the whole session.

### Additional context

- Frequency (automated pty launches, no input, 15 s each): dropped **5/6** with a user-level agent (`--agent my-agent`), **4/6** with a plugin agent (`--agent myplugin:my-agent`).
- When MCP startup failed (`Failed to start MCP Servers: session not found`), the agent was **never** dropped, which points to the MCP reload / agent-list refresh path clearing the selection.
- Workaround: run `/agent my-agent` after startup.
- macOS (Apple Silicon, arm64), zsh, launched via shell alias with `--allow-all` and several `--deny-tool` flags.

issues.body:
After a Windows restart, I asked Copilot CLI to restore my existing sessions in named Terminal tabs. Instead, the interaction became a lengthy loop of refusals and manual instructions. This is unacceptable friction for a basic recovery task.

Observed on October 12, 2026, with Copilot CLI 1.0.95 on Windows ARM64: Computer Use rejected even a read-only get_window_state request for Windows Terminal with: "actions are blocked for this application by built-in safety policy."

Previous restores succeeded through native PowerShell scripts. That does not prove the UI policy recently changed or that native restoration is blocked. The assistant nevertheless repeatedly treated the UI denial as a blanket restoration ban. Both the recovery experience and that misleading explanation need attention.

Please route this to the Computer Use safety and CLI session-recovery owners. Explain the restriction and provide a clearly supported, consent-based recovery path that preserves sessions, tab identity, and a short status recap. Improve tool guidance so assistants distinguish a UI-tool restriction from native CLI capabilities without bypassing safeguards.

Please test the actual restart-to-recovery workflow before shipping changes around it. Users should not have to reverse-engineer tool boundaries while urgently recovering their work.

issues.title: userPromptSubmitted: only the last plugin's additionalContext reaches the model (sessionStart was fixed in #3589)

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When two or more plugins each return `additionalContext` from a `userPromptSubmitted` hook, only the text of the plugin that is loaded **last** reaches the model. The other plugins' hooks do run, but their text is dropped silently: it does not appear anywhere in the session's `events.jsonl`.

This is the same last-writer-wins behaviour that #3589 reported for `sessionStart`/`subagentStart`, which was fixed in v1.0.88 ("Session and subagent start hooks combine successful additional-context contributions within the hook-output limit"). `userPromptSubmitted` still behaves the old way.

What I observed, with two minimal plugins `alpha` and `beta` (one run per case):

| plugin order (`--plugin-dir`) | `sessionStart` context injected | `userPromptSubmitted` context injected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| alpha, beta | alpha **and** beta (combined) | **beta only** |
| beta, alpha | alpha **and** beta (combined) | **alpha only** |
| alpha, beta — beta's hook prints nothing | — | alpha |
| alpha, beta — beta's hook prints `{}` | — | alpha |

So an empty answer does not override an earlier one, but a non-empty one replaces it instead of being added. A small log written by each hook confirms that both hooks ran in every case.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.95 (`copilotVersion` in `events.jsonl`).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create two plugins, each with a `hooks/hooks.json` that registers a `UserPromptSubmit` (and, for comparison, a `SessionStart`) command hook.
2. Each hook prints a different marker, e.g.
   `{"additionalContext": "Probe marker from alpha: COBALT", "hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "UserPromptSubmit", "additionalContext": "Probe marker from alpha: COBALT"}}`
3. Run `copilot -p "Reply with every probe marker word given to you in this conversation's context, comma-separated." --plugin-dir ./alpha --plugin-dir ./beta`
4. Only the last plugin's `UserPromptSubmit` marker is reported, and only that one appears in `events.jsonl`. Swap the `--plugin-dir` order and the other one wins. Both `SessionStart` markers always appear.

### Expected behavior

`userPromptSubmitted` contributions from several hooks are combined, in execution order, the same way `sessionStart` contributions now are.

### Additional context

This matters for anyone who ships more than one plugin: today, two plugins that both add per-prompt context silently cancel each other out, and which one survives depends on load order.

issues.body: ### Describe the bug When Copilot CLI crashes or exits abruptly, it doesn't restore the terminal modes it enabled. The parent shell then echoes every mouse movement and focus change as raw escape sequences, which leaves the tab unusable. ```text PS C:\...> [555;50;35M[555;49;34M[555;48;34M[555;48;35M ... 1M[O[I[O[I[104;20m ... ``` These modes are left on after the process has exited: | Mode | DECSET | Symptom | | --- | --- | --- | | Mouse tracking | `1000` / `1002` / `1003` / `1006` / `1015` | `[555;x;yM` on every mouse move | | Focus reporting | `1004` | `[I` / `[O` on focus in/out | ### Affected version GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.93 ### Steps to reproduce the behavior 1. Start `copilot` in PowerShell 7 inside Windows Terminal. 2. Use it normally until the CLI crashes or exits abruptly. This is intermittent and I don't have a reliable trigger. 3. At the PowerShell prompt, move the mouse or switch focus away from the window and back. 4. Escape sequences are typed into the prompt. **Workaround:** reset the modes manually: ```powershell Write-Host -NoNewline "`e[?1000l`e[?1002l`e[?1003l`e[?1005l`e[?1006l`e[?1015l`e[?1004l" ``` ### Expected behavior Terminal modes are restored on **every** exit path, including crashes, unhandled errors and forced termination, so the parent shell is left usable. ### Additional context | | | | --- | --- | | **OS** | Windows 11 (10.0.26200), x86_64 | | **Terminal** | Windows Terminal 1.24.12741.0 | | **Shell** | PowerShell 7.6.6 | The session's process log ends abruptly with routine `INFO` entries. There's no error, panic or shutdown entry, which suggests a hard crash rather than a handled exit.

issues.title: Windows: uninstalling an installed plugin fails with Access is denied (os error 5)

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When I try to uninstall the installed `workiq` plugin on Windows, the uninstall fails with an access-denied error.

The UI reports:

```text
Uninstalling plugin "workiq"...
Failed to uninstall plugin: Request plugins.uninstall failed with message: Failed to uninstall plugin: 拒绝访问。 (os error 5)
```

`拒绝访问` means "Access is denied". I asked the agent to inspect which processes were keeping the plugin resources in use. It found that Copilot CLI itself still had the plugin's MCP server running and holding those resources, preventing the uninstall.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI `1.0.96-2`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Observed:
1. Have the `workiq` plugin installed on Windows.
2. Request plugin uninstall through the Copilot plugin UI (`plugins.uninstall`).
3. The operation fails with `Access is denied (os error 5)`.

After the failure, I asked the agent to check process usage. It identified the CLI's own running MCP server for the plugin as the resource holder.

### Expected behavior

Uninstall should complete without requiring the user to terminate the CLI manually. If the CLI owns an active MCP server or other resources for the plugin, it should stop/dispose those resources and release relevant handles before removing the plugin files.

If another process prevents removal, report the affected path and actionable recovery guidance rather than only the generic OS error. A failed uninstall should not leave inconsistent plugin registration or partially deleted files.

### Additional context

- Operating system: Windows.
- Plugin: `workiq`.
- Operation: `plugins.uninstall`.
- Process inspection by the agent identified Copilot CLI's own running plugin MCP server as keeping the plugin resources in use.
- Related reports: #4095 and #4570 describe similar access-denied failures involving plugin directory handles on Windows. This report records the uninstall failure and asks that CLI-owned MCP server teardown also be checked; the failures may share a root cause.

issues.title: Configurable prompt-cache TTL per agent and per provider/model (opencode.jsonc)
Remote MCP servers fail to connect when endpoint RTT is above ~250ms (autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout too small)
issues.body:
## Description

Remote MCP servers whose endpoint RTT exceeds ~250ms never load. On every session start opencode logs:

```
level=WARN run=7f94844c message="server unavailable" key=deepwiki type=remote status=failed
```

The server's healthy and reachable. curl completes a full MCP `initialize` handshake against the same URL and gets a valid result. The client's own TCP connect is what fails, so the tools never get registered. Startup drags too, since `connectRemote` tries StreamableHTTP and then SSE, and each attempt burns its own timeout before the warning shows up.

## Plugins

None

## OpenCode version

1.18.34 (the `opencode` deb package, `@opencode-ai/desktop`). 

## Steps to reproduce

1. Be more than ~250ms RTT from the remote MCP endpoint. Much of the world is, for anything hosted in US or EU regions.
2. Add a remote server: `"deepwiki": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp", "enabled": true }`
3. Start opencode and watch `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` for the line above.
4. Reproduce outside opencode on the same host:

```
$ node -e "fetch('https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp',{method:'POST'}).catch(e=>console.log(e.code||e.cause?.code))"
UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT

$ NODE_OPTIONS=--network-family-autoselection-attempt-timeout=2000 \
  node -e "fetch('https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp',{method:'POST'}).then(r=>console.log(r.status))"
400
```

Three runs fail without the flag, three succeed with it. The 400 is expected, since that POST carries no MCP body. The point is that the TCP and TLS handshakes now complete.

## Screenshot and/or share link

Not applicable, there's no UI to capture. The log line above is the whole symptom.

## Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64

## Terminal

n/a, opencode desktop app

## Root cause

`mcp.deepwiki.com` returns 3 A and 3 AAAA records, and the addresses rotate between lookups. TCP connect to the A records measures 263-412ms from here, 3 samples each. Node's happy-eyeballs connect windows every address attempt at 250ms by default (`autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout`), so each attempt gets destroyed just before it finishes. Sweeping that value on this host with `net.setDefaultAutoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout()`:

```
250ms (default) -> no connect, attempt destroyed and no error surfaces
300ms           -> CONNECTED @901ms
400ms           -> CONNECTED @395ms
600ms           -> CONNECTED @294ms
```

Two failure signatures come out of this, depending on which addresses the pool hands back. Sometimes `fetch` fails in ~825ms with an `AggregateError [ETIMEDOUT]` listing every address. Other times `fetch` and `net.connect` hang with no error at all, which undici reports as `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` after its 10s default. Instant failure and indefinite hang are the same bug.

For whoever picks this up: the warning comes from `Effect.logWarning("server unavailable", ...)` in `create`, and remote connects run through `connectRemote` in `packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts`. Nothing in that path touches `autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout`, and a search of the repo turns up zero references to it anywhere, so the 250ms default is inherited untouched. Config can't reach it either: `connectRemote` wraps each transport in `withTimeout(client.connect(t), mcp.timeout ?? 30_000)`, which sits well above the point where the TCP connect dies. In practice the failure surfaces earlier than that, at undici's 10s connect timeout, once per transport.

I couldn't instrument the Electron process directly. The connect path was verified with Node's `net` and `fetch` on the same host, and the client log line matches.

## Suggested fix

```ts
net.setDefaultAutoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout(1000)
```

early in the process, before any MCP client is created. The cliff sits near 300ms and I measured up to 412ms, so 1000ms leaves headroom, and the value's a stagger interval rather than a wait, so fast connects aren't affected. Both Node and Bun implement the API. Retrying with `family: 4` after a connect failure would cover the remaining cases.

Workaround I'm using for now that works: pin one endpoint IP in /etc/hosts. Single-address lookups skip the race entirely so the connect completes. But it's obviously fragile.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Show why an agent needs a permission before the user approves it
issues.body:
## Problem

Permission prompts show the requested operation or scope, but generally lack an explicit explanation of why it is needed for the current task. Existing tool-specific metadata and task descriptions do not provide a consistent requester-to-user explanation across clients.

For example, access to `~/.config/example/*` identifies the resource but leaves the user to infer why the agent needs it and how it relates to their request. This becomes harder during longer workflows and subagent operations.

## Requested enhancement

Allow requesters to attach an optional human-readable `reason` to permission requests and display it before approval, alongside the authoritative command, path, or scope.

```text
Run command: npm test

Reason:
Run the project tests to verify the requested change.

Allow once / Allow always / Reject
```

```text
Access external directory: ~/.config/example/*

Reason:
Read the existing provider configuration before updating
the setting requested by the user.

Allow once / Allow always / Reject
```

When no reason is supplied, existing behavior should remain unchanged.

## Implementation considerations

Source inspection at commit `ecbc6ccac85b3e8087b6445e584318419b9e2b34` found both legacy `PermissionV1.Request` requests and Core V2 requests, whose canonical schema is `Permission.Request` in `packages/schema/src/permission.ts` and which Core exposes as `PermissionV2.Request`.

The value should survive request construction, events, pending-request APIs, generated clients, and client compatibility conversions. In particular, the browser application converts both V2 live events and pending-list responses into legacy-shaped requests; both paths need to preserve the explanation.

Custom tools could supply the field through `ToolContext.ask`. Core tools use `PermissionV2.Service.assert`. Supporting ordinary agent-generated reasons also requires an explicit way for selected tools to receive task-specific intent: adding a transport field alone will not make tools populate it.

A possible legacy custom-tool API shape, after adding the optional field, is:

```ts
await ctx.ask({
  permission: "external_directory",
  patterns: ["~/.config/example/*"],
  always: ["~/.config/example/*"],
  metadata: {},
  reason:
    "Read the existing provider configuration before updating the requested setting.",
})
```

The exact implementation is up to the maintainers. A first-class optional field would give clients a consistent contract rather than requiring them to infer intent or agree on an undocumented metadata key.

## Acceptance criteria

- Requests may omit the reason without changing existing behavior.
- Supplied reasons survive both live events and pending-request retrieval.
- Generated API/SDK contracts expose the optional field.
- TUI and the shared Desktop/browser permission UI display the reason alongside the actual permission scope.
- Requesters can provide short, task-specific explanations; the UI does not invent generic reasons.
- Reasons remain untrusted explanatory text and do not affect matching, approval, denial, automatic-response decisions, or saved scope.
- Tests cover propagation, absence, rendering, and unchanged authorization behavior.

## Security considerations

The actual command, path, permission type, and scope must remain visible and authoritative.

A reason must not bypass permission rules, override denial, automatically approve an operation, broaden access, or hide or replace the actual operation. It is an explanation from the requester, not evidence that the action is safe.

## Related work

#37164 requests native permission creation from `tool.execute.before`, including plugin-computed explanations. This proposal concerns explanation transport and display for permission requests generally; the two could share the same field and UI without making plugin-hook permission creation a prerequisite.

Human approval/rejection feedback is a separate, opposite-direction flow:

- This proposal: **agent/tool → explanation → human, before authorization**.
- Rejection feedback: **human → explanation → agent, after deciding**.

The goal is to help the user understand both **what is requested** and **why it is needed** before making the permission decision.

Claude progress updates written before a tool call never show
issues.body:
### Description

Claude 5.5 models (and Fable 5+, Mythos 5.1+) send the short notes they write for the user between tool calls as "progress update" thinking blocks, not as text blocks. See https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#progress-updates.

opencode never shows these notes, for two reasons:

1. With adaptive thinking, Anthropic's default display is `omitted`, so the progress-update block comes back with empty text. Only the signature is left.
2. Even when the block has text (display `summarized`), the TUI renders it as collapsed reasoning, not as a message.

So when the model writes "Here is the draft: ..." and then calls a tool, the user never sees the draft. The model then refers to "the draft above", which isn't on screen.

This is the same bug as #52735, which was closed when v1 was frozen. It still happens on `dev` (v2).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` (or `claude-opus-5-5`).
2. Ask for something where the model writes a message for you and then runs a tool, e.g. "write a two-line poem, then run `ls`".
3. The poem doesn't show. In the stored session, the assistant message contains a reasoning part with empty text whose signature decodes to a `narration` block, right before the tool call.

`dev`

issues.title: Agent request body and headers do not reach V2 model requests
issues.body:
### Description

V2 accepts agent-level `request.body` and `request.headers`, but the Session model-request builder does not use them. A subagent can declare `temperature` in its Markdown frontmatter and load successfully while the provider request omits that value.

The Agents documentation currently notes this limitation. Related: #49550, which also covers `request.settings`. This report is limited to body/header overlays; it does not cover settings such as transport or timeouts.

### OpenCode version

V2 dev at 15b24ae12d (package version 2.0.27).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create `.opencode/agents/reviewer.md`:

```markdown
---
description: Reviews changes
mode: subagent
request:
  body:
    temperature: 0.2
  headers:
    x-agent-probe: reviewer
---
Review the current changes.
```

2. Use an OpenAI-compatible model that supports temperature and dispatch the reviewer subagent.
3. Inspect the provider request. The agent's temperature and custom header are not applied.

A local regression at `SessionModelRequest.prepare` reproduces the omission without a live model: the configured temperature is absent before the context hook. Config loading populates the agent record, but callers pass only the agent ID to the request builder.

Expected: apply the selected agent's body/header overlays to its model requests, retaining plugin overrides and runtime-owned session headers.

### Plugins

None required by the regression.

### Operating System

macOS; the omission is in the platform-independent request builder.

issues.body:
### Description

## Summary

Follow-up to #38064 (auto-closed by stale bot on Sep 21 after 60 days of inactivity — this bug is still present and still causing real damage). `opencode acp` still persists an empty session row on `session/new`, and nothing ever cleans it up. Confirmed on **v2.0.26** with an IntelliJ IDEA integration (not just Zed): one machine accumulated **1,672 junk sessions in ~4 months** (1,648 `New session - <ISO>` stubs + 24 untitled rows from ACP client initializations), burying ~400 real sessions in the session picker.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.26
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.19045 (win32 x64)
- Shell: C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest
- ACP client: IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 plugin launching `opencode acp` per project (also reproducible with any client that eagerly calls `session/new`)
- Active plugins: none in opencode config (MCP servers only)

## Reproduction

1. Configure an ACP client to launch `opencode acp` (observed process chain: `idea64.exe` → `cmd.exe /c opencode.cmd acp` → `opencode acp` → `opencode serve --stdio --port 0`, one instance per project directory).
2. Let the client initialize a thread (`session/new`), then abandon it without prompting (close panel, switch project, restart IDE).
3. Open the session list in the TUI or `GET /api/session`.

Each initialization left behind sessions with:

- `title: null` (v2.0.26 path) or `title: "New session - <ISO>"` (earlier versions)
- all token counters 0, `model: null`, `agent: null`
- `time_created == time_updated`, zero rows in `message`
- **created in pairs** (10–60 ms apart per client initialization)

## Expected Behavior

Same as #38064: sessions should only be persisted once they contain user activity (lazy persist on first `session/prompt`), and/or empty ACP sessions should be swept on close/connect. Option 3 (defer persistence) from the original issue remains the correct long-term fix — the V2 ACP port did not adopt any of the suggested fixes.

## Actual Behavior

Empty sessions persist forever. Hard numbers from one machine (SQLite `session_v2` table):

- 1,648 sessions titled `New session - <ISO>`, zero tokens, zero messages, spanning 2026-05-28 → 2026-09-24
- 24 untitled sessions with `model = NULL`, `agent = NULL`, from v2.0.26 ACP initializations between 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-13
- vs. only ~400 sessions with real content

Every IDEA AI-panel initialization produced exactly 2 empty rows. Server log correlates 1:1: each `cli starting args=["acp"]` is followed by the matching empty-session pair seconds later.

## Additional Context

- Cleanup via `DELETE /api/session/{id}` works fine (bulk-deleted all 1,672 through the API as a workaround), but the stubs keep coming back with normal IDE usage — the fix has to be server-side.
- The original issue's mechanism analysis (`newSession` eager persist, `closeSession` only aborting, no `session/delete` in ACP 0.21) still matches v2.0.26 behavior exactly.

issues.title: ai: OpenAI Chat tool-content guard aborts session drain without identifying the offending part
issues.body:
### Description

An email/MCP workflow on a locally patched OpenCode 2.0.28 backend failed to send with a local request-lowering error, rather than an HTTP error from the model:

```text
2026-10-13T22:18:58.032Z level=ERROR message="Failed to drain Session"
AI.Error: OpenAI Chat tool messages only support tool-result content for now
  OpenAIChat.fromRequest
  LLM.compile
  SessionStep.attempt
  SessionRunner.runStep
  SessionRunner.drain
cause: AI.Error.InvalidRequest: OpenAI Chat tool messages only support tool-result content for now
```

The guard also exists in the unmodified `v2.0.28` source: `packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts`, `lowerToolMessages`, rejects each top-level tool-message content part that fails `ProviderShared.supportsContent(part, ["tool-result"])`. This is a **message-envelope content-type rejection**, not rejection of a media MIME type nested inside a valid tool result. The request never reaches the provider.

I am not proposing that the guard be removed. The unresolved question is how the core/plugin pipeline produced a tool-role message containing a different top-level content part. At minimum, please include the offending message/part index and content type in the error, and surface a recovery path rather than only a failed-drain exception. If this input should be impossible, a regression at the core-to-AI request boundary would help identify the producer. Any fallback must retain tool-call/result pairing; silently discarding arbitrary tool history would be unsafe.

Related but different: #50775/#50776 concern a non-array `tool-result.result.value` during core preparation; #52448/#54798 concern unsupported MIME types inside tool results. Neither addresses this top-level role/content guard.

### Plugins

OpenChamber integration, OMO, context-mode, Meridian, EnvSitter guard, OpenCode Claude provider, and Superpowers. MCP tools were available. No specific plugin or MCP server has been isolated as the producer.

### OpenCode version

2.0.28, Windows x64, local r1 build carrying six runtime/location/plugin fixes. The OpenAI Chat lowering guard is unchanged from the release tag. This is not yet a clean-stock end-to-end reproduction.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Observed: use an existing tool-using email/MCP session through the OpenAI Chat route, then send another prompt. Session drain failed with the stack above. Exact model and offending history part were not captured in the redacted log evidence.
2. Suggested isolating test: supply a tool-role message with a non-`tool-result` top-level content part to `OpenAIChat.fromRequest`; confirm this precise `InvalidRequest` guard, distinct from media lowering errors.
3. To isolate the real producer, capture only role, message/part index, and content-type discriminants immediately before `LLM.compile`, then replay a redacted minimal request. Do not log email contents or credentials. I have not yet performed that capture or established that every later prompt fails.

Expected: actionable validation at the producer boundary and an identifiable recovery path. Actual: sends in the affected workflow failed with the generic failed-drain exception.

### Screenshot and/or share link

Redacted stack above; private email history is not shared.

### Operating System

Windows 11, win32 x64.

### Terminal

OpenChamber desktop client.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: models: TUI picker cannot distinguish identical model names across providers
issues.body:
## Summary

When multiple providers define models with the same name/ID (e.g., the same
model served through different API keys or accounts), the TUI model picker
shows several entries with identical display names and no indication of which
provider each entry belongs to, so users cannot tell them apart when selecting
a model.

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.0.28
- OS: Darwin 27.0.0 (darwin arm64)
- Terminal: Apple_Terminal, TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: None found in config

## Reproduction

1. In `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, configure several
   `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` providers that each define the same model IDs —
   e.g. providers `sensenova`, `sensenova-copy`, `sensenova-copy2`,
   `sensenova-copy3`, `sensenova-copy4`, each with models `deepseek-v4-flash`,
   `glm-5.2`, `sensenova-6.8-flash-lite`, `sensenova-u1-fast` (same baseURL,
   different API keys).
2. Open the model picker in the TUI.
3. Notice multiple entries with exactly the same display name.

## Expected Behavior

Each entry in the TUI model picker should display a provider identifier — e.g.
`provider/model` (the `opencode models` CLI already prints
`sensenova-copy2/glm-5.2`), a provider column, or provider grouping — so
entries from different providers can be distinguished and searched.

## Actual Behavior

Picker entries render with only the model name. The config above produces
5 providers × 4 identically-named models = 20 visually identical entries, with
no way to tell which provider/API key a given entry will use.

## Additional Context

- Use case: multiple API keys/accounts for the same provider (separate
  quota/billing) configured as separate provider entries; the provider ID is
  the only differentiator.
- `opencode models` CLI already shows `provider/model`, so the TUI picker
  appears inconsistent with the CLI output.
- Frequency: consistently reproducible with the config above.
- No good workaround: renaming the model `name` field per provider works but
  pollutes the displayed model name everywhere.
- Config API keys redacted; provider baseURLs are public endpoints.
