prs.title: fix(core): watch for skills/ inside existing .agents and .claude roots
prs.body:
Fixes the flaky `config plugin reloads > loads skills when <root> appears after startup` test.

Failing runs:
- [dev run 38482970830](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/38482970830/job/115589739988) (linux, `.agents`)
- [PR run 38419395049](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/38419395049) (windows, `../.claude`)

```
error: Timed out waiting for config plugin reloads
(fail) config plugin reloads > loads skills when .agents appears after startup [1217.60ms]
```

## Cause

- **Product bug:** `ConfigCompatibilityPlugin` only watched `<root>/skills` when it already existed. If `.agents` or `.claude` existed without `skills/`, a later `skills/` was never loaded until restart.
- **Same race in the test:** `Bun.write(".agents/skills/probe/SKILL.md")` creates the directories one by one. When the refresh ran between `mkdir .agents` and `mkdir .agents/skills`, the skill was lost.
- **Second gap:** each refresh cleared every watch and reattached it, and the scan did not wait for the new watch. Writes made before the watch attached were lost.
- **Test timing:** each wait polled for about 1 second of wall-clock time, so slow CI runners also failed.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant T as Test / user
  participant C as Config parent watch
  participant P as Compatibility plugin
  T->>C: mkdir .agents
  C->>P: change event, refresh
  P->>P: realPath(.agents/skills) fails, no watch (before)
  T->>T: mkdir .agents/skills, write SKILL.md
  Note over P: nothing is watching, skill is never loaded
```

## Fix

- `compatibility.ts`
  - Watches `<root>/skills` as a `file` target when it is missing, so its creation triggers a refresh. This is the same approach as `ConfigSkillPlugin`.
  - Passes a readiness callback to `watcher.subscribe`, so a newly attached watch triggers one rescan. `Config` uses the same pattern.
  - Removes only the stale watches. Live watches stay attached, so readiness does not loop.
- `reload.test.ts`
  - Replaces the 1-second polling with `settle(events, action, condition)`. It subscribes to `config.updated` or `skill.updated` before the action and checks the condition on each event. The test runner timeout is the only time limit.
  - Creates the root before `skills/`, which covers the product bug. Recreating the whole tree in one write still covers the concurrent case.

## Not in this PR

- **Exit code 139 in the dev run:** turbo crashed, not Bun. The log shows `error: Failed to run "turbo" due to signal SIGSEGV` after `bun test` exited normally with code 1. In this window it happened in 2 of 19 failed linux `unit` jobs, and only after a task failed. That matches a known turbo 2.10.x crash when a run ends with a failed task. The repo pins `turbo` 2.10.2.

prs.title: feat(plugin): let plugins assert permissions
prs.body:
## Summary

Plugins had no in-process way to ask for permission. Built-in tools call `Permission.assert`, but the plugin permission domain only exposed `list`, `get`, `reply`, and the `evaluate` hook. The HTTP `session.permission.create` route doesn't wait for the reply, and a plugin can't reliably reach its own server anyway. V1 plugin tools had `ctx.ask`; V2 had no equivalent.

This adds `ctx.permission.assert` to the plugin context, for both Effect and Promise plugins. It goes through the same permission engine as built-in tools: configured rules, saved "always allow" decisions, and the native approval prompt.

The input is a new `AssertInput` schema in `packages/plugin/src/permission.ts`, shared by both plugin flavours like `options.ts`, and built from the canonical `Permission.Request` fields: `sessionID`, `action`, `resources`, and optional `agent`, `save`, `metadata`, `source`. Effect plugins use its typed form; Promise plugins use its encoded form (plain strings), which the adapter decodes with the same schema.

Outcomes:

| Outcome | Effect plugins | Promise plugins |
|---|---|---|
| Allowed | succeeds | resolves |
| Deny rule | fails with `Tool.Error` (`BlockedError` attached) | rejects with that `Tool.Error` |
| Rejected with feedback | fails with `Tool.Error` (feedback as message, `CorrectedError` attached) | rejects with that `Tool.Error` |
| Plain rejection | defect, so the step ends, as with built-in tools | rejects with `DeclinedError`; rethrowing it from a tool ends the step (#54913) |

Failing with `Tool.Error` matches the tool error type, so an Effect tool can `yield*` the call without mapping errors, and `tool.execute.before` hooks can use it to gate a call. No error classes are added to `@opencode/schema`.

Addresses the in-process request in #52540 and the plugin-side gating in #37164. A tool-context shortcut and enforcing `options.permission` for tools that never assert (#50652, #47177) are left for follow-ups.

## Tests

`packages/core/test/plugin/permission-assert.test.ts` covers both plugin flavours against a permission service that returns each outcome: input forwarding (including decoding plain Promise input), deny and feedback becoming `Tool.Error` with the original attached, and a plain rejection staying a decline.

The core plugin and permission tests pass, and so does typecheck, apart from one existing `@opencode/app` error that is also on `dev`.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55250

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

After a reconnection the location sync can transiently fail while the server/proxy is still settling (the issue reproduces with `/api/agent` answering 502 for about a second after the event stream reconnects). Any single failed request in that sync set the location error, so the session view was replaced by the "location unavailable" recovery prompt even though the directory was fine.

This gives the sync a small bounded retry (3 retries, 500ms apart) before declaring the location missing. Supersession and stale-target behavior is unchanged: a newer sync still cancels an older one's pending retries and retained error. As part of making this testable, the sync/retry logic moves into a `createLocation` creator consumed by `LocationProvider` -- the same pattern as `context/session-retention`.

Limitation (per review discussion): this retries rather than classifying failures -- a location that stays unreachable past the retry window (~1.5s) still surfaces the recovery prompt, and a genuinely missing directory takes that long to report. Distinguishing `location.get` failures from resource-load failures (in `data.location.sync`, or by inspecting `cause` in the session route) is the follow-up the issue points to.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New `packages/tui/test/context/location.test.ts`:
  - "a transient sync failure is retried before the recovery prompt surfaces" -- with a single 502 on one of the sync requests the error must stay unset and the request must be re-issued; fails on the base (the error surfaces immediately), green after.
  - "a persistent sync failure still surfaces the location error" -- errors are not swallowed; they surface once retries are exhausted.

### Issue for this PR

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

`Session.create` already inherits location, metadata and permissions from a parent -- the comment on the inherited fields says children carry them "the way they inherit location, so host policies that read them treat the family uniformly". The in-memory session environment (`SessionEnvironment`, set via `PUT /api/session/{id}/environment`) was the one inheritable thing missed: children created by the `subagent` tool fell back to the service process environment, so e.g. `MARKER` set on the parent never reached the child's shell.

This copies the parent's variables onto the child at creation, at the same central `create` point -- snapshot semantics: later updates to the parent do not retroactively change children (matching the replace semantics of the environment API). No event/durable schema changes; the environment remains in-memory.

### What does this PR do?

The TUI builds its client with plain `OpenCode.make(...)`, so its requests inherit Bun's default five-minute fetch deadline. A plugin command whose `execute` stays pending is accepted by the server (`packages/core/src/command.ts` awaits it with no timeout), but the stock client transport drops the `POST /api/session/:sessionID/command` request at ~5-6 min -- the server logs `499`, the UI restores the composer and navigates away, and the executor keeps running.

`packages/cli/src/run/run.ts` already treats long-running requests this way (`fetch: (request, init) => fetch(request, { ...init, timeout: false })`, with the comment about Bun's deadline terminating long-running streams). This PR gives the TUI client the same treatment at both construction sites -- the initial client and the service reconnect path -- via a small shared `noTimeoutFetch` util.

Scope note: this addresses the transport drop. The issue's second observation -- Promise executors keep running with no cancellation signal -- is not changed here; that belongs with the command lifetime/cancellation work referenced in the thread (#53913 / #53914).

### How did you verify your code works?

- Reproduction from the issue run against base and this branch (see review): on the base the TUI drops the command by t+380s and restores the composer; on this branch it stays through t+400s and the command completes cleanly once released.
- `cd packages/tui && bun run typecheck` -> clean
- `bunx oxlint` on the touched files -> 0 warnings / 0 errors

prs.title: fix(plugin): resolve the figma plugin's peer from the workspace
prs.body:
Every `publish` run on `dev` has failed since #55049 added the Figma plugin (last success 2026-10-13 07:54 UTC). Example: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/38488804727

```
error: No version matching "@opencode/plugin" found for specifier "^2.0.27" (blocked by minimum-release-age: 259200 seconds)
  at prepareReleaseFiles (script/publish.ts:27:9)
```

**Cause**

- `packages/plugins/figma` declares its peer as the registry range `"@opencode/plugin": "^2.0.27"`. Every other workspace package uses `workspace:*`.
- A dev publish sets every workspace version to `0.0.0-dev-<run>` and then runs `bun install`. The workspace plugin no longer satisfies `^2.0.27`, so Bun looks for it on npm.
- On npm, `bunfig.toml`'s `minimumReleaseAge` (3 days) blocks the recently published 2.0.27 and 2.0.28, so the install fails.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[publish.ts sets versions to 0.0.0-dev-N] --> B{"0.0.0-dev-N satisfies ^2.0.27?"}
  B -- no --> C[resolve from npm] --> D[minimumReleaseAge blocks 2.0.27] --> E[bun install fails]
  B -. workspace:^ .-> F[workspace package]
```

**Fix**

- Declare the peer as `workspace:^`. It always resolves to the workspace plugin, and `bun pm pack` rewrites it to `^<version>` when the package is packed.
- Update `bun.lock` to match.

prs.body:
The daily `stats` job has failed every run (most recently https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/38395255551). `STATS.md` last updated on 2026-08-27.

```
remote: error: GH013: Repository rule violations found for refs/heads/dev.
remote: - Changes must be made through a pull request.
! [remote rejected]   dev -> dev (push declined due to repository rule violations)
```

**Cause**

- The job pushes `STATS.md` straight to `dev` with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and the `dev` ruleset only accepts pull requests.
- `publish` already pushes its release sync commit to `dev` through `setup-git-committer` (the OpenCode app token), which the ruleset allows.

**Fix**

- Push through `setup-git-committer`, as `publish` does.
- Add `[skip ci]` to the stats commit. Pushes made with the app token trigger workflows, unlike `GITHUB_TOKEN` pushes, and a stats-only commit should not start a full dev test and publish run.
- Move `POSTHOG_KEY` to the step that runs `script/stats.ts`. It was set on the commit step, so the script always logged `POSTHOG_API_KEY not set, skipping PostHog event`. With this change the job sends its daily download events to PostHog again.

prs.title: fix(session-ui): grow markdown live tail in place
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #36043 — jointly with the tui-delta-coalesce PR. Each applies
independently (different layer, no shared code, merge in either order);
only together do they remove O(n²) from both client-side stages of the
stream path and fully close the freeze. Builds on the freeze diagnosis in
#41472.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

While streaming, the markdown projection re-parsed the entire accumulated text
on every delta, even when the previous text was unchanged and the new suffix
was small. Each re-lex is O(length), so a stream of n small deltas costs
O(n²) — the dominant cost in the TUI freeze once deltas are batched.

`project()` in `markdown-stream.ts` now grows the open `live` tail in place
instead of re-lexing, and only re-lexes when the new suffix contains a
blank-line block boundary or the raw text exceeds a 2048-char cap. A single
giant boundary-less paragraph/list/table therefore never re-parses per delta.

Because the projection lives in the shared `session-ui` package, web and
desktop also inherit the cheaper `project()` as a free performance win, even
though their per-token rendering is not the freeze described in #36043.

Counterpart on the store side: the tui-delta-coalesce PR (coalesces
`message.part.delta` events per part in a delta buffer, flushing to the store
on a 32 ms timer instead of once per event). Together they remove O(n²) from
both halves of the TUI stream path — the markdown projection here, the store
writes there.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test`: 26 `markdown-stream` tests (incl. a new test growing a
  boundary-less oversized tail in place without splitting) — 86 tests, 0
  failures.
- `bun typecheck` clean in `packages/session-ui`.
- `oxlint`: 0 errors.
- Micro-benchmark streaming 6–15 KB through `project()` in small deltas
  (Bun): paragraphs 1399 ms → 20 ms, single 15 KB paragraph 32345 ms → 161 ms,
  growing list 4467 ms → 60 ms.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A — no visual change; it's a rendering-perf fix (benchmark above).

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #36043 — jointly with the markdown-live-relex PR. Each applies
independently (different layer, no shared code, merge in either order);
only together do they remove O(n²) from both client-side stages of the
stream path and fully close the freeze. Supersedes #41472, which was
closed unmerged — this reworks that approach for the current `sync.tsx`
wiring (32 ms timer instead of per-frame, plus dropping deltas superseded
by authoritative events).

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Every `message.part.delta` was applied to the TUI store immediately,
re-rendering the whole growing part per token — O(n²) over the stream,
which freezes the TUI on fast reasoning streams. Deltas now accumulate per
part in a small buffer (`delta-buffer.ts`) and flush to the store on a

discard buffered deltas for the part they replace, and the buffer drains on
cleanup so `*.ended` handlers still see the final text. The
markdown-live-relex PR covers the other stage: growing the open markdown
tail in place instead of re-lexing per delta.

prs.title: fix(plugin): keep each Promise hook rejection on its own tool call
prs.body:
Fixes #50331

## Summary

When several tool calls in one parallel batch were rejected by a Promise plugin's `tool.execute.before` hook, every rejected call showed the first hook's error message.

The Promise adapter wrapped hook callbacks in `Effect.promise`, so a thrown hook error became a defect. The step runner keeps only the first defect in a batch and applies it to every unsettled call. Effect plugin hooks don't have this problem, because `execute.before` is allowed to fail with `Tool.Error`, which settles per call.

The adapter now turns a Promise `execute.before` rejection into a `Tool.Error`, the same way #54913 handles Promise tool throws. A thrown `Tool.Error` is kept as is; anything else becomes a `Tool.Error` with the original attached. Each rejected call fails immediately with its own message. `execute.after` can't fail, so its rejections stay defects as before. The shared conversion is a small `toolError` helper used by both tools and hooks.

## Credit

@1052326311 reproduced and diagnosed this in #50399 and wrote the regression test used here. That PR fixes defect attribution in the step runner instead; this one fixes the Promise hook boundary so these rejections are ordinary tool failures. Co-authored accordingly.

## Tests

`packages/core/test/session-runner.test.ts` > "preserves each parallel Promise hook failure" (from #50399): two parallel calls rejected by different hook errors and one allowed call, through the real Promise adapter and session runner. It fails on the old adapter with both results showing `HOOK BLOCK ALPHA`.

Core session runner, plugin, and tool execution tests pass. All typecheck tasks pass except 9 existing errors in `@opencode/app` that are also on `dev`.

## Why

After #55018 moved binary workspace files to `Uint8Array`, `FileContent` still kept a required `content: string` and optional `encoding?: "base64"` alongside `bytes?: Uint8Array`. Binary entries had to carry an empty `content: ""` placeholder, and `packages/app/src/runtime/server/types.ts` also retained an unused duplicate `FileContent` definition.

## What Changes

`FileContent` in `@opencode/gui-extensions/sdk` is now a discriminated union of `TextFileContent` and `BinaryFileContent`:

| Kind | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| Text | `{ type: "text", content: string, mimeType?: string }` |
| Retained binary | `{ type: "binary", bytes: Uint8Array, mimeType?: string }` |
| Unretained binary | `{ type: "binary", size: number }` |

- `fileContentFromBytes` returns `{ type: "binary", bytes, mimeType }` (or `{ type: "binary", size }` above the media cap / for unknown binaries) without `content: ""`.
- `approxBytes`, `contentBytes`, `bytesFromContent`, and `blobUrlFromContent` branch directly on `content.type === "binary"` vs `content.type === "text"` without base64 decoding.
- Removes the unused duplicate `FileContent` type from `packages/app/src/runtime/server/types.ts`.

## Scope

Follows up on #55018 across the workspace file model, GUI extension SDK, and file/review viewers. `PresentationFileContent` in `@opencode/session-ui` remains unchanged for inline diff media data URLs.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #51107

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature

### What does this PR do?

V1 loaded admin-managed config from the system directory (`/Library/Application Support/opencode`, `/etc/opencode`, `%ProgramData%\opencode`) and, on macOS, from MDM profiles in the `ai.opencode.managed` domain. Managed paths are set through `Config.Options` (defaulting to the platform locations) rather than env vars, so a user can't point them elsewhere. Tests pass explicit paths, and the core test preload keeps a host's real MDM profile out of other suites.

    AWS profile / ambient chain          → BedrockAuth.defaultChain + BedrockAuth.signRequest (GET)
  in parallel, 10s timeout
    bedrock.<region>/foundation-models        → base IDs with ON_DEMAND
    bedrock.<region>/inference-profiles       → us./eu./global./… profile IDs usable here

  Mantle model → keep if in Mantle list

  never adds models outside the catalog

packages/ai: signRequest exported, method/body optional (POST default unchanged)

us-east-1, Bedrock API key: 186 → 121 models
  hidden: eu./jp./au./apac./in./ca./us-gov. profiles, profile-only base IDs
          (anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6, llama 3.x/4, writer), qwen3 235b/coder, xai.grok-4.6

issues.title: Skill discovery drops the leading / from ignore patterns, breaking root anchoring

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

I hit this in my dotfiles repo (<https://github.com/for13to1/dotfiles/commit/ef8838e246f1afe8c68f50c86488283b42985940>), where `~/.agents/skills` is stowed straight from the working tree and mixes tracked skill directories with machine-local symlinks. To keep the symlinks out of git while tracking the rest, `skills/.gitignore` uses a root-anchored whitelist:

```gitignore
/*
!/commit-summarizer/
```

**pi** then loaded none of the skills, silently. The same patterns behave the opposite way under git (`git check-ignore` says the skill is not ignored), because skill discovery strips the leading `/` before matching, turning a root-anchored pattern into an unanchored one. At the scan root, `/*` is applied as `*` (matches at every depth) and `!/commit-summarizer/` only un-ignores the directory entry, not `commit-summarizer/SKILL.md`.

I know #1072/#5145/#8748/#2947 settled that ignore files may filter discovery ("as per design"). This is narrower: if discovery follows gitignore semantics, it must follow the leading-`/` anchor too. Git does; **pi** does not. Confirmed against `main` (`e6220e131`) with `pi -ne`.

The strip is in `prefixIgnorePattern()` at `packages/coding-agent/src/core/skills.ts:39`:

```ts
if (pattern.startsWith("/")) {
 pattern = pattern.slice(1);
}
```

The same function is duplicated at `packages/coding-agent/src/core/package-manager.ts:259`, so package resource scanning is affected as well.

### Steps to reproduce

```text
skills/
├── .gitignore          # "/*" then "!/commit-summarizer/"
├── commit-summarizer/
│   └── SKILL.md
└── vendor-link         # any non-whitelisted entry
```

`skills/.gitignore`:

```gitignore
/*
!/commit-summarizer/
```

- `loadSkillsFromDir({ dir: "skills" })` returns `{ skills: [], diagnostics: [] }`.
- `git check-ignore skills/commit-summarizer/SKILL.md` reports it is not ignored.
- Reproduces with `pi -ne`.

### Expected behavior

A leading `/` stays anchored to the scan root, matching git. Strip it only when prefixing a nested ignore file:

```ts
if (prefix && pattern.startsWith("/")) {
 pattern = pattern.slice(1);
}
```

With this change the skill loads, and a nested `grp/.gitignore` containing `venv` still ignores `grp/venv/` correctly.


### Version

1.2.0

> The text above was generated with AI; I reviewed it and it matches what I observe.

issues.title: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview is missing from the generated catalog

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

`MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` works against MiniMax's Anthropic-compatible endpoint but is absent from Pi's generated catalog, so it cannot be selected or used. Nothing else is wrong — the endpoint, the wire protocol and the reasoning controls all behave correctly. This is a catalog entry.

## Reproduction

The model does not appear in `pi --list-models`, and neither `minimax` nor `minimax-cn` carries it. `MiniMax-M2.7`, `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` and `MiniMax-M3` are all present.

It also cannot be added by hand. Per `docs/models.md`, `modelOverrides` changes metadata for an **existing** built-in or extension-provided model, and *"Unknown override IDs are ignored."* So this is silently discarded and the model still does not appear:

```json
{
  "modelOverrides": {
    "minimax-cn/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview": {
      "reasoning": true,
      "input": ["text", "image"],
      "contextWindow": 1000000,
      "maxTokens": 512000
    }
  }
}
```

That silent discard is arguably the more useful half of this report: a user following the documented path gets no error and no model.

## Expected

`MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` selectable under `minimax-cn`.

## Verified specs

From MiniMax's Anthropic SDK docs, cross-checked against the canonical `sst/models.dev` record (`models/minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview.toml`):

| field | value |
|---|---|
| context window | `1_000_000` |
| max output | `512_000` |
| input modalities | `text, image, video` |
| reasoning | **forced on** — `thinking: {type:"disabled"}` returns 400 |
| depth control | `output_config.effort` ∈ `low \| medium \| high \| xhigh \| max`, default `max`; `none` returns 400 |
| audio | **not supported** — `type:"audio"` returns `unsupported content type 'audio'` (error 2013) |

The `input` line is the interesting one: the generator cannot currently express `video`, which is why that entry needs the modality widened too. See the discussion on video input for the measurement and a reference implementation — the two changes are related but separable, and this one should land first because it is the smaller.

Note there is **no `off` reasoning level and no `minimal`** for this model. Thinking cannot be disabled, so a catalog entry that offers `off` will produce a 400 when selected.

## Suggested change

In `packages/ai/scripts/generate-models.ts` the MiniMax variant loop collapses modality to text/image:

```ts
input: m.modalities?.input?.includes("image") ? ["text", "image"] : ["text"],
```

Passing through `video` when the source record declares it fixes the metadata; widening `MODEL_INPUT_MODALITIES` (or leaving the entry as `["text","image"]` for now) decides how far that goes.

`sst/models.dev` already publishes `providers/minimax-cn-coding-plan/models/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview.toml` with `reasoning_options` `low|medium|high|xhigh|max` and zero cost, so the source data exists.

## Cost / availability note

MiniMax's docs state the model is *"available only through M Plan and MiniMax Code for now."* The entry should carry the zero-cost pricing the token plan implies, matching what `sst/models.dev` publishes, rather than pay-as-you-go rates.

## Reproducing by hand

This returns 200 and the model reads the frames correctly:

```
POST https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/v1/messages
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer $MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY

{
  "model": "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview",
  "max_tokens": 300,
  "output_config": { "effort": "low" },
  "messages": [{
    "role": "user",
    "content": [
      { "type": "video",
        "source": { "type": "base64", "media_type": "video/mp4", "data": "<base64>" } },
      { "type": "text", "text": "What colour is the background, and what text is drawn on it?" }
    ]
  }]
}
```

> The background is bright blue, and the text reads "FRAME 85" in yellow.

The fixture is a 4-second 320×240 mp4 with the frame number rendered into the picture, so the answer cannot have come from metadata. I can supply it.

## Prior art

**#7326** — *"fix(ai): preserve MiniMax M3 video input capability"* — is essentially the same generator change for `MiniMax-M3`. It was auto-closed by the new-contributor bot seconds after opening rather than reviewed. I'm not aware of a reason it wasn't merged, so this may only need re-landing with a `lgtm`.

## Environment

`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.2.0 / `@earendil-works/pi-ai` 1.2.0, Linux.

issues.title: Switch coding-agent from proper-lockfile to a maintained fork

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Replace the proper-lockfile dependency in packages/coding-agent with @bybrave/proper-lockfile2, a drop-in fork I maintain. Same API, bundled types (so @types/proper-lockfile goes away), exact version pin. The diff is the dependency swap, 8 import lines and the two lockfiles.

### Why?

proper-lockfile has had no release since 2021 and pi leans on it hard: many pi processes share auth.json and settings.json and reclaim stale locks (#4919, #8928, #10798). Two upstream bugs matter here. Reclaiming a stale lock is done with rmdir + mkdir, so two processes that both see a stale lock can both end up holding it (moxystudio/node-proper-lockfile#121). And releasing a lock while a failed mtime update is being retried throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'updateTimeout')" (moxystudio/node-proper-lockfile#113). The fork fixes both with regression tests, and installs the signal-exit handler on the first lock instead of at require time, which is the thing the #5724 regression test is about.

### How? (optional)

Branch is ready: npm run check passes, the lockfile-related tests pass, ./test.sh is green apart from local environment failures (fd/rg download, Bun, the Rust daemon) that fail the same way on main. Full disclosure: I maintain the fork; Prettier uses my json5 fork the same way. Happy to adjust anything.

issues.title: Extension factory cache is cleared by any cwd switch — multi-project hosts re-import all extensions on every new session

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

The extension factory cache in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/loader.ts` is keyed by a **single global cwd slot**. Any `DefaultResourceLoader.reload()` with a different cwd calls `clearExtensionCache()` and drops **all** cached extension factories. In long-running hosts (pi-web spawns one Node server serving many projects), this means every new-session spawn re-imports the full extension graph through jiti even when nothing changed.

Combined with `moduleCache: false` (and `tryNative: false` in the bundled-Node runtime), each re-import re-evaluates every module of every extension's dependency graph with per-module read/transform/eval. For TypeScript-source extensions this is seconds each.

## Code path

`loader.ts` (dist/core/extensions/loader.js in 1.2.0):

```ts
let extensionCacheCwd: string | undefined;
let extensionCacheGeneration = 0;

function useExtensionCacheCwd(cwd) {
  const resolvedCwd = resolvePath(cwd);
  if (extensionCacheCwd !== undefined && extensionCacheCwd !== resolvedCwd) {
    clearExtensionCache();          // ← drops ALL factories for a mere cwd switch
  }
  extensionCacheCwd = resolvedCwd;
  return { cwd: resolvedCwd, generation: extensionCacheGeneration };
}

async function loadExtensionModule(extensionPath, cacheToken) {
  if (isCurrentCacheToken(cacheToken)) { /* in-memory hit */ }
  // miss → full jiti.import, ~seconds per TS-source extension
}
```

`isCurrentCacheToken` requires `extensionCacheCwd === cacheToken.cwd && extensionCacheGeneration === cacheToken.generation`, so after one cwd switch the previous project's factories are gone.

## Why hosts hit this constantly

pi-web creates loaders with different cwds for different features:

- new session for project A → `createAgentSessionServices({ cwd: A })`
- `/api/auth/providers`, `/api/models/enabled`, auth login/logout → `createModelRuntimeWithExtensions()` → `createAgentSessionServices({ cwd: agentDir })` (lib/model-runtime.ts)
- `/api/skills`, `/api/skills/check`, `/api/skills/content` → `loadSkillsWithInstallInfo(cwd)` → fresh `DefaultResourceLoader.reload()` (lib/skills-service.ts)

Alternating between two projects and opening Settings once is enough to invalidate the cache several times per minute. Back-to-back spawns for the **same** cwd measured 15.1s and 15.7s on a warm server because the slot had been switched away and cleared in between.

## Measured (Windows, Node 24, pi-web 0.12.1, SDK 1.2.0, 9 npm extensions)

Per-extension `module import` via the SDK's own `PI_TIMING=1`, cold (jiti fs-cache warm, in-memory factory cache cold):

| extension | module import |
|---|---|
| pi-hashline-edit-pro (TS source, 16 MB incl. vendored parsers) | 23.5s |
| @juicesharp/rpiv-ask-user-question (TS source) | 18.6s |
| pi-cache-optimizer (TS source) | 5.6s |
| pi-add-dir (TS source) | 4.6s |
| pi-codex-goal (TS source) | 3.5s |
| others | <1s |
| **total** | **57.2s** |

Same process, same cwd, factory cache warm (this is the number hosts should be getting on every spawn): ~1-2s for `createAgentSessionServices` — the cache works, it is just thrown away by cwd switches.

## Suggested fix

Make the in-memory factory cache multi-slot instead of single-slot:

- `Map<cwd, { generation, factories: Map<path, factory> }>` with a small LRU cap (e.g. 4-8 cwds), so switching A → agentDir → B → A keeps A warm.
- Keep `clearExtensionCache()` only for real invalidation (reload of the same cwd after extension files change).

This plus the `tryNative`/parallelization work in #7957 would remove the remaining per-session re-import cost for multi-project hosts.

issues.title: Export a side-effect-free Bun runtime-shim registration for SDK embedders (OAuth flows, Bedrock)

labels.name: last-read
labels.description: A marker label for triaging

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Problem

A host that embeds `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` and ships a Bun-compiled binary has to run the same registrations that `dist/bun/runtime-setup.js` runs:

```js
registerBunOAuthFlows();                          // @earendil-works/pi-ai/bun-oauth
setBedrockProviderModule(bedrockProviderModule);  // @earendil-works/pi-ai/compat + /bedrock-provider
```

Without them, subscription OAuth fails in the binary with `Cannot find module './openai-codex.js'`, and Bedrock falls back to a dynamic import Bun cannot embed.

These calls only work if they reach the same `pi-ai` instance that pi-coding-agent uses. A host can't reliably make that happen today. `openai` 7.x declares `undici` as an optional peer, and Bun's isolated linker keys each `pi-ai` copy by how that peer resolves. So when the host's tree resolves `undici` to a different version than pi-coding-agent's exact `8.10.2` pin, the host gets its own `pi-ai` copy, and its registrations never reach pi. In our case, `discord.js` pins `undici@6.21.3`. The registrations then silently do nothing. We hit this in Archon (coleam00/Archon PR 3537, issue 3724) on pi 1.0.0 and confirmed it on 1.0.2.

Our current workaround is to pin `undici` to exactly the version pi-coding-agent pins, plus a test that asserts both resolve the same `pi-ai` file. That works, but it's a hand-kept pair that breaks whenever pi changes its `undici` pin.

## Request

Export a side-effect-free function from pi-coding-agent that runs these registrations against pi-coding-agent's own `pi-ai`. For example:

```js
import { registerBunRuntimeShims } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/bun";
registerBunRuntimeShims();
```

It would register the OAuth flows and the Bedrock module (and anything else a compiled embedder needs). It would not set `process.title`, replace `process.emitWarning`, or touch the QuickJS wasm path, which `runtime-setup.js` also does and which belong to pi's own CLI. Hosts would then call into pi's instance by construction, with no version matching.

Related: #9787 (the nested `undici` 8.10.2 becoming the process-global dispatcher in embedded hosts) comes from the same `undici` pin.

issues.title: pi-durable: on a Durable Object, a sleeping task wakes only on the next request

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

On the [Durable Object storage](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/7bd01fb92485c06f92ecfff7ccf3197148bc16af/packages/durable/README.md?plain=1#L663), a task that calls `runtime.sleep()` doesn't wake at its deadline once the object restarts. It stays `pending` until some request happens to open the Harness and call `resume()`. Generation [retry](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/7bd01fb92485c06f92ecfff7ccf3197148bc16af/packages/durable/src/harness/generation.ts#L225) and [deferred poll](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/7bd01fb92485c06f92ecfff7ccf3197148bc16af/packages/durable/src/harness/generation.ts#L240) sleep the same way.

The deadline itself is safe; what's lost is the wake-up. [`#sleep`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/7bd01fb92485c06f92ecfff7ccf3197148bc16af/packages/durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts#L1812) is an in-memory `setTimeout`, and a Durable Object runs code only for a request or an alarm. A pending timer keeps the object alive for at most 15 minutes, and none survives a deploy or runtime restart ([lifecycle](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/concepts/durable-object-lifecycle/)). Pi never sets an alarm. The app can’t set one either, because it has no way to learn when a task wants to wake up: only the task’s own code knows the deadline.

So a sleep longer than 15 minutes misses its deadline every time, and a shorter one misses it whenever a restart lands in between.

### Steps to reproduce

Deployed to Cloudflare: a SQLite-backed Durable Object over `openDurableObjectSqliteStorage(ctx.storage)`, one task that sleeps 2 minutes, a redeploy partway through, and no further requests (UTC):

| Event | Time (UTC) |
|---|---|
| Sleep starts | 20:45:26.570 |
| Redeploy | 20:46:06 |
| Deadline (nothing runs) | 20:47:26.570 |
| Next request; task wakes (66 s late) | 20:48:32.632 |

A 20 s sleep without a redeploy woke on time.


### Expected behavior

A sleep that wakes on time in a long-running process should wake on time on a Durable Object too, with no extra app code. Waking the object is Pi’s job, not the app’s.

### Proposal

On Cloudflare that takes an alarm set for the next deadline, which should be the durable harness' not the app code's job. Should pi-durable ship a Durable Object base class, like codemode’s CodemodeSandboxDurableObject, that runs the Harness and sets that alarm? I have one working. Happy to send it.

### Version

1.1.0

A change made during a tool loop would apply at the next user message, since that’s where the API accepts it.

issues.title: [Contribution]: Recommended extension pattern or hook for background/detached tasks without blocking the session turn

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?
Provide guidance, hook points, or a standard extension pattern for running long-running operations (e.g. 5–30 min batch scripts, test suites, or heavy subagents) in the background / detached, so they do not freeze the interactive agent session turn.

### Why?
In interactive sessions, tool execution (`execute()`) is strictly blocking request-response. When an agent invokes a long operation:
- The entire turn loop freezes in `(running...)` for the duration of the command.
- The user cannot submit prompts, ask questions, or steer the session while the turn is blocked.
- TUI/context compaction cannot proceed until the tool resolves.

In Claude Code, operations can be dispatched with `run_in_background: true`, returning control to the conversation immediately. Because Pi's core is intentionally minimal, we want to know the maintainer/community consensus on the right architecture for this in Pi.

### How? (optional)
We are considering building an extension and would welcome pointers before doing so:
1. **Detached Job Manager extension**: Custom tools (`job_start`, `job_poll`, `job_kill`) that spawn detached OS child processes, spool logs to `.pi/jobs/<id>.log`, update status via `ctx.ui.setStatus()`, and notify completion via `ctx.ui.notify()`.
2. **Asynchronous subagent delegation**: Extending subagent tools with a detached mode rather than awaiting child process termination in `execute()`.
3. **Core primitives / streaming**: Are there existing or planned primitives in `AgentSession` or `onUpdate` to stream heartbeat progress or deliver background completion events cleanly without queueing issues (as seen in #10610)?

If this should live entirely in userland/extensions, we are happy to build and publish it as an extension.

issues.title: google-vertex: gemini-4-argon requests fail with 400 "Thinking budget is not supported" (usesGoogleThinkingLevel misses gemini-4)
issues.body:
**What happened?**

Requests to `gemini-4-argon` (new on Vertex AI; it uses the discrete thinking-level API like Gemini 3) fail with HTTP 400 when the model is defined with `"reasoning": true`:

```json
{"error":{"code":400,"message":"Thinking budget is not supported for this model. Use thinking level instead. See https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking for details.","status":"INVALID_ARGUMENT"}}
```

`streamSimple` in `packages/ai/src/api/google-vertex.ts` only sends `thinkingLevel` when `usesGoogleThinkingLevel(model)` returns true, and that check in `packages/ai/src/api/google-shared.ts` matches Gemini 3 IDs, `gemini-flash-latest`, `gemini-flash-lite-latest`, and Gemma 4 only. `gemini-4-argon` matches none of them, so pi sends `thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget` instead (`getGoogleBudget` returns -1 for unknown models) and Vertex rejects the request.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Authenticate to Vertex with ADC (`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`).
2. Define the model in `models.json` (it isn't in the pi.dev catalog yet):

   ```json
   {"providers":{"google-vertex":{"models":[{"id":"gemini-4-argon","name":"Gemini 4 Argon","reasoning":true,"input":["text","image"],"cost":{"input":2,"output":10,"cacheRead":0.1,"cacheWrite":0},"contextWindow":1048576,"maxTokens":1048576}]}}}
   ```

3. `pi -ne -p --model google-vertex/gemini-4-argon "hi"`

**Expected behavior**

`gemini-4-argon` requests go out with `thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel`, i.e. Gemini 4 should be recognized as a thinking-level model in `usesGoogleThinkingLevel`. Workaround that works today: set `"reasoning": false` for this model, which makes pi omit `thinkingConfig` entirely.

**Version**

1.1.0 (also present on `main`, unchanged in v1.2.0).

_(This report was written and filed by the reporter's pi agent on their behalf.)_

The `minimal` level is also listed as [not supported (error)](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/thinking#thinking-levels) for `gemini-4-argon`, in case that matters for how the disabled-thinking path resolves a level.

issues.title:
parseStreamingJson silently prefix-salvages final tool-call
arguments, corrupting tool calls without any diagnostic

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**Package:** `@earendil-works/pi-ai` (observed on 1.0.4; code lives in `packages/ai`)
**API path:** `openai-responses` (`processResponsesStream`)

## What happened

In a live agent session, the model emitted a `cad_ui` tool call whose full argument string failed strict JSON parsing at `response.output_item.done`. `parseStreamingJson` (`dist/utils/json-parse.js:90-109`) fell back to `repairJson`, then to `partial-json`, whose object parser returns **the keys parsed so far** when any later value throws. The final tool call therefore arrived as:

```json
{"action":"apply"}
```

— the first key of what the model actually sent (an `actions` array was constructed and intended, per the model's visible reasoning). `processResponsesStream` (`dist/api/openai-responses-shared.js:611-619`) then assigns the salvaged fragment as the call's final arguments and emits `toolcall_end` with **no decode-failure diagnostic**.

## Reproduction (verified against 1.0.4)

```js
import { parseStreamingJson } from '@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/utils/json-parse.js';

// Stream cut after the first value — what output_item.done hands the decoder:
parseStreamingJson('{"kind":"viewport.seekAnimation",');
// => { kind: 'viewport.seekAnimation' }        // silent prefix salvage

// Stream cut mid-string-value — partial-json CLOSES the truncated string:
parseStreamingJson('{"kind":"viewport.seekAnimation","clipId":"clip-fl');
// => { kind: 'viewport.seekAnimation', clipId: 'clip-fl' }  // fabricated value
```

No error, no warning, no flag: the decoder manufactures arguments the model never sent, and downstream validation passes because the fragment is a valid subset of the intended schema.

## Live-session evidence: an 18-call blind retry loop

A transcript export from the affected session (downstream app: PartMode, a browser CAD agent using `@flue/runtime` over `pi-agent-core`/`pi-ai`, OpenAI-compatible `openai-responses` streaming) shows the same signature at scale:

- **18 consecutive `cad_ui` apply calls** each carried animation actions shaped `{"kind":"viewport.seekAnimation"}` (or `playAnimation`/`pauseAnimation`) — the kind key parsed before the cut, everything after silently dropped.
- **16 of them** received the consuming app's "That animation clip no longer exists" — a semantically misleading error, because the real problem was that `clipId`/`time` never arrived.
- The model's visible reasoning repeatedly states it constructed the full argument object and hypothesizes harness serialization bugs — from its side it sent complete arguments, so it retried **the identical call** for ~13 minutes (2026-10-13, timestamps 16:24–16:37), never converging.

A consumer cannot self-correct: the salvage is invisible at every later layer, and the resulting validation error contradicts the model's own output.

## Why silent salvage is wrong for *final* arguments

Prefix salvage is exactly right **during** streaming (partial `toolcall_delta` events are genuinely incomplete). But at `output_item.done` the buffer is final: if strict parsing fails there, the model's emission was malformed, and salvaging a prefix manufactures arguments the model never chose to send.

Note the mid-string case is arguably worse than the between-keys case: `partial-json` **closes the truncated string value**, fabricating a complete value (e.g. `clipId: "clip-fl"`) that passes downstream existence checks as a plausible-but-wrong id.

## Suggested fix (either or both)

1. At `output_item.done`, if strict `JSON.parse` fails, **fail loudly**: surface a stream error or an `isError` tool call rather than assigning the salvage.
2. Or attach a diagnostic to the tool call — e.g. `decodeTruncated: true` (plus the failure reason and, ideally, whether a string value was closed by the parser) — so consumers can distinguish "model sent this" from "decoder salvaged this prefix".

## Environment

- `@earendil-works/pi-ai@1.0.4` (bundled for browser via Bun.build)
- Provider: OpenAI-compatible `openai-responses` streaming
- The trigger requires the model to emit invalid JSON as its complete final argument string — rare, but when it happens the corruption is silent, the agent-visible error is misleading, and the loop is non-converging.

## Downstream evidence artifacts

The consuming app has since shipped two downstream guards against this signature (a required-field echo naming the received keys, and batch recipe validation) — both exist only because the salvage is silent. Transcript excerpt and repro available on request.

issues.title: ChatGPT OAuth ID token is not persisted, preventing extensions from accessing account identity
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

In Pi 0.99.2, the ChatGPT OAuth login flow requires the token response to contain an ID token, but credentialFromTokenResponse omits that field when constructing the saved credentials. Token refresh uses the same conversion function.

Source: [openai-chatgpt.ts in v0.99.2](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.99.2/packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openai-chatgpt.ts#L136-L183)

### Why?

As a result, extensions cannot obtain account identity information, such as the email address, from a persisted ID token.

### How? (optional)

issues.body:
## Problem

Pi defaults to a single context window variant per model (e.g., 1M for Luna), even when users have access to multiple context options. This limits discoverability and forces users to manually select different context windows, missing opportunities to optimize for their specific use case.

## Solution

Expose all available model context window variants in model discovery, displaying them with their context size:

- gpt-6-luna@272k [github-copilot]
- gpt-6-luna [github-copilot]
- gpt-6-luna@1m [github-copilot]

This enables users to see all available options and make informed choices about context windows and performance trade-offs. The improvement applies to all models across all providers, enhancing the discovery experience for everyone.

issues.title: Agent turns with empty `content` and no tool call end silently — user sees a blank reply

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

# Agent turns with empty `content` and no tool call end silently — user sees a blank reply

## Environment

- pi: `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` **1.2.0**
- Provider: local OpenAI-compatible engine (`api: "openai-completions"`), Strata 0.1.43.1, model `qwen3.8-flash-next-UD-IQ4XS`
- `reasoning` enabled, `compat.requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages: true`

## Symptom

The agent loop ends and **nothing is rendered**. No error, no retry, no notification. From the user's side the model simply stopped answering.

The transcript shows the assistant message was persisted with a thinking block and **empty `content`**:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": [{ "type": "thinking", "thinking": "... 2173 chars of analysis ..." }],
  "stopReason": "stop",
  "usage": { "input": 13, "output": 736, "cacheRead": 78629 }
}
```

`stopReason` is `stop` (not `error`), `output` tokens are non-zero, so pi treats the turn as a clean final answer and settles. With `hideThinkingBlock: true` the user sees literally nothing.

In one session, **12 of 86 assistant turns** were like this. The user's only workaround was disabling thinking entirely.

## Why this needs a client-side guard

The model produced a malformed completion — that is an upstream defect (filed separately against the engine/model). But **no client should render silence as a successful answer.** Any local model can emit a malformed turn; pi is the layer that can tell the user "that produced no output, retrying" instead of going quiet.

## Reproduction

Replayed the real session history against the live engine. The failure is deterministic enough to measure:

| history shape | turns with empty final text |
|---|---|
| short prompt, no history | **0/6** |
| real session history (assistant turns with long `tool_calls` arguments) | **8/8**, **10/10** |
| same history, tool-call structure rewritten as prose | **0/4** |
| single assistant turn with a short `tool_calls` argument | **0/6** |
| single assistant turn with one real long `tool_calls` argument | **6/6** |

So the trigger is a specific shape in the replayed history, not length, not temperature, not randomness. It is reproducible on demand.

Things that did **not** change the failure rate (each 4/4):

- deleting every empty-content assistant turn from history
- replaying history without `reasoning_content` (`preserve_thinking: false`)
- back-filling `reasoning_content` on turns that had none
- dropping or truncating tool results

`enable_thinking: false` does eliminate it (0 failures across the session after the user switched it off).

## Requested change

When an assistant turn completes with `stopReason: "stop"` and produces **no text and no tool call**, pi should not settle silently. Suggested, smallest first:

1. **Retry the request once** (optionally with thinking disabled for that attempt).
2. If it repeats, surface a visible message: `Model returned no output — retry with /retry, or lower the thinking level.`
3. Optionally log a warning so this is diagnosable rather than invisible.

Detection is cheap and model-agnostic: `content` has no `text` part and no `toolCall` part. It does not require knowing why the model misbehaved, which is why it is the right place for the guard.

## Notes on what was ruled out

For completeness, these were tested and are **not** the cause: extension payload mutation (`prompt_cache_key`, `prompt_cache_retention`, tool ordering — 0/10 each), GPU/RAM health (control prompts 0/6 at the same moment), KV-cache spill (15K-token and 72K-token contexts failed identically), thinking level (`low`/`medium`/`high` all 4/4 — the engine template maps `high` to the default `xhigh`).

## Environment detail that makes this more visible

`hideThinkingBlock: true` in settings. Worth noting that when a turn contains *only* a thinking block, hiding it renders an empty message rather than "thinking only". Even a placeholder would be an improvement.


### Steps to reproduce

## Steps to reproduce

### A. Against any local model (fastest — stub the provider)

Point pi at a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint that always returns an empty completion:

```python
# empty-model.py  —  python3 empty-model.py
import json, http.server

BODY = json.dumps({
    "id": "x", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 0, "model": "stub",
    "choices": [{"index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop",
                 "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "",
                             "reasoning_content": "I will now summarize my findings."}}],
    "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": 9, "total_tokens": 19},
}).encode()

class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(BODY)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(BODY)
    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(200); self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b'{"object":"list","data":[{"id":"stub"}]}')
    def log_message(self, *a): pass

http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8899), H).serve_forever()
```

1. `python3 empty-model.py`
2. Add the provider in `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (`api: "openai-completions"`, `baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:8899/v1"`, one model with `reasoning: true`).
3. `pi`, select that model, send any prompt.

**Actual:** pi renders nothing, shows no error, and settles. The prompt is consumed; the user has no signal that anything happened.
**Expected:** pi detects "no text and no tool call" and retries, or prints a visible message.

### B. Against a real local reasoning model (the case I actually hit)

1. Load a local reasoning model that can emit `reasoning_content` + empty `content` (here: Strata + `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS`, thinking enabled).
2. Run an agent-style task that produces many tool calls with **long tool arguments** — multi-line shell commands, heredocs, embedded JSON. Debugging/investigation tasks do this naturally.
3. Keep going for 20–30 tool rounds, then ask for a summary.
4. Some final turns render as blank.

Measured by replaying a real session against the live engine:

| history shape | turns with empty final text |
|---|---|
| short prompt, no history | **0/6** |
| real session history (assistant turns with long `tool_calls` arguments) | **8/8**, **10/10** |
| same history, tool-call structure rewritten as prose | **0/4** |
| single assistant turn with a short `tool_calls` argument | **0/6** |
| single assistant turn with one real long `tool_calls` argument | **6/6** |

Reproducible on demand — not length, not temperature, not randomness. Upstream cause filed separately against the engine; **this issue is only about pi not catching it.**

### How to confirm the state in a transcript

```bash
python3 - <session.jsonl> <<'EOF'
import json,sys
for l in open(sys.argv[1]):
    o=json.loads(l); m=o.get("message") or {}
    if m.get("role")=="assistant":
        k=[c.get("type") for c in m.get("content",[])]
        if "text" not in k and "toolCall" not in k:
            print(o.get("timestamp"), m.get("stopReason"), k)
EOF
```

Turns printed with `stopReason: "stop"` and `['thinking']` (or `[]`) are the silent ones.

### Expected behavior

## Expected behavior

An assistant turn that ends with `stopReason: "stop"` while producing **no `text` part and no `toolCall` part** is not a valid final answer. pi should not settle on it silently.

Requested, smallest first:

1. **Retry the request once** — optionally with thinking disabled for that attempt, since disabling thinking reliably avoids the upstream failure.
2. If it repeats, surface a visible message rather than silence:
   `Model returned no output. Try /retry, or lower the thinking level.`
3. Log a warning so the event is diagnosable after the fact.

Detection is cheap and model-agnostic — `content` has no `text` and no `toolCall` — and it does not require pi to know *why* the model misbehaved. That is exactly why the guard belongs here: any local model can emit a malformed turn, and this one check covers the whole class.

## Why this needs a client-side guard

The malformed completion is an upstream defect. But no client should render silence as a successful answer. As shipped, the failure mode is indistinguishable from "the agent decided to stop", so users reasonably conclude pi or the model has hung — and the only reliable workaround (thinking off) costs reasoning quality across every task.

## Ruled out (so the cause is not misattributed)

Tested and **not** the cause: extension payload mutation (`prompt_cache_key`, `prompt_cache_retention`, tool ordering — 0/10 each), GPU/RAM health (control prompts 0/6 at the same moment), KV-cache spill (15K- and 72K-token contexts failed identically), thinking level (`low`/`medium`/`high` all 4/4 — this engine's template maps `high` to the default `xhigh`), and prompt-cache reuse (fails at `reused: 0` and `reused: 72462` alike).

## Minor related papercut

With `hideThinkingBlock: true`, a turn containing only a thinking block renders as a completely empty message. A placeholder such as `(model produced no response text)` would make the state visible even without the retry logic above.

### Version

1.2.0

issues.title: codemode: an abort or timeout waits for a non-interruptible built-in on Bun, and values crossing the bridge skip the memory limit
Compaction summarisation inherits the session thinking level on adaptive models and deterministically hits the output cap at high efforts
issues.body:
## Summary

On adaptive-thinking Anthropic models (`compat.forceAdaptiveThinking`), compaction summarisation runs at the session's thinking level while its output budget stays at `0.8 * reserveTokens` (~13k with the default 16384). Thinking tokens count against `max_tokens` on these models, so at `high`/`xhigh`/`max` the summary generation deterministically stops on `length`, and since #7048 that correctly fails the compaction instead of persisting a truncated summary. Net effect: every compaction (manual `/compact` and threshold auto-compaction) fails after a long generation, on sessions whose thinking level is exactly the kind that produces huge contexts.

## Mechanics (0.84.4)

- `createSummarizationOptions` in `core/compaction/compaction.ts` forwards the session `thinkingLevel` as `reasoning` when the model supports it.
- `generateSummaryWithUsage` caps output at `maxTokens = Math.min(0.8 * reserveTokens, model.maxTokens)`, ~13107 by default.
- On the Anthropic adaptive path, `streamSimple` maps the level to `output_config.effort`; thinking spend then shares the `max_tokens` budget with the summary text.
- `getSummarizationFailure` turns the `length` stop into "Summarization failed: generation hit the token cap and the summary is incomplete".

Observed on a real session (1M-window adaptive model, `xhigh`): two summaries succeeded at 12811 and 12815 output tokens, right at the 13107 cap; every subsequent attempt stopped on `length` and failed. The failure repeats indefinitely because nothing lowers the effort or raises the cap on retry.

## Suggested fix

Either or both:

1. Run summarisation at a fixed moderate effort (e.g. `medium`) instead of inheriting the session level. A summary is transcription work; deep reasoning mostly produces thinking spend that competes with the output.
2. Account for thinking overhead in the summarisation budget on models where thinking counts against `max_tokens`, or retry a `length`-stopped summary once with thinking reduced/disabled.

## Workaround

An extension can rewrite the summariser request via `before_provider_request` (detectable by the summarisation system prompt and absent tools), clamping effort and raising `max_tokens`. Works, but relies on payload sniffing.

issues.title: Hardware cursor jumps to the wrong column while a mouse selection is active (1.2.0)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

With `showHardwareCursor: true`, pi positions the terminal cursor using a
zero-width marker (`\x1b_pi:c\x07`) that the editor puts in the line. The column
is computed in `extractCursorPosition()` as the visible width of the text before
that marker.

When a mouse selection is active, `applySelection()` splits the line into
before / selected / after and rebuilds it. The slicing helper
`sliceWithWidth()` (utils.js) mishandles zero-width escape sequences:

- a sequence at or after the end of the range is dropped
- a sequence before the range is buffered and prepended to the next slice,
  so it is duplicated into a later slice

So the cursor marker can end up on the other side of the selection, and
`extractCursorPosition()` then reads the column from the wrong place.

Measured over all combinations of cursor position × selection range, for
`"ab中文def"` and `"abcdefgh"` (1406 combinations):

| Symptom | Count |
|---|---|
| Cursor placed at the wrong column | 70 (max off by 2 cells = one CJK char) |
| Text outside the selection rendered in reverse video | 175 (`showHardwareCursor: false`) |

Example: line `ab中<marker>cursor-on-文def`, selection covering columns 0-3.
The cursor should be at column 4, pi puts it at column 2.

This bug is not new in 1.2.0 - pi-tui 1.1.0 has the same 35 wrong-column cases.
What changed in 1.2.0 is that `showHardwareCursor: true` no longer draws pi's own
reverse-video cursor, so the misplaced terminal cursor is no longer covered by a
correctly positioned one.

### Steps to reproduce

Deterministic, no terminal needed:

```js
const T = await import("<pi>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/tui.js");
const A = await import("<pi>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/tui-alt-screen.js");

const terminal = { columns: 60, rows: 12, write(){}, start(){}, stop(){}, hideCursor(){}, showCursor(){}, on(){}, off(){}, setTitle(){} };
const tui = new A.TuiAltScreen(terminal, true, undefined, { copyOnSelect: false });

const line = `ab中${T.CURSOR_MARKER}${T.renderFakeCursor("文")}def\x1b[0m`;
let lines = tui.resolveFakeCursors([line]);           // cursor is at column 4

tui.selectionAnchor = { row: 0, col: 0, scrollView: undefined };
tui.selectionFocus  = { row: 0, col: 3, scrollView: undefined, boundary: true };
lines = tui.applySelection(lines, null);

const pos = tui.extractCursorPosition(lines, 12);
console.log(pos.col);   // prints 2, should be 4
```

Interactively: enable `showHardwareCursor`, put the cursor in the middle of the
input box, then select text with the mouse so the selection covers the cursor
position. The cursor moves to the wrong cell.

## Suggested fix

Take the cursor position before the selection highlight is applied, so the
marker is already stripped when the line is split. In `doRender()`
(tui-alt-screen.js):

```diff
-screen = this.applySelection(screen, nextLayout);
-screen = this.compositeFlashes(screen, width, height);
-const cursorPos = this.extractCursorPosition(screen, height);
+const cursorPos = this.extractCursorPosition(screen, height);
+screen = this.applySelection(screen, nextLayout);
+screen = this.compositeFlashes(screen, width, height);
```

The highlight does not change visible widths, so the column is unchanged in the
cases that already worked. With this change the 70 wrong-column cases above drop
to 0, for both `showHardwareCursor` settings, and the selection highlight is
unaffected.

The same reorder should be applied to the bundled copy in
`dist/bundle/chunks/`, which is what the pi CLI actually loads.

A more complete fix would teach `sliceWithWidth()` to keep zero-width sequences
in the slice they belong to instead of dropping or duplicating them, but that
touches every caller.


### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Version

1.2.0

issues.title: 1.2.0: keyboard input stops after an unterminated terminal reply (StdinBuffer waits forever)

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

Since 1.2.0, pi sometimes stops accepting keyboard input right after startup. Typed text and Enter are silently ignored. Pressing an arrow key makes input work again, but everything typed before that is lost.

It happens when the reply to the startup color query arrives without its terminator. `StdinBuffer` recognises the reply header and waits for the terminator with no timeout, so every later keystroke is appended to the pending reply and never emitted.

This comes from edb2eb96 ("keep delayed terminal replies out of keyboard input"), and it is still on `main`. In 1.1.0 the same input times out after 50 ms and typing continues.

### Steps to reproduce

Save as `repro.mjs` in the repo root and run `node repro.mjs`:

```js
import { StdinBuffer } from "./packages/tui/src/stdin-buffer.ts";
const sb = new StdinBuffer();
const got = [];
sb.on("data", (d) => got.push(d));
sb.process("\x1b]11;rgb:1e1e/1e1e"); // OSC 11 reply that never gets its BEL/ST
setTimeout(() => sb.process("hello\r"), 300); // user types afterwards
setTimeout(() => { console.log(JSON.stringify(got)); process.exit(0); }, 1000);
```

- v1.2.0: `[]`
- v1.1.0: `["\u001b]11;rgb:1e1e/1e1e","h","e","l","l","o","\r"]`

Removing only the `if (TERMINAL_REPLY_HEADER_PATTERN.test(this.buffer)) return;` line in `process()` brings input back.

### Expected behavior

An unterminated reply should not block keyboard input forever. Some upper bound on the wait (well above the 50 ms key timeout) would keep the fix for slow replies and still let typing through.

### Version

1.2.0 (also current `main`)

---
AI disclosure: drafted by an AI agent (pi) at my direction and reviewed by me; the repro was run on my machine.

issues.title: Resuming a session drops dynamically activated tools
issues.body:
### What happened?

After resuming a session, tools that were previously enabled dynamically become inactive again. The next turn records their removal from the tool list.

This affects optional tools registered with `defaultActive: false`, as well as explicitly activated `exposure: "deferred"` tools.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Register an optional tool and activate it with `setActiveTools()`.
2. Run a turn so the tool activation is recorded in the transcript.
3. Resume the session with the same tool registered, without explicit tool-selection overrides.
4. Check the active tools: the previously enabled tool is missing.

An isolated SDK reproduction also reproduces the state loss with extension discovery disabled and synthetic tool definitions, without third-party extensions or model requests.

### Expected behavior

Resume should restore the transcript's active tool selection, subject to explicit tool restrictions, rather than reset it to registration defaults.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.1.0

issues.body:
### What happened?

Pi's MCP implementation sends `User-Agent: undici` on every request, which makes it hard to identify Pi in stateless MCP server implementations.

Imo Pi should set a correct user agent and also send `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo"]` as per the latest spec.

For context I'm trying to identify Pi in Polar's mcp server so we disable codemode in the server and let Pi's client do codemode. Opencode appends a `?codemode=false` to the URL to signal to the server to not do codemode, might be worh stealing.

I can contribute this if you think it's okay.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a dummy MCP server and send requests to it. Observe that the User-Agent is generic `undici` and `clientInfo` is only sent on the `initialize` request and not on subsequent mcp requests.

### Expected behavior

Pi sets a user agent that correctly identifies it and sends the `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo"]` on every request as per the newest mcp spec.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep leading / root-anchored in skill ignore patterns
prs.body:
## Summary
Skill discovery (and the duplicated package-resource scanner) always stripped a leading `/` from ignore patterns. At the scan root that turns git root-anchored whitelist rules such as:

```gitignore
/*
!/commit-summarizer/
```

into unanchored `*` / `!commit-summarizer/`, so `loadSkillsFromDir` returns no skills while `git check-ignore` still keeps them.

This keeps the leading `/` when there is no directory prefix, and only strips it when prefixing a nested ignore file — the same rule described in #10877.

Fixes #10877

## Test plan
- [x] `npx vitest --run test/skills.test.ts` (29 passed, including new root-anchored whitelist case)
- [x] Temp dir with `/*` + `!/commit-summarizer/` loads only `commit-summarizer`
- [x] Existing nested ignore behavior unchanged for the skills suite

Happy to mirror the same regression under `package-manager.test.ts` if you want both call sites covered explicitly.

prs.title: docs: move documentation to the repository root
prs.body:
The docs now cover more than the coding agent (pi-ai, pi-durable, ...), so they move from `packages/coding-agent/docs` to `docs/` at the repository root.

## Bundling

npm can only pack files inside a package, so the coding-agent build copies `docs/` into `packages/coding-agent/docs/` (generated, gitignored) via `scripts/copy-docs.mjs`. Every release path packs after the build (npm tarballs, release binaries via `build-binaries.sh`, Nix, the evals image), so releases keep shipping `<package>/docs` with no changes to `files`, `build-binaries.sh` or the Dockerfile. The generated copy is byte-identical to the docs the package shipped before this change.

`copy-docs.mjs` is the place to filter what gets bundled later, since `docs/` will include pages unrelated to the coding agent.

## Links

Docs link to coding-agent files through the repository layout, e.g. `../packages/coding-agent/examples/sdk/`, so links work in the repository and on GitHub. `copy-docs.mjs` rewrites links that point into the package back to package-relative paths (`../examples/sdk/`) in the bundled copy. Links to other repository files are left unchanged.

## Runtime

- `getDocsPath()` returns the repository `docs/` in source checkouts and `<package>/docs` in npm installs and the binary.
- Compact rendering of `read` calls recognizes pages under `getDocsPath()`, which is outside the package root in source checkouts.

## Other references

Root README, coding-agent README (`../../docs/...`), the extensions URL in `migrations.ts`, the documentation test, the documentation audit eval, `.pi/prompts/pr.md`, `.pi/skills/add-llm-provider.md`.

## Before merging

pi.dev fetches docs from `packages/coding-agent/docs` on `main` and resolves `../` links against the package path. It needs to read `docs/` (with a fallback to the old path for older refs) and resolve `../` links against the repository root before this lands.

## Verification

- `npm run check`
- `test/documentation.test.ts`, `test/tool-execution-component.test.ts`, `test/config.test.ts`, `test/system-prompt.test.ts`, `test/changelog.test.ts`
- `npm pack --dry-run` includes all 46 docs files

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): resolve model references through one provider selection policy
prs.body:
Fixes #10160

## Problem

When the named provider lacks a model but several gateways expose `provider/id` as a raw id, `--model provider/id` picked the first gateway in catalog order, ignoring credentials:

```text
pi --model anthropic/claude-opus-5.5   # only vercel-ai-gateway has a key
-> openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 (listed first)
```

Provider selection was spread across branches that discarded ambiguity, so results also depended on input shape: `shared` picked the authenticated provider, `shared:high` picked by catalog order.

## Change

`resolveModelReference` in `core/model-resolver.ts` resolves every model reference (`--model`, `--models`/`enabledModels`, `/model`, `pi auth print-*`) in one pipeline. It collects all candidates, then applies one rule: the named provider's match if usable, else the sole usable raw match, else the named provider's match, else ambiguous. Fuzzy matching runs only when no reference candidate exists and prefers usable providers.

## Behavior changes

- No unique authenticated provider among exact matches is now an error, not catalog order.
- Fuzzy matches prefer authenticated providers; an identical best id on several providers is ambiguous.
- With `--api-key`, stored credentials no longer pick the provider.
- `--models`/`enabledModels` patterns add every provider offering the same id.

`provider/id` still prefers the named provider's exact or fuzzy match.

prs.title: fix(ai): inline $ref tool schemas for NVIDIA NIM models
prs.body:
Fixes #10270.

`nemotron-3.5-super-vl-preview` and `qwen3.8-flash-next` return an object described only by a local `$ref` as a JSON string. `validateToolArguments` rejects that:

```
schema:  "settings": { "$ref": "#/$defs/Settings" }
model:   "settings": "{\"notifications\":false}"
```

With the definition inlined, both work. Kimi K2.6 on the same route works either way. Thanks @itayzit for the report, the reproduction, and the [first patch](https://github.com/itayzit/pi/tree/schema-ref-compat).

### Changes

- New `OpenAICompletionsCompat.inlineSchemaRefs`, wired like `supportsStrictMode`:
  - `detectCompat()` and `NVIDIA_OPENAI_COMPAT` default it to true for NVIDIA NIM; it is false everywhere else.
  - `models.json` can enable it for other endpoints, for example Qwen on vLLM.
  - When it is on, `convertTools` sends the inlined schema.
- Other providers are unchanged.
- New `packages/ai/src/utils/json-schema-refs.ts` does the inlining:
  - Expands local `#` and `#/...` references only.
  - Leaves recursive, external, and unresolved refs in place, along with refs that have non-annotation siblings, and keeps the root `$defs` they point into.
  - Sends the schema unchanged if a nested `$id` or anchor is present, or if inlining would add more than 1,000 nodes.
  - Never mutates the input, and caches the result per schema object.
- Argument coercion and optional-null cleanup in `validateToolArguments` now run against the inlined schema. Before, `{"notifications": "false"}` was coerced to `false` in an inline schema but rejected behind a `$ref`. `Check` still runs against the original schema. This applies to all providers and changes nothing that is sent.

Not included:

- Repairing stringified objects during validation, which was declined in #3336.
- Keeping `$defs` in Anthropic non-strict schemas, which is #9557.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance.

prs.title: fix(ai): drop images from Anthropic error tool results
prs.body:
Hello! This fixes https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10794 Before Example session: https://pi.dev/session/#b030644c0109dc893108c67c904cd273 After : https://pi.dev/session/#0edc1eddb7242e81e79c62966b4d3109 Investigation session: https://pi.dev/session/#a74d1c66f4d82b5fcd6e76eddfaefc24 Implementation session: https://pi.dev/session/#2186f127955bef0d1d4896cf49a93b5a Let me know if you want/need any changes or if this should be done another way! ------
Summary by synthetic/Kimi-K3:

## Summary Anthropic's Messages API rejects a `tool_result` block with `is_error: true` unless its content is text-only (`all content must be type 'text' if 'is_error' is true`). Pi can produce exactly this shape from codemode: a script that emits images with `image()` and then fails (e.g. a failed `read`, ENOENT) returns a tool result with `isError: true` whose content still contains the already-emitted image blocks. Partial output before the failure is preserved on purpose, so the next Anthropic request 400s and the session stalls. Anthropic is the only adapter that sends an error flag on tool results at all: Bedrock sends `status: ERROR` with image blocks (accepted), the OpenAI formats have no error flag, Gemini attaches images to error responses (accepted), and Mistral flattens images to text placeholders. So only the Anthropic adapter needs to normalize this shape. ## Changes - `packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts` — `convertToolResult` now filters image blocks out of the content when `isError` is set, falling back to an `"(error)"` placeholder when the result carried only images. Successful tool results are unchanged. - `packages/ai/test/anthropic-error-tool-result-images.test.ts` — new regression test that drives the Anthropic adapter against a local HTTP server capturing the request body, using a transcript with an erroring `read` tool result that carries an image, and asserts the sent `tool_result` is text-only. ## Verification - `vitest --run packages/ai/test/anthropic-error-tool-result-images.test.ts` — passes. Before the fix, the captured request carried `is_error: true` alongside an image block, reproducing the production 400 at the request-construction level. - `vitest --run packages/ai/test/anthropic` — 18 files, 100 passed, 35 skipped (endpoint-gated e2e). - `npm run check` — passes (also runs in the pre-commit hook).

prs.title: feat(ai): send GPT-6 effort changes as configuration_update items
prs.body:
Closes #10853

Switching thinking levels on GPT-6 currently changes the request-level `reasoning.effort`, which rewrites the prompt prefix and misses the cache. On Codex it also drops the WebSocket continuation.

This keeps the first effort at the request level and sends later changes as a `configuration_update` item before the next user message. Each response records the effort it ran with (`providerThinkingLevel`, same as the Anthropic path), so later requests replay the updates in the same spots and the prefix stays identical.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant pi
    participant OpenAI
    pi->>OpenAI: effort low, input [user a]
    OpenAI-->>pi: reply 1, recorded as low
    Note over pi: user switches to high
    pi->>OpenAI: effort low, input [user a, reply 1, update high, user b]
    Note over OpenAI: cached through reply 1
    OpenAI-->>pi: reply 2, recorded as high
    pi->>OpenAI: effort low, input [user a, reply 1, update high, user b, reply 2, user c]
    Note over OpenAI: cached through reply 2
```

Notes:

- The `supportsMidConvoEffort` flag is set for the GPT-6 models on `openai` and `openai-codex`, so it shows up once the model catalog is republished. The tests set it directly.
- A change made during a tool loop applies at the next user message, since that's the only place the API accepts it.
- Flagged models always send `reasoning.summary` and encrypted reasoning, since the effort in force can differ from the request-level one.

`npm run check` and the OpenAI, Codex, and Azure tests pass. `./test.sh` only failed locally on tests that need built packages or `fd`. I haven't verified it against the live API yet.
