prs.title: fix(sessions): explain messaging suppression across guidance surfaces
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Aligns cross-session messaging guidance with the existing `--bare` and `--safe-mode` suppression rules. Both recipient-error paths identify the active mode, with safe mode taking precedence when both flags are set. Updates controller guidance, setting help, its generated editor schema and session documentation.

## Why it's needed

The current setting-only guidance can suggest a remedy that cannot restore messaging in a suppressed session. It also confuses being listed with being messageable: interactive Ink sessions can remain listed without a peer address, while suppressed hosted ACP sessions do not register. This addresses all five remaining surfaces identified in #12866.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Exercise an unknown recipient with disabled peer transport, both without a team and after a team reports the recipient missing. `--safe-mode` and `--bare` must produce the corresponding explanation; enabling both must explain safe mode. Ordinary setting/inbox suppression keeps its previous guidance. The eight regression cases cover these combinations; controller tests also require the flag guidance. The newly built CLI was additionally exercised with isolated controller add/list/remove operations: each exited 0, the emitted guidance included both flags, and the temporary grants were removed. Regenerate the settings schema and confirm it matches the committed artifact.

- On the latest source baseline: eight isolated diagnostic regression cases passed, with mocked peer transport. The earlier built CLI also completed isolated controller add/list/remove operations with the expected flag guidance; no real peer socket or message was used.
- On the combined verification checkout at `23add5e`, frozen dependency installation, formatting, lint, build and typecheck completed successfully. These were not three independent full-preflight runs.
- **Full preflight did not pass on Windows.** The ACP suite reported 2,624 passed, 14 failed and eight skipped; its 14 failures occurred creating symlink fixtures (`EPERM`). CLI tests also reported failures, including relaunch expectations and file-lock cleanup; the recorded workspace run did not finish all suites. Separate script tests reported 1,805 passed, 26 failed and 202 skipped, including symlink restrictions, missing Git metadata/skill assets in the temporary validation copy, and shell fixture failures. Not all failures have been reproduced on clean upstream or classified; no all-tests-pass claim is made.
- The publication base is `e17ad4c`. Its three intervening commits do not overlap any files in these PRs. Candidate file contents were checked against the verification copy, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review found no remaining issue after corrections. The Qwen-specific CLI `/review` orchestration was not run.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, the safe-mode and bare-mode reproduction cases failed because the actual returned explanation was `agents.crossSessionMessaging is off, or its inbox did not start`. After, both returned explanations name the suppressing flag. This is a diagnostic-text and documentation change; N/A for a graphical demo. Unit reproduction uses mocked peer transport, not a real socket or hosted session.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Tested: Node 22.23.2 |
| Linux | Not tested |

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk: inaccurate guidance; tested both error branches and mode precedence against the existing suppression policy.
- Not validated: real CLI/IPC/hosted reachability. The global `qwen` command is unavailable locally. Child environment inheritance is outside this issue's wording sweep.
- Breaking changes: none; no registration, routing or admission policy changes.
- AI disclosure: Codex assisted with analysis, implementation, tests, review and this description. No personal human code-review confirmation is asserted.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12866

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

使跨会话消息说明与已有 `--bare`、`--safe-mode` 抑制规则一致。两个收件人错误路径均说明当前模式，两个旗标同时启用时优先说明安全模式。同时更新 controller 指引、设置帮助、生成的编辑器 schema 和会话文档。

## 修改原因

目前只提设置开关的指引可能建议无法恢复受抑制会话消息功能的操作，也混淆了列出会话与可发送消息：交互式 Ink 会话可能仍列出却没有 peer 地址，而受抑制的托管 ACP 会话不注册。本修改覆盖 #12866 列出的五处剩余说明。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 验证方法

在 peer transport 禁用时尝试未知收件人，分别验证无团队与团队报告找不到收件人的情况。`--safe-mode`、`--bare` 必须返回相应解释；同时启用时应解释安全模式。普通设置关闭或 inbox 未启动时保持原指引。八个回归案例覆盖这些组合；controller 测试也要求包含旗标说明。此外，在隔离设置目录实际执行了新构建 CLI 的 controller add/list/remove：均退出 0，输出包含两个旗标指引，临时授权已删除。重新生成设置 schema 并确认与提交产物一致。

- 最新源代码基线上的八个隔离诊断回归案例通过，使用模拟 peer transport。此前构建的 CLI 在隔离目录中完成 controller 添加/列出/移除，输出包含两种禁用模式；未使用真实 peer socket 或发送消息。
- 在 `23add5e` 的合并验证副本中，冻结依赖安装、格式、lint、构建和类型检查已完成并通过；并非三个独立分支各跑了一次完整 preflight。
- **全量 preflight 未通过。** Windows 的 ACP 测试为 2,624 通过、14 失败、8 跳过；这 14 项均在创建符号链接夹具时遇到 `EPERM`。CLI 测试也报告了重启预期和文件锁清理等失败，记录的工作区测试未完成全部套件。独立脚本测试为 1,805 通过、26 失败、202 跳过，包含符号链接权限、临时验证副本缺少 Git 元数据/skill 文件及 shell 夹具失败。尚未在干净上游复现并归类全部失败，不声称所有测试通过。
- 发布基线为 `e17ad4c`；中间新增的三次提交没有修改本轮 PR 涉及的文件。候选文件内容与验证副本一致，`git diff --check` 通过。
- 修正发现的问题后，独立源代码审阅未发现剩余问题；未执行 Qwen 专用 CLI 的 `/review` 编排。

### 修复前后证据

修复前，安全模式和 bare 模式复现案例因实际返回说明为 `agents.crossSessionMessaging is off, or its inbox did not start` 而失败。修复后均说明具体抑制旗标。本修改涉及诊断文字与文档，图形演示不适用。单元复现模拟 peer transport，并非真实 socket 或托管会话。

### 测试平台

| 操作系统 | 状态 |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | 未测试 |
| Windows | 已测试：Node 22.23.2 |
| Linux | 未测试 |

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：说明不准确；已按现有抑制规则测试两个错误分支及模式优先级。
- 未验证：真实 CLI、IPC 和托管会话可达性。本地没有全局 `qwen` 命令。子进程环境继承不属于此问题的文案范围。
- 破坏性变更：无；不修改注册、路由或消息准入策略。
- AI 使用披露：Codex 协助分析、实现、测试、审阅及撰写说明。不声称本人已完成人工代码审阅。

## 关联问题

修复 #12866。

</details>



## Follow-up verification — 2026-10-13

Addressed R1-1 through R1-8: safe-mode guidance names its environment variable and the setting that may also be off; the unreachable bare-mode tool branch and artificial cases were removed; unknown no-inbox states are described without inventing a disabled setting or a startup failure. The empty agent roster also explains suppressed peer visibility. Controller guidance checks the presence of ipcPath and names OpenTUI. The settings documentation and hosted-session paragraph now match actual registry and child-environment behavior.

Related core tests passed (85), including message routing and agent listing. Changed-file ESLint, Prettier and diff whitespace checks passed. Core TypeScript compilation completed, but the full build did not pass: Browser Use runtime/copy verification resolves playwright-core 1.58.2 instead of the required 1.62.1 in this local dependency setup. Full preflight, release-bundle, real socket and real model checks were not rerun. The previous triage run failed because the model API connection timed out (ETIMEDOUT/ENETUNREACH), rather than because an application test failed; this follow-up does not claim that infrastructure failure is fixed. An independent local source review found no additional finding. Codex assisted with the follow-up; no personal human-read certification is asserted.

### 中文：本轮修订

落实 8 条审阅建议，统一 safe-mode 环境变量、设置可能仍关闭及 inbox 缺失的说明；去掉不可达的 bare 工具分支，补齐 agent 列表、controller 和文档。core 相关测试 85 项通过，修改文件 lint、格式和空白检查通过。完整构建仍受本地 Browser Use 的 playwright-core 版本冲突阻塞；未重跑全套 preflight 或真实服务。此前 triage 是模型 API 网络连接失败，不能称为代码测试失败。

Controller follow-up validation: 21 tests passed using a temporary adapter retaining the official CLI setup and aliases while omitting only the unavailable workspace-dist guard. Five load-time mutations (environment-variable name, possible-setting hedge, ipcPath, list_agents suppression, unknown-inbox fallback) each caused the corresponding new assertion to fail. This adapter is not included in the PR and is not a full CLI preflight run.

## Review follow-up — 2026-10-14

Addressed the new wording and coverage findings. Both tools now use one core-local reason selector. A missing readable own peer address is described as `this session publishes no peer inbox address`, without asserting that no socket was bound or inferring that another named session cannot exist. When no own identity is available, the roster says other sessions cannot be discovered **from this session**; machine-wide unreachability is reported only on the branch that actually queried the peer directory. Healthy-inbox tests explicitly reject suppression guidance. Documentation and the regenerated settings schema distinguish interactive registration, messaging-gated daemon/editor-hosted registration, and independently listed Agent View managed rows.

Verification: 85 related core tests passed with the official configuration. Three test-only mutations restoring the false bind claim, machine-wide claim, or healthy-session suppression each failed their new assertions. Core TypeScript checking, changed-file ESLint, Prettier, whitespace checks and settings-schema generation passed. An independent engineer verified the tests and mutation results. No new release-bundle, full preflight or real-socket/model E2E run is claimed; the previously disclosed local Browser Use dependency conflict remains a full-build limitation. Codex assisted with implementation, verification and this description; this is not personal human code-review certification.

### 中文：本轮修订

两工具共用原因说明，不再由注册表地址缺失推断 socket 未绑定或其他会话不存在；没有查询目录时只说明本会话无法发现其他会话。补齐健康会话不会误报停用的断言，统一交互会话、托管会话和 Agent View 的文档与生成 schema。官方配置下相关测试 85 项通过，三个变异检查捕获对应错误，core 类型检查、lint、格式和 schema 生成通过。未重跑完整 preflight 或真实 socket/模型 E2E，仍披露原本地完整构建限制。

CI baseline follow-up: merged upstream main at 1f39a80bf01f7064e23acda7146cabf398070f85 using a normal two-parent merge after the lint-gate freshness check required it. The earlier lint job stopped at that freshness gate, before application lint/tests. The refreshed CI is pending; no green claim is made.

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): restart-proof the held-Runtime drain across Harness takeover (#13930)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

In the Hosted Harness, a turn that ends with its Runtime held (its routine release was refused `runtime_session_held` by design) owes the Session's close that Runtime's drain release. The obligation was recorded only in the holding process's memory, so a Harness restart or a replacement takeover silently lost it: the reloaded Session's close answered 204 while the worker's run was still alive and the workspace mount stayed pinned past the Session's own end. This change makes the obligation durable. The Runtime Broker's execution ledger already knows which of a Harness Session's Runtime Sessions carry provably live hold rows; the broker now answers that as a read-only harness-scoped listing, and a fresh load of a hosted Session restores the owed set from it — restored, never discharged (an eager drain on load would stop a run the live Session still wants). A load that cannot prove the listing fails honestly with 409 `hosted_runtime_broker_unavailable` instead of silently re-leaking at close.

## Why it's needed

Deferred Critical R1-2 from the deep review of the H3 enablement slice (issue #13930): the close's held-Runtime drain obligation died with the process, leaving runtimes and workspace mounts pinned invisibly past session close. The scope of this PR is R1-2 only; the review's Suggestion batch follows separately.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. On an original Harness, settle a turn whose routine Runtime release is refused `runtime_session_held`, then end that Harness without invoking the close route.
2. Have a replacement Harness (new boot id, same durable session store) load the same Session: expect 200 and no Runtime released as part of the load itself.
3. DELETE the Session on the replacement: expect the held turn's Runtime Session to be released with `{"drain": true}` — this is the new takeover acceptance case pinned beside the #13856 drain test.
4. Failure arm: make the Broker's hold listing unreachable — the load answers 409 `hosted_runtime_broker_unavailable` and nothing is discharged; re-arming the Broker and retrying the load succeeds (proves the refused attempt freed its writer lease).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (server-internal behavioral change, covered by unit tests below).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit/integration only: `packages/cli` vitest suites, `packages/sdk-java/runtime-broker` Maven suite, `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run bundle`, and `mvn checkstyle:check`.

**Measured results on the final rebased tree (origin/main @ 163e4686):** `hosted-harness-session.test.ts` 461/461; `hosted-workspace-broker.test.ts` 45/45; `mvn clean test` in the runtime-broker module 820/820; checkstyle 0 violations; build/typecheck/bundle/eslint all exit 0.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a takeover load of a workspace-profile Session now queries the Broker once; a Broker that cannot answer fails the load honestly rather than leaving its close with nothing owed. Sessions without a workspace tool profile take no new call.
- Not validated / out of scope: the JDBC `harness_session_id` query currently scans the append-only ledger (no index) — deferred to the follow-up batch because the index needs a Flyway migration plus the schema.sql lane; the three Suggestion groups from the same issue are intentionally not in this PR.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; new read-only broker route is additive.

Design doc: updated in both languages — `docs/design/2026-10-11-managed-h3-enablement.md` and `docs/design/2026-10-11-managed-h3-enablement.zh-CN.md` (matching D4 paragraph on the obligation traveling with the Session, not the process).

## Linked Issues

Refs #13930 — this PR closes only the deferred Critical R1-2; the Suggestions batch follows in later PRs.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

Hosted Harness 中，一个被持有（routine release 按设计被 `runtime_session_held` 拒绝）结束的 turn，把那次 Runtime 的 drain release 亏欠给 Session 的 close。这份亏欠此前只记在持有进程的内存里：Harness 重启或被替补接管后，重开 Session 的 close 回答 204，而 worker 的 run 仍存活、workspace mount 继续被钉住，越过 Session 本身的结束。本修改让这份亏欠变得持久：Runtime Broker 的执行账本本来就记录一个 Harness Session 的哪些 Runtime 携带可证明存活的持有行，本次把它作为只读的 harness 级清单应答；新挂载 hosted Session 时按这份清单恢复亏欠集——只恢复、绝不清偿（挂载时抢先 drain 会停掉活 Session 仍然要的 run）；清单无法证明时，挂载诚实失败，返回 409 `hosted_runtime_broker_unavailable`，而不是在 close 时刻静默泄漏。

## 为什么需要

它是 H3 启用片深评审中被推迟的 Critical R1-2（issue #13930）：close 对被持有 Runtime 的 drain 亏欠随进程死亡而消失，导致 Runtime 与 workspace mount 在 Session 关闭之后仍被钉住。本 PR 范围只含 R1-2；同一 issue 的 Suggestion 批次另行跟进。

## 评审验证方案

1. 在原 Harness 上结算一个 routine release 被拒为 `runtime_session_held` 的 turn，随后不走 close 路由结束该 Harness。
2. 让替补 Harness（新 boot id、同一份持久化 session store）挂载同一 Session：预期 200，且挂载本身不释放任何 Runtime。
3. 在替补上 DELETE 该 Session：被持有 turn 的 Runtime Session 应带着 `{"drain": true}` 被释放——这是挂在 #13856 drain 用例旁新增的接管验收用例。
4. 失败臂：让 Broker 持有清单不可达——挂载应答 409 `hosted_runtime_broker_unavailable`，且什么都不被清偿；恢复 Broker 后重试挂载成功（证明被拒尝试已释放其 writer lease）。

Tested on：macOS ✅（Windows/Linux：N/A）。

实测结果（重基到 origin/main @ 163e4686 后）：461/461（hosted-harness-session.test.ts）、45/45（hosted-workspace-broker.test.ts）、820/820（runtime-broker 模块 mvn clean test）、checkstyle 0 违规、build/typecheck/bundle/eslint 全部 0 退出。

## 风险与范围

- 主要取舍：workspace profile Session 的接管挂载多一次 Broker 查询；Broker 无法证明时挂载诚实失败，不再悄悄亏欠。非 workspace 的 Session 不新增调用。
- 未验证/不在范围：JDBC `harness_session_id` 查询当前对追加式大表全表扫描（无索引）——迁往后续批次，因索引需要 Flyway 迁移与 schema.sql 两通道落地；同 issue 的三组 Suggestion 刻意不在本 PR。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无；新增只读 broker 路由为纯增量。

## 关联 Issue

Refs #13930 —— 本 PR 只关闭被推迟的 Critical R1-2；Suggestions 批次在后续 PR 跟进。

</details>

prs.title: feat(cli): report interactive program status with OSC 7501
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds OSC 7501 status reports to the interactive Ink CLI with the stable identifier `qwen-code`: idle, working, blocked (permission/question/auth), done, and error. Completed and failed turns remain latched until the next turn; cancellation returns to idle. Reports are TTY-only, use existing OSC/multiplexer framing, and are cleared on unmount, exit, and inherited-terminal editor handoff. Terminal diff editing is bracketed before the confirmation callback runs; GUI editors retain CLI terminal ownership. Returning from an editor or resuming the process restores the current report only while the CLI owns the terminal. Per-turn failures are independent of retained error banners, including delayed finalization failures.

## Why it's needed

Terminals can show which agent tabs are working, awaiting input, or finished without parsing screen text. This follows the maintainer's requested hook-based scope, TTY gate, no new setting, and deliberate omission of focus-based completion resets. The small additional lifecycle wiring handles the handoff concern raised in triage and distinguishes cancellation from successful completion.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

In a supporting terminal, start an interactive session and submit a prompt. Expect idle → working → done, with done retained until the next turn. Trigger a permission, question, or authentication dialog and expect the corresponding blocked kind. A failed API turn should latch error; cancelling or declining every tool approval should return to idle. Exit or open an inherited-terminal editor and confirm the record clears; returning from the editor should restore it. Headless text, JSON, stream-JSON and ACP output must contain no OSC 7501 bytes.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the baseline source has no OSC 7501 reports. A global CLI baseline could not be run because `qwen` and tmux are unavailable.

After: isolated raw-PTY tests with a deterministic local model server observed idle → working → done → clear, idle → working → error → clear, idle → working → idle → clear on cancellation, and blocked/auth → clear. Headless text, JSON and stream-JSON completed successfully without OSC 7501; JSON/NDJSON parsed. ACP initialization returned valid JSON-RPC without OSC 7501. See the separate E2E report comment for exact evidence.

Focused tests: 1,669 passing and one existing skipped test across AppContainer wiring, program status, stream lifecycle, editor handoffs, headless output, and ACP. Twenty targeted mutation checks detected removed fixes or injected OSC output. Full build, typecheck, bundle, changed-file ESLint, Prettier, and diff checks passed; validation results are recorded in the E2E comment.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ not tested |

### Environment (optional)

macOS ARM64, Node 26.10.0, pinned pnpm 11.24.0, local bundle and isolated PTY/mock-model harness. The final build uses an 8 GB Node heap because the default 4 GB limit was exhausted.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: turn results are inferred from existing UI state and error history; terminals choose how to display the protocol.
- Not validated / out of scope: presentation in a supporting terminal, live-provider auth, OpenTUI, focus resets, and pre-suspend clearing. SIGCONT restores status, but no SIGTSTP handler is added because it would change Node's default suspension semantics.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; no settings or dependencies added.

Design: [English](https://github.com/maxffarrell/qwen-code/blob/feat/osc-7501-program-status/docs/design/program-status.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/maxffarrell/qwen-code/blob/feat/osc-7501-program-status/docs/design/program-status.zh-CN.md). Both versions cover the same decisions, constraints, validation and follow-ups.

## Linked Issues

Closes #13870

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 的改动

为交互式 Ink CLI 增加 OSC 7501 状态报告，使用稳定标识 `qwen-code`：idle、working、blocked（permission/question/auth）、done 和 error。完成或失败的轮次保持锁存，直到下一轮开始；取消时返回 idle。仅在 TTY 输出报告，复用现有 OSC/多路复用帧格式，并在卸载、退出和继承终端的编辑器交接时清除。终端差异编辑在确认回调执行前后进行交接；GUI 编辑器保留 CLI 的终端所有权。编辑器返回或进程恢复时，仅在 CLI 拥有终端的情况下重新发送当前报告。轮次失败独立于保留的错误提示，包括延迟的收尾失败。

## 为什么需要

终端无需解析屏幕文本即可显示哪些代理标签页正在工作、等待输入或已经完成。本改动遵循维护者要求的 hook 范围、TTY 门控、不新增设置，以及明确不实现焦点完成重置。少量额外生命周期连接处理分诊提出的终端交接问题，并区分取消与成功完成。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

在支持的终端中启动交互式会话并提交提示词。应观察到 idle → working → done，done 保持到下一轮。触发权限、提问或认证对话框，应观察到相应 blocked 类型。API 失败应锁存 error；取消或拒绝全部工具审批应返回 idle。退出或打开继承终端的编辑器时记录应清除，编辑器返回后恢复。headless text、JSON、stream-JSON 和 ACP 输出不得包含 OSC 7501 字节。

### 证据（前后对比）

之前：基线源码没有 OSC 7501 报告。由于环境没有全局 `qwen` 和 tmux，无法执行全局 CLI 基线。

之后：使用确定性本地模型服务器的隔离原始 PTY 测试观察到 idle → working → done → clear、idle → working → error → clear、取消时 idle → working → idle → clear，以及 blocked/auth → clear。headless text、JSON 和 stream-JSON 成功完成且不包含 OSC 7501，JSON/NDJSON 可解析。ACP 初始化返回有效 JSON-RPC 且不包含 OSC 7501。精确证据见单独的 E2E 报告评论。

聚焦测试：AppContainer 连接、程序状态、流生命周期、编辑器交接、headless 输出及 ACP 等八组共 1,669 项通过，另有一项现有测试跳过。20 项定向变异检查检测到了移除修复或注入 OSC 输出。完整构建、类型检查、bundle、改动文件 ESLint、Prettier 和 diff 检查均通过；验证结果记录在 E2E 评论中。

### 测试平台

| OS | 状态 |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 已测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未测试 |

### 环境（可选）

macOS ARM64、Node 26.10.0、固定 pnpm 11.24.0、本地 bundle 及隔离 PTY/模拟模型测试。默认 4 GB 堆限制耗尽，因此最终构建使用 8 GB Node 堆。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：轮次结果由现有 UI 状态和错误历史推断；终端决定如何显示协议。
- 未验证或范围之外：支持终端的显示效果、真实服务商认证、OpenTUI、焦点重置及挂起前清理。SIGCONT 恢复状态，但不添加 SIGTSTP 处理器，以免改变 Node 的默认挂起语义。
- 破坏性改动或迁移：无；不新增设置或依赖。

设计：[English](https://github.com/maxffarrell/qwen-code/blob/feat/osc-7501-program-status/docs/design/program-status.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/maxffarrell/qwen-code/blob/feat/osc-7501-program-status/docs/design/program-status.zh-CN.md)。两个版本包含一致的决策、约束、验证及后续工作。

## 关联 Issue

Closes #13870

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): keep OpenTUI hook content reachable (MYWO-3, MYWO-13)
prs.body:
Frozen rework head `7cb0a86fbf709da0da24f6acb0a14465e59b9c36`, stacked base `e16490eccc5aeffbb680da7c0935b5aebfe82f1b`. MYWO-17 fixes the newly identified word-boundary regression while preserving hard wrapping and whitespace. Old-SHA review outcomes do not certify this head; Leader acceptance and independent retest/reviews remain pending.

冻结返工 head `7cb0a86fbf709da0da24f6acb0a14465e59b9c36`，stacked base `e16490eccc5aeffbb680da7c0935b5aebfe82f1b`。MYWO-17修复新增词边界回退，保留硬折及空白。旧SHA审查结论不用于证明新head；待Leader验收及独立复测复审。

## What this PR does

Keep hook details and empty hook explanations scrollable inside their popup region. Long literal commands retain all lines and wide glyphs at narrow widths. The sandboxed Diff notice now uses the same bounded content policy as the working-tree preview. Short regions keep a usable row; Esc still walks back through hook menus or closes Diff.

## Why it's needed

At the stacked base, a 40-column hook detail occupied 102 rows with no scrollbox: the head appeared, but the middle and tail could not be reached. The sandbox notice occupied 12 rows at 20 columns and painted beyond regions 1–6. Matching the measured title wrapping, paying the scrollbar column, and stacking narrow label/value pairs address additional native rendering counterexamples found during verification.

This is the second batch for MYWO-3 / MYWO-13, stacked on open PR #14034, branch `fix/MYWO-7-short-dialog-budgets`, fixed base `e16490eccc5aeffbb680da7c0935b5aebfe82f1b`. First-batch changes are dependencies. Latest inspected main is `83ffe4540c7df15c46a8893f8919801fac58295b`. Six historical chrome leads already use measured runs or clipped labels; representative native runs agree with their charges, so those modules are unchanged.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open Hooks with a multiline command containing distinct head, intermediate and tail markers, Chinese characters, and trailing timeout/options/status fields. Enter event → matcher → handler → details. At 20/28/29/40/100 columns and regions 1–6/15/40, scroll through every marker and the final edit instruction. Arrow/page keys and Home/End should move the viewport; four Esc presses should return through the menus and close once.
2. Resize details while scrolled: a width or content-budget change returns to the head; an unchanged viewport preserves the offset. No painted border or content should appear below the popup region. Empty matchers and handlers should also remain bounded with explanations reachable by scrolling.
3. For word boundaries, at width29/region15 scroll details to see intact `settings.json`; at width40/region15 scroll empty explanations to see intact `event` and `settings.json`. Words wider than the actual text width may hard-wrap.
4. Open Diff with sandboxing both enabled and disabled. Shrink and resize between short/narrow and normal regions. Both branches should fit and Esc should close once; sandboxing must not launch Git.
5. Confirm the final matcher is highlighted, Enter commits that matcher, and existing hook configuration, permission gates and asynchronous behavior remain unchanged.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Native `captureCharFrame` plus actual node geometry, using a canvas with 60 spare rows below the popup, establishes painted overrun and content reachability. Input is mocked; these frames are not PTY recordings. Before: detail width40/region15 has native height102 and missing middle/tail; sandbox Diff width20/region1–6 has height12 with border overpaint. After: every tested frame stays within its region; all 87 distinct literal/status glyphs are painted across 40 detail cases. Independent probes also cover last-matcher selection and the timeout/options/edit-instruction tail. Eight precise production regressions trigger business AssertionError/exit1, with restored source green. Evidence correction: the historical author `detail-cap` actually targeted the empty state, now named `empty-cap`; the old ZIP/log remain unchanged. New `true-detail-cap` uniquely targets detail key plus height and has its own detail-path stack. A word-wrap mutant also fails the empty-state assertion, and separately the detail assertion. MYWO-17 delivery contains new command exits, both diffs, raw logs and fingerprints; independent reviewer evidence is not relabeled as original author evidence.

Local validation for the rework: 102 related OpenTUI/Ink test files, 2173 tests; native component parity; build, bundle, full typecheck, lint, formatting and whitespace checks. Original command exits, including failed development attempts and their successful reruns, are retained in the delivery evidence.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ native headless renderer and related unit/build gates |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ pending |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ pending |

### Environment

macOS arm64, Node 24.19.0, Bun 1.4.0. tmux is unavailable. Native mock-key testing is the local fallback.

## Risk & Scope

- Main tradeoff: very short regions hide optional chrome; Esc remains active. A changed detail viewport resets scrolling to the head.
- Empty working-tree Diff regression only; large Diff remains unverified.
- Pending: real PTY, tmux, Windows/Linux and assistive-technology verification; 11-column body visibility remains an independent upstream limitation. The six chrome samples do not certify all six complete dialogs. Leader must schedule frozen-head testing and independent Qwen/Codex reviews.
- No migration required. No default renderer switch, Ink removal, merge, Bun S2, clipboard, confirmation or upstream FFI change.

Design: [English](docs/design/2026-10-13-opentui-hook-content.md), [简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-13-opentui-hook-content.zh-CN.md); decisions, limits and requirements are synchronized.

## Linked Issues

Refs #13758, #12612, #8662; MYWO-3 / MYWO-13. Composite issues remain open.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

让 hooks 详情及空 hooks 说明在 popup 区域内滚动。长 literal 命令保留全部行与窄列宽字符。sandboxed Diff 提示现与工作区预览使用相同限高策略。短区域保留可用内容行；Esc 仍逐级返回 hooks 菜单或关闭 Diff。

## 修复原因

stacked base 上，40 列 hooks 详情占 102 行且无 scrollbox：头部出现，中尾无法到达。sandbox 提示在 20 列占 12 行，绘出 region1–6。使标题实际包行与测量一致、支付滚动条列、窄列标签和值上下排列，也修复了验证时发现的原生绘制反例。

这是 MYWO-3 / MYWO-13 的第二批，stacked 在仍开放的 PR #14034 分支 `fix/MYWO-7-short-dialog-budgets` 上，固定 base 为 `e16490eccc5aeffbb680da7c0935b5aebfe82f1b`。首批改动仅计作依赖。已检查的最新 main 为 `83ffe4540c7df15c46a8893f8919801fac58295b`。六项历史 chrome 线索已使用 measured runs 或标签裁剪，代表性原生 run 与预算一致，未改对应模块。

## 审查者测试计划

### 验证方法

1. 配置包含不同头中尾标记、汉字及后续 timeout/options/status 的多行命令，进入 event → matcher → handler → details。在 20/28/29/40/100 列、region1–6/15/40 下，滚动到每个标记及最终编辑说明。方向/翻页键与 Home/End 应移动 viewport；四次 Esc 应逐级返回并只关闭一次。
2. 详情滚动后 resize：宽度或正文预算变化回到头部；viewport 不变时保留偏移。popup 区域外不应绘出边框或内容。空 matchers 和 handlers 同样限高，说明可滚动到达。
3. 词边界：宽29/region15详情滚动可见完整`settings.json`；宽40/region15空态滚动可见完整`event`与`settings.json`。词长超过实际正文宽度时允许硬折。
4. 分别启用和禁用 sandbox 打开 Diff，在短窄与正常区域之间缩放。两分支均应容纳，Esc 只关闭一次；sandbox 不应启动 Git。
5. 确认最后一个 matcher 实际高亮，Enter 提交该 matcher，已有 hooks 配置、权限 gate 和异步行为保持不变。

### 前后证据

使用 `captureCharFrame` 与真实节点几何，并在 popup 下方保留 60 行画布余量，验证真实越界绘制与内容可达。输入是 mock，这些帧不是 PTY 录像。修复前：详情宽40/region15 的 native height102，中尾缺失；sandbox Diff 宽20/region1–6 高12行且边框越界。修复后：全部测试帧位于区域内，40 个详情场景中全部 87 个不同 literal/status glyph 可实际绘制。独立 probe 还覆盖末 matcher 选择及 timeout/options/编辑说明尾部。八个精准生产回退均触发业务 AssertionError/exit1，恢复源码后通过。证据纠错：作者历史`detail-cap`实际命中空态，现准确命名`empty-cap`；旧ZIP与日志不改写。新增`true-detail-cap`用detail key与height唯一定位，保留独立详情路径堆栈。词包行反例被空态断言捕获，另行隔离后也被详情断言捕获。MYWO-17交付包含新逐命令退出码、两份diff、原始日志及fingerprint；不挪用独立reviewer证据冒称作者原有。

本轮返工验证：102 个相关 OpenTUI/Ink 测试文件共2173项测试；native component parity；build、bundle、完整 typecheck、lint、格式和空白检查。交付证据保留所有原始退出码，包括开发失败尝试及成功重跑。

### 测试平台

| OS | 状态 |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 原生 headless renderer、相关单测与构建门禁 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 待验证 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 待验证 |

### 环境

macOS arm64，Node24.19.0，Bun1.4.0。tmux 不可用，本地采用原生 mock-key 测试替代路径。

## 风险与范围

- 主要取舍：极短区域隐藏可选 chrome，Esc 始终有效；详情 viewport 改变时滚动重置到头部。
- 非sandbox工作区Diff仅验证空态；大型Diff仍待验证。
- 待验证：真实 PTY、tmux、Windows/Linux 及辅助技术；11 列正文可见性仍是独立上游限制。六项 chrome 样例不构成六个完整 dialog 认证。Leader 需安排冻结 head 测试与 Qwen/Codex 独立双审。
- 无迁移要求。不切默认 renderer、不移除 Ink、不合并，不改 Bun S2、剪贴板、confirmation 或上游 FFI。

设计：[English](docs/design/2026-10-13-opentui-hook-content.md)、[简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-13-opentui-hook-content.zh-CN.md)，决策、限制和需求完整同步。

## 关联 issue

Refs #13758、#12612、#8662；MYWO-3 / MYWO-13。复合 issue 保持开放。

</details>

## Developer fast loop

The whole point of this decomposition: once a sub-EPIC's crate exists (EPIC-006 Feature 3 and later), day-to-day development happens **entirely outside the TUI monolith** (\~700k lines). The TUI is only compiled when you explicitly need it — TUI integration tests, `cargo test --workspace`, or the final pre-PR validation.

```bash
cargo check -p codewhale-commands          # production change check — seconds, not minutes
cargo test -p codewhale-commands           # test loop — compiles only the commands crate + thin test binaries, never the TUI
cargo watch -x "check -p codewhale-commands"  # continuous check while editing (cargo-watch)
cargo nextest run -p codewhale-commands    # optional: parallel test runner, faster startup
```

Why this stays fast:

* `cargo build` / `cargo check` never compiles `#[cfg(test)]` code, so production iteration is bounded to the small crate.
* `cargo test` compiles each `tests/` file as its **own small binary crate** depending only on the public API — a production change recompiles/relinks only those thin binaries, in parallel.
* The Gherkin acceptance harnesses live in separate test binaries (or a dedicated acceptance crate), so thousands of acceptance-test lines are **never part of the production crate compile**.
* Small white-box unit tests that need private access stay inline — they are cheap and cannot live outside the crate.

**Acceptance criterion for every extracted crate:** `cargo test -p <crate>` must compile only that crate and its test binaries — if it pulls in `codewhale-tui`, the boundary was cut wrong.

The numbers and impact motivating this are documented in [#4991](<https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4991>) (Discussion: Compilation times and the TUI crate monolith): 476k lines / 82% of the workspace in one crate, 8–16 min release builds, 30+ min test suite, 2–3 iterations per hour.

issues.title: Release: guard the crates.io 10 MiB tarball cap before the first upload (v0.10.1: tui/cli stranded by HTTP 413)

labels.name: release-blocker
labels.description: Must be fixed before the next release

labels.name: packaging
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

issues.body:
**0.10.2 candidate update (2026-10-13).** The complete strict no-upload preflight passes for all **29** workspace crates at [6e72400bbb](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/6e72400bbb5182473e6971abcd18bd8953c2f4cc), including the new saved-DeepSeek-key correction. Every package built from its packaged source with dirty inputs disallowed; all archives carry that exact clean Git SHA, and 1,319 non-generated payloads match committed blobs with no unexpected/mismatched files. TUI is **9,431,125 bytes / 8.994222 MiB** (956 files), below the 10,485,760-byte cap, with no installed Node dependency payload. All29 pass; no Codewhale crate was uploaded. The preceding7bf pass and its29 archives are retained as historical evidence.

The audit also found and fixed two preflight defects in [2750a5d124](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/2750a5d124): Cargo’s separate build directory was being ignored, so the checker measured stale target-directory archives, and four ignored installed Node dependency files entered the TUI tarball. The checker now selects the active build directory, and the manifest explicitly excludes those installed dependencies. The frozen vendored `codewhale-ratatui` 0.1.2 dependency was [published with founder approval](https://crates.io/crates/codewhale-ratatui/0.1.2) and its downloaded bytes match the verified dry-run package.

This establishes candidate packaging readiness, with final-main freeze, RC/dist acceptance and actual all-29 registry/install readback still required before closing this issue. It does not repair or relabel the historical 0.10.1 packages. The original failure record follows.

Founder followup2026-10-09: Cargo should be0.10.1 and updatewinget. Fresh cache-busted registryreadback verifies26/28 packages published0.10.1; TUI+CLI still0.10.0. Independently rehashed frozenfead51ee TUIcrate is12,504,591bytes SHA2560dc03f1fa6d2dd977477051745dca2770bc8c2ea1ac2e1b796f8187391edefd6, exceeding10MiB and matching recordedHTTP413; CLI depends onTUI. Current0.10.2 contains packagingtrim+beforefirstuploadsizeguard, but it doesnot fill0.10.1 retroactively. No tags changed and no packages published inthisfollowup. Missing stableTUI/CLI publication needs historical packaging/provenance resolution; do not relabel dirty0.10.2as0.10.1. All29 0.10.2 tarballs+actualregistry/installreadback remain releaseacceptance gates. Winget0.10.1 alreadyexists in microsoft/winget-pkgs#448554 at1aaee6b99689: hashes/manifest/schema/scanpass, installationNEUTRAL/Validation-Executable-Error andMicrosoftreviewrequired. Parenthas noMicrosoftmergeauthority; no duplicatesubmission/comments. Verified3-manifest/x64binarypacket andCargo sourceevidence: artifacts/packaging-repair-20261009/winget-0.10.1/EVIDENCE.md. Rootowns publicationreconciliation and claims existingissue ratherthannewqueue.

**What happened (2026-10-08, v0.10.1).** The [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) publish uploaded 26 of 28 crates and then failed:

```
error: failed to publish codewhale-tui v0.10.1 to registry at https://crates.io
Caused by: the remote server responded with an error (status 413 Payload Too Large): max upload size is: 10485760
```

The packaged tarball was 11.9 MiB compressed ("Packaged 1796 files, 53.9MiB (11.9MiB compressed)"). 0.10.0 was 8.94 MiB, so the crate crossed the 10 MiB cap in one cycle. `codewhale-tui` and its dependent `codewhale-cli` never reached [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) for 0.10.1; The missing TUI/CLI versions leave the older published CLI available until a complete later release is published; 0.10.2 has not shipped yet.

**Why the existing gates did not catch it.** `cargo publish --dry-run` cannot see the limit — it is enforced server-side, and the dry run passed cleanly. The 413 surfaces only during the real upload, after all 28 crates have been packaged and verified (\~40 minutes in), which is also where it strands the release half-published.

**Proposal.** After the preflight packaging (the dry run already writes every `target/package/<crate>-<version>.crate`), stat each tarball and fail before any upload when one exceeds 10,485,760 bytes compressed, naming the crate and pointing at `exclude`/`include` in its `Cargo.toml`. A warning threshold around 9.5 MiB would give notice as a crate grows toward the cap.

0.10.2 already carries the content fix for `codewhale-tui`: `exclude` in `crates/tui/Cargo.toml` trims test sources from the published package (1796 → 1176 files; 11.9 → 9.5 MiB compressed, verified with `publish-crates.sh dry-run`).

**Receipts.** Publish log lines quoted above; `scripts/release/check-published.sh 0.10.1` lists `codewhale-tui`/`codewhale-cli` as not published; [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) size history for `codewhale-tui`: 8.42 MiB (0.9.13) → 8.94 MiB (0.10.0) → 11.9 MiB (0.10.1, refused).

issues.title: Saved DeepSeek key reads back as missing while DeepSeek is not the active provider (root vs [providers.deepseek] auth_mode marker mismatch)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

After saving a DeepSeek API key, an engine restart keeps reporting DeepSeek's credential as missing as long as another provider is active (e.g. zai). The key is present in the durable secret store but is never read for a non-active DeepSeek route.

Root cause: DeepSeek's save path writes the api-key marker at the ROOT of config.toml only, while the non-active-provider read gate only probes the durable secret store when that provider's own [providers.<name>] table carries auth_mode = 'api_key'. The marker the save writes is not the marker the read checks.

Observed home (macOS):
- ~/.codewhale/secrets/secrets.json holds the deepseek slot.
- ~/.codewhale/config.toml has root auth_mode = 'api_key' and [providers.deepseek] model = '...', but no [providers.deepseek] auth_mode.
- the active provider is zai.
Result: the provider picker / GET /v1/providers reports DeepSeek as missing on every restart.

Code pointers:
- crates/tui/src/config.rs save_api_key_for_identity: for Deepseek returns save_api_key() (~L12062).
- save_api_key() -> save_root_api_key_for_secret_slot(key, 'deepseek', 'deepseek') (~L11443).
- save_root_api_key_metadata_without_plaintext writes only root auth_mode, never [providers.deepseek] auth_mode (~L11546-L11566).
- Every other provider goes through codewhale_config::credentials::prepare_provider_api_key_metadata (crates/config/src/credentials.rs), which sets the per-table auth_mode.
- Non-active read gate: secret_slot_save_marker_on_shared_slot (crates/tui/src/config.rs ~L12572) checks provider_config_for(..).auth_mode, consumed by crates/tui/src/config/credential_resolve.rs (~L262-L292). A test already pins this asymmetry: crates/tui/src/config/tests.rs picker_and_request_path_disagree_when_the_secret_slot_marker_is_missing (~L15618).

Workaround: add auth_mode = 'api_key' under [providers.deepseek], or re-save the key while DeepSeek is the active provider.

Suggested fix: in save_root_api_key_metadata_without_plaintext also set ['providers', table, 'auth_mode'] = 'api_key', so DeepSeek writes the same marker prepare_provider_api_key_metadata writes for every other provider.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Make a non-DeepSeek provider active (e.g. zai) and leave DEEPSEEK_API_KEY unset.
2. Save a DeepSeek key via the provider picker / onboarding (path: save_api_key() -> save_root_api_key_for_secret_slot(.., 'deepseek', ..)).
3. Inspect ~/.codewhale/config.toml: root auth_mode = 'api_key' is set and the deepseek slot is present in ~/.codewhale/secrets/secrets.json, but [providers.deepseek] has no auth_mode.
4. Restart the engine (or the host app) and open the provider picker, or call GET /v1/providers.
5. DeepSeek is reported as missing key, even though making DeepSeek active resolves the saved slot fine.

### Codewhale version 版本

0.10.2 (built from a git checkout)

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

macOS

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

Built from a git checkout

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

deepseek / deepseek-flash

### Terminal and shell 终端

_No response_

### codewhale doctor (optional)

```text

```

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Hit from the VS Code extension (CodeWhale-VSCode), which launches the engine as a backend, but the root cause is engine-side only. No secrets are included; only the config shape and code pointers.

issues.title: Release: check the Windows import floor before shipping (Windows 10 1607 regression guard)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: packaging
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

labels.name: ci
labels.description: CI, test harness and build infrastructure

labels.name: windows
labels.description: Windows-specific behaviour

issues.body:
Follow-up from #6953. v0.10.1 failed to start on Windows 10 1607: an unresolved load-time import of `DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName` gave 0xC0000139. 830b86fddd fixes that import, but nothing stops the next release from adding a load-time import that the oldest supported Windows lacks.

**Proposal.** During the release build, list the import table of each Windows binary (for example with `dumpbin /imports`, or a small PE parser on the hosted runner). Then check each imported function against the floor for the oldest supported build, Windows 10 1607. Fail the release dry run on any import above the floor that is not delay-loaded or resolved at run time.

## Done when

- A release-time check runs on the Windows artifacts and fails on an import above the floor.
- The floor is written down in the release docs.

Refs #6953

issues.title: A saved session document larger than 8 MiB can no longer be resumed or forked, and the refusal names no remedy — the journal is what pushes it over

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed for: `"transport bound"`, `"exceeds full-history"`,
session document size limit, resume + size, journal + resume. Closest matches:

- **#6842** (open) — the session journal has no bound and grows without limit.
  That is the growth side of the same structure; this report is the *access*
  side: once the file crosses a hard 8 MiB transport bound, the session can no
  longer be opened at all.
- **#6688** (closed) — same class (an oversized input is refused before anything
  runs), different path (`exec` argv vs the session document).
- #6161, #6175, #6361 — unrelated changes that only matched the search terms.

# What happened?

```
$ codewhale resume 481c2659-…
error: selected saved history could not be captured; no mutation attempted
  caused by: session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained
```

The source is retained (good), but there is no way forward. `codewhale fork`
refuses the same way, and I could not find any CLI path that reduces a saved
document: `codewhale --help` lists no prune/compact command, and `codewhale thread`
offers only list/read/resume/fork/archive/set-name/clear-name. The message does
not name the size, the field that dominates it, or any remedy.

Measured on the affected session (the file is 13 982 336 bytes against an 8 MiB
bound, i.e. 8 388 608 bytes):

| part of the document | size (approx, as serialized in the file) |
|---|---|
| whole file | 13.98 MB |
| `journal.entries` (3870 entries) | 8.96 MB |
| `messages` (1361 messages) | 2.96 MB |
| `work_state` / `metadata` | 0.38 MB / 0.13 MB |

The conversation itself is well inside the bound. Only the 1361 journal entries
on the active leaf path are projected into messages
(`crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs:262`, `:329`); the remaining 2509 entries
are abandoned branches — yet the whole document has to fit.

# Steps to reproduce

The check is a plain file-size comparison, so any saved document over the bound
reproduces it deterministically; I did not build a synthetic one, my numbers are
from a real session (a long session with heavy sub-agent use, which is what grows
the journal — see #6842).

1. `stat -c%s ~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json` — compare against 8 388 608.
2. `codewhale resume <id>` (and `codewhale fork <id>`) → the error above.

Code path, read from `main`:

- `prepare_mounted_session` reads the source with
  `load_session_snapshot_bounded(&id, MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES)`
  (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs:9943`). Every `codewhale resume` goes through this
  (`run_interactive_with_notice`).
- The read refuses before parsing when the *file* is larger than the limit:
  `crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs:3406`
  ("session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained").
- `MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`
  (`crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:79`; the entry-count sibling is at `:78`).
- The same constant bounds the serialized mutation request, which embeds the
  whole document as JSON: `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:221` —
  so raising only the read would not be enough; the transport itself is bounded.

Recovery that worked by hand (and is what a supported path would need to do):
keeping only the active leaf path in `journal.entries` took the file from
13.98 MB to 7.61 MB and the session resumed. It costs the abandoned branches'
structure (`/branch` history), which is why it should be an explicit,
maintainer-designed operation rather than a user's manual surgery. The same
operation is not the only lever — any bound change has to keep the request under
the same limit, because the document travels inside it.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
today (`MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES` is unchanged).

# Where did it happen?

- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Impact: the session is readable in files but unreachable from the product; the
only routes left are manual surgery on the JSON or discarding the session.

Options as I see them (maintainer's call):

- **A. Transport only what the operation needs.** The canonical handoff needs
  the messages, the journal witness (leaf + entry count) and the metadata; the
  journal body is copied only because the target document is the source document.
  A host-side rebuild of the target document would remove the journal from the
  payload entirely.
- **B. Make the bound count the projected history, not the file**, or expose it
  as a bounded, documented knob. `messages` here was 2.96 MB of a 13.98 MB file.
- **C. Keep the bound and make the failure actionable**: name the size and the
  dominant field, and provide a supported prune/compact command that drops
  journal entries outside the active path (with a dry run and a backup), so an
  oversized session is recoverable. Also worth a pointer to #6842.

Open questions: is 8 MiB a memory/allocation guard or an API payload guard? Should
a journal that is not projected into messages count against it at all? What is a
user expected to do today when a session crosses it — is discarding the session
the intended outcome?

Verification (for A/B/C, once the direction is chosen):

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs
```

Out of scope:

- Bounding the journal itself (#6842).
- Changing the conversation, or auto-truncating history on resume.

issues.title: Windows runtime floor blocks read-only piped commands under Full Access, on a native (non-npm) install

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

labels.name: windows
labels.description: Windows-specific behaviour

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

## Summary

Follow-up to #6827. The Windows runtime floor (`SessionRuntimeRisk`, `crates/tui/src/core/authority/auto_review.rs`) refuses ordinary read-only commands that pipe test output, with `UnclassifiedWindowsInvocation`. It does this while the session shows **Full Access**, although the floor's own test says Full Access skips it.

Refused:

```
cd C:\Users\me\repo; .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests\runner -q --tb=line 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 6
cd C:\Users\me\repo\apps\extension; node .\node_modules\vitest\vitest.mjs run 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 30
cd C:\Users\me\repo; .\.venv\Scripts\ruff.exe format .; Write-Output "fmt=$LASTEXITCODE"; .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests\e2e --collect-only -q 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 3
```

Every refusal reads:

> Built-in safety gate requires approval: Windows command input cannot be classified safely enough to exclude termination of Codewhale npm launchers; use a direct PID- or port-specific command.

The same commands without `2>&1 | Select-Object ...` run fine. None of them stops a process.

## Two problems

1. **Full Access does not skip the floor.** `windows_runtime_floor_holds_across_reviewing_postures_but_skips_full_access` (around line 2104) asserts that under `ApprovalMode::Bypass` "Full Access skips the platform hold with the rest of the floor". The TUI status bar shows `Full Access` and `operate`, and the operator and its Fleet sub-agents are still blocked. Either the operate/Fleet posture does not carry `Bypass` into tool review, or sub-agents get a different `ApprovalMode`.
2. **Unparseable means blocked, even for read-only pipelines.** When `command_invocations(command)` returns `None`, `windows_session_runtime_risk_scoped` returns `UnclassifiedWindowsInvocation` (around line 1371). A pipeline into a read-only cmdlet (`Select-Object`, `Select-String`, `Where-Object`, `Format-*`, `Out-String`, `Measure-Object`) with `2>&1` cannot terminate anything, but it is held. Agents use this pattern constantly to trim test output.

3. **The npm-launcher hold fires on a non-npm install.** This machine uses the native installer, so there is no `node.exe` launcher in Codewhale's process tree. Yet the hold's reason is "termination of Codewhale npm launchers". `windows_tool_runtime_risk` does not check the install method, so the floor applies to every Windows install. #6906 already detects npm installs with `codewhale_release::current_install_method()`, and the same check could scope this hold. (A broad `node.exe` kill could still hit *another* npm-launched session on the same machine. That is a narrower risk, and it does not apply to read-only pipelines either way.)

## Impact

In one Fleet run of about 70 minutes (DeepSeek V4 Flash, about 8 workers), one implement sub-agent had 12 refused or failed tool calls out of about 60. 4 were this gate; each refusal costs a model turn while the agent re-plans. The operator hit it repeatedly as well. It is avoidable: the agent can drop the pipe. But every model reaches for this pattern first, so it fails again and again.

## Expected

- Under Full Access, the floor does not apply, as the existing test asserts. Or, if the floor is meant to apply under Full Access in operate/Fleet mode, the test and the docs should say so.
- A pipeline whose stages are all known read-only cmdlets, with stream redirection like `2>&1`, is classified as non-terminating rather than unclassified.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Windows 11, Codewhale from the native Windows installer (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CodeWhale\bin\codewhale.exe`, launched through `codewhale.bat`; **not** npm), started from PowerShell in Windows Terminal.
2. Select Full Access and run in operate mode, with Fleet sub-agents.
3. Have the agent run: `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 5` (any command, piped into `Select-Object`).
4. It is refused with the message above. Without `2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 5`, it runs.

### Codewhale version 版本

codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f)

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

Windows

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

GitHub Releases download (native Windows installer)

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

deepseek / deepseek-v4-flash

### Terminal and shell 终端

Windows Terminal + PowerShell 5.1

### codewhale doctor (optional)

_No response_

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

- Evidence: `.codewhale/state/subagents.v1.json`, worker events marked `refused or failed`, and checkpoint tool results carrying the safety-gate text.
- Related: #6827 (the original gate), #6906 (agent environment line for the npm launcher), #6011 (tool-call error diagnostics).

The installed Engine can retain a dead local owner publication and refuse the next native-app startup, leaving the app offline until an operator repairs task-owned metadata. issues.title: Windows 10 1607: v0.10.1 fails to start — unresolved load-time import DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName (0xC0000139)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

After updating from v0.10.0 to v0.10.1 on a Windows 10 Pro 1607 (build 14393.447) machine, the app no longer starts. Before anything runs, Windows shows the loader dialog:

```text
无法定位程序输入点 DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName 于动态链接库 …
(EN: The procedure entry point DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName could not be located in the dynamic link library …)
```

and the process exits with 0xC0000139 (STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND) — no stdout, no logs. v0.10.0 (official asset, same machine) starts fine and prints `codewhale 0.10.0 (1be1a703b975)`.

Root cause: the v0.10.1 executable has exactly one load-time import this Windows build cannot resolve — `api-ms-win-security-base-l1-2-2.dll!DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName` (that API set forwards to KERNELBASE.dll; on this build, KERNELBASE/kernel32/userenv and the security API sets do not export the function). Because it is a static, non-delayed import, the loader fails before `main` — regardless of the fact that the only consumer (the extension-host LPAC sandbox, `crates/tui/src/extension_host/windows.rs`, the `registryRead` capability SID derivation from the 0.10.1 LPAC work `af5fa5c23` / `935c08662`) is experimental and off by default (`extension_host = false`).

Import-surface audit of the two official Windows binaries (every imported (dll, function) pair checked with GetProcAddress on this 1607 system):

- v0.10.0 — 411 imports / 29 DLLs — 0 unresolved
- v0.10.1 — 454 imports / 31 DLLs — 1 unresolved (the symbol above); nothing else is missing, and no OS-version gate or PE-header OS-version bump was introduced

The current `main` still contains the same call, so any 0.10.2-line build will fail the same way on this OS.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. On Windows 10, version 1607 (build 14393), take the official v0.10.1 asset `codewhale-windows-x64.exe` (sha256 `76a6156b…d22729`, matching the release's `codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt`).
2. Run `codewhale.exe --version` (or the `.bat` launcher).
3. The loader dialog appears and the process exits with `0xC0000139`; no output. For contrast, the v0.10.0 asset on the same machine prints `codewhale 0.10.0 (1be1a703b975)` and exits 0.

### Codewhale version 版本

0.10.0

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

Windows

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

GitHub Releases download

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

_No response_

### Terminal and shell 终端

_No response_

### codewhale doctor (optional)

```text

```

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

## Proposed solution

Requirement-level scope (implementation follows the project's own conventions; no specific files or code are prescribed):

1. The `registryRead` capability SID does not have to come from that API — it is a stable, deterministic value that can be checked against the OS API on any Windows runner that has it. The sandbox can obtain it without a static import from a module that older Windows builds do not provide (runtime resolution, or obtaining the value another way — the project's call).
2. On builds without the capability API, refuse Native-host activation with a clear, feature-scoped error (consistent with the documented macOS/Linux "otherwise activation is refused" behavior) instead of failing the whole process at startup.
3. Keep LPAC behavior and the token checks unchanged on Windows versions that support them today.
4. Consider documenting the oldest supported Windows build and keeping release binaries within it, with a release-time check that every import resolves on that floor — this class of regression would then be caught before shipping.

issues.title: Deferred-toolbox eviction is economically net-negative under provider prompt caching: full-prefix re-prefill + write premiums, permanent stale recovery notes, wire-byte-blind budget

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### What happened? 发生了什么？

The bounded deferred-tool toolbox (`ToolActivationCache`, 8 names / 16 KiB, `crates/tui/src/core/session.rs:17-19` at HEAD `008d21d69`) is **cost-blind**, and under current provider prompt-cache pricing its eviction path is economically net-negative. Concretely:

**1. Eviction invalidates the entire downstream prefix — the one toolbox operation with no offsetting benefit.**
The prefix fingerprint is `SHA256(system) + SHA256(tools wire array)` with order load-bearing (`crates/tui/src/prefix_cache.rs`), and tools sit at the front of the rendered prompt on every provider. Any admission/eviction mutates the tools array, so system + tools + the **entire conversation history** re-prefills at miss price. `docs/CACHE.md` calls this "an expected, one-request miss" (lines 39-40) — wording written when cache writes were free:

| Provider/API | Cached-input read | Write premium | Tool-change invalidation |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat/Responses | 0.1x | 1.25x (GPT-5.6+) | prefix from that point (tools are first) |
| Anthropic Messages | 0.1x | 1.25x (5m) / 2x (1h) | **any tool change invalidates the entire cache** (tools are block 1) |
| DeepSeek | 1/30 – 1/50 | none | prefix-based |
| Moonshot Kimi k3 | 0.1x | 1x (5m) / 2x (1h) | prefix from that point |

Break-even for evicting one ~400-token schema from a session with H tokens of history: pay ≈ 0.9–2.25 × H once, save ≈ 0.9 × 400 per later request → needs ~75 further tool-free requests at H = 30K. Real conversations run 6–40 requests. Admission at least unlocks a needed capability; **eviction only pays when the session is about to end anyway**. LRU position alone is the eviction trigger today — no hysteresis, no cost term, and two alternating overflowing searches would re-prefill the full prefix every round.

**2. The eviction→recovery cycle multiplies the loss (relevant to the in-flight reporting work).**
Reporting evictions (as the Pinvou fork's open PR #101 does) is necessary for correctness — silent eviction caused a live incident where a model fabricated tool results for tools that had vanished from its `<functions>`. But the recovery contract ("re-search to re-activate") completes a cycle whose full cost stack, for one eviction of 4 browser tools (~460 tokens of schema) in a 30K-token history with 20 requests remaining (0.1x reads, 1.25x writes):

| # | Cost item | Tok-eq |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Eviction invalidation (re-prefill + write premium) | ~34,500 |
| 2 | Eviction note in history (≈72–147 tokens/event; rides the result forever; 1 + 19×0.1x) | ~427 |
| 3 | Recovery re-search round trip | ~3,050 |
| 4 | Search-result payload becomes history | ~1,160 |
| 5 | Re-activation invalidation (tools array changes again — second re-prefill + write) | ~34,500 |
| | **Total vs never evicting** | **≈ 73,600 (~2.5× the entire history)** |

Two structural gaps in the reporting design: (a) **notes are never retracted** — ride-time netting (`render_toolbox_eviction_notes`) only trims the note at the moment it attaches to a result; once in history it is permanent, and the only "compaction" that removes it is generic conversation compaction; (b) **re-activation carries no supersession marker** — the re-admitting search result is byte-identical to a first-time hit (`tool_references` list only), so after recovery the model's history permanently contains "these tools are no longer callable" next to a tools array that has them again. (Compare: the direct-call hydration path does emit an explicit "was deferred and has now been loaded" receipt.)

**3. The headline saving is first-turn-only, and the budget does not measure wire bytes.**
The historical justification ("reduce catalog tokens 73%") measures a first-request, native-tools-only, `bytes/4`-estimated ratio — no provider, no tokenizer, no MCP, caching never modeled. Under caching, both an eager stable header and the deferred header are hit-priced after request 1; the durable steady-state saving is ~0.1x-scale. Separately, the 16 KiB toolbox budget is measured in engine-side serde bytes (`ToolActivationCache::serialized_bytes`), while the same tool serializes differently per wire family (Chat Completions wrapper ~69 B/tool, Anthropic ~40 B, Responses ~71 B) and per-provider sanitizers (Moonshot MFJS, root-level `oneOf/anyOf` flattening) change schemas further — so the budget is a proxy that matches no provider's actual token accounting.

**4. In practice the mechanism survives by accident.**
Across five real sessions on k3/DeepSeek (93–94% hit ratios with heavy `tool_search` churn vs 92.5% baseline without), activation happened at request 1 (short history) and the surface then stayed stable within turns. The measured re-prefill drivers were skill loading and engine restarts — not tool_search. The one live failure (mid-task silent eviction) is exactly the case with no offsetting saving.

### Expected 期望

Surface-change decisions — especially LRU eviction — should be cost-aware or at least cost-attributed, and the eviction-recovery loop should not leave permanent stale statements in history:

1. **Hysteresis / eviction economics**: a minimum activation lifetime, or an eviction cost term once current re-prefill size exceeds a few multiples of the evicted schema. Pure LRU position makes mid-task eviction the default worst case.
2. **Update `docs/CACHE.md`**'s "expected, one-request miss" for the write-premium era, and reconcile observed `cache_hit_tokens`/`cache_miss_tokens` against declared `change:<what>` re-pins — today telemetry and decisions never meet (`calculate_cache_savings` is `#[cfg(test)]`-only).
3. **Supersession semantics for recovery**: when a reported-evicted tool is re-activated, emit an explicit restored/re-admitted marker (hydration-receipt style) so the history's "no longer callable" note is not left as the last word; consider bounding note persistence (e.g. drop after the next successful activation of the named tools, or fold into compaction).
4. **Evaluate append-in-context injection** for dynamic tools (Moonshot's documented pattern: keep the top-level `tools` array stable, append dynamic declarations as a trailing system message inside `messages`) — zero prefix invalidation by construction, which sidesteps items 1 and 5 of the cost stack entirely.
5. **Measure the toolbox budget in wire-shaped bytes** (or tokenizer tokens) per active wire format rather than engine serde bytes.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Economic issue rather than a crash; the observable sequence:

1. Start a conversation that activates ≥8 deferred tools (e.g. a browser task: `tool_search` for browser tools, then a second search for page-management tools).
2. Observe the second search silently evicting earlier activations from the request tools array (no model-visible signal at HEAD `008d21d69` — `delta.evicted` is consumed by `remove_evicted_cache_activations` in `execute_tool_search_inner`, `tool_catalog.rs:1546-1551`).
3. Watch `/cache stats` + provider usage: the next request reports a miss covering the full history; on Anthropic routes the write premium applies; re-searching to recover triggers a second full miss + write.
4. Cross-check the arithmetic against `calculate_turn_cost_from_usage_with_prision`-billed totals for the session.

### Codewhale version 版本

`008d21d69` (workspace 0.10.2; latest tag v0.10.1) — verified at this HEAD on 2026-10-13; the mechanism is unchanged from v0.9.12 through HEAD. Observed live via the Pinvou downstream (fork pinned at v0.9.12 + maintenance), engine-level, platform-independent.

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

Engine — affects all surfaces (TUI / CLI / Desktop / Web) and all providers with prefix caching, which in 2026 is all of them.

### Before you start 前置确认

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。（recent 100 issues swept for tool/cache/deferred/eviction — no overlap）

> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
Timed-out or dropped children are not killed or reaped (`kill_on_drop`/process-group), descendants survive shutdown, and a restart can overlap a surviving worker. A dropped future, an early error return, or a stop request can leave the child and its grandchildren running; the replacement then races the survivor over the same state. Windows adds process-group and reaping wrinkles where a plain kill is not enough. Adopt one containment policy: process group, kill-on-drop, explicit reap, and verified teardown before replacement.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **9** (reassessed severity noted per line).

## Scope / Plan
1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. Adopt one process-containment policy: process group, kill-on-drop, explicit reap, and verified teardown before replacement.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

## Key files
- `crates/app-server/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/tui/plugins/computer-use/src/browser-cdp.mjs`
- `crates/tui/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tools/verifier.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/work_graph/runtime.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs`
- `crates/mcp/src/stdio_client.rs`
- `crates/lane/src/runtime.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every listed candidate is either fixed with a test, or downgraded with a written reason in the PR.
- [ ] No new instance of this class is introduced (guarded by the test/budget).
- [ ] Existing behavior for unrelated paths is unchanged.

## Verification
```sh
cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-app-server -p codewhale-lane -p codewhale-mcp
cargo test  -p codewhale-tui --lib
cargo test  -p codewhale-mcp -p codewhale-lane
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
```

## Out of scope
- Findings that belong to another systemic class or to the localized backlog.
- Re-architecture beyond the listed sites.

## Related existing work (do not duplicate)
#4864/#4868 (resource admission + kill descendant groups), #6169 (job-control handshake), #3958, #4547, #1475

## Candidate findings (9)
- [ ] **CU01-08** · CU01 — Computer-use · `crates/tui/plugins/computer-use/src/browser-cdp.mjs:151` — unanswered CDP command hangs forever and blocks kill/release.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: high_
- [ ] **T01-11** · T01 — TUI entry, process lifecycle, support · `crates/tui/src/lib.rs:10541` — unbounded child pipes, incomplete process-group cleanup and Windows `cmd /C start` URL injection.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **R03-05** · R03 — Agent, app-server, models, protocol, state, shared tools · `crates/app-server/src/lib.rs:1762` — POST retry without operation_key, response_end before stream error, duplicate/orphan turn.

- [ ] **D04-04** · D04 — Registry, tasks, workflow, verifier · `crates/tui/src/tools/verifier.rs:378` — foreground gate unbounded output and does not reap/kill child on cancellation.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **F02-11** · F02 — Skills, hooks, LSP, snapshots, REPL, RLM, work graph · `crates/tui/src/work_graph/runtime.rs:1070` — plan/todo replacement leaves live orphan nodes selectable as parents.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **U02-02** · U02 — Event loop, dispatch/apply · `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:2030` — empty/control-only deltas bypass `events_drained`, loop can spin forever.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **R04-09** · R04 — Exec-policy, secrets, MCP, hooks, shared contracts · `crates/mcp/src/stdio_client.rs:967` — Signal after reap/PID reuse and unjoined detached reaper can kill/retain wrong processes.

> Source: static audit of `main@384439634`. Candidates are static and not reproduced — confirm each before changing code.
> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
State, session, ledger, goal, and job records are written with non-unique temp names, without fsync, or as multi-step commits. A crash, power loss, or a second writer can then leave a truncated file or a half-applied batch that later code reads as valid — losing claims, decisions, or session history, or reviving deleted records. The fix is one atomic durable-write contract per record set: unique temp name, fsync, rename, and batch/transaction semantics for multi-file commits. Non-atomic Windows replacement and mirror-write ordering belong to the same contract.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **8** (reassessed severity noted per line).

## Scope / Plan
1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. One owner for atomic durable writes: unique temp file, fsync, rename, and batch/transaction semantics per record set.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: reliability
