issues.body:
Hi — Brian from AICraft (the AICraft row in `docs/PROVIDERS.md`). Not asking for anything. Three things we ran into while running the endpoint, all measured on our own traffic. Take whatever's useful.

## 1. A cold model looks broken

First call to a cold model, across three different models: 145s, 105s, 91s. The same three calls once warm: 2s, 0.5s, 0.5s. With the catalog pre-warmed, a full sweep is about 25s.

The gap between those two sets of numbers is what makes this worth writing down. The latency is per-model and it disappears after the first call. Nothing is wrong with the model; it has not been loaded yet.

A client timing out at 60s will report those models as unavailable, and the report will be wrong. Our first probe did exactly that, and we read it as 23 broken models. Raising the probe timeout to 180s or more, and sending one cheap call per model when a provider is selected, removes the problem.

## 2. Listed and callable are two different states

Two entries in our catalog were enabled and visible to users. Every call to them returned 502 for several days. Not intermittently — every call.

Two things made that hard to see. Upstream's message was "resources busy" every time, which reads like a temporary condition; it isn't, when it is the same message on every attempt, because a genuinely busy upstream returns successes in between. And the error text our gateway passed to clients was a generic placeholder, with the original only in the container logs, so from the client side there was nothing to diagnose.

Whether this is fixed on the provider side or the client side, the useful distinction is the same: an entry that is listed is not an entry that works. Only offer one after a probe has succeeded, and drop it if the probe keeps failing.

## 3. A truncated response can report success

We asked for a long code generation with `max_tokens: 16000`. It came back cut off halfway through a file, and `finish_reason` said `stop`, not `length`. Of the 16000 tokens, about 10,900 were reasoning and about 5,100 were output. Raising the cap to 64000 changed nothing.

The same mechanism shows up wherever a reasoning model is used for something small. We had an inline classification step configured at `max_tokens: 50`; reasoning consumed the budget, the content came back empty, and the step degraded quietly instead of failing.

In both cases the response is well-formed and the terminal frame is valid. Only the arithmetic disagrees. A genuine `stop` leaves the budget unfilled, so if `completion_tokens` equals the `max_tokens` that was requested, the response was cut at the ceiling. Retrying does not help, because the same prompt stops at the same token count; that is what distinguishes it from a 502 or a timeout, which are worth retrying.

This is the one of the three with a client-side half, and while writing this I went looking for it in your tree. What I found instead was the two other halves already handled: `error_taxonomy.rs` separates a permission failure from a server error rather than collapsing both into something retryable, and the retry state is keyed per provider, so one route's 429 doesn't stall another. But in the streaming path I could not find anything that compares the reported `completion_tokens` against the ceiling the request asked for, and `finish_reason` is checked only for being non-empty. That is the right test for whether a stream ended cleanly, and the wrong one for whether the model finished its answer. `tools/truncate.rs` shows you already have the instinct for this on tool results — it stamps `truncated: true` and names a recovery route — and the same treatment doesn't reach a turn the model stopped short.

If that distinction is deliberate, ignore this part; I only had the source to go on.

issues.title: codewhale resume refuses any session whose saved history still holds a raw sub-agent handoff — the canonical acknowledgement compares the Engine-restored messages with the saved document

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed in this repository: `"mailbox acknowledgement"` → 0,
`"selected saved history"` → 0, `"exceeds full-history"` → 0, `"retained outcome"`
→ 6 unrelated results (release and PR titles). Closest reports, each a different
mechanism: #6102 (closed — resume failed with ENOENT while resolving the runtime
store dir), #6225 (closed) and #6418 (closed) — older "cannot restore/resume"
reports. None of them mention this comparison.

# What happened?

`codewhale resume <id>` fails deterministically for a saved session, and no
retry or recovery route works:

```
$ codewhale resume f5ba9347-…
error: canonical history operation mounted-history:48204ec8-…; retained outcome must be recovered using this exact key
  caused by: canonical history mailbox acknowledgement changed
```

Expected: the session resumes. The suggested recovery ("retained outcome must be
recovered using this exact key") cannot succeed, because the recovery path runs
the same acknowledgement: `settle_prepared_history_operation` also calls
`synchronize_history_operation` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1032`;
the fresh path is `:1663`).

# Steps to reproduce

1. In a project, run `codewhale` and have the session spawn a sub-agent (the
   `agent` tool) so a `subagent_completion` handoff is appended to the live
   history. Let the turn end and quit.
2. Confirm the saved document still holds the RAW envelope: the message has
   exactly two text blocks, block 2 is exactly
   `<turn_meta>\nInput provenance: subagent_handoff (non-authoritative)\n</turn_meta>`
   and block 1 starts with `<codewhale:runtime_event kind="subagent_completion"
   visibility="internal">` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:15`).
3. `codewhale resume <id>` → the error above.

Observed on a 351-message, 3.97 MB session with 5 such envelopes: every attempt
failed. After neutralising the recognition of those 5 messages in the saved data
(renaming the transport tag so the restore projection becomes a no-op), the same
command resumed normally and printed `Resumed session: …`.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
(today): `synchronize_history_operation` is unchanged at
`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs`.

# Where did it happen?

- TUI (terminal interface)
- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Written from reading `main` (not a guess at the cause):

- `RuntimeThreadManager::synchronize_history_operation`
  (`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:11684`) sends `Op::SyncSession` and then
  requires `observed.messages == session.messages` (`:11708`-`:11713`), i.e. the
  Engine's post-restore messages must equal the saved document byte for byte.
- The Engine's restore first replaces every live sub-agent handoff with a
  restored checkpoint: `Engine::restore_session_history`
  (`crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs:2931`) calls
  `runtime_handoff::project_owned_messages_for_restore`
  (`:2959` → `crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:918`,
  rewrite decision in `rewrite_message_for_restore`, `:927`, recognition in
  `raw_runtime_handoff_text`, `:1042`).
- So the two sides are structurally different objects whenever the saved
  document still holds a raw envelope, and the equality can never hold. The
  document only becomes "projected" after a *successful* restore persists it,
  which is exactly the step this check forbids — the first canonical resume of a
  session that used sub-agents is the failing case.

Suggested fix directions (maintainer's call):

- **A. Make the acknowledgement projection-aware.** Compare against
  `project_owned_messages_for_restore(session.messages.clone())` (plus the
  compaction checkpoint step `compaction::restore_compaction_checkpoint`, to
  mirror `restore_session_history` exactly). The same codebase already does this
  for the sibling rollback check: `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:1406` projects
  `.messages` before demanding that the Engine acknowledged them.
- **B. Persist the projected form** so a saved document is always in the form a
  restore produces (bigger change; it would drop raw envelopes from saved
  sessions earlier than today).

Related, found while recovering this session: a refused canonical attempt still
publishes a holder thread plus an uncommitted turn operation in the Runtime
store. Once the document is repaired, the next attempt then stalls on the holder
checkpoint (`saved holder checkpoint differs from the saved history; refresh
history`, `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1255`) and, with the
checkpoint refreshed, on `saved holder has a successor outside the selected
document` (`:1281`) — the holder fingerprints the pre-repair bytes. A refused
attempt could avoid publishing a holder, or the repair path could refresh it.

Done when:

- [ ] a saved session whose history still contains a raw `subagent_completion`
      (or `subagent_failed` / `waiting_for_subagents` / `agent_topology`)
      envelope resumes through the canonical path;
- [ ] `codewhale fork` works for the same session;
- [ ] the acknowledgement still refuses a genuinely changed history (an Engine
      that did not install the document), i.e. the check is not simply removed;
- [ ] a regression test in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs` (`mod mounted_history_tests`)
      saves a fixture session containing one raw handoff envelope and asserts the
      mounted resume succeeds.

Verification:

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/lib.rs mounted_history_tests::
```

Out of scope:

- The sub-agent handoff wire format and the restore rendering itself.
- The size bound on the saved document (separate report).

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against 0.9.13 (filed 2026-09-14); idle-PTY sub-report reproduced against 0.10.0.
>
> **What remains**
> - Input attribution: add user-vs-agent origin to stdin/input on crates/tui/src/runtime_api/jobs.rs and runtime_api/terminal.rs, with permissions still enforced
> - Restart-safe identity: land the keyed job creation and Lost/Unknown projection claimed on 2026-10-07 (runtime_api/jobs.rs, runtime_threads.rs, runtime_api.rs), coordinated with #6556
> - Windows: make /v1/terminal/* exist on Windows via ConPTY and qualify PTY jobs there (terminal.rs is cfg(unix) end to end)
> - Readiness field (accepting input vs blocked) and a long-poll wake for /v1/terminal/{name}/output; one fixture proving bytes + input + resize + exit
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Terminal byte routes exist at v0.10.1: /v1/terminal/{name}/output, /input, /resize, /kill at crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:2263-2269, owned by tools::terminal_session (runtime_api/terminal.rs:1-8)
> - Client job routes exist at v0.10.1: POST/GET /v1/threads/{id}/jobs plus /output, /stdin, /kill, /resize at crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:2379-2397; documented at docs/RUNTIME_API.md:1809-1844
> - Bounded cursor read is served: cursor/next_cursor/offset/exit_code in crates/tui/src/runtime_api/jobs.rs:386-415, non-consuming multi-client reads (:420-422)
> - Idle-PTY liveness regression from 0.10.0 is fixed in v0.10.1: commit 14792c3a6e (PR #6716, merge 1cdec0f81e) is an ancestor of v0.10.1 and not of v0.10.0; crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs:1714-1720 exempts jobs with terminal_size from STALE_NO_OUTPUT_AFTER
> - Windows/ConPTY not done for the terminal routes: crates/tui/src/runtime_api/terminal.rs 'Known limitations' says 'Unix only ... on Windows these routes do not exist yet. ConPTY qualification is its own slice'
> - Reconnect across Engine restart not done: terminal.rs limitations say live sessions only, a restarted Engine reports no session; no long poll and no scrollback recovery either

---

GPUI needs a Codewhale-owned interactive terminal, not a second PTY in the desktop. Opened from [Hmbown/codewhale-platform#565](<https://github.com/Hmbown/codewhale-platform/issues/565>) so the native pane ([Hmbown/codewhale-platform#566](<https://github.com/Hmbown/codewhale-platform/issues/566>)) is not blocked on a comment.

Do not start this if a live issue already covers the HTTP terminal session. Reconcile `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs` and `crates/tui/src/tools/terminal_session.rs` against today's tip first.

## Serve

1. Stable session id that survives the client window closing; reconnect is the same process or a truthful loss (never a silent new shell).
2. Authenticated raw byte read with a bounded cursor (replay/window). Shell-tool text is not this.
3. Authenticated input with user vs agent attribution; sandbox/permissions stay enforced.
4. Resize (cols/rows) with a receipt.
5. Readiness: will accept input vs blocked.
6. Exit status + cleanup receipt; no orphaned store lock.
7. Native Windows ConPTY (Unix-only portable-pty is not acceptance).

## Reply with

Claimed files and routes, what exists vs what you will add, ConPTY status, and the smallest fixture that proves bytes + input + resize + exit.

GPUI will show “Not available from this Codewhale” plus the real route name until those routes exist. No second shell owner in the desktop.

### 2026-09-28 idle PTY liveness fix claim — Codex

Reproduced against released 0.10.0: a live client-owned PTY idle for more than 60 seconds reports status=Running, stdin_available=true, stale=true, tty=null, with terminal_size retained. This makes reconnect inventory treat a live shell as unavailable and the resize route reject it as no longer running. Source root cause: BackgroundShell::job_snapshot applies STALE_NO_OUTPUT_AFTER to interactive PTYs waiting for input. Claim exact Core paths crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs and crates/tui/src/tools/shell/tests.rs in the existing clean checkout from b36a34774. Exclude owned PTYs from the no-output staleness heuristic; preserve real process-exit and historical stale records, and non-PTY silent-job behavior. Reuse existing PTY resize/input/exit regression with an aged output clock. No transport, permission, storage or release changes. Per-OS/ConPTY qualification remains open.

### 2026-09-29 remote handoff

Saved the idle-owned-PTY repair to branch fix/idle-terminal-liveness, commit 14792c3a6e, draft PR [Hmbown/Codewhale#6716](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6716>). Exact source scope: crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs and crates/tui/src/tools/shell/tests.rs. Required npm test && npm run check:web passed: 68 package, 16 runtime SDK, 50 extension-host and 502 web tests (636 passed / 0 failed); type/lint/build, formatting and diff checks passed. Released 0.10.0 reproduced the 65-second idle failure. The first focused Rust compilation was interrupted without a result; a resumed five-filter run is still compiling at handoff. No Rust pass, updated Engine runtime result, release or Windows/ConPTY qualification is claimed. Keep draft unmerged until relevant Rust checks and exact-head CI pass. Full targeted command is in the PR body. Broader issue acceptance remains open.

### 2026-09-29 focused Rust verification of [Hmbown/Codewhale#6716](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6716>) — Claude (app stabilization session)

Exact head `14792c3a6eeede15d4248b41b244747d463de496`, Linux x86_64 cloud container, rustc 1.94.1 (the Core `stable` toolchain present there): `cargo test --locked -p codewhale-tui --lib -- tools::shell::tests::pty_resize_updates_live_terminal_and_rejects_finished_or_pipe_jobs tools::shell::tests::running_job_snapshot_marks_no_output_stale_after_threshold tools::shell::tests::test_job_list_poll_cancel_and_stale_snapshot --exact` → **3 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored, 13,804 filtered out**. That covers the extended real-PTY regression (the idle PTY stays non-stale, then resize/input) and both existing stale-job tests (silent non-PTY jobs still go stale). The first attempt was OOM-killed while the app built alongside it; this re-run is a clean, isolated result. prs.title: refactor(commands): adopt portable config shapes for the complete config group (FEAT-028)
prs.body:
## Summary

Refs #5316

This is a large, behavior-preserving refactor: remove the `config` Slash Command Group's concrete `App`/TUI dependencies and replace them with **Shapes** connections. The PR is large because the existing Slash Command Group is large—that is how it was designed. No product-behavior change is intended.

The migration covers all 19 current registrations, including upstream's `/connect` and `/disconnect`. The physical crate move remains separate work.

## What changed

- Portable command contracts, narrow facets, capability declarations and shared actions replace direct App/TUI dependencies.
- Parsing and command rendering live in the portable group; adapters retain concrete observation, persistence and host effects.
- Typed settings/audit/subagent reports and import outcomes cross the boundary.
- Prepared templates validate message contracts; malformed replies fail without a successful action. Host-contract violations remain explicitly outside the prepared-message guarantee.
- The proof compiles the actual group root as an independent library; the migration frontier becomes `["core"]`.
- Upstream behavior retained includes plugin-provider connect/disconnect, pet style/language, localized Work/Full Access receipts and legacy sandbox-token cleanup.

## Current status: draft — CI repair

At the owner's request this PR remains **draft** while CI is verified.

Head `599119aa5` fixes the five failures reported on `593d7d717` by both the [macOS job](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38441020291/job/115447780813) and the [Linux job](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38441020291/job/115447780694):

- `/mode` metadata now shares the handler's Work-mode usage, restoring help filtering.
- `/login` again directs plugin-provider sign-in to `/connect`.
- The migrated-command test inventory includes `/connect` and `/disconnect`.
- The moved YOLO test expects upstream's Full Access (Work) receipt, retaining all permission/state assertions.

These were real reconciliation defects, not unrelated upstream failures. Earlier broad local verification did not establish that those fixes were present in the pushed tree; this follow-up records the committed repair explicitly.

prs.title: test(sessions): the picker search check no longer depends on the temp directory's name
prs.body:
## What and why

`session_control_acceptance::tests::tui_and_api_listings_agree` fails now and then on my Mac:

```
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: ["charlie", "bravo", "alpha"]
 right: ["bravo"]
```

The test saves its sessions with a workspace under `TempDir`, searches for `brav` and expects only `bravo`. The matcher looks at `title id workspace` and falls back to a subsequence match, so the random `.tmpXXXXXX` part of the path can supply the missing letters. When it does, every session in that workspace matches.

How often depends on the machine's temp path. On my Mac the per-user part of the path already contains `b…r`, so the random part only needs `a…v`: about 1 run in 70 by simulation. Under `/tmp` it is about 1 in 57,000, which is why CI doesn't show it. With `TMPDIR` pointing at a directory named `brav` it fails every time.

`search_sort_and_preview_are_one_projection` in the same file already avoids this, and its comment says why: it pins all three haystack fields. This test now records `/repo` and `/other` as the workspaces, the same way. The session store stays in the private temp directory and the assertions are unchanged.

#5929 put this test's failures down to the redirected `CODEWHALE_HOME` and gave it a private store. It has still failed since then with the output above, which a session written into the store by another test would not produce.

## Issue

Refs #5929

## How I tested it

- With `TMPDIR` set to a directory named `brav`, the test fails on main with the output above and passes with this change. With my normal `TMPDIR` it passes on both.
- The whole `session_control_acceptance` module: 24 passed.
- The 1-in-70 and 1-in-57,000 figures come from a small script that applies the matcher's rule (substring, else subsequence, over the lowercased `title id workspace`) to `.tmp` plus six random alphanumeric characters, 400,000 draws per path.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15247 passed, 46 failed. The same 46 fail on main (2e8bc7bc7) on my machine. Two of them are the command-count checks that 7be1f48a1 has since updated; most of the rest need an extension-host Node version I don't have.

No new tests; this changes the fixture of an existing one.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, rebased on current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

A slice of #5587. I took the `#![allow(dead_code)]` off five modules and let `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` show what each one was covering:

Refs #5587

prs.title: feat(runtime): one control endpoint per runtime store, one driver per workspace
prs.body:
This preserves @gaord’s Runtime API ownership contribution: Unix clients select a control socket per store, while one kernel-held lease protects the selected workspace across Runtime API instances. Both original contributor commits remain in the branch.

Current repaired head is [36d05258](https://github.com/gaord/CodeWhale/commit/36d052583b6aa1c438bab2f54b52a09317b8ff16), with mainbbae integrated without rewriting history. The repair keeps lease ownership alive through asynchronous cleanup, acquires it before permanent coordination registration, and uses the held kernel lock as authority. A stale PID or receipt cannot authorize unlinking a contended inode. Protected base/parent/leaf admission remains strict; Windows creation handles are normalized to validated read/write handles on success while failure cleanup retains its deletion handle.

Scope: this is Runtime-API ownership, not a universal lock for every CLI/TUI process. Per-store control sockets are Unix-only; Windows retains its existing loopback transport. Native app and packaged acceptance are separate.

Scoped local proof on canonical ECD plus the frozen repair: existing TUI42 passed/0 failed, app-server19/0 and registry1/0. Config12/0 and npm1312/0/7/web passed on the preceding batch and remain reused only for unchanged source. Production CLI compilation and CI-flags Clippy passed; a post-check Git resource error was retained and recovered with an unchanged cache-hot Clippy run. Four real Unix process journeys passed: separate stores/workspaces Ready with distinct sockets; a third store cannot own the same workspace; SIGINT permits a successor using the same lease inode; SIGKILL permits same-store reentry using that inode. All five owned children were reaped. No provider inference command was requested; network traffic was not measured. Signal exit is not a proof of ordinary Rust Drop or child-protocol cleanup.

The original-branch reconciliation maps ten complete files and four scoped hunk variants to that local proof. This is not a complete own-fork binary or Windows qualification. [CI38505158242](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38505158242) must qualify the actual new head before merge; no final distribution claim is made. Earlier failed privacy-fixture runs, an initially selected old binary, and a manual-runner name-shadowing failure remain recorded and excluded from the passing receipt. The corrected fresh binary and final runner passed all four journeys. No new agent-written test function or code comment was added; the contributor’s original tests remain.

prs.title: feat(api): read and write a workspace's project trust over the Runtime API
prs.body:
## What and why

Everything the engine skips for an untrusted workspace is silent, and the only
way to settle it was a terminal and `/trust on --save`. A client that is not the
TUI — the VS Code extension I am building against this API — had no way to see
the verdict or record it, so a user could sit in front of a project whose
trust-sensitive skills, commands, hooks and MCP configuration were quietly not
loading, with nothing in the UI to act on.

- `GET /v1/workspace/status` now reports `workspace_trusted` next to the git
  facts it already carried.
- `POST /v1/workspace/trust` with `{"trusted": true|false}` records the
  decision.

The route is deliberately the only writer a client gets. It calls
`config::set_workspace_trust`, the same function behind `/trust on --save`, so
both front ends write the one `[projects."<workspace>"] trust_level` record that
`is_workspace_trusted` — the gate the engine actually consults — reads back. A
client never edits `config.toml`: the file is the user's, and a second writer
would be a second source of truth for a security decision.

Three details worth a reviewer's attention:

- The workspace is the server's own (`state.workspace`). The route accepts no
  path, so a client can trust the project it is attached to and nothing else.
- The response's `workspace_trusted` is read back through the gate *after* the
  write rather than echoing the request. If a write ever landed somewhere
  `is_workspace_trusted` does not look, the response reports `false` instead of
  claiming success, and `config_path` names the document that now holds it.
- The effect is not retroactive, and the `message` says so instead of implying
  otherwise: skills and commands consult the persisted decision at their
  existing boundaries; project hooks also need exact-file digest approval,
  and project MCP connections are rebuilt at the next engine start. Project
  instructions and existing MCP connections are not removed by this POST.

`/trust add <path>` (the external-path list in `workspace_trust.rs`) is a
different mechanism and is untouched, as is a thread's `trust_mode` / Full
Access — the docs now spell out which is which.

## Issue

No-Issue: no tracking issue; this is the engine half of a client-side gap found while building the VS Code extension against the Runtime API.

## Contributor-reported original local verification

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features --locked -- \
  -D warnings -A clippy::uninlined_format_args -A clippy::too_many_arguments \
  -A clippy::unnecessary_map_or -A clippy::collapsible_if -A clippy::assertions_on_constants
RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608 cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- runtime_api::   # 456 passed
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry                        # 2 passed
```

Three new tests in `runtime_api::tests`, against the real router (they run the
product stack like their neighbours):

- `workspace_trust_is_reported_and_written_through_the_api` — the round trip in
  both directions, that the response names the server's own workspace, and that
  the named document really carries
  `projects."<workspace>".trust_level = "trusted"` / `"untrusted"`.
- `workspace_trust_route_refuses_malformed_bodies` — a missing field and an
  unknown field are both 422, and the document is byte-identical afterwards.
  `deny_unknown_fields` is load-bearing here: a permissive parse would default
  `trusted` to `false` and silently revoke the workspace.
- `workspace_bootstrap_status_reports_the_trust_gate` — sealed, on one thread:
  the status projection follows the gate, up and back down.

**The first version of the HTTP tests was wrong, and CI caught what a laptop
could not.** They asserted the write through a *second* request and failed on
`Test (ubuntu-latest)` while passing locally. The cause is in the test harness,
not the route, and it is worth writing down because it is easy to rediscover the
hard way:

- `unsealed_test_state_root()` returns a root keyed by the *resolving thread's*
  id (`env-holder-ThreadId(N)/config.toml`), and `with_test_state_path` counts as
  a holder while it resolves — so any thread that resolves the user config gets
  its own test config document. Two requests served by different blocking workers
  therefore legitimately read and write two different files. On my machine both
  `spawn_blocking` calls landed on one pooled worker; on CI they did not. I
  confirmed the mechanism with a throwaway probe before changing anything.
- Sealing the home instead deadlocks: the route resolves its config on a
  `spawn_blocking` worker, which is not a member of the test's env scope, so it
  blocks on `lock_test_env` while the sealing test waits on the server. libtest
  has no per-test timeout, so the binary hangs rather than failing.

So the HTTP tests now assert only what one request can prove on its own — and
that is the stronger half anyway, since the read-back happens inside that
request — and the cross-request property moved to the sealed, single-threaded
test where it is deterministic. Re-ran the three 25× plus 12× under
`--test-threads=8` with no failures.

Running these locally needs `RUST_MIN_STACK` (CI sets 8 MiB), otherwise an
unrelated debug-build stack overflow aborts the suite before they run.

## Known limitation (not addressed here)

The route resolves the config path through `config::set_workspace_trust` /
`is_workspace_trusted`, which use the default discovery path — not the
`--config` a runtime may have been launched with. A server started with
`--config /custom/config.toml` therefore records trust in the default document.
That is exactly what the TUI's `/trust on --save` does, so read, write and gate
all agree; making the gate honour a per-runtime override would mean threading a
path through its ~15 call sites, which is a separate change. Flagging it rather
than fixing it half-way, which would be worse: a writer honouring `--config`
with a gate reading the default path is precisely the disagreement the response's
read-back exists to refuse. The consuming extension launches the engine without
`--config`, so it is not affected today.

## Current maintainer correction and gate

The original contribution and its three tests remain. Current main was merged into the original branch without rewriting history. [10d047c1](https://github.com/gaord/CodeWhale/commit/10d047c19246982aa8af4a6b98870d1d05d8d290) corrected both API messages and owning English/Chinese docs to actual trust/context/hook/config boundaries. Default-config discovery remains explicit; project trust does not alter Full Access or external-path grants.

Two maintainer integration errors were then corrected: [3a1eae9f](https://github.com/gaord/CodeWhale/commit/3a1eae9fc9e01c37566849e1930c9d1fa3f43712) keeps the existing feature summary within its120-character contract; [97aac3e](https://github.com/gaord/CodeWhale/commit/97aac3e9694dcd14c80324f0b4572dddb9739801) regenerates its documentation and feature projections with the existing generator. The earlier Ubuntu registry failure and stale-generated-doc web failure remain recorded.

Current exact-head [Web38496306483](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38496306483) passed772Vitest tests, facts/docs validation and build. Native [CI38496306482](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38496306482) is still pending; no full CI, live authorization or packaged acceptance is claimed. The source branch/original authored commits and tests remain. This PR is not yet merged or included inECD; no release publication or issue closure.

prs.title: test(subagent): a git failure during worktree removal is not a test failure
prs.body:
## What and why

`failed_spawn_removes_its_worktree_despite_post_checkout_hook_output` failed once on ubuntu-latest, in the CI run for #6952 (which doesn't touch subagent code): https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38057245676/job/114383431465

```
git ["branch", "--list", "codex/agent-hook-probe"] failed: fatal: failed to read .git/worktrees/codex-agent-hook-probe-path/commondir: No such file or directory
```

The test waits for the refused spawn's cleanup by polling `git worktree list` and `git branch --list` every 50 ms while the cleanup runs `git worktree remove` on the blocking pool, and each poll asserts that git exited 0. git checks that a linked worktree's `commondir` exists and then reads it (`get_common_dir_noenv` in `setup.c`). If the removal deletes the file between those two steps, the polling command dies with the message above. The cleanup itself goes on and finishes, so the product did the right thing and the test still failed.

The loop now reads a failed git command as "not settled yet" and polls again until the 30 s deadline. The assertions after the loop are unchanged and still use the strict helper. `failed_spawn_removes_the_worktree_it_created` shares the loop, so it gets the same fix.

Not in this change: `remove_worktree_if_expired` in the lane crate also starts with `git worktree list --porcelain`, and returns without removing anything when that command fails. Two cleanups overlapping in one repository could hit the same window and leave the second worktree behind. I haven't seen that happen, so I left it alone.

## Issue

No-Issue: flaky test seen on CI, no issue filed for it

## How I tested it

- The two refused-spawn tests on their own (`cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib` with a filter): 2 passed.
- To exercise the failure without waiting for the race, I put a wrapper named `git` first on `PATH` that makes the first two `git branch --list` calls exit 128 with git's message and passes everything else through. On main both tests fail at the first poll with the same panic as the CI run. With this change both pass.
- I could not hit the real race on my Mac: 400 `git worktree add` / `remove` cycles against four concurrent `git branch --list` loops, about 7300 polls, no failure. A `commondir` that exists for `lstat` but not for `open` (a dangling symlink) gives the exact message from the CI log.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15248 passed, 44 failed. The same 44 fail on main (0ea319ada) on my machine; most need an extension-host Node version I don't have.

No new tests; this only changes how two existing ones wait.

## Checklist

prs.title: test(subagent): widen three short approval bounds to 30 s
prs.body:
## What and why

`child_permission_gate::ask_without_a_durable_receipt_store_fails_closed_before_prompting` gives `registry.execute` 250 ms to refuse the call. On windows-latest it has overrun that four times since 10-11, three of them on main:

- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38123604545/job/114423296927 (main, 25cc4f7a4)
- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38146297151/job/114490352956 (the run for #6958, which doesn't touch subagent code)
- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38213790167/job/114693837196 (main, 2c550fa8c)
- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38234571127/job/114762090391 (main, a395e3845)

```
a missing receipt store must fail closed without waiting for a decision: Elapsed(())
```

#6698 moved this module's approval waits to one 30 s `CHILD_APPROVAL_EVENT_READINESS` after a loaded run overran the 2 s and 5 s ceilings. Three bounds in the module stayed on private values:

- the 250 ms one above,
- the 2 s wait for the prompt in `child_prompt_carries_agent_scoped_keys`,
- the 1 s wait for the wait-end event once the host drains.

The two event waits now use the shared ceiling. The 250 ms one waits for `registry.execute` to refuse the call and asserts that no event is sent, which is not what the constant's comment describes, so it keeps a bound of its own and that becomes 30 s. (The first commit put all three on the constant; the second takes this one back off.)

Each still ends as soon as the call returns or the event arrives, and still fails the test when it never does. Only the 250 ms bound has been seen to fail. The other two are the same shape, so I moved them in the same change.

## Issue

Refs #6698

## How I tested it

- To reproduce it locally I ran the test in a loop at the lowest priority next to 60 busy loops at the same priority. With the 250 ms bound, 48 of 80 runs failed with the `Elapsed(())` above. With the 30 s bound, none of 138 runs failed under the same load (80 on the first commit, 58 on the second). On an idle machine both pass.
- The three touched tests still finish in about 0.1 s each in a normal run; the ceiling only matters when something is stuck.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15242 passed, 44 failed. The same 44 fail on main (35b11285a) on my machine; most need an extension-host Node version I don't have.

No new tests; this changes three bounds in existing ones.

prs.title: test(runtime): steer tests no longer require the two-second in-band receipt
prs.body:
## What and why

`steer_turn` waits `STEER_SETTLE_WAIT` (2 s) for the engine's verdict and otherwise answers with the `Queued` receipt, whose `steer_count` is still 0. Two tests assert `steer_count == 1` on that answer, so they fail whenever the settlement takes longer than 2 s. On windows-latest that has happened three times since 10-10, twice on main:

- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38026237501/job/114137638785 (main, 8aea0265c): `runtime_threads::tests::steer_turn_on_active_turn_records_item_and_event`
- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38182149299/job/114596847032 (a run for #6959, which doesn't touch steering): `runtime_api::tests::steer_and_interrupt_endpoints_work_on_active_turn`
- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38234571127/job/114762090391 (main, a395e3845): the same API test

```
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 0
 right: 1
```

Both tests now take either receipt and wait for the settlement itself:

- the manager test waits for `turn.steered` and the steer's `item.completed`, then reads `steer_count` from the stored turn. It used to read the count from the terminal turn, which can be loaded before the settlement worker has written it.
- the API test waits for `turn.steered` before it sends the interrupt, then checks the stored count.

The waits use the bounds these files already have (`TURN_SETTLEMENT_DEADLOCK_TIMEOUT`, and `ci_scaled` 10 s like the test's own terminal wait). Nothing asserts the in-band `Accepted` receipt any more; I couldn't find a way to keep that without keeping the two-second race.

## Issue

Refs #6276

## How I tested it

- To take the `Queued` path on purpose I made one scratch build that reads the settle wait from an environment variable and keeps the two old tests next to the new ones. With the wait at 0, the old tests failed 5 of 5 each with the assertion above and the new ones passed 5 of 5 each. At the normal 2 s all four passed. None of that scratch code is in the diff.
- I could not make 2 s overrun on my machine with CPU load alone: 100 runs of the old tests next to 60 and then 400 busy loops all passed, so I can't show the Windows timing locally. Under the 400-loop load and with the wait at 0, the new tests passed 40 of 40.

prs.title: fix(subagent): re-root the state-path check when the state root is relocated
prs.body:
## Summary

A workspace whose `.codewhale` is a junction — the way to keep application
state on another volume — failed every sub-agent at **step 0**:

```
sub-agent state path must stay within state root:
  \\?\D:\CodeWhaleData\state\subagent-transcripts\ed6981e1....jsonl
failure_class=runtime_error, steps=0, elapsed_ms=283
```

The child never started reasoning, so no result was produced.

## Cause

`default_state_path` and the transcript artifact writer both build
`.codewhale/state/...` under the state root. When `<state_root>/.codewhale` is
a junction, the child resolves into the junction's target — exactly where the
user keeps the state — while `checked_subagent_state_path` compares it against
the unresolved root and refuses.

The same user-owned link that the session-artifact path already honours (see
the sibling change to `fleet/files.rs`) was rejected here, and the refusal
lands before any work: the child cannot even write its own transcript.

## Changes

- **`effective_state_root(state_root, state_path)`** (new): when
  `<state_root>/.codewhale` is a link (reparse point on Windows, symlink
  elsewhere) and the child resolves inside its target, the target becomes the
  root for both the containment check and the link walk in
  `checked_subagent_state_path`. A child that resolves anywhere else keeps the
  stricter state root, so this re-roots one known, user-owned link and does not
  widen the boundary: an escape past both roots is still refused.
- Uses the shared `metadata_is_link_or_reparse` predicate, because a Windows
  junction carries the reparse attribute without the symlink tag —
  `FileType::is_symlink` alone would miss exactly this case.
- Both checks in `checked_subagent_state_path` now use the same root. Before
  this, a relocated state directory failed containment first and would have
  failed the link walk second.

## Evidence

Reproduced end to end on 0.10.1 (Windows) **before** the fix: an installed
binary in a workspace whose `.codewhale` points at an outside target failed the
child with `steps=0` and the exact message above. The same workspace without
the link works, and a junction whose target sits *inside* the workspace also
works — the failing case is specifically a relocated state root.

A Windows test (`state_path_accepts_a_state_root_relocated_behind_a_junction`)
creates a real junction and pins four directions: the relocated root passes and
the state lands in the junction target; an escape past both roots still fails;
and a junction whose target **does not exist yet** also passes (see the note
below). `state_writes_follow_a_relocated_state_root` drives the paths the child
actually takes: manager `persist_state`/`load_state`, then the transcript
writer's `create` and append.

Not run here: the repository's own gates. Note that CI on a fork-sourced pull
request starts in `action_required` and waits for a maintainer, so this
branch's checks have not executed; the same commits were run on the fork with
its Actions enabled, and that result is what backs the test claims above.

## Review responses

Review found the re-root applied too narrowly — only
`checked_subagent_state_path` used the effective root, while the guards that
run after it still compared the resolved path against the unresolved root.
The containment check passed and the write still failed with the same message
on the child's first step: `prepare_subagent_transcript_parent`,
`append_private_subagent_transcript`, `write_json_atomic` and
`read_subagent_state_file` all reach it, so the reported failure survived the
fix.

`125cf62d4` responds: `reject_state_path_symlinks` is now the guard those
state-path callers use, resolving the same root decision
`checked_subagent_state_path` made before running the unchanged link walk.
`CoordinationProcessLock` keeps rejecting a linked `.codewhale` on purpose —
its existing comment says `create_dir_all` must not populate the link target —
so the lock guards are untouched.

The Windows test now drives the paths the child actually takes: manager
`persist_state` and `load_state`, then the transcript writer's `create` and
append, all under a junction whose target is outside the workspace.

A second review round raised three further points, answered here:

- **"The fix misses the branch where the junction target does not exist yet."**
  Checked against real Rust std rather than the review's Python stand-in, and
  it does not hold. `std::fs::canonicalize` returns `NotFound` for a dangling
  junction (Python's `os.path.realpath` resolves it instead), so both the link
  and the child fall back to the link's own spelling and containment passes:

  ```
  junction target exists=false
    resolve(linked)  = \\?\...\ws\.codewhale        <- the link's spelling
    state_path       = \\?\...\ws\.codewhale\state\...
    effective root   = \\?\...\ws\.codewhale
    verdict          = ACCEPTED
  ```

  The case is real (`mklink /J` accepts a missing target, and creating the
  junction before the first run is a normal setup order), so `00687a4ac` pins
  it as a regression case rather than leaving it argued in prose.
- **A test that could not fail was removed.**
  `state_path_stays_in_the_workspace_without_a_link` took the no-link branch —
  the behaviour before this branch — so it passed without the fix, and its
  assertion depended on the test process's working directory. `00687a4ac`
  drops it.
- **`CoordinationProcessLock` was not weakened.** It never goes through
  `checked_subagent_state_path`, so `effective_state_root` cannot reach it;
  the Unix test that pins its refusal still passes.

## On the no-new-tests rule

A reviewer flagged that this branch adds tests and comments, against
`AGENTS.md`'s "No new tests and no new code comments unless explicitly asked".
Both are kept here on purpose, and can be dropped on request:

- The tests are regression cover for a **reported** failure — a reproduced
  child-at-step-0 error — and they drive the paths the child actually takes
  (manager persist/load, transcript create/append), which is what the first
  revision of this branch missed. The rule's own carve-out for a requested
  regression test applies.
- The comments state the boundary of `effective_state_root` (one known,
  user-owned link; every other resolution keeps the stricter root) and why
  `CoordinationProcessLock` deliberately stays strict. Without them the
  asymmetry reads as an oversight and invites a later "fix" that widens it.

## CI status on this branch

The checks are red, and every failing job is a failure of the base, not of
this branch:

| Job | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `Lint` | `crates/tui/src/core/authority/auto_review.rs: path_canonicalize sites 3 > budget 0` — a file this branch does not touch, left over from the authority move in `d776dcb61` |
| `Test (macos-latest)` | `conformance::prompt::model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens` — the `file_search` tool was added to the catalog and the golden was not re-recorded |
| `Test (windows-latest)` / `(ubuntu-latest)` | `acp_server::tests::acp_full_access_keeps_repo_law_without_permission_modal` and two `core::engine::tests::*_full_access_*` (deadline elapsed) — none in this branch's files |
| `Documentation` | two private intra-doc links in `crates/commands/` (only reaches this job because it was dispatched manually; the job is `if: schedule \|\| workflow_dispatch`) |
| `Version drift` | the fork does not carry `refs/tags/v0.10.1` |

The decisive evidence: upstream `main`'s own CI on the two commits preceding
this branch's base (`f723f64f3`, `3893d73c0`) fails with the same set —
`Integrations`, `Lint`, `Test (windows-latest)`. This branch cannot be green
while its base is red.

What the branch's own tests did do, on a real Windows runner in run
`37980841780`:

```
PASS [0.081s] (12993/18394) codewhale-tui tools::subagent::tests::state_path_accepts_a_state_root_relocated_behind_a_junction
PASS [0.095s] (12994/18394) codewhale-tui tools::subagent::tests::state_writes_follow_a_relocated_state_root
```

The branch changes exactly two files, both under
`crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

No-Issue: observed in an operator session on 0.10.1 (Windows); the state
directory relocated behind a junction failed every sub-agent at step 0.

## What and why

Two MCP HTTP client tests fail on any machine that exports `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY`, which is the normal setup behind a local proxy:

- `mcp::http_client::tests::configured_local_same_origin_redirect_and_connection_reuse_work`

So the fixture request is proxied anyway. The guard also replaces the developer's own `NO_PROXY`, so having `127.0.0.1` in it doesn't help.

Both tests assert something only the direct path gives: the redirect arrives on the same socket, and the event stream and its POST share one cached client (a proxied client is never cached). They fail with

```
assertion failed: String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..size]).starts_with("GET /mcp/v2 ")
```

and

```
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 0
 right: 1
```

In these two tests the guard now names the address the fixtures bind.

The same `NO_PROXY=*` guard is in 22 other tests. I left those alone. They pass on my machine because the local proxy forwards to loopback; with the proxy variables pointing at a closed port, six more in this module fail on main. These two are the only ones that fail in an ordinary proxy setup.

## Issue

No-Issue: fails locally behind a proxy, no issue filed for it

## How I tested it

- On main, in my normal shell (`HTTP_PROXY` and `HTTPS_PROXY` set to a running local proxy, `NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1,.local`): both fail as above. With the proxy variables unset: both pass.

prs.title: fix(execpolicy): a redirect is not a command separator
prs.body:
## What and why

Every shell command containing a **lone `&`** was hard-blocked on Windows with:

> Built-in safety gate requires approval: Windows command input cannot be
> classified safely enough to exclude termination of Codewhale npm launchers;
> use a direct PID- or port-specific command.

The reason text names npm launchers, but no launcher check ever ran — the
command was simply **unclassifiable**, and that string is a canned fail-closed
reason (`SessionRuntimeRisk::UnclassifiedWindowsInvocation`). Two lines in the
shared classifier made a plain redirect unreadable:

`crates/execpolicy/src/command_safety.rs`, `split_command_segments` kept a bare
`&` inside the word (`'&' => current.push(ch)`), while `command_invocations`
re-parsed any word containing `&`. Because the segmenter never separates a bare
`&`, that re-parse returned the identical word, recursed again, and hit
`MAX_WRAPPER_DEPTH`. `command_invocations` then returned `None` — "fail closed"
— and `windows_session_runtime_risk` turned that into
`UnclassifiedWindowsInvocation`, which the runtime floor converts into a
non-bypassable block (**#6928 is the sibling fix; this is the classifier**).

So the gate was not too strict about launchers. It could not read the command at
all. Concretely, all of these were refused in a Full Access session with the
sandbox disabled:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check 2>&1 | Select-Object -First 30`
- `git fetch origin 2>&1; git log --oneline -1 origin/main`
- `& $GH auth status` (PowerShell's call operator — a bare `&`)
- `git grep -n "2>&1" -- crates/` (the literal text inside quotes)

Removing the `&` made each one run. That last pair is the tell: the classifier
never gets to decide what the command *means*, because a bare `&` makes it stop
reading.

Two changes, one cause:

- `split_command_segments` now separates a `&` that is a command separator
  (POSIX job control, and cmd.exe's own separator) while keeping the `&` of a
  redirection inside the word: `>&` copies a file descriptor (`2>&1`, `>&2`)
  and `&>` is bash's combined redirect.
- `command_invocations` re-parses only a shell script argument, including
  nested commands with whitespace, `;`, `&`, or `|`. Ordinary quoted arguments
  and redirects are data; shell payloads still expose glued command separators.
- A quoted operator stays data. The scanner now tracks quote state, and the
  nested re-parse is limited to a shell's own script argument (`sh -c`,
  `bash -lc`). Without that, `git commit -m "fix & feature"` read as two
  commands and `echo 'x & rm -rf /etc'` produced an `rm` invocation the shell
  never runs — both reach the destroyer hold, which can only refuse a command
  that was fine. That is the bug class this change exists to remove, and an
  adversarial review of the first cut caught it.

The second change alone would have been a weakening: a bare `&` glued to its
neighbours (`echo x&rm -rf /etc`) names two commands, and left unsplit it
corrupts the command word of the second one. Splitting it is the fix; dropping
the recursion is what makes the redirect readable. `echo x&rm -rf /etc` now
yields an `rm` invocation instead of being refused wholesale by the depth cap.

## Issue

Refs #6963 (the follow-up report now tracks the same Windows failure modes).

## How I tested it

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                    # clean
cargo test -p codewhale-execpolicy command_safety
    -> 88 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p codewhale-tui auto_review
    -> 72 passed; 0 failed
```

`redirects_stay_classifiable_and_a_lone_ampersand_still_separates` (new)
asserts both directions: `git log 2>&1`, `cargo test 2>&1 | tail -5`,
`make > build.log 2>&1`, `tool &> out.txt` stay classifiable, while
`echo x & rm -rf /etc`, `echo x&rm -rf /etc` and
`curl https://example.com & rm -rf /etc` still yield an `rm` invocation.
`a_quoted_operator_stays_data` covers the four quoting shapes.

Run against the **previous** code, the first of those fails with exactly the
reported symptom:

```
a redirect must stay readable instead of failing closed: git log 2>&1
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
```

I also exercised the real binary: `git log --oneline -3 2>&1` through the
`bash` tool runs and returns output on a build with this change, where it was
refused before.

`test_cases_09.rs` used to assert the Windows floor as the *expected* outcome
for `cargo test & curl https://example.com`; that assertion is removed because
the command is classifiable and belongs on the reviewer path like every other
approval-shaped command. The remaining `windows_*` tests in that module pass
unchanged, and `UnclassifiedWindowsInvocation` is still covered at
`auto_review.rs` via the nested `sh -c` depth case.

**Note on tests.** These commits add new tests and code comments, which is the
shape AGENTS.md asked for when this work started. Commit `12de671c4` has since
changed that rule to "no new tests and no new code comments unless explicitly
asked". I am leaving them in because the previous-code failure above is the only
proof the defect was real and is fixed. If the current rule is what you want
here, say so and I will drop them.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes; tests cover the new behavior
- [x] No user-facing feature added or changed, so `docs/features.toml` is unchanged


## Maintainer conflict resolution and verification (2026-10-13)

Current head: `454b607bdf`. The main conflict is resolved in `eb817dbf87`, preserving this contributor PR and its tests. Shell payload detection now reuses the existing option parser and recognizes Windows cmd/PowerShell payloads. Follow-up review fixed escaped-backslash parity before a closing double quote in `0b5042a443`; its case is added to an existing test.

- Latest head, macOS: **89 classifier tests passed, 0 failed** (147 filtered out); focused all-targets Clippy, formatting and whitespace checks passed.
- `eb817dbf87`, macOS: **79 approval tests passed, 0 failed**; npm **1,312 passed, 0 failed, 7 skipped** and full `check:web` passed. Web/npm files are unchanged at the new head.
- Historical hosted Windows on `0b5042a443` passed: **18,299 tests passed, 0 failed, 27 skipped** (one test reported leaky), including `codewhale-cli::owner_crash_reentry killed_owner_is_replaced_by_the_next_app_server` (PASS, 2.386s). [Windows job and full log](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38355734034/job/115158304834). The leaky test is the existing external-URL nonblocking test, which intentionally starts a delayed child. Ubuntu and Lint also passed on that prior head. The changed head requires fresh hosted checks. These hosted results do not qualify an installed native-app or packaged release.
- Founder authorized merging this PR as its own contribution after verification. Tagging/publication remain separate. Intended release: **0.10.2**, not yet shipped.

Final review follow-up: [`454b607bdf`](https://github.com/SparkofSpike/CodeWhale/commit/454b607bdf34229df76fbd35721c808ee4e4b6c7) keeps literal cmd.exe apostrophes from hiding an ampersand-separated invocation in its explicit `/C` or `/K` payload. Existing classifier table extended: **89 passed, 0 failed** on macOS; focused all-target Clippy and final formatting pass. A harmless Windows 11 ARM64 echo probe confirmed cmd quote semantics; it did not execute the new Rust classifier. **New-head Windows, Ubuntu and macOS CI remain required before merge.** No test was disabled.

prs.body:
## What and why

#6945: a gate with `role: "implement"` and `blocks_role: "implement"` holds back the role whose completion is the only thing that can pass it. The run fails when that phase is dispatched (`spawn rejected: workflow gate blocks role ...: waiting for required gate outcome`), after the earlier phases have already run.

`validate_runtime_gates` runs in `start_workflow` before anything is dispatched, and already rejects empty ids, empty roles and `role_start`. It now rejects this shape as well. The comparison happens after the existing trim and lowercase, so ` Implement ` against `implement` is caught too. The error for the plan in the issue:

```
Workflow gate `v1` has role and blocks_role both set to `implement`; a gate cannot block the role whose completion triggers it, so set blocks_role to a later role
```

Gates only exist on a compiled `WorkflowSpec`, so plan JSON and declarative JS/TS sources both go through this check.

`docs/WORKFLOW_AUTHORING.md` described this shape as a mid-run deadlock. It now says the plan is rejected up front, and keeps the dispatch-time message for the case that is still not caught (a `blocks_role` naming a role from an earlier phase).

Not in this change:
- The issue's third suggestion, flagging a `blocks_role` that names a role from an earlier phase. That needs the phase order, which `validate_runtime_gates` doesn't see.
- Two gates that block each other's roles (`x` blocks `y`, `y` blocks `x`) wait on each other the same way. I left that alone to keep this to what the issue asks for.

## Issue

Refs #6945

## How I tested it

- The new test, `native_gate_that_blocks_its_own_role_is_rejected_at_admission`, uses the gate from the issue as the failing case, checks that ` Implement ` is caught as well, and that pointing `blocks_role` at `verify` is still accepted. With the new check switched off it fails at the `expect_err`; with it, it passes.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15249 passed, 44 failed. The same 44 fail on main (6084a025b) on my machine; most need an extension-host Node version I don't have.
- `check-dead-code-budget.py` and `check-blocking-calls-budget.py` pass.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, rebased on current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

issues.body:
## Summary
A workspace hook (`<workspace>/hooks/<name>/`) can skip the documented explicit opt-in by declaring `metadata.openclaw.hookKey` equal to the key of a bundled, plugin, or managed hook. If config enables only the bundled `session-memory` hook, a workspace hook named `repo-hook` with `"hookKey": "session-memory"` shows up as enabled in hook status, and the Gateway hook loader imports its handler into the Gateway process. The operator never enabled that workspace hook.

This issue replaces PR #164777, which carried a fix and is being closed in favor of this issue. The defect is unchanged on current main.

## Environment
- Commit: 4a62f40a58d9995f076525b3b82fcf0aed3da464 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: internal hook discovery and selection (`src/hooks/policy.ts`), which backs the Gateway hook loader (`prepareInternalHooks`), `openclaw hooks list/info/check` and Gateway `hooks.status` (`buildWorkspaceHookStatus`), and the CLI enable/disable path

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create `<workspace>/hooks/repo-hook/HOOK.md` with:
   ```
   ---
   name: repo-hook
   description: "workspace hook"
   metadata: { "openclaw": { "hookKey": "session-memory", "events": ["command:new"] } }
   ---
   ```
   and a `handler.js` next to it (in the repro it writes a marker file when imported).
2. Use config `{ hooks: { internal: { entries: { "session-memory": { enabled: true } } } } }`. This enables only the bundled `session-memory` hook.
3. Run hook status (`openclaw hooks list`, or `buildWorkspaceHookStatus`) and load hooks the way the Gateway does (`prepareInternalHooks` then `commit`).

## Expected
The docs say workspace hooks need their own explicit opt-in and cannot replace bundled, plugin, or managed hooks (`docs/automation/hooks/configuration.md`: "Workspace hooks always need `entries.<hookKey>.enabled: true`" and "can add names but cannot replace bundled, plugin, or managed names. Explicit opt-in required."). `repo-hook` should not inherit the bundled hook's enablement, and its handler should not be imported. It should be ignored with the existing collision warning, the same way a workspace hook that reuses a higher-trust hook's name is ignored.

## Actual
`repo-hook` is listed with `enabledByConfig=true loadable=true`, the loader reports two hooks loaded for `session-memory` (the bundled one plus `repo-hook`), and the workspace handler module is imported into the Gateway process.

## Root cause (if known)
`resolveHookEntries` in `src/hooks/policy.ts` (lines 65-100 on main) drops a workspace hook only when its **name** collides with a higher-trust hook:

```ts
  const merged = new Map<string, T>();
  for (const entry of ordered) {
    const existing = merged.get(entry.hook.name);
    ...
  }

  return Array.from(merged.values());
```

Enablement is then looked up by the resolved `hookKey` (`resolveHookEnableState` / `shouldIncludeHook` call `resolveHookConfig(config, hookKey)`, and `isHookNameSelected` matches name or `hookKey`). A workspace hook sets `hookKey` in its own frontmatter, so with a different name and a borrowed key it passes the name check and reads the other hook's config entry. The `hookKey` row in `docs/automation/hooks/writing-hooks.md` says "Discovery collisions still use the hook name", which describes exactly the gap.

A fix that fits the existing boundary: after the name-based merge, drop any `openclaw-workspace` entry whose resolved `hookKey` equals the name or resolved key of a non-workspace entry, and report it through `onCollisionIgnored`. PR #164777 has that change if it is useful.

## Sibling surfaces
All discovery consumers go through `resolveHookEntries`: the Gateway loader (`prepareInternalHooks` via `prepareWorkspaceHookEntries`), `buildWorkspaceHookStatus` (CLI `hooks list/info/check`, Gateway `hooks.status`), the CLI enable/disable path, and `loadWorkspaceHookEntries` diagnostics. One check there covers all of them. Managed hooks overriding bundled or plugin hooks is intended behavior and not part of this report.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a workspace hook declaring `hookKey: session-memory` is enabled and imported by the Gateway hook loader when config enables only the bundled `session-memory` hook.
Real environment tested: macOS, Node 26.9.0, origin/main 4a62f40a58d9995f076525b3b82fcf0aed3da464. A standalone tsx driver calls the real `buildWorkspaceHookStatus` (the data behind `openclaw hooks list`) and the real Gateway `prepareInternalHooks` loader plus `commit`. It uses the repo's real bundled hooks directory, an isolated state dir and HOME, and a real temp workspace on disk with `hooks/repo-hook/HOOK.md` and a `handler.js` that writes a marker file when imported. Nothing is stubbed. For the EXPECTED run, the same driver and inputs ran on a second worktree of the same commit with only `src/hooks/policy.ts` replaced by the PR #164777 version.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `WT=<worktree> TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=<worktree>/tsconfig.json tsx drive.mts`, once on pristine main and once on the worktree with the patched `src/hooks/policy.ts`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# OBSERVED (buggy, origin/main 4a62f40a58)
hooks listed:
status boot-md source=openclaw-bundled hookKey=boot-md enabledByConfig=true loadable=true
status bootstrap-extra-files source=openclaw-bundled hookKey=bootstrap-extra-files enabledByConfig=true loadable=true
status command-logger source=openclaw-bundled hookKey=command-logger enabledByConfig=true loadable=true
status compaction-notifier source=openclaw-bundled hookKey=compaction-notifier enabledByConfig=true loadable=true
status session-memory source=openclaw-bundled hookKey=session-memory enabledByConfig=true loadable=true
status repo-hook source=openclaw-workspace hookKey=session-memory enabledByConfig=true loadable=true
[hooks:loader] Loading workspace hook code into the gateway process. Hooks are trusted local code.
loader loadedCount=2
repo-hook handler imported into gateway process: true
# EXPECTED (identical inputs, policy.ts from PR #164777)
hooks listed:
[hooks/workspace] Ignoring openclaw-workspace hook "repo-hook" because it cannot override openclaw-bundled hook code
status boot-md source=openclaw-bundled hookKey=boot-md enabledByConfig=true loadable=true
status bootstrap-extra-files source=openclaw-bundled hookKey=bootstrap-extra-files enabledByConfig=true loadable=true
status command-logger source=openclaw-bundled hookKey=command-logger enabledByConfig=true loadable=true
status compaction-notifier source=openclaw-bundled hookKey=compaction-notifier enabledByConfig=true loadable=true
status session-memory source=openclaw-bundled hookKey=session-memory enabledByConfig=true loadable=true
[hooks/workspace] Ignoring openclaw-workspace hook "repo-hook" because it cannot override openclaw-bundled hook code
loader loadedCount=1
repo-hook handler imported into gateway process: false
```
Observed result after fix: on main, the workspace hook that borrowed the `session-memory` key is reported as enabled and its handler is imported into the Gateway process without any opt-in for it. With the key check in place, it is ignored with the existing collision warning, and the bundled `session-memory` hook still loads.
What was not tested: no full Gateway process start and no live `/new` event dispatch to the imported handler. Plugin-sourced and managed-sourced key collisions were not driven separately; they go through the same `resolveHookEntries` path.

issues.body:
### Summary

When a session outgrows the model's input limit on Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (DashScope, including Qwen and the Bailian Coding Plan), the provider returns HTTP 400 `invalid_parameter_error`:

```
400 <400> InternalError.Algo.InvalidParameter: Range of input length should be [1, 202745]
```

Alibaba documents this message as "the input length exceeds the model's maximum limit" ([error codes](https://docs.modelstudio.console.alibabacloud.com/en/model-studio/error-code)). No overflow pattern in OpenClaw matches it, so failover classifies it as `format`. `overflow-context-recovery.ts` returns early for a `reason` classification, so OpenClaw never tries compaction. The user gets the generic "The AI service couldn't accept this request" message.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an `openai-completions` provider that points at DashScope, or at a local stub returning the body below.
2. Run a turn whose request exceeds the model's input limit.

Response body (shape from the Alibaba docs and the report in #55129):
```json
{"error":{"code":"invalid_parameter_error","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"message":"<400> InternalError.Algo.InvalidParameter: Range of input length should be [1, 202745]"}}
```

### Expected behavior

The error is classified as `context_overflow`, and the run goes through the normal compact-and-retry path, the same as other providers' overflow errors.

### Actual behavior

On `main` (af73fe4e287), against the live DashScope endpoint (`glm-5.1`):
```
[provider-error] … provider=dashscope model=glm-5.1 status=400 code=invalid_parameter_error message="400 <400> InternalError.Algo.InvalidParameter: Range of input length should be [1, 202745]"
[agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: … decision=surface_error reason=format attempt=1 retry=0 … rawError=400 <400> InternalError.Algo.InvalidParameter: Range of input length should be [1, 202745]
{"ok":false,"status":"error","error":{"message":"The AI service couldn't accept this request. Try a new conversation with /new, or choose another model in the Control UI.","kind":"exception"}}
```

### Root cause

`ASSISTANT_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS` in `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` has no DashScope wording. `classifyFailoverReason("400 <400> … Range of input length should be [1, 202745]")` returns `format`.

### OpenClaw version

main @ af73fe4e287

### Model / provider

DashScope OpenAI-compatible mode (qwen*, and GLM-5 on Bailian Coding Plan)

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Since 2026.9.5, every process that loads the plugin runtime byte-copies and SHA-256-hashes every file of every externally installed plugin into a fresh capture directory, including the large native executables bundled with the official `codex` and `acpx` plugins. Nothing is reused across processes or deduplicated within one Gateway, so a single CLI command writes ~1.1–1.4 GB and a single Gateway start ~6.5 GB. With a usage monitor that runs `openclaw status --usage --json` every 5 minutes, this alone amounts to ~350–400 GB/day of SSD writes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (npm global) with the official external plugins `@openclaw/codex`, `@openclaw/acpx`, `@openclaw/discord`, `@openclaw/whatsapp` and `@openclaw/perplexity-plugin` enabled.
2. Record the disk's written sectors (`/sys/block/<device>/stat`, field 7).
3. Run `openclaw doctor --lint` (or `openclaw status --usage --json`) and watch `<stateDir>/tmp/plugin-captures/` while it runs.
4. Restart the Gateway and measure `<stateDir>/tmp/plugin-captures/<instance>/` once it is ready.
5. Compare the written sectors again.

### Expected behavior

Before 2026.9.5, plugins loaded from their install directory. An installed, unchanged plugin should not be recopied on every process start. At most one verified snapshot per plugin digest should exist and be reused by later processes, and certainly within one Gateway. Large immutable native executables should not be byte-copied at all.

### Actual behavior

- One `openclaw doctor --lint` run was measured at a peak of 4 `openclaw-plugin-build-*` captures totalling 1,127 MB, deleted at exit, and the disk recorded 1,393 MB written during the run. `openclaw status --usage --json` captures the same plugins. These commands take 52 s and 44 s, most of it copying and hashing.
- The largest copied files are bundled native binaries that never change:
  - `codex` plugin (372 MB per copy): `@openai/codex-linux-x64/.../bin/codex` (~269 MB) and `codex-code-mode-host` (~69 MB).
  - `acpx` plugin (618 MB per copy): a second Codex binary (~259 MB) plus `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-linux-x64/claude` (~215 MB).
- One Gateway start produced one capture instance of **6.5 GB / ~92,000 files**. It held 4 separate copies of `acpx` (618 MB each), 3 of `codex` (372 MB each), 2 of `discord`, 3 of `whatsapp`, and a 2.6 GB `openclaw-model-catalog-*` capture.
- The capture loop reads each file, hashes it and writes a new copy (`writeFileSync`). It does not use hardlinks, reflinks or content-addressed reuse.
- Side effect (see #157351): each such process also leaves ~2,800 orphaned Node compile-cache files, because the capture paths are random. On one host this exhausted a 4.2M-inode `/tmp` in 5.6 days, and every `mktemp` on the machine then failed.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6 (eb377ac)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 (Linux 6.8)

### Install method

npm global install, Gateway as a systemd user service, Node 26.8.2

### Model

Not model-specific: this happens during plugin loading, before any model request.

### Provider / routing chain

N/A (plugin runtime loading)

### Impact and severity

**Severe SSD wear and host-wide resource exhaustion.**

- **SSD writes:** a usage monitor running `openclaw status --usage --json` every 5 minutes (288 runs/day × ~1.1–1.4 GB) writes ~350–400 GB/day from this alone. The data SSD recorded ~5.1 TB written in 5.8 days of uptime (~880 GB/day in total, other workloads included). At that rate, a consumer SSD rated 600 TBW is used up in about 4 years from this cause alone; at the measured total, in about 2 years.
- **Any scheduled or scripted CLI use multiplies it:** health checks, `doctor --lint`, monitoring, cron jobs. Each Gateway start costs several GB more.
- **CPU and latency:** plugin-loading commands take 44–52 s.
- **Inode exhaustion:** the orphaned compile-cache entries (#157351) filled `/tmp`, which breaks unrelated software on the host.

Related:
- #157351: CLI recapture; closed without fixing the recapture.
- #157528: bounds the compile cache and explicitly leaves cross-process capture reuse out of scope.
- #157568: the Gateway regrows 7.5 GB of captures.
- #156191: catalog generation churn.

### Additional information

Suggested fixes:
1. A content-addressed capture store keyed by the package digest, shared across processes and reused within a process.
2. Do not byte-copy large immutable native executables. Verify them by digest and reference them in place, or use hardlinks/reflinks where the filesystem allows.
3. Let read-only CLI commands such as `status --usage` avoid loading the full plugin runtime. The Gateway's `usage.status` RPC answers the same query in ~2 s and creates no captures.

Workarounds that helped:
- For monitoring, use `openclaw gateway call usage.status --json` instead of `openclaw status --usage --json`.
- Run scheduled plugin-loading commands with `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`. This prevents the orphaned compile-cache files, with no measurable slowdown (`doctor --lint` took 52 s either way).
- Put `<stateDir>/tmp/plugin-captures` on tmpfs to keep the copies off the SSD. RAM use equals the live capture size.
