issues.body:
# [upstream] Gateway startup spends ~60 s re-inspecting plugin generation source trees on every boot

> Draft ticket — OpenClaw gateway startup performance / plugin-generation sandbox.
> Prepared from live diagnosis on one machine (cold boot + 3 warm restarts + CPU profile).

## Title

**Slow gateway startup: ~60 s/boot spent re-validating plugin generation source trees (full fs walk + identity compare of every file in `node_modules`), independent of cache warmth**

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8) |
| Platform | macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64, Mac Studio |
| Node | 26.10.0 (bundled runtime, `--max-old-space-size=16384`) |
| Plugins | 13 enabled: browser, cua-computer, discord, discord-voice, lobster, lossless-claw, memory-core, memory-wiki, ollama, openai, telegram, tool-preflight, workboard |

## Symptoms

- Gateway `[gateway] ready` at **~85 s after boot** (cold), **~72 s on warm restart**. Consistent across every restart: 64–91 s over a full day of restarts (measured 2026-10-05 → 2026-10-06).
- The span `"listening (...; 85.3 s)"` counts from **before** any plugin work; with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1` enabled the attribution is exact (see below).
- Older version comparison: with OpenClaw 2026.5.x (5 plugins, before the npm plugin generation sandbox) the same log line read `listening (...; 1.8 s)`.

## Reproduction

Any `openclaw daemon restart` reproduces on this machine (3/3 boots traced). The cost reproduces on a **warm** restart, minutes after the previous boot, with **zero files modified between boots** — it is not a cold-cache artifact.

Repro + attribution:

```sh
launchctl setenv OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE 1
openclaw daemon restart
grep "startup trace:" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
```

## Instrumentation data

### Startup trace (warm restart, boot of 2026-10-06 09:37)

```
process.bootstrap (cli bootstrap, config, db admission)      8 780.7 ms
plugins.runtime-post-bind                                   59 488.7 ms   ← dominant
runtime.post-attach                                         60 602.9 ms
sidecars.control-ui-assets                                  61 089.9 ms   (first publish of
                                                                            generation after asset
                                                                            update; fast path after)
sidecars.total (everything else: channels, plugin services)  1 074.2 ms
total                                                        71 611.9 ms
```

The other trace steps (config snapshots, secrets, channels, sidecars) are all < 1 s.

### Per-plugin load times (`plugins.gateway-load.plugin.<id>` metrics, 3 boots, consistent)

| Plugin | node_modules | files walked | `loadMs` | ~µs/file |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| discord-voice (local extension) | 1.4 GB | 47 186 | 29 416–30 840 ms | ~640 |
| lossless-claw (`@martian-engineering/lossless-claw` 0.11.2) | 536 MB | 26 694 | 21 918–22 195 ms | ~820 |
| discord (`@openclaw/discord`) | 69 MB | 6 082 | 5 043–5 316 ms | ~870 |
| lobster (`@openclaw/lobster`) | 13 MB | — | 1 347–1 439 ms | — |
| workboard | 2.1 MB | — | 199–205 ms | — |
| memory-core / memory-wiki / browser / ollama / telegram / openai / tool-preflight / cua-computer | ≤ 0.1 MB | — | 9–27 ms each | — |

`loadMs` (module **import**, not `registerMs`) scales **linearly with file count of the plugin's source tree**, at ~0.6–0.9 ms per file. Disabling the two heaviest plugins would cut ~52 of the 59 s.

### CPU profile (node `--cpu-prof` on a manual gateway boot during the slow window)

Main event loop stays responsive (`eventLoopMax ≈ 14 ms` in trace) but one dedicated loader thread pegs ~100 % CPU. Aggregated non-idle self time across the hot window:

```
17.0 %  structuredClone              deep-copying prior fact members
10.4 %  lstat (fs)                   per-file stat of source tree
 8.4 %  open (fs)
 6.4 %  copyFile
 3.9 %  realpath
 3.0 %  isCapturedPathInside         plugin-generation-artifact
 2.0 %  finishPluginNativeNamespace  plugin-generation-artifact
 2.0 %  nativeMemberForSource        plugin-generation-artifact
 1.8 %  innerDeepEqual/comparisons   identity map comparison
 1.5 %  update [hash]
 1.4 %  readdir / realpathSync / relative (path)
```

No copy took place in these boots (0 files under `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/**` touched after 09:20; the generation directories retain 2026-09-29/2026-10-03 mtimes) — **100 % of the time is pure re-validation**.

## Root cause analysis

The plugin generation mechanism (`src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.ts`, `plugin-generation-file-capture.ts`, `plugin-generation-receipt.ts`, `plugin-native-namespace.ts`) persists per-plugin "facts" capturing file identities for native-namespace safety. On **every gateway start**, the reuse check

```ts
// src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.ts
function pluginNativeNamespaceIsCurrent(fact, boundary, outputRoot) {
    const source  = inspectDirectory(fact.sourceDirectory, boundary, outputRoot);
    const captured = inspectDirectory(pluginNativeNamespaceDirectory(fact), ...);
    return source.size === Object.keys(fact.members).length &&
           [...source].every(([relative, member]) =>
               prior?.source === member.source &&
               prior.sourceIdentity === member.identity &&     // dev:ino:mode:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs
               prior.capturedIdentity === captured.get(relative)?.identity);
}
```

walks the **entire plugin source root (including `node_modules`, tens of thousands of files)** with `inspectDirectory`, then compares each entry's `dev:ino:mode:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs` identity against the persisted fact via deep map comparison (`structuredClone` + `keyCheck`/`innerDeepEqual` dominate the profile).

Key properties:

1. **No stat-level cache** — the previous identity table is only used as the *comparison target*; the source side is re-walked from scratch each boot.
2. **No fs-event invalidation** — a cheap pre-check (root dir stat, or recursive dir mtime/size aggregate, or a watcher) would let an unchanged tree skip the walk entirely.
3. **Content-hash receipts already exist** (`plugin-generation-receipt.ts`) for tamper detection — per-boot full identity re-verification of *every* JS/text file adds nothing for those; what actually needs tamper checking is the **native namespace** (native binaries), which is a tiny subset of the tree.

## Security framing (why this exists, and what a fix can keep)

The full re-inspection is presumably there so a boot can always detect external modification of plugin payloads. The proposal below keeps that guarantee with a cheaper invalidation scheme:

1. **Cheap fast-path, correct-by-construction**: persist a rolling digest over the source tree's *directory metadata* (e.g. recursive (mtime,size) aggregates with directory-count), and skip the full `inspectDirectory` walk when it matches the value recorded at the last verified capture. Any file edit forces a directory mtime change, so edits are never missed; deletions of the last entry of a directory change `(count, mtime)` too. Fall back to the existing full walk on mismatch — the invariant "boot never trusts an unverified tree" is preserved.
2. **Narrow the verified set**: per-boot content verification is only meaningful for **native members** (binaries with content hashes in the receipt); JS/text files are re-hashable at first use.
3. **Short-term stop-gap**: parallelize `inspectDirectory` across a worker pool / do it per-plugin concurrently (today it appears serialized into sequential `loadMs` per plugin).

Expected effect on this machine: plugin revalidation 59.5 s → < 1 s per boot (files unchanged, fast path hit).

## Related observations (same boot path, smaller)

- ~22 s cold-start import of the gateway bundle itself — `dist/package-update-activation-recovery.mjs` is a single 63 MB / >1.2 M-line module; splitting lazy-loading it would shave the cold-boot tail.
- `cli.bootstrap.admission.database-readiness` ≈ 1.0 s (160 MB state DB, `agentCount=11`, canonical-validation workers each ~0.7–1.4 s during startup reclamation) — acceptable, but visible.
- `sidecars.control-ui-assets` takes ~61 s **once** after a Control UI asset update (first retained-generation publish of 35–53 MB), then hits the fast utimes path on subsequent boots — fine, worth documenting that the one-off cost lands inside gateway startup.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A model_not_found failure on one model puts the entire shared Ollama auth profile into cooldown for up to 5 minutes, blocking a different, healthy fallback model on the same profile — even though that fallback model works fine on its own.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure agents.defaults.model.primary to a model id Ollama doesn't currently serve (e.g. an untagged/removed local model), with fallbacks pointing to a different, working model on the same ollama provider/auth profile.
2. Run a single agent turn (openclaw agent --agent main --verbose on --json --message "..."). The primary fails with a real model_not_found (404); the fallback dispatch to the working model also fails within milliseconds — not because the fallback model is broken, but because the shared ollama:default auth profile is already in cooldown from the primary's failure.
3. Re-run the exact same fallback model in isolation (--model ollama/<fallback-model>, no forced primary failure) more than ~5 minutes later: it succeeds immediately with a full real response.

### Expected behavior

A model_not_found failure on one model should only cool down that model, per the same design already applied to rate_limit (#49834) and timeout (#87462/#87538). A healthy sibling model sharing the auth profile should remain immediately available for fallback.

### Actual behavior

The fallback dispatch fails within ~13ms with a synthetic model_not_found-class error, even though the fallback model is confirmed to exist and resolve fine (verified independently via a direct check against Ollama's own API). Gateway log:

auth profile failure state updated: runId=<redacted> profile=sha256:9c018ec112cf provider=ollama reason=model_not_found window=cooldown reused=false
model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=ollama/qwen3:14b candidate=ollama/qwen3:14b reason=model_not_found next=ollama/llama3.2:1b
model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=ollama/qwen3:14b candidate=ollama/llama3.2:1b reason=model_not_found next=none detail=ollama can't find the model you're using right now.

Note the identical profile=sha256:9c018ec112cf on both the primary's real failure and the fallback's synthetic one — confirming both models share one auth-profile entry and the cooldown gate does not distinguish between them.

### OpenClaw version

2026.6.11

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu-based host, kernel 7.0.0-28-generic)

### Install method

docker compose

### Model

ollama/qwen3:14b (primary), ollama/llama3.2:1b (fallback)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> ollama (local, host.docker.internal)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Single Ollama auth profile (ollama:default) shared by every configured Ollama model. agents.defaults.model.fallbacks set to a different, smaller model specifically to survive primary failures. Config lives in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json under agents.defaults.model.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: any deployment with multiple models sharing one auth profile (all local-provider users; any provider with one shared API key across models)
Severity: Medium-High — defeats the purpose of a configured fallback specifically for the failure class most likely to occur when a primary model is renamed, removed, or mis-tagged
Frequency: deterministic — reproduces every time a primary hits model_not_found while a fallback shares its profile
Consequence: agent turn fails entirely for up to 5 minutes after what should have been a transparent, immediate fallback

### Additional information

Root cause: isModelScopedCooldownReason() in src/agents/auth-profiles/usage-state.ts only returns true for "rate_limit" and "timeout". Every other failure reason, including "model_not_found", clears cooldownModel and applies profile-wide, per computeNextProfileUsageStats() in usage.ts. Same bug class as #99809 (subscription_limit not scoped by model), different failure reason. #49834 established model-scoped cooldown for rate_limit; #87462/#87538 extended it to timeout; this asks for the same treatment for model_not_found, which neither prior fix included. Confirmed via source inspection that this is unaddressed by the most recent related open PR, #115911 (adds "overloaded" to the scoped list, keeps other reasons profile-wide). No existing issue covers model_not_found specifically.

Note: GitHub's duplicate-detection flagged #49168 as a potential duplicate. That issue is a different bug with a different root cause and fix location — the fallback candidate list itself was being dropped on cross-provider session overrides (fixed in src/agents/model-fallback.ts / agent-command.ts / agent-scope.ts via f3c37a946cc4, closed Apr 24). In this issue, the fallback candidate is correctly retained and attempted (visible in the log as next=ollama/llama3.2:1b) — the failure is in the auth-profile cooldown gate (src/agents/auth-profiles/usage-state.ts) blocking that attempt, unrelated to #49168's fix. This report is on 2026.6.11, already well after the #49168 fix landed, and still reproduces.

## Bug: Memory index rebuild writes text chunks but vectors don't persist to sqlite-vec store

### Summary

After running `openclaw memory index --force --agent main --verbose`, the rebuild completes successfully ("Memory index updated (main)") but vector search remains paused with "index provider settings changed" error. The sqlite-vec virtual table only contains 9 rows despite 9169 text chunks being indexed and 8134 embedding batches running.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)
- OS: macOS 26.3 (arm64) — Mac mini M2
- Node: v24.18.1
- Embedding provider: gemini (gemini-embedding-001)
- Vector dims: 3072
- sqlite-vec: sqlite-vec-darwin-arm64/vec0.dylib (dated Jul 30 13:27)

### Symptoms

1. `memory_search` returns: `"error": "index provider settings changed"` — vector search paused
2. `openclaw memory status --index --agent main` shows:
   - Indexed: 5101/8322 files · 9169 chunks
   - Dirty: yes
   - Vector store: ready (but functionally empty)
   - Index identity: "index provider settings changed"
   - Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt
3. Direct SQLite inspection:
   - `memory_index_chunks` table: 9169 rows ✅
   - `memory_index_chunks_vec_chunks` table: 9 rows ❌
4. Rebuild log shows 8134 "batch start" entries, 0 "batch completed" entries, ends with "Memory index updated (main)."

### What happened before

- Mac mini was restarted
- Tailscale VPN wasn't connected yet, so GLM-5 proxy (litellm-aiswe.query.prod.telnyx.io:4000) was unreachable — model fell back to Anthropic
- Multiple rebuild attempts were SIGKILL'd due to disk filling up with temp reindex files (~10GB across 3 failed attempts) and zombie `openclaw-memory` processes eating RAM
- Cleaned up temp files, restarted Mac, retried with fresh resources (60GB disk free, no zombies)
- Rebuild completed but vectors didn't persist

### Additional context

- A "Legacy state detected" migration prompt appeared and was accepted — it resolved a Memory Core legacy memory index conflict for agent "main" but left a sidecar in place because a `.migrated` file already exists
- `memory_index_meta` table shows: `{"model":"gemini-embedding-001","provider":"gemini","providerKey":"bd50811302958e0a342bc8a1d2687cb549fc6642bd40ff5466adad80ccd051bf",...,"vectorDims":3072}`
- sqlite-vec extension file exists at `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/node_modules/sqlite-vec-darwin-arm64/vec0.dylib`
- FTS search still works — only vector similarity search is broken

### What still works

- `memory_get` — direct file reads ✅
- FTS (full-text search) ✅
- Hindsight recall ✅
- All other OpenClaw functionality ✅

### Expected behavior

Vector embeddings should persist to `memory_index_chunks_vec_chunks` during rebuild, and `memory_search` should return semantic results after `openclaw memory index --force` completes.

### Actual behavior

Rebuild reports success but only 9 vectors persist out of 9169 chunks. Vector search remains paused with "index provider settings changed" error.

issues.body:
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without a crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

In a Telegram forum topic backed by the native Codex app-server runtime, an explicit `/steer <message>` sent during an active turn was not delivered through `turn/steer`. The command payload appeared only after the original turn ended as a new normal prompt, while diagnostics reported a stale slash-command session with queued work and no active run.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw `2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4)` with the Telegram channel and the native Codex app-server runtime.
2. Leave `messages.queue.mode` unset so the documented default, `steer`, applies.
3. In a Telegram forum topic, start a multi-step read-only request that remains active long enough to emit progress and execute several tool calls.
4. After progress is visible, send an explicit command such as:

   ```text
   /steer CANARY-STEER: stop the current analysis and finish with exactly STEER_OK
   ```

5. Observe the active turn, its trajectory, `/status`, and gateway diagnostics.
6. As a control, start another long turn in the same topic with queue depth zero and send `/stop` without first sending `/steer`.

This was observed in two Telegram forum topics. Restarting the gateway before the controlled reproduction did not change the `/steer` result.

## Expected behavior

The documented `/steer` behavior says that it targets the current session's active run and uses the active runtime's steering path so the model receives the guidance at the next supported runtime boundary. For the native Codex runtime, active-run steering maps to a `turn/steer` request.

The command should therefore reach the active topic turn at a supported boundary. If steering is unavailable and the documented normal-prompt fallback is used, the command lane should not remain in stale queued state.

## Actual behavior

- The active turn continued until normal completion.
- The trajectory contained no `turn/steer` event and no mid-turn user message.
- Session status showed `Queue: steer (depth 1)` while the original turn continued.
- Gateway diagnostics detected `queued_work_without_active_run` on the slash-command session and ran stale-lane recovery.
- After the original turn ended, the `/steer` prefix-stripped payload appeared as a new user prompt and produced `STEER_OK` in a separate turn.
- A clean `/stop` control test in the same topic succeeded immediately, which shows that the topic's active run could be aborted when no steer message was pending.

## OpenClaw version

`2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4)`

## Operating system

macOS 26.5.2, build 25F84, arm64

## Install method

Global npm package under the Homebrew prefix (`/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw`), Node.js `v24.15.0`.

## Model

`openai/gpt-5.6-sol`

## Provider / routing chain

Telegram forum topic -> local OpenClaw gateway -> direct execution -> bundled native Codex app-server runtime -> OpenAI provider.

## Additional provider/model setup details

- Queue configuration has no explicit root, agent-default, or `messages.queue` override. Runtime status reports the default `steer` mode.
- The controlled reproduction was performed after a gateway restart.
- No API keys, tokens, chat IDs, user IDs, or full local session identifiers are included below.

## Logs, screenshots, and evidence

Sanitized evidence from the failed `/steer` reproduction:

```text
2026-07-31T09:58:56.145Z session.started sessionKey=agent:main:telegram:group:<group>:topic:<topic>
2026-07-31T09:58:56.148Z prompt.submitted turnId=<active-turn>

# Multiple tool-call/result boundaries occurred while the same turn remained active.
2026-07-31T09:59:25.302Z tool.call
2026-07-31T09:59:25.308Z tool.result
...
2026-07-31T10:02:40.576Z tool.call
2026-07-31T10:02:40.759Z tool.result

2026-07-31T10:01:35.343Z [diagnostic] stuck session:
  sessionId=unknown
  sessionKey=agent:main:telegram:slash:<user>
  state=processing
  age=141s
  queueDepth=1
  reason=queued_work_without_active_run
  classification=stale_session_state
  recovery=checking

2026-07-31T10:01:35.347Z [diagnostic] stuck session recovery:
  sessionKey=agent:main:telegram:slash:<user>
  action=release_lane
  aborted=false
  drained=true
  released=0

2026-07-31T10:03:09.476Z model.completed turnId=<active-turn>
2026-07-31T10:03:09.477Z session.ended turnId=<active-turn>
2026-07-31T10:03:09.967Z session.started
2026-07-31T10:03:09.970Z prompt.submitted turnId=<new-turn>
2026-07-31T10:03:09.980Z user prompt recorded:
  CANARY-STEER: stop the current analysis and finish with exactly STEER_OK
```

The failed turn's trajectory had no `turn/steer` event between `prompt.submitted` and `session.ended`.

Sanitized control evidence for `/stop` with queue depth zero:

```text
2026-07-31T10:41:11.332Z Telegram topic prompt received
2026-07-31T10:41:22.482Z [diagnostic] lane task error:
  lane=session:agent:main:telegram:group:<group>:topic:<topic>
  error="AbortError: Reply operation aborted by user"
2026-07-31T10:41:22.817Z Telegram abort acknowledgement sent
```

## Impact and severity

- Affected surface: Telegram forum topics controlling long-running native Codex turns.
- Severity: blocks reliable mid-run correction through `/steer`; no data loss was observed.
- Frequency: reproduced in a controlled test after a gateway restart and observed in another topic during the same session.
- Consequence: guidance intended for the active run is applied only after that run has already finished, so unwanted work can continue and later control commands may encounter a stale slash lane.

## Additional information

- A gateway restart reduced process memory pressure but did not change this behavior.
- An isolated `/stop` test passed, so the evidence does not support a general `/stop` failure.
- Last known good version: `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO`.

issues.body:
## Summary

The Control UI can silently discard an explicit session refresh when a gateway event refresh fires while `sessions.list` is already in flight.

## Failure sequence

1. A session list request is in flight.
2. An explicit refresh with specific list or hydration options is queued.
3. A subsequent gateway event starts the debounced event-refresh timer.
4. The timer fires before the active request finishes.
5. The generic event refresh overwrites the explicit request in `queuedRefresh`.
6. The explicit refresh never executes.

## Impact

The session list can remain stale or incomplete because requested filters, replacement hydration, or other explicit refresh options are lost without an error.

## Expected behavior

Gateway event invalidation must not discard or replace an explicitly queued refresh request.

## Relevant code

- `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.ts:730`

issues.body:
## Summary

During a long single-turn tool-use loop (47 tool calls over 35 minutes), OpenClaw intermittently drops the **user message body** from the prompt while preserving the runtime-context metadata block. The model receives the `<<<BEGIN_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>` block (with `message_id`, `sender`, `timestamp`) but the user's actual message text is missing from the messages array. The loss is **intermittent** (visible in some iterations, not others), indicating a race condition or non-deterministic context-construction path rather than deterministic compaction or token-limit truncation.

## Environment

- **OpenClaw**: 2026.7.1-2 (npm global install)
- **Model**: `minimax/MiniMax-M3` (contextWindow: 1,000,000), via `anthropic-messages` API compat
- **Agent**: vidforge (custom workspace agent)
- **Channel**: Telegram direct message
- **OS**: WSL2 Kali Linux

## Reproduction

1. User sends a Telegram message to the agent (e.g. a multi-paragraph instruction).
2. Agent begins a tool-use loop in response (in this case: SAU video-upload to 3 platforms, which kept failing on path format + missing Chrome).
3. Agent retries the failing operation repeatedly without stopping — 47 tool calls, 35 minutes, no user interaction in between.
4. Starting around tool-call ~#10, the model's thinking shows it can no longer see the user's message body. It only sees the runtime-context metadata block saying `message_id: 3234` and the conversation history ending at the *previous* assistant turn.

## Expected behavior

The user message body must be present in the messages array on every model call within a tool-use loop. If the body cannot be included for any reason, OpenClaw should either (a) fail loudly with a prompt-construction error, or (b) inject a visible placeholder — never silently drop it while keeping the metadata block, which causes the model to hallucinate intent and continue operating blind.

## Actual behavior

The model sees the runtime-context metadata block but not the user body. Sample model thinking (verbatim, from trajectory):

> "The runtime says: `timestamp: Tue 2026-07-28 01:34:00 GMT+8`, `message_id: 3234`. So message 3234 is the user message I need to respond to NOW. But where is the content of message 3234? [...] Looking at the conversation context, the highest-numbered message I see is 3233 [...] there's NO user message body visible at all in the 01:34 message."

The model then continued operating for 28 minutes based on "inferred intent from historical hard rules", executing 40+ blind tool calls.

## Evidence

**Session file**: `~/.openclaw/agents/vidforge/sessions/<session-id>.jsonl`

- **Line 173** — user message stored **intact**: `role: user`, `content` is a string of 493 chars (the full instruction). Storage is correct.
- **Lines 174–196** — assistant turns; thinking confirms it **can** see the body ("Master said: 1. He doesn't have confidence in my export ability... 2. Immediately use SAU to upload to 3 platforms...").
- **Line 198** — first occurrence of body loss. Thinking: "message_id 3234 [...] But where is the content?"
- **Lines 202, 220, 230, 244, 251, 254, 256** — body loss recurs.
- **Line 204** — body **visible again** (intermittent, not persistent).
- **Lines 198–256** — 28 minutes of blind operation, 47 tool calls total.

**Trajectory file**: `<session-id>.trajectory.jsonl`

- `context.compiled` and `prompt.submitted` events are **truncated** by trajectory-event-size-limit (originalBytes 422089 / 348706 vs limitBytes 262144), with `droppedFields: ["prompt", "systemPrompt", "messages", ...]`. So the actual per-call prompt is not directly inspectable from trajectory — but the model's thinking across 7+ iterations consistently describes the same missing-body state.
- `model.completed` (final): `usage.input = 517577`, `usage.output = 73282`, `compactionCount = 0`, `promptErrorSource = null`.
- No `compaction` or `context.truncated` events in trajectory.

**Token budget**: 517K input << 1M contextWindow. **Not** a token-limit issue.

**Scope**: Same symptom ("消息正文没看到" / "message body not visible") appears 16 times across 2 vidforge session files. Not observed in `main` / `vidhound` / `codeanchor` agents — correlates with vidforge's long tool-use loops.

## Root cause analysis (suspected)

### Confirmed facts

1. User message is stored correctly (string content, 493 chars).
2. Body is visible in early loop iterations, lost in later ones, visible again intermittently.
3. No compaction triggered. Context well within window.
4. Runtime-context **metadata block** is preserved on every call; only the user **body** disappears.

### Suspected mechanism

In `internal-runtime-context-BW7WOTKc.js`:

- The runtime context is carried as a `role: "custom"` message (`openclaw.runtime-context` customType).
- Before each model call, OpenClaw runs `stripHistoricalRuntimeContextCustomMessages` (keeps only current-turn carriers adjacent to the last user message) and `relocateCurrentRuntimeContextCarrierToTail` (moves carriers to the absolute tail for prompt-cache optimization).

Hypothesis: under a large messages array (47 accumulated tool-call/tool-result pairs) combined with the **Anthropic Messages API compatibility layer** for MiniMax-M3, this carrier-relocation + user-message-content (string type, not array-of-blocks) handling intermittently drops the user body from the serialized request. The metadata carrier survives because it's explicitly tracked; the plain `role: user` + string `content` is not.

This is a hypothesis — confirmable by adding a per-call prompt dump (not truncated) and checking whether the user message is present in the actual HTTP request body sent to the model API on the failing iterations.

## Impact

- **Token waste**: 517K input + 73K output = ~590K tokens consumed in a single blind loop.
- **Wrong actions**: agent operated for 28 minutes on inferred intent without seeing the actual instruction — risk of executing commands the user never asked for.
- **User experience**: user observed the agent reporting "message body not visible" and continuing to act anyway, eroding trust.

## Workaround (applied)

Added three guardrail rules to the agent's `AGENTS.md` (always-loaded bootstrap file):

1. **Body-loss → immediate stop**: if runtime-context metadata is present but user body is not, halt the tool loop and report to the user. Do not infer intent from history.
2. **3-strike retry cap**: any operation failing 3 consecutive times → stop, report last error, wait for user instruction.
3. **15 tool-call soft cap per turn**: pause and report progress before continuing.

These are behavioral mitigations on the agent side; they do not fix the underlying context-construction bug.

## Suggested fix (upstream)

1. **Never silently drop user body**: if the user message content is empty/missing during prompt construction, raise a `promptErrorSource` instead of sending a bodyless prompt.
2. **Per-call prompt integrity check**: assert that the active user message has non-empty content before each model call in a tool-use loop.
3. **Investigate the interaction** between `relocateCurrentRuntimeContextCarrierToTail` + string-typed user content + Anthropic-Messages compat serialization on long tool-use loops.
4. **Optional**: allow a configurable `maxToolRounds` per agent to bound tool-use loop length and prevent the 47-call scenario from arising.

## Repro artifacts

Can provide the full session `.jsonl` (259 lines, ~1.3MB) and trajectory `.jsonl` (84 events, ~1.8MB) on request. Key line numbers cited above.

issues.body:
## Summary
Memory Wiki ChatGPT rollback unconditionally deletes or overwrites conversation pages even when the user edited them after the import. Rolling back an import can therefore silently destroy newer user-authored memory content with no recovery copy.

## Environment
- Commit: 9e8cc6fe8a6f516bc8d4d976f3132b79a108457a (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: Memory Wiki ChatGPT import rollback, exposed as `openclaw wiki chatgpt rollback <run-id>`

## Steps to reproduce
1. Run `openclaw wiki chatgpt import --export <export-path>` so a conversation page is created.
2. Edit the created page and add a user-authored note.
3. Run `openclaw wiki chatgpt rollback <run-id>`.
4. Observe that the entire page, including the newer note, is deleted.
5. The overwrite branch can be reproduced by importing once, importing changed conversation content so the existing page is updated, editing that page again, and then rolling back the second import. The edit made after the second import is replaced by the old pre-import content.

## Expected
Rollback must not delete or overwrite a page whose current content differs from the content written by that import. It should refuse the conflicting page or preserve its current content in a recovery location before changing it.

## Actual
Every path recorded as created is force-deleted, and every path recorded as updated is overwritten with its pre-import copy. There is no current-content comparison, output hash, conflict check, or backup of edits made after import.

## Root cause (if known)
`writeTrackedImportPage` records only a path for created pages and only a path plus the pre-import copy for updated pages:

```ts
if (!params.existing) {
  await fs.writeFile(absolutePath, params.rendered, "utf8");
  params.record.createdPaths.push(params.relativePath);
  return "create";
}
// ...
params.record.updatedPaths.push({
  path: params.relativePath,
  snapshotPath: snapshotRelativePath,
});
```

`rollbackChatGptImportRun` then deletes and restores those paths unconditionally:

```ts
for (const relativePath of record.createdPaths) {
  await fs
    .rm(path.join(params.config.vault.path, relativePath), { force: true })
    .catch(() => undefined);
  removedCount += 1;
}
// ...
for (const entry of record.updatedPaths) {
  // ...
  await fs.writeFile(targetPath, snapshot, "utf8");
  restoredCount += 1;
}
```

Current locations are `extensions/memory-wiki/src/chatgpt-import.ts:697-725` and `extensions/memory-wiki/src/chatgpt-import.ts:864-905`.

The CLI routes directly to this function at `extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.ts:944-959`, and registers the public rollback command at `extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.ts:1209-1221`.

The import-run record does not store a hash of the content written by the import. Rollback therefore cannot distinguish an untouched imported page from a page changed later by the user or another operation.

## Sibling surfaces
Both rollback record branches are affected:

- `createdPaths`: the current page is removed in full, including all later edits.
- `updatedPaths`: the current page is replaced by the pre-import copy, including removal of all later edits.

The nearest existing reports are distinct. #102230 and #102294 cover pruning imported source pages and salvaging their human Notes blocks. #99708 covers `$` replacement expansion during ChatGPT re-import. None covers rollback acting on pages modified after the import.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: ChatGPT import rollback destroys user edits made after the import.
Real environment tested: Real `importChatGptConversations` and `rollbackChatGptImportRun` production functions against real on-disk vaults at commit 9e8cc6fe8a6f516bc8d4d976f3132b79a108457a.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: No patch was applied. Ran `FS_SAFE_NATIVE_MODE=off node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/chatgpt-rollback-user-edits/repro.mts` from the repository checkout.
Evidence after fix:
```text
# OBSERVED (buggy, origin/main 9e8cc6fe8a6f516bc8d4d976f3132b79a108457a)
CREATED-PAGE BRANCH
user edit present before rollback: true
rollback removedCount: 1
page exists after rollback: false
user edit recoverable after rollback: false

UPDATED-PAGE BRANCH
second import updatedCount: 1
user edit present before rollback: true
rollback restoredCount: 1
user edit present after rollback: false
pre-second-import content restored: true

# EXPECTED (correct behavior on identical inputs)
CREATED-PAGE BRANCH
page retained or current content moved to recovery
user edit recoverable after rollback: true

UPDATED-PAGE BRANCH
stale restore refused or current content moved to recovery
user edit recoverable after rollback: true
```
Observed result after fix: On pinned main, both rollback branches remove content written after the import and leave no recovery copy.
What was not tested: The proof drove the exported production functions rather than the CLI wrapper. The CLI is covered by the repository at `extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.test.ts:716-784` and calls the same rollback function directly. No concurrent multi-process writer was involved.

issues.body:
## Summary
The Ollama memory provider currently supports batch embeddings at the client level, but the OpenClaw memory adapter does not surface a `batchEmbed` runtime method. As a result, the memory manager treats batch mode as unavailable and keeps `batch.enabled` off even when the configuration explicitly enables it.

## Impact
- Batch indexing cannot be enabled reliably for Ollama-backed memory setups.
- The configuration is misleading because `batch.enabled = true` does not become effective unless the adapter exposes batch capability.
- Local deployments on resource-constrained hardware are forced into single-item embedding mode even when Ollama can handle batched requests.

## Current behavior
- The Ollama adapter returns a memory runtime with provider metadata and cache key data.
- The memory manager only enables batch mode when the provider runtime exposes `batchEmbed`.
- The Ollama embedding client already supports `embedBatch`, but that capability is not forwarded by the adapter runtime.

## Expected behavior
If the configured Ollama embedding backend supports batched embeddings, the Ollama memory adapter should expose a `batchEmbed` runtime implementation so the memory manager can enable batch mode when configuration allows it.

## Proposed fix
- Add `batchEmbed` to the Ollama memory adapter runtime.
- Forward the chunk texts to the Ollama embedding client's `embedBatch` implementation.
- Add a regression test that verifies the adapter exposes `batchEmbed` and calls the underlying batch client with the expected texts.

## Verification notes
A targeted provider-lane test was added locally to confirm the adapter bridge works as expected, and the batch capability becomes visible to the memory manager once the runtime method is present.

## Acceptance criteria
- `batch.enabled` can become `true` for Ollama-backed memory when batch is enabled in config.
- The adapter forwards batched chunk texts to the Ollama client.
- A regression test covers the adapter bridge.
- The change does not alter non-batch Ollama embedding behavior.

issues.body:
## Summary
On macOS, a Gateway service environment value that contains a newline (for example a PEM private key from `~/.openclaw/.env` or config env vars) is written correctly to the generated LaunchAgent env file at install time, but the next `openclaw gateway restart` truncates it. The restart rewrite rereads the env file with the lenient reader, keeps only the first physical line of the value plus a stray leading `'`, and republishes that. After the restart the Gateway receives `'-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` instead of the full key. The same lenient read backs the service `readCommand` that install and repair flows use to preserve existing environment, so a reinstall can carry the truncated value forward.

This supersedes PR #164668, which proposed a fix and is being closed in favor of tracking the defect here.

## Environment
- Commit: 4a62f40a58d9995f076525b3b82fcf0aed3da464 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: macOS LaunchAgent Gateway service (`src/daemon/launchd-plist.ts`, `readLaunchAgentEnvironmentFile`)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Install a Gateway LaunchAgent whose service environment includes a multi-line value, for example `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY` set to a three-line PEM block.
2. Inspect `~/.openclaw/service-env/<label>.env`: the value is written as one single-quoted shell literal spanning three lines, which is correct.
3. Run `openclaw gateway restart` (which calls `rewriteLaunchAgentPlistForRestart` before kickstarting launchd).
4. Inspect the env file again, or source it with `/bin/sh` and print the variable.

## Expected
The restart rewrite reads the multi-line literal back byte for byte and republishes the same value. The Gateway receives the full three-line key.

## Actual
The env file is rewritten to `export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY=''\''-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----'`. The Gateway receives `'-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`. The service `readCommand` already reports the truncated value before the rewrite.

## Root cause (if known)
`src/daemon/launchd-plist.ts`, `readLaunchAgentEnvironmentFile` (lines 157-188 on 4a62f40a58). The writer (`quoteLaunchAgentEnvironmentValue`) emits a single-quoted literal that spans physical lines when the value contains a newline, but only the strict `requireEffective` branch joins continuation lines:

```ts
const line = options?.requireEffective ? rawLine.trimStart() : rawLine.trim();
...
let parsedValue = parseGeneratedEnvValue(value);
if (options?.requireEffective) {
  // The writer's quoted literals can span physical lines; retain their exact newline bytes.
  while (
    quoteLaunchAgentEnvironmentValue(parsedValue) !== value.trim() &&
    index + 1 < lines.length
  ) {
    value += `\n${lines[++index]}`;
    parsedValue = parseGeneratedEnvValue(value);
  }
  ...
}
environment[key] = parsedValue;
```

Without `requireEffective`, `export KEY='line1` is parsed alone: `parseGeneratedEnvValue` sees an opening quote with no closing quote and returns `'line1` verbatim, and the remaining lines of the literal are skipped as unrecognized syntax. `rewriteLaunchAgentPlistForRestart` (`src/daemon/launchd-service-files.ts:471`) reads with these lenient options and republishes the env file from the result, so the truncation becomes durable. The lenient branch also uses `trim()` on the first line, which would drop whitespace that sits inside the literal at the end of its first line.

A fix needs the lenient path to join continuation lines while the literal is still inside an open single quote (POSIX `sh` rules, so the writer's `'\''` escape stays balanced), without letting a hand-edited unquoted line such as `export A=$(id)` swallow the following lines.

## Sibling surfaces
All callers of the lenient reader are affected: `rewriteLaunchAgentPlistForRestart` (`openclaw gateway restart` and bootstrap repair), `readLaunchAgentProgramArguments` (service `readCommand` used by install and repair to preserve env, status, doctor), and `launchd-update-jobs.ts:141`. The strict `requireEffective` path already handles multi-line literals. Checked systemd and Windows Scheduled Task: unaffected, because their writers reject CR/LF in env values at write time (`assertNoSystemdLineBreaks`, `assertNoCmdLineBreak`), so only the macOS path can store a multi-line value.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: on macOS, the LaunchAgent restart rewrite truncates any multi-line service environment value to its first line with a stray leading quote.
Real environment tested: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0), Node 26.9.0, origin/main 4a62f40a58. A standalone tsx driver calls the real production `writeLaunchAgentPlist` (install writer), `readLaunchAgentProgramArguments` (service readCommand), and `rewriteLaunchAgentPlistForRestart` (the restart rewrite step), with a throwaway HOME and OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and an isolated profile label (`ai.openclaw.issue164668`). Real filesystem, the written plist validated with real `/usr/bin/plutil`, and real `/bin/sh` sourcing of the rewritten env file. Nothing stubbed. The EXPECTED run used the identical driver and inputs on the same commit with only `src/daemon/launchd-plist.ts` patched to join continuation lines in the lenient path (the change proposed in #164668).
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `WT=<tree> node --import tsx drive.mts` from each tree. The driver installs a LaunchAgent definition with `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY` set to a three-line PEM-style value, reads it back via the service readCommand, runs the restart rewrite, then sources the rewritten env file with `/bin/sh` and prints the value the Gateway would receive.
Evidence after fix:
```
# OBSERVED (buggy, origin/main 4a62f40a58)
env file after install:
  export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY='-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
  MIIEvQIBADANBg
  -----END PRIVATE KEY-----'
service readCommand SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY = "'-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----"
env file after restart rewrite:
  export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY=''\''-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----'
value the gateway receives after restart = "'-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----"
value preserved: false
# EXPECTED (same commit, lenient reader joins the quoted literal, identical inputs)
env file after install:
  export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY='-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
  MIIEvQIBADANBg
  -----END PRIVATE KEY-----'
service readCommand SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY = "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIEvQIBADANBg\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----"
env file after restart rewrite:
  export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY='-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
  MIIEvQIBADANBg
  -----END PRIVATE KEY-----'
value the gateway receives after restart = "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIEvQIBADANBg\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----"
value preserved: true
```
Observed result after fix: on current main the install writes the multi-line value correctly, but the readCommand and the restart rewrite reduce it to `'-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`, which is what the Gateway would receive after restart.
What was not tested: no full `openclaw gateway restart` against a live launchd job (no `launchctl kickstart` or `bootstrap`), only the file rewrite step it performs before those calls. Linux and Windows service paths were not run because their writers reject multi-line values.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Durable outbound recovery re-runs modifying plugin hooks against the original pre-policy payload, so a recovered delivery can bypass an earlier cancellation/redaction or repeat hook side effects.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Register a modifying `message_sending` hook whose result can differ between calls.
2. Start a durable outbound delivery with content that the hook cancels or rewrites.
3. Preserve the pending queue row by inducing either an acknowledgement failure after pre-send cancellation or a proven pre-dispatch provider failure after rewrite.
4. Recover the pending outbound row.
5. Observe that recovery invokes the modifier again against the original payload and can produce a different delivery decision.

Focused Testbox reproduction demonstrated both cases:

- a cancelled first attempt became a visible send during recovery;
- a first redaction was replaced by a different second redaction during recovery.

### Expected behavior

Modifying hooks run once per logical durable payload. The queue stores the accepted post-policy payload and recovery delivers that exact prepared payload without re-running modifiers.

### Actual behavior

The `outbound` queue stores the original pre-hook payload and serialized reply-hook context. Recovery rebuilds the normal delivery call from that row, which invokes `reply_payload_sending` and `message_sending` again.

### OpenClaw version

Current `main` at `d1d2ad707bfd77caa0e3f827f272af4daa353d88`; reproduced on `12b9e7c683a9ba92a401229e2be5f0ec6178379f`. The intervening 24 commits do not touch the affected queue, hook, state, durable-message, or durable-turn paths.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (Blacksmith Testbox)

### Install method

Source checkout with repository-pinned Node/pnpm

### Model

Not applicable; the reproduction exercises the durable outbound lifecycle directly.

### Provider / routing chain

Core durable outbound delivery with the Matrix adapter boundary used as the deterministic provider seam.

### Logs and evidence

- Testbox Actions run `30576047063`: current modifier-rerun reproduction 3/3 and corrected migration/crash model 6/6 passed.
- Testbox Actions run `30576573736`: typed migration/crash model 6/6, permanent stable-suppression receipt 1/1, and real modifying-hook timeout/fail-open behavior 1/1 passed.
- Testbox Actions run `30577275139`: same-schema pre-change reader isolation plus actual release-tag fail-closed rollback behavior passed 4/4.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any channel using the shared durable outbound queue with modifying hooks.
- Severity: high policy/integrity risk in a rare recovery window.
- Frequency: requires a retained queue row after policy evaluation, such as acknowledgement failure or a proven pre-dispatch provider failure.
- Consequence: content previously cancelled or redacted can be reconsidered under changed plugin/config state, and arbitrary modifier side effects can run twice.

### Accepted fix boundary

- Prepare one typed post-policy batch before canonical enqueue.
- Persist no pre-policy payload or serialized modifying-hook context in the canonical queue.
- Recover the exact prepared batch without invoking modifiers.
- Migrate existing pending rows with async preparation followed by an authoritative synchronous SQLite compare-and-move.
- Isolate the new prepared namespace from the same-schema pre-change reader and preserve stable producer ownership with terminal fences.
- Move best-effort `message_sent` observation after logical queue settlement; add no durable plugin outbox or public SDK identity.
- Exclude provider replay identity and Matrix transaction-id work from this issue.

issues.body:
## Summary

When any edit in an `edit` call falls back to fuzzy matching, the tool rewrites the entire matched line from a Unicode-normalized copy of the file. Every character on that line that sits outside the requested `oldText` span is silently replaced with its NFKC / quote / dash / space folded form on disk, and the tool still reports plain success.

This is the residual of the closed P0 #89994 ("Bug: a fuzzy edit silently normalizes and rewrites unrelated lines across the whole file", closed as completed on 2026-07-10). The fix that landed for it (`applyReplacementsPreservingUnchangedLines`, introduced in 5ea80c8d80 / #99949) narrowed the blast radius from the whole file down to the touched lines, but it restores original bytes at LINE granularity only. It did not implement that issue's own stated fix direction of normalizing only the matched substring and leaving untouched bytes identical. #89994 is scoped by its title to unrelated lines across the whole file, which excludes the matched line itself, so this is the unimplemented remainder rather than a reopen or a duplicate.

## Environment

- Commit: 9e8cc6fe8a6f516bc8d4d976f3132b79a108457a (origin/main at time of filing). `src/agents/sessions/tools/` is byte-identical between 90a22b4f50 and this commit, so the observed run pins to the same code.
- Surface: `edit` tool in the coding tool set, with `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` both true and false. Reached through `createOpenClawCodingTools` -> the `tool.name === "edit"` branch in `src/agents/agent-tools.ts:715-724` -> `createHostWorkspaceEditTool` (`src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:933`) -> `createEditToolDefinition` (`src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.ts:391`).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a file whose line contains a character the model is likely to retype as ASCII, plus other non-ASCII content elsewhere on the same line. The gap in `RETRY MAX` below is U+00A0:

```
export const RETRY MAX = 3; // 再試行（最大３回）ｱｲｳ — 設定
export const OTHER = 1;
```

2. Call the `edit` tool with `oldText` copied back using a plain space instead of the U+00A0, which is exactly the case the fuzzy fallback exists to absorb:

```json
{ "path": "config.ts", "edits": [{ "oldText": "export const RETRY MAX = 3;", "newText": "export const RETRY_MAX = 5;" }] }
```

3. Read the file back from disk and compare the code points of the trailing comment, which no part of the request referenced.

## Expected

Only the bytes covered by the matched `oldText` span change. Everything else on the line, including the full-width parentheses, the full-width digit, the half-width katakana and the em dash in the comment, stays byte-identical, exactly as it does when the same edit takes the exact-match path.

## Actual

The tool returns `Successfully replaced 1 block(s)` and writes the whole line back from the normalized copy. On disk: U+FF08 and U+FF09 become `(` and `)`, U+FF13 becomes `3`, U+FF71 U+FF72 U+FF73 become U+30A2 U+30A4 U+30A6, and U+2014 becomes `-`. None of those characters appear in `oldText` or `newText`.

The same folding applies to smart quotes, the other Unicode dashes, NBSP and narrow NBSP and ideographic space, ligatures, circled and enclosed forms, fraction and unit characters, and trailing whitespace, because the base is the whole file passed through `normalizeForFuzzyMatch`. In source files this silently changes string literals, regex literals and fixture bytes on any line a fuzzy edit happens to touch.

## Root cause

`src/agents/sessions/tools/edit-diff.ts:361-364` picks the replacement base:

```ts
const usedFuzzyMatch = initialMatches.some((match) => match.usedFuzzyMatch);
const replacementBaseContent = usedFuzzyMatch
  ? normalizeForFuzzyMatch(normalizedContent)
  : normalizedContent;
```

`normalizeForFuzzyMatch` (`edit-diff.ts:26`) runs the WHOLE file through NFKC, per-line `trimEnd`, and smart-quote / dash / space folding. One edit anywhere in the call that needs the fuzzy fallback switches the base for every edit in that call.

The two restoration helpers, `applyReplacementsPreservingUnchangedLines` (`src/agents/sessions/tools/edit-replacements.ts:97-128`) and `applyReplacementsPreservingLineEndings` (`:166-240`), then restore original bytes only for lines the match does not overlap. Any line the match does overlap is emitted wholesale from the normalized copy:

```ts
result += originalLines.slice(originalLineIndex, group.startLine).join("");
...
result += applyReplacements(
  baseContent.slice(groupStartOffset, lastLine.end),
  group.replacements,
  groupStartOffset,
);
```

`src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.ts:460-465` then writes that content to disk.

The trigger is the fuzzy fallback's designed case, not an exotic input. The model copies `oldText` back with a plain space where the file has U+00A0, or a straight quote where the file has a smart quote. That is the normal reason fuzzy matching exists, so the collateral fires routinely.

Honest note on visibility: the diff returned to the model does render the corrupted line as a whole-line minus/plus pair, so the collateral is technically present in the diff text. It is indistinguishable from the intended change, no warning is emitted, and the tool result is plain success.

## Suggested fix direction

Keep matching in fuzzy space but splice at byte granularity. Carry the fuzzy match's `index` and `matchLength` back to the original `normalizedContent`. The normalizations are all per-character or per-line-suffix, so a normalized-to-original offset map is derivable in the same pass as `normalizeForFuzzyMatch`. Applying replacements against `normalizedContent` would then delete both `applyReplacementsPreservingUnchangedLines` and the line-count guards, because untouched bytes would never be rebuilt in the first place.

## Sibling surfaces

- `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` true and false both reproduce identically, driven live.
- The sandboxed variant `createSandboxedEditTool` shares the same `createEditToolDefinition` core, so it inherits the same base selection.
- `apply_patch` had a different but adjacent defect (#116124, closed, fixed by merged #116128). That fix lives in the apply_patch hunk-application path and does not touch the `edit` fuzzy base selection.
- Merged #116011 fixed line endings on lines `edit` did not touch. It preserves terminators, not the character content of touched lines, so it does not cover this.

## Novelty

- #89994 is closed as completed. Its landed fix narrowed whole-file to touched-lines and stopped there. Its title scopes it to unrelated lines across the whole file; this report is about the matched line itself.
- PRs #99573, #96636, #96814 and #90060 all attempted the region-scoped fix and are all closed unmerged.
- `git log --oneline -20 -- src/agents/sessions/tools/` shows the two most recent adjacent fixes are #116011 and #115738; neither touches this path.
- No open pull request touches `edit-diff.ts` or `edit-replacements.ts`. #115993 is the only open pull request touching `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit*`; it changes no-op mutation handling in `edit.ts` and does not reference `normalizeForFuzzyMatch`, `replacementBaseContent`, or either restoration helper.

## Real behavior proof

issues.body:
## Summary

When `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode` is set to `"non-main"`, sub-agents spawned via `sessions_spawn` fail to initialize. Sessions are accepted (return valid `childSessionKey` and `runId`) but never start executing — zero tokens, zero messages, no transcript files created. **No errors appear in gateway logs.**

## Environment

- OpenClaw Version: 2026.3.2 (85377a2)
- OS: macOS 15.3.0 (Apple Silicon, arm64)
- Node: v25.8.0
- Docker Desktop: running (coding agent sandbox works fine)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode: "non-main"` in config
2. Restart gateway
3. From main agent, spawn a sub-agent:
   ```
   sessions_spawn(task="Reply with: test", model="sonnet")
   ```
4. Check `sessions_history` or `subagents list` after 30+ seconds

## Expected Behavior

Sub-agent starts within seconds, `systemSent: true`, tokens accumulate, task completes.

## Actual Behavior

- `sessions_spawn` returns `status: "accepted"` with valid session key
- Sub-agent appears in `subagents list` as `running`
- `sessions_history` returns `messages: []` indefinitely
- No transcript file created on disk
- `systemSent` never set to `true`
- `totalTokens` never set
- **Zero error output in gateway logs**
- Eventually times out via `runTimeoutSeconds`

## Bisect Results

Systematically tested with a simple one-line task (`Reply with exactly: ...`):

| Test | sandbox.mode | Docker settings | Result |
|------|-------------|----------------|--------|
| 1 | non-main | network: bridge, readOnlyRoot: true | stall |
| 2 | non-main | network: bridge, readOnlyRoot: false | stall |
| 3 | **off** | (same as test 2) | **works (4s)** |
| 4 | non-main | minimal (image + workdir only) | stall |

The issue is **not** caused by specific Docker settings (network, readOnlyRoot, tmpfs). Any `sandbox.mode` that enables Docker for subagents causes silent failure.

## Notes

- **Cron isolated sessions work fine** with `sandbox.mode: "non-main"` on the same config — they appear to use a different code path that bypasses container initialization.
- **Per-agent sandbox overrides are unaffected**: a coding agent with `sandbox.mode: "all"` and its own Docker settings works correctly.
- Possibly related to #5813 (similar symptoms, different attributed cause).
- The silent failure with zero log output makes this very difficult to diagnose.

## Workaround

Set `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode: "off"` and use per-agent `sandbox.mode: "all"` overrides for agents that specifically need sandboxing (e.g., coding agents with `tools.exec.host: "sandbox"`).

issues.body:
## Summary

Select GitHub Copilot's fresh-onboarding starter model from the authenticated account's usable live catalog instead of persisting a static model that can be disabled by plan or organization policy.

## Reproduction on current `main`

At `2b639649b317c2866edc37b274981581d8284c1a`, the bundled provider configured `github-copilot/claude-opus-5` during fresh non-interactive onboarding. The authenticated account's live Copilot catalog returned that model as picker-visible but policy-disabled. The immediately following ordinary local agent turn failed twice with HTTP 400 `model_not_supported`.

This is concrete setup breakage: the GitHub credential and subscription were valid, and the same catalog exposed other policy-enabled chat models with streaming and tool-call support, including `claude-sonnet-5`.

## Root cause

Fresh interactive and non-interactive auth returned one static starter without validating it against the authenticated catalog. The existing live catalog parser read `model_picker_enabled` but ignored it and the account's `policy.state`, so disabled or internal rows could also remain visible in model selection.

GitHub documents that Copilot model availability varies by client, plan, and organization policy and can change over time. A static starter is therefore a preference, not proof that the account can use it.

## Fix contract

Keep the decision provider-owned and reuse the existing authenticated catalog path:

1. Treat the provider's current general-purpose model (`claude-sonnet-5`) as a preference only.
2. Use it only when the authenticated catalog marks it picker-visible, policy-enabled, streaming-capable, and tool-capable.
3. Otherwise choose a deterministic eligible fallback: non-preview first, then the provider's picker category (`versatile`, `lightweight`, `powerful`), larger context/output limits, and finally model id.
4. Hide picker-disabled and policy-disabled/unconfigured rows from the visible live catalog, while preserving request-time resolution for an explicitly configured model.
5. Fail fresh non-interactive setup before writing a new auth profile if no eligible default can be selected.
6. Retain a valid interactive credential if catalog discovery is transiently unavailable and let the model picker/manual selection recover.
7. Never replace an existing explicit default. There is no persisted provenance that can safely distinguish a former provider-generated default from a user selection, so no runtime shim or doctor migration is included.
8. For app-guided manual-secret setup, temporarily remove an unrelated existing primary from the provider input so the verified dynamic candidate is returned; the original config remains the activation merge base.

## Alternatives considered

- Another unconditional static default repeats the same account-policy failure mode.
- Copilot SDK `model: "auto"` is not a drop-in direct-provider model. Live SDK proof showed that it uses a session-scoped `Copilot-Session-Token` and may select the underlying wire protocol; routing it through OpenClaw's direct provider would be a separate, larger transport change.
- Upstream response order is not a deterministic product contract.
- Hiding every model without tools/streaming would regress valid explicit chat-only choices, so those capabilities constrain only automatic defaults.

## Validation plan

- Reordered, policy-limited, hidden, preview, capability-limited, and empty catalog fixtures.
- Fresh non-interactive onboarding followed by an ordinary Copilot turn.
- Retained-auth onboarding and a second turn without ambient credential injection.
- Existing explicit model preservation and inference.
- Live catalog visibility plus request-time explicit-model resolution.
- Focused provider/auth contract tests, changed checks, pre-commit review, and PR CI.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Evidence

- Provider setup: `extensions/github-copilot/index.ts`
- Live catalog: `extensions/github-copilot/dynamic-models.ts`, `extensions/github-copilot/models.ts`
- GitHub supported-model and policy documentation: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/ai-models/supported-models
- Official Copilot SDK model contract and live `auto` probe were inspected before choosing the direct-provider design.
- Prior related catalog work: #75349, #79566, #113681.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When legacy Voice Wake JSON differs from already-canonical shared SQLite rows, every Gateway startup repeats the same migration warning and exits with code 1; `openclaw doctor --fix` reruns the same non-converging branch and cannot repair it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Write canonical Voice Wake triggers and routing into shared SQLite through the runtime setters.
2. Create `settings/voicewake.json` and/or `settings/voicewake-routing.json` with different values.
3. Run Gateway startup so startup state migrations execute.
4. Observe the migration warning and startup refusal. Repeat startup or run `openclaw doctor --fix`; the legacy files remain, so the same state is rediscovered.

### Expected behavior

SQLite is the canonical store after import. Migration/doctor should preserve its rows and retire the conflicting legacy JSON so the next startup does not rediscover the conflict.

### Actual behavior

`migrateLegacyVoiceWakeSettings` leaves conflicting legacy files in place and returns a warning. Gateway startup treats any migration warning as a hard refusal, while doctor records the warning but has no conflict-resolution path. The state therefore cannot converge without manual file deletion/editing.

### OpenClaw version

Current `main` at `67ef07863fbb24d751e20f022e216118924ae15d`; reproduced in a focused regression against that source. The defect was also verified at `b680843eb7570b427439555978f46ac38404f27f`.

### Operating system

Linux (source-level regression test using an isolated temporary state directory and shared SQLite database).

### Install method

Source checkout.

### Model

N/A (state migration fails before model execution).

### Provider / routing chain

N/A.

### Additional provider/model setup details

N/A.

### Logs

```text
Left legacy voice wake triggers in place because shared SQLite state already has different triggers: <stateDir>/settings/voicewake.json
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- `src/infra/state-migrations.runtime-state.ts`: conflicting trigger/routing branches leave `shouldArchive` false.
- `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts`: startup accumulates migration warnings and throws `ExitError(1)` before readiness.
- Focused regression constructs divergent legacy JSON and SQLite data and verifies the legacy source must be archived without changing SQLite.

### Impact and severity

Affected: installations carrying legacy Voice Wake JSON plus already-populated shared SQLite state.

Severity: High; Gateway readiness is blocked.

Frequency: deterministic whenever the two stores differ.

Consequence: repeated startup failure with no converging `doctor --fix` repair; manual state-file intervention is required.

### Additional information

The storage contract makes SQLite canonical after import. The bounded fix is to preserve SQLite and archive the legacy source; archive failures remain migration warnings so startup still fails closed when cleanup actually cannot complete.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect ownership/state without a crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Android phone and Wear device work can remain bound to stale Activity, permission, route, or realtime-channel owners during lifecycle transitions, causing dropped callbacks, stale commands, or interrupted audio.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the Android Play app and paired Wear app from a source checkout.
2. Start a share or permission-gated device action, then recreate or replace the foreground Activity before the result returns.
3. For Wear, reconnect or replace a route/realtime channel while an earlier route generation or audio frame is still active.
4. Observe the callback, command, or frame being handled by a stale owner, or the active operation being interrupted.

The audit also reproduced adjacent Android build/proof defects: benchmark variant selection, stale cron copy, non-configured SDK selection, and performance scripts installing a non-specific app variant.

### Expected behavior

Device work remains attached to the current retained owner across Activity recreation. Permission results reach the current host, stale Wear routes cannot act, and reconnecting a realtime channel does not interrupt an in-flight frame. Android build and benchmark tooling should select deterministic configured variants and SDK tools.

### Actual behavior

Activity-owned waiters and last-resumed host selection could strand callbacks after recreation or split-screen transitions. Wear route and realtime ownership could be replaced by stale generations or transport arrival order. A same-path reconnect could close the stream beneath a frame already selected for delivery.

### OpenClaw version

Source checkout based on `db4ad84d7f0b22664f65a2e98a73a8cdd599f7b7`.

### Operating system

Android 16 / API 36 emulator; Wear OS emulator for visual route checks.

### Install method

Source checkout using Gradle debug builds.

### Model

N/A - device lifecycle and transport behavior is model-independent.

### Provider / routing chain

N/A - device lifecycle and transport behavior is model-independent.

### Logs

No secret-bearing logs are required. Focused regression tests reproduce the ownership races deterministically.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Full Android matrix: 273 tasks, including Play and third-party unit tests, phone/Wear assemblies, lint, and ktlint.
- Connected Play instrumentation: 6/6 on API 36.
- Connected benchmark instrumentation: 3/3 on API 36.
- Phone routes visually checked: home, chat, settings, gateway, and voice wake.
- Wear routes visually checked: chat, voice, and controls.
- Fresh aggregate autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Android phone and paired Wear users during Activity recreation, split-screen/top-resumed changes, route replacement, or realtime reconnect.

Severity: Medium to high. The edge cases can drop permission/share completion, execute stale Wear actions, or interrupt active talk audio.

Frequency: Transition-dependent and deterministic under the covered race tests.

Consequence: Device actions can fail or target stale state even though the current UI and connection appear active.

### Additional information

The proposed fix keeps long-lived ownership in retained runtime state, uses generation/attempt identities for Wear operations, serializes channel retirement with selected writes, and adds focused regression coverage plus exact-head device proof.

issues.body:
### Summary

A concurrent Codex WebSocket request can clobber the shared session cache during the acquire path's `connectWebSocket()` await, orphaning the socket that carries the real `previous_response_id` continuation and corrupting multi-turn Codex conversations. A prior fix (#105634 / `4b09214866b`) added owner-checked delete to the **release** path but the **acquire** path still used unconditional `delete`/`set`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. With a cached Codex WebSocket session (transport `websocket-cached`, fixed `sessionId`), trigger an acquire where the cached entry is expired (`connection_age_limit`, ≥55min) or non-reusable (server closed).
2. The acquire path (`acquireWebSocket` in `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts`) does `delete(sessionId)`, then `await connectWebSocket(...)`, then `set(sessionId, entry)` — all unconditional.
3. During that `await`, a concurrent request B sees the empty cache, opens its own socket, and installs a busy entry carrying the live `lastResponseId` continuation.
4. The first acquire resumes and its unconditional `set` overwrites B's entry. The cache now points at the first acquire's socket; B's socket (with the real continuation) is orphaned.
5. The next request reuses the wrong entry: it sends a missing or stale `previous_response_id`, losing multi-turn context or continuing from the wrong branch.

### Expected behavior

The acquire path should use the same owner-checked cache mutation as the release path (already fixed in #105634): only delete its own entry, and only install when no concurrent request installed a newer entry during the await.

### Actual behavior

The acquire path's `delete`/`set` around `connectWebSocket()` are unconditional (`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts`, acquire branch ~lines 1170-1209), so a concurrent install is clobbered. The release path and idle-expiry already use `deleteOwnedWebSocketSession`; the acquire path does not.

### OpenClaw version

Source-review against `main`. Not a regression of a specific version; the acquire path was not covered by #105634's owner-checked fix.

### Operating system

Platform-independent (WebSocket session cache).

### Install method

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (source-review finding; any Codex WebSocket-cached transport install is affected).

### Model

OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT Responses (transport `websocket-cached`).

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openai (ChatGPT Responses WebSocket).

### Impact and severity

Concurrent Codex requests plus a cache expiry/non-reusable boundary corrupt multi-turn conversation continuation (`previous_response_id`): later turns lose context, answer wrong, or continue from a wrong branch. Reachable in high-frequency or long-session scenarios (55min connection-age boundary + concurrency). Core runtime data-integrity issue.

### Logs

`git show main:packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` acquire path:

```
// idle-expired (unconditional delete)
if (!cached.busy && isWebSocketSessionExpired(cached)) {
  websocketSessionCache.delete(sessionId);   // unconditional
}
// not-reusable (unconditional delete)
if (!isWebSocketReusable(cached.socket)) {
  websocketSessionCache.delete(sessionId);   // unconditional
}
// post-await (unconditional set clobbers concurrent B)
const socket = await connectWebSocket(url, headers, signal);
websocketSessionCache.set(sessionId, entry); // unconditional
```

Release path already fixed (same file): `deleteOwnedWebSocketSession(sessionId, cached)` (owner-checked). The acquire path's sibling fix is missing.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Each agent turn writes the full conversation state into the runtime trajectory three times: `context.compiled` records `messages` + `systemPrompt` (its job), `prompt.submitted` re-inlines the same `messages` + `systemPrompt` next to the actual `prompt`, and `model.completed` re-inlines it again as `messagesSnapshot`.

The duplicates push heavy-turn events past `TRAJECTORY_RUNTIME_EVENT_MAX_BYTES` (256 KB), and oversize truncation replaces the whole `data` block (preserving only `usage`/`promptCache` since #96811). The user's `prompt` dies with it, and unlike the duplicated history it has no other source in the trajectory: the surrounding events and the transcript carry the history, but subagent sessions write no plain transcript, so their prompts are unrecoverable.

On 2026.6.1, `prompt.submitted` did not inline conversation history: 0 truncated prompts in 3,218 events on one long-lived deployment. On 2026.7.1 the same workload profile loses every heavy-turn prompt.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run any embedded-runner agent with a long session (context above roughly 250 KB serialized, which is a few tool-heavy turns).
2. Read the session's `*.trajectory.jsonl`.
3. Every `prompt.submitted` event for those turns is `{"truncated":true,"reason":"trajectory-event-size-limit",...}` with the prompt in `droppedFields`.

### Expected behavior

The trajectory records what the model saw once per turn (`context.compiled`), and the user's prompt survives in `prompt.submitted` regardless of how large the surrounding conversation state is.

### Actual behavior

A 17 KB prompt is dropped because 207 KB of already-recorded history is packed beside it in the same event. Measured on a live fleet instance (2026.7.1, 256 trajectory files, 6,965 events, 162 MB):

- 46% of all trajectory bytes are redundant copies: `prompt.submitted` carries 26.0 MB of duplicated `messages` + 8.3 MB of duplicated `systemPrompt` beside 2.1 MB of actual prompts; `model.completed` carries 39.7 MB of `messagesSnapshot`, which is 96% of that event type's bytes (607 of 607 events).
- 169 events are truncated (83 `context.compiled`, 58 `model.completed`, 28 `prompt.submitted`); all 111 prompt-carrying truncated events lost the prompt.
- The largest surviving `prompt.submitted` (256,355 bytes, just under the cap) is 81% duplicated `messages`, 12% duplicated `systemPrompt`, 6.6% prompt.

Source, current main (18e107f494f):

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-submit.ts:115` inlines `activeSession.messages` + `systemPrompt` into `prompt.submitted`.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-finalize.ts:57` inlines `result.messagesSnapshot` into `model.completed`.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-observability.ts:98` already records the same state canonically in `context.compiled`.
- `src/trajectory/runtime.ts:69` oversize truncation drops all `data` keys except `usage`/`promptCache`.
- Nothing reads the duplicates: `src/trajectory/export.ts` takes prompts from `prompt.submitted.data.prompt` and systemPrompt from `context.compiled`, and no consumer reads `prompt.submitted.data.messages` or `model.completed.data.messagesSnapshot` (only a legacy-media guard inspects old files' snapshots).

### OpenClaw version

Observed on 2026.7.1 (`ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.7.1`); emission sites and truncation behavior verified in source on current main (18e107f494f).

### Operating system

Linux (containerized, OpenShift)

### Install method

Container image managed by the claw-operator

### Model

Not model-specific (observed across anthropic and openai models)

### Provider / routing chain

Not provider-specific

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```json
{"type":"prompt.submitted","data":{"truncated":true,"originalBytes":483706,"limitBytes":262144,"reason":"trajectory-event-size-limit","droppedFields":["prompt","systemPrompt","messages","imagesCount"]}}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Recorder-level reproduction: a heavy turn (~400 KB serialized conversation state, 17 KB prompt) recorded through `createTrajectoryRuntimeRecorder` on current main truncates all three events and the prompt is destroyed everywhere (`droppedFields` includes `prompt` in `context.compiled` and `prompt.submitted`). Fleet measurements in Actual behavior above.

### Impact and severity

Session forensics, replay, and any fleet observability built on trajectories silently lose exactly the turns most worth inspecting (the heaviest ones). Storage cost is roughly 2x what the same information needs. Data loss biased toward the most expensive turns, same class as #96804.

### Additional information

Proposed fix:

1. Stop re-inlining conversation state: `prompt.submitted` keeps `prompt` + `imagesCount`; `model.completed` drops `messagesSnapshot`; `context.compiled` stays the single record of what the model saw. This removes roughly 46% of trajectory bytes and makes heavy-turn `prompt.submitted` events effectively untruncatable.
2. Defense in depth: add `prompt` to the oversize-preserved keys (`TRAJECTORY_RUNTIME_OVERSIZE_PRESERVED_DATA_KEYS`), the mechanism #96811 introduced, so the prompt also survives truncation of `context.compiled` events that legitimately carry large history.

The Codex app-server recorder is intentionally unaffected: its `context.compiled` does not record `messages`, so its `messagesSnapshot` is that trajectory's only history record, not a duplicate.

If the duplicates turn out to have consumers I could not see, the fallback is a truncation drop order that sacrifices `messages`/`messagesSnapshot`/`systemPrompt` before the prompt, keeping the schema as-is. A PR implementing the proposed fix is ready and will be linked here.
