issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Since #138204, a streamed reply that mentions a tool-call tag anywhere (even inside a code block, e.g. `<invoke>` or `<parameter>` in an XML example) makes the Gateway re-parse the whole reply as Markdown on every delta, so a 20k-character answer costs about 17 s of Gateway main-thread CPU instead of under 0.1 s.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out `main` at `8197f6f8cf4`.
2. Use a provider whose stream messages carry no phase (Anthropic Messages, OpenAI-compatible completions, Ollama).
3. Ask the agent to explain a tool-call format, for example "why did the model print `<function_calls><invoke name="exec">…` as text?", so the answer contains a fenced XML example with `<invoke>` / `<parameter>`, followed by a long explanation.
4. Watch Gateway CPU while it streams, or drive `subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` → `handleMessageUpdate` with token-sized deltas.

### Expected behavior

Streaming cost stays roughly linear in reply length, as before #138204. (The delivered text is already correct: code examples that mention tool-call tags are shown as written.)

### Actual behavior

The streaming tool-call XML filter added to the raw projection (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.update.ts`, `toolCallXmlTextFilter({ stripFunctionCallsXmlPayloads: true, streaming: true })`) is an activated projector that runs its transform on the whole accumulated text on every delta once `<` has appeared. The transform (`stripToolCallXmlTagsInternal` in `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.ts`) returns early unless `TOOL_CALL_QUICK_RE` matches somewhere in the text, including inside code. Once a reply contains such a token, every later delta runs `findCodeRegions` (a full micromark parse) over the whole reply, and a second full parse in `unwrapStandaloneParameterTags` when `<parameter` is present.

The OpenAI Responses path already has the same cost before #138204 (`createAssistantVisibleStreamText("final_answer")` plus the non-streaming stage in `sanitize-user-facing-text.ts`), so it is shipped there.

Measured through the real `subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` → `handleMessageUpdate` path, 3 to 6 character deltas, median of 3 runs, on `626eeac26d6` (parent of #138204) and on current `main`. `claudeXml` is a reply that opens with a fenced XML example of a leaked `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` call and continues with ordinary prose, lists, and Python code:

| Stream shape | Reply | Before #138204 | `main` |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `anthropic-messages` | 20k plain prose and code | 70 ms | 89 ms |
| `anthropic-messages` | 20k with ordinary `<` (generics, HTML, `a < b`) | 76 ms | 298 ms |
| `anthropic-messages` | 8k `claudeXml` | 26 ms | 3,325 ms |
| `anthropic-messages` | 20k `claudeXml` | 75 ms | 17,291 ms |
| `openai-completions` | 8k `claudeXml` | 26 ms | 2,854 ms |
| `openai-responses` | 8k `claudeXml` | 5,593 ms | 5,513 ms |

At 20k, each late delta costs about 6.8 ms of synchronous Gateway time on `main` (0.01 ms before). A CPU profile of the 8k `anthropic-messages` case puts 96% of `handleMessageUpdate` time in `stripToolCallXmlTagsInternal`; the full parses split about evenly between its own `findCodeRegions` call and the one in `unwrapStandaloneParameterTags`.

### OpenClaw version

`main` at `8197f6f8cf4`. #138204 is not in `v2026.10.3` or `v2026.10.5-beta.3`; the Responses-path cost is in `v2026.10.3`.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x64 (Node 26.11)

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

Any streaming model; reproduced with fixture streams for `anthropic-messages`, `openai-completions`, and `openai-responses` message shapes.

### Provider / routing chain

Embedded runner, any channel or Control UI with a live consumer of the stream.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Default config.

### Logs

No errors.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Timings and the profile above come from driving the real `subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` → `handleMessageUpdate` path in-process with fixture streams.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: replies that quote tool-call markup anywhere, for example when users debug agents or leaked model output (Claude `function_calls`/`invoke`, Hermes/Qwen `tool_call`) or work with XML that uses `<parameter>` (TestNG, Tomcat).
- Severity: the Gateway main thread stays busy for seconds per reply (about 17 s for a 20k reply), so live delivery lags generation and other sessions wait.
- Frequency: every delta after the first such token in a reply.

### Additional information

Last known good: `626eeac26d6` (parent of `3666e847aac`, #138204). Replies with an ordinary `<` (generics, HTML, comparisons) but no tool-call token pay much less (76 → 298 ms at 20k), because only deltas ending in a possible tag prefix take a full parse.

A fix that reuses code regions across appends, when the appended text cannot move an earlier code boundary, brings the cases above to 200 ms (8k), 1,102 ms (20k), and 324 ms (Responses 8k) in a prototype, with identical delivered output. It has to encode several retroactive CommonMark constructs outside markdown-core (table delimiter rows, link reference definitions, link destinations containing code, a leading BOM), so I would like to know whether that direction is acceptable, or whether maintainers prefer a different owner for this, before opening a PR.

issues.body:
### Summary

Bringing the already-running OpenClaw macOS client to the foreground repeatedly brings Google Chrome to the foreground and shows its **“Allow remote debugging?”** consent dialog (Chinese UI: “要允许远程调试吗？”). This happens on ordinary app activation, not just app launch or an explicit browser automation action.

Clicking **Allow** does not prevent the prompt on the next activation. Clicking **Cancel** also does not stop the recurring prompts. The focus-stealing loop makes the native client difficult to use.

### Environment

- OpenClaw macOS app: **2026.9.6**, build **2609000690**
- macOS: **26.2**
- Google Chrome: **154.0.8037.58**
- Native macOS client connected to a Gateway; local installed Gateway package inspected during triage.
- Last known good version: unknown.
- Exact minimal browser-profile configuration needed to reproduce: not yet isolated.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Keep Google Chrome and the OpenClaw macOS client running.
2. Bring the OpenClaw client window to the foreground, without requesting a browser action.
3. Chrome takes foreground focus and displays the remote-debugging consent dialog.
4. Click **Allow**, then bring OpenClaw back to the foreground.
5. The dialog appears again.
6. Repeat with **Cancel**: the recurring behavior is not resolved.

The user reports this occurs every time the client is brought to the foreground; an instrumented reproduction captured the correlated events below. A clean-profile reproduction has not yet been performed.

### Expected behavior

Ordinary app activation and passive status refresh should not initiate a new connection to the user's Chrome session, steal focus, or repeatedly request remote-debugging consent. Explicit browser connection actions should continue to honor Chrome's consent requirements.

### Actual behavior / captured evidence

Sanitized excerpts from one reproduction (timestamps share the same local clock; process IDs, request IDs and device/account information omitted):

```text
11:04:07.140 OpenClaw / PermissionsService:
  Checking live screen recording permission
  Screen recording permission: true

11:04:07.235 OpenClaw / LaunchServices:
  Application display name changed from "node" to "chrome-devtools-mcp"

11:04:07.464 Google Chrome / AppKit:
  Browser window ordered front from a non-active application

11:04:07.481 OpenClaw / LaunchServices:
  Lost-frontmost notification; foreground application is Google Chrome

11:04:07.869 Gateway:
  browser.request completed successfully in 685 ms
```

These establish a temporal association between activation, Chrome MCP activity, a browser RPC, and Chrome taking foreground focus. They do **not** yet establish the exact RPC route or a complete caller stack. Permission-check messages are included as timing context, not as proof they caused the attach.

### Suspected code path — not yet proven as the runtime root cause

Inspection of the installed distribution found:

- `dist/server-context-Dq7PUDOo.mjs`, `listProfiles()` (around lines 1360–1385): Chrome MCP profiles are probed with `profileCtx.isTransportAvailable(300, signal, { onResult: ... })`.
- The same module's `isTransportAvailable()` (around lines 273–285) calls `ensureChromeMcpAvailable(..., { ephemeral: true, timeoutMs, signal, pageProbe })`.
- `dist/chrome-mcp-Dv8r0jMD.mjs`, `ensureChromeMcpAvailable()` (around lines 1280–1299): with a page probe, obtains a lease and calls `listChromeMcpTargetsWithLease()`.

This suggests that a nominally passive profile-list/status probe may create a temporary Chrome MCP connection and query pages, potentially triggering consent on every refresh. **We have not confirmed that the captured `browser.request` was the profile-list route**, so this is an investigation lead rather than a confirmed attribution.

### Suggested investigation / regression coverage

- Trace app activation/focus through browser RPC dispatch to identify the actual route and caller.
- Ensure passive status/profile listing does not start an unsolicited Chrome attachment.
- Check whether ephemeral probing discards an approved connection and repeats consent.
- Verify that cancelling consent does not create an activation/retry/focus loop.
- Preserve consent for explicit user-initiated browser control; disabling Chrome's safety prompt is not the requested fix.

### Impact and current status

Repeated focus stealing and consent dialogs interrupt ordinary native-client use. Allow and Cancel are not durable workarounds. No fix has been applied or verified.

The original screenshot and raw logs are intentionally not attached because they include unrelated browsing/authentication context; only sanitized diagnostic excerpts are included above.

issues.body:
### Feature Request

Telegram Bot API 10.2+ introduces native live drafts for AI bots via `sendMessageDraft` and `sendRichMessageDraft` (with `InputRichBlockThinking`), rendered natively by clients at the bottom of the chat with live fade-in and elapsed time counter (docs: https://core.telegram.org/api/bots/ai).

### Current Behavior
OpenClaw streams reasoning and progress using `sendMessage` + `editMessageText` preview messages. Docs note:
> `ephemeral 30-second "typing" drafts (sendMessageDraft) are not used for answer streaming.`

### Proposed Behavior
Use `sendMessageDraft` / `sendRichMessageDraft` with `InputRichBlockThinking` for reasoning streaming when:
- `channels.telegram.richMessages` is enabled
- Destination is a private 1-on-1 chat (where live drafts are supported)
- `/reasoning stream` is active

This provides the native Telegram AI bubble with elapsed timer and clean automatic cleanup upon final message delivery.

issues.body:
Observed on OpenClaw `2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)`, macOS gateway (Node 26.9.0),
scheduled jobs from the Automations scheduler.

## Summary

A session lane can hold a task that is counted as active ahead of every waiter
while nothing is actually running. Waiters queue behind it indefinitely — observed
waits from 24 s to **24.3 minutes** — and a waiter that carries a wall-clock
budget is killed by that budget while still queued, with no dispatch at all.

The scheduler's own log line is the clearest statement of the state:

```
lane wait exceeded: lane=session:agent:agent-a:main waitedMs=1459526 queueAhead=0 activeAhead=1 activeNow=0 queueBehind=3
lane wait exceeded: lane=session:agent:agent-b:main  waitedMs=825031  queueAhead=0 activeAhead=1 activeNow=0 queueBehind=0
lane wait exceeded: lane=session:agent:agent-c:main waitedMs=55011 queueAhead=0 activeAhead=1 activeNow=0 queueBehind=0
```

`activeAhead=1` with `activeNow=0` is self-contradictory at the moment of the
log line: one task is registered as active ahead of the waiter, and zero tasks
are running.

**Confirmed at gateway restart (2026-09-28 18:25:37Z).** The restart drain
aborted the stuck registrations and logged how long they had been "active":

```
lane task error: lane=session:agent:agent-b:main durationMs=18492716 error="This operation was aborted"
lane wait exceeded: lane=session:agent:agent-b:main waitedMs=16708119 queueAhead=1 activeAhead=1 activeNow=0
lane task error: lane=session:agent:agent-a:main durationMs=11194092 error="Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted"
lane wait exceeded: lane=session:agent:agent-a:main waitedMs=10268267 queueAhead=1 activeAhead=1 activeNow=0 queueBehind=6
```

5h08m and 3h06m of "active" with nothing running; waiters behind them waited
4h38m and 2h51m. Each registration starts at the moment its session's *last*
transcript event was written (13:17:05 vs. 13:17:16; 15:19:03 vs. 15:19:03),
i.e. the task registration outlives the run that created it. In the same second
as the `agent-b` lane's start: `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session
writer claim changed before transcript persistence` for a child session,
and later `Subagent announce give up (expiry)` for the same run id — a turn
whose transcript persistence failed. (Inferred: the registration is released
only on a normal completion path; an aborted or persistence-failed turn leaks
it.)

**Secondary finding:** a queued run's wall clock appears to start at *enqueue*,
not dispatch. After the restart a manual heartbeat run queued behind a
legitimately busy turn for 10+ minutes of its 3600 s budget. So the same
`cron: job execution timed out` with zero dispatch can also be produced by real
work rather than a phantom — the budget should start at dispatch, or a run that
has not dispatched should surface as deferred, not timed out.

## Recurrence 2026-09-29 — same phantom, and this time the trigger is on the record

A second incident began ~2026-09-28 19:43Z, 1h18m after the restart above had
cleared the first. New facts this occurrence adds:

**1. Trigger identified: a subagent-announce give-up on the requester's session.**
The `agent-b` work turn (18:55–19:10Z) spawned run `a65ef0af` (child
`agent:agent-b:child:2bb6a157`). The child ended ~19:10Z but its
completion announce back to `agent:agent-b:main` never completed:

```
[warn] Subagent announce give up (expiry) run=a65ef0af-f6d7-4238-b931-10feafa33ba2
       child=agent:agent-b:child:2bb6a157-29b1-4c7d-aeaa-83dcbe25efa1
       requester=agent:agent-b:main retries=1 endedAgo=1816s
       deliveryError="delivery path none did not complete"
```

The session's transcript goes silent at 19:43:00Z, and every scheduled run on it
from 21:34:54Z onward dies at its wall clock with zero dispatch. `delivery path
none` is a deliberate early return in `subagent-announce-delivery` (`path:
"none"` on `stale_run`, `transcript_commit_wait_unsupported`, inactive requester,
…) — a no-op resolution is indistinguishable from a lost completion, the same
shape as the `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError` seen beside the first
incident's registration.

**2. Starved runs hang before the turn starts — and log nothing at all.**
Four consecutive runs (21:34:54, 22:35:24, 23:36:24, 00:41:24Z — the last killed
01:41:25Z) contain **zero** transcript events, **zero** model fetches and
**zero** gateway log lines in their windows. The healthy control run
(18:27:12Z) logs workspace bootstrap + first model fetch within 25s of
admission.

**3. `lane wait exceeded` is emitted only when a waiter *starts*** (in
`drainLane`, at dequeue) — never while it is starved. A run that queues until
its budget kills it leaves no lane line whatsoever. Both incidents are
invisible to the log-based lane check: a health check derived only from these
log lines read `ok lane waits
over 10m: 0` while four runs were being strangled.

**4. A reaper exists and did not engage.** `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery`
(`recoverStuckSession` → `resetCommandLane`, with
`resolveStaleActiveLaneTaskReleaseMs`) is exactly the missing release path, but
`stuck session recovery` appears nowhere in the gateway log across either
incident. The stale registration currently survives indefinitely.

**5. Retry amplification confirmed.** Each kill is `errorReason: "timeout"` →
`retryCategory: "timeout"`, retried with backoff 30s → 60s → 300s
(`consecutiveErrors` 1→4), so one stuck lane produces a stream of hour-long
failures rather than one alarm (six receipts 14:28Z–00:41Z across the two
incidents).

**6. Wall-clock-at-enqueue re-confirmed:** `durationMs: 3600080` with zero
dispatch.

**Second restart drain confirms the shape (2026-09-29 02:15:50Z).** An
`openclaw gateway restart` flushed:

```
lane task error: lane=session:agent:agent-b:main durationMs=25553887 error="This operation was aborted"
lane wait exceeded: lane=session:agent:agent-b:main waitedMs=25410264 queueAhead=1 activeAhead=1 activeNow=0 queueBehind=9
```

7h06m "active" with nothing running, and **nine** queued waiters up to 7h03m.
The registration's start (25 553 887 ms before the flush = **19:09:56Z**) is the
session's last transcript event — the work turn that spawned run `a65ef0af`,
whose announce then gave up at 19:40:12Z. The trigger and the leak now share a
timestamped timeline rather than mere neighbourhood, and the draft's rule from
the first incident ("the registration starts at the moment its session's last
transcript event was written") held exactly. After the flush a manual run
completed `ok` (02:17:32Z→02:30:52Z, 13m20s) and the scheduled cadence resumed
(02:30:54Z dispatch).

Sibling symptom on the same delivery layer, same evening: `sessions_send
announce flow failed` 30+ times 18:34Z–23:52Z and inbound `sessions_send`
messages arriving with an empty body. Whether the announce-layer fault and the
phantom registration are one defect or two is not established from here.

*Expected* gains two additions on top of the above: the existing
`diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery` should reclaim a stale active registration on
the same timescale as the run it belongs to; and a waiter that has not started
within its own budget should emit a lane line *before* the budget kills it, so
the state is observable while it is happening rather than only after a restart
drain.

## Impact

Scheduled heartbeat jobs (system-owned Automations jobs, `sessionTarget: main`)
are the worst hit: each tick is admitted, queues behind the phantom, produces
**no transcript entry, no model call and no tool call**, and is aborted at its
3600 s run budget with `error: "cron: job execution timed out"`,
`errorReason: "timeout"`. Five such runs in 4 hours on two agents (2026-09-28
13:35Z–17:29Z), each burning a full hour. Since the error is classified as a
*transient timeout*, the scheduler retries (`retryCategory: "timeout"`, backoff
30s → 60s → 5min), so one stuck lane produces a stream of hour-long failures.

The failure is invisible from the agent side: the run simply never appears, so
an operator sees "job execution timed out" with no way to tell which job or why.

## Reproduction

1. Run several agents with scheduled heartbeat jobs on `sessionTarget: main` and
   ordinary chat traffic on the same session.
2. Wait for a run to end abnormally on one session (observed near such events:
   `Subagent announce give up (expiry)`,
   `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session writer claim changed before
   transcript persistence`, `sessions_send announce flow failed: agent tool
   caller authority is no longer active`, and turns cut by their own timeout).
3. Later turns on that session log `lane wait exceeded ... activeAhead=1
   activeNow=0` and sit. A heartbeat run started during the stall is recorded
   `running` in `cron_run_receipts`/`task_runs`, writes nothing to
   `transcript_events`, and ends `cron: job execution timed out` at exactly
   `heartbeat.timeoutSeconds`.

Not deterministic — the phantom clears eventually (or on gateway restart) — but
the `activeAhead=1 activeNow=0` fingerprint appeared every day in a 2-day window
on 4 of 5 agents.

## Expected

Either the lane should not report an active task when `activeNow=0` (the
registration is released on every exit path), or a waiter should not queue
indefinitely behind one — a stuck active registration should be reaped on the
same timescale as the run it belongs to. A queued run whose budget expires
without dispatching would ideally surface as a distinct error
(e.g. `stalled before execution start`, which already exists for setup phases)
rather than the generic `cron: job execution timed out`, which reads like a slow
turn.

## Evidence

- Gateway file log `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-09-2{7,8}.log` (JSON lines): the
  `lane wait exceeded` lines above, plus the `cron: job run returned error
  status` / `cron: scheduling recurring retry after transient error` pairs.
- State DB `cron_run_receipts`: five `error` rows with `error_text =
  'cron: job execution timed out'`, durations 3599–3600 s.
- Agent transcript DBs `transcript_events`: zero events inside every one of the
  five run windows (no `[OpenClaw heartbeat poll]` marker, so the prompt was
  never delivered).
- Control: another agent's heartbeat runs on the same gateway completed normally
  (28 s, 80 s) during the stall, so the scheduler and model path are healthy.

## Possible workaround

Gateway restart clears the in-memory lane registration. There is no operator
surface to release a single stuck lane task, which is what makes this painful:
the workaround costs a fleet-wide restart.

issues.body:
### Summary

On Matrix with Element Web, attaching an image sends it as its own event the moment the upload is confirmed; the text the user typed in the composer follows as a second event a few seconds later. The gateway starts a run on the media-only message at once, replies to the bare image (a description or comment nobody asked for), and then runs a second turn for the text. Users expect one answer that treats the attachment as part of the question, as chat assistants with a built-in composer do.

### Version / channel

openclaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), Matrix channel, self-hosted gateway. Checked the 2026.9.6 release notes and open issues; found nothing covering this.

### Repro

1. Element Web, a direct chat with the bot. Type a question, click the paperclip, pick an image, confirm the upload.
2. Element sends the `m.image` event immediately; press Enter to send the text 2–20 s later.
3. Two runs: the first replies to the bare image; the second answers the text (the image is already in context, so the second answer is fine — the first is the problem).

### What I checked

- `messages.queue.mode` / `messages.queue.debounceMs`: the debounce only batches messages that arrive while a run is active. A media-only reply finishes before the text arrives, so the text starts a new run.
- Element Web has no caption support (MSC2530), so the text cannot ride on the media event from that client.

### Proposal

A short hold for media-only inbound messages, e.g. `messages.queue.mediaHoldMs` (with a per-channel override like `debounceMsByChannel`): when an inbound message carries media and no text, wait up to N ms for a text message from the same sender in the same room/thread and run them as one turn — the text as the prompt, the media as its attachment. A media message that already has a caption, and any text message, are unaffected. Default `0` keeps today's behaviour.

### Workaround

Use a client that sends captions (Element X), or instruct the agent to acknowledge a bare attachment briefly and wait for the text.

issues.body:
**Observed on 2026.9.6.** Gateway uptime continuous since ~08:16 ET today (no restart), OAuth re-authenticated for both affected servers around 08:00 ET this morning.

## Summary

Two OAuth-gated remote MCP servers (`vercel`, `vercel-personal`, both `mcp.vercel.com`, `auth: "oauth"`, streamable-http transport) log an "expired credentials" warning from one code path essentially continuously, while a separate code path successfully authorizes and uses the same connection at other points in the same time window. The two paths disagree about live credential state.

## Evidence (today's gateway log, single instance)

Counted every occurrence of the "expired" line in today's log: **848 occurrences since 00:00 ET**, fired every ~1-3 minutes without exception, still firing as of the most recent log line at the time of filing:

```
bundle MCP skipped unavailable OAuth server vercel: MCP server "vercel" has expired OAuth credentials. Run openclaw mcp login vercel.
bundle MCP skipped unavailable OAuth server vercel-personal: MCP server "vercel-personal" has expired OAuth credentials. Run openclaw mcp login vercel-personal.
```

(Note: `logLevelName` on these lines is `None` in the structured log — not `WARN`/`ERROR`, which may itself be worth checking.)

Meanwhile, a different log line for the same two servers shows a **successful** authorization within the same day, e.g.:

```
2026-09-29T20:03:18.482-04:00 - vercel: streamable-http oauth authorized
2026-09-29T20:03:18.502-04:00 - vercel-personal: streamable-http oauth authorized
2026-09-29T20:03:24.324-04:00 - vercel: streamable-http oauth authorized
2026-09-29T20:03:24.342-04:00 - vercel-personal: streamable-http oauth authorized
```

So the servers are not actually broken — an operator who checks live status (`openclaw mcp status` equivalent) sees "oauth authorized" and a real tool call succeeds — but the "bundle MCP" path (whatever assembles the tool catalog / bundle for a session) independently and repeatedly decides the same credentials are expired and skips the server, hundreds of times a day, without ever converging.

## Impact

- Noisy/misleading logs at high volume (848 near-identical lines/day for two servers) make real log review harder.
- Unclear whether "bundle MCP skipped" actually means the tool was unavailable for whatever session/turn triggered that check, which would mean intermittent, silent tool-catalog gaps for these MCP servers even though the credentials are genuinely fine — worth confirming whether any agent turns actually lost Vercel tool access during one of these windows, or if this is purely a cosmetic double-check that doesn't affect availability.

## Not (yet) established

- Root cause of why the two paths disagree — didn't have source access to trace it, reporting from log evidence only.
- Whether this is the same underlying cause as #160611 (offline_access scope never requested) or #98377 (closed: tokens not refreshed by long-running gateway) — neither issue's described symptom (permanent failure requiring manual re-login) matches this one (self-recovering / inconsistent-but-not-permanently-broken), so filing separately rather than commenting on either.

## Ask

Please confirm whether "bundle MCP skipped" actually gates tool availability for real agent turns, or is a redundant/stale check that doesn't affect functionality — that determines whether this is cosmetic-log-noise or a real intermittent-availability bug.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a WhatsApp direct chat, `ask_user` fails before the question is shown: the prompt dispatch throws `ReplyDispatchDeliveryError: queued reply delivery failed` about 80 ms after the tool starts, so the question never reaches WhatsApp.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the gateway with the bundled WhatsApp channel linked, and make sure `ask_user` is not in `tools.deny`.
2. From the owner's WhatsApp direct chat (routed to the agent's main session), send: `Use your ask_user tool to ask me whether I pick A or B.`
3. The agent calls `ask_user` with one single-select question: options `A` and `B`, no `timeoutSeconds`.

### Expected behavior

Per `docs/tools/ask-user.md`, "Answers work on every supported conversation surface", and prompts "degrade to readable text on messaging channels". The question should appear in the WhatsApp chat, and a plain-text reply should answer it.

### Actual behavior

No question is sent to WhatsApp. The tool fails right away and the tool result is:

```
Error: ask_user prompt delivery failed | queued reply delivery failed | REPLY_DISPATCH_DELIVERY_ERROR
```

The agent then fell back to asking in plain text. Nothing hung and no inbound message was lost; the next WhatsApp message was handled normally.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6 (7fedff7)

### Operating system

macOS 27.0

### Install method

git checkout, built and activated as a local runtime generation; gateway under launchd

### Model

openai/gpt-6.1-sol

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw gateway -> openai (native Codex responses route, ChatGPT subscription auth); the tool call ran through code mode (`exec` -> `ask_user`)

### Additional provider/model setup details

WhatsApp is the bundled plugin (2026.9.6), direct chat from the owner, session `agent:main:main`. Nothing else in `tools.deny` affects messaging.

### Logs

```
19:40:11.068 [gateway/channels/whatsapp] embedded run tool start: tool=ask_user
19:40:11.140 [openclaw] tool result delivery failed: ReplyDispatchDeliveryError: queued reply delivery failed
19:40:11.140 WARN [gateway/channels/whatsapp] failed to deliver ask_user prompt: ReplyDispatchDeliveryError: queued reply delivery failed
19:40:11.146 [gateway/channels/whatsapp] embedded run tool end: tool=ask_user
```

The `ReplyDispatchDeliveryError.outcome` value is not logged, so which dispatch outcome was hit is unknown. The error is thrown from `dispatch-from-config.turn-ledger.ts`.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Impact and severity

- Affected: WhatsApp direct chats.
- Severity: the tool can't be used on WhatsApp. The agent falls back to plain text, so the workflow isn't blocked.
- Frequency: 1/1 attempts with the tool enabled.
- Consequence: questions only reach the user if the agent decides to re-ask in plain text.

### Additional information

Related, but on other channels: #140085 and #150795 (Telegram delivery), #132525 (Codex harness), #158494 (Discord thread). We keep `ask_user` in `tools.deny` as a workaround.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

With `talk.realtime.model: gemini-3.8-live`, Control UI (browser) Talk shows the user's spoken lines during the call, but none of them are saved: after Stop and a reload, chat history holds only the assistant's voice replies.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Gateway with a Gemini API key and `talk.realtime: { provider: "google", model: "gemini-3.8-live" }`.
2. Open the Control UI on the main session and click **Start voice input**.
3. Ask two questions out loud, for example "What is two plus two?" and "And what is the capital of France?", and wait for both answers.
4. Click **Stop voice input**, reload the page, and read `chat.history` for the session.

## Expected behavior

Both spoken questions are saved as `user` voice rows next to the answers, as they are with `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` on the same build, and as the Gateway relay transport does for 3.8 since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152680.

## Actual behavior

Captured on upstream main `e80558a4da0`, isolated Gateway, headless Chromium with a fake microphone, real Gemini Live.

Gemini 3.8 sends each utterance as one complete `inputTranscription` message without `finished`:

```text
{"serverContent":{"inputTranscription":{"text":"What is 2 + 2?"}}}
{"serverContent":{"inputTranscription":{"text":"And what is the capital of France?"}}}
```

`chat.history` after Stop and reload:

```text
assistant | Two plus two is four.           | provenance realtime_voice / talk
assistant | The capital of France is Paris. | provenance realtime_voice / talk
```

The same steps with `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` produce the same frame shape and save both `user` rows.

## OpenClaw version

Source checkout at upstream main `e80558a4da0` (2026.10.3).

## Operating system

Linux (x86_64), Node 24.18.0, headless Chromium.

## Install method

Source checkout, `pnpm build`.

## Model

google/gemini-3.8-live (Talk realtime model)

## Provider / routing chain

Control UI browser -> Google Live API (browser-owned `provider-websocket` session with a constrained token from the Gateway)

## Impact and severity

Affected: Control UI Talk users who select `gemini-3.8-live` or `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking`.
Severity: the user's half of every voice conversation is lost from the session transcript; later turns and other clients see only the assistant's replies.
Frequency: every utterance in the observed runs.

## Additional information

The browser transport in `ui/src/pages/chat/talk/google-live.ts` treats input transcripts without `finished` as complete only for Gemini 3.1 Live; for other models it waits for `finished`, which 3.8 never sends, and the pending text is discarded at Stop. The Gateway relay already treats 3.1 and 3.8 the same (`emitsCompleteInputTranscripts` in `extensions/google/realtime-voice-model-contract.ts`).

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Behavior bug (incorrect state without crash)

## Summary

`openclaw plugins update <pkg>` applied **without a gateway restart** leaves the running gateway resolving that plugin from its **ephemeral build/staging directory under `TMPDIR`**, not from the canonical install under `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/`. Because `package.json` is re-read lazily per operation, the plugin keeps working until something reaps that temp directory — then it fails with `ENOENT`, potentially hours later and far from the cause.

`TMPDIR` is by definition reclaimable (tmpfs cleared on reboot, `systemd-tmpfiles`, any operator cleanup, and — per #158390, #153617, #152852, #154322, #158938 — tooling that exists specifically because these dirs leak). Binding a live plugin root there makes correctness depend on nobody ever cleaning temp.

Observed on **2026.9.5**. I have not re-verified the binding on 2026.9.6, so the mechanism may have changed — but the capture layout in 9.6 still places plugin build output under `tmp/`.

## What happened

1. Updated four plugins live, no restart:
   ```
   openclaw plugins update @openclaw/acpx@2026.9.5 @openclaw/brave-plugin@2026.9.5 \
                           @openclaw/discord@2026.9.5 @openclaw/tokenjuice@2026.9.5
   ...
   Updated discord: 2026.9.4 -> 2026.9.5.
   Applied plugin updates in Gateway generation 3.
   ```
   Everything reported healthy; Discord kept working.

2. Hours later a scheduled cleanup removed stale `openclaw-plugin-build-*` directories under `TMPDIR`. It skipped anything held by a live process — no open fd or cwd referenced them, because the gateway had already read what it needed.

3. **~9 hours after step 2**, Discord broke:
   ```
   [ws] ⇄ res ✗ message.action errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory,
     open '/home/ec2-user/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-plugin-build-tpVfPc/package-0/node_modules/@openclaw/discord/package.json'
   [discord] ingress: spooled update 1550891014841958463 failed; keeping for retry: ENOENT ...
   [discord] ingress: spooled update ... reached retry limit after 8 attempts; dead-lettered
   ```
   One inbound message was permanently lost to the dead-letter path.

4. The canonical install was intact the entire time:
   ```
   ~/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-discord-c0892df945__openclaw-generation__g-40c440cfd6c2e487/
     node_modules/@openclaw/discord/package.json   ← present, correct version
   ```

5. A gateway restart fixed it immediately — plugins re-resolved from `npm/projects`.

The same thing then happened to the `codex` plugin from a different reaped directory (`openclaw-plugin-build-5AinKr`), which additionally de-registered its CLI command:
```
"codex" is a runtime slash command (/codex), not a CLI command.
```

## Why this is hard to diagnose or defend against

The binding is **only in gateway memory**. Nothing exposes it:

- `openclaw plugins list --json` reported **zero** references to any `openclaw-plugin-build-*` path; every entry pointed at `npm/projects`.
- `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` contained no live reference either — the only matches were historical `channel_ingress_events.last_error` strings from the failure itself.
- No process held an fd or cwd in the directory, since `package.json` is re-read lazily.

So an operator writing a cleanup job has **no supported way** to ask "which temp directories are load-bearing right now?" Every available signal says the directory is unused. The failure then surfaces hours later, on a code path unrelated to the cleanup.

## Suggested fixes (any one would resolve it)

1. **Re-resolve to the canonical path after a live reload** — bind the generation to `npm/projects/...`, treating the build directory as write-only staging.
2. **Copy, don't reference** — materialize the plugin into its canonical location before activating the new generation.
3. **Hold an open fd / advisory lock** on any temp directory that is load-bearing, so `lsof`-style checks and existing reapers can see it.
4. **Expose the live resolution path** in `plugins list --json` (e.g. `activeRootDir`), so operators can exclude it.
5. **Fail loudly at reload time** rather than lazily: validate the bound root at generation activation, so breakage surfaces at the update, not nine hours later.

(1) or (2) also removes the failure mode entirely on reboot for anyone whose `TMPDIR` is tmpfs.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.5 at time of incident (now 2026.9.6)
- Amazon Linux 2023, x86_64, 2 vCPU / 7.8 GB, Node 24, npm global install
- Gateway as a `systemd --user` service
- `TMPDIR` redirected to disk via a service drop-in (the same failure is reachable with the default `/tmp` on tmpfs, which clears on reboot)

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When `sessions_spawn` is called with `runtime="acp"` and `agentId="claude"` (acpx backend), the runtime creates a `<parent-agent-workspace>/claude/` subdirectory and populates it with a full copy of the parent agent's workspace files (~164 KB of identity/context files + `.git` directory). This directory persists across restarts and grows with each spawn.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an agent workspace at `agents.defaults.workspace` (e.g. `~/.openclaw/workspace`) with identity files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.) and a git repo.
2. Call `sessions_spawn` with `runtime: "acp"`, `agentId: "claude"`, and any task.
3. After the spawn, check the parent workspace for a `claude/` subdirectory.
4. Observe that `<parent-workspace>/claude/` now exists and contains a copy of the parent workspace's files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, HEARTBEAT.md, IDENTITY.md, TOOLS.md, USER.md, BOOTSTRAP.md, plus `.git/` and `.openclaw/`).

**Confirmed on disk:**
```
~/.openclaw/workspace/claude/
├── .git/           # cloned git state
├── .openclaw/
├── AGENTS.md       (7835 bytes)
├── BOOTSTRAP.md    (1511 bytes)
├── HEARTBEAT.md     (226 bytes)
├── IDENTITY.md      (696 bytes)
├── SOUL.md         (1806 bytes)
├── TOOLS.md         (920 bytes)
└── USER.md          (537 bytes)
Total: ~164 KB
```
Directory `mtime` 2026-05-24T10:36 — created during first `runtime="acp"` spawn.

### Expected behavior

The acpx runtime should write its working state into its own state directory (e.g. `~/.openclaw/state/acp/<sessionId>/` or equivalent), not into a `<agentId>/` subdirectory inside the parent agent's workspace. The parent workspace should be untouched by ACP spawns.

### Actual behavior

A `<agentId>/` subdirectory (`claude/` in this case) is created inside the parent agent's workspace and populated with copies of the parent's workspace files on every spawn. Over repeated spawns, this directory persists and accumulates state.

### Additional impact

- **Privacy / identity leak**: Parent agent's identity files (SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, USER.md, AGENTS.md) are copied into a subdirectory that the ACP child process can discover via filesystem traversal — unintended identity exposure to the child.
- **`.git` clone in subdirectory**: The git state is copied into `claude/`, which causes `git status` / `git log` in the parent workspace to show a nested repo.
- **Repeated spawns**: Unclear whether the directory is overwritten or accumulated each time; both behaviors are problematic.
- **Confusing to parent agent**: The parent agent sees a `claude/` directory in its own workspace that it didn't create, and must treat it as noise or clean it up manually.

### Workaround

Manually move `claude/` to a temp location after each ACP spawn:
```bash
mv ~/.openclaw/workspace/claude /tmp/lyssa-acp-clone-$(date +%s)
```
Adding `claude/`, `codex/`, `gemini/`, `opencode/` to `.gitignore` prevents git tracking, but does not prevent creation.

### OpenClaw version

2026.5.17 (e923ca4)

### Operating system

Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (WSL2 on Windows 11)

### Install method

Local source / dev build

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw → anthropic → claude-sonnet-4-6

### Suggested fix

The acpx spawn path should be modified to write child working state into `~/.openclaw/state/acp/<agentId>/<sessionId>/` (or a similarly isolated, non-workspace path), rather than resolving a `<agentId>/` subdirectory relative to the parent agent's `cwd`/workspace.

issues.body:
### Summary

When heartbeats run in the agent's main session with direct Anthropic (API key, `anthropic-messages`), no heartbeat run ever reads the previous run's prompt cache. Every run rewrites the whole session history at the cache-write price. For us that came to about $0.40–0.95 per heartbeat on a 10-minute cadence, roughly 93% of spend in cache writes.

### Version / setup

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6, Node 24, gateway as a systemd user service.
- One agent on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`, `params.cacheRetention: "long"`.
- Heartbeat: `every: "10m"`, `session: "main"`, `target: "owner"`, custom `prompt`.
- `contextPruning: { mode: "cache-ttl", ttl: "1h" }`. No compaction occurred.

### Evidence

Across 50 heartbeat runs, the first model call of each run had `cacheRead` fixed at 18,859 tokens (tools plus the stable system prompt). `cacheWrite` was the rest of the context, 20k–130k tokens depending on history size. The history itself was unchanged between runs: `NO_REPLY` heartbeat turns are not carried into later runs.

### Cause

1. `applyAnthropicCacheControlToMessages` (in `dist/worker/worker.mjs`) places the only message-level `cache_control` marker on the last user text block. On a heartbeat's first call, that block is the heartbeat prompt.
2. The heartbeat runner builds that prompt with `appendCronStyleCurrentTimeLine(prepared.prompt, cfg, startedAt)` (`dist/heartbeat-runner-run-*.mjs`, heartbeat `Body`). It therefore differs every run: `Current time: … / Reference UTC: …`, added in #44993.
3. So the only cache entry a run writes ends in a block the next run never sends again. Nothing before it, including the unchanged history, can be read from cache.
4. Heartbeat turns that do stay in history are replayed as `[OpenClaw heartbeat poll]`, not the prompt that was sent. That also shifts the prefix: `replayed thinking dropped … prefix_binding_mismatch`.

### Workaround (tested: not sufficient on its own, see the follow-up comment)

With the time line removed from the heartbeat `Body`, the prompt should be identical each run. Each run's first call should then match the previous run's cache entry, as long as the history is unchanged.

### Suggested fixes (any one helps)

- Put a cache breakpoint at the end of the conversation history, before the per-run prompt. Anthropic allows up to 4 breakpoints.
- Or send the current time as a separate block after the cached prefix, or make it configurable (e.g. `heartbeat.includeCurrentTime: false`). Related: #148304.
- Replay heartbeat turns with the exact text that was sent, so kept turns don't shift the prefix.

> Agent-written on behalf of @Oldrich333 · agent: hive-admin/executor · model: claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 · origin: agent-initiated

### Summary

`workboard_stats` / `workboard.cards.stats`: add per-status counts split by archive state (`activeByStatus`, `archivedByStatus`) next to the existing archive-inclusive `byStatus`.

### Problem to solve

- today: `WorkboardStore.stats` (`extensions/workboard/src/store-core.ts`) returns scalar `total` / `active` / `archived`, but `byStatus` and `byAgent` count archived cards too.
- gap: "how many non-archived cards are `todo` / `running` / `blocked` on board X" has no aggregate answer; the only route is paging `workboard_list` and counting.
- observed: agents asked for non-archived counts by status could not answer from the aggregate and fell back to paging `workboard_list`.
- the data is already there: `listStatsAggregates` returns `archived` per status/agent row; `stats` sums it into the scalar only.

### Proposed solution

- same aggregate pass in `stats`: `activeByStatus[status] += row.total - row.archived`, `archivedByStatus[status] += row.archived` (zero entries omitted, like `byStatus`).
- `byStatus`, `byAgent`, `active`, `archived` unchanged → additive, backward compatible.
- `WorkboardStatsResult` gains both optional maps; tool description names the three scopes ("byStatus includes all cards, activeByStatus and archivedByStatus split the same scope").
- invariant for tests: `Σ activeByStatus = active`, `Σ archivedByStatus = archived`, `activeByStatus[s] + archivedByStatus[s] = byStatus[s]`.

### Alternatives considered

- `includeArchived: false` filter on `stats`: needs a second store query per call and changes nothing for callers that want both views; the split costs nothing extra.
- list + count client-side: unbounded pages for a count; what the aggregate exists to avoid (#146210, #146237).

### Impact

- affected: agents and UIs using Workboard stats for queue sizes on boards that archive finished cards.
- severity: wrong counts or extra paging; no data loss.
- frequency: every status-count question on such boards.

### Evidence/examples

Running as a local patch on 5 gateways (2026.9.5, 2026.9.6); arithmetic invariants above verified on each gateway at activation.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

Related: #146210 / #146237 (stats aggregate without loading cards — this builds on that path).

### Summary

Config default sidebar group (`category`) for new sessions, keyed by who created them: operator-created (Control UI) vs agent-created (`sessions_spawn` visible, `sessions.create` from an agent, runs/probes).

### Problem to solve

- Agents now create many visible sessions (spawned work sessions, benches, probes, review runs). Without an explicit `group` they land ungrouped, in the same "Other" bucket as the operator's own new chats.
- Measured on one gateway, last 3 days: ~280 agent- or run-created visible sessions vs 16 operator-created dashboard chats; operator chats get buried.
- No config sets a default group. Today's only levers: every caller passes `group`/`category` explicitly, or the operator uses the group-header `+` (New session `?group=<name>`). Top-level `+` always creates ungrouped.
- Related, not duplicate: #161017 (`/new` reset drops `category`), #137107 (nested groups), #103431 (sidebar rethink, closed).

### Proposed solution

- config, e.g. `session.defaultGroup`: `{ operator?: string, agent?: string }` (or keyed by `createdVia`: operator | spawn | run | channel | cron).
- applied once at session creation, only when the caller passed no explicit `group`/`category`; explicit value always wins; later manual moves never overridden.
- group missing from the catalog → registered on first use (same path as `sessions.patch` category).
- optional: Control UI top-level `+` honours `operator` default.

### Alternatives considered

- rule in every agent prompt to pass `group` on every spawn/create → works for well-behaved agents only; scripts/benches still land ungrouped.
- plugin `agent_end`/`session_start` hook + `runtime.agent.session.patchSessionEntry` setting `category` on young ungrouped sessions → works, but every deployment rebuilds the same thing, and it runs after the first turn (row visible ungrouped until then).
- operator always uses group-header `+` → easy to forget; top `+` is the prominent control.

### Impact

- affected: operators running agents that create visible sessions (multi-agent setups, benches, delegated work sessions).
- severity: organisational/UX; no data risk.
- frequency: every agent-created visible session.
- consequence: operator's own chats hard to find among agent sessions.

- `SessionCreatedVia` / `createdActor` already stamped on every session entry (`src/config/sessions/session-entry-provenance.ts`) → classification data exists.
- `category` applied only from explicit `sessions.create` / `sessions.patch` / `sessions_spawn group` (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-create.ts`, `sessions-patch-effects.ts`); no config key reaches it.

issues.body:
## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I can implement this myself, unless maintainers prefer to pick it up given the implementation details below.

## Summary

`openclaw mcp serve` should send `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` on the Gateway WebSocket upgrade, with a repeatable `--header` overlay, matching TUI / probe / gateway call — so a trusted-proxy Gateway can tell operators apart.

## Problem to solve

`openclaw mcp serve` is a stdio MCP server whose bridge opens a Gateway WebSocket as a CLI client (`GATEWAY_CLIENT_MODES.CLI`, display name `"OpenClaw MCP"`).

That connect path only passes token/password into `GatewayClient`. It never sets `edgeAuthHeaders`.

Trusted-proxy does **not** disable `mcp serve`. Two paths exist today:

1. **Same host, local password (works, Gateway-blind).** `openclaw mcp serve` with no public URL talks to localhost. `gateway.auth.password` still authenticates (local-direct fallback). A Streamable HTTP wrapper can already do this. Fine for a single operator: The spawning wrapper may know the hosted user, but every child looks like the same local operator to OpenClaw.
2. **Remote / multi-operator (broken).** Shared token is forbidden in trusted-proxy. Password is local-direct only. Off-box `mcp serve --url wss://…` cannot present identity, so the upgrade fails — or, if you keep using path 1 from a wrapper on the Gateway host, the Gateway still cannot tell users apart.

Config `edgeAuth` only **sends headers the process already has** (for example, a configured secret or spawn-time `--header`). Same as TUI.

Meanwhile:

- `GatewayClient` already sends `edgeAuthHeaders` on the WebSocket upgrade.
- Probe (`src/gateway/probe.ts`) and one-shot RPC (`src/gateway/call.ts`) already resolve `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` via `gatewayEdgeAuthValueForTarget` + `resolveEdgeAuthHeaders` and pass the result in.
- TUI documents the same config: for a configured remote Gateway, it resolves `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` and sends those headers only to that origin.
- A Gateway in `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"` authorizes the upgrade from `authorizeTrustedProxy`: source IP in `gateway.trustedProxies`, required headers present, `userHeader` present. It does not verify a JWT. Token auth is mutually exclusive with trusted-proxy. Password fallback is local-direct only.

The proxy does **not** inject headers into stdio. Stdio has none. The process that *spawns* `mcp serve` (Claude Code, Codex, a Streamable HTTP wrapper) supplies Gateway upgrade headers via config and/or `--header`. The Gateway believes `userHeader` only when the **source IP** is in `trustedProxies` (the trusted proxy hop, never an untrusted client spoofing `x-forwarded-user`).

This is a Feature: trusted-proxy + `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` already exist; `mcp serve` never grew the client path that every other remote Gateway caller uses. It is not a trusted-proxy protocol bug.

## Proposed solution

Reuse the existing client machinery. Do not change `authorizeTrustedProxy` or the Gateway auth protocol.

### Behavior

1. **Config default** (same as TUI / probe / call). When the connect target origin matches `gateway.remote.url`, resolve `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` with the existing helpers and pass the materialized map as `GatewayClient` `edgeAuthHeaders`. Keep the current `resolveEdgeAuthHeaders` rule: config edgeAuth is `wss://` only and origin-scoped.

2. **CLI overlay.** Add repeatable `mcp serve --header <key=value>`. Parse with the existing `collectOption` + `parseKeyValueEntries` helpers already used by `mcp add --header`. Validate with the same `normalizeEdgeAuthHeadersConfig` / `findEdgeAuthIssue` rules as config (reject transport-owned names, invalid names, empty values, case-only duplicates). Overlay onto config headers: CLI wins on the same header name, compared case-insensitively; a repeated identical `--header` key keeps the last value. CLI `--header` values are spawn-time literals and apply to whatever URL `mcp serve` connects to (not origin-scoped like config). Both config and CLI headers stay **`wss://` only**. `GatewayClient` already refuses edge auth headers on `ws://` (`edge auth headers require a wss:// Gateway URL`), and this PR does not relax that.

3. **Connect.** `OpenClawChannelBridge` passes the merged map into `new GatewayClient({ ..., edgeAuthHeaders })`. Headers go on the WebSocket upgrade request. They are not MCP initialize params, not stdio framing, and not something the Gateway pushes into the child.

4. **Auth exclusivity** (no protocol change). Trusted-proxy remains mutually exclusive with a shared Gateway token (already enforced in `src/gateway/auth.ts`). Remote trusted-proxy still does not accept password fallback (local-direct only, already enforced). This PR does not invent a new auth mode.

### UX

**TUI parity.** Config only:

```json5
{
  gateway: {
    mode: "remote",
    remote: {
      url: "wss://gateway.example",
      edgeAuth: {
        "X-Edge-Auth": { source: "env", provider: "default", id: "EDGE_AUTH_TOKEN" },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

```bash
openclaw mcp serve --url wss://gateway.example
```

The trusted proxy validates the request and supplies the configured `userHeader`. `mcp serve` does not establish trust itself; it only sends the configured upgrade headers.

**Multi-operator wrapper (the reason to implement this).** An MCP gateway already authenticated the hosted client over HTTP. It copies that user onto spawn. The Gateway lists the **wrapper IP** in `trustedProxies`:

```bash
openclaw mcp serve \
  --url wss://gateway.internal \
  --header "x-forwarded-user=nick@example.com" \
  --header "x-forwarded-proto=https"
```

Same flags from an untrusted IP fail (`trusted_proxy_untrusted_source`). One child per user: stdio is single-tenant (in-memory event queue, one `GatewayClient`).

Env-backed secrets stay in `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` SecretInputs (`env` / `file` / `exec` / `store`). No new `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_*` header env dialect.

### PR scope

**In this PR:** `mcp serve` connect auth (config `edgeAuth` + `--header` overlay into `GatewayClient.edgeAuthHeaders`) + tests + docs.

That is the whole feature. Separate scopes:

1. Centralize `edgeAuthHeaders` inside `resolveGatewayClientBootstrap`.
2. Global CLI `--header` on `tui`, `gateway call`, `gateway status`, etc.
3. Treat headers as explicit credentials in `ensureExplicitGatewayAuth` / `hasExplicitGatewayConnectionAuth`.
4. First-class Streamable HTTP / SSE `mcp serve` transport.
5. In-process multi-user identity.
6. Gateway `authorizeTrustedProxy` / JWT verification / new auth modes.
7. Teaching `mcp serve` to receive HTTP headers from the MCP client.
8. Any one proxy’s config.
9. Edge headers over plaintext `ws://`.

### Files to change

> **Note on drift:** file paths and context were taken from `openclaw/openclaw` `main` at `28885d3f8745f51e39ecb54389283dc391c15381`. Treat this as a map of intent, not a patch.

| # | File | Change |
|---|------|--------|
| 1 | `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts` | Add `--header` to `mcp serve`, parse + validate, pass `gatewayEdgeAuthHeaders` down |
| 2 | `src/mcp/channel-server-runtime.ts` | Add `gatewayEdgeAuthHeaders` to opts, forward to the bridge |
| 3 | `src/mcp/channel-bridge.ts` | Resolve config `edgeAuth`, overlay CLI headers, pass `edgeAuthHeaders` to `GatewayClient` |
| 4 | `src/gateway/edge-auth.ts` | New helper `overlayEdgeAuthHeadersConfig` (case-insensitive overlay) |
| 5 | `src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts` | New `--header` parse / validation cases |
| 6 | `src/mcp/channel-bridge.startup.test.ts` | New `edgeAuthHeaders` cases (config, CLI, both, neither, `ws://`) |
| 7 | `src/gateway/edge-auth.test.ts` | Tests for the new helper |
| 8 | `docs/cli/mcp/serve.md` | Usage, `--header` option, client config example, security section |
| 9 | `docs/gateway/remote.md` | Note that `mcp serve` sends `edgeAuth` like TUI, plus `--header` |

**Not changed:** `src/mcp/channel-server.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-secret-options.ts`, `src/gateway/client-bootstrap.ts`, `src/gateway/auth.ts`, `src/gateway/client.ts`, `packages/gateway-client/src/client.ts`.

## Alternatives considered

- **Wrapper-only / colocated password, no OpenClaw change.** Already works for a single operator, but not when several people share a Gateway.
- **Classify as a Bug.** Missing capability, not a regression in `authorizeTrustedProxy`.
- **New auth mode just for MCP.** Unnecessary. `GatewayClient.edgeAuthHeaders` is the connect mechanism.
- **Put identity in MCP initialize params or stdio env by convention only.** Would introduce a new protocol rather than use existing config/CLI patterns.
- **Require `--token` / `--password` even when headers are present.** Breaks trusted-proxy.
- **Allow `--header` on plaintext `ws://`.** Existing `GatewayClient` rejects this; relaxing it is a separate transport security change.

## Impact

- **Affected:** Multi-operator trusted-proxy Gateways that expose `mcp serve`.
- **Severity:** Blocks per-user Gateway identity for remote/`--url` `mcp serve` under trusted-proxy. Does not turn off local password `mcp serve`.
- **Frequency:** Always, when more than one person should show up as themselves in OpenClaw (sessions, approvals, `identityScopes`).
- **Consequence:** Without it, a remote MCP wrapper either shares one Gateway identity or cannot connect through the trusted-proxy path at all. With it, the Gateway sees the same user the MCP gateway already verified.

`mcp serve` is the same class of CLI Gateway client as TUI. TUI already sends `edgeAuth`. Serve does not.

## Evidence/examples

Current `mcp serve` has URL, token/password, Claude channel mode, and verbose options, but no Gateway upgrade header flags.

Current bridge connect resolves token/password and constructs `GatewayClient` without `edgeAuthHeaders`.

By contrast, `src/gateway/call.ts` and `src/gateway/probe.ts` resolve configured edge auth and pass `edgeAuthHeaders`; the gateway client already sends them on the upgrade and rejects them for non-`wss://` URLs.

Trusted-proxy authorization already checks trusted source IP, required headers, and `userHeader`. Password fallback remains local-direct only, and token auth is mutually exclusive with trusted-proxy.

Failure modes without this include `trusted_proxy_user_missing`, `trusted_proxy_untrusted_source`, `trusted_proxy_missing_header_*`.

## Additional information

Must remain backward-compatible: no `--header` and no `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` means today’s token/password `mcp serve` is unchanged, including trusted-proxy + local password.

`mcp serve` does not grow a new authentication flow. Configure `gateway.remote.edgeAuth`, or have the spawning wrapper pass `--header` after it has authenticated the user.

### Related

- #125700 added `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` for TUI, probe, and `gateway call`; #125982 applied it to session-URL targets. Neither touched `mcp serve`.
- #127358 (per-session identity for stdio MCP servers) is the opposite direction: OpenClaw *spawning* stdio MCP servers and telling them who called. This issue is about `openclaw mcp serve` *being* the stdio server and telling the Gateway who it is.

### How to verify

- Existing `mcp serve` token-file test passes unchanged.
- Config only: `gateway.remote.url` + `edgeAuth` → mocked `GatewayClient` receives those headers on a `wss://` target.
- Overlay: `--header x-forwarded-user=a@b` wins over config for that name, case-insensitively.
- `--header Host=gateway.example` fails validation before connect.
- `--header` with a `ws://` target fails with the existing `wss://` error before any `GatewayClient` is constructed.
- No `src/gateway/auth.ts` or `packages/gateway-client` test changes.
- `pnpm test:docker:mcp-channels` stays green if maintainers want it run.

### AI assistance

I drafted this issue together with an AI agent in Cursor, using Claude Opus 5.5 and Grok 4.7 High Fast. The file paths, symbols, and behavior it describes were checked against `openclaw/openclaw` `main` at `28885d3`.

issues.body:
## Problem
The iOS and Android apps can only reach a gateway over whatever network path the phone already has. For the most common private setup (gateway on a home machine or VM, reachable only over Tailscale), that means:
- the user must install and run the separate Tailscale app, and keep its VPN on;
- iOS may suspend or disconnect the VPN in the background, so the node and chat sessions drop;
- onboarding breaks when the tailnet is not reachable yet.

Related open reports:
- #138430 iOS: Tailscale onboarding leaves operator disconnected
- #153903 iOS background location over Tailscale reconnects then fails
- #142529 Android resets the connection screen when Tailscale is unavailable
- #98062 (closed) iOS app fails to connect over Tailscale CGNAT
- #94695 alternative transport discussion (Iroh), which asks for the same seam

## Proposed solution
Two parts, kept separate on purpose.

### 1. A small transport seam in the shared kit (core)
A route decision per gateway host, owned by `OpenClawKit`:

```swift
public enum GatewayNetworkRoute: Sendable, Equatable {
    case direct                          // today's behaviour, the default
    case proxy(GatewayProxyEndpoint)     // a transport exposes a local proxy
    case unavailable                     // fail closed; never leak to the public path
}

public final class GatewayNetworkRouter {
    public func publish(hosts: some Sequence<String>, route: GatewayNetworkRoute)
    public func route(forHost host: String?) -> GatewayNetworkRoute
    public func apply(to: URLSessionConfiguration, forHost: String?) -> GatewayNetworkRoute
    public func apply(to: NWParameters, forHost: String?) -> GatewayNetworkRoute
}
```

- With no transport registered, every host routes `.direct`. **No behaviour change for existing users.**
- `GatewayChannel` (and the Watch/Share paths) ask the router when they create their session. That is the only core call-site change.
- Transports only publish routes. They do not touch pairing, auth, TLS pinning or the protocol.
- The same seam carries Iroh, WireGuard or a corporate proxy later.

### 2. Embedded Tailscale transport (optional module)
- Runs a userspace Tailscale node inside the app via Tailscale's official `libtailscale`/TailscaleKit (BSD-3-Clause). No system VPN and no separate Tailscale app.
- The node exposes a loopback proxy. The module publishes `.proxy(...)` for the gateway's tailnet hosts, or `.unavailable` while the node is not connected (fail closed).
- **Pairing:** the existing setup code gains an optional `tailnet` block. Gateways reachable only on the tailnet (`*.ts.net`, `100.64.0.0/10`, `fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48`) are detected. The user signs in to Tailscale in-app once, and the node is staged before pairing.
- **User control:** a Tailscale on/off toggle, a sign-in step, and clear errors ("tailnet not signed in", "gateway not on your tailnet").
- **Opt-in for builds:** it sits behind a build setting, and the TailscaleKit xcframework is built from a pinned `libtailscale` commit by script. Builds without it are unchanged.

## Alternatives considered
- **Keep requiring the Tailscale app:** this is the status quo and the source of the issues above.
- **Tailscale Funnel or a public tunnel:** exposes the gateway publicly, which is the wrong default for a personal agent.
- **Hard-wire Tailscale into core:** adds a Go/xcframework dependency for everyone. The seam avoids that.

## Implementation status
- **iOS:** implemented on a fork and tested in the simulator against a real gateway. Branch: https://github.com/saju01/openclaw/tree/tailnet-transport ; design doc with diagrams: https://github.com/saju01/openclaw/blob/tailnet-transport/TAILNET.md Built on current `main`: 6 commits. The shared-kit seam is about 340 lines plus tests.
- **Tests:** unit tests for routing, setup-code parsing and tailnet inference, plus simulator UI tests, with synthetic fixtures only.
- **Android:** not built. The same design applies (Tailscale's library supports Android). We'd like agreement on the seam first so it is built once, to the same contract.

## Suggested PR split, if maintainers are interested
1. `OpenClawKit`: `GatewayNetworkRouter` plus the call sites, all `.direct` by default, so behaviour is unchanged.
2. The setup-code `tailnet` block, with parsing and tests.
3. iOS embedded Tailscale transport module, with its toggle and onboarding.
4. Watch/Share direct-mode ordering fixes found along the way.
5. Android transport (later).

Happy to open (1) as a draft first, or to package this as a plugin instead if that is the preferred route.

## Summary

`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.responses-output-limit.live.test.ts` › "continues from a committed receipt after a real truncated tool call" (native-live agents lane) fails deterministically. It failed on four consecutive 2026.9.7 release candidates, on the 2026-09-27 FRV targeting `4ec35b53` (job 108547912431), and locally at `01d7131999ca`.

## Two separate problems

1. **Settled-turn finalization lost the host transcript for detached runs (fixed on a branch).** The built-in harness rebuilt the finalization attempt from a restricted field copy (introduced in `6eea20ce181e`). That copy dropped `sessionManager` and `sessionPersistence`, so detached runs finalized against an empty transcript. This affects memory flush, the update repair agent, Skill Workshop experience review and the setup inference turn. The fix is on branch `fix/r97-detached-finalization-transcript` (`2f0845a357a3`), with a regression test. With it, the live test's receipt assertions pass: the receipt is in the third request's input and in the final payload.
2. **The output-limit recovery path no longer runs (open).** After the fix, the test still fails at `expect(run_status events with reason "output_limit").toHaveLength(1)`, which receives 0. The truncated `write` call (`max_output_tokens=256`) is handled by the settled-turn finalization path, not by output-limit recovery (`run-loop.ts`). The recovery decision needs structured evidence of the second response's terminal state to find the rejected condition. No verified passing run exists after 2026-09-17, so this may predate 9.7.

## Evidence

- FRV 36534008742, job 109297826498 (release `01d7131999ca`): `expected '[{"type":"message","role":"user",...The previous assistant turn completed its tool calls but did not produce a user-visible answer...' to contain 'RECEIPT_<uuid>'`
- Local run with the harness fix: receipt assertions pass, then `expected [] to have a length of 1` at the `output_limit` run_status check.

Waived from the 2026.9.7 stable live selection pending problem 2.

issues.body:
## Summary

`src/gateway/gateway-progress-refresh.live.test.ts` › "steers the active parent and refreshes an idle card without resuming work or adding chat" fails deterministically in the native-live Gateway core lane. It failed on four consecutive 2026.9.7 release candidates, and a local isolated run at `01d7131999ca` reproduces it.

## What fails

The steering and refresh parts now work: the refresh lands in the active run, and `inFlightRun.runId` matches the root run. The failure is the final reply. The model (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna`) appends a status sentence after the required marker.

CI:

```
- WORK_COMPLETED_<uuid>
+ WORK_COMPLETED_<uuid>
+
+ The authorized work is complete. The second run remains pending because it still requires explicit user authorization.
```

Local run:

```
+ First run completed successfully. The second run remains unstarted because it lacks authorization.
```

## Likely cause

The progress-card refresh steer message (`src/gateway/server-methods/progress-card-refresh.ts`, `REFRESH_MESSAGE`) asks the model to reconcile completed and remaining work, and says the refresh is not authorization. The task prompt also mentions a pending second step that needs authorization. The model carries that status reasoning into its final chat reply, even though the refresh says "Do not acknowledge this request or send a chat reply. The updated card is the response."

Two possible fixes:
- Product: keep refresh-driven status out of the final answer, for example by strengthening the refresh instruction or scoping it to the card write.
- Test: use a prompt that does not invite a status recap.

This needs a decision on which contract the test protects.

## Evidence

- FRV 36534008742, Release Checks 36534953519, job 109297826522 (release `01d7131999ca`)
- Earlier release SHAs `56fb8872`, `e61efb6c` and `01d71319` show the same final-text mismatch.
- The pre-#160830 failure mode (a steer silently queued as a follow-up) is fixed; the in-flight run assertion passes.

Waived from the 2026.9.7 stable live selection pending this fix.

issues.body:
## Summary

The release live lane **Docker live gateway MiniMax** (`live-gateway-minimax-docker`) is flaky: MiniMax-M3 intermittently fails the gateway `tool-read` probe, and when both selected models (`minimax/MiniMax-M3`, `minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3`) miss in the same run the lane fails with `completed zero successful live model run(s) ... skipped=2`.

This is model behavior under automatic Code Mode, not an OpenClaw tool-result regression. It was waived for the 2026.9.7 stable live selection.

## Evidence

**Product path works.** A local live run of `src/gateway/gateway-models.profiles.live.test.ts` against `minimax/MiniMax-M3` at the 2026.9.7 release SHA (`01d7131999ca`) passed tool-read, tool-exec, and image. The provider payload log shows the whole sequence. Because MiniMax-M3 is a preferred Code Mode model, the model sees only `exec`, `wait`, `sessions_yield`, and `view_image`. Its first move was a direct call to the hidden `read` tool, which returned `Tool read not found`. It then retried through Code Mode `exec`, the nested `read` returned the probe file text (`kind: "text"`, catalog of 36 OpenClaw tools), and the model answered with both markers.

**Failing runs are the model giving up after the same first step.** In the failing CI job 109300784027 (FRV 36534008742, 2026-09-29 00:22 PT), both models answered the plain prompt correctly. On tool-read they either:

- told the user Code Mode had no filesystem access and asked for the file contents to be pasted, or
- called the undeclared direct `read`, got `Tool read not found`, and concluded no read tool exists.

Retries run in the same session, so the model stays anchored to its earlier refusal.

**Same code both passes and fails.** Per-model outcomes on identical or near-identical targets:

| Target | minimax/MiniMax-M3 | minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3 | Lane |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| f773aa06 (run A) | done | nonce-miss skip | pass |
| f773aa06 (run B) | nonce-miss skip | done | pass |
| f773aa06 (run C) | done | done | pass |
| 56fb8872 (9.7 prep) | done | done | pass |
| 8634a334 | done | nonce-miss skip | pass |
| 46147f5e | nonce-miss skip | done | pass |
| 1b919d5e | nonce-miss skip | nonce-miss skip | **fail** |
| 27aa6213 | nonce-miss skip | nonce-miss skip | **fail** |
| e61efb6c | nonce-miss skip | nonce-miss skip | **fail** |
| 01d7131999ca | nonce-miss skip | nonce-miss skip | **fail** |

Across the last 30 Release Checks runs, this lane passed 25 times and failed 5 times. Per-model misses were already present on the 2026.9.6-era target `f773aa06`. A second model used to hide them, and the lane went red only when both models missed in the same run.

## Proposed fixes (pick at the owner)

1. **Product, all Code Mode models:** when a model directly calls a tool that Code Mode hides in its catalog, return an actionable error instead of the generic `Tool <name> not found`. For example: "`read` is available inside `exec` as `await read({ path })`". Today the model has to infer this, and MiniMax-M3 often does not.
2. **Harness:** run tool-read retries in a fresh session, so one refusal does not anchor every later attempt. Also decide whether a run where every model is a tolerated tool-nonce-miss skip, after a successful live prompt exchange, should count as coverage. A genuine all-fail must still fail.
3. **Model policy:** revisit whether MiniMax-M3 should stay on the automatic Code Mode preferred list if (1) does not raise its tool-read reliability.

Restore `live-gateway-minimax-docker` to the stable live selection once the lane is reliable again.

issues.body:
### Problem
`subagents.maxConcurrent` caps the *number* of concurrent children. On small hosts the binding constraint is memory, not count: with the `claude-cli` runtime every child is a separate process (~250–400 MB RSS), plus browser/embedding workers inside the same gateway cgroup. On a 10 GB VM the OOM killer hit processes in the gateway unit twice within five minutes while 6 claude children (2 turns + 4 subagents, ~250 MB each) ran alongside the gateway and browser. Every individual limit was respected. A tighter `MemoryHigh` on the unit is not a fix either: at 5G systemd throttled the unit into swap and the event loop stalled for 13 minutes.

As a workaround we run a local pre-spawn gate script (MemAvailable, swap-out rate, PSI `full`, cgroup headroom against `MemoryHigh`, with hysteresis) that the agent must call before each spawn. That is fragile: it relies on the agent following a rule, and isolated cron runs bypass it.

### Proposal
An admission check in the spawn path (subagents and isolated cron/agentTurn runs):
```json5
subagents: {
  maxConcurrent: 4,
  admission: {
    minAvailableMb: 1500,          // or perChildHeadroomMb × running children
    maxPsiFullAvg10: 5,            // /proc/pressure/memory
    respectCgroupHigh: true,       // headroom against the gateway unit's memory.high
    onBlocked: "queue"             // queue | reject
  }
}
```
Blocked spawns queue (with a visible status) instead of failing silently, and a diagnostic line records the reason.

### Why in core
The gateway owns the spawn path and the cgroup; only it can enforce this for every caller, including scheduled runs.

issues.body:
### Problem
`cron.failureAlert` (docs/cli/cron.md, Failure delivery) covers jobs that run and fail. Several other failure modes stay silent:
- **Overdue:** a job's `nextRunAtMs` is in the past by more than N× its interval and no run has started (scheduler stall, gateway down during the slot, clock jump).
- **Skipped:** runs recorded as skipped (e.g. busy lane, disabled dependency) for K consecutive slots.
- **Dead man:** a job that is supposed to emit a heartbeat/artifact did not do so within its window, even though the scheduler thinks it is fine.

On 2026.9.6 we run a local script next to the gateway that reads the cron run history every few minutes and alerts on these three cases. It keeps working, but it is exactly the kind of out-of-tree watcher that should not be needed.

### Proposal
Extend the failure-delivery block with optional staleness rules, reusing its routing, cooldown and recovery notice:
```json5
cron: {
  failureAlert: { after: 2, cooldownMs: 3600000, /* existing */ },
  staleAlert: {
    overdueFactor: 2,        // alert when now - nextRunAtMs > factor × interval
    skippedAfter: 3,         // consecutive skipped runs
    includeOneShot: false
  }
}
```
Per-job override (`job.staleAlert: false | {…}`) for jobs with deliberately irregular schedules.

### Why in core
The scheduler already knows `nextRunAtMs`, run outcomes and skip reasons; an external watcher has to reconstruct this from logs or the CLI and breaks on schema changes.
