issues.body:
## Summary

Supplement to #158147, which documents this symptom for **reply-to-bot** messages in a Telegram **forum topic**. On a second deployment the loss also occurred on a **plain, non-reply** message in a **direct 1:1 chat** — a combination the existing report explicitly observed as unaffected ("0 of ~15 plain messages lost" / "plain messages always arrive with text intact").

Same symptom (gateway logs a full character count, the agent turn processes an empty body), different and simpler trigger path.

Related: #158147

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | 2026.9.5 (npm/Gateway package) |
| Node | v24.16.0 |
| OS | Linux x86_64, containerised gateway |
| Channel | Telegram, long-polling |
| Chat shape | **direct 1:1 chat** (no forum supergroup, no topics) |
| Bot identity | redacted — see privacy note |

> **Privacy note:** the bot username and chat ID are redacted from this report. The original report in #158147 already provides a usable sample identifier, so omitting them costs no diagnostic value.

## Observed instances

All eight lines are verbatim from the gateway log, with chat ID, bot username and timezone offset redacted. `N chars` is the gateway's own count of the inbound payload.

```
2026-09-27T09:58:58.411 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:<chat-id> -> @<bot> (direct, 4 chars)
2026-09-27T09:59:53.231 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:<chat-id> -> @<bot> (direct, 4 chars)
2026-09-27T23:59:12.313 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:<chat-id> -> @<bot> (direct, 26 chars)
2026-09-28T09:53:38.919 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:<chat-id> -> @<bot> (direct, 25 chars)
2026-09-28T09:55:17.959 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:<chat-id> -> @<bot> (direct, 99 chars)
2026-09-28T22:20:15.226 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:<chat-id> -> @<bot> (direct, 6 chars)
2026-09-28T22:20:46.796 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:<chat-id> -> @<bot> (direct, 28 chars)
2026-09-28T23:59:06.539 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:<chat-id> -> @<bot> (direct, 110 chars)
```

In every instance the agent's user-visible response asked the sender to resend, matching the symptom description in #158147.

## What is confirmed vs. not

**Confirmed**

- The gateway receives a non-empty payload for all eight messages (the `N chars` value above).
- For at least two of these (the 99-char and 110-char messages), the full body is present in the session transcript when it is read afterwards. This matches the reporter's own refinement in #158147: the store keeps the body, the loss is downstream.
- The loss occurs in a direct 1:1 chat, not only in forum topics.
- It is not universal: most messages in the same window arrived intact and were acted on normally.

**Not confirmed / explicitly unverified**

- That the `22:20:15` (6 chars) message was sent without using Telegram's reply feature. The sender states this, but the gateway's `Inbound message` log line does not record reply metadata, so it could not be verified from logs. Reported here as sender testimony, not as a checked fact.
- The exact model-boundary prompt for any failing turn. The session store backing this transcript is a SQLite database that the runtime guard blocks from external inspection, so the "store has it, prompt does not" transition could not be captured directly. This is the same gap flagged in the review on #158147.

**Not attempted**

- No controlled reproduction. These were live observations across a two-day window on an unattended deployment.
- No current-main run.

## Code observation (adjacent — offered as a lead, not a root-cause claim)

Read against both the local bundled build and the `main` branch of `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts`, the reply-quote rendering path is:

```ts
function resolveInlineReplyQuote(ctx: TemplateContext): string | undefined {
  return sanitizeTranscriptField(ctx.ReplyToQuoteText) ?? sanitizeTranscriptBody(ctx.ReplyToBody);
}

function formatTelegramCurrentMessageContext(ctx: TemplateContext): string | undefined {
  if (!isTelegramInboundContext(ctx)) return undefined;
  const quote = resolveInlineReplyQuote(ctx);
  if (!quote) return undefined;            // <-- no reply quote => no block emitted
  const messageId =
    normalizePromptMetadataString(ctx.MessageSid) ??
    normalizePromptMetadataString(ctx.MessageSidFull);
  const header = messageId ? `#${messageId}:` : undefined;
  return ["Current message:", `[Replying to: ${JSON.stringify(quote)}]`, header]
    .filter((line) => line !== undefined)
    .join("\n");
}

export function resolveInboundUserContextPromptJoiner(ctx: TemplateContext): " " | undefined {
  return formatTelegramCurrentMessageContext(ctx) ? " " : undefined;
}
```

Two observations, both consistent with the report in #158147:

1. The emitted block contains **only** the quoted parent message plus the `#id:` header. The user's own body is not part of it — it is expected to follow, joined by a single space returned from `resolveInboundUserContextPromptJoiner`.
2. `sanitizeTranscriptField` caps its input at `MAX_UNTRUSTED_TRANSCRIPT_FIELD_CHARS = 500`, so a long quoted parent is truncated to roughly 486 characters before this block is built.

**Tension worth flagging:** the early return in `formatTelegramCurrentMessageContext` means a message with no reply quote should not produce this block at all, which is consistent with the original report's "plain messages are always fine". That does **not** explain the non-reply instance above, so this path is at best a partial explanation. Reporting it because it is the same boundary the review named, and because the mismatch between this code path and the observed non-reply case is itself a useful triage signal.

## Suggested next step

Consistent with the review on #158147, extended to the non-reply path:

1. Trace a real inbound message end to end — Telegram `RawBody` → shared `agentText` → final model-boundary input — and identify the first owner that drops the text.
2. Assert the regression on the **final model-boundary input**, not on the gateway's ingress character count. As the review notes, a non-zero ingress count does not prove the text reached the prompt.
3. Cover both paths in the regression: reply-to-bot **and** plain non-reply messages, in a direct chat as well as a forum topic.

Happy to provide additional redacted log excerpts on request. I did not attach the raw gateway log — it is large and contains unrelated private conversation history.

issues.body:
## Problem

Event asset integration needs a directly testable validator for the complete emitted file set before a build writes its manifest. File hashes alone do not establish safe paths, supported document and stylesheet references, or the absence of recognizable worker and code-generation capabilities.

## Proposed solution

Add a source-only asset validator with focused Node tests. Validate paths, MIME types, byte and inventory limits, document/style references and bundle metadata. Track recognizable JavaScript capability transfers by lexical binding, including aliases and nested/defaulted patterns, and fail closed for unsupported recognized transfers.

The static analysis is deliberately bounded. It does not prove arbitrary JavaScript is capability-free; runtime origin isolation and worker/CSP enforcement remain separate requirements.

## Alternatives

Validation could be embedded directly in a future build plugin, but a separately testable validator lets that integration reuse one asset contract. A connected event interface and complete asset/runtime qualification are broader follow-up work.

## Impact and validation

This foundation makes no runtime or UI change and introduces no dependency or lock-file change. It exposes a direct test command using the existing Acorn dependency. The prepared source has 31 passing focused Node tests, including harmless local controls and recognized capability denials. A future PR will disclose its exact review and validation results; full asset build, browser, provider and runtime qualification are not part of this source step.

issues.body:
### Summary

Allow an operator to disable host-requested settled-turn finalization for an individual agent while keeping the current default.

### Problem to solve

When tools settle without a final answer, the host may run a separate tool-free summary through the selected harness. Some operators need to keep an agent on its normal turn-preparation path, or prefer the original incomplete-turn result over an additional model request. There is no per-agent switch for this host-owned recovery pass.

### Proposed solution

Add the optional Boolean `agents.entries.<id>.embeddedAgent.settledTurnFinalization`. Omitted or `true` preserves automatic finalization. `false` skips the host summary pass and keeps the original terminal result, including any incomplete-turn warning or tool failure.

```json5
{
  agents: {
    entries: {
      assistant: {
        embeddedAgent: { settledTurnFinalization: false },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

The option applies to the selected agent across providers and harnesses. Ordinary turns, continuation, compaction and harness-internal behavior keep their existing contracts. Completed tool actions are neither undone nor replayed by the switch.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep the current recovery behavior: appropriate for the default, but does not meet this operator preference.
- Replace the harness or intercept provider calls: considerably broader than opting out of this one host-owned recovery operation.
- Change ordinary prompts: does not control whether the host schedules an isolated summary.

### Impact

Affected: operators configuring agents with a strict model-request preparation policy or a preference to inspect incomplete turns directly. Frequency: only when a settled tool turn lacks a final answer. Tradeoff: disabling recovery can leave a warning instead of a helpful summary. Other agents and existing configurations retain their current behavior.

### Evidence/examples

A candidate against `ddd8fc96ee71ba8836959d02f5a3d9d682111c31` covers the actual embedded runner, resolved session-agent selection, and failure preservation for omitted/true/false. Its 82 focused tests and all 32 selected maintained checks pass; independent review found no actionable defects. A linked PR will include the implementation and measured test costs.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, the source change is prepared for review.

issues.body:
## 2026.9.6: gateway hangs at 100% CPU in `media-persistence-detection` startup migration after a deleted transcript-archive folder (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded)

### Summary

After updating **2026.9.3 → 2026.9.6**, the gateway cannot start. It hangs in the `startup migration` phase at the new `media-persistence-detection` step, pegging one CPU core at ~100%, and port `20789` never binds. Reproduces on every restart. The update itself reports `state-migrated-no-rollback`.

### Root cause

A folder of archived transcripts (`~/.openclaw/agents/moneta/session-sqlite-import-archive/`, populated by the earlier session-sqlite migration) was **deleted**. The new `media-persistence-detection` step then encounters a "mass of missing copies" — many archived media/transcript references whose on-disk files no longer exist — and recurses/loops indefinitely.

### Evidence

1. `sample` of the hung process shows a tight loop:
   `fs.lstat → ENOENT → UVException → stack-trace capture → repeat` (never exits).
2. `openclaw doctor` during the update's `activating` phase failed with:
   `Failing check plugin-doctor-post-session-state (blocked-by-session-repair-failure): prerequisite session repair failed: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`
3. Gateway log shows slow SQLite transactions stuck in the migration:
   `slow SQLite transaction hold ... operation=media-persistence-detection database=.../agents/moneta/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` (and same for `vilica`).
4. The two affected agent DBs are large: moneta ~2.2 GB, vilica ~1.3 GB. Doctor flagged both.
5. The 357 archive blobs are still present inside moneta's `session_transcript_archives` table (BLOB `archive_blob`), but the on-disk published archive folder is gone — so the crash is "references point at files that no longer exist," not "data wiped."

### Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** a missing/deleted archive folder should not hard-crash or hang startup. The migration should tolerate missing copies (skip them, or count them) and let the gateway come up.
- **Actual:** infinite recursion / stack overflow + 100% CPU hang, gateway never binds its port.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), upgraded from 2026.9.3 (skipping 2026.9.4 / 2026.9.5)
- Platform: macOS 26.6.2 (arm64), Node 26.4.0
- Gateway: LaunchAgent `gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, port 20789
- State dir ~61 GB, ~35 GB free

### Workaround / recovery

- `openclaw triage` recommended "Restore the deleted archive folder" (not possible — no copy exists) or "a maintainer fix for how a mass of missing copies is handled."
- No rollback path available (schema already at `user_version=18`).

### Request

Please fix `media-persistence-detection` to tolerate missing/deleted archive copies (skip/count, not recurse), so a routine upgrade cannot hang the gateway on a deleted folder. Any guidance on a safe recovery (so the machine can boot on 2026.9.6 without restoring the deleted folder) is appreciated.

issues.body:
### Summary
On the Telegram channel with the `claude-cli` backend and the default queue mode (`steer`), a message that arrives while a turn is running is sometimes **lost entirely**, not just delayed. When the queued message is drained, the gateway logs the **new** message's length but builds the prompt from the **previous** message's body. The new message is never sent to the model, and its ingress row is still marked `completed`.

This is different from #124731 / #156848 (steer silently degrades to a delayed followup) and #110727. Here the message never reaches the session at all.

### Version / setup
- OpenClaw 2026.9.6
- Agent runtime: `claude-cli`
- Channel: Telegram direct chat
- `messages.queue.mode` unset (defaults to `steer`)

### Evidence (5 drops between 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-28, all during an active turn)
- Case A: message A2 arrives mid-turn. After the turn ends, the gateway logs `[telegram] Inbound message … (86 chars)` (A2's length), but the prompt the CLI receives, per the Claude Code session jsonl, carries **A1's** text. A2 is absent from the native transcript (`transcript_events`), and A1 and A3 are present.
- Case B: the same off-by-one. The log shows a 520-char inbound (B2), and the prompt body is B1 (107 chars).
- Cases C and D: messages sent during the same long turn never produce any user turn.
- Case E: `Inbound message` is logged twice for the same message during a 23-minute turn, and still no user turn is recorded.
- Separately, 4 messages were delivered 75–81 minutes late (same condition).

In every case the ingress row in `openclaw.sqlite` is `completed`, so nothing retries.

### Expected
Every message received while a turn is running gets delivered, in order, after the turn ends. At minimum, the prompt body should match the message being logged and marked complete.

### Workaround being tested
`messages.queue.byChannel.telegram: "collect"`. I'll report back whether it avoids the drop.

I can share a small read-only detector script that cross-checks the Telegram message cache against both transcript stores, if that's useful.

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Marked as stale due to inactivity

labels.name: P2

labels.name: impact:security
labels.description: Security boundary, credential, authz, sandbox, or sensitive-data risk.

issues.body:
### Problem

A broker or wrapper may approve a specific target, but the ACPX filesystem client currently performs the actual resolution/open/write after receiving the client request. A pre-write approval check in an external stdio relay cannot bind that approval atomically to the file ACPX ultimately opens.

In the inspected ACPX 0.19.1 implementation, `methods.client.fs.writeTextFile` is registered on the client endpoint and dispatched to a handler that resolves the request path, awaits write approval, separately resolves/opens a writable workspace target, then writes through the resulting handle. The check and filesystem mutation are separate operations. A path component or symlink can change between them; a relay-side realpath comparison is therefore stale by the time ACPX opens the target. The relay does not hold ACPX’s opened descriptor and cannot prove which object received the first mutation.

There is also a separate direct-edit route: an agent runtime may perform an edit through its own tool implementation without emitting an ACPX `fs/write_text_file` request. A wrapper that observes only ACP frames cannot authorize or block that route. Workspace-wide Landlock confinement limits the writable area but does not enforce the broker-approved per-target boundary. Do not infer from this report that every current ACPX-enabled runtime uses the direct route; the captured direct-edit evidence is from an earlier capability mode.

### Requested behavior

Please provide an ACPX-owned, execution-time authorization hook at the filesystem mutation boundary for whole-file writes, covering `Filesystem.writeTextFile` / `handleWriteTextFile` and every equivalent create/truncate/write path:

- A dispatch/session-scoped authorization identifies the approved target and request, is authenticated to the active dispatch, and can be claimed only once.
- ACPX claims and validates authorization immediately before any create, truncate, content write, or other namespace/content mutation. Missing, late, repeated, cross-dispatch, expired, or mismatched authorization fails closed.
- Authorization must bind to the object ACPX actually mutates, not only the lexical request path. Use descriptor-relative / race-safe resolution under a pinned workspace root, rejecting symlinks and aliases unless the opened object (or pinned parent descriptor plus leaf for a new file) can be proven to be the approved target.
- The result is dispatch-bound and auditable without relying on post-write matching as enforcement. IPC, validation, and audit failures fail closed.
- Identify and expose controls for runtime-owned direct-edit routes that bypass ACPX client filesystem requests. Either disable and verify those routes under the selected capability contract, or provide equivalent execution-time per-target mediation for them.

### Why an external relay is insufficient

A relay can compare a request path with a pending approval and consume that approval once, but forwarding the request leaves ACPX to resolve/open/write later. That cannot close the TOCTOU interval or attest the actual opened target. Nor can it see an edit performed without an ACPX filesystem frame. This needs to be enforced where ACPX owns the mutation, with an explicit contract for any bypass path.

### Evidence and scope

The local feasibility review of ACPX 0.19.1 found the separate approval, workspace resolution/open, and write operations described above. It also examined an earlier direct Antigravity ACP-client harness whose approved `Run edit_file?` requests and persistent diff had no `fs/write_text_file` frames; that is evidence that a direct route exists in that earlier capability mode, not proof of its exact behavior in every current ACPX configuration.

This request is for an upstream enforcement capability and design discussion. It does not claim that a local wrapper currently enforces execution-time per-target writes, nor that Landlock alone supplies that guarantee. A local ACPX fork is not proposed.

### Acceptance criteria for the ACPX change

1. A write succeeds only when its active dispatch presents a valid, unused authorization for the exact object actually mutated.
2. Path replacement, symlink retargeting, aliasing, and parent-directory races between authorization and open are denied or remain bound to the approved object.
3. Replay, cross-dispatch use, unapproved target, malformed authorization, and authorization/audit transport failure fail closed before mutation.
4. Tests cover create, overwrite, truncation, failure paths, and any other filesystem mutation API exposed by the client.
5. Tests demonstrate direct-runtime editing is either unavailable under the declared capability mode or subject to equivalent target authorization; an ACP-frame-only test is insufficient.
6. The documented security claim distinguishes per-target enforcement from workspace-wide sandbox confinement and from after-the-fact audit detection.

### Related

Related to #159058 (ACP-only agent identity/admission). That issue concerns which agent identities may be admitted; this one is a distinct request for enforcement at the filesystem mutation boundary, and does not amend identity or admission policy.

### Source

Evidence is summarized from the S1 feasibility review of ACPX 0.19.1. Relevant inspected implementation points were the `client.fs.writeTextFile` registration/dispatch and its `isWriteApproved`, `workspace.resolve`, `workspace.openWritable`, and `writeFile` sequence. No secrets, credentials, or local filesystem paths are included here.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6
- @openclaw/xiaomi-provider 2026.9.6
- provider: xiaomi-token-plan (https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/v1)
- model: mimo-v2.6-flash (primary), fallbacks configured: mimo-v2.6-pro -> deepseek-flash

## Symptom

An agent turn fails with: Agent run failed (model: xiaomi-token-plan/mimo-v2.6-flash) - and no reply is delivered.
The provider returned HTTP 200, and a fallback chain was configured, but the chain was never used.

## Log evidence

- [model-fetch] response provider=xiaomi-token-plan api=openai-completions model=mimo-v2.6-flash status=200 elapsedMs=4365 contentType=text/event-stream
- embedded_run_agent_end ... isError: true, rawErrorPreview: "Provider finish_reason: content_filter", failoverReason: null, providerRuntimeFailureKind: "unclassified"

## Analysis

The xiaomi provider plugin does not implement the provider-owned classifyFailoverReason hook (verified against the shipped dist/index.js of 2026.9.6), so a provider-side content-moderation finish reason lands in unclassified and never triggers the configured model fallbacks. The whole agent run is lost even though the fallback chain exists.

## Expected

Provider-side content moderation should be treated as a retryable/failover-worthy condition so the next model in the chain is attempted.
Note: FAILOVER_REASONS currently has no content-filter bucket (auth, auth_permanent, format, rate_limit, overloaded, billing, server_error, timeout, tls_certificate, context_overflow, model_not_found, session_expired, empty_response, no_error_details, unclassified, unknown). Mapping to empty_response would work; a dedicated reason could also be added.

## Notes

- Repro is content-dependent and hard to force; a unit test asserting classification for finish_reason=content_filter would cover it.
- Local workaround used here: a patched classifyFailoverReason that maps /content[_ -]?filter/i in errorMessage to empty_response.

issues.body:
### Summary
Let coordinator agents maintain their own Markdown memory through an independently grantable capability, without general filesystem write/edit or exec access.

### Problem to solve
A coordinator can be intentionally restricted to planning and delegation yet still need to retain decisions and preferences. Granting workspace-wide writes also exposes unrelated files; prompt instructions alone are not an enforced boundary. Keeping all writes disabled makes routine memory maintenance depend on another actor.

### Proposed solution
Provide a narrowly scoped capability for eligible `MEMORY.md` and `memory/*.md` targets within the agent's own workspace, preserving file-backed memory.

Desired constraints:
- Trusted runtime path enforcement, including traversal/symlink escape handling; no arbitrary files, prompt files, or configuration writes.
- Independent admission from general write/edit/exec tools.
- Read-before-edit and concurrency/conflict guards for any updates.
- Integration with memory provenance and indexing rather than a parallel untracked writer.

Append-only versus bounded edits is an open design choice, as is whether this belongs in a plugin or a core capability. These are requirements to discuss, not claimed security guarantees.

### Alternatives considered
Delegate writes to a permitted agent or human; grant broad writes; switch to LanceDB. These either add coordination, broaden access, or change the Markdown storage model.

### Impact
Affected: restricted multi-agent coordinators. Workflow friction whenever durable notes need updating; consequences are manual handoffs or overly broad permissions. No measured frequency or performance claims.

### Evidence/examples
Related design discussion: #116499. Prior art: #21003, closed for inactivity, not an explicit rejection of memory tools.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?
No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information
This is a concrete use-case/interest check, not a claim of no prior work or a replacement for #116499. Do others need this? Would maintainers prefer consolidating this use case there?

issues.body:
# OpenClaw Feature Request: Final-message-only delivery per channel

**Title:** Option to deliver only the final assistant message per request (suppress intermediate text turns)

**Component:** Channels / message delivery (Telegram, and likely all chat channels)

## Summary

In a multi-step agent request, the assistant often produces several text turns while working — orientation notes, progress narration, thinking-out-loud — before emitting the final answer. OpenClaw currently delivers **every** assistant text turn to the channel as its own message. The user's chat gets flooded with the model's internal process instead of just the result.

## Reproduction

1. Send the agent a task that requires multiple tool calls (e.g., "build this report and send me the file").
2. The model emits visible text alongside its tool calls in intermediate turns ("Let me check X", "Now let me process Y").
3. Each of those text turns is delivered to the Telegram chat as a separate message, before the final answer.

Observed on OpenClaw 2026.9.4–2026.9.6, Telegram direct chat, model ollama/glm-5.3-flash:cloud. The user received 6+ intermediate "thought process" messages for a single request.

## Impact

- Chat flooding: the user receives the model's internal monologue as messages they never asked for.
- Confusion: intermediate notes look like incomplete or broken replies.
- Privacy/comfort: the user sees the agent's raw internal process, which many will find unsettling even when it's benign.
- It cannot be fixed by prompting alone: the model may commit to keeping turns text-free, but any slip re-introduces the leak, and the discipline has to hold for every future model upgrade.

## Proposed solution

A per-channel delivery setting, e.g.:

```json
channels:
  telegram:
    deliveryMode: final-only   # "all-turns" (current behavior) | "final-only"
```

- **final-only:** suppress delivery of assistant text turns that are followed by additional tool calls in the same request; deliver only the last text turn of the request (the actual reply). Intermediate text still stays in the session transcript for auditability — it is simply not pushed to the channel.
- Optionally: a `deliveryMode: final-only-quiet` variant that also suppresses the "tool started / finished" progress notices for users who want strictly one bubble per request.

## Workarounds tried and why they are insufficient

- Prompting the model to emit no intermediate text: partially works, but slips are frequent across long tasks and model changes (observed repeatedly over multiple sessions).
- `channels.telegram.streaming: off`: controls streaming/partial display, not which turns are delivered.
- No existing configuration key suppresses intermediate-turn delivery (checked the channel and gateway configuration docs for 2026.9.6).

## Request

Please add a per-channel (or per-account) option to deliver only the final assistant message of a request, keeping intermediate turns in the transcript but out of the user's chat. This would make multi-step agent work usable in chat channels without leaking the model's internal process.

issues.body:
### What happened

Switching between chats in the Control UI (sidebar / agent chips) frequently lands the transcript **near the top** of the loaded history instead of at the most recent messages. The user then has to scroll down manually to reach the newest turn.

This is reproducible across chats belonging to different agents, and the landing point is not the position that was last visible before leaving — it is well above it.

### Expected

Opening or switching back to a chat should show the newest message (bottom of transcript), consistent with the documented "returns to the latest message" behavior. At minimum, a restored reading position should match the position the reader actually left.

### Actual

The restored scroll offset resolves against a shorter transcript than it was measured on, so the viewport ends up high in the loaded history. Likely contributors:

- History loads in pages (~80 recent messages on open, older pages fetched on scroll back).
- Content *above* the anchor (images, expanded tool output) finishes resizing after the restore offset is computed, shifting the anchor.
- A saved position is restored instead of "newest message" being the default for an unread/advancing session.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Control UI and select a long chat (enough to require paging).
2. Scroll to the bottom so the newest messages are visible.
3. Switch to a different chat (different agent/session).
4. Switch back to the first chat.

Result: the transcript opens near the top of the loaded history rather than at the newest messages.

### Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.9.6 (eb377ac)
- npm `latest` = `beta` = 2026.9.6; `extended-stable` is older (2026.7.35), so this is the newest build
- Platform: macOS 15.7 (arm64), Chrome
- Surface: Control UI webchat, authenticated Gateway profile
- No configuration key or Control UI setting appears to control this; `configuration-reference.md` has no scroll-related key and Control UI Settings exposes no toggle.

### Notes

The 2026.9.6 changelog already contains a fix in this area ("Chat layout: … settle saved scroll positions once, prevent Chrome crashes during delayed scrolling"), so this may be a remaining edge of that same class of bug, specifically for the session-switch path (as opposed to in-chat delayed scrolling).

Possibly related open issues (none cover this exact path):

- #149727 — WebUI: measurement scroll compensation can trigger extra history loads
- #152831 — WebUI: expanded activity groups lose reading position after virtual remount
- #152819 — WebUI: toggling Tool calls loses active and retained conversation reading positions

### Workaround

- Use the transcript's down-arrow (jump to latest) after switching.
- Sending any message snaps the view to the newest part.
- Scroll to the bottom before leaving a chat, since the position is remembered per session.

### Impact

Low severity, high frequency: it is a small manual correction on every chat switch, and it directly contradicts the "read latest messages" intent when the newest turn is what you came to see.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Control UI / Workboard

### Summary

In the Workboard card actions menu, the **Move to** status picker displays a status that does not match the column the card is actually in, and choosing a status from that picker does not move the card.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed repeatedly on a live board (not a synthetic fixture):

1. Open the Workboard page in the OpenClaw Control UI in a browser.
2. Have cards present in the **Triage** column.
3. Click the `...` (Card actions) trigger on a card that sits in **Triage**.
4. Look at the **Move to** select inside the popover.

Observed on both a phone browser and a desktop browser, against the same gateway. The board is filtered by agent (`Agente: ...` chip, `All work` scope).

### Expected behavior

The **Move to** select shows the card's current status (`Triage` for a card in the Triage column), and selecting a different status moves the card to that column.

### Actual behavior

The select shows a status belonging to a **different column**, while the card itself is still rendered in Triage:

- Card `Ir a Betel??` in **Triage** (column count 2) - picker shows **Pendientes** (`todo`).
- Card `Lavar el carro` in **Triage** (column count 1) - picker shows **Programado** (`scheduled`).

Selecting a status in that picker has no visible effect: the card does not move and the picker does not correct itself.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6 (eb377ac)

### Operating system

Gateway host: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2, Node v24.20.0. Reproduced from both a mobile browser and a desktop browser.

### Install method

npm global install (`openclaw`)

### Model

Not model-dependent; this is a Control UI rendering issue.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable; the defect is in the Control UI Workboard surface.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Two screenshots attached below, both taken on the reporting user's phone browser, showing the Triage column and the open card actions popover with a mismatched **Move to** value.

### Impact and severity

The status control misreports a card's state, so the board cannot be trusted at a glance. Because the picker is also the control used to move the card, the user is left unable to change that card's status from the menu.

### Additional information

Investigation notes from a contributor, offered to save triage time. These are things that were **ruled out**, not conclusions:

An initial hypothesis was that `.value=${card.status}` on the status `<select>` (`extensions/workboard/browser/pages/workboard/view-card-actions.ts`, `extensions/workboard/browser/widgets/render.ts`) needs Lit's `live()` directive, since the surrounding `cards.map()` has no key and reuses DOM across cards.

DOM reuse across cards was confirmed with instrumentation: a `<select>` element first attached to one card was later attached to a different card after the first card left its column.

However, the stale-value hypothesis could **not** be reproduced in a real browser (Chromium, Playwright, `--fixture=workboard` mock dev server), in seven scenarios, both on the Workboard page and the dashboard widget, with and without the `live()` change:

- moving a card out of a column and reopening another card's popover
- the same flow at a narrow mobile viewport
- the dashboard widget, where the selects are always visible rather than inside a popover
- a move request that is never acknowledged
- a move request rejected by the gateway
- externally desynchronising the control value and then forcing a re-render

In every case the displayed value self-corrected, because each `<option>` carries `?selected=${status === card.status}`, which Lit refreshes on re-render.

So the `.value` binding alone does not appear to explain the reported symptom. Two observations that may be more relevant:

1. In the second screenshot the Triage column holds only one card, yet the picker shows `Programado` (`scheduled`) - a status with its own separate column. That looks less like a stale value and more like the popover content not corresponding to the card whose trigger was clicked.
2. `moveCardToStatus` (`view-card-actions.ts`) returns early when `status === card.status`. Once the control is showing a status the card does not actually have, the user's attempt to select the card's real status is silently dropped, which matches the reported "selecting does nothing" behavior.

The reporting environment differs from the fixture in ways that were not reproduced locally: a live gateway with background card movement by agents, an agent filter applied to the board, and a custom set of populated statuses.

issues.body:
## Problem

Selecting and copying text from chat messages in the WebChat UI is very difficult. On the message bubble, text selection frequently fails or gets lost — the selection jumps, clears, or only partially covers the intended lines, so copying a specific piece of an answer requires many attempts.

This comes up whenever a user wants to copy something the assistant produced: an answer, a block of code, a command, a hardware link list, etc. What should be a one-second select-and-copy turns into a frustrating fight with the UI.

## Expected behavior

- Click-drag inside a message should reliably select text (normal browser selection behavior).
- A copy button (or menu item) per message to copy the whole message as plain text/markdown.
- Ideally an export/copy-as-markdown for a longer exchange.

## Actual behavior

- Selection inside message bubbles is unreliable: highlight jumps or disappears mid-drag, making precise selection hard.
- No per-message copy affordance to fall back on.

## Environment

- Surface: WebChat / Control UI (browser)
- Happens in current stable build; reproducible by simply trying to select several lines inside any assistant message.

## Suggestion

At minimum set user-select-friendly styles on message content (avoid interception of pointer/selection events on the bubble, don't clear selection on hover/scroll), and add a copy button per message as a fallback.

issues.body:
## Summary

In a long-running Telegram direct conversation used to manage several parallel projects, context compaction omitted one active project (**Avenbot**) from the compacted summary. The session itself continued, but when the user later asked the agent to list the projects discussed, Avenbot was missing.

The normal recovery path also failed: repeated calls to `agent_knowledge_recall` returned only:

```
recall failed: {"error":"Upstream Hindsight request failed."}
```

This combination makes a single long-lived personal agent unreliable for managing multiple project streams: a fact dropped by compaction becomes unrecoverable unless the user repeats it manually.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.7.1`
- Channel: Telegram direct conversation
- Conversation shape: long-lived, tool-heavy session with several parallel project streams
- Memory/recall path: Hindsight-backed `agent_knowledge_recall`

No Telegram IDs, credentials, raw chat text, or user-specific configuration are included here.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use one Telegram agent session for several independent, ongoing projects.
2. Let the conversation grow until automatic compaction occurs.
3. Have one active project mentioned in older conversation history but not promoted into the workspace `MEMORY.md`.
4. After compaction, ask the agent to enumerate the projects discussed.
5. Observe that one active project is absent from the compacted summary.
6. Try to recover it with `agent_knowledge_recall`.
7. Repeat the recall on later turns.

## Actual behavior

- The post-compaction session remains usable, so this is not a complete session reset.
- The compacted summary omits an active project.
- `agent_knowledge_recall` fails repeatedly with the generic upstream Hindsight error.
- Workspace memory contains other projects but cannot restore the omitted one.
- The assistant has to ask the user to repeat information that was already provided.

The recall failure was observed repeatedly across separate turns rather than as a single transient call.

## Expected behavior

At least one recovery layer should preserve continuity:

1. Pre-compaction memory flush should retain active project/entity names and their current status; or
2. Hindsight recall should retrieve facts from pre-compaction history; or
3. If Hindsight is temporarily unavailable, OpenClaw should fall back to searching the prior session transcript / last valid checkpoint; or
4. The error should expose an actionable status and correlation information instead of only `Upstream Hindsight request failed`.

A useful invariant would be: after compaction, every active project present before compaction is either represented in the compacted summary, promoted to durable memory, or retrievable through recall.

## Impact

For personal agents that coordinate multiple workstreams, this appears to the user as selective amnesia. It undermines the core expectation that one bot can maintain several concurrent projects.

## Related issue

- #60213 describes total session loss/orphaning after compaction. This report is different: the session continued, but compaction was lossy and the memory fallback failed, producing selective unrecoverable loss.

## Suggested diagnostics/tests

- Add an integration test with multiple named active workstreams across a compaction boundary.
- Simulate a Hindsight outage during post-compaction recall and verify transcript/checkpoint fallback.
- Log a non-sensitive failure category/correlation ID for Hindsight upstream errors.
- Verify that pre-compaction flush captures active entities/workstreams, not only recently repeated facts.

issues.body:
## Summary

When one plugin fails to load on boot, the gateway crash-loop breaker suppresses autostart for **every** channel, turning a single-plugin problem into a total outage. Separately, `openclaw update` still proceeds when a configured plugin has no release for the target version — the exact configuration that triggers this.

## Observed

Host upgraded to 2026.8.1 while `@openclaw/whatsapp` was one release behind. The plugin crashed on boot against the new plugin SDK; three unclean boots within five minutes tripped the crash-loop breaker, which then suppressed autostart for all channels. Slack and every other surface went dark because of one plugin. Recovery required a manual `launchctl kickstart` after bumping the plugin.

## Current update behavior

`docs/cli/update.md` ("Plugin sync details"): post-core plugin sync is a big improvement, but "an unavailable target remains a named warning while the core update continues." Target-cohort plugins also declare `peerDependencies.openclaw >= <target>`, so they cannot be pre-updated on the old host — the operator has no safe ordering if a target is missing.

`openclaw update --dry-run --json` lists "Run plugin update sync after core update" but does not report per-plugin target availability.

## Asks

1. **Breaker scope:** attribute boot crashes to the plugin whose load threw, quarantine that plugin (disabled with a loud diagnostic and a channel-status entry), and boot the gateway without it rather than suppressing every channel.
2. **Update preflight:** when a configured, enabled plugin has no target-cohort release (or its peer range rejects the target), fail the update or require an explicit `--allow-plugin-drift`, instead of warning and continuing.
3. **Dry run:** have `--dry-run` report per-plugin target availability and peer-range compatibility.

## Local workaround

We gate upgrades with a preflight that checks each enabled npm plugin has `<pkg>@<target>` published with a peer range accepting the target, and HOLDs otherwise.

Environment: macOS (arm64), launchd-managed gateway, npm global install, currently 2026.9.5.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a multi-agent install with no channel-wide Telegram route, a Telegram conversation that has an active session binding fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError`: ordinary agent selection runs before the binding is consulted. This is the Telegram counterpart of #159080 (LINE, fixed by #159116) and #123159 (iMessage).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure two agents (`main`, `codex`) and no `bindings` entry for Telegram.
2. Bind a Telegram direct conversation to a session owned by `codex` (e.g. `agent:codex:acp:session-1`).
3. Receive a message in that conversation.

### Expected behavior

The bound agent is selected, as it already is with a single agent and as LINE and iMessage now do.

### Actual behavior

```
AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but telegram account default routing has no explicit owner. ...
```

`prepareTelegramConversationRoute` in `extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route.ts` calls `resolveAgentRoute` first and applies the runtime binding afterwards. With no route owner the first call throws, so the binding is never reached. This affects both `resolveTelegramConversationRoute` (inbound) and `inspectTelegramConversationRoute` (native command authorization).

### OpenClaw version

`main` at f3b6fecc63d (2026-09-27); same code in 2026.9.5

### Operating system

macOS 26 (reproduced in the unit suite; platform-independent)

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

N/A — fails during inbound routing, before any model call.

### Provider / routing chain

N/A — Telegram inbound routing.

### Logs

See Actual behavior.

### Impact and severity

Messages in a runtime-bound Telegram conversation are not processed on multi-agent installs that rely on the binding rather than a channel-wide route. Adding a channel-wide Telegram binding works around it.

A fix with regression coverage follows in a linked PR.

issues.body:
## Summary
Matrix picks a room's `tools` policy and `requireMention` setting by matching the room's display name (`m.room.name`) against `channels.matrix.groups` keys. Any room member allowed to rename the room controls that name. A room renamed to `!trusted:example.org` inherits the trusted room's tool policy and skips the `"*"` entry, so tools denied everywhere else (for example `exec`, `write`) become available in that room.

## Environment
- Commit: 58108eeecc526d16bbdf42fbb761b4719a02e82e (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: Matrix channel plugin, group tool policy and requireMention resolution

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure Matrix with `groupPolicy: "open"` and `groups: { "*": { tools: { deny: ["exec", "write"] } }, "!trusted:example.org": { tools: { allow: ["exec", "write"] } } }`.
2. In another room the bot is in (for example `!attacker:evil.example`), set the room name to `!trusted:example.org`.
3. Message the bot in that room and resolve its tool policy.

## Expected
The room resolves to the `"*"` entry (deny `exec`, `write`), because its room id is not configured.

## Actual
The room resolves to the `!trusted:example.org` entry (allow `exec`, `write`).

## Root cause (if known)
`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler-context.ts:276` sets `GroupSubject` to the room name:

```ts
GroupSubject: isRoom ? (roomName ?? roomId) : undefined,
```

Matrix never sets `GroupChannel`, so core fills `groupChannel` from `GroupSubject` (`get-reply-run-execute.ts`, `get-reply.ts`, `agent-runner-embedded-candidate.ts`) and `resolveGroupToolPolicyOutcome` in `src/agents/agent-tools.policy.ts` passes it to the plugin. `extensions/matrix/src/group-mentions.ts` then treats it as a trusted alias:

```ts
const groupChannel = normalizeMatrixResolvableTarget(params.groupChannel ?? "");
return {
  tree,
  path: resolveMatrixRoomScopePath({ tree, roomId, aliases: groupChannel ? [groupChannel] : [] }),
};
```

The unlisted room id misses, so the room-name alias matches the trusted entry ahead of `"*"`. Ingress gating already avoids live room names (it uses server-verified canonical aliases, and name matching sits behind the dangerous name-matching flag), but this lookup has no such guard.

## Possible fix
Only use `groupChannel` when it names the same room as the trusted `groupId` (case-insensitive), so a display name can never select another room's entry. A three-line change in `group-mentions.ts`; the existing case-preserved room id behavior keeps working. A branch with this change and regression coverage is ready if maintainers want a PR.

## Sibling surfaces
`resolveMatrixGroupRequireMention` uses the same scope lookup, so a renamed room also inherits the trusted room's `requireMention: false`. Ingress allowlisting is unaffected (it does not trust live room names).

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a Matrix room renamed to a configured room id inherits that room's tools policy instead of the "*" deny.
Real environment tested: the real core resolveGroupToolPolicy with the real matrixPlugin registered, on origin/main 088ff09b59 and with the proposed change applied, identical config and inputs.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: a node --import tsx script that registers matrixPlugin, then resolves group tool policy for room !attacker:evil.example named "Lobby" and named "!trusted:example.org", plus the real !trusted:example.org room.
Evidence after fix:
```
# OBSERVED (origin/main 088ff09b59)
room=!attacker:evil.example m.room.name="Lobby" -> policy={"deny":["exec","write"]}
room=!attacker:evil.example m.room.name="!trusted:example.org" -> policy={"allow":["exec","write"]}
room=!trusted:example.org m.room.name="Ops" -> policy={"allow":["exec","write"]}
# EXPECTED (proposed change, identical inputs)
room=!attacker:evil.example m.room.name="Lobby" -> policy={"deny":["exec","write"]}
room=!attacker:evil.example m.room.name="!trusted:example.org" -> policy={"deny":["exec","write"]}
room=!trusted:example.org m.room.name="Ops" -> policy={"allow":["exec","write"]}
```
Observed result after fix: on main the attacker room named "!trusted:example.org" resolves to allow exec and write; with the change it resolves to the "*" deny, while the real trusted room keeps its allow.
What was not tested: a live Matrix homeserver session and a full Gateway run; the policy resolution path above is the same one the Gateway calls per message.

## Purpose

Track evidence-backed Control UI hardening for 30 people using OpenClaw concurrently. This is an issue-only investigation of frozen main `10e9c41a9af7e57e0b5e27abfc156f4131dd50bf`; it does not propose a deployment or weaken session safety checks.

## Confirmed findings

- [ ] **#159332 — Collaborator drafts displace the conversation.** With one observer and 29 active drafts, the typing previews occupy 2,813 px in a 578 px desktop thread viewport, and 2,697 px in a 669 px mobile thread viewport. At the bottom, the observer sees unsent drafts while the agent response is several screens above. The existing draft #159263 targets this behavior; the captures below provide reproduction evidence.
- [ ] **#159330 — Concurrent first sends can be rejected as branch changes.** In the completed real-Gateway run against an empty shared conversation, seven of 30 sends were accepted and 23 returned `active-leaf-changed`, although nobody changed branches. All rejected prompts remained recoverable with **Not sent / Retry / Discard**. All seven accepted inputs settled; reconnect and verified database snapshot checks passed. One accepted request was an ordinary send and six used the native steer action after the run became active; the probe did not override queue behavior. The ratio depends on scheduling; this does not establish lost messages.

## What was exercised

| --- | --- | --- |
| 30 independent sessions | 30/30 complete replies matched exact native message retrieval and rendered text; unique sender identities; empty queues; database integrity checks passed | Real Gateway, SQLite, WebSockets and Chromium; deterministic local provider |
| Input, reading anchor and rich streaming | Focus and unsent text retained; no sampled anchor drift or blank frames in the controlled reading scenario | Production renderer with synthetic Gateway events |
| Slow reader isolation | One stalled reader disconnected; one healthy witness received the complete burst; all 29 healthy connections remained responsive | Real transport with existing model/plugin mocks; adversarial 80 MiB burst |
| Uncertain send acknowledgement | No automatic duplicate send; explicit retry retained its idempotency key; exact history proof settled the pending item | Existing native admission test plus browser tests with mock transport |
| Shared active conversation | 30 inputs admitted and four reconnects completed while inputs were pending; full drain did not finish within the 120-second observation window | Input remained accounted for and processing continued; latency cause is not isolated |

### Summary

On 2026.9.6 (Windows, single gateway, SQLite WAL), every **cold agent-database open performs a synchronous whole-DB integrity validation** before admission. On a 1 GB agent DB that blocks for ~4.5 minutes per open, and the validation re-runs roughly every 8-10 minutes. Any agent turn that overlaps it exceeds the 300 s per-chat cap and is evicted, so the user's message silently gets no reply while the gateway itself is healthy.

### Evidence (one agent's DB, `state/agent-db` op log)

```
phaseDurationsMs:     { open: 5, validation: 261564, configuration: 13, schema: 0, registration: 9 }
integrityGateMs:       261396
integrityCheckSyncMs:  261388
integrityGateOutcome:  "healthy"
admissionMode:         "sync"
```

Same operation on a 58 MB agent DB: `validation: 27206 ms`, `integrityGateMs: 27123` -> roughly **0.25-0.47 s per MB, linear in DB size**.

Three consecutive samples on the large DB: **261.6 s, 267.3 s, 271.0 s** (07:29, 07:39, 07:46 local), i.e. the gate recurs ~every 8-10 minutes and on a 1 GB DB roughly half of wall-clock time is spent inside a blocking integrity check.

### Impact

```
per-chat task exceeded 300000ms cap (key=feishu:<agent>:<chat>); evicting from queue
stalled session: sessionKey=agent:<agent>:feishu:direct:master state=processing   (every 30 s, ~10 min)
```

The turn's reply is discarded and the user sees nothing. In the same window we also see lane-level admission blocks (`Agent database execution admission is closed` for other agents), `failed to record session participant`, and one `failed before reply`.

### Docs contradiction

`docs/auth-credential-semantics.md` (~line 91) says:

> Cold agent opens validate integrity asynchronously and recheck ownership before writing.

The runtime path is clearly synchronous (`integrityCheckSyncMs`, `admissionMode: "sync"`), i.e. it blocks admission for the whole validation instead of running off the admission path.

### Asks

1. Make the cold-open integrity validation asynchronous (off the admission path), as the docs describe.
2. Or bound it: incremental / `quick_check` with a TTL, full check scheduled off-peak.
3. Expose configuration (interval / disable / budget) so operators can trade integrity confidence against reply latency on large DBs.
4. When a turn is dropped because of local DB latency, distinguish "gateway busy, please resend" from a genuine failure in the user-visible copy.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Windows Server, node 24.18.0, single gateway, loopback WS, SQLite WAL, `integrityGateOutcome: healthy` (no corruption found), 10 agents, largest agent DB ~1052 MB vs 49-174 MB for the others.

issues.body:
### Summary
Add an optional, pluggable content-quality judge that runs only on the promotion apply path (the actual MEMORY.md write), as an additional gate that rejects only high-confidence noise, and fails open on any error.

### Problem to solve
Deterministic promotion ranking scores frequency/recency/diversity and cannot see CONTENT-EMPTY snippets. In a production sample, bare session-metadata fragments scored 0.57-0.59 deterministically — above a 0.75 promotion threshold in some configs, and always above `--min-score 0` previews — while an LLM judge rated them ~0.01/3 at ~0.99 confidence. Such fragments pollute MEMORY.md.

### Proposed solution
- Apply-path ONLY (never in preview/dry-run): an additional gate after existing ranking/thresholds, before the writer.
- Reject only when the judge is BOTH clearly negative (score <= 0.5) AND high-confidence (>= 0.8) — ordinary low-but-real judgments are never rejected on this gate alone.
- FAIL OPEN by construction: missing config/key, network error, timeout, or malformed response keeps the candidate. A flaky third-party call must never silently shrink what gets promoted.
- Judge behind a small pluggable hook (any HTTP endpoint returning {score, confidence}); no vendor baked in.

### Alternatives considered
- Distillation gate (#98092, closed not_planned): different problem — rewriting entries rather than filtering empty ones; this proposal changes neither content nor ranking, it only drops confidently-empty candidates.
- Tightening deterministic thresholds: would also drop real low-frequency memories (measured overlap).

### Impact
Affected: deployments with auto-promotion (dreaming) writing into MEMORY.md.
Severity: medium (long-term index hygiene).
Frequency: each apply run with candidates.
Consequence: empty metadata fragments permanently enter the curated index today.

### Evidence / examples
Pilot: 10 real production candidates through `openclaw memory promote --json`; the two noise cases scored 0.57-0.59 deterministically vs 0.01 with confidence 0.99 from the judge.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?
Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information
Gate must stay opt-in and fail-open; no behavior change when unconfigured.

issues.body:
### Summary
The queued file writer re-runs the full symlink-walk safety sequence (parent walk, lstat, open, fstat, lstat again, write, close) for every single line. When `maxFileBytes` is undefined the cap cannot be tripped mid-batch, so lines can be coalesced into one identical append.

### Problem to solve
Per-line appends pay the whole safety protocol N times for what is logically one write; high-frequency line sinks (logs, diagnostics) amplify this into measurable syscall overhead.

### Proposed solution
When `options.maxFileBytes === undefined`: accumulate lines (batchLines/batchBytes) and let the queue link drain them into a single `safeAppendFile(drained.join(""))` — callers already newline-terminate lines, so output is byte-identical. When a cap IS configured, keep the exact per-line path so the cap still trips at the same byte offset. Diagnostics remain per-line; `yieldBeforeWrite` still runs once per drained batch as the backpressure hook.

### Alternatives considered
- Always batching: rejected — would move where `maxFileBytes` trips.
- Relying on OS append coalescing: does not avoid the repeated safety walk in user space.

### Impact
Affected: any hot queued-file sink (transcripts/diagnostics).
Severity: low-medium (CPU/syscall waste, scales with line rate).
Frequency: every batch of writes.
Consequence: unnecessary IO overhead.

### Evidence / examples
Diff prototype: uncapped path only; capped path byte-for-byte identical to current behavior (same test suite passes).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?
Maybe, with maintainer guidance

issues.body:
### Summary
SQLite databases in WAL mode currently inherit synchronous=FULL, fsyncing on every commit. Defaulting to NORMAL for WAL (keeping FULL for rollback-journal DBs) cuts commit cost ~90x in our measurements without risking corruption.

### Problem to solve
Measured on ext4: 1.79 ms per commit at FULL vs 0.02 ms at NORMAL. State databases under agent load commit frequently, so FULL pays a constant, avoidable tax.

### Proposed solution
In `configureSqliteConnectionPragmas`: when no explicit `synchronous` option is provided AND `PRAGMA journal_mode` resolves to `wal`, apply `NORMAL`. Explicit options always win; rollback-journal databases keep current behavior (FULL stays required there — NORMAL can corrupt a non-WAL DB). Rationale: under WAL the write-ahead log already survives a process crash; NORMAL only risks losing the most recent commits to an OS/power failure and never corrupts the database.

### Alternatives considered
- Leaving FULL: safe but pays 1.79 ms/commit indefinitely.
- Global NORMAL regardless of journal mode: rejected — unsafe for rollback-journal databases.

### Impact
Affected: all WAL state databases (gateway state, agent DBs).
Severity: medium (steady-state write latency).
Frequency: every commit.
Consequence: measurable event-loop/CPU savings under write-heavy load.

### Evidence / examples
Micro-benchmark on the deployment host (ext4): FULL 1.79 ms/commit vs NORMAL 0.02 ms/commit; SQLite docs: NORMAL + WAL is the commonly recommended durability/performance tradeoff.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?
Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information
Backward compatible: any caller already passing `synchronous` is unaffected.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A valid, funded OpenRouter API key — confirmed working via direct curl against https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions — is consistently rejected by OpenClaw with 401/403 "authentication failed" errors, both via the desktop app's onboarding wizard and via CLI (models auth login + models status --probe). This persists across two full version updates (2026.9.4 → 2026.9.6) and multiple freshly-generated API keys.

Related and possibly overlapping root causes:

#145016 (staged route mismatch in onboarding wizard verify step)
#145929 / 
#148557 / 
#149993 / 
#151103 (auth store "lock may be busy" — false lock contention from a stale-snapshot comparison bug)
#59205 (same class of bug — valid key via curl, 401 via OpenClaw — previously seen with Ollama Cloud after an update)

Environment
OpenClaw version: 2026.9.4 → updated to 2026.9.6 (eb377ac) during troubleshooting, issue persists on both
OS: macOS GoldenGate(Apple Silicon, arm64)
Node version: v26.8.2
Install method: Homebrew npm global install + macOS desktop app 
Provider: OpenRouter, API key auth
Model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 (also reproduced with openrouter/auto)

### Steps to reproduce

Install OpenClaw desktop app on macOS, fresh workspace
Enter a valid OpenRouter API key either via the app's onboarding "Connect with an API key" screen, or via CLI:
   openclaw models auth login --provider openrouter --method api-key --agent main
Set the model explicitly:
   openclaw models set openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5
Probe the connection:
   openclaw gateway stop
   openclaw models status --probe
   openclaw gateway start

### Expected behavior

The request should succeed (200), matching direct API behavior with the identical key and model.

### Actual behavior

[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=openrouter api=openai-completions model=anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 status=403 elapsedMs=1924
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=openrouter api=openai-completions model=anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 status=401 elapsedMs=99
⚠️ openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 request failed (authentication failed, HTTP 401). Re-authenticate the provider and try again.

Note the inconsistent status code across immediate retries of the same request (403 then 401) — this alone suggests non-deterministic request construction rather than a stable, correct rejection.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6

### Operating system

GoldenGate 27.0

### Install method

Npm global 

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5

### Provider / routing chain

open claw / Openrouter

### Additional provider/model setup details

Proof the key and model are valid (isolates this to OpenClaw)

Direct curl with the exact same key used in the failing OpenClaw probe:

bash
curl https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-or-v1-...-066c14f5" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}'

Result: 200, valid completion returned, real cost billed to the account (confirmed in OpenRouter dashboard usage).

Additional observed issues along the way (may be related or separate bugs)
Doubled model prefix: openclaw models set openrouter/auto silently saves the model as openrouter/openrouter/auto instead of openrouter/auto. Setting an explicit model (openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5) avoids this specific duplication.
Auth store / models.json desync: Across this session, openclaw models status repeatedly showed different key suffixes in the sqlite auth store (effective=profiles:...sqlite) versus models.json, even after using models auth login to set the key explicitly. The models.json value appears stale/unused once a sqlite profile exists, but is never cleaned up or reconciled, making models status output confusing/misleading.
The 2026.9.6 update's own migration duplicated the OpenRouter profile: post-update, models status --probe showed two profiles — openrouter:default and a new, previously-nonexistent openrouter:models-json — both independently failing with 401. It appears the update's doctor migration ([update] Doctor migration: openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 model configured, enabled automatically.) created a second profile from the stale models.json value rather than reconciling it with the existing sqlite profile.
models auth logout false "lock may be busy": Attempting to clean up the duplicate/stale profile via openclaw models auth logout openrouter:default --yes fails with Failed to remove auth profile "openrouter:default"; the auth store lock may be busy, reproduced with:
Gateway fully stopped (launchctl unload confirmed no process on port 18789)
PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE); returning clean (busy: 0)
agent_database_leases table containing only a lease matching a confirmed-dead PID (removed manually, did not resolve the logout failure)
This matches the exact pattern described in 
#145929/
#148557/
#149980 (stale-snapshot comparison misreported as lock contention).
Desktop app appears to silently rewrite the OpenRouter key on launch/quit, independent of CLI-set values — observed the effective key change across multiple app relaunches without manual intervention, contributing to the desync in point 2.
Suggested starting points for maintainers
Given #59205 describes the identical class of symptom (valid key confirmed via curl, 401 via OpenClaw) for a different provider (Ollama Cloud) after an update, and diagnosed it as an Authorization-header construction issue — worth checking whether OpenRouter's provider adapter shares that same request-building code path.
The inconsistent 403→401 status codes across immediate retries of the identical request point at either non-deterministic header construction or a race between two now-duplicated auth profiles both being tried per request.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

[openclaw-openrouter-auth-bug-report.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32836748/openclaw-openrouter-auth-bug-report.md)

### Impact and severity

Severity: High — complete, unrecoverable loss of function for an entire provider integration, with no user-side workaround.

Scope: Blocks 100% of OpenRouter usage through OpenClaw. OpenRouter is one of the primary "bring your own model routing" backends OpenClaw advertises, and this affects both onboarding paths into it (desktop app wizard and CLI), not an edge case within it.
Not user-fixable: This isn't a misconfiguration. It was reproduced with multiple independently-generated API keys, across a fresh workspace, across two full version updates, with the Gateway stopped, with stale state manually cleaned (dead leases removed, WAL checkpointed), and with the key's validity independently confirmed via direct curl. There is no sequence of user-side steps found that resolves it.
Silent data corruption risk: Beyond the auth failure itself, the bug actively damages user config during normal operation — the update process's own migration logic duplicated a working single auth profile into two conflicting ones (openrouter:default / openrouter:models-json), and the desktop app appears to silently rewrite the stored key on its own launch/quit cycle. A user who hasn't gone as deep into CLI/sqlite inspection as this report would have no way to detect that their config is being altered out from under them — they'd just see intermittent, unexplained auth failures.
Misleading diagnostics compound the problem: The "auth store lock may be busy" message actively misdirects troubleshooting effort toward lock contention (the natural read of that message) when the actual cause, per 
#149980, is a stale-snapshot comparison bug. This cost significant investigation time here chasing leases, WAL locks, and process ownership — all red herrings — before finding the real pattern.
No safe recovery path: The one built-in recovery mechanism attempted (openclaw update, hoping a newer release would fix it) instead made state worse by duplicating the auth profile. Version rollback was considered but not attempted, since none of the related open issues indicate a known-good prior version to roll back to.
User-facing consequence: A new user following the documented/expected setup flow (app onboarding → paste key → done) hits a hard, unexplained wall on their very first setup attempt, with the UI's own error message ("Review model runtime policy and retry") giving no actionable path forward. This is a first-run blocker, not a power-user edge case.

### Additional information

_No response_

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Windows 11 x64, multi-agent install (several agents plus platform-owned scheduled jobs).

Problem: the agent-facing automations/cron listing surface is agent-scoped: from inside an agent session it shows only that agent's jobs. Platform-owned jobs and other agents' jobs are invisible from the tool surface, while the CLI (`openclaw cron list`) shows the authoritative full inventory. The asymmetry is not documented where agents will read it.

Real incident (2026-07-25): an agent archived what looked like a plain conversation because its own listing showed no attached scheduled job; a hidden platform-owned job then misfired 23 times against a stale target before anyone correlated the two. Our workaround is a recurring cross-check that runs the CLI, which only works because the agent learned to distrust its own tool view.

Request: an opt-in full-inventory view from the agent tool surface (list all / include platform jobs, read-only job metadata), and/or at minimum: (a) document the scoping prominently in the tool description, and (b) include the owning agent/session in every job row so scoping mismatches are detectable from the partial view itself.

issues.body:
## Summary

Expose previous `/new`/`/reset` segments of a channel-routed conversation in the Control UI as human-readable history, with an explicit way to fork a historical segment into a new, independently resumable UI thread.

## Problem to solve

In a Telegram DM routed to the main session, `/new` gives a fresh conversation context and internal session ID, but keeps the stable routing key (`agent:main:main`). The Sessions list shows the current main conversation, not each previous segment. The old transcript remains stored and agent-side transcript search can find its messages, but the user cannot treat a prior Telegram segment like a named Web UI conversation: locate it in a conversation list, read it as a coherent segment, and resume work from that point in a separate thread.

This makes `/new` useful for clearing context but awkward for a workflow that alternates among topics in a channel. It also creates an asymmetry: explicitly created Web UI threads can be named and reopened, whereas prior channel-chat segments are not first-class conversations in the UI. This request is about discoverability and controlled resumption, not about automatically restoring old messages to the model after a reset or rebinding Telegram to an old session.

Observed on OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Telegram DM -> default `main` agent, with transcript search enabled. The installed session documentation also says: “Session lists show the current live conversation, not every historical session id behind it.”

## Proposed solution

- From the main/channel conversation in Control UI, provide a **Previous segments / History** view of retained reset segments under its stable session key. Show dates, reset boundaries, channel, and a derived or editable title where available.
- Let the user open each segment as a readable conversation without changing the live Telegram route or silently injecting that segment into the current model context.
- Offer **Continue in new thread** (fork) from a selected historical segment or message. This should create a separate, named UI session that can be reopened and continued independently. The Telegram DM should continue to route to the current main session unless explicitly supported routing is added separately.
- Keep existing permissions and retention rules: only authorized viewers may see historical content, and removed/expired history must not be resurrected.

A smaller first increment—read-only, linked historical segments in the UI—would already solve the discoverability part. Forking solves the distinct “resume this old topic” need.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use `/new` only:** clears context but does not create a separately addressable conversation in the UI.
- **Create all long-lived topics in Web UI:** works for new topics, but is not practical when the conversation starts naturally in Telegram and does not expose prior Telegram segments.
- **Agent-side transcript search or Sessions → Search transcripts:** useful for finding facts; not a coherent user-facing conversation browser or a reliable resume/fork workflow.
- **Usage/history views:** may provide read-only transcript inspection, but should not be the only path to find and continue a conversation from the Sessions/Chat experience.

## Impact

Affected: users who use Telegram or other channel DMs as their primary interface and reset the rolling session with `/new` or `/reset`.

Severity: UX/workflow friction, not observed data loss.

Frequency: every time a user wants to return to a topic discussed before a reset.

Consequence: users must ask the agent to reconstruct the conversation through search or manually recreate the task in a new UI thread; they cannot directly browse and fork the prior channel segment as they can with an explicit UI thread.

## Evidence/examples

- Related older request for per-key `/new` history in Sessions UI: #4655 (closed not planned in February 2026).
- Report that old reset segments do not appear in the session selector: #42336 (closed as duplicate/superseded).
- Logical history across rolled sessions: #43929 (closed as superseded; includes a channel DM + Web UI example).
- Archived transcript browsing in Usage: #42980 (closed as implemented). This covers read-only access in a separate surface, not the requested conversation-list/fork UX.
- Storage/history issues #45003 and #92062 were closed after the SQLite migration with a maintainer note inviting fresh reports if the user-facing gap persists.

Concrete workflow: discuss topic A in Telegram DM → send `/new` → discuss topic B → later open Control UI and try to reopen topic A as a conversation. The current main session is listed; topic A is not a separate resumable thread, although its messages can be found through transcript search.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

The request intentionally separates **view old transcript**, **fork into an independent UI thread**, and **route future Telegram messages**. Only the first two are requested. Reusing an old session ID as the live Telegram target could undo the semantics of `/new` and is not needed here.

issues.body:
## Summary

Allow Logbook to capture multiple selected displays during each capture interval and use them together to build the activity timeline.

## Problem to solve

I use macOS with a laptop screen and two external monitors. Logbook currently captures one display, selected by `screenIndex`. Work on the other two displays is missing from its input, so the resulting journal can miss relevant activity.

Changing `screenIndex` only changes which single display is captured.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional way to select multiple displays, for example `screenIndices: [0, 1, 2]`. The exact configuration can follow maintainer guidance.

Expected behavior:

- Capture each selected display during the same interval and store its screen index and timestamp.
- Keep the existing single-display default and configuration compatible.
- Detect unchanged frames per display.
- Include screen identity in analysis and sample across selected displays within a bounded image budget.
- Continue capturing available displays when one selected display is disconnected or fails.

## Alternatives considered

- Choosing a different single display still misses work on the others.
- Rotating displays between intervals misses simultaneous activity.
- Stitching all displays into one image may make text harder to read at the existing image-size limit.

## Impact

Affects Logbook users who work across multiple monitors. This is a recurring limitation whenever activity happens outside the selected display, reducing the completeness of the journal.

## Evidence/examples

Maybe, with maintainer guidance.
