prs.title: feat(tts-local-cli): declare and select voices for the local CLI provider
prs.body:
Related: #165598 (staged delivery: this PR covers voice listing/selection for `tts-local-cli`; `talk.catalog` / `tts.providers` payloads stay out of scope, see below).

## What Problem This Solves

`tts-local-cli` users cannot see or switch voices: `/voice list` and `/voice set` (`/talkvoice` on Discord) fail with `speech provider tts-local-cli does not support voice listing`, so changing the voice of a multi-voice local engine (Kokoro, Piper, anything with a `--voice` flag) means hardcoding it into `command` and reloading.

## User Impact

Operators declare the voices their command accepts once, under `tts.providers.tts-local-cli`, and pass the active one with `{{VoiceId}}`:

```jsonc
// tts.providers.tts-local-cli
{
  "command": "/usr/local/bin/my-tts --voice {{VoiceId}}",
  "args": ["{{OutputPath}}"],
  "outputFormat": "wav",
  "voices": ["af_jessica", "af_bella", "am_michael"],
  "voiceId": "af_jessica"
}
```

`/voice list` shows those voices, `/voice set <voice>` switches Talk playback without a config edit, and TTS replies keep using `voiceId`. No migration: both keys are optional, and a command without `{{VoiceId}}` behaves exactly as before (the voice list is simply empty).

## Why This Change Was Made

The command owns its voice catalog, so the provider config declares it; the plugin adds `listVoices`, a `{{VoiceId}}` template key, and a `resolveTalkConfig` hook. Two rules keep the Talk path correct (both from ClawSweeper review of `1688d278`):

- **Talk selection wins.** `resolveTalkConfig` merges the TTS provider block (executable, args, catalog) with the Talk record, then drops speaker aliases (`speakerVoiceId`, `speakerVoice`, `voice`, `voiceName`) inherited from the TTS record. Core normalization ranks `speakerVoiceId` above `voiceId`, so before this an inherited alias silently replaced the `/voice set` choice with the TTS default. The CLI only reads `voiceId`; core re-derives the aliases from the merged value.
- **One catalog.** `voices` is read from the TTS provider block only. `/voice list` receives that record and Talk synthesis merges over it, so both see the same list; a `voices` list under `talk.providers` is ignored rather than consulted as a second source. The Talk record only carries the selection (`voiceId`), which is what `/voice set` writes.

Out of scope: `talk.catalog` / `tts.providers` payloads read the static `provider.voices` field and keep reporting `[]` for this provider; making them consult `listVoices` means making them async.

## Evidence

### Live Gateway, real `/voice` command path (head `f431a9ec`)

Isolated Gateway in WSL (Node 24, own state dir and port, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`), `tts.providers.tts-local-cli` as above with a stub voice CLI that writes a valid WAV containing `{"voice": <--voice arg>}` and logs each call. `talk.provider = tts-local-cli`, `talk.providers.tts-local-cli = {}`. Commands go through `chat.send` (plugin command dispatch), replies read from `chat.history`.

```text
## /voice list
$ openclaw gateway call chat.send --params {"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","message":"/voice list"}
tts-local-cli voices: 3
- af_jessica   id: af_jessica
- af_bella     id: af_bella
- am_michael   id: am_michael

## talk.speak before set
$ openclaw gateway call talk.speak --params {"text":"hello"}
{ "provider": "tts-local-cli", "outputFormat": "wav", "mimeType": "audio/wav", ... }
stub log: voice=af_jessica

## /voice set af_bella (operator.write client)
⚠️ /voice set requires operator.admin.          <- existing admin gate, unchanged

## /voice set af_bella (operator.admin client)
✅ tts-local-cli Talk voice set to af_bella
config: "talk": { "provider": "tts-local-cli", "providers": { "tts-local-cli": { "voiceId": "af_bella" } } }

## talk.speak after set
stub log: voice=af_jessica
          voice=af_bella                        <- Talk selection beats the TTS voiceId default (P1)

## add talk.providers.tts-local-cli.voices = ["talk-only"], then /voice list
tts-local-cli voices: 3 (af_jessica, af_bella, am_michael)   <- TTS catalog only (P2)
```

`openclaw gateway call` connects with `operator.write`, so the admin `/voice set` used a small scratch client calling the repo's `callGateway({ method: "chat.send", scopes: ["operator.admin"] })` against the same Gateway and token.

### Real engine (earlier head; provider behavior for these inputs unchanged)

Kokoro ONNX behind a `--voice` wrapper, `openclaw infer tts voices` / `infer tts convert --local` from a clean `pnpm build`:

```text
voices: af_jessica, af_bella, am_michael    (main: "does not support voice listing")
voiceId=af_jessica   bytes=139756 sha256=d327338d29a98ce2
voiceId=af_bella     bytes=141804 sha256=946f88c260afc60a
voiceId=am_michael   bytes=147948 sha256=4ee50265dfd9ea62
```

Three voices produce three distinct WAVs, so `{{VoiceId}}` reaches the engine.

### Tests and checks (WSL, Node 24, head `6bf157f0`)

```text
pnpm test extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  -> 39 passed; 37.2s wall
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/tts-local-cli
  -> 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check (4 touched files)  -> clean
git diff --check                 -> clean
pnpm build                       -> ok (needed to run the Gateway above)
```

New regressions: a TTS record carrying core-normalized `speakerVoiceId: af_jessica` plus Talk `voiceId: af_bella` resolves without the alias and synthesizes `--voice af_bella`; a Talk-declared `voices` list is ignored and list/synthesis agree; `listVoices` does not read other config scopes.

Base-failure runs (same test file, provider swapped):

| Provider source | Result |
|---|---|
| this PR | 39/39 pass |
| previous head `1688d278` | 36 pass, **exactly the 3 new regressions fail** (Talk selection vs inherited `speakerVoiceId`; Talk-declared `voices` ignored; no cross-scope reads) |
| `main` | 13 fail: all voice tests, plus the full-Talk-record compat test (main has no `resolveTalkConfig`) |

New compat test: a pre-existing Talk record that carries its own `command`/`args`/`outputFormat` (required before Talk merging existed) resolves unchanged when TTS has no CLI block.

### Upgrade trace: stable `2026.10.2` → this PR, same state dir and config

Config shaped like today's users: no `voices`, `voiceId` or `{{VoiceId}}`; `tts.providers.tts-local-cli` passes `--voice af_jessica`, and `talk.providers.tts-local-cli` is a full executable record passing `--voice am_michael`.

| Step | stable 2026.10.2 | this PR (`f431a9ec`, after `doctor --fix`) |
|---|---|---|
| `talk.speak` | stub argv `--voice am_michael` | stub argv `--voice am_michael` (saved Talk record preserved) |
| `tts.convert` | `--voice af_jessica` | `--voice af_jessica` |
| `/voice list` | `does not support voice listing` | `tts-local-cli voices: 0` (empty, no error) |
| config sha256 across the gateway run | unchanged | unchanged (PR gateway does not rewrite config) |

The upgrade itself needed `openclaw doctor --fix`: the current-main checkout refuses the stable-created agent DB (schema v24, exit 78) until doctor migrates it. Doctor rewrote `openclaw.json` formatting and added unrelated keys (`agents`, `plugins.entries`, `wizard`, `meta`), but the `tts` and `talk` subtrees were content-identical before and after. That migration comes from `main`, not this PR. `/voice set` on the upgraded state was not re-run here; the live trace above covers it.

### Not covered

Telegram Test Server userbot proof (`proof: telegram-e2e`): that lane needs Convex-leased QA credentials that are not available to contributors. The live Gateway run above exercises the same plugin command handler and `talk.speak` path the channel uses; a maintainer-run Telegram lane would be appreciated if still required.

Needs an owner call: the new optional `voices` / `voiceId` keys on `tts.providers.tts-local-cli`, and accepting this as a partial step toward #165598.

Note for triage: the branch now touches only `extensions/tts-local-cli/**` and `docs/tools/tts/field-reference.md`; the `plugin: azure-speech` and `extensions: fish-audio` labels look left over from an earlier bad merge that has since been rebuilt.

prs.title: chore: update stock Bun to 1.4.3
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stock Bun installations in CI, Docker builds, and package-install smoke tests still select 1.4.2 instead of the latest supported stable release, 1.4.3.

## User Impact

Stock Bun paths now use 1.4.3, including authenticated cached ZIPs and the macOS proof bootstrap. The pinned OpenClaw Bun fork is unchanged. Current docs distinguish supported latest-stable/fork runtimes from minimum API capability checks; historical release notes are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the policy of supporting the latest stable Bun and the pinned OpenClaw fork. The Docker image uses the verified multi-architecture OCI index `sha256:ec06c3b6cea04192ae6770c434f668ca41d343ad19fa6472216c7b48be39c598`; cached Linux ZIPs use the 1.4.3 release checksums.

Bun 1.4.3 fixes the JSC grapheme lookup bug, so message splitting and terminal formatting now use native segment lookups and the obsolete private workaround is removed. SQLite close admission, PTY fallbacks, installed WebSocket transport, and worker CPU guards remain: there is no complete 1.4.3 fix proved for those paths.

## Evidence

- [Upstream release](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.4.3), published October 10; [release notes](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.3) identify the segment lookup fix.
- Registry inspection verifies the index, both amd64/arm64 manifests, and raw-index SHA256. The repository Dockerfile's `bun-binary` stage builds, and the pinned image reports 1.4.3.
- Downloaded optimized/baseline Linux ZIPs and macOS ARM ZIP match the upstream SHA256 list.
- An iteration-based probe passes 2,046 segment lookups on stock 1.4.3 and the pinned fork; stock 1.4.2 fails. The repository's native SQLite-close worker still reports retained WAL resources on both stock versions.
- Behavior suites pass 50 tests on Node 24, 50 on stock Bun 1.4.3 (25.59s), and 50 on the pinned fork (44.11s). No tests were added.
- Workflow/action validation, targeted lint, formatting, diff hygiene, and the import-cycle check pass. Independent Codex autoreview is P2 scoped-clean.
- Setup/action consumer tests pass: `setup-node-env-bun.test.ts` (6 tests, 8.97s test time) and `install-smoke-no-push-workflow.test.ts` (13 tests, 17.72s). The invocation took 368.35s, mostly worker startup.
- The changed macOS Bun bootstrap cases pass in `crabbox-wrapper.test.ts`. The broader file was stopped after the unrelated source-capsule directory-open fault-injection child timed out (129.95s); clean-main comparison remains in progress. prs.title: fix(cli): avoid false failures after generated media delivery
prs.body:
Closes #169118. Reported by @Oldrich333.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes generated-media completion turns on CLI backends being marked failed and producing a retained-media notice after the model independently sends the image.

## User Impact

Queue-owned completion turns honor their existing message-tool restriction on CLI backends. Automatic delivery remains owned by the completion queue; normal CLI turns keep their message tool. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI attempt dropped `disableMessageTool`, which the embedded path already forwards. Carry this existing restriction through the shared run parameters and host-owned MCP grant into the existing tool factory. The queue's unexpected-side-effect checks remain intact.

## Evidence

Validation head: `a2ce38b5b97e6e43667097f87998197173d6538d`.

- Real `runAgentAttempt` → CLI preparation → scoped tool resolution → MCP JSON RPC regression: before the repair, the restricted case still advertised `message` (**1 failure / 1 passing unrestricted control**, **86.70 s**). After the repair, the restricted case omits `message` from `tools/list` and rejects `tools/call`; the unrestricted control retains it.
- `pnpm test src/agents/command/attempt-execution.cli-mcp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **6 passed**, **36.48 s wall time**. Three relevant grant-context, MCP-runtime and tool-resolution files: **43 passed**, **98.38 s wall time**. The added cases reuse the existing suite fixture; no new process boots, real timers or polling. Cold imports dominate this integration file; helper-only tests would miss the dropped attempt parameter. CI seconds are not yet measured.
- Core production types passed (**240.64 s**). Related test type graphs passed: commands **15.8 s**, agents-other **194.7 s**, gateway-other **213.9 s**. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, changed-source guards and relevant storage/media/pairing guards passed; runtime value cycles are zero. `pnpm build:runtime` passed (**182.81 s**, including runtime bundles, CLI bootstrap checks and UI). Full `pnpm build` was interrupted during package declaration generation (exit **130**, **2016.41 s**); it is not a completed full declaration build.
- The whole-repository unused-export guard still fails: **14 production / 10 full-tree / 1 script** findings. An exact official `4243ae96d654` tracked-source overlay reproduces all 25 entries with the same scanner (**217.783 s**); candidate source/index and existing unknown files were restored and verified. No scanner exclusion, export deletion or baseline/rule change was made. This is a qualified baseline failure, not an all-checks-green claim.
- Independent review found a test-side use of an undeclared resolver property; it now uses the existing schema builder, and the correction review is clean. Native test typechecking also found an implicit-any fixture parameter, repaired with the existing fixture's exact parameter type.

The provider executor and loopback server startup are fixtures. This proves production tool preparation and RPC rejection, not live image generation, an actual channel send, or full queue settlement/restart behavior. No real Gateway, vendor API or paid resource was used.

### Bounded Gateway attempt — incomplete (2026-10-14)

Executed the explicitly approved, isolated reviewed-head `a2ce38b5b97e6e43667097f87998197173d6538d` with Node24.19.0 / pnpm12.9.0, a clean exact-head private-QA runtime, four shipped plugins, synthetic credentials, an owned QA transport and loopback Images endpoint, and a self-authored native Claude CLI protocol fixture. No vendor CLI/API, paid resource, existing Gateway or real user data was used.

Two attempts ended **failed**, before image generation, at the strict ordinary-turn warm-process assertion (288.233s / 262.004s overall). In each attempt, both ordinary turns advertised `message` and successfully called it through actual authenticated MCP HTTP with owned QA send receipts. After each turn, actual stale `tools/list` and attempted `message` calls returned401 with zero extra outbound messages. However, the two ordinary turns used distinct CLI processes and bearer/capture identities, so warm grant transfer is **not proven**.

After the first attempt, a separately reviewed fixture protocol correction honors host-supplied `--session-id` / `--resume` and verifies later input identity, rather than inventing a native session ID. Offline contract probes show the old fixture ignored both supplied modes and the correction preserves both; this does not prove why the Gateway restarted. The recovery kept the same product head, authority and strict warm assertions. Its two initialization prompt hashes match, but both actual invocations request a new session ID rather than resume. The missing native-session binding/reuse decision remains unexplained; this is not an established defect in this PR or a claim of full vendor compatibility.

**Not executed:** generated-media completion restriction/refusal, image attachment delivery, actual public abort, and durable queue-settlement checks. The existing focused regressions remain separate evidence. Native lifecycle confirmed each owned Gateway tree stopped, both owned services stopped, and temporary synthetic credentials/state removed; lead readback also verified the known Gateway/fixture PIDs and private state directories absent. No failing warm assertion was removed or converted to a pass, and no CI rerun/source push occurred. The next proof needs metadata for binding selection and process-close reasons before another live attempt.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject malformed UTF-8 source imports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: automatic Memory Wiki source imports silently replace malformed UTF-8 bytes with U+FFFD and record the damaged version as synchronized. A later unchanged poll can then skip that corrupted source page.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the exact source buffer before decoding in `writeImportedSourcePage`, the existing shared owner for bridge and unsafe-local imports. Rendering, guarded vault writes and tracked metadata stay with their existing owners. No charset conversion, new option or separate importer is introduced; existing unchanged-source fast paths are retained.

## User Impact

User impact: a malformed source refresh fails with its path and a concrete recovery instruction, preserving that source's existing imported page and synchronization metadata. Valid Unicode, including a literal U+FFFD character, still imports and refreshes normally.

## Evidence

Product head `7bac65cdac5a5c94f439bf08ea61d3325c6176a1`; RED base `44c918f3900770412a3cd912eaa0c718b2e3356c`. The affected owner is unchanged through checked current main `c17dabc484fa31f05c0a970dc3109076af84b4cf`. Both normal `pnpm build cliStartup` builds had matching clean-head build stamps. Linux, Node 24.16.0, 2026-10-14.

Same actual packaged CLI entry and scenario on both versions:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs wiki unsafe-local import --json
```

The isolated configuration enabled only `memory-wiki`, selected a local vault/search backend, and configured one synthetic source file under `unsafeLocal.paths`. A valid `Café 🤖 � original` source first created an imported page. The same source was replaced by raw bytes `ff 41 44 5f 42 59 54 45 20 63 68 61 6e 67 65 64 0a`, with an advanced modification time.

| Scenario | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valid Unicode seed | exit 0, one imported page | exit 0, one imported page |
| Malformed source refresh | exit 0, writes `�AD_BYTE changed` and advances tracked source metadata | exit 1, preserves page, two indexes and tracked metadata |
| Valid Unicode repair | exit 0, writes repaired content | exit 0, one updated page containing `Café 🤖 � repaired` |
| Unchanged valid source | exit 0, one skipped source | exit 0, one skipped source; zero updates and no index refresh |

Head CLI diagnostic, with the fixture root abbreviated:

```text
Imported source file must be valid UTF-8: $ROOT/source.md. Restore the source as valid UTF-8 and retry the sync.
```

Readback crossed real filesystem and SQLite boundaries. The source page SHA-256 was `35454a653f6cf44795e8ac4d3b488781ada55b518f65e51457e37e92acf9d481` before and after rejection; `index.md` and `sources/index.md` were byte-identical too. The source input bytes were unchanged. A read-only connection to the actual isolated `state/state/openclaw.sqlite` read `plugin_state_entries` rows for namespace `source-sync`; the `memory-wiki` row, including `value_json` and `created_at`, was identical before/after on the head, whereas the base recorded the malformed version. This exercises the unmocked unsafe-local importer, shared writer, persistent state store and compiler.

Validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-page-shared.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/unsafe-local.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: RED two new cases fail / six existing owner cases pass; final GREEN 25 tests pass, 14.48s runner. Both shared-owner source groups retain page/state on rejection; existing bridge and unsafe-local contracts remain covered. Formatting, targeted type-aware lint/type checking with native selected plugin-boundary declarations, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent adversarial review: PASS, no P0–P3 findings.

Scope: two files; production +8/-1, tests +49/-0. Existing-solutions preflight found no current encoding guard in this owner. ChatGPT JSON ingestion and manual Markdown ingestion use different loaders and are outside this patch. No config/default, protocol/schema, permissions, dependency or upgrade migration changes.

Not tested: a real bridge artifact import, optional remote search or the full suite. This is per-source preservation, not a claim of whole-batch atomicity; initialization and independent concurrent valid sources can still write. No production service, account, channel or user data was changed. Synthetic proof files and logs are retained outside the product branch for inspection and can be removed after review.

prs.title: fix: keep lean local-model Tool Search prompts compact
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes lean local-model turns increasing prompt size when removing optional tools lets the remaining Tool Search directory expand its descriptions.

Related: #168744. Thanks @chitowntony for the reproduction that exposed this prompt-cost issue. This does not claim to fix the original timeout report.

## User Impact

Lean Tool Search directories list names and owners, with full descriptions and schemas still available through search. Existing capability filtering and explicitly required tools stay intact. Ordinary system instructions, skills, and workspace context are preserved. No new configuration or CLI change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The directory renderer chooses progressively shorter descriptions to fit the context budget. Removing one tool could move every remaining entry to a longer description tier. Lean mode now starts with names only, and its cache key includes that presentation choice. The harness also preserves the selected agent when refreshing the directory, including per-agent opt-outs.

Production: +8/-3 lines (net +5); tests: +86/-0; docs: +3/-1. The production growth selects and caches the compact representation using the existing renderer and retains its ordinary budget-shrinking path.

## Evidence

Native Ollama on macOS, through isolated `pnpm openclaw --profile lean-mode agent exec` runs with the same create/read-file task. Exact first requests were captured, then replayed with `stream:false` and `options.num_predict:1`:

| Model / Tool Search | Non-lean | Lean before | Lean after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| qwen2.5-coder:1.5b-instruct / automatic | 7,801 | 7,687 | 7,296 |
| qwen3:4b / automatic | 7,773 | 7,656 | 7,259 |
| qwen2.5-coder:1.5b-instruct / explicit structured | 7,301 | 7,607 | 7,194 |

With each comparison's timestamp/session envelope held identical, the corresponding counts are **7,801 / 7,684 / 7,289**, **7,773 / 7,656 / 7,261**, and **7,301 / 7,606 / 7,198**. Current automatic Ollama defaults mask the original increase after web-fetch direct visibility changed; explicit `tools.toolSearch: { mode: "tools" }` still reproduces it on the base.

- Before/after lean schemas are byte-identical (12 automatic, 11 explicit). Only the deferred-tool directory changes in the system prompt; automatic directory section shrinks 4,607 → 2,565 characters, explicit 4,692 → 2,584. Skills, bootstrap/workspace text, and other instructions are identical. Full-vs-lean also removes the existing `automations` cross-references from `exec`/`process` descriptions.
- Real task behavior is limited: baseline qwen3 lean called `write` then `read` and produced `DIRECT_OK`; post-fix qwen3 emitted prose, and post-fix qwen2.5 emitted JSON-looking text without native calls. All three post-fix turns returned successfully through the CLI, but did not create the file. Token savings are proven; improved tool-call reliability is not claimed.
- Two new regressions fail before the fix: 3,244-character lean directory vs 1,285 non-lean, and descriptive rendering for a lean agent. They pass after the fix, including per-agent cache and prompt-refresh behavior.
- 96 focused tests passed across directory, lean filtering, catalog, harness, and prompt-refresh suites (Vitest group wall times 122.24s / 73.04s / 189.25s; cold worker preparation 88.15s). Final-head regression rerun: 2 passed, bodies 7ms/1ms; total 1,030.28s due to shared-host filesystem/transform stalls.

- Final-head isolated Codex branch autoreview: scoped-clean through P2. `pnpm build qaRuntime` passed in 7m21.7s, including 54 built-module/doctor closure checks. Full local `pnpm build` was stopped after 22m21s in declaration generation without compiler errors; broad build validation is delegated to PR CI.

Live proof is local macOS only. Shared-host delays are not treated as latency benchmarks. The remaining model tool-call limitation is outside this prompt-size fix.

prs.title: fix(ui): allow complete selected usage exports while other sessions refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes complete selected usage exports being blocked when an unrelated session in the same reporting range is still computing or stale.

Related: #171613

## User Impact

Users can export a complete selection as JSON, sessions CSV, or daily CSV while other sessions refresh. Missing, computing, or stale selected data still produces an error instead of a partial download.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway’s cache status covers the whole session roster, while export totals cover the explicit selection. The report builder now records whether every explicitly selected source is complete before applying query, day, and hour filters. The export controller consumes this fact, including selections outside daily CSV’s 50-row table page. This preserves selection/filter intersections without mistaking a still-computing row excluded by a usage filter for a complete selection. The global guard remains for unselected exports and uncertain or older responses; the Gateway’s roster status is unchanged.

- All three new selected-export regressions fail on the original guard and pass with the fix. Thirty focused shared-owner and UI/export tests pass in 7.740 seconds combined wall time. With one worker, the six-test export file takes 3.658 seconds wall (35 ms bodies); the 20-test shared-owner file takes 3.063 seconds wall (about 23 ms bodies).
- Coverage includes a complete selection outside daily CSV’s first 50 rows, computing family subtotals, stale timestamps, refreshing rows, missing usage, missing selected keys, a complete selection intersected with a provider filter, and a still-computing selected row hidden by a token filter.
- The real browser Export menu downloaded six files (three formats for selected-only and selection/filter cases) with only the selected session’s 100 tokens and $0.50; no pending-session data appeared. The original guard instead displayed the incomplete-data error. Synthetic browser proof took 7.769 seconds.
- UI typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Fresh independent Codex P2 review passed after fixing its selection/filter finding. Exact-head CI remains required.

After: the same selection exports successfully; incomplete selections remain blocked.

prs.title: fix(commands): session export truncates filenames containing spaces
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/export-session monthly report.html` truncated the output path to `monthly` instead of retaining the requested filename.

## User Impact

Export filenames can contain spaces, including repeated spaces and directory components. The shared decoder continues to discard leading flags and enforce the existing path-length limit. Workspace confinement and trajectory export approval remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the complete single path argument serialized by the command registry rather than selecting its first whitespace-delimited token. Thanks to @zhangguiping-xydt for the report and fix.

## Evidence

Built-artifact proof used an isolated Linux Gateway and an authenticated `operator.admin` client. A normal chat turn completed against a scripted provider before the export commands; no session database or transcript was hand-written.

Captured, redacted output:

```text
BASE 9cc6124bcf156bb332747121d0b4de09a0ebab80
normal chat turn: status=ok, sourceReplyDelivered=true
/export-session monthly report.html
workspace: [..., "monthly", ...]
/export-session plain.html
workspace: [..., "monthly", "plain.html", ...]
/outside-export.html: absent
PASS base
cleanup: confirmed-stopped, errors=[]

HEAD bd72155d6662ff4284df47a748d1fc860e507c19
normal chat turn: status=ok, sourceReplyDelivered=true
/export-session monthly report.html
workspace: [..., "monthly report.html", ...]
/export-session plain.html
workspace: [..., "monthly report.html", "plain.html", ...]
/export-session /outside-export.html
reply: Output path must be a regular file inside the workspace.
/outside-export.html: absent
/export-trajectory --include-tools trajectory report.json
Output: trajectory report.json
exec denied: Headless runs cannot wait for interactive exec approval.
PASS head
cleanup: confirmed-stopped, errors=[]
```

Focused registered export suite: **30 tests passed** (session export, trajectory approval/encoding, oversized paths, and filesystem boundaries). Targeted Oxfmt and Oxlint checks passed. The real Gateway stripped the leading trajectory flag, retained `trajectory report.json`, and denied execution at the existing headless approval boundary. No unapproved bundle was created. The focused suite checks the encoded path and approval boundary. No live provider check is claimed or needed for this parser-only change.

Simplification: one shared decoder remains; no new abstraction or compatibility path. Production delta **+2/-1**, tests and test support **+28/-9** against the merge base. The added cases protect whitespace preservation and the length/security boundaries affected by retaining the complete path.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous argument decoding and requires no state migration. Blast radius is owner-authorized session and trajectory export commands with explicit output paths; no channel delivery or authorization logic changed.

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Operators cannot defer only MCP tools behind Tool Search while keeping core, non-MCP plugin, client, and frequently used MCP tools directly available.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: operators can choose which authorized tools need discovery without removing execution permission or exposing every MCP schema.

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "toolSearch": {
      "mode": "tools",
      "include": [{ "source": "mcp" }],
      "exclude": [{ "source": "mcp", "name": "github_read_*" }]
    }
  }
}
```

Existing defaults are unchanged; no threshold or migration is introduced. These are presentation controls, not authorization. Direct-only and runtime-required trusted tools retain their existing guarantees. Directory mode still keeps client tools direct; the Copilot harness retains its existing directory-to-tools mapping. Independent Code Mode and Codex-native search are unchanged.

**Review requested:** published for review at the author's request. Maintainer product/design agreement is still requested for this new configuration surface. The repository-required canonical autoreview remains blocked by local CLI authentication, as detailed below; it is not claimed as passed. Marking ready does not establish merge readiness.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The existing policy-filtered compactor and dispatcher now accept include/exclude selectors. Each selector has a source, registered name, or both; names reuse policy normalization and `*` matching without regex support or implicit tool-group expansion. Fields are ANDed, lists are ORed, and exclusion wins. Omitted inclusion retains existing eligibility; empty inclusion defers nothing.

Source qualification prevents unintended name-only matches across origins. Client registration, prompt allowlists, registry ownership, and worker presentation follow the selected surface without granting tools through a same-named tool from another owner. Public documentation and schema/help/labels are included. No MCP activation, connection, deployment, or dependency changes are part of the PR diff.

Prior art: openclaw/openclaw#118335 proposed a name-only `alwaysVisibleTools` option and was closed unmerged. Its closure reason is unverified; this implementation does not infer Code Mode from Tool Search mode or promote tools through a name-only trusted-tool rule.

```js
  finalEffectsBySource: Object.fromEntries(["plugin", "mcp", "client"].map((source) => [source, records.filter((entry) => entry.source === source).length])),
  forbiddenEffects: denied.length,
  searchAndDescribePayloadsVerified: ["mcp", "client"],
  sameNameClientCases: ["direct", "deferred"],
  refreshCases: ["client inventory and prompt cap", "MCP tools/list_changed with removed and added tools"],
  externalModelProvider: false,
};
await fs.writeFile(new URL("verified-runtime-receipt.json", root), `${JSON.stringify(summary, null, 2)}\n`);
console.log(JSON.stringify(summary, null, 2));

```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Published-driver upgrade harness (upgrade-proof.mjs)</summary>

```js
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { once } from "node:events";
import fs from "node:fs/promises";
import { createWriteStream } from "node:fs";
import { setTimeout as delay } from "node:timers/promises";
import { applyMockOpenAiModelConfig } from "/harness/scripts/e2e/lib/fixtures/mock-openai-config.mjs";

const root = "/proof";
const home = "/tmp/selector-upgrade-home";
const state = `${home}/.openclaw`;
const cli = "/opt/upgrade-global/bin/openclaw";
const resume = process.argv.includes("--resume");
const env = {
  ...process.env, HOME: home, OPENCLAW_HOME: home, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR: state,
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH: `${state}/openclaw.json`, OPENAI_API_KEY: "synthetic-upgrade-model-key",
  PATH: `/opt/upgrade-global/bin:${process.env.PATH}`, NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX: "/opt/upgrade-global",
  npm_config_prefix: "/opt/upgrade-global", OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BONJOUR: "1",
  OPENCLAW_SKIP_STARTUP_MODEL_PREWARM: "1", OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS: "1", OPENCLAW_SKIP_CRON: "1",
};
async function json(path, value) {
  await fs.writeFile(path, `${JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)}\n`);
}
async function run(label, args, executable = cli) {
  const child = spawn(executable, args, { cwd: "/tmp", env, stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] });
  let stdout = "";
  let stderr = "";
  child.stdout.on("data", (data) => { stdout += data; });
  child.stderr.on("data", (data) => { stderr += data; });
  const timeout = setTimeout(() => child.kill("SIGTERM"), 900000);
  const [code, signal] = await once(child, "exit");
  clearTimeout(timeout);
  await fs.writeFile(`${root}/${label}.stdout`, stdout);
  await fs.writeFile(`${root}/${label}.stderr`, stderr);
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ label, code, signal }));
  assert.equal(code, 0, `${label} failed: ${stderr.slice(-3000)} ${stdout.slice(-3000)}`);
  return stdout;
}
let mock;
try {
  await fs.mkdir(`${state}/workspace`, { recursive: true });
  if (!resume) await fs.writeFile(`${state}/workspace/preserved.txt`, "UPGRADE_WORKSPACE_SENTINEL\n");
  const config = {
    gateway: { mode: "local", controlUi: { enabled: false } },
    agents: { defaults: { workspace: `${state}/workspace`, heartbeat: { every: "0m" } } },
    memory: { search: { enabled: false } },
    plugins: { slots: { memory: "none" } },
    tools: { codeMode: false, toolSearch: { enabled: false, mode: "tools", searchDefaultLimit: 7, maxSearchLimit: 13 } },
  };
  applyMockOpenAiModelConfig(config, { mockPort: 44180, modelRef: "openai/gpt-5.5" });
  if (!resume) await json(env.OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, config);
  const log = createWriteStream(`${root}/upgrade-model.log`);
  mock = spawn("node", ["/harness/scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs"], {
    env: { ...env, MOCK_PORT: "44180", SUCCESS_MARKER: "UPGRADE_AGENT_OK", MOCK_REQUEST_LOG: `${root}/upgrade-model-requests.jsonl` },
    stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
  });
  mock.stdout.pipe(log);
  mock.stderr.pipe(log);
  let ready = false;
  for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
    assert.equal(mock.exitCode, null);
    try {
      if ((await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:44180/health", { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(1000) })).ok) { ready = true; break; }
    } catch (error) {
      if (!(error instanceof TypeError) && error.name !== "TimeoutError") throw error;
    }
    await delay(1000);
  }
  assert(ready, "Mock provider did not start");
  const baseline = resume
    ? await fs.readFile(`${root}/upgrade-baseline-version.stdout`, "utf8")
    : await run("upgrade-baseline-version", ["--version"]);
  assert(baseline.includes("b8952d4"), "Baseline must be the resolved published stable package");
  let beforeConfig;
  if (resume) {
    beforeConfig = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(`${root}/upgrade-before-config.json`, "utf8"));
    await run("upgrade-repair", ["update", "repair", "--yes", "--no-restart", "--json", "--timeout", "600"]);
  } else {
    await run("upgrade-baseline-config", ["config", "validate"]);
    const before = await run("upgrade-baseline-turn", [
      "agent", "--local", "--agent", "main", "--session-key", "agent:main:upgrade-proof",
      "--message", "UPGRADE_HISTORY_SENTINEL before installing the candidate.", "--json",
    ]);
    assert(before.includes("UPGRADE_AGENT_OK"));
    beforeConfig = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(env.OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, "utf8"));
    await json(`${root}/upgrade-before-config.json`, beforeConfig);
    await run("upgrade-published-driver", ["update", "--tag", "file:/proof/openclaw-candidate.tgz", "--yes", "--no-restart", "--json", "--timeout", "600"]);
  }
  const candidate = await run("upgrade-candidate-version", ["--version"]);
  assert(candidate.includes("f142599"), "Updater must activate the exact candidate build");
  await run("upgrade-candidate-config", ["config", "validate"]);
  const afterConfig = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(env.OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, "utf8"));
  assert.deepEqual(afterConfig.tools, beforeConfig.tools);
  assert.equal(afterConfig.agents.defaults.workspace, beforeConfig.agents.defaults.workspace);
  assert.equal(await fs.readFile(`${state}/workspace/preserved.txt`, "utf8"), "UPGRADE_WORKSPACE_SENTINEL\n");
  const beforeRequests = (await fs.readFile(`${root}/upgrade-model-requests.jsonl`, "utf8")).split("\n").filter(Boolean).length;
  const after = await run("upgrade-candidate-turn", [
    "agent", "--local", "--agent", "main", "--session-key", "agent:main:upgrade-proof",
    "--message", "Confirm the upgraded session still works.", "--json",
  ]);
  assert(after.includes("UPGRADE_AGENT_OK"));
  const newRequests = (await fs.readFile(`${root}/upgrade-model-requests.jsonl`, "utf8")).split("\n").filter(Boolean).slice(beforeRequests).map(JSON.parse);
  assert(newRequests.some((entry) => entry.body.includes("UPGRADE_HISTORY_SENTINEL")), "Prior conversation must be present in candidate model input");
  const selectors = { ...afterConfig.tools.toolSearch, enabled: true, include: [{ source: "mcp" }], exclude: [{ source: "mcp", name: "github_read_*" }] };
  await run("upgrade-set-selectors", ["config", "set", "tools.toolSearch", JSON.stringify(selectors), "--strict-json"]);
  await run("upgrade-selector-config-valid", ["config", "validate"]);
  const persisted = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(env.OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, "utf8"));
  assert.deepEqual(persisted.tools.toolSearch, selectors);
  const restarted = await run("upgrade-selector-turn", [
    "agent", "--local", "--agent", "main", "--session-key", "agent:main:upgrade-proof",
    "--message", "Confirm the persisted selectors load after a new process starts.", "--json",
  ]);
  assert(restarted.includes("UPGRADE_AGENT_OK"));
  await json(`${root}/upgrade-summary.json`, {
    status: resume ? "passed-after-recovery" : "passed", baseline: baseline.trim(), candidate: candidate.trim(),
    initialUpdateExitCode: resume ? 143 : 0, harnessDeadlineSeconds: 900,
    cleanOneShotUpgrade: !resume, recoveryPassed: resume,
    publishedUpdater: true, preserved: ["toolSearch settings", "workspace", "session history"],
    selectorsPersistedAndLoadedInNewProcess: true,
  });
} finally {
  if (mock && mock.exitCode === null && mock.signalCode === null) {
    mock.kill("SIGTERM");
    await once(mock, "exit");
  }
}
```

- **Post-merge focused tests passed:** **207 tests in 9 files**, six routed Vitest shards, **467.39s** wrapper wall time.
- **Production and test types passed:** core production plus `agents-other`, `agents-tools`, `config-cli`, `packages`, and `services-cron`.
- **Targeted lint, formatting, config documentation metadata, and feature-diff whitespace checks passed.**
- **Runtime boundary proof:** synthetic MCP tools remain searchable, describable, and callable through the real `tool_search`/`tool_describe`/`tool_call` controls; unselected tools retain direct schemas and execution. The real client/session registry exercises partial deferral, ownership, hook caps, restoration, and refresh.

The regressions now reject those calls while preserving authorized direct tools, explicit name grants, and restoration. These are synthetic local boundary tests, not live MCP/provider evidence.

**Evidence gaps:** no live commercial-provider/production-MCP-service E2E, full local `pnpm check`, or full local `pnpm test` was run. Installed-runtime and focused upgrade proof is supplied above. Earlier draft checks included a passing **PR context and evidence** check; broad CI was skipped while draft, and no broad-CI success or CI timing evidence is claimed. There is no visual UI change requiring screenshots. Maintainer edits are enabled. prs.title: perf(agents): retain fork context as encoded data
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-history model requests allocate a second conversation object graph solely to retain an optional cache-parity fork.

## User Impact

Normal model requests retain an immutable encoding instead of deep-cloning the prepared history. Fork replay still gets a private mutable context, preserves the parent's request prefix, and does not execute parent tools or hooks. No API, config, schema, retention-limit, or authority changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The allocation stack was initially attributed to `streamWithPayloadPatch`, but that helper already mutates request-owned payloads in place. The actual clone runs in `wrapStreamFnWithSessionFork` before the provider stream starts. Encode that context before streaming and decode it only when a fork is requested, extending the existing encoded wire-payload retention pattern. Later publications retain their existing independent clone and unsupported-value behavior; separate publications preserve pending-tool pairing.

Production delta: **+1 line** (13 added, 12 removed). The separate publication boundary is needed to keep pending-tool placeholders and replay isolation while retiring the large per-request clone. No parallel capture path or cache was added.

## Evidence

- Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**, clean through P2. Autoreview refused because its selected provider did not match operator config; config was left unchanged.
- Frozen-history and publication-isolation coverage exercises real OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages request preparation. Existing replay, one-shot hooks, unsupported publications, pending tools, expiry/resource cleanup, and send-authority tests remain in the owning file.
- Local changed-file `oxfmt`, repository focused syntax lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Type-aware lint preparation was stopped when it attempted package artifacts; CI owns broad checks.
- Existing payload-wrapper/proxy checks: 2 files, 21 tests passed (66.65 s wall time on a busy host).
- Owning focused file: 15 tests passed, 554.40 s wall time on the saturated Mac (503.85 s Vitest duration; 70% transform, 26% test time). Existing real provider/lifecycle coverage makes this file expensive; the new cases extend that owner rather than adding another fixture stack.
- Sandbox measurement: Node 26.8.2, baseline `93e8fe353765`, candidate `c8707fbdc8ae`; default team-shape seed 967 with 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, 12 real synthetic worktrees, 64 MiB logical transcripts, and a 235,978,752-byte agent database. The selected long-session content was extended to the same 800,000-byte / 15-message history on both revisions (nominal 200k tokens at 4 bytes/token; actual provider tokenization was not measured). Three paired runs of 400 model-request captures each, 30 warmups, 4 KiB heap sampling with collected major/minor-GC objects included, and GC PerformanceObserver durations.

| Median per request | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Allocated bytes | 3,219,751 | 2,410,857 (**−25.1%**) |
| `structuredClone` allocated bytes | 809,759 | 1,131 (**−99.9%**) |
| Capture time | 0.953 ms | 0.797 ms (**−16.3%**) |
| Observed GC time | 0.0204 ms | 0.0139 ms (**−31.7%**) |

Allocation ranges were 3,219,601–3,219,912 before and 2,410,760–2,411,060 after. Capture-time ranges were 0.874–0.959 ms before and 0.669–0.803 ms after; GC ranges were 0.0198–0.0221 ms before and 0.0139–0.0162 ms after. These short GC measurements are a boundary-level observation, not a production-GC claim. Every sandbox command used CPU affinity, a 64 GiB memory bound, nice/ionice, and isolated HOME/state/temp directories.

No leases, production data, or production Gateway were used. Measurement is at the request-capture boundary with synthetic fixture history; it does not establish whole-Gateway throughput or production GC improvement.

prs.title: refactor(ui): render agent and theme artwork with Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Deterministic agent faces still used Lit, and native theme consumers could not reuse the existing claw/mark/custom-art selection policy directly. Pending native avatar fallback artwork could also settle through a retired Lit child during palette or sidebar updates.

## User Impact

The same agent IDs keep the same faces. Native consumers share the existing theme artwork policy. Avatar changes and teardown retire pending face artwork with their Solid owner. Mobile drawer focus does not open a tooltip that claims Escape.

## Why This Change Was Made

Port the sole face renderer to Solid and add `ThemeBrandingIcon`, adopted by the command palette. Preserve the existing lazy plugin-artwork loader and a small interop adapter for remaining legacy callers. Remove the unused panel-error adapter and Solid wrapper. The native avatar fallback now uses Solid `lazy`/`Loading` instead of rendering a pending Lit `until` region.

The drawer uses its existing `focusWithoutTooltip` handoff. The mobile E2E now taps the drawer control in its touch browser context: a mouse click leaves the cursor over the animated drawer and opens a hover tooltip, which correctly consumes the first Escape. Its drawer-close assertions are preserved.

No dependency changes or new state owner. The 34-line production increase supplies native reactive artwork and its owned lazy fallback; palette values, SVG geometry, host classes, and lazy boundaries remain intact.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Codemod | Dry-ran all four legacy source files; manual ownership decisions resolved |
| Focused tests | 69 tests / 3 files pass: native avatars, palette session drafts, native shell; 142.20 s command wall |
| UI typecheck | Pass |
| Independent review | Repaired production candidate clean through P2; touch-only test delta reviewed separately |
| Targeted lint | Source-backed core configuration passes; UI-config attempt timed out preparing unrelated plugin-SDK declarations |
| Production Knip | Same-command head and exact-base runs fail only on unchanged `ui/src/components/web-awesome-tabs.ts`, already orphaned by #171552; no artwork orphan or new ignore |
| Build / strict startup comparison | Both builds and strict checks pass on one machine: exact base `2c130c7039f2`, 348,663 B → 348,660 B gzip (−3 B), 8 JS requests unchanged, 1 CSS request / 49,703 B unchanged |
| Route boot | Chat/new JS +389/+390 B; request counts remain 32/28; route CSS unchanged |
| Visual proof | Synthetic 24-face and theme gallery byte-identical; fresh mobile touch screenshots are byte-identical and show preserved drawer Escape behavior |
| Browser boundary | Head touch sequence focuses first drawer control without tooltip, then one Escape closes drawer; no page errors |
| Replacement CI | Run `38507866469` on `775616b15378`: avatar errors are absent; UI 3/3 fails the unchanged markdown file-tooltip copy test (line 51). Attribution in progress; latest scheduled main UI 3/3 passed |
| LOC | Full touched files: production 1,458 → 1,492; tests 1,052 → 1,149 |

The original full CI run `38502649724` exposed native avatar lifetime errors in `app-sidebar.people.test.ts` and `palette-session-draft.test.tsx`, plus the mobile drawer case. The avatar owner repair and focused tests cover those lifetimes; the touch probe covers the mobile interaction. The plugin uninstall-feedback failure, “retains uninstall feedback through during inspection,” also failed on scheduled main run `38502084044` and is independently inherited. The unrelated tabs orphan is unchanged at the exact merge base: `7d1c4a8177d0` (#171552) already removed its last production import. It belongs to the final Web Awesome sweep. Fresh full CI runs on the replacement head before landing.

The repaired production tree was built before its commit, then committed unchanged. The later touch correction changes only the test action, so both build artifacts remain valid for the final production input. All captures contain synthetic fixtures; no application account data or desktop content. No leases were acquired.

![After: Solid agent and theme artwork](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03679c5c-5eb9-4d99-b906-17a5d5345fb9)

![Before: baseline touch drawer closes with Escape](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d3aa113-6b99-4c52-9f56-888018835809)

prs.title: fix(update): say a missed original capture does not require a restart
prs.body:
## Summary

Original-state capture stays one best-effort attempt. The warning no longer tells the operator to retry the update. It says the update continues without this capture, and that a completed update does not need to be restarted because of this warning.

No retry is added. The install is not stopped. The shared inspection diagnostic that ends with "then retry the update." is unchanged. Only this best-effort warning rewrites that trailing sentence, and it closes the sentence before the continuation.

Related #170332

<!-- today-update-evidence:2026-10-12 -->
## Production baseline — October 12 update

Captured from the real npm-global update on October 12, 2026 (Halifax time): Debian 13, Node v24.16.0, `2026.10.5-beta.1 (f283c3c)` → `2026.10.5-beta.2 (467e83d)`, using `openclaw update --channel beta --tag 2026.10.5-beta.2 --yes`. The saved terminal capture and read-only update-run record agree that the run finished with `phase: finished`, `status: succeeded`. Private paths and capture identifiers are redacted; unrelated logs are omitted.

The same real update warned that original-state capture failed while reading the live state database, advised a retry, and then installed and finished:

Selected terminal lines, with unrelated output omitted:

```text
Warning: Original state capture is unavailable: Original update capture failed; evidence retained at $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR.update-captures/<capture-id> | State schema inspection failed (exit): [redacted-diagnostic]; after 4.215 seconds during shared database discovery for $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite (scope: 1 source paths): SQLite file generation changed while reading: $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite. Check access to the reported source, free space, and storage performance, then retry the update.
✓ package-install (15.69s)
Gateway: restarted and verified.
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.5-beta.2 (from 2026.10.5-beta.1).
Recorded verification: service running (2026.10.5-beta.2); version verified; channels ready; HTTP ready.
```

The capture diagnostic reports a generation change after 4.215 seconds. This establishes the contradictory retry advice during an otherwise successful update and preserves the intended best-effort continuation described by the maintainer.

**Remaining proof gap:** This was the official unpatched beta update. It proves the original warning and successful continuation, but does not show the revised warning from an installed CLI containing this PR. The patched command-boundary proof below remains the after-change evidence.

## Installed-driver proof (this PR as the running updater)

Docker (`openclaw-published-driver-update-e2e` image, Linux, Node v24.21.0), synthetic state only. The branch at `3551492b0ab` was packed and installed with `npm install -g` as the **driver**. Doctor ran, then a managed Gateway was started through the repo's systemd fixture (`/readyz` 200). A synthetic second writer committed net-zero schema transactions to `state/openclaw.sqlite` every 25 ms; it was stopped as soon as the capture warning printed (244 commits). Then `openclaw update --tag <same build relabeled 2026.10.3>.tgz --yes` ran from the installed driver.

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.2 (3551492)
$ openclaw update --tag openclaw-candidate.tgz --yes
Warning: Original state capture is unavailable; the update continues without it. A running Gateway or another active writer changing state during capture is expected to cause this. Database rollback uses the pre-migration snapshots taken after the Gateway stops. A completed update does not need to be restarted because of this warning. Cause: Original update capture failed; evidence retained at $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR.update-captures/8b2566c3-a8bc-4aa0-910b-7022f1bfa349 | State schema inspection failed (exit): [redacted-diagnostic]; after 0.297 seconds during database generation verification for source scope [$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite, $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite] (scope: 2 source paths): SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified: $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite.
  ✓ package-install (32.3s)
  ✓ candidate-state-snapshot (9.07s)
  ✓ candidate-doctor (10.62s)
  ✓ candidate-doctor-lint (6.59s)
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.3 (from 2026.10.2).
Phases: requested (34.92s) → staging (12ms) → validating (129.16s) → activating (111.7s) → restarting (7.37s) → verifying (82.14s)
Recorded verification: service running (2026.10.3); version verified; channels ready; HTTP ready.
$ openclaw update status --json   # lastRun
"phase": "finished", "status": "succeeded"

OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (3551492)
```

The revised warning leads with continuation guidance, has no retry advice, and names the real phase ("database generation verification") and both source paths. The update finished and the Gateway restarted on the candidate. The warning appears in full (no truncation).

That run exposed one more gap: the public summary still printed `[redacted-diagnostic]` because the generation check's WAL-commit causes ("SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified" and "SQLite WAL commit header is unavailable or changing") weren't on the fixed-cause allowlist. `351d54b90d1` adds both, with cases in `diagnostic-support-redaction.test.ts` (59 passed, 1.6s). That commit only changes the allowlist; the Docker run above was against `3551492b0ab`.

**Rerun at the current head `351d54b90d1`** (same harness and concurrent writer; 257 commits, stopped when the warning printed). The public summary now prints the WAL commit cause where it used to print `[redacted-diagnostic]`, and the update still completes:

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.2 (351d54b)
$ openclaw update --tag openclaw-candidate.tgz --yes
Warning: Original state capture is unavailable; the update continues without it. A running Gateway or another active writer changing state during capture is expected to cause this. Database rollback uses the pre-migration snapshots taken after the Gateway stops. A completed update does not need to be restarted because of this warning. Cause: Original update capture failed; evidence retained at $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR.update-captures/5406080c-acc6-4c46-ab31-95c5fdf2bdc0 | State schema inspection failed (exit): SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified; after 0.599 seconds during database generation verification for source scope [$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite, $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite] (scope: 2 source paths): SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified: $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite.
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.3 (from 2026.10.2).
Phases: requested (30.25s) → staging (11ms) → validating (148.06s) → activating (107.25s) → restarting (10.1s) → verifying (79.54s)
Recorded verification: service running (2026.10.3); version verified; channels ready; HTTP ready.
$ openclaw update status --json   # lastRun
"phase": "finished", "status": "succeeded"
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (351d54b)
```

Not this PR: the same run later warned "Automatic database restoration unavailable: databases changed after snapshot capture". That is #170335's false generation change, which #170351 fixes.

### Real Gateway writer (head `6a158a8baef`)

Same Docker harness, with no synthetic writer this time. The managed Gateway served real agent turns against the mock OpenAI provider (`scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs`): one `openclaw agent --agent main --session-key live-1-N` turn every 2 s, continuing through the whole update, Gateway downtime included. The installed driver is this PR at `6a158a8baef`; the candidate is the same build relabeled 2026.10.3.

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.2 (6a158a8)
turns before update: 8
$ openclaw update --tag openclaw-candidate.tgz --yes
Warning: Original state capture is unavailable; the update continues without it. A running Gateway or another active writer changing state during capture is expected to cause this. Database rollback uses the pre-migration snapshots taken after the Gateway stops. A completed update does not need to be restarted because of this warning. Cause: Original update capture failed; evidence retained at $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR.update-captures/e94dbeb3-7b73-418e-8d0e-48f4ed1bd6cb | Original database generation changed or could not be verified; capture is unsealed.
$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite: generation changed after its snapshot.
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.3 (from 2026.10.2).
Recorded verification: service running (2026.10.3); version verified; channels ready; HTTP ready.
Gateway downtime: 132.18s.
$ openclaw update status --json   # lastRun
"phase": "finished", "status": "succeeded"
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (6a158a8)
readyz after: 200
turns: ok=130, failed=42 (all inside the 132 s Gateway downtime, "connection closed"), post-update turn ok
sessions after update: 131 of 131 completed turn sessions present, 0 missing
```

The Gateway's own writes are enough to trigger the warning, which is the reporter's case. Across three real-Gateway runs at this head and the previous one, the capture failed in a different way each time:
- `generation changed after its snapshot` (above);
- `SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified` (two loops, one turn per second);
- `SQLite snapshot hash mismatch` on `openclaw-agent.sqlite-wal` (four continuous loops).

The last cause still printed as `[redacted-diagnostic]` at `351d54b90d1`. `6a158a8baef` adds it to the fixed-cause allowlist, with a case in `diagnostic-support-redaction.test.ts` (60 passed, 7.1 s). The hash mismatch run happened before that commit, so it isn't reproduced at the new head; the unit case covers it.

Not this PR: with four back-to-back turn loops (473 turns), candidate admission refused the update. Its error was "could not inspect agent database …: SQLite source did not stabilize after 10 read-only inspection attempts (the database may be under concurrent write activity)". The previous Gateway kept serving (`/readyz` 200), and all 473 sessions were intact afterward. That is the existing admission retry budget, which is outside this warning-text change, so it goes on the follow-up list.

## Proof

No live Gateway update was rerun. `updateCommand({ yes: true, json: true, restart: false })` ran with `captureUpdateRecoveryBaseline` rejecting the generation-changed inspection error. The command resolved. The visible warning and the completed ledger step `warning:original-state-capture:` were:

```
Warning: Original state capture is unavailable: State schema inspection failed (exit): generation changed. Check access to the reported source, free space, and storage performance. The update continues without this capture. A completed update does not need to be restarted because of this warning.
```

The admitted run finished `phase: finished`, `status: skipped`, `reason: already-current`.

## Base / head

The same boundary test against the parent initializer, which warns with the raw inspection error, failed (exit 1). That run printed:

```
Warning: Original state capture is unavailable: State schema inspection failed (exit): generation changed. Check access to the reported source, free space, and storage performance, then retry the update.
```

Head of the same test passed (exit 0) and printed the continuation warning above.

## Test

`update-command-fresh-preview.test.ts` — "continues a completed update when original-state capture fails". The helper-only wording test is removed. The boundary test requires the continuation sentence in both the visible warning and the ledger step, rejects "retry the update", and requires the run to finish already-current.



## Maintainer update (fix at the producer)

Pushed on top of this branch (merged current `main`, no history rewrite): `fix(update): report original capture failures accurately`. It replaces the post-hoc regex rewrite with a fix where the message is produced, and keeps this PR's "does not need to be restarted" sentence.

- The storage/retry advice is no longer appended for the best-effort original capture (a `retryAdvice` option on the inspection diagnostics; restore and Doctor checks keep it). `formatBestEffortOriginalCaptureWarning` is removed.
- Warning: "Original state capture is unavailable; the update continues without it. A running Gateway or another active writer changing state during capture is expected to cause this. Database rollback uses the pre-migration snapshots taken after the Gateway stops. A completed update does not need to be restarted because of this warning. Cause: …" The guidance comes first because the warning is length-bounded.
- The failing step is named correctly ("database generation verification") with its real input paths, instead of "shared database discovery … scope: 1 source paths".
- `[redacted-diagnostic]` is replaced by the fixed phrase "SQLite file generation changed while reading" (paths stay out of the public summary).
- `docs/cli/update/repair-and-recovery.md` updated.

Evidence: a real `database-generations` worker with a preload writing between its two reads reproduces the issue's message before the change; the `updateCommand` test keeps this PR's name with the new assertions. Focused runs of `update-command-fresh-preview`, `update-candidate-state.schema`, and `diagnostic-support-redaction` pass (320s). `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check` clean.

Supersedes my duplicate #170396, now closed.

prs.title: feat: resume saved question answers without repeating interrupted tasks
prs.body:
Related: #167266. Parent: #171666. Split from #168399; this prerequisite must land before recovery wiring and tool handoff.

## What Problem This Solves

A saved question answer needs one native continuation, while interrupted attempts must remain visible without automatically repeating their side effects.

## User Impact

This prerequisite supplies continuation and restart-recovery ownership; production question wiring and default tool behavior are activated by later slices. Failed, timed-out, and cancelled continuation attempts retain the existing interrupted receipt with instructions to start a new user turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse native turn admission and the existing session lane. Claim the saved answer before acceptance under the original caller's current authority, repair only decided terminal receipts, and exclude exact question-owned runs from ordinary restart replay. Existing crash-loop quarantine still owns admission.

Also addresses the concrete finding on #168399 from @sjwilczynski: an RPC final frame can succeed while its native outcome is error or timeout. Only an ok outcome now settles successfully; failure never grants a replay. Longer question deadlines and changing the fate of pending questions on new ordinary messages remain outside this slice.

## Evidence

- Native regression: error and timeout finals both failed before the fix; continuation, receipt-repair, final-frame passthrough, and recovery-owner proof passed afterward (62 cases, native wrapper 50.17 seconds).
- Unchanged restart-recovery composition: 155 native cases passed on cleaned full candidate ca3b5dc (303.14 seconds Vitest; combined 191 cases / native wrapper 354.98 seconds). This is qualified unchanged-path evidence, not exact-head CI.
- Core production types, targeted typed lint, and formatting passed. Independent P0–P2 autoreview found zero actionable findings (provided patch/dependency scope). A lint-only variable rename followed that review without changing behavior.
- No claim of full multi-day support or issue closure. No new migration in this slice; storage is in #168917.

prs.title: fix: allow guest child startup after parent yields
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves A guest can receive an accepted visible worktree child, yield to wait for its result, and then have the child fail before inference with `This turn has ended; ask again in a new turn.` This happens when workspace preparation finishes after the spawning parent has ended: the child's initial reply preparation still sees the parent's personal-tool participant context. ## User Impact Accepted child work can proceed after its parent yields. Guest scopes remain limited to session access, sandbox requirements remain attached to the child, and revoking the original requester still prevents execution. The closed-turn guard continues to reject actions belonging to an ended turn. There is no configuration, schema, or protocol change. This contribution repairs child startup. Delivery of the child's eventual completion or failure to its parent is a separate boundary. ## Why This Change Was Made Chat admission already retains the original source authority for independent work and validates the parent through input acceptance. The missing handoff was the ambient caller and operator-invocation context: sandbox rename availability consults it while preparing the child's reply policy, before the child establishes its own runtime caller. The post-acceptance dispatch now exits those two turn-local contexts using the existing owner helpers. The admitted source authority, request scope, session custody and cancellation checks remain in place. The existing child-custody regression now closes the real parent participant registry and exercises the actual sandbox rename availability function during delayed child preparation. ## Evidence The frozen baseline was reproduced through a real TLS Gateway, narrow guest scopes, Node Code Mode `sessions_spawn`, a visible managed worktree, and actual `sessions_yield`. Child workspace readiness was released only after the parent's terminal receipt. The child retained required sandboxing, failed with the ended-turn error, and made no inference request to the synthetic HTTP provider. The strengthened custody file fails on the original production source in the selected-parent continuation case; its other 20 cases pass. Candidate formatting, lint, and the selected production/test type groups pass. All 53 tests across five focused custody, authority, ordering and session-binding files pass; the native test batch took 77.45 seconds (73.86 seconds in Vitest). Hosted CI timing is pending. No additional timing-only test run was made. A local real-Gateway comparison of the same candidate tree shows the yielded parent's child reaching inference and displaying `CHILD_REACHED_PROVIDER`, with required sandboxing and narrow guest scopes retained. The comparison and focused recording below show this path. The remote real-Gateway candidate controls also pass: child inference succeeds after parent yield and with the parent open; actual guest-role revocation before readiness release denies inference. Required sandbox assertions pass in all three cases. That three-case test stage took 84.75 seconds. The existing narrow-session-scope file also passes all 11 cases (52.70 seconds). Independent engineering and adversarial review is clean for this startup change. Hosted CI and the required automated review remain pending. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Child session fails with This turn has ended after its parent yields](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1608d70-db9c-4297-88e1-87f4a02b989d) | ![Child session produces CHILD\_REACHED\_PROVIDER after its parent yields](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/597bdcd7-46e0-4449-b9e3-b544ec04f5e3) | ### API\-triggered child startup with the corrected authority lifetime https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5188b8a1-665c-4e28-85b7-9926d7c98ffa ### Visual verification - Baseline: 72ccf6ff92931fff2d49473fe1571f39e8311ad2 - Exact head: `91f88b304e6edb9796ce58087761ef391fbdeccf` - Scenario: A guest creates a parent through the real sessions\.create API\. The scripted provider spawns a visible child with its own worktree and isolated context, then calls sessions\_yield\. Release only the real child workspace promptReady promise after the actual parent terminal receipt, and inspect the child session\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.3; candidate tracked tree 2ac630dda17d7827545dc57c986480c11fdaa4c6; UI built from base72 with unchanged inputs; assets/index\-DMC2tnen\.js sha256 2a6232da0c7a1e791d2aad875a9fe18ef7602e4942c9d30c1eae6c87b4996610 - Trigger: Real API sessions\.create, visibly labeled in recording - Child inference requests: Before: 0; after: 1 - Gate order: Parent yielded terminal precedes child promptReady release in both runs - Child terminal: Before: ended\-turn error; after: ok and visible reply - Guest restrictions: Required sandbox and only operator\.sessions\.read/write preserved - Capture equivalence: Identical UI bytes, viewport, theme, locale, task and gate\. Fresh fixture IDs change decorative guest avatar color\. - Actual before and after UI states captured; no injected product messages - Served UI entry asset byte\-for\-byte matches the built bundle in both runs - Scenario assertions pass; candidate runner exit1 occurs only in subsequent inner cleanup - Outer cleanup and Docker inspection confirm no task\-owned runtime remains - Original recordings retained; focused recording inspected across its full chronological contact sheet - Author commit91f88b304e6edb9796ce58087761ef391fbdeccf has the exact tested tracked tree2ac630dda17d7827545dc57c986480c11fdaa4c6; proof reused without rerun\.
