prs.title: feat(muse): sign in to Muse Code from Model Setup
prs.body:
## Problem

Meta Muse Code needed terminal setup: `muse login`, `openclaw plugins enable muse`, and a hand-written `agentRuntime: { id: "muse" }` on the Meta model. Model Setup offered only "Meta: API key". Other subscription logins (xAI, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex) already work from the Models page.

## Solution

- **Meta provider owns a "Muse Code" device-code choice** (`extensions/meta/muse-login.ts`). It runs `muse login` under supervision, shows the device code in the wizard, honors cancel, and gives an install hint when `muse` is missing. The Gateway login always uses Muse's file credential store under `<stateDir>/muse`, so one browser approval is enough. The macOS Keychain write fails for background Gateway processes.
- **The credential stays Muse-owned.** No fake OpenClaw profile is written. The muse harness uses the managed credential when present and otherwise falls back to Muse's own store. Model availability uses the harness's existing catalog/readiness hooks over the same authenticated MSP `model/list`; it does not grant the direct Meta Responses route.
- **Setup installs and routes the runtime.** `runtime-plugin-install.ts` gains a Muse descriptor beside Codex and Copilot. The auth result enables `muse` and returns an `agentRuntimeId: "muse"` hint; setup writes it only to the activated agent's model entry (`agents.entries.<agent>.models[<model>]`). Global `agents.defaults.models` rows, including an explicit `openclaw` policy, and other agents are unchanged.
- **Activation verification without a tool-free turn.** Muse cannot guarantee a zero-tool turn (MSP has no all-tools-off switch), so activation's `disableTools` probe cannot pass honestly. This adds an optional, activation-only harness `verifySetup`, used only for profileless native auth. Muse checks MSP `model/list` and requires `source: "providerCatalog"` that contains the selected model. A rejected credential returns a bundled catalog and fails setup. Core binds the plugin owner/artifact fingerprints and re-runs the check before commit. Other runtimes keep the existing probe.
- **Live authority.** The `models.authLogin` setup branch carries the existing connection/choice guard through activation; an invalidated device token stops the flow before `muse login`, verification or runtime install run.
- **Catalog/UI.** The provider-login catalog marks native-setup choices `requiresSetup`. AI Setup → Connect provider lists them and dispatches through setup activation with connection-owned cancellation. The plain Provider Access list stays credential-only.

## Evidence

Live run on an isolated Gateway built from this branch. Real `muse` 1.3.0, real Meta device approval, no `META_API_KEY` in the environment:

1. Models → AI Setup → Connect provider → Meta → **Muse Code**: device code shown, one approval, then "Account verified and selected for this agent's default model".
2. Config written: `plugins.entries.muse.enabled: true`, `agents.entries.main.model: meta/muse-spark-1.3` with `agentRuntime.id: "muse"` on main's entry only (no `agents.defaults.models` write); credential at `<stateDir>/muse/muse/auth.json`. Re-run on the final head: one approval, verified, chat reply `KIWI` from Muse Spark 1.3.
3. Chat: "Reply with exactly one word: PINEAPPLE" → `PINEAPPLE` from Muse Spark 1.3; `muse serve` ran as a child of the Gateway.

Before (main): Meta offers only an API key.

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7e9bc73-25d8-4ece-8260-6c40e1f7b392)

After: Muse Code choice, device code, verified, chat turn.

![Muse Code choice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7f50faa-79e7-415e-be36-75473db3dd96)
![device code](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/487fb2d2-e4fc-4be7-b886-47d0268c1012)
![verified](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86a4bafc-fa83-4d67-9a7b-9309538a645d)
![chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f4e91a8-02df-4f0f-9948-8c71be66ad9e)

Focused tests: device-code approval/cancel/missing binary/one-approval, managed vs native credential selection, PATH-preserving env with a missing workspace, `verifySetup` success/rejection/pre-commit revocation and no-hook fallback, alternate-model routing with an API-key Spark row preserved, catalog `requiresSetup` and `models.authLogin` dispatch/disconnect, UI setup-dialog visibility. Shrink-only ratchet baseline updates.

Authority and route regressions, run on the final head (production entry points with a recording fake `muse` binary):

| Case | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Invalidated admin connection (signals not aborted) cannot spawn `muse login` | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/system-agent/setup-inference-credentials.authority.test.ts -t 'blocks native Muse login after the admin connection is invalidated without aborting'` | 1 passed; spawn log absent |
| Invalidation during pending browser approval kills the child; no credential file written | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/meta/muse-login.test.ts -t 'kills a pending login when authority is revoked without aborting the signal'` | 1 passed |
| Revocation at the pre-commit recheck leaves config bytes unchanged | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.test.ts -t 'does not activate a native sign-in revoked before commit'` | 1 passed |
| Meta proxy `baseUrl` that the Muse harness does not support: setup fails before `verifySetup`, no commit | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/system-agent/setup-inference-credentials.authority.test.ts -t proxy` | 1 passed |

The native-login child persists the credential itself; OpenClaw stops it on lost authority (checked every 100 ms) and rechecks authority before verification, install and config commit. A credential written in the final instant before a kill stays in the plugin-owned Muse store and is not activated or selected.

Live authority proof on a real Gateway built from this head (real `muse` 1.3.0, isolated state, redacted):

Pending-login revocation (Control UI started Muse Code; device code shown, not approved):
```
## before revoke
22637 muse login
ls: cannot access '<state>/muse/muse': No such file or directory
c1ff53b4…b6cd openclaw-control-ui operator
$ openclaw devices revoke --device c1ff53b4…b6cd --role operator   # 03:30:13Z
## after revoke (03:30:16Z)
no muse login process
ls: cannot access '<state>/muse/muse': No such file or directory
Error: <state>/openclaw.json: No such file or directory   # no config commit, no plugin enable
```
The dialog closed and Models still shows "Model required".

Non-admin caller (`operator.read` + `operator.write`, shared token) calling `models.authLogin` for `muse-code`:
```
{"phase":"connect","ok":true,"requestedScopes":["operator.read","operator.write"],"grantedScopes":["operator.read","operator.write"]}
{"phase":"models.authLogin","ok":false,"error":{"code":"FORBIDDEN","message":"missing scope: operator.admin"}}
after: no muse login process; no <state>/muse dir; no config written
```

Existing data: a production 2026.10.x config copy passes `openclaw config validate` on this build (exit 0, only unrelated missing-env warnings), and the file bytes stay unchanged after load. The PR adds no schema, stored-row or config migration.

Upgrade cell (pre-PR main build `2026.10.3 (f183f38)` writes the state, then this head reads the same state):
```
$ old config set 'agents.defaults.models["meta/muse-spark-1.3"].agentRuntime.id' openclaw
$ old models auth paste-token --provider meta --profile-id meta:default   # synthetic key
Auth profile: meta:default (meta/token)
== old build
[{"id":"meta:default","provider":"meta","mode":"token"}]
{"meta/muse-spark-1.3":{"agentRuntime":{"id":"openclaw"}}}
== new build (this PR) on the same state
[{"id":"meta:default","provider":"meta","mode":"token"}]
{"meta/muse-spark-1.3":{"agentRuntime":{"id":"openclaw"}}}
validate_exit=0
```
The SQLite-backed Meta API-key profile and the explicit runtime policy load unchanged.

## Update behavior

No config or stored-data migration; no schema change. Existing configs load unchanged: Meta API-key profiles and explicit `agentRuntime` policies are never rewritten (setup writes only the activated agent's entry), and terminal `muse login` users keep working through the native-store fallback. A warm Muse host is retired when the credential source changes, so a later Model Setup sign-in never reuses a host bound to the old store.

prs.title: refactor(ui): separate presentation contract from Lit adapters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native Solid surfaces still imported their presentation event and types from the Lit directive module.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Retained surfaces keep the same presentation, hiding, restoration, and cleanup behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing event and presentation contract unchanged into a plain TypeScript owner. All contract consumers import that owner directly; only actual directive consumers retain the Lit adapter. The existing WebKit selection rule follows both files, so moving the contract preserves its coverage without adding runner rows.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| Markdown presentation regression | 1/1 passed: hide, restore, and disposal |
| WebKit CI selection tests | 14/14 passed |
| Targeted UI, script, and test lint | Passed using their owning configurations |

prs.title: fix(cli): reject nonregular model image inputs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `infer model run --file` can wait indefinitely when an image path names a FIFO without a writer. The shared image loader calls `readFile` before checking image type, so neither local nor Gateway probes reach dispatch or report an unsupported input.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing core `readRegularFile` owner, resolving the input first to retain supported symlink paths. That owner rejects nonregular files before opening and validates the opened descriptor with nonblocking flags. The import stays lazy inside the image-only branch. Existing MIME detection, HEIC conversion, input metadata and local/Gateway dispatch remain with their current owners.

## User Impact

User impact: nonregular image inputs fail promptly with the affected path and a recovery instruction. Regular images and image symlinks continue to reach the model with the original input path and exact image bytes. No new per-file or aggregate byte limit is introduced.

## Evidence

Product head `659e16cf1166e5dee4e53721cfcb4bd8239b0222`; RED base `44c918f3900770412a3cd912eaa0c718b2e3356c`. The shared image loader is unchanged through checked current main `c17dabc484fa31f05c0a970dc3109076af84b4cf`. Both normal `pnpm build cliStartup` builds had matching clean-head stamps. Linux, Node 24.16.0, 2026-10-14.

Same packaged CLI entry and fixtures on both versions:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs infer model run --local --model image-proof/image-proof --prompt 'Describe this image' --file "$FILE" --json
```

An isolated configuration used a synthetic image-capable model and a loopback HTTP/SSE provider recorder. No production configuration or external model credentials were used. The recorder returned `image proof reply`; real CLI JSON output reported that final text. Four inputs were exercised: a valid 1×1 PNG, a symlink to that PNG, a real FIFO made with `mkfifo`, and an ordinary non-image text file. Local `strace -f -tt -e trace=openat` observed the actual CLI process.

| Scenario | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular PNG | exit 0; one HTTP image request and final reply | exit 0; one HTTP image request and final reply |
| PNG symlink | exit 0; original symlink path retained | exit 0; original symlink path retained |
| FIFO without writer | traced blocking open; continues only after controlled writer admission | exit 1 without opening the FIFO; zero provider requests |
| Ordinary text file | exit 1; unsupported-image diagnostic; zero provider requests | exit 1; same unsupported-image diagnostic; zero provider requests |

Acceptance RED was an observed unfinished syscall, not a process timeout:

```text
openat(AT_FDCWD, "$ROOT/input.pipe", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC <unfinished ...>
```

After observing this wait, a controlled writer was admitted 1,001ms later and supplied non-image bytes, releasing the baseline CLI for clean exit 1. No provider request occurred during that scenario. On the head no writer was admitted, no FIFO `openat` appeared, and the command exited 1 in 5,957ms including cold CLI startup. JSON stdout contained:

```text
Cannot read model image file: $ROOT/input.pipe. Use a readable regular file containing an image and retry.
```

Both successful controls crossed the actual runtime-to-HTTP boundary: the recorder received `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model=image-proof`, prompt `Describe this image`, and an `image_url` exactly equal to `data:image/png;base64,` plus the original PNG bytes. CLI `inputs[0].path` retained the supplied regular/symlink path, MIME was `image/png`, and `outputs[0].text` was `image proof reply`. Exactly two HTTP requests were recorded across all four head scenarios. The input PNG remained byte-identical and the FIFO remained a FIFO. Head FIFO trace SHA-256: `610cc773013c556b359adadf35ad16c6a71bc38bc81d6f29efd169a2735cef22`.

Validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'FIFO image inputs|prepares local model content|normalizes HEIF|rejects non-image'`: RED two FIFO regressions fail / five controls pass; final GREEN seven pass, 83 unselected, 36.16s runner. The registered CLI regressions exercise both local and Gateway pre-dispatch rejection, valid PNG/symlink payloads, existing ChatGPT instructions, HEIF normalization and text rejection. The FIFO fixture retries writer admission so a regression fails without leaving a blocking reader hung. Formatting, targeted type-aware lint/type checking, normal build and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent adversarial review: PASS, no P0–P3 findings.

Scope: two files; production +9/-1, tests +82/-39 (existing content table extended and reformatted). Existing-solutions preflight selected the canonical descriptor-aware reader. The earlier broader [#110767](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110767) was closed by its author; this repair leaves image budgets and concurrency unchanged. Both transports use the same loader. No config/default, protocol/schema, permissions, dependency or migration changes.

Not tested: a live Gateway or external model provider, Windows/macOS FIFO behavior, parent-directory symlink controls or the full suite. POSIX-only FIFO and file-symlink cases are excluded on Windows. No service, channel, account or production data was changed. The isolated recorder is closed and synthetic trace/log fixtures remain outside the product branch for inspection and later cleanup.

prs.title: perf(worktrees): bound repository housekeeping across archive cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Frequent session archives repeatedly launch Git housekeeping for every managed repository, even though the Gateway's periodic cleanup is hourly. Repository deduplication already exists; the missing bound is across cleanup passes.

## User Impact

Archive and orphan cleanup remain immediate, while automatic repository housekeeping runs at most once per hour per repository. A repository first encountered by the service is maintained immediately. `openclaw worktrees gc --retry-deferred` still forces immediate pack/object repair before cleanup and resets suspended tasks. Snapshot-specific pack lookup repair remains immediate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing maintenance owner retains one in-memory deadline per repository. It checks that deadline before any housekeeping Git command and reserves it before awaiting work. No filesystem watcher, mtime/ref cache, schema, configuration option, second scheduler, or request-path work is added. Restarting the service resets its deadlines. Large pack backlogs now converge over hourly passes rather than on every archive notification; explicit retry remains available.

Production LOC delta: **+6**. This small growth supplies the requested cross-pass cadence contract, which the existing per-pass repository deduplication cannot provide. No existing cleanup or repair machinery is superseded by this change.

## Evidence

Synthetic Linux sandbox, CPU affinity 64–127, 64 GiB memory cap, low CPU/idle I/O priority, isolated HOME/state/temp paths. No production data or service was accessed. Fixture: one repository, **6,900 unique small packs and 128 real linked worktrees**.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Paced steady run, six cleanup calls in one minute | 24 maintenance Git spawns | 0 |
| Median cleanup time in that run (six samples) | 57.2 ms | 10.4 ms |
| Ten further calls with the service clock advancing one minute per call (accelerated, not wall-clock minutes) | 70 maintenance Git spawns | 0 |
| First housekeeping pass on fresh identical fixtures | 9 Git spawns; 6.63 s | 9 Git spawns; 5.99 s |
| Packs after first housekeeping pass | 5,877 | 5,877 |

The initial pass is behaviorally identical; its timing variation is not claimed as a cold-path speedup. Both repositories pass `git fsck --no-dangling`. The paced baseline has drained its small-pack backlog; the paced head still retains thousands of packs, yet launches no housekeeping during the cooldown. Counts use the existing `worktree.maintenance` spawn diagnostic. This isolates the cleanup owner, not a production Gateway load test; post-deployment production rates remain unmeasured.

The new integration regression failed on the original code because an in-hour cleanup launched three maintenance Git commands after deleting its orphan. It exercises the real service and Git boundary, including new-repository admission, the exact hourly boundary, and explicit retry. Existing suspension coverage advances the service clock between intended maintenance passes.

Validation: changed-file `oxfmt`, repository core-config lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Focused lifecycle/GC-performance tests: 17 pass, one Linux-only native pack-cleanup test skipped on macOS. Both configured pre-commit content guards pass against the exact committed files. Gateway maintenance tests: 22 pass. GC sibling tests: 22 pass, including the read-only orphan dependency, symlink/hardlink, failure/replacement, authority, and retry contracts from #171305; its existing 180,000-entry index test hit its subprocess's 60-second timeout on the saturated local host. That timeout is recorded, not masked or retried for green; PR CI owns broad gates and Linux validation. An initial lint invocation timed out preparing unrelated plugin declarations; the documented source-backed core lint command passed. No Testbox/Crabbox leases, local full builds, or standalone typecheck lanes were run.

Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)** — no actionable P2+ findings, including a second pass over the final test placement. Autoreview refused startup because the selected provider did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

## What Problem This Solves

Immutable snapshot descendants are walked again when consumed separately or reused in a new publication, even though the snapshot owner already validated and froze the whole graph.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a reply loses all text after a legacy `[TOOL_CALL]` or `[TOOL_RESULT]` block when the payload quotes its closing marker inside inline or fenced code.

## User Impact

The sanitizer removes the internal block and retains the following answer. Literal code examples stay literal, and truly unclosed tool payloads remain hidden. No configuration, prompt, tool-dispatch, or stored-transcript changes are required.

Raw interim Gateway assistant events still contain the legacy scaffold before the final sanitized replacement; this PR fixes final/delivery truncation and does not claim complete suppression of those interim events.

No live Telegram Test Server send/receive proof is claimed; the remaining Telegram-only proof hold is for maintainer judgment. Proof here is on macOS arm64.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared scanner previously checked only the first closing-marker candidate. If that candidate belonged to Markdown code, it treated the whole block as unclosed and discarded the rest of the answer. It now advances past protected candidates to the real closer, using the existing code-region owner. Payload bounds come directly from that match rather than a second sentinel offset.

Thanks @bodapatisaikrishna for the repair and regressions. Contributor commits are preserved, followed by a merge from current main and the focused cleanup.

## Evidence

- Current-main baseline `976cc974fab1912c696d1101bd17a1abf05eb77e`: a real isolated Gateway receives `Before`, a recognized tool block quoting its closer, and `Visible reply continues here`; delivery returns only `Before` while the raw durable transcript retains the full input. Telegram's production outbound sanitizer returns the same truncated result in both rich and plain modes.
- The contributor's legacy-bracket test file fails 4/5 cases on that baseline; the truly unclosed control passes (17.87 s command wall time, 4.81 s Vitest total). The final head covers inline/fenced closers, TOOL_RESULT, multiple blocks, unclosed payloads, and literal-code controls.

- Core and scoped test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-export, config-docs, and plugin-inventory ratchets all pass against the merged main baseline. The runtime build (`OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build`) passes in 691.41 s command wall time, including plugin imports, CLI bootstrap, UI performance, and 14 runtime postbuild phases. Full bundled declarations were omitted; standalone core and scoped test types pass. On the built isolated Gateway, the quoted-marker fixture preserves the complete final answer in 26.511 s, and the literal-marker control remains byte-for-byte unchanged in 1.586 s; neither dispatches tools. A real Ollama `qwen3:4b` response through the same Gateway completes in 47.966 s with no tools. This is an inference control; scripted SSE establishes the malformed-byte regression. prs.title: fix(config): reject blank heartbeat.every before disable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every ''` (or whitespace) persists `every: ""`, which `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs` treats as disabled (same as `"0m"`), silently turning off heartbeat instead of rejecting the typo.

## User Impact

User impact: blank `heartbeat.every` is rejected before save; existing cadence is preserved. Explicit `"0m"` still disables heartbeat; nonempty durations like `"30m"` are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`HeartbeatSchema` only ran `parseDurationMs` when `val.every` was truthy, so `""` skipped validation and was written. Runtime then `normalizeOptionalString("")` → null interval. The fix rejects blank/whitespace `every` in schema superRefine and keeps `"0m"` as the explicit disable.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`; colocated test in `zod-schema.agent-defaults.test.ts`
- Packaged CLI: base RED (`config set … every ''` → rc=0, disk `every:""`) / head GREEN (rc=1, validation message, disk unchanged `"30m"`); `"0m"` still accepted
- Unit: rejects blank / whitespace; accepts `0m` and `30m`
- Dedup: no open PR on blank `heartbeat.every` rejection

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Blank `agents.defaults.heartbeat.every` must not disable heartbeat; `"0m"` remains the explicit disable; `"30m"` remains valid.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every ''` → config mutation validation → `HeartbeatSchema.superRefine` → declined write → disk unchanged.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Schema-only; `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs` unchanged. `"0m"` still yields a null interval by design.

### Real environment tested

CLI via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts` with temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json
printf '%s\n' '{"agents":{"defaults":{"heartbeat":{"every":"30m"}}}}' > "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"
CLI=(node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts)
"${CLI[@]}" config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every ''; echo blank_rc=$?
"${CLI[@]}" config get agents.defaults.heartbeat.every --json
"${CLI[@]}" config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every '0m'; echo zero_rc=$?
"${CLI[@]}" config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every '30m'
"${CLI[@]}" config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every '  '; echo ws_rc=$?
"${CLI[@]}" config get agents.defaults.heartbeat.every --json
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
blank_rc=1
Config validation failed: agents.defaults.heartbeat.every: must not be blank (use "0m" to disable heartbeat)
Config change declined. No settings were saved.
readback: "30m"
zero_rc=0
readback: "0m"
ws_rc=1
(same blank rejection; after reset to 30m) readback: "30m"
```

## Update (2026-10-14 CST)

Addressed ClawSweeper P1: Doctor compatibility migration now normalizes saved blank/whitespace `heartbeat.every` to `"0m"` at defaults and per-agent scopes before schema validation, preserving disabled cadence and unrelated fields (prompt kept). New blank writes still reject.

### Upgrade compatibility proof (source CLI)

```text
Seeded config: defaults.every="" + prompt keep-defaults; ops.every="   " + prompt keep-ops
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts doctor --fix
→ Updated config; backup written
readback: defaults.every="0m" prompt="keep-defaults"; ops.every="0m" prompt="keep-ops"
$ … config validate → Config valid
$ … config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every '' → blank_rc=1
  must not be blank (use "0m" to disable heartbeat)
$ … config set … every '0m' → zero_rc=0
```

Unit: doctor-legacy-config.migrations.test.ts + zod-schema.agent-defaults.test.ts.

prs.title: refactor(plugins): remove older-host fallback paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bundled plugins release with the host, but still carried implementations and capability probes whose only purpose was running on older hosts. This removes that duplicate code and uses the current host's async APIs.

## User Impact

Bundled plugins require the current matching OpenClaw host. Current-host behavior and persisted-data migrations remain intact. FaceTime's declared host floor now matches its package/API version. Released SDK adapters used by third-party plugins remain available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reef now uses its worker stores and composed outbound operation exclusively; its three legacy implementations, native cursor path, synchronous channel hooks, and obsolete prepare/record API are deleted. FaceTime uses V2 conditional deletion. Matrix and Discord register only async thread-binding hooks, while retaining their released public synchronous exports.

The same cutoff removes missing-host-API branches in diagnostic capture, realtime context, worker accounting, config access, migration helpers, and X guest-helper availability. Reef flow fixtures now exercise actual worker stores instead of a fake trust implementation that always selected the retired path.

### Removed checks and accepted edge cases

| Removed check/path | Accepted edge case |
| --- | --- |
| Reef missing `createOperation`, native inbox cursor and synchronous channel hooks | Older hosts cannot run this bundled plugin; current worker errors still propagate. |
| Reef legacy prepare/record path and duplicate identity/delivery checks in its shared writer | The current owner already checks the same facts inside the same synchronous transaction; send-time authority checks remain. |
| FaceTime missing V2 comparison operations and old-host authenticated-consult version check | Older hosts are unsupported; actual caller authentication and sender authority propagation remain. |
| Matrix/Discord sync channel hook registrations | Older hosts cannot select these hooks; third-party runtime API exports remain. |
| Discord missing runtime picker, direct HTTP agent, tracked worker, and shared voice composer | Missing current-host APIs are errors, rather than selecting a reduced legacy implementation. |
| Missing async diagnostic capture, managed reaper and migration helper exports | Older hosts are unsupported; current API failures retain their existing handling and offline custody checks remain. |
| Optional `config.current` and X helper capability downgrade | Current runtime config and helper containment are required; Active Memory's real lifecycle fallback and X access restrictions remain. |
| Codex legacy question persistence callback and duplicate numeric worker limits | Current recorder and host-owned worker limits remain authoritative. |

### Retained contracts

- Discord and Matrix sync persistence exports serve the released `conversation-binding-sync-mutations` SDK contract (`src/plugins/compat/registry-records.ts`).
- Comfy/OpenAI and required speech/realtime sync provider hooks still serve released synchronous SDK resolvers; removing them would change the SDK contract.
- Matrix's shared chunk reader accepts Doctor's published V1 store (`PluginDoctorMigrationContext.openPluginStateKeyedStore`), where `lookupMany` is optional. Removing that fallback requires a separate SDK change.
- Reef's operation API remains optional in the published V1/V2 type; this PR does not expand that SDK type. Disk migrations and all live security/effect checks remain.

## Evidence

- Frozen-lockfile installation and changed-file formatting/basic lint completed. Both Codex autoreview rounds completed with no actionable P0/P1 findings. CI owns type-aware lint, tests and static gates. Local type-aware lint preparation timed out before examining changed code.
- Initial CI passed all type and lint lanes, source contracts and package boundaries. It found stale Reef sync-hook assertions, a missing broker-enabled test-pool assignment, missing `config.current` fixtures in Diffs/ACPX, partial SDK mocks, and a shrink-only assertion-baseline update. The repair commit updates these tests and baseline without production changes; the next CI run validates the repair. A focused Reef rerun also exposed a short polling deadline around cold worker preparation; the test now waits for the actual guard-entry signal, preserves its assertion and propagates send errors, without changing production behavior or timeout budgets.
- Current warmed-turn SQL/request paths are unchanged. No warmed-turn reduction is claimed, so no SQL harness run is needed under the campaign's compute-conservation policy.
| Inventory | Before | After | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| T1, repository | 224 | 224 | 0 |
| T1, affected bundled plugins | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| T1-compat, repository | 12 | 12 | 0 |

CI run `38505646814` passed the database-worker and dialect ratchets. Removed older-host implementations were compatibility paths, not current-host T1 sites. No current warmed-turn statements or requests are removed or added by this cleanup.
- LOC: 113 files, +981/−3,743 (net −2,762), including CI fixture repairs.
- Published-driver × candidate update cell: pending the exact candidate commit, because migration-helper and lifecycle capability probes were removed.
- No SDK source, runtime API exports, schema, retention, or durability changes. The X UI edit deletes an unreachable older-host hint; current-host rendering is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve whitespace in explicit workspace paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw agents add --workspace` silently retargets a workspace directory whose name ends in a space to a neighboring path without the trailing space, then persists that wrong path in config (and may seed the wrong directory).

## User Impact

User impact: literal `--workspace` paths (including trailing/leading spaces) are kept through CLI → `createAgent` → `ensureAgentWorkspace` → `openclaw.json`. Ordinary paths without edge whitespace behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three stacked trims caused the retarget: CLI `opts.workspace?.trim()`, `resolveUserPath` (always trims), and `ensureAgentWorkspace` (`params.dir.trim()` then `resolveUserPath`). After list/Activity-style ownership fixes elsewhere, this is the agents-add mutation path that still wiped path identity. Aligns with connect `#167116` / config provider-path literal preservation.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/commands/agents.commands.add.ts`, `src/agents/agent-create.ts`, `src/agents/workspace.ts`
- Packaged CLI: base RED / head GREEN on the same commands below; independent `openclaw.json` + marker-file readback
- Dedup: no open PR on `ensureAgentWorkspace` / agents add workspace whitespace; distinct from `#168261` (secrets provider-path) and `#167116` (connect target-file)

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

`--workspace` ending in a space must be stored and used literally; must not bind the neighbor directory without the trailing space.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw agents add <id> --non-interactive --workspace <path>` → `agents.commands.add` → `createAgent` → `ensureAgentWorkspace` → write `agents.entries.<id>.workspace` → disk readback.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses `readNonBlankString` + `path.resolve`/`expandHomePrefix` instead of `resolveUserPath` for these explicit user dirs only. Other `resolveUserPath` call sites unchanged.

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`) on current `upstream/main` vs this branch; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
ROOT=$(mktemp -d)
WS="$ROOT/workspace "
mkdir -p "$WS" "$ROOT/workspace"
printf 'KEEP\n' > "$WS/marker.txt"
printf 'WRONG\n' > "$ROOT/workspace/marker.txt"
node openclaw.mjs agents add spaced --non-interactive --workspace "$WS"
python3 -c "import json,pathlib; cfg=json.loads(pathlib.Path('$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json').read_text()); ws=cfg['agents']['entries']['spaced']['workspace']; print(repr(ws)); print(pathlib.Path(ws+'/marker.txt').read_text())"
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
--- base
workspace '/tmp/.../workspace'
marker WRONG

--- head
workspace '/tmp/.../workspace '
marker KEEP

--- control (no trailing space)
workspace '/tmp/.../normal' unchanged
```

## Update (2026-10-14 CST)

Completed consumer cutover ClawSweeper flagged:
- `resolveAgentWorkspaceDir` / `resolveEffectiveAgentDir` use `readNonBlankString` + `resolveUserPathLiteral`
- workspace prep, bootstrap load, and workspace-state snapshot/setup/attestation/guard/identity all resolve via `resolveUserPathLiteral`
- unused `resolveUserPath` removed from agent-create

### Runtime + state identity proof

```text
Config workspace = "/tmp/.../workspace " (neighbor has WRONG)
resolveAgentWorkspaceDir → "/tmp/.../workspace "
runtime_marker=KEEP
mergeWorkspaceSetupState + readWorkspaceStateSnapshot:
  state_setupCompleted=true
  state_identity.workspacePath="/tmp/.../workspace "
neighbor_marker=WRONG
uses_literal=true
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set … --provider-source file --provider-path` trims the path before writing `secrets.providers.*.path`, so a credential file whose name ends in a space is silently rewritten to a neighboring path (or a missing path). The same trim hits `--provider-command` and `--provider-trusted-dir`.

## User Impact

User impact: provider builder paths keep their literal whitespace (matching `--batch-file` / `connect --target-file`), so trailing-space filenames no longer retarget the wrong secret file on disk. Ordinary paths without edge whitespace are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildProviderConfig` used `opts.providerPath?.trim()` (and `.trim()` on command / `normalizeStringEntries` on trusted dirs) before persisting into config. Alix’s `#167116` already preserved connect target-file literals via `readNonBlankString`; this applies the same contract to the secrets provider builder.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts`; regression in `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts`
- Packaged CLI: base RED / head GREEN on the same commands below; independent `openclaw.json` readback
- Dedup: no open PR on provider-path whitespace; distinct from Alix `#167116` (connect only) and `#167118` (UTF-8 config bytes)

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

`--provider-path` ending in a space must be stored literally and must not resolve to a neighbor file without the trailing space.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw config set secrets.providers.<alias> --provider-source file --provider-path <path>` → `buildProviderConfig` → write `openclaw.json` → disk readback of `secrets.providers.<alias>.path`.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses existing `readNonBlankString` (already imported). `--batch-file` already used it; connect `#167116` is the sibling. Callers of this builder: config set provider mode only.

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`) on current `upstream/main` vs this branch; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
ROOT=$(mktemp -d)
SECRET="$ROOT/secret "
printf 'GOOD\n' > "$SECRET"
printf 'WRONG\n' > "$ROOT/secret"
node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.vault --provider-source file --provider-path "$SECRET" --provider-mode singleValue
python3 -c "import json,pathlib; cfg=json.loads(pathlib.Path('$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json').read_text()); print(repr(cfg['secrets']['providers']['vault']['path'])); print(pathlib.Path(cfg['secrets']['providers']['vault']['path']).read_text())"
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
--- base (upstream/main)
written '/tmp/.../secret'
content WRONG

--- head (this PR)
written '/tmp/.../secret '
content GOOD

--- control (no trailing space)
written '/tmp/.../secret-value.txt' unchanged
```

## Update (2026-10-14 CST)

Addressed ClawSweeper P2 incomplete cutover: added `resolveUserPathLiteral` and wired it through `readFileProviderPayload` + `assertSecureExecCommandPath` (command + trustedDirs) so OpenClaw resolution keeps the literal trailing-space path.

### OpenClaw resolver proof (not Python readback)

```text
Packaged: node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.vault --provider-source file --provider-path '/tmp/.../secret ' --provider-mode singleValue
OpenClaw resolveSecretRefString(...):
  stored_path_repr="/tmp/.../secret "
  resolved_value="GOOD"   # neighbor /tmp/.../secret contains WRONG
```

Unit: resolveUserPathLiteral home-dir tests; resolve.test trailing-space file provider; exec-provider validation green.

prs.title: fix(cron): reject whitespace-only --tools/--fallbacks; keep empty grants
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw cron add/edit --tools ''` (or whitespace-only) silently persists `toolsAllow: []`, stripping every tool from the job. Omitting `--tools` correctly defaults to `["*"]`.

## User Impact

User impact: an explicit blank `--tools` is rejected before the Gateway write, so a typo or empty shell variable cannot create a tool-less automation. Omitting `--tools` still defaults to unrestricted `["*"]`; nonempty lists are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`parseCronStringList("")` returned `[]`, and the add/edit paths persisted that empty grant. Empty arrays are truthy, so the omit-vs-blank distinction was lost. The fix rejects blank string lists (with `--tools` / `--fallbacks` flags) before Gateway access, matching other cron blank guards (`--script`, `--command-cwd`).

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts`, `register.cron-add.ts`, `register.cron-edit.ts`, `register.cron-edit-options.ts`; colocated tests
- Packaged CLI against live Gateway `ws://127.0.0.1:18991`: base RED (`toolsAllow: []`, job created) / head GREEN (exit 1, `--tools must not be blank`, no job)
- Unit: `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts`, `cron-cli.test.ts`, `register.cron-edit.test.ts` — 189 passed
- Dedup: no open PR owning blank `--tools` / `parseCronStringList` empty-list rejection

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Explicit blank `--tools` must not persist `toolsAllow: []`; omit `--tools` must still default to `["*"]`; nonempty `--tools read` must still work.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw cron add … --tools ''` → `parseCronStringList` → `CronCliError` before `cron.add` Gateway RPC.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Only `parseCronStringList` (cron CLI). Callers: cron add/edit `--tools` and `--fallbacks`. No change to Gateway tool-policy defaults.

### Real environment tested

CLI via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts` against Gateway on `ws://127.0.0.1:18991` with temporary state `/tmp/ochunt-gw1`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/ochunt-gw1 OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/ochunt-gw1/openclaw.json
CLI=(node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts)
URL=(--url ws://127.0.0.1:18991 --token "$TOKEN")
"${CLI[@]}" cron add "p1-green-blank" --cron "0 * * * *" --message "hello" --tools '' --json "${URL[@]}"; echo rc=$?
"${CLI[@]}" cron add "p1-green-omit" --cron "0 * * * *" --message "hello" --json "${URL[@]}"
"${CLI[@]}" cron add "p1-green-read" --cron "0 * * * *" --message "hello" --tools read --json "${URL[@]}"
"${CLI[@]}" cron list --json "${URL[@]}"  # readback: no p1-green-blank; omit/read present
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
--- blank --tools
{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","message":"--tools must not be blank"}}
rc=1
readback: has p1-green-blank False
--- omit --tools
toolsAllow ['*']  (job created)
--- --tools read
toolsAllow ['read']  (job created)
```

## Update (2026-10-14 CST)

Addressed ClawSweeper P1 / Decision needed: **restored documented empty grants**.
- `--tools ""` / `--fallbacks ""` again persist `[]` (tool-free / strict-model), matching #149375 and docs
- Only **whitespace-only** lists (e.g. `--tools "  "`) are rejected as accidental blank input

### Parser proof

```text
parseCronStringList("", "--tools") → []
parseCronStringList("   ", "--tools") → throws "--tools must not be blank"
parseCronStringList("read", "--tools") → ["read"]
```

prs.title: feat(slack): create public channels from message actions
prs.body:
Closes #163782

## What problem this solves

OpenClaw’s Slack message tool cannot create a project channel, forcing operators to leave the workflow or use a separate integration.

## User impact

An operator can explicitly enable Slack channel creation with `channels.slack.actions.channels: true` (or the selected account’s equivalent). The action creates a public channel in the trusted workspace, invites the trusted requester when Slack permits, and returns a reusable workspace-qualified target.

## Design and security boundary

Channel creation is **disabled by default** and is no longer part of the ordinary `messages` action gate. This makes workspace administration an explicit operator choice while preserving existing message permissions.

The generated Slack manifest requests bot-compatible `channels:manage` for creation and `channels:write.invites` for requester invitation. Existing Slack apps must be reauthorized after adopting these scopes.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/slack/src/channel-create.test.ts extensions/slack/src/action-runtime.test.ts extensions/slack/src/message-tools.test.ts extensions/slack/src/setup-surface.test.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-actions-setup-status.contract.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 5 files, 108 tests passed.
- `pnpm docs:check-links` — 15,215 internal links checked; 0 broken.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

## Current-head live proof

The reauthorized disposable-workspace proof on current head `2d9f3f66e992430b6ff397a5b7b4225c8672a6cb` created a public channel, invited the verified non-admin requester, delivered to the returned target, and rejected disabled-account creation before Slack I/O. [Inspectable redacted terminal evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-6159613571) records the final API boundary and managed-Gateway health without identifiers or credentials.

[Isolated v2026.10.3-to-candidate compatibility evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-6159849038) validates the persisted reauthorized configuration with both runtimes, proves the reauthorized credential with `auth.test`, and shows a matching non-secret settings/data fingerprint without touching the managed Gateway.

## Before merge

- [x] **Real behavior proof:** published inspectable, redacted current-head terminal evidence for the allowed create/invite/send path and disabled-account pre-I/O rejection. Remaining live Enterprise Grid final-effect coverage is called out below.
- [x] **Data-model compatibility evidence:** published the isolated `v2026.10.3`-to-candidate reauthorization/configuration compatibility record. Reviewer acceptance determines whether it closes the merge gate.
- [ ] **Enterprise Grid limitation:** the contributor has no access to a Slack Enterprise Grid organization. The existing local adapter-to-client trace does not claim to substitute for a live Grid proof; a reviewer/maintainer must either accept that trace or supply a Grid test environment.
- [ ] **Upstream OpenClaw maintainer decision required:** accept, reject, or specify the administrative-delegation/default OAuth-grant contract. This is not a Dillon approval and is not a contributor-owned repair.

No contributor-owned code repair or Slack-proof setup remains open.

prs.title: fix(recovery): yield between store recovery iterations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #149935: On systems with many agent session stores (especially on slower storage volumes, SD cards, or external drives), `recoverRestartAbortedMainSessions` iterates sequentially over all store targets without yielding to the Node.js event loop. Each store recovery executes synchronous SQLite queries, filesystem operations, and transcript reads. While individual store checks are fast, across dozens or hundreds of agent stores (reported 63.6s with 237 agents), this synchronous I/O accumulates into a multi-second or multi-minute continuous event-loop block. During this time, the Gateway is completely unresponsive—HTTP requests hang, WebSocket pings fail, and health checks timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup session recovery consists of two distinct synchronous phases:

1. **Store Discovery Phase (`discoverRestartRecoveryStoreTargets`)**:
   As noted in [issue #149935 comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/149935#issuecomment-5696431792), discovery is a separate synchronous phase: it resolves session directories, validates agent database admission, and queries each store via `hasSessionEntriesByStatusReadOnly` (`main-session-restart-recovery-shared.ts:107`) to filter candidate store targets. In our production-path measurement across 20 stores, discovery executed in ~29.87 ms (~1.49 ms/store).
2. **Store Recovery Loop Phase (`recoverRestartAbortedMainSessions`)**:
   The recovery loop iterates through all discovered store targets and calls `recoverStore`, performing deep transcript inspection, state transitions, and session resumption. The accumulated synchronous I/O across stores in this loop represents the primary multi-second stall reported in #149935.

### The Fix: Yielding Strictly Between Store Recoveries
- **Strictly Between Stores**: The recovery loop now yields only when transitioning between stores (`if (i < targets.length - 1)`). This ensures no unnecessary trailing timer is scheduled after the final store, eliminating fake-timer deadlocks in single-store startup tests (`vi.useFakeTimers()`).
- **`setTimeout(resolve, 0)`**: Yielding via `setTimeout(..., 0)` turns the Node.js event loop through the timer phase, interleaving concurrent Gateway requests, WebSocket heartbeats, and health checks between store recoveries without altering recovery semantics, execution order, or store ownership checks.

## Evidence

Executed on revision: `397581f05477d1218f3626231b1ac8707e5de8c6`

### 1. Production Recovery Path Execution (Real SQLite Session Stores)

```
✓ Gateway responsiveness verified: heartbeats increased from 0 to 49.

All verification assertions PASSED.
```
</details>

### 3. Automated Regression Test Suite
`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-yield.test.ts`:
- Spies on `recoverStore` across multiple stores.
- Enqueues an independent event-loop callback (`gateway-callback`) immediately when store A completes.
- Asserts that the callback executes strictly *between* `end:A` and `start:B` (`["start:A", "end:A", "gateway-callback", "start:B", "end:B"]`).
- **Negative Verification**: Temporarily commenting out the yield causes this test to fail with `AssertionError: expected -1 to be greater than 1` because `start:B` runs in the same tick as `end:A`, starving the callback until after `end:B`.
- **Backoff Test Verification**: Verified that single-store recovery under `vi.useFakeTimers()` in `main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts:4247` (`retains canonical retry backoff when startup recovery begins immediately`) passes without hanging because no yield is scheduled when `targets.length === 1`.

## Safety & Invariants

- **Zero Semantic Changes**: Recovery logic, error handling, session mutation, and ownership admission rules in `recoverStore` remain identical.
- **Zero Trailing Delay**: When only one store exists or after the last store is recovered, no extra timer is scheduled.
- **Lockfile & Changelog Integrity**: `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md` are completely untouched.
- **Boundary & Linter Cleanliness**: Passes all boundary checks (`scripts/run-additional-boundary-checks.mts`), `oxlint`, and Knip unused-export validation (`scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts`).

Closes #149935

prs.title: fix(gateway): omit media-store URIs from the workspace file projection
prs.body:
Fixes #150322.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI file panel offered an inbound chat attachment as an openable workspace file, and every click failed. `sessions.files.list` projected the assistant's `read` of `media://inbound/<id>` as a workspace entry with `missing: true`, and `sessions.files.get` answered `INVALID_REQUEST session_file_not_found` for that path. The attachment itself was healthy — the same bytes preview in the chat bubble — so the panel was advertising an action that could never succeed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The touched-file projection in `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts:85-108` resolves every tool-argument path against the session root. `expandPath` (`src/agents/sessions/tools/path-utils.ts:33-47`) understands `file://` URLs, so an absolute `file://` path lands outside an out-of-tree root and is already excluded. A media-store identity had no such handling: `path.resolve(root, "media://inbound/x.png")` collapses the double slash and lands at `<root>/media:/inbound/x.png`, which is lexically inside the root. The entry survived the workspace filter, failed `stat`, and was reported as a missing workspace file.

Repair classification: **behavior-completing**. The projection already excludes `file://`, parent-relative, home and out-of-root shapes — `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.touched-files.test.ts:446` encodes exactly that contract — and the media-store URI was the one non-workspace shape that slipped through it.

The exclusion belongs at this projection boundary rather than inside the shared `resolveToCwd` (the `read` tool resolves `media://` URIs through it), and rather than granting the workspace file RPCs media-store access: the media store owns those bytes and already serves them through the authenticated `/__openclaw__/assistant-media` route (`src/gateway/control-ui-resource-routes.ts:7`). The predicate reuses the existing non-throwing scheme classifier `classifyMediaReferenceSource(...).isMediaStoreUrl` (`src/media/media-reference.ts:54`) instead of adding another URI guard.

## User Impact

The file panel no longer offers a dead attachment entry. Write paths are unaffected because `setSessionWorkspaceFile` only accepts a candidate that already exists as a file (`src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts:555-570`), which the phantom path never does.

## Evidence

### Inherited required-check failure: `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` (2026-10-11)

The only red required lane on this head is a Control UI end-to-end timeout, and it is **not caused by this diff**:

Two unrelated diffs failing one canvas-visibility case in the same hour is an inherited lane failure, not a diff-caused regression.
- Per the review's own instruction ("repair only a demonstrated diff-caused failure"), no repair is attempted here.

### ### Rebase note (2026-10-11)

This revision's head is `2b57a7808702016484afcd8dbb031e78fd1621dc`, rebased onto `main` @ `3529142cc84` because the previous base (`9f049a640d5f0c22628747a926b8ebd29377a4a5`) predated a material amount of merged work. The rebase replayed the same commits with no conflicts and the patch is unchanged: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` still reports +57/-3 across 3 files. The proof receipts below were captured on the pre-rebase head and were not re-run on this base; CI re-runs on this head.


Handler-level: the real `sessions.files.list` and `sessions.files.get` handlers over the real touched-file projection chain (`collectTouchedFilesFromMessage` → `resolveTouchedFilePath` → `toSessionFileEntry`), with the suite's standard mocks for the session entry and the transcript reader (`sessions-files.test-support.ts`). Before and after use the same input: an assistant `read` of `media://inbound/image---15547f7e.png` plus ordinary workspace paths. The projection code is byte-identical between the revision the before-state was captured on and `main` (`git diff --stat origin/main -- src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.ts` is empty; current `main` is `79121743a16`).

prs.title: fix(codex): project raw outer tool-call lifecycles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Codex harness projects native app-server items (`commandExecution`, `dynamicToolCall`, and so on) to the `codex_app_server.item` agent-event stream with `started`/`completed` phases. Outer model tool calls that Codex records as raw response items have no projected lifecycle: function calls, custom tool calls (for example the code-mode JS `exec` wrapper), local shell calls and tool-search calls. A plugin that must know whether any tool call is still running therefore sees the run as idle while an outer code-mode call is still open, because its child shell commands have already completed.

This was found live with the Advisor plugin (#169564). It must not fork a session while a call is still open, because codex-rs normalization then fabricates an `aborted` output for the open call.

## Fix

`handleRawResponseItemCompleted` now also projects raw call receipts as `codex_app_server.item` `{ phase: "started", itemId: call_id, type }`, and their recorded outputs as `{ phase: "completed", itemId: call_id, type }`. Only phase, id and type are copied, never arguments or results. The app-server forwards raw response items after codex-rs records them in history, so `completed` means the output is persisted. Call and output receipts share `call_id` (codex-rs `protocol/src/models.rs`).

## User Impact

None by itself. Plugins that track in-flight work on Codex runs (with `payload: "metadata"`) can now see outer tool calls start and finish. The existing subscriber (`run-attempt.steering-settlement`) is unaffected.

## Evidence

- Projector test: raw function, custom, local-shell and tool-search calls produce paired started/completed events with ids and types only.
- The steering-settlement subscriber tests still pass.
- Live (Advisor, Codex runtime): before this change, a review boundary was reached while the outer code-mode call was open, and the Gateway logged a missing custom-tool output. Advisor's regression, an outer call open while its children are complete, holds the review until the outer output is recorded.

prs.title: fix(msteams): keep debounced channel thread replies isolated by thread root
prs.body:
Fixes #149303

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when `messages.inbound.debounceMs` is enabled, replies sent to different Microsoft Teams channel threads within one quiet window are collapsed into a single agent turn. The inbound debounce key only used the normalized conversation id + sender, and `normalizeMSTeamsConversationId` strips the `;messageid=<thread-root>` suffix, so replies in distinct thread roots shared one debounce bucket. The merged turn reads and replies across thread boundaries, polluting thread context and misrouting the reply.

## User Impact

User impact: with inbound debouncing on, replies in different Microsoft Teams thread roots now produce separate agent turns, each bound to its own thread, so thread context stays isolated and each reply lands in the thread it came from. No configuration change is required — the behavior now matches what already happens when debouncing is off, and matches the per-thread session routing used for the rest of the inbound pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The debounce `buildKey` in the Microsoft Teams message handler now mirrors `resolveMSTeamsRouteSessionKey` session routing: for channel conversations it appends the thread root (the `;messageid=` conversation-message root when present, else `replyToId`) to the key, so distinct thread roots debounce independently. Direct chats and group chats are unaffected — the thread-root dimension only applies to channel conversations.

## Evidence

### Real runtime trace (real handler, debouncer, ingress queue, and timers)

The regression harness drives the **real** `createMSTeamsMessageHandler`, the **real**
SDK inbound debouncer, and the **real** ingress lifecycle with **real** timers
(`debounceMs: 40`). Two channel replies in different thread roots
(`;messageid=root-a` / `;messageid=root-b`) arrive within one debounce window.

- **Before this fix:** 1 dispatch — both bodies merged into one turn. Test failed
  with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 2 times, but got 1 times` (reproduced on the
  parent commit `d49937902`).
- **After this fix:** 2 dispatches, each body bound to its own thread root. Test
  passes.

The strengthened regression also asserts **correctly routed replies**: each turn
resolves to a **distinct per-thread-root session key** through the real
`resolveMSTeamsRouteSessionKey` path (the same routing owner used for the rest of
the inbound pipeline):

- `ctx.SessionKey` for thread A contains `:thread:root-a`
- `ctx.SessionKey` for thread B contains `:thread:root-b`
- the two session keys are distinct (`new Set(routeKeys).size === 2`)

So within one debounce window the two thread turns stay separate *and* each reply is
routed to its own thread session — the exact behavior the fix guarantees.

### Real Teams Gateway trace (loopback Bot Framework Connector)

New QA scenario `msteams-debounce-thread-root-isolation` runs the **real** Gateway,
the **real** bundled `msteams` plugin, the **real** agent dispatch (mock provider),
and a **loopback Bot Framework Connector** — the repo's sanctioned live-channel
harness for Teams. It passed on this branch:

- Two channel messages in **distinct thread roots** (`;messageid=<rootA>` /
  `;messageid=<rootB>`) sent inside one `debounceMs: 1500` window produced **two
  isolated dispatches**, and each marker reply was placed in its own thread root:
  ```
  outbound "… QA-DEB-THREAD-A-OK"  threadId=7f8e883d-…   (thread root A)
  outbound "… QA-DEB-THREAD-B-OK"  threadId=bae5438d-…   (thread root B)
  assert crossA.length === 1 && crossB.length === 1 && distinct threadIds → PASS
  ```
- Two channel messages in the **same thread root** sent inside one debounce window
  still batched into **one** dispatch / **one** reply (batching preserved):
  ```
  outbound "… QA-DEB-THREAD-Z1-OK"  threadId=843530ee-…   (thread root Z, one reply)
  assert sameOutbound.length === 1 → PASS
  ```
- Full trace and receipt: `qa/scenarios/channels/msteams-debounce-thread-root-isolation.yaml`
  (committed), run via `pnpm openclaw qa msteams --scenario msteams-debounce-thread-root-isolation
  --provider-mode mock-openai` → suite result `pass`.

The loopback connector exercises the real Bot Framework activity path end-to-end
(inbound activity → real plugin handler/debouncer → real agent dispatch → real
outbound reply delivery). Graph-backed *thread history* enrichment (the plugin
fetches parent/reply context from `graph.microsoft.com`) is not reachable from this
sandbox, so that enrichment is absent here — the same limitation applies to the
repo's pre-existing `msteams-thread-message-tool-final-dedupe` scenario, which also
fails without Graph. The debounce-key isolation this PR changes is fully exercised
and proven by the trace above.

### Suites

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/`: 11 files, 135 tests passed.
- Full extension unit suite `extensions/msteams/src` (excluding live tests): 99/100 files passed (1619 tests). The one failing file (`setup-surface.test.ts`) is unrelated and environment-only: it fails under this host's `zh_CN.UTF-8` locale because the setup wizard renders prompts in Chinese, and passes 11/11 under `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`.
- Typecheck: both `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` lanes exit 0.
- Net diff: **+101 / −8** lines across 4 files (the handler fix, its regression test now with routed-session-key assertions, and a one-line docs clarification in `docs/concepts/messages.md`).

Gap: the repo's `autoreview` skill could not run from this environment — the Codex engine is blocked by the corporate network (`api.openai.com` returns 403 Forbidden), the Kimi CLI is below the required version (0.28.0 < 0.30.0), and Claude/Amp/Pi are not installed. All validation above was performed directly against the current source.

> AI-assisted: yes

prs.title: fix(agents): drop throttled exec update events
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: exec live output throttling capped detailed payloads, but throttled `tool_execution_update` events still emitted generic tool/item updates with no new user-visible payload.
- Solution: make throttled exec updates a true no-op until the next allowed live update or final result.
- What changed: `handleToolExecutionUpdate` now returns before emitting generic exec update traffic when the live exec update throttle suppresses the detailed output, with regression coverage for global agent events and `onAgentEvent` emissions.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): final exec result events, command completion items, non-exec tool updates, and the existing live exec output size cap are unchanged.

## Motivation

- #84850 captured a 60s gateway sample with average CPU at 83.66%, 42/60 samples at or above 100% CPU, and 0.00 kB/s average read I/O during an embedded exec tool run. Dropping redundant throttled update events reduces avoidable gateway projection/broadcast work in that hot path.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #84850
- Related #78645
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Gateway CPU saturation from #84850 during embedded exec tool output. Throttled exec updates should not continue producing generic tool/item event traffic when they carry no new visible output.
- Real environment tested: Local Linux OpenClaw worktree on Node 24, using the repo Vitest wrapper plus the redacted pidstat/gateway log evidence from the affected run.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`, `git diff --check`, and `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access review --uncommitted`.

Final result handling remains covered by the existing exec result tests.

prs.title: fix(agent): agent exec reports configured OAuth MCP servers as unauthorized
prs.body:
Related: #124768
Related: #143744 (provider OAuth profiles; this PR covers the MCP OAuth store, the sibling credential owner)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw agent exec` with an OAuth-protected MCP server they had already signed in to with `openclaw mcp login` would see the server fail at run start with:

```
[bundle-mcp] failed to start server "linear" (https://mcp.linear.app/mcp): MCP server "linear" requires OAuth authorization. Run openclaw mcp login linear.
```

The run then proceeds without that server's tools, and following the printed advice cannot help: `openclaw mcp login` writes to the operator's shared state store, which `agent exec` never reads. Observed on a production Gateway host (2026.9.4) where coding workers call `openclaw agent exec` from their shells: 12–13 such failures per day while `openclaw mcp probe linear` on the same machine reported 66 tools and a valid 24h token, and a fresh `openclaw mcp login linear` changed nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

`agent exec` runs against a disposable state root, and the MCP OAuth store, its pending-authorization rows, and the cross-process refresh lease all resolved through whatever `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` pointed at during the run. MCP OAuth sessions are operator credentials, so they now follow the original shared state root exactly the way stored auth profiles already do: `agent exec` pins the MCP OAuth store to that root for the run, and every read, rotated-token write, and lease acquisition resolves there. The temporary state never holds a credential copy, the run never becomes a second refresh owner (the lease lives beside the rows it guards), and `--auth-env-only` keeps disabling stored credential access, MCP sessions included. No new config or CLI surface.

## User Impact

Operators and coding agents can run `openclaw agent exec` against OAuth-protected MCP servers (Linear, Calendly, …) with their existing `openclaw mcp login` session: the server connects and its tools are available in the run, with no second login and no misleading "run mcp login" advice. `--auth-env-only` behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Live, source-built CLI, isolated state root.** A local OAuth-protected streamable-http MCP server (`proofsrv`) that returns 401 unless it receives `Authorization: Bearer stored-access` and logs every request; one MCP OAuth session seeded into the operator state root via the real store API; then `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<operator root> openclaw agent exec --config <config with proofsrv auth: oauth> --cwd <dir> --json "Call the proof_echo tool …"`.

Before (shipped 2026.9.4 CLI, same state root and config):

```
[bundle-mcp] failed to start server "proofsrv" (http://127.0.0.1:47311/mcp): MCP server "proofsrv" requires OAuth authorization. Run openclaw mcp login proofsrv.
```
proof server log: `POST /mcp REJECTED authorization=absent` — the run reached the server with no token at all; the model then answered "The `proof_echo` tool isn't available in this session".

After (this branch, `pnpm build` then `pnpm openclaw agent exec …`): no `bundle-mcp` failure line; proof server log for the run:

```
POST /mcp AUTHORIZED bearer=stored-access rpc=initialize                -> responded 200
POST /mcp AUTHORIZED bearer=stored-access rpc=notifications/initialized -> responded 202
POST /mcp AUTHORIZED bearer=stored-access rpc=tools/list                -> responded 200
```

Not covered by the live run: the model turn itself still ended in an OpenAI 401 in this isolated exec (no provider credential reachable from the temporary state), which is the separate provider-OAuth gap tracked in #124768 / #143744, not MCP OAuth. Nothing in this PR touches provider auth.

**Regression tests** (fail on `upstream/main` for the intended reason):
- `src/commands/agent-exec.mcp-oauth.test.ts`: inside an `agent exec` run the seeded session reads as `authorized`, `resolveMcpOAuthAccessToken` returns the stored token through the lease, a rotated token persists on the original root, and the temporary state has zero `mcp_oauth_stores` rows; under `--auth-env-only` the session is `unauthenticated` and resolution throws `requires OAuth authorization`. Pre-fix failure: `expected { state: 'unauthenticated' } to match object { state: 'authorized' }`.
- `src/agents/mcp-oauth-store.test.ts`: reads, writes, prefix listing, and pending-authorization state inside `withMcpOAuthSharedStateDir` hit only the scoped root; the ambient root never sees them.

**Local gates:** `pnpm test src/agents/mcp-oauth src/commands/agent-exec src/gateway/mcp-oauth-callback src/cli/mcp-cli src/agents/mcp-config-mutation.test.ts src/agents/mcp-transport` green (the `cli-process` probe-exit test hit its 30s cap once under CPU contention and passes standalone); `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` green on every lane (typecheck core + core tests, lint, format, boundaries, ratchets), with the dead-export scan re-run directly (`scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts`: 0 entries) after its wrapper timed out under the same contention; `pnpm build` clean; `.agents/skills/autoreview` (Codex, P0–P2): no findings.

**Production LOC:** +26 / −12 across `mcp-oauth-store.ts`, `mcp-oauth.ts`, `agent-exec.ts`; growth is the one credential-ownership scope (`withMcpOAuthSharedStateDir` + `mcpOAuthStateDatabaseOptions`) that mirrors `withAuthProfileStoreAgentDir`, plus threading its options into the six existing database/lease call sites. Tests +132, docs +1/−1.


**CI note (head 487071d, 2026-09-18):** the single red shard `checks-node-compact-small-37` fails on `test/scripts/tsgo-core-test-shards.test.ts` with `messaging: 701 test roots exceeds the 700 limit`. That shard covers `src/auto-reply`, `src/channels`, and `src/infra/outbound`; this PR adds no file there (its only new test is `src/commands/agent-exec.mcp-oauth.test.ts`). The count is 701 on `upstream/main` itself since 10169f0489e (#151067) and is identical with or without this branch, so it is main-owned shard headroom, not this change. Every other check on this head is green.

prs.title: fix(macos): restore node auth after SecretRef upgrades
prs.body:
Refs #149804

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the approved-role upgrade path where the macOS app can remain in a recurring `auth=none` / `token_missing` loop after SecretRef migration leaves its Gateway-scoped node credential unavailable while the operator connection still works.

## User Impact

Affected Macs automatically reissue their missing scoped node credential through the already-authenticated operator connection and reconnect. If guarded repair fails, the menu bar exposes a **Repair Mac node** action and keeps that action available across subsequent disconnects and exhausted automatic retries.

## Scope

This repair applies only when the existing node role remains approved and the operator and node intentionally share the same persisted device identity. It does **not** restore a removed node role, widen onboarding or pairing admission, promote a distinct node identity, migrate or claim legacy unscoped tokens, resolve SecretRefs in Swift, or expose shared Gateway credentials.

The broader removed-role/onboarding path reported in #149804 remains outside this PR, so this PR references rather than closes the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair reuses `device.token.rotate` on the exact current device-token-authenticated operator lease. It requires the operator and node profiles to share the same device ID, binds persistence to the current Gateway ID and endpoint generation, validates the returned node role and empty scopes, and persists only the Gateway-scoped v2 credential before reconnecting.

Automatic repair is limited to one attempt per endpoint generation/device after structured `AUTH_TOKEN_MISSING`. Concurrent or stale work is coalesced or rejected. Failed repair state is retained only for the matching endpoint-generation/device key, stale callbacks cannot overwrite the current status, and the manual action resets the attempt latch without weakening admission policy.

## Evidence

- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` — passed; app and all Swift test targets compile.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` with pinned Swift tools — passed.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` with pinned Swift tools — passed with zero violations.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` through the exact pinned pnpm 12.4.0 entrypoint — passed (`changed=false`).
- Native-state schema guard, conflict-marker check, and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Fresh mandatory Codex autoreview at P0–P2 — scoped clean; no actionable correctness or security findings.
- Regression coverage includes successful same-device rotation and persistence, restart reuse without another rotation, legacy-token preservation, distinct-device rejection, withheld responses, structured-error eligibility, attempt budgeting, repair presentation, stale endpoint-result rejection, and repair-action retention across matching disconnects and exhausted retries.
- Exact-head CI for `a5cf1e5bc773b93a296299c1f607b06e100ec161` — green, including the macOS Swift and Node shards: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35181180307

The aggregate local changed-file command was not run because it selects `test:macos:ci`; repository policy forbids executing native tests on the operator desktop. Exact-head CI is the test-execution owner for this change.

## Evidence limitation

We do not have access to a disposable, interactive macOS environment. Exact-head automated macOS CI can be provided, but real before/after UI screenshots and a manual upgrade observation remain unavailable. This documents the limitation; it is not a waiver. A maintainer must either provide the required environment or explicitly accept the missing evidence before merge.

prs.title: fix(a2a): agent card advertises http:// behind a TLS-terminating proxy
prs.body:
Closes #150087

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: the A2A well-known agent card advertises an http:// endpoint when the Gateway sits behind a trusted TLS-terminating reverse proxy.

## User Impact
User impact: operators running the A2A channel behind a trusted reverse proxy (nginx, Traefik, etc.) now get an accurate https:// endpoint in the published agent card, without needing to manually set channels.a2a.advertisedUrl as a workaround.

## Why This Change Was Made
`resolveRequestOrigin` derived scheme only from `request.socket.encrypted`, ignoring `X-Forwarded-Proto`. The fix trusts that header only when the connecting peer's address matches a configured `gateway.trustedProxies` entry, reusing the existing `isTrustedProxyAddress` primitive (already exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/core`, backed by `src/gateway/net.ts`) instead of duplicating proxy-trust logic. Untrusted peers, or deployments with no `trustedProxies` configured, keep the prior fail-closed `http://` behavior. An explicitly configured `channels.a2a.advertisedUrl` always takes precedence and is unaffected.

## Evidence

**Unit tests** (`extensions/a2a/src/http.test.ts`, 3 new cases, 39/39 pass):
- trusted-proxy peer sending `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` → advertised scheme becomes `https`
- untrusted peer sending the same header → ignored, stays `http` (spoof rejection)
- explicit `advertisedUrl` configured → always wins, even behind a trusted proxy with `https` forwarded (added after review feedback below)

**Red/green proof the bug and fix are both real:** reverted the production fix and reran the new tests against the *original* code — the trusted-proxy test failed with `http://` instead of `https://`, reproducing the exact symptom from the issue. Restored the fix and confirmed it passes.

**Live proof through a real TLS-terminating reverse proxy (not mocked)**, requested by ClawSweeper review: a standalone script starts the actual, unmodified `createA2aHttpHandler` (the same function `extensions/a2a/src/gateway.ts` wires into the Gateway) behind a real `node:https` server terminating TLS with a genuine self-signed certificate, forwarding to the backend over a real loopback socket with `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`:

```
=== Scenario 1: direct HTTP request, no proxy, no trustedProxies configured ===
(baseline: unchanged pre-existing behavior)
agent-card.json supportedInterfaces[0].url = http://localhost:48311/a2a/v1

=== Scenario 2: real HTTPS reverse proxy, gateway.trustedProxies trusts it ===
(the actual bug fix: X-Forwarded-Proto now trusted from a configured proxy)
agent-card.json supportedInterfaces[0].url (via real TLS-terminating proxy) = https://localhost:48312/a2a/v1

=== Scenario 3: same real TLS proxy, but operator set an explicit advertisedUrl ===
(proves the explicit config always wins over trusted-proxy detection)
agent-card.json supportedInterfaces[0].url (explicit advertisedUrl configured) = https://operator-configured.example.test/a2a/v1
```

**Other checks (all clean):**
- `pnpm test:extension a2a`: 39/39 pass
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: clean
- Plugin/SDK import-boundary checks (`check-sdk-package-extension-import-boundary.mts`, `check-src-extension-import-boundary.mts`): clean
- `oxfmt` / `oxlint --type-aware`: clean
- `pnpm build`: clean (full monorepo)
- `pnpm check`: clean
- `pnpm test:contracts:plugins`: 1090/1128 pass; remaining failures are a pre-existing, unrelated Windows-only SQLite temp-file EBUSY flake in `session-entry-projection.contract.test.ts`, reproduced identically in isolation, not touched by this change
- CI on this PR: all ~50 checks green
