prs.title: fix(secrets): yield during multi-agent auth-store preparation
prs.body:
Fixes #149933.

## What Problem This Solves

`prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot` (`src/secrets/runtime.ts`) loads and
`structuredClone`s every candidate agent's auth store in one synchronous
`for` loop before it ever yields to the event loop. Both call sites in the
function (the fast-path branch and the resolver-path branch) share this
loop via `loadAuthStoresWithMigrationIsolation`, and it runs on **every**
config hot reload via `activateRuntimeSecrets` in
`src/gateway/server-reload-managed-secrets.ts` — even a reload that only
flips which agent is `default`.

On a multi-agent deployment (the report cites 237 agents on a slow disk)
this synchronous scan blocks the Node event loop for the entire duration of
the reload, so the Gateway cannot service any other request (chat replies,
health checks, etc.) until every agent's auth store has been read and
cloned. The reporter measured ~47s of blocked time on their deployment.

The issue's own suggested fix — skipping the secrets rebuild entirely when
only `agents.list` default flags changed — was reviewed by the repo's
automated triage and rejected as imprecise: unchanged agent IDs don't
guarantee unchanged credential dependencies, so skipping the rebuild could
serve stale runtime state. The triage instead recommended a scheduling fix
that keeps full-refresh semantics but makes the multi-agent preparation
cooperatively yield, which is what this PR does.

## The Fix

`loadAuthStoresWithMigrationIsolation` now yields to the event loop every
25 agent directories (`setImmediate`-based, matching the existing
`SWEEP_YIELD_BATCH_SIZE` batching pattern already used by the task-registry
maintenance sweep in `src/tasks/task-registry.maintenance.ts`), and both
call sites now `await` it. Publication/activation semantics, atomic
snapshot commit, and the credentials-revision watermark are untouched —
only the read loop's scheduling changes.

## Evidence

New regression test
(`src/secrets/runtime.fast-path.test.ts`, "returns control to the event
loop before finishing a large multi-agent auth-store load") drives
`prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot` with 30 synthetic agent dirs and asserts
that control returns to the caller (a still-pending promise) before all 30
auth stores have been loaded — i.e. the event loop gets a chance to run
other queued work partway through the scan.

Confirmed this test fails on the pre-fix code by reverting only the
source file and rerunning:

```
$ git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/secrets/runtime.ts   # (pre-fix state in this session)
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/secrets/runtime.fast-path.test.ts -t "returns control to the event loop"
 × secrets runtime fast path > returns control to the event loop before finishing a large multi-agent auth-store load
   → expected 30 to be less than 30
 Tests  1 failed | 13 skipped (14)
```

Restored the fix and reran — passes, along with the full related suites:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/secrets/runtime.fast-path.test.ts src/secrets/runtime.auth-migration-isolation.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts
 ✓ |gateway-server| src/gateway/server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts (8 tests)
 ✓ |secrets| src/secrets/runtime.fast-path.test.ts (7 tests, incl. the new one)
 ✓ |secrets| src/secrets/runtime.auth-migration-isolation.test.ts (1 test)
 Test Files  2 passed (2) / 1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15) / 8 passed (8)
```

Also ran, both clean:

```
$ pnpm tsgo:core
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/secrets/runtime.ts src/secrets/runtime.fast-path.test.ts
[exited with code 0]
```

`git diff --check`: clean (no whitespace errors).

## Real-behavior reload responsiveness proof

Addressing the "needs real behavior proof" review: ran a standalone script
(not committed — scratch-only, deleted after use) that drives the actual
`prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot` production path against 250 real,
SQLite-backed agent auth-profile stores on disk (via `saveAuthProfileStore`,
the same persistence the Gateway uses), while a real `http` server stands in
for a concurrent Gateway request. It logs when the `prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot`
call itself returns control (i.e. how long the caller is blocked before the
function can yield at all), when the concurrent HTTP request completes, and
when the reload finishes.

Pre-fix (`git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/secrets/runtime.ts`), calling
`prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot` blocks the event loop for the *entire*
synchronous scan before returning any promise at all, so nothing —
including accepting the concurrent request's connection — can run until
then:

```
[proof] agents=250
[proof] prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot() call returned control after 468.8ms (synchronous portion before first real yield)
[proof] concurrent HTTP request completed at +495.1ms
[proof] reload finished at +495.2ms, auth_stores_loaded=250
```

Post-fix (restored, `git checkout HEAD -- src/secrets/runtime.ts`), the call
returns almost immediately and the concurrent request completes well before
the reload itself finishes:

```
[proof] agents=250
[proof] prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot() call returned control after 52.4ms (synchronous portion before first real yield)
[proof] concurrent HTTP request completed at +168.9ms
[proof] reload finished at +515.2ms, auth_stores_loaded=250
[proof] concurrent request completed before reload finished: true
```

So pre-fix, the caller (and by extension any other queued Gateway work) is
blocked for ~469ms out of the ~495ms total reload before the function can
even yield once; post-fix it's blocked for only ~52ms before yielding, and a
concurrent request completes in ~169ms while the reload is still running
(~515ms total) — i.e. the Gateway can service other requests during the
scan instead of only after it. This sandbox's tmpfs-backed SQLite reads are
far faster than the reporter's "slow disk", so absolute numbers here are much
smaller than the reported ~47s, but the relative before/after behavior
(fully blocking vs. yielding-and-interleaving) is the same mechanism the fix
targets.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change was written by an autonomous Claude Code agent (Sonnet 5).

## What Problem This Solves

On the standalone `/approve` page in light theme, the **Allow once** button keeps white foreground text while the light-theme rule `:root[data-theme-mode="light"] .btn` overrides the background to a near-white surface. prs.title: fix(ui): session detail selects keep a rejected value after a failed patch
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on the Sessions page, when the Gateway rejects a change to a session's Thinking, Fast, Verbose, or Reasoning override (or to its group), the error banner appears but the dropdown keeps showing the rejected pick instead of the session's stored value.

## User Impact

User impact: after a failed save, the session detail dropdowns and the "Move session to a group" dropdown snap back to what the session actually has, so operators are not misled into thinking a rejected override took effect.

## Why This Change Was Made

These selects set the shown option only through the `selected` attribute on each `<option>`. Once a user has picked an option in a select, browsers ignore later `selected` attribute changes for it, so the re-render after a failed `sessions.patch` could not move the select back. The selects now also bind their value with Lit's `live()` directive on every render, the same pattern the Devices exec node binding select uses. `?selected` stays on the options to seed the first paint. The Group-by select is unchanged because it only drives local page state and has no failure path.

## Evidence

Before (mocked Gateway rejects `sessions.patch`; the session's stored Thinking is `medium`, the user picked the other option): the banner shows the failure but the Thinking dropdown still shows the rejected pick.

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Piyushrathoree/openclaw/caf0207cd39ed4b14e9db1488e4bdd0b5eca9ed0/before.png)

After (same steps on this branch): the Thinking dropdown is back on `Medium`.

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Piyushrathoree/openclaw/caf0207cd39ed4b14e9db1488e4bdd0b5eca9ed0/after.png)

Captures come from the repository's Control UI E2E harness (`installMockGateway` with a `sessions.patch` `__mockError`, real Chromium).

- New regression test in `ui/src/pages/sessions/view.test.ts` (`snaps selects back to the stored session values after a failed patch`) covers both the group select and the Thinking override select; it fails on `main` with `expected 'Ops' to be 'Research'` and passes with the fix.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/sessions/` — 12 files, 201 tests pass.
- `pnpm --dir ui test` (full UI lane) — 1,227 files, 21,236 tests pass, 0 failures.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check` clean. `lit-analyzer` reports 15 pre-existing findings in this file that are identical on `main` and not on the changed lines.

prs.title: fix: session trajectory export rewrites SQLite database permissions to 0600
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150012

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw sessions export-trajectory` changes the agent and state SQLite files from 0640 to 0600, writes the shared state database, and opens the agent database writable, although the export only reads the stored session.

## User Impact

User impact: exporting a session trajectory no longer changes database file permissions or contents, and it no longer opens the agent database writable, so group-readable databases stay readable to backup, monitoring, and support tools. Cold-archived sessions still export as before. No config, schema, or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI command already looks up the session with the read-only accessor, but the exporter then reads the session entry again through writable accessors: three session-entry identity checks and the legacy marker listing. The exporter now uses the existing read-only accessors for all of them: `loadSessionEntryReadOnly` and `listSessionEntriesReadOnly`. This follows the same pattern as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/136010 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149627.

Update after rebasing onto current main: main now loads export transcripts through the worker-backed `loadTranscriptEvents` read, which already restores cold-archived transcripts through its own owner. The earlier version of this PR replaced both transcript loads with a read-only snapshot plus a cold-archive fallback in a new `export-session-entries` module; that part is no longer needed and has been dropped, so the change is now limited to the four session-entry reads in `src/trajectory/export.ts` and one regression test in a new sibling test file (`export.test.ts` is already over the line cap).

The trajectory recording sink in `src/trajectory/runtime.ts` writes runtime events and is out of scope.

## Evidence

Tested at `6df0955393d` (base `upstream/main` `0257a7dab0f`, the merge base).

**Real CLI, before and after.** Each side is the built CLI with its own isolated home and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. A synthetic session (`agent:main:proof`, two messages) is seeded through that side's own session accessor, all databases are closed, and the agent and state databases are set to 0640. Then `node openclaw.mjs sessions export-trajectory --session-key agent:main:proof --workspace <workspace> --json` runs under `strace -e trace=openat`. Both sides exit 0 with `eventCount=2` and the same bundle files (`manifest.json`, `events.jsonl`, `session-branch.json`).

Before (base `0257a7dab0f`):

```text
FILES BEFORE EXPORT (mode size sha256/16 path)
  640   684032 1f6e461744a852ab agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
  640  1466368 5fcf983cea7bb280 state/openclaw.sqlite
FILES AFTER EXPORT
  600   684032 1f6e461744a852ab agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
  600  1466368 97bf4331afa09d22 state/openclaw.sqlite
OPENAT OF SQLITE MAIN FILES (flags, count):
  2   openclaw-agent.sqlite O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC
  1   openclaw-agent.sqlite O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC
  2   openclaw.sqlite O_RDWR|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC
```

After (this PR, `6df0955393d`):

```text
FILES BEFORE EXPORT (mode size sha256/16 path)
  640   684032 b97bb246ef074bad agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
  640  1466368 4336e14ad45e6e74 state/openclaw.sqlite
FILES AFTER EXPORT
  640   684032 b97bb246ef074bad agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
  640    32768 fd4c9fda9cd3f9ae agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite-shm
  640        0 e3b0c44298fc1c14 agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite-wal
  640  1466368 4336e14ad45e6e74 state/openclaw.sqlite
OPENAT OF SQLITE MAIN FILES (flags, count):
  2   openclaw-agent.sqlite O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC
```

Observed result: on main the export rewrites both databases to 0600, changes the state database contents, and opens the agent database `O_RDWR|O_CREAT`. With this change both files keep 0640 and identical hashes, the agent database is opened read-only only (the `-shm`/`-wal` files are the read-only reader's shared memory, also 0640), and `openclaw.sqlite` is not opened at all. The excerpts omit the quarantine database line (0600 from creation on both sides; opened read-write by both, but its contents change only on main); it is in the full captures.

Full captures: [before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/pr-150013/before-export-trajectory.txt), [after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/pr-150013/after-export-trajectory.txt), [diff](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/pr-150013/before-after.diff); harness: [run script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/pr-150013/harness-run.sh.txt), [seed script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/pr-150013/harness-seed.mts.txt).

**Regression test** (`src/trajectory/export-session-storage.test.ts`, head `6df0955393d` on main `0257a7dab0f`):

- `exports SQLite-backed sessions without joining the writable database lifecycle` exports a closed 0640 store through a complete session target and through a legacy marker with a session key. This covers all three entry lookups and the marker listing. It asserts no retained writable handle, no active writer lease, and mode 0640. On main's `export.ts` it fails at `getOpenClawAgentDatabaseIfOpen(...)` -> `toBeUndefined()`; with this change it passes.

**Local checks on the rebased head:**

| Test file | Local wall (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`) | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/trajectory/export-session-storage.test.ts` (new) | 27.1 s for the file (1 test, mostly worker startup); the case itself 0.73 s | 0.85 s for the case ([`checks-node-changed-compact-large-10`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37351779893/job/111904863294), shard `core-unit-src-security-3`: 2 files in 27.8 s, 87% transform) |

- `pnpm test src/trajectory/export.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 43 passed; `pnpm test src/commands/export-trajectory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main`: exit 0 (typecheck, lint, line-cap and SQLite worker ratchets, dead-export scan, guards).

Not covered: a live Gateway running at the same time as the CLI export. The Gateway's in-process export uses the same exporter and borrows its already-open handle through the read-only accessors.

prs.title: fix: SMS sends unsupported MMS media to Twilio when its Content-Type is constructor or __proto__
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/149999

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the SMS plugin sends MMS media to Twilio, and serves it with a filename like `mms-<id>function Object() { [native code] }`, when the media server replies `Content-Type: constructor` or `__proto__`, instead of rejecting it locally like every other unsupported type.

## User Impact

User impact: MMS sends whose media has a `constructor` or `__proto__` Content-Type now fail before any Twilio call with the existing "Twilio MMS does not support media type ..." error, and the hosted-media route answers `415` for such entries instead of serving them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Twilio MMS type-to-extension allowlist was a plain object indexed with the remote header value, so inherited `Object.prototype` members counted as supported types at both the send-time check and the hosted-media filename check. Since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143673, media loading keeps these header strings instead of throwing, so they now reach that allowlist. The table is now a `ReadonlyMap`, like the neighboring `Set` allowlists, so both readers only match real entries. The entries are unchanged, and no other code reads this table.

## Evidence

**Regression test.** Two rows (`constructor`, `__proto__`, expected `unsupported`) added to the existing `$outcome detected $contentType media` table in `extensions/sms/src/media.test.ts`.

- With the old `media.ts`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/sms/src/media.test.ts -t "unsupported detected"` gives `2 failed | 1 passed`. Both new rows fail with `AssertionError: promise resolved "'https://gateway.example.com/public/sm…'" instead of rejecting`, and `application/msword` passes.
- With this PR: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/sms/src/media.test.ts extensions/sms/src/media-limits.test.ts extensions/sms/src/send.test.ts` passes (119 + 20 tests).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base d886b8e374e` exits 0. This covers extension and test typecheck, changed-file lint, dead-export scan, storage/media/sidecar guards, and 0 import cycles.

**Real-path Before/After.** This used a temporary, uncommitted harness. A loopback HTTP server replies with the given `Content-Type` and feeds the real `loadWebMedia`. The SSRF policy allows only that loopback origin. Media then goes through the real `prepareSmsMediaAttempt` / hosted-media staging, backed by plugin state in an isolated state directory, and on to `sendPreparedSmsMediaAttempt`. Only the Twilio Messages call is replaced with a recorder. The hosted URL is fetched through `tryHandleHostedSmsMediaRequest` on a loopback server.

Before (base d886b8e374e):

```text
[constructor] prepareSmsMediaAttempt ACCEPTED
[constructor] sendSmsViaTwilio calls: 1
[constructor] hosted GET status=200 content-type="constructor" content-disposition="inline; filename=\"mms-6e831c33d4function Object() { [native code] }\""
[__proto__] prepareSmsMediaAttempt ACCEPTED
[__proto__] sendSmsViaTwilio calls: 1
[__proto__] hosted GET status=200 content-type="__proto__" content-disposition="inline; filename=\"mms-ff7acc8bec[object Object]\""
[application/x-openclaw-probe] prepareSmsMediaAttempt REJECTED: PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError: SMS media preparation failed before Twilio dispatch: Twilio MMS does not support media type application/x-openclaw-probe.
[application/x-openclaw-probe] sendSmsViaTwilio calls: 0
```

After (this PR):

```text
[constructor] prepareSmsMediaAttempt REJECTED: PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError: SMS media preparation failed before Twilio dispatch: Twilio MMS does not support media type constructor.
[constructor] sendSmsViaTwilio calls: 0
[__proto__] prepareSmsMediaAttempt REJECTED: PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError: SMS media preparation failed before Twilio dispatch: Twilio MMS does not support media type __proto__.
[__proto__] sendSmsViaTwilio calls: 0
[application/x-openclaw-probe] prepareSmsMediaAttempt REJECTED: ... media type application/x-openclaw-probe.
[application/x-openclaw-probe] sendSmsViaTwilio calls: 0
```

To check the serve-time gate, the harness staged `application/pdf` media through the real path, then rewrote the stored metadata `contentType`. This mimics an entry staged before the fix, which stays until its TTL expires.

```text
After:  [serve constructor] hosted GET status=415 content-type=null content-disposition=null
After:  [serve __proto__]   hosted GET status=415 content-type=null content-disposition=null
After:  [serve application/pdf] hosted GET status=200 content-type="application/pdf" content-disposition="inline; filename=\"mms-5631c3d62f.pdf\""
Before: [serve constructor] and [serve __proto__] both returned 200 with the malformed filenames above
```

Gap: this was not run against the live Twilio API or with a live Gateway. The Twilio call was recorded at the plugin's send boundary instead of being sent.

CI seconds (per-test durations reported by Vitest, summed per file from the CI job log on head `fb18b7a0f98`; module import and worker startup are not included):
- `extensions/sms/src/media.test.ts`: 110 tests, 1.21 s in `checks-node-changed-extensions-config-7` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35087824036/job/104767082384)

prs.title: fix(ui): recover when IndexedDB is unavailable on the first open
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openControlUiDatabase` checks `typeof indexedDB === "undefined"` inside the promise executor and rejects there. That rejection runs before the function caches the promise, so the cached value is an already-rejected promise — after one visit where IndexedDB was unavailable (private window, sandboxed iframe, third-party storage blocked), every later `outboxPayloadUnavailable` / draft-store call keeps failing until a full page reload, even though IndexedDB is back.

## Why This Fix

The availability check moved before the promise is constructed: the unavailable case now returns a fresh rejection without touching the cache, so the next call can open normally. The success and `request.error` paths keep their existing `release()` behavior, and the deliberate `blocked` case (which keeps its rejected promise so a queued open stays behind it) is unchanged.

## User Impact

A WebChat session that hits an unavailable IndexedDB recovers on its next attempt instead of staying broken until a reload — the outbox and draft stores open again as soon as the browser exposes IndexedDB.

## Evidence

- New `control-ui-database.runtime.test.ts`: the first call with IndexedDB unavailable rejects, a later call with IndexedDB present opens and resolves; a second case pins that one successful open is still reused. The recovery case fails against the previous code (verified by reverting only the source change).
- `ui` typecheck clean, boundary-guard lint and formatting clean.

Closes #149887

prs.title: fix(sandbox): admit docker bind targets as exec workdirs like file tools
prs.body:
Closes #149941

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `exec` rejects `workdir` under a `sandbox.docker.binds` target with `workdir "<path>" is unavailable or not a directory: command was not executed.` even though file tools read/write/list that same folder.

## User Impact

User impact: agents with an extra bind-mounted folder can run commands with `workdir` set inside it, consistent with the file tools' access to the same directory, instead of falling back to in-command `cd` on every call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exec workdir resolver still validated against a pre-#148893 mount view (workspace + read-only skill mounts) while file tools moved to the authoritative `resolveSandboxMountSelection` (binds included), so the two tool families disagreed about the same configured mount. This adds a `bindMounts` field to the exec sandbox config, populates it in `createCoreCodingTools` from `buildSandboxFsMounts` (the same selection owner the file tools' fallback admission uses), and includes those mounts in the container→host workdir mapping table. Precedence stays deterministic (longest container root wins); binds shadowed by managed/protected targets are already excluded by the selection, and missing host directories still resolve to `unavailable`.

## Evidence

Red-green regression (pre-fix code via `git stash` of the production files):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-workdir.bind-mounts.test.ts` → new tests **fail pre-fix** (`{kind:"unavailable", requestedCwd:"/data"}`), **pass after** the fix (56/56 across both exec-workdir test files).
- Sibling suites green: `core-coding-tools.exec-workdir.test.ts`, `core-coding-tools.sandbox.test.ts` (70/70), `sandbox/workspace-mounts.test.ts` + `sandbox/fs-paths.test.ts` (41 passed, 3 skipped).

Runtime probe composing the exact production chain (`createSandboxTestContext` with `docker.binds: ["/tmp/bind-probe/data:/data"]` → `buildSandboxFsMounts` → exec sandbox config → `resolveExecWorkdir`), verbatim output:

```
selected bind mounts: [{"hostPath":"/tmp/bind-probe/data","containerPath":"/data"}]
=== exec workdir=/data, pre-fix config (no bindMounts) ===
{"kind":"unavailable","requestedCwd":"/data"}
=== exec workdir=/data, fixed config (bindMounts from mount selection) ===
{"kind":"sandbox","hostCwd":"/tmp/bind-probe/data","containerCwd":"/data","scriptPreflightCwd":"/tmp/bind-probe/data"}
```

Gates: `oxfmt` clean, `run-oxlint` 0 warnings/0 errors, `pnpm tsgo` (core) exit 0, `git diff --check` clean.

Not tested: a live Docker-sandbox exec (no Docker daemon on this host); the resolver and mount-selection layers above the engine are covered by the tests and probe, and the container-side `docker exec -w` behavior for an existing bind directory is unchanged. The autoreview helper's codex engine failed with an infra error (`codex engine failed (1)`, also seen on another PR today), so the pre-submit review was manual: additive optional config field, one call-site population, one mapping-table inclusion; no public SDK surface touched (`check-plugin-sdk-api-baseline` scope untouched).



Rebased onto current `main` (`26505c528b5`, head `9929483460b`): main renamed the boolean `includeShellTools` option to the tri-state `shellTools` in `CoreCodingToolsOptions`; the bind-mount admission now gates on `shellTools !== "disabled"` (same predicate main uses for sandbox admission). The `BashSandboxWorkdirMount` export flagged by the dependency scan is module-private again (no production consumer outside `bash-tools.shared.ts`). Gates on the new head: focused suite `bash-tools.exec-workdir.bind-mounts.test.ts` 3/3, `pnpm tsgo` exit 0, `run-oxlint` 0/0 on changed files, `oxfmt` clean, `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: feat: add signed bundled Bun to Windows desktop
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adds explicit Windows x64/ARM64 bundled-Bun adoption to the Tauri desktop companion. Main supplies fresh Windows setup; this change lets an existing Node Gateway move to the signed bundled runtime through the canonical service owner. The branch consumes main's signed production Windows pins and removes the obsolete unsigned preparation entry.

## User Impact

**Windows publication remains OFF. The PR remains draft because native qualification and CI attribution are incomplete.** There is no Windows release asset, updater feed or automatic updater activation.

Passive startup, reconnect, Quit and app replacement preserve the existing Gateway's runtime and registration. Switching requires **Use bundled runtime…** and confirmation. Fresh installation and Startup adoption remain unelevated. Protected S4U adoption uses one UAC handoff while the desktop stays unelevated; cancellation and stale consent must preserve the existing Gateway.

Azure federation, Foundation signing access, the first signed x64/ARM64 fork release and generated production pins are complete. Shared release `openclaw-v1.4.3-20261010-65d94e7156-webkit-01f208ae7a-r2` admits both Windows architectures with `authenticodeSigned: true` and `testOnly: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The desktop passes confirmed observations to the canonical CLI. The existing Windows service owner controls the replacement transaction: native lock, expected runtime pin/definition, backup, stop, publish, start, readiness and guarded recovery. Startup registration stays Startup registration. Protected S4U adoption invokes the installed CLI once through `ShellExecuteExW("runas")` with `--expected-runtime-pin`; a private, same-account, nonce-bound receipt returns the result. There is no resident privileged helper or automatic migration.

The shared stager verifies archive/payload hashes and stores immutable signed runtime bytes per user. Main's pin validator, exact bigint file identities, backup matching and Windows test targets remain intact. Qualification repairs preserve effective Node heap settings and recognize equivalent native home/temporary paths without relaxing explicit-environment or foreign-profile checks.

The existing desktop release owner gains a **nonpublishing signing rehearsal**. Only protected-main `workflow_dispatch`, with source SHA equal to workflow SHA, may enter. Separate native x64/ARM64 build and signing jobs use the existing `release-signing` environment, Azure OIDC and Artifact Signing, Foundation account/profile, SHA256 and RFC3161 timestamping. They verify pinned Bun and installer identity. Outputs are three-day Actions artifacts; the rehearsal cannot reach a release, tag, feed, public asset or publication credential. Signing access and branch policy are unchanged. Existing Linux publication and historical mixed-platform recovery remain intact.

Qualification also repaired partial-setup Retry through the existing bootstrap owner, Linux handled-navigation behavior, and Windows release executables opening an extra console. Release builds now select the GUI subsystem; native CI checks the built PE header. Debug builds retain console output.

## Evidence

Current pushed head: **`76a8560ec6f4694699f606e26ae071e065b9b0a4`**. Its three-file delta from `f7602c3bba68d2cf6cfcec4065e8e72a1541e7f7` fixes the Windows release subsystem, adds a built-PE guard, and documents the behavior. Independent P2 autoreview is **scoped-clean**. The selected case in `test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` passes on Node 24 and pinned Bun (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts -t "keeps Windows rehearsal artifacts isolated from release and feed publication" --maxWorkers=1`; 19.39s / 27.22s wrapper wall time); scoped `check-changed` passes in 280.13s, with rustfmt and diff checks passing. Both actual f760 Windows artifacts were PE console-subsystem binaries, and the new guard failed against the installed x64 binary before the fix. Both current-version Windows packages are now independently verified; native console-free launch proof remains pending.

### Current-head packaged binaries

[Native run 38368593003](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38368593003) is terminal **SUCCESS, 4/4 platform jobs, attempt 1**. Both archives match their GitHub service digests and exact run/head identity. Selected 2026.10.2 apps have the correct architecture and **GUI subsystem 2**; their Bun manifests/hashes match the signed production pins and independently pass Foundation Authenticode, digest, RFC3161 timestamp, chain and CRL verification.

Both ZIPs also retain an older cached 0.1.0 app with console subsystem 3. Those byte-identical older payloads are separately identified and excluded from current-version proof. The rehearsal builds without that Cargo cache and rejects anything except one installer of its admitted version. App and NSIS files remain unsigned, unpublished CI proof artifacts. No Windows executable from this new head was run locally or on a lease; artifact inspection does not establish interactive qualification.

The matching current-head CLI package from [main run 38368686521](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38368686521), artifact `11798088528`, has verified service digest and tarball SHA256 `8b3e8fac6f097d6efd124a8bae0f4e5ce6ba2d9ad8791c72ea5af161fd3b2b0a`. Its build metadata embeds the exact 76a commit and its complete runtime pin matches source. This is metadata verification, not package execution.

### Retained native x64 proof — f760 artifacts

The last executed app and CLI are **f760**, not the new GUI-fix head. [Native build run 38356676815](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38356676815) passed all four platforms. The x64 NSIS SHA256 is `acd4663393b2f4c91ffde0dd0829452cdf2d43455e91adeb4dfca1579f23b1f6`; packaged app SHA256 is `480d2435040a390870e82f6865893c85bce3a24884ea72def8807b09649445d3`. prs.title: fix: native app messages fail after reconnecting
prs.body:
Related: #151441, #165434

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: messages from the native apps' embedded Control UI stay **Not sent** after reconnecting because the Gateway rejects their internal reconnect marker before dispatch.

## User Impact

User impact: native Mac, Linux, iOS, and Android UI clients can send again after reconnecting. Pairing, scopes, and session authorization remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded Control UI authenticates with its native app identity, but reconnect normalization recognized only the browser/terminal operator UI identities. Its marker consequently leaked into the strict public request validator, and every retry failed because the UI clears the marker only after an accepted send.

Reuse the existing native-app UI predicate, moving it to the shared client identity utility and updating the handshake imports. The allowlist and exact UI-mode comparisons are unchanged. Reconnect handling honors a strictly `true` marker for those native UI identities without widening the global operator UI class; other clients and invalid marker values still fail validation.

This isolates the native reconnect repair from the broader changes in #151441. Unlike #165434's unconditional marker removal, recognized native UI requests retain the existing reconnect-resume path.

Honoring native resumes extends the matching-session idle/daily freshness exception to native embedded UIs. A maintainer decision on that policy is still required before merge.

## Evidence

- **Inspectable base-fail/head-pass runtime capture:** [authenticated reconnect, stale-session preservation, public-client rejection, and subsequent send](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171528#issuecomment-6160352164).
- Tested head `6730dab9323fc1d1407b44c5eb12a11366735cf8`; production code is unchanged from the reviewed `bf7559ab9fab`. The identical runtime fixture fails on base `1b8cd600649` with the original unexpected-marker error and passes on this head.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server.chat-dashboard-title-rollover.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **2 passed**, 76.13 seconds wall time (native scenario 10.98 seconds). Real Gateway, token-authenticated signed clients, real WebSocket disconnect/reconnect, real agent reply pipeline, and a deterministic local HTTP/SSE model provider. No dispatch/session-initialization mocks. The fixture asserts a 48-hour-old daily-stale session preserves its ID, lifecycle revision, and start time on the marked reconnect send; authenticated public WebChat metadata is rejected; the next unmarked native send completes and follows ordinary rollover policy.
- Earlier focused request-normalization/Linux admission run: **45 passed**, 49.33 seconds wall time; the production code and those tests remain unchanged.
- Targeted Gateway-server test type check, lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and independent Codex AutoReview passed for the proof update. Core production type checking and local runtime build passed for the production fix.
- Scope: Mac-hosted full-runtime transport proof using the native Mac protocol identity. Packaged-app UI replay and live Linux/iOS/Android behavior are not claimed; all four native identities have request-boundary coverage. Captures contain only synthetic data and omit credentials, addresses, and private paths.
- Hosted CI timing/results and the maintainer policy decision remain pending. ClawSweeper re-review requested with the proof comment.

prs.title: fix(signal): status reaction targets a fractional id when the inbound timestamp is not an integer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Signal status/ack reaction is attached to a bogus message id when an inbound event carries a non-integer timestamp.

The status-reaction target resolves its id from the inbound timestamp, and the numeric branch accepted any finite positive value 鈥?so a fractional timestamp such as `1.5` was passed straight through as the reaction target instead of falling back to `unknown`.

## User Impact

Signal status reactions no longer target a fractional id when an inbound event has a non-integer timestamp; they fall back to `unknown`, exactly as they already do for other unusable timestamps. Integer timestamps behave as before 鈥?no user-visible change on the normal path.

## Why This Change Was Made

A Signal message id is a base-10 millisecond timestamp, so only a positive integer is a usable id. The status-reaction resolver had two loose paths: a numeric branch that accepted any finite positive number (`1.5` included), and a string branch that used `Number()`, which also accepts `0x10`/`1e3`/`0b101`/`0o17` spellings.

The numeric branch is tightened to `Number.isSafeInteger`, and the string branch reuses `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` 鈥?the same helper the message-action reaction path already uses at `extensions/signal/src/message-actions.ts:149` 鈥?so both Signal reaction paths agree on what a valid timestamp is.

Note on reachability: the string branch is defense-in-depth. `entry.messageId` is produced only as `String(inboundTimestamp)`, which is always canonical decimal, so the hex/exponent spellings are not reachable from the current producer. The genuinely reachable defect is the fractional **numeric** timestamp, which is what the tests target.

## Evidence

**Scope of the change:** `3 files changed`.

### 1. Real HTTP client transmit proof (added in this revision 鈥?newest layer)

The harness added in the previous revision mocks **only** `../client.js`, the signal-cli JSON-RPC
HTTP boundary. It proves the production stack *assembles* the right request, but the final
transmission is still a `vi.fn()`. This revision adds a second harness that closes that last hop:
it leaves `client.ts` **completely unmocked** and stands up a real `node:http` server, pointing
`deps.baseUrl` at it. `resolveSignalRpcContext` (`extensions/signal/src/rpc-context.ts:7,12`)
honors that override and `event-handler.ts:382` forwards `deps.baseUrl`, so the full chain runs
for real:

```
createSignalEventHandler()(receiveEvent)      real receive ingest
  -> resolveSignalStatusReactionTimestamp()   the changed function
    -> createStatusReactionController()       null target => no controller
      -> sendReactionSignal()                 real send-reactions.ts
        -> signalRpcRequest()                 real client-adapter.ts
          -> client.ts  HTTP POST /api/v1/rpc <- REAL network I/O
```

Assertions are made on the bytes the server actually received 鈥?not on a spy.

**Command**

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.status-reaction-real-client.test.ts \
  --project extension-signal
```

**Result 鈥?with the fix (current head):**

```
 鉁?transmits a valid integer reaction through the real client (positive control)
 鉁?keeps every transmitted target a safe integer across mixed traffic

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The server-side observation for the positive control is a real inbound HTTP request:

```
<- POST /api/v1/rpc
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"sendReaction",
    "params":{"emoji":"馃","targetTimestamp":1700000000002,
              "targetAuthor":"+15550002222","groupIds":["g1"]},
    "id":"18cf90be-edfd-409b-9819-d77549f985c6"}
```

The positive control is asserted **first and asserted non-empty**. This matters: an earlier
attempt to port a real server into this chain produced `expected [] to include 1700000000002`
because the control silently fired zero RPCs, which would have let the negative assertions pass
for the wrong reason. That vacuity is now guarded explicitly.

**Negative control 鈥?the same file against pre-fix `event-handler.ts`** (resolver from this PR's
base `fe7f80ddca98`, restored afterwards; the test file itself was not modified):

```
 鉁?transmits a valid integer reaction through the real client (positive control)
 脳 never transmits a fractional target through the real client
     AssertionError: expected [ 1.5, 1.5 ] to deeply equal []
 脳 keeps every transmitted target a safe integer across mixed traffic
     AssertionError: expected false to be true

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
```

Against the old code the **real HTTP client transmitted `targetTimestamp: 1.5` on the wire**,
twice. The tests therefore fail on the original defect and pass on the fix, on a transport that is
genuinely real in both runs.

### 1b. Production receive-to-transport proof (mocked HTTP boundary only)

`extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.status-reaction-real-path.test.ts` mocks only
`../client.js`; everything above it is real production code, and the assertion is made on the
assembled JSON-RPC request. With the fix:

```
 鉁?issues NO sendReaction RPC for a fractional inbound timestamp                   6749ms
 鉁?DOES issue sendReaction RPC for a canonical integer inbound timestamp           4690ms
 鉁?never sends a non-integer targetTimestamp on the reaction transport            35650ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### 2. No regression in existing coverage

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run extensions/signal/src/monitor/ \
  --project extension-signal

 Test Files  10 passed (10)
      Tests  145 passed (145)
```

### 2b. Line-cap ratchet

`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` is shrink-only and rejected an earlier revision:
`event-handler.ts: 1336 -> 1337 counted lines (cap 700)` and
`inbound-context.test.ts: 1433 -> 1470 counted lines (cap 1000)`. Both files are already far
over their caps and are grandfathered, so any growth fails. This revision folds the resolver's
two branches onto one shared validity check (bringing `event-handler.ts` to **-1 counted
lines** versus base) and moves the superseded inline receive tests out of the oversized
inbound-context file into the dedicated harness above (back to **+0**).

### 3. Static checks on the changed files

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Lint | `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <changed files>` | 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| Format | `oxfmt --check <changed files>` | All matched files use the correct format |

### Environment notes (honest gaps)

- The harness pays a cold module-transform and plugin-resolution cost that exceeds Vitest's
  default 120s timeout on a cold worker, so the new cases declare an explicit 180s timeout.
- A separate "empty set" assertion for the fractional case was implemented and then deliberately
  removed: the status-reaction controller debounces and can flush a *previous* message's reaction
  after the next case begins, which made any empty-set claim race against unrelated in-flight work
  (observed as an intermittent failure). The mixed-traffic case states the same property
  race-free 鈥?the integer target is present (proving the transport is live) and `1.5` is absent.
- The proof harness stubs `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`'s dispatch entry points. That is
  orthogonal to this change: it only stops the agent turn from blocking on workspace/agent
  roster resolution. The reaction transport 鈥?the surface under test 鈥?is entirely real.
- `## Channel note:` this is a Signal plugin path and no live Signal environment is available
  in this setup. The change is a pure parse of an already-received value, and the proof above
  exercises the real transport boundary rather than a live Signal account.

PR-first change: reported and fixed directly, with no tracking issue.

prs.title: [codex] Expire Telegram message-cache plugin state
prs.body:
## Summary
- gives Telegram prompt-context message-cache plugin-state rows a seven-day TTL
- normalizes existing no-expiry rows in a TTL-enabled namespace on the next write so upgraded `telegram.message-cache` rows can age out too
- preserves sibling namespace budgets and adds focused coverage for the Telegram message-cache persistent store options

Refs openclaw/openclaw#87332 and openclaw/openclaw#87357.

## Notes
Current `main` already contains the generic plugin-state cap fix from `e3395867507` (`fix(plugin-state): evict current namespace on plugin row cap`). This PR addresses the remaining `telegram.message-cache` permanence angle from #87332.

The follow-up commit also addresses the review concern about pre-existing `expires_at = NULL` rows. When a namespace writes with a TTL, plugin state now updates live rows in that same namespace that were previously immortal to expire at the same deadline as the write. That keeps the upgrade path bounded without touching sibling namespaces.

## Verification
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.test.ts -t 'plugin-state store|persistent'`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.test.ts -t 'default TTL|Telegram sibling|plugin row cap|plugin overflow'`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.sqlite.ts src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.test.ts`

Behavior addressed: Telegram message-cache plugin-state entries now get a TTL instead of being permanent live rows, and old no-expiry message-cache rows receive a bounded expiry after the namespace writes under the new TTL policy.
Real environment tested: local macOS source worktree at `upstream/main`.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: focused Vitest and oxfmt commands above.
Evidence after fix: Telegram message-cache tests passed for persistent/default store coverage; plugin-state tests passed for TTL normalization, sibling namespace budget, and plugin cap behavior.
Observed result after fix: default Telegram message-cache plugin state opens with namespace `telegram.message-cache`, max entries `3000`, and a seven-day default TTL; existing no-expiry rows in that namespace are assigned the new expiry deadline on the next TTL write.
What was not tested: live Telegram traffic or a production SQLite file from a real user profile.

prs.title: fix(skills): keep background reviews out of user reply hooks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Detached Skill Workshop reviews inherit the foreground user trigger, so user-only reply hooks can mistake background maintenance for a new user turn.

## User Impact

Background learning no longer starts user-only reply hooks such as Advisor. Foreground user turns remain eligible; the review's model, tools, source snapshot, and permission checks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The review is admitted as system work but reuses the foreground prompt context. Clear its inherited trigger at the producer so every hook sees the correct distinction, rather than adding session-key exclusions to individual plugins. The trigger taxonomy has no generic system-maintenance value, so this run leaves the optional trigger unset.

## Evidence

- Production experience-review regression proves a user-eligible claiming hook handles the foreground turn, then does not dispatch for the detached review through the real review forwarding and reply-hook dispatcher; review model work proceeds.
- 33 focused tests passed: experience review (9), review scheduler (12), and reply-hook boundaries (12).
- Scoped Oxfmt and Oxlint passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` passed.
- Madge import-cycle check: 0 cycles.
- Documented that background reviews are internal system work, not user turns.

prs.title: fix(gateway): expose session model selection provenance
prs.body:
Closes #149341

## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.list` reports the same model for a configured default and an explicit selection, without telling callers which source supplied it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSessionSelectedModelRef` labels its answer as `runtime`, `override`, or `configured`. The existing selection owner derives this result on reads; the row and `sessions_list` forward it.

## User Impact

The optional `modelSelectionSource` distinguishes identical values. It reports the existing resolution stage, not the model used by every execution path. Selected and active values retain their meanings. No UI display changes.

## Evidence

### Current head (2026-10-13)

The current head is `c121729b65eb6a9ee25a6f09c5f4904922161348`. It merges main
`e0bb91e1542957cbab98326753a38fa667ce4d5f` into `8396b904b78715528788fbdf2891625801f592bf`
without conflicts. The PR diff against main is unchanged (ten files, +156/-5); this
merge adds no PR code. [CI run 38352360624](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38352360624)
completed successfully for this head on 2026-10-13 at 05:50 UTC. That includes `build-artifacts`
and the shard that runs `src/gateway/session-utils.metadata-perf.test.ts`, where both
thinking cases below pass.

**Attribution of the three red checks on `8396b904b78`.** [CI run 38348089309](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38348089309)
tested `8396b904b78` merged into main `78410c7b949614e158c1be8bd8d64f5a6a0ec7a2`.
Both failures were already present on that main commit, and main fixed both shortly after it:

- **`build-artifacts`** reported `extensions/workboard/openclaw.plugin.json` as stale.
  Main regenerated exactly that file in [`faa8ad8e598`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/faa8ad8e598)
  ("fix(workboard): regenerate browser asset manifest"), whose parent is `78410c7b949`.
  This PR does not touch `extensions/workboard/`. On `8396b904b78` (base `c86edb99b3d`),
  rebuilding the Workboard Control UI reproduced the committed manifest bytes. On the
  current head, `pnpm plugins:assets:check` reports "Generated bundled plugin assets
  match the committed bytes."
- **`checks-node-changed-compact-large-19`** failed the two cases
  "preserves a stored level with a missing/identity-only catalog after warming thinking
  facts" in `src/gateway/session-utils.metadata-perf.test.ts`. This PR does not touch
  that file or the thinking-facts code. Both cases failed locally the same way on main
  `c86edb99b3d` with this PR's ten files reverted to main: `thinkingOptions` fell back to
  the default ladder, and the policy call count was 2 instead of 1. Main fixed this in
  [`7b871cd72f2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7b871cd72f2) (#170659,
  "retain thinking facts across partial catalog rows"), which also updates that test
  file. On the current head the file passes 7/7, and it passes 7/7 on main
  `e0bb91e1542` with this PR's files reverted.
- **`openclaw/ci-gate`** only aggregates the two jobs above.

No PR-caused failure was found, so this update contains no code change.

**Local validation on the current head:** all five PR test files passed (46 tests).
Lint, line ratchets, and the core typecheck were not rerun locally for this conflict-free
merge; the PR's ten files are byte-identical to `8396b904b78`, where they passed, and the
CI run above covers them on this head.

### Conflict resolution in `8396b904b78` (2026-10-13)

`8396b904b78` merged main `c86edb99b3d363c2b7e519289668f4fbab37a2c4`. Main had moved the
selection owner to prepared runtime ownership and reworked the row Golden test, so the
branch had become conflicting. These notes still describe the current code:

- **Conflict resolution keeps main's structure:** the [selection owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8396b904b78715528788fbdf2891625801f592bf/src/gateway/session-utils-model-selection.ts#L45)
  keeps main's prepared-ownership path and its new async wrapper. The sync
  resolver still labels the `runtime`, `override`, and `configured` branches,
  and the async wrapper inherits the field through its return type. The
  [row projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8396b904b78715528788fbdf2891625801f592bf/src/gateway/session-utils-row.ts#L586) keeps main's
  removal of the undefined active-model placeholders and copies
  `modelSelectionSource` as before.
- **Golden pins unchanged from main:** main now pins sorted wire values and
  asserts additive fields separately. This head follows that pattern: the
  [Golden hashes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8396b904b78715528788fbdf2891625801f592bf/src/gateway/session-utils-row.materialize.test.ts#L34)
  are main's values byte for byte, `modelSelectionSource` is excluded from the
  hashed wire fields, and a [separate assertion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8396b904b78715528788fbdf2891625801f592bf/src/gateway/session-utils-row.materialize.test.ts#L509)
  checks it for every fixture and timestamp: `override` for the three fixtures
  with a stored or inherited selection, `configured` for the other twelve
  (45 rows). The remaining wire fields still hash to main's unchanged pins, so
  the merge changes nothing else in those rows.
- **Moved test:** main removed `session-utils-model.identity.test.ts`. Its
  selection-ref case now lives in `session-utils-model.thinking-default.test.ts`,
  which expects `selectionSource: "override"` there. The registered
  `sessions.list` regression now prepares the runtime config snapshot before
  seeding entries, as main's session-store path resolution requires.
- **Local validation on this head:** all five PR test files passed (46 tests),
  plus 11 adjacent session row, projection, list, and chat-metadata suites
  (141 tests). Type-aware oxlint on the ten changed files, both line ratchets,
  the conflict-marker check, and the core typecheck (`tsconfig.core.json`)
  passed. Swift generation was not rerun; the schema file merged without
  conflict.

### Previous head and compatibility evidence (2026-10-03)

The previous head was `67faa4d505387eb8f5b655a736f01a679030039d`, which merged main
`9c32426f5c19dbef12803c9a2952c14a658a29b3`. [CI run 37044752947](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37044752947)
completed successfully for that head on 2026-10-02 at 18:17:30 UTC.

- **Read-time metadata, not stored state:** the [selection owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/67faa4d505387eb8f5b655a736f01a679030039d/src/gateway/session-utils-model-selection.ts#L30)
  labels the existing runtime, override, and configured branches. The [row projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/67faa4d505387eb8f5b655a736f01a679030039d/src/gateway/session-utils-row.ts#L567)
  copies that result into `modelSelectionSource` on reads. This PR adds no field
  to stored `SessionEntry`, no storage writer, and no database migration.
- **Old/new response contract:** [SessionRowSchema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/67faa4d505387eb8f5b655a736f01a679030039d/packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions-row.ts#L273)
  makes the field optional and retains `additionalProperties: true`. Old rows
  may omit it; existing consumers can ignore the additive field. The earlier
  compatibility proof exercised actual new rows against the prior expected
  shape, old-shaped rows against the new schema, and old/new literals against
  packed public declarations with both optional-property modes. Those are
  retained earlier proofs, not new executions on this merge head.
- **Exact merge-head Golden evidence:** the 2026-10-02 merge validation compared
  17 fixtures at three timestamps, **51/51 exact matches** against main
  `9c32426f5c19dbef12803c9a2952c14a658a29b3` after removing only
  `modelSelectionSource`. `snapshotAt` was excluded by the existing test;
  all remaining JSON bytes and property order were preserved. Only then were
  the [Golden hashes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/67faa4d505387eb8f5b655a736f01a679030039d/src/gateway/session-utils-row.materialize.test.ts#L33)
  updated. The temporary comparison instrumentation was removed and the regular
  test passed again.
- **Merge validation:** all five PR test files passed (35 tests); type-aware
  lint, both line ratchets, conflict-marker checks, Swift generation, and the
  Swift protocol check passed. Main's move of generated Swift output to
  `.build/protocol` was preserved; no generated native source remains in this
  PR's tracked diff.

The authenticated create/patch/list and three-row reopen observations below are
prior runtime evidence retained by the review. They are not a claim that the
full live scenario was rerun on either merge head. Source, Golden comparison,
targeted tests, and CI are the merge-head evidence.

### Earlier runtime and registered-handler evidence

Authenticated `sessions.create`, `sessions.patch`, and `sessions.list`: before, identical values had no source; after, configured and explicit selections have distinct markers. Reopening the same three stored session rows preserves every field and derives the markers again. No inference was requested.

The registered `sessions.list` regression also fails on main at `ece550b7c2df5a88c97ecc9a3d9938766ffdf83d` because the response omits the source. It passes with the fix, checking configured, explicit, inherited, and runtime selections with identical values, then runtime ownership removal. It calls the registered handler through `coreGatewayHandlers`; no row builder or list response is mocked.

## Compatibility

This additive response change was approved by the owner on 2026-09-16. The row schema already allows additional properties. Actual new rows pass the prior expected row shape, and old-shaped rows pass the new schema. Native protocol types were regenerated and checked. An external consumer compiled old and new row literals against packed public declarations with both optional-property modes. No storage migration, version bump, or new setting is needed.

## Consumers

Gateway clients and `sessions_list` receive the optional field. Search and placement retain their existing selection behavior.

## Invalidation

Each row derives the source from current ownership, overrides, and configuration; it is not stored independently.

## Change Size

Growth accepted under the owner's standing acceptance (2026-09-15).

At the current head, the diff against merged main is +27/-3 production lines across five files and +129/-2 test lines across five files. There is no tracked generated-native diff.

## Earlier test evidence

The earlier checked source includes main at `ece550b7c2df5a88c97ecc9a3d9938766ffdf83d`, merged in `7d385ec31b02c2e7af8b1d478529567e9e70cdce`. The earlier 310-test owner, schema, and tool result and unchanged generation/declaration proofs remain valid. Duplicate helper provenance checks were replaced with the registered handler case; identity, cache-order, context-window, and selected/active assertions remain.

Those earlier corrected suites passed 281 tests (not a new run on the current head):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read-metadata.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-utils-model.identity.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts
```

The same-value regression command is:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read-metadata.test.ts \
  -t 'sessions.list distinguishes selection sources'
```

prs.title: fix(memory): avoid owner errors for configured dreaming workspaces
prs.body:
Closes #149215

## What Problem This Solves

### Summary

Fixes an issue where dreaming workspace enumeration fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError` in an explicit multi-agent configuration when the runtime primary workspace is already present in the configured roster, but no primary agent is repeated in the call.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root Cause

`resolveMemoryDreamingWorkspaces` first collects configured workspace owners. Its final primary-workspace branch nevertheless resolves a default agent before checking whether that canonical workspace already exists. In an explicit fleet without a default owner, that unnecessary lookup throws.

### Changes

- Reuse a known canonical workspace entry when no primary agent association was requested.
- Normalize optional owner IDs before that decision, including empty/whitespace input.
- Continue adding explicitly supplied owner associations.
- Continue requiring an owner for an unknown primary workspace.
- Cover real paths, symlink aliases, nullable optional ownership, explicit associations, and unknown-workspace rejection.

## User Impact

Callers can include an already-configured runtime workspace without adding an ambient/default agent or repeating an owner the roster already records. Existing owner sets remain intact.

This is a narrow configuration-resolution repair related to #147157. It does not claim to resolve that report's separate long-running model call or fleet-wide starvation symptoms.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

Ran the supported built CLI through a small synthetic plugin that imports the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-status` API. Each run used a fresh real configuration file and five existing workspace directories, `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, no default/system agent, and no model or Gateway calls. The resolver was not mocked.

The command handler was:

```js
import { resolveMemoryDreamingWorkspaces } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-status";

api.registerCli(({ program }) => {
  program.command("workspace-proof")
    .option("--agent <id>")
    .option("--primary-owner <id>")
    .action(options => {
      const rows = resolveMemoryDreamingWorkspaces(api.config, {
        primaryWorkspaceDir: api.config.agents.entries.primary.workspace,
        primaryAgentId: options.primaryOwner,
      });
      console.log({
        workspaceCount: rows.length,
        owners: rows.flatMap(row => row.agentIds).sort(),
      });
    });
}, { commands: ["workspace-proof"] });
```

Invocation: `pnpm openclaw workspace-proof --agent primary`.

| Source | Public SDK call | Observed result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main `ca7c90068054dae7378d9d3bef42f11823bc1212` | Roster-only control | Exit 0, five workspaces and the five configured owners |
| Same main | Already-configured primary workspace | Handler entered; `AgentSelectionRequiredError`; exit 1 |
| Intermediate fix `21f5d8196b5eb3c47562c79848a78f7197f756cd` | Whitespace-only primary owner | Handler entered; `AgentSelectionRequiredError`; exit 1 |
| Final repaired tree, committed as `45398ad44ce03a2bca697b6f5f479d0e75895898` | Same primary workspace call, owner omitted or whitespace-only | Both exit 0, five workspaces and unchanged owners |

Repaired CLI output:

```text
CLI_WORKSPACE_ENTERED
CLI_WORKSPACE_PROOF {"workspaceCount":5,"owners":["editor","ops","primary","research","reviewer"]}
CLI_PROOF_EXIT 0
```

The `--agent` option selects the CLI/plugin context; the fixture deliberately does not repeat that option as `primaryAgentId` in the SDK call. The configuration itself already owns the selected workspace.

### Test

- Red-first owner regression failed on the original implementation with `AgentSelectionRequiredError`.
- After merging current `main` (which removed lower-value cases from this file in #159120 and conflicted only on an adjacent test name): `pnpm test src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.test.ts` passed 15 tests.
- Changed test file cost: `pnpm test src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` reports 1.24 s in Vitest for 15 tests (tests 7%), or 6.9 s wall including pnpm and worker startup.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` passed on the earlier merged head. The current head `49378d9` merges current `main` again to pick up the Bun plugin retention fixture deflake (#160200) behind the last CI failure. On it, `pnpm test src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.test.ts` passes 15 tests and `pnpm tsgo:core` plus oxlint on the changed files pass; `check-changed` now stops at the env-var budget ratchet because current `main` itself is over budget (`OPENCLAW_*` 484 > 483 since `670415932ee`).
- `pnpm build`: passed before and after the repair.
- Formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent Codex review through P2: no accepted/actionable findings.
- The first native Codex review found the normalized-empty ID gap; it was reproduced in both the regression and built CLI, fixed using the existing normalizer, and the staged final tree passed a fresh P2 review.
- Final `codex review --base origin/main`: `findings: []`, `patch is correct`, exit 0.

## Risk

- Ownership/compatibility: no new owner is inferred for an existing workspace. An explicit primary owner still adds its association; an unowned primary workspace in an explicit fleet still fails closed.
- Canonical paths: symlink aliases are checked against the same workspace identity used to build the roster map.
- No schema, storage-format, protocol, configuration-option, or model-inference changes.

## CI history and recovery

CI on the current head `49378d9`: `openclaw/ci-gate` fails only on two UI e2e shards, both outside this diff: `ui/src/e2e/chat-user-avatar-alignment.e2e.test.ts` and `ui/src/e2e/model-catalog-partial-refresh.e2e.test.ts`. The same tests also failed in 5 and 3, respectively, of 18 other PR CI runs sampled between 09:35 and 22:07 UTC on 2026-09-28. The history below covers earlier heads.

The first non-draft CI run is **not green**: [34996372730](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34996372730) finished with 145 successful jobs, 17 skipped jobs, and five failed tooling shards plus the aggregate gate.

The failed files are `pr-main-refresh.test.ts`, `pr-operation-lock.test.ts`, `pr-merge-hosted.test.ts`, `pr-cross-checkout.test.ts`, and `pr-crabbox-merge-bypass.test.ts` under `test/scripts`. They fail on unhandled repository metadata queries such as:

```text
Unexpected GitHub operation: api --hostname github.com repos/fixture/repo -H Cache-Control: max-age=0
```

The CI merge checkout included main `0a64ea33db7ac4e060c9c9b4d9bd7b0a53d86a83`. That base contains #149230 (`7e8a52c3f76`), which changed `scripts/pr-lib/merge-outcome.sh` to request the authoritative repository identity and changed the locator JSON request. The surrounding test fixtures do not handle those calls. These tooling files are outside this PR's two-file diff.

I reproduced the same six `pr-cross-checkout` failures on a separate, unchanged latest-main checkout at `7bc9893a0818426f07c32293cc03ba81cb33df73`:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/pr-cross-checkout.test.ts
# 6 failed | 4 passed; same Unexpected GitHub operation error
```

This is an observed main-baseline failure, not a flake claim or a green CI claim. No unrelated fixture edits, skipped tests, or relaxed checks have been added to this repair.

Upstream #149294 (`7dc8a1e79659afb833df4bbfe363744c8d775e5c`) repaired those fixtures. On clean main `40e6f12380e306c92c47e96f3d0caa8fe94fb825`, all five previously failing files now pass: **279 passed, 1 skipped**. This PR was rebased onto that verified main at `c6e53e4137135ab95b10de1827547b7da1b9343b`.

Both repair commits are patch-identical according to `git range-diff`, and both changed files are byte-identical to reviewed head `45398ad44ce03a2bca697b6f5f479d0e75895898`. The existing real CLI evidence therefore describes unchanged repair code. The rebased dreaming suite passes **21 tests**.

The new exact-head run [35007354698](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35007354698) finished with **147 successful jobs, 17 skipped jobs, and three installation failures plus the aggregate gate**. The three jobs failed before tests while `@matrix-org/matrix-sdk-crypto-nodejs` downloaded its native artifact:

```text
Download Failed Error: Response status was 500
ReferenceError: err is not defined
Error: ERR_PNPM_EXECUTOR_LIFECYCLE_SCRIPT_FAILED
```

Affected jobs: `checks-node-compact-large-20`, `checks-node-compact-large-27`, and `checks-node-changed-extensions-config-2`. A failed-job-only rerun was requested with `gh run rerun ... --failed`, but GitHub rejected it with `Must have admin rights to Repository.` No second attempt started. This run remains red pending a maintainer-authorized retry; no dependency overrides or test suppression were added.

## Changelog

Release-note context: dreaming no longer rejects a runtime primary workspace whose configured owners are already known. No release-owned changelog file was edited.

## Notes

AI-assisted: yes. Fully tested for the workspace-resolution and built-CLI surface described above; no live dreaming/model run is claimed.

prs.title: refactor(ui): simplify structured config drafts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Structured config drafts still crossed a Lit compatibility bridge even though their config-form and plugin-settings callers both render with Solid. The boolean editor also expressed four mutually exclusive layouts as nested fallbacks.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Drafts remain local until valid, rejected saves retain their values and error message, and host tags, caller-specific classes, controls, and lazy loading stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Render structured drafts directly in their Solid owner, remove the optional legacy renderer/bridge contract, and cut over both callers together. Keep the existing identity-based reset behavior and validation owner. Use one `Switch` for the boolean layouts, preserving their precedence.

Production LOC across the five changed production files: **1,060 → 1,007 (−53)**. No dependencies added.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Config array draft + rejection browser files | 17 passed; 7.69s total |
| Plugin settings browser file | 19 existing tests passed; new test's alert selector corrected |
| New plugin draft regression, targeted rerun | Passed; 22.07s command, 93ms test |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| Targeted lint / formatting | Passed (the final type alias recheck is clean) |
| Production Knip | Same existing unused `ui/src/components/web-awesome-tabs.ts` on both head and merge base `72ccf6ff9293`; no new findings |
| Independent Codex review | Clean; no actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Same-run CI base/head builds and performance check | Passed; head startup **348,391 B gzip**, **1 CSS request**; CSS **49,703 → 49,703 B** |

The new plugin regression covers partial required input, an unrelated model refresh, and a rejected atomic save. The existing form proofs retain coverage for nested draft identity, row removal, validation, and rejected writes. The first plugin run selected an empty hidden field-validation alert; the corrected selector targets the draft's visible rejection message.

No screenshot comparison is needed for this internal rendering cleanup: the rendered host tags/classes and visible controls are preserved. No startup modules or lazy imports changed. CI built the base and head with the same runner/toolchain and passed the strict performance check; head startup JS is 348,391 B gzip against the 374,285 B committed budget, with 1 startup CSS request. Chat/New route boot gzip changed by only +28/+29 B. Full UI CI was selected because the config renderer is shared.

### CI attribution

The only UI E2E failure in the completed PR run is `Control UI plugin lifecycle > retains uninstall feedback through during inspection` in [PR run 38505869555](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38505869555/job/115663550631). The same test failed in the latest completed scheduled [main run 38502084044](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502084044/job/115651277712). The newest scheduled [main run 38507129576](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38507129576/job/115667390436) also fails the exact same test, with the uninstall notice missing the configuration-reload error. The test and its uninstall controller have identical blobs in the CI baseline and tested PR merge. All other PR CI jobs passed or were skipped.

prs.title: fix: /tools verbose advertises automations scope the turn cannot execute
prs.body:
Related: #142663

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/tools verbose` shows the full Automations action set (including `add`) during a management-only turn, whose runtime tool only accepts `list`, `get`, `update`, `run`, and `remove`, so discovery and execution disagree about what the turn can do.

## User Impact

User impact: In a restricted management-only turn, `/tools verbose` now describes exactly the actions that turn can execute. Execution authorization is unchanged.

This covers the verified discovery mismatch only. The issue also reports a Telegram `add` rejection; that path is not reproduced or claimed fixed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron tool chose its description and schema from the bound management grant. Inventory construction (`/tools`, `tools.effective`) has no run id, so it fell back to the unrestricted description. The change splits read-only admission metadata from exact-run execution grants:

- `resolveCronToolManagementMode` resolves the admitted management scope (entitlement, liveness, run id) without requiring the execution grant.
- `bindCronManagementGrant` keeps its full exact-run authority checks, including the live `approvalAuthority` and operational instance match.
- The description, display summary, and schema all derive from the same resolved mode, so discovery and runtime stay consistent.

A no-run-id inventory outside an admitted turn still reports the configuration surface rather than promising per-turn authority.

## Evidence

- Real command-handler regression: `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.management.test.ts` exercises `handleToolsCommand("/tools verbose", ...)` inside a management-only admitted turn. It fails before the fix (full description with `add job`) and passes after, and asserts the discovered parameters equal the runtime tool's parameters.
- Grant-isolation coverage: `src/agents/cron-creator-authority-context.test.ts` confirms metadata resolves without the execution grant while `bindCronManagementGrant` stays undefined without caller identity, and that a foreign run id resolves nothing.
- Focused tests (418 total, 3 shards): `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.management.test.ts`, `src/agents/cron-creator-authority-context.test.ts`, `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`.
- `pnpm build` and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base <upstream main> -- <changed files>` on the exact commit.
- Independent `autoreview` (pi engine, P2): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

Not covered: the reported Telegram `add` rejection. The supplied arguments there also lack a schedule, so a successful creation is not established by this change.
