prs.title: fix(agents): tool-heavy turns stop after rejected tool calls
prs.body:
Related: #147040, #135111
Follow-up to #142176

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: terminal-confirmed Responses turns stop after a rejected tool call even though their earlier tool work has already finished.

## User Impact

For terminal-confirmed Responses rejections, the agent can continue from recorded results instead of abandoning completed work or replaying the original task. Refusals, cancellation, pending approvals, asynchronous work, and intentionally terminated turns stop this recovery. No configuration or migration is required. This avoids automatic replay of the original task; it does not make arbitrary tools idempotent or prevent the model from choosing an action again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Continue through the existing transcript owner only when the previous tool batch is proven settled, including recorded tool failures and prior visible progress. Recognize malformed-call rejections and structured `incomplete_tool_call` evidence from completed Responses output; keep output-limit and EOF recovery separate.

This refresh resolves conflicts with current main and uses the existing provider retry budget rather than adding a second counter or retry loop. Parsing remains strict, and rejected partial arguments never execute.

**Coverage is intentionally conservative:** this new post-effect continuation requires positive, coherent producer-recorded terminal facts before every malformed-code or legacy-text shortcut. Replay-safe attempts retain their existing retry policy, including when visible text makes that policy decline a retry. Early malformed item completions without terminal facts stop rather than guessing what an unread response would say. Providers/cadences without this terminal contract do not qualify. #149071 has now landed on main. This refresh preserves that canonical drain rather than copying or stacking its implementation: an early malformed item completion may recover only when the drain actually records coherent terminal facts. EOF or unsafe later facts still stop.

Both reported terminal-coherence gaps are repaired. The existing output tracker records bounded refusal, provider-error, and incomplete-detail facts before validation can throw, including refusal events observed while draining rejected output. Terminal status, canonical stop, and these facts take precedence over malformed-call codes and legacy rejection text. Failed, cancelled, refused, nonterminal, unknown, and contradictory terminal facts cannot authorize this continuation. No raw refusal or provider-error payload is copied into the new diagnostics. Omitted wire status remains compatible only through an explicit producer-recorded `absent` value; missing diagnostic metadata is not treated as that compatibility case.

Original implementation by @lraesly; the original contributor commit is preserved. Cleanup and additional regression coverage are co-authored with Dallin Romney.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/bc8ef321-823d-43cc-b6a5-1b4007712b09)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/34d86ce2-2c0a-4a5c-83cf-082c15f8faf0)

## Evidence

**September 29 conflict repair:** incorporated main after #149071 landed and this PR became conflicting. Current-head review is complete, but CI has two failed test groups under investigation. This is not RFR; no merge or auto-merge is requested.

- **Head/tree:** `07f3cfe72d05cf89a6e9fb38e79b554c97b3f980` / `4f5889456300c1ce501411910c7ceb501106ead4`, incorporating main `9b5b439dcb6e11b929c982d9b40e8ddcb4c9b2e5`. The signed merge preserves published `e980b8c1` and original contributor `b14f3008` ancestry. Both requested coauthors parse on this new commit; the separate historical trailer-metadata question is unchanged.
- **Conflict resolution:** retained both the bounded terminal-coherence tests and main's expanded rejection/ending fencing matrix. The canonical drain implementation is byte-identical to main. No new retry owner or relaxed safety condition was added.
- **Focused proof:** 113 transport tests and 218 recovery/controller tests passed locally. All 15 actual loopback cases passed in the configured clean Blacksmith environment; local loopback failures were traced to the host egress proxy, with no proxy or assertion changes.
- **Fresh Gateway composition proof:** one real Gateway/Responses HTTP/file-tool test passed all **11 scenarios**: two coherent positives continued with four requests; nine refusal/error/status/EOF negatives stopped after three. Every scenario preserved the single write and failed read without executing the rejected edit or repeating the write. Positives required exactly one `tool_call_rejection` retry and preserved the original prompt/results; negatives required none. The added actual HTTP EOF case supplies no terminal facts. Test body **22.079s**; build-backed E2E lane **512.49s**.
- **Source-bound execution:** [Blacksmith backing run 36514790813](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36514790813), sealed carrier `655b77b90547c08f9a1fc759952b85882b9fb027`, exact tree above, input checks before/after, delegated command exit **0**, settled/stopped lease. The backing workflow can be cancelled by one-shot cleanup: this is a delegated-command receipt, not green workflow CI. Complete stdout, timing, manifest and lease receipts are retained in the implementation session. No live-provider inference is claimed.
- **Checks/review:** the supported staged, pinned-main changed-check plan reached clean final lint, including types and guards. Its quiet-success contract was inspected after the native process receipt expired; final lint was narrowly reconfirmed with exit 0, without repeating the full plan. Independent AutoReview returned no actionable P0–P2 findings. [Exact-head ClawSweeper R16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147611#issuecomment-5657488597) rates overall/patch platinum 4/6 and proof diamond 5/6, with no actionable or security findings. Sweeper did not execute the proof and could not independently inspect the backing receipt.

**Current CI failures:** [collector settlement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36516569050/job/109240425657) lacks the expected collector-completion record after terminal execution; [Gateway deletion lifecycle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36516569050/job/109240425514) has three SQLite pathname/active-owner errors. Both were observed on tested merge `a7b25b83719f` (base `59490dc752778` + this head). Cause and attribution remain unresolved: unchanged files do not establish a main-baseline failure or permit a waiver. #160838 is already present in that composition, so it is not treated as an absent fix. Exact-plan replay and owner analysis are in progress; no GitHub CI rerun or cancellation has been requested.

<details>
<summary>Retained earlier evidence and limits</summary>

September 25 head `e980b8c1` had green required CI/security gates and ClawSweeper platinum overall/patch with diamond proof. Those are prior-head results, not current-head admission. Earlier exact-merge and corrected-composition replays each passed 4,456 tests/327 files: [original merge replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36098563678), [corrected composition](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36099165775). The historical Discord third-preflight failure was not reproduced or conclusively attributed; #155965 independently corrected fixture ordering while preserving security assertions. No original GitHub CI cancellation/rerun or baseline waiver was used.

The earlier September 29 retry-policy composition on pinned main `da0b5812` supplied 331 existing passes at retained summary/tally granularity plus 31 corrected custom passes with direct command receipts. This refresh has separate fresh Gateway proof; older results are not relabeled as latest-main execution. Budget exhaustion and unsettled/async/approval/replay-safe controls remain covered by focused recovery-owner tests, not an inflated Gateway matrix.

</details>

prs.title: fix: recover frozen Gateway startup through gateway stop
prs.body:
Fixes #171513

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway frozen before binding its listener can hold state ownership indefinitely while its worker keeps the heartbeat fresh. On Windows, stop then tells the user to leave the unpublished owner running, so subsequent starts have no recovery path.

## User Impact

After five minutes without a listener-bound readiness fact, `openclaw gateway stop` can terminate the exact recorded startup holder and verify process exit plus state ownership release. Contention names the PID, startup phase, elapsed time, and exact stop command. PID reuse or changed ownership is refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical state lock records the starting phase and acquisition timestamp; the existing owner lease records the listener-bound timestamp. The HTTP transport publishes that fact at bind, independently of worker renewal. Its payload mutation stays in the existing lease-store boot primitive and startup checkpoint transaction; the immutable lock bytes are never rewritten. Recording failure warns while current physical custody remains valid.

Managed stops and the unmanaged fallback share recovery; Scheduled Task stop can use the canonical holder even before lease publication. Existing published legacy leases keep their established stop path. There are no new schema, dependency, configuration, or CLI options.

Net production growth is **+211 LOC**, exceeding the requested +60 target. The extra code preserves immutable lock custody, publishes readiness through the existing lease owner, shares exact-incarnation validation across stop paths, and supplies bounded POSIX escalation plus confirmed exit/custody release. Tests add **172 LOC**; docs add **8 LOC**. Collapsing this into heartbeat staleness or unverified PID termination would lose the required safety contract.

## Evidence

- Baseline contender regression failed against the original lock implementation: the error omitted the startup age and stop command. The Scheduled Task regression failed against the original stop implementation with `Gateway lifecycle ownership is held without a published identity; leave it running and retry after startup finishes.`
- Focused proof: **46 tests passed** across Gateway owner leases, real process recovery, and Scheduled Task owner publication. A fresh worker heartbeat does not defeat recovery; a recycled process start time is refused; forced termination leaves an unrelated live child untouched and permits new state ownership.
- Additional proof: **26 tests passed** across state lease acquisition/diagnostics and Gateway transport/boot identity before the disk cutoff. Windows control is exercised with synthetic native-command fixtures on macOS; native Windows execution remains CI proof.
- Final core lint, formatting, targeted services typecheck, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. Two isolated Codex P0/P1 reviews reported no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix: delivery queue update no longer resurrects terminalized rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a race where a delivery queue entry that was terminalized (dead-lettered or completed) concurrently could be silently resurrected back to `pending` by an update. The entry was read as pending, then a concurrent writer moved it to `failed`/`completed` — or deleted it when no retention fence was authored — between the read and the write, and the blind overwrite wrote the stale payload back over the terminal state. This re-enqueues already-settled deliveries for retry and can drop terminal outcomes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`updateDeliveryQueueEntryInDatabase` (src/infra/delivery-queue-sqlite.kernel.ts) previously did a read-modify-write: it loaded the pending row, applied the transform, then issued a blind `upsert` with no `updatePendingOnly` guard. The `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` therefore rewrote every column unconditionally.

The fix now performs an **update-only pending write**: the pending upsert mode mutates only a row that is still `pending` at write time, and fails closed with the existing `ENOENT` contract when the row is no longer pending — whether it was retained as a terminal `failed` row or **deleted outright** when no retention fence was authored. This matches the pattern already used by `reserveDeliveryQueueEntryAttemptInDatabase` and the platform-send transitions, and closes the remaining deletion-to-insertion path that an upsert's `INSERT` fallback previously resurrected.

## User Impact

Operators no longer risk dead-lettered or acknowledged deliveries being revived as pending and retried after the terminal state was recorded. Delivery queue state transitions are atomic with respect to concurrent recovery and settlement, for both retained terminal outcomes and deleted (no-retention) terminal rows.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `src/infra/delivery-queue-sqlite-atomicity.test.ts` cover both independently committed outcomes through a concurrent writer on its own physical connection, interleaved between the update's pending read and its write:
  - `fails closed when a concurrent retained terminalize lands inside the update window`: the row is dead-lettered (retained) on a separate committed connection between the read and the write; the update throws `ENOENT`, the committed `failed` status survives, and pending reads return null.
  - `fails closed when a concurrent deleting terminalize lands inside the update window`: without a retention fence the concurrent settlement deletes the row; the pending-mode write fails instead of `INSERT`ing the stale row, throwing `ENOENT`, and the deleted row is not resurrected as pending.
- `delivery-queue-sqlite-atomicity.test.ts`: 2/2 pass.
- `delivery-queue-sqlite.test.ts` + `delivery-queue-sqlite-claim.test.ts` + `delivery-queue-terminal.test.ts`: 59/59 pass.
- `session-delivery-queue.storage.test.ts` + `outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts`: 24/24 pass.
- `outbound/delivery-queue.producer-recovery.test.ts`: 10/10 pass.
- oxfmt, oxlint, and `tsgo` (core) clean on the changed files.

## Review feedback addressed

- **P2 — prevent the update from inserting a deleted terminal row:** resolved. The pending upsert mode is now update-only (a real `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'pending'`, no `INSERT` fallback), so a terminalize that deleted the row cannot be resurrected by a stale insert. Covered by the `deleting terminalize` regression above.
- **Low-value sequential tests consolidated:** per review, the two sequential settlement-before-update cases (which rejected at the pre-existing pending read and passed without this fix) were removed; the independently committed read/write-window regression is retained and extended to the deletion case.
- **Test owner routing:** the real-caller test that required the main-thread host broker was removed with the sequential cases, so the infra-owner routing entry in `vitest.unit-fast-paths.mjs` was reverted; the atomicity file now runs in the unit-fast lane and passes there.

Fixes #169161

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: serialized tool-call syntax appears briefly in replies when a provider splits a stream inside a function or Harmony marker.

## User Impact

The covered marker splits now produce the same visible text as one-chunk delivery. Literal text, reasoning order, content indexes, terminal snapshots, and the existing request-scoped tool allowlist remain intact. No configuration or prompt changes are required.

Pre-existing limitation: arbitrary malformed false-prefix/cumulative-snapshot replay and the disclosed two-space indentation case are not claimed to be universally chunk invariant. No live Telegram send/receive proof is claimed. ClawSweeper accepts the macOS SSE/Gateway evidence for this unchanged transport path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep unfinished candidate tails buffered until the existing grammar can decide them. The contributor's replay accounting preserves each content block's offset and interleaves retained reasoning when a decided prefix is replayed. The existing oversized-payload suppression state machine is extracted into a sibling module so the coordinator does not grow past the current line-cap ratchet; its byte bound and behavior are unchanged.

Thanks @JasonBuildAI for the original repair and regression cases. All contributor commits are preserved, followed by a merge from current main and the focused extraction/test follow-up.

## Evidence

macOS arm64, isolated state/config/workspace, loopback fixture and Gateway only; shared Ollama models were left loaded.

- Current-main baseline `976cc974fab1912c696d1101bd17a1abf05eb77e`: real OpenAI-compatible SSE transport through the production agent wrapper emits no visible text for an unsplit call sequence, but leaks the second call for splits inside `<function=`, `<|channel|>`, and `<|channel|>comm`. Terminal messages agree on two parsed `read` calls. Through a real isolated Gateway, the split function appears in an assistant event before a later replacement clears it; the durable transcript retains the two parsed calls. The empty second call is rejected for missing arguments, rather than executing another action.
- Baseline regressions: 12 failed / 53 passed on main using the contributor test file (61.48 s command wall time). After merging main, 67 focused tests pass: 58 normalizer cases plus 9 production-wrapper buffering/adjacency cases (170.21 s command wall; 5.34 s normalizer file, 137.31 s wrapper files dominated by cold transformation; individual wrapper tests 3–6 ms). Added coverage checks every split inside both opening markers and explicit expected visible text for cumulative snapshots.
- Exhaustive opening-marker split probe: baseline leaks at 9/14 function positions and 17/20 Harmony positions; this head leaks at 0/14 and 0/20.
- Independent Codex review of `6caf20c659cac6efa86f143912f2b5ae44167913`: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- A real Ollama `qwen3:4b` turn through the Gateway returned a complete sentence without tools in 46.19 s on the baseline. This is inference control; scripted SSE establishes the malformed-byte regression.

Runtime proof (`6caf20c659cac6efa86f143912f2b5ae44167913`; unchanged at final head `b593f059b977ecb0aeb3b97f7edc40555734406d`):

- The real compatible transport emits no marker text for all three split shapes. With reasoning enabled, the wire replay preserves `[read]` → thinking `checking` → newline in arrival order, with the same terminal content.
- A built, isolated Gateway emits only `Fixture complete.` for unsplit (8.990 s), split function (4.719 s), split channel (0.473 s), and split commentary (0.637 s); all retain two parsed read calls in history. The replay control retains `[read]` without leaking the incomplete function (0.402 s). A real Ollama `qwen3:4b` turn completes through that Gateway in 22.295 s with no tools. These timings include RPC/history work and are not performance comparisons.
- `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build` passed in 8m24.6s, including bundled-plugin, CLI import, and runtime postbuild checks. The full declaration-bundle attempt was intentionally stopped during its slow shared-package phase; standalone `pnpm tsgo:core` and a scoped test typecheck both pass.
- Scoped type-aware lint and formatting pass. Max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-export, config-docs, and plugin-inventory ratchets pass without baseline changes.
- Initial exact-head CI [38504961005](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38504961005) found the new suppression helper missing from the archived PR-wrapper inventory. The follow-up registers that file. The contributor independently added the identical inventory fix in `b593f059b977ecb0aeb3b97f7edc40555734406d`, which is retained. Its Git tree matches the locally tested correction exactly. Both failing eager-import-closure tests pass (2/2 selected; 46.95 s command wall, 37.08 s Vitest duration). This follow-up changes only inventory metadata, so the runtime proof above is reused. ClawSweeper’s review of `6caf20c` accepts the Mac SSE/Gateway proof and identifies only this inventory omission; that finding is repaired by the retained contributor commit. Corrected-head [CI 38507202210](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38507202210) passes, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. ClawSweeper reviewed exact head `b593f059b977ecb0aeb3b97f7edc40555734406d`: ready for maintainer review, zero findings, no before-merge items. No earlier-head green result is reused.

- Independent Codex review of final head `b593f059b977ecb0aeb3b97f7edc40555734406d`: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Dreaming admits assistant scratch notes such as `Need commit PR.` and `Now inspect.` as durable session-corpus candidates.

The shared session scanner rejects whole-body assistant chatter before candidate construction, leaving generic transcript export and existing admission/provenance controls unchanged.

This preserves the focused approach from #80666 and #111922 by @ArthurNie, including @vincentkoc's durable-signal boundary refinement. The October 13 update merges current main and resolves the scanner conflict without expanding the three-file contribution.

## User Impact

User impact: Dreaming and session backfill exclude narrowly defined assistant process notes while retaining user text and assistant evidence containing PR numbers, commit SHAs, or results. Previously ingested memory is not rewritten.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `dc71f9a026c25135b26e068ad3fd78af4d3f15c2` (merged main `983f4a3bdbf7`). Fresh main `7c1b789ca5b` has no intervening changes to memory-core or the applicable contribution policy; the candidate merges cleanly. prs.title: fix(ai): turns fail without compaction when Hugging Face TGI rejects an over-long prompt
prs.body:
Related: #158159, #167878

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a turn fails without compacting when Hugging Face TGI rejects an over-long input with `Input validation error`.

## User Impact

TGI input-length and combined input/output-token rejections enter the existing context-overflow recovery path. An output-only `max_new_tokens` validation failure remains a request error. Output budgets, configuration contracts, and stored data are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical AI overflow matcher lacked TGI's two exact validation messages. This preserves @amittell's four-line repair in the assistant and strict failover scopes, merges current main into the contributor branch without rewriting its history, and keeps main's later request-budget fixes and test cleanup.

The classifier corpus now runs a representative subset, so the new TGI rows are explicitly selected. Regression coverage includes the output-only exclusion. The compaction documentation names the supported messages.

Production: +4/-0 lines; tests and test support: +36/-0; docs: +1/-0. The production additions extend two existing scopes; removing unrelated provider clauses just to offset them would weaken supported behavior.

## Evidence

Fresh macOS Apple Silicon proof uses an isolated Gateway and task-owned HTTP/SSE proxy in front of Ollama `qwen2.5:7b`. The fixture counts serialized message characters / 4 (rounded up), enforces a lower server cap, and emits TGI's exact HTTP-200 SSE error shape with `http_status_code: 422`. Accepted requests go to the real local model. No operator Gateway or shared model was stopped.

Baseline main `976cc974fab1912c696d1101bd17a1abf05eb77e`: OpenClaw admits the final request (`route=fits`, estimate 13,061; configured context 131,072). The proxy rejects 12,657 synthetic input units against a 9,000-unit cap. Four identical requests are rejected; no compaction runs; the CLI returns an empty error result (exit 1, 13.51 seconds).

On head `50bac1ed6e81b53eac34d5089de9e50e1f3bc886`, the same input-cap scenario rejects 12,752 synthetic input units once, invokes overflow compaction, summarizes through real Ollama at 8,384 units, and retries at 5,019 units below the 9,000-unit cap. The CLI delivers `LOCAL_RECOVERY_OK`, records one compaction, and exits 0 (53.46 seconds; summary inference 6.793 seconds, retried inference 3.378 seconds).

```text
TGI SSE: Input validation error: `inputs` must have less than 9000 tokens. Given: 12752
context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for tgi/qwen2.5:7b
auto-compaction succeeded for tgi/qwen2.5:7b; retrying prompt
proxy: retry input=5019 < server_cap=9000 -> real Ollama
CLI: LOCAL_RECOVERY_OK; lastTurnCompactions=1; stopReason=stop; exit=0
```

The total-token control also succeeds: `12,746 inputs + 1,024 max_new_tokens > 13,000` produces the exact TGI total-budget error, then a real Ollama summary (`8,377 + 4,096 <= 13,000`) and retry (`4,998 + 1,024 <= 13,000`) deliver `LOCAL_RECOVERY_OK`. One compaction, exit 0, 29.44 seconds; summary and retry inference took 5.175 and 1.942 seconds.

The output-only negative control, on the already-compacted session, returns exactly ``Input validation error: `max_new_tokens` must be <= 512. Given: 1024``. It remains a request error, retries without shrinking the 5,071-unit prompt, performs no compaction, and exits 1 as expected (27.32 seconds).

The proof config disables proactive compaction and memory flushing and uses `keepRecentTokens: 1024` to isolate provider-error recovery. Native TGI tokenization, GPU TGI, Linux, and Windows are not covered; this is exact-wire Gateway boundary proof plus live Ollama inference.

Regressions fail with main's original matcher: both new assistant cases return false, and both classifier cases return `reason: format` instead of `context_overflow`. The output-only controls pass. With the fix:

| Focused suite | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AI overflow | 11/11 | 15.84 s |
| Failover classification | 57/57 | 10.70 s |
| OpenAI-compatible request budgets | 33/33 | 9.98 s |
| Existing context-overflow policies | 5/5 | 114.66 s |

The last suite is import-bound (94.31 seconds inside Vitest); the new AI and classifier files took 2.72 and 5.67 seconds inside Vitest. CI seconds are pending.

`pnpm build qaRuntime` passed (4m 51s). Core and package-test type checks, scoped oxlint, formatting, docs MDX sanity, max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, database-worker/dialect, timeout-race, mock-export, config-doc, and plugin-inventory checks passed. The gateway-only setup needed the already-declared `@openclaw/solid-lint` workspace installed before scoped lint could run; no dependency or lockfile was changed.

Independent Codex review: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The review and size-ratchet rechecks use incorporated main `711a46bcdf649cdf872ae560cc5a4f76064ec1d2`; the relevant AI/recovery/classifier owners are unchanged from the baseline proof. Earlier budgeting work is already covered by #167878 and #168326 and is outside this patch.

Maintainer action before merge: the enforced Security Review flags `failover-classification.auth-format.cases.ts` via its credential-path glob and requires a fresh `/allow-security-sensitive-change` approval for this head. This file change is the output-only TGI negative fixture; no production credential code changed.

`openclaw channels login` and `openclaw channels logout` could persist the entire global plugin auto-enable result while resolving a channel. An unrelated model-derived Codex activation could therefore be written to `openclaw.json` even though the user only requested channel authentication.

Channel auth now gives plugin resolution the validated authored source config and commits only genuine install-on-demand config changes. Omitted-channel discovery still uses the active runtime's auto-enabled view, but that view is no longer treated as authored config.

## User Impact

Logging a channel in or out no longer enables unrelated bundled plugins or rewrites configuration solely because global auto-enable found a candidate. Channel inference, runtime-resolved account values, and install-on-demand writes continue to work.

## Evidence

- The revised regression failed in four expected assertions on the original production code: explicit auth invoked global auto-enable, omitted-channel auth invoked it twice, and the Codex-bearing view reached the write/runtime path.

- Fresh Claude autoreview and independent exact-head Claude review found no actionable issue.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The startup stylesheet still shipped the old sidebar brand row and page-header controls after the rail migration removed their consumers.

## User Impact

Startup CSS is 331 B gzip smaller with the same single stylesheet request. Current sidebar appearance and interactions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove only selectors verified absent from production consumers. Keep shared icon rules used by the current rail, footer, and attention panel. No route, tag, class, lazy import, or budget changes.

Production CSS: **4,893 → 4,756 lines (−137)**.

## Evidence

Same-machine builds against merge base `120e515260d7`:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup CSS gzip | 49,703 B | 49,372 B |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 |
| Startup JS gzip | 348,650 B | 348,655 B |
| Startup JS raw | 1,059,829 B | 1,059,829 B |

The 5 B JS difference is compressed build-metadata variation; raw JS is identical. Both strict performance checks pass. CSS remains above the 46,080 B advisory target; the remaining Web Awesome theme layers contribute roughly 6.3 KB gzip in an offline attribution and are owned by the ongoing removal lane.

- `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed.
- Targeted stylesheet lint passed.
- Dense-label performance tests passed (6 tests): unseen labels do no geometry/style reads; unchanged refreshes across 100 labels do no measurements; measurements precede writes.
- Independent Codex review finished with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The source audit and zero-pixel browser comparisons verify the removed selectors are retired.
- Transcript scale tests passed (7 tests), including zero retained-message reads across answer and reasoning deltas over 3,000 messages. The initial setup failure during the main merge was resolved on the stable source snapshot.
- Production Knip reports exactly the same unused files/exports/types on merge base `120e515260d7` and this head. These inherited retired exports belong to other active migration lanes; no ignores were added.

Browser capture used 500 synthetic sessions, with the Sessions page's existing 25-row pagination. Both pages produced zero browser errors, and inspected Chat and Sessions before/after screenshots are pixel-identical (0 changed pixels each). Playwright traces remain local.

| One-run browser observation | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold Chat ready | 3,870 ms | 4,566 ms |
| Sessions route ready | 766 ms | 650 ms |
| Return to Chat | 512 ms | 249 ms |
| Rendered Sessions rows | 25 | 25 |

These timings ran under concurrent host load and are not a statistical speedup claim. The sampled transcript DOM node was replaced on the route round trip on both builds; that baseline observation was sent to the migration ledger for the shell/chat owners. The measured improvement claimed here is the startup byte reduction.

![Before: Chat and sidebar with synthetic sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6d9c517-7003-41c6-9379-b061e6a828f5)

![After: Chat and sidebar with synthetic sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ce0ac2d-d8dc-43e1-80aa-586a75889fb0)

![Before: Sessions page with synthetic sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72491233-d324-4d60-95dd-af5325309aa9)

![After: Sessions page with synthetic sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3123c0db-60d8-4d8c-8c22-5ef55262f009)

The first opened event selected partial UI E2E before the `ci:full` label was applied. The unchanged PR was reopened once with the label present; the resulting full UI run is the landing proof.

prs.title: fix(agents): emit before_model_resolve on the CLI-backed turn path
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`before_model_resolve` never fires for CLI-backed models (`agentRuntime.id = "claude-cli"` and siblings). `runAgentAttempt` dispatches those turns to `runCliAgent` and returns before the embedded runner's model setup, which is the only place the hook was emitted. Plugins therefore cannot do per-turn model routing on the CLI runtime — every turn stays on the configured primary model (#156038).

## What Changes

- New `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.ts`: emits `before_model_resolve` once per CLI-backed turn, before CLI preparation normalizes the model for the child process, via the shared `resolveHookModelSelection` seam. It reports the logical provider (e.g. `anthropic`) in the hook context, not the execution backend.
- Override acceptance on the CLI path is bounded: only overrides that resolve back to the already selected CLI execution backend are applied to the child's `--model`; cross-runtime overrides preserve the caller's selection and log a warning instead of silently changing the transport. `modelSelectionLocked` sessions skip the hook, matching the embedded path. Isolated completions and backend control operations never enter agent hooks.
- ~~`before_prompt_build` hook context reported the logical provider~~ — reverted in round 3 per review: the prompt-build context keeps reporting the execution backend (`params.provider`) as on main; only the new `before_model_resolve` context reports the logical provider.
- `resolveHookModelSelection`'s local `HookContext` type gains an optional `modelProviderId` passthrough.

## How It Was Verified

- New unit suite `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.test.ts` (5 tests, all passing):
  - no hook registered → caller selection untouched;
  - same-backend override (`anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` → `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, both mapped to `claude-cli`) is applied and the hook fires exactly once;
  - cross-runtime override (`openai/gpt-5.6` mapped to `openclaw`) is rejected and reported via `rejectedOverride` with the caller selection preserved;
  - hook context reports `modelProviderId: "anthropic"` (logical provider, not `claude-cli`);
  - `modelSelectionLocked` session never invokes the hook.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` (184 tests) passes unchanged — covers the `before_prompt_build` context change including the `modelProviderId` assertion.
- `tsgo`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` clean for all touched files.

## Notes

- The hook can only act before the child process is spawned, so a same-backend override replaces the model passed to the backend; a cross-runtime override cannot be honored without changing the execution transport, which is why it is explicitly rejected rather than applied.
- `runCliAgentInternal` stays under the file's line budget by owning the wiring in `model-resolve-hook.ts`.

## Evidence

Before fix: `resolveHookModelSelection(...)` was called only from embedded-runner model setup (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/model-setup.ts`), and `runAgentAttempt` returned into `runCliAgent` before that setup, so a plugin registering `before_model_resolve` never saw CLI-backed turns — the reported repro (hook log line absent, effective model stays `claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5`) follows directly from that dispatch structure.

After fix (new suite, all 5 passing):

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

- Same-backend override applied: `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 → anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` (both mapped to `claude-cli` via `agentRuntime.id`), hook fired exactly once, hook context reported `modelProviderId: "anthropic"`.
- Cross-runtime override rejected: `openai/gpt-5.6` (mapped to `openclaw`) → `applied: false`, `rejectedOverride` reported, caller selection preserved.
- `modelSelectionLocked` session never invoked the hook.
- Regression: `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` — 184 tests passed, including the `before_prompt_build` `modelProviderId` assertion.
- `tsgo`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` clean for all touched files.


### Round 2: review findings and CI fixes (head 36c8074b707)

- CI: the turn helpers are no longer production exports — `resolveCliModelOverrideForTurn` and `runCliModelResolveHookForTurn` are module-private behind the exported `applyCliModelResolveHookForRun` seam (clears the knip `check-dependencies` red and the `check-test-types-core-2` TS2488, which the test rewrite fixes by typing the mock call non-optionally). Local knip production run is clean.
- Provider-only override rejection: a hook response that changes only the provider (model unchanged) previously hit the unchanged-selection early return and was silently dropped. It now falls through to backend resolution and is reported via `rejectedOverride` with the warning log, same as a cross-runtime override.
- Channel routing context: the CLI hook context now carries the same channel/account projection the prompt-build hook context reports (`buildAgentHookContextChannelFields` → `channelId`/`accountId`), so both CLI-side hooks see identical routing fields. `HookContext` gains an optional `accountId` passthrough.
- Test suite rewritten against the exported seam (`vi.mock` of the global hook runner) and extended: 7 tests passing, including the provider-only rejection and channel-routing assertions.

### Round 3: real-plugin proof and review findings (head c2dce2f3962)

- **[P1] prompt-build provider value preserved:** `before_prompt_build` hook context again reports `modelProviderId: params.provider` (the execution backend), the value current main reports; the logical-provider projection is now limited to the new `before_model_resolve` hook context. `prepare.test.ts` still passes unchanged (184 tests, `modelProviderId` assertion included).
- **[P2] auth-profile-aware override check:** the backend-resolution comparison in `model-resolve-hook.ts` now passes the caller-selected `authProfileId` to `resolveCliRuntimeExecutionProvider`, mirroring how `runAgentAttempt` resolves the configured runtime (`attempt-execution.ts` passes `selectedAuthProfile?.id`), so a same-backend override on a profile-selected CLI runtime is no longer rejected as cross-runtime.
- **Real-behavior proof:** new committed CI test `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts` — a plugin file on disk is loaded through the production `loadOpenClawPlugins`, activated through the production `initializeGlobalHookRunner`, and a CLI-backed turn is driven through the exported `applyCliModelResolveHookForRun` seam (the exact call site `runCliAgent` invokes before CLI preparation):
  - the plugin's `before_model_resolve` handler fires exactly once and appends a trace record showing the hook context it received: `{"prompt":"route this turn","modelProviderId":"anthropic","sessionId":"session-1","trigger":"agent-turn","channelId":"chan-1"}` (logical provider + channel routing);
  - the same-backend override (`claude-opus-5-5` → `claude-sonnet-5`, both on `claude-cli`) is folded into the run's model before the child is prepared;
  - pre-fix check: with `src/agents/cli-runner.ts` and the hook module restored to the pre-fix parent (735e46e75b8), the same test fails with `TypeError: applyCliModelResolveHookForRun is not a function` — the CLI path had no emission point.
- CI TS red fixed: the stub hook runner's `runBeforeModelResolve` mock now declares its `(event, ctx)` parameters so the call assertions typecheck (`TS2493`/`TS2532`).


### Round 4: attachment metadata and full-turn child proof (head dd10a7c9b8a)

- **[P2] attachment metadata forwarded:** the CLI hook call now passes `attachments: buildBeforeModelResolveAttachments(params.images)` — the same projection the embedded runner derives from prompt image refs (`model-setup.ts`) — so image-aware routing plugins see identical `before_model_resolve` input on embedded and CLI turns. New test covers an image-bearing turn: the hook event arrives as `{ prompt, attachments: [{ kind: "image", mimeType: "image/png" }] }`.
- **Real-behavior proof at full turn depth (no adapter invocation, no spawn mocks):** new committed CI test `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts` drives one complete turn through the exported production entry `runCliAgent`:
  - a plugin file on disk is loaded via `loadOpenClawPlugins`; it registers a plugin-owned CLI backend (`registerCliBackend`, `modelProvider: "stub"`, command = a real local executable) and a `before_model_resolve` router;
  - the turn completes against a **real spawned child process** (the stub CLI executable logs the exact argv it was spawned with) and returns its reply: `finalAssistantVisibleText === "stub reply after routing"`;
  - the child's recorded argv contains `exec` and `--model stub-routed-model`, and does not contain the caller's `stub-base-model` — the loaded plugin's override reached the CLI-backed child;
  - the hook handler itself traced exactly one `before_model_resolve` firing with the turn prompt;
  - nothing on the spawn path is mocked — the test never imports `execute.test-support`, so the real process supervisor spawns the child.
  - `--model` here is the backend-configured model flag (`modelArg`), the same argv slot `claude-cli`'s `--model` occupies.
- Suite totals: `model-resolve-hook.test.ts` 6 tests (incl. image-bearing turn), `model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts` 1, `model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts` 1 — all passing.
- CI note (head c2dce2f3962): the single `checks-node-changed-compact-large-22` failure is `src/gateway/session-utils.queued-collector-admission.test.ts` ("Queued collector session changed before cancellation publication"), a gateway/session admission test in a subsystem this PR does not touch (`src/agents/cli-runner/*` only); it belongs to the known gateway SQLite/session flaky pool. Re-run requires admin rights this fork account does not have.

### Round 5: measured test cost (head 596e27e02a6)

Measured one-worker wall time per new test file (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file> --pool=forks --maxWorkers=1`, this machine, head 596e27e02a6):

| Test file | Tests | One-worker wall time |
|---|---:|---:|
| `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.test.ts` | 8 | 97.1s (worker includes spawn-prep overhead; vitest in-run test time 2.5s) |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts` | 1 | 33.0s (in-run test time 0.4s) |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts` | 1 | 64.1s (in-run test time 2.0s) |

CI seconds (run 36113720283, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-31/-32`, branch CI on the predecessor head dd10a7c9b8a — same three files, per-test durations identical in kind to 596e27e02a6 whose shard rerun was cancelled by the unrelated compact-large-19 flake):

- `model-resolve-hook.test.ts`: 8 tests, 2.5s summed test time in shard `agentic-agents-support-hosted-1` (shard total 419.49s for 137 files).
- `model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts`: 1 test, 384ms in shard `agentic-agents-support-hosted-2`.
- `model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts`: 1 test, 2049ms in shard `agentic-agents-support-hosted-1` (real spawned child dominates).
- Job totals: `checks-node-changed-compact-large-31` 14m25s (success), `-32` 7m08s (failed on the gateway flake above, before agents shard rerun).

Per-file budget is dominated by per-worker runtime preparation (identical for pre-existing files in the same shard); the marginal in-run test time added by these three files is ~4.9s CI seconds.



## Round 8 — CS Rev7 finding: logical provider on subscription-auth dispatch

- **[P2] Pass the logical provider from subscription-auth dispatch**: `runEmbeddedAgentViaCliBackend` now passes `modelProvider: params.provider` to `runCliAgent` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/cli-backend-dispatch.ts`), so the CLI-side `before_model_resolve` hook on the subscription-auth caller sees the caller's logical provider (e.g. `anthropic`) instead of the CLI backend name (`claude-cli`), and a same-backend override naming the logical provider is folded into the routed model instead of self-rejecting. Callers that never resolved a provider pass `undefined`, which keeps the runner's existing `modelProvider ?? provider` backend fallback — behavior identical to before for those.
- **Tests** (`cli-backend-dispatch.test.ts`, 41/41 green): the canonical-ref dispatch cases now pin `modelProvider: "anthropic"` on the dispatched `runCliAgent` params (pre-fix red: `undefined` under the same assertions, 4 failed), and a new case pins that a caller without a resolved provider still dispatches with `modelProvider: undefined` (fallback preserved). Together with the existing full-turn test (override reaches the spawned child's routed `--model` when the hook receives the logical provider), this covers the subscription-auth caller end to end: dispatch → hook context → child model.
- Repo `tsgo`, oxlint, and oxfmt clean on the changed files. Head `ed965f23360`.


## Round 9 — CS Rev8 P1: keep backend-keyed tool policy on subscription-auth dispatch (head 69cfcf25234)

- **[P1] The Rev7 fix routed the logical provider into preparation's policy input**: `modelProvider` is preparation's tool-policy input ("Selected model provider used for tool policy; distinct from a CLI runtime id", `src/agents/cli-runner/types.ts`). Supplying `anthropic` from dispatch also changed turns with no model hook: preparation feeds that value into the MCP capability profile (`prepare.ts` `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile`), whose `tools.byProvider` lookup matches provider keys, so a restriction keyed to `claude-cli` stopped matching and a previously denied MCP tool could reach the child.
- **Fix — carry the logical provider to the hook without replacing the policy input**: dispatch now passes the new hook-only field `hookModelProvider: params.provider` and leaves `modelProvider` untouched (`undefined`, exactly the pre-Rev7 shape — the entire preparation policy surface is byte-identical to main for subscription-auth turns). `applyCliModelResolveHookForRun` reads `logicalProvider: params.hookModelProvider ?? params.modelProvider ?? params.provider`, so the hook's routing context still reports `anthropic` and same-backend overrides keep working; every other `modelProvider` consumer (synthetic-turn meta, settlement, transcripts, diagnostics) falls back to the backend name, which is main's existing behavior for this dispatch.
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green**: with the new assertions on `HEAD~1` (`hookModelProvider: "anthropic"` and `modelProvider` untouched on the dispatched params), 4 tests failed; with the fix, `cli-backend-dispatch.test.ts` is 41/41. The pin now enforces both halves of the invariant: the hook surface routes on the caller's logical provider, and dispatch never replaces the policy input.
- **Regression suites**: `cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.test.ts` + `model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts` 9/9, `model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts` 1/1 (hook still receives the logical provider through the new field — the fallback chain keeps every existing caller green). `tsgo`, oxlint, `oxfmt --check` clean on the four touched files.
- **On the remaining proof request** (denied MCP tool rejected before execution on a subscription-auth child): the code-level invariant is now pinned by test — dispatch leaves the preparation policy input at its main-state value, so backend-keyed `tools.byProvider` denials resolve exactly as they do on main. The full-chain child-level observation (deny firing before final I/O) is environment-gated on a real spawned child with a configured backend-keyed denial; we will add it as a follow-up evidence round rather than claim it from the unit surface.



## Round 11 — CS Rev10 P2: report the selected model id in the CLI hook context (head de55d10a68d)

- **[P2] The CLI-side `before_model_resolve` context omitted `modelId`**: the embedded path passes both `modelProviderId` and `modelId` in the hook context (`run-orchestrator.ts` `hookCtx` → `resolveEmbeddedRunModelSetup` → `resolveHookModelSelection`), but the CLI-side emission reported only the provider (`src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.ts`). A routing plugin reading `ctx.modelId` received `undefined` on CLI-backed turns and could not compare the caller-selected model before proposing an override.
- **Fix — same selection the embedded context reports**: the CLI hook context now carries `modelId: params.modelId` (the caller-selected model), and the shared hook-context projection in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/setup.ts` gains the optional `modelId` field (additive; the embedded path already supplied the value, so its behavior is unchanged).
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green**: the new assertions (`ctx.modelId === "claude-opus-5-5"` on a CLI turn, in both the stubbed seam and the loaded-plugin trace) fail on the predecessor head (`modelId` observed `undefined`); with the fix, `model-resolve-hook.test.ts` + `model-resolve-hook.real-plugin.test.ts` + `model-resolve-hook.full-turn.test.ts` are all green on the rebased head. The loaded-plugin path now traces and pins `modelId` alongside `modelProviderId`, so the context contract is enforced end to end through the production loader.
- Repo `tsgo`, oxlint, and `oxfmt --check` clean on the touched files. Head `de55d10a68d` (rebased onto the round-5 merge of main).
- **On the remaining Rev10 proof request** (subscription-auth child denied at a backend-keyed forbidden MCP tool before execution): unchanged from Round 9's note — the policy-input invariant is pinned by test; the child-level final-I/O observation is environment-gated and will land as a follow-up evidence round.


## Round 12 — CS Rev19 P2: refresh vision capability after a same-backend hook override (head 5a2ca9e47b2)

- **[P2] Stale `modelHasVision` after routing**: a same-backend `before_model_resolve` override rewrote `params.model` (and `requesterModel`) but left `params.modelHasVision` carrying the caller's original selection (`src/agents/cli-runner/model-resolve-hook.ts`). CLI preparation copies that value into the MCP grant, and vision-dependent tool surfaces resolve against it — so routing between models with different image support exposed or suppressed the wrong tool surface.
- **Fix — re-derive from the same catalog preparation reads**: when an override is applied, the routed model's image support is re-derived from the manifest + configured catalog overlay (the identical `loadManifestModelCatalog` + `overlayConfiguredModelCatalog` pair preparation uses) with a literal provider/id match. A routed model without a catalog entry keeps the caller's value — an entry is the only evidence that can overturn the caller's derived capability. Rejected overrides never touch it.
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green**: new regressions in `model-resolve-hook.test.ts` — routing vision→text-only must flip `modelHasVision` to `false` and text-only→vision must flip it to `true` — both fail on the predecessor head (stale caller value observed); the routed-model-without-entry and rejected-override cases pin the keep semantics. Full file 12/12 green; tsgo and oxlint clean on the touched files.
- `findModelInCatalog` was deliberately not used for the re-derivation: its miss path consults the provider policy surface (route canonicalization), which is an aliasing side quest for a hook-supplied literal id and would keep the caller's capability anyway on a miss.


## Round 13 — CS Rev21 P2: resolve CLI aliases before deriving routed vision capability (head 178531188b0)

- **[P2] Alias routes miss the catalog row**: the Round 12 re-derivation matched the hook's literal model id against catalog rows only, but a hook can route to a CLI alias (e.g. `sonnet` on claude-cli) whose catalog entry lives under the alias target — the literal lookup missed it, kept the caller's `modelHasVision`, and passed the stale value into the MCP grant.
- **Fix — mirror preparation's alias contract**: candidate identities are now the literal routed id, the claude-cli context alias (`CLAUDE_CLI_CONTEXT_MODEL_ALIASES`, the same table preparation consults), and the backend alias-table normalization (`resolveCliBackendConfig` + `normalizeCliModel`). All candidates still match catalog rows only — a total miss keeps the caller's capability, never consulting the provider policy surface.
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green**: two new regressions — routing to `sonnet` (text-only catalog target) must clear `modelHasVision`, routing to `fable` (vision-capable target) must grant it — both fail on the predecessor head; an alias-target-without-entry case pins the keep semantics. Full file 15/15 green; sibling suites (full-turn, cli-backend-dispatch) green; tsgo and oxlint clean on the touched files.
- **CI true red also fixed**: the merge head's `check-test-types-core-2` failure (TS2322 ×3) came from main tightening `ModelDefinitionConfig`/`ModelProviderConfig` (`name`, `reasoning`, `cost`, `maxTokens`, `baseUrl` now required); the test fixtures were brought up to the new schema.
- **On the remaining Rev21 proof request** (final MCP tool surface after alias routing through the production path): the same environment-gated final-effect observation noted in earlier rounds; the helper-level contract is now pinned by the alias regressions above.


## Round 14 — rebase onto current main via preparation's alias resolver (head 885779c885b)

- **CI true red after the rebase**: `TS2459` in `model-resolve-hook.ts` — main made the claude-cli context alias table module-private behind the new `resolveClaudeCliContextModelId` export in `prepare-claude.ts`, so the Round 13 import of the raw `CLAUDE_CLI_CONTEXT_MODEL_ALIASES` table no longer type-checks.
- **Fix**: the hook now calls preparation's resolver and treats an unchanged result as "no alias" (pushing only when the resolver actually maps the routed id elsewhere) — the candidate set and its catalog-matches-only contract are unchanged. 15/15 `model-resolve-hook` and the full-turn case green; oxlint and oxfmt clean.


## Round 15 — CS Rev24 P1: guard the CLI model hook with the live session generation (head f216ae01da4)

- **[P1] Hook context lacked claiming-hook admission**: the CLI emission built its `before_model_resolve` context without the admission assertion, so `resolveHookModelSelection` ran routing hooks without the session-generation assertion and its guarded-request authority. A routing plugin awaiting work could still reach transport after the generation was revoked; revocation was only observed during later CLI preparation — too late.
- **Fix — mirror the reply hook and embedded selection path**: `runCliAgentInternal` already owns `generation.assertCurrent`; it is now threaded through `applyCliModelResolveHookForRun` into `withClaimingHookAdmission` on the hook context, so the shared selection seam asserts before the hooks and wraps their network I/O in `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority`.
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green**: two regressions — the hook context must carry the caller's assertion through `readClaimingHookAdmission`, and a revoked generation must reject the turn before `runBeforeModelResolve` is invoked (both fail on the predecessor head). Full `model-resolve-hook` file 17/17 green; full-turn and real-plugin suites green; oxlint/oxfmt clean on touched files.
- **On the outstanding transport proofs** (revoked-generation rejection at the real boundary; allowed/forbidden MCP outcomes after alias/image routing): the unit regressions now pin the admission seam and revocation-before-hook behavior; the production-path observations remain environment-gated as noted in earlier rounds.


## Round 16 — CS Rev25 P1: fence ordinary-turn hook work behind all live turn authorities (head 138e62ee8a5)

- **[P1] Admission carried only the cron-generation assertion**: both CLI hook seams received `generation?.assertCurrent`, and `prepareCronRootSessionGeneration` returns undefined for non-cron sessions — so ordinary turns ran their `before_agent_reply` and `before_model_resolve` handlers with **no admission at all**, and even cron-rooted turns were unguarded against caller revocation, a fired abort signal, or a rotated gateway lifecycle while a routing hook awaited plugin work. The subsequent guarded fetch had no assertion for those authorities and could start network I/O after they changed; the checks at the top of `runCliAgentInternal` (and the later preparation checks) sit outside that await boundary.
- **Fix — one composed admission closure**: `runCliAgentInternal` now builds `assertHookAdmission` (lifecycle generation + abort signal + caller `assertCurrent` + session-generation assertion) and hands it to both seams, so every hook-owning turn is fenced behind the same authorities the post-hook preparation re-checks. No new surface: the fences already exist on the run path, the hooks now observe them too.
- **Pre-fix red → post-fix green** (`cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts`, 20/20): the new ordinary-turn regression asserts the admission exists for a non-cron turn and rejects on caller revocation and on a fired abort signal; the existing "ordinary session" scenario updated from "no claim held" to "no generation claim, but the caller/abort/lifecycle fence is live" (it fails on the predecessor head exactly as the new test does). `model-resolve-hook` 18/18 unaffected; oxlint clean on touched files.

prs.title: perf(ui): load filtered sidebar rows before group metadata
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A sidebar with a saved owner or status filter waits for custom group metadata before loading its visible session rows. A slow group catalog therefore delays the first populated sidebar.

## User Impact

The filtered roster now enters the existing bootstrap queue before the group catalog. Rows can paint while group metadata is pending; group names and ordering still update when it arrives. The existing two-request concurrency and selected-chat readiness gate remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser tracing against 5,000 synthetic sessions showed the initial roster request already starts immediately after hello. Its roughly 200 KB response parses in about 0.5 ms, and the expanded Coding group renders ten rows, rather than the whole inventory. The filtered roster starts much later, behind queued metadata work. This removes its dependency on the group catalog without adding a cache, virtualizer, configuration option, protocol, or scheduler mode.

Production LOC delta: 0 (+3/−3); this is an ordering correction within the existing owner. Removing the queue would break its concurrency and foreground-chat contract. The redundant group callback wrapper is removed. Tests shrink by three lines.

## Evidence

- Focused local proof: 37 tests passed across `app-sidebar.background-scope.test.ts` and `session-data-controller.event-refresh.test.ts`, with `--maxWorkers=1` (60.06 s wall time, including transforms; changed file test time below 5 s).
- Regression control: the saved-owner scenario fails on the original production code because the filtered RPC does not start while group metadata remains pending. The same scenario passes after the change and asserts rendered session text before releasing the group reply.
- Changed-file oxfmt, repo focused oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed. Full build/typecheck/UI performance budgets and broader suites belong to PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped-clean P0–P2. The autoreview helper refused the provider selector because it does not match the operator config; no configuration was changed. Direct callback safety was verified against the lexical group-loader owner.
- Team sandbox measurement and sanitized before/after screenshots are in progress against a 5,000-session/6,000-run synthetic fixture with 4,641,595,392 bytes of agent data. Results will be added before landing. No production Gateway or database is used.
- Local development timings are noisy and are not landing evidence. The broader HTML/JS boot and reactive setup remain follow-ups; this PR makes no virtualization or whole-startup speedup claim.

prs.title: fix(macos): finish bundled Gateway repair during update recovery
prs.body:
Related: #170724

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Retry can restart an app-owned bundled Gateway without repairing its configured plugin host links or completing the ordinary app-update receipt.

## User Impact

Retry repairs the selected runtime while its Gateway is stopped, verifies health, and completes required core work through the existing post-update owner. Required repair refusals keep recovery pending; a settled failure can restore the captured predecessor, while unconfirmed Doctor cleanup keeps the Gateway stopped. The existing failure window shows the actual runtime/inspection or failed-step error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses Doctor's existing external-owner repair policy and native hosting-change owner. The captured service environment survives the handoff. Native service and runtime custody are checked before effects and after awaited work; receipt settlement uses the dispatched receipt. Conditional plugin warnings and pending records remain visible in the existing Gateway diagnostics. The landed newer-Node recovery policy remains intact.

The native stdout adapter delegates to the existing secure file IPC and child-process settlement owner before Doctor admission. A missing classified result remains missing; required failure facts cannot certify success. Generic thrown failures remain failures. This changes diagnostic provenance through existing controls and layout, so this is a behavior-only fix rather than an appearance change.

## Evidence

- Real isolated `pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` through integrated predecessor `500cc559`’s stdout bridge: exit 0, one classified `ok` result, unchanged independent config SHA-256 and classified config hash, four warnings retained, no failure facts or maintenance refusal. The command joined in 383.56s including canonical runtime compilation and Doctor’s UI-asset repair; postflight inspection found no task-state holders. No operator Gateway or state was modified.
- Two separate same-version physical installations: registered peer links initially pointed at the wrong package; actual offline Doctor repaired both to the selected runtime, public SDK imports succeeded, and a real owned Gateway reported the plugin loaded with no plugin errors. Pre-repair core health could already pass because SDK aliases masked the wrong raw peer link. That earlier physical cell predates the integrated base; the exact candidate app-host cell below remains pending.
- Actual CLI parent/child IPC: seven cases cover normal completion, interruption with joined writer extinction, an unsettled reservation, complete classified recoverable cleanup, missing-result/nonzero, required refusal, and required error. Existing secure file/stdout IPC: 14 cases. After integrating the named main ratchet repair, the combined command passed all 21 cases in 101.68s wall; bridge file duration was 78.08s including cold compilation. CI seconds pending.
- Native decoder/restoration: 12 selected cases passed in 0.008s. The new `ok` plus required-failure-fact case fails without the repair. Existing restoration controls also fail if uncertain cleanup is allowed to restore the predecessor.
- App/all-test compilation passed in 58.55s; core and scripts types, targeted lint, source localization inventory verification, and pinned workflow validation passed. Workflow routing: five cases, 6.63s wall. Launcher owner: 18 cases, 31.31s wall on its prepared source. CI seconds pending.
- Initial PR CI exposed an eager runtime import and an obsolete numeric native-job budget assumption. The correction keeps runtime loading inside the stdout branch and evaluates the ordinary 30-minute budget; the app-host completion decoder now matches literal function-ID substrings instead of constructing a regex from arguments (CodeQL finding). CLI sibling tests: 150 passed, 101.55s wall (73.61s test duration); result IPC: 14 passed, 10.05s wall; cache owner: 15 passed. Five affected launcher completion controls passed in the isolated landing clone, 20.31s wall (11.23s test duration). A preceding local launcher run had two subprocess-budget failures, including unchanged ordinary launch setup; those remain recorded as execution-resource uncertainty, not a code fix inferred from the later pass. Core/scripts types, targeted lint, and fresh P0–P2 review passed.
- Main was integrated to resolve the specific mock-export ratchet failure from a concurrently added launcher test. The existing narrowed isolation annotation fixes that owner; the canonical guard passed against the integrated base. Core/scripts types and the 21 IPC cases passed on the integrated candidate. This is a named-gate integration, not an attempt to replay CI for green.
- ClawSweeper identified a real line-cap violation (startup module 1282 → 1288 counted lines). The complete early Doctor selection now lives in a lazy sibling adapter, while the existing dotenv-presence predicate moves into the established startup-policy owner. No baseline/rule exception or test seam was added. The actual line-cap and max-lines ratchets, core types, formatting, typed lint, and fresh P0–P2 review passed. Existing runCli profile/preflight and policy boundaries: 34 cases passed in 123.52s wall. The earlier real Doctor proof retains its prior-head identity; this exact semantic extraction is separately qualified, and final runtime/app-host/published-driver artifacts will bind the final head.
- The prior MCP Docker red was reproduced at its actual waiter: the Gateway supplied 48 HTTP 200 `ready:true` responses after one initial pending-admission 503, while no one-time ready log appeared. The strict helper now consumes that authoritative JSON on the explicit owned port, while preserving legacy log/TCP and inferred-port contracts. Generic 200 bodies, `ready:false`, and HTTP failures remain negative controls. Existing helper owner before conflict integration: 39 cases passed in 19.24s wall (13.40s test duration), types/lint/format/syntax and fresh P0–P2 review passed. The same verified e9 product tarball and 1,422 exact harness files, with only that helper replaced, then passed the actual MCP forwarding, permission, media, and seven-notification flow in 170.41s including image rebuild. This is Linux ARM64 runtime proof; the final published-head CI remains separately required. Both task containers were cleaned up.
- A new main change caused one test-table conflict before the full proof started. The integration preserves main’s current listener marker for port discovery and gives its positive fixture real `ready:true` JSON; all generic/false/503 and legacy/TCP controls remain. The resolved owner passed 40 cases in 20.35s wall (15.40s test duration), core types and actual branch/index size ratchets passed, and two independent relevant reviews found no issue. Main’s SQLite admission/retirement changes were preserved and audited; prior Doctor/MCP artifacts retain their earlier identities. The final exact app-host/published-driver cells will qualify the merged runtime input.
- Release-only app-host fixture calls the public Retry/startup owners, uses a real protected Bun `--no-install` service, requires a real newer-schema Doctor diagnostic before restoring its fixture database, checks core receipt and actual plugin health, and launches a second fresh host against the same profile. Both phase event streams are exported. Actual `95a6c33e` execution in [full validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38505146296) **failed before Retry**: the staged host selected one ordinary-retry function, but its initial setup recorded an AppKit activation-policy failure, a `/tmp` versus `/private/tmp` URL-equality failure, and then an initial Gateway connection refusal. The receipt/Retry/refusal/relaunch composition did not run to completion. [Its real phase event stream](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38505146296/artifacts/11869020699) is retained while the fixture and launch/service owners are diagnosed; no passing recovery claim is made. Ordinary main-tier CI does not execute this composition.

The full-tier macOS test job reuses the canonical exact-source runtime builder and staging owner. Its 75-minute budget accommodates the observed 28–47-minute full package preparation plus approximately 10-minute native suite; ordinary/compatibility native jobs retain 30 minutes and no runner rows are added. The existing full-tier published-driver update cell also supplies the required shipped-driver × candidate update proof using the canonical exact candidate package and its SHA-256; the `95a6c33e` cell passed as detailed below. Shipped updaters retain their normal file IPC contract, while only new app-owned repair invocations select the stdout adapter. This cell is separate from the native ordinary-receipt composition. Signed installed-app delivery is not claimed by this nonpublishing validation.

The existing published-driver harness may relabel a behind-driver candidate to the published driver floor solely for fixture update mechanics, retaining the exact build commit. This does not change the source version or publish a release.

- Exact published-driver proof: [job 115667314529](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38505146296/job/115667314529) passed the published `2026.10.3` updater against candidate commit `95a6c33eb55d49e34c1cb2fb9721e09f7ea131cf`. Candidate package SHA-256: `50200a8642a71a46b234da341106bbc2bc549babe883a787605957aabcde9d80`; [candidate artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38505146296/artifacts/11868020967), [preservation proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38505146296/artifacts/11869010787). The canonical fixture-floor relabel produced `2026.10.3` while retaining that commit; its verified running build ID was `2026.10.3-95a6c33eb55d-2026-10-14T03-16-29.994Z`. The updater finished with a succeeded durable run, the running build matched, and readiness was HTTP 200. Existing harness assertions passed for durable session ID/content, incognito content absence, orphan-sidecar bytes, package build info, and managed PID replacement. This proves that existing state loads through the shipped updater; it does not claim every RPC projection is byte-identical or prove the Mac receipt/relaunch path.
- Native `95a6c33e` coverage before the app-host failure: 2,551 tests in 288 suites passed in 557.768s; named-profile two tests passed in 7.134s, and the remaining 14 tests passed in 7.737s. The full run also identified missing translations for the two new recovery messages and three readiness fixtures that still supplied the old response. Those repairs are prepared with canonical localization and actual Linux fixture proof; the published head still retains the observed failures until the repairs are published and qualified. Two additional PR-CI failures (a Linux service-inspection/schema-fence expectation and a pending-Doctor ledger timeout) passed focused macOS runs but retain their original CI failures and platform/execution uncertainty.
