prs.title: perf(sessions): avoid futile maintenance writer work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stops repeated futile session maintenance from delaying foreground writes when the remaining entries are protected, while restoring cleanup when those entries become eligible. Retention policy and operator configuration remain unchanged.

**Current head: `26897c734771e5fb83d81a22e6513b78014b5e0e`. Performance qualification is still pending; merge is held.** Exact-head CI is complete, and its two causal failures meet the authorized unrelated-flake criterion described below.

## User Impact

Protected-only passes become quiet instead of replanning on ordinary activity. Clearing recovery claims still wakes cleanup, retries cannot be postponed indefinitely by sustained writes, and retention yields between writer batches. Below-high-water physical probes skip needless checkpoint/vacuum work. Native checkpoint I/O remains uninterruptible; batch targets are not a hard wall-clock guarantee.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing maintenance owner now retains an exhaustive durable-protection result until eligibility, identity, policy, removal, or the existing age deadline changes. Runtime/recent protection cannot set this durable latch. Creation facts and committed actor receipts carry authoritative preimage/postimage changes; removing a recovery claim wakes idle cleanup. Compound commands and large transfers preserve the first transaction preimage, and proof consumption stays inside its current native snapshot boundary.

Runtime preservation uses the existing off-FIFO metadata planner, with selected victims revalidated at commit. The duplicate writer-held scan and retired private write-required continuation are removed. Intrinsically protected rows and directly active keys use captured facts before requesting provider/ancestry preparation. Runtime-only protected no-ops remain non-durable. Metadata planning/statistics/age retain their canonical worker claim without an empty host-retain FIFO reservation.

Standard per-agent legacy and SQLite locators share one physical budget owner; custom aggregate scopes remain distinct. Archive selection runs outside writer admission; retention deletes 16-row batches with current authority and reference checks, yielding between them. Free-page reclamation uses bounded units and retries retained WAL when readers release it. Policy, config, schema and dependencies are unchanged.

Production LOC: **439 added / 224 removed, net +215**, excluding tests/docs. Growth carries protection/identity publication, correct invalidation and idle wake-up, plus typed archive/free-page facts. These are needed to preserve cleanup correctness after backing off. Removed machinery includes the planning reservation, duplicate archive-existence wrapper and duplicate per-agent queue ownership.

## Evidence

### Trigger and correctness

The synthetic fixture has **9,546 rows: 6,034 protected active entries and 3,512 protected archives**, with 45,656 transcript events and **42,981,588,992 database bytes**, `maxEntries: 5000` and `maxDiskBytes: 60gb`. Archives do not consume the active cap. The fixture's remaining active set cannot meet that cap; the production archive count alone does not prove every active row is protected.

At reported production source `488bd9fa`, `trigger: initial` identifies the physical-budget sweep phase. Its only production caller enters after the captured initial physical total exceeds the captured max budget; this is separate from the logical-entry cap. The old pruner nevertheless checkpoints/vacuums after its newer measurement falls below high water. A read-only numeric extraction from the task-named production log confirms:

| Production observation (UTC) | Whole pass | Checkpoints | Max checkpoint | Physical bytes before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2026-10-13 16:10:20 | 31,451 ms | 65 | 475 ms | 43,694,795,165 → 43,593,904,818 |
| 2026-10-13 16:15:15 | 8,252 ms | 32 | 1,596 ms | 43,602,096,322 → 43,575,952,714 |

Both recorded an incomplete blocked checkpoint. The eight-second pass is not one uninterrupted hold, but one native checkpoint did occupy 1.596 seconds. The log contains no matching disk-budget warning in the named interval. The initiating effective max budget and initial byte components are absent from these pruning records; stale accounting or an effective-config mismatch is not proven. This change adds high-water context and skips below-high-water work. Raw locator keys also permitted alias scopes to overlap physical passes; canonical ownership closes that source-level possibility without claiming it caused the production sample.

A production-path synthetic diagnostic found 6,054 protected active entries, including 20 completing recovery claims. All 20 claims cleared successfully, yet no eligibility fact reached the scheduler; 611 later write kicks still skipped cleanup. Committed actor receipt publication fixes that lost wake-up. The regression fails on prior source and passes with real archival after delivery settles, without an unrelated write kick. Other owning regressions cover retry starvation, lazy insertion/high-water wake-up, protected-proof reuse, physical alias ownership, retained-WAL retry and foreground progress between retention batches.

### Measurement status

The latest head is being compared with baseline `6194f02f62e736585bfc428b8ad21f1c0aa525d1` in three independent pairs, in predeclared head/base, base/head, head/base order. Every run gets a newly seeded fixture. The independently reviewed protocol keeps normal artifacts, INFO logging, synthetic model delay, both post-ready installation observations and continuous failure guards, original deadlines and the 60-second qualification anchor. Twenty creates are offered at Gateway ages 65/90/120 seconds. Background work is fixed at 80 public inputs: 20 initial qualification inputs plus 20 at ages 63/88/118 seconds. Every real submission, ACK, owned terminal and persisted acknowledgement is checked. Missed timing, unfinished prior rounds, recording/native failures or verification failures invalidate the run and stop the whole series. This narrower workload has quiet intervals and fewer turns than the original sustained closed-loop load; it cannot guarantee identical execution phases.

Earlier results remain negative or mixed and are not classified as noise:

| Baseline → prior candidate, protocol | InitialTurn p50 at 65 / 90 / 120 seconds (ms) | All-60 median |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `6194f02f → 41b60b8f`, closed-loop | 1095.5 → 1309; 980.5 → 1327; 1507 → 1688.5 | 1161 → 1346 (+15.9%) |
| `6194f02f → 1a028598`, post-ready closed-loop | 1174.5 → 1002.5; 977.5 → 1102; 740.5 → 952.5 | 965 → 1020 (+5.7%) |

Both complete comparisons settled all 120 measured creates. Natural archival improved **0/60 → 60/60**, with protected seed hashes unchanged; the baseline suppresses cleanup and does not perform equivalent archival. The post-ready pair completed 530 → 536 background turns, but later RPC medians increased 14.1%/42.0%. Main buffers had zero drops. Maintenance directly overlapped the three candidate create windows by only 38/39/39 ms, insufficient alone to explain the increase. Anonymous actor overlap and differing completions inside measured intervals prevent causal attribution.

Older `1e6a5af0 → 809450b9` pairs improved warm medians by 24.7%/48.3%, with reversing cold direction and one unresolved candidate terminal error. A debug nonreproduction is not a repair. Another older matched-age comparison increased later medians by 30.6%/27.3%. These are historical evidence, not qualification for current source.

An unchanged-protocol `6194f02f → 1a028598` attempt completed baseline's 60 creates and 479 background turns, but candidate timed out opening background WebSockets before any measured create or admitted background turn. Gateway SIGSEGV occurred after teardown began. The cause is unresolved. A separate native startup profile did not reproduce it and is disqualified from timing comparison.

The current-head SDK diagnostic settled all 60 creates and 415 background turns, naturally archived 60/60 and preserved seed hashes; Gateway exited zero. Its 100,000-event buffer dropped 8,893 tail events, correctly failing delivery coverage and holding the baseline. No paired timing claim is made. Candidate-only p50 was 1537.5/1152.5/1163.5 ms; maintenance occupied 40/39/37 ms. The complete zero-drop main writer buffer records 242 more session writes over 11.112 seconds after the final maintenance plan, with no further maintenance. Diagnostic observer overhead and missing tail coverage prevent comparing this run with uninstrumented results.

### Validation and review

Changed-file oxfmt, scoped repo lint and diff checks pass. The latest three complete maintenance read/worker/excluded-row files pass **54/54**, including directly active runtime protection and later eligibility. Removing only the new active-key condition makes its owning regression fail. Previous complete read/worker/kick proof passes **71/71**, key-order/encoding proof **25/25**, scheduler/actor/message **77/77**, writer ownership **6/6**, history eviction **22/22**, bindings **20/20**, and deletion receipts **10/10**. Required fixture repairs use valid retention/time inputs and join existing writer/database owners; they preserve semantic assertions. Interrupted and zero-test preparation failures are retained rather than counted as passing proof.

Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**. The helper refused provider/route preflight; operator config was unchanged. Independent full-diff, incremental and actual CI-merge integration reviews are clean after actionable findings were addressed. All six review threads are resolved.

Current CI [run 38502810936](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502810936), attempt 1, tested immutable merge `17565f3a851f89d785e22d62f3263f7e43f5222c` with ordered main parent `92d1623767cb237e2e98040895e2eb0e23710932`: **110 success, 23 skipped, two causal failures plus aggregate**. Broad selected typecheck/lint/source-contract/security/UI gates passed. Export collision guard passed, whole eager-import closure **17/17** and wrapper closure **3/3** passed on that exact merge. No new module or test file was added; the existing WAL owner exports its shared read-only free-page probe.

The two causal failures qualify as unrelated flakes under the explicit lane rule:

- [Startup admission job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502810936/job/115653886948): `doctor-config-preflight.admission.process.test.ts:592`, invalid shared ownership metadata expected exit 78, got 0/readiness. The original whole file passes **13/13 in five runs on each exact revision**. Executed startup readiness/ownership paths are unchanged and do not enter changed session maintenance/free-page probe branches.
- [Pending Doctor job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502810936/job/115653886996): `update-command-package-doctor.test.ts:407`, pending activation ledger timed out at its original 120-second deadline. The original whole file passes **25/25 in five runs on each exact revision**. Deferred process mock, fake timers, config/progress/ledger execution are unchanged; no actual Doctor child or changed session maintenance runs.

All 20 whole-file attempts use Node 24.19.0 and original source, fixtures, assertions and timeouts inside independently reviewed private mount/PID/network namespaces with real libraries and service tooling. These replays do not reproduce the full hosted shards, identify the hosted cause or claim a fix/inherited failure. All native processes/transfers joined, tracked source copies are clean and the owned-process/full-namespace audit is empty. **96 raw artifact hashes independently verified**; attribution manifest SHA-256 `734f4a9848d7471f133b29b7ac09714d5a1c151d2ccd092e8420abd540ade120`. An initial single-inode audit falsely matched a recycled kernel namespace ID; retained lifecycle facts show different mount/network identities, and no unrelated process was signaled.

CI logs were fetched once. An invalid cached aggregate ZIP used the supported job-log API fallback. No CI rerun, full local suite, Testbox/Crabbox lease or production Gateway/database/config change was performed. Historical CI failures and fixture/source preparation faults remain in the retained lane evidence; prior-head passes are not current-head waivers. Performance qualification remains held pending the latest paired measurements.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep stopped conversations ready for the next reply
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the next reply failing with “Codex loaded thread has no owned inference route; reconnect before retrying” after stopping a running command in a conversation.

## User Impact

Users can stop a turn, reload the Web UI, and send another message in the same conversation without reconnecting the Gateway. Stop still cancels the active work and revokes its execution authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

Unsubscribing discarded both a disposable fork-settings snapshot and the loaded thread’s inference provenance. Native unsubscribe can leave the thread loaded, so the next turn could no longer validate its route. Keep bounded provenance for that loaded thread and release it on actual close, archive, delete, or client teardown. Per-turn admission and cancellation remain independent.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the real Web UI with OpenAI: start a command, click Stop, reload, and send another message. The original code rejected that follow-up before inference. With the candidate, the same sequence delivered `CEDAR_FIXED`; another conversation then delivered `ATLAS_STILL_OK`.
- Strengthened the existing interrupted-turn lifecycle test to use owned inference routing while another thread remains active. It fails on the original code and passes with this fix. Added coverage that close/archive/delete release only the matching bounded route.
- 53 focused routing and subscription tests passed. Combined `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall time: 61.66 seconds, including cold imports; routing test bodies: 1.63 seconds. The strengthened regression took 1.177 seconds. CI run 38507310341 passed all 30 executed jobs without retries; the strengthened interrupted-thread case took 0.933 seconds and the three teardown cases totaled 0.083 seconds.
- Codex plugin typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, runtime build, and independent Codex review passed. The live Gateway rebuilt the candidate and served verified current UI assets.
- Inspected the native unsubscribe, loaded-thread resume, and close-notification contracts. No fallback provider was used for the live proof. Exact-head PR CI passed.

Before: the next message fails after Stop.

![Before: a stopped conversation rejects the next reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d57e2391-5166-4750-92b4-5c5c296312da)

After: Stop, reload, and another message succeed in the same conversation.

![After: the same conversation replies successfully](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8cd93a48-f4e4-4402-8a4e-ca097ee3cd3b)

prs.title: refactor: prepare durable question session custody
prs.body:
Related: #167266. Prerequisite for #168399; stacked on #171649.

## What Problem This Solves

Durable question registration needs one prepared conversation identity and authorization snapshot rather than a separate session-access implementation.

## User Impact

Question tools remain transient in this prerequisite. Newly created non-incognito inbound conversations receive lifecycle identity at creation, so subsequent durable custody can bind their original generation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extract the existing prepared-session owner and retain physical-store, generation, recipient, and live-authority checks. No schema or timeout changes. Later PRs activate durable registration and handoff.

## Evidence

- Native session-access and inbound-provenance tests: 32 cases passed across two shards, 86.86 seconds including setup/cleanup.
- Core production types, targeted typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Worker-access inventory regenerated through its native owner.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview: zero actionable findings; scope was this prerequisite patch, not an independent audit of every unchanged dependency.

prs.title: fix(security): prevent unsafe approval patterns from hanging command authorization
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Exec approval, cron, and plugin model argPattern values can use nested alternation or adjacent overlapping repeats such as a*a*...b or (a|b)*(b|c)*z. Those patterns hang the JavaScript regex engine (catastrophic backtracking) and can freeze command authorization. A zero-minimum separator (?, {0,n}, or *) can be omitted, so a*x?a* and a*x*a* are still adjacent on that path. The shared safe-regex compiler must reject those shapes, including complete branch unions, without banning required separators (a*xa*), disjoint optionals (a*x?b*), JWT-style {10,}.{10,} redact patterns, or safe Unicode class pairs used by group mentions.

Non-alternating grouped sequences such as (ab)*(cb)* must keep their complete languages. Reducing a group to its last token made (ab)* and (cb)* look like b vs b, so a safe pattern that should match abcb was rejected. Wrapping groups still flatten inner unions so ((a|b))*((b|c))* stays rejected.

Equal character-class twins such as corp-[A-Z]+[A-Z]+ are valid custom redaction patterns. Tightening adjacent-repeat checks on the shared compiler would drop those patterns from redactSensitiveText. Shared compileSafeRegex keeps those twins. Exec stays fail-closed so they cannot hang command authorization.

Braced Unicode \u{hex} is a code point only when flags include u or v. Without those flags, \u{2} is identity u plus {2}, so ^(\u{2}|u)+$ is overlapping (uu|u)+ and must be rejected.

Disjoint mixed alternatives of equal consumed length such as ab|[c]d must stay accepted. An unconditional mixed-structure fallback treated corp-(ab|[c]d)+ as overlapping even though both branches consume two characters and are disjoint. That dropped custom redaction and let Doctor delete ^(ab|[c]d)+$. Shared analysis now compares equal-length atom sequences. Exec stays fail-closed on unsafe overlap such as (aa|a.)+ and (a+)+.

The mixed extractor must not treat every simple token as one consumed character. No-flag \141 is octal a and \x61 is hex a, so ^(\141\x61|aaaa)+$ is overlapping (aa|aaaa)+. Splitting \141 into \1, 4, 1 made 4 versus a look disjoint and let that ReDoS reach native matching. Decode complete escapes, or mark unknown-width atoms unproven, before positional disjointness.

Safe capturing wrappers such as ((ab)|(cd))+ must stay accepted. Both branches are fixed-width and disjoint. Treating group tokens as unknown overlap dropped corp-((ab)|(cd))+ from custom redaction and let Doctor delete ^((ab)|(cd))+$. Unwrap those groups. Conservative uncertainty is not grounds for deletion.

Decoded scalars must keep literal identity when overlap probing re-parses them as regex source. \x24 is `$`, not an end-anchor, so ^(\x24a|[$]a)+$ must reject. `\.` is a literal dot, not a wildcard, so corp-(\.a|[b]a)+ must stay accepted and still mask. Legacy octal first digit 4-7 consumes at most two digits, so \400 is \40 plus literal 0 and ^(\400| 0)+$ must reject.

Two-digit and three-digit numeric escapes are backreferences when that capture exists. The two-digit high-octal rule treated \40 as space even with 40 capturing groups, so ^ + 39 empty groups + (a)(\40b|abab)+$ compared space-plus-b with abab and accepted. Native JavaScript repeats overlapping ab|abab. Count captures before decoding decimal escapes, or keep potentially valid backreferences unproven. Same for three-digit \141 when capture 141 exists.

Escaped dollars in alternatives are literals. corp-(a\$|b[!])+ is a safe disjoint two-char pair. Stripping the final `$` from a\$ left a dangling escape, so atom extraction failed and the fallback rejected. Redaction then stopped masking corp-a$b!, and Doctor deleted the equivalent approval. Strip only actual anchor tokens.

Safe nested alternatives such as corp-((ab|cd)e|(fg|hi)j)+ have disjoint fixed-width languages (abe, cde, fgj, hij). Atom extraction used to return null at the inner `|` and the overlap fallback marked the outer `+` unsafe. Custom redaction then dropped the pattern, and Doctor deleted the equivalent anchored approval. Expand inner group alternatives into finite sequences so those languages stay accepted.

Unequal-length alternatives are not ReDoS by length alone. ^(a|[b]c)+$ safely matches abc because the first characters are disjoint, so repetition is unambiguous. An unconditional unequal-length return labeled that rule unsafe, so exec denied it and Doctor deleted it. Check prefix disjointness first. Prefix overlap such as (a|aa)+ still rejects.

Property escapes are flag-dependent. Without u or v, \p{L} is identity p plus {L}, so ^(\p{L}a|p\{L\}ap\{L\}a)+$ is overlapping (p{L}a|p{L}ap{L}a)+. Tokenizing \p{L} as one Unicode atom and probing it with u compared a versus { and accepted that hang. Decode property escapes with the actual flags before positional comparison.

Analysis budget exhaustion is not the same as an unsafe pattern. The 32-atom cap used to abort extraction for ^([a] + 32 b's | [c] + 32 d's)+$ even though the first characters are disjoint. Keep truncated prefixes so proven-disjoint languages stay accepted. Equal-length truncated prefixes that already overlap, such as 33 versus 66 copies of [a]a{32}, are proven overlap and must reject.

Decoded non-ASCII scalars must keep that identity in the selected probe mode. Flag selection removes u, so emitting \u{e9} made ^(\u00E9a|[é]a)+$ look disjoint. Emit \xNN or \uXXXX instead.

The 16-sequence expansion cap is unproven, not overlap. ^((a|b|c|d|e|f|g|h|i|j|k|l|m|n|o|p|q)x|zx)+$ is disjoint fixed-width. Returning unsafe at that cap dropped custom redaction and let Doctor delete the stored rule. Returning no-overlap at that cap is also wrong: ^((a|...|q)x|axax)+$ never compared ax with axax, so repeating ax plus a failing suffix reached native matching. Collapse single-atom unions so the 17-way |x versus zx rule stays accepted and the axax prefix language still rejects. Leftover overflow is not permission to execute.

Incomplete equal prefixes are not proven overlap. p=[a] plus 31 a's, then p+b versus p+c, is fixed-width disjoint. Both truncated to the same 32 atoms. Unconditional true deleted that stored rule and dropped custom redaction. Keep a stored continuation atom so b versus c stays disjoint, while 33 versus 66 overlapping [a]a{32} prefixes still reject.

Shared Unicode atoms must be compared as languages. A class containing U+0100 versus a U+0100 literal (each followed by ASCII a, then repeated) share that code point, but the finite probe set never visits it, so first positions looked disjoint and redaction compiled it. Probe characters named by each atom. Disjoint [猫]|[犬] stays accepted on the shared compiler. Exec's stricter unprobed fallback does not protect redaction.

Overlap probes must inherit the s flag. ^(.a|\na\na)+$ with s lets dot consume newline, so the branches overlap. Comparing them without s declared them disjoint.

Exec approvals keep a stricter unprobed-Unicode fail-closed helper that is not part of the public plugin SDK. Runtime still refuses those conservative patterns. Doctor --fix must not delete a stored manual rule that the shared compiler accepts. Only unsafe or invalid entries are removed. Detect must not create or migrate shared approval state.

The same persisted allowlist is also evaluated by the native macOS app. Node and JavaScriptCore share compileExecArgPattern.

Ref #90014

## Evidence


Latest head [`01fb611710d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01fb611710dc053b65805ba24663fea7d02a7036). Isolated worktree `/tmp/oc-82950`. Shared compiler keeps disjoint overflow `^((aa|bb|...|qq)|zz)+$` and mixed class `^([0\p{Script=Greek}]|[1])+$` with `u`. Exec still refuses those (Doctor-conservative). Overlapping `\p{L}` vs `[0\p{Script=Greek}]` still rejects. Native `ExecArgPatternSafetyJS.generated.swift` regenerated. `pnpm check:exec-arg-pattern:swift` exits 0.


Live production proof on isolated OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR (not ~/.openclaw). Called production compileSafeRegexDetailed, compileSafeRegexForExec, compileExecArgPattern, matchAllowlist, redactSensitiveText, collectRejectedExecArgPatterns, and repairRejectedExecArgPatterns.

```console
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-82950-state-iJFEBC HOME=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-82950-state-iJFEBC node --import tsx /tmp/proof-82950-rev83.mjs
STATE_DIR /var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-82950-state-iJFEBC
COMPILE
two-char-overflow shared=unsafe-nested-repetition exec=unsafe-nested-repetition execArg=unsafe-nested-repetition
seventeen-way shared=accepted exec=accepted execArg=accepted
truncated-disjoint-32 shared=accepted exec=accepted execArg=accepted
greek-letter-u shared=unsafe-nested-repetition exec=unsafe-nested-repetition
truncated-overlap shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
e-acute shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
nested-plus shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
ALLOWLIST two-char-overflow refused
ALLOWLIST seventeen matched
ALLOWLIST truncated-disjoint-32 matched
REDACT two-char-overflow id=corp-axaxax
REDACT seventeen id=corp-ax***
REDACT truncated-disjoint-32 id=corp-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaabaaaaaa…aaac
REDACT greek-letter id=corp-αaαa
DOCTOR removed 2 /bin/unsafe,/bin/two-char-overflow
DOCTOR remaining /bin/seventeen-way /bin/truncated-disjoint /bin/truncated-disjoint-32 /bin/long-disjoint /bin/safe
```

Two-character expansion overflow stays refused and visible in redaction. Incomplete 32-repeat prefixes with disjoint suffixes still mask and stay stored. Letter versus Script=Greek under u stays refused. 17-way, truncated 31, long disjoint, and nested plus keep their prior outcomes.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Shared compilation no longer treats incomplete equal prefixes as proven overlap, no longer treats expansion overflow as safe, and no longer declares unobserved Unicode property languages disjoint.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Node v26.8.2, OpenClaw worktree on fix/exec-approval-redos-guard at b8d332b9bbe, isolated OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-82950-state-iJFEBC (not ~/.openclaw).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Set OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR to a fresh temp directory. Called production compileSafeRegexDetailed, compileSafeRegexForExec, compileExecArgPattern, matchAllowlist, and redactSensitiveText on the three remaining cases plus the keep set (17-way, truncated 31, é, truncated 33 versus 66, s flag, nested plus). Seeded persisted exec approvals through production saveExecApprovals, then ran production collectRejectedExecArgPatterns and repairRejectedExecArgPatterns. Command: node --import tsx /tmp/proof-82950-rev83.mjs from the patched worktree.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the isolated production run:

  ```console
  STATE_DIR .../oc-82950-state-iJFEBC
  two-char-overflow shared=unsafe-nested-repetition exec=unsafe-nested-repetition
  seventeen-way shared=accepted exec=accepted
  truncated-disjoint-32 shared=accepted exec=accepted
  greek-letter-u shared=unsafe-nested-repetition exec=unsafe-nested-repetition
  truncated-overlap shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
  e-acute shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
  nested-plus shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
  ALLOWLIST two-char-overflow refused
  ALLOWLIST seventeen matched
  ALLOWLIST truncated-disjoint-32 matched
  REDACT two-char-overflow id=corp-axaxax
  REDACT seventeen id=corp-ax***
  REDACT truncated-disjoint-32 id=corp-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaabaaaaaa…aaac
  REDACT greek-letter id=corp-αaαa
  DOCTOR removed 2 /bin/unsafe,/bin/two-char-overflow
  DOCTOR remaining /bin/seventeen-way /bin/truncated-disjoint /bin/truncated-disjoint-32 /bin/long-disjoint /bin/safe
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Two-character expansion overflow no longer authorizes `axax`. Incomplete 32-repeat prefixes with disjoint `b`/`c` suffixes stay stored and still mask. Unprobed Letter versus Script=Greek overlap no longer compiles as disjoint under `u`. Nested plus, é overlap, and truncated 33 versus 66 still refuse.
- **What was not tested:** Live click-through in the shipping menu-bar app against a private production allowlist. A published npm release upgrade on a user machine. Current native JavaScriptCore matching of this HEAD.

## Summary

Fixes remaining Revision 83 P1s: reject two-character expansion overflow ((ax|...|qx)|axax)+, keep truncated equal prefixes p+b versus p+c after 32 atoms, and fail closed when Unicode property languages are not both observed so Letter versus Script=Greek with u rejects without banning [猫]|[犬]. Prior 17-way accept, long disjoint accept, é overlap reject, truncated 33 versus 66 reject, s flag overlap reject, and (a+)+ reject still hold. Native matcher still shares compileExecArgPattern. Detect stays read-only. Repair stays on updateExecApprovalsSync.

Ref #90014

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix(agents): prevent unknown models after creating secondary agents
prs.body:
Closes #58289

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a secondary agent created through `agents.create` can fail with `Unknown model` when its selected custom model exists only in the configured system agent's `models.json`.

## User Impact

User impact: secondary agents without a local catalog can use the system agent's custom model inventory while retaining their own authentication; existing secondary catalogs remain authoritative, and no secondary `models.json` is created, copied, or overwritten.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepared model runtimes now use the configured system agent's catalog as a read-only fallback only when the secondary agent has no local `models.json`. The fallback participates in runtime identity and worker serialization so startup and on-demand discovery agree.

The inherited catalog is inventory, not credential authority. It is parsed with the same JSONC-compatible parser as `ModelRegistry`; provider API keys plus authorization, cookie, and token-like provider/model headers are removed. Safe route headers are preserved only for the matching provider/model/transport route, and current runtime configuration still wins. Embedded transport now forwards the sanitized headers returned by model resolution, while authentication remains request-scoped to the secondary agent.

## Evidence

The September 22 follow-up, `2243dfbc60`, changes only `test/pr58373-secondary-catalog.e2e.test.ts`, adding the missing credential-free rejection proof. No production behavior changed in this follow-up.

- Real Gateway E2E: **1/1 passed** locally with Node 24.20.0. Command: `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr58373-secondary-catalog.e2e.test.ts`. The full prerequisite build had completed successfully from this candidate's unchanged production sources (11/11 TypeScript stages, 92 plugins, CLI bootstrap guard, and runtime postbuild); the successful run reused those artifacts.
- The real flow creates the secondary agent through `agents.create`, verifies its catalog is absent, restarts the Gateway, executes account B, and reassigns the secondary auth profile to account C without another restart. Both requests succeed and the loopback provider receives exactly two requests using B then C, preserving safe route headers and excluding stale Authorization/Cookie headers.
- **New negative final-effect proof:** after those successful requests, the test clears both main/shared and secondary/local auth profile stores through the normal store API. The custom provider has no configured API key or environment credential mapping. With the same Gateway/session and stale credential headers still present in the inherited JSONC catalog, the third turn settles through `agent.wait` with `status: "error"` and `No API key found for provider "mock-openai".`. The provider request count remains **exactly 2**, proving zero additional provider HTTP requests in the credential-free turn.
- The main catalog remains byte-for-byte unchanged, and the secondary `models.json` remains absent after all three turns.
- Focused regression tests: **72/72 passed** across `prepared-model-runtime.sources.test.ts`, `stream-resolution.test.ts`, and `stream-resolution.request-headers.test.ts` on this follow-up candidate.
- Targeted formatting, lint, both line-count ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh independent review of this test change found no P0-P2 issues; the repository AutoReview engine was unavailable, so that tool is not reported as passing.
- Full test-root typechecking was started but interrupted to prioritize the covering E2E; it is **not** reported as passed. Hosted CI and maintainer approval remain separate gates, not implied by the local proof.

## Remaining gates

- Hosted checks must be evaluated on the newly pushed head. Earlier unrelated-area CI failures are not proof that the new run passes, nor have they been proven to reproduce on the base revision.
- Maintainer approval of the security-sensitive change is still required for the exact head. This contributor update does not supply or bypass that approval.

prs.title: fix: preserve subagent completion delivery outcomes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading blocked-completion warnings and duplicate retry attempts when a subagent's result handoff succeeds but receipt bookkeeping fails.

## User Impact

Confirmed subagent results remain delivered. Real delivery failures retain their concrete cause across retries, and blocked warnings identify the affected child run. No configuration or migration is required; unconfirmed handoffs are not treated as delivered.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the transport outcome before notifying the receipt observer, report otherwise-unreported exceptions through the existing retryability policy, and preserve the delivery owner's error during cleanup. This keeps transport confirmation authoritative without weakening source-owner checks.

Reported and requested by @steipete.

- 413 focused tests passed across announcement delivery, announcement flow, registry lifecycle, completion queue receipts, and the announce-loop guard.
- Regression tests reproduced concrete-error loss and receipt-callback delivery regression on the original code; the concrete-error negative control failed as expected and the fixed source was restored before final validation.
- Production and affected session-test typecheck graphs passed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep wizard step authority through setup-inference probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

macOS Companion setup failed at the setup-inference probe with "Gateway caller authority is no longer active", every time on the same connection, so onboarding could not finish (#168553).

## Why This Change Was Made

The hosted setup wizard's runner captured operator authority from the `wizard.start` request. That request's authority hold is released when `wizard.start` responds, so later step work (the setup-inference probe captures authority at `src/gateway/operator-run-authority.ts:295`) ran against an expired hold and threw from `src/gateway/device-revocation.ts:281`. The wizard owner now refreshes its scope from the answering `wizard.next` request and retains that authority until the runner settles, including after progress replies. Revocation checks are unchanged: a revoked device still fails.

## User Impact

Companion/wizard onboarding can complete the setup-inference step. No config or migration changes.

## Evidence

- Three regressions (normal completion; completion after an early progress reply; revoked device still rejected) fail before the fix and pass after.
- Changed-file checks passed 21 steps; independent review found no P0–P2 issues.
- Production +15 LOC, tests +179, docs +1.
- Left to PR CI: importing suites and core typecheck, which did not finish locally because the host was overloaded (declaration build stalled).

Fixes #168553

prs.title: fix(state): admit same-version columns before session readers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway startup and session reads after an update adds same-version session columns while an older clean-close seal carries completed validation facts without those columns. Related: #171449 and #171038.

## User Impact

Each affected agent stays unavailable until the existing writable startup owner installs its required additive columns. Readers then use the admitted catalog. The schema version, stored column definitions, and deployment authority remain unchanged; no operator SQL repair is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

One declaration set now drives the same-version installer, pending-repair detection, compatibility inspection, and seal identity. Seal loading checks the saved catalog before publishing any completed-validation facts. Startup inspection defers same-version repair to writable preparation, and cold readers refuse pending repairs before compiling session queries. Unchanged compatible builds retain seal reuse without validation SQL.

## Evidence

The synthetic regression models five previously sealed agent databases missing both row-transcript columns, including a matching current seal identity. It exercises startup readiness, the actual writable admission owner, and the production transcript-row query. Every agent must remain fenced until preparation succeeds; both columns must then exist and the query must run without a reader error.

A second behavioral guard enumerates columns actually installed by the same-version installer and verifies that withholding each one is detected by admission facts. A third guard verifies that additive requirements alone change seal identity. Existing unchanged-seal startup proof verifies no snapshots or comparison templates.

Validation: changed-file oxfmt, repository core lint, focused single-worker tests. PR CI owns typecheck, broader lanes, and full gates. No Testbox/Crabbox lease or live database was used. This is an urgent correctness repair; no large-state timing benchmark or live deployment was performed. Production source LOC delta: +30 lines (84 added, 54 removed). This correctness repair grows only to establish the required seal/catalog precondition and cold-reader refusal, while deleting the separate per-column pending checks.

Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), clean after correcting version-refusal ordering and adding its regression. The autoreview preflight refused the requested provider because it did not match the operator's active configuration; configuration was left unchanged.

Local proof: 14 tests passed across the three changed test files. The fleet regression took 5.67 s; the migration file took 0.18 s test time; seal-identity tests took 0.04 s. The focused command took 91.24 s including compiler-cache preparation on the saturated Mac. CI test seconds will be recorded when available.

Before/after: the same incident regression on the unchanged original production code fails with `no such column: row_transcript_window.row_transcript_json`; after the repair, all five stores complete writable preparation and transcript reads succeed. Existing matching-seal startup continues to use zero snapshots and zero comparison templates.

Export-name collision guard passed.

Additional focused proof: export-name collision guard passed; both required source/eager closure files passed (20 tests); the agent integrity-cache sibling passed (10 tests). Total focused proof: 44 tests across six files. The extra command took 226.85 s including cached worker preparation and the unchanged wrapper closure contracts.

CI follow-up: the older pending-input tests assumed reads were permitted before their same-version writer/Doctor/first-use repair. They now assert the required pre-admission refusal, then verify input preservation after each repair path. The whole file passed locally (9 tests), and independent review found the cutover clean. Total local focused proof is 53 tests across seven files. The first CI run also missed the restart-handoff E2E's five-second shutdown bound (5,450 ms); no restart behavior or timing limit was changed to address that result.

prs.title: fix(agents): avoid false Windows local service shutdown failures
prs.body:
Closes #171472.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed local-model shutdown on Windows can reject an already-closed service while its process-tree termination helper is still completing.

## User Impact

Local services remain owned until bounded termination work and final exit confirmation settle. Existing timeouts, tree-liveness checks, and protection against signaling a replacement PID remain intact. No configuration or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The local service's two-second forced-exit observation could finish before Windows taskkill's three-second completion contract. Join the signaling owner's completion promises before starting final exit observation, rather than treating outstanding helper work as proof of a surviving service.

## Evidence

Initial CI failed only an inherited Gateway-fixture mock-export guard, already repaired on main by [e7a07c5aee57](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e7a07c5aee577be3a2425ec4d88cad17813b7505). This branch was refreshed to pinned main `4aa62334122e` for that concrete blocker. Range-diff confirms an identical Windows patch, with its direct owner/test/dependency inputs unchanged; the original focused proof and review are reused. The repaired native guard passes.

- Both controlled regressions fail before the fix and pass afterward, using real provider lifecycle and signal owners with fixed process/health I/O.
- Final settlement file: 6 passed, 2.13s Vitest / 12.93s wall. All four real shutdown siblings passed, including stubborn descendants, replacement ownership, and recovery.
- Agents-root typecheck, targeted lint/format, and mock-export validation passed. Independent AutoReview through P2 on the original patch: no findings; reused after the patch-identical base refresh, not claimed as a new review.
- Native Windows execution was not run locally; unrelated local VMs were not changed. Current-head hosted coverage is determined by the selected CI plan.
- Additional provider breadth was 30/31 passing: the unchanged healthy-external-process socket-close assertion at `provider-local-service.test.ts:477` also failed alone. That flow never reaches the edited shutdown owner. This inherited/unresolved failure is not counted as a passing check.
- Current head `b147f288607b` has [passing ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38491297159), including the repaired baseline ratchet, and [passing dependency/security review and aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38492355281). The native Windows matrix job was skipped, so Windows OS execution is still unverified.
- [User-requested ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171498#issuecomment-6158596848) completed on exact head `b147f288607b5d88c71bd5ac1015f2f460a99c4f`: 0 findings, P2, no before-merge blockers. The review also retains the missing native Windows proof.

## Release Consideration

This is a narrow production reliability repair, not only a test flake: a false cleanup failure can abort managed-provider recovery/reacquisition or cancel a foreground update. Remote-only providers do not enter the edited owner. Incident frequency, actual surviving Windows processes and native Windows after-fix execution remain unproven; no P0/security or broad P1 outage is established.

Recommend planned backports after main landing to the next `release/2026.10.5` candidate and the eligible `extended-stable/2026.9.33` maintenance set. Both retain the affected owner. The full patch applies to 10.5; September needs its existing shutdown API in the tests and no absent mock-export baseline row. Published stable 10.3 is also affected, but a separate hotfix/re-cut of active frozen qualification is not proposed here. No release branch or frozen candidate was changed by this assessment.

prs.title: fix(openshell): exclude nested .git from mirror sync
prs.body:
## Summary
The OpenShell docs say workspace synchronization excludes `.git`, `hooks`, and `git-hooks` in both directions so repository credentials, history, and trusted hook code stay on the Gateway host (`docs/gateway/openshell.md`, "Security hardening"). The mirror only applied that list to the workspace root. A nested repository such as `sub/.git` (its `config` and `hooks/`) was mirrored from the sandbox onto the host and staged from the host into the sandbox upload. When the sandbox deleted the parent directory, the host's nested `.git` was deleted as well.

This is a docs mismatch and hardening fix: nested `.git` now gets the same treatment as the root `.git`.

## Root cause
`extensions/openshell/src/mirror.ts`, `reconcileMirrorDirectory` filters entries with `excludeDirs`, but the recursion through `reconcileMirrorPath` drops the list, so every level below the root runs with no exclusions:

```ts
// before
const preservedEntries = await reconcileMirrorDirectory({
  sourceDir,
  targetDir: params.targetPath,
  replace: params.replace,
});
```

Both `replaceDirectoryContents` (sandbox to host) and `stageDirectoryContents` (host to sandbox upload) route through this one function, so both directions were affected.

## Fix
`reconcileMirrorDirectory` passes `.git` down the recursion when the caller excludes it, and counts excluded target entries as preserved so a remote delete or file replacement does not remove the directory that holds them:

```ts
// after
const nestedExcludeDirs = params.excludeDirs?.filter((dir) =>
  NESTED_MIRROR_EXCLUDE_DIRS.has(normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(dir)),
);
...
excludeDirs: nestedExcludeDirs,
...
let preservedEntries = targetEntries.some(isExcluded);
```

Depth semantics follow what each entry names:
- `.git` is repository metadata wherever a repository lives, so it matches by name at every depth.
- `hooks` and `git-hooks` name the workspace hook directories. Workspace hooks load only from `<workspace>/hooks` (`src/hooks/workspace.ts`), and the original exclusion (#54657) targeted that root directory. They stay root-scoped, so ordinary nested source folders such as `src/hooks` keep syncing. Matching them at every depth would silently stop syncing common application code.

The docs paragraph now states these semantics explicitly.

## Why this is the right boundary
`reconcileMirrorDirectory` is the single shared walker for both sync directions, so one change covers download and upload staging. Workspace-root matching stays case-insensitive. Nested names match `.git` exactly, without trimming or case normalization, so ordinary names such as ` .git ` remain synchronized. Callers that do not pass `.git` in `excludeDirs` see no change. The workdir validation in `backend.ts` (`validateMirrorWorkdir`) still checks only the first path segment. That check rejects exec workdirs inside root excluded directories and does not copy files, so I left it unchanged.

## Verification
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openshell/src/mirror.test.ts`: with `mirror.ts` reverted to `upstream/main` 9a18261098 the two new cases fail (`Tests 2 failed | 12 passed (14)`); with the patch, `Tests 14 passed (14)`, file duration 6.54s. After the warning commit, `Tests 15 passed (15)` on head 66bcec0576.
- New cases: a sandbox file colliding with a host directory holding `.git` keeps the directory and warns once with the path, nested `.git/hooks` is not copied to the host, a nested `hooks` source folder still syncs, a host nested `.git` survives the sandbox deleting its parent, and nested `.git/config` is not staged for upload.
- Follow-up verification below adds a real extension `tsgo` check on the earlier head. Local lint and `tsgo` were not re-run for the rebase and warning commit; hosted CI covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: OpenShell mirror sync copied nested repository metadata (`sub/.git/config`, `sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit`) in both directions and deleted a host nested `.git` when the sandbox removed or replaced its parent, although the docs say `.git` is excluded in both directions. When a sandbox file collides with a host directory that holds `.git`, the host directory is now kept and a warning names the skipped path, so the mismatch is no longer silent.
Real environment tested: macOS, Node 26.9.0, head `66bcec0576b4867f191f8406c4f8a99c25c4049b` rebased on `origin/main` `ebc4e6de603c5c1ce55086f13565e21feb1c297d`. The real exported `replaceDirectoryContents` and `stageDirectoryContents` were driven with `DEFAULT_OPEN_SHELL_MIRROR_EXCLUDE_DIRS` against real temporary directories on disk, first with `mirror.ts` from `origin/main` `ebc4e6de60` and then with this head. No sandbox CLI or SSH transport was involved; the on-disk filesystem, the production mirror walker, and the production subsystem logger stayed real.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `tsx drive-proof.mts base|patch`, a standalone driver that seeds `sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit`, `sub/.git/config`, `sub/src/hooks/useThing.ts`, and `sub/README.md`, runs sandbox-to-host `replaceDirectoryContents` and host-to-sandbox `stageDirectoryContents`, then runs a replace where the sandbox has a plain file `sub` and the host has `sub/.git/HEAD` plus `sub/notes.txt`, and prints whether each path exists. Same driver and inputs for both runs; only `mirror.ts` was swapped. Temp paths shortened to `$TMPDIR`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (origin/main ebc4e6de60)
sandbox -> host (replaceDirectoryContents)
  host/sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit: present
  host/sub/.git/config: present
  host/sub/src/hooks/useThing.ts: present
  host/sub/README.md: present
host -> sandbox upload stage (stageDirectoryContents)
  stage/sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit: present
  stage/sub/.git/config: present
  stage/sub/src/hooks/useThing.ts: present
  stage/sub/README.md: present
sandbox file sub vs host directory sub/.git (replaceDirectoryContents)
  host/sub type: file
  host/sub/.git/HEAD: absent
  host/sub/notes.txt: absent
# AFTER (head 66bcec0576, identical inputs)
sandbox -> host (replaceDirectoryContents)
  host/sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit: absent
  host/sub/.git/config: absent
  host/sub/src/hooks/useThing.ts: present
  host/sub/README.md: present
host -> sandbox upload stage (stageDirectoryContents)
  stage/sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit: absent
  stage/sub/.git/config: absent
  stage/sub/src/hooks/useThing.ts: present
  stage/sub/README.md: present
[openshell] mirror kept host directory $TMPDIR/oc-proof-QsGqjB/host2/sub because it contains preserved host entries; skipped the sandbox file at that path.
sandbox file sub vs host directory sub/.git (replaceDirectoryContents)
  host/sub type: directory
  host/sub/.git/HEAD: present
  host/sub/notes.txt: absent
```
Observed result after fix: nested `.git` content no longer crosses the mirror in either direction. Ordinary nested files, including a nested `src/hooks` folder, still sync. When the sandbox has a file where the host has a directory holding `.git`, main replaced the directory and lost the host Git metadata; this head keeps the directory and its `.git`, removes the other stale host entries, and emits one warning naming the skipped path.
What was not tested: no live OpenShell gateway or sandbox round trip over SSH (`pnpm test:e2e:openshell` needs Docker and a local OpenShell gateway); Windows case-insensitive paths were not exercised beyond the existing lowercase matcher.

## File vs preserved directory decision
Maintainer question: if the sandbox has a plain file `sub` and the host has `sub/` containing `.git`, should the mirror replace or preserve? This PR preserves and now warns. Reasoning: main already applies the same rule to host entries the mirror cannot represent (symlinks, FIFOs, sockets): "A remote file cannot replace a directory containing preserved host entries." Host `.git` is now one of those preserved entries, so the same rule applies, and the sandbox cannot delete host repository metadata by replacing its parent with a file. The new `log.warn` in `reconcileMirrorPath` names the kept host directory and says the sandbox file was skipped, so the divergence is visible. The docs paragraph states this behavior. If maintainers prefer source-wins replacement, that is a one-branch change in `reconcileMirrorPath`, but it would let the sandbox delete host Git metadata, which is what this PR is meant to stop.

## Exact-name follow-up verification
Contributor commits and credit are retained. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

On candidate `9eab39c8a0d756d7b12ae9d6e76ecd6eb03cea14` (runtime and test sources unchanged from `5b48d963db77f677ead9a30679eefbd98cbbffc7`), a secretless Linux/Node 24 container exercised the production `replaceDirectoryContents` and `stageDirectoryContents` entry points used by `backend.ts:995` and `backend.ts:1048`. The baseline used the mirror owner from current main `e7546f2e40cc1d75d3a253fae40243be0eea8548`. Both used the same real-filesystem driver and a real `git init` at `sub/repo`.

| Control | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nested `sub/repo/.git` mirrored/staged | yes | no |
| Submodule-style `.git` file mirrored/staged | yes | no |
| Root `.git` mirrored/staged | no | no |
| Normal-file checksums identical in both directions | yes | yes |
| Ordinary nested ` .git ` file copied | yes | yes |

SHA-256 listings were identical at source, download target, and upload stage on both versions:
```text
d7379507842868a936d38e05b250f8409cd5773edf03515312477243ccd85ed2  README
d614708341dc1c9880a1c3b44c47864dc9756bbfd0a0c1206e733ca4552e8b30  sub/ .git 
ee40a44130b3386b475b0a3ed6a811f9bd3c5c343eb69c00eb45a5272be02b2c  sub/linked/normal.txt
7f5996bcec7b8b4992b8bb5de78bb7696e6e7698393eaddf78a157149817ca14  sub/repo/normal.txt
```

Ancestor replacement control: with a source plain file `sub` and target directory `sub/.git`, main replaced the directory with the file. Candidate preserved the target directory and Git metadata, did not copy the replacement file, and left the source file unchanged. This deliberately preserves host Git metadata; no ordinary files were lost in this control.

- Original PR tests against main's mirror owner: 2 failures, 12 passes (nested metadata unexpectedly present).
- Spaced-name regression against contributor head `d4a16dc8607`: 2 failures, 12 passes (`ENOENT` reading `sub/ .git `).
- Candidate: all 14 tests pass, 4.66-second Vitest duration, 6.22-second wrapper wall time. Existing cases extended; no new process fixture or test added.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: passed.
- Real OpenAI call through the candidate AI runtime: `gpt-5-mini`, reasoning low, max output 4096; returned `MIRROR_GATE_OK` with stop reason `stop` (14 input, 52 output tokens).

Limit: this is the real filesystem owner, not a Gateway/SSH/OpenShell service round trip. That requires an installed OpenShell CLI, reachable OpenShell gateway, and supported compute runtime. This isolated environment has no OpenShell CLI, gateway registration, or Docker daemon; sharing the host Docker socket or running privileged is not allowed. OpenShell supports local gateways without a paid account, but no isolated local gateway deployment is available here. The repository's `test:e2e:openshell` requires those same prerequisites.

Final-head documentation repair: replaced whitespace-bearing inline code with explicit prose because Markdown formatting removes the delimiter-adjacent spaces. Scoped `oxfmt --check` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed; the live provider gate also passed again on final head. The prior head’s `check-lint` and `check-docs` formatting failures were caused by this PR and are repaired, not claimed as inherited.

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover ACP-only stores after slow startup
prs.body:
Fixes #171395

## What Problem This Solves

Configured ACP-only session stores could block slow Gateway startup or remain degraded afterward because deferred admission required native auth and model publications they never receive.

## User Impact

Healthy ACP-only stores configured through `acp.defaultAgent`, `acp.allowedAgents`, or an ACP runtime alias can finish preparation in the background and become available without restarting the Gateway. Native agents retain their auth/model prerequisites; database ownership, migration, cancellation, deletion and configured-path checks remain in place. No configuration or schema migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preflight now uses the existing configured session-store inventory for deferred scheduling and ownership inspection. After database and session preparation, the Gateway requires native publications only for IDs in the native roster. Configuration is read after the lazy imports, avoiding a stale snapshot across that await; superseded native publication still uses the bounded retry from #171054.

Original fix by @ericcaiwx-star; maintainer cleanup simplifies the native-owner check, removes the additional import wait, consolidates the duplicate slow-start fixture, and documents ACP-only recovery. Thanks to @potterdigital for the incident report.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. Local tests, typechecks, negative controls and live Gateway proof were intentionally skipped; no Crabbox/Testbox lease was created. The contributor's earlier live/upgrade results apply to their original head, not the revised candidate.

Regression coverage run by CI:

- `admits configured ACP-only stores without native runtime publication` checks that deferred ACP-only admission clears without native secrets/model publication.
- `keeps pending ACP-only stores fenced without inspecting or copying them again in bootstrap` checks the five-second foreground cutoff, the pending refusal, and bootstrap reuse. The same table retains the native-store case.
- Existing preparation cases cover native auth/model publication, bounded config/secrets supersession, failed preparation, deletion and shutdown.

Changed-file `oxfmt` and core `oxlint` pass; `git diff --check` passes. Lint uses the parent checkout's installed tools and the core rules, with only the non-applicable UI plugin override omitted because that plugin is absent from the parent install. No dependency installation or local typecheck was performed.

Autoreview: isolated Codex branch review completed `scoped-clean` through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings. The final candidate source was reviewed before commit; no tests were executed by the reviewer.

CI: [run 38501534003](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501534003) **passed** for exact head `9116e2d79d48c6cfded8e54005a7f4e0c110f4fb`: 46 successful jobs, 28 intentionally skipped, zero failures. This includes changed test shards, production and test typechecks, core lint, documentation, baseline ratchets and `openclaw/ci-gate`. `origin/main` (`976cc974fab1`) was merged without rebasing before push; the five changed files are byte-identical to the reviewed candidate.

Original CI attribution: run [38493790464](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38493790464) failed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (job 115625205627) on the untouched `worker-turn-launcher.lazy.test.ts:212` mock-export check; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` reflected that failure. Scheduled main run [38493374007](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38493374007/job/115623794517) failed on the identical file/check. Main fixed it in `4a8b9b5b1d3d`; the later scheduled-main baseline job [115634308885](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38496717898/job/115634308885) passed. Neither original red was caused by this PR.

ClawSweeper revision 6 reviewed exact head `9116e2d79d48` and found no actionable code issues; there were no human review findings. Its sole remaining request is revised-head live Gateway/upgrade/negative-control proof. That proof-only request is intentionally not followed under Peter's October 13, 2026 override: PR CI is the proof gate, and no live Gateway, lease or local test/typecheck execution is permitted. Earlier missing-publication and scheduling concerns are covered by both owner changes and the regressions above.

Scope versus main: production +10/-4 (net +6), tests +88/-53 (net +35), docs +5/-0. The small production increase expresses the two distinct ownership contracts without weakening admission checks or adding unrelated cleanup. Tests use controlled promises and fake time; no new real timer waits. Local test wall times were not measured under the maintainer policy; CI owns execution timing.
