prs.title: fix(cron): stop gateway restarts from spending a job's auto-disable budget
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cron/heartbeat job that was `running` when the gateway died is repaired on startup by `markInterruptedStartupRun`, which recorded the interruption as an ordinary failed run: `lastErrorReason` was cleared to `undefined`, `consecutiveErrors` was incremented, and `maybeAutoDisableCronJobAfterRunFailure` was then applied to the inflated streak. Ten gateway restarts that happened to land on a long-running job therefore auto-disabled a perfectly healthy schedule, leaving exactly the same evidence trail as a job that is genuinely broken. The comment on `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_RUN_FAILURES` even documented "restart-interrupted runs count too" as intended behaviour — but a job meant to simply resume on its next natural tick after an interruption should never be disabled by that interruption.

## Why This Change Was Made

An interruption is infrastructure dying, not the job failing, so it must not be counted as evidence against the job. Two report-only scheduler facts now carry that distinction on `CronJobState`:

- `lastRunInterruptionReason` (`"gateway-restart"`) marks the last run as interrupted rather than failed.
- `consecutiveRestartInterruptions` records how much of the current error streak is infrastructure, not genuine failure.

`maybeAutoDisableCronJobAfterRunFailure` subtracts the latter from `consecutiveErrors` before comparing against the auto-disable threshold, via a new `resolveCronJobRunFailureCount` helper.

`consecutiveErrors` itself is deliberately left incrementing: it also feeds retry backoff (`resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs`) and the failure-alert threshold/text, and none of those should change for an interrupted run — only the auto-disable decision needed to learn the difference. Both new fields are added to `CronJobStateSchema` but not to the state patch schema or `CronJobStateInput`, matching `autoDisabled` / `streamSourceIdentity`: the scheduler owns them and callers cannot spoof them.

### The offset must describe the streak it is subtracted from

Because the offset is subtracted from `consecutiveErrors`, it is only meaningful for the streak it accumulated against, and every owner that rewrites that streak has to reconcile it. There are four:

| Owner | Reconciliation |
|---|---|
| `applyJobResult` (a run reports its own outcome) | clears both counters |
| `resetJobFailureState` (explicit re-enable) | clears both counters |
| `applyTriggerNoFireResult` (successful non-firing trigger evaluation) | clears both counters |
| `applyJobPatch` (public `state.consecutiveErrors` patch) | calls `reconcileCronRestartInterruptionOffset`, restoring `consecutiveRestartInterruptions <= consecutiveErrors` |

The patch owner needs the helper rather than an inline zero because it merges a caller-supplied count it cannot inspect first: `consecutiveErrors` is patchable and the offset deliberately is not, so a patch that clears or shortens the streak would otherwise leave the scheduler-owned offset describing a streak that no longer exists. A job that never recorded an interruption keeps the field absent rather than gaining a zero.

## Upgrade and data-model compatibility

A row written before these counters existed can hold `lastError: "cron: job interrupted by gateway restart"` with `consecutiveErrors: 9` — eight genuine failures plus one known interruption — and no offset at all. Defaulting the offset to zero would disable that job on its *ninth* genuine failure.

Doctor's existing migration owner, `normalizeStoredCronJobs`, now attributes the one interruption such a row still proves. `lastError` describes only the most recent run, so exactly one interruption is provable; nothing is guessed about earlier entries in the streak. The normalization reports a `legacyRestartInterruption` issue, so the repair is previewed and offered like every other legacy cron normalization instead of mutating the store silently.

Doctor matches the stored historical error string rather than importing the scheduler's live constant. This is operator data written by older versions and has to stay recognizable even if the live message is reworded, and the module that owns the live constant would pull the whole cron run-outcome graph into Doctor's import surface.

### Persisting the repair without clobbering live runtime state

The repaired fields are *runtime* state, and Doctor's definition write deliberately preserves runtime state: `applyLegacyCronStoreRepair` saves with `preserveRuntimeState: true`, and `upsertCronJobRow` then builds its `onConflict` update from `definitionValues`, which strips `state_json` and `runtime_updated_at_ms` (`src/cron/store/row-codec.ts:501-506`, `:554`). ClawSweeper Revision 4 found the consequence: for a row that already exists the repair was computed and discarded, and the job still auto-disabled on its ninth genuine failure.

Turning the preservation off is not the fix, and neither is writing Doctor's normalized store back wholesale. Doctor's snapshot guard fingerprints definitions only — `fingerprintCronJobRows` hashes `job_id` / `job_json` / `sort_order`, and `readCronJobsFingerprint` is explicitly documented as "reads only definition JSON and order while excluding runtime-owned state" — so Doctor cannot detect a run outcome the scheduler committed while it was waiting. Persisting its earlier read would reintroduce exactly the clobber `preserveRuntimeState` exists to prevent.

So the repair is **re-applied to the row's live state inside the same write transaction**, behind the same pre-repair backup and the same snapshot assertion, through an `afterWrite` transaction hook:

- `src/cron/store/state-repair.ts` (new) — `applyCronJobRuntimeStateRepairs` reads each named row's current `state_json`, runs the caller's repair predicate against it, and writes back only when the predicate still changes something.
- `legacy-repair.ts` passes the normalization's own predicate, and reports the rows it actually persisted (`Recorded a retained gateway-restart interruption on N cron jobs…`), so the change line describes the write rather than the computation.
- `store-migration.ts` exports `normalizeLegacyRestartInterruption` and returns the canonical ids it repaired. The predicate is already a no-op once `consecutiveRestartInterruptions` exists, which is what makes re-application safe and a second `openclaw doctor --fix` inert.
- `scripts/database-worker-inventory.mjs` registers the new module `T3` alongside the `row-codec` cron operations it sits beside, with its Doctor-only caller as evidence. The SQLite worker ratchet reports no T1 call-count growth.

## User Impact

A cron/heartbeat job that happens to be mid-run across several gateway restarts stays enabled. Genuine failures still auto-disable exactly as before — the fix narrows what counts as evidence, it doesn't weaken the auto-disable guard itself.

Jobs written by a release without the counters keep their full remaining budget after `openclaw doctor --fix`, and the repair now survives the reload — see the scenario 6 evidence below, which drives the real Doctor repair/reload boundary rather than asserting on Doctor's in-memory result. A run the scheduler commits between Doctor's read and its write is left intact (scenario 7).

## Evidence

Validated in the branch worktree on head `590e3cbb963`, with linuxbrew git 2.55 shimmed onto `PATH` (see the withdrawal note below) and node 24.18.0.

### Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm check:changed` | **exit 0**, terminal `=== exit[check:changed]=0 ===`, **38 lanes**, zero failures |
| `pnpm tsx scripts/proof-3i95-cron-restart-interrupt-budget.ts` | **7/7 scenarios**, `All runtime assertions passed.` |
| focused vitest, 11 cron + Doctor-cron files | **147 passed / 0 failed** (3 shards: `unit-fast` 44, `cron` 83, `commands` 20) |
| Knip unused-export scans | **0 entries** on script, production and full-tree |
| SQLite worker ratchet | **ok** — no T1 call-count growth; the new module is registered `T3` with its Doctor caller as evidence |
| `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only upstream/main <this head>` | the **same two** conflicting files as the reviewed head `db404548348`, probed before and after the push; this round adds none |

Three lanes went red on the way to that exit and were fixed in this round, all of them this change's own: the **assertion SAFETY comment ratchet** (a `raw.id as string` in `store-migration.ts`, replaced with the file's existing `storedCronJobId` helper), the **SQLite worker ratchet** (the new module's two sync SQL calls counted as main-thread T1 growth until registered), and **format changed files** (`oxfmt` on the new module). Logs `check-changed-1.log` through `check-changed-4.log`.

### Base-fail → head-pass, measured per finding

Each finding was measured with **only that finding's source files reverted**, so neither fix can stand in for the other. Every predicate lives in its own `it`, because one `it` stops at its first failed assertion.

| Reverted | Test file | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto-disable.ts`, `timer-outcomes.ts`, `jobs.ts` | `src/cron/service/auto-disable.restart-interruption-offset.test.ts` | 5 failed / 1 passed | 6 passed |
| `store-migration.ts`, `repair-plan.ts` | `src/commands/doctor/cron/store-migration.restart-interruption.test.ts` | 2 failed / 5 passed | 7 passed |
| `legacy-repair.ts`, `store-migration.ts`, `state-repair.ts` | `src/commands/doctor/cron/legacy-repair.restart-interruption-persistence.test.ts` | 3 failed / 1 passed | 4 passed |

The cases that pass in both columns are the controls: a patch that leaves the streak alone must not touch the offset, and a row with no retained streak, no streak counter, or a genuine last error must get nothing attributed to a restart.

The persistence file has **two** controls, because a test set that only fails without the fix does not show the fix is the *right* one:

- **Control A — this round's source hunks reverted:** 3 failed / 1 passed. The three bug cases fail; the one that passes is `leaves runtime state a writer committed after the snapshot alone`, which is correct — with no write at all there is nothing to clobber.
- **Control B — the naive fix** (persist Doctor's normalized state unconditionally instead of re-applying the predicate to the live row): **1 failed / 3 passed**, and the single failure is exactly that concurrency case.

The two controls partition the four cases, so none of them is decorative: A pins the defect, B pins the design.

### Real behavior proof

`scripts/proof-3i95-cron-restart-interrupt-budget.ts` drives the production `CronService` facade, its real `start()` startup repair, the real on-disk cron store, the real `applyJobResult` / `applyTriggerNoFireResult` run-outcome owners, the real `maybeAutoDisableCronJobAfterRunFailure` budget decision, and — new in this round — Doctor's real `loadLegacyCronRepairState` + `applyLegacyCronStoreRepair`, including its pre-repair backup and snapshot guards. Only `runIsolatedAgentJob` / `enqueueSystemEvent` / `requestHeartbeat` are inert, and scheduling is paused so every outcome is applied explicitly rather than by wall clock.

```
proof-3i95: cron restart interruptions must not spend the auto-disable budget
  scenario 1: survived 12 gateway restarts (consecutiveErrors=12, restartInterruptions=12, enabled=true)
  scenario 2: restart survived, tenth genuine failure auto-disabled with consecutiveErrors=10
  scenario 3: uninterrupted tenth genuine failure still auto-disables
  scenario 4: a completed run clears both the error and interruption streaks
  scenario 5: a quiet trigger tick clears the offset; ten later genuine failures still auto-disable
  scenario 6: doctor --fix persists the upgrade repair; the row keeps its full budget and still disables on the tenth genuine failure
  scenario 7: doctor's repair leaves a run the scheduler committed after the snapshot intact
All runtime assertions passed.
```

**Scenario 6 was rewritten this round and now crosses the boundary it used to skip.** The previous version normalized the row in memory and re-saved it by hand with `saveCronStore`, so it never went through `preserveRuntimeState` and certified a repair the operator's store never received — it passed at the reviewed head while the defect was live. It now seeds the legacy row, runs the real Doctor repair over the already-persisted store, and reads the result **back out of the store** before asserting; it still carries its own in-scenario control (the same row, un-repaired, auto-disabling on its ninth genuine failure) and still checks that the repaired row disables on the tenth.

Scenario 7 is new and pins why the write is a merge rather than a rewrite: the scheduler commits a successful run between Doctor's read and its write, and the repair must leave the cleared streak alone.

With this round's source hunks reverted, the harness exits 1 on scenario 6 with `ASSERTION FAILED: doctor's repaired interruption offset did not survive the existing-row write` — and scenarios 1–5 still pass, so the failure is isolated to the persistence boundary.

### What is NOT proven here

The before-merge end-to-end item stands unmet. A real Gateway restart during an executing recurring job, and a real upgrade from an installed v2026.9.9 with existing settings, cannot be staged from this fork; the harness above runs in-process and is **not** offered as that proof. Scenario 6 now exercises the production Doctor repair against a real SQLite store, which is strictly more than it did before, but it is still one process driving that code — not an operator upgrading an installed release. No terminal output from a live Gateway is claimed anywhere in this description.

## Corrections to earlier revisions of this description

Explicitly withdrawn rather than quietly reworded:

1. **"Both fields reset wherever `consecutiveErrors` resets — a run that reports its own outcome, or an explicit re-enable."** This was false. It named two of the four owners and missed `applyTriggerNoFireResult` and `applyJobPatch`, which is exactly the defect ClawSweeper reported twice. The table above replaces it, and both missing owners now reconcile.
2. **"`pnpm check:changed`: conflict-markers clean. The 'line-cap growth ratchet' sub-check fails on this host independent of any branch (git 2.34.1 doesn't support `cat-file --batch -z`) … so it's a host tooling gap, not this change."** Withdrawn, and it was concealing real failures. The git-2.34 observation was true, but reporting one passing sub-check as the gate result hid the fact that the gate had never reached a terminal exit code on this branch. With git 2.55 shimmed onto `PATH`, the line-cap ratchet lane reports **ok** — there is no violation there — and taking the run to a terminal exit surfaced **three genuinely red lanes, all of them this branch's own**, now fixed in this round:

   | Lane | What was red | Fix |
   |---|---|---|
   | `dead export scan` | `resolveCronJobRunFailureCount` was an unused **production** export — its only consumer is in its own file | un-exported; `reconcileCronRestartInterruptionOffset` stays exported because `jobs.ts` genuinely consumes it |
   | `lint core` | `run-recovery.test.ts` imported `type CronServiceDeps` and never used it (added by this branch, absent from `origin/main`) | import removed |
   | `lint scripts` | eight `no-unnecessary-boolean-literal-compare` errors in the proof harness, four pre-existing | every enabled-flag assertion uses the truthy/falsy form through a `readEnabled()` accessor |

   The only oxlint output left in `lint core` is `max-lines` **warnings** on files byte-identical to `origin/main` and outside this branch's diff — for example `src/gateway/server-runtime-subscriptions.test.ts` at 1003 lines against a 1000 cap, with no entry in `config/max-lines-baseline.txt`. Inherited, and not touched here.
3. **The whole Evidence block was pinned to head `0872b7e40c1`**, including `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test` and a `240 files / 2327 tests` cron-project vitest run. Those numbers are not restated for this head; the gate table above is what was actually run here, and the typecheck lanes are covered inside `check:changed`.
4. **"4/4 real-runtime scenarios"** is now 6/6, and the word "real-runtime" is qualified: the harness is in-process. See "What is NOT proven here".
5. **"Jobs upgraded from a release without the counters keep their full remaining budget after `openclaw doctor --fix`."** Withdrawn the same day it was written, because ClawSweeper Revision 3 found the repair was not persisted. **The claim is restored at head `590e3cbb963`** — not by rewording it, but because the write now exists and is measured at the real repair/reload boundary (table and scenario 6 above). The withdrawal stays recorded here so the history reads honestly: the claim was false for the two heads it was made against.
6. **"Scenario 6 … does not prove the upgrade path."** True of the previous harness, and now obsolete. The scenario was rebuilt around the production Doctor repair rather than deleted, and its own negative control shows it failing without this round's fix.
7. **"`pnpm check:changed`: exit 0, 37 lanes."** Re-measured at this head rather than restated: **38 lanes**, because this round adds a file that classifies into the tooling surface. The count is from the run's own lane headers; `check:changed` prints no summary block on a clean exit.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Solid tool-result views still send their built-in content through a Lit template and directive before returning to a Solid renderer.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Built-in tool-result controls and plugin replacement views keep their existing appearance, selection, recovery, and operation lifetimes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a native `PluginSurface` projection and use it in both Solid tool-result callers. Native defaults and companion controls mount under the originating Solid owner; plugin selection, synchronous composer revocation, and the existing plugin view remain with their current owners. Keep the transparent default span because direct-child CSS selectors depend on it.

The original Lit directive remains for the true Lit callers in `chat-tool-cards.ts` and `chat-pane-embedded-panels.ts`. It also serves Solid islands mounted by unported Lit callers without an `ApplicationProvider`, such as `renderGroupedMessage`. The directive owns live DOM context replacement, reconnect, registry subscriptions, and cleanup; `solidContent` does not supply that contract. Native callers with the Solid provider stay direct. Remove the fallback when those legacy callers disappear or their adapter supplies application context. This PR does not move the directive or weaken its contract.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| Native surface + existing plugin view tests, one worker | 21 passed across 2 files before the legacy-context correction |
| Codemod dry-runs | Completed; original directive/cancellation owners deliberately retained |
| Independent review | P0–P2 clean, including the layout and legacy-context corrections |
| `pnpm ui:build` + strict performance | Passed on the corrected implementation; startup JS 349,028 → 349,023 B gzip, startup raw bytes unchanged at 1,060,610; 1 CSS request, 49,703 B gzip |
| Final-head CI performance | Passed in run 38507542161 at ce947e24a038: startup JS 348,454 B gzip; 1 startup CSS request, 49,702 B gzip. Same-host baseline comparison remains the local row above. |

| Legacy-context regression tests | Both exact regressions passed in full CI run 38505446550 at 6bf610c: selected tool replacements retain context/projection/disposal (UI2), and the pane raw global owner reaches transcript/tool replacements (UI3). The local two-file run stalled before tests executed and was terminated after 120,000 ms; no local pass claimed. Final naming-only head CI remains pending |
| Visual proof | Synthetic expanded tool result, desktop light, before/after inspected; pixel-identical at 1440×960 (0 changed pixels); native transparent span preserves direct-child spacing |

Production LOC in the three changed renderers: 1,669 → 1,727 (+58). The temporary growth is the native surface API and the existing legacy-context path while Lit callers still require their original adapter; this removes two Solid→Lit→Solid round trips for application-owned Solid views. Adds 201 lines of native-boundary tests; retains the existing legacy contract suite.

An additional production export audit reports unused exports owned by other migration lanes, including legacy chat renderers; no ignores were added.

prs.title: chore: refresh dependencies with seven-day release cutoff
prs.body:
Closes #171650

## What Problem This Solves

Refreshes dependencies across the repository using a fixed seven-day release cutoff of **2026-10-07 02:36:46 UTC**, rather than updating only the root npm manifest.

## User Impact

Runtime integrations, native dependency graphs, browser tooling, and development/CI tools receive eligible upstream updates. Existing configurations and supported runtime floors remain unchanged. Optional Lightpanda deployments move to 1.0.0; its default CORS enforcement is documented. No services are deployed or restarted by this change.

Native app builds and Linux Docker browser-route conformance are not claimed by the local proof. PR CI supplies the broad integration checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audit covers 745 direct npm specifications in 201 manifests, pnpm and release-tool locks, native Cargo/Swift/Ruby/Gradle dependencies, CI actions, tools, and container pins. It updates 92 npm declarations across 55 manifests (41 distinct direct packages), pnpm to 12.10.1, 31 Rust lock entries, five Swift dependencies, three Ruby gems, Gradle to 9.8.0, Lightpanda to 1.0.0, and eligible CI/tool/image pins. Newly selected releases meet the cutoff; existing newer pins are preserved, not downgraded.

TypeScript's new retained-source API and filesystem snapshots require a small integration migration. The selected compiler is `7.1.0-dev.20260928.1`: every eligible September 29–October 6 compiler reproduces TS5115 on a valid Zod JSON-record contract. Five contextual-default-parameter sites are rewritten equivalently for the selected compiler. The filesystem migration removes the local overlay implementation in favor of the upstream owner.

Vitest 5.0.3 scopes cache-key generators per project. Registering the existing compiled-worker discriminator for every project fixes cross-mode cached-transform reuse while retaining one shared artifact owner. The existing regression now exercises both projects. Matrix, Vitest, and WebAwesome patches are regenerated against their new upstream versions without adding patch semantics.

<details>
<summary>Intentional holds and compatibility boundaries</summary>

- MXC stays at 0.9.0: eligible 1.0.0 removes the public root API used by the integration and replaces it with a different sandbox/network-policy contract. No private deep imports or type shims are introduced.
- TypeScript 5 consumers used by Lit analysis/Solid lint retain their actual compiler-API contracts. Existing reviewed Solid, fs-safe, proc-safe, Bun-fork, and native pins newer than the cutoff are not downgraded.
- Rust, Swift, and Ruby transitive families retain versions required by their upstream owners. Cargo's initial reassignment of 13 broad-range edges to older coexisting versions was corrected through Cargo; final version and edge checks show no downgrades. The Windows updater fork remains necessary because the eligible upstream release still lacks its launch-failure repair.
- CodeQL packs, newer Android command-line-tools archives, and a newer OpenWebUI image remain unchanged where publication-age/complete artifact verification was unavailable. Existing GitHub Action pins were already the latest eligible versions.
- Supported runtime lines, compiler/OS floors, Android API targets, release baselines, and historical fixtures are not dependency pins to retarget blindly.

</details>

## Evidence

- Publication-age and registry-integrity audit passes for all 173 added npm resolution entries (170 unique package versions). Dependency-pin and patch guards pass. Native lock metadata, checksums, publication ages, and owner constraints are verified.
- Frozen pnpm installation, script and extension typechecks, Control UI build/performance hard gates, workflow sanity, targeted formatting, and CRLF-aware whitespace checks pass.
- Focused browser/UI dependency proof: 52 tests pass across three files, 24.39 seconds wall time.
- Focused CI/runtime pin proof: 233 tests pass, nine skip, across eight files, 483.51 seconds wall time. Patch guard: eight pass.
- Compiled-worker cache regression: three pass, 90.37 seconds wall time, including both Vitest projects. Native TypeScript, Codex version selection, Matrix saved-sync routing, and Matrix media metadata: 18 tests pass across four files/shards, 532.91 seconds wall time, dominated by compiled prerequisites.
- Focused CI planner owner cases: ten pass, 117 unselected, 90.03 seconds wall time. Existing passing suites were not rerun.
- The unchanged Lightpanda browser fixture passes navigation, snapshots, typing/clicking, exactly-once submission, unsupported-capability handling, single-page limits, and stale-target rejection against the checksum-verified macOS arm64 1.0.0 binary. Linux arm64 image identity and CDP connection pass; full Docker route proof remains unverified after host-fixture networking failures. Task-owned processes/containers are stopped.
- Gradle's native wrapper generator and `--version` pass. The JAR's SHA-256 `238e777fcddd7e34f9708186085def2abd6e08e658505b38718d79d74c21abd5` independently matches both official Gradle checksum surfaces. With explicit operator approval, the unsupported binary is verified separately from isolated text autoreview; no binary is silently omitted from the overall assessment.

Isolated Codex autoreview completed both text partitions at P2 with a terminal `scoped-clean` result. The staged textual candidate is byte-for-byte identical to the reviewed snapshot; only the explicitly approved, independently verified Gradle JAR uses separate binary assessment. Generated Vitest patch-context whitespace is preserved and verified as upstream context, not added payload.

All targeted lint scopes pass. Extension lint's SDK declaration prerequisite and an initially overbroad core lint invocation hit the existing five-minute timeout while the local host's load average was approximately 141. Only the failed scopes were retried: extension lint passed with the supported 15-minute declaration timeout (12,968 SDK declarations emitted), and core lint passed with its correct focused configuration. No source timeout or CI policy was changed, and passing tests were not repeated.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38507489334) is running for `c14df1c964d67c9c5d77b5cf54e8bcfeebb73595`; final results will be recorded before landing.

No changelog is edited; this body preserves release-note context.

prs.title: fix(agents): avoid false managed local-model shutdown failures
prs.body:
Closes #171472. Replaces #171498 with Dallin Romney's repair and regression coverage, refreshed onto current main. GitHub reports maintainer edits disabled on the original PR; contributor credit is preserved in the commit.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed local-model shutdown on Windows can report a failure after the service has already exited while its termination helper is still completing.

## User Impact

Managed services stay owned until their bounded termination helpers and final process-exit observation settle. Child-close, tree-liveness, and replacement-PID checks remain intact. No configuration or migration changes.

Native Windows validation remains an accepted gap: this work was verified on macOS with controlled Windows process I/O, not a Windows host.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two-second final exit window could expire before Windows taskkill's three-second completion contract. The local-service owner now joins existing helper completion promises before starting final exit observation. It does not add another timeout or cleanup owner. CLI cleanup retains its separate reporting grace and joins pending cleanup before automatic exit.

Production: +15/-7 lines (net +8); tests: +110/-24 (net +86); docs: +2; mock-export baseline: -1. The production growth records completion promises in the existing signal map; reducing it further would obscure completion cleanup or discard the completion facts being fixed.

## Evidence

- Baseline `c33cd2c41ad8d1ef4e54f0c88551351e47dac600`: both controlled regressions fail with `Local model service process tree 12345 did not stop`; the four existing settlement cases pass. Wall time 35.93s.
- Repaired head: all six settlement cases and four native macOS shutdown siblings pass (10/10), including stubborn descendants, late retired-lease release, and reacquisition after failed exit observation. Combined wall time 19.28s; Vitest duration 7.31s.
- The delayed-helper regressions use the real provider lifecycle and process-tree signal owner with fixed spawn, process-probe, health I/O, and fake timers. They cover helper close at 2.5s and the helper's bounded timeout at 3s. These are boundary tests, not native Windows proof.
- Fresh independent Codex review through P2 on the replacement head: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-export, config-doc, and plugin-inventory checks pass. Agents-root typecheck and formatting pass.

- Native macOS live control: `pnpm openclaw --profile local-svc-shutdown infer model run --local --model llama-cpp/qwen3.5-4b-q4_k_m --thinking off --prompt "Reply with exactly: shutdown-control-ok" --json`, using isolated state/config and loopback port 19672. OpenClaw's installer verified llama.cpp b10809 and the pinned 2.7 GB Qwen3.5 4B artifact. The CLI started the service, the model returned exactly `shutdown-control-ok`, and normal host cleanup exited it with code 0. Readiness: 8.004s; observed stop-to-exit: 0.222s; whole command: 52.792s. The owned PID and listener were absent afterward. This proves the one-shot CLI/provider lifecycle on macOS, not a Gateway chat or native Windows run.
- `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build` passed (7m 42.2s). A broader full declaration build was deliberately stopped during unrelated package declaration compilation; it is not counted as passing. The scoped agents-root typecheck passed separately.
- Targeted type-aware lint passed after installing the existing `@openclaw/solid-lint` workspace dependencies omitted by the gateway-only setup. No dependency declarations or lockfile were changed.
- [Ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38504553855) passed on exact head `6612ecabfdb11f66b5b4d3ae45a9f5e777b25022`: 38 successful jobs including `openclaw/ci-gate`. [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171587#issuecomment-6160043722) completed on that exact head with no findings and no Before merge items; native Windows remains the accepted proof limitation. No merge was performed.

prs.title: fix(update): service definition refresh skipped when the config snapshot is large
prs.body:
Closes #170331

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` warns `candidate-config-read-failed: reader process exited with code 1 without a result` and leaves the Gateway service definition unrefreshed when the operator's config snapshot is larger than the reader pipe buffer (~64 KB on macOS, ~200 KB on Linux).

## User Impact

User impact: updates with moderately large configs refresh the service definition again instead of warning and skipping it. When an optional read does fail, the warning now names the real next step: run `openclaw gateway install --force` with the same `--profile` or `--dev` option as the update. The old text was "Retry with the updated CLI", which pointed at the CLI that was already running.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generated `dist/io.runtime.js` reader child touched `process.stdout`, which makes fd 1 non-blocking, and then wrote its result frame with `fs.writeFileSync(1, …)`. Once the frame exceeded the pipe buffer, the write threw `EAGAIN` partway through. The catch then appended an error frame, and the parent could not parse either one. The worker now writes the single frame through the stream, which queues and flushes it before the process exits naturally. The worker never calls `process.exit`.

The recovery advice is part of the generated alias, which runs inside the older installed updater. That process cannot load the candidate's `formatCliCommand`, so the message names the profile selection instead of rendering a qualified command. `--container` doesn't apply because `formatCliCommand` never adds it to update commands.

Update behavior: the updater loads the candidate's alias after the package swap. This fix therefore takes effect for updates *to* a release containing it, including updates driven by beta.1 and beta.2.

**Retained alias hash, without a fixture.** The old template's body hash (`13537ac9…`) stays in `isUpdateConfigRuntimeAlias` so update-compat tracing still recognizes published releases. I checked it against the real npm tarballs (`npm pack openclaw@<v>`) by running the actual recognizer over each published `dist/io.runtime.js`:

| Published release | Recognized with the hash | Without it |
|---|---|---|
| 2026.10.2 | yes | yes (older hash) |
| 2026.10.3 (current `latest`) | yes | **no** |
| 2026.10.5-beta.2 | yes | **no** |
| 2026.10.5-beta.3 (current `beta`) | yes | **no** |

The hash is required: `update:compat:check` must trace the current `latest` and `beta` dist-tags. The earlier draft added a 123-line `.txt` copy of the beta.2 alias as a fixture. That file is removed; the table above replaces it.

## Evidence

**Real package boundary, before and after.** Each package is installed from its tarball into an isolated prefix. Its `dist/io.runtime.js` is then imported the way an older updater imports it after replacement (`OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS=1`), using an isolated `HOME`/state and a valid 1,000,095-byte config, and `readConfigFileSnapshot()` is called:

```
== before (published 2026.10.5-beta.3), macOS Node 26.9
[update:warning:candidate-config-read-failed] Candidate config read failed: reader process exited with code 1 without a result. The existing service definition was left unchanged. Retry with the updated CLI.
== after (this branch, packed)
{"ok":true,"ms":3126,"valid":true,"rawBytes":1000095,"lastRunCommandChars":1000017}

== before (published 2026.10.5-beta.3), Linux Node 24.21 (Docker)
[update:warning:candidate-config-read-failed] Candidate config read failed: reader process exited with code 1 without a result. The existing service definition was left unchanged. Retry with the updated CLI.
== after (this branch, packed)
{"ok":true,"ms":1194,"valid":true,"rawBytes":1000095,"lastRunCommandChars":1000017}
```

The before output matches the reporter's beta.2 warning byte for byte.

**Real update from a published beta updater, before and after.** `scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh` accepts only stable drivers, and stable drivers hand finalization to the fresh candidate driver, so they never do the failing read. I ran a proof-only copy of the cell, not committed, that changes three things:
- It accepts a beta driver.
- It pads the config with a schema-valid 3,200-entry custom provider catalog, leaving 1,341,665 bytes on disk right before the update.
- It records the systemd unit before and after.

The beta-driver acceptance is the only harness change; the rest is the stock cell: managed user-systemd service, Doctor-seeded state, sessions, `openclaw update --tag <tgz> --yes --json`.

| Cell (Docker, Linux) | `candidate-config-read-failed` warnings | Update result |
|---|---|---|
| Published `2026.10.5-beta.2` updater → published `2026.10.5-beta.3` | **7** (4 at activation, 3 after post-install Doctor) | finished/succeeded, readyz 200, running version verified |
| Same beta.2 updater → this branch (`5b960707702`, relabeled `2026.10.5-beta.4`) | **4** (activation only), **0** after post-install Doctor | finished/succeeded, readyz 200, running version verified |

```
== before: beta.2 updater → published beta.3 (after post-install Doctor)
└  Doctor complete.
[update:warning:candidate-config-read-failed] Candidate config read failed: reader process exited with code 1 without a result. The existing service definition was left unchanged. Retry with the updated CLI.
[update:warning:candidate-config-read-failed] Candidate config read failed: reader process exited with code 1 without a result. The existing service definition was left unchanged. Retry with the updated CLI.
[update:warning:candidate-config-read-failed] Candidate config read failed: reader process exited with code 1 without a result. The existing service definition was left unchanged. Retry with the updated CLI.

== after: beta.2 updater → this branch (after post-install Doctor)
└  Doctor complete.
(no candidate-config-read warnings)
```

The before output matches the reporter's beta.2 → beta.3 log on Debian. An instrumented copy of published beta.3 logged one of those reads exiting 1 after only 146,176 bytes of its frame. That is the partial `fs.writeFileSync(1, …)` write.

**What remains.** All four warnings left in the after cell carry the old "Retry with the updated CLI" text, which this branch no longer emits. The installed beta.2 updater's own reader produces them during activation, and a candidate cannot change that code. The fixed alias's new wording never appears because none of its reads failed.

**Unit.** In both cells, the candidate's managed-service reconciliation still refreshed the unit afterward. The only diff was `Environment=PATH`, which gained the pnpm bin directories. prs.title: fix: avoid per-token Markdown parsing after quoted tool XML
prs.body:
Fixes #171363

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway CPU spikes and delayed streaming when a reply quotes tool-call XML inside a Markdown code block and then continues with a long answer.

## User Impact

Quoted XML examples remain visible and later reply text can stream without repeatedly parsing the entire answer. Real leaked tool XML and partial tag prefixes remain hidden. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The filter added by #138204 stayed active after any `<`, so a harmless fenced `<invoke>` or `<parameter>` caused a full Markdown parse on every later token. The XML filter now carries its scan position across appends and retires candidates that Markdown Core has classified inside block code after its opening line is complete. Ordinary continuations inspect only the appended bytes. Source replacements reset this state through the existing text-projection owner.

Markdown Core still owns code recognition. Unprotected tags and ambiguous inline markup retain the canonical sanitizer; this does not claim a universal linear bound for streams repeatedly introducing new or ambiguous XML candidates. The XML parser and filter now share one dedicated module, preserving the existing exports, to keep both owner files within the lint line limit.

Production/config LOC is +503/-449 (net +54); tests +32/-1 (net +31); docs +0/-0. The added production code holds streaming classification state and reuses its parsed regions. Unrelated behavior was not removed to meet the nonpositive-LOC target.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test gate, per the maintainer proof policy for this campaign.

- New regression: `bounds Markdown parse work after quoted tool XML in token-sized deltas`, through the real message-update handler for Ollama, Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Completions, and OpenAI Responses. It bounds total parsed characters rather than wall-clock time and checks the delivered text.
- Existing regressions cover every split of GLM/invoke/function_calls payloads, restored terminal literals, adjacent native text, and native tool/thinking boundaries. The matrix now also includes Anthropic Messages.
- Changed-file oxlint and oxfmt pass; `git diff --check` passes. The initial max-lines lint failure was fixed by extracting the XML owner.
- Fresh isolated Codex autoreview of final head `75dfbbbe90443c487362fe8c74cb115abb3b7de4` through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Main (`13310d7446e5c`) was merged without rebasing.
- **Final-head [CI run 38502452566](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502452566) passed: 44 successful jobs, 25 skipped, zero failures**, including production/test types and lint. All 52 tool-markup handler tests passed, including the four new parse-work cases (63/49/23/127 ms), plus the XML sanitizer sibling suites. The handler file took 38.94 s wall including cold transformation (36.98 s Vitest duration; 90% transformation, 2% tests).
- The first run caught the extracted module missing from the PR wrapper source inventory. The final head includes that one-line packaging correction, and its wrapper runtime-import-closure test passes. No CI rerun was requested.

prs.title: feat(android): validate phone and Wear releases in CI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android phone and Wear OS releases lack an unattended application qualification gate comparable to iOS release validation.

## User Impact

Developers can qualify onboarding, multi-turn chat/history, native Wear input, process-restart recovery, and long-reply reading on fresh standard SDK emulators before store signing/upload. The existing APK publication workflow remains unchanged.

The change preserves the Wear native-input callback fix and regression, and fixes an observed final-event timestamp mismatch that could duplicate Wear assistant replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Test-only adapters replace the Google Data Layer delivery/discovery boundary through existing transport interfaces. Real wire encoding/decoding, the process-owned phone bridge/controller, an authenticated isolated published Gateway, and response handling remain in the path. Responses come from the existing local release-validation provider fixture; the phone executes requests instead of supplying canned successful responses.

Android Release E2E runs directly, in exact-source full manual CI when Android is selected, and before manual store release accesses credentials/signing/upload. The aggregate CI gate requires the selected qualification. Each run freezes its stable Gateway version and dependency lock; reruns restore the same selection. Bounded public failure facts retain SDK operations and native source locations without command arguments, assertion text, or raw logs.

This validates application behavior and protocol integration. It excludes real Google capability discovery, listener-service delivery, and Play services package/signature enforcement. A separate physical-device smoke is documented. Google accounts, companion APKs, and prepared images are not CI prerequisites. Instrumented Debug APKs are checked; release/R8 runtime and store signing remain owned by the archive/release lane.

## Evidence

- Fresh macOS ARM64 phone API36/round Wear API34: seven native phases, eight expected provider requests once each, actual restart PID/protocol-path checks, complete reader head/tail glyph visibility, return-to-chat/draft/keyboard behavior, APK contract checks, matching source fingerprint and cleanup passed.
- The [hosted Linux diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38498406739) passed all seven phases, eight provider requests and cleanup with unchanged application/test inputs plus disposable telemetry. All13 screenshots were inspected. Its explicit dirty-source fingerprint means it is supporting evidence, not clean-source release qualification.
- 92 focused Kotlin contracts, original native-input regression/evidence, workflow admission/aggregate contracts, targeted type/lint/format and workflow checks passed. The new public-diagnostic safety tests passed3/3 in2s wall time; scripts/root-script types and targeted lint/format passed. Independent P0-P2 reviews are scoped-clean.
- The [controlled Linux startup comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38489262585) proved the target-compiled process-owner repair. The [headless query comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38495054358) proved default version query127/missinglibpulse and headless query0. That full diagnostic later failed Wear long-reply work; the [prior clean-source run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38495093082) failed after phone initial readiness. Those later failures were not reproduced by the full diagnostic and remain unexplained; no fix is claimed.
- The [clean hosted Android qualification at060a36fc5b4c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38500527332/job/115646436831) passed all seven phases, all eight expected provider requests exactly once, actual restart PID/protocol-path checks, APK checks and cleanup. It retained13 screenshots. The parent full manual run is still active; GitHub refused the planned job replay before parent completion. Saved-selection replay and aggregate success are not yet claimed.
- A subsequent [clean diagnostic wrapper run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38503265133) reached five phases, then failed Wear long-reply work; cleanup passed. Application and harness inputs matched060a36fc5b4c. Early emulator boot retries filled the public diagnostic buffer, so the actual native failure was dropped. Commitbe324e8d50a retains the latest16 facts instead; no native assertions, timeouts, production transport or application inputs changed. A bounded failure diagnostic is pending; unattended reliability is not yet established.
- The [store-gate rehearsal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38486639786) passed its verifier: real qualification failed and an inert signing/upload sentinel was skipped. The probe used an adapted ref; the unchanged canonical main-ref predicate passed success/failure controls. No protected environment, credentials, signing or upload ran.
- Exact-head normal [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38500528345) completed red with two unaffected failures: UI hovercard cache test timeout and a successful memory-provider probe leaving one fake timer where its test expects zero. All11 determining owner/test/fixture/config blobs match actual merge6082b5e7 and base338c79ce. Native classification is new/unknown because baseline scope is not comparable; the UI blocked stage and timer identity remain unobserved. No repair or passing baseline is claimed. Security-fast passed independently. Earlier prior-head failures remain recorded in task/native review evidence.

## Summary
Loopback `openclaw gateway probe` / `security audit --deep` looked up the cached operator token in the legacy `device_auth_tokens` table. After schema v13 the token lives in `gateway_origin_device_tokens` keyed by origin (including `ws://127.0.0.1:18789`), so the probe attached no device identity, connected token-only in `mode: PROBE`, lost `operator.read`, and reported `gateway.probe_failed`.

Use the origin-scoped lookup for loopback the same way remote probes already do. Tests now expect `loadOriginDeviceTokenReadOnly` for loopback URLs.

Fixes #159121

- [x] `vitest run src/gateway/probe.test.ts` (29 passed)

prs.title: fix(ui): browser Talk on Gemini 3.8 Live drops spoken user turns from history
prs.body:
Fixes #171505

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: browser Talk on Gemini 3.8 Live displays spoken questions during the call but drops them from saved chat history after Stop or reload.

## User Impact

Spoken user turns from `gemini-3.8-live` and `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking` are finalized during the call and saved in order with the assistant's replies. Gemini 3.1 and older models retain their existing transcript behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gemini 3.1 and 3.8 send each input utterance as one complete `inputTranscription` message without `finished`. The browser previously recognized only 3.1, leaving 3.8 input provisional until teardown discarded it. The transport now applies the same input-finality rule as the Google relay's `emitsCompleteInputTranscripts` contract. Final events flow through the existing serial transcript queue and `talk.client.transcript` persistence owner.

Input finality remains separate from 3.1-only tool scheduling and control speech. No protocol, configuration, or storage changes are needed. The regression also checks the `models/` prefix and ensures a later finish-only frame and Stop do not emit duplicate final turns. The Talk documentation now names both 3.8 variants.

Original fix by @masatohoshino; maintainer cleanup tightens the regression, shortens the contract comment, updates the documentation, and integrates current main.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test and typecheck gate per maintainer policy (2026-10-13). Live proof was intentionally skipped during this maintainer pass; no Gateway, Crabbox, or Testbox was started, and no local tests or typechecks were run. Contributor evidence from the original head is preserved below and is historical evidence, not a new live run.

- Regression: `Google Live browser transcript finality > finalizes both live $name spoken turns before the session closes`, covering default 3.1, 3.8, 3.8 Extended Thinking, and `models/gemini-3.8-live`. The assertions require both user finals before any finish-only frame, preserve answer ordering, and reject duplicate finals after finish/Stop. Existing 2.5 fragment, interruption, and transcript-budget tests remain in the same file. CI covers the changed test plus UI tests, typechecks, lint, and applicable integration checks.
- Local static checks: changed-file oxlint and `oxfmt --check`, plus `git diff --check`. The nested install has no local dependencies; static tools use the parent's installed binaries. The lint config preserves the root rules and applicable overrides, omitting only the unrelated `ui/**/*.tsx` Solid plugin override because that plugin is absent from the shared install; both changed code files are `.ts`.
- Autoreview: both the pre-commit review and committed-branch Codex review were scoped-clean through P2. The branch review included the relay model contract, browser test support, transcript queue, and session callback owner; no actionable findings remained.
- Exact-head CI: **passed** at `d5730b03de24617507540cec19a2e0d3fab31d3e` in [CI run 38502283608](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502283608). All UI suites, production/test typechecks, lint, docs, and the aggregate gate passed. No inherited CI failures remain on this head.
- Test cost: all **9 tests passed** in `google-live-transcripts.test.ts`; [UI job 115652131528](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502283608/job/115652131528) reports **53.9 ms test execution** for the file. This is Vitest test time, not whole-command wall time. The contributor reported 3.0 seconds wall time for the previous file; no local test command was run in this pass. No new test file or real waits were added.
- Diff against current main: production **+4 / -2** (net +2), tests **+36 / -16** (net +20), docs **+4 / -3** (net +1). The two additional production lines cache input finality independently of 3.1-only tool behavior; the comment was shortened without removing existing bounds or checks.

### Original CI failures

At contributor head `c370b6806b94ad26e34e5a7bad1c1fb610a0b328`, [CI run 38490350460](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38490350460) failed `check-prod-types` and `check-test-types-core-1` through `-5` with the same unrelated `TS2349` at `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-node-artifacts.ts:490`: a participant publication object was called as a function. The aggregate CI gate failed as a consequence.

Main repaired that call in [4aa62334122ed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4aa62334122ed29f605f9820c4604539b3ccee77). The subsequent [scheduled main run 38496717898](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38496717898) passes all six affected jobs: production types [115634310345](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38496717898/job/115634310345), and core test types 1–5 (115634310429, 115634310318, 115634310285, 115634310321, 115634310413). These failures originated outside this PR and are resolved by the main integration; they are not claimed as failures that remain on current main.

### Review feedback

The full [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171506#issuecomment-6158186801) of the exact pushed head reports no actionable findings and complete issue coverage. prs.title: fix: keep Agents API retries working after steering
prs.body:
## Why This Change Was Made

Accepted steering must preserve the ability to retry an active conversation.

## What Problem This Solves

A steering message accepted during an Agents API run rewrites its transcript metadata. That rewrite changes the transcript generation and invalidates the earlier foreground input, so a retry can fail with `Current-turn transcript admission identity changed` instead of continuing the conversation.

## User Impact

Retries can continue after accepted steering while retaining the same session and its earlier conversation context. Existing checks still reject changed, copied, foreign, or rebound transcript authority. No configuration or data migration is required.

## What Changed

The accepted-steering path confirms its transcript update through the existing SQLite writer and refreshes the original recorder only when its earlier input is still unchanged. Receipt capture and publication stay within the writer queue so overlapping steering messages remain ordered.

The optional recorder argument and its compatibility, acceptance ordering, object identity, and preserved-prefix requirements are documented in `docs/plugins/sdk-agent-harness/attempt-runtime.md`.

## Evidence

- Public-base reproduction: all four new core steering cases fail at the transcript read fence. With the fix, all 43 tests in the two affected files pass. Another 64 neighboring persistence and transcript tests pass.
- The regression covers the registered message queue, real SQLite transcript storage, prompt preparation, and a retry after an injected attempt failure. Coverage includes sequential and overlapping steering, incognito and detached transcripts, and invalid transcript authority.
- Test cost: `pnpm test src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-attempt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 314.67 seconds wall including worker compilation. Vitest reported 30.50 seconds for the core file and 152.29 seconds for the plugin file. The four sibling files took 343.57 seconds wall including compilation. These measurements are unit-test wall times; current CI coverage was interrupted by the unrelated failures recorded below.
- A native ARM64 Docker image built and passed offline package verification. A real Slack message reached the Docker Gateway and actual Agents API session, a steering message was accepted during a native shell call, the transcript recorded its original target run and both user inputs exactly once, and the final Slack reply matched the replacement marker. The turn settled with no pending inputs.
- A separate actual-client check on `ca6f25f45d8f777666fa7f1b290f568dbdac83e9` passed: real steering POST accepted, original entry preserved with refreshed generation, old admission rejected, controlled host attempt failure, explicit successful retry on the same native binding, and one durable copy of each user input. The proof-created remote session was deleted after settlement.
- The controlled failure is a call-through artifact-list wrapper throwing after an actual completed native turn and successful artifact listing. It is an explicit attempt-wrapper retry, not an automatic Gateway retry, failed remote turn, or observed provider rate limit. It does not acquire the outer harness binding lease or claim exact placement of every native tool receipt.
- The Docker and 107 targeted tests used `c6d28b67c76f93eb30a9121b2b46fd11c48d7dbe`. The real-client retry used `ca6f25f45d8f777666fa7f1b290f568dbdac83e9`, whose production files were byte-identical. Later production edits only rename a shadowed variable and use equivalent bracket property access. Test-only edits explicitly supply an undefined target field and wrap concurrent optional callbacks in async functions; the affected 39-test core suite passed again on `e114cb8c89bfe066f619f73be32d5c5e83385707` in 49.31 seconds after worker compilation, and targeted lint passed.
- Independent source review found no actionable P0-P2 issues. Core, core-test, extension, and corrected extension-test type checks pass. Documentation formatting and MDX checks pass. The remaining guards and extension/scripts lint pass. Full core lint remains blocked by an unchanged public-base UI file: `ui/src/pages/model-setup/model-setup-page.ts:745:2: error eslint(max-lines): File has too many lines (705).` The configured maximum is 700. The three errors in changed core files were fixed and their targeted lint rerun passed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): use monotonic clock for cron failure repair wait deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a cron run fails and an owner-conversation repair is dispatched, the repair turn is bounded by `runGatewayCronFailureRepair`'s agent-wait deadline, which was seeded and read on the wall clock (`Date.now()`) while `waitForAgentJob` consumes the remaining budget through monotonic `setTimeout`. An NTP step between seed and read distorts the budget: a rewind inflates it (the repair hangs far past its `failureRepairTimeoutMs`), and a forward jump shrinks it toward zero, killing a healthy repair — so a failed cron run is left unrepaired.

Solution: use `performance.now()` for both the seed and the remaining-budget read, putting the deadline and its monotonic consumer in the same clock domain. No parser, policy branch, or configuration surface changes; the deadline is process-local, so switching from a wall-clock epoch to a monotonic timestamp changes nothing for consumers that only subtract to compute a remaining budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runGatewayCronFailureRepair` is the canonical owner of this deadline: it seeds the deadline and hands the remaining budget to `waitForAgentJob` → `setSafeTimeout`. Fixing both the seed and the read there unifies the clock domain for this path. `performance.now()` is global on Node 16+; `resolveSafeTimeoutDelayMs` already `Math.floor`s and clamps, so no extra `Math.floor` is needed. This mirrors the monotonic-clock fixes already shipped for sibling deadlines (#168144, #155855, #155863).

## User Impact

Owned cron runs that fail during a host clock adjustment (NTP correction, sleep/resume) now keep a repair bounded by the configured `failureRepairTimeoutMs` instead of hanging far past it (on a rewind) or being killed immediately (on a forward jump). Normal operation with no clock skew is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Real cron-triggered end-to-end proof** (isolated real Gateway via `startGatewayServer`, real `registerGatewayRecoveryRuntime` principal, real `createCronServiceState` + real `createTestGatewayScheduler`, real `createGatewayCronFailureRepair` factory closure, real `dispatchGatewayLifecycleMethod` (lifecycle dispatch) and real `waitForAgentJob` (repair observer) — nothing mocked). The repair is driven through the **real cron notification dispatch chain that ships with the gateway**:

```
dispatchCronNotification(state, { kind: "failure-repair", job, text })
  → requestFailureRepair(state, notification)        // real shipped function (notification-dispatch.ts)
     → state.deps.runCronFailureRepair(request)      // real createGatewayCronFailureRepair closure
        → runGatewayCronFailureRepair                 // real shipped function
           → dispatchGatewayLifecycleMethod           // real shipped (NOT mocked)
           → waitForAgentJob                          // real shipped observer (NOT mocked)
```

A 60,000ms wall-clock rewind was injected in a window that opens at the deadline seed and closes once the observer's budget timer is captured; the real observer's armed `setTimeout` delay was captured. The repair is not a WS-RPC method: it is triggered by the cron failure path (`cron/service/notification-dispatch.ts` → `runCronFailureRepair`) and dispatched through the real lifecycle dispatch inside the running Gateway.

| head | wall-clock seed armed? | real observer armed delay |
|---|---|---|
| pre-fix (`Date.now()`) | yes | **90,000ms** — inflates far past the 30,000ms timeout (repair would hang ~60s extra) |
| post-fix (`performance.now()`) | no | **29,998ms** — stays bounded at the configured timeout despite the 60s wall rollback |

pre-fix terminal: `[skew] armed -60000ms rewind ... rewind window OPEN` → `[observer] real waitForAgentJob observer armed timer: 90000ms` → `BUG REPRODUCED: ... real observer armed 90000ms (~timeout+rewind=90000ms)`.

post-fix terminal: `VERDICT (mode=postfix): observer armedDelay=29998ms (configured timeout=30000ms)` → `PASS: no wall-clock seed armed; real observer stayed bounded (~timeoutMs) despite a 60s wall rollback`.

**Regression test** (`server-cron-notifications.repair.test.ts`) drives `runGatewayCronFailureRepair` through `createGatewayCronFailureRepair`, changing both clocks precisely between the seed and the read. It fails on `origin/main` for the expected reason (budget distorted) and passes here (2 tests green). pre-fix RED: `expected +0 to be 29995` (forward jump collapses); post-fix GREEN: `Test Files 1 passed, Tests 2 passed`.

What was not tested: a wall-clock rewind was injected into the live isolated Gateway process's `Date.now` (a real monotonic-safe rollback on the running repair), not an NTP step on the host kernel clock. Collision check: no open PR touches `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts`; the sibling webhook delivery deadlines in the same file are a separate function and out of scope (one bug, one PR).

prs.title: perf(config): reuse plugin schema validation across revisions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated config snapshot reads and edits spend main-thread CPU validating unchanged plugin settings.

## User Impact

User impact: config reads and edits use less CPU with many configured plugins while preserving validation errors, defaults and strict checks. No user action, config option, stored-shape migration or schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compiled schemas were cached, but prepared results only survived one runtime/strict validation pair. Extend that existing owner across config revisions within a manifest registry generation. A bounded 512-entry LRU retains only slots visited by the latest successful full validation; rejected candidates never publish temporary inputs. Removed slots retire at publication, and metadata-free empty revisions invalidate prior settings without triggering discovery. Registry replacement also retires its results; schema contents, input, origin and defaults mode determine reuse. Clone returned results so caller mutations cannot contaminate later reads. Registry replacement retires its results, and input/schema edits revalidate the affected slot. Core validation, activation, policy, diagnostics and strict semantic checks still run.

Ordinary RPCs consume the runtime snapshot. With an active watcher, config.get caches its response by config and registry revision; without an active watcher it reads a snapshot per request. Reload consumers share one snapshot per observed source revision. Startup, uncached snapshot reads, config submissions/writes and observed hot reloads remain the full-validation triggers. Remove the per-call cache plumbing rather than introducing a second validator or worker.

Production LOC delta: **+27** (60 added, 33 removed), excluding tests. The additional lines enforce the config-lifetime contract: stage visited slots and publish only after successful full validation, so removed settings and rejected inputs are not retained. Per-call async cache plumbing is still removed; there is one schema validator and one memo owner. Release-note context: repeated plugin config validations reuse unchanged schema inputs without changing defaults, diagnostics or validation semantics.

## Evidence

Five paired before/after runs in an isolated Linux sandbox, restricted to CPUs 64–127 and 64 GiB, using the production async validation entry point. The synthetic fixture has 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approval recovery records, 100 disabled cron jobs and 12 projects with real worktrees. Configure 41 synthetic plugin identities using 41 real bundled manifest schema shapes that accept empty settings; no plugin runtime executes. Each workload performs 120 validations after 10 warmups. Values below are medians of five runs, normalized to **60 config validations/minute**; these are controlled workload counts, not observed production traffic.

| Workload | Plugin schema checks/min before → after | Main-thread CPU ms per 60 validations before → after | p50 ms before → after | p95 ms before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unchanged config | 2,460 → 0 | 52.748 → 38.432 (27% less) | 0.818 → 0.597 | 1.247 → 0.865 |
| Edit outside plugin settings | 2,460 → 0 | 46.987 → 32.779 (30% less) | 0.757 → 0.532 | 0.958 → 0.594 |
| Edit one plugin entry | 2,460 → 60 | 45.330 → 33.973 (25% less) | 0.730 → 0.539 | 0.962 → 0.763 |

The last workload changes one optional field in an unrestricted synthetic copy of one manifest schema. Same schemas, configs, request counts and instrumentation on base and head; counters were added only to the disposable benchmark checkout. Main-thread CPU uses process.threadCpuUsage around the validation loop, excluding imports/fixture generation. Total process CPU for editing one plugin was 65.575 → 46.170 ms per 60 validations (30% less). This proves the owning validation cost; it does not measure production Gateway ELU or production validation frequency. No production load was generated. The fixture was generated locally first and then independently in the sandbox. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated.

Changed-file oxfmt and repository focused oxlint passed. Focused local tests: **67 passed** across validation.async, config.plugin-validation and validation-plugin-config.identity (158.55 s including first artifact preparation); **14 sibling tests passed** across config.model-ref-validation, validation.channel-schema-errors and validation.channel-metadata (29.70 s). The new reuse/edit/schema-replacement/result-isolation regression took 15 ms. It fails on the unchanged base at the reuse assertion (two schema checks rather than one); the other seven tests in that file pass on base.

**Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean.** Autoreview refused because the requested route does not match operator configuration; configuration was left unchanged. PR CI owns full typecheck, suites, builds and broad gates. The first CI run caught two optional fixture accesses in the new test; explicit required-fixture guards fixed both TS2532 diagnostics. The corrected file passes all 8 tests (40.70 s including wrapper preparation), and a fresh independent review of the correction is clean. The second head passed all CI gates (68 successful checks), then final review identified retained removed slots. This revision adds successful-validation publication and removed-slot/rejected-input regression coverage, with refreshed five-pair measurements above. Independent retention review found one misplaced helper parameter type, corrected before publication. Final retention revision focused proof: all 65 tests in validation.async, validation-plugin-config.native-catalog and config.plugin-validation pass (110.19 s including compiled preparation and verification). Changed-file formatting/lint passed, and the final independent retention review is clean. A first test invocation was invalidated by a source edit during execution; the stable-source rerun above passed. Final exact-head CI run 38506656879 passed; full production/test typechecks, changed lanes, boundary guards, lint and UI e2e are green. No inherited-failure exception or CI rerun was needed.

Accepted edge: the memo follows completion order, not the currently applied config revision. A delayed older validation can become the latest successful memo until another full validation or registry replacement. It cannot yield stale results because reuse compares all schema/input facts. A final bot suggestion to compare the memo generation at publication was declined after independent review: preparation and publication run synchronously after the metadata await, so that comparison would not prevent the described ordering. Applied-config revision fencing would require a new ownership contract and is not warranted for this bounded memo.

The composer takes more vertical space than needed when an existing conversation is already visible.

## What Problem This Solves

The remaining Control UI copy, provider-icon, and loading adapters still built redundant Lit templates around components already rendered by Solid. An unused second MCP form renderer also remained after its consumers moved to Solid.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change. Existing classes, icons, copy behavior, and loading states keep the same Solid implementation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return the existing interop directive directly, remove the unused MCP renderer, and keep the remaining legacy type contract inside the designated interop module. The native MCP form now registers its own fallback copy. Its real card tests continue to cover the form; the obsolete duplicate Lit-form case is removed from the cold-copy test, which still verifies validation fallback and locale preservation.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Codemod dry run | Reviewed all seven affected legacy source files; no unresolved migration markers |
| Focused tests | 25 original focused tests pass; CI follow-up adds 20 passing tests across debug overlay and markdown tooltip. Repaired pair: 359 s command wall, mostly tool startup |
| UI typecheck / targeted lint | Pass |
| Production Knip | Pass (`pnpm deadcode:knip`) |
| Startup JS (same host, base → head) | 349,028 B → 349,041 B (+13 B); 1 startup CSS request / 49,703 B unchanged |
| LOC in touched files | Production 753 → 661; tests 700 → 696; net -96 lines |

Independent Codex review is clean through P2. No leases were acquired.

No visual rendering changed: the same Solid components and interop hosts are used, with only their redundant outer template removed. No new packages or lazy import boundaries.


CI repair: regenerated the raw-copy baseline after removing the old MCP form (two obsolete placeholders), and pruned its one obsolete assertion allowance. `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` and the owning assertion generator pass; no runtime source changed in the repair. The two-file repair received an independent clean review.


The full UI run exposed two fixture synchronization gaps: debug samples could start after the test advanced its fake clock, and the tooltip reopen sequence reused the just-dismissed pointer position. The follow-up waits for lazy overlay content before advancing time, then explicitly closes, leaves, and re-enters the tooltip trigger before checking reset feedback. All prior assertions remain, and the tooltip now checks the exact reset path text.

Both the exact pre-fix head and merge base passed the same 20 tests locally, so this is not submitted as an inherited-failure exception. The corrected fixtures also pass all 20 tests; fresh CI must confirm the replacement head.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep Responses tool-call history stable across turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes prompt-cache history rewrite warnings after a Responses tool turn with no reasoning: the next request changed the assistant's paired tool-call ID at `content[0].id` (and its matching result ID).

## User Impact

Assistant history keeps the same canonical tool-call and tool-result IDs across live tool loops and transcript reload. Unexpected history changes now identify safe block field paths such as `content[0].thinkingSignature` or `content[0].arguments`; diagnostics contain hashes and static field names, never content or dynamic extension keys. No schema, config, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runner's orphan-function policy stripped the `|fc_*` suffix in both history loading and stream preparation. The request observer runs before stream preparation, so it compared the live paired ID with the rewritten next-turn ID. The shared Responses serializer now owns omission of orphan function item IDs on the wire, without rewriting conversation history. Both replay paths and the obsolete helper/export/test are removed; reasoning, foreign-model, compaction, and storeless wire policies retain their owners.

This fixes a demonstrated history invariant, not a proven cause of provider cache misses. The existing storeless wire path already omitted these item IDs, and continuation/full-replay transitions can independently affect provider reuse.

## Evidence

The existing admitted-runner canned-provider test now checks assistant history through the first four turns, including tool responses without reasoning, then continues its ten-turn wire-prefix/restart/recovery checks. On the original production code it failed on turn two at the first assistant message; the removed policy independently reproduces `content[0].id` and the paired result-ID rewrite.

Team sandbox microbenchmark (Node 26.8.2, 264 messages alternating assistant tool calls without reasoning, paired results, and user turns; 18 KB synthetic text/arguments; nine alternating rounds of 100 requests, after warmup): the affected history-policy plus fingerprint work measured **4.659 ms before → 4.628 ms after** median per request. This is neutral within noise (ranges 4.573–4.795 ms and 4.432–4.690 ms). It excludes storage, networking, and whole-Gateway latency. The diagnostic-only experiment added ~0.27 ms; deletion of the rewrite offsets that in the affected workload. The benchmark sandbox was removed after measurement. Benchmarks used an isolated `/srv/perf-sandbox/prompt-cache-assistant-diff/` directory, restricted CPUs 64–127, 64 GB memory cap, lowered CPU/I/O priority, and synthetic fixtures; no production load or database access.

Cache-read tokens per canned-provider turn are **0 → 0 by fixture definition** (the synthetic provider does not implement caching), so these are not live cache measurements. No live before/after provider cache-read improvement or Gateway tail-latency claim is made. The reported production cache drops remain an attribution gap; the more precise diagnostic enables the next observation without logging content.

Production LOC delta: **−34** (69 additions, 103 deletions; tests/docs excluded, including the shrink-only ratchet entry).

Validation follows the lane's current light-local rule: changed-file `oxfmt`, changed-file repo lint using `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`, and focused single-worker tests. Replay sanitizer, compaction sibling, reasoning replay at both converter entry points, user-facing helper, and prompt-history diagnostics passed. The admitted-runner Responses case passed all ten turns (54.9 s test; 93.1 s wrapper), with the other three provider routes deliberately excluded from local execution; PR CI supplies broad sibling coverage. The diagnostic investigation temporarily added synthetic reasoning to answer outputs and exposed an unrelated fixture key-order discrepancy at recovery; that extra fixture change was removed, restoring the original provider outputs and prefix expectations. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated; full typecheck/suites/E2E belong to PR CI.

Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable). The configured autoreview helper refused an operator-provider mismatch before inference; no operator configuration was changed. The fresh-context reviewer returned no actionable P2+ findings, then confirmed the clean verdict after the test-only fixture simplification.

Initial PR CI run [38504467475](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38504467475) passed typecheck, changed-file lint, build, docs, architecture/source guards, prompt snapshots, UI E2E, and the other planned test lanes. Its four failing jobs exposed three sibling expectations for the retired ID downgrade plus the assertion-safety ratchet requiring 17 → 11 after deleting six casts. The sibling tests now require paired transcript IDs and orphan wire-ID omission; the exact per-file baseline was regenerated using the canonical syntax counter on only the changed file. The three corrected sibling files passed locally (86 tests, single worker, 63.1 s wrapper), as did changed-file formatting/lint. The independent reviewer returned a clean verdict for this correction. No CI job was rerun to chase green.

Automated review found that incomplete reasoning without a string `rs_*` ID must not preserve a following function item ID. That existing condition is now enforced after wire replay preparation, with focused regressions for absent/null/numeric/foreign-prefix identities at both converter entry points. The tests failed before the correction and passed afterward (68 tests in the reasoning replay and SDK sibling files, single worker; 11.6 s wrapper). The independent reviewer confirmed the correction is clean.

Final exact-head PR CI [38506592552](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38506592552) is green on `be8b97274b39109ed8ae0accdefbc67619ae590b`, including the aggregate CI gate and security check. All broad test lanes and ratchets passed; no inherited-failure exception or CI rerun was needed. The automated review finding is fixed and resolved.
