prs.title: improve(acp): add reusable runtime turn contract suite
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR turns the existing `AcpRuntime.startTurn` behavior into a reusable conformance suite and makes ACPX its first adopter.

- Adds one shared suite for the modern ACP turn boundary
- Replaces adapter-by-adapter reinvention with executable contract checks
- Keeps the testkit private and out of production and published package surfaces
- Changes no runtime behavior and no public API

## What Problem This Solves

As OpenClaw gains more ACP runtime adapters, each implementation needs to preserve the same observable semantics: event ordering, request identity, prompt readiness, authoritative terminal results, cancellation, and stream cleanup. Today those expectations are implicit and easy for adapters to reproduce inconsistently.

A shared suite makes that boundary explicit and independently verifiable. Existing TypeScript adapters, container-backed runtimes, and future implementations in languages such as Rust can all prove compatibility without sharing internals or being forced into one architecture.

This is intentionally a small first step: codify behavior OpenClaw already depends on, demonstrate it against ACPX, and give subsequent runtime work a stable target.

## Contract Coverage

The suite verifies:

- ordered event projection and stable request identity
- authoritative completed and failed terminal results
- result settlement before event-stream closure
- successful and rejected `promptStarted` handling
- cancellation forwarding and its cancelled terminal outcome
- `closeStream` unblocking a live consumer while its terminal result remains independent and pending

## Scope And Public Contract Impact

**302 insertions, 0 deletions across 11 files:**

- 254 lines: reusable contract testkit
- 34 lines: ACPX adoption
- 14 lines: private QA/build metadata

This does **not** change a public or production contract:

- existing `AcpRuntime` types are imported, not modified
- there is no user-visible runtime behavior change
- the new `openclaw/plugin-sdk/acp-runtime-contract-testing` subpath is private and local-only
- its JavaScript and declarations are excluded from published artifacts
- it is omitted from production SDK entrypoints and package exports

## Deliberate Non-Goals

This suite proves semantic turn projection. Process termination, crash cleanup, container readiness, trust boundaries, and per-user isolation need separate qualification evidence and can be layered on without expanding this PR.

## Evidence

Current head `713d51e5832` (rebased onto upstream `main`):

- **7/7 focused ACPX contract cases passed** with one worker in **42.22 seconds**
- **18/18 plugin SDK package guardrails passed** on the prior head; the current test-wiring-only change does not affect packaging
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` pass
- three independent runtime, repository, and container/trust reviews completed; accepted findings are addressed
- ClawSweeper reports no actionable findings and marks the PR ready for maintainer review (4/6)

The host's borrowed dependency tree contained TypeScript 7.0.2 while the frozen lock requires `typescript@7.1.0-dev.20260920.1`. Validation used standalone Vitest with explicit shard configs; the package guardrail run resolved `typescript/unstable/sync` to that exact lockfile version from an isolated frozen-install store. No source, lockfile, or production dependency was changed.

A broader ACPX diagnostic run also passed 79 tests; five unchanged Windows lease/path assertions failed outside this PR's contract suite. The focused changed surface is green.

The current broad CI failures are outside this PR's changed surface: pre-existing cron timing/notification assertions, a Discord transcript E2E timeout, and an existing update-command architecture cycle. The ACP contract, type, lint, security, and package-boundary checks pass.

prs.title: refactor(state): engine-neutral state database handles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared-state handles and their SQL consumers still require Node's native SQLite handle type, preventing the state owner from returning an admitted engine-neutral connection.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Production shared state remains SQLite; this prerequisite neither enables PostgreSQL state nor changes schemas, configuration, migration, or durability.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing leaf SQL connection contract for state handles, carry admitted physical identity through generic owners, and retain publication-anchor keying. SQLite-only operations narrow explicitly instead of exposing native methods on PostgreSQL. The broad consumer diff follows the propagated handle type; it does not port those consumers' SQL to PostgreSQL.

This is PR2b-1, the independently budgeted type prerequisite. The state-owner cutover and PostgreSQL conformance remain separate work. Related: #170266, #170059. Admission owner #171518 is merged; the final rebase preserves its seven overlapping admission functions and extracted reader unchanged, retaining only the three uncovered admission type widenings.

Design section 2: “Types distinguish SQLite native facts from PostgreSQL facts; never cast a PostgreSQL handle to `DatabaseSync`, synthesize `SqliteSchemaFacts`, or implement a fake `.location()`.”

Design section 5: “Before edits, capture complete ordered raw SQL executions at the native boundary in synthetic isolated fixtures; compare candidate arrays byte-for-byte.”

## Evidence

Current candidate `74e0d2650cef9fff45682b49a574faf612a59926` is rebased onto main `5dd456acfa35575c342b43b944a9d0dbb911b68e`.

- Fresh SQLite captures on that main and the candidate are completely byte-identical under Node 24: cold 48, restart 43, write 4, read 8, close 1 (104 executions). Full capture SHA256: `3adc8735b6d3fe1cf50addbf7fcd4de70e51ec64322e913cb844b3e55ae53b37`. The earlier auxiliary diagnostic discrepancy was different Node versions; aligned-runtime captures include identical envelopes.
- After the auth worker move, `store-update.test.ts` and `store-update-commit.test.ts` pass (21 tests, `--maxWorkers=1`). Wrapper inventory and eager-import closure pass (20 tests). Core `tsconfig.core.json` typecheck and Madge pass again.

Both reproduced on main `fd1eeeb685b11c47dc5417d423ccc19b21d42570` with `SQLite database changed identity before admission`. They are explicitly retained as inherited failures; no expectations were weakened.
- Database-worker, assertion-safety, dialect, and max-lines ratchets passed against the initial verified main; subsequent rebases were type-only conflict resolutions. T1 calls remained 224; T1-compat remained 12. No baseline expansion.
- One Codex autoreview invocation completed scoped-clean at P0–P2 (two internal evidence chunks, no actionable findings). Mechanical rebases preserve that reviewed implementation.
- CI fixture repair: native-only tests now check the same SQLite handle before using native methods, statement spies, or named bindings. No assertions or SQL were weakened. All 19 affected core test-type graphs, extension/script typechecks, and the root integration-fixture typecheck pass. Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and max-lines pass without baseline growth. Focused proxy-capture (27 tests), Gateway config-revision (2 tests), extension fixtures (37 tests; 11 PostgreSQL integration cases skipped locally), and benchmark tests (4 tests) pass. After #171484, kept its worker-admission file unchanged and reapplied only session-row parameter types. After #171510 moved the auth kernel into `store-update.worker.ts`, kept main's worker code and reapplied only two database parameter types; the retired kernel path stays absent.

Current-head [CI run 38503211422](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38503211422) completed. PostgreSQL conformance, the repaired type checks, inventory/closure, lint and other selected static checks passed. Five runtime jobs failed, with no cancelled jobs: required-native same-session marker delivery; Gateway service-capability schema fencing; update-run heartbeat timeouts; package Doctor pending-child timeout; and restart handoff drain timeout. Those two failed update jobs are inherited. The full baseline plan does not schedule the two failing E2E files; they and the service-capability failure remain unclassified. prs.title: fix(doctor): bound media scans and isolate lost maintenance leases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor media persistence repair can lose maintenance ownership while processing large offline agent databases, then reuse the failed owner for every remaining agent. A 64-row batch also does not bound memory when historical transcript events are large.

## User Impact

Doctor keeps media scans byte-bounded, rolls back a rewrite whose maintenance lease is lost, and attempts unrelated agents with fresh maintenance ownership. No schema, configuration, retention, or public API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stream the ordered SQLite scan into batches capped at 64 rows or 4 MiB, servicing the existing heartbeat owner during synchronous work. Remove repeated keyset-query construction. Rewrites keep the scan's ordering keys unchanged and retain their all-or-nothing transaction. Check current maintenance authority both before rewriting and before commit, including already-current schemas. Discovery/recovery, individual agents, and legacy archives retain sequential stopped-writer custody through the existing owner.

Retained memory is bounded by a batch plus the incoming historical row; a single oversized identity event still needs memory proportional to its own size. Production grows by 32 lines to implement the requested byte limit, authority checks, and independent maintenance lifetimes; no second scan path, cache, schema, or lease owner is introduced.

## Evidence

- Both new regression controls fail on the original production code: 65 eight-MiB identity events exhaust a 256 MiB heap, and revocation after a real transcript UPDATE permits the first rewrite to commit and prevents the next agent from completing. The repaired path preserves the first database's snapshot and repairs the next agent.
- A slow synchronous scan outlasting a shortened lease passes on both versions. This is a contract check, not proof of the reported starvation cause.
- Focused tests: 33 passed across the three media migration files (531.78 seconds on the saturated local host). Changed-file format/lint passed. The memory-cap fixture writes 520 MiB and launches the real migration under a 256 MiB heap; this resource contract requires subprocess proof and costs more than a mock or helper test. PR CI owns full gates; no validation leases were allocated.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean, including transaction-end revocation and the oversized-payload regression.

The production-shaped synthetic measurement is running in an isolated 128-core Linux sandbox. Before/after wall time and peak RSS will be added before landing. No operator database was copied or modified. The reported 35 GB incident peak and exact heartbeat-loss trigger remain unconfirmed until those measurements finish.

prs.title: fix: plugin before_tool_call hooks are skipped under openclaw agent exec
prs.body:
Closes #158824

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `before_tool_call` plugin hooks never run when an agent is started with `openclaw agent exec`, so a policy plugin that blocks a tool call is silently skipped and the call goes through.

## User Impact

User impact: plugins that guard tool calls (for example, refusing a destructive shell command) now apply in headless `openclaw agent exec` runs as they already do elsewhere.

## Why This Change Was Made

A headless run loads its plugin registry scoped to the run without activating a process-wide root, so the global hook runner was never created and tool-call policy found no runner to dispatch through. The run now makes sure the runner exists; the runner already reads the current run's scoped registry on every dispatch, and keeps the same fail-closed policy for `before_tool_call`, `before_agent_run` and `before_install`.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `src/agents/runtime-plugins.hooks.integration.test.ts`: a plugin with a blocking `before_tool_call`, no process registry activated, then a tool call through the run's registry. It fails without the fix (`blocked` is false) and passes with it. On main 1844d933: without the fix, 1 failed / 8 passed (`expected false to be true`); with it, 9 passed. Cost: the new test runs in 19 ms; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/runtime-plugins.hooks.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes about 21 s wall for the whole file.
- Neighbouring tests pass with the fix (on 813169e2): `hook-runner-global` 6, `state-migrations.outbound-preparation` 6, `agent-tools.before-tool-call.{decision,embedded-mode,network-error,voice-authority}` 18/26/11/6, `runtime-plugins.{channel-ownership,config-capture,decisions,memory-corpus,work}` and `runtime-plugins.test.ts` 12/1/1/2/2/36. Not run: `runtime-plugins.context-engine.integration`, which rebuilds `dist` on a dirty tree.
- End to end (on an earlier main, 813169e2, with a built `dist`): `openclaw agent exec --json` with a before_tool_call policy plugin loaded from the config, asked to run `git push --force origin main` in a scratch repo whose `main` was rewritten, against a local bare remote.
  - Released 2026.9.6: the exec tool ran the command (0 tool failures), and the remote's `main` moved to the rewritten commit.
  - With this fix: the plugin blocked the call (1 tool failure, the model reported it was refused), and the remote's `main` was unchanged.

prs.title: fix(matrix): resolve room policy by room id, not display name
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Matrix, a room's user-editable display name could select another room's configured policy (`tools`, `requireMention`). Matrix set `GroupSubject` to the display name and never set `GroupChannel`, so core fell back to the display name as `groupChannel`, and Matrix group policy matched that value as a trusted alias before the `"*"` fallback (#168134).

## Why This Change Was Made

Policy must key on stable identity. Ingress now sets `GroupChannel` to the room id and carries the homeserver-resolved room tool policy through the existing trusted context field, so configured aliases resolved from server state keep working. `groupChannel` only recovers the same room id's casing; display names stay presentation-only. DMs are unchanged (both additions are room-only).

## User Impact

A renamed room can no longer take on another room's tool policy or mention requirement. Rooms configured by id or canonical alias resolve as before.

## Evidence

- Three regressions (rename → `"*"` policy; configured alias still resolves; handler carries room id + resolved policy) fail before the fix and pass after.
- 173 Matrix tests across 15 files pass; typecheck, lint, format, line-cap and mock-export checks pass.
- Independent review: no P0/P1 findings.
- Production +5 LOC, tests +108.
- Follow-up (separate): Slack and Discord also accept channel-name policy candidates; Zalo Personal behind explicit opt-in.

Fixes #168134

prs.title: fix(ui): file-tooltip reopen checks accept closed popups
prs.body:
Related: #168703

## What Problem This Solves

Browser tests can mistake closing file-tooltip content for successful reopening.

## User Impact

No user-visible or runtime change. The file-tooltip checks stop accepting stale closing content as a reopened popup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the existing file-tooltip owner before Escape, then arm its completion event before hovering the same link. The original visibility, exact-path, reset, focus, file-open and clipboard-cancellation assertions remain unchanged. No retries, polling, longer deadlines, zero-motion overrides or production seams are added.

This is a separate base-fixture repair needed by #168703, not part of its wording changes. A normal direct main push was refused by the repository's pull-request rule; no bypass was attempted.

## Evidence

- Final focused Chromium file: **13/13 passed**, 9.20s runner wall / 2.703s file time. The unchanged natural baseline also passed 13/13; that alone did not reproduce the hosted timing failure.
- Controlled boundary proof held a finite native exit animation, used real Escape and link hover, and canceled exactly the next public show request. Old visibility readiness settled while the tooltip was closed and inert; the negative control failed. The repaired completion wait did not settle for the canceled reopen and did settle for an admitted reopen. **13 original cases plus 2 temporary controls passed**; the diagnostic controls are not in the published diff.
- Targeted UI-components types pass on the published signed head (13.134s). Scoped lint, format, assertion safety, timeout safety and mock-export checks pass. Other focused proof is reused after patch/input qualification; no full local suite or plugin build was run.
- P0–P2 AutoReview: scoped-clean. The exact 13-line patch and tooltip contracts are unchanged across the signed base refreshes; that review is reused, not claimed fresh on a different tree.
- [Natural exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38505265452) is **green: 46/46 terminal, 18 passed / 28 skipped**. The [actual Chromium file](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38505265452/job/115661600187) executed all 13 cases successfully (22.959s file); the two formerly failing reopen cases passed in 2307ms and 1853ms. Required CI/security gates are green. No CI rerun or dispatch was used. The original #168703 failure remains [UI shard 3, run 38498851765](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38498851765/job/115641125534).

prs.title: fix(browser): stop shared profiles from mixing session tabs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes browser panels and tab-targeted agent actions mixing tabs from different conversations when they share a browser profile.

## User Impact

Each conversation lists, selects, and acts on its associated tabs. Browser profiles, cookies, and logins remain shared; this does not launch a separate browser per chat. Global administrative and CLI browser controls remain global. Tabs without a provable current-session association are not automatically adopted. Update paired browser nodes alongside the Gateway; older nodes reject scoped routes rather than falling back to global tab access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selected tab was session-specific, but the underlying tab list came from the whole profile. This applies the existing tab registry and session lifetime to both UI requests and ordinary browser tools. Ownership follows the exact session revision, native popup provenance, and the captured node route. Failed opens clean up only their own allocation and registration, without closing a replacement or dashboard-owned tab.

## Evidence

- After the test audit, 273 focused tests passed across five files/four shards, including the real Chromium panel and registered managed/existing-session scenarios. The audit removed five redundant cases and a duplicate request: 106 net test/support lines, with production code unchanged.
- Deferred local/node CDP, MCP-lock, and Playwright-resolution tests verify that a dashboard takeover prevents the native close. Reset, original-invocation, popup, failed-open, successor-registration, and capacity regressions are covered.
- Core, UI, and extension typechecks; changed-file type-aware lint; formatting, size, and repository invariant guards passed. Public SDK export count is unchanged.
- Full `pnpm build` passed for the unchanged production code, including SDK declarations, plugin packaging, and Control UI performance budgets. Original independent-review findings were addressed and regression-tested; a fresh P0–P2 autoreview of the test reduction found no actionable issues.

### Browser panel regression

Before

![Both conversations show both tabs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be5f0748-5656-4f6d-bc2c-ebfc3301cad6)

After

![Each conversation shows only its own tab](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46806782-66d5-42bb-8357-810cc64b5ef0)

Visual evidence uses the real browser panel in Chromium with synthetic test pages. Backend/node scenarios exercise registered handlers and the native command dispatcher with controlled CDP responses, not a live remote host. No authenticated website login flow was exercised.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/f143eda1-0c84-48d9-a1f9-22695f574637)

Tests of already migrated Solid components still depend on Lit to mount their fixtures.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This removes legacy renderer dependencies from 17 test files and the shared session-menu fixture while preserving their assertions. A nearby sidebar fixture now waits for the overlay close lifecycle before asserting native occlusion release.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mount Solid components directly, update reactive props without remounting, and dispose roots explicitly. Keep plain DOM construction where tests exercise the custom-element bridge's native propagation, context replacement, or reconnect behavior. The skill upload tests now use the existing GatewayPageBinding directly instead of an otherwise empty Lit host.

Existing tests whose actual subject is a Lit directive or interoperability contract remain with that owner. No production code, dependencies, styles, or startup imports change.

prs.title: fix: redundant catalog and local agent plugin registrations
prs.body:
Related: #157568

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes redundant plugin registrations during provider-catalog refresh and local agent turns, and prevents a completed nested local command from retaining callable plugin callbacks.

## User Impact

Provider workers no longer load native-only harnesses or unrelated setup code. Local commands avoid an intermediate discovery registry, while native model inventory, CLI preloading, recipient/account selection, credentials, and resource cleanup retain their existing owners. No configuration, permissions, stored-data, or migration changes are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loader now records its actual scoped registration inputs together with the exact metadata inventory, including empty provider scopes. Catalog requests consume these facts instead of rerunning broad setup preparation. Local execution binds invocation authority to its already-admitted prepared registry and closes that authority when the command ends.

This replaces the earlier 42-file draft with a 13-file residual repair based on main. The shared inbound registry handoff already landed in #160658 and is not duplicated. The old eager HTTP-provider startup change, full-root borrowing manager, recipient-routing redesign, and supporting mechanical extractions are removed. The previous ambient-recipient finding does not describe this replacement: command preparation and CLI preaction are unchanged.

Requested by @RomneyDa; original incident reported by @hurtlovewow. Related catalog/capture regression work by @htuyer121 remains credited in merged #157300.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @RomneyDa](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/b1aeb723-16b1-4b62-a923-986563624022)
- [Catalog residual audit and implementation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/98e8f674-8181-4339-98bd-7098b867440f)
- [Combined implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/2086e6c3-cd93-4f47-827a-f741a9e157bc)

## Evidence

- Real provider-worker red/green: the baseline executed native registration and unrelated setup import/probes in the worker, producing four capture graphs; the candidate produced two. Native picker rows remained available from the parent. Existing provider-scope growth and request-local credential controls passed.
- Loader regressions failed on the baseline and passed on the candidate, covering actual runtime values versus authored SecretRefs, empty scopes, explicit environments, config/environment/workspace/metadata mismatch rejection, cache identity, and conflicting source inventories.
- Real CLI preaction through local admission: three registrations before, two after; direct-host execution uses one. The strengthened regression captures an executable `tool.execute` callback, not another factory lookup. Parent and nested callbacks append to an isolated synthetic file. After the nested command settles, that same captured callback is rejected with `Plugin invocation scope is closed` before any additional write; the still-active parent writes successfully. Both direct-host and CLI-preaction cases pass. Command config/session preparation is mocked; plugin loading, prepared runtime admission, callback ownership, and filesystem I/O are real. The baseline allowed the retired callback to return `written` instead of rejecting.
- The earlier isolated qualification passed 110 tests across 11 files; production sources are unchanged by the follow-up. The two updated test files now pass 13 focused tests (41.24 s process wall including worker preparation). Local final-I/O test bodies total 495 ms. The catalog-capture and loader-config test-body costs remain 1.56 s and 2.98 s from the prior qualification. These are proof costs, not a startup-speed claim.
- A fresh full `pnpm build` and canonical package build passed from final source tree `2c38cdceba08d671161baa7cbd6e5a2bf52e5d85` in one managed-synchronization invocation. Full build took 8m 31.4s under 16 GiB / 4 CPU / 512 PID limits. The candidate package version is `2026.9.6`, built from this PR—not borrowed from another task or described as an already-published release.
- Selected production/test types, formatting, lint, dead-export and lifecycle/schema/import guards passed. The initial aggregate exposed four test lint errors; those were fixed, affected checks rerun, and valid completed production/type evidence retained. The initial failed aggregate is not relabeled as successful.
- CI on `92fa1767cde7e3befcf801de5c2f25e753890fc9` exposed one PR-related stale equality expectation in `src/plugins/runtime/load-context.test.ts`: it omitted the newly forwarded metadata inventory. The follow-up adds that required expected field without weakening the assertion. Focused tests, affected test typechecks, formatting, lint, and fresh independent review pass. This failure is not attributed to main.
- Fresh final AutoReview found no actionable P0/P1 finding. Built Codex cold-import profiling qualified at 188.1 MiB peak RSS with verified child/process-group cleanup; this is an import snapshot, not authenticated Codex execution.
- [Earlier configured Blacksmith qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36498303964) retains the 110-test and import-profile evidence for the unchanged production sources. It is not the fresh package/upgrade proof below. Both task leases have been stopped; backing Actions workflows may show cancellation during lease cleanup, so their command receipts are distinct from hosted PR CI.
- [Fresh published-driver upgrade proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36503403864): maintained `published-upgrade-survivor-2026.9.4-custom-plugin-siblings` passed from published `openclaw@2026.9.4` to this candidate using the installed updater. Baseline configuration/runtime, update, private-canary runtime, and candidate runtime phases passed. The enabled custom memory plugin, memory-slot selection, and original sibling source files were preserved. Seven actual plugin executions resolved sibling sources in the private canary. The lane took 82 s (93.30 s orchestrator wall), reported `updateOutcome: success`, no recovery, and joined cleanup.
  - The preliminary recoverable-error classifier did not apply to the custom fixture; the maintained strict successful-update validator passed (`updateOutcome: success`, no recovery).
  - Source head `af4c4bfd1a13cacb17ba25835849b2577d66013d`; artifact build carrier `59ff11126fb65e68937e3939ab235154a3bb89f5`; package SHA-256 `f095b32c4807d593f8b71c25dc596e00ffc6c39bdd6a3d89b9ff3a85065df1bf`. The later artifact readbacks verified the same source tree and unchanged package digest.

```text

candidate: enabled sibling-import plugin loaded
UPGRADE_EXIT=0
```

## Current readiness

- Refreshed head incorporates pinned main d3008b2d5ee76e6f858380da5935db305305b005, including the landed OnePassword dependency fix 4ed0cb36ac3297b0bbd0896b7529f95fc42082ab. This addresses the actual shared CI failure rather than retrying unchanged inputs or adding a dependency exception.
- The topical 13-file patch is identical before and after integration (stable patch ID a1f76e5255e87d384b1696b12115f898c011bd84); the eight changed production-file postimages are unchanged. Existing behavioral/build/upgrade evidence above remains attached to its recorded sources, not relabeled as a new full build.
- On the integrated candidate, the complete extension-runtime dependency contract passes **484/484 tests** (5.82 s command wall). The focused local callback-I/O and load-context suites pass **13/13 tests** (72.62 s wall, including compiler preparation). Canonical frozen dependency installation and diff checks passed.
- **Current head c83fc8f1d83f1fc9fd9aec34d027ae5e1065b2a5 is ready for review.** [Exact-head CI run 36514523612, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36514523612) passed: 116 successful jobs, 21 skipped, zero failed/cancelled CI jobs. The actual tested merge was c3a0a2e90c26f5ec19179ae92f7a80e980f63d17 (main673a44e9bc9834692d47c8b6590dc2a1093d3468 + this head). Required CI/dependency/security status contexts passed. Current-head ClawSweeper is **Platinum 4/6**, **Diamond proof 5/6**, with no code/security findings or before-merge items; this is automated review, not human approval. Two auxiliary context/dispatch checks remain cancelled in the raw rollup; they are not counted as success, and the exact-head review completed separately. The previous inherited-failure run remains historical failed/cancelled evidence, not green.
- The PR stays non-draft and unmerged; auto-merge is off.

**Limits:** proof uses tiny real-loaded plugins, real catalog workers, CLI preparation composition, synthetic file/model/channel edges, and one maintained published-install upgrade scenario with existing custom plugin settings. It is not a WSL affected-host soak, SSD benchmark, live channel send, authenticated native model run, full-fleet soak, or exhaustive upgrade matrix. Earlier four-plugin installed evidence belongs to the superseded draft and is not claimed for this replacement. Wall/RSS proof-run costs are not an apples-to-apples startup-speed claim. Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper readiness are tracked separately.

prs.title: fix: recover uploaded chat images after loading fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: uploaded and local chat images remain broken without a recovery action when metadata succeeds but the image request fails or its bytes cannot be decoded.

## User Impact

Failed previews now show **Unavailable** with **Retry**. Retry checks current availability and access before loading again; permissions, existing ticket expiry, and tolerance for temporary renewal failures on already-mounted images stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native image errors do not expose an HTTP status. Report them through the existing attachment availability owner instead of ignoring local sources, and require an explicit retry rather than replaying possibly denied or missing requests. Metadata 403/404 responses also wait for an explicit retry. Canonical upload handoff failures use the same recovery path.

Reported and directed by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/ba984d5b-ba7f-46f2-9a31-362cc80eda05)

## Evidence

- Reproduced before the fix in Chromium: metadata succeeds, the native uploaded-image byte request returns 404, and no unavailable card or Retry appears.
- **10 browser tests passed:** uploaded-image 404, 503, network, and decode failures; successful explicit retries; 403/404 retry admission without further byte requests or automatic metadata retries; virtual remounts and sharing/role revocation.
- **72 focused tests passed:** local/native image presentation, canonical handoff error and timeout recovery, ticket expiry, bounded renewal, mounted-image tolerance, and attachment/resource lifecycles.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues.
- Deterministic mocked-Gateway browser tests exercise real native image requests. The original user's exact HTTP failure status remains unconfirmed; this does not claim to reproduce that historical status. No deployment is included.

### Before

![Before: a native 404 leaves a broken uploaded image with no recovery action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2edbdf5e-4f5e-498b-a4b3-fbda341933c0)

### After

![After: the failed uploaded image shows an Unavailable card and Retry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5ca075d-cafa-4f32-9d12-98c26f6760e6)

prs.title: fix(codex): materialize native tool-output images from raw response items
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #153949.

Codex's native `ImageView` tool (and other native tools that hand back an
image) surfaces to OpenClaw as a raw `function_call_output` /
`custom_tool_call_output` response item whose `output` array contains a
nested `{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:image/png;base64,..."}`
entry. `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` (the Codex media owner)
only recognized raw `image_generation_call` items and returned immediately
for anything else, so this event shape was silently dropped.
`readCodexResponseOutput` deliberately omits non-text tool output from the
text transcript on the assumption that the media owner picks it up
(`extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-tool-output.ts:129`), so
the image bytes never reached the transcript or Control UI at all: the
assistant's reply referenced "the screenshot above" while no attachment
existed anywhere.

## What Changed

- `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` now also inspects
  `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output` raw items, scanning
  their `output` array for `input_image` entries.
- Each `image_url` is validated through the existing
  `sanitizeInlineImageDataUrl` guard (same validation already used for
  Codex history payload sanitization) and decoded via the existing
  `parseImageDataUrl` helper.
- Valid images are materialized through the exact same
  `recordImage`/`materializeImage` path already used for
  `image_generation_call` results, so they get the same size cap,
  concurrent-completion dedupe, and delivery/transcript wiring as
  generated images, and are marked as a side effect
  (`hadPotentialSideEffects`).
- Invalid or missing `image_url` values are skipped (fail closed): no
  placeholder, no partial write.

This is scoped to the raw-response-item media owner only; it does not
touch the `image_generation_call` path, billing/side-effect
classification for actual image generation, or the separate
dynamic-tool-image rendering path added in #120577 (which covers a
different event shape — dynamic tool results carried on typed thread
items, not this nested raw `input_image` payload).

## Evidence

New regression test, reverted against the pre-fix source
(`git checkout HEAD~1 -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts`)
to confirm it fails without the change:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
...
FAIL  |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media
AssertionError: Target cannot be null or undefined.
 ❯ extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts:394:34
    392|     const mediaUrl = result.toolMediaUrls?.[0];
    393|
    394|     expect(result.toolMediaUrls).toHaveLength(1);
```

Restored the fix and reran — passes:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media 51ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed | 29 skipped (30)
```

Full relevant suites, all passing (89 tests):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.replay-safety.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.final-media.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.test.ts
...
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # media.test.ts + replay-safety.test.ts: 50 passed
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # run-attempt.final-media.test.ts: 9 passed
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # tool-media-payloads.test.ts: 24 passed
```

Formatting/lint on the changed files:

```
$ npx oxlint extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts
(no issues)
$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
$ git diff --check
(clean)
```

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs`'s repo-wide "line-cap growth ratchet"
check fails in this checkout, but it fails identically (same file list,
same counts) on unmodified `upstream/main` with these two files stashed
out — it's flagging pre-existing large files unrelated to this change,
not anything this PR touches.

`tsgo --noEmit` on the `extensions/codex` project reports 1618 errors in
this checkout, all `TS2307: Cannot find module 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/*'`
(missing generated plugin-sdk type declarations from a partial/source-only
dependency setup) plus pre-existing `any`/`unknown` findings in unrelated
files (e.g. `src/supervision-tools.ts`, `src/session-cli.ts`). Confirmed
the exact same 1618-error count with this branch's two files stashed out
against unmodified `upstream/main` — the type-resolution gap is an
environment limitation of this sandbox, not something introduced here.

Was not able to run a live Codex app-server round-trip in this sandbox (no
Codex credentials/harness available here); the evidence above proves the
event-projection behavior through the same test harness and fixtures the
existing `image_generation_call` regression tests in this file use.

prs.title: fix(msteams): approval cards in 1:1 chats never update after a decision
prs.body: Closes #157676 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Microsoft Teams approval cards in 1:1 chats stay on their pending buttons after the user approves or denies, and expired cards in DMs are never marked expired. ## User Impact User impact: in Teams personal chats, approval cards that expire, or are resolved anywhere other than by clicking that card (another approver, CLI, Control UI), now switch to their final state instead of keeping live buttons. Clicking a card already showed its resolved state via the invoke response, and the decision itself was always applied. ## Why This Change Was Made The native approval runtime updated the card using the stored conversation id as a bare recipient. Personal-chat ids (`a:…`) don't match the recipient parser's conversation patterns, so they were looked up as AAD user ids and failed with `No conversation reference found for user:a:…`. The update is now addressed explicitly as `conversation:`, the form the send-context parser already expects for personal chats. Channel and group ids resolve to the same stored conversation as before, so entries already pending need no migration. A broader follow-up could let the recipient parser recognise bare `a:` ids itself (there is already an `isBotFrameworkPersonalChatId` helper). I kept this diff to the one call site. ## Evidence - Observed live on 2026.9.6 against a real tenant: `msteams approval resolved {applied:true, status:"allowed"}` followed by `failed to finalize resolved native approval entry … No conversation reference found for user:a:1CgH…`, and the card stayed pending. - New regression test in `approval-handler.runtime.test.ts`: a plugin approval delivered to a personal chat is finalized with `to: "conversation:a:…"`. It fails before the change and passes after. The existing channel expectation is updated to the prefixed form. - `vitest run extensions/msteams/src/approval-handler.runtime.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/send-context.test.ts`: 23/23 passed after rebasing on current `main`. The wider approval/send suites (approval-native, approval-card-submit, approval-card, send) also passed before the rebase (79/79). - Verified live on a real tenant (2026.9.6 + this PR); redacted before/after screenshots below and in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157682#issuecomment-5831843546. **Live screenshots** (Before (card expired, buttons still live) · After (pending → finalized)): - No overlap with open approval PRs #125365 (monitor-handler / approval-control) or #148215 (approval-card-submit).

prs.title: fix: backport October update, model, and stability fixes to 2026.9.33
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: 2026.9.33 users hit update failures on pnpm/npm/Windows, missing model support (Muse Wonder, MiniMax M3.1 thinking, MiniMax OAuth refresh), lost or stalled agent work across restarts, and stalled delivery, even though October already fixed them. The September Full Release Validation also cannot start, because a dated compatibility record expired.

## User Impact

Backports **52 source commits** from `release/2026.10.5` to **extended-stable/2026.9.33**, plus three line-cap follow-ups, one compat-record status change, and the 2026.9.33 release notes. Versions, state schema (v19), dependencies, protocols, and config are unchanged. One internal type change shows up in the Plugin SDK diff (see the SDK/config warning below).

- **Updater (11):** #169665, #169563 plus its follow-up, #169658 plus its test, #169283, #170195, #170003, #170131, #170170, #170256.
- **Models/providers (12):** Muse Wonder #170232, MiniMax M3.1 #160089, MiniMax OAuth refresh #160459 (plugin-only), live thinking levels #168566 plus its fast-path follow-up, LM Studio #168039, llama.cpp #168232, DeepSeek #169728, OpenAI WebSocket close #167512, response-header deadlines #168282, Codex #168400 and #169431.
- **Runtime stability (28):** outbound #169010, channel authority #159396 with its #164848 startup-context slice, node pairing #169486 and #169575, acpx #164272, Talk #170083, session-delete cancellation ordering, routed blocking questions #170039, one-shot cron alerts #169102 (alert-only), cron writer admission #168291, restart recovery #170162 and #170252, worker replies #170223, worker claims #170161.
- **Release harness (4):** #169567, #170178, #170702, and the gateway worktree test await. These are part of this candidate's Q=C qualification closure.
- **Compat record:** `deprecated-session-store-beta5-api` moves to `removal-pending`. It passed `removeAfter` 2026-10-12, which made plugin-compatibility readiness fail every September FRV ([run 38463967274](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38463967274)). The exports keep shipping on this line; main removed them. This is a maintainer decision.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each fix is a `cherry-pick -x` that keeps the original author, adapted to September's owners. Each adapted commit's message has a `Backport adaptation:` paragraph. October architecture was not imported.

- **Audit window:** `467e83dea27` (exclusive, the prior cursor) to `1808b57b75f` (inclusive): 93 commits on `release/2026.10.5`.
- **Already covered:** 12 commits are behaviorally present on the target through #169605 or #170476.
- **Not affected:** 12 commits fix code paths the target does not have.

**Held** (these need architectural adaptation or a schema change; carried forward):
- #169410 and #170046: package-activation settlement would change the persisted journal schema.
- #168210: the synchronous ledger would need a redesign.
- #170130 and #170207: depend on #167760.
- #168077: missing admission owners.
- #169093: needs an async transcript read.
- #169144: subset port possible in a separate lane.
- #168650: needs a new subscription design.
- #153032: would widen the SDK.

**Skipped:** October version/changelog commits, macOS-app-only changes, the `--session-host` default change (#168623), the Testbox redaction change (#170113), WAL scheduler pause (#170022), and the #168361 receipt follow-ups.

**SDK/config warning:** the Plugin SDK API diff from trusted tooling between `3e97e46be43` and this head has no entrypoint or export additions or removals. Its only declaration change is an optional `resolveGatewayContext?: GatewayContextResolver` on the internal channel-manager options type. That type is reachable from public declarations, which is why 123 reachable-only rows appear. It comes from the 13-line #164848 slice that #159396 needs for the operator-client case. **The maintainer accepted this.** The config manifest is unchanged.

**Notes:**
- The interrupted worker-reply save (#170223) uses the same `.text` buffer that September already uses for placement moves. #167054 `displayText` is not available on this line.
- The claim recovery in #170161 re-reads through the existing synchronous `placements.get` accessor that the launcher already uses at about ten sites. It runs only for claims marked interrupted at startup.
- `main-session-restart-abort.integration.test.ts` (#170162) does not exist on this line, so end-to-end custody after a restart drain is a coverage gap.

## Evidence

- **Per-lane focused proof:** every adapted fix's owning and sibling suites pass. Each new regression was confirmed to fail without its production change. Lane typechecks passed: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `tsgo:scripts`, `tsgo:test:src`, and `tsgo:test:root`.
- **Changed-scope gate:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 3e97e46be43 --head 5fe263e4471` exits 0. That covers line-cap and max-lines ratchets, plugin boundaries, every tsgo lane, core/extension/script lint, the native schema guard (v19), import cycles, and the storage/pairing guards. Five unchanged files carry pre-existing max-lines warnings, not errors.
- **Release notes:** `verify-release-notes.mjs --base v2026.9.9` reports 41 PRs verified, and `pnpm changelog:check` passes.
- **Codex harness fixes:** checked against the sibling Codex source at `bf2aee99c5`. See `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/streaming.rs:127-139` and `316-330`, and `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1328-1356`.
- **New test costs:**
  - `llm-idle-timeout.request-deadline.test.ts`: about 4.0 s
  - Codex warm-cleanup unit test: about 43 s; the native variant is release-only
  - routed-question test: about 6–8 s
  - cron admission deadline cases: about 2 s each
  - The donor's 22–61 s loopback transport test was dropped.
- **Not yet run:** release qualification. A publish-purpose Full Release Validation runs on the merged tip.

## Additions after review: 2026.8.35 → 2026.9.33 upgrade path

npm `extended-stable` currently points to 2026.8.35, so most extended-stable users will reach 9.33 from 8.35. Five read-only audits covered the 8.35 updater handoff, state migration, config/auth/plugins, services/platforms, and field reports/coverage. These fixes came out of them:

- **FRV now qualifies from the extended-stable predecessor.** The `.33` upgrade baseline becomes `openclaw@2026.8.35`, with survivors `[2026.8.35, 2026.9.9]`. The cross-OS and survivor lanes run 8.35's real `extended-stable` dist-tag selection. `update:compat:check` covers the `extended-stable` tag. Landed on main as #171565; cherry-picked here with `-x`.
- **Updater inventory** adds 2026.8.33–2026.8.35, with integrity-verified tarballs and regenerated bridges plus `update-first-hop-compat-2026.8.3x` lanes.
- **Doctor time budget for old drivers.** When the 8.35 updater drives Doctor without a run ledger, optional inspections now get the bounded activation window. They are deferred instead of risking 8.35's fixed 30-minute kill.
- **pnpm 12 service units.** A unit 8.35 left pointing at a deleted `.pnpm/openclaw@2026.8.35` generation is now rewritten to the durable install link, instead of being refused as a foreign installation.
- **Kubernetes.** The manifest uses `args:`, so the image entrypoint runs `doctor --fix`. The startup probe window grows from 5 to 15 minutes.
- **Stale official plugins.** The update no longer silently keeps an official `@openclaw/*` plugin whose `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` imports don't resolve on the host. This affects 8.35 Codex/Copilot, which import the removed `agent-harness-task-runtime`.
- **CI repairs:**
  - relative import for the extracted live-switch test helpers;
  - plugin-boundary-report expectations for the new removal-pending record;
  - `MessagePort` in the registration worker mock (needed by the #168291 backport; the mock change came from October's #168008);
  - `update-rehearsal-paths.ts` added to the PR wrapper inventory (needed by #170195).

**Follow-up PRs (kept out of this one to bound its size):**
- carrying 8.35 cron "allow-always" standing grants forward;
- #162085: release the state-DB read seal after a failed drain and re-seal on retry.

**Not included:** the stopped-channel warning residual of #169037 (the recorded-success portion already shipped in #170476).

prs.title: refactor(ui): render chat previews and annotation chips with Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes another legacy rendering chain from chat: tool/browser previews, source cards, sent annotations, and their shared attachment chips still passed through Lit after the surrounding views moved to Solid.

## User Impact

The same chat controls, tags, classes, and lazy-loading boundaries are preserved. Annotation chips retain focus and identity when their attachment source is admitted or refreshed; obsolete reads abort on source replacement or disposal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser-preview caches now contain plain descriptors; the consuming Solid view owns the rendered cards. Source previews mount directly in the agent frame. Sent-comment rendering and shared chip/row markup use Solid, while the remaining Lit composer/pasted-text callers use the existing interop boundary. Test-only tool renderers move to test support instead of remaining production exports.

This is the first focused final-chat slice. Widget iframe ownership, the remaining composer/pane renderers, and PDF/HTML previews stay in their separate migration slices. Production Lit imports decrease by five files. The touched files contain 8,531 lines before and 8,574 after (+43); the remaining interop wrappers and explicit cancellation/ref ownership account for the growth.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck | Passed |
| Focused tests | 46 cases passed across source previews, tool cards, and attachment-chip admission |
| Production build, base and candidate | Passed on the same Mac |
| Strict startup performance | 349,028 → 349,047 B gzip; 1 → 1 CSS request; below 374,285 B budget |
| Visual proof | Synthetic transcript and expanded annotation, 1440×1000; before/after inspected |
| Production Knip | No new findings; 14 unused-export locations and 2 types also fail on exact base. Removed the newly dead admission adapter and obsolete tool test exports. |
| Independent review | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Broad UI and retention coverage | Final `ci:full` run [38502886690](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502886690): one inherited plugin-lifecycle failure, described below. No local full suite or E2E battery. |

The only final-run test failure is `Control UI plugin lifecycle > retains uninstall feedback through during inspection`, at `plugins-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts:269`: the notice has the two uninstall warnings but is missing `Configuration reload failed after removal.` The **same test and assertion** fail on scheduled main run [38502084044](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502084044/job/115651277712), head `c33cd2c41ad8d1ef4e54f0c88551351e47dac600`. This PR does not change the plugin lifecycle inputs. Landing uses the documented inherited-failure exception and does not claim green CI.

The first PR CI run caught a parser-to-renderer re-export cycle and two typed-lint defects. Parsing now stays in its leaf module, rendering callers import the native module directly, and cleanup/test promises are explicit. The corrected UI typecheck and typed lint pass; the architecture check passes with zero import cycles.

Five E2E cases in the first CI run exposed an eager tooltip-presentation import through the annotation renderer. The renderer now uses the lightweight tooltip custom-element entry point. A bounded cold-module browser probe confirms that chat reaches its composer with **zero requests** for the held tooltip implementation; the original candidate requested that module before chat was ready. The final startup delta is +19 B, below same-host build variance.

The first admission run exposed a fallback component being created in an ownerless effect. The fallback now renders lazily under the component owner; the seven admission cases passed on the corrected implementation. No dependency, route, Gateway, or live-state changes.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): typed level directives ignore digit and underscore aliases
prs.body:
Closes #168254

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: typed level directives ignore digit aliases such as `/verbose 1` and partially consume underscore aliases such as `/think think_hard`, selecting the wrong level.

## User Impact

Typed commands now accept the same digit and underscore aliases as native commands. `/verbose 1` enables verbose and `/think think_hard` selects low; ordinary prose and existing letter-only levels retain their interpretation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing level parser now includes digits and underscores in its token, while retaining the existing normalizers and invalid-token/prose handling. No new parsing owner, configuration, or state migration is introduced.

Thanks to @DonnieFi for this fix and to @yetval for reporting #168254 and the earlier fix in #164698.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Built baseline `72ccf6ff92931fff2d49473fe1571f39e8311ad2` and candidate `49a43655b23f31a9dec7cb763a2bc74734de6143` in an isolated Node 24 container. Started the real built Gateway with qa-channel and the repository QA bus/mock provider. Submitted each input through `POST /v1/inbound/message` and captured replies through `GET /v1/state`:

```text
Input: /verbose 1
Base: Current verbose level: off. Options: on, full, off.
Head: Verbose logging enabled.

Input: /think think_hard
Base: Thinking level "minimal" is not supported for openai/gpt-5.6-luna.
      Use one of: off, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra.
Head: Thinking level set to low.

Control: /think high
Base and head: Thinking level set to high.

Control: /verbose 3d printing tips
Base: Current verbose level: off. Options: on, full, off.
Head: Current verbose level: on. Options: on, full, off.
```

The prose control queries the current setting without changing it (head was enabled by the first input). The focused parser regression additionally verifies that `3d printing tips` remains intact as prose.

- Focused parser file: 74 tests passed; 1.09s Vitest duration, 2.15s runner wall time.
- Changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint: passed.
- Simplification: retained the existing parser and normalizers; no redundant machinery added. Production delta +1/-3, test delta +17/-0 against the merge base. Added cases cover digit aliases, underscore aliases and digit-prefixed prose.
- Both Gateway runs stopped cleanly with no cleanup errors. No live provider claim; this change only repairs typed directive tokenization.

### Telegram Test Server proof

Also exercised both builds through real Telegram DMs using a Convex-leased user/bot pair and the repository TDLib recorder. Native commands and native skills were disabled at both the root and Telegram config levels, so these messages exercised typed-text parsing. The lease was released and credential files removed in `finally`.

Captured replies (same five messages, in order):

```text
Input                         Base reply                 Head reply
/verbose 1                    OPENCLAW_E2E_OK            Verbose logging enabled.
/think think_hard             OPENCLAW_E2E_OK            Thinking level set to low.
/think extra_high             OPENCLAW_E2E_OK            Thinking level set to xhigh.
/verbose 3d printing tips      OPENCLAW_E2E_OK            OPENCLAW_E2E_OK
/think high                   Thinking level set to high. Thinking level set to high.
```

`OPENCLAW_E2E_OK` is the mock provider's response, not a directive acknowledgment. Baseline provider requests received the leaked user-text tails `1`, `_hard`, and `extra_high`. The head produced **zero agent turns for all three repaired aliases**. Its only agent turn was the prose control, whose prompt retained exactly `3d printing tips`; background activity-recap and embedding requests were counted separately. Both runs retained the `/think high` control.

TDLib captured head acknowledgments at 2.501s, 11.712s, and 21.503s after recording began, following sends at 0.416s, 10.383s, and 20.238s. Each run completed successfully and removed its private runtime scratch.

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting fully restores the old parser without a schema migration. Blast radius is typed level directives across text channels; native strict command parsing is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): stop inheriting Claude Code's prompt and memory surfaces on the Agent SDK path
prs.body:
Stops an OpenClaw agent on the `claude-cli` backend from inheriting Claude Code's own prompt and memory surfaces on top of its own.

Two changes, both in `agent-sdk.runtime.ts`:
1. Replace the `claude_code` preset system prompt with OpenClaw's, so the agent runs with one system prompt instead of two.
2. Disable Claude Code's auto-memory index and `CLAUDE.md` pickup — the same two keys OpenClaw already sets on its restricted-run path.

Part of #137124.

> **Scope was reduced twice.** Earlier revisions also flipped `systemPromptMode` on the backend descriptor (inert — reverted in 492c42d) and added `--tools Skill` to restrict Claude Code's built-in tools (**wrong and harmful** — reverted in 452b406, see [Withdrawn](#withdrawn-the---tools-restriction)). What remains is the `agent-sdk.runtime.ts` change and its test update.

## What Problem This Solves

`resolveClaudeAgentSdkOptions` consumes the backend args itself and `continue`s past every `--*system-prompt*` flag (they are members of `CLAUDE_STREAM_PROTOCOL_VALUE_FLAGS`), then hardcodes:

```ts
systemPrompt: { type: "preset", preset: "claude_code", append: context.systemPrompt }
```

A second branch (`excludeDynamicSystemPromptSections`, active for Claude Code ≥ 2.1.98) does the same. So OpenClaw's own `cli_backend` system prompt always ran *on top of* the full Claude Code harness prompt, and the backend descriptor's `systemPromptFileArg` / `systemPromptMode` were never the owner for normal agent runs.

Two prompts means two identities. In production the harness identity reached an end user over Telegram:

> "I need the original … screenshot to redo this properly, but I don't have image access in this CLI context — that request needs to run in the OpenClaw session where the image lives."

A chat user has no concept of "this CLI context".

## Change

```diff
- systemPrompt: { type: "preset", preset: "claude_code", append: context.systemPrompt }
+ systemPrompt: context.systemPrompt
```

…at both sites. Per the Agent SDK contract a string `systemPrompt` is a full custom prompt and no preset is loaded (`sdk.d.ts`: `systemPrompt?: string | string[] | { type: 'preset'; … }`).

And, after the arg loop:

```ts
options.settings = {
  autoMemoryEnabled: false,
  claudeMdExcludes: ["**/CLAUDE.md", "**/CLAUDE.local.md", "**/.claude/rules/**"],
};
```

These are not new policy — they are two of the four keys already in `CLAUDE_RESTRICTED_SETTINGS` (`cli-shared.ts`):

```json
{"disableAllHooks":true,"enabledPlugins":{},"autoMemoryEnabled":false,
 "claudeMdExcludes":["**/CLAUDE.md","**/CLAUDE.local.md","**/.claude/rules/**"]}
```

A restricted run already declines the host's memory surfaces; a normal agent run never did, so a gateway agent carried Claude Code's auto-memory index and any `CLAUDE.md` reachable from cwd alongside its own `AGENTS.md` / `MEMORY.md`. `disableAllHooks` and `enabledPlugins` are deliberately **not** copied — the former would also kill OpenClaw's own `UserPromptSubmit` and `PreToolUse` hooks, which carry its context injection and permission gate.

OpenClaw's `cli_backend` prompt is self-contained for this: `system-prompt-params.ts` forces tool guidance, the skills section, and the read-tool name on for that surface, so nothing downstream was relying on the preset to describe the agent's own tooling.

## Evidence

Live 2026.8.1 gateway, Claude Code 2.1.241, on a **real Telegram turn** (not a CLI-initiated probe). A temporary probe inside `resolveClaudeAgentSdkOptions` recorded what the SDK actually received:

```json
{
  "spType": "string",
  "spIsPreset": false,
  "spHead": "You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw.\n## Tooling\nTools policy-filtered. Names case-s",
  "spLen": 30892,
  "plugins": ["/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-claude-skills-Js5c01/openclaw-skills"]
}
```

`spIsPreset: false` and the prompt opening with OpenClaw's own first line confirm the `claude_code` preset is no longer loaded and OpenClaw's prompt is the whole system prompt.

For the memory settings, the probe confirms they reach the SDK:

```json
{"settingSources":[],"settings":{"autoMemoryEnabled":false,
 "claudeMdExcludes":["**/CLAUDE.md","**/CLAUDE.local.md","**/.claude/rules/**"]},"spType":"string"}
```

and the agent, asked whether a Claude Code memory index is present in its context, went from describing one ("`claudeMd` … Claude Code 那边自动带的 memory index，跟 OpenClaw 的 MEMORY.md 是两套不同系统") to answering plainly: **没有** (no).

Skills are unaffected — `--plugin-dir` delivery still works with a string prompt. A normal gateway turn lists `openclaw-skills:browser`, `:oracle`, `:summarize`, and in a standalone control a plugin-provided skill was both discovered and successfully invoked under `--system-prompt-file`.

## Withdrawn: the `--tools` restriction

An earlier revision added `--tools Skill` to `CLAUDE_CLI_DEFAULT_ARGS`, arguing Claude Code's built-ins duplicated OpenClaw's MCP tools. **That premise was wrong and the change broke the backend.** Recording it here because the reasoning may save someone else the same mistake.

On the `cli_backend` prompt surface OpenClaw describes its own `exec` as *"Run shell on connected node; sync; host=node"* and ships no `read`/`write`/`edit`/`process` MCP tools to that surface at all. Local shell and filesystem access are **delegated to the harness's native tools by design** — which is what `nativeToolMode: "selectable"` and `selectedNativeToolsProvideFileAccess` are reasoning about. `exec` (remote node) and native `Bash` (local) are different execution targets, not duplicates.

With `--tools Skill` applied, the agent had no local execution and no file access. Asked to write and read back a file:

> "没做成。exec 工具报错：`requires a paired node (none available)` … 我没有可用的文件写入/读取工具" — task BLOCKED, file never created.

After reverting, the same request succeeded via native `Bash` and the file was created.

Worse, my original evidence *was* that failure: I cited the agent reaching for `exec` instead of `Bash` as proof the restriction worked, and quoted the `host=node requires a paired node` error in this PR body without registering that it was the breakage. Retracted.

## Notes

- `agent-sdk.runtime.test.ts`'s warm-restart assertion expected `systemPrompt: objectContaining({ append })` and is updated to expect the string. It was the only test asserting the preset shape.
- `--setting-sources` is a related but separate issue and is **not** touched here. `normalizeClaudeArgs` forces `CLAUDE_SAFE_SETTING_SOURCES = "user"` unconditionally, so a gateway inherits whatever Claude Code plugins the host operator has enabled and their hooks fire on every agent turn — on my machine a third-party plugin's `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit` hooks inject a large document plus per-turn "MANDATORY: You must run Skill(...)" text. `[]` is the same isolation argument taken further (and matches what running the model over the plain API looks like), but it also drops the operator's user-level skills and plugins, so it reads as a config knob — ideally defaulting to `[]` for unattended runs — rather than a straight flip. Worth noting OpenClaw already passes `--setting-sources ""` on its own restricted-run path, so the empty value is not foreign to the design.
- The paired-node path (`src/node-host/invoke-agent-cli-claude.ts`) still uses `--append-system-prompt-file`; separate execution path, left untouched.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: perf(control-ui): avoid covered Inbox refreshes on reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link can repeat Inbox list reads even when the first response already includes the invalidating events. The campaign evidence records eight session-list requests (about 1,038 KB) and five mention-list requests in roughly 11 seconds; this PR addresses the proven mention-owner redundancy.

## User Impact

The Inbox fills from one scoped snapshot when its response covers the boot events. Refreshes still fetch genuinely newer events, and a delayed list cannot restore an already-dismissed mention. No protocol, server schema, config, or layout changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway may publish `mentions.changed` while preparing `mentions.list`, then return that same revision. The client previously always queued a follow-up. The existing owner now tracks the admitted and requested revisions, joins explicit in-flight reads, and retains one trailing refresh only for uncovered events. The old loaded flag is removed. The cold-load probe now captures request parameters and caller stacks for attribution. One initial Inbox read remains because the application attention badge consumes its data even when the presenter is closed; deferring every read while preserving that badge would require a different server contract.

The synthetic Team-scale bench's six session-list calls represent two agent-roster pages, the selected-agent sidebar, the independent owner-count facet, and two child-session pages. Their scope, ordering, enrichment, or aggregate contracts differ, so projecting one from another would not preserve membership. Seven message subscriptions cover the transcript and six visible roster narrations. Six plugin activation reports target distinct plugins; the existing method accepts one plugin per call. One cron list comes from Inbox health. No speculative session-list dedupe or protocol batching was added.

## Evidence

The production-bundle Team-scale bench was augmented to advertise the Inbox, return revision 4, and emit four targeted mention revisions alongside the existing synthetic boot events. The supplied WS census probe and source-mapped request stacks confirmed:

| Method | Before → after requests | Before → after response bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `mentions.list` | 2 → 1 | 298 → 149 |
| `sessions.list` | 6 → 6 | 552,282 → 552,282 |
| `plugins.controlUi.report` | 6 → 6 | 558 → 558 |
| `sessions.messages.subscribe` | 7 → 7 | 1,013 → 1,013 |
| `sessions.describe` | 30 → 30 | 26,772 → 26,772 |
| `cron.list` | 1 → 1 | 84 → 84 |

Total RPCs: 87 → 86. These are synthetic counts, not a reproduction of every live-census request. Wall-clock timing on the loaded Mac is noisy and is not used to claim a speed improvement. No private captures or content are included.

Focused owner tests: 26/26 passed, 55.02 s wall time with `pnpm test ui/src/app/mentions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (26/26; focused wrapper also passed in 17.33 s). Three added/extended regressions failed before the fix for redundant reads. Covered events, replayed revisions, manual joining, real trailing invalidations, stale dismissal replies, scope changes, retries, and revocation remain covered. Independent autoreview: scoped-clean through P2.

AWS Crabbox `cbx_f8e271238720`, run `run_ad1e53cf03ff4185f9bcd6c644095336`, verified exact head `c4cc6b159ec17519ec8950c7835f2522fb1f761f` and hashes of the three changed files. Focused tests passed 26/26 in 4.23 s. Formatting, lint, ratchets, i18n, all core type graphs, and UI typecheck passed. `check-changed` failed only its unused-export scan, listing symbols outside this diff; comparison with main is pending.

On the same lease, run `run_d326003c848366824f84710924bdfe8d`: `inbox-dismissal-clarity.e2e.test.ts` passed 2/2 and `mobile-inbox-sheet.e2e.test.ts` passed 3/3, each invoked separately with one worker. Full UI e2e is running.

Exact-head CI is red in [checks-ui (2/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38503287205/job/115655280896): two existing terminal reconnect assertions expect `terminal.open` / `terminal.attach`. The saved failing log was fetched once. These cases pass in observed main Node evidence, while this PR ran the pinned Bun fork; inherited status is not yet proven. No CI rerun or unrelated terminal change was made.

Production LOC delta: +24 (34 added, 10 removed): +10 in the Inbox owner to honor the existing revision contract and +14 in the benchmark probe for requested caller attribution. Tests excluded; no changelog edit. Release-note context: reduce redundant Control UI Inbox requests during reload/reconnect and preserve dismissals against delayed list replies.
