prs.title: fix: honor silent turn endings without fabricated answers
prs.body:
Related: #170147, #150539

## What this fixes

An agent turn must end with a real answer, an intentional silent outcome, or an honest failure. This removes fabricated completion messages and makes the terminal producer own the reply protocol once, before display transforms. Delivery, history clients, and channel adapters no longer guess the outcome from already-prepared text.

**Non-goal:** this separates intentional silence, missing output, and a completed answer; it does not judge whether visible narration is accurate. “I started the watcher” remains ordinary visible text. No factuality judge is added.

## User impact

- An exact uppercase `NO_REPLY`, ignoring surrounding whitespace, ends an external-chat turn silently. This also applies after cross-chat sends, reactions, group chatter, or a deliberate yield. Already-sent messages and pending delegated work remain intact.
- A literal leading `NO_REPLY\n` removes that one line. The suffix remains visible, even if it is another `NO_REPLY`. Punctuation, quotes, JSON, lowercase, and prose are ordinary text rather than silence.
- Streaming holds at most eight control-token characters (plus surrounding whitespace), released immediately on disambiguating text or terminal completion.
- Where silent-reply guidance remains present—in group, channel, messaging, and spawn prompts—it explains that `NO_REPLY` discards unsent text, so confirmations must be sent first. Direct-message prompts keep their existing omission.
- Private completions, subagents, and Control UI result-required turns still need a result. Progress-only message-tool mirrors do not satisfy that requirement; a completed current-source final does.
- Empty finals remain failures. Existing bounded tool-free recovery is retained. When an admitted user request still has no answer, its status notice is: **No answer was returned. Ask again if you still need one.** It does not claim that actions succeeded or that none occurred. The ordinary missing-answer notice is not saved as a fabricated assistant answer.
- Heartbeat, cron, and other internal failures stay recorded without periodic missing-answer notices. Existing actionable provider guidance and once-per-incident uncertain-delivery notices remain.
- Failed-child delivery uses the same concise copy but keeps shipped requester-history mirroring unchanged. Successful child mirrors are unchanged.
- If retention removes a completed child's full transcript, the existing `[truncated-by-retention: complete child answer unavailable]` note identifies its retained partial result. It is not presented as a complete answer.
- Waiting for a run returns that run's full stored final, not a later run's answer from the same session. A recorded visible completion retains its full answer even if the same run later emits `NO_REPLY`.

No new database schema, transport field, channel callback, recovery loop, or configuration flag. The separate provider carrier/cache repair is not part of this PR.

## Ownership and compatibility

Existing CLI native-control and isolated strict-visible operations keep their valid-empty completion contract, including when the surrounding policy requires a result. Their terminal fact remains `empty`, not fabricated silence. Ordinary result-required agent turns still reject empty or silent output.

`prepareAgentRunTerminalReply` is the single raw-final preparation entry point: classify, remove one literal leading line, then render the suffix without classifying it again. Embedded, CLI, ACP, native harness, and worker producers publish terminal facts. Consumers use those facts plus the full prepared body, never the bounded lifecycle snapshot as the delivered answer. Stored assistant readers honor existing display/phase/final-source facts before the raw protocol check; user rows are not classified.

This intentionally removes the two silence-parser exports and redundant `SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN` re-export from `reply-chunking`. The exact raw-input helper and token remain in `reply-runtime`; delivery plugins must not use the helper on prepared payloads. The approved removals are recorded in the existing SDK compatibility registry and migration guide, without shims or a public export-budget increase.

A provider failure cannot become success merely because recovery is silent. A background completion rejected by the existing terminal permission check stays failed rather than being reported completed; that rejected path made no destination send attempt. Permission checks are unchanged.

Maintainer-intent check: no new Pash/Sarah overlap in the reconciled agent, reply, Gateway, runtime-evidence, native-projector, or memory owners. Existing contributor attribution is preserved.

## Why one PR

These independently reviewable prerequisite fixes are retained because the cutover relies on truthful terminal facts:

- **CLI terminal facts:** `src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.ts` (`buildCliRunResult`) and `src/agents/cli-runner.ts` can publish the existing terminal snapshot for every terminal outcome without changing silence policy.
- **Truthful follow-up failure:** removing the post-settlement overlay in `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.ts` is independently correct. It undoes an earlier iteration of this PR; that overlay deletion leaves no separate diff against the merge base. The retained error-copy fallback in that file preserves real failure metadata.
- **Finite-cap rejection:** `src/gateway/mcp-http.exec-completion.test.ts` pins the existing terminal ownership rejection and absence of any destination send. Once producers publish every terminal fact, restoring `completed` here would mask a rejected `onTerminal` callback with a second outcome classification. Permission checks in `session-event-handoff.ts` and `session-event-target.ts` are unchanged.

The behavior-neutral streaming-predicate import change stays in its already-touched owner; it adds no separate behavior. `reply-completion.ts`'s imports support its new policy responsibilities. No independent user-visible cleanup is bundled with the contract.

The remaining groups depend on one shared cutover:

- **Terminal producers and completion/recovery** (`agent-run-terminal-reply.ts`, `reply-completion.ts`, embedded/CLI/ACP/native/worker producers): the exact raw decision and the once-stripped full body must be published together. Empty output must keep recovery while explicit silence must stop it.
- **Delivery, channel adapters, and clients** (`src/auto-reply/reply`, `src/infra/outbound`, Slack/Teams, Gateway live projection, Control UI, and native narration): removing downstream parsers alone would leak controls; changing producers alone would let old tolerant parsers silently discard newly visible punctuation, JSON, or literal suffixes.
- **Stored history and memory** (`message-visibility.ts`, `chat-history-text.ts`, Gateway history projection, `transcript-visible-record.ts`, and `packages/memory-host-sdk`): reload and archive readers must apply the same raw rule while respecting already-prepared display/source facts, or the delivered answer changes after reload.
- **Child, A2A, and cron result delivery** (`subagents/announce`, `subagents/completion`, `run-wait.ts`, `sessions-send-tool.a2a.ts`, and `cron/isolated-agent`): these consumers must distinguish the terminal fact from the complete retained transcript body. Otherwise silent results resurrect text or bounded snapshots truncate reports.
- **Missing-answer and continuation UX** (`agent-runner-failure-reply.ts`, settled-turn finalization, waiting status, and pending delivery): canned stand-ins can be removed only with honest empty-result failure and retained continuation custody; deliberate silence must not be mistaken for either.
- **SDK, prompts, and docs** (`reply-chunking.ts`, `reply-runtime.ts`, harness SDK exports, compatibility registry, and the documented prompt owners): the exported contract and instructions must match the producer/consumer behavior in the same release. No compatibility parser or alias is retained.
- **CI-required dependency and contract plumbing:** the browser-safe stored-row owner, memory visibility leaf bridge, wrapper source-closure update, mock/export ratchets, and removal of a redundant SDK export keep the cutover loadable and its existing gates meaningful. The memory bridge removes the demonstrated runtime import cycle; none of these is an unrelated style cleanup.

## Validation

Proof-window head: `6d0e361ded2dda50d921916dc2e0c4e25f65fb07`.

- **Focused regressions:** 67 files expected and 67 executed in the original cutover batch, followed by exact-file reruns for corrected owner and fixture seams. Additional memory, registered-store, and callback regressions pass. Commands use `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts <files>` directly.
- **Progress parity:** the WebChat progress-card regression passes. Required internal results retain progress, failure surfacing, and stalled-turn recovery; only explicit-silence acceptance differs from external chats.
- **Static checks:** changed-file formatting and lint pass. The enforced SDK surface check passes at 3,758 public exports and 2,193 callable exports within the repository budgets; neither budget was increased.
- **Builds:** both the supported private-QA runtime build and normal public package build pass on the proof-window head. The local full private-QA build failed its declaration-size check; no declaration-size pass is claimed or budget changed.
- **Real-boundary integration:** four expected files executed, 76 tests passed. The exhausted-empty and direct-fallback QA scenarios also pass through the built Gateway and QA transport, without changing the empty mock into an authored answer.
- **Latest-stable upgrade:** the existing published-driver Docker lane passes from stable `2026.10.3` to this candidate through `openclaw update`; readiness is 200, the running commit matches, settings and durable history survive, and repeat maintenance passes. This lane has fixed seeds, so the approved complementary existing archive/legacy tests cover the exact control rows and retained child results: four expected files executed, 40 tests passed.

### Live Telegram results

All recordings below use proof-window head `6d0e361ded2dda50d921916dc2e0c4e25f65fb07`, real OpenAI and Anthropic providers, and Telegram Test Server. Empty-output cases remove visible text at the provider HTTP boundary, including recovery output. Other calls are unmodified.

| Scenario | OpenAI | Anthropic |
|---|---|---|
| Cross-chat send, then `NO_REPLY` | One destination message; no source text | One destination message; no source text |
| Reaction | One thumbs-up; no source text; authored `NO_REPLY` | One thumbs-up; no source text; direct tool completion, not authored `NO_REPLY` |
| Group chatter, then `NO_REPLY` | No text or notice | No text or notice |
| Exhausted empty final | One status notice; zero notice assistant rows | One status notice; zero notice assistant rows |
| Deliberate yield | One ACK, then one complete child result | One ACK, then one complete child result |
| `NO_REPLY` plus literal suffix | Only the suffix delivered | Only the suffix delivered |
| Ordinary answer | `Paris` delivered once | `Paris` delivered once |
| Punctuated `NO_REPLY.` | Delivered verbatim | Not part of the requested matrix |

Coverage limits: the reaction's direct-tool completion on Anthropic and the two explicit `sessions_yield` cells do not prove an authored `NO_REPLY` after those actions; focused regressions cover those exact protocol combinations. All 15 runs released leases, removed secret scratch, freed ports, and deleted their test topics/messages.

Final CI head: `6b053fc106d33aeb2731ac71761fa0b9f4115658`, after one merge of main `f36667c0b167e20b3704cb644055bd463529413b` and the bounded public-share repair below. The sole merge conflict was main's extraction of the Talk test helper; its producer fixture retains the visible terminal fact. The conflict-owner suite passed: one expected file executed, 19 tests passed, three existing skips.

The final review found a public-share consumer that still rendered raw leading control lines and lost prepared literal text through a heartbeat projection. It now uses the existing stored-row preparation helper and heartbeat-only text handling. Raw string/block rows and already-prepared display/mirror rows render the same literal suffix; both public rendering/reader files pass (two expected, two executed, 35 tests). This repair affects only public-share rendering, not the shared producer, core delivery, Telegram scenarios, or upgrade inputs, so their frozen-head proof is retained. PR CI and exact-head ClawSweeper review are pending. **HOLD: do not merge.**

## Retained follow-ups

- Failed-child status classification and requester mirror.
- Text-independent progress handoff for media continuation. This PR keeps the shipped waiting text where existing transports need it to adopt the media progress card; there is no new Telegram/Discord hook.
- Native interrupted-status handling without the host's abort receipt; existing abort ownership is unchanged.

## Inherited CI evidence

The earlier asset check was compared on candidate and unchanged merge base `3e4745caacd` with identical dependencies and Node 24.21.0. Both produced byte-identical ClawRouter manifest drift (`58dc1ca82e99` to `e9d84b43efd3`); no candidate-only asset difference was found. The generated gate was not overridden or repaired by hand.

The earlier admitted-worker auth fixture and mocked browser recovery failures were also reproduced on untouched CI base `95b3b97`. Those independent failures and their previous evidence remain recorded; new-head CI results will be reported separately.

prs.title: fix(irc): disconnect when an inbound line exceeds 512 bytes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The IRC client already refuses to send a line longer than 512 bytes. Inbound bytes were different. Socket data was appended until a line feed arrived, with no maximum. A peer that never sends LF keeps that buffer until the process runs out of memory.

Complete lines and the still-pending record are now measured in UTF-8 bytes. More than 510 bytes of payload (512 including CRLF) reports `IRC inbound line exceeds the 512-byte limit` and destroys the socket. A legal 512-byte line, including one split across two writes, still parses, and PING still receives PONG.

Closing the socket from this limit sets the closed flag before the socket emits close. The close listener therefore never runs. After registration, the client now calls the disconnect callback once so the channel monitor can reconnect. Before registration, and on an ordinary quit, that callback stays silent.

This client does not parse IRCv3 message tags. A server that sends a tagged line over 512 bytes will be disconnected. That is the same wire cap already used for outbound PRIVMSG.

Pull request 107376 added this bound earlier and was closed by its author on 2026-07-19. The unbounded buffer is still on main. There is no open issue for this defect.

## Evidence

Terminal output from production `connectIrcClient` against a loopback TCP server on 127.0.0.1. Node v26.9.0. The command ran in the patched tree and is not part of the diff.

Before the bound, the same unterminated 1 MiB write left the socket open for more than one second. Before the disconnect callback, a registered client closed on that write without notifying the monitor.

After the bound and the disconnect callback:

```console
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-irc-line-limit.mts
node v26.9.0
legal line bytes 512
legal ping seen true
ready after legal line true
PONG bytes 510
disconnects after legal line 0
oversized close ms 5
oversized errors ["IRC inbound line exceeds the 512-byte limit"]
disconnects after oversized 1
ready after oversized false
open sockets 0
before ready error IRC inbound line exceeds the 512-byte limit
disconnects before ready 0
open sockets before ready 0
disconnects after quit 0
open sockets after quit 0
DONE
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Inbound IRC data with no line feed was retained with no size cap. Complete lines and the pending record now close the socket when the UTF-8 payload exceeds 510 bytes. After registration that close notifies the disconnect callback once. Before registration, and on quit, it does not.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node v26.9.0, production connectIrcClient from the patched tree, loopback TCP on 127.0.0.1.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** From the patched tree, start a loopback TCP server, call connectIrcClient, write a 510-byte PING split after 200 bytes followed by CRLF, then write 1 MiB with no line feed. Repeat with 600 bytes before the welcome numeric, and with quit after welcome. Command: pnpm exec tsx proof-irc-line-limit.mts
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output copied below.
```console
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-irc-line-limit.mts
node v26.9.0
legal line bytes 512
legal ping seen true
ready after legal line true
PONG bytes 510
disconnects after legal line 0
oversized close ms 5
oversized errors ["IRC inbound line exceeds the 512-byte limit"]
disconnects after oversized 1
ready after oversized false
open sockets 0
before ready error IRC inbound line exceeds the 512-byte limit
disconnects before ready 0
open sockets before ready 0
disconnects after quit 0
open sockets after quit 0
DONE
```
- **Observed result after fix:** The 512-byte PING was accepted, the client stayed ready, and the PONG line was 510 bytes. The disconnect callback stayed at 0. The unterminated 1 MiB write closed the peer in 5 ms, reported IRC inbound line exceeds the 512-byte limit, called the disconnect callback once, left isReady false, and left no peer socket open. The same oversized write before welcome rejected registration, called the callback 0 times, and closed the socket. quit after welcome also called the callback 0 times.
- **What was not tested:** A public IRC network, TLS, and IRCv3 tagged lines longer than 512 bytes. Those oversized tagged lines now disconnect. The channel monitor reconnect delay was not part of this loopback run. The monitor already schedules that delay from the same disconnect callback.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): project Claude's automatic compaction boundary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`parseClaudeCliJsonlLifecycleEvent` matches only `status: "compacting"` and `compact_result`. Both records accompany an **operator-driven** `/compact`. **Automatic** compaction emits neither — its only record is a `compact_boundary` — so when Claude Code compacts a session on its own, OpenClaw observes nothing: no `compaction` lifecycle event and no operator-facing notice.

`cli-output.test.ts` pins `{type:"system",subtype:"compact_boundary"}` to `null` under a test named "without inferring from the boundary". That guard is sound: `compact_result` reports **both** success and failure, while a boundary appears only on success, so inferring from a boundary the status lifecycle already covers would double-report the same compaction.

The gap is narrower than the guard. Automatic compaction produces no status record at all, so there is nothing to double-report there. This projects the boundary **only** when its metadata says `trigger: "auto"`:

- `trigger: "auto"` → `{ kind: "compaction", phase: "end", completed: true }`
- `trigger: "manual"` → `null` (the status lifecycle owns it)
- absent or unrecognized trigger → `null`

The existing assertion passes unchanged, because a bare boundary carries no metadata.

## Evidence

A genuine automatic-compaction record from a local Claude Code transcript under `~/.claude/projects/` (a Claude Code CLI session on my machine, not an OpenClaw-driven one — see Limits below):

```
type            = "system"
subtype         = "compact_boundary"
compactMetadata = { trigger: "auto", preTokens: 1001529, postTokens: 10687,
                    cumulativeDroppedTokens: 990842, durationMs: 150520,
                    preservedMessages: {...}, preservedSegment: {...} }
```

That session contains **zero** genuine `compact_result` system records, so on the current projection this compaction produced no lifecycle event at all. Scanning every transcript in that directory, `compact_boundary` appears in 96 lines but only 1 is a real system record; the other 95 are the string quoted inside message content, which is why a substring scan alone overstates it.

Field spelling: the Agent SDK types this as `SDKCompactBoundaryMessage.compact_metadata.trigger: 'manual' | 'auto'` (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.239, `sdk.d.ts`), while the on-disk transcript above spells the same payload `compactMetadata`. Both are accepted so the projection does not depend on which reaches the stream.

Replaying that exact transcript line through the changed projection (extracted verbatim, run outside vitest — see Limits):

```
before (current filter): line contains neither "compacting" nor "compact_result" -> dropped (null)
after:                   {"kind":"compaction","phase":"end","completed":true}
```

The same harness re-checks the behaviours this must not disturb — bare boundary, `status: "compacting"`, `compact_result` success and failure, `status: null`, manual boundary, trigger-less boundary, unrelated records: 10/10 unchanged or as specified.

Tests: `cli-output.test.ts` adds a case covering both spellings for `trigger: "auto"` and asserts that `manual` and trigger-less boundaries still project nothing. The pre-existing bare-boundary assertion is untouched.

## Limits

The observed record is from a plain Claude Code session, not one driven by OpenClaw's `claude-cli` backend — I have no captured instance of an OpenClaw-driven session auto-compacting. The record's shape is what this patch keys on and it is Claude Code's own output either way, but I have not confirmed end to end that the projection fires inside a gateway run.

## Scope

This restores the observation only. It does not change compaction ownership, does not touch `ownsNativeCompaction`, and does not by itself re-arm the pre-compaction memory flush discussed in #137613 — the lifecycle event currently feeds the live `compaction` event stream, not session accounting. Wiring it to `compactionCount` is a separate change that needs the maintainer decision already open on that issue. This is the prerequisite: without a signal, that decision has nothing to act on.

## Follow-up: replay dedup (2026-09-23)

A resumed or retried stream replays history byte-identically, so a replayed automatic `compact_boundary` would be reported as a second, new compaction. The streaming JSONL parser now remembers which source lines already produced a compaction lifecycle event and skips re-emission within one stream; distinct boundaries still each report.

### Evidence (production path)

A local harness (`proof-138010.ts`, not committed) exercises the real production composition — `buildAnthropicCliBackend()` → `createCliJsonlStreamingParser()` with the registered `parseClaudeCliJsonlLifecycleEvent` → `onCompaction`:

- live automatic boundary (`trigger: "auto"`) → exactly one `{phase: "end", completed: true}`
- operator `/compact` (status lifecycle + manual boundary) → `{phase: "start"}` + `{phase: "end", completed: true}`, no double-report from the manual boundary
- the same automatic boundary record twice through one parser (resume replay within a stream) → one call, not two
- two distinct automatic boundaries in one stream → two calls (no over-suppression)

`src/agents/cli-output-stream.test.ts` gains a regression test pinning the replay behavior. All touched-area suites pass locally: `cli-output-stream.test.ts` (36), `cli-output-events.test.ts` (13), `extensions/anthropic/cli-output.test.ts` (34). (Run under bun with a minimal vitest shim — no pnpm install in this checkout; the shim is harness-only and not committed.)

### Known residual

A brand-new parser (fresh CLI process) cannot tell a replayed boundary from a live one, so cross-run resume replay of an old boundary still reports once per new stream. Suppressing that would need a durable compaction owner (checkpointed boundary, resume offset, or provider-owned transport state), which this change deliberately does not invent.

prs.title: fix: clear stale errors after suggested task retry
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an error banner remains after a failed suggested-task launch succeeds on retry.

## User Impact

User impact: a confirmed retry removes its stale error without clearing unrelated or newer chat errors, including errors with identical text. Launch behavior, permissions, and recovery controls are unchanged; no migration or user action is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The suggested-task controller already owns the retry outcome, but its earlier error was copied into two shared chat fields without a cleanup owner. Shared error writes now retain independent identity, and a successful retry clears only the writes still owned by that failed acceptance. Cleanup stays behind the existing current-operation and valid-response checks.

Requested and reproduced by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/f311ad5d-02b4-4438-9599-ee3f472c2c65)

## Evidence

- Red/green through the real pane controller with only Gateway requests mocked: synthetic session-creation rejection, same-task retry, valid task ID/session key, recovered card hidden, both owned error fields cleared. All four recovery variants failed on the original implementation.
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-task-suggestions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **32 passed**, **8.99 s command wall time** (5.56 s Vitest). Includes independently replaced fields, identical-text newer errors, another task failing during recovery, and unrelated errors on first-attempt success. Six added cases took approximately **0.03 s test-body time** locally; hosted UI shards completed in 427/348/411 s (1,186 runner-seconds total including setup and the broader UI suite; incremental cost of these cases is not isolated). Exact-head [CI run 38506036732](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38506036732) and the required CI gate passed.
- Shared-state sibling proof: **156 passed** across `chat-state.test.ts` and `chat-state-queued-edit.test.ts`.
- Targeted oxlint, UI typecheck, formatting, line-cap/max-lines ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Production Control UI build passed (23.82 s Vite build).
- Independent review: no actionable findings.

This is an error-lifecycle correction with no template, layout, or styling changes. Proof is at the controller boundary rather than a live Gateway.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep ordinary turns available without Computer Use
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary Codex text and image turns fail to start when the optional Computer Use plugin, marketplace entry, or MCP server is unavailable.

## User Impact

User impact: ordinary Codex turns remain available without Computer Use; explicit Computer Use status, installation, and invocation-time approval/security behavior remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Non-strict Codex app-server startup treats unavailable optional Computer Use setup as non-blocking. Existing `autoInstall` setups still install or re-enable the plugin before startup, and explicit `strictReadiness` setups still require a successful readiness check. Periodic health checks discover the available MCP tool dynamically, while explicit status/install commands continue to explain and repair availability.

Related: #155440

## Evidence

- Real native runtime, deliberately nonexistent Computer Use marketplace: non-strict startup logged the setup failure and returned `ORDINARY_CODEX_TURN_OK` from `openai/gpt-6-astra` (`ok: true`, `status: ok`).
- The same real setup with `strictReadiness: true` failed before model execution with `AgentHarnessPreflightError`, preserving the released opt-in contract.
- Focused regression suite: 310 tests passed across both owning shards in 64.57 seconds, including a startup-level assertion that `autoInstall` issues `plugin/install` before the ordinary turn.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed on exact head `32b7907eff375931b94d9ea02ff67a31ac4f1cbd`.

prs.title: fix(agents): yield CLI binding affinity to a cooled-down auth profile
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a CLI-backed run has no explicit auth pin (`authProfileIdSource === "auto"`, or no selection at
all), `resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId` takes the auth profile from the session's existing CLI
binding rather than from the resolved auth order. That binding affinity is deliberate and correct in
the normal case: it keeps the backend's native `--resume` valid so the session transcript is not
lost.

The problem is that the affinity is unconditional. If the bound profile is *currently unusable* —
disabled for billing, disabled by `auth_permanent`, or in an active cooldown window recorded in the
auth store's `usageStats` — the run is still dispatched onto it. The run then fails for that exact
reason, and the binding survives the failure, because
`isCliSessionInvalidatingFailoverReason` (`src/agents/cli-session.ts`) only clears a CLI session
binding for `session_expired`:

```ts
export function isCliSessionInvalidatingFailoverReason(reason: FailoverReason): boolean {
  // Auth identity changes are handled by the reuse fingerprint's auth epoch.
  // Other execution failures say nothing about the persisted transcript.
  return reason === "session_expired";
}
```

So a `billing` or `auth_permanent` failover leaves the binding pointing at the dead profile, and the
next turn repeats the identical failure. The session is stranded until the underlying account
recovers on its own — even when the auth order already leads with a perfectly healthy profile that
the run could have used.

This PR makes binding affinity yield in exactly that case: when the selection is **not** an explicit
user pin and the bound profile is unusable right now, resolution falls through to the automatic auth
order so failover can pick a healthy profile. Explicit user pins are deliberately left unchanged —
a user-locked profile must continue to fail closed rather than silently run as a different account.

## Evidence

**Production observation.** On a 2026.9.5 deployment, **218 sessions** were bound to a single
billing-exhausted auth profile and erroring on *every* turn. The auth order at the time already led
with a healthy profile, so the failover target existed and was eligible — it simply was never
consulted, because the bound profile won before the order was ever resolved. The sessions logged
`reuse=reusable-drift` against the bound profile and kept re-dispatching onto it; because `billing`
is not in `isCliSessionInvalidatingFailoverReason`, nothing ever cleared the binding. The failure
was self-sustaining rather than self-healing.

**Mechanism confirmed on `upstream/main`** (unchanged from the running dist):
`src/agents/command/attempt-execution.ts` sets `cliAuthNeedsSessionBinding` when the pin is absent or
`auto`, and then calls `resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId({ ..., sessionBinding })`; inside that
function the bound profile was returned without any usability check.

**The check reuses existing helpers, not new logic.** The fix calls `isProfileInCooldown` from
`src/agents/auth-profiles/usage-state.ts` — the same predicate `order.ts`
(`resolveAuthProfileOrderWithMetadata`) already uses to sort cooled-down profiles behind available
ones. It resolves through `resolveProfileUnusableUntil`, so a single call covers `blockedUntil`,
`cooldownUntil` **and** `disabledUntil` (the billing/`auth_permanent` case), including the
model-scoping rules. No new notion of "unusable" is introduced.

**Scope.** One conditional in `resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId` and one import. The reuse resolver
is untouched, the explicit-pin path is untouched, and `src/system-agent/inference-route.ts` — the
other caller — never passes a `sessionBinding`, so it is unaffected.

### Tests

Added to `src/agents/cli-execution-auth.test.ts`, under a `session binding affinity` block:

- `keeps an automatic run on a healthy bound profile` — unchanged behavior; native `--resume` stays
  valid.
- `fails over from a bound profile disabled for billing` — `disabledUntil` in the future now yields
  to the auth order's first eligible profile.
- `fails over from a bound profile in cooldown` — same fallthrough via `cooldownUntil`.
- `keeps a user pin on a disabled profile instead of switching accounts` — explicit pins still
  return the pinned profile; no behavior change.

```
 ✓ |agents-core| src/agents/cli-execution-auth.test.ts > resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId > session binding affinity > keeps an automatic run on a healthy bound profile 13ms
 ✓ |agents-core| src/agents/cli-execution-auth.test.ts > resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId > session binding affinity > fails over from a bound profile disabled for billing 7ms
 ✓ |agents-core| src/agents/cli-execution-auth.test.ts > resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId > session binding affinity > fails over from a bound profile in cooldown 6ms
 ✓ |agents-core| src/agents/cli-execution-auth.test.ts > resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId > session binding affinity > keeps a user pin on a disabled profile instead of switching accounts 6ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

The full file is green (20 passed: the 16 pre-existing cases plus the 4 above), so the added
fallthrough does not disturb any existing forwarding, retirement, or provider-ownership behavior.

The companion PR #153352 (`auth.historyEquivalenceGroups`) lets the CLI session be reused across the
resulting profile swap, so the failover this PR enables preserves conversation context instead of
starting a fresh session. The two are complementary but independent: this change is mergeable on its
own, and on its own it already converts a permanently stranded session into one that fails over.

## Summary
- `openclaw tasks dismiss` keyed only on a live task record. After task retention pruned that row, outstanding `subagent_runs` with `delivery=failed` kept injecting **Child results awaiting delivery** with no operator path to retire them (#155163).
- Dismiss now accepts the surviving run id when no task row remains, marks the delivery as intentional non-delivery, and does not recreate a pruned task.
- Gateway write access still checks the orphaned run's requester session before discard.

## Test plan
- [x] Added regression: dismiss an outstanding failed run after deleting its `task_runs` row.
- Local `pnpm test` / vitest shard failed to start in this tree (`defineCacheKeyGenerator is not a function` — pnpm 12.4.0 shim ENOEXEC). CI should run `src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-delivery.test.ts`.

Fixes #155163

## What Problem This Solves

Session progress cards still depend on Lit rendering and directive lifecycles after their board, chat, and session-summary callers moved to Solid.

## User Impact

Progress cards keep their existing appearance, refresh/dismiss actions, step status, disclosure gestures, and transcript scroll behavior. There are no new settings or dependencies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Render cards directly in Solid at all four production callers, removing their card-specific Lit content adapters. Keep the existing presentation, markdown, and disclosure owners; replace only the Lit directives with owner-scoped refs. Timers and scroll observers follow the existing presentation context, and a retained disclosure controller preserves expansion across card snapshots.

The older Lit scroll directive remains for other chat renderers. The native scroll ref has its first production caller here.

Full CI exposed two timing-sensitive fixtures outside the card renderer. The terminal reconnect cases now settle the viewport commit and lazy terminal import before checking requests; the fenced-action case advances its existing 10 ms timeout explicitly. The parent-session fixture settles initial lazy work before injecting the descriptor failure, keeping the same absence, retry-count, and recovery assertions. prs.title: refactor(channels): simplify older plugin paths and keep content out of diagnostics
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Older channel-plugin code duplicates shared SDK ownership and carries defensive machinery for unsupported internal inputs, synthetic clocks, and throwing diagnostic hooks. Several normal inbound paths also put message content or pairing codes into diagnostics.

## User Impact

Message delivery, account/security policy, conversation identity, provider features, and ordinary shutdown/restart durability remain supported. Inbound message text, malformed Teams consent payloads and pairing codes no longer appear in the repaired diagnostic paths. No configuration, CLI, protocol, SDK export, dependency, schema, retention, or permission changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the second old-code channel-plugin pass. Only production files with no origin/main commit in the preceding seven days are included; eligibility is refreshed before every push. The overlapping Feishu Markdown fence repair was removed from this branch once main independently landed it in #171222.

The packet removes **512 net production lines** (+503/-1015; tests, fixtures, test support, generated files, and declarations excluded). It reuses existing public SDK owners for plugin setup composition, secret-contract wiring, receipts, status summaries, process-global maps, error traversal, and account-scoped DM policy. There are no private-core or cross-plugin imports.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

Each removed mechanism below was checked against callers, dependency behavior, and introducing history. Synthetic tests and hypothetical PR race descriptions are not treated as human production reports. Actual incident fixes, live security authority, FIFO, resource bounds, and accepted-write settlement are retained.

- Discord identify clock-skew observation (`c767b37e3b2`): the only added proof jumps the clock from a trillion milliseconds to zero; no human report is linked. A drastic backward clock jump can now prolong reconnect until clock recovery/restart; ordinary five-second parallel identify spacing remains.
- WhatsApp second synchronous close observation (#109886, `bf413374cca`): native Baileys uses EventEmitter and cannot asynchronously close between synchronous check/listener registration. A nonstandard reentrant `newListener` hook can reach the existing bounded timeout; transport-confirmed close and cleanup remain.
- Tlon formatter fallback (#1837, `51720980736`): validated decimal BigInt input cannot fail the pinned @ud formatter. A broken dependency now fails visibly instead of sending the incorrect raw ID that the original threading fix rejected.
- Matrix second private sync waiter (#62779, `0c00c3c2306`): the actual monitor waits once; only a synthetic test calls twice. An unsupported second call may replace the first callbacks; real outage/fatal/abort settlement remains.
- ClickClack outer setup catches (`752567dbc8e`): network/config failures are already caught by their owners; the extra path catches a broken logger/formatter then invokes the same logger again. Such internal failures now surface; ordinary setup diagnostics remain.
- ClickClack second workspace snapshot (`3e352d67278`): verification now resolves ID/name/slug from one provider response. A concurrent rename/removal is observed on the next verification/runtime request rather than an opportunistic second fetch.
- SMS generated-fragment revalidation (#118665, `0758316883f`): raw URL validation stays; only URLSearchParams-generated fragment bytes were checked twice. A monkeypatched/broken encoder is no longer revalidated; length, auth, URL and retry bounds remain.
- Feishu timeout-warning catch (`0028e6040a7`): the cited stuck-task/FIFO issues concern the retained five-minute cap, not a throwing logger. A broken warning hook now rejects that queue call visibly; subsequent same-key work continues.
- Feishu private timeout customization (`0028e6040a7`, `fab8d29d211`, #101949): only tests passed disabled/oversized/custom values. Unsupported direct imports can no longer tune/disable the private cap; all production callers retain five-minute progress/FIFO behavior.
- Reef logger-fatal deferred/race (#162669; synthetic hook in #110870): ordinary transport-error containment and shutdown from the recorded live relay incident stay. A throwing error logger is reported by the scheduler instead of intentionally killing an otherwise healthy inbox.
- Matrix nonfinite media size fallback (`9b71382efb6`, #149128): the sole production producer passes Buffer.byteLength; NaN cases were synthetic cleanup fixtures. Unsupported private NaN calls now carry that supplied value; MIME, encryption, image fields and duration remain.
- Buzz subscription count coercion (`6c7a96e588e`): the sole caller supplies array.length. Unsupported negative/fractional private values are not repaired; the actual room/resource cap remains.
- Teams upload-byte coercion (#104120, `0c8220ebf9a`): both callers supply Buffer.length. Unsupported malformed private counts follow transfer arithmetic; timer clamping and upload budgets stay.
- Nostr zero-count score fallback (`7b6cbf58697`): private entries are synchronously created and incremented together. An unsupported new zero-outcome insertion could score NaN; actual outage/circuit-breaker/failover behavior stays.
- Buzz profile-limit coercion (`ba2510e8fa8`): the only explicit producer supplies the bounded integer budget. Unsupported direct malformed limits are not normalized; ordinary caps, zero-budget and untrusted-event checks stay.
- Feishu card-launcher clock injection/max-Date guard (`05634708e05`): only a synthetic year-275760 test supplies the private clock. A corrupt clock may create an unusable expiry until recovery/restart; effect-side expiry, actor/chat and approval validation stay.
- QA private empty media-batch guard (#115290, `641c82b5bd0`): all three callers prove a nonempty batch. Unsupported direct empty calls take the ordinary text path; real media caps and atomic loading remain.
- Slack private global-map slot revalidation (original sharing fix `55318df83ff`): normal module sharing/replacement is retained. No human private-slot corruption report is linked; third-party mutation/deletion of our private Symbol slot is no longer checked on every read, and restart repairs unsupported corruption.
- Buzz synchronous subscription-construction compensation (`b48984792f4`, `828f88c5ca5`, #130300): native nostr-tools construction emits no callbacks and authored filters are plain/nonempty. Unsupported throwing/cyclic private filters or replaced constructors surface without immediate count/generation/timer compensation; close/deadline/restart recovers temporary state.
- Buzz post-construction inline-EOSE/abort retry (same provenance): native callbacks are asynchronous. A non-native constructor emitting EOSE inline no longer gets a second cleanup attempt; real EOSE-before-CLOSE, late EOSE, close-once, deadlines, queued slots, abort listeners, membership authority and shutdown remain. Fixtures now schedule EOSE with queueMicrotask while retaining assertions.
- Signal clean-end recovery duplication (#10240, `dff4a04c1f5`): clean EOF and transient failures share one backoff tail. An impossible non-abort internal sleep rejection or broken status/logger callback now surfaces rather than entering compensating reconnect; real sleep rejects on abort and actual recovery stays.
- WhatsApp optional native socket-end fallback (`69225003820`): actual callers use WASocket with required end(). An unsupported fake without end fails plainly; normal teardown and its error reporting stay.
- Nextcloud post-synchronous-route abort check (#159067, `5fd7c3d95e0`): the old awaited server-start path became synchronous route registration. A reentrant registry callback abort may briefly publish ready; installed abort cleanup, post-spool-ready check, auth and durable settlement stay.
- Buzz history-count clamps (`132e39bff64`): the actual positive room count and queue-capacity invariant guarantee the result. Unsupported private negative/oversized counts are not repaired; actual FIFO/resource reservations remain.
- LINE frozen-error wrapper (#100996, `f859d78b612`): native SDK HTTPFetchError is mutable; Object.freeze was a synthetic fixture, not a cited human incident. An unsupported frozen replacement error can now fail annotation with TypeError; actual partial-send/recovery contracts stay.
- LINE duplicate missing-receipt invariant (`05eda57b3c7`, #99600, #142092, #165718): all native sends return validated IDs and required receipts. Unsupported fake results use canonical bridge normalization instead of the former private throw; physical-send progress, caption quoting, receipt order and declared capabilities stay. The bridge also preserves already-sanctioned chatId metadata.
- Feishu display-cache extreme-clock guards (`23e1aac9b2c`): introduced with a synthetic max-Date test, no linked human report. Corrupt clocks follow ordinary arithmetic; account scope, positive/negative TTL and the 500-entry bound remain.
- Mattermost reaction-identity extreme-clock guards (`77b334a9845`): only invalid/max-Date tests support the machinery, no linked human report. Corrupt clocks follow arithmetic; token/base-URL scope, ten-minute expiry, delegated conversation/post/self-DM checks and request authority remain.

Other cuts remove duplicate facts/checks under one existing owner and introduce no additional failure tradeoff: Signal subscription/abort state, Zalouser Promise settlement and DM setter, Nextcloud claimed version/lane validation, Teams media/header validation and empty-array merging, Buzz refresh-state identity, Nostr flush identity, Matrix encryption gating, Mattermost runtime-config guard, immutable plugin setup bases, and private Discord/iMessage test overrides.

Matrix's private zero-answer poll fallback is also removed: its sole caller has already passed the shared minimum-two-options validator (`c49b6cc241a`, #163574). No reachable input loses a fallback. Teams attachment header rejection remains owned by the canonical bounded media saver; malformed/oversize headers now use the existing `attachmentView save failed` warning instead of the special malformed-header tag or silent oversized-header skip. The unavailable result and byte protection remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused owning-boundary/sibling tests and independent isolated reviews were run per checkpoint. Latest batches passed: Discord/LINE/Matrix/Synology 76 cases (157.00s wrapper), LINE/Feishu/Mattermost 66 cases (132.62s), Mattermost reaction 12 cases, Zalo Personal setup 17 cases (48.97s), and Teams consent/parser/lifecycle 52 cases (29.18s). The Teams malformed-content regression failed on the original handler before the one-line repair. The new Zalo test fixture initially assumed the wrong promotion target; source inspection and an explicit two-account fixture corrected it without changing production behavior or weakening retained assertions.

Production/test extension typechecks and targeted type-aware lint/format pass. Runtime and Madge checks report zero cycles. Existing SDK export checks pass. Earlier fresh cliStartup build and affected built-entry import proof passed; no performance improvement is claimed from dirty-tree profiling. No live accounts, operator state, driver installation, Gateway or remote lease was used.

Final Matrix poll/send/shared-normalization proof passes 55 cases across three shards (138.50s wrapper). Independent full-branch review and the supplemental poll review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Two local baseline gates are inherited from the branch base: suppression inventory expects 87 versus the untouched proxy's 88 (current main has repaired the entry); aggregate check-changed stops on stale untouched max-lines entry src/agents/btw.ts after conflict/line-cap gates pass. No allowlist/budget expansion was made. Earlier cold-start timing-sensitive failures remain observations, not claimed repaired/inherited; the complete changed cold-start file subsequently passed all eight cases with unchanged timers/assertions.

The first exact-head hosted run [38503961141](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38503961141) completed in 643 seconds: 51 jobs passed, 25 planned jobs skipped, and the baseline ratchet plus its aggregate gate failed. The defect was ours: removed Slack/Twitch assertions and two removed ClickClack mocks needed exact inventory shrinkage. Those four inventory items are corrected without adding allowances or changing behavior. All actual tests, types, lint, architecture, package boundaries, QA and security jobs passed on that production patch. Final exact-head run [38505676106](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38505676106) passed on `86922ccf92825d4b53b77005119590d1e7759a32`: 55 successful jobs, 25 planned skips, zero failed/cancelled jobs, 643 seconds wall time and 9,679 summed reported job seconds. The exact-head required CI/security gate passes. CodeQL also reports a neutral warning for unselected main configurations; those skipped configurations are not claimed as proof. No CI rerun, inherited-failure admin exception, or green-seeking push was used.

auto_merge.commit_message:
## What Problem This Solves

Older channel-plugin code duplicates shared SDK ownership and carries defensive machinery for unsupported internal inputs, synthetic clocks, and throwing diagnostic hooks. Several normal inbound paths also put message content or pairing codes into diagnostics.

## User Impact

Message delivery, account/security policy, conversation identity, provider features, and ordinary shutdown/restart durability remain supported. Inbound message text, malformed Teams consent payloads and pairing codes no longer appear in the repaired diagnostic paths. No configuration, CLI, protocol, SDK export, dependency, schema, retention, or permission changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the second old-code channel-plugin pass. Only production files with no origin/main commit in the preceding seven days are included; eligibility is refreshed before every push. The overlapping Feishu Markdown fence repair was removed from this branch once main independently landed it in #171222.

The packet removes **512 net production lines** (+503/-1015; tests, fixtures, test support, generated files, and declarations excluded). It reuses existing public SDK owners for plugin setup composition, secret-contract wiring, receipts, status summaries, process-global maps, error traversal, and account-scoped DM policy. There are no private-core or cross-plugin imports.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

Each removed mechanism below was checked against callers, dependency behavior, and introducing history. Synthetic tests and hypothetical PR race descriptions are not treated as human production reports. Actual incident fixes, live security authority, FIFO, resource bounds, and accepted-write settlement are retained.

- Discord identify clock-skew observation (`c767b37e3b2`): the only added proof jumps the clock from a trillion milliseconds to zero; no human report is linked. A drastic backward clock jump can now prolong reconnect until clock recovery/restart; ordinary five-second parallel identify spacing remains.
- WhatsApp second synchronous close observation (#109886, `bf413374cca`): native Baileys uses EventEmitter and cannot asynchronously close between synchronous check/listener registration. A nonstandard reentrant `newListener` hook can reach the existing bounded timeout; transport-confirmed close and cleanup remain.
- Tlon formatter fallback (#1837, `51720980736`): validated decimal BigInt input cannot fail the pinned @ud formatter. A broken dependency now fails visibly instead of sending the incorrect raw ID that the original threading fix rejected.
- Matrix second private sync waiter (#62779, `0c00c3c2306`): the actual monitor waits once; only a synthetic test calls twice. An unsupported second call may replace the first callbacks; real outage/fatal/abort settlement remains.
- ClickClack outer setup catches (`752567dbc8e`): network/config failures are already caught by their owners; the extra path catches a broken logger/formatter then invokes the same logger again. Such internal failures now surface; ordinary setup diagnostics remain.
- ClickClack second workspace snapshot (`3e352d67278`): verification now resolves ID/name/slug from one provider response. A concurrent rename/removal is observed on the next verification/runtime request rather than an opportunistic second fetch.
- SMS generated-fragment revalidation (#118665, `0758316883f`): raw URL validation stays; only URLSearchParams-generated fragment bytes were checked twice. A monkeypatched/broken encoder is no longer revalidated; length, auth, URL and retry bounds remain.
- Feishu timeout-warning catch (`0028e6040a7`): the cited stuck-task/FIFO issues concern the retained five-minute cap, not a throwing logger. A broken warning hook now rejects that queue call visibly; subsequent same-key work continues.
- Feishu private timeout customization (`0028e6040a7`, `fab8d29d211`, #101949): only tests passed disabled/oversized/custom values. Unsupported direct imports can no longer tune/disable the private cap; all production callers retain five-minute progress/FIFO behavior.
- Reef logger-fatal deferred/race (#162669; synthetic hook in #110870): ordinary transport-error containment and shutdown from the recorded live relay incident stay. A throwing error logger is reported by the scheduler instead of intentionally killing an otherwise healthy inbox.
- Matrix nonfinite media size fallback (`9b71382efb6`, #149128): the sole production producer passes Buffer.byteLength; NaN cases were synthetic cleanup fixtures. Unsupported private NaN calls now carry that supplied value; MIME, encryption, image fields and duration remain.
- Buzz subscription count coercion (`6c7a96e588e`): the sole caller supplies array.length. Unsupported negative/fractional private values are not repaired; the actual room/resource cap remains.
- Teams upload-byte coercion (#104120, `0c8220ebf9a`): both callers supply Buffer.length. Unsupported malformed private counts follow transfer arithmetic; timer clamping and upload budgets stay.
- Nostr zero-count score fallback (`7b6cbf58697`): private entries are synchronously created and incremented together. An unsupported new zero-outcome insertion could score NaN; actual outage/circuit-breaker/failover behavior stays.
- Buzz profile-limit coercion (`ba2510e8fa8`): the only explicit producer supplies the bounded integer budget. Unsupported direct malformed limits are not normalized; ordinary caps, zero-budget and untrusted-event checks stay.
- Feishu card-launcher clock injection/max-Date guard (`05634708e05`): only a synthetic year-275760 test supplies the private clock. A corrupt clock may create an unusable expiry until recovery/restart; effect-side expiry, actor/chat and approval validation stay.
- QA private empty media-batch guard (#115290, `641c82b5bd0`): all three callers prove a nonempty batch. Unsupported direct empty calls take the ordinary text path; real media caps and atomic loading remain.
- Slack private global-map slot revalidation (original sharing fix `55318df83ff`): normal module sharing/replacement is retained. No human private-slot corruption report is linked; third-party mutation/deletion of our private Symbol slot is no longer checked on every read, and restart repairs unsupported corruption.
- Buzz synchronous subscription-construction compensation (`b48984792f4`, `828f88c5ca5`, #130300): native nostr-tools construction emits no callbacks and authored filters are plain/nonempty. Unsupported throwing/cyclic private filters or replaced constructors surface without immediate count/generation/timer compensation; close/deadline/restart recovers temporary state.
- Buzz post-construction inline-EOSE/abort retry (same provenance): native callbacks are asynchronous. A non-native constructor emitting EOSE inline no longer gets a second cleanup attempt; real EOSE-before-CLOSE, late EOSE, close-once, deadlines, queued slots, abort listeners, membership authority and shutdown remain. Fixtures now schedule EOSE with queueMicrotask while retaining assertions.
- Signal clean-end recovery duplication (#10240, `dff4a04c1f5`): clean EOF and transient failures share one backoff tail. An impossible non-abort internal sleep rejection or broken status/logger callback now surfaces rather than entering compensating reconnect; real sleep rejects on abort and actual recovery stays.
- WhatsApp optional native socket-end fallback (`69225003820`): actual callers use WASocket with required end(). An unsupported fake without end fails plainly; normal teardown and its error reporting stay.
- Nextcloud post-synchronous-route abort check (#159067, `5fd7c3d95e0`): the old awaited server-start path became synchronous route registration. A reentrant registry callback abort may briefly publish ready; installed abort cleanup, post-spool-ready check, auth and durable settlement stay.
- Buzz history-count clamps (`132e39bff64`): the actual positive room count and queue-capacity invariant guarantee the result. Unsupported private negative/oversized counts are not repaired; actual FIFO/resource reservations remain.
- LINE frozen-error wrapper (#100996, `f859d78b612`): native SDK HTTPFetchError is mutable; Object.freeze was a synthetic fixture, not a cited human incident. An unsupported frozen replacement error can now fail annotation with TypeError; actual partial-send/recovery contracts stay.
- LINE duplicate missing-receipt invariant (`05eda57b3c7`, #99600, #142092, #165718): all native sends return validated IDs and required receipts. Unsupported fake results use canonical bridge normalization instead of the former private throw; physical-send progress, caption quoting, receipt order and declared capabilities stay. The bridge also preserves already-sanctioned chatId metadata.
- Feishu display-cache extreme-clock guards (`23e1aac9b2c`): introduced with a synthetic max-Date test, no linked human report. Corrupt clocks follow ordinary arithmetic; account scope, positive/negative TTL and the 500-entry bound remain.
- Mattermost reaction-identity extreme-clock guards (`77b334a9845`): only invalid/max-Date tests support the machinery, no linked human report. Corrupt clocks follow arithmetic; token/base-URL scope, ten-minute expiry, delegated conversation/post/self-DM checks and request authority remain.

Other cuts remove duplicate facts/checks under one existing owner and introduce no additional failure tradeoff: Signal subscription/abort state, Zalouser Promise settlement and DM setter, Nextcloud claimed version/lane validation, Teams media/header validation and empty-array merging, Buzz refresh-state identity, Nostr flush identity, Matrix encryption gating, Mattermost runtime-config guard, immutable plugin setup bases, and private Discord/iMessage test overrides.

Matrix's private zero-answer poll fallback is also removed: its sole caller has already passed the shared minimum-two-options validator (`c49b6cc241a`, #163574). No reachable input loses a fallback. Teams attachment header rejection remains owned by the canonical bounded media saver; malformed/oversize headers now use the existing `attachmentView save failed` warning instead of the special malformed-header tag or silent oversized-header skip. The unavailable result and byte protection remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused owning-boundary/sibling tests and independent isolated reviews were run per checkpoint. Latest batches passed: Discord/LINE/Matrix/Synology 76 cases (157.00s wrapper), LINE/Feishu/Mattermost 66 cases (132.62s), Mattermost reaction 12 cases, Zalo Personal setup 17 cases (48.97s), and Teams consent/parser/lifecycle 52 cases (29.18s). The Teams malformed-content regression failed on the original handler before the one-line repair. The new Zalo test fixture initially assumed the wrong promotion target; source inspection and an explicit two-account fixture corrected it without changing production behavior or weakening retained assertions.

Production/test extension typechecks and targeted type-aware lint/format pass. Runtime and Madge checks report zero cycles. Existing SDK export checks pass. No live accounts, operator state, driver installation, Gateway or remote lease was used.

Those four inventory items are corrected without adding allowances or changing behavior. All actual tests, types, lint, architecture, package boundaries, QA and security jobs passed on that production patch. ## What Problem This Solves

Queued-message Edit actions still depend on Web Awesome during the Control UI migration to owned native controls.

## User Impact

Editing a queued prompt keeps its existing pointer and keyboard flow, editor focus, disabled action slots, and protection against double-clicking the menu trigger.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queue now uses the shared native Menu for navigation and dismissal while its existing queue owner still controls editing. The old Web Awesome selectors and panel styling are removed. No new dependencies or state owners are added.

Production TypeScript and CSS: **1,209 → 1,216 LOC (+7)**. The per-mount menu identity, native item description, and activation-modality handling add twelve TypeScript lines; five obsolete CSS lines disappear. Tests: **509 → 613 LOC (+104)**, plus one WebKit discovery entry.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed on corrected source, 189.92 s wall |
| `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-queue.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 14/14 passed; 515.16 s wall (346.02 s Vitest including slow collection) |
| `OPENCLAW_UI_WEBKIT=1 pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/chat/chat-composer-queue.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1` | 8/8 passed; 157.41 s wall (38.67 s Vitest) |
| Keyless i18n baseline + verification | Passed; no generated changes |
| Scoped format/lint and `git diff --check` | Passed: oxfmt, oxlint, stylelint |
| Codex review, P0–P2 | Initial port, activation-modality fix, and menu-sizing fix scoped-clean; no actionable findings |
| Exact-base build / strict performance | `5dd456ac`: 23.73 s; startup JS 349,028 B gzip, CSS 49,703 B gzip / 1 request |
| Head build / strict performance | `9a5eae5a9`: 207.13 s; startup JS 349,043 B gzip (+15 B; raw bytes and 8 requests unchanged), CSS 49,703 B gzip / 1 request; strict budget passes |
| PR full CI | Requested with `ci:full`; results pending |

The first Chromium run caught a pointer-selection regression: native programmatic item focus can remain `:focus-visible`. Selection now records the real click modality at the existing item boundary. Visual proof also caught the copied 132 px width clipping the native label; the queue now retains its minimum width and lets the native overlay size to content within viewport bounds. The corrected browser cases pass in both engines and use the production queue and native menu: pointer and keyboard Edit selection must focus the existing draft, preserve the focus-origin marker, reject opening another row's disabled menu, and keep a double-click on the trigger from starting an edit. The existing unit assertions retain the action slots and disabled triggers without assuming closed menu items are eagerly materialized.

Synthetic before/after screenshots cover the desktop menu/editor and the menu at 400 px; they are inspected locally. Capture setup corrections affected the fixture's accessible-name and editor locator only; there were no page errors in the successful capture.

prs.title: docs(acpx): expose the Grok Build harness target
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ACPX already resolves `grok-build` to `grok agent stdio`. OpenClaw's quickstart, example allowlist, bundled router and live ACP selector did not expose that existing target consistently. This aligns those surfaces without adding another runtime adapter.

Related: #99191. That issue closed for inactivity, not because this downstream alignment landed. Its separate xAI model-selection request is not implemented or automatically closed by this PR.

## What Changed

- Exposes the existing Grok Build target in setup and quickstart guidance and the example `acp.allowedAgents` list.
- Routes Grok Build intent to `agentId: "grok-build"` in the bundled ACP router.
- Keeps that agent target distinct from the OpenClaw xAI model reference `xai/grok-build-0.1`.
- Extends the existing opt-in live ACP bind selector to accept `grok-build`.

The contribution has no production runtime, dependency, manifest or lockfile changes. ACPX remains the owner of the harness command and transport; OpenClaw's agent allowlist still governs dispatch.

## User Impact

Users with Grok Build installed and authenticated can discover and select the supported ACPX target without confusing it with an xAI model selection.

## Current Integration and Evidence

Head: `411e4cb59724b90bb1418975ea58f4e9a40881a5`. This normally merges main `c66da3d764b0ba7996aa77c98a885298bb0dc2c4`, preserving the six-file contribution, 28 insertions and 5 deletions. [Canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38293669155) passed, including the final CI gate, with 20 successful jobs and no failures.

The preceding integration's [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38289264503) failed because its trusted base lacked `scripts/ci-pr-failure-report.mjs`, which the newer CI workflow invoked. The normal main integration includes that script and its existing dependencies. The six contributor files remain byte-identical to the independently reviewed predecessor. No reporter workaround, test bypass or Grok runtime change was added.

All six files passed pinned formatting and contributor whitespace checks. Independent Codex/OpenAI review of the complete six-file integration found no actionable P0–P2 issue. The frozen reviewed tree matches the published commit.

This head pins ACPX **0.19.4** through main. The [official registry at that release](https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/blob/8e396609238086dee6a407fdb3b3ac46dbdedd70/src/agent-registry.ts) still maps `grok-build` to `grok agent stdio`; [its harness guide](https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/blob/8e396609238086dee6a407fdb3b3ac46dbdedd70/agents/GrokBuild.md) documents the installation and authentication requirements. ACPX implementation #426 is merged; no downstream reimplementation is needed.

The September 26 CI failure at predecessor `99b9305` reports SQLite teardown and read-admission failures outside these six paths. Its cause remains unconfirmed; this integration is not presented as a Grok-specific repair for that failure.

## Retained Live Behavior Proof

Earlier head `7f38ffd4761c92758c85e3593782315b42941e14`, with ACPX **0.13.2** and Grok Build CLI **1.0.13**, passed the real OpenClaw ACP bind flow in an isolated checkout and temporary Gateway state. The harness used the already-authenticated Grok CLI without modifying the operator Gateway.

```text
OPENCLAW_LIVE_ACP_BIND=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_ACP_BIND_AGENT=grok-build OPENCLAW_LIVE_ACP_BIND_IMAGE_PROBE=0 pnpm test:live src/gateway/gateway-acp-bind.live.test.ts
```

Observed: OpenClaw created `agent:grok-build:acp:<uuid>`, completed the initial and follow-up turns, recalled the prior token in the same bound session, and retained the final marker in the transcript. **One test file and all 8 tests passed.** The optional post-bind cron probe reported `AgentSelectionRequiredError`; cron behavior is not claimed.

That is revision-pinned live behavior proof, not a fresh provider run on the current integration. No new credentials or provider traffic were used for this refresh.

<details>
<summary>Historical published-registry verification</summary>

The exact ACPX 0.13.2 npm tarball was inspected without installation or script execution. SHA-256 was `B483B20EA1DB5FFDEB0EB2E3105283FFDA0B88CCF37E034D500522AAEEF8D12B`; the compiled registry and bundled skill both mapped `grok-build` to `grok agent stdio`. This supported the earlier 8-test live result. Current source qualification uses the official 0.19.4 registry above.

</details>

## Remaining Work

Obtain maintainer review. Current source, formatting and canonical CI are verified; the live evidence above remains at its actual earlier revision. No claim of a new full provider or cron proof is made.

prs.title: fix(discord): replies to bot-posted notifications lose the quoted message text
prs.body:
Closes #151853

Related: #93277, #138503, #86238

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a Discord user replies to a message the bot account posted from a cron announce, an operator `send`, or a script's `message` tool send, the agent can't tell which message they mean, because the quoted text is removed.

## User Impact

Replies to bot-posted notifications now reach the agent with the quoted text, including after a Gateway restart. Replies to the bot's own conversational replies still omit the quoted text, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the direction from the #93277 review: durable Discord-owned state keyed by account and platform message ID, with provenance carried through a typed generic seam and no Discord literals in core.

- `ReplyPayload` gains `isHostNotification`. Core sets it on cron direct and announce deliveries, on `send` requests that are not bound to a live agent run, and on `message` tool sends that have no authorized source conversation. That last check is the same one `annotateSourceDelivery` uses to decide whether a send can be a reply in the current conversation, so the model's own message-tool replies stay unmarked.
- A top-level field survives payload normalization and the durable delivery queue, reaching `afterDeliverPayload` without forcing the `channelData` transport route that #93277 needed a special case for.
- Discord's `afterDeliverPayload` records the platform message IDs of marked payloads, including every chunk, in a plugin keyed store (`notification-reply-context`, 10,000 entries, evict-oldest).
- When a user replies to a bot-authored message, the Discord monitor passes `suppressSelfQuoteBody: false` only if that message ID is recorded for the receiving account. Quote media stays suppressed. Unknown IDs and store failures keep the default suppression from #86238.

## Evidence

**Live Discord run with a Gateway restart in between.** Production Gateway on 2026.9.1 with this change backported; the backport differs only in where the `ReplyPayload` type lives and how `message-action-send` hands the authorization context to `executeSendAction`. The model request was captured with `diagnostics.cacheTrace` (`stream:context` stage), which was switched off again afterwards. IDs are redacted; the test text is Chinese, with translations in brackets.

1. 2026-09-17 12:31:57Z: a script posted a notification into a Discord thread through `POST /tools/invoke` (`message` tool, `action: "send"`), the same path the affected deployment uses for its digests. The Discord plugin recorded it:

   ```
   plugin_state_entries  discord / notification-reply-context  <account>:<notification-id> = true   (12:31:58Z)
   ```

2. 2026-09-17 23:17Z: the Gateway restarted (full process restart).
3. 2026-09-18 14:05:06Z: a user used Discord **Reply** on that notification and wrote only 「回覆」 ["reply"]. The model request carried the quoted text:

   ```
   Reply target of current user message:
   {"message_id":"<notification-id>","sender_label":"<bot>","body":"🧪 測試通知（模擬題庫日報，由腳本經 /tools/invoke 貼出）\n暗號：藍色長頸鹿-0917"}
   ```

   The agent answered `藍色長頸鹿-0917` [the code word].
4. Control, same thread: a reply to the agent's own answer still omits the body.

   ```
   Reply target of current user message:
   {"message_id":"<answer-id>","sender_label":"<bot>"}
   ```

Before this change, the same kind of reply in the same deployment carried only `{"message_id","sender_label"}`, and the agent had to read the whole thread through tools to guess which item was meant (see #151853). Over the first 25 hours the store held 522 IDs from the deployment's regular cron and script posts, well below the 10,000-entry cap.

**Tests**

- `extensions/discord/src/notification-reply-context.test.ts` writes through the real plugin state store, resets it, and reads the IDs back (restart). It also covers chunk receipts, account isolation, skipped sends, and a store failure falling back to suppression.
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.session-routing.test.ts`: a recorded notification keeps `ReplyToBody` while its media stays hidden. The existing "does not inject the bot's previous message body" case still passes.
- `extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts`: only marked payloads are recorded.
- `src/infra/outbound/deliver.host-notification.test.ts`: the marker reaches `afterDeliverPayload` for queued and direct sends, and for a notification restored from the durable queue.
- `src/infra/outbound/outbound-send-service.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts`, and the cron delivery tests cover which producers set the marker.

**Lanes**

- On the current base `1f807cb`: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm test:extension discord` (285 files, 4,032 tests), and the targeted files above pass.
- On the previous base `9ab4738`: `pnpm test:contracts` passes; `pnpm test src/cron` (230 files, 3,280 tests) and the `src/gateway/server-methods` shard (367 files, 6,464 tests) pass. `src/infra/outbound` passes except 5 macOS-only failures in `deliver.test.ts` (`/tmp` resolves to `/private/tmp`); they fail the same way on that base without this change. `pnpm check` and `pnpm lint` each reported one failure, both in files this PR does not touch: the assertion ratchet in `src/plugins/native-module-require.ts`, and an oxlint error in `scripts/lib/ci-changed-node-test-plan.mts`.
