prs.title: fix(system-agent): use configured fallbacks when primary admission fails
prs.body:
Closes #151605.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw/system-expert maintenance admission could stop at an unavailable primary even when that same agent had a working configured fallback. This PR tries only the owner's authored model chain and binds the successful model route, credential, and runtime to the session. Empty or strict chains remain strict. Changing the chain, credential, runtime, or policy invalidates the old binding; a different owner needs fresh verification. Admission does not rewrite the default model, authentication, or quota. Related reports: #136592 and #112300.

**The maintainer must still accept or reject this exact-owner/fresh-session recovery policy before merge.** Green CI and the isolated proof do not make that product decision.

## Scope and final effects

- A verified **fallback** may read state and perform operator-approved, pinned config set/unset or SecretRef changes. The config writer rechecks the bound owner after validation, with config/include revision and final-write CAS. The actual state worker rechecks the owner at the SecretRef transaction and commit admission.
- A fallback may **not even propose** multi-stage privileged actions: agent/team creation, plugin install/uninstall/artifact activation, setup or masked wizards, Gateway lifecycle, and default-model switching are refused at the model-facing tool boundary before approval or effects. The CLI MCP tool receives host-verified fallback scope through an existing per-turn transport field; stale pending proposals are cleared before a later approval. A fresh verified primary session or direct operator action is required for those actions. Primary-route behavior is unchanged.
- Config-set still permits exactly approved model-related configuration paths even though the dedicated default-model-switch action is unavailable to a fallback. Whether this write authority is acceptable is an explicit maintainer/security-owner decision, not something these tests approve.
- A failed config publication after a new SecretRef insert retains that entry for explicit, newly approved reference-only recovery; it is not blindly deleted. SQLite and config publication are **not** one atomic transaction. No automated repair is dispatched.

## Evidence

- **Exact source head:** e2a08931614b8d4ac6411ceb9fdd851f1b8f5c20. On the local three-file candidate, fallback-only tool/model-schema regressions and unchanged primary/MCP behavior passed **63/63** focused tests; production core and affected test TypeScript graphs passed; scoped type-aware lint found **0 warnings, 0 errors**; formatting, max-lines and line-cap passed. The assertion-safety ratchet now passes against the previous failed CI run’s exact main parent `08b746571eaf70536b49cfa00b92df3010e07d09`: the new parser lookup has a truthful non-null-object `// SAFETY:` invariant, with no baseline or threshold change. Prior-head broader regression results (30/30, 70/70, 110/110) are supporting history, not current-head CI.
- **Current candidate isolated behavior:** synthetic HTTP primary **401**, configured fallback **200**; a verified bound turn and approved config publication occurred, then old-owner use was rejected. A fresh verified owner admitted the real state worker SecretRef effect (exactly one store entry, matched by config). Revoked fallback or reassigned credential yielded **zero** new secret entries or alternate-owner requests. Eight disallowed model-tool actions were refused before proposal or final I/O; a guarded config action staged only an approval proposal. All **4/4** isolated cases passed on the candidate runtime. A later parser change adds only a source comment required by the assertion-safety ratchet; it does not change executable behavior.
- **Redacted request/response and final-effect trace (isolated fixture, not production):**
  ```text
  identity: per-run nonce echoed; listener PID owned by test process (both verified)
  requests: primary/first → HTTP 401; configured fallback/second → HTTP 200
  response contract: 401 invalid_api_key; 200 SSE assistant delta "OK" then stop
  allowed effects: approved config applied=true; worker secret-store entries=1; config reference matches entry=true
  denied: fallback removed / credential reassigned → configUnchanged=true, secretEntries=0, alternateOwnerRequests=0
  model tool: restricted actions deniedBeforeApproval=8; guarded config proposal staged with no immediate write
  runner: infra 4/4 passed, exit=0, listener closed; redacted log SHA-256 d764cd4da80de514225d24b4bdcdae4a201c6d31ac76a89f5e0bc16fd25d1277
  ```
  Request/response statuses and effect booleans are captured test markers; response body wording comes from the pinned fixture contract, not a production wire dump.
- **Limits:** synthetic credentials and isolated test state only—not a production Gateway, vendor account, or UI/channel transport. The HTTP negative cases revoke before approval; focused tests cover later writer and worker boundaries. No claim that a fallback can complete multi-stage operations.
- **CI status:** previous public head `d8e526dc43a8be3d2600968775a47bfc75141cfa` has a failed full CI run <https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36619086906> (11 direct failures plus aggregate); the authored PR-context check subsequently passed. The PR-caused assertion-safety failure is repaired and locally checked against that run’s main parent. Ten other changed-node failures remain un-attributed and must be checked on any newly published head. New-head CI must be authenticated and read back after any separately approved publication; no green result is claimed from local proof. Security-owner acceptance of fallback write authority remains separate.

prs.body:
Closes #151006

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes oversized background-task completion notices when a backend returns a long diagnostic or terminal summary.

## User Impact

Terminal and blocked-follow-up notices now contain a detail preview of at most 120 characters, ending in an ellipsis when shortened. Short actionable errors stay visible; full task diagnostics remain stored. Information beyond the preview still requires inspecting the task or child session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing task-status sanitizer and compact-detail limit at terminal formatting sites. This preserves current sanitization, delivery routing, parent-review instructions, and diagnostic storage without a new setting or API.

## Evidence

On public base `a1cc9b38c1c89a0d1d41d71a4160a7b14cd04d02`, the real ACP error formatter → lifecycle event → registry path produces a 1,801-character notification on both direct and parent-session routes. The fix produces 168 characters for that fixture, including its title/run label. Both route tests assert that the full stored error is unchanged.

- Six new bound checks fail on the unmodified base; all seven new cases pass with the fix, including short `Error:`-prefixed prose.
- 192 tests pass across the four selected suites below.
- Complete build, core types, task-containing test type shard, focused lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.

prs.title: improve(sessions): omit storage-only data before cloning model context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Model-context preparation deep-copies storage-only submitted text and tool evidence before immediately discarding it.

## User Impact

Avoid copying data the model will never receive, while preserving visible context, durable evidence and mutation isolation. The benefit depends on discarded metadata being present.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing canonical projection before the final deep clone. Shallow-replace only entries whose message changes; the final clone still detaches every surviving nested value. Private-field and missing-tool-result-marker policies retain their existing owner.

## Evidence

- Linux baseline/candidate owner suites pass 23 codec + 32 cohort cases. Actual cohort context hashes match, durable rows remain exact and nested mutations are isolated on Node 24/26 and stable/pinned Bun. Actual initial preparation clone input is 3,002→2,636 bytes in the small correctness fixture; this is not a universal saving. Removal of the final clone is detected by the isolation regression.
- Full canonical builds, package checks, strict installation/postinstall, and installed continuation/restart pass for baseline, each candidate and combined on Linux Node 24/26. All 18 Gateway groups closed and transcript prefixes stayed exact.
- Core/owning-test typechecks, lint/format, independent P2 review and [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501869492) pass. Linux baseline combined owner wrapper took 111.66s under build pressure; final codec wrapper took 26.63s.
- [Native Windows replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502498805) passes 23/23 codec cases, but 21/32 unchanged cohort cases hit 120s test deadlines (11 pass). This is not a mismatch assertion. A [baseline control](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38506942625) of that identical cohort file is running; neither candidate responsibility nor exoneration is established.

**Hold merging: performance/platform qualification remains unresolved.** Six quiet same-baseline clusters cannot resolve the 2% large-visible-context CPU budget within the frozen sample cap; position-dependent CPU cost and arm bias are retained. No candidate acceptance ran. A separate 50µs spin is detected in both blocks, which validates substantial-cost sensitivity rather than 2% power. Matched real-Gateway calibration is running. No sustained-RSS or universal latency benefit is claimed.

prs.title: improve(sessions): avoid reserializing retained transcripts for accounting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Updating a cached transcript serializes its previous contents again just to subtract the charge already recorded in the cache total.

## User Impact

Repeated retention performs 50% less transcript-sizing serialization in the tested 256 KiB, 1 MiB and 8 MiB ASCII fixtures. This is work-volume evidence, not a claim of 50% faster turns or lower sustained RSS.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remember the charged size on the existing cache cell, subtract that value on replacement, and reset it on discard. Incoming contents are still measured once, so this does not assume transcript objects are immutable. One numeric field is added per existing cell.

## Evidence

- Actual owner suites pass 28/28 on Linux and native Windows/Node 24. Independent full-JSON accounting checks pass on Linux Node 24/26 and stable/pinned Bun; missing-update and missing-reset mutations fail their intended eviction assertions.
- Full canonical builds, package checks, strict installation/postinstall, and installed continuation/restart pass for baseline, each candidate and combined on Linux Node 24/26. All 18 owned Gateway groups closed; prior transcript bytes remained exact.
- Core/owning-test typechecks, lint/format, independent P2 review and [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501721689) pass. [Windows owner proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502599373) passes 28/28 in 96.22s; the new eviction case takes 3.449s. Linux cold owner-suite wrapper took 135.04s under build pressure.

**Hold merging: performance qualification is inconclusive.** Eight quiet identical-baseline clusters found bimodal 8 MiB admission cost, with a +0.482ms mean arm gap (7.72%). Its variance exceeds the frozen 1% neutral-CPU precision cap; this is not candidate regression evidence. No candidate timing was launched. A separate injected-serialization check detects approximately +99% CPU, establishing substantial-cost sensitivity rather than 1% power. Matched real-Gateway calibration is running. No ordinary-turn or long-run memory benefit is claimed.

prs.title: fix(ui): accepted message shows "Waiting for reconnect" when a chat pane is shown again
prs.body:
Related: #158190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a chat message the Gateway already accepted shows "Waiting for reconnect" on a live connection when a chat pane is shown again and restores its composer while that message is still in flight.

## User Impact

User impact: messages sent while a reply is running keep their in-flight state after pane switches and split/dock handoffs, instead of briefly showing a false reconnect warning. Reload recovery is unchanged: after a real reload, an unconfirmed send is still restored as "Waiting for reconnect".

## Why This Change Was Made

The outbox deliberately stores in-flight sends under reload-safe aliases (`sending` is stored as `waiting-reconnect`), and the outbox owner normally overlays the live `sending` state when it presents the queue. Restoring a pane's composer copied the stored rows straight into the visible queue, bypassing that owner, so the alias showed until the next outbox publish. `restoreComposer()` now re-presents the outbox owner's projection right after the restore. All three restore callers (pane mount, composer handoff, outbox recovery) go through it.

This PR intentionally does **not** change the storage codec. Mapping `sending` to `waiting-reconnect` on write is the reload-recovery contract (see `needsReview` in `chat-outbox-owner.ts`), so the two storage-level tests described in #158190 fail by design.

<details>
<summary>Findings on the rest of #158190</summary>

I reproduced the reporter's flow against current `main` with the real submit, send, and drain code:

- After a follow-up gets a `started` ACK, storage holds `waiting-reconnect` / `sendAttempts: 1` while the live queue shows `sending` and a thread row with no reconnect label.
- The "third message held in `waiting-idle`, `sendAttempts: 0`" state reproduces when the third message is sent after the page sees the first reply finish while the Gateway still holds the second as queued custody. The drain keeps FIFO order behind that accepted head. Once the Gateway reports the second input as consumed, the next drain wake retires it and sends the third. That is ordering, not a permanent stall.
- If the third message is sent while the page still shows the reply as running, it is sent immediately and does not wait behind the second.

Follow-ups, deliberately left out of this fix:

- `restoreChatComposerState` still writes `chatQueue` itself. In production that write is now always superseded by the owner projection. Removing it means reworking several persistence tests that rely on it.
- `confirmQueuedMessageCustody` compares the live row (`sending`) with the stored row (`waiting-reconnect`), so custody stamping waits until the live send settles. I saw no user-visible effect from this.

</details>

## Evidence

- New regression test in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-recovery.test.ts`. It mounts a real `ChatStateController`, sends a follow-up during an active run, and has the Gateway acknowledge it as `started`. It then restores the composer and asserts two things: the visible row stays `sending`, and storage still holds the `waiting-reconnect` reload alias.
  - Without the fix: fails at the post-restore assertion (`"sendState": "sending"` expected, `"waiting-reconnect"` received).
  - With the fix: passes.
- Test cost: the new test runs in 22 ms. `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 86 s wall on my Windows machine, almost all of it Vitest import and transform (tests are about 2% of the time). No timers, sleeps, or polling.
- Related suites pass, 769 tests in total:
  - `composer-persistence`, `chat-send-submit`, `outbox-identity`
  - `chat-pane-attachment-handoff`, `chat-state`, `chat-state-queued-edit`
  - `composer-persistence-restore`, `chat-composer-queue`, `chat-send`
  - `chat-outbox-attention`, `chat-outbox-loading`, `chat-input-scroll-ownership`
  - `outbox-payloads`, `outbox-store`
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`:
  - Passed: conflict markers, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety ratchets, the i18n catalog, and all core-test `tsgo` graphs, including `ui-chat`.
  - Not completed: the Knip dead-export scan timed out at 600 s on this host (this change adds no exports). That run also ended before its remaining lanes finished and was not rerun on the final commit; CI covers those gates.
  - `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` are clean.
- An independent code review found no correctness issues. It confirmed that the restore and the owner filter the same rows, so re-presenting cannot drop anything the restore intended to show. The `autoreview` skill was not available in my environment.
- Gap: no real-browser capture. This is a state-only fix with no styling change, proven at the controller boundary; my browser automation was unavailable. I also could not reproduce the "Reconnected before delivery was confirmed" copy quoted in the issue. That text needs a history read with no receipt for the send, while the reported trace shows the input as queued custody.

prs.title: fix(gateway): hand task suggestions a host-resolvable cwd from sandboxes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves



Fixes #143980.



Accepting a task suggestion created inside a Docker-sandboxed session

(`agents.defaults.sandbox = { mode: "all", backend: "docker" }`) failed deterministically with

`INVALID_REQUEST "sessions.create cwd is unavailable: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '/workspace'"`.



**Root cause:** `suggest_task` runs inside the sandbox, so the recorded `cwd` is the container path (Docker

`WorkingDir=/workspace`, bind-mounted from the host sandbox workspace). `taskSuggestions.accept` then calls

`sessions.create` on the host, where `prepareSessionCreateFilesystemRoot()` runs `fs.realpathSync()` on that

container path, which cannot exist on the host.



**Fix** — decided by the session's sandbox configuration and its host↔container workspace mapping, never by

path shape (a POSIX-absolute path is equally valid on a Linux host):



- `taskSuggestions.create` resolves the source session's sandbox workspace

  (`ensureSandboxWorkspaceForSession`) and translates a container-workspace path back to the host directory it

  is bind-mounted from, reusing the existing sandbox↔host translation used for sandbox media paths

  (new export `mapSandboxContainerWorkspacePath` in `src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts`, built on the existing

  container-workdir normalizer).

- A cwd the host still cannot resolve is refused at create time with an actionable error instead of persisting

  a doomed path, e.g. `task suggestion cwd is unavailable: /sandbox-only/folder is missing on the host;

  sandboxed sessions run in a container, so use a host path under <host workspace> or a container path under

  /workspace.`

- Non-sandboxed sessions keep their exact previous behavior (absolute-path check only); host-path cards from

  sandboxed sessions pass through unchanged, and container subpaths map onto the host workspace tree.



## Evidence



- New regression test `src/gateway/server-methods/task-suggestions.sandbox-cwd.test.ts` (5 tests, real

  handler + real temp state), covering: container root mapping, container subpath mapping, mapping to the

  session sandbox workspace (`workspaceAccess: none`), create-time refusal of an unresolvable sandbox cwd,

  and pass-through of a host path. The first test also runs the full accept flow end to end and asserts

  `spawnedCwd === <host workspace>`.

- Pre-fix (baseline code, test added only): `Tests 4 failed | 1 passed (5)` — the container cwd was stored

  verbatim and the doomed path was recorded without error.

- Post-fix: `Tests 5 passed (5)`.

- Regression suite: `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts task-suggestions

  session-create-root` → `Test Files 5 passed (5)`, `Tests 66 passed (66)`.

- Sandbox path translation touched by the shared refactor: `vitest run --config

  test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts sandbox-paths` → `1 failed | 52 passed | 4 skipped`; the same

  single failure reproduces with the pre-change `sandbox-paths.ts` restored (dev-machine Windows symlink

  semantics in `sandbox-paths.test.ts:214`, unrelated to this change).

- `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts infra/outbound/message-action-params` →

  `Tests 91 passed | 23 skipped`; `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-tools.config.ts

  tools/task-suggestion-tools` → `Tests 3 passed`.

- Lint/format clean on the changed files (`oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`); core typecheck

  (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`) exits 0.



Test command used for the new file:



```bash

node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run \

  --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts \

  src/gateway/server-methods/task-suggestions.sandbox-cwd.test.ts \

  --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism

```

# Docker + real-parser cross-validation — openclaw PR #146075 (nested sandbox bind → host cwd)



- Repo: openclaw/openclaw, worktree `D:/code/wt-oc-143980`

- **After** (fix): `de425fb47b337e5057a8e10f35ad1079932b365e` — "fix(gateway): resolve task suggestion cwd from the session's effective sandbox"

- **Before**: `220e2460859c` — "fix(gateway): hand task suggestions a host-resolvable cwd from sandboxes" (first commit of the PR; it prefix-strips the container workdir and ignores nested binds)

- Host: Windows, Docker 29.6.2, node v26.4.0 + the repo's tsx loader (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`)

- Artifacts (all under `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Temp`): `ocproof-143980-docker.mjs` (script), `ocproof-143980-docker.after.txt`, `ocproof-143980-docker.before.txt`, `ocproof-143980-docker.groundtruth.txt`



## Scenario under test



Host directory `C:/Users/Administrator/AppData/Local/Temp/ocproof-143980/bind-target` (containing `marker.txt` = `PROOF-BIND-TARGET-143980`) is mounted as a **nested bind** `-v <bind-target>:/workspace/project` inside a sandbox whose workspace root `<agent-workspace>` is mounted at `/workspace`. A sandbox session records cwd `/workspace/project`; the task-suggestion path must resolve that back to `bind-target` on the host — **not** to `<agent-workspace>/project`.



## Step 1 — Docker ground truth (real container, real bind)



The container path really is the host directory — same bind the gateway config below uses:



```text

$ docker run --rm -v "C:/Users/Administrator/AppData/Local/Temp/ocproof-143980/bind-target:/workspace/project" alpine sh -c 'cat /workspace/project/marker.txt'

PROOF-BIND-TARGET-143980

exit=0



$ ls -l C:/Users/Administrator/AppData/Local/Temp/ocproof-143980/bind-target/marker.txt

-rw-r--r-- 1 Administrator 197121 24  9月 13 02:39 C:/Users/Administrator/AppData/Local/Temp/ocproof-143980/bind-target/marker.txt

```



## Step 2 — How the script exercises the real code



`ocproof-143980-docker.mjs` (run from the worktree root, so the revision checked out there is what runs):



1. Scaffolds the real host dirs, writes the marker, and runs the **real `docker run` bind above** inside the script, asserting the marker read through `/workspace/project` equals the host marker.

2. Imports the **real exported gateway entry** `resolveTaskSuggestionHostCwd(...)` from `src/gateway/server-methods/task-suggestion-host-cwd.ts` (not a re-implementation; the script is revision-agnostic and runs whichever revision is checked out).

3. Config: `agents.defaults.sandbox = {mode:"all", backend:"docker", scope:"session", workspaceAccess:"rw", docker:{binds:["<bind-target>:/workspace/project"], workdir:"/workspace"}}`, agent workspace = `<agent-workspace>`. It logs the sandbox view the entry itself builds (`workspaceDir`, `containerWorkdir=/workspace`, `dockerBinds`) via the real `ensureSandboxWorkspaceForSession`.

4. **Scenario A** — no host counterpart `<agent-workspace>/project` exists; **Scenario B** — an unrelated same-named decoy `<agent-workspace>/project` exists on the host (marker `DECOY-NOT-THE-BIND-TARGET-143980`).

5. Asserts the outcome expected of the checked-out revision and asserts the accepted cwd against the Docker ground truth.

## Result diff



| Scenario | BEFORE `220e2460859c` | AFTER `de425fb47b3` |

|---|---|---|

| A: `/workspace/project` has no `<agent-workspace>/project` counterpart | `{ok:false}` — falsely rejects a directory that exists inside the container ("maps to …\\agent-workspace\project … but that path is missing on the host") | `{ok:true, cwd:<bind-target>}` — the real nested-bind host dir |

| B: unrelated decoy `<agent-workspace>/project` exists on the host | `{ok:true, cwd:<agent-workspace>/project}` — silently accepts the **wrong** host dir (marker `DECOY-…` ≠ the container's `PROOF-BIND-TARGET-143980`) | `{ok:true, cwd:<bind-target>}` — nested bind wins over the workspace root |



## Honest claims



**Proven here.** With a real Docker container proving that `<bind-target>` is what `/workspace/project` points at, and the real exported gateway entry `resolveTaskSuggestionHostCwd` running the code checked out in the worktree, the fixed revision maps the container cwd `/workspace/project` to `<bind-target>` in both scenarios (accepted cwd's `marker.txt` matches what the container reads), while the pre-fix revision either falsely rejects the same cwd (scenario A) or accepts an unrelated same-named host directory (scenario B) — the exact defect the PR fixes.



**Not proven here (limits).** No gateway accept flow was driven end-to-end: no websocket/JSON-RPC accept request, no openclaw-managed sandbox container was started (Docker was used only to establish mount ground truth; the sandbox "view" came from the real `ensureSandboxWorkspaceForSession` against the real config). Only the cwd-mapping entry point and its inputs were exercised, on one nested-bind shape on a Windows host.



**No repo mutation.** `git status --porcelain` empty, `HEAD = de425fb47b337e5057a8e10f35ad1079932b365e`, and the three temporarily checked-out files were restored byte-identical (`git hash-object` == `git rev-parse de425fb47b3:<path>`):

```text

src/gateway/server-methods/task-suggestion-host-cwd.ts  c3f2882c554914e58c36a94c096d17edc50d711d

src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts                             c540f274f17bf1afac091e13dc0027670c5c745c

src/gateway/server-methods/task-suggestions.ts          a29a3734278687207c05db2ecd962ef650730e74

```

Side effect outside the repo: the skill sync inside `ensureSandboxWorkspaceForSession` wrote into the app state dir (`~/.openclaw/sandbox/skills-workspaces/...`), which is the app's own scratch space, not the repository.



Reproduce:

```text

printf 'PROOF-BIND-TARGET-143980' > "$LOCALAPPDATA/Temp/ocproof-143980/bind-target/marker.txt"

cd D:/code/wt-oc-143980

node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs "$LOCALAPPDATA/Temp/ocproof-143980-docker.mjs" after  "$LOCALAPPDATA/Temp/ocproof-143980"

# then the before/after checkout pair from Step 4 and mode=before

```





### Rework — disposition of the three P1 findings



**P1 — Resolve the source session's effective workspace before mapping.** `task-suggestion-host-cwd.ts` now loads the source session entry (`loadGatewaySessionEntryReadOnly`) and resolves the run's workspace through `resolveIngressWorkspaceOverrideForSessionRun({ spawnedBy, workspaceDir, cwd })` — the same override resolution `sandbox-explain` and runtime preparation use — instead of always supplying `resolveAgentWorkspaceDir`. A sandboxed dashboard session with a selected folder or managed worktree now maps against the workspace that session actually mounts.



**P1 — Use the existing mount-aware resolver for container directories.** The partial workspace-prefix mapper is gone. Container cwd resolution now goes through `buildSandboxFsMounts` + `resolveSandboxFsPathWithMounts`, which own mount precedence (longest container root first) and container containment, so nested binds (`/srv/other` at `/workspace/project`) resolve to the bind host directory. The now-unused `mapSandboxContainerWorkspacePath` was removed; `SandboxWorkspaceInfo` carries the resolved `agentWorkspaceDir`/`dockerBinds` from the same `ensureSandboxWorkspaceForSession` layout the runtime uses.



**P1 — Preserve suggestions that can run in their existing session.** Creation-time host-directory rejection is gone: `create` resolves best-effort and keeps the original cwd when it cannot. At acceptance, `mode === "session"` delivers the prompt to the source conversation without touching cwd; the host-launch modes resolve-and-reject only where a host session actually starts, and a failed host launch restores the claim so the card remains acceptable via session mode.



Regression coverage (`src/gateway/server-methods/task-suggestions.sandbox-cwd.test.ts`, 8 tests): selected-folder mapping, inherited spawned workspace, nested bind mapping, container-only cwd still acceptable in its source session, root mapping, unresolvable rejection on host launch, host-path passthrough, plus the create→accept chain assertion. `pre` (source at `220e2460859c`, tests kept): `4 failed | 4 passed`; `post`: `8 passed`. Sibling suites green: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 51 passed (51)`.

$ git checkout de425fb47b3 -- <3 source files> && git status --porcelain

Boundaries, stated plainly: this cross-validates the resolver against a **real Docker bind** (container ground truth + the real exported resolver), but it is not a full Gateway-accept end-to-end; the repo's managed sandbox container was not started. The `ssh` backend and `readOnlyResourceMounts` remote-workspace semantics still resolve via the local docker/podman mount table. And the changed `src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts` still requires listed sandbox-owner involvement, which is not something I can supply.



---



### Sandbox-mount-root handoff + acceptance coverage (revision `3d5123f6c7c4c9572b72aee21b3bea1ae5a1c8f0`)



Addresses the two open items: **Complete local acceptance for mapped isolated sandbox roots (P2)** and the **P1 "no approved handoff contract"**.



**What changed** (new commit `3d5123f6c7c`, on top of `a17697477fc`):



- The sandbox cwd mapping layer now marks the owning mount root on the **trusted session-creation provenance it already supplies** (`client.internal.sessionCreation` / `TrustedSessionCreation` — the in-process channel documented as never accepted from Gateway wire params). New module: `src/agents/sandbox/mount-root-handoff.ts`; marker shape `{ kind: "sandbox-mount-root", agentId, hostRoot }`.

- `prepareSessionCreateFilesystemRoot` admits a cwd outside the agent workspace **only** after consuming that marker and re-deriving the sandbox-owned host roots for this agent from config (configured sandbox workspace root incl. every isolated scope, materialized skills workspaces, declared bind host roots). A forged/stale marker (wrong agent, root no sandbox owns, missing root) fails closed; callers without the marker keep the existing containment check unchanged.

- Covers both mapped forms: isolated sandbox workspaces (`workspaceAccess: "none"`) and external bind targets.



**Red -> green (owner re-runs on this revision, Windows host):**

| `vitest.gateway-methods`: `session-create-root.test.ts` + `task-suggestions.sandbox-cwd.test.ts` (28 tests) | **4 failed** - the two acceptance e2e cases fail with `UNAVAILABLE: sessions.create cwd is outside the sandboxed agent workspace`; 2 unit cases red on the missing param | **28 passed** |

| `vitest.agents-support`: `src/agents/sandbox/fs-paths.test.ts` | - | **13 passed** |

| Big board control `server.sessions.create.test.ts` (164) | 11 failed | 11 failed - **identical sets** (pre-existing Windows EPERM/timeout failures), zero fix-only failures |



`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` exit 0; `oxfmt --check` clean; `oxlint` clean (incl. the `max-lines` budget).



**Open decision requests for the sandbox owner / maintainers:**



1. Approve the handoff contract itself (marker on the existing in-process provenance + consumer-side re-derivation of sandbox-owned roots), or ask for a different shape (e.g. an explicit handler-options field instead of provenance).

2. Should a verified handoff also satisfy the `operator.admin` gate at `sessions-create.ts:285`? Not touched - that would be a second containment relaxation and needs an explicit decision.

3. Intentionally still refused: a source session pinned to a workspace-external directory (`workspaceAccess: "rw"` selected folder / inherited workspace) - its root is not sandbox-owned, and widening to "any host directory" needs a broader decision.



**Honest limits:** no live container acceptance for this revision yet (would need a container-backend run); covered acceptance is at the `sessions.create` boundary plus the mock-harness e2e, not a real docker container.

### Revision `5eb02be87db` — findings fixed: ro admission is now fail-closed, workspace continuity preserved

- **[P1] Read-only binds are never admitted** (`mount-root-handoff.ts:50-53`; security: "read-only bind becomes a writable workspace alias"): the admitted-root list now uses `resolveWritableSandboxBindHostRoots()` — `:ro` binds and writable roots shadowed by a `:ro` child are never admitted. The producer withholds the marker unless the owning mount is one the sandbox layer serves writable; the consumer re-derives the allowlist from config and refuses even a forged/in-process marker for a `:ro` root. `:ro` sources keep creation's containment error for a "new local session" follow-up (refuse, never silently widen); "start in this session" still works. The PR's now-unused ro-inclusive helper `resolveSandboxBindHostRoots()` was deleted.
- **[P2] Workspace continuity** (`session-create-root.ts:63-68`): the sandbox owner reuses a directory it already owns — if the handed workspace sits inside `<workspaceRoot>/workspace-<32hex>` (re-derived from config, the sandbox's own scope-slug marker), the follow-up mounts the source session's isolated copy at the workdir instead of deriving a fresh `wrap-<hash>`. `workspaceAccess rw` is unchanged; shared scope and unrelated directories keep the old copy-per-scope behavior.
- **[P2] Canonicalization moved inside the sandboxed branch** (`session-create-root.ts:53`): `realpathSync(workspaceDir)` now runs only when sandbox containment actually needs it; unsandboxed creations with an explicit existing cwd no longer fail on an unrelated missing workspace. Sandboxed fail-closed behavior is unchanged.

**Evidence (owner re-verified):** each fix proved load-bearing by mutation (removing the consumer's writable/ro-shadow filter, the producer's `!owner?.writable` gate, the workspace-reuse hunk, or re-hoisting `realpathSync` each reds its own pinned tests). Green: gateway-methods 38 passed / 1 skipped (incl. prs.title: feat(browser): discover and execute page WebMCP tools
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents and CLI users need a narrow way to discover and invoke page-provided WebMCP tools through the Browser plugin's existing-session Chrome MCP connection. Related: #143413.

## User Impact

Adds `webmcp_list` and `webmcp_execute` through the agent tool, CLI, and authenticated Browser control routes. Enable Chrome's WebMCP testing flag and `--categoryExperimentalWebmcp=true` on an existing-session profile. Page metadata/results remain untrusted and bounded; unsupported profiles fail explicitly.

**Browser-owner product/security acceptance remains required.** Chrome MCP has no atomic expected-document argument. A replacement after the final check can execute the named tool on the replacement page before OpenClaw reports an unknown outcome. The live race below demonstrates the mutation; the post-check does not prevent it. Do not use this experimental path where that stronger guarantee is required.

**Decision requested:** Is that demonstrated final-effect behavior acceptable for this explicitly enabled experimental Browser action? If not, should this PR ship discovery only while execution waits for a document-bound upstream contract? The current implementation should not merge without that decision.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keeps two fixed Browser actions and reuses the existing profile, tab, policy, session-lock, and transport owners. Execution errors preserve timeout identity while removing generic retry advice. Numeric MCP SDK request deadlines now map to the shared timeout identity; ordinary numeric MCP errors remain failures. The caller must inspect the page before deciding to retry a mutation whose response was lost.

Refreshed against `main` at `9c93bc347ceca939d4dfd8d934f15ecc94b7a45a` on September 29, 2026, including the latest Browser helper refactor. The refresh resolves merge conflicts and migrates to current lazy CLI registration, the shared Browser request transport, and the root route registrar. Retired `core-api`, URL-helper, and `routes/agent.ts` owners stay retired. No new configuration fields, dependency changes, or storage migrations are introduced; the existing profile setup and installed updater remain the input.

Rechecked fetched `main` at `ece1294b31` on September 29: the only repository-wide `WebMCP` reference is the Chrome extension's allowed `WebMCP.enable` CDP command. The Browser action roster still has neither `webmcp_list` nor `webmcp_execute`; [the paired feature issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/143413) remains open. [The earlier closed request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48028) concerned attaching to the user's Chrome session and listing tabs, which shipped separately. Since this PR's refresh base, the intervening Browser-tree change only removes tests; no Browser production implementation supersedes these actions.

## Evidence

- Final refreshed source: 272 behavior tests passed across 12 files (255 in the focused behavior run, plus all 17 plugin-registration tests in an isolated run with the same assertions and hook limit). Coverage includes CLI lazy registration, agent binding/schema, root routes, loopback auth, node transport uncertainty, and native-session mocks. The actual numeric SDK timeout regression failed before the fix and passes afterward; the ordinary numeric-error control also passes.
- Extension production and test type checks passed; all three pinned Knip export scans passed with zero findings. Formatting, ownership/boundary guards, MDX sanity, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The full build passed on the initial refresh base `89217d3b875373f5ba4f63dfc5e23fa9ca744ba6`. After incorporating the newer main revision, native proof and types/export checks were repeated. Final extension lint is unverified locally: SDK boundary declaration preparation exceeded its unchanged 300-second limit twice, including an isolated attempt, before lint could execute. The combined registration suite hit its 180-second import hook limit; the final isolated run passed all 17 tests within that unchanged limit. Before this body-only update, `gh pr checks` reported 63 passes and 51 skips on refreshed head `e794b303d3759f104e8edc1de9a4a4cc932d5427`; no code check failed. [ClawSweeper's fifth review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144078#issuecomment-5619740118) confirms the document-race finding and requests a Browser-owner decision.
- Independent review completed. Its numeric timeout finding was reproduced and corrected. Its confirmed P1 document-race finding remains the Browser-owner acceptance blocker described above; this PR is not claimed ready to merge.

Fresh native proof used Node 24.19.0 and Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.34 with both the repository's patched Chrome MCP 1.9.0 and upstream 1.10.1. Each completed five checks through authenticated Browser HTTP -> registered root route -> real Chrome MCP -> native WebMCP:

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Unauthenticated discovery | HTTP 401 |
| Native discovery | `get_counter` and `increment_counter` advertised |
| Ordinary increment | Counter 3; one independent page mutation receipt |
| Reload observed before execution | Stale context rejected; replacement counter 0; no additional receipt |
| Replacement after final check, before invocation | Replacement counter 2; one replacement mutation receipt; unknown-outcome error; no automatic retry |

The race harness forwards the actual MCP protocol unchanged, except that it holds `execute_webmcp_tool` until an independent Playwright/CDP observer loads the replacement fixture and confirms native tool registration. The fixture records mutation receipts independently of the tool response. This is Browser-route/native API proof, not a full model-agent or live Gateway end-to-end claim.

The current upstream [Chrome MCP execution contract](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/blob/e52c6b59b476c5e04d8dd9fd4bd017ba3b3d65df/src/tools/webmcp.ts) still invokes by page and tool name; [Puppeteer's CDP implementation](https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/blob/043cd46e594b39ea77343e221a59724183448059/packages/puppeteer-core/src/cdp/WebMCP.ts#L380-L389) sends frame ID, tool name, and input without an expected-document token. Chrome's current [setup documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp) places the origin trial at Chrome 149 and describes the local testing flag.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized final-effect diagnostic</summary>

```json
{
  "barrier": "after final OpenClaw document check, before real execute_webmcp_tool dispatch",
  "replacementReady": true,
  "replacementCounter": 2,
  "replacementMutationReceipts": 1,
  "error": "WebMCP execution outcome unknown. Inspect the page before retrying.",
  "automaticallyRetried": false,
  "conclusion": "Replacement mutation occurred before post-check rejection."
}
```

</details>

prs.title: feat(google-meet): send and answer in-call chat
prs.body:
Related: #2717 (the broader meeting-chat assistance use case; this PR does not integrate Vexa).
Builds on #152327.

## What Problem This Solves

Google Meet agents can participate through audio but cannot yet read and answer the meeting’s native in-call messages.

## User Impact

Chrome and Chrome-node meetings can observe native chat and send exact written replies through `send_chat`, the CLI, or generic participation requests. Agent/bidi modes can answer fresh incoming requests in writing; observe-only mode never replies automatically. Native-chat-triggered speech requires a current participant request explicitly asking for voice. Ordinary manual speech and Teams/Zoom behavior remain unchanged.

Requests retain stable IDs and durable results. Cancellation after native dispatch remains best effort: an `uncertain` result may already have produced an effect and must not be retried under a new request ID.

**Inherited participation limitations remain:** source age starts at first host observation, the 10,000-identity session bound fails closed, and direct source-free written requests do not gain a new host-attested operator-versus-model origin grant in this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Port the native-chat layer onto the merged participation owner instead of replaying its old foundation. The plugin owns native message discovery and delivery while the shared runtime continues to own source authority, replay protection, speech readiness, and cleanup.

The migration preserves transcript provenance and speaker metadata, pinned browser routes, corrections, literal guarded speech, and the written-default response policy. It also prevents a slow optional chat inventory read from holding the browser-tab lock long enough to terminate existing meeting audio. Inventory reads stay outside the audio-critical lock; page evaluation remains serialized and revalidates the session and URL.

## Evidence

Refreshed onto `main@76beb5685887`; tested candidate `5ca7f4ecaca0` (tree `0371b163aaa2`). Both attributed commits are preserved. The audio-lock fix replayed unchanged.

- **Tests:** 786 passed across 31 files, zero failures/skips, in 173.17s. All seven native invocations completed and joined; original JSON reports match the requested selection. Coverage includes every changed suite plus shared meeting, Talk, browser transport, Google/OpenAI/xAI voice and SDK siblings.
- **Compile/static checks:** the complete 67-path changed-check plan passed in 24m 26.7s, including core production, all 27 core-test type graphs, extension production/test and script types, formatting, lint, SDK/boundary/storage/import guards. Three nonblocking max-lines warnings are byte-unchanged from the pinned main base; no lint errors.
- **Clean build:** normal guarded `pnpm build` passed in 7m 8.7s. Build metadata matches this clean commit. Frozen dependencies; Node 26.8.2 and pnpm 12.5.1.
- **Integration review:** conflict resolution preserves upstream shared parameter-type ownership and combines both test inventories. No additional runtime behavior was introduced by this refresh; previous behavior reviews are retained for unchanged code.
- **Reliability fixes retained:** explicit leading voice intent, final native-source freshness, retired provider audio/transcript fencing, cancellation cleanup, and preserving consecutive exact spoken replies. These have failing-before/passing-after regressions from the preceding local work and pass on this refreshed head.
- **SDK:** 3,651 public exports / 2,113 callables; 151 public entrypoints and zero public wildcard re-exports. The existing browser-lock helper remains +1 export / +1 callable; this refresh adds no SDK surface.

**Still draft / before merge:** no live Meet, authenticated provider or device proof was run. The existing review’s source-free-send authority, page-session capacity and session-visible observer-error concerns remain open. Local validation does not resolve those concerns or establish merge readiness.

prs.title: fix(cron): keep legacy jobs on maintenance timer
prs.body:
<!-- Source-first cron code bug; no public issue is linked. -->

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where legacy persisted cron jobs that omit the optional `enabled` field could stop receiving scheduler maintenance wakes when their next-run timestamp was missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron scheduling already treats a missing `enabled` value as enabled through `isJobEnabled`, and next-wake selection follows that rule. The maintenance-timer summary used a different explicit-true check, so it could report no enabled jobs and leave the scheduler without a recovery timer. The summary now uses the canonical enabled predicate, with a focused regression covering the legacy shape.

## User Impact

Older cron records continue receiving the 60-second maintenance wake that repairs a missing 
extRunAtMs`, instead of remaining silent until another mutation or restart.

## Evidence

- **Persisted production path:** The focused regression first writes a cron job to the real SQLite-backed cron store, removes only `job_json.enabled` from the stored row (leaving the supported current-schema record with the legacy omission), then calls production `ensureLoaded(..., forceReload)` before `armTimer`. This is distinct from the merged schema-v13 migration repair, which reconstructs `job_json.enabled` during an upgrade from an older wide row.
- **Inspectable result on exact head:**
  ```text
  persisted job after production load: enabled=undefined
  timer diagnostic: jobCount=1 enabledCount=1 withNextRun=0 delayMs=60000
  maintenance wake: armed (60000 ms)
  maintenance callback: nextRunAtMs restored and persisted (> now)
  ```
- **Focused proof:** 
ode scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.armtimer-tight-loop.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — 1 file, 6 tests passed, including the persisted-row case.
- **Real service timer proof on exact head:** A real `CronService.start()` loaded the persisted SQLite row with `enabled=undefined`; after `resumeScheduling()`, the actual 60-second maintenance callback ran and persisted 
extRunAtMs=1789066128525` (> proof start `1789062593261`).
- **Checks:** Targeted `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Proof boundary:** No external channel, provider, or user account was used; the proof covers the local production SQLite loader and scheduler timer path only.
- **Exact candidate head:** `5f5d662a101c86c2615c6eb677e26c51ccbed040`.

prs.title: fix(clickclack): ingest message attachments
prs.body:
Related: #136029

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes ClickClack attachments reaching agents as text-only input, permanently missing uploads blocking later messages, and attachment effects continuing after admission is retired.

## User Impact

Agent-mode bots receive admitted attachments through managed media storage. Missing uploads receive a re-upload notice; oversized files receive a reduce-or-split instruction; text-only model bots ask for the relevant content as text. Terminal media rejection lets the next message proceed. Downloads, file publication, and attachment notices retain the existing live authority and cancellation checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The connector fetches upload IDs with bot authentication, stages bytes through the existing media owner, and supplies ordered media facts to the agent. Upload HTTP 404 is terminal; transient retrieval and notice-delivery failures remain retryable. Limits, bounded reads, redirect rejection, correlation, duplicate protection, and bot-loop protection are preserved.

The review against `98f00833506476465c8f9feae890b6e6056c854d` identified two remaining admission gaps. One abort-and-current-access callback now reaches download requests, response-media publication, and both notice paths. Notices use the existing `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback, so the sender rechecks authority after asynchronous DM preparation and before the final POST. `saveResponseMedia` accepts an optional synchronous `assertCurrent` callback and reuses the existing media read scope to compose ambient authority, cancellation, streaming, and cleanup. Existing callers remain compatible; the plugin uses public SDK contracts.

Integrated main `87b0295824773d53c51b1056534a045249f832cb`, preserving its access, lifecycle, and SDK contracts. The companion server's atomic initial-message/upload association merged in https://github.com/openclaw/clickclack/pull/239. Independently adding an attachment after the creation event remains a separate server/event contract.

## Evidence

[Sanitized native transport receipts, audit, provider facts and source binding](https://github.com/sercada/clickclack/blob/dc8faa320de626236bf5b7d7ae097122f7e53b30/openclaw-native-proof-20261013/attachments/README.md).

Current head: `2608831af10df189d3e27965346b63963b6c3ba7`. After the first six-brace repair in `3fd`, native PR CI identified 27 more test lint errors. This update only changes four tests: required braces, inferred default void arguments, one shadowed parameter, and explicit URL/JSON-body narrowing. Eight existing HTTP cases move intact with their mock to `http-client.media.test.ts`. Conditions, table rows, assertions and all six affected production blobs are unchanged. The immutable [CI repair addendum](https://github.com/sercada/clickclack/blob/32b2ddc62cfcf575a7b6cd118ed35ea74022935a/openclaw-native-proof-20261013/attachments-ci-repair/README.md) records identities, source review and execution limits; it does not relabel old proof as new test execution.

A real running source Gateway and native ClickClack candidate `2eabd69dfd4b81ceef226409a3190f13782d7e49` completed this transport matrix with synthetic, isolated state:

| Contract | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Admitted image | Native GET 200; identical 68-byte PNG retained; one real provider `input_image`; persisted `ATTACHMENT_ALLOWED_OK` reply |
| Unadmitted human | Authoritative native message lookup; zero upload GET, published files, or provider calls |
| Account retirement during stream | Physical 512-byte temporary PDF observed; native `channels.stop`; zero final files, provider calls, or replies |
| Account retirement during awaited DM preparation | Native DM preparation 201 held; native `channels.stop`; zero final notice POST, files, provider calls, or replies |
| Missing upload | Native backend 404; one re-upload notice; the next message reaches the provider and receives a durable reply |
| Transient failure | One named loopback proxy 503; native backlog retry GET 200; image reaches provider; one durable reply and native socket reconnect |

The Gateway used the repository-pinned OpenClaw Bun fork `1.4.3-canary.1+65d94e715` with the production CLI's real managed lifecycle/recovery owner. Runtime proof under this engine is distinct from Node build evidence. The two race cases retired the account's AbortSignal/lifetime with `allowFrom` unchanged. Saved `allowFrom` changes whose channel reload was deferred are not claimed as active policy revocation. The two retired synthetic inputs were cleaned through the native API only after the stopped-owner assertions, with before/tombstone readbacks preserved. All fixture processes joined without cleanup errors.

- Four media-owner cases pass (20.37 seconds including the wrapper): allowed and caller-revoked saves call `saveResponseMedia` directly, matching the connector; ambient-revoked and aborted cases check scope composition. A real streamed PDF writes its first bytes to disk before revocation. Rejected saves preserve the exact owner reason, release the reader, and leave no output. With the same direct-call test on old `98f`, the promise incorrectly resolved and published the full PDF (expected negative-control failure; 20.96 seconds).
- All 27 connector tests pass across `inbound.media.test.ts` and `gateway.media.test.ts` (73.61 seconds in Vitest; 79.10 seconds including the wrapper). They use the actual inbound path, outbound sender, and HTTP client with synthetic fetch responses to prove policy revocation during DM preparation produces zero final notice POST. They also cover ordered ingestion, loop/limit contracts, media callback wiring, and 404/503 cursor behavior. Old `98f` incorrectly completed all three revoked notice variants (three expected negative-control failures; 81.50 seconds). These focused regressions remain distinct from the native transport matrix.
- [Native fork CI on exact production head `68d`](https://github.com/sercada/openclaw/actions/runs/38448248664) passed the Node build, production typecheck, all five core test-type stripes, and extension test types. The `build-artifacts` job took 1,108 seconds, including a 262-second dist build and built artifact checks. Local SDK/type-aware preparation exhausted finite resource/deadline budgets without completed analysis; it is not reported as passing. The same CI identified six test `curly` errors fixed in `3fd`; focused lint, format, normal hooks, peer review, and canonical P2 review all pass for that repair.
- Canonical autoreview returned `scoped-clean` through P2 for the full `68d` repair against `98f`, with committed media, authority, access, outbound, HTTP, and fixture context. Independent peer review covered production and the direct filesystem/composition oracle. The brace-only `3fd` delta also passed canonical P2 review with no production changes.

Focused source-test reproduction uses Node 24.21.0 and the documented finite source route:

```bash
node scripts/test-projects.mts src/media/fetch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --watch --run -t 'saved-response publication'
node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.media.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.media.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --watch --run
```

The four-test repair passes formatting, AST lint, normal hooks, independent peer review and canonical P2 delta review (scoped-clean, confidence 0.94). These are historical classifications and granted no gate exception. No workflow reevaluation remains pending for this head. SDK/security owner acceptance of the optional callback is still a separate before-merge decision.

The latest hosted review explicitly covers exact head `2608831af10df189d3e27965346b63963b6c3ba7` (durable review updated 2026-10-13 21:29 UTC). It inspected the native transport artifacts, finds no actionable code defect and regards real behavior proof as sufficient. Its enforcing-workflow item is now resolved by the successful current gate. Closes #153453

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes delayed WhatsApp replies when the agent's plugin registry selects an unconnected channel adapter after the inbound message was accepted by a connected one.

## User Impact

Replies use the inbound transport on the first attempt, avoiding the observed 5–10-second delivery-recovery wait. Model response time is unchanged. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the inbound channel registration before agent dispatch and carry it only into durable reply delivery. Capability checks and sending use that same adapter. Keep the current request scope so caller authority and agent policy hooks remain current, and keep managed adapter lifecycle checks so a revoked connection owner cannot be revived or replaced by a same-ID sender.

The binding is channel-generic; there is no WhatsApp-specific state store or retry-timer change. Unrelated channel sends keep their normal registry selection.

## Evidence

- On unmodified main `4e002cf7`, the new DM/group integration regression fails through the real durable reply pipeline with the synthetic unconnected adapter's missing-listener error. Both pass with the fix and send exactly once via the connected adapter.
- Five new tests cover those two flows plus current caller scope, unrelated-channel selection, and adapter revocation. Existing delivery, durable-delivery, and channel-resolution tests also pass: 62 tests across five files in total.
- A version-specific equivalent was tested live on OpenClaw/WhatsApp 2026.9.5: three replies sent on the first attempt; two warm requests took 3.726 and 3.828 seconds. This source revision itself has not been deployed to the live WhatsApp account.
- Full `pnpm build`, core TypeScript check, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent source review found no further concerns.
- The broader `check:changed` run and automated Codex review were not completed before submission. The automated review was stopped at the operator's request to publish; no automated clean verdict is claimed. CI and maintainer review remain pending.

prs.title: fix(agents): stop messaging dedupe from dropping replies that extend a tool send
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A final reply that starts with a successful message-tool send can be discarded even when it adds a correction: `Deployment finished.` followed by `Deployment finished. Actually it failed.` leaves the correction invisible.

## Fix

Keep @amittell's fix at the shared messaging-dedupe owner. Exempt only the existing forward-substring case when the reply starts with a prior send and its remaining tail contains letters or digits after removing prior sends. Remove longest sends first so overlapping sends remain duplicates. Preserve the existing length threshold, ratio, reverse-substring behavior, and non-prefix cases. Pass all normalized sends together so concatenations do not become new replies.

This deliberately delivers the entire final reply, including its repeated opening. The predicate cannot infer whether newly authored text is a correction or a harmless addition; it must not silently discard either.

Simplified the contributor diff from 139 insertions/3 deletions to 64 insertions/3 deletions: removed duplicate transport-builder tests and explanatory repetition, retained the shared predicate's boundaries and the distinct streamed-reply regression. Production: +19/-3; tests: +45/-0 against the merge base. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Secretless Node 24 Docker, built Gateway and qa-channel, with a local scripted OpenAI-compatible provider. Each independent inbound DM gets a real `message` tool send with `final:false`, then the scripted final. State is created through Gateway/QA bus entry points, never by writing databases. Baseline: `72ccf6ff92931fff2d49473fe1571f39e8311ad2`; candidate includes current main `43b0c022b84`.

Captured `/v1/state` output (non-deleted, non-error outbound text):

```text
                         BASE                              HEAD
correction               Deployment finished.              Deployment finished.
                                                           Deployment finished. Actually it failed.
exact repeated final     Deployment finished.              Deployment finished.
punctuation-only tail    Deployment finished.              Deployment finished.
concatenated sends       Deployment finished.              Deployment finished.
                         Tests passed.                     Tests passed.
```

The base briefly previews then deletes the correction; head retains it. All three controls still suppress the redundant final. Both builds also emit the existing no-visible-reply error for suppressed controls; the base emits it for the correction too. That neighboring finalizer behavior is unchanged and not hidden by the table.

Focused helper + streamed-reply tests pass in isolation (two Vitest shards, 45.51 seconds total); changed-file oxfmt and oxlint pass. No broad suite or local full typecheck was run; hosted CI owns those checks.

Telegram Test Server native-user proof also passed on `d5c72b8f050861c788b7ee9d425f2df117dd3a90`: a leased user sent the deployment request; the real bot's later TDLib message contained `Deployment finished. Actually it failed.`. Two scripted-provider requests occurred (message-tool call, then final). The credential lease was released and the credential file and container mount removed.

## Revert and blast radius

Two-way door: code-only change, no state/config/schema migration. A revert restores the old suppression rule. The shared predicate affects final and streamed replies across channels; the risk is repeating the opening of a message when the model appends substantive text, rather than losing that text.

prs.title: doctor: warn when sandboxed agents allow core tools excluded by sandbox policy
prs.body:
## Problem

A sandboxed agent's `agents.entries.<id>.tools.allow` can list a core tool (e.g. `"secrets"`) that is **never actually surfaced to the agent at runtime**, because sandboxed agents are independently gated by the effective sandbox tool policy computed by `resolveSandboxToolPolicyForAgent()` (`src/agents/sandbox/tool-policy.ts`): `allowConfig ∪ alsoAllowConfig ∪ DEFAULT_TOOL_ALLOW` (`src/agents/sandbox/constants.ts`).

**Root cause, fully pinned:** `DEFAULT_TOOL_ALLOW` is a small fixed list (`exec`, `process`, `read`, `ls`, `write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`, `view_image`, `sessions_*`, `subagents`, `session_status`) applied whenever `tools.sandbox.tools.allow` is not explicitly set — **even if `alsoAllow` is set**. Any core tool not in that list and not explicitly added to `tools.sandbox.tools.allow`/`alsoAllow` (globally or per-agent) is silently excluded from the sandboxed agent's tool catalog, with **zero diagnostic signal anywhere**. `openclaw doctor` already catches the equivalent misconfiguration for MCP/bundle tools via `collectSandboxMcpAllowlistWarnings`, but there was no analogous check for core tools.

### Real-world repro

Found this debugging why an agent (`main`, sandboxed via `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode: "all"`) could not use the `secrets` tool despite it being explicitly present in `agents.entries.main.tools.allow`:

- `tool_search({"query":"secrets"})` only ever returned `exec` — `secrets` was invisible.
- The agent's global `tools.sandbox.tools.alsoAllow` list had `ask_user`, `web_fetch`, `browser`, etc., but **not** `secrets` — and `secrets` is not in `DEFAULT_TOOL_ALLOW` either.
- Adding `"secrets"` to `tools.sandbox.tools.alsoAllow` immediately fixed it — `tool_search` then returned the tool and it became callable. Verified end-to-end against the live production session (not just a test harness): `secrets({"action":"list"})` now succeeds.
- **Important generalization found while pinning the exact mechanism**: this isn't specific to having an `alsoAllow` list that merely omits the tool. Even a sandboxed agent with **zero `tools.sandbox.tools` config anywhere** hits the same bug the moment its `tools.allow` includes any core tool outside `DEFAULT_TOOL_ALLOW` — this is likely the most common way operators hit it.

## Fix

Add `collectSandboxCoreToolAllowlistWarnings`, which:
- For every sandboxed agent, takes its agent-level `tools.allow` (filtered to known core tool ids via `isKnownCoreToolId`).
- Calls **the real runtime resolver**, `resolveSandboxToolPolicyForAgent(cfg, agent.id)` + `isToolAllowed(policy, toolName)`, directly from `src/agents/sandbox/tool-policy.ts` — not a re-derived approximation — to determine whether each tool is actually reachable.
- Warns, per agent, listing exactly which core tool names are allowed at the agent level but not reachable under the resolved sandbox policy, with the config path to fix.
- Wired into `collectPluginToolAllowlistWarnings` unconditionally (even when `plugins.enabled === false`), since this check is unrelated to the plugin system.

Using the actual resolver (rather than reimplementing the allow/alsoAllow/wildcard logic in the diagnostic) was a deliberate, verified choice: an earlier draft of this check re-derived the gating rules and had two correctness bugs caught only by testing against the real resolver:
1. **False positives** for tools already covered by `DEFAULT_TOOL_ALLOW` (e.g. `exec`).
2. **False negatives** for the "no `tools.sandbox.tools` config at all" case, which I had wrongly assumed meant "allow everything" — it does not; it falls back to `DEFAULT_TOOL_ALLOW`.

Reusing the real resolver means this diagnostic can't drift from the actual enforcement logic as that logic evolves.

## Tests

9 new unit tests in `plugin-tool-allowlist-warnings.test.ts`:
- Warning fires for a core tool missing from the resolved sandbox policy.
- No warning when the sandbox list already covers it.
- Warning still fires correctly when **no** `tools.sandbox.tools` config exists at all (the common case).
- No warning when the sandbox policy has an explicit wildcard (`allow: ["*"]`).
- No warning for tools already covered by `DEFAULT_TOOL_ALLOW` (e.g. `"exec"`) — proves no false positives.
- No warning when the agent isn't sandboxed.
- Agent-level sandbox override correctly suppresses the warning.

Ran the full doctor test suite locally: **107 files / 1340 tests pass**, no regressions.

Closes #163703

Related: #171373

## User Impact

This fixes the media-comparison portion of #171373, not its changed-archive recovery state. `historical_transcript_deferred: Archived original changed since migration` comes from archive identity validation before transcript comparison. Those modified archives still need their original receipts and verified pre-reconciliation backups assessed; this PR does not reset fingerprints or certify all nine reported conflicts.

SQLite's transcript writer already normalizes legacy `MediaPath`, `MediaPaths`, `MediaType`, and `MediaTypes` into `__openclaw.media`. Verification previously staged raw legacy JSON. It now uses the same existing canonicalizer before the unchanged exact payload and identity comparisons. The source/history confirms the mismatch on main; no schema, retention, or archive-identity policy changes are needed.

Original fix by @he-yufeng; maintainer cleanup removes the redundant comment and expands the regression to cover ordered, contained, and appendable verification, real differences, and history preservation.

prs.title: feat(mcp): let trusted hosts attach protected request metadata
prs.body:
Related: #170910

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where authorization-sensitive first-party MCP services cannot receive host-verified per-call context without either trusting a broad workload credential or exposing identity fields to model-controlled tool arguments.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a generic optional callback at the embedded-run boundary. After the model selects the MCP server, exact tool, and arguments, the trusted host may return namespaced request metadata that OpenClaw forwards as params._meta for that call. OpenClaw core defines no identity format, signing, allowlist, or service-specific policy, and existing MCP calls are unchanged when the callback is absent.

## User Impact

Embedding hosts can bind protected MCP calls to trusted invocation context while keeping that context outside model arguments. Ordinary OpenClaw users and MCP servers see no behavior or configuration change unless the host opts in.

## Evidence

- The original focused implementation passed 96 tests covering materialization, MCP runtime forwarding, and the embedded-run boundary.
- The branch was then rebuilt onto current upstream main, whose runtime already owns generic request _meta forwarding; the final diff adds the protected host factory and production run-boundary propagation around that owner.
- Exact-head formatting and git diff --check pass.
- Exact-head focused tests are delegated to PR CI because refreshing the current 191-package workspace dependencies exhausted the local host disk; no test result is claimed for the rebased SHA yet.

AI-assisted. I understand the code and verified the production run-boundary propagation as well as request materialization and runtime ownership.

prs.title: fix(feishu): unset groupPolicy admits unlisted groups
prs.body:
Closes #152605

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a configured Feishu bot answers every group it has been added to, and allows group reads outside `groupAllowFrom`, when `groupPolicy` is left unset.

## User Impact

User impact: unset Feishu `groupPolicy` now matches the documented allowlist default. Unlisted groups are dropped; allowlisted groups require an @-mention unless `requireMention` is set. Group reads of a non-current, unlisted chat are denied.

Operators who relied on the undocumented open fallback need `channels.feishu.groupPolicy: "open"` explicitly. `channels.defaults.groupPolicy` and explicit Feishu policies are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu declares `groupPolicy` default `allowlist`, but the exported input-mode schema never materializes that value. The inbound handler and read-action gate then used the open-provider resolver, which maps configured-provider plus unset key to `open`.

Both call sites now use `resolveAllowlistProviderRuntimeGroupPolicy`, the resolver the Feishu security-audit collector already uses. Explicit policies and the missing-provider fail-closed path are unchanged.

## Evidence

Old red (unfixed resolvers, same commands):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/read-policy.test.ts -t "fails closed to allowlist for group reads when groupPolicy is unset"
```

Failed: `expected [Function] to throw an error` — `oc_unlisted` was allowed.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts -t "drops unlisted group messages when groupPolicy is unset"
```

Failed: inbound log was `received message ... in oc-group` instead of `not in groupAllowFrom (groupPolicy=allowlist)`.

New green (this head): the same two commands passed. Mention-gated allowlisted groups also pass.

Owner files:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/read-policy.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts
```

prs.title: fix(mcp): reject mixed command and URL server configs
prs.body:
Related #72111

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an MCP configuration ambiguity exposed by #72111: a server record containing both a command and an HTTP URL historically ran as stdio while silently ignoring its HTTP fields. Rejecting that shape only at runtime would disable already-shipped configurations without giving operators a safe upgrade path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical root and node-host MCP configuration now rejects non-empty `command` + `url` records before they can be persisted. `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates existing shared mixed records to their historically effective stdio form by removing the URL and HTTP-only transport, header, OAuth, and TLS fields while preserving stdio launch settings and shared timeouts/tool filters. The transport resolver retains a fail-closed guard for raw plugin or bundle records that bypass the core schema.

Known legacy MCP `type` aliases are now detected in both root and node-host scopes and normalized through the same shared `canonicalizeConfiguredMcpServer` path before mixed-transport cleanup. This replaces the previous root-only conversion loop. A node-host record such as `{ command, url, type: "streamable-http" }` therefore becomes canonical first, then migrates to stdio without retaining `type`, `url`, or HTTP transport fields; a second Doctor pass is a no-op.

Entries declaring `oauth.identity: "per-requester"` are retained for explicit operator repair, including malformed entries missing `auth`. Mixed cleanup does not remove their HTTP/auth fields or choose shared stdio for them. The existing Doctor hint asks the operator to choose HTTP-only requester access or a separately configured stdio server; existing independent alias migrations still run.

Command-only stdio, URL-only HTTP, and stdio records with a blank or whitespace-only URL keep their existing behavior. The implementation was informed by the focused proposal in #72515 from @Bojun-Vvibe; it is linked as related work rather than claiming that mixed-field precedence was the only cause of the reporter's historical OpenSpace incident. Its integration baseline and current limitations are recorded below.

## User Impact

New mixed configurations fail immediately with a precise validation error and are not written. Existing shared mixed root and node-host records receive an explicit Doctor finding and can be migrated idempotently without changing the stdio behavior they had in prior releases. Raw/plugin records are skipped with an actionable warning instead of silently choosing one transport.

## Review finding disposition

- Resolved the P2 node-host alias migration gap by extending the existing legacy-type rule to both MCP scopes and routing both through the shared canonicalizer.
- Removed the root-only 20-line type conversion loop instead of adding another migration path.
- The regression now uses node-host `type: "streamable-http"`, checks the alias finding, verifies the canonicalization and HTTP-field cleanup messages, and proves a second pass produces no changes.
- Sanitized the mixed-transport warning's configuration-controlled server name with the existing `sanitizeForLog()` helper and added a newline/ANSI injection regression.
- Moved the new CLI no-write regression into a focused 45-line test file because current main's existing `mcp-cli.test.ts` is already near the enforced max-lines budget.

## Current follow-up status

The review's introduced P1 is corrected by preserving per-requester identity before mixed-transport cleanup. This does not yet make the full PR merge-ready: integration with current main, final tool-registration/process-I/O proof, and maintainer acceptance of the migration boundary remain outstanding.

Follow-up commit: `ce78e90abe34f0903dfb601e94bae2dcfa06e1de`.

- Actual-source migration/resolver probe: all four root/node-host × auth-present/missing cases fail before the correction and pass afterward. prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/152234

## What Problem This Solves

Skill Workshop needs to use the selected typed judgment provider for semantic experience and collection review, rather than always running an open-ended generative reviewer.

## User Impact

Otherwise-enabled Workshop reviews use `judgments.provider` (for example, a separately installed TypeSafe/Jev adapter). Accepted no-change decisions finish without a generative reviewer; accepted changes go to a focused author with the selected action, targets, and evidence. Unavailable, ambiguous, incomplete, or stale decisions explicitly fall back to the existing reviewer. Cancellation does not launch fallback work.

Workshop activation and publication permissions remain unchanged: off stays off, propose stages changes, and auto retains its existing maintenance authority. Selecting a provider does not schedule reviews. No vendor adapter, memory integration, new consumer switch, or persisted-state migration is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Experience review asks for one concrete plan first, then requests grounding only for writes. Both provider phases and intervening catalog checks share a two-second budget.
- Evidence projection preserves semantic content and exact tool-call/result linkage. Bounded or incomplete evidence cannot establish complete no-change coverage.
- Collection review evaluates a bounded complete catalog and routes accepted changes directly to focused authorship, including transient cron payload replacement without changing persisted job prompts.
- Catalog revision, cancellation, and current-authority checks remain in force. Judgment output does not grant publication authority.

## Stack and Scope

**Draft stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152237**, using `openclaw/jev-pr-judgments-foundation` as its GitHub base. That foundation itself depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152236.

The branch also contains the independent scheduler prerequisite https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152235. Its two scheduler files therefore appear in this PR's current comparison with foundation; they are not new consumer behavior. Reconcile the stack after prerequisites land so each fix is reviewed/merged once. This feature is not stacked on memory.

## Evidence

- Prior composed-tree verification: **235 focused tests passed**: 66 guidance/experience, 155 Gateway cron, and 14 cron payload tests.
- Tests cover registered-provider entrypoints, no-change without a reviewer, focused authorship, fallback, exact target identity, evidence linkage, whole-batch validation, catalog changes, cancellation, and deadline sharing.
- Fresh pre-publication source review found no production blocker. Fixed its documentation anchor finding and corrected the result-before-call fixture so that case actually exercises out-of-order evidence.
- Fresh corrected guidance suite: **29 tests pass**, including the repaired out-of-order linkage case; compiled-source verification passes.
- Fresh formatter and diff checks pass. Regular docs link audit: 13,886 links checked, zero broken links. Full anchor audit does not pass: it reports fragments in untouched documentation, with no failures in either changed documentation page. This is not claimed as a green full docs audit.

## Remaining Before Ready for Review

Composed Workshop type/lint/full-build checks, current-main integration, CI, and live tuned end-to-end quality validation remain outstanding. Existing focused tests use synthetic provider responses and prove routing, not Jev model quality. Historical frozen-benchmark results do not measure this tuned branch; no accuracy, latency, or cost improvement is claimed.
