prs.title: fix(auth): keep OAuth refresh fence timeout monotonic across clock skew
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An OAuth token refresh could hang past its configured timeout or trip a spurious timeout on a healthy refresh when the system clock jumped (NTP correction, container clock drift, sleep resume). The fence now reads its deadline from the monotonic clock so wall-clock skew cannot warp the remaining budget.

- Problem: `observeOAuthRefreshSettlementBeforeDeadline` seeded its deadline with `Date.now()` and fed `deadline - Date.now()` to `setTimeout`. `setTimeout` is a libuv monotonic timer, so this crossed clock domains: a wall-clock rewind inflated the remaining budget (fence hung past timeout), and a forward jump shrank it to zero (healthy refresh misjudged as timed out).
- Solution: seed the deadline from `performance.now()` and read the remaining budget from the same monotonic clock, flooring before handing to `setTimeout`/`sleepWithAbort`.
- What changed: `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-fence.ts` — 5 `Date.now()` → `performance.now()`; two timer delays now `Math.floor`-ed (matches #155323). Tests updated for fake-timer compatibility.
- What did NOT change: refresh logic, retry strategy, error semantics, and the fence ownership/settlement contract. Only the clock source for the deadline moved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix lands at the canonical owner of the OAuth refresh fence timeout — `observeOAuthRefreshSettlementBeforeDeadline` and its two callers (`observeOAuthRefreshSettlement`, `observeOAuthRefreshFenceSettlement`). Every OAuth provider's token refresh flows through this single fence. Mirrors the already-merged canonical wall-clock fixes (#155323, #155603, #156979) which established `Date.now()` → `performance.now()` + `Math.floor` as the project's monotonic-deadline pattern.

## User Impact

OAuth-authenticated providers (OpenAI, GitHub, Google, etc.) now respect the configured refresh timeout reliably even when the host clock is adjusted mid-refresh. No more intermittent "exceeded hard timeout" failures on healthy refreshes after NTP sync, nor refresh fences that hang beyond their configured budget after a clock rewind.

## Evidence

### Clock-skew proof matrix (both entry points × both skew directions)

Exercises **both** code paths that received the `performance.now()` fix — the polling loop (`observeOAuthRefreshFenceSettlement`, `oauth-manager.ts:657`) and the setTimeout+finally guard (`observeOAuthRefreshSettlement`, `oauth-manager.ts:983`) — under **both** rewind (−5s) and forward-jump (+5s) wall-clock skew:

```console
$ # PRE-FIX (origin/main)
[1A: poll loop + rewind (-5s)]        total: 5201ms  ❌ BUG — 200ms budget inflated to 5201ms (26x)
[1B: poll loop + forward (+5s)]       total: 26ms     ❌ BUG — premature timeout at 26ms (13% of budget)
[2A: setTimeout + forward skew]       total: 101ms    ❌ BUG — false timeout on healthy refresh (finally guard fired)
[2B: setTimeout baseline (no skew)]   total: 150ms    ✅ correct (baseline control)

$ # POST-FIX (this PR)
[1A: poll loop + rewind (-5s)]        total: 201ms    ✅ timed out on schedule despite rewind
[1B: poll loop + forward (+5s)]       total: 200ms    ✅ timed out on schedule despite forward jump
[2A: setTimeout + forward skew]       total: 101ms    ✅ healthy settlement accepted under forward skew
[2B: setTimeout baseline (no skew)]   total: 151ms    ✅ correct (baseline control)
```

Cell 2A reveals a second defect path: the `settlement.finally` guard (`Date.now() >= deadline`) fires a **false timeout** when the wall clock jumps forward while a healthy refresh is settling — the monotonic fix eliminates this too.

### Production store reader path with wall-clock rewind (real SQLite)

Exercises the production store reader (`loadStoredOAuthRefreshStore`, same as `oauth-manager.ts:657`) against a pending fence persisted in a real SQLite auth-profile store, rewinding `Date.now` 5,000 ms mid-observation:

```console
$ # PRE-FIX: poll iterations: 180 | total: 5203 ms | 200ms budget stretched to 5203ms (BUG)
$ # POST-FIX: poll iterations: 8 | total: 202 ms | timed out at ~202ms despite 5000ms rewind (fixed)
```

### Pre-fix RED → post-fix GREEN (behavioral regression test)

```console
$ # PRE-FIX: × times out on schedule when the wall clock rewinds mid-poll — 1 failed | 10 passed (11)
$ # POST-FIX: ✓ 11 passed (11) — oauth-refresh-fence.async.test.ts
$ # POST-FIX: ✓ 22 passed (22) — oauth-refresh-fence.test.ts
```

### Real Gateway E2E under injected forward clock skew

Full CLI/Gateway OAuth refresh — a real WS client drives a real agent run with an
expired OAuth credential; a controlled provider refreshOAuth settles healthily in
~8s (well under the 120s budget); the wall clock jumps +119s mid-wait:

```console
$ # PRE-FIX (origin/main)  healthy 8s refresh → observer MIS-REPORTED TIMEOUT (120000ms)  ❌
$ # POST-FIX (this PR)     healthy 8s refresh → observer ACCEPTED the settlement           ✅
```

### What was not tested

- Real NTP-triggered clock skew at the OS level (requires system clock manipulation). The monotonic-clock contract guarantees immunity to wall-clock jumps.
- Real provider credentials were not used; the end-to-end Gateway refresh above drives the same `refreshOAuthCredential` observer path with a controlled adapter.

prs.title: fix(agents): stop model-catalog worker from discarding incrementally-loaded plugins on scope growth
prs.body:
## Closes/Related

Closes #162230

Related:
- #161379 — Gateway prepared-model-catalog refresh CPU loop reports.
- #166115 — plugin source capture re-materialization / stale captures (closed, but relevant historical context).
- #156571 — model-catalog worker capture leak / disk pressure.
- #157989 — plugin source capture rewrite volume / SSD wear.

## What Problem This Solves

The model-catalog worker could lose the benefit of already-loaded plugin generations when catalog scope grew from a narrow request to a broader one. That made later catalog refreshes pay repeated plugin registration/source-capture costs and complicated ownership handoff for retained plugin instances.

This PR frames the issue as incremental lifecycle correctness and efficiency. Kiralee's 2026-10-03 A/B benchmark found that the original endless loop no longer reproduces on current `main` / 2026.9.8 because of independent fixes, but this branch still improves current `main` by reducing repeated plugin-build work and tightening registry lifetime behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scope growth is a normal catalog path: a worker may first prepare a narrow auth/catalog request and later need a superset of providers. Exact-match reuse alone is not enough for that path. The worker must carry the previous prepared generation into the real loader so unchanged plugin records can be retained, while new providers are added without re-registering everything already owned by the prior generation.

The same path also needs clean handoff semantics: registration resources and instance ownership must move forward or roll back together so predecessor cleanup cannot dispose a retained successor instance, and failed successor builds do not strand ownership.

## User Impact

- Less repeated plugin-build/source-capture work during catalog refreshes.
- Lower steady-state Gateway overhead when model-catalog scope expands.
- Safer plugin lifecycle behavior during prepared model runtime generation handoff.
- No intended user-facing behavior or configuration changes.

Kiralee's benchmark against current `main` showed the improvement is incremental rather than an active production-down emergency:
- ~40% fewer plugin-build captures.
- ~45% less capture disk usage.
- ~29% less Gateway CPU time.
- ~22% lower RSS.
- No GC spike.

## Solution

- Keep the model-catalog worker's previous prepared generation available on fingerprint misses and pass its registry through as `previousRegistry` for incremental loader reuse.
- Rebuild fingerprint-miss worker generations from the current request's `pluginMetadataSnapshot`; the predecessor registry remains only the registry reuse/retention candidate.
- Continue routing model-catalog requests through the real loader so the loader's signature-matched retention path, ownership-transfer path, and cleanup machinery run instead of bypassing them with an outer exact-match shortcut.
- Preserve clone-capable plugin source copying without statically importing optional `@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced` exports. When `copyRootFileSync` / `createRootFileCopyBatchSync` are available, the source path still uses `clone: "auto"` and source identity checks. When those exports are unavailable, capture falls back to an admitted descriptor path using `COPYFILE_FICLONE` where supported, then to descriptor-to-descriptor copying with the same source-identity guard.
- Handle the Windows/runtime case where `@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced.copyRootFileSync` is absent rather than callable. The descriptor-guarded fallback is now used before attempting to call the optional helper, avoiding `TypeError: (options.copyFile ?? getCopyRootFileSync(...)) is not a function` during plugin source capture.
- Match runtime discovery candidates back to manifest-registry winners by canonical source path, with Windows case-insensitive fallback, so a persisted/transferred manifest snapshot whose source spelling differs from fresh discovery does not silently drop the candidate before module evaluation.
- Scope internally prepared runtime plugin metadata around the real registry load, not only caller-supplied metadata snapshots. This keeps the metadata snapshot's cache/native-admission state active while the runtime loader materializes/evaluates plugin modules.
- Make the real-pool reuse integration observe module evaluation with a process-local `globalThis` counter keyed by `Symbol.for(...)` instead of file appends. This removes filesystem append/read behavior from a test whose intent is module-body evaluation and incremental reuse. The A+B/A+B+C path remains implicit-metadata coverage after the copy fallback fix.
- Include `src/plugins/registry-inspection-resource-map.ts` in the wrapper inventory.
- Move catalog worker request/input/result type contracts to a leaf contract module to break a madge-detected catalog-worker fingerprint cycle.
- Break the runtime import cycle around `plugin-instance-scope`, `registry-inspection-resources`, and `registry-registration-resources` with a small inspection transfer-target map; instance ownership can now transfer registration custody without importing the inspection disposal implementation.
- Add provider-catalog callback lifetime coverage for successful handoff, failed-build recovery, stale callback rejection before the registered callback performs I/O, and source-spelling drift between metadata snapshots and runtime discovery.

## Evidence

Validation at final head `371ecc103d60e2237e7af9cfafcf05dc8603d8d5`:
- Windows targeted serial validation from `C:\dev\openclaw-freshstart`:
  - `npx vitest run src/agents/runtime-plugins.test.ts` — PASS, 1 file / 27 tests.
  - `npx vitest run src/agents/runtime-plugins.real-pool.test.ts` — PASS, 1 file / 1 test.
  - `npx vitest run src/agents/runtime-plugins.real-pool.integration.test.ts` — PASS, 1 file / 2 tests.
  - `npx vitest run src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.worker.base-plugin-ids.test.ts` — PASS, 1 file / 2 tests.
  - `npx vitest run src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.plugin-generation-reset.test.ts` — PASS, 1 file / 3 tests.
  - `npx vitest run src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.plugin-lifetime.generation-handoff.test.ts` — PASS, 1 file / 9 tests.
  - `npx vitest run src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.plugin-lifetime.registration-resource-transfer.test.ts` — PASS, 1 file / 2 tests.
  - `npx vitest run src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.plugin-lifetime.transactional-rollback.test.ts` — PASS, 1 file / 3 tests.
  - `npx vitest run src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-preflight-transfer.test.ts` — PASS, 1 file / 2 tests.
  - `npx vitest run src/plugins/registry-registration-resources.test.ts` — PASS, 1 file / 3 tests.
  - `npx vitest run src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.reuse.integration.test.ts` — PASS, 1 file / 1 test.
- Windows line/max checks from `C:\dev\openclaw-freshstart`:
  - `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mts --base upstream/main` — PASS, `Line-cap ratchet OK: 36 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.`
  - `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-max-lines-ratchet.mts --base upstream/main` — PASS, `max-lines ratchet OK: 589 grandfathered suppressions.` and `OPENCLAW_* count 455/455`.

The final Windows run covers the previously failing real-pool module-evaluation path, model-catalog base plugin ids, prepared-model generation reset, plugin lifetime handoff/rollback/resource-transfer, reload preflight transfer, registration-resource disposal, and worker reuse/auth/materialization integration after merging current `origin/main`.

Earlier validation on this PR is retained only as historical context:
- Focused plugin source / worker reuse validation at `9452ef520015959dbdec6ba5eb87241f0ddd2e3c` passed locally.
- Full targeted local Vitest at `9452ef520015959dbdec6ba5eb87241f0ddd2e3c` passed for the then-current targeted list.
- Import-cycle checks at that earlier point passed.

## Known Remaining Gaps

- Released-install upgrade evidence has not been produced in this PR update.

prs.title: fix(agents): WebChat reaction failures suggest external-channel setup
prs.body:
Related: #170050

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: WebChat runs without a current-prompt reaction grant enter external-channel selection and return channel-setup guidance instead of explaining that the current prompt cannot receive a reaction.

## User Impact

Prompt-targeted reaction attempts now fail locally with the actual limitation. This is a guidance-only fix: both baseline and candidate reject the no-grant request. No reaction misdelivery or successful external-channel reaction was reproduced or is claimed.

Admitted WebChat reactions remain available. Explicit external reactions retain their routing path. A reaction with `target`/`messageId` but no explicit `channel` is treated as prompt-targeted on a session advertising prompt reactions, consistent with its tool definition and admitted-turn behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

#170050 intentionally keeps reaction definitions stable across admitted and background runs. The existing message-tool owner now rejects a prompt-targeted attempt without a grant before external-channel selection. Tool definitions, config, permissions, and schemas stay unchanged.

Thanks @Yigtwxx for reporting and fixing this. Sarah's #164848 tool-history documentation is an unrelated hunk in the same docs page and remains unchanged; no runtime overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

### Primary proof: built CLI, scripted model

The real shipped CLI ran in isolated Docker state with `tools.toolSearch: false`. A local OpenAI-compatible server called `message` with `{"action":"react","emoji":"👍"}` and captured the tool result from the next model request:

```sh
openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> agent --local --channel webchat \
  --session-key agent:main:reaction-proof \
  --message 'React to my prompt' --json
```

Baseline `72ccf6ff92931fff2d49473fe1571f39e8311ad2`:

```text
status: error
tool: message
error: Channel is required (no configured channels detected). Run openclaw channels add to configure one, or pass --channel <channel> after enabling a channel. Use openclaw channels list --all to see available channel ids.
```

Candidate `43b79c4d3e9ecc05874dd725c0e252f0f4708d0f`:

```text
status: error
tool: message
error: No prompt here permits reactions; pass channel, target, and messageId.
```

Neither request succeeded or delivered a reaction. The changed observable outcome is the error returned to the model.

### Supporting evidence: real model final replies

With fresh isolated state, the same WebChat no-grant prompt (`React to my prompt`) and real `gpt-5.4-mini`, built clean main `794ae696f11b7ee105180de2f4dbe369affc42b2` returned the external-channel setup error. The model retried with `channel:"webchat"`, received an unknown-channel error, and asked the `openclaw` tool to configure/connect a channel. Its final reply was:

> [blocked] I couldn’t post the reaction because this session has no configured webchat channel, and `webchat` isn’t a valid channel id here. The available channels are other platforms like Slack, Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, Matrix, etc., but I can’t self-connect them from this turn.

The candidate returned the local no-prompt error. Its final reply was:

> [blocked] I can react, but this chat surface doesn’t expose the target message for a reaction, and the fallback question prompt needs gateway auth I don’t have here.
>
> If you want, send the exact message to react to, or re-run this from a surface that allows message reactions.

These replies illustrate how the guidance can affect the user-facing answer; they are not proof of routing or delivery. The candidate's separate `ask_user` fallback lacked Gateway authentication in this local-only fixture, as the quoted reply records.

### Controls and checks

- A real Gateway protocol-v4 signed WebChat connection uses `chat.send`; candidate returns `ok:true`, `channel:"webchat"`, `changed:true`, one reaction from `agent:main`, referring to the admitted user prompt. `chat.history` retains the successful tool result.
- Explicit `channel:"discord"`, `target`, and `messageId` still enter the external Gateway path on both versions. This control returns the same connection-refused class in an intentionally Gateway-less CLI fixture; it does not prove successful Discord delivery. Focused coverage also checks that explicit external reactions dispatch normally.
- Current-prompt reaction suite: **18 passed**. Wrapper import/extraction suites: **20 passed** on clean current main and candidate. Earlier compact-small-1/-8 inventory failures are resolved by upstream [c9907c3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c9907c3dcce), which adds the exact five missing files. No wrapper repair is included in this PR.
- Scoped Oxfmt and Oxlint pass. Simplification removes a duplicate normalization case and incidental argument-copy assertions while retaining the distinct no-grant and external-dispatch boundaries. Delta against merge base: production **+8/-7**, tests **+45/-3**, docs **+5/-0**. Production growth is one local-denial branch in the existing owner.

Merge danger: **two-way door**; a revert restores the previous selection/error path, with no state or config migration. Blast radius: error guidance for `message(action=react)` in sessions advertising prompt reactions; admitted reactions and explicitly routed external reactions retain their existing paths.

prs.title: fix(codex): restore bound chats after gateway restart
prs.body:
Closes #126923

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex-backed channel conversations that stop replying after a Gateway/app-server restart when the public conversation attachment survives but its private native thread binding is absent or points to a vanished thread.

The initial native binding preparation ran outside the missing-thread recovery boundary. In addition, current Codex app-server reports a vanished durable thread as exact `thread not loaded` or `no rollout found` RPC errors, which the old recovery classifier did not recognize.

## User Impact

Existing Codex-bound chats recover automatically on the next authorized message after restart. Separate Telegram topics keep independent native bindings. When Codex definitively proves that the recorded thread is gone, OpenClaw creates one fresh replacement without requiring `/codex bind` or database edits. `/new` retires the OpenClaw session generation without detaching explicit conversation bindings.

Missing native history cannot be reconstructed. Connectivity failures, overload, unsafe subscription state, and ambiguous resume failures do not authorize replacement.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Include initial restore/reattach preparation in the existing one-shot missing-thread recovery boundary.
- Match only structured app-server `-32600` failures for the expected thread and RPC method (`thread/read`, `thread/resume`, or `turn/start`), while retaining the existing exact legacy `thread not found` fallback.
- Continue using the binding repository/runtime APIs for restoration, replacement, and session retirement; no manual state mutation is needed.
- Document restart, topic scoping, and `/new` behavior.

## Evidence

- New restart regression matrix failed 5/5 on the pre-fix implementation and passes 5/5 after the fix.
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/codex/src/conversation-binding.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-retirement.conversation-binding.test.ts --project extension-codex -t 'recovers independent Telegram topics after restart|keeps explicit Telegram topic bindings independent across /new and restart' --reporter=dot` — 6 passed, 97 skipped.
- New tests cover two independent Telegram topics, absent and stale native bindings, reattach, exact missing-thread replacement, replacement reuse, and `/new`/restart persistence.
- New test bodies complete below 1 second each (slowest observed: 523 ms).
- Changed TypeScript files pass targeted Oxlint; all changed files pass Oxfmt and `git diff --check`.
- One completed Codex extension batch passed 407/407 tests before the full 430-file lane was interrupted; focused tests were rerun successfully after rebasing onto current `main`.
- Verified exact missing-thread responses against current `openai/codex` app-server source (`thread/read`: `thread not loaded`; `thread/resume`: `no rollout found`; `turn/start`: `thread not found`).
- No live state/database edits and no deployment were performed.

Independent autoreview was attempted with the repository workflow. The isolated Codex reviewer could not authenticate (401), and the allowed Claude fallback was unavailable due account credits; neither engine produced a code finding or verdict.

## What Problem This Solves

The Usage session card rebuilds its row projections whenever selection, sort controls, totals, or callbacks change. This removes the broad rendering snapshot left by the Solid migration.

## User Impact

prs.title: fix(sessions): portable transcript reader SQL for PostgreSQL
prs.body:
Related: #171466, #171484

## What Problem This Solves

Transcript history, model context, mirror lookup, and retained suffix-copy queries contain SQLite-specific JSON and boolean expressions that PostgreSQL cannot prepare.

## User Impact

These transcript reader queries and retained reparent copies now execute on PostgreSQL 16+ while preserving SQLite statement text and bindings, apart from the intentional integer/boolean corrections described below. PostgreSQL JSON projections may normalize whitespace and key order. There is no schema, configuration, retention, or release change; FTS remains out of scope.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared engine helpers own JSON path reads, validation, updates, removal, object projection, and array expansion. The existing transcript owners pass their connection through these helpers, including their internal callers. PostgreSQL history queries omit SQLite's index hint, and mirror UNION queries order by the output column. Checkpoint flags remain integers on both engines, without boolean bindings.

Retained reparent copies stay inside SQL. PostgreSQL writes the rewritten JSON and computes its exact UTF-8 length with `octet_length` in the same INSERT SELECT, matching the writer's `Buffer.byteLength(eventJson, "utf8")` rule. SQLite keeps its original copy SQL.

## Evidence

### Accepted PostgreSQL byte-sizing delta

`jsonb::text` includes formatting spaces (for example, `{"a": 1}`) where SQLite emits compact JSON. PostgreSQL-computed `modelBytes`, `modelWithoutCheckpointBytes`, `withoutCustomDataBytes`, and retained-data byte budgets therefore slightly overestimate the equivalent SQLite projection. This is accepted: PostgreSQL context budgeting is conservative, not incorrect. Stored reparent-copy accounting remains exact for the PostgreSQL text actually written.

### Committed conformance coverage

`src/infra/database-engine/transcript-reader.conformance.test.ts` seeds the same fixture corpus into SQLite and a real PostgreSQL conformance schema. It compares model navigation, all four checkpoint/omission model views, reset projection (including malformed and non-object passthrough), retained-data projection, and actual retained reparent copies with exact PostgreSQL byte accounting. The existing conformance runner's `src/infra/database-engine` target and the CI manifest's matching path pattern include it without workflow changes.

The committed test is 199 lines. Local PostgreSQL 17 conformance passed: 1 file / 1 test, 328 ms test time (70.60 s runner total, including canonical-schema preflight and source verification). The disposable cluster was stopped and removed. Command:

```sh
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:56439/postgres -- src/infra/database-engine/transcript-reader.conformance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

New-test lint and format checks pass; the `core-test-infra` type graph passes. One isolated Codex autoreview of this follow-up delta completed with no actionable findings.

Original reader implementation frozen-source run: 17 owner/gateway/tooling test files, 182 tests, all passed with `--maxWorkers=1` (176.44 seconds). This includes the gateway model-context/history flow, retained opaque-data reparent/rollback, PR wrapper inventory, and the eager-import closure test. The prior run was rejected by the compiled-source freshness guard after a source edit; the final run completed with source verification intact. Changed test files: JSON helpers 3 tests (0.675 seconds including startup) and transcript payload owner 10 tests (1.66-second dedicated run); CI timings remain pending.

Formatting, touched-file lint, Kysely guardrails, core typechecking, and the infra/session test type graphs pass. Against `origin/main`: database-worker calls remain 224/224; assertion-safety and max-lines pass; SQLite dialect design occurrences shrink 88 → 66 (mechanical 10 → 10). Independent Codex review is clean after narrowing the new JSON setter's type contract to its supported text/JSON-producing inputs.

PostgreSQL 17.11 (Homebrew), disposable local cluster, no Docker.

| Owner / variant | PREPARE |
| --- | --- |
| metadata | 2/2 pass |
| read-reset | 1/1 pass |
| read-match | 1/1 pass |
| mirror-idempotency | 2/2 pass |
| mirror-run | 2/2 pass |

| model-entry-false-true | 4/4 pass |

SQLite complete statements: 41 captured instances (37 scoped PostgreSQL PREPARE instances plus 4 additional history-by-ID/history-boundary variants). 32/41 have identical SQL and all 41 have identical parameter arrays. The nine changed captured instances contain only history CASE TRUE/FALSE (five instances) and model-context size/payload statements with omitCheckpoint=true (four instances) (2 paths × 2 tool-result-omission variants); the flag becomes CASE WHEN seq IN (...) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END.

Additional AST source call captures: 64/64 byte-identical compiled SQLite expressions and parameter arrays, covering 19 production files including the mechanical helper-argument propagation.

Model projection: 8/8 JSON.parse-equal outputs (assistant/toolResult × omitCheckpoint on/off × omission notice on/off); PostgreSQL model sizing also equals output UTF-8 byte length.

Retained reparent: 2/2 JSON.parse-equal copies for parent=null and parent="repaired-parent". Stored event_utf8_bytes = PostgreSQL octet_length(event_json) = Buffer.byteLength(event_json, "utf8"): 155 and 168 respectively.

The disposable cluster was stopped and removed after verification.

Navigation regression: 25/25 matched values/raw preservation across model/reset views for user, assistant tool calls, missing call keys, >8 content elements, synthetic/legacy missing result, empty message, system prompt/update, reset, compaction, null/scalar/array, and malformed reset input.

## CI follow-up

The original reviewed head passed PostgreSQL conformance in [run 38499010150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38499010150/job/115641706317); its job log confirms that `src/infra/database-engine/transcript-reader.conformance.test.ts` executed and passed (174 ms). The only failing job was the type-suppression inventory, which omitted the new test's documented PostgreSQL bridge annotation. One follow-up commit adds that exact inventory entry without changing runtime behavior. The affected inventory file passes all 4 tests, targeted lint, formatting, and independent review. Current-head [CI run 38501839785](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501839785) passed, including PostgreSQL conformance; its job log confirms that the transcript-reader conformance test executed and passed (153 ms).

prs.title: feat(android): keep chat calls visible while sharing photos
prs.body:
Related: #151078, #150178

## What Problem This Solves

Android users need a dedicated conversation page without changing their active call or original chat. The previous inline card did not provide that view, and the first full-page layout left the avatar oversized, Details in the middle, technical diagnostics on the main screen, and speech captions and controls poorly grouped.

This also fixes valid locally admitted photos displaying “Unsupported attachment” and needing to leave the conversation page just to send them. The mascot no longer loses its mouth when idle or thinking. Native Talk also stops inserting fixed Talk/ElevenLabs instructions into the user's visible chat message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing Android shell, red mascot, Talk, camera, attachment renderer, composer/outbox and foreground-service owners. Conversation activity is a bounded, read-only projection of the captured conversation—not another speech-result or chat-history writer. Call **End** remains separate from agent-task **Stop**.

The cleanup consolidates duplicate completion/reset logic and question metadata, removes unused state and delegation wrappers, and repairs demonstrated ordering and ownership defects at their existing owners. No new transport lifecycle, audio/avatar engine, decoder or second assistant.

## User Impact

- Native Talk and push-to-talk now send only the recognized utterance. Existing history is not rewritten. Reply style follows the active agent's instructions instead of a per-turn concise-tone override; configured speech synthesis and optional response voice directives remain.
- A fixed header places **Go to chat** on the left, the captured agent identity once in the center, and **Details** at the top right. Technical activity diagnostics are inside Details; genuine connection/microphone failures remain visible.
- The existing red avatar is smaller and balanced in available space: preferred cap **216 dp instead of 264 dp**, shrinking on short screens. Its mouth follows actual playback and remains visible as a closed mouth during pauses/thinking; reduced-motion behavior is retained.
- A restrained, theme-aware caption surface shows up to **four lines** of the latest real user/assistant utterance, with a small left-aligned role label. No empty caption box or second chat. Captions stay with their captured call, including when speaker audio is muted.
- One concise status reflects real listening, speaking, thinking, reading, writing/editing, searching, tools, approval/input waits or errors. Lost activity coverage is recorded and recovered from existing authoritative metadata, rather than silently treated as idle.
- Camera choice, photo previews and explicit **Send photos** are grouped above persistent **Audio / Photo / End** controls. Existing safe-area handling and bounded scrolling keep actions accessible on short screens and at large font sizes.
- Front/rear still capture uses the existing camera owner and original bytes. Only the displayed photo snapshot is sent through the original conversation’s canonical outbox; hidden drafts, other files and newer/replaced attachments remain untouched. Capture never sends automatically.
- Talk reopens the existing call. Go to chat, Return to conversation and Android Back change the view without restarting or ending it. Final speech roles remain in canonical chat history without mirroring, duplicate turns or automatic speech from observed finals.
- Foreground-admitted chat-call continuity is retained across navigation/background transitions; actual connection, permission or ownership loss retires the affected call. Reconnecting does not silently start another call.

No Gateway/protocol, provider implementation/configuration, authentication, global-default, permission-policy, dependency, SDK, schema, release or phone-installation changes. **No continuous camera/video streaming:** the original live-vision objective remains outside this still-photo scope.

## Evidence

**Current head:** [`3f6ba0f03963dd8c6d30e2ef530f206eb1128a27`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3f6ba0f03963dd8c6d30e2ef530f206eb1128a27), parent `83167ee2003775f150b492e3a7ae050c61c4a25c`. Exact final tree: `f51b683ebed2298fa3cb474c0c2934bbaef733ae`. Normal hooks and a fast-forward push preserve existing history; no force push or PR merge.

- **Native-input regression:** five cases failed on the old producer's exact prefixed wire message. Coverage spans the production Shell/normal-chat history, generic native Talk, captured calls, PTT and before/after-ACK completion orders, including multiline and instruction-like speech. The fixed path sends the utterance directly; there is no display filter, second writer or hidden instruction field.
- **Final-tree validation:** **771 tests across 22 suites passed with zero failures, errors or skips on the exact final tree**, retaining all 771 prior test IDs. Play/ThirdParty debug APK builds and Play, ThirdParty and Wear-shared Android lint completed without lint errors. **Kotlin formatting is still red:** `:app:ktlintTestSourceSetCheck` reports 37 formatting diagnostics in `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/node/CameraCaptureOwnershipTest.kt` (unchanged by this follow-up). The quality command exited 1; the aggregate ktlint gates are not claimed passed. The six production-camera formatting errors are corrected. [Runner provenance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35444877121); proof manifest SHA-256 `ad220ae2e575b292ab84b8a7a622054d8a799c672bf9b8d4a372383b60ab64e8`. Command/JUnit receipts establish these outcomes, not the enclosing workflow conclusion after lease cleanup.
- **Fresh independent follow-up review:** P0–P2, normal local mode over the complete staged fourteen-path follow-up against the published parent; scoped-clean, exit 0. Report SHA-256: `f50c71a70e4853967363c5f52cdb563bd6caa3b8e8ade4bbfab3b6cce65ea977`. This is not a zero-finding review of the older complete PR; that qualified review is retained below. The interrupted whole-PR attempt produced no final report and is not counted as approval.
- **Complete-PR cleanup:** all 41 source-owned PR paths were audited separately from the ordinary review. Removed unused ViewModel forwarding APIs, the duplicate request-only draft snapshot, an unrendered speech-mouth calculation, an unused effect restart key, and duplicate attachment-width plumbing. Shared gap-test setup keeps both original named cases. Call/generation/lease/cancellation, CameraX, question/sequence, draft recovery and snapshot-sensitive attachment protections remain. No tests were deleted.
- **Follow-up LOC:** production +21/−48 (**net −27**, including formatter-only camera layout); tests +62/−44; docs +6. The functional cleanup removes a net 33 production lines before the required camera formatting correction. No generated localization output, dependency, schema or protocol changes.
- **Hosted PR CI:** The exact-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35446568616) was **skipped**. No hosted product-suite success is claimed. Local/Testbox results are not substituted for this head's hosted status. The PR remains a draft for normal review and physical-device acceptance.

### Native Talk input — before and after

Actual production Android Shell/ChatController/normal-message rendering, driven by synthetic SpeechRecognizer input through the real Talk finalizer and socket payload. The mock Gateway records that exact submitted text in history; the UI is not manually seeded. Same 945 × 2100 viewport, theme and input. - **Camera cancellation:** rejected. `CameraCaptureManager.withCapture` obtains the capture Job inside the scoped `withContext(Main)` child and catches cancellation outside that scope. </details>

### Mouth visibility — actual before and after

Retained production Android Shell/Canvas captures from the earlier `83167ee` integration, using the same synthetic conversation and active motion clock. prs.title: fix(gateway): prepare current sharing facts after history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A public shared-session read can return no content after a worker commits metadata while history is being read, because current sharing facts are not prepared after that await.

## User Impact

Still-authorized shared links retain their content after metadata publication, while revocation and session reset during post-history readiness release no content. This independent PR stays draft-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing exact-row readiness owner after history, then consume the current grant synchronously without weakening the final response authorization checks.

## Evidence

The historical normal-profile comparison failed exactly the three added cases on the original reader and passed all18 with the repair. Both source files match the donor exactly. Fresh pinned-main comparison passes its exact expected original/repair outcomes, sibling coverage and format; measured cost is below. Draft PR CI is deliberately skipped, not green full qualification.

## Summary

Prepare the current public-session sharing facts after awaited history, through the existing exact-row readiness owner, before synchronously consuming the grant and returning content. Keep the existing session/grant/store-generation and final HTTP response guards.

This is a **draft-only extraction** of the unrelated two-file Gateway repair formerly bundled in #135895. It is independent of Talk attachments; no Talk, configuration, dependency, SDK or test-pool changes are included. Current upstream has the original reader; both donor-parent file blobs exactly match base `390fcec17863174dda480f563f87927738b9ee24`. Scoped main history and open-PR checks found no equivalent repair.

## Regressions

Keep the three cases in the existing Gateway database-worker fork profile:

- A real worker metadata commit during history retains the grant and returns the new label/content.
- Revocation during the added readiness await returns no content.
- Session reset during that await returns no content.

## Evidence and limits

Head: `08b49cea773a27c322bb1389ebe7d83b95033219` (two files, byte-identical to donor `5e1b301753952216179b4d2a975e84f61acf5d49`). Fresh scoped source review found no P0–P2 issue; this is not test execution.

Historical [normal-profile comparison](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/37504459609) passed 15 existing tests on both readers: only the three new cases failed on original source; repaired passed 18/18. [Historical candidate qualification](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/37505135131) passed 20 complete-file samples, original ordered shards, public-reader siblings and types/format/lint. Whole-file single-worker sample: 83.042–95.732 seconds, median83.514, 1,682.443 process-wall seconds total across20 runs; four job wall durations sum4,424 seconds including setup, not CPU/billing time. The base has since advanced, so these receipts are historical, not a claim of current-head green CI.

### Fresh pinned-source comparison and cost

[Focused GitHub execution](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/37565755622) checked out draft head `08b49cea773a27c322bb1389ebe7d83b95033219`. The original-reader control restored only the production reader from pinned main `390fcec17863174dda480f563f87927738b9ee24`, retaining the identical regression file. Frozen install and canonical QA build passed on both jobs.

- Original reader: **15/18 passed; exactly the three added sharing regressions failed**, expected exit1; **101.49 seconds process wall**.
- Repaired reader: **18/18 passed**, zero failed/pending, exit0; `pnpm test src/gateway/session-row-projection.prepared-read.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **94.57 seconds process wall**.
- Public-reader siblings: **23/23 passed in three complete files**, zero failed/pending; **93.65 seconds process wall**. Focused format passed.
- Existing database-worker/fork profile was retained. Original/repaired CI jobs occupied **275/336 seconds wall** respectively, **611seconds combined including setup/build/controls/upload**; not CPU/billing time.
- [Receipt-only verification](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/37566351491) passed SHA-256 validation of every retained receipt, exact source heads/counts/assertion outcomes and unchanged repaired source. It did not rerun tests. The original focused workflow is globally red because the independent Talk job's final validator used stale totals; both Gateway jobs are green.

[Draft PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37565630812) is terminal **skipped** (all40jobs), not full qualification. This draft remains a preserved independently tested repair, not a ready-to-merge or release claim. The separate Talk PR's broader merge CI has an unresolved X-publication503 failure; these Gateway controls do not prove a remedy for that distinct composition failure. No live runtime, service, canary or credential changes. Leave this PR in draft; no merge or release requested.

prs.title: feat: browse active device-folder session files
prs.body:
Related: #169722

> Stacked on #169722; base branch: `feat/device-existing-folder-sessions`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI Files panel cannot browse or edit an existing-folder session even while its paired-device worker is active.

## User Impact

User impact: active existing-folder sessions can list, preview, and save files through the paired device; stopped sessions show a clear start-the-session error and never fall back to Gateway-local files.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Files RPCs now use the worker's existing workspace-inspection command only when the exact session, device-folder binding, active placement, owner epoch, attached environment, and paired device remain current before and after awaited work. Saves use the session lifecycle mutation lock shared with stop, archive, and session-identity rewrites. Device folders have no Gateway checkpoint or reconciliation owner, so the repository checkpoint mutation service intentionally does not apply.

Workspace reveal remains unavailable because there is no Gateway checkout. `sessions.diff` is unchanged and still returns an unavailable/empty result for device-folder sessions rather than inspecting the paired device.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.device-folder.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3 passed, 31.20s wall time.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.device-folder.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 44 passed, 1 existing platform skip, 42.73s wall time.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check docs/nodes/session-hosting.md src/gateway/server-methods/session-device-folder-workspace-access.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.device-folder.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/gateway/server-methods/session-device-folder-workspace-access.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.device-folder.test.ts` — 0 warnings/errors.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Isolated live proof through real authenticated `sessions.files.list/get/set` RPCs and the Control UI: active list/open/save passed; the device file changed, the same-named Gateway file stayed byte-identical, and reclaim restored the typed `device_folder_files_unavailable` error. Fresh synthetic Gateway/node state, system Chrome, port 18971, no provider call; all task processes stopped.

### Screenshots

Idle session (historical screenshot) — shows the explicit paired-device start requirement:

![Inactive device-folder Files panel error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b046cce-2eeb-4a6c-ac2f-3b80484038b6)

After — active session lists and opens `same.txt` from the paired-device folder:

![Active device-folder file opened in Files panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11099420-6bc4-4b8d-9373-539a7716a4f1)

Broad typecheck and test suites were not run locally; hosted CI owns those gates.


### Exact rebased-head proof (2026-10-13)

HEAD: `70d4566ba31e9f53afc3d69805389cf75d6ae7f1`, stacked on BASE `8fc04f9ceef2d23142f295c43bddd35f84ccbbc2`.

- Five focused Files suites passed: **70 tests passed, 1 existing skip**. Scoped formatting/lint and `git diff --check` passed.
- Isolated live proof used a foreground paired session-host node, fresh synthetic Gateway/node state, and the QA loopback mock provider. BASE showed the previous explicit refusal. On this exact head, the Files panel listed both synthetic files, opened `same.txt`, and saved `DEVICE saved through Control UI`.
- Shell verification after the UI save: paired-device file SHA-256 `4e8d3de8cea4be4e9e9d0844668c682f8d51c98fb77da3e9fafe629bd2e022ae`; same-named Gateway file remained `GATEWAY original` with SHA-256 `c562e941208308e7c478414ee9f7ed993acf2a3f9baaa49f8d541a48e127574b`. Proof processes stopped and ports 18971/18972 were free after collection.

Before on BASE — active existing-folder session still refuses Gateway Files access:

![BASE active existing-folder Files refusal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cea2b46-5424-4459-9151-4ce4097a8b67)

After on exact STACK head — paired-device folder listed in Files:

![Exact-head active device-folder file list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40a81e2c-a591-40db-b20c-1fcbf856fe2c)

After UI save — device-owned file contains the saved text:

![Exact-head device-folder file saved through the UI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f95c5d5b-8dc1-4234-bdbf-cd551e9c2b18)



### Remaining authority decision

ClawSweeper's exact-head review found no definite code defect, but blocks merge pending proof that an operator-device revocation while a remote save is already queued prevents the final device mutation. The current one-command node boundary rechecks requester/session authority before dispatch and after completion; the node can enforce transport/environment aborts during its atomic save, but it cannot independently revalidate a Gateway-side operator revocation at the final write. Guaranteeing that case requires an owner-approved authority contract across the Gateway/node boundary (for example a two-phase prepare/commit or equivalent protocol), which is outside this PR's approved schema/protocol scope. This PR remains draft.

prs.title: fix(plugins): preserve Windows Doctor dependencies between phases
prs.body:
Related: #169586

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Windows Doctor contract loading when source custody copies retain dependency junctions into a capture that is subsequently disposed.

## User Impact

Doctor can load the same captured dependency graph across maintenance phases, including dependency resource reads. Migration declarations, immutable action order and authority checks remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery copies now relocate absolute links whose targets belong to the capture being copied. Windows junctions store absolute targets even when their producer supplies a relative path. Relative links and external targets remain verbatim; native references still use their existing retention and validation path.

The regression extends the existing Doctor custody fixture with real filesystem junctions and a shared external dependency. It exercises seed disposal, retained-source forks, two independent callback instances and a dependency resource read. No filesystem mock or platform override is used. Production changes are limited to the recovery-copy owner; `linkDependency` is not weakened.

## Evidence

Windows 11 x64, build 26300; Node 26.10.0; pnpm 12.9.0. Native proof used main `1f5c14590afaaea66944ef6b36e76236b0618e6b` plus the exact two-file patch committed as `ef3bdd16125b3bb59e8470b95ff3896a961f4525`.

- Unpatched custody suite: 2 passed / 2 failed, including the new external-junction case (257.91 s wall time).
- A diagnostic baseline rerun retained the actual contract-load warning: `EEXIST` while creating the shared dependency alias. The caller then reported the immutable declaration/authority refusal. The new case passes after relocation.
- Required four-file native selection (261.96 s wall time):

| Test file | Result |
| --- | --- |
| doctor-contract-registry.custody.test.ts | 4/4 pass |
| doctor-contract-registry.capture.test.ts | 1/1 pass |
| plugin-generation-artifact.native-reference.test.ts | 8/8 pass |
| plugin-generation-artifact.test.ts | 28/29 pass |

The one artifact failure is inherited: `does not capture the discarded prefix of an absolute path.resolve asset` constructs an invalid Windows path with an embedded drive colon before product capture runs. The same failure was reproduced on the unpatched base; it is not masked or changed here.

The targeted `validates frozen live post-session actions without applying candidate-only refusal` case also passes on Windows (190.22 s wall time; 1 selected case, 10 filtered out). This verifies that unplanned actions remain refused and a matching plan remains accepted.

Independent Codex autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Current-head core, plugins-platform and commands-doctor typechecks pass, as do changed-file typed lint (0 warnings/errors), native schema, legacy-store, media-helper, sidecar-loader, import-cycle, webhook and pairing-auth guards.

### Full changed-check limitations

The full Linux `pnpm check:changed` run on parent `372e20ac` passed all 28 test type graphs and core typechecking, then failed its unused-export scan. The two core export findings are already removed by the PR's base commit #169616. Five UI findings remain: PanelToggleElement, ApprovalPage, CustodianPage, QuestionPage and SkillWorkshopViewProps. The same UI findings were independently reproduced on unmodified `1f5c1459` and with this patch. All remaining planned guard commands were subsequently run successfully on the current patch. A wholly green full `check:changed` invocation or hosted exact-head CI is not claimed.

The supporting Linux four-file run had 35 passes and 7 Unix-socket setup failures caused by the host's `listen EPERM` policy; a standalone Node socket probe confirms that restriction.

This proves the source defect and its synthetic Windows Doctor custody consequence. It does not establish the cause of the original installation's later LINE migration authority refusal. No production Gateway restart, real LINE migration or installed-runtime modification was performed.

AI-assisted: yes. Maintainer edits enabled.

---

## Additional installed Windows CLI evidence (2026-10-14)

This is a **redacted real installed-CLI before/after observation**, not a synthetic-only fixture. Environment: Windows 11 x64, Node.js 26.10.0, npm-installed OpenClaw **2026.10.5-beta.3**, matching official LINE plugin.

**Before the capture fix:** The installed `openclaw update repair` CLI exited `1`; Doctor reported `EEXIST` while loading LINE's `doctor-contract-api.js`, then refused `plugin-doctor-state` and skipped `plugin-doctor-post-session-state`.

**After applying this PR's source-capture relocation logic** to the installed compiled core module (with SHA-256-verified original retained for rollback; no changes to migration declarations, authority checks, SQLite records, or settings):

- The installed LINE Doctor contract loaded successfully (`exit 0`); the action inventory contained `line-pre-drain-spool-rows` and declaration validation reported `DECLARATION_OK true`.
- A new run of the **shipped CLI** `openclaw update repair --yes --no-restart --json --timeout 2400` completed `finalize:preflight`, `finalize:targetConfigValidation`, `finalize:configSnapshot`, and importantly **`finalize:doctor`**. No `EEXIST` or immutable LINE migration declaration refusal appeared through the Doctor phase.
- Six existing SQLite stores were backed up before repair, and each backup passed `PRAGMA quick_check = ok`. Existing profiles and settings were retained.

Sanitized excerpt (status fields only) from the installed CLI finalization log:

```text
[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:preflight","status":"completed"}
[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:targetConfigValidation","status":"completed"}
[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:configSnapshot","status":"completed"}
[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:doctor","status":"completed"}
[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:plugins","status":"in_progress"}
```

**Scope/limitations:** The real installed example is **beta.3, not latest stable**. This is an in-place post-update repair, **not** proof of a completed latest-stable upgrade. Doctor completion included separate pending plugin install-record convergence warnings; `finalize:plugins`, Gateway activation, and end-to-end LINE delivery were **not yet verified** when the excerpt was collected. This is not a claim of full service recovery or clean stable-upgrade proof. It supports the narrower Windows capture fix without claiming the remaining upgrade/service concerns are resolved.

No credentials, customer data, IP addresses, phone numbers, private endpoints, or profile files are included.

---

## Latest-stable Windows package-upgrade evidence (2026-10-14)

A real **Windows shipped-CLI upgrade from the latest stable release** was run in a separate npm prefix and pre-existing isolated profile. This is an actual package replacement and schema upgrade, not `update repair`, a unit-test invocation, or the beta.3 observation above. The target is an **unreleased PR merge candidate**, not a newly published stable release. Both package manifests say `2026.10.3`; an explicit local tarball was supplied, and the installed build identity and actual database schemas changed.

### Identity and execution

- Windows 11 x64, build 26300; Node `v26.10.0`; npm `11.19.1`; candidate built with pinned pnpm `12.9.0`.
- Published starting package: [v2026.10.3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.3), released 2026-10-13 13:49:25 UTC; installed build `2026.10.3-release-59cb44796b0f-2026-10-13T07-33-17.552Z`. Before upgrading, all **11,876** `package.json`, `openclaw.mjs`, and `dist/**` payload files matched the integrity-verified official npm tarball byte-for-byte (no missing or mismatched files).
- Fixed candidate: `f72e26c170731beb6ee914ed0bf216d4616f89a1`, with parents `9690a6d7fa9cdb0df6aaec32008a04b55e527499` and this PR's reviewed head `ef3bdd16125b3bb59e8470b95ff3896a961f4525`. Its diff against the first parent contains exactly the two PR files. The pinned merge snapshot is used here; this is not a claim about later main commits.
- The source archive was pinned to that commit; package.json and both changed source files were verified against the pinned GitHub tree. The native `ciArtifacts` build and canonical self-contained package/tarball integrity checks completed with exit `0`. A full release declaration build is not claimed.
- Candidate tarball SHA-256: `605a3eb329d8ce08e456af18b48a2b2ecab4ab4fd9a6220ed784025940a67626`.
- Upgrade started **02:14:50 UTC**; the original CLI exited **0 at 02:53:44 UTC**. There was one upgrade invocation; no subsequent repair/Doctor migration was needed for this evidence.

Redacted command, executed by the unmodified published stable CLI:

```powershell
node "<ISOLATED_ROOT>\prefix\node_modules\openclaw\openclaw.mjs" update --tag "<ISOLATED_ROOT>\candidate-artifact\openclaw-pr169672-f72e26c.tgz" --yes --no-restart --json
```

Selected fields from its actual JSON result, with paths omitted:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "mode": "npm",
  "before": {
    "version": "2026.10.3",
    "buildId": "2026.10.3-release-59cb44796b0f-2026-10-13T07-33-17.552Z"
  },
  "after": {
    "version": "2026.10.3",
    "buildId": "2026.10.3-f72e26c17073-2026-10-14T01-33-43.950Z"
  },
  "steps": [
    {"name": "package-install", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "candidate-doctor", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "candidate-config", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "candidate-plugins", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "candidate-recovery", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "candidate-gateway-startup", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "package-swap", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "openclaw doctor", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "update-driver-handoff", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "post-plugin doctor", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "finalize:plugins:0", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "finalize:plugins:1", "exitCode": 0},
    {"name": "post-plugin-doctor-lint", "exitCode": 0}
  ]
}
```

The durable native run `2fb3c9ae-88a5-46d3-adae-da54ee1c0ccf` ended with `phase=finished`, `status=succeeded`, `reason=null`; post-update verification completed. The actual installed `dist/build-info.json` commit is the pinned candidate. This was not an `already-current`/skipped package update.

### Actual cross-phase dependency loading

The enabled, operator-managed proof plugin has two declared migrations, before and after session repair. Its real Windows junction layout is:

| Junction | Target under the isolated root |
| --- | --- |
| plugin/node_modules/consumer | dependencies/consumer |
| plugin/node_modules/shared | dependencies/shared |
| dependencies/consumer/node_modules/shared | dependencies/shared |

The contract imports `consumer`, which imports `shared` and reads `shared/resource.txt`. Each migration validates both values and records a SHA-256-derived private module URL identity and callback counter through the native Doctor migration API; no filesystem mocks, authority overrides, or hand-written migration-ledger records were used.

Both success markers were absent before the upgrade. At **02:30:58 UTC**, after candidate Doctor rehearsal completed, they were **still absent in the original isolated state**, whose shared schema was still `20`. The rehearsal used its disposable namespace and was cleaned up.

The installed candidate's actual post-plugin Doctor then created these records in `<ISOLATED_STATE>/pr169672-junction-pre.json` and `<ISOLATED_STATE>/pr169672-junction-post.json`:

```json
{"phase":"junction-pre","dependency":"first","resource":"first","instance":"cee1d629c7f50725","callbackCalls":1}
{"phase":"junction-post","dependency":"first","resource":"first","instance":"5bba48693d68a7cf","callbackCalls":1}
```

Their filesystem modification times were **02:44:25 UTC** and **02:46:20 UTC**, within the same upgrade. Matching `PR169672_PROOF` receipts appear in the actual CLI stderr (the boxed post-phase output wraps the JSON). The different identities and counters of one establish separate private callback instances with readable dependencies/resources across the two phases. No `EEXIST` occurred in either captured CLI stream.

The output retained a preflight readiness advisory for the proof plugin. A later **read-only** query of its canonical `migration_runs` row confirmed `status=completed`, `finished_at=1791945997821`, and **zero pending obligations** for that plugin. This was native post-session settlement, not a manual clear or an extra repair run.

### Existing settings and data preservation

The isolated profile was initialized by the published stable Doctor before the upgrade, with two agents and existing canonical transcript rows, authored settings, a workspace note, a disposable credential sentinel, and Unicode/embedded-NUL canary data in each database. **These are pre-existing synthetic test data, not copied production/customer data.**

Actual read-only database inspection after the upgrade:

| Database | Actual PRAGMA user_version | quick_check | Foreign-key violations | Existing data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shared state | 20 → 22 | ok | 0 | Canary row bytes unchanged |
| main agent | 24 → 26 | ok | 0 | 2 canonical transcript events and canary row bytes unchanged |
| second agent | 24 → 26 | ok | 0 | 2 canonical transcript events and canary row bytes unchanged |

The native transcript payload decoder was used to compare the four existing canonical event JSON UTF-8 payloads after migration, rather than comparing their storage encodings. Both retained user files have unchanged SHA-256 hashes.

Gateway mode/bind/port/auth settings, update setting, full Agent roster/default-owner/workspace settings, proof-plugin enabled/config/sentinel values, and plugin load paths were preserved. The pre-upgrade snapshot already used keyed `agents.entries`; the entire Agent config is deeply equal afterward. The only plugin selection/config delta is the documented native Codex route repair: exactly append `"codex"` to the original allowlist and add `entries.codex={"enabled":true}`; all original entries remain deeply equal. This is reported as an explicit migration delta, not config byte-for-byte equality.

The first extra verification harness exited `1` because it used Windows' default `cp950` decoder on a UTF-8 config. Its legacy roster assumption was also corrected against the recorded pre-upgrade snapshot. The UTF-8 read-only verifier and exact native-delta audit then passed; **the shipped upgrade itself exited 0 and was not rerun**.

### Scope and remaining advisories

This proves the latest-stable Windows package-upgrade path, actual Doctor cross-phase dependency/resource loading, schema advancement, and retention of the pre-existing isolated profile. It does **not** claim a later released version contains this fix, production-data migration, final Gateway activation, LINE delivery, exec, or MCP acceptance.

The upgrade is **not warning-free**: `postUpdate.plugins.status=warning`. The proof plugin is deliberately operator-managed through `plugins.load.paths`, so its source payload was not automatically updated. The disposable test auth token produced a plaintext-secret advisory; its value is omitted. Update budgets deferred local-audio, runtime-tool-schema, Skill Workshop policy, workspace-status, skills, WhatsApp-responsiveness and memory-search inspections; agent database path repair was skipped during update Doctor. Candidate lint also reported deferred inspection and a 498 ms disposal warning. The updater retained a private old runtime because exact process-command census was unavailable on Windows. These retained artifacts were not force-deleted or their guards bypassed.

`--no-restart` was intentional; native service management also refused the non-default home/state/config identity. All install/state/config/cache/workspace writes were under the isolated root. The separate production installation remained **2026.10.5-beta.3**, and its health/readiness endpoints both returned **200** after the test; those production checks are isolation observations, not candidate Gateway acceptance.

Only allowlisted status fields and synthetic proof values are included here. No credentials, IP addresses, phone numbers, non-public endpoints, customer transcripts, or raw profile/database files are published.

prs.title: feat(sessions): run sessions in existing folders on paired devices
prs.body:
Related: #136048 (non-Git directory semantics) and #142521 (non-Git worker workspace context; this PR does not implement ephemeral cloud workspaces).

## What Problem This Solves

Device-hosted sessions required a Git repository or managed worktree, a constraint inherited from ephemeral cloud sessions, even when a paired personal machine should simply work in an existing non-Git folder.

## User Impact

Users can choose **Existing folder on device** in New Session and run a session directly in an existing folder on a paired session-host device. OpenClaw does not create Git metadata, copy the folder to the Gateway, or sync, reconcile, reset, or delete it.

- `nodeHost.workerRuns.folders` is node-local consent: unset allows existing directories, a non-empty list restricts selection to those roots and their descendants, and `[]` disables the feature and its capability advertisement.
- The session stays pinned to that device: Auto/cloud dispatch, Move, and Continue on Gateway are refused. Attachment staging and the Gateway Files panel are unavailable for these sessions.
- Worker HOME stays in private node storage. Files are not locked against external changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `sessions.create` accepts `deviceFolder: { deviceId, path }` (requires `operator.write`); the binding is stored on the existing session entry and the `device-folder` workspace kind reuses the worker execution and lifecycle owners.
- The node owns folder policy and re-validates on every use: absolute or `~` paths only, realpath resolution (symlinks cannot escape a root), no filesystem root, no overlap with private worker storage, and a dev/ino fence between acquisition and execution. One shared rule in `node-workspace-protocol.ts` forbids preparing, resetting, transferring, seeding, or quiescing a device folder, for both ingress parsing and direct node execution.
- Gateway shutdown reads the teardown scope from the durable placement, so stopping an attachment with no in-memory tunnel no longer reaches closed worktree admission.
- A restored existing-folder create retry is owned by its frozen request; current device capacity or runtime no longer blocks it.
- Attachments are refused for device-folder sessions before anything is persisted: `chat.send` rejects them with a clear message, New Session blocks Send while attachments are attached, and worker media preparation never restages historical attachments into a device folder, so one refused file cannot make later turns fail.
- Security tradeoff: a session-host node already runs operator-directed agents with exec, so the allow-all default does not widen that boundary. The folder list is a selection guardrail, not an exec sandbox or a boundary against a compromised Gateway. Deployments that contain `operator.write` with `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` should also set a root list; the docs say so.
- Control UI selection/path input, plus docs for node configuration, session hosting, operator scopes, and workspace behavior.

## Screenshots

Synthetic mocked-Gateway captures (no real paths or tokens).

**Before — only the managed/new-workspace choice**

![Before: no existing-device-folder option](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9697664-c8ed-414f-95e3-e34f987051d8)

**After — desktop existing-folder input**

![After: existing folder on device, desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b721aeec-7e23-495a-b454-d85d97af8c79)

**After — mobile layout**

![After: existing folder on device, mobile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f2ff9fe-0c1f-4a85-9db7-9a1d9a5e534b)

## Evidence
- **Cross-machine E2E on the final feature code:** a disposable Gateway on one Mac (tailnet TLS, token auth, QA mock model) and a session-host node on a second Mac, both on the same exact head, with `folders` unset and an existing non-Git target folder on the second Mac. Pairing and capability advertisement; create + explicit dispatch (`active`, workspace = the device folder); hosted exec wrote `pwd` and `hostname` into the folder, confirmed by independent readback on that Mac; node restart and an unclean Gateway restart, then a second turn appended to the same file; `~` and a Gateway-only path rejected; reclaim + delete left the folder, sentinel, and absence of `.git` unchanged with no copy in Gateway state.
- **Isolated single-host E2E (25 checks, all pass):** missing/root/file/relative/private-storage rejections; auto-dispatch rejection; node restarts; clean Gateway shutdown with a live tunnel and with a durable attachment but no tunnel; Gateway restart and resume; symlink escape and outside-root rejection under a root list; `[]` disables the capability.
- **Attachment refusal, live:** on the isolated Gateway, a `chat.send` with a text attachment to a device-folder session returns the refusal, the attachment never enters history, and the next text turn and later turns after node and Gateway restarts complete in the folder.
- **Authority, live (real Gateway WebSocket, no mocks):** an operator client granted only `operator.read` + `operator.sessions.write` sends `sessions.create` with `deviceFolder` and gets `FORBIDDEN` / `missingScope: operator.write`; no session row exists afterwards and a debugger logpoint on the node records no workspace command for that request. The full `operator.write` client creates and dispatches the same folder (`active`).
- **Device revocation during awaited admission, live:** with the node process tree stopped (`SIGSTOP`) while `sessions.create` and `sessions.dispatch` wait on it, `devices remove` succeeds, then `SIGCONT`. Create fails with `Selected device changed during folder validation; retry` and leaves no row; dispatch fails with `Device worker installation connection is no longer current`; the node is then disconnected and its old token is rejected. Known bounded behavior: the read-only folder validation request already delivered to the stopped node still runs once on resume (1 ms after removal) before the close frame arrives; its result is discarded, nothing is persisted, and no session command runs. Unit coverage also revokes the caller (real `captureGatewayDeviceRevocation` capture) and the device during validation.
- **Requesting-operator revocation during awaited admission, live:** separate signed operator devices with `operator.write`, real paired node stopped with `SIGSTOP`. Removing the operator while `sessions.create` waits on folder validation: the client gets `gateway closed (4001): device removed`, `sessions.describe` returns `{"session":null}`, the key is absent from `sessions.list`, and the node trace has no worker execution command. Removing a different operator while `sessions.dispatch` waits: the session moves from `provisioning` to `{"state":"failed","terminalReason":"Gateway requester authority changed"}`, `hasActiveRun` is false, and no worker command runs. As with device revocation, one already-delivered read-only folder validation runs on resume and its result is discarded.
- **Inline initial turns are refused:** `sessions.create` with `deviceFolder` plus `message`, `task` or `attachments` is rejected before node I/O; the UI already sends the first message through `sessions.send` after dispatch. The three new cases fail with the validator removed (`3 failed | 12 passed`) and pass with it (`25 passed`).
- **Upgrade compatibility, live:** the `main` merge-base build created a plain session and an explicit-cwd session (turn `ok`); the PR build on the same state dir lists and describes both with their original IDs, a new turn on the old session completes `ok`, and Doctor exits 0 with no session-row load errors.
- **Upgrade from stable `v2026.10.3`, live:** the stable build created a plain session with a completed turn, an explicit-cwd session, a custom model alias and a non-default `thinkingDefault`. Direct startup on the new build exits 78 with "uses schema version 24; … run openclaw doctor --fix" on both this PR and the plain `main` merge base (inherited). After `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` (`v24 -> v26`), the PR Gateway starts, both old sessions list and describe with their original IDs, both settings read back unchanged, a new turn on the old session returns `ok`, and a new device-folder session created after the upgrade dispatches and runs a turn in the folder. One session-event publication warning about an unsettled worker-environment mutation appeared during that dispatch; the turn still succeeded.
- **Focused tests:** device-folder node, tunnel, create, protocol, media, submit-gate and draft-state suites pass; the restored-retry and history-restage regressions fail before their fixes.
- **Hosted CI:** on the exact head `364a000`, every job passes on the first attempt, and so does the Security Review, except `checks-ui-e2e (8/9)`. That job runs `plugins-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts`, which also fails the same way on plain `main` (see the maintainer override comment). Earlier heads hit flaky qa-lab E2E tests and `main`-side ratchet failures that plain `main` also reproduces.

## Merge Danger

Additive optional protocol field and session-entry JSON field; no SQL schema change. Older Gateways reject the new `sessions.create` parameter; older nodes do not advertise the capability, so the option is not offered. Revert removes the feature; existing device-folder sessions would then be unrecognized but their folders are untouched.

prs.title: feat: support host-provided acquisition for native web_fetch
prs.body:
Sponsored same-repository copy of #167751 to allow repository-owned validation on Carmen's implementation. This preserves Carmen commit authorship; the original cross-repository PR remains the source context.

Original PR: #167751 by @carmenberndt.
Related: #167328

## What Problem This Solves

Embedding hosts need to enforce their acquisition boundary before native `web_fetch` makes any outbound request, without replacing the tool or maintaining separate extraction logic.

## User Impact

Hosts can supply an optional invocation-bound transport through ordinary coding-tool assembly while retaining native extraction, truncation, output presentation, and untrusted-content wrapping. Standalone acquisition is unchanged without a transport; user disable settings and normal deny-policy filtering remain in place.

**Draft, not merge-ready:** this changes the public/security-sensitive `WebFetchTransport` / `webFetchTransport` authority boundary. Maintainer/API-owner signoff is required before merge, and ClawSweeper must be clean.

## Why This Change Was Made

Provider fallback occurs after direct HTTP, so it cannot enforce pre-request host admission. This adds a narrow `webFetchTransport` option to the existing native tool rather than a replacement or a general egress framework. Selecting it forbids direct HTTP and provider fallback on refusal, HTTP failure, and extraction failure. Trusted invocation context stays closure-bound, with authority checks around asynchronous processing and cleanup. Weakly held host cache scopes are separate from the standalone cache. The transport contract and responsibility split are documented.

## Evidence

Current head: `8b4daa874a72636a54f3a29fa19ff42d9ad6122c`.

- **Added current-head behavior proof:** `src/agents/openclaw-tools.web-fetch.test.ts` exercises `createOpenClawCodingToolsAsync` with native `web_fetch` assembly and concrete loopback HTTP host adapters. The proof covers allowed host dispatch, directly denied destinations, denied redirects before the redirected server sees traffic, revocation during awaited admission before dispatch, and invocation retirement blocking cached delivery, spill creation, and HTTP error-detail exposure.
- **Redacted final-effect proof output:**
  - `allowed_dispatch`: host HTTP hits `1`; denied HTTP hits `0`; result text contains redacted allowed host content.
  - `denied_destination`: denied HTTP hits `0`; result error `host policy refused destination`; no provider/direct fallback observed.
  - `denied_redirect`: allowed origin hits `1`; redirected denied origin hits `0`; result error `host policy refused redirect`.
  - `revoked_admission`: admission entered; invocation revoked before dispatch; host HTTP hits `0`; result error `invocation closed`.
  - `retired_cache_delivery`: seed host HTTP hits `1`; post-retirement cache read rejected with `invocation closed`; host HTTP hits remained `1`.
  - `retired_spill`: delayed real host body completed after retirement; `writePrivateTempFile` calls `0`; result error `invocation closed`.
  - `retired_http_error_detail`: delayed `403` body contained redacted private detail; published error was `invocation closed`; private error detail was not exposed.
- **Passed locally:** `pnpm test src/agents/openclaw-tools.web-fetch.test.ts -- --reporter=dot --coverage.enabled=false` passed 13 tests.
- **Passed locally:** `pnpm test src/agents/tools/web-fetch.transport.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.web-fetch.test.ts -- --reporter=dot --coverage.enabled=false` passed 37 tests across 2 Vitest shards.
- **Passed locally:** `pnpm format:check src/agents/openclaw-tools.web-fetch.test.ts`.
- **Passed locally:** `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`.
- **Passed locally:** `git diff --check`.
- **Remote proof note:** Crabbox/Blacksmith Testbox run `pr171052-web-fetch-transport-v7` on previous head `0367edcc4d4c0629b003f486c550bb45ca81ed8c` verified source/tree and passed the focused remote Vitest command, but the wrapper exited `1` during Blacksmith/GitHub cleanup settlement and the linked Actions run completed cancelled. I am not claiming that as clean merge evidence. A clean current-head Crabbox/Blacksmith result is still needed unless a maintainer accepts equivalent evidence.

## Merge Gates

- ClawSweeper must clear the PR.
- Maintainer/API-owner must explicitly sign off on the public/security-sensitive host transport contract.
- Repository checks and Crabbox/Blacksmith evidence must be clean for the merge decision.
