prs.title: fix(gateway): server tests time out when a parallel shard starts cold
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway server tests time out (and then cascade into fixture-ownership and `EnvironmentTeardownError` failures) when the parallel `gateway-server` shard starts cold, e.g. `agentic-control-plane-runtime-state-hosted-3` in run 38385657488 (`checks-node-changed-compact-small-2-1`) and the same 21-file plan replayed locally on main.

## User Impact

No user-visible product change. `sessions.create` without an initial turn no longer loads the chat-dispatch and embedded-agent execution graphs on its request path, which shortens the first cold `sessions.create` after Gateway start. CI and local Gateway server shards stop failing the first test in each worker on cold module loading.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway-server project runs files in `forks` with `isolate: false`, so each worker pays the Gateway's cold module evaluation once — and that cost was landing inside the first test's 30 s body budget or the first RPC's 10 s budget. Timestamped profiles of the replayed shard showed:

- **Cold startup in test budgets.** A test-only model-catalog reset (`resetPreparedGatewayModelCatalogForTest`) imported `server-start.ts` just to clear caches; removing that incidental import is right, but the startup graph still has to load somewhere. The Gateway test fixture now loads `server-start.ts` (the same graph the production `gateway-prewarm` entry compiles) once per worker in its setup hooks, so behavior budgets measure behavior. The model-catalog reset now only resets owners that are already loaded, via the existing global test-API pattern.
- **Over-broad `sessions.create` imports.** `sessions-create.ts` statically imported initial-turn chat dispatch, and `session-create-service.ts` imported the `embedded-agent.ts` barrel for one predicate, pulling the embedded runner, queued compaction, harness and tools into every session creation. Chat dispatch now loads only when an initial turn is requested (authority rechecked after that await), and the predicate is imported from its owner `embedded-agent-runner/active-run-projections.ts`. Measured first `sessions-create` family import: 7.26 s → 1.22 s. An import-boundary test guards both edges.
- **Teardown after a timeout.** Vitest timeouts do not cancel the body, so a timed-out file's in-flight startup and lazy imports kept running into the next file of the same worker (fixture "open/closing" errors) and past environment teardown (`Cannot load '/src/config/io.ts' … after the environment was torn down`). Fixture ownership now starts before listener/module acquisition; teardown joins setup, reset, late acquisition and native close before releasing state. A normal test or suite that leaks a Gateway still fails (after it is closed so successors stay clean); native close failure still retains ownership.

Ruled out with timestamps: post-ready handler prewarm contention (64 ms overlap with the first worker RPC; disabling it did not fix the timeout) and config-reload/hot-apply waits after `writeConfigFile` (reload RPCs ~0.3 s; MCP fixture has no reloader). Production prewarm and reload behavior are unchanged.

No timeout, hook budget, RPC deadline, worker count, isolation list, serial pin, retry, schema, config, or public surface changes.

## Evidence

Shard replay of the exact 21-file plan from the failing CI job via `scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` (gateway-server config, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2`, forks, `isolate:false`) on a shared macOS host (32 cores, background load avg 25–60 from other jobs):

| Head | Wall | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| main 0f13444e2a6b | 333 s | 20/21 — `portals.session` timed out (32.1 s), `app-sdk-composed-resources` 30.2 s |
| main 6eb267563d78 (rebase base) | 207 s | 20/21 — `worker-placement-startup-context` timed out (45.3 s) |
| this branch, run A | 186 s | 21/21, 59/59 |
| this branch, run B | 184 s | 21/21, 59/59 |
| this branch, run C (same-base A/B with the 207 s main run) | 210 s | 20/21 — one warm `plugin.approval.resolve` RPC timeout in `native-hook-request-lifetime` |

Every main run fails the first full-startup file in a worker (the reported class); no branch run did, and no branch run showed fixture-fence or `EnvironmentTeardownError` cascades. `worker-placement-startup-context` first case: 45.3 s timeout on main → 21.7 s on the branch. Whole-shard wall time is not a controlled comparison on this shared host: cold module evaluation moved into setup hooks rather than disappearing, except for the narrowed `sessions.create` graph.

Remaining gap: under heavy host load, isolated warm RPCs can still stall (run C above; a 2-file probe also caught a 13 s `sessions.create` snapshot stall). Probes attributed those intervals to SQLite worker ↔ host admission exchanges waiting ~1.3 s with <0.3 ms worker CPU — a starved host thread, not a request awaiting unrelated work — so no product change was made for them. PR CI on dedicated runners is the broad proof.

Focused tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall on the loaded host):

- `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.test-support.test.ts` — 2 passed, 4.5 s
- `src/gateway/server-import-boundary.test.ts` — 3 passed, 8.2 s
- `src/gateway/test-helpers.acquisition.test.ts` — 13 passed, 37.4 s
- `src/gateway/server.sessions.fixture-lifecycle.test.ts` — 13 passed, 62.6 s (includes the existing real retained-close subprocess)
- `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-create-timeout.test.ts` — 3 passed, 76 s (initial-turn dispatch still reaches chat dispatch with forwarded timeouts)
- `src/gateway/session-create-preparation.test.ts` — 18 passed, 63 s (active-run checks unchanged)

prs.title: fix(control-ui): load earlier messages when chat is underfilled
prs.body:
Related: #171009

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a conversation can leave a mostly empty chat pane stuck on **Show earlier**, even though older messages are available.

## User Impact

User impact: visible conversations automatically load earlier pages until the pane is filled or history ends, including empty pages and pages containing only hidden tool activity. No configuration or migration is required. Hidden panes and programmatic scroll placement still do not trigger pagination; failed loads still require reader input to retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore the underfilled-viewport bootstrap removed in #171009 without reverting its settled-position safeguards. The existing history owner serializes loads and stops nonadvancing cursors; its existing single-page staged prefetch remains unchanged. Full transcripts still wait for upward reader intent rather than fetching just because the boundary is within the prefetch margin.

Requested and regression reported by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/0622f671-6a6d-4a27-ae38-c9e97b7cdf2c)

## Evidence

- The focused regression failed before the fix: a visible underfilled pane made zero history requests. The history pagination unit suite passes after the fix (27 tests).
- Real Chromium / production Control UI bundle with a synthetic Gateway: empty, short, and hidden-activity pages fill without a gesture; consecutive sparse pages advance; loading remains visible while waiting; filling stops when scrollable. Cold-load anchoring, stale-geometry restoration, and reconnect/pending-message adoption are covered (15 browser tests across five files).
- UI TypeScript check, scoped lint/format, docs MDX sanity, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent fresh review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Broad suites run in PR CI.
- The initial sibling run exposed an obsolete manual-only assertion added in #171009; restored its automatic-loading contract and verified the unchanged geometry/receipt assertions. No expected-failure or baseline exemption was added.

### CI qualification

Run [38494747057](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38494747057) is **failed**, not green. This PR was landed using the native inherited-failure exception for two unrelated baseline failures: the worker mock-export guard at `worker-turn-launcher.lazy.test.ts:212`, reproduced on unchanged main; and the existing terminal-upload readiness wait at `terminal-panel-upload.test.ts:80` (retry and expired-retry cases). The terminal/component/app/test-helper/config/dependency input trees are identical between the tested merge and its main parent. An isolated main replay passes 8/8 terminal tests but does not prove the intermittent readiness issue fixed. Both were reported to the existing CI repair lane. Security-fast, UI E2E/performance, and other selected checks passed.

### Before

Synthetic conversation after startup, waiting for a manual click:

![Before: empty chat waiting on Show earlier](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2047494-2d50-40bf-a5b1-d26c92613a7c)

### After

The same conversation loads its earlier messages automatically, without scrolling or clicking:

![After: earlier conversation loaded automatically](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7552ca8-2cf6-4acd-be41-af8c8e5ddd36)

prs.title: refactor(automations): migrate periodic heartbeats and retire the executor
prs.body:
Related: #134994. Final sequential slice of #164265, following #166889 and #167113; adopts the approved design from #135933 under Peter's October 3 and October 12 decisions.

## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled monitoring still has a separate heartbeat execution, delivery, and recovery path alongside Automations.

## User Impact

Existing monitors become ordinary editable Automations. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` before startup after upgrading. The July-2026+ migration preserves job identity/history, scratch bytes and revisions, disabled state, schedule anchors, pending occurrences, quiet hours, allowed model selections, target routing, and tool authority. It verifies durable conversion before retiring legacy inputs and retains ambiguous input with recovery guidance. Repeated Doctor runs preserve operator edits and deleted jobs.

Migrated jobs use **standard Automations delivery**, with no `delivery.duplicateWindowMs` or `delivery.skipIfNoRoute` options. Doctor emits this notice once when the cutover receipt completes:

> Migrated heartbeats now use standard Automations delivery. Heartbeat-specific duplicate suppression and no-route skipping were removed: repeated updates can be delivered, and a missing route no longer skips the run before execution. Delivery failures follow ordinary automation handling. Review the migrated jobs' delivery settings if you relied on either behavior.

This is a **breaking plugin-SDK change**: heartbeat execution and reply exports are removed outright, without deprecated aliases. Upgrade affected plugins using `docs/plugins/sdk-migration/removed-surfaces.md`. The deprecated `reply-runtime` export budget remains **1**. The existing nondeprecated prompt hook and protocol-v4 projections retain their documented contracts.

The approved shared-state compatibility fence now advances **22→23** so older Gateways cannot ignore migrated job policies. Main consumed version 22 for its separately approved portable ACP/cursor identities; this integration preserves that migration and the prior predicate columns. This is the same fence approved in #134994 (originally numbered 16); this cutover adds no tables or columns. Its existing regression checks schema-22 reader refusal while retaining identical stored job and catalog bytes. It preserves main’s separately landed agent schema **26**, without adding a per-agent schema migration. Keep the verified pre-update backup for rollback. Automatic updater admission normalizes supported July fields through the existing Doctor transforms; it preserves main's prior retirement of global `includeReasoning`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor conversion and periodic retirement land together because the old reconciler could otherwise recreate converted or deleted monitors. The ordinary scheduler owns periodic jobs, and the already-landed ordinary session event owner handles immediate follow-ups. The periodic runner, reconciler, dispatcher, response tool, SDK aliases, obsolete callers, and private status wrapper are deleted.

Immediate Slack interactions use ordinary occurrence receipts: failures are reported and settled. The old pre-adoption passive queue could retain a notice through a soft restart or later turn; there is no retained passive mirror or automatic failed-event replay in the new owner.

Durable migration receipts, portable Claw custody, and guarded scheduler admission account for the production growth. Idle deferral preserves unstarted slots and stream buffers; on-exit admission retains its exact receipt and command output while foreground work settles. Main's worker-backed deletion owner, terminal-write drainage, first-session identity, and memory-plugin lifecycle are preserved. Deferred notices stay with their selected scheduled occurrence and are accepted only when the complete batch fits the existing prompt limit.

Phase E's standalone memory backend remains intact, including its factory, registry, expiry, federation, and meaningful coverage. Its heartbeat-specific adapters use ordinary Automations. Protocol-v4 controls and the existing nondeprecated prompt hook delegate to ordinary job receipts; they do not retain a heartbeat executor.

The fresh-main integration preserves main's worker-owned recovery, configured-owner authority, output-accumulator deletion, cron blocker-report wording, empty-mutation worker handling, and speech-only delivery. Main’s separately landed #170716 now owns the original physical-database custody repair. This integration keeps its native-consent implementation unchanged and removes S3’s duplicate repair, without restoring repeated absence queries. Memory tests exercise main's explicit session-maintenance trigger and virtual quiet-window scheduler while retaining their retry and completion assertions.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

Peter approved default-model fallback on October 12: when a legacy heartbeat explicitly selected a model outside the agent's model policy, Doctor drops that override and the migrated automation uses the agent's allowed default. Doctor records a visible migration notice naming the agent, job, dropped model, and effective default, with the next step: pick an allowed model or add it to the agent's `modelPolicy.allow`. Allowed explicit models are preserved. This avoids blocking conversion while preserving the ordinary automation permission boundary; no allowlist, grant, or configuration option is added. The original duplicate-suppression/no-route notice above remains unchanged.

Release-note context: heartbeat migration can switch a disallowed legacy model to the agent's allowed default and records the replacement with repair guidance. Ordinary automations still reject disallowed explicit model overrides. The breaking plugin-SDK export removals and standard Automations delivery change described above remain part of this release context.

## Credential-writer guard precision

The proactive receipt key now has the enforced return type `automation-default:${string}:${string}`. The credential-writer guard uses the native TypeScript template-literal API to inspect its fixed head. Only a head that cannot form a prefix of `authProfiles.store` is excluded; empty, matching, credential-prefix, plain-string, and unsafe union variants remain guarded. Trimming remains conservative, so whitespace cannot hide a credential key. This adds no allowlist, cast, indirect dispatch, or owner exception, and preserves the existing persisted keys and atomic job/receipt transaction.

The new safe case failed against the old guard; all 92 existing and added guard cases now pass (12.10s wrapper). The pre-rebase suppression guard passed 3/3 (25.15s wrapper); main's later inventory repair is incorporated and the current inventory passes, as recorded below. Independent P2 review is scoped-clean (0.98). The schema-23 package declaration and Voice Call migration descriptor are aligned; the original idle-WAL admission regression passes (241.88s wrapper), with unchanged assertions. The full failed database-worker ratchet command passes: T1 calls decrease 454→453 and deprecated-only calls stay 9; its resolved merge base is `71692b03a277790e5781705dcdfeb6f4ba0c810f`. Exact-head hosted CI remains required.

## Visual comparison

[Inspected synthetic before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167796#issuecomment-6150693557) show the scheduler diagnostics cutover and the ordinary automation policy controls. The comment names the historical capture revisions and source continuity; it does not claim a new exact-head capture or main's later layout changes. Images are embedded on this PR, and GitHub's rendered HTML plus attachment round-trips are verified.

## Evidence

The schema-cache integration correction includes active-run and pacing policy in the existing key: its regression fails before the fix and the complete file passes 13/13 afterward (schema plus suppression wrapper 94.72s), without adding fields or raising the cache budget. Independent P2 review is scoped-clean (0.98). Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. No broad local check-changed or SDK preparation is repeated. Final exact-head hosted CI remains required.

Earlier separately landed main-owner repairs preserve distinct source and aggregate terminal-delivery facts, actual queued-finalizer synchronization, authorized raw diagnostics, bounded history fixtures, and requested-placement acknowledgment custody. Their earlier positive replays remain historical evidence; the newer full-order placement failure above reopens that flow's diagnosis. One earlier local compiled invocation was invalidated by a concurrent patch and is not counted.

Doctor's observed model-policy case migrates forbidden `openai/gpt-4o-mini` to the allowed default `openai/gpt-5.4`, records agent/job/dropped/default and next-step notice, and executes through ordinary automation. A distinct ordinary automation still refuses the forbidden override before provider invocation. Migration/profile/notice proof passes three cases (123.51s wrapper); execution proof passes (112.02s wrapper), using synthetic provider adapters.

The native TypeScript credential-writer precision guard passes all 92 cases, including unsafe plain-string/auth-prefix variants. The original database-worker ratchet passes (T1 454→453; deprecated-only calls remain 9). SDK baseline generation records the nine approved heartbeat export removals and no deprecated heartbeat aliases; the reply-runtime deprecated-export budget stays 1. Trusted-Git security findings were fixed in code through existing owned helpers and exact named reads, without detector changes. The earlier Mattermost dispatch failure did not reproduce in three main and three S3 full-file runs, and later hosted execution passed; no causal fix is claimed. Final hosted SDK/API, build, types, lint, security and every selected runtime gate remain required.

Historical natural-flow proof at `b5ed970d2c1d2fb2ee6f5fd884f008a53b103b22` exercises CLI, Doctor, Gateway, storage, natural scheduling and delivery on isolated AWS with synthetic loopback transports. Identity, schedule, routing, history and scratch survive; the notice appears once, and identical updates deliver 60,011ms apart. Both Gateways stopped and both leases are released. This is historical flow evidence, not final-head external inference. [Natural-flow run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7e3843b5e9fb0f6fed82f863010f9bd3).

Published-driver package recovery was proved with disabled heartbeat configuration. Interrupted published-driver recovery with an active heartbeat/history/scratch dataset remains a gap. [Recovery run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_135e177e5bf7355440fb54ce06d71f76).

## Current integration corrections

Pushed head: `9da2014b1ac87302cc225b45b727879d6069f95b`, rebased onto main `72ccf6ff92931fff2d49473fe1571f39e8311ad2`. Full hosted CI on this exact head is pending.

Conflict-only integration retains main's memory-only incognito architecture and standalone memory capability, extracted prompt/terminal helpers, prepared session actors, deletion-journal custody, required-native placement facts, requester receipt proof, lazy performance-clock fixtures, and canonical native seal helper. Retired heartbeat executor, storage, reconciliation and SDK alias paths remain removed. Doctor's delivery notice above stays verbatim.

The immediate interrupted terminal receipt exposed stale recovery custody on a successor start. The private start publisher had also dropped non-enumerable lifecycle generation and claim fields. The existing lifecycle owner now retires a superseded interruption only on an accepted current-generation successor while retaining live reservations, foreground claims, tombstones, delivery and continuation custody. Private fields go only to persistence; public event broadcasts are unchanged. Both original shutdown replacement cases reproduced failure before the fix and pass unchanged afterward. Independent P2 review is scoped-clean (0.90); the final integrated correction review is scoped-clean (0.91).

Focused integrated proof passes **205/205 tests in six files** (130.56s wrapper), including Claw cleanup, ordinary cron reload, recovery, terminal preparation and standalone memory side effects. The separate exact-CI-merge recovery proof passes 89/89 (148.42s wrapper). Placement admission plus ordinary cron shutdown had 26 passing cases in the earlier wrapper; a duplicate rebased import was then corrected and the full Claw file passes. Typed placement fixtures expose main's real `prepareRead` method. Claw refusal assertions now match main's exact deletion-owner error and retain all safety assertions. One new-main test for the retired runtime monitor-reconciliation API was removed; ordinary loading, publication and custody coverage remains.

Final core production types and the Gateway test graphs pass. Runtime and Madge cycles are both zero. Suppression inventory passes 3/3 (22.89s wrapper) after separately fixing main's Solid status CSS prop contract in `72ccf6ff929`; no exception or baseline entry was added. The mock-factory ratchet prunes 9,635 to 9,598 through its owner. Config-doc baselines were regenerated through repo tooling, retaining main's plugin fields and removing approved legacy heartbeat fields. No SDK declaration preparation or full local check-changed was repeated. Hosted build, lint, SDK API, security and every selected runtime job remain the gate.

Retained disjoint proof: cron's deferred marker now participates in its first atomic terminal write (original ten failures reproduced; 22/22 unchanged pass, 266.55s). Chat history uses the existing prepared metadata owner (six unchanged cases pass, 248.66s), preserving zero host SQL reads. Doctor's optional Claw migration import is delayed past its no-findings return (eight selected migration/provenance cases pass, 152.47s). The loading change is not a timeout-fix claim.

The prior-head ordinary run [38439137625](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38439137625) is complete: **203 jobs, 177 successful, 12 failed, 13 skipped, one cancelled**. The full exact-head check census retains 281 checks (228 successful, 13 failed, 37 skipped, two cancelled, one neutral), including superseded PR-context checks. Every failure is attributed below; none supplies a current inherited-only waiver.

They remain recorded, not relabeled. prs.title: fix(workers): reclaim idle buffers and reduce catalog decoder memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Catalog decoder workers retain unrelated runtime modules, and completed large buffers can remain uncollected when JavaScript heap growth stays below the idle-GC threshold.

## User Impact

Lower catalog-decoder memory overhead and automatic reclamation of dead external buffers while keeping workers warm. No configuration, schema, or supported public SDK changes are required.

This is a bounded improvement, **not a demonstrated fix for the separate multi-GiB Gateway memory report**. Reclaimed buffers do not guarantee that RSS returns to the OS, and the prepared-model worker showed no material improvement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep catalog routing, terminal text helpers, and admission transport on lightweight imports. Observe heap and external-memory growth independently in the existing idle collector, preserving its threshold, burst debounce, cancellation, and worker reuse.

The terminal helper remains an official-plugin-private runtime surface; it does not expand the supported public SDK.

## Evidence

### CI repair

[The initial CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38500253249) at `1a7f44bf` exposed an incomplete PR-wrapper source inventory: the new `gateway-state-owner-errors.ts` and `sqlite-database-admission-context.ts` imports were not extracted. The follow-up adds both to `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`; no runtime logic, timeout, assertion, or workflow is changed.

Focused repair proof on Node 24.16.0 / macOS arm64:

- Three wrapper/tooling files: **37 cases passed**, including import closure, extracted runtime execution, older-anchor handoff, and native provisioning diagnostics.
- Native provisioning file: **15 passed, one platform skip, one failure**. prs.title: fix(bench): report the RPC budget when concurrency benchmarks fail
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrency benchmark RPC failures do not record whether the request used its normal 65-second cap or the time left in the aggregate benchmark deadline.

## User Impact

Benchmark operators can inspect the selected timeout, issue/expiry/rejection times, and remaining aggregate budget alongside the original error. Gateway behavior, timeout selection, and benchmark workload are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the monotonic deadline snapshot where the benchmark issues each request, then attach it only on rejection while retaining the original cause. A later phase cannot relabel an outstanding request, and socket failures are not reported as timer verdicts.

## Evidence

- Final RPC fixture: 8/8 tests passed, covering the default cap, aggregate clipping, explicit cap, minimum timer, a midflight deadline change, exhausted-budget refusal, socket closure, success, and server rejection.
- Corrected fixture lint, benchmark lint, targeted formatting, `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, and all four `pnpm tsgo:test:root` shards passed. The receiver verified the final source tree and unchanged input hashes before and after the checks.
- The 99 existing benchmark, CLI, and WebSocket sibling tests passed before a formatting-only production adjustment; the corrected RPC fixture was rerun on the final bytes.
- Independent automated review completed with no P0–P2 findings. Production delta: +34/-12; tests: +156. The added production lines retain timing facts that were previously lost.
- Small mocked success-path measurement: median 207.25 ns/request before vs 220.38 ns/request after, five alternating 1,000-call rounds after 200 warmups. This is noisy diagnostic overhead evidence, not a Gateway performance result.

The remote wrapper originally exited 1 after the checks passed because its exact GitHub settlement read failed. Supported native reconciliation subsequently cleared the owned resource and local custody; the original wrapper failure remains recorded. The integrated performance cohort remains pending, and exact-head PR CI is still required.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep claimed hook replies in conversation history
prs.body:
Closes #149985

Related: #150011

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a case where plugin replies claimed by `before_agent_reply` can be delivered without being recorded in session history. Media-only and captioned replies also lose attachment references when a text-only transcript receipt suppresses downstream mirroring.

## User Impact

Claimed replies remain available in conversation history and follow-up context without duplicate assistant entries. Media replies retain stable attachment filenames alongside captions. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why Change Was Made

Both CLI and embedded early-return paths persist through the existing transcript owners before returning ownership and idempotency metadata. Media history uses the existing outbound-media transcript-mirror projection; delivered payloads are unchanged. Session writer guards and detached/room-event no-persistence behavior are retained. Run-current assertions now also reach asynchronous transcript commit admission.

## Evidence

### Conflict repair and validation (`e38c83e212cf7da6a94603af26cd80722e8b4dfc`)

Merged the fixed upstream `main` baseline `5dd456acfa35575c342b43b944a9d0dbb911b68e` into the PR. Resolved four conflicts while retaining both the claimed-reply history tests and upstream's newer authority/diagnostic behavior:

- Embedded claimed replies now reuse upstream's `preReplyAssertCurrent` through transcript preparation and final commit admission.
- CLI transcript persistence retains both the PR's current-run assertion and upstream's `onMessageCommitted` handling.
- The extracted embedded return keeps `providerStarted: false`, so hook-authored replies are not counted as model responses.
- No new test cases, schema/configuration changes, dependency overrides, or weaker assertions were added.

**Functional proof: 248 selected tests passed.** The four-file runner/transcript/diagnostic run passed 245 tests across three shards (691.59 seconds wrapper wall time). A separate reliability selection passed the three existing “keeps a committed final reply successful” cases (63.63 seconds); its other 59 tests were excluded by the filter, not executed. Coverage includes claimed text/media delivery and real SQLite/history readback, once-only persistence, cancellation before commit, replaced-writer authority, silent claims, provider-started diagnostics, and post-commit ownership.

  src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-transcript.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.shared-integration.test.ts \
  src/agents/diagnostic-model-response.test.ts

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/cli-runner.reliability.test.ts \
  -t 'keeps a committed final reply successful'
```

**Static proof and limitations:** core production typecheck, `agents-root` and `agents-other` test typechecks, changed-file formatting and targeted type-aware lint passed. Conflict/line/assertion/SQLite/mock-export ratchets, dependency/config/plugin-boundary checks, coercion/deprecation checks, native schema, legacy-store, media, sidecar, import-cycle, webhook, and pairing guards passed. Staged `git diff --check` against the incorporated baseline passed.

The complete local changed-file gate is **not green**: it was deliberately stopped after the two relevant test type graphs passed, before completing the remaining 26 broad graphs (exit 143). Its remaining non-type checks were run separately. The unused-export check exited 1: **21 production findings and 9 full-tree findings, all in UI source, match the unmodified pinned upstream baseline exactly**. Both candidate and baseline used the same repository scanner/configuration and Knip `6.32.2`; the baseline was independently executed from an exported upstream source tree with the same installed dependencies. The script export scan passed on both. No UI exports, ignore rules, or scanner baselines were changed. Broad remaining type coverage belongs to the new-head CI; no full-local-gate success is claimed.

Static selection:

The preceding head `45014fa84c8cc44de442725c47f88137e11073cf` had [green CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38110161411) and ClawSweeper Revision 27 reported no findings. Those results do not certify this new merge commit. This update is local real-runner/SQLite proof, not a fresh installed-plugin, live-channel, or live-model capture. ### Previous conflict repair and validation (`45014fa84c8cc44de442725c47f88137e11073cf`; historical)

Merged upstream `main` at `8c9999b298c4a5db2d60b531efff7f8ec20acbeb`. Resolved conflicts in the CLI hook test, embedded run orchestrator, and reply normalization. - **304/304 tests passed across 9 files and 4 shards** (896.11 seconds wrapper wall time). - Environment: Node `24.21.0`, repository-pinned pnpm `12.9.0`, `@openclaw/fs-safe 0.26.0`. Tested and reviewed candidate tree: `56e4b74f1b37031cee7290f8b1fa950aff910faf`.

Functional validation:

```sh

  src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts \

After its unused-export failure, the remaining commands from the same repository-generated plan were executed separately without skipping or weakening their guards. `git diff --cached --check` against that base passed.

This is local real-runner/SQLite evidence, not a new installed-plugin, live-channel, or live-model capture. Earlier installed-plugin evidence below remains labelled by its original head. Hosted CI must validate the new head; no all-green or merge-ready claim is made.


### Previous conflict resolution and validation (`cd4bfe4222412efde2fd1701f4bd77889cc68e28`; historical)

Merged upstream `main` at `43856f78ec629f0c72180359a0ce85f06759974f`. A claimed reply could still add an assistant history event when the run was cancelled after transcript preparation but before asynchronous commit admission. CLI and embedded runners now pass their existing run-current assertion to the same transcript append/worker owner; session fences, write hooks, and idempotency remain unchanged. - **RED:** on unfixed `b974ef10871c10bd7accd406e4999ce0482314db`, with the new tests and lockfile-matching dependencies, both "cancelled after transcript preparation" cases failed: real SQLite history contained one `late claimed reply` assistant event instead of zero.

- **Static gates:** the complete changed-file gate against pinned upstream parent `214bb47b4ec0809e357d2e497e0bf8fd5d9f31eb` exited 0, including core production typecheck, all 27 core-test type graphs, three unused-export scans, formatting, type-aware lint, ratchets, and boundary/legacy-store/import-cycle guards. `git diff --check` also passed.

This is real-runner/SQLite regression evidence, not a new installed-plugin, external-channel, or live-model trace. The head-labelled installed-plugin/local-channel-adapter proof below is historical. Hosted CI on the updated head remains the merge gate.

### Earlier evidence (historical; see head labels)

- Before the media repair, all three CLI media cases failed SQLite history assertions; text-only passed.
- Registered plugin hooks exercise the real runner entrypoints and SQLite persistence for text-only, media-only, captioned, and multiple-attachment replies.
- CLI delivery exercises the `routeReply` durable outbound pipeline, asserting unchanged transport arguments and once-only assistant history after delivery.

### Installed plugin -> claimed text/media -> delivery -> SQLite/history proof

Executed against exact PR head `f57cd074e95ba2e0bbedb527d5c41ecfb7948cec` with Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.4.0, using isolated `HOME`, config, state, and session storage.

1. The production installer copied a local plugin package into `state/extensions/claimed-reply-proof` and enabled it. A fresh process reported plugin version `1.0.0`, `status: loaded`, and channel `claimed-proof`. The plugin declared `before_agent_reply`, and the isolated operator config explicitly granted `hooks.allowConversationAccess: true`.

This is a real disk installation and real routed-delivery adapter execution with SQLite/history readback. The adapter is a local proof channel; this is not a live external-channel API or live-model test.


### Revalidated on PR head (2f60a04dc02c7c98cf6539027013e28df36b15bf)

- Merged upstream main `fabbb3462b7e77c2207c44a4c0ace86254ab6a26` into the prior PR head. The two conflicts were an import moved into the upstream model-admission owner and a test-file routing list; the resolved PR diff retains the same claimed-reply persistence behavior.

### Silent-claim follow-up and exact-head proof (348ff0510adf6760dd093e6b52585e537cefcaa0)

ClawSweeper's Revision 10 found that a hook returning `{ handled: true }` without `reply` could persist the synthetic `NO_REPLY` token as an assistant message. - New CLI and embedded regressions use real session storage. Both failed before the fix because SQLite history contained a `NO_REPLY` assistant message, then passed after the fix with zero assistant messages for silent claims.
- The focused silent tests passed: 2 tests in 2 files, Vitest duration 27.85s and wrapper wall time 86.30s. The final silent plus text/media selection passed 18 tests in 2 files, Vitest duration 33.13s and wrapper wall time 50.22s.
- Core typecheck, `core-test-agents-root`, `core-test-agents-other`, focused oxlint/oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. An independent P0–P2 review of the follow-up diff found no actionable findings. Full exact-head CI remains the merge gate.
- On this head, a fresh local CLI process loaded the installed proof plugin and returned `deliveryStatus.status = sent` with one payload result. Its local channel adapter recorded exactly one captioned-media outbound call. The production `loadTranscriptEvents` accessor returned 2 events, including exactly one assistant message containing `CLAIMED_TEXT_PR150078\nCLAIMED_MEDIA_PR150078.png` with idempotency key `before-agent-reply:8c457f24-5170-4e51-8de6-dc96116e9286`. Direct SQLite readback found one assistant event and one distinct idempotency key for the same session.

The installed-plugin proof uses an isolated local channel adapter and intentionally unreachable model endpoint, not an external-channel API or live-model test.

### Cancellation authority and exact-head proof (31a58fd33c10576b0d750e440838e4f5391e3439)

- Revision 11 identified a stale-run write after an asynchronous `before_agent_reply` hook. CLI and embedded paths now check current run authority after the hook, immediately around transcript preparation, and after persistence returns, before releasing a claimed payload.
- Real-session/SQLite regressions cancel a claimed turn (1) while the hook is pending and (2) inside transcript preparation, after the initial check but before the database write. The two new write-boundary cases failed on the preceding patch because SQLite contained one `late claimed reply` assistant event each; both pass now with zero assistant events. The focused `before_agent_reply` suites pass 63/63 tests across CLI and embedded entry points.
- The final change passed core typecheck and the agents-root/agents-other test type graphs. The earlier full core-test typecheck passed all 25 graphs; after removing an unused test-support export, the affected graphs, focused lint, formatting, and tests passed again. The standalone dead-export scan passed all three scans; remaining changed-file static guards passed separately. Full exact-head CI is still the merge gate.
- On this exact commit, a fresh local `openclaw agent --local --deliver` process loaded the installed proof plugin from isolated state. The plugin claimed a captioned-media reply; the local channel adapter recorded exactly one media send with unchanged caption `CLAIMED_TEXT_PR150078` and media URL `https://example.invalid/CLAIMED_MEDIA_PR150078.png`. CLI reported `deliveryStatus.status = sent`, `succeeded = true`, and `resultCount = 1`.
- Production `loadTranscriptEvents` read 2 session events, including exactly 1 assistant message with text `CLAIMED_TEXT_PR150078\nCLAIMED_MEDIA_PR150078.png` and one `before-agent-reply` idempotency key. A direct read-only SQLite query independently returned assistant count 1 and distinct idempotency-key count 1 for that session. This is installed-plugin/local-adapter proof, not an external-channel API or live-model test.

### Explicit silent-token claim regression (941a8a3bc30f1ad6b713697ec670b0c32d77f8a4)

ClawSweeper Revision 14 identified a distinct edge: a plugin can return `{ handled: true, reply: { text: "NO_REPLY" } }`. Outbound normalization suppresses that content-free payload, but both claimed-reply paths wrote an assistant `NO_REPLY` event. Both runners now use the shared payload-level silent-content decision before transcript persistence; media, other sendable content, heartbeat-owned replies, and the existing cancellation fences keep their prior paths.

- **Before fix, on `c237892331314cdb5309159e832c7afa3a23c853`:** the new CLI and embedded runner tests each failed through the real runner entrypoint and SQLite history readback. Each found one assistant event containing `NO_REPLY` where zero were expected.
- **After fix, on `941a8a3bc30f1ad6b713697ec670b0c32d77f8a4`:** the same two targeted tests passed (2/2). The nearby `before_agent_reply` suites passed 65/65, including text/media persistence and cancellation/replaced-writer cases. Delivery normalization suites passed 102/102, including silent-token, media, and heartbeat cases.
- Full affected files with one worker: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot` passed 44/44 in 52.51s wall; `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.shared-integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot` passed 167/167 in 213.50s wall. The shared embedded integration file is costly because it exercises the real runner/session/SQLite boundary and adjacent authority/media behavior; no new full-runner fixture was added.

Core typecheck, all 25 core-test type graphs, and all three unused-export scans completed successfully during `check:changed`. That broad local gate was **interrupted during full-tree core lint after more than 30 minutes**, so it is not claimed as a full pass. A separate lint command scoped to the six changed files completed without diagnostics. Exact-head GitHub CI remains the merge gate.

The prior installed-plugin captioned-media proof was collected on `31a58fd`, not rerun on this incremental silent-token fix; the new SQLite regressions above ran on the pushed head.




### Revision 15 follow-up: silent token with media (`1a58c8cf89772187adbc0b45f3e18b2a04890473`)

- **Before the fix (`147394dfdb90c3e0915b98f257031510b8128810`):** the new registered-plugin CLI case delivered a media-only reply for `{ text: "NO_REPLY", mediaUrl: "https://example.com/photo.png" }`, but its SQLite/history readback contained `NO_REPLY\nphoto.png` instead of `photo.png`. The new assertion failed on that exact mismatch.
- **After the fix:** the transcript projection uses the same existing silent-text predicate as outbound normalization. In the CLI registered-plugin case, routed delivery sends the media with an empty text field, SQLite/history contains one assistant event with `photo.png`, and delivery does not add a second event. The embedded real-session matrix also reads back `photo.png` for persistent turns and preserves its existing non-persistent-turn expectations.
- **Local validation:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.shared-integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed; targeted oxlint and oxfmt passed for all five changed files; `tsconfig.core.json`, `agents-root`, and `agents-other` typechecks passed; `git diff --check` passed. Independent incremental autoreview through P2 exited successfully.
- The installed-plugin/local-channel captioned-media proof above predates this edge-case fix. The new token-plus-media evidence is from the registered-plugin CLI route and embedded real-session/SQLite tests, not a separate live external-channel run. Full `check:changed` was not rerun locally; exact-head CI is pending.



### Upstream conflict resolution and revalidation (`a0c2eb36ac86c73a7111386ee540b54f775e372e`)

- GitHub reported a real merge conflict after the Revision 15 fix was pushed. Merged upstream `main` at `a1ba139b5697bef432ad0d2d28e0aba75b8a43a6`; the only manual conflict was the CLI test import block. The resolution retains both the PR's registry/SQLite imports and upstream's test scheduler import.
- On the merged tree, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passed. The full CLI and embedded integration test files passed together with `--maxWorkers=1` (about five minutes of local wall time, including worker rebuild). Focused oxfmt and oxlint on the five changed files, production core typecheck, `agents-root` and `agents-other` test typechecks, and staged `git diff --check` passed.
- The token-plus-media proof above remains a registered-plugin CLI delivery and real-session/SQLite regression, not a new live external-channel or installed-plugin run. Full local `check:changed` was not rerun. Exact-head GitHub CI for this merge commit remains to be checked.



### Mixed silent-token text alignment (`e0010a48fd116ca88595d60033010e2d0c9f3ff7`)

- ClawSweeper Revision 17 identified a second history/delivery mismatch: for `Hello NO_REPLY`, delivery removes the trailing control token while the claimed-reply transcript previously retained it. This affects text-only replies and media captions.
- **Before fix:** new registered-plugin CLI and embedded real-session cases for text-only and captioned media failed on the previous head `a0c2eb36ac86c73a7111386ee540b54f775e372e`. The transcript projection still passed the raw mixed text to SQLite.
- **After fix:** delivery normalization and the claimed-reply transcript projection use one shared mixed-token stripping helper. The CLI cases verify routed delivery text `Hello`, SQLite/history text `Hello` or `Hello\nphoto.png`, and no second assistant event after delivery. Embedded real-session cases verify the same history projection for persistent turns and retain the non-persistent-turn expectations. The exact `NO_REPLY` plus media case remains covered.

The existing reply-normalization test file passed. prs.title: chore: run qualified commands tests on Bun
prs.body:
Related: #167038

## What Problem This Solves

CI currently limits Bun admission for the commands test owner to three explicitly listed files, even after the broader owner has completed its qualification campaign.

## User Impact

The commands CI owner can use the repository-pinned Bun runtime for its complete selection and verified owner-local subsets. Ambiguous or mixed-owner selections keep Node. This changes CI routing, not the installed CLI's runtime or behavior; no user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime selector now uses the existing whole-owner admission path for the commands leaf instead of maintaining a three-file allowance. It preserves commands-light, database-worker, and unit-fast ownership, along with the existing pools, exclusions, and worker limits. The routing regressions cover complete owners, canonical patterns, literal files, excluded siblings, and uncertain or foreign selections; the shard regression checks the actual child configuration.

Qualification includes the merged prerequisite repairs: #170022 for SQLite WAL snapshot retention, #170638 for complete Doctor inventory links in bounded failure reports, and #170867 for deeply nested SQLite backup destinations.

## Evidence

The accepted Linux qualification on source `d0554f4a2507370865e94fce53a7e431a82d472a` completed **78/78 fresh Node/Bun pairs across 521 files, 18 groups, and 17 serial jobs**. The accounting is **15 five-pair groups covering 503 files, plus three single-pair integration bridges covering 18 files**: `15 × 5 + 3 = 78` and `503 + 18 = 521`. The obligation breakdown is 52 remaining pairs, 22 contract-refresh pairs, and four additional authentication requalification pairs.

The aggregate verified exact raw and unredacted case/status/multiplicity parity without normalization, and all 17 segment acceptances were audited before acceptance. Each execution environment retained its own verified source and prepared-input provenance; identical prepared artifacts across environments are not claimed. Earlier 30-pair and 40-pair evidence remains separate and is not added to these totals.

S3's original transport failure remains recorded as **native exit 7, broker exit 255, and unknown controller OS exit**. Separate completion and collection operations each exited 0 after the existing consumer results were verified. Those consumers were not replayed, and the original failure was not relabeled as a successful run.

Known intermittent issue #170107 remains limited to archived switch, local-cut refusal, and retired-owner rewind. It is not a waiver for other failures, and no reruns were used to clear those cases.

The final admission proof passed both complete routing files through the repository-native runner on Node 24.21.0 and the SHA-verified pinned Bun: **102 passed, zero skipped per runtime**, with exact raw and unredacted case/status parity. Owner-scope took **17.054 s Node / 17.338 s Bun**; shard routing took **33.841 s Node / 41.060 s Bun**. Scoped changed-file checks passed in **954.007 s** and Madge passed in **31.393 s**. Canonical preparation, source/index stability, runtime identity, and prepared-input stability all passed. The successful bootstrap, admission and collector used three distinct native runs on the same isolated environment; the final archive audit passed all 121 retained files.

The largest qualification pair cost **2158.094 s**, including the unchanged 600-second setup reserve, within the existing 3600-second CI envelope. No comparator, test timeout, heap limit, worker count, skip policy, or CI budget changed.

Qualification aggregate SHA-256: `6bcb431126657a5c130472a7e93e2063752a252fbfaccf1da93a27427f6feb48`. Final admission archive SHA-256: `bf70268e94d872c65313f16407753474185f3f9707d39d389633b6882f15dd5f`.

Independent code and concrete-proof reviews were scoped-clean at P2; the exact-head GitHub Codex review reported no findings.

[Exact-head CI run 38496713736](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38496713736) completed with **42 successful, 24 skipped and three failed jobs**, including the aggregate gate. The two root failures are retained for the native inherited-failure exception:

- [SDK surface-report assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38496713736/job/115634401946): public exports 3759 > 3758 and callable exports 2194 > 2193. The SDK scanner, budgets, dependency metadata and complete relevant source trees are identical between the CI baseline and tested merge; the commands routing change does not enter that scan.
- [UI HTML-attachment assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38496713736/job/115634401645): both HTML parameterizations timed out waiting for a rendered element. Independent source review verified unchanged UI source, harness, runtime selection, environment and shard contract. The precise rendering stage and timing/cache cause remain unresolved.

The automated classifier reports both jobs as new because the selected scopes were not compared with the passing scheduled-main jobs. The inherited attribution above is a separate, reviewed comparison against actual CI baseline `fd1eeeb685b11c47dc5417d423ccc19b21d42570` and tested merge `9ea47e1046e0698bc35859a157b19aa47c80dc39`; it does not claim a matching baseline execution, a known UI flake, or green CI. Neither job was rerun.

[ClawSweeper completed on the exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171536#issuecomment-6159402011) with no findings and no before-merge items. It retained two proof limitations: the hash-identified archives were not linked for its own inspection, and a base-failing execution of the added routing cases was not supplied. The independently audited qualification and admission evidence above remains separate from the bot's source review.

prs.title: perf(cron): retain committed job views after run completion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a cron run completes, the first `cron.list` or `cron.status` unnecessarily fetches the entire job store through the shared state worker, even though finalization has already installed its committed row postimages. That fetch extends the serialized read queue under worker pressure.

## User Impact

List and status reads can reuse the newly committed resident state after completion. Job contents, pagination revisions, scheduling, public response shapes and durability are unchanged. Sibling writers and unavailable commit replies still invalidate the view. No schema or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The store owner advances its existing loaded revision only when it matched the revision observed before finalization and no other publication intervened. Finalization installs the returned upserts/deletions before advancing that fact. This removes the redundant reload without introducing another cache or weakening sibling invalidation.

Production delta: +17 lines (22 added, 5 removed). The two revision comparisons preserve the supported sibling-writer contract: partial postimages must never certify an already stale inventory as complete.

## Evidence

- A warmed post-completion regression fails on unchanged production with one worker operation where zero is required; it passes with this patch. The existing test now observes the shared worker transport, which also covers loads dispatched through `scope.execute`.
- Real service execution verifies the completed job state, immutable list/status behavior, and a sibling job added during execution. Pagination, filtering, snapshot reuse and failure diagnostics remain covered.
- `pnpm test src/cron/service.read-ops-nonblocking.test.ts src/cron/service.list-page-sort-guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 17 tests passed; 69.48 seconds command wall time, approximately 3.5 seconds test time. Cold worker compilation accounts for most local wall time. The exact-head PR CI workflow passed, including the selected cron/boundary tests, types, lint, architecture/source guards and UI E2E checks.
- Changed-file `oxfmt --check`, repository `run-oxlint.mjs` with the core config, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean, no actionable findings. The configured review route refused preflight because its provider selection did not match the operator config; no config was changed.
- No Testbox/Crabbox leases allocated; PR CI owns the broad gates.

## Measurement

An isolated Linux sandbox used the repository's production-shaped synthetic fixture: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 12 projects with real worktrees and 114 seeded cron jobs (115 after bootstrap). The agent database was approximately 4.6 GB. The Gateway used a private loopback port, its own home/config/state/temp directories, a 64-CPU allowed scope and 64 GB memory cap. No production database or Gateway was touched.

Baseline: `976cc974fab1912c696d1101bd17a1abf05eb77e`; patched production sources: `7430401917f9d68be0f92dba3655d423f45b0370`. Each runtime was built with `pnpm build:runtime` for measurement only. Source checksums matched the committed patch. No builds or broad test gates ran locally.

The driver used real WebSocket RPCs, a compact 50-row page including disabled jobs, five warmup iterations, 150 warm-read samples per order and 60 completion-read samples per order. Synthetic system-event jobs were forced through `cron.run` with terminal waiting; pacing respected its 30-per-minute rate limit and occurred outside the timed read window. List and status were each requested first in separate passes.

| Read requested first | Case | Before p50 / p99 (ms) | After p50 / p99 (ms) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `cron.list` | Warm | 0.31 / 8.85 | 0.34 / 7.85 |
| `cron.list` | After completion | 2.07 / 13.04 | 2.17 / 9.09 |
| `cron.status` | Warm | 0.20 / 8.51 | 0.21 / 9.22 |
| `cron.status` | After completion | 0.68 / 8.80 | 0.69 / 2.72 |

The RPC median result is neutral: list 2.07 → 2.17 ms and status 0.68 → 0.69 ms after completion. Observed first-read tails were lower (list 13.04 → 9.09 ms; status 8.80 → 2.72 ms), but with 60 samples p99 is the maximum and is not a robust tail estimate. Warm reads remain in the same sub-millisecond median range; their alternate-order p99 samples also varied by several milliseconds. This is a bounded removal of a proven redundant worker fetch, not a claim that the reported 1.7–1.9 second production stalls are eliminated. It lands under the requested-change/no-regression rule with the neutral median result stated explicitly.

Full PR CI: [run 38503348738](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38503348738), successful on exact head `7430401917f9d68be0f92dba3655d423f45b0370`; all 59 reported checks passed with no failed or pending checks. No CI retries or baseline-failure exception were needed.

prs.title: perf(plugins): avoid cloning payloads for metadata subscriptions
prs.body:
Related: #171534

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins that need tool IDs and phases still pay to clone large tool results when they subscribe to completion events.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can opt into metadata-only event delivery without copying tool output. Existing subscriptions retain full payloads by default. Opted-in handlers receive only own enumerable top-level `data` fields containing strings of at most 256 characters, numbers, booleans, or null; other values and accessors are omitted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host filters metadata before cloning, rather than asking each plugin to discard a full clone. Stream/phase filtering and terminal run-context cleanup keep their existing behavior. This follows the phase-filter capability in #171534 and enables Advisor to observe tool settlement cheaply.

## Evidence

- Before the dispatch change, the new metadata snapshot regression failed while default and explicit full-payload cases passed.
- `host-hooks.contract.test.ts`: 67 passed, including invalid payload-mode registration cases.
- `agent-event-payload.contract.test.ts` and `run-context-lifecycle.contract.test.ts`: 29 passed. Getter-backed payloads remain unread for metadata handlers; primitive/length filtering, clone isolation, default full delivery, and terminal cleanup are covered.
- Scoped Oxfmt and Oxlint passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` passed.
- Madge import-cycle check: 0 cycles.

No whole-run performance percentage is claimed; the getter-based contract proves that metadata subscribers do not read or clone discarded payloads.

prs.title: fix(text): replies quoting tool-call XML re-parse the whole reply on every streamed delta
prs.body:
Closes #171363

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: once a streamed reply quotes tool-call markup anywhere, even inside a code example (for example a fenced `<function_calls>` / `<invoke>` / `<parameter>` block), the Gateway re-parses the whole reply as Markdown on every later delta, so a 20k-character answer costs about 17 s of Gateway main-thread CPU instead of under 0.1 s.

## User Impact

User impact: replies that explain or debug tool-call formats stream without holding the Gateway event loop. In the handler path a 20k-character reply with a fenced tool-call example drops from about 16.8 s to about 1.4 s; replies without such markup are unchanged. Visible text is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`toolCallXmlTextFilter` was an activated projector: after the first `<`, every delta re-ran `stripToolCallXmlTagsInternal` on the whole reply, which runs `findCodeRegions` (a full micromark parse) whenever a tool-call token appears anywhere, plus a second parse in `unwrapStandaloneParameterTags` for `<parameter`.

The filter now gets a `create()` built on `createSettledCodeProjector`, which reuses the settledness rule maintainers wrote for reply directives in #166782 (`findDirectiveCodePrefix`): block code that ends at or before `retainStart`, or inline code inside a completed paragraph without a reference candidate. The transform only acts at tool-call tokens (`TOOL_CALL_QUICK_RE`) and at an unfinished tag head at the end of the text; every other `<` stays literal however the text grows. Once every such marker sits in code whose ownership cannot change, later appends that add no new marker skip the transform. Anything uncertain still runs the full transform.

- The settledness rule moves from `src/utils/directive-tags.ts` into `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts` (`startsLineAfter`, `findSettledCodeEnd`) so directives and tool-call markup share one owner instead of two copies. `inlineDirectiveDisplayTextFilter.create()` now uses the same projector, which replaces its hand-written copy of the policy; `findDirectiveCodePrefix` keeps its result for the stream owner.
- Markers that can never settle (tool tags in prose, inline code in list items, headings, or tables) keep main's per-delta transform. Failed proofs are spaced geometrically, and the proof is skipped when the text has no code delimiter, so those shapes cost the same as on `main`.
- The one-shot transforms in `handlers.messages.snapshot.ts` and `handlers.messages.stream.ts` are unchanged; they are most of the remaining cost and would need owner-held projection state, so I left them out of this change.

## Evidence

### Running Gateway with a real WebSocket client

The built `dist` of the base (`1a5f3774fcd`) and of this branch (`3bb7f7f8162`) ran side by side on loopback with isolated state and a scripted local mock OpenAI provider. A real operator WebSocket client did `sessions.messages.subscribe` + `chat.send`; a second client polled `health` every 200 ms. The `toolxml` reply opens with a fenced `xml` tool-call example (`<function_calls>`, `<invoke name="exec">`, `<parameter name="command">`) and continues with ordinary Markdown (headings, prose, lists with inline code, Python fences); `control` is the same body without the example. Cumulative 3 to 6 character deltas at 250 deltas/s, 3 interleaved runs per tree per cell, medians from `chat.send` to `final`:

| Path | Reply | Main-thread CPU, base → this PR | Wall, base → this PR | `health` p50 while streaming | Event-loop delay p99 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Responses `final_answer` | toolxml 8k | 10,334 → 2,697 ms | 11.3 → 7.7 s | 10.1 → 1.2 ms | 34 → 9 ms |
| Responses `final_answer` | toolxml 20k | 54,335 → 6,914 ms | 55.8 → 18.5 s | 17.4 → 1.3 ms | 70 → 8 ms |
| raw (no phase) | toolxml 8k | 6,347 → 2,686 ms | 8.1 → 7.8 s | 3.0 → 1.2 ms | 28 → 11 ms |
| raw (no phase) | toolxml 20k | 29,769 → 6,320 ms | 31.8 → 18.5 s | 12.3 → 1.3 ms | 48 → 14 ms |
| both | control 8k / 20k | same (1.0x in all four cells) | same | same | same |

- On the base, the 20k Responses run keeps the main thread about 99% busy for the whole 62 s: the provider finishes after about 19 s, when live chat has delivered 10,679 of 20,020 characters, and the backlog drains over the next 43 s. On this branch live chat tracks the provider within about 100 characters.
- With this change the `toolxml` reply costs about what `control` does (6.9 s vs 6.2 s at 20k).
- CPU profiles of the 20k `toolxml` runs: `stripToolCallXmlTagsInternal` is 84% (46.3 s) of busy main-thread time on the base and 12% (0.64 s) on this branch for Responses, 81% (25.3 s) versus 20% (0.90 s) for raw; `parseMarkdownOwnership` follows the same curve. What remains is mostly the end-of-message snapshot and final sanitize passes, which call `transform` directly.
- Delivered text is unchanged: in all 56 sessions the final `chat` event and `chat.history` after a Gateway restart (`maxChars: 200000`) match the scripted reply byte for byte, with one SHA-256 per fixture across both trees.
- The OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions path does not stream these replies per delta on either tree (its reasoning-tag partitioner withholds text after the second code construct), so the raw projection was measured through a phase-less Responses stream instead; see capture (vi).

### Captured output from those runs

Raw captures from two built Gateways (main = PR base, fix = PR head) running side by side on loopback (`gateway run --bind loopback --auth none`, isolated state, OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1) with a scripted local mock OpenAI provider, a real operator WebSocket client (sessions.messages.subscribe + chat.send) and a second client polling `health` every 200 ms. Only local paths, ports and pids are redacted.

Paths: `resp` = OpenAI Responses stream whose message item has phase final_answer (visible-stream projection); `raw` = the same stream without a phase (raw projection, as for messages without phase). Fixtures: `toolxml` = short explanation + fenced ```xml example with <function_calls>/<invoke name="exec">/<parameter name="command">, then long Markdown (headings, prose, lists with inline code, Python fences); `control` = the same body without the example. 3-6 char cumulative deltas at 250 deltas/s; 3 interleaved runs per tree per cell after one warm-up turn per path.

prs.title: fix(ci): Security Review stays pending when GitHub fails large CI job pages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Security Review leaves the combined `openclaw/ci-gate` status pending when GitHub persistently returns 5xx for a 100-job page of a CI attempt.

## User Impact

PRs whose CI attempt hits this GitHub failure now get a final Security Review result in the same run instead of a pending combined status that blocks native landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

On 2026-10-13, CI run 38447134368 attempt 2 for PR #170343 consistently returned HTTP 502 for `attempts/2/jobs?per_page=100`, while `per_page=50` and `per_page=30` succeeded and attempt 1 (97 jobs) listed fine at 100. Each 502 takes about 10 seconds. The shared client retries `GET` 5xx in-request with 1/2/4-second waits inside its 30-second request deadline, so the slow 502s surfaced as a read timeout rather than a 502. Read timeouts restart the complete evaluation, which requested the same URL again until Security Review run 38450787473 (attempts 2 and 3) reported `GitHub API recovery budget exhausted; security review remains incomplete.`

The CI job listing now reads at 100, then 50, then 25 jobs per page. Above 25, a 5xx is not retried in-request (new `retryServerErrors` request option; it defaults to `true`, so every other caller is unchanged), and the same job range is requested again at half size: page `p` at size `s` becomes page `2p - 1` at size `s / 2`. The 25-job floor keeps the existing read retries, 30-second deadline, and recovery restarts. Enumeration must still reach GitHub's reported `total_count`, so incomplete or inconsistent listings fail closed as before.

Read timeouts are intentionally not a fallback trigger: after a read deadline the reviewed design restarts with fresh PR, approval, role, and CI data (#156176), and that remains true. Accepted tradeoffs: a transient 5xx at size 100 moves the rest of that listing to smaller pages (more requests, same result), and the existing 100-page cap now bounds a floor-size listing at 2,500 jobs (CI currently has about 100).

Release-note context: CI-internal Security Review reliability fix; no user-facing product change.

## Evidence

- New CLI-level regressions in `test/scripts/security-review-script.test.ts` run the real script against the fake GitHub API: a 502 for `per_page=100` only on the first page; a 502 for page 2 at 100 and page 3 at 50, which exercises both range mappings, with any off-range request answered by 404; and every size failing, where only the 25-job floor uses the 1/2/4-second retries and the review fails closed. All three fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- Security Review suites (`security-review-script`, `dependency-guard-script`, `security-sensitive-guard-script`, `security-review-event`, `security-review-rollout`, `security-review-workflow`): 6 files, 430 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, scoped oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Live read-only API check on 2026-10-13: `actions/runs/38447134368/attempts/2/jobs?per_page=100&page=1` returned 502 after about 10 seconds; `per_page=50&page=1` returned 50 jobs with `total_count: 97`.
- No production status, comment, or rerun was triggered during validation.
- Independent Codex review (P2 scope, with the full script, shared client, and fixtures as context): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Review governance: landed at the direction of @steipete, an active openclaw-secops member and organization admin. The live `Require CODEOWNERS review` ruleset exempts openclaw-secops; the team review request stays open for post-merge review.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session Stop leaving a Codex parent blocked for new messages or rewind when its native child had already been interrupted.

## User Impact

Stop can retire that child and release the parent's ownership claim without resetting the session, losing history, or stopping a sibling request.

## Why This Change Was Made

An interrupted native turn is already terminal, but its resumable task still needs cancellation settlement. Reuse the exact recorded interruption and the existing cancellation owner instead of trying to interrupt the finished turn again. Caller custody, current-assignment, and session-generation checks stay intact. The existing deadline wait moves unchanged into a sibling module to keep the oversized monitor from growing.

No configuration, schema, or public SDK changes.

## Evidence

- The new owner-boundary regression fails before the fix with incomplete cancellation and passes afterward. It verifies that selected interrupted children release the real parent claim, while unselected children retain it.
- 35 focused tests pass across cancellation, direct authority/follow-ups, and session retirement: `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.cancellation.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.direct-authority.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-retirement.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (116.91s wrapper wall time). The final changed-file run passed 10 cases in 152.16s; individual cases took 4–37ms, with cold worker compilation/import startup accounting for the wrapper cost.
- Independent AutoReview through P2: no actionable findings.
- Full `pnpm build` passes (36m 1.8s cold build). Extension production/test types, targeted lint, formatting, line-cap, database-worker/dialect, timeout-race, and import-cycle checks pass. The test-types check caught a timer-cleanup callback returning the Vitest helper; it now returns `void`, and test types plus the changed test pass on recheck.
- The broader changed-file check is not fully green: the global mock-export guard has an inherited failure at `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.lazy.test.ts:212`. It reproduces against the untouched base `f36f240ab323` with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --staged --base f36f240ab323` before staging this fix. The production dead-export scan also flags `ui/src/components/web-awesome.ts:26` (`consumeDropdownKeyboardDismissal`), which is byte-identical to the base and has only test consumers there. Neither unrelated finding was hidden with an allowance or repaired in this PR.
- Checked the native interrupt contract against [Codex rust-v0.162.1](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs#L1610): a finished turn can return `no active turn to interrupt`.

Proof uses isolated state and a fake Codex transport. The original live session and Gateway were not changed or used for validation; this PR fixes the reproduced failure condition, not a conclusively attributed live incident.

prs.title: fix: avoid duplicate deferred tool results
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #169492. Deferred tool execution used to serialize a target's structured payload twice: once in its text content and again in `result.details`. Keep the model-facing result's content and status fields, but retain the complete result only in the control tool's structured details for runtime/UI consumers. Images and termination/error handling remain intact.

Original fix by @TUARAN; reported in #169492.

## Evidence

Built CLI, isolated state, recording OpenAI-compatible scripted provider. The scripted turn searches for `sessions_list`, dispatches it, then records the next provider request. State was created through the shipped agent command, not database writes.

Captured, redacted output:
```text
                         structured count payload occurrences   nested result.details
base deferred                           2                              present
candidate deferred                      1                              absent
base direct                             1                              absent
candidate direct                        1                              absent
```

The direct-call control retains the same result fields (`count`, `sessions`, `hasMore`, `limitApplied`). Session identifiers and timestamps naturally differ between isolated runs. Current main renamed the deferred dispatcher from `tool_call` to `dispatch_action`; the integrated candidate uses that shipped name.

Exact-head checks: 60 Tool Search tests passed; changed-file formatting and lint passed. Simplification retained the existing result-projection owner and extended the existing regression rather than adding scaffolding. Production delta: +4/-7; tests: +2/-1.

Live gate on `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, explicitly using the OpenClaw runtime:
```text
tool_search -> sessions_list discovered
dispatch_action -> sessions_list(limit=1) returned one session
final: Success — I found `sessions_list` and listed one session.
exit=0
```
The persisted live transcript confirms both tool execution and the final reply.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous context projection without changing persisted state or configuration. Blast radius is model context for deferred Tool Search calls; direct tool calls are unchanged. Runtime/UI consumers still receive the complete structured result.
