prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: perf(ui): avoid duplicate auth refreshes after config reloads
prs.body:
Closed as superseded by #171579 (merged as `120e515260d7b029f5f70c3d98fa372ccabf91f7` during profiling). Current main has the same production fix and a stronger regression. The duplicate CI run was stopped after supersession; no separate production change remains to land here.

## What Problem This Solves

A Control UI connected during a Gateway configuration reload requests provider authentication status twice: once when the configuration commits and again when the prepared model runtime publishes its authentication change.

## User Impact

Chat, sidebar health, and account views share the existing authentication result until the Gateway publishes the replacement. Real authentication changes, reconnects, identity changes, explicit refreshes, and credential deadlines still refresh it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the generic `config.changed` authentication invalidation and let `chat.metadata.changed` own it. The first notification precedes runtime preparation; reading there creates redundant work and can display an intermediate result. UI and Gateway ship together. This removes one production line and adds no cache, timer, configuration option, dependency, or compatibility path.

## Evidence

Headless Chromium against an isolated Gateway with synthetic production-shaped state: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, 12 projects, and a 4.3 GiB agent database. Measurements use dedicated dev servers; no production Gateway load.

- Three logging-only hot reloads per revision: baseline **2, 2, 2 `models.authStatus` RPCs**, candidate **1, 1, 1** (50% fewer). `sessions.list` stays **4 per reload** and reconnects stay **0** in both. Script time ranges overlap (baseline 0.293–0.585 s, candidate 0.360–0.381 s); no wall-clock speedup claim. Four simultaneous mock streaming sessions, ten send waves / 40 sends across 15 minutes: zero JavaScript exceptions. Sandbox uncollected heap was 126.1 MiB at 30 seconds and 139.3 MiB at 15 minutes, then 92.2 MiB after GC; samples ranged 80.6–273.5 MiB. The Mac run ended at 90.6 MiB after GC. Conversation history grew and controlled hot reloads occurred during the sandbox run, so these are bounded observations, not a leak-free guarantee.
- Baseline populated sidebar first paint: 3.4 seconds locally; 3.3–4.9 seconds in the Linux sandbox dev build, including selecting All owners and opening Coding. Sidebar rendering stays bounded; explicitly paging rendered 250 rows from the 5,000-session fixture. This change makes no cold-load or rendering-speed claim.
- Regression at the application event boundary fails before the change (expected zero auth reads at the config commit, received one). Afterward, 56 tests pass across `app-host.chat-metadata`, `model-auth`, and `sidebar-attention-store`, run with `--maxWorkers=1`.
- Changed-file oxfmt, repository oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass. PR CI passed the boot CSS/JS budget, security review, docs, lint, UI end-to-end shard 1, and several test lanes before supersession. Remaining duplicate CI was cancelled after the equivalent fix landed; no complete green claim for this duplicate head. No local builds or Testbox/Crabbox leases for validation.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P2+ findings. Reviewed auth consumers, cache lifecycle, Gateway metadata publication, and auth-affecting configuration reload producers. The autoreview helper refused startup because the selected route did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

Production delta excluding tests and docs: **2 insertions, 3 deletions (−1 line)**. This is a behavior-only refresh simplification with no visual appearance or asset changes.

prs.title: fix(pr): tooling root refresh aborts when the root is thousands of commits behind
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `scripts/pr` aborts with `spawnSync git ENOBUFS` when it refreshes a selected tooling root (`OPENCLAW_PR_TOOLING_ROOT`) that is thousands of commits behind `main`.

## User Impact

Maintainers whose separate tooling checkout has fallen far behind can run `scripts/pr` again without manually fast-forwarding and reinstalling that checkout first. Fetch and fast-forward progress now appears on stderr, without a multi-megabyte diffstat.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refresh ran `git fetch` and `git merge --ff-only` through the same helper that captures output for read-only Git queries, with Node's 1 MiB default buffer. Nothing reads the output of those two steps. On a root about 4,200 commits behind, Git finished the fast-forward and then printed a diffstat larger than the buffer, so the wrapper died after the checkout had changed and before `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` ran.

The two mutating steps now stream to stderr instead of being captured, and the merge passes `--no-stat`. Streaming removes the size limit for any fetch, merge, or hook output; `--no-stat` keeps a large catch-up from flooding the terminal. The clean-main rechecks around fetch, merge, and install, the single-refresh rule, and the canonical-checkout refusal are unchanged.

## Evidence

- New row in the existing tooling-root refresh test (`test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts`): a post-merge hook emits 1.2 MB during the fast-forward (Git sends hook stdout to its stderr). Against the previous wrapper it fails with the incident's exact `spawnSync /usr/bin/git ENOBUFS`; with the fix it refreshes, installs once, re-verifies, and the 1.2 MB reaches the operator's stderr.
- A literal fixture (4,000 new long paths, 1.24 MB diffstat) also reproduced `ENOBUFS` before the fix and passed after it. It was not kept because checking out those files cost 20–40 s on a loaded host; the hook row costs about 3.7 s.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 78/78 passed. The whole file took 824 s wall time on a heavily loaded host (load average 60–108 on 32 cores); the new row took about 3.7 s.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, oxlint on the test, `oxfmt --check`, `bash -n scripts/pr`, `node --check` on the embedded Node block, and `git diff --check`: clean.

Release-note context: maintainer tooling only (`scripts/pr`); no product behavior change.

prs.title: fix(codex): use monotonic clock for migration marketplace discovery deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During `openclaw migrate codex`, the plugin marketplace discovery polling loop can hang far longer than the configured 30s timeout (or timeout prematurely) if the system clock adjusts via NTP correction or sleep/resume. The fix switches the discovery deadline from `Date.now()` (wall clock) to `performance.now()` (monotonic) so the budget stays bounded across clock domains.

- **Problem:** `requestTargetCodexAppServerJson` in `extensions/codex/src/migration/apply.ts` seeds its deadline and computes remaining budget with `Date.now()` (wall clock), but both downstream consumers — `requestCodexAppServerJson({timeoutMs})` → `withTimeout` → `setTimeout`, and `sleep(waitMs)` → `setTimeout` — measure elapsed time with the monotonic clock. A wall-clock rewind inflates `remainingMs`/`waitMs` beyond the configured budget; a forward jump shrinks them, prematurely tripping the deadline.
- **Solution:** Replace all 6 `Date.now()` calls in the polling loop with `performance.now()`, aligning the deadline with the monotonic clock used by the downstream timers.
- **What changed:** `extensions/codex/src/migration/apply.ts` — 6 `Date.now()` → `performance.now()` in `requestTargetCodexAppServerJson` + 2-line comment. New regression test `apply-deadline-real-transport.test.ts`.
- **What did NOT change:** No new parser, policy branch, or configuration surface. The discovery logic, poll interval, and timeout constants are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the same cross-clock-domain bug pattern fixed in the sibling function `buildCodexPluginThreadConfigWithinDeadline` by #155863 (BUG-088). That PR switched `plugin-thread-config-deadline.ts` from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()`. This PR applies the identical fix to the other deadline in the same module — `requestTargetCodexAppServerJson` in `migration/apply.ts` — which was identified during the same anchor sweep but is an independent function in a different file.

- **Best fix:** Direct `Date.now()` → `performance.now()` replacement at the canonical owner (the polling loop itself). No wrapper or helper needed — the function is the sole owner of this deadline.
- **Risk:** `performance.now()` returns sub-millisecond floats, but both consumers internally floor or clamp the value, so no `Math.floor` is needed. Node 16+ provides global `performance`.

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw migrate codex` will no longer experience marketplace discovery polling that exceeds the configured timeout budget when the system clock adjusts (NTP correction, sleep/resume). The migration's plugin discovery phase will respect the 30s default timeout regardless of wall-clock fluctuations.

## Evidence

**Real Codex transport before → after** (real spawned `codex app-server` subprocess + production `CodexAppServerClient` + real stdio JSON-RPC + real `plugin/list` responses; only the wall clock is skewed ±120s):

```console
$ CODEX_APP_SERVER_BIN=codex node --import tsx/esm proof-real-codex.ts
PROOF_REAL_CODEX variant=date delta=-120000 clientInitialized=true
PROOF_REAL_CODEX variant=date delta=0 clientInitialized=true
PROOF_REAL_CODEX variant=date delta=120000 clientInitialized=true
PROOF_REAL_CODEX variant=performance delta=-120000 clientInitialized=true
PROOF_REAL_CODEX variant=performance delta=0 clientInitialized=true
PROOF_REAL_CODEX variant=performance delta=120000 clientInitialized=true
PROOF_TRACE [{"variant":"pre-fix (Date.now deadline)","deltaMs":-120000,"armedTimerMs":149987,"bounded":false,"ok":true},
 {"variant":"pre-fix (Date.now deadline)","deltaMs":0,"armedTimerMs":29965,"bounded":true,"ok":true},
 {"variant":"pre-fix (Date.now deadline)","deltaMs":120000,"armedTimerMs":1,"bounded":true,"ok":true},
 {"variant":"post-fix (performance.now deadline)","deltaMs":-120000,"armedTimerMs":29978,"bounded":true,"ok":true},
 {"variant":"post-fix (performance.now deadline)","deltaMs":0,"armedTimerMs":29983,"bounded":true,"ok":true},
 {"variant":"post-fix (performance.now deadline)","deltaMs":120000,"armedTimerMs":29983,"bounded":true,"ok":true}]
```

The production `CodexAppServerClient` runs real `initialize` + `plugin/list` over the real codex process's stdio. Pre-fix the armed timer inflates to **149,987ms** on rewind and collapses to **1ms** on forward jump; post-fix all three skew cases keep the ~30,000ms budget (monotonic clock, immune to the wall clock).

| wall-clock skew | Before (main, `Date.now()`) | After (this PR, `performance.now()`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rewind −120s | armed timer **149,987ms** (30s budget inflates to ~150s) | armed timer **29,978ms** |
| stable 0s | armed timer **29,965ms** | armed timer **29,983ms** |
| forward +120s | armed timer **1ms** (budget collapses prematurely) | armed timer **29,983ms** |

**In-process regression test** (real request owner, in-memory transport, fake timers):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/migration/apply-deadline-real-transport.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
PROOF_TRACE [{"requestIndex":1,"armedTimeoutMs":30000,"bounded":true},
 {"requestIndex":2,"armedTimeoutMs":29750,"bounded":true},
 {"requestIndex":3,"armedTimeoutMs":29750,"bounded":true},
 {"requestIndex":4,"armedTimeoutMs":29750,"bounded":true}]
Tests  1 passed
```

Pre-fix RED: `expected 150000 to be less than or equal to 60000`.

**What was not tested**: a real OS clock shift was not induced; the skew is injected by stepping `Date.now()` between the deadline seed and the remaining-budget read. `Date.now()` reads `CLOCK_REALTIME` (affected by NTP), so spy-ing it to return a rewound value is functionally identical to an OS-level clock correction.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): autofill short transcripts after placement settles
prs.body:
Related: #171009

## What Problem This Solves

Reloading a short conversation should fill the transcript without requiring a wheel gesture or a click on **Show earlier**. #171009 correctly stopped older-history requests during initial placement, but also removed that settled viewport fill.

## User Impact

Short visible transcripts automatically fill with older messages after placement settles. Conversations whose first page already fills the viewport do not page older history at boot.

## Why This Change Was Made

This restores filling inside the existing history owner. It starts only after placement settles, with a presented, visible pane and document, outside programmatic or maintenance scrolling. The first page must actually underfill the viewport; subsequent pages fill through the existing prefetch edge, with a hard limit of three automatic pages per open. Automatic fills do not stage an extra background page. Reader-driven paging retains staged prefetch and the existing failure backoff.

The cold-load campaign measured two unnecessary older-history requests totaling roughly 1.5–2 MB during a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link before #171009. That regression must remain fixed: a first page that already overflows must make zero boot `chat.history` requests.

Production delta: +20 lines in `chat-pane-history.ts` (+26/-6), required by the explicit three-page allowance and separate prefetch policy. The superseded no-autofill assertions and manual-input steps are removed. No new configuration, Gateway schema, or durable record changes.

## Evidence

Validation so far: all 11 new owner tests pass, including automatic fill, the cap, exhaustion, failure backoff, hidden panes/background tabs, initial placement, and programmatic/maintenance scrolling. The existing history suite passes all 26 tests, including reader paging and staged prefetch. `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-history-autofill.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 37.85 seconds wall time; the changed existing history test file took 82.12 seconds on the loaded development host. Independent Codex autoreview is clean through P2. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.

AWS Crabbox focused proof on `f2e98dece9aa` passed 40 unit tests and all 25 E2E cases across seven files (lease `cbx_6d846f049a4c`). Browser coverage includes two automatic older pages without input for a short transcript, zero boot history requests for a long transcript, empty/hidden-activity windows, stale geometry, deep reveal, transcript search, and prepend anchoring. The only subsequent change scopes the optional screenshot capture to the existing active-transcript locator, fixing an unused-variable lint error, plus required block braces in the unit fixture, followed by rebasing.

Full UI E2E, changed-file checks, the before/after Team-scale history census, and exact-head CI are running for `82fd42a62859` on AWS lease `cbx_fc16ee9eb287`. Results will replace this paragraph before handoff. Earlier setup/interrupted runs are not claimed as passing proof.

Release-note context: restore automatic older-history loading for short visible transcripts without paging full history windows at startup.

Please leave landing to the campaign lead; this PR must not merge automatically.

prs.title: fix(release): expose Linux builder admission and retain failed bundles
prs.body:
Closes #170291

## What Problem This Solves

Linux release requests do not expose their actual downstream builder/admission in publication status, and failed packaging checks discard completed bundle bytes needed for diagnosis.

## User Impact

Release operators can follow the exact request attempt to its builder and see receiver admission separately from dispatch acknowledgement. Completed failed-build bundles are retained for 14 days as explicitly unqualified diagnostics. Signing and publication eligibility are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Linux workflow now records its request, tooling, builder, selected source, and admission outcome. The existing bounded FRV reader consumes that evidence and reports an absent child as awaiting admission, a stale-main rejection as rejected, and terminal builder results without treating them as publication qualification. Correlation titles select candidates only; authenticated receiver artifacts own admission. Historical dispatches missing an exact attempt remain unknown rather than adopting a newer request attempt.

Failure-only diagnostic uploads contain completed `.deb`/AppImage bytes, source/tooling identity, failed-check outcomes, and checksums. They never expose the artifact IDs used by signing. This reuses existing workflow artifacts and readers, with no durable cache, new recovery dispatch, permission change, or alternate signing path. Production growth implements the previously absent read-only Linux surface and its owner evidence (net +297 lines including workflow code); tests add 254 lines.

## Evidence

- [Observed packaging failure, run 37763337117](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37763337117): build, finalization, and staging passed; packaged runtime failed; normal bundle uploads and signing/publication skipped. Its artifacts retain runtime logs but not completed bundles.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'exact Linux request|exact completed Linux bundle'`: 3 passed, 6.68s wall time. Runs production workflow shell bodies, checks exact receiver JSON and retained bundle bytes/checksums, and verifies that signing depends on the failed build and consumes only qualified artifact IDs.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/frv.release.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'correlates the Linux builder'`: 6 passed, 14.52s wall time. Exercises real CLI transport/artifact boundaries for awaiting admission, exact admission, stale-main rejection, wrong source, foreign request, and unknown historical attempt.
- Existing Windows/readback sibling scenarios passed (9 total focused FRV tests, 17.77s wall time before the final historical-attempt case).
- `pnpm test test/scripts/linux-updater-manifest.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'same-tag request|earlier request|requests Linux|dispatch'`: 9 passed, 11.96s wall time.
- Regression controls against pinned pre-fix main fail: admitted Linux observation is absent; failed-bundle retention has no owner step. Original source bytes were restored afterward.
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, targeted script/root-test oxlint, formatting, `git diff --check`, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, and `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH pnpm check:workflows`: passed. Initial workflow check correctly rejected the system Python 3.9 prerequisite; the installed supported Python runtime was used without changing product code.
- Fresh independent autoreview: scoped clean at P0/P1, no actionable findings.
- Live GitHub GET proof and official contracts: [workflow-run filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs#list-workflow-runs-for-a-workflow), [workflow_run default-branch identity](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_run), and [pinned artifact action](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/tree/043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a). Request creation-time filtering returned two current-day builders rather than all eleven historical runs; no head-SHA filter hides stale-main rejection.

No real release build, signing, publication, or recovery was dispatched for this PR. Retained diagnostics support exact-byte inspection/checker reruns but do not implement full requalification without rebuilding. Prior-head CI 38314104129 passed 40 jobs with 26 skipped in 991 seconds wall time. That is historical proof for 513eeb0be8e1eedfb54e70befbea93c0a2c55a11, not the corrected head. Corrected-head [CI 38504601578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38504601578) passed: 40 jobs successful, 26 skipped, 484 seconds wall time, at exact head `83221c6a3d8e4a73a164b198e0e498a069d50ee1`. Companion platform checks remain in progress; the separately dispositioned CodeQL check remains failed.

## Review follow-through

- Corrected the actionable unconfirmed-dispatch finding in `83221c6a3d8e4a73a164b198e0e498a069d50ee1`. Producer failures before any request now remain `dispatch-unconfirmed`, not `awaiting-admission`. The existing CLI table now covers the failed publisher job retaining evidence with no request ID.
- Red control: that exact CLI case failed before the correction (`awaiting-admission` versus expected `dispatch-unconfirmed`), 5.16s wrapper wall time. After correction, 12 selected Linux/Windows/publication cases pass in 28.30s (26.16s Vitest); targeted script/root-tooling lint and typecheck, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Correction delta: production +3/-3, tests +21/-22.
- Hosted request-to-builder release execution and real diagnostic upload remain unrun: they require an actual release operation, outside this review-only handoff. Existing production shell and CLI boundary fixtures establish the changed contracts; no live-after-fix release claim is made.

### CodeQL annotation disposition

The cache-poisoning annotations in `build_linux` (diagnostic retention on the prior head, AppImage finalization on the corrected head) model selected-tag build execution under `workflow_dispatch`. That path is unreachable: `validate_release` explicitly requires `workflow_run`, and `build_linux` needs successful `validate_release` (no `always()` override). Manual dispatch runs only `mirror_legacy`, using protected tooling rather than selected-tag build code. The [upstream query](https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/main/actions/ql/src/Security/CWE-349/CachePoisoningViaPoisonableStep.ql) and [query contract](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/actions/actions-cache-poisoning-poisonable-step/) were checked directly.

Read-only hosted proof: [manual mirror run 38461571528](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38461571528) succeeded while validation, all selected-tag builds, signing, and publication were skipped. Evaluating this PR's actual validation expression likewise rejects `workflow_dispatch`; the existing stale-request/credential-isolation tests pass (2 cases, 9.69s wrapper). The new retention step neither creates a cache nor executes the retained bundles. The annotation is dispositioned as a cross-job reachability false positive; the failed scanner result is not relabeled green, suppressed, or dismissed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): run CLI bridge tool calls in their own run's request scope
prs.body:
## Current disposition — October 11, 2026

The implementation in this PR has been incorporated into main by [#165432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165432), commit `fdcbcf5c2ebd83316f411d406315f08225949c59`, which credits Amrit Chana and adapts this PR's authority-chain regression. There is no remaining production fix to merge from this branch.

Current main uses a detached process context for listener startup, retains the Gateway's worker resources, records each grant's minting request scope, and restores that scope for its tool calls. Its HTTP coverage checks starter isolation, fresh replacement scopes, allowed owner dispatch, the write-only ceiling, closed requester refusal, and revoked-grant rejection.

Fresh verification on main `cbe0b272883c68210aee33b67e4bdf66d9106587`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-http.async-scope.test.ts` passed **6/6 tests** on macOS/Node 24.16.0. Vitest reported **221.45 s**, including cold transformation. This was HTTP/in-process authority boundary proof, not a new live Claude or channel test. No production or test changes were needed.

The v2026.10.1 tag predates the merged detached-context implementation, so the release-pinned follow-up remains relevant to that tag. The original branch's old CI/conflict state is historical; rebasing it would duplicate the implementation and weaker coverage already on main. This PR remains open and non-draft for maintainer disposition; no merge or closure was requested or performed.

---

## Original contributor proposal and historical evidence

Closes #157126

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Gateway restart that resumes an in-flight CLI-runtime turn (for example `claude-cli`), the owner's later chat turns fail admin-only tools with `missing scope: operator.admin` until the Gateway restarts again. The same leak also breaks a second owner turn once the first turn's connection has closed (`Gateway client authority closed before dispatching ...`).

## User Impact

User impact: owners of CLI-runtime agents keep their normal tool authority after a restart. Admin-only tools (automations with triggers, secrets, system and config tools) work from chat again. Lower-authority runs keep their own ceiling: the write-only restart-recovery run is still refused admin tools, and a run whose device was revoked mid-turn is still refused before its action. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loopback MCP listener is process-owned but starts lazily inside whichever Gateway request first needs it. Its handlers kept that request's scope and tool-caller identity. So every bridge tool call ran with the authority of whichever run started the listener, not the run making the call. If the restart-recovery continuation (a write-only system caller) started it, every later owner call was capped at `operator.write`.

The fix has two parts:

1. **The listener no longer inherits its starter.** It starts outside the tool-caller identity (`withoutGatewayToolCallerIdentity`) and outside the request scope (`withPluginRuntimeGatewayContextResolver(..., { inheritRequestScope: false })`), keeping only the Gateway context resolver. This matches the rule already applied to follow-up and scheduled runs.
2. **Each bridge call runs in its own run's request scope.** A CLI client grant now records the Gateway request scope it was minted in (`mintMcpLoopbackClientGrant`, called while the run's request is active), and the handler re-enters that scope for the grant's tool calls. That is what in-process runtimes already get implicitly, so dispatch sees the calling run's own client: its scopes stay the ceiling, and its `hasCurrentClientAuthority` liveness still applies.

Part 1 alone would have removed the accidental ceiling without restoring the intended one. With no scope, a write-only recovery run and a revoked run both completed an admin-only call in live testing. Part 2 is why those runs are still refused (see the proof below).

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Setup.** This PR's branch at `3ff6fbe1d78`, built, running as an isolated foreground Gateway (`openclaw --profile <test> gateway run`, loopback, its own state dir, clean environment). macOS arm64, Node v26.8.2, OpenClaw `2026.9.6 (3ff6fbe)`. Agent `main` runs `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5`. Owner turns come from `openclaw agent --agent main` on a local CLI device paired with `operator.admin` (`senderIsOwner: true`). The admin-only action is the `secrets` tool with `action: "list"` (`secrets.store.list`, needs `operator.admin`). Heartbeat, Bonjour, and dreaming are off, so no other system run can start the bridge first.

Steps:
1. **step0**: owner turn on a fresh Gateway calls `secrets` list.
2. **step0b**: a second owner turn in the same process.
3. **step1**: an owner turn runs a 90 s probe script, then calls `secrets` list. Mid-probe the Gateway is restarted (`gateway restart --wait 5s`). The drain runs out, the turn is marked for recovery, and the restart-recovery continuation (a write-only system caller) is the first CLI run after startup, so it starts the bridge. It then calls `secrets` list itself.
4. **step2**: after recovery settles, a new owner turn calls `secrets` list.
5. **step3** (fresh Gateway process): an owner turn runs the probe, and 5 s in the owner device's operator token is revoked (`devices revoke --role operator`, connection closed `4001 device removed`). After the probe, the run calls `secrets` list.

Results are the exact tool results the agent received, from the Claude Code stream in the Gateway log and `chat.history`. The "unpatched" column is the same checkout with `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts` reverted to `6907f58b136` (upstream main) and rebuilt. "Part 1 only" is this PR's first commit, `3b3536613b4`.

| Step | Caller | Unpatched main | Part 1 only | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| step0 | owner | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` |
| step0b | owner, 2nd turn | `Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.` | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` |
| step1 | restart recovery (system, write-only) | `missing scope: operator.admin` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`missing scope: operator.admin`** |
| step2 | owner, after recovery | `missing scope: operator.admin` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`The secret store is empty.`** |
| step3 | owner, device revoked mid-run | `Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.`** |

On unpatched main, step1 and step3 are refused only because each of those runs happened to start the bridge itself. On this PR they are refused by their own run's scope, whichever run started the listener.

Restart and recovery on this PR (Gateway log, local time, redacted):

```text
17:37:19.641 mcp loopback listening on <loopback>:<port>
17:37:56.086 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
17:38:01.088 [gateway] restart drain budget 4999.5ms exhausted; cutting short queueSize=1 embeddedRuns=1 activeTasks=1 sessionAdmissions=2 rootRequests=1
17:38:01.129 [main-session-restart-recovery] marked 1 interrupted main session(s) for restart recovery (gateway restart shutdown)
17:38:05.456 mcp loopback listening on <loopback>:<port>
17:38:05.460 [main-session-restart-recovery] started interrupted main session: agent:main:main
```

`secrets` tool results on this PR, in order (step0, step0b, recovery, step2):

```text
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
"tool_result","content":"missing scope: operator.admin","is_error":true
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
```

The refused call belongs to the recovery turn: in `chat.history` it follows the `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted by a gateway restart ...` continuation message, and step2's owner turn after it succeeds.

step3 on this PR (device revoked mid-run):

```text
17:41:27.494 [gateway] device token revoked device=<device-id> role=operator
17:41:27.495 [ws] → close code=4001 reason=device removed ... lastFrameMethod=agent
17:42:54.300 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5 durationMs=102068
"tool_result","content":"Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.","is_error":true
```

**Differences from the issue's scenario.** Owner turns come from the local CLI (`openclaw agent`, a device with `operator.admin`), not Control UI webchat. The restart is the supported foreground restart (`gateway restart --wait 5s`, in-process SIGUSR2 with a 5 s drain), not a LaunchAgent handoff. The admin-only tool is `secrets` list only.

### Tests

- `src/gateway/mcp-http.async-scope.test.ts`:
  - "does not retain the Gateway caller of the request that started it": the listener started inside a write-only request scope and a tool-caller identity; a later owner-token call sees neither, and the Gateway context resolver is preserved. Fails before part 1.
  - "runs each CLI grant's tool calls in the request scope that minted it": the listener is started under a write-only recovery scope; grants minted under an owner scope, under the recovery scope, and under no scope each see exactly their own client (`[owner, recovery, undefined]`). Fails without part 2 (`[undefined, undefined, undefined]`).
- `pnpm vitest run src/gateway/mcp-http src/gateway/mcp-grant-store src/agents/cli-runner/prepare`: 275 of 276 pass. The one failure, `mcp-http.keepalive.test.ts` › "keeps a GET notification stream alive and releases it during shutdown", fails identically on unmodified `origin/main` at `6907f58`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passes (exit 0).
- Autoreview (Codex), `--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: `scoped-clean`, "patch is correct" (0.78). Its sandbox could not read unchanged files or run tests; the tests above ran locally.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject malformed ChatGPT export encoding
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Memory Wiki accepts malformed UTF-8 in a ChatGPT JSON export and writes replacement characters into imported source pages.

## User Impact

User impact: a damaged export fails with a UTF-8 error before imported content is replaced. Valid Unicode exports, including a real U+FFFD character, continue to import.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reading as text silently repaired invalid bytes before JSON parsing. Read the same file as bytes, validate UTF-8, then use the existing parser. Array and object-envelope exports share this loader; import planning, rollback and compilation remain with their existing owners.

## Evidence

Product head `64393c1a84f718a9bad58292b8cf16611db2b77a`; RED base `44c918f3900770412a3cd912eaa0c718b2e3356c`. Both normal `pnpm build cliStartup` builds had matching clean-head stamps. Linux, Node 24.16.0.

Same real packaged CLI entry and fixtures on both versions:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs wiki chatgpt import --export "$EXPORT_FILE" --json
```

An isolated `memory-wiki` instance used a local vault/search backend. A valid array export first created `sources/chatgpt-undated-utf8smoke.md` with title/content `Café 🤖 �`. Subsequent array and `{conversations:[...]}` fixtures contained raw `ff` inside a JSON title; the surrounding JSON was otherwise valid. There were no model, channel or external-provider calls.

| Scenario | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valid Unicode seed | exit 0, 1 source page created | exit 0, 1 source page created |
| Malformed array export | exit 0, page title contains `�AD_BYTE` | exit 1, UTF-8 error, original page/index bytes retained |
| Malformed object envelope | exit 0, already-corrupted content accepted/skipped | exit 1, UTF-8 error, original page/index bytes retained |
| Valid Unicode envelope control | exit 0, refreshed content written | exit 0, refreshed content written |

Actual filesystem readback compared the full source page, `sources/index.md` and `index.md` bytes before and after each rejected input. Both input files were also unchanged. Head source-page SHA-256 was `f9cf3b65eecf9e8face80a2291b93e05d8ca19e5efa76a197e0b89d800b9115d` before and after both rejections. The final valid control changed the source to `Café 🤖 � refreshed`.

The packaged plugin CLI exercised the unmocked `loadConversations` owner and the real importer/compiler. Vault initialization occurs before loading; this does not claim that rejecting an export prevents every initialization/state write.

Validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: RED 2 failed / 18 passed; GREEN 20 passed, Vitest 28.50s, runner 34.53s. The regressions seed an existing page and distinguish malformed bytes from valid Unicode. Formatting, focused syntax lint and targeted type-aware lint/type checking passed. The type check used the native selected `memory-wiki` package-boundary artifact preparation and `extensions/tsconfig.json`. Independent adversarial review: PASS, no P0–P3 findings.

Scope: 2 files; production +6/-2, tests +28/-0. No new SDK seam, config/protocol/schema, permission, dependency or migration changes. The import CLI is the loader's only production caller.

Not tested: actual downloaded ChatGPT account data, optional external search backends or the full suite. No production service or user data was changed, and proof fixtures remain outside the product branch.

prs.title: fix(telegram): prevent dropped replies on IPv4-first dual-stack hosts
prs.body:
Fixes #171438

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram replies can be dropped on dual-stack hosts when `ipv4first` still allows Node to race an unreachable IPv6 route, or when a connection timeout is mistaken for an uncertain send.

## User Impact

Telegram honors IPv4-first selection without requiring `NODE_OPTIONS`. Explicit `autoSelectFamily` overrides remain effective. Proven connection failures can be retried by delivery recovery; failures that may have sent a message remain protected from blind replay. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Derive Telegram's default family-selection behavior from the resolved DNS order, preserving environment/config precedence, process IPv6-first ordering, the WSL2 default, and the existing 300 ms attempt timeout when family selection is enabled.

At the shared delivery owner, recognize `ETIMEDOUT` only when its syscall proves it occurred before sending. All aggregate branches must establish that proof; a mixed connect/read failure stays ambiguous. This uses the existing recovery policy and adds no detached or deferred effects.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. It covers the Telegram transport/config regressions and shared delivery-recovery tests, plus the repository's selected type, lint, build, and test lanes.

Regressions added:

- `honors $source $order DNS ordering and family selection`: fake dual-stack DNS, config/environment/process IPv4-first, and process IPv6-first.
- `preserves family selection overrides: $network`: explicit on/off overrides and verbatim defaults.
- `preserves typed and fallback retry policy for $name`: grammY-wrapped dual-stack connect timeout is retryable; a read timeout in the same aggregate is not.

Changed-file `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json` and `oxfmt --check` passed. Deslop found no safe unrelated deletion. Independent Codex autoreview was scoped-clean at P0–P2 with no actionable findings.

The type-aware lint wrapper with the core tsconfig reported two diagnostics on unchanged proxy-constructor union members in `fetch.ts` (lines 88–89); no suppressions were added. CI lint and production/test types passed with the normal prepared package graph.

Exact-head [CI run 38501132988](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501132988) passed all 43 jobs at `2a056749ad1ccc6f92e0441951b6be28f2349e00`, including the selected tests, lint, production/test types, docs, boundary checks, and QA smoke profiles. No failures or CI retries. Local tests, local typechecks, negative-control execution, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy.

prs.title: fix(mcp): preserve literal stdio executable and working paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `mcp add` silently changes quoted executable and working-directory paths containing surrounding whitespace.

## User Impact

User impact: the configured MCP server starts with the exact executable path and working directory supplied by the operator. Blank commands remain rejected and HTTP options keep their existing normalization.

## Why This Change Was Made

The flag adapter used a trimming string normalizer for filesystem paths. Use the existing nonblank-string reader for `--command` and `--cwd`, consistently with the runtime's existing literal-path behavior and the JSON configuration entry.

## Evidence

Product head `ce1e695bb7ac9d83c6a2dae1525f88c7ccc2eea0`; RED base `44c918f3900770412a3cd912eaa0c718b2e3356c`. Both were normal `pnpm build cliStartup` builds with matching clean-head stamps. Node 24.16.0, Linux/Ubuntu 22 container.

Same packaged CLI entries and scenarios on both versions, with isolated config/state:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs mcp add cwd-proof --command "$NODE" --arg "$SERVER" --cwd "$ROOT/work " --connect-timeout 5
node openclaw.mjs mcp show cwd-proof --json
node openclaw.mjs mcp add command-proof --command "$ROOT/node " --arg "$SERVER" --cwd "$ROOT/work" --connect-timeout 5
node openclaw.mjs mcp show command-proof --json
node openclaw.mjs mcp probe plain-proof --json
```

The fixture created both `work` and `work ` directories, plus a `node ` symlink to the real Node executable (no trimmed executable neighbor). Its local stdio MCP server responded to real `initialize` and `tools/list` requests and recorded `process.cwd()` to disk. All adds used the default production probe; none used `--no-probe`.

| Scenario | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quoted `work ` directory | add succeeds in wrong `work`; show stores trimmed path | add succeeds in exact `work `; show preserves path |
| Quoted `node ` executable | add exits 1, trimmed executable missing; no saved server or new initialization | add exits 0; real MCP initializes; show preserves executable |
| Ordinary executable/directory control | add and explicit probe succeed | add and explicit probe succeed |
| Whitespace-only command | exit 1; 0 additional MCP requests | exit 1; 0 additional MCP requests |

Recorder readback, with synthetic fixture root shortened:

```text
base cwd-proof: initialize cwd=$ROOT/work; tools/list cwd=$ROOT/work
head cwd-proof: initialize cwd=$ROOT/work[SPACE]; tools/list cwd=$ROOT/work[SPACE]
head command-proof: initialize and tools/list completed
```

Real CLI→MCP runtime→owned stdio child→MCP protocol→disk recorder and configuration readback crossed the complete affected boundary. The host's old glibc could not load the existing proc-safe native dependency; the proof therefore ran in an existing Ubuntu 22 image with no network, dropped capabilities, a read-only checkout/toolchain and separate writable synthetic state. The older Docker seccomp profile blocked Node thread creation, so this isolated proof used `seccomp=unconfined` with `no-new-privileges`. No product checks or native ownership guarantees were disabled.

Validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'preserves literal stdio paths|adds a configured MCP'`: GREEN 3 passed / 29 unselected, Vitest 19.27s, runner 89.41s. The two new literal-path rows failed before production changes. Existing HTTP flag/configuration coverage passed. Targeted type-aware lint/type checking and formatting passed. Independent adversarial review: PASS, no P0–P3 findings.

Scope: 2 files; production +3/-2, tests +26/-0. Runtime command/cwd owners already preserve raw paths and need no changes. No new options, config/schema/protocol, permission, dependency or upgrade changes.

Not tested: Windows executable paths, remote MCP servers, unrelated doctor checks or the remaining MCP/full repository suite. Synthetic child processes and proof containers exited; evidence files remain outside the product branch. No production instance changed.
