prs.title: fix(shell-env): unblock PATH discovery when login startup ignores termination
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway session catalog loading can wait indefinitely when login-shell startup ignores SIGTERM during automatic PATH discovery. Thanks to @zhangguiping-xydt for the report and original fix.

## User Impact

PATH preparation settles at its existing deadline, force-cleans the probe's detached process group, and lets subsequent lookups retry. The default timeout and synchronous environment import behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The spawn timeout only sends SIGTERM; it does not guarantee exit. The asynchronous probe must retain ownership of the deadline until process and output completion. This reuses the existing process-tree termination helper rather than adding another kill mechanism.

## Evidence

Built Linux arm64 artifacts, isolated HOME, real `/bin/bash` login startup, loopback Gateway, and shipped CLI command:

```sh
openclaw --profile p169507basefinalhang gateway call sessions.catalog.list \
  --params '{"catalogId":"opencode"}' --url ws://127.0.0.1:19697 \
  --token '<isolated-test-token>' --timeout 22000 --json
```

Profile fixture: `trap '' TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done`. Probe timeout: **15000 ms**. Baseline: `5dd456acfa35575c342b43b944a9d0dbb911b68e`. Runtime proof: `9ce687aba355bd99b3d8abfef5ac56564b62b54c`; current head `05ea4c5129cfa5593600a81ac99c66b5a6e0ff1d` changes only the test mock to preserve real module exports, with identical production code.

Captured output (redacted):

```text
base: elapsedMs=22568, exit=1
  gateway timeout after 22000ms
  ps: PID=7416 PPID=7328 PGID=7416 /bin/bash -l -c printf '\0'; env -0
  ps: PID=7518 PPID=7416 PGID=7416 sleep 1
head: sessions.catalog.list 15145ms; elapsedMs=17062, exit=0
  {"catalogs":[{"id":"opencode","label":"OpenCode","hosts":[]}]}
  ps: probe PID=7752 absent; no remaining login shell or its sleep child
  unrelated detached sentinel remains alive; Gateway remains alive
normal-profile control: base exit=0, 2890ms; head exit=0, 2789ms
```

CLI elapsed includes CLI startup and transport overhead. The server's measured request completes at the 15-second probe deadline plus 145 ms of catalog/transport work. On base it still has not returned by the client's 22-second deadline. The probe is spawned detached and termination targets only its own process group; the distinct Gateway and sentinel groups survive.

Focused check on the final test revision: `pnpm test src/infra/shell-env.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **38 passed**, runner wall time **3.23s** (Vitest 1.77s). Scoped formatting and lint passed. An earlier local check stalled because the harness left the intentional bad profile active for a pre-existing synchronous-shell test; restoring the fixture resolved it. The harness now restores the profile. The initial CI mock-export ratchet finding is fixed by preserving the real process helper exports.

Simplification retained the existing probe and termination owners and the focused settlement/cleanup/retry regression; no new abstraction or configuration. Production **+14/-10**, tests **+27/-0** against merge base.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the old behavior; no persisted-state, schema, configuration, or API migration. Blast radius is asynchronous login-shell PATH preparation on Unix; a regression could affect executable discovery or session catalog loading for shells with slow startup.

prs.title: fix(desktop): reclaim unused runtime seeds after healthy activation
prs.body:
Rebased onto main at `61ed7497922beb4013a4b2bfa599904cc75e3681` after #171117 landed. Only the four seed-retention commits remain; all are patch-identical to the previously reviewed version.

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated Tauri desktop runtime activations retain every immutable seed, adding roughly a gigabyte per development build that includes the bundled package.

## User Impact

After successful activation and Gateway health checks, Linux and Windows reclaim obsolete runtime seeds while retaining the current and previous selections, managed launcher/package references, installed service and runtime pin references, and live executables. Failed activation does not collect seeds.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collection stays in the existing seed and activation owners. The existing managed launcher marker stores the previous successful selection; no additional state store or service authority is introduced. A wrapper's pinned executable is retained for rollback. Unreadable references or process inventories defer cleanup, as do independent/unrecognized CLI launchers that cannot persist the rollback selection. Startup and desktop updates still do not switch an existing Gateway automatically.

Release-note context: Linux and Windows desktop apps now reclaim unused bundled runtimes after a healthy activation while preserving rollback and active uses.

## Evidence

- Rebased-head local Rust activation tests: 21 passed, 0.92 seconds test time / 6.12 seconds wall time including rebuild. Seed tests: 9 passed, 0.27 seconds test time / 2.71 seconds wall time. Both used `cargo test --locked --bin openclaw-desktop` with the respective `runtime_action` and `bundled_runtime` filters.
- The activation/rollback regression fails on the original branch because no previous selection is persisted. A pinned-wrapper regression also failed before the follow-up fix; both now pass through the real activation path with a fixture CLI. No operator Gateway or personal state was used.
- Five existing runtime-boundary checks passed with `node --test apps/linux/scripts/test-runtime-boundary.mjs` (0.22 seconds wall time after rebase). `cargo check --locked --all-targets` passed after rebase (24.56 seconds wall time), as did Rust format and diff whitespace. Earlier unchanged-patch checks passed: native state-schema guard, max-lines/line-cap/assertion-safety/test-timeout/test-mock ratchets, config docs, plugin inventory, protocol, native locale check/verify, and UI locale checks passed.
- Independent autoreview is clean at P0–P2 after fixing its Linux test-ordering finding. The conflict-free rebase preserved every commit patch, so no new autoreview was needed. Production: +314/-38 lines (net +276); tests: +224/-0, excluding the unchanged test-file move.
- Exact-head (`91d11f97213f1102ac7b28cbc00ed988c516fde5`) [native CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38494631235): Linux Rust tests passed (41 seconds including build), Windows runtime/installer boundary tests passed (35 seconds), and macOS companion tests passed (42 seconds). `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. Linux candidate and Windows installer builds remain running after the 15-minute bounded wait. No failed checks; three duplicate metadata jobs were canceled.
- The native process tests use small executable fixtures and a stdin/stdout handshake. Linux validates the exact fixture PID because the hosted runner hides unrelated same-user processes; full-census failures still defer all deletion. Collection and activation persistence/failure contracts are tested at their respective owners. No full live Gateway activation was attempted.
- Initial Linux CI exposed test-only digest formatting and process-inventory assumptions; both are fixed. The optional Testbox lease was stopped when execution queued; no remote proof is claimed for it.

ClawSweeper reviewed the exact head with no actionable code findings; its proof-only hold remains: stable-to-head upgrade compatibility for persisted launcher metadata, settings, service references, and rollback has not been demonstrated. No visual UI change. Do not merge as part of this lane.

prs.title: fix: configured Codex chats compact prematurely after durable completion
prs.body:
Related: #158606

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes premature context-engine compaction when a configured Codex chat loses its successful assembly budget during durable completion or recovery.

## User Impact

Existing exact-model `contextTokens` limits consistently bound assembly and reach accepted-turn commit and maintenance; smaller current allowances still win. Unconfigured and pinned native sessions keep their existing ownership. No new configuration keys, capacity discovery, database migration or Codex fork.

This PR is now **budget-only**. Native history projection, thread reuse and assembly-error fallback remain unchanged. The separate history-delivery work is preserved as [a clean stacked draft](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/pull/1); this PR does not claim to repair history clipping. The companion https://github.com/Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw/pull/1247 consumes the current host allowance throughout plugin maintenance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reserve current prompt overhead before assembly, capture only a bounded, source-fenced successful attempt, and carry its normalized settings through the existing durable outbox, commit and maintenance paths. Failed, cancelled, mismatched or unrelated attempts do not donate a prior budget.

Credit to @aounakram for the original report and @NianJiuZst for the prior investigation and PR #158740. This independently implemented work does not change that author's branch. The scope split isolates the history-item/lifecycle concerns raised by ClawSweeper; it does not present a budget-only fix as the complete history remedy.

## Evidence

[Split baseline/current-source proof](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38500334640) reproduced exactly 15 intended budget failures with 7 controls passing. Repaired source passed 279 cases in 10 unchanged files; the new Codex file’s two trailing-whitespace fixtures and three unbound-method lint errors were repaired in a test-only revision.

[Final one-file qualification](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38502084568) passed all22 Codex cases in88.635seconds, including configured prompt/image reservations, real prior-history bootstrap, unchanged unauthored allowance and configured assembly-error fallback. Identical tests on original production source failed exactly the2 intended budget cases with2 controls passing. Fresh file format/lint passed; strict one-test-file delta and hash checks retain the279 previously passed unchanged cases plus successful core/extension production types and assertion-safety. This is component/delta qualification—not a claim that one final-source run repeated all301 cases. Canonical build and broad merged-tree checks run in normal upstream PR CI; prior combined-source evidence is not labeled current split proof.

The full shipped CLI/Gateway budget-to-commit/recovery/maintenance and existing-install upgrade trace requested by automated review remains an explicit proof gap. No installed/live-session test or production update is claimed, and no live settings, plugin, database or Gateway was changed. Test/trace execution stays in isolated GitHub environments.

[Budget-only upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502812349) passed on head `cf4186f7d2154842b1686961b393d39e243799ef`: 55 successful jobs,26 skipped,no failures, including canonical build artifacts, bundled assets and CLI smoke checks. This is execution qualification, not maintainer approval; the shipped-flow proof gap above remains explicit. The history draft targets our fork’s budget branch and is not represented as an upstream-approved or merge-ready PR.

prs.title: fix(agents): reject malformed UTF-8 identity files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `agents set-identity --identity-file` reports success and saves corrupted identity text when the input file contains malformed UTF-8.

## User Impact

User impact: explicit identity import rejects invalid encoding before saving config; valid Unicode identities continue to work. Optional workspace presentation treats an invalid file as unavailable, consistently with existing unreadable-file behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared bounded descriptor reader decoded with replacement characters. Validate the bytes before parsing, return a distinct internal snapshot classification, and report a useful error for explicit import. The existing worker cache already evicts all non-loaded results, so both synchronous and worker-backed readers retain one admission policy.

## Evidence

Product head `a3cddeb9f006353c510a975119456ac0e4b69189`; RED base `44c918f3900770412a3cd912eaa0c718b2e3356c`. Normal `pnpm build cliStartup` builds had matching clean-head stamps. Linux, Node 24.16.0.

Same packaged CLI command on both versions, with an isolated config/state/workspace:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs agents set-identity --agent main --identity-file "$IDENTITY_FILE" --json
```

Malformed input bytes were `2d204e616d653a20436166e90a` (`- Name: Caf`, raw byte `e9`, newline). Input SHA-256: `af5f675d09f0c608f836d4f3a90793ce11d855360abfbe73fbae3fcb4ea70c1e`.

| Scenario | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Malformed identity file | exit 0; config name becomes `Caf�` | exit 1; UTF-8 diagnostic; config byte-identical |
| Input-file readback | original bytes retained | original bytes retained |
| Valid `Café 🤖 �` control | exit 0; exact name saved | exit 0; exact name saved |

Readback used the actual written config file (`agents.entries.main.identity.name`), compared full config bytes for the rejected import, and re-hashed the input file. The valid control includes a legitimately encoded U+FFFD character, so valid replacement-character text is not rejected. The packaged CLI exercised the worker-backed identity admission owner before the normal config writer.

Validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: RED 1 failed / 16 passed; GREEN 17 passed, Vitest 82.22s, runner 89.63s. Coverage includes explicit and optional synchronous/asynchronous readers, size/missing classifications, worker-cache reuse, replacement/deletion/recreation and symlink controls. Targeted type-aware lint/type checking and formatting passed. Independent adversarial review: PASS, no P0–P3 findings.

Scope: 2 files; production +8/-1, tests +13/-2. No config/schema, protocol, permission, dependency or migration changes; the invalid-encoding discriminator is internal.

Not tested: a live Gateway/avatar UI, external providers or the full suite. No production config or service was touched; isolated synthetic files were retained outside the product branch.

prs.title: perf(agents): retain encoded session fork payloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every embedded parent turn deep-clones its complete provider request solely to retain it for an optional read-only session fork, then serializes the same payload again for snapshot byte accounting.

## User Impact

Read-only forks preserve the parent's prepared request prefix, provider cache markers, one-shot hook behavior, tool denial, and live authority checks. Normal parent turns avoid an extra payload clone. No configuration or schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the JSON wire payload instead of a mutable object graph. Count its UTF-8 bytes separately from the saved context/model/options while preserving the exact existing envelope budget. Each fork inference attempt parses a private request, so replay no longer needs another full-payload structured clone. Expiry, session cleanup, bounded retention, and completed-message publication keep their existing owner.

Production LOC delta: -1 (17 additions, 18 deletions); no parallel fast path or compatibility shim.

## Evidence

- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean P0–P2 review of the diff, complete owner, fork contract, and behavioral proof guidance. The configured review helper refused the requested provider route; no configuration was changed.
- Changed-file `oxfmt --check` and repository focused syntax lint passed. Broad type-aware lint/typechecks belong to PR CI.
- Focused tests: `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-fork.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.session-fork.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 13 tests in 245.46 s. The changed test took 0.49 s; owner file 47.90 s, integration sibling 120.73 s (real provider HTTP request/authority/async-publication contracts). An earlier run was invalidated by a source comment edit during worker execution; final-source rerun passed. Full CI passed on the exact PR head: [run 38503495104](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38503495104). The individual changed-file test timing is not separated in the CI metadata; local per-file and changed-test times are above.
- Isolated Linux benchmark sandbox, Node 26.8.2, 64 CPUs (affinity 64–127), 64 GiB memory ceiling; all processes at nice 10 / idle I/O priority. Baseline `976cc974fab1912c696d1101bd17a1abf05eb77e` versus candidate `d0f7c052084e6fe3a25edad05ded23d6065a1419`; candidate source blob matched the PR exactly. `pnpm build:runtime` passed for each revision as benchmark preparation (82.1 s baseline / 62.4 s candidate). No Testbox/Crabbox lease or broad local test gate was run.

| Main-thread CPU measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Parent request capture, median ms/request | 1.3931 | 0.56981 |
| Streaming, median ms/primary turn | 333.021 | 343.670 |
| Streaming, median ms/delivered session-event copy | 0.41267 | 0.42586 |

Request capture improves 2.44× (59.1% less CPU). This exercises `wrapStreamFnWithSessionFork` with a 1,078,720-byte synthetic provider body, 256 messages and 40 tool schemas: 20 warmups, seven rounds of 100 captures, `process.threadCpuUsage()` deltas. Both revisions retain the same pre-stream context capture and quota/expiry work. Total timed capture runtime across the 700 requests was 0.989 / 0.417 seconds.

RSS cross-check: with an explicit GC outside each timed round, peak process RSS was 238.25 / 230.70 MiB; post-GC live heap was 35.21 / 35.16 MiB. CPU remained lower (0.9294 / 0.6186 ms/request medians; 1.50×). An ordinary-GC repeat produced peak RSS 234.89 / 259.67 MiB, showing that allocation/GC cadence can move peak RSS despite equivalent live retention. These are process-wide readings, including module loading; **no peak-memory reduction claim**. Controlled rounds yield once and collect between 100-request cohorts, outside the measured CPU/wall interval.

Overall streaming is **neutral within round-to-round noise** (+3.2% median point estimate). All five measured rounds are included. First-round outliers were 1,559 / 1,163 ms per turn; full ranges were 252–1,559 / 270–1,163 ms. Aggregate CPU was 55.642 / 48.498 seconds across 100 primary turns, but the outliers make that unsuitable as a whole-Gateway speedup claim. Each revision sustained 20 overlapping primary streams per round with 60 subscribers; all per-client delivery, sequence, overlap, and completion checks passed. Utility requests varied between 20 and 22 per round.

Streaming command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts --state-dir <synthetic-fixture> --clients 60 --runs 20 --rounds 5 --chunks 100 --port 41047 --mock-port 41048`. Fixture: `team-shape-fixture.ts --transcript-mib 1500`, 5,000 sessions / 6,000 retained runs / 200 approvals / 100 disabled cron jobs / 12 projects with real synthetic worktrees; agent database 4,641,595,392 bytes. The standard driver resets its 20 child sessions before each revision while retaining the large inventory. A default fixture generation also completed locally first.

This is a measured request-capture simplification with neutral streaming results, so it meets the performance lane's deletion/simplification landing rule. Worker serialization, immutable-data admission, and production-wide CPU effects remain outside the measured improvement.

Performance claims are limited to synthetic measurements. No production Gateway load, production database access, live model calls, or user desktop/browser activity.

The review request for before/after runtime and RSS is addressed by the measurements above, replied to, and resolved. Required CI/security/dependency gates passed on `d0f7c052084e6fe3a25edad05ded23d6065a1419`; no CI rerun or inherited-failure exception was needed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin configuration reloads repeatedly refetch provider sign-in status across open Control UI panels, even before updated authentication facts are ready.

## User Impact

Provider sign-in status stays visible until the Gateway publishes its updated facts. Credential changes, explicit refresh, reconnects, and expiry deadlines continue refreshing status. Model access and model-list invalidation keep their existing authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

`config.changed` invalidated the shared auth request cache and triggered sidebar reads before the prepared metadata owner published `chat.metadata.changed`. That publication could then invalidate the same readers again. Remove the premature invalidation and sidebar auth dispatch; the existing metadata publication owns freshness. Production delta: 4 insertions / 6 deletions, net −2 lines. No schema or configuration changes.

The server already caches model-list projections by its prepared generation, coalesces provider/native discovery, and retains prepared auth facts. The Codex resident-catalog warnings in the investigation belong to session pagination, not model discovery; this change adds no competing server cache.

## Evidence

- New shell-boundary regression failed on the original code: 40 readers across ten config events refetched before authoritative auth publication. With the fix, they retain the shared result and refresh once after publication.
- Focused UI files: `app-host.chat-metadata.test.ts`, `model-auth.test.ts`, `sidebar-attention-auth-deadline.test.ts`, `sidebar-attention-store.test.ts`. 65 tests passed (11.32 s wall); final sidebar rerun: 42 tests passed (18.02 s wall). Changed-file oxfmt, repository oxlint and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean at P0–P2, with the exact diff and server publication/credential dependencies reviewed. Autoreview refused the selected provider because it did not match operator configuration; configuration was preserved.
- Isolated Linux sandbox, baseline `976cc974fab1912c696d1101bd17a1abf05eb77e` versus this UI change on the same Gateway: 40 real loopback WebSocket clients, three auth consumers per connection, five watched plugin toggles. Auth-status RPCs fell **600 → 400 (33.3%, 1.5× fewer)**, consistently **120 → 80 per toggle**. Both runs received the same 120 metadata deliveries per toggle (three events per client). The remaining reads follow the authoritative publications.
- After startup settled, `models.list {agentId:"main", view:"configured", preparedOnly:true}`: 200 warmup requests, then 400 measured requests per variant. **p50 6.47 → 6.68 ms; p99 12.12 → 12.54 ms**: neutral within noise, with no server change. Initial startup-overlapping measurements were excluded from this warmed comparison.
- Fixture: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approval recovery records, 100 disabled cron jobs and 12 real synthetic projects; 235,978,752-byte agent database and 11,812,864-byte state database. Generated locally first (99.7 s), then in the sandbox (17.3 s). Benchmark preparation used the repository `sourcePerformance` profile (70.1 s); the unnecessary default declaration build was stopped.
- Gap: this credential-free configured-catalog fixture does not reproduce the production 3.3 s tail or exercise authenticated native/provider discovery. Existing server caches were retained; no additional cache was added. The sampled production slow interval also included cron RPCs, so these numbers do not claim to repair the shared Gateway stalls.
- Server metadata lifecycle: 20 tests passed; 191.43 s wrapper wall, dominated by a 95.5 s compiler-cache preparation.
- PR CI on `a2239aaaf662b408c432b6d86e37dcde95dca91e`: typecheck, lint, changed Node lanes, UI shards 1/3 and 2/3, UI end-to-end, localization and performance passed. The only non-aggregate failure is `checks-ui (3/3)`, run [38502470436](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502470436), job [115652736247](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502470436/job/115652736247): two terminal-panel pending-open cancellation cases expected one `terminal.open` request and observed none; 597 other files passed in that shard.
- Unrelated-flake attribution: `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-cancellation.test.ts` passed **5/5 runs on baseline `976cc974fab1912c696d1101bd17a1abf05eb77e` and 5/5 on the exact PR overlay** (11 tests/run, 110 total passing cases), in the isolated sandbox with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` and CI's checksum-pinned Bun fork. The test and terminal request/cancellation owners are unchanged; no changed production module is on that path. Under the operator's five-run rule, land using the unrelated-failure exception. prs.title: perf(github): avoid redundant cached preview credential reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cached GitHub hover previews unnecessarily wait for two live credential reads. Slow preview diagnostics currently show only total RPC duration, leaving identity preparation, cache/load wait, and upstream delays indistinguishable.

## User Impact

Cached previews require one live credential read before delivery. Every credentialed network dispatch still revalidates independently; public-repository, redirect, token-rotation, caller-lifetime, timeout, and explicit-refresh behavior remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cache lookup has no external effect, so its preliminary asynchronous credential read is redundant with the existing dispatch and delivery boundaries. The plugin remains the sole preview-cache owner, using the existing 200-entry, credential-scoped, 60-second stale-while-revalidate cache and two-second upstream deadline. No second cache or background service is introduced.

Reads taking at least 500 ms now record numeric phase timings and fixed categories: identity preparation, cache/load wait, delivery auth, metadata rendering/decorations, upstream auth, and response-header network wait. Response-body work remains within metadata/decorations. Logs omit URLs, preview contents, credentials, and arbitrary upstream errors.

## Evidence

Read-only sampled successful RPC evidence confirmed 1,064–1,145 ms previews during the observed stress window, plus earlier 1,248–1,851 ms successes and a 2,006 ms upstream timeout. These samples do not establish a population p99 or identify the delayed phase. Production phase attribution remains pending deployment of the diagnostics.

An isolated Linux sandbox ran the production preview loader against a synthetic loopback HTTP server. Ten sequential warm/stale reads per cell:

| Scenario | Before p50 / p99 | After p50 / p99 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warm cache, fast credential | 0.006 / 0.019 ms | 0.005 / 0.022 ms |
| Warm cache, injected 500 ms credential read | 1,004.146 / 1,005.385 ms | 501.846 / 504.251 ms |
| Stale cache, 500 ms HTTP latency | 0.002 / 0.311 ms | 0.003 / 0.463 ms |
| Stale cache, 1,000 ms HTTP latency | 0.002 / 0.385 ms | 0.002 / 0.272 ms |
| Stale cache, 2,000 ms HTTP latency | 0.002 / 0.303 ms | 0.002 / 0.186 ms |

The injected credential-delay case improves approximately 2×. Fast credentials and stale network-delay cases are neutral within noise. Stale delivery already runs without joining the network refresh; this change preserves that behavior. These are loader measurements, not full-Gateway or live GitHub measurements. The synthetic 5,000-session/6,000-run fixture was generated independently; the loader benchmark does not exercise its session inventory.

The new fake-clock regression fails on the old code because delivery has not occurred after one 750 ms credential read, and passes after the removal. Existing tests cover single flight, deadlines, visibility, redirects, caller loss, and credential retirement/rotation.

Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable). The requested autoreview route failed preflight because it did not match operator configuration; configuration was unchanged. The isolated reviewer found no actionable issues.

Local validation uses only changed-file formatting, focused repo lint, and focused test files; broad typechecks/builds/suites are delegated to PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox leases were allocated. Production was observed read-only.

Focused proof: `pnpm test extensions/github/src/preview.test.ts extensions/github/src/github-api.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 46 tests (68.60 s wrapper wall time); `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/control-ui.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/control-ui.github-preview-refresh.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 44 tests (111.92 s wrapper wall time). After the handler-call simplification, the two changed test files passed 80 tests in 104.29 s, with the preview file completing in 8.30 s (new regression 4 ms). The final transport timing edit passed its seven API tests in 17.23 s. Most local wall time was worker preparation/import on the busy host, not test execution.

Formatting: `oxfmt --write --threads=1` on changed files; `git diff --check` clean. Focused lint: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --openclaw-focused-config --config .oxlintrc.json <changed TS files>` passed. The initial type-aware lint invocation was stopped when it requested package artifact preparation; that proof belongs to CI.

Production LOC grows by 47 lines: the behavior change deletes one asynchronous check and simplifies the refresh call; the requested phase diagnostics account for the added code. No schema, dependency, configuration, public-contract, or update migration changes. Existing installs pick up the behavior and diagnostics with a normal update. Cold upstream network latency is unchanged, and this PR does not claim to resolve the measured production p99 until deployed phase evidence identifies it.

PR CI: all 38 executed CI jobs passed on `b314f12d663d749129385beb7c3d77b9050828ff`; the [full CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38503599825) completed successfully in approximately 491 seconds. The required `openclaw/ci-gate` was green before squash merge. No CI failures or reruns. Merged as `3ed952999701c039289d6209e0ea22412e22a48e`.

prs.title: perf(worktrees): reuse branch inventories with large pack directories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Git subprocesses when the worktree base-branch picker reads repositories with large pack directories.

## User Impact

Repeated branch inventories remain cached on large repositories, while changed refs, HEAD, configuration, and damaged object storage still invalidate them. No fetch, schema change, configuration option, or migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing revision recorder gave up after 1,024 filesystem entries. A repository with thousands of packs therefore never retained its branch inventory and repeated checkout admission and branch enumeration on every read. Stream the same ordered metadata into a SHA-256 revision instead of retaining an array with an entry-count ceiling. This keeps the existing worker, cache, single-flight, and bounded enumeration owners. Production LOC: 8 additions / 9 deletions, net -1.

`sessions.branches.list` reads transcript branches and performs no Git work. This change addresses the Git-backed `worktrees.branches` path; checkout context already has a separate revision cache. There are no ahead/behind calculations to batch in branch enumeration.

## Evidence

Isolated Linux sandbox measurement at base c33cd2c41ad8d1ef4e54f0c88551351e47dac600: 6,900 valid packs with indexes, packed HEAD, 24 real linked worktrees, and 325 branches. The production Git worker operation ran unchanged, with subprocess counts read from its diagnostics counters. Each case used 100 sequential samples after warming every selected checkout; every returned inventory matched the baseline exactly.

| Workload | Before p50 / p99 | After p50 / p99 | Git spawns before / after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One checkout, 6,900 packs | 78.03 / 106.04 ms | 41.06 / 50.58 ms | 300 / 0 |
| Rotate 24 worktrees, 6,900 packs | 243.29 / 431.71 ms | 36.88 / 44.90 ms | 300 / 0 |
| One checkout, 12 packs | 1.28 / 2.54 ms | 1.20 / 2.85 ms | 0 / 0 |
| Rotate 24 worktrees, 12 packs | 1.04 / 1.48 ms | 1.11 / 1.61 ms | 0 / 0 |

The small-repository result is neutral at sub-millisecond noise. There is a cold-admission tradeoff: the 24 large linked worktrees' first-read p50/p99 rises from 259.31/282.17 ms to 320.40/345.02 ms because complete metadata is checked before and after Git admission. Subsequent reads avoid native Git admission entirely. The first worker-start read is excluded from steady-state comparisons.

Proof:
- `pnpm test src/agents/worktrees/service-branches.test.ts src/infra/git-read-cache.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/worktrees.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 73 passed, 1 platform-specific skip.
- New large-pack-directory regression fails against unchanged production code: expected zero Git launches on a warm read, received three. It passes with this change.
- Changed-file repository lint, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. Autoreview preflight refused the selected provider because it did not match operator configuration; configuration was preserved.

Measurements cover the production Git worker boundary, not complete WebSocket RPC latency, production background load, or transcript branch-list latency. No production Gateway was load-tested or modified. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated; PR CI owns broad gates under the current validation rule.

The live rollup has 58 successful checks, including production/test typechecks, changed Node lanes, source contracts, documentation, lint, guards, and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. prs.title: perf(approvals): avoid unrelated writer waits during session replay
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow session opening when approval replay for `sessions.messages.subscribe` queues behind unrelated shared-state writes.

## User Impact

Subscriptions with `includeApprovals: true` can replay already committed pending approvals while an unrelated writer is occupied. Expiration, corrupt-row repair, reviewer/audience filtering, ordering, and live authority checks retain their existing contracts. No schema, configuration, or stored-format change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sampled slow subscriptions spent roughly 1.1–3.4 seconds in replay preparation rather than transcript reads. Replay unconditionally queued two writer transactions: expiry reconciliation and pending-approval listing. Initial subscription does not read the transcript snapshot.

Use the existing shared-state read worker to detect a no-op expiry and read clean pending approvals. The existing writer remains the sole owner of actual expiry and corrupt-row repair. A repair retains its original approval FIFO lease instead of releasing and re-enqueuing behind a later mutation; committed receipts and publication remain unchanged. One ordered selector serves both read and repair paths.

Production LOC delta: +105 lines (183 added, 78 removed across four production files). Growth preserves the existing transactional corruption-repair and expiry-publication contracts while adding two typed commands to the existing read worker; this does not introduce a cache, replica, schema, or second mutation owner. Idle median has a small extra read cost, accepted for removing unbounded unrelated-writer wait.

## Evidence

Isolated Linux sandbox measurement through real Gateway request dispatch, subscription handler, approval replay, read worker, and native shared-state writer. Synthetic fixture: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, 12 projects/worktrees, 1.5 GiB logical transcripts, approximately 4.6 GB agent database. The subscribed session has an additional multi-MiB transcript. Fixture generation also completed locally before the comparison.

100 warmed samples per cell, identical fixture and harness before/after. Busy runs hold an unrelated native writer for 100 ms and append a synthetic transcript turn between samples. The hold isolates writer queueing; these are dispatch measurements, not production or end-to-end WebSocket latency predictions.

| Subscription | Before p50 / p99 | After p50 / p99 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Approvals, idle | 4.16 / 8.32 ms | 5.38 / 7.58 ms |
| Approvals, writer occupied | 106.23 / 109.41 ms | 5.92 / 8.49 ms |
| No approvals, idle | 0.34 / 2.41 ms | 0.35 / 2.45 ms |
| No approvals, writer occupied | 0.52 / 0.80 ms | 0.59 / 0.76 ms |

Occupied-writer approval p99 improves 12.9×; idle median increases 1.22 ms. No claim of speeding transcript serialization or a long-running approval mutation ahead of replay in its own FIFO.

Focused proof:

- Held-writer regression uses the real replay/read/write paths and completes before writer release. It times out at 10 seconds against the original store implementation; patched replay file passes all 14 tests.
- Approval store and worker files: 29 tests pass, including corrupt-row repair retaining FIFO ordering ahead of a concurrent denial.
- Subscription approval and performance sibling files: 8 tests pass.
- Export-name collision guard passes; eager-import and PR-wrapper closure guards pass (20 tests).
- Changed-file formatting, repository lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad checks run in PR CI; no Testbox/Crabbox lease allocated under the lane validation rule.

Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable). The configured helper refused the provider/route mismatch; configuration was not changed. The independent reviewer identified a FIFO ordering issue in the first version; it was fixed and re-reviewed with no remaining actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(release): publication status omits release and Windows source identities
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes publication status omitting the release identity and Windows source tag while showing their verification results.

## User Impact

Operators can see the publisher's expected version, tag, npm dist-tag and source SHA, plus the Windows target/source tags, without reconciling the original artifacts manually. Mac assets/feeds and website deployment remain explicitly **not observed** by this reader, with guidance to their existing owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

The read-only FRV report already authenticates these producer diagnostics and Windows dispatch records, but discarded their release fields before rendering. Carry those recorded facts into the existing projection instead of adding another reporter or publication authority. Preserve unknown values when diagnostics are absent.

This is a bounded reporting repair, not automatic cross-repository Mac/site tracking: retained stable-orchestration facts and the website owner's read-only production checks remain their canonical paths. There are no new network reads, configuration, retention, schemas, dependency changes or release operations. Production growth is 31 lines for the missing projection fields and honest next-step text; tests add 12 lines to existing cases without new subprocesses.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced through the real `frv status --publication-run ... --json` CLI fixture before the production change: the authenticated diagnostic's release identity was missing (`undefined`). It passes after the repair.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/frv.release.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (native wrapper for `pnpm test test/scripts/frv.release.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`): **107/107 passed**, 93.62s wrapper wall time (88.25s Vitest). The existing file is a CLI transport/evidence suite; no new test boot or timer was added. Exact-head hosted CI passed in 548 seconds wall time (21:45:41–21:54:49 UTC).
- The seven changed-path cases pass in 12.99s wrapper wall time, covering partial/failed publishers, unattempted verification, text output and pending/failed Windows children.
- Targeted script and root-test typechecks, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent review through P2 found no accepted/actionable findings.
- Existing unknown-state, identity mismatch, detached-child, privacy and output-bound cases remain green. The guidance link was checked against the current website README; no website deployment or release dispatch was performed.

Local tool limitation resolved: a first check run rejected a shared dependency symlink at the declaration containment gate; a task-private frozen dependency install replaced it. Completed guards were retained and the remaining targeted checks resumed. No shared dependencies were modified.

A broad optional dead-export scan reported three unchanged core exports (`hasActiveDeliveryOwner`, `listOpenClawStateFeatureSchemas`, `OpenClawStateFeatureSchema`). The touched scripts scan and full-tree scan passed; the two owning core files are byte-identical to the pinned base. This is an unresolved local guard result, not a claim about hosted CI attribution.

No live successful publisher/validation pair or current public registry readback is claimed. The production CLI boundary uses fixed GitHub GET/ZIP fixtures; the change adds no API behavior. [Exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38312631475) is attached to `11ef37d14d9c5de33487bdf5c347a61d4260be90` completed successfully; the required CI gate is green. Skipped jobs are not claimed as executed.

Final handoff: current head is non-draft and mergeable; all checks settled with no failures. Latest ClawSweeper review reports no findings. No merge or release operation performed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session identities still passed through retired Lit template helpers inside the Solid sidebar, chat header, sharing menu, and command palette.

## User Impact

The same owner chips and Activity links now render through their existing Solid implementations. Host tags, CSS classes, browser link gestures, and the distinction between standalone and name-adjacent avatar links are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the duplicate owner-chip template module, move its type-only callers to the session-owner domain module, and use the existing Solid person-name/avatar components. The standalone avatar component is shared by the chat header and sharing control. The two browser geometry fixtures now mount native Solid content. The picker's leading-content callback retains its existing opaque-template contract through `solidContent`; this keeps native avatar rendering inside the callback owner.

Production LOC across changed files falls from 7,891 to 7,797 (-94). Test/helper LOC changes from 1,296 to 1,372 (+76), including focused checks for keyboard targets, modified clicks, and an identity change. Total LOC: 9,187 → 9,169 (-18).

| Chromium session-glyph browser tests | 4 passed; 4.29 s |
| Production UI build | Passed |
| Strict performance check against same-machine base | Passed, no violations |

| Targeted lint and diff check | Passed |

| Independent review | Complete identity head reviewed clean after fixing one test-only leftover call; CI correction reviewed separately |

The screenshots use the repository's synthetic mock Gateway on the merge base and candidate builds. The full chat frame is pixel-identical, and the shown sharing-owner crops are pixel-identical. The sharing-owner region is unchanged; the refreshed full sharing frame differs only at subpixel color precision. No local E2E suite or repeat loop was run. `ci:full` covers the wider chat and shared-component consumers before landing.

The first CI run caught the missing adapter at the picker callback boundary and an owner-name assertion that included decorative avatar initials. Both are corrected. The focused repair run preserves owner selection, Archived filtering, keyboard navigation, phone sheets, and sharing actions.

Exact-head full CI run [38502577449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502577449) passed the UI unit, type, performance, browser-extension, real-Gateway, and other selected checks. Fixes Details offering empty pull-request and automation expanders while hiding attached work behind extra clicks.

## User Impact

Populated sections open automatically; empty sections disappear. Session metadata stays visible, PR and automation titles wrap, and manual collapse survives ordinary updates. Loading and failed automation reads remain visible without an empty disclosure. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use native disclosure state for populated sections and let the existing automation loader own whether its section has content. prs.title: fix(workboard): keep chat catalog reads out of card history
prs.body:
Fixes #171078

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes desktop chat stalls and disconnects when the Workboard sidebar repeatedly downloads the entire card history.

## User Impact

Opening chat loads board summaries and cards linked to the visible session. Sidebar and header-chip rendering stays identical; this is a data-loading change, so no visual screenshots are needed. Existing unfiltered card-list callers retain full-list behavior. No configuration, schema, migration, or protocol version change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog's `catalogOnly` path fetched and hydrated every card, including notes, comments, and events. The sidebar now uses `workboard.boards.list`; the chip uses an optional additive `sessionKey` filter on the existing `workboard.cards.list`. The bundled Workboard plugin selects matching IDs before loading heavy details. Direct, execution, attempt, and event session links remain eligible. Each consumer refreshes its own data, skips unchanged card revisions, and rejects stale responses. Full-card views retain their existing full-list and card-revision behavior.

Comparison has one owner: `@openclaw/normalization-core/session-key-comparison`. The UI retains its bounded cache; the plugin imports through the existing private-local `session-key-runtime` SDK facade. The pure function and its tests moved unchanged. Neither the package index nor `string-normalization` re-exports it, keeping it outside the trusted PR wrapper closure. The Vite source alias and its precedence regression cover the new subpath. The SQL prefilter remains because link tables grow with history: it avoids transferring ordinary unrelated keys into JavaScript while retaining Unicode and whitespace candidates for exact shared comparison.

Two supporting changes are necessary. The canonical coercion inventory registers this new helper/module so the existing ownership guard passes and rejects duplicates. PostgreSQL read-only snapshots end with `ROLLBACK`: the new filtered read otherwise publishes a false `COMMIT` write receipt, advances card revisions, and repeatedly refreshes the consumers. This retains repeatable-read consistency; write transactions still commit normally.

Changes versus merged main base `4239ea349a2bcbe674af117e89422474ab7c9d1d`, including tooling and generated metadata:

| Category | Added | Removed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 392 | 150 |
| Tests | 412 | 105 |
| Docs | 23 | 6 |

The old shared hydration path and duplicate normalizer are removed. Production grows for independent request lifecycles and pre-hydration selection; the canonically regenerated boot manifest also includes recent main UI migrations.

## Evidence

- Current exact-head [CI run 38494291065](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38494291065), head `87e5fa141f16d0cd4c69be1386a407a0f33653d1`: **142 checks passed, 15 skipped; two jobs and their dependent aggregate gate failed.** All three UI unit shards, all nine UI E2E shards, PostgreSQL conformance, builds, production/test types, ordinary lint, source contracts, and architecture guards passed.
- Merged main `4239ea349a2bcbe674af117e89422474ab7c9d1d` without rebasing. The only conflict was generated Workboard Control UI entry/styles. Rebuilt through `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/workboard`, retaining all main metadata, including backup resources, and this PR's browser changes. Every non-`controlUi` manifest field matches merged main. Reviewed the new checkout-independent asset builder and chunk-name owner; the additive filter's method schema, pre-hydration selection, consumers, and docs remain consistent. No other application-code changes were made.
- Regression coverage includes connect/change request count and size, session-scoped chip requests, stale responses, unchanged card revisions, and selection before malformed or oversized unrelated historical cards are decoded. Names include `loads only summaries on connect and changes without hydrating card history`, `refreshes only the visible session and ignores stale lookups after navigation`, `keeps session-filtered payloads and revision receipts separate from full card lists`, and `selects session links before hydrating unrelated card history`.
- Changed authored-file oxlint with `.oxlintrc.json`, oxfmt, and diff whitespace checks passed. Full-branch isolated Codex autoreview and the alias/artifact follow-up were clean through P2; only mechanical main merges followed. The generated manifest is formatter-excluded and was regenerated by its owner.
- Generated artifacts used their owners: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/workboard` and `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ui/scripts/control-ui-boot-manifest.mts`. No generated output was hand-edited.
- Live proof was intentionally skipped per maintainer policy; PR CI is the test gate. No new local tests, local typechecks, production negative controls, or Gateway proofs were run. The earlier focused Testbox request queued and was stopped without executing tests; backing run `38473013130` was cancelled. No task lease remains.
- ClawSweeper has only acknowledged the PR, with no P0-P2 code findings. The PR remains open, ready, and unmerged.

### Current failures

| Check | Result and classification |
| --- | --- |
| [checks-node-changed-7 / 115626861345](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38494291065/job/115626861345) | **Accepted inherited timing failure.** The only failed test in this job is `test/gateway-restart-handoff.e2e.test.ts:322`: clean exit took **5427 ms**, exceeding the **5000 ms** assertion. This is the same main-side timing-margin remainder; the coordinator reports that the native inherited-failure verifier accepted the prior evidence and that the same disposition applies. No timing bound or assertion was changed. |
| [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets / 115626859008](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38494291065/job/115626859008) | **Inherited, exact main signature.** The mock-export guard rejects `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.lazy.test.ts:212`, `./worker-turn-execution.js`. Latest scheduled main [run 38493374007 / job 115623794517](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38493374007/job/115623794517), head `f122878c82ad2ff43630954d84609ddc007a7cae`, reports the identical file, line, module, and missing-isolation diagnostic. Main added this mock in `a1ac97bcbe7b4`; neither the test file nor guard is changed by this PR. Latest observed main push `38494689290` skipped this gate (`115629153846`). |
| [openclaw/ci-gate / 115633853033](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38494291065/job/115633853033) | Dependent aggregate failure for the two jobs above. |

`test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/node-worker-launch-wire.e2e.test.ts` passed in [job 115626860969](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38494291065/job/115626860969): **142125 ms**, with normal cleanup and exit 0. All five `test/gateway-subagent-restart.e2e.test.ts` cases passed in job `115626861345` (**237940 ms** total). The earlier seal-oracle, SIGKILL, and subagent failures did not recur.

Workboard's stop/drain/persistence-close paths are unchanged. The restart fixture issues no catalog/card-list request, the shared comparison function has no initialization effects, and the SQLite fixture cannot enter the PostgreSQL transaction branch. No causal link to this PR was found. Each failed job log and the matching scheduled-main log was fetched once.

prs.title: fix(macos): preserve node command lookup after Finder or Dock launch
prs.body:
Closes #169882

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Mac node commands can fail with `command not found` after OpenClaw is opened from Finder or the Dock, even though the same tools are available after login startup.

## User Impact

Mac node commands use the app's existing preferred search folders regardless of launch method. Request-level PATH overrides remain blocked, and approval resolution and execution use the same prepared environment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The login LaunchAgent already uses `CommandResolver.preferredPaths()`, but native command approval and execution inherited the app process's PATH. This change obtains preferred paths through the existing concurrent resolver before policy evaluation and passes them explicitly to `HostEnvSanitizer`. The resulting environment continues through the existing execution path.

## Evidence

A controlled local probe used the original and edited sanitizer followed by `/usr/bin/env` to run the harmless `rg --version` command. The candidate probe supplies trusted search folders directly, including `/opt/homebrew/bin`.

| Probe | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Finder-style inherited PATH omits Homebrew | Exit 127, `env: rg: No such file or directory` | Exit 0, `ripgrep 15.1.0` |
| Login-style inherited PATH includes Homebrew | Exit 0 | Exit 0 |
| Finder-style PATH with a request PATH override | Exit 127, override ignored | Exit 0 through app-owned PATH, override still ignored |
| Finder-style PATH with an absolute tool location | Exit 0 | Exit 0 |

- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw` passed in 107.58 seconds.
- All nine `HostEnvSanitizerTests` passed in an audited standalone SwiftPM bundle containing exact copies of the candidate sanitizer, generated security policy, and edited test file. Reported test time was 0.001 seconds, about 0.048 seconds including runner startup. The new parameterized regression checks app-owned PATH replacement and request override rejection for direct and shell-wrapper modes. Existing environment-security cases also passed.
- Targeted SwiftLint, SwiftFormat lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex review found no actionable P0-P2 defects in the final three-file candidate.

The probe and focused tests ran in a dedicated OS sandbox. The complete Finder/Dock-to-Gateway workflow and full native Mac app test suite were not run on the operator desktop.

- Hosted `openclaw/ci-gate` passed for head `564e4b3f47709783ad44cf3742f889c105da86fb`. [CI result](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38483948375/job/115593707472).
- The sanitizer probe is lower-level evidence. It does not establish the packaged app's CommandResolver, native approval, or Gateway-to-node execution behavior.
- Baseline regression now demonstrated against exact parent production files from `8f164a15f2d6ffaf06ba48e6932a5dc3f8b7768f`. Only the new `searchPaths` argument was removed from baseline test calls to match the old API; all assertions were unchanged. With inherited `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`, the original code failed the two app-owned PATH expectations in each of the direct and shell-wrapper cases, four assertion failures total. All other tests passed. The exact candidate source and test copies passed all nine tests. Both runs used the same restrictive OS sandbox. Process wall times were 0.073 seconds for baseline and 0.050 seconds for candidate.

```text
Original implementation:
Test "app owned search paths replace inherited path and reject request overrides"
  2 test cases failed, 4 issues
  actual PATH: /usr/bin:/bin
  expected PATH: /app-owned/bin:/usr/bin
Test run with 9 tests in 1 suite failed with 4 issues.

Candidate implementation:
Test "app owned search paths replace inherited path and reject request overrides"
  2 test cases passed
Test run with 9 tests in 1 suite passed.
```

- Outstanding behavior proof: native node command results after Finder/Dock launch and login launch, plus a latest-stable upgrade preserving existing settings. These are still open validation items; the green CI and focused regression results do not close them.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep in-flight tool calls pending in session forks
prs.body:
Related: #169564

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes read-only built-in session forks reporting a still-running tool call as aborted, which can make a background reviewer recommend repeating successful work.

## User Impact

A fork taken during tool execution now describes the result as pending, not as a tool error. Parent execution and persisted results are unchanged. Ordinary `/btw` and normal-run transcript repair keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The built-in fork retains the last prepared request and appends subsequently published messages. When an assistant tool call has been published but its result has not, provider replay pairing repair inserts an error result (`aborted` for OpenAI Responses). The fork now supplies a non-error pending result only for those new, unmatched publications, before provider serialization. It keeps the actual prepared request prefix unchanged and never writes the placeholder back to the parent snapshot.

Known limitation: Codex has its own upstream missing-result repair (`codex-rs/core/src/context_manager/normalize.rs:104-107`, `CustomToolCallOutput` with `output: "aborted"`; function calls at lines 59-64). This PR does not rewrite native Codex tool outputs. Mid-call Codex forks remain subject to that upstream behavior; consumers should review at a settled boundary.

## Evidence

- Live evidence from Advisor #169564 at `1b75f3ab75f4e77a349387ef26f661e491ffa922`: six requested sequential `echo N; sleep 10` calls became ten actual executions after three false-abort corrections passed verification. All ten persisted tool results were successful. A captured verification request contained `function_call_output` with `output: "aborted"` for the still-running third call.
- Root cause: `packages/ai/src/transcript-transform.ts:154-170` synthesizes the error while replaying the fork, not in the parent's persisted transcript or its original prepared request. The assistant publication is appended by `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.ts:82-91`.
- Regression covers synchronous and asynchronous pending calls through the real OpenAI Responses and Anthropic transports, and verifies a later fork sees the genuine completed result instead of retaining the placeholder. All four cases failed before the fix for the intended missing-pending-result reason.
- Focused tests: **26 passed across 3 files** (13 fork boundary tests, 2 tool-ID preservation tests, 11 replay sanitization tests).
- Scoped TypeScript project, changed-file oxlint and oxfmt checks passed; `check:madge-import-cycles` reported **0 cycles**. No full typecheck, broad suite, `check-changed`, or autoreview was run.
- Live re-proof: cherry-picked onto the Advisor head as `b31c3fcf879eda6cf23c3b409b6d548571b7b78e` (local only), retaining its old tool-start scheduler. The identical six-command built-in case completed with **exactly 6 successful exec calls**. Reviews during calls 3 and 6 both returned **NO_CHANGE** (3013 ms and 1982 ms); no verification or steering occurred. Both captured fork input arrays contain the pending call's result as `This tool call is still running. Its result is not available yet.`, with no `aborted` tool output. All six genuine persisted results are successful and the parent transcript contains no pending placeholders. Gateway and isolated temporary state were cleaned up.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Android chat composer starts sentences in lowercase when typing with a keyboard that supports automatic sentence capitalization.

## User Impact

Users can start messages and subsequent sentences with automatic capitalization, subject to their keyboard settings. No settings, migration, or changes to existing drafts are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The composer does not request sentence capitalization from Android's input method. This three-line change supplies `KeyboardCapitalization.Sentences` through `KeyboardOptions`, leaving autocorrection and all other keyboard defaults unchanged. It does not rewrite typed text or include the unrelated changes from the closed proposals above.

## Evidence

- Real Android/Gboard reproduction using identical on-screen key positions, with no Shift taps or injected text: the GitHub v2026.10.3 baseline produced `h. h`; the repaired composer produced `H. H`. Android input flags changed from `0x228001` to `0x22c001`, adding only `TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_CAP_SENTENCES` (`0x4000`). Autocorrection was already enabled in both.
- The isolated candidate built from base `4a538d5fb3665c6af278e32026ae8fe4e722de69`, with the exact three-line patch submitted here, also produced `H. H` with actual Gboard taps. Only its test package identity differed. The test was offline; no message was sent, and the synthetic draft was cleared afterward.
- Passed `:app:compileThirdPartyDebugKotlin`, `:app:ktlintCheck`, and `:app:assembleThirdPartyDebug`, including Mermaid asset generation and package identity verification.
- Fresh independent review of the scoped patch reported no P2-or-higher findings. Repository commit hooks passed. No full cross-platform suite or alternate-keyboard coverage is claimed.

AI-assisted implementation and validation; the change is limited to the existing Android chat composer.

prs.title: fix(update): keep updates working after the updater replaces its own files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update` replaces its own installation while the old updater is still running. When that updater lazily imports one of its own modules after the swap, the old hashed chunk is gone and the import fails. Today every release ships about 300 generated update-compat bridge chunks at old hashed names to cover this. A wrong or missing bridge breaks updates from that version, as happened with the 2026.10.1 cleanup bridge.

## User Impact

From the release that includes this change, `openclaw update` keeps loading its own release's modules after the swap, on both Node and Bun, whatever the new package renamed or removed. This is defense in depth:
- Bridges stay the guaranteed path for every supported release and are still generated exactly as on `main`. This PR retires none of them.
- Nothing is written: no new files, config, SQLite rows, sidecars or package fields. A later release can change or remove this mechanism without affecting any installed updater.

## Why This Change Was Made

`withRetainedUpdateRuntime` already copies the updater's `package.json`, `dist` and `node_modules` before the swap and moves worker threads onto that copy. Main-thread lazy imports, however, still resolved against the replaced tree. The updater now redirects them to the retained copy for the rest of the process.

**Node: `module.registerHooks`.**
- Resolution runs against the retained copy. This covers relative and bare requests, `new URL(..., import.meta.url)`, and `__dirname` joins.
- ES modules keep their installed URL but get the retained bytes. Modules loaded before the swap are reused, and `import.meta.url`, query strings and fragments stay stable.
- CommonJS modules and addons load from their retained path, unless they're already in the require cache.
- A `.js` file's format follows the retained package's `type`, never the replacement package's.
- Anything outside the retained roots resolves as before.

**Bun: the existing runtime resolver owner.** Bun ignores Node's module hooks. The updater therefore registers a binding with `registerCapturedPluginModuleResolver`, the shared `Bun.plugin` `onResolve` owner that plugin loading already uses, rather than installing a second plugin.
- Requests from the updater's modules resolve from the retained copy. This covers relative and absolute requests and bare dependencies.
- A target already loaded before the swap keeps its installed path. Bun keys loaded modules by path, so the earlier instance is reused instead of a second copy being evaluated from the retained bytes.
- A Bun without the plugin API, or one that skips the hook, keeps today's behavior: bridges.

An earlier revision of this PR handled Bun differently. The build wrote `dist/update-preload-imports.json`, and the updater imported every chunk on it before the swap. That is gone, along with its post-build scan, the computed-import build guard and the pre-swap preload, which cost about 0.3 s and about 28 MB RSS.

The redirect also has better coverage than the preload. The preload reached only the 55 listed chunks, not the roughly 180 further old chunk names they lazily import. The redirect applies to every import, at any depth.

`retainedImports` is recorded in the existing `updater-runtime-retention` step diagnostics.

## Evidence

### Bun redirect (current head)
- `src/infra/update-retained-imports.bun.test.ts`, upstream Bun 1.4.2, through the real `withRetainedUpdateRuntime`:
  - After `dist` and `node_modules` are deleted, the old chunk, a dependency the new package removed, and a module loaded before the swap all resolve: `old:old-dep:1`. The `1` proves the shared module was reused, not duplicated.
  - Without retention, the same import fails with `ENOENT`.
  - It runs in the `checks-fast-bun-launcher` CI task, where a missing Bun fails instead of skipping.
- The real Bun `openclaw update` (packed install → target, managed service) on this head, now that #170519's `database is locked` fix is on `main`, is still running. Results will be added here.

### Node (code unchanged since these runs)
- Real `openclaw update`, packed install A → target B (Docker, Node 24.21, managed service through the systemd fixture). B has all 8,306 top-level hashed chunks renamed and none of this code.
  - A → B passed: exit 0, B installed, service replaced, no missing-module output, and the post-activation Doctor inspections ran.
  - The negative control (mechanism stubbed out) recorded `Cannot find module …/dist/doctor-health-contributions-rbvQnEa0.mjs` as a warning and skipped the post-activation Doctor inspections.
- The published-driver cell passed: stable 2026.10.1 → this candidate → a bridge-free target, exit 0, 1,254 s (`scripts/e2e/update-first-hop-compat-docker.sh`).
- Windows, native Node 24.21: `update-retained-imports` and `update-retained-runtime` replay passed ([run 38199985755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38199985755)), including the miscased-install retention case.

### Tests (current head, `--maxWorkers=1`)
- `update-retained-imports`: 1 passed. `update-retained-imports.bun` under Bun 1.4.2: 2 passed.
- `update-command`: 15 passed. `runtime-postbuild`: 149 passed. `ci-check-family-scope`: 36 passed. `ci-workflow-planning`: 600 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, type-aware oxlint and oxfmt are clean.

### CI
- Red checks on the previous head were inherited. `checks-ui (3/3)` (a sidebar test timeout) and `docker-seed-e2e` (`mcp-channels`) fail the same way on unrelated PRs; details in the PR comments.

## Gaps
- Bun on Windows and the full Windows update flow have not been run.
- No published updater carries this mechanism yet. The first release that ships it makes the next release's first-hop lane the published proof.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): reduce live-event shell redraws
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link keeps invalidating unrelated shell components while live Gateway events arrive. The campaign census recorded 125 events in about 20 seconds and recurring sidebar/chat-page churn. This lane narrows event publications at their existing owners.

Current head: `081f68689642`, based on main `5e9608dec7c5`. Matched measurement and fresh review are complete. Exact-head UI CI passed; broader CI has inherited static failures. Final-head full UI E2E completed with one unresolved presentation-fixture timeout, detailed below.

## User Impact

Live content stays with its pane; the chat page no longer redraws for every roster publication. The sidebar ignores unchanged or undisplayed presence facts, hidden catalog packets, unchanged workload counts, and snapshot-write receipts. Visible presence, title, attention, unread, workload, and hovercard facts keep their existing owners.

**Remaining scope:** held hidden/outside-window roster changes still forward to the sidebar projection. That forwarding also owns child loading, cache capture, narration, pagination, and rail/filter projections. Removing it without moving those responsibilities would break behavior. Fine-grained Solid child work and agent-card renders are not measured by this fixture.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pane's existing presentation owner derives accepted titles; the parent roster subscription and redundant title binding are deleted. SessionDataController compares presentation/loading/group/error and UI-owned archive/deletion/PR/prepared-work facts before publishing through its existing shared frame. A paired subscription module owns setup/teardown while authoritative data stays in the controller.

Presence comparisons cover displayed identities, watches, and activity. Hovercards consume Gateway presence directly; the per-shell-render notification loop is deleted. Snapshot completion changes only its receipt attribute. Workload counts publish meaningful map/error changes.

Main migrated the sidebar to Solid during this lane. The rebase keeps that implementation and drops the superseded Lit Inbox/stable-card-callback patch. The footer acquires its own Gateway projection so name/avatar changes do not require a sidebar publication. Post-render expiry synchronization occurs only when displayed membership changes, preserving the existing pre-render wakeup when a deadline crosses during projection.

## Evidence

Pinned main `5e9608dec7c5` versus final head `081f68689642`, with identical final synthetic fixture/probe and matching build-ID metadata. After a dashboard reload settles, 125 live frames are scheduled over 20 seconds. Fixture: 300 sessions, 120 people, 30 pins, six agents/plugins, 240 messages, and 12 widgets.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Solid sidebar owner invalidations | 168 | 75 |
| Solid sidebar prepare/commit passes | 168 / 168 | 75 / 75 |
| Lit chat-page renders | 76 | 0 |
| Lit chat-pane renders | 111 | 122 |

Sidebar invalidations/projection passes fall **55.4%**. Recorded-window averages are **7.66 → 3.59/s**, over **21.943 → 20.906 seconds**, including post-stream settle. There is no exact-20-second snapshot API. One baseline idle pass before the first live event is retained in the total/table. Loaded-host timers, frame coalescing, refresh scheduling, and event attribution make counts/timings noisy. **Pane counts increased by eleven (+9.9%); their cause is unresolved and no pane improvement is claimed.** Request stacks identify the existing ChatStateController and virtualizer owners, but do not establish whether the difference is scheduling variation or a regression.

| Event label | Frames | Owner invalidations before→after | Prepare passes before→after | Commit passes before→after | Lit chat page before→after | Lit chat pane before→after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| presence.offscreen | 25 | 48→3 | 48→3 | 48→3 | 0→0 | 1→4 |
| presence.visible | 10 | 16→7 | 16→7 | 16→7 | 6→0 | 10→6 |
| sessions.changed.visible | 10 | 15→10 | 15→10 | 15→10 | 20→0 | 0→0 |
| sessions.changed.hidden-held | 10 | 14→10 | 14→10 | 14→10 | 14→0 | 1→0 |
| sessions.changed.outside-window | 10 | 16→13 | 16→13 | 16→13 | 4→0 | 1→3 |
| session.message.open | 10 | 12→14 | 12→14 | 12→14 | 24→0 | 41→45 |
| chat.delta.open | 25 | 12→6 | 12→6 | 12→6 | 4→0 | 55→63 |
| catalog.host | 10 | 12→0 | 12→0 | 12→0 | 2→0 | 1→0 |
| cron.unrelated | 5 | 3→0 | 3→0 | 3→0 | 2→0 | 1→1 |
| run-state.unrelated | 10 | 19→12 | 19→12 | 19→12 | 0→0 | 0→0 |
| idle | 0 | 1→0 | 1→0 | 1→0 | 0→0 | 0→0 |

Mapped origins show **direct offscreen-presence invalidations 25→0** and **direct hidden-catalog invalidations 10→0**, with six visible-presence publications retained. All final sidebar requests use the existing session frame owner. The three final requests labeled offscreen presence originate from trailing roster/lineage work. Hidden-held/outside-window labels still have 10/13 projection passes, including trailing refresh work.

Solid counters measure owner invalidations and projection lifecycle passes, not full component renders or all binding work. The temporary benchmark tap restores the native setter and forwarded receiver; wrappers restore at capture end. Measured method time excludes stack-capture overhead. Lit zeroes for migrated sidebar/roster/attention/app-shell tags are coverage gaps. The grouped-roster fixture does not mount agent cards.

Both full screenshots were inspected and are synthetic-only. Streaming progress stays visible, the selected visible row remains in the viewport, and target hidden/outside-window rows remain absent. Final snapshots do not prove intermediate presence/unread/run transitions; focused correctness E2E covers those.

Before:

![Synthetic Solid-sidebar baseline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2bf4979f-2ee4-45c8-b77b-6ab1321b4f0d)

After:

![Synthetic Solid-sidebar final head](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11e64bae-d7bb-4299-9c5f-98b8b8ae1c5c)

## Proof

Focused contracts fail on the original broad publishers and pass after the fix: no-op presence leaves the shell idle, visible changes update, live/late-open cards retain current facts, unchanged workload counts do not publish, and pending archive/cancel/PR facts update held rows.

After the Solid rebase: sidebar people **148/148** (28.95 s runner; expiry, visible presence, cards, footer name/avatar); Online **19/19** (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, 9.44 s wall); session-data event refresh **29/29** (4.31 s wall). Earlier focused pnpm wall times: person data 5.67 s, chat page 7.91 s, page refresh 4.02 s, pane menu 6.88 s, pane presentation 3.70 s. Attention/row/pane-frame/identity contracts also passed. Fresh isolated reviews are clean with no accepted P0–P2 findings.

Prior focused AWS `cbx_e35b12354a42`, run `run_cf468a4e79d6aab86ff5e6b66b3ab4db`: **21 browser tests/seven files passed**, covering archive batch, archive, PRs, attention scope, viewer presence, activity connections, child attention. Released. Prior-head full configured projects completed with 769 passed files/3,404 passed tests and one existing fixture-gated skip, across `cbx_bf34b4ae857e` and `cbx_b3ebd8080d15`; that is historical proof, not final-head proof.

Final AWS `cbx_da2f7ff4f36e`, changed-check run `run_73e019504bf4fa9c970b4e2a4f513d58`: all gates passed except the inherited first-party mock-export violation in `test/helpers/openclaw-test-process.test.ts:5` (15m17.94s command). Core test graphs, UI/scripts types, lint, format, and all dead-export scans passed. The chained tests were not admitted after that failure. Full default UI E2E completed independently as `run_39e491e151db971e341838eb9419f775` on unchanged `081f68689642`: **771 passed files, one failed file, one skipped file; 3,414 passed assertions, one failed assertion, one skipped assertion; 6,686.70 s**. All four configured projects ran; five source hashes matched and all skip/prebuilt flags were unset. The sole failure was `presentation-primitives.e2e.test.ts`, Lit light desktop in `ui-e2e-serial-standalone`: the initial settings fixture never reached its ready marker within 30 s. The other seven cases in that file passed. No changed runtime owner is in its static import graph, but diagnostics contain no browser error establishing a cause. Project inventory: bundled 695 files/3,147 assertions passed; standalone four/26 passed; serial 14/36 passed; serial-standalone 58 files/205 assertions passed, one file/assertion failed, one file/assertion skipped. Existing skip: `desktop-resize.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, configured-worker-carrier case. The complete per-file inventory is retained in the lane evidence.

The unchanged final-head targeted replay `run_3009ff55724be62334e2c262683f5ad6` passed all eight cases in 24.26 s (27.09 s command), with native sync and no skip/prebuilt flags. This does not establish a fix. The 95-file fixture/dependency/startup closure is byte-identical on head, pinned baseline, and CI main base. Diagnostics cannot classify the timeout: this suite does not install the error-event ring, and Playwright’s installed clock returns empty resource-entry lists. The original full-run failure remains unresolved.

Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38488789849 is red on inherited static failures. All three `checks-ui` shards and selected `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` passed. CI tested generated merge `abcc55b2` into main `653003a01098`. Its TS2349 at `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-node-artifacts.ts:490` is absent from pinned base `5e9608dec7c5`; the mock-export violation is already present there. Both failing files in the generated merge match main `653003` byte-for-byte. The mock file also matches pinned base and lane head. Logs are retained. AWS run `run_1fdcb30ffe0940c88db4096afdd67fe0` extracted the hash-verified committed main `653003` archive, verified matching dependency manifests/lockfile, copied dependencies inside its isolated source root as required by the compiler owner, and ran its own `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`: the exact TS2349 at line 490 reproduced (exit 2; 27.31 s command). Validation recovery: a prior 90-minute lease expired during serial tests; explicit-project recovery initially omitted CLI/UI prerequisites, then completed through the canonical preparer. An unused fixture type export, intentional native-probe lint exceptions, and activity membership ordering were corrected with clean review. The previous Solid-head full-suite attempt was canceled before command admission when probe lint failed.
