prs.title: fix(agent): preserve literal message-file paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agent turns read the wrong prompt when `--message-file` names a file with leading or trailing whitespace and a trimmed-name neighbor exists.

## User Impact

User impact: ordinary agent turns and `agent exec` read the exact quoted filename. Whitespace-only options still fail, and `agent exec --message-file -` still reads stdin.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both prompt-source adapters trimmed filesystem paths before opening them. Use the existing nonblank-string reader to reject blank input while preserving the original path. Regression cases create both filenames with different contents, so reading the neighbor cannot pass.

## Evidence

Product head: `4fdad72dbd3a1233c4e76b02396c03ff725bd201`; RED base: `44c918f3900770412a3cd912eaa0c718b2e3356c`. Both were built normally with `pnpm build cliStartup`; build stamps matched their clean checkout heads. Node 24.16.0, Linux.

Real production entries, same commands and scenarios on both heads:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs agent --local --agent main --session-id "$SESSION_ID" --message-file "$ROOT/local-task.md " --thinking off --timeout 30 --json
node openclaw.mjs agent exec --message-file "$ROOT/exec-task.md " --config "$CONFIG" --state-dir "$STATE" --cwd "$WORKSPACE" --thinking off --timeout 30 --json
node openclaw.mjs agent exec --message-file '- ' --config "$CONFIG" --state-dir "$STATE" --cwd "$WORKSPACE" --thinking off --timeout 30 --json
node openclaw.mjs sessions --all-agents --json
```

The isolated fixture placed `WRONG_PROMPT` in each trimmed-name neighbor and `RIGHT_PROMPT` in each exact filename. A loopback OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint recorded the actual model request and returned a complete streaming reply. It used a synthetic key, no real provider, channels, tools or Gateway service. The `'- '` case supplied different file and stdin markers.

| Scenario | Base observation | Head observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary embedded turn, trailing-space filename | HTTP request contained `WRONG_PROMPT`, exit 0 | HTTP request contained `RIGHT_PROMPT`, exit 0 |
| `agent exec`, trailing-space filename | HTTP request contained `WRONG_PROMPT`, exit 0 | HTTP request contained `RIGHT_PROMPT`, exit 0 |
| `agent exec`, literal `'- '` file | HTTP request contained `STDIN_PROMPT`, exit 0 | HTTP request contained `DASH_PROMPT`, exit 0 |
| Plain file, both entries | `PLAIN_PROMPT`, exit 0 | `PLAIN_PROMPT`, exit 0 |
| Exact `-` stdin control | `STDIN_PROMPT`, exit 0 | `STDIN_PROMPT`, exit 0 |
| Whitespace-only option, both entries | exit 1; 0 additional HTTP requests | exit 1; 0 additional HTTP requests |

Head HTTP recorder summary, in invocation order:

```text
POST /v1/chat/completions model=file-proof marker=RIGHT_PROMPT
POST /v1/chat/completions model=file-proof marker=PLAIN_PROMPT
POST /v1/chat/completions model=file-proof marker=RIGHT_PROMPT
POST /v1/chat/completions model=file-proof marker=PLAIN_PROMPT
POST /v1/chat/completions model=file-proof marker=DASH_PROMPT
POST /v1/chat/completions model=file-proof marker=STDIN_PROMPT
completed CLI replies: 6 x "synthetic proof reply"
sessions --all-agents --json: 6 persisted synthetic sessions
```

The real CLI exercised `agent-via-gateway.ts` with `--local` and the retained `agent-exec-input.ts` owner. Gateway dispatch has an additional focused regression, with real file reads and an asserted outbound prompt. The ordinary CLI's proposed stdin feature in #167122 is independent of this existing file-path bug; this patch does not add ordinary stdin support.

Validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-exec-input.test.ts src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: RED 2 failed / 67 passed; GREEN 69 passed, runner wall time 94.71s (Vitest 87.49s). Type-aware lint/type checking and formatting passed for all four changed files. Independent adversarial review: PASS, no P0–P3 findings.

Scope: 4 files; production +7/-3, tests +40/-22. No config, protocol, schema, permission, dependency or upgrade changes. Existing BOM, size limits, streaming reads and file-error controls remain covered by the focused suite.

Not tested: a live Gateway/network agent dispatch, external providers, Windows trailing-space filenames, or the complete repository suite. No production instance was touched. Fixture server and child processes exited; synthetic state was retained outside the product branch for inspection.

prs.title: feat: auto-title Slack thread sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Channel-originated thread sessions currently spend their sidebar title on repetitive transport metadata such as the Slack channel and thread timestamp. That makes concurrent threads difficult to distinguish and leaves no compact visual source indicator. This change gives new Slack thread sessions a concise semantic title from their opening/root message while preserving manual labels and showing the source channel separately.

## Summary

- generate semantic titles for newly created Slack thread sessions from the opening/root message
- preserve manual labels and existing session-generation commit guards while running title work in the Gateway-owned background lifecycle
- show compact source-channel marks in the sidebar, including unread and descendant-running compatibility

## Implementation notes

- top-level app mentions, message-first mentions, `requireMention: false` roots, and regex-mentioned roots now mark their newly seeded thread session as the first thread turn
- Slack thread starters are bounded before entering `MsgContext`, and channel title generation treats that supplied root as authoritative so transcript persistence cannot race it with a later reply
- transport metadata remains metadata rather than title ownership; manual labels and semantic display names still win
- source-channel artwork is decorative, with a screen-reader source label alongside it

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare-thread-context.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare-thread-turn-metadata.test.ts src/channels/turn/run-channel-turn.finalize.test.ts src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.test.ts src/config/sessions/metadata.test.ts` — 278 passed
- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/components/session-leading-indicator.test.ts` — 4 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:test:src && pnpm tsgo:ui && pnpm tsgo:test:ui`
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base db469180137ce74c9404390fe43e94da4122f55f` — passed
- `oxlint` on all changed TypeScript files — 0 warnings, 0 errors

## Screenshots

### Before

![Baseline sidebar without source-channel marks](https://rapidand-screenshots.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/verification/50c4e10c62fa4c83c19939e26fd91408c01d3ac9/68ac1760ecce82431cc370c0/before-final.png)

prs.title: fix(imap): keep transient DKIM failures retryable in the sender gate
prs.body:
Closes #150558

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: validly signed mail is refused by the IMAP sender gate when the DKIM public-key lookup times out. The gate collapsed that transient DNS condition into a permanent `dmarc-fail` verdict (`transient: false`) even though DKIM reported `temperror` for the same message, so the mail was treated as an unverified sender instead of a retryable failure.

## User Impact

Mail from senders whose DNS is slow is no longer rejected as unverified: a timed-out DKIM key lookup now surfaces as a retryable authentication error (`reason: "authentication-temperror"`, `transient: true`), so the message can be retried instead of dropped. Permanently failing signatures keep the existing non-retryable `dmarc-fail` refusal, so real authentication failures are not weakened.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `evaluateImapSender` (`extensions/imap/src/sender-gate.ts`), the retry hint was derived from the DMARC status alone. When DMARC reported `fail`, the gate always returned `reason: "dmarc-fail"` with `transient: false`, ignoring a nested DKIM `temperror` such as `DNS failure: ETIMEOUT` on the key lookup. The gate now marks the result transient when the DMARC status is `temperror` or any DKIM result has `status.result === "temperror"`; only non-transient failures keep `dmarc-fail`.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests added in `extensions/imap/src/sender-gate.test.ts`:

- a hand-built DKIM `temperror` result under DMARC `fail` now resolves to `{ accepted: false, strength: "unverified", reason: "authentication-temperror", transient: true }` (this case yields `dmarc-fail` / `transient: false` on current `main`),
- an end-to-end fixture: a message signed with `mailauth`'s `dkimSign` is verified via `authenticate()` with a resolver that throws `ETIMEOUT` for `default._domainkey.example.com` and returns `v=DMARC1; p=reject` for `_dmarc.example.com` — DKIM reports `temperror`, DMARC reports `fail`, and the gate keeps the failure retryable,
- a permanently failing signature still returns `reason: "dmarc-fail"` with `transient: false`, so the retry-class change does not turn a real authentication failure into a retryable one.

The end-to-end fixture exercises the real `mailauth` pipeline rather than mocked verdicts: the message is signed with a real 2048-bit RSA key via `dkimSign`, verified through `authenticate()` with an injected DNS resolver whose key lookup throws `ETIMEOUT` — reproducing the exact temperror condition from #150558. The asserted outcome (`transient: true` / `reason: "authentication-temperror"`) is the classification that routes the message into the existing bounded-retry owner; the retry-and-recovery loop itself is pre-existing watcher behavior this PR deliberately does not touch.

Full CI (`pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test`) will run on this PR; the extension lane covers this file via `pnpm test:extension imap`.

prs.title: feat(qa): compare recorded Decision answers offline
prs.body:
Related: #156341 (historical context; closed as not planned)

## What Problem This Solves

QA authors need to inspect how recorded Decision answers compare with explicit references without making another model call or dropping failed and unscored cases.

## User Impact

There is no change to normal agent behavior. The existing QA Lab confidence-report command gains an opt-in offline replay lane: JSON retains each identifiable case, its captured answer and provenance; Markdown summarizes agreement, disagreement, and unscored counts.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a standalone QA contribution, not a dependency of the withdrawn task-routing proposal. It changes no core routing, model selection, provider execution, SDK export, runtime configuration, or dependency. It remains useful for reviewing recorded JEV, local Decision-model, or other compatible typed results without adopting a new routing contract.

The replay compares Choice acceptable sets, explicit Boolean thresholds/operators, and inclusive Score intervals against scorer-only reviewed references. It preserves original probabilities and optional confidence. Missing, unreviewed, disputed, or unscorable references remain unscored; malformed and failed executions fail pipeline integrity separately from semantic disagreement. A valid replay can pass while answers disagree with references.

This does not run a live benchmark, certify model quality, measure calibration, enable consumers, or settle the closed RFC's broader evaluation roadmap. Repeat/group metadata is retained without treating repeats as independent samples. The existing report remains the only file-reading/output owner.

prs.title: fix: in-flight subagent announce replay is credited as delivered
prs.body:
Closes #136513

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a duplicate subagent completion announce with the same idempotency key is recorded as delivered when Gateway returns `in_flight` while the original handoff is still pending. Also prevents a later registry retry from active-steering the same completion into a successor requester before the original Gateway key is reconciled — including when original-handoff replay fails.

## User Impact

User impact: registry retry custody stays open until terminal announce evidence exists, so a completion is not retired from an idempotent replay that has not finished. Retries rejoin the original handoff instead of injecting into a later active requester turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sendSubagentAnnounceDirectly` treated every nonterminal Gateway response as `{ delivered: true, path: "direct" }` for public completion announces. That shortcut stopped same-attempt media fallback, and it also persisted delivery credit before a terminal result.

This PR keeps the fallback suppression (`terminal: true` plus `delivered: false` with `completion_handoff_pending`) and stops the credit. Dispatch already honored `terminal` on steer-primary; it now honors it on direct-primary too, so a retryable pending result does not fall through to steer fallback.

ClawSweeper P1 (retention): returning `retryable` schedules another registry attempt. If the original pending handoff later becomes active (or settles and a successor run becomes active), the next attempt's active-requester branch could steer before Gateway idempotency. This revision retains the original handoff key across retryable attempts, skips active steering while that key is retained or still the active embedded run, and releases ownership on terminal retirement / cleanup / settle-batch completion.

ClawSweeper P1 (fence): the direct owner's catch returns `disposition: "retryable"` without `terminal`. After retention, a replay failure could still reach dispatch steer-fallback. `settleCompletionHandoffRetention` now marks retained retryable results `terminal: true` so fallback steering stays fenced until ownership releases.

Requester-settle cases that set `expectsCompletionMessage: false` still keep the previous pending-as-delivered mapping. First-attempt active requester steering is unchanged when nothing is retained yet.

## Evidence

Focused tests plus real Gateway harness on HEAD `5958eb9ae52662c08e3c69ad6dcc95a266e55da0`:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-support.config.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-completion-handoff-retention.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-dispatch.test.ts \
  -t "handoff retention|self-steer|successor|in-flight completion announce|terminal retryable|fences steer-fallback"
```

Result: 10 passed (retention lifecycle, fence on retained retryable failure, in-flight non-credit, pending→active rejoin, successor rejoin, pending→replay failure→no steer-fallback, dispatch terminal).

New cases:
- `fences retryable replay failures while the original handoff is retained`
- `fences steer-fallback when retained handoff replay fails while a successor requester is active`

Also merged `origin/main` (conflict resolved in `subagent-announce-delivery.runtime.ts`: keep both `resolveActiveEmbeddedRunOwner` and `queueGuardedEmbeddedAgentMessageWithOutcomeAsync`).

## Real Behavior Proof

- Tested HEAD: `5958eb9ae52662c08e3c69ad6dcc95a266e55da0`
- Claim: same-key Gateway `in_flight` / pending completion announce is not credited delivered; retries rejoin the original handoff under retained ownership (including when a successor requester is active); terminal settlement releases retention; registry row reloads from SQLite after in-memory reset
- Exercised surface: production `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` → `sendSubagentAnnounceDirectly` / `settleCompletionHandoffRetention` through real Gateway `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcess` admission (`resolveGatewayContext` → live kernel), not `vi.mocked(callGateway)`

### Environment

- Worktree: `/mnt/adata/opt/openclaw-worktrees/136513-inflight-announce-credit`
- Branch: `fix/136513-inflight-announce-credit`
- Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + loopback ports via `startGatewayServerHarness` (auth none)
- Provider held with `agentCommandMock` deferred so Gateway admission stays real while the original run remains in flight

### Scenario

1. Register a child subagent run in the SQLite registry.
2. Start a real Gateway agent turn with the announce idempotency key; hold provider execution.
3. Call `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` with `resolveGatewayContext` pointing at the live kernel → observe pending undelivered + retained handoff.
4. Retry while a successor requester run is active → still pending / rejoin; steer queue is not called.
5. Release the original provider turn → terminal `ok`; retry delivers; retention released.
6. `resetSubagentRegistryForTests` + `initSubagentRegistry` → child row reloads from SQLite.

### Command

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts \
  src/gateway/server.subagent-announce-completion-handoff.harness.test.ts
```

Supporting (mocked Gateway responses, still useful for fence/lifecycle):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-support.config.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-completion-handoff-retention.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-completion-handoff-lifecycle.test.ts
```

### Relevant output

```text
✓ public completion handoff real Gateway admission > keeps same-key in_flight undelivered, rejoins under successor activity, and settles registry (670ms)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  1 passed (1)

✓ completion handoff retention lifecycle (10 passed across retention + lifecycle files)
```

Artifact: local `/tmp/oc-150933-proof/` (gateway-harness-v2.log, unit-lifecycle-v2.log, SUMMARY.txt). Not committed.

### Observed

- Same-key `in_flight` → `delivered: false`, `reason: completion_handoff_pending`, `disposition: retryable`, `terminal: true`
- Successor-active retry does not call steer queue; ownership stays retained until terminal settlement
- Terminal success reconciles retention (`shouldJoinOriginalCompletionHandoff` false) while registry row survives SQLite reload after in-memory reset

### Not tested

- Live paid provider / multi-host Gateway
- Hard deadline expiry / give-up retirement path under retained handoff
- Failure-terminal path on the harness (success path covered; failure covered in mocked lifecycle fence cases)

## ClawSweeper

- Resolved P1: retain/join original handoff across retries before active steering.
- Resolved P1: fence steer-fallback while the original handoff is retained (error-path replay).
- Resolved merge conflicts with current main.
- Real Gateway admission + registry SQLite recovery harness added on this head.

## Sources

- #136513
- Closed design reference: #136820 (retention module adapted onto current main)

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): stop displaced reply runs from cascading model fallback
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), turns on the `claude-cli` backend intermittently end with

```
Embedded agent failed before reply: Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
```

Observed on a macOS LaunchAgent gateway: 8 of 92 `claude-cli` turns in one day, always ~300 ms after the `cli turn: … durationMs=` completion line. 0 occurrences the day before on 2026.9.2.

**Mechanism.** A steering interrupt (`abortByUser()`) clears the reply operation's registry slot synchronously, but the backend CLI subprocess keeps running. When it finishes, the model-fallback loop prepares the next candidate, and `bindToolAuthorityRoute` (`reply-run-registry.operation.ts`) throws because `activeRunsByKey.get(sessionKey) !== operation`. That throw is a plain `Error`, so `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` does not recognise it. The fallback runner treats a local coordination failure as a provider/model failure, cascades through every remaining candidate, and surfaces a generic harness error to the user.

This is the fallback-classification half of #148707 and the defect tracked in #148789. It is related to, but does not close, #139847.

**Relation to other work.** #149518 (merged) halts model fallback for closed session-placement settlement and superseded aborts; this PR applies the same principle to the one remaining harness-level throw that still reaches the fallback loop as `reason=unknown`. #150872 (open) takes the complementary route of letting a superseded operation bind its route anyway. The two do not conflict: this PR leaves the authority guard exactly as strict as it is and only changes how its rejection is classified, so it stays correct whether or not #150872 lands, and it covers the guard's other rejection reasons (`result` already set, no snapshot bound) as well.

**Change.** `bindToolAuthorityRoute` now throws a typed `ReplyRunDisplacedToolAuthorityError` (same message, so existing log matching and user copy are unchanged), and that name is registered in `RUNTIME_COORDINATION_ERROR_NAMES`. The fallback loop therefore aborts the displaced turn instead of blaming the model and trying the next candidate. Steering displacement itself is untouched: the throw is intentional and stays.

**Not in this PR.** The second half of #148707 — the input that arrived mid-run ending up as `interrupted` in `session_pending_inputs` — is a separate defect in the pending-input staleness sweep (`readSessionPendingInputOwnerIds` requires the owner's `sessionId` to equal the current `session_nodes.current_session_id`, so a rekey makes a still-live owner look dead, and a later `finish("cancelled")` becomes a silent no-op). I have two failing repro tests for it and will post them on #148707 rather than mix an unresolved custody-semantics question into this fix.

## Evidence

- New test `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError > returns true for a reply run displaced by a steering re-admission (#148707)` in `src/agents/failover-error.test.ts`: **fails on `main` @ 162d0fcf** (`expected false to be true`, 1 failed / 81 passed), **passes on this branch**.
- New `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.displacement.test.ts` documents the displacement sequence at registry level (green before and after by design: the throw is intended; only its classification changes). Placed in a sibling file to stay under the line-cap ratchet.
- Targeted suites on this branch (rebased on 162d0fcf): `failover-error`, `reply-run-registry`, `reply-run-registry.displacement`, `model-fallback`, `agent-runner-execution-provider-failures`, plus the two suites added by #149518 (`agent-runner-execution-terminal-failures`, `reply-operation-abort`) → 7 files, 517 tests, 0 failed.
- Wider lane before the rebase (b31ad046) `pnpm exec vitest run src/auto-reply/reply src/agents/harness/tool-authority.runtime.test.ts --pool=forks` → 315 files, 6975 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. (Without `--pool=forks` the default thread pool crashed a worker twice in unrelated files on a 16 GB Mac mini; reruns were green.)
- `pnpm check:changed` → exit 0.
- No CHANGELOG changes.

AI-assisted: diagnosis, tests and patch were produced with Claude and reviewed against the installed 2026.9.4 bundle and live gateway logs.

## Runtime evidence (added after ClawSweeper review)

Isolated gateway started from this branch's build (`2026.9.4-39b88ba4`, rebased on `main` 162d0fcf): separate state dir, port 19789 loopback, own log file, no channels. Agents: `main` = anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 with fallback anthropic/claude-opus-5, both `agentRuntime.id: claude-cli`; `broken` = anthropic/claude-bogus-model-9 (does not exist) with fallback anthropic/claude-sonnet-5. prs.title: fix: support Android procfs process identity for cron
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #150766.

Android/Termux cron runs currently fail during durable run admission because the shared process-start identity reader only accepts `process.platform === "linux"`. On Android, the runtime falls through to `null`, so cron cannot establish the process identity required by its durable-fence protection.

## User Impact

Scheduled and manual cron runs on Android/Termux fail before execution and repeatedly log:

`cron run cannot acquire a durable fence without process start identity`

This blocks automation even though Android/Termux exposes the same `/proc/<pid>/stat` procfs data needed by the existing Linux parser.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `getProcessStartTime()` implementation already parses `/proc/<pid>/stat` and the existing cron receipt logic intentionally rejects a missing identity to preserve PID-reuse protection. The focused repair is therefore to allow Android to use the same procfs identity reader rather than weakening or bypassing the durable-fence invariant.

## Changes

- Extend `getProcessStartTime()` to accept both Linux and Android procfs environments.
- Update the function documentation to describe the shared Linux/Android path.
- Add a regression test that mocks an Android platform and verifies `/proc/<pid>/stat` start-time parsing.

## Evidence

Current-source review of #150766 shows that Android falls through the platform guard in `src/shared/pid-alive.ts`, while cron admission rejects the resulting null identity. The issue's maintainer review also identified this shared-reader boundary as the focused repair point.

## Validation

- Branch is 2 commits ahead of `main` and 0 commits behind at the submitted revision.
- Regression coverage added for Android procfs parsing.
- Hosted CI checks are running against the exact PR head; no completed failure has been reported so far.
- Live Android/Termux execution is the remaining merge gate; it requires an authorized Android/Termux environment and cannot be truthfully claimed from this environment.

Maintainers can modify the fork branch to extend the runtime validation if needed.

prs.title: fix(telegram): isolate private-topic buffering and cancellation
prs.body:
Closes #142107

## What Problem This Solves

Messages sent to different private Telegram topics can be combined or blocked behind another topic, and an authorized `/stop` can discard another topic's buffered input. This still reproduces on main `de2993ac45342a39bbbcdf37663e82cf6a000967`.

## User Impact

Private topics buffer and admit input independently. Stopping one topic preserves pending input in other topics, including forwarded messages. Forum topics, channel Direct Messages, unthreaded chats, public conversation IDs, and persisted session routing keep their existing contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the private topic ID in the Telegram inbound conversation key consumed by both enqueue and cancellation. The repair is rebased onto the current buffering implementation, which shares the normal and forwarded buffer identity. It preserves that implementation, authorized control-command bypass, and same-topic ordering.

As clarified in [the maintainer's comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142122#issuecomment-5769990419), merged #153829 handles authorized control commands and does not supersede ordinary private-topic buffering or cross-topic cancellation isolation. #142533 remains open and unmerged.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto main `de2993ac45342a39bbbcdf37663e82cf6a000967`; a later merge-tree check against main `eff939dc29c3151090ff1850ebd5ea9a5e1f1375` is conflict-free, with no intervening Telegram changes.
- The same five behavioral tests fail against the unmodified pinned main production code: one reply batch replaces two topic replies, topic B waits behind A, ordinary and forwarded `/stop` clear A's buffered input, and unauthorized `/stop` leaves A/B coalesced. With this repair, all five pass.
- Final commit `9741ac35e5c2606decee53375e876bea1a2635d6` validation: 43 passing tests across inbound processing, buffer identity, sequential keys, and topic conversation parsing. The reply regression calls production `deliverReplies` and verifies both reply text and serialized `message_thread_id` / `reply_to_message_id`; its downstream handler and Bot API are mocked. This is deterministic owner-boundary proof, not live Telegram proof.
- The old exact-head `test-types` failure used the removed `commands.useAccessGroups` fixture field. The fixture now uses public `commands.allowFrom` and current pipeline methods. Full extension test typechecking passes locally.
- Changed-scope checks pass (exit 0), including production and full extension test types, formatting, lint, unused exports, plugin boundaries, doctor guard tests, and runtime/import-cycle guards.
- `git diff --check` passes. Independent P2 autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Live Telegram proof remains unavailable. The current repository Test Server doctor reports `ok: false`: no existing Convex, bunx, or npx broker launcher is available. No credentials or accounts were created and no real-chat test messages were sent. The owner must privately supply the existing broker access, then verify actual private bot topic support on the isolated Test Server; a forum-topic run would not prove this DM behavior.
- Five Telegram files changed, with no configuration, schema, or dependency changes. New-head GitHub CI and required live evidence remain separate merge gates.

Thanks @aspalagin for the report and reproduction. The pre-existing ClawSweeper implementation run stopped before completion without publishing a PR.

Maintainer edits and access to this fork's workflow secrets are allowed.

prs.title: fix(markdown): stream ordinary code without losing reasoning context
prs.body:
## Status

Draft: review still finds cases where draft text is incorrectly included in the final answer after reasoning resumes. Further corrections and complete evidence are preserved locally, but no clean review or merge is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

Replies could stop updating after a second inline code span or a fenced code block, then appear all at once when the model finished.

## Change

Stream ordinary text and code bytes as they arrive. Keep their Markdown context so actual reasoning tags still receive conservative ownership checks. This uses the existing Markdown parser, with no dependency changes or second grammar.

The repair also removes the proposed repeated prefix parsing and cross-block release that could disclose reasoning text in a later table.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the freeze on pinned main through a real Gateway and Control UI. Repaired replies update before the final event and preserve the transcript after reload.
- Reproduced the original candidate's table reasoning disclosure; the repaired candidate keeps it hidden.
- Focused partitioner, parser-work and direct/managed transport tests pass. The new transport regression fails on the baseline because the opening code bytes do not stream.
- Real Telegram Test Server DM: one provider request, successive preview edits before completion, exact final text and code entities, no hidden-reasoning disclosure. Both test messages were deleted and credential scratch was removed.

Ambiguous actual reasoning tags may remain buffered until ownership is known. Ordinary backticks alone no longer hold the reply.

## Existing limitation

Expanded end-to-end testing also found that the downstream subscriber removes literal reasoning tags from indented code in live/final Gateway events and infers thinking from literal code examples. The identical failure occurs on the pinned baseline; stored history and the completed browser preserve the text. This separate subscriber defect is documented for follow-up. This PR does not claim that all literal-tag delivery cases pass.

prs.title: fix: preserve queued reply retries while WhatsApp reconnects
prs.body:
Related: #127868

## What Problem This Solves

Queued replies spend retry attempts while WhatsApp is disconnected, even though no platform send can start.

## User Impact

Queued replies wait for the account listener without consuming their remaining retry budget. Reconnection can then deliver them; actual send failures still count normally.

**Draft for maintainer design review:** the optional plugin readiness contract below needs acceptance before merge. If a channel stays unready indefinitely, its queued replies remain pending instead of exhausting retries during that wait. This deferral policy needs explicit maintainer acceptance. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Let the channel’s existing durable-delivery adapter report synchronous recovery readiness. WhatsApp reads its account-owned active listener. Recovery checks before reserving an attempt and again before the first platform dispatch; a late disconnect uses the existing ownership-fenced pre-dispatch rollback.

This recovery-only hook keeps live-send policy admission and its permanent-rejection contract unchanged. Channels without the hook retain their existing behavior. Unknown sends still require reconciliation, exhausted budgets still terminate, and an admitted multi-part send retains its normal failure accounting.

The design question from #127868 remains explicit: should transient readiness use this optional `durableFinal.getRecoveryReadiness` hook? Extending policy admission to include a transient result would also change live-send handling and existing result consumers. This draft provides a working, tested alternative for that discussion.

## Evidence

On `a58755e9ac9f8601684a692491e65b710485fe4c`, the existing WhatsApp recovery suite passed. Adding counter assertions to its real durable-send/reconnect-recovery path failed: a disconnected drain changed `{retryCount: 1, attemptCount: 0}` to `{retryCount: 2, attemptCount: 2}`.

With this change, six disconnected drains preserve the entire pending record; reconnection sends once. Focused tests also cover account isolation, disconnect during pacing, pre-dispatch rollback, ambiguous-send reconciliation and real failures after dispatch.

- **315 tests passed in 7 selected files:** WhatsApp recovery (8), queue recovery/reconnect/producer recovery (116), outbound-payload contract (27), SDK channel-message (5), plugin-shape contract (159).
- Full `pnpm build`, core and infra-test type checks, changed-file formatting/lint, and the source/extension import-boundary check passed. The built WhatsApp entrypoint import profile passed.
- Scoped autoreview reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. It reviewed source and supplied context; it did not run tests.

Validation used Node 24.21.0 with isolated state and one forked test worker. The full repository test/check lanes and an authenticated live WhatsApp reconnect were not run on the shared runtime host. The focused reconnect integration uses a fake platform listener.

The [upstream review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150130#issuecomment-5700098665) found no actionable code defect, but requires two things before merge: acceptance of the optional hook and indefinite-deferral semantics, and redacted evidence through a real WhatsApp transport showing unchanged counters while disconnected followed by one delivery after reconnect. Neither requirement is complete. The fake-listener integration above is not represented as that live proof.

prs.title: feat(ios): manage session groups from their header
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves The iOS drawer lacks the group controls available on the web and Mac, the Sessions tab offers only a smaller device-local menu, and helper sessions appear as flat rows beside their parent. ## User Impact - Long-press a group header in the drawer or Sessions tab to create a session in the group, edit new-session defaults, rename or create a group, reorder it, or delete it. Saved folder and working-copy defaults apply to grouped creation; Overview move targets use the same group model. - Tap anywhere on a header to fold or unfold the group. The drawer keeps its trailing caret, the Sessions tab its leading caret; a pending mutation shows a spinner. The drawer count appears only while folded and reserves its space while expanded. - Helper sessions fold under their parent using a trailing caret, with a count only while folded. Search results and the selected descendant stay visible; independent pin and category placement is preserved. - Folded groups survive relaunches and reconnects and are pruned against a loaded catalog. Name prompts remain open with the keyboard and through a dropped connection to the same Gateway, including on empty groups. Rejected mutations retain their error; defaults editing is unavailable on older Gateways. ## Why This Change Was Made Both iOS surfaces share group controls backed by the Gateway catalog, with the existing local-group fallback for older Gateways. The drawer preserves parent/child relationships through group and pinned placement and renders visible descendants as indented rows. Device-local group names migrate once using the web UI's existing rule: copy them only into an empty, writable Gateway catalog, never merge them into an existing catalog, and remove the local copy only after successful requests for the current connection. Read-only connections retain the local copy; Gateways without the catalog method retain local-only behavior. ## Evidence ### Native tests and regression results - **Sub-session folding:** 48 focused iOS tests / 7 suites and 56 shared sidebar tests / 1 suite pass; iPhone and iPad UI pass 3/3 on each size for folding, group controls and rejected mutation. Full shared kit: 2,302 Swift Testing tests / 194 suites pass; XCTest 61 executed, 2 skipped, zero failures. The source-reverted runs show two pinned-tree failures from children becoming page roots, one grouping failure from an uncategorized child leaving its parent, and the missing child-fold caret UI failure; both red native builds succeed. - **Header controls:** the missing-header assertion fails on both iPhone and iPad before the fix and passes afterward. Each size passes 2/2 UI tests; typography and grouping pass 29 tests / 2 suites. Full shared kit: 2300 tests / 194 suites pass; XCTest 61, 2 skipped, 0 failures. - **Migration:** the two writable cases fail without the fix: an empty catalog receives no put and keeps local names, while a populated catalog keeps the local key. The red run has 7 tests / 2 suites and 11 issues; all seven parameter cases pass with the fix, within 41 tests / 5 suites. Read-only connections retain local names without a put; Gateways without the method list local names without a request. Stale list/put responses and failed puts retain local names. - **Persistence and reconnects:** 41 iOS tests / 5 suites pass, including folded-state persistence, retained catalog across a dropped link, catalog removal when the method is unavailable, and fold pruning. iPhone and iPad each pass 2/2 UI tests, including header taps and rejected mutation. Source-reverted assertions fail for header-tap folding, local-group fallback (`["Catalog Only"]` instead of `["Device Local"]`), and pruning (`["Kept", "Gone"]` instead of `["Kept"]`). Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.2 to 4.38.3
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

4.37.8 - 21 Aug 2026

No user facing changes.

4.37.7 - 13 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.3. #4085

4.37.6 - 04 Aug 2026

  • Changed the default filepath for the new remote file address format that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 / 3.37.0 to .github/codeql-config.yml to align it with the suggested path that is used elsewhere. #4070

4.37.5 - 03 Aug 2026

  • Fixed a bug where a network error while streaming the download of the CodeQL bundle could terminate the init Action instead of falling back to downloading the bundle before extracting it. #4061

prs.title: fix(ui): keep keyboard focus while earlier history loads
prs.body:
Related: #149618. Umbrella: #149361.

## What Problem This Solves

Keyboard focus falls to the page body when automatic older-history loading disables the focused **Show earlier** button, even though that button remains in the transcript.

## User Impact

The candidate keeps focus on the control while history loads, suppresses busy activation, and lets readers Tab away without completion moving focus back.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `aria-disabled` while busy and detach the click listener until loading finishes. The existing main-chat and task-detail request guards remain authoritative. Current loading copy, live status, animation, 44 px boundary geometry, automatic prefetch, and retained-message anchoring stay intact.

This ports the existing candidate onto current source and preserves the newer loading-copy/hydration changes. [Holny's investigation is acknowledged on the issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/149618#issuecomment-5696450458).

## Evidence

- Fresh Chromium component regression fails against unchanged production source with `BODY` focused and passes with this patch. It covers Tab entry, busy Enter/Space suppression, activation after loading, and Tab-away without focus theft.
- Fresh focused validation: 477 unit/state tests plus that browser regression passed. Coverage includes cached hydration, pagination click/retry, in-flight joining, task-detail state, and retained-message anchoring.
- All nine existing bundled-app, mock-Gateway prepend-anchor browser cases passed, including manual retry, grouped messages, exhaustion, and simulated touch/momentum. This is functional boundary proof, not real-Gateway or performance-equivalence evidence.
- Fresh independent review of the five-file patch found no actionable P0–P3 findings. The required changed-file checks passed, including core/UI typechecking, i18n, formatting, lint, stylelint, and all three export scans. These runs used prepared base `27a4a5c9fe46e6f4d8906310b1e9e4e949cbe4da` plus the reviewed patch.
- The [frozen-base recorded evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/149618) reports three real-Gateway pairs: focus lost in 3/3 originals and 0/3 candidates, each loading 72 → 1,072 messages. A controlled-delay cell suppressed repeated busy activation and respected intentional Shift+Tab away. Those captures and the [earlier changed-file run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35050859402) used base `4ea8cf97fe96cf3c5800e299b9168178983304fb`; they are not fresh-head runs.

## Risk and coverage

- Shared reach includes main chat, catalog history, cached hydration, and task-detail history. Busy controls intentionally remain in the keyboard Tab order; activation is suppressed until the load owner releases the busy state.
- Exhaustion removes the focused control through a separate, unimplemented transition. This draft does not resolve the issue's full scope and uses no closing keyword.
- Fresh-head real-Gateway replay, complete real error recovery, live task-detail, physical mobile/touch, and inspected before/after screenshots in both originating chat and PR remain open. Existing automated captures do not satisfy that delivery gate. This is a draft candidate, not an accepted or completed fix.
- Frozen captures retain the same +82.5 px transient / 0 px final anchor change tracked in #149619. Observer overhead and differing builds prevent a causal speedup or performance-equivalence conclusion.

prs.title: fix: macOS native startup leaves interrupted identity import stuck
prs.body:
Related: #137085

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: macOS native startup can stay stuck after an interrupted identity import when the canonical SQLite identity already exists.

## User Impact

Affected macOS upgrades can resume a fully verified interrupted native identity import, carry matching legacy device auth into the first native Gateway connect, and stop leaving a completed `.native-importing` claim behind.

Canonical startup remains available when legacy evidence is malformed, belongs to another device, conflicts across roots, changes during recovery, cannot be imported, or cannot be cleaned up. In those cases this PR leaves the remaining auth files and claims available for retry or Doctor.

This is intentionally narrow. It does not repair divergent multi-root identity/auth states; those need a separate preflight/operator recovery path.

## Why This Change Was Made

When SQLite already owns the canonical identity, native startup previously returned before inspecting legacy sources. That preserved ordinary downgrade-recreated `device.json` files, but it also skipped a pre-existing `device.json.native-importing` claim created by an earlier native import.

This change inspects only that pre-existing native claim in the canonical-SQLite path. A matching claim is eligible for recovery, but cleanup now has two read-only gates:

1. Before reconciliation, every cross-root auth source is bounded-read, parsed, normalized, matched to the canonical device ID, and checked for cross-root conflicts. The resulting path/bytes/file-snapshot set is retained as a receipt.
2. After the committed SQLite identity is re-read, the complete auth receipt is revalidated. Only an exact match may be imported; only a successful import may retire the claim.

If either gate fails, the verified auth cannot be imported, or claim cleanup fails, startup returns the existing canonical identity and preserves the remaining recovery artifacts. The fresh/noncanonical migration path keeps its prior strict failure-and-restore behavior.

Ordinary `device.json` files remain untouched for Doctor. The matching three-way state (`SQLite` + ordinary `device.json` + `.native-importing`) revalidates both identity files, preserves the ordinary source, and retires only the completed claim. If the source changes before cleanup, the claim is preserved.

Follow-up shape from the issue discussion:

- A separate "2+" PR should preflight native identity/auth consistency before opening the WebSocket so mismatched roots stop retrying as opaque handshake timeouts.
- The broader solution 3 should live with the existing operator recovery/state-machine work in #136149, because it needs an explicit product decision for choosing or repairing divergent identities.

## Retained-claim replay correction (current revision)

The Revision 6 P1 was reproduced before changing production code. After a verified cross-root import, an undeletable claim left its legacy auth available; each of the real role, gateway, and all-token clear APIs was followed by credential resurrection on subsequent identity loads. A real `URLSession` loopback connection also sent the retired token in its connect frame.

The correction records completion once per canonical `(device_id, profile)` in `device_auth_import_receipts`, in the same SQLite immediate transaction as the imported credentials. Empty verified snapshots are complete too. Clearing credentials does not delete completion; retrying claim cleanup therefore cannot replay the snapshot. Receipt failure rolls back token import. No cross-root auth means identity recovery does not consume or quarantine unrelated same-root auth.

This is a **proposed persistent-contract change awaiting explicit maintainer design acceptance**, not a claim of merge readiness. See the accompanying contributor comment for owner, alternatives, lifecycle, rollback, compatibility, and validation limits. The canonical SQL, Swift descriptor, generated Node types, lazy-additive contract and native-v0 bootstrap allowlist agree. Schema version remains 17 under the additive-table convention, but the schema itself changes.

Compatibility boundaries: old readers with the previous native-v0 table allowlist reject a database containing the new table. This does not reconstruct token clears that happened before any completion receipt existed, and does not claim to fix the separate same-root legacy-reader race. Do not delete receipts as a rollback while replayable legacy claims/auth remain.

Current-revision verification:

- Full `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --jobs 2`: exit 0; the main Swift Testing runner reported 1,736 tests in 135 suites.
- After formatting, focused identity, native transport, and native SQLite suites: 74 tests passed (53 identity, 7 native transport, 14 native SQLite).
- Node state database and schema-compatibility suites: 239 passed, 1 existing skip.
- SwiftFormat source scopes, SwiftLint all scopes, changed TypeScript formatting/lint, generated Kysely types, native v17 guard and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Independent final read-only review: no new actionable code blocker; the persistent-design acceptance and evidence boundaries remain open.
- Production dependency audit: 16 advisories, including 3 high, in the existing dependency tree; this revision does not change dependencies or the pre-existing local lockfile edits.

The new network proof uses production native connection code and a loopback fixture that captures outbound auth; it is not an installed-app upgrade run or a real Gateway credential-policy check. The installed-app proof below applies only to the older exact head. A current-head installed-upgrade/retirement run and maintainer storage-design acceptance remain explicit before-merge review items.

## Historical evidence (head `adf99e1`, before the replay correction)

- `swift test --filter DeviceIdentityStoreTests` passed after the final rebase: 49 tests. New coverage includes verified auth resume, wrong-device and malformed auth, conflicting auth across roots, auth mutation between preflight and cleanup, verified auth that cannot be imported, and repeated startup with an undeletable claim. Canonical-recovery failure cases verify identity availability plus preserved evidence; fresh migration remains strict.
- `swift test --filter GatewayNativeTransportDeviceAuthTests` passed: 6 tests, including a loopback `URLSessionWebSocketTask` proof that imported legacy auth is sent on the first native connect.
- Full `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit` passed before the final rebase: 1,745 tests across 137 suites, with 2 existing live-audio skips and no failures.
- `PATH="$PWD/.build/swift-tools:$PATH" ./scripts/format-swift.sh all` passed: 0 files require formatting.
- `PATH="$PWD/.build/swift-tools:$PATH" ./scripts/lint-swift.sh all` passed after the final structural split: 0 SwiftLint violations across macOS, shared, iOS, watchOS, and extension sources.
- `node scripts/check-native-state-schema-version.mjs` passed: native state schema version guard passed (v17).
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- Two independent final read-only reviews reported no actionable findings.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <changed files>` was attempted on the earlier head. It passed the earlier gates and SwiftLint, then the broad macOS CI lane exited 143 in `test/scripts/mac-elevation-host.test.ts` while retaining a Vitest temporary resource claim. I do not see that failure touching the changed identity/auth files, so I kept the focused Swift evidence visible here instead of hiding the local gate gap.

### Historical installed macOS published-upgrade proof

Exact head `adf99e1ebc369d9b4831fb8e72c623c27955b0ff` was built as a real app and run in a disposable macOS 26.5.2 arm64 VM with the default profile, production root discovery, and no state/root overrides. This evidence has not been rerun for the receipt-adding revision; the schema-digest equality below is historical, not a claim about the current head.

- Official v2026.7.1 and v2026.8.2 apps generated the legacy and canonical state. A natural v2026.7.1 → v2026.8.2 upgrade produced one canonical identity, two auth rows, no claim, and SQLite integrity `ok`.
- From those unmodified published-generated identity/auth artifacts, the exact interruption boundary was deterministically reconstructed: canonical identity `1`, auth rows `0`, matching claim `1`, matching legacy auth `1`. This is disclosed as boundary reconstruction, not a randomly timed crash.
- Official v2026.9.4 launched from that snapshot but left it stuck at identity `1`, auth `0`, claim `1`, legacy auth `1`.
- The PR app launched from the same restorable snapshot and produced identity `1`, auth `2`, claim `0`, legacy auth `0`; the second launch retained the same result.
- Built-in status reported `local / connected` to a real v2026.7.1 Gateway, and Gateway logs recorded successful WebSocket RPCs.
- A fresh-state control created one canonical identity and one paired auth row, with no claims or legacy files, and connected successfully.
- `PRAGMA integrity_check` remained `ok`, and the SQLite schema digest was identical across the natural v2026.8.2 migration, reconstructed boundary, official v2026.9.4 control, and both PR launches. The source-level schema v17 guard also passed.

The proof build was debug/ad-hoc signed because no Developer ID identity was available; deep strict signature verification passed on the host and in the VM. The optional MLX TTS helper was omitted. No raw identities, credentials, tokens, keys, device IDs, IP addresses, endpoints, or databases are published. Full redacted methodology and result details are in the latest contributor comment.

No screenshots: this is a non-visual macOS identity/auth migration fix.

prs.title: fix: message-tool sends drop model-based reply prefixes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `messages.responsePrefix` uses model or thinking tokens (`{model}`, `{provider}`, `{modelFull}`, `{thinkingLevel}`), replies sent through `message(action=send)` go out with no prefix at all, while normal replies keep it. The tool send path only had the agent identity, so any template with a model token stayed unresolved and the prefix was skipped.

## User Impact

In shared chats where several agents or models post, people rely on the prefix to tell who's speaking. Message-tool sends, which are often the ones that cross into another conversation, lost that label.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool already runs inside an agent turn that knows its provider, model and thinking level. This passes that run metadata through the message-tool options into `runMessageAction`, so the send path interpolates the prefix the same way direct replies do. Callers without run metadata keep the existing behavior: unresolved placeholders still skip the prefix instead of sending a literal `{model}`. The prefix helper moves into its own small module so the tool execution and the model-context wiring share it.

## Evidence

- `src/infra/outbound/message-action-send.core.test.ts` gains two cases at the real send boundary: active metadata renders on the requested recipient, and an already-prefixed message isn't prefixed twice.
  - Against the pre-fix production code, both fail on their assertions (the send receives no prefix); the other 24 cases pass.
  - With the fix: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts src/infra/outbound/message-action-send.core.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 26/26.
- Docs: `docs/gateway/config-agents/messages-and-talk.md` notes that message-tool sends use the active run metadata.

prs.title: feat(update): select an exact package release from the Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #165899

## What Problem This Solves

Browser clients cannot request a selected package release through `update.run`; omitting the target can install a different version as update availability changes.

## User Impact

Operators can request an exact numeric package version on npm-owned global installations using the stable or beta channel. Existing permission, installation-owner, integrity, migration, service, and recovery checks still apply. This is a per-operation target, not a persistent version pin or a channel change.

Older Gateways still reject this request. Clients must not retry without the target, and a started handoff is not a completed upgrade. No existing client, release, or compatibility range is changed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds the package alternative to the existing request target and carries its exact version through campaign matching, the durable run record, acknowledgement, restart sentinel, and the existing updater handoff. A mismatching campaign remains untouched; an applying campaign cannot start another update. Host-owned, immutable, OCM, and external-supervisor boundaries remain in force.

No new updater, supervisor, state store, permission scope, dependency, or protocol version is introduced. Untargeted updates and exact tracked-Git targets retain their behavior.

## Evidence

Rebased after GitHub reported merge conflicts onto upstream `d0298744306f8bc30468cf9d2726544c6a2517c0` (package version `2026.10.2`). The acknowledgement conflict retains both the exact package version and main's awaited durable record write. Main's system-package ownership inspection remains before campaign adoption and updater launch.

- Pinned `oxfmt@0.71.0 --check` passes for all nine changed files (0.483 seconds); `git diff --check` passes.
- New cases exercise real request validation and campaign matching, exact version retention as availability advances, unsupported installation/channel refusal, duplicate campaign admission, and handoff cancellation after sentinel persistence failure. The OCM test also covers explicit package-target refusal.
- Fresh test/typecheck qualification is unavailable: the supported focused Vitest wrapper exits before collecting tests because dependencies are absent. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` cannot download the pinned `pnpm@12.9.0` from the public registry due to TLS handshake failure. The configured registry has that pnpm version but reports HTTP 404 for upstream's unchanged `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.26.2` pin. No dependency pin, registry policy, or TLS verification was changed.
- Fresh independent review through the shared autoreview workflow, with the full affected owner files supplied, reports `scoped-clean` with no actionable P0-P2 findings. This is source review, not executed test proof.
- This PR remains draft until the candidate's verification gap is resolved. Prior product CI was skipped/cancelled, not passing; no executed product-test wall time or product-test CI seconds are available for this candidate.

Live published-driver-to-candidate upgrade, interruption recovery, and retained-state A-to-B qualification have not been run. No real Gateway or service was started or changed on the shared development host. Isolated tests do not establish stock-release support for this new request contract.

prs.title: fix(anthropic-vertex): bound googleAuthFetch requests with AbortController timeout
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

`googleAuthFetch` is used by `google-auth-library` as the HTTP transport for OAuth token requests (`https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`). The old implementation had no AbortController, no timeout, and no `connectTimeout` on `EnvHttpProxyAgent` — a hung or unresponsive OAuth endpoint would block the request indefinitely, stalling the entire Vertex AI stream.

### Why This Change Was Made

Without timeout protection, any transient network issue between the OpenClaw process and Google's OAuth infrastructure can permanently block the stream. The `googleAuthFetch` wrapper is the single entry point for all Google Auth HTTP calls in the Anthropic Vertex provider, so adding timeout there covers the widest surface with the smallest change.

### User Impact

- Hung OAuth token requests now abort after 30s instead of hanging forever
- TCP connect timeouts after 10s when the proxy is unreachable
- Callers can cancel pending auth requests via `AbortSignal`

### Evidence

**Real terminal proof — both automatic timeout paths (redacted live output):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/anthropic-vertex/proof-timeout-paths.test.ts --reporter=verbose

  [PROOF-10s] EnvHttpProxyAgent({ connectTimeout: 10_000 }) (direct)
  [PROOF-10s] Proxy: http://198.51.100.1:3128 (silent-drop SYN)
  [PROOF-10s] Request started at 2026-07-20T07:09:35.365Z
  [PROOF-10s] Waiting for proxy connect timeout...
  [PROOF-10s] ✓ Rejected in 10527ms
  [PROOF-10s] ✓ Error: fetch failed
  [PROOF-10s] ✓ Cause: Connect Timeout Error
                  (attempted address: 198.51.100.1:3128, timeout: 10000ms)

  [PROOF-30s] Hanging server at 127.0.0.1:40029
  [PROOF-30s] GOOGLE_AUTH_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000
  [PROOF-30s] Request started at  2026-07-20T07:09:46.027Z
  [PROOF-30s] Waiting for automatic 30s timeout...
  [PROOF-30s] ✓ Rejected in 30008ms
  [PROOF-30s] ✓ Error: This operation was aborted

  [PROOF-cleanup] Request 1: HTTP 200 in 16ms
  [PROOF-cleanup] Request 2: HTTP 200 in 7ms
  [PROOF-cleanup] Request 3: HTTP 200 in 3ms
  [PROOF-cleanup] Request 4: HTTP 200 in 4ms
  [PROOF-cleanup] Request 5: HTTP 200 in 3ms
  [PROOF-cleanup] Shared signal not aborted: true

 ✓ googleAuthFetch real timeout proof > 10s proxy connect timeout 10661ms
 ✓ googleAuthFetch real timeout proof > 30s automatic request timeout 30018ms
 ✓ googleAuthFetch real timeout proof > Listener cleanup 40ms
```

**Listener lifecycle fix (ClawSweeper P2).**  The original code used an anonymous `() => controller.abort()` listener — no reference, so it could never be removed.  A long-lived shared caller signal would accumulate one listener per completed request, preventing GC of old controller/signal pairs.

Fix: name the listener as `onAbort`, register with `addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true })`, and remove in `finally` via `init?.signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort)`.  The regression test (above, 5 rapid requests on one shared signal) proves no listener leak.

**CI fix (checks-node-changed).**  The earlier proxy test stubs `HTTP_PROXY` and creates the `EnvHttpProxyAgent` singleton with a proxy.  After unstubbing, the singleton still routes through the now-dead proxy for any host not in `NO_PROXY`.  Set `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1` before the timeout/abort tests so local test servers are reached directly regardless of CI environment.

**Full suite**: 7 test files, 68 tests — all passed.
```
 Test Files  7 passed (7)
      Tests  68 passed (68)
```

**Code quality**:
- `oxlint`: 0 issues
- `tsgo` (ext tsconfig): 0 errors
- File diff: +56/-4 lines across 2 files

**Files**:
- `extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts` — `googleAuthFetch` with AbortController, connectTimeout, and named listener cleanup
- `extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.test.ts` — 4 tests in `googleAuthFetch timeout and abort` describe block (pre-abort, mid-request abort, normal success, shared-signal regression)

prs.title: feat(provider): add Databricks Unity Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #155633

## Problem and user impact

Organizations routing inference through Databricks Unity Gateway currently hand-author workspace routes, credentials, transport and model metadata. This adds provider-specific onboarding and model resolution through an externally distributed plugin.

Operators install `@openclaw/databricks-provider`, supply `DATABRICKS_HOST` and `DATABRICKS_TOKEN`, and run `openclaw onboard --auth-choice databricks-token`. Models use `databricks/<catalog>.<schema>.<model-service>`.

Same-workspace onboarding preserves existing routes, APIs, model entries, aliases and primary selections. Fresh setup uses `/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1` with `system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5`. Non-interactive onboarding refuses reuse of a saved profile when `DATABRICKS_HOST` selects a different workspace, and rejects invalid explicit hosts before persistence. Trusted manual provider-config edits remain operator-controlled routing changes; this does not introduce immutable workspace identity in the credential format.

## Implementation and distribution

- Databricks host validation, auth, onboarding and model resolution stay in `extensions/databricks`.
- Reuses the existing OpenAI-compatible streaming transport and credential store.
- Follows the in-repo-source / external npm and ClawHub package pattern used by official providers such as Cerebras and Radius; excluded from the core npm tarball.
- Adds `DATABRICKS_HOST` to untrusted workspace `.env` filtering, with a regression. Credential environment filtering comes from the manifest.
- No new external runtime dependencies, generic transport, credential owner, schema or migration. The lockfile adds only the workspace importer and existing `@openclaw/plugin-sdk` workspace devDependency.

## Current candidate

Head `edda4d7bf4c717a627015024ab7c61ed9ef27a43`, rebased onto main `9828e28906f50d674625bb1474814bd5c4b4681e` on October 13, 2026. Conflicts were confined to generated config baseline artifacts and resolved through their generator. Package version/build compatibility is aligned to `2026.10.2`; minimum host remains `>=2026.9.6`. Plugin inventory was regenerated.

Databricks production code and its tests are byte-identical to previously reviewed head `ad52f68faf19ccdf8ca0315201561927739f7e72`. Prior-head CI is historical evidence, not current-head CI.

## Live installed-package proof — October 13

Executed against a real Databricks workspace using the current candidate. The token existed only in the child process environment; onboarding used `--secret-input-mode ref`. Workspace and token are redacted.

| Boundary | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Core runtime build | Completed successfully, 83.3 seconds |
| Release-pipeline plugin pack | `openclaw-databricks-provider-2026.10.2.tgz`, 8 files, 3 runtime JS modules, manifest, package metadata, README and 2 assets; no runtime dependencies |
| Managed install | `plugins install npm-pack:<tarball> --force --accept-capabilities`, exit 0 |
| Runtime identity | `plugins inspect databricks --runtime --json`: loaded, global origin, installed `node_modules/@openclaw/databricks-provider/dist/index.js`, provider `databricks`, no diagnostics |
| Source exclusion | Both bundled discovery and bundled source overlays disabled throughout install, onboarding and agent turns |
| Onboarding | Exit 0, primary `databricks/system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5`, `openai-completions`, environment SecretRef; token absent from `openclaw.json` |
| Streaming and real tool round trip | `agent exec` exited 0; two HTTP 200 `text/event-stream` responses; exactly one successful `read` call; final reply exactly matched random file nonce `DBX-baf85764f87acf9d` |
| Non-catalog model | `databricks/system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-6` resolved dynamically; real streamed agent turn exited 0 and replied `DYNAMIC_OK` |
| Invalid explicit workspace | Browser URL containing `?o=1234` rejected with exit 1 before inference; active `openclaw.json` SHA-256 unchanged |

This proves local package installation and real inference through the installed runtime. It does not claim that the package is published or that catalog-linked official publisher trust has been established.

## Installed-runtime authority and stable-upgrade proof

Using the same packed plugin with bundled discovery and source overlays disabled:

- Started with published latest stable `openclaw@2026.10.2` (`b8952d4`), created an existing Databricks Serving route and saved synthetic workspace-A credential through its published SDK, then installed the candidate and ran candidate onboarding. Exit 0; deep comparisons confirmed provider route/API/model metadata, primary selection, aliases/model entries and saved credential including workspace metadata were unchanged.
- Positive control: saved workspace-A credential was reused successfully without a token environment variable.
- Workspace-B selection without a fresh token exited 1 before network access; active configuration hash was unchanged.
- Hostile cwd `.env` supplied an attacker workspace and token. A benign dotenv witness was loaded, proving the actual cwd loader ran, while `DATABRICKS_HOST` stayed absent. Onboarding exited 1 for missing trusted workspace; configuration hash was unchanged.
- A Node preload denied and recorded fetch, HTTP(S) and socket connection attempts. Both negative cases recorded `attempts: []`; it did not modify provider auth/config logic. Synthetic credentials were used for these boundary probes.
- The real-token live run above was separately scanned across 23 isolated state files: zero occurrences of the supplied token.

## Validation

- Focused provider, real-transport loopback and workspace `.env` suites: 28 tests passed across 3 files. Combined wall time 80.44 seconds on a heavily loaded macOS arm64 host, Node 26.5. Provider files: 19 tests, 28.32 seconds wall, individual transport scenario 416 ms. No new tests were added in the rebase.
- Extension package-boundary production typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, and changed-source formatting passed.
- Config baseline, plugin inventory and version-sync checks passed.
- Full docs checks passed: formatting, Markdown/MDX, glossary, links, config examples and changelog checks.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Fresh independent review was completed. Findings were checked against owning paths:

- The proposed interactive SecretRef failure did not reproduce through the registered auth method with source overlays disabled and an explicit plugin load path. The reviewer retracted it.
- The proposed dynamic API override failure is prevented by core's `applyConfiguredProviderOverrides`; the final resolution probe retained `anthropic-messages` and the configured route. No duplicate override was added to the plugin.
- The proposed immutable credential/workspace binding would change the trusted manual-config contract and credential semantics. The implemented guard covers onboarding workspace selection, not arbitrary operator edits; that scope is explicit above.

Current-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38397087861) completed with 167 successful jobs, 22 skipped jobs and 6 failed jobs (5 shards plus the aggregate gate). The Databricks shard, production/test types, lint, package boundaries, docs, source contracts and npm-lock checks passed. The failing shards were OpenAI realtime auth fixtures (missing admitted database worker), Codex dynamic-tool host instructions, node-worker launch wire timeout, Telegram emoji gateway timeout, and QA POSIX SIGTERM lifecycle timeout. These are outside the Databricks diff; only the OpenAI failure was independently reproduced and repaired in separate #171064 (18 unchanged tests pass). Other failures are attributed by hosted logs and unchanged source scope, not claimed baseline reproductions. Dependency approval remains separate from the failed CI gate.

## Limits and maintainer decision

This is Unity Gateway support. Existing workspace Serving configuration is preserved, but broader Serving compatibility belongs to dependent #163202, which still requires its own repair, restack and validation. OAuth token minting/refresh, automatic live model discovery and per-workspace pricing are outside this change; unknown model services use fallback metadata.

The remaining product decision is whether Databricks receives official provider catalog sponsorship and in-repository maintenance. Maintainer edits are enabled. If accepted, the final head requires the existing maintainer dependency-change approval path; publishing/release is a separate action.
