prs.title: fix(models): make app-server runtime choices selectable
prs.body:
Supersedes #130639; this keeps the provider/runtime chooser repair in one PR.

## What Problem This Solves

An app-server-backed provider can have a usable runtime but no corresponding choice in the model picker. Conversely, a `/model ... --runtime ...` selection could persist a runtime whose owning plugin is disabled, leaving the next turn unable to start.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker and `/model` directive share provider/runtime compatibility and plugin-availability checks. Known app-server bindings become visible, disabled runtime owners are rejected before session persistence, and providers without an applicable binding retain their default route. Startup still validates previously persisted overrides rather than silently choosing a different execution backend.

The binding table is **additive, not exclusive**. A row tells the chooser which runtime to offer for a provider; it is not a claim that the runtime serves only that provider. Applicability for anything outside a row stays with the canonical owner — registered harness, then manifest, then the CLI alias table — exactly as on `main`. Round 8 repairs a regression where this branch had conflated the two: see Evidence.

The repair keeps app-server bindings out of synchronous CLI-backend discovery on the native-slash fast path. The availability gate resolves the agent-harness owner from the manifest activation plan first, which answers fixed-table and dynamically-routed harnesses alike without touching the plugin setup registry. The shared binding lookup is pure metadata; normal plugin activation remains responsible for loading runtime owners. Existing special handling for the virtual Codex namespace is preserved.

## User Impact

Users get consistent runtime choices between the picker and the textual directive, and a disabled owner is refused at selection time instead of saving a choice that breaks the next turn. A session that already pins a compatible runtime keeps that pin and its native-runtime consent through model selection.

This is not a claim that every documented custom-provider shape is *discoverable* in the picker. That gap is real, is unchanged from `main`, and is the open maintainer decision below.

## Evidence

Current signed topic head: `d7af16cd228c7adc2dd1e27aca1624f8cb8f1ee2`, on top of fork main `ea7cc1066568fbbeece9151c497ecab15923bd2a`.

### Round 8 — compatibility regression repaired, with a three-way control

The branch previously read a binding row as exclusive, which rejected provider/runtime pairings that `origin/main` accepts. Driving the real `resolveCompatibleAgentRuntimeForProvider()` in one worktree against the same `node_modules`, on three refs:

| provider + runtime | `origin/main` | `eb8fb1847e4` (prior head) | this head |
|---|---|---|---|
| `github-copilot` + `copilot` | `copilot` | `copilot` | `copilot` |
| `proof-byok` + `copilot` | `copilot` | `undefined` | `copilot` |
| `anthropic` + `copilot` | `copilot` | `undefined` | `copilot` |
| `anthropic` + `agentsapi` | `agentsapi` | `undefined` | `agentsapi` |
| `anthropic` + `codex` | `undefined` | `undefined` | `undefined` |
| `openai` + `codex` | `codex` | `codex` | `codex` |
| `codex` + `codex` | `codex` | `codex` | `codex` |
| `zai` + `acp-opencode` | `acp-opencode` | `acp-opencode` | `acp-opencode` |

This head is identical to `origin/main` on every case. Three pairings had regressed; all three are restored and nothing else moved.

Also in round 8: the new typecheck shard is appended rather than inserted, restoring every pre-existing CI stripe assignment (verified by recomputing `(index % stripeCount) + 1` for all 27 base shard names at stripe counts 2, 3 and 5 — zero drift); the proof's fixed-binding coverage scenario now shares its dynamic-harness exclusion with the unit guard instead of carrying a stale copy, and asserts that exclusion non-vacuously; and the availability gate resolves the harness owner before any CLI-setup probe, so a dynamic harness selection cannot reach synchronous setup discovery on the native fast path.

### Gates and tests at this head

- `pnpm check:changed`: **exit 0, all 37 lanes green**, including both typecheck graphs (28 core-test shards), the dead-export and unused-file scans, import cycles, and both lint lanes.
- Focused suites through `scripts/run-vitest.mjs`: 4 files / 37 tests passing — `app-server-runtime-bindings` 1, `session-runtime-compat` 24, `directive-handling.model-runtime` 10, `commands-models.app-server-runtime-choices` 2. Test counts were reconciled against the requested files, so no path filter silently matched nothing.
- New regression coverage: a bound runtime still reaching the canonical applicability owner for an unowned provider (with Codex held closed as the control); a compatible inherited pin plus its `nativeRuntimeConsent` surviving selection, and an incompatible one still being cleared; and a dynamic harness selection resolving without probing CLI setup discovery, asserted with the setup seam stubbed to throw.

### What the runtime proof does not establish

`scripts/proof-app-server-runtime-chooser-bindings.ts` **does not complete at this head**, and this body does not claim it does. It stops at its first scenario because the bundled Codex/Copilot extensions fail to load with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` on `unicorn-magic@0.3.0`, whose `exports` map offers only `import` conditions while the plugin loader reaches it through `require`.

That blocker is inherited, not introduced here, and was demonstrated rather than asserted: a bare `require("npm-run-path")` fails identically with `origin/main` checked out in the same worktree; the failure is unchanged after a full `pnpm build` when the proof is pointed at the built `dist/extensions/*/index.js` entries instead of source; and `src/plugins/native-module-require.ts`, `loader-module-runtime.ts`, `plugin-module-loader-cache.ts`, `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are byte-identical between `origin/main` and this head. This diff touches no file under `src/plugins/`, `extensions/`, or any dependency manifest. It is not repaired here, because it is outside this change's scope.

Consequently the proof's round-8 corrections are reviewable but **not executed end to end** at this composition. Proof output captured at earlier heads (`192f3b77e41`, `a2f94770e34`) predates the upstream plugin-loader churn between those heads and this one and is not offered as evidence for this composition.

Still outstanding and not satisfiable from a fork without credentials: a real installed Copilot harness completing a provider-backed reply, before/after picker images, and an upgrade-survival run showing an existing stored custom-provider pin loading after the change.

Because the PR is `CONFLICTING` there is no merge ref, so the heavy `pull_request` CI matrix does not dispatch; the lightweight lanes are the ones to judge by.

## Maintainer Decisions Requested

### Harness-to-model-provider applicability

Please confirm the supported owner for generic app-server applicability metadata before extending a built-in table or adding a new public contract. Current plugin metadata declares harness identifiers but does not generally associate them with every model-provider route they serve. `sessionRouteStateOwners` describes session-route namespaces; those identifiers are not interchangeable with model-provider compatibility.

The existing provider-owned `ProviderModelRouteRuntimePolicy.compatibleIds` contract is relevant for owned providers, but does not by itself describe an external harness accepting an otherwise unowned custom provider. A declaration or policy hook should belong to the canonical plugin/runtime owner rather than be inferred independently by each picker, directive, and startup consumer.

ClawSweeper's current recommendation is harness-owned applicability. @VACInc's 2026-09-21 instruction set the pin/consent/rejection semantics to satisfy — all three now hold, see above — but did not choose between the two designs, so this remains open. No new config field, persistence index, or plugin schema is introduced here to bypass that decision.

### Documented Copilot custom providers

Copilot supports eligible unowned custom `models.providers` entries with a non-empty `baseUrl` and supported API shape. A table of canonical provider IDs cannot enumerate those, so such a provider still gets **no chooser entry**; proof scenario 13a pins that gap as an executable control.

What is *not* missing any more is applicability: an explicit `--runtime copilot` and an inherited `agentRuntimeOverride: "copilot"` for such a provider are accepted, as on `main`. Scenario 13b and the new unit tests pin that, with incompatible-pin and incompatible-request controls alongside.

Once the discovery contract is agreed, the acceptance proof should include an actual installed harness and eligible custom provider through selection, persistence, and a subsequent turn, with disabled/incompatible controls.

### Merge hold

@VACInc's hold from 2026-09-21 stands and is not being contested. `upstream/main` has not been merged into this branch: that sync is the fork owner's call, so the `CONFLICTING` state is reported rather than resolved.

*Written by Tank (Claude), an AI agent operated by Eddie Abrams (zeroaltitude).*

prs.title: fix: catalog list fails when Codex thread previews are huge
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the session catalog fails to parse Codex `thread/list` pages when stored previews are huge, then one bad host stalls `sessions.catalog.list`.

Fixes #156831

## User Impact

User impact: large Codex homes keep listing. A hung or unparseable host is fail-soft instead of blocking sibling hosts until the 60s deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog decoding drops the tail of a native `preview` string before JSON.parse, but only once the retained prefix already fixes the displayed text: the selector's 2,048-unit prefix, no terminal controls, and more than 500 units of collapsed, trimmed text. Each whitespace run is kept as one unit while reading, since the projection collapses runs anyway, so text after a long whitespace run survives. Controls before the first ANSI introducer (ESC, CSI, OSC) are deleted in place by the sanitizer, so each run of them is kept as one unit too. Only previews whose ANSI sequences leave the display undetermined are cut at 64 KiB. The displayed preview matches the existing projection and 8–24 MB pages still stay under the 8 MiB incomplete-frame recovery.

Each local catalog host gets one fail-soft deadline that covers page reads and adoption projection, on both the non-progressive path and progressive `finishLocalHost` / publication. It uses the existing 60s default request allowance (`CODEX_CATALOG_LOCAL_HOST_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS`), so slow large homes are not marked unavailable earlier than today; paired nodes stay at 8s.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest, all passing at f200f2f87f:

- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-catalog-preview-bound.test.ts` (19 tests): oversized preview parse, escaped quotes while skipping, skipped fragments vs the 1000-line recovery cap, and displayed-preview parity with the canonical selector for whitespace-heavy prefixes, escaped newlines, sparse words, terminal controls and a surrogate at the display boundary, text after whitespace, escaped newlines or removable controls beyond the 64 KiB fallback, removable controls between whitespace runs and before an ANSI sequence, and whitespace-only preview lines vs the recovery cap.
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-catalog-worker.test.ts` (25 tests): 9 MiB preview recovery, plus worker vs inline projection parity for a whitespace-heavy prefix, a control-laden preview, `" ".repeat(65_536) + "meaningful text"`, and `"\u0007".repeat(15_000) + "meaningful text"` (the last two fail before this change, pass after).
- `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-list-operation.test.ts` (16 tests): progressive and non-progressive host timeouts with sibling fail-soft, and a new case that holds the adoption read after paging completes (fails before this change, passes after).

`oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean.

Not yet attached: an after-fix `sessions.catalog.list` trace from a real large Codex home.

prs.title: fix(memory): parse nested managed Markdown blocks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A synthesis update can erase an earlier human Notes block when a candidate generated range contains a marked `## Notes` section and another Notes section follows. The parser can classify the earlier block as generated, then compare only the later block during its preservation check.

## Changes

- Detect non-code human markers in a Notes section contained inside a candidate generated range and reject before mutation.
- Add parser and apply-boundary regressions proving rejection leaves existing content unchanged.
- Keep the new Notes-preservation guard in the Memory Wiki wrapper; this follow-up does not change the existing SDK helper refactor.
- Merge current main `475aada27d0e6bc67722840bf5ba7f46dbf5a84b` into the PR head, preserving both histories. Three test-file conflicts were resolved by retaining the PR tests alongside current-main tests; the production files merged cleanly.

## Recovery scope

The current PR branch’s existing SDK refactor changes how generic callers handle malformed standalone markers: unmatched full-line starts and orphan-only ends now reject, and stray standalone end markers can be removed alongside a balanced block even when `recoverInlineOrphanEnds` is unset. This compatibility choice remains under maintainer/user scope review; this follow-up does not add or narrow it. Memory Wiki remains the caller opting into inline orphan recovery. No existing-vault compatibility exercise has been run.

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/memory-host-markdown.test.ts` — 53 passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on the three resolved test files — passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.test.ts","extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.test.ts","src/plugin-sdk/memory-host-markdown.test.ts"]' --concurrency 1` — all 28 selected core test type graphs passed.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` — completed from the merged lockfile.
- Independent review approved merge commit `84795249b1f6cc08d0508859322239b011d37ef3`; the merge has PR head `ccab9028e92a56d05c42cc56f44544cbf1e1b580` as first parent and current main `475aada27d0e6bc67722840bf5ba7f46dbf5a84b` as second parent.

## Evidence limits

No live existing-vault CLI or tool update was run, so these fixture tests do not establish personal-vault behavior. No stored-data format or migration is changed. A full build was not run.

prs.title: fix: preserve config acknowledgements and recovered reply delivery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes config updates losing their acknowledgement when the new policy revokes the requesting client, and recovered answers losing final speech/media payloads after their text becomes visible.

## User Impact

Admitted policy updates finish with their canonical result. Recovered answers retain final artifacts while pending delivery and committed message-tool replies keep their existing custody protections. No configuration migration or new operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requester authority is checked synchronously immediately before root/include publication; writer ownership remains valid through post-commit reread. Terminal preparation returns its already-reconciled source custody, and finalization uses that fact instead of aggregate transcript completion.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171090. Its ordinary-chat TTS repair is already on main and is preserved. This PR retains the remaining recovery and config repairs, plus CI fixture corrections: ordered provider cleanup through the existing test facade, real-export-preserving mocks and a controlled browser clock for the Sessions debounce test. Assertions and timeouts remain intact.

Against the pinned integration baseline below, production changes are +22/-11 (net +11), justified by synchronous requester admission, carried source-custody facts, and existing test-facade reuse. Tests/support are +317/-45. No new config or schema surface is introduced. Canonical auth-reader fixes from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171321 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171299 are preserved in the baseline; they are not new repairs attributed to this PR.

The Telegram routing fixture now uses the complete canonical baseline repair from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171443 and is no longer part of the residual PR diff.

## Evidence

- Final candidate: `996b93733b36a647c58592fc4740f7f08bb8c862`, tree `8df317acc80964c168412152315029c6b8fbeae3`, integrated with pinned main `44c918f3900770412a3cd912eaa0c718b2e3356c`. The residual change covers 20 paths: config publication admission, recovered reply source custody, and connected QA/Sessions fixtures. All 20 residual file blobs are unchanged from the reviewed e8 predecessor. Canonical Telegram, Muse, dependency-hygiene and auth-reader repairs remain baseline-owned.
- [Exact-candidate focused proof 38500733760](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38500733760): **3 files /40 tests passed**, Node **24.21.0**, serial canonical projects and one worker. Routing, thread binding and reconciliation cover the canonical conflict resolution and relevant storage siblings. Exact source/tree and proof-complete were verified; this is owner/harness proof, not live-provider or full-release qualification.
- The focused tests passed before native cleanup made the wrapper exit 1. Subsequent independent native reconciliation exited 0 and verified claim absence with zero inventory problems. Runtime success and final cleanup settlement are separately established.
- Fresh independent source/dependency review and exact-candidate autoreview found no actionable issue. Integration preserves source-custody facts, terminal diagnostic text, host-text suppression, asynchronous cron-owner resolution, and synchronous requester admission immediately before publication. Direct Codex source inspection at `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6` included `codex-rs/protocol/src/items.rs:99`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:231,1201`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs:394`, and `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs:359,409`. Lifecycle completion is distinct from OpenClaw delivery custody.
- **Fresh hosted validation is pending:** [ordinary CI 38501786282](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501786282) and [exact-head release gate 38501955154](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501955154). Remote head and merge-commit second parent were verified before dispatch. The release gate keeps the existing defaults, including UI capture disabled. No full-CI success or landing readiness is claimed.

These are not relabeled as final996b passes.

The two runtime failure causes remain unresolved; passing diagnostic replays do not establish a fix. Final-head hosted coverage and native admission remain required. prs.title: improve(ui): explain dashboard widget sizes and saved width
prs.body:
Closes #149363. Related: #149450 adds the separate full-width action.

## What Problem This Solves

Dashboard users cannot tell why a widget that fills a narrow pane becomes much narrower when the window is widened, because Widget options does not explain preset widths or show the saved width.

## User Impact

Users can see the saved column width and choose clearly labeled quarter/half/two-thirds/full-width presets. Hints explain narrow dashboards and automatic height. This PR changes feedback and documentation only; it does not restore width or alter resize behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The menu displays saved width independently of height, including custom widths from dragging. Short hints explain responsive full-width placement and fixed-height presets.

The full-width automatic-height action has been split into #149450 so it can be reviewed and merged independently. This PR is back to its original UX scope, with its existing discussion retained. Either PR can land first; their shared menu and guide may need a small context-conflict resolution when the second lands.

## Evidence

- **34 focused tests pass** after refreshing to main base `5e97d76908d`: nine sizing tests and 25 Chromium layout tests.

prs.title: fix(qa-lab): retain lease recovery details after cancellation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cancelling Mantis while Crabbox warms a desktop could discard the early lease identity and final cleanup diagnostics.

## User Impact

Mantis waits for the child process and its output pipes to close before reporting cancellation. Failed warmups report bounded recovery candidates for inspection; candidates never authorize commands or automatic cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node emits an abort error before the child finishes. The runner now retains that original error through close and keeps bounded diagnostic snapshots outside routine error serialization. The session records native acquisition markers separately from a successfully acquired lease. Successful output, explicit options, environment defaults, existing lease ownership, and sibling command behavior remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Observed baseline: a real desktop warmup reached its 600-second abort and returned only the abort message, losing the buffered lease marker. Separate native reconciliation subsequently confirmed that lease was released.
- Added real-child tests for delayed cleanup output, abort followed by exit zero, spawn failure, pre-aborted signals, complete large JSON/UTF-8 output, bounded candidate extraction, and session/report ownership.
- Current-head [CI job 115650089242](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501611459/job/115650089242): **13 files / 100 tests passed** on `ac87a2efe9e5205e12b14790e3703898f94ff342`, including real-child cancellation and report tests plus Slack desktop and visual-task siblings (39.21 seconds for the lane). The tested synthetic merge is `7c60341efba64827f3320c616eaae4debf948a26`. Extension lint also passed.
- [ClawSweeper reviewed the current head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171482#issuecomment-6157694530) with no findings and no before-merge requirements. Its optional rank-up asks for an actual after-fix warmup cancellation capture. We are not allocating and deliberately cancelling another cloud desktop solely for that optional evidence: the real-child tests above prove delayed cleanup, original AbortError retention, and non-authoritative recovery reporting. One bounded post-merge tiny desktop proof is planned and will retain its actual success or cancellation evidence.

- The prior baseline-ratchet failure came from a main-branch mock factory. Canonical main repair `e7a07c5aee577be3a2425ec4d88cad17813b7505` resolved it; repaired main `976cc974fab1912c696d1101bd17a1abf05eb77e` is now merged into the branch. All four reviewed Mantis file blobs and the PR diff are unchanged. Fresh CI completed successfully with 47 passing checks, all four QA smoke profiles, and passing required CI/dependency/security statuses; ClawSweeper has no findings on `ac87a2efe9e5205e12b14790e3703898f94ff342`.
- Focused Testbox allocation queued before payload; cancelled and verified completed. No tests ran there; CI supplied the execution proof.
- Targeted oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass. Independent source review and autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issue.
- Production: +60/-6 lines (net +54); tests: +207. The added state separates private failure diagnostics and recovery identity from acquired lease authority.

prs.title: improve(ui): restore full-width auto-height dashboard widgets
prs.body:
Related: #149363. Independent of #149371, which only improves size labels and saved-width feedback.

## What Problem This Solves

After resizing an HTML dashboard widget to a smaller preset, **Auto height** keeps the smaller width. Users lack a single action to return to full width with automatic height.

## User Impact

**Full width + auto height** fills all 12 dashboard columns and enables automatic height in one step. Existing layouts remain unchanged until the user selects it; **Auto height** alone still preserves width.

## Why This Change Was Made

The HTML-widget menu uses one existing resize operation to set width and height mode together. The action follows existing mutation permissions and error handling. It adds no Gateway method, persistence migration, dependency, or widget permission.

The workflow was reproduced in the live Gateway web UI: XL followed by Auto height stayed full width; LG followed by Auto height stayed two-thirds width. This provides an explicit way back to full width rather than changing the meaning of height-only sizing. The shared Control UI also supplies this menu in the macOS Companion.

This branch starts directly from main and does not depend on the labels or saved-width UI in #149371. Either PR can be reviewed and merged independently; both touch the same menu and guide, so the later PR may need a small context-conflict resolution.

## Evidence

- **56 focused tests pass**: 11 sizing tests, 25 Chromium layout tests, and 20 MCP App/plugin cell tests. Coverage includes small, custom, automatic-height and full-width/fixed-height starting states, one resize operation, iframe preservation, and read-only menus.
- UI TypeScript checking, focused lint, English/raw-copy verification, production Control UI build and diff whitespace checks pass on main base `5e97d76908d`.
- Independent autoreview found no actionable P0-P2 findings. The split exposed a missing test-helper import; it was corrected and all focused tests were rerun successfully.
- Chrome against the synthetic board fixture: SM then Auto height left the widget at 333 px in a 1368 px grid. The new action expanded it to 1368 px, with Auto height checked.

prs.title: fix(chat): pending internal-system input shown as user message in Control UI
prs.body:
Fixes #133938

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Control UI rendered a pending recovery prompt as a message from "You" while the same input rendered as a system notice after promotion. Oversized history placeholders also dropped the provenance needed for that distinction, so large internal-system messages could lose attribution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pending item builder unconditionally emitted `kind: "message"` without checking `provenance.kind === "internal_system"`. Canonical history already classified those inputs via the typed provenance registry (`resolveSystemNoticeKind`). This change reuses that registry for pending items (preserving the pending disposition and without assigning turn/reply/fork authority) and retains minimal `{kind, sourceTool}` provenance through `buildOversizedHistoryPlaceholder`. The sentinel path remains metadata-free.

## User Impact

Operators no longer see generated recovery prompts misattributed as their own messages during the pending interval. Oversized internal-system messages keep their system-notice presentation after projection. Ordinary user messages with identical text continue to render as user messages.

## Evidence

- New regression tests: `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pending-system-notices.test.ts` (6 tests) and `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-budget-provenance.test.ts` (5 tests) fail on base and pass after the fix.
- Existing tests: `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pending-inputs.test.ts` 30 passed, `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-budget.test.ts` 4 passed.
- Combined suite: 45 tests passed across 4 files.
- No change to runtime authority, deduplication, or search filtering.

Supersedes #134278（原PR分支已删，按原提交重建）

prs.title: fix(ui): hard-disable ineligible session hosts with stacked reasons
prs.body:
## Summary

Refs #135378

After #135453, command-state tooltips were accurate, but the session host picker still:

- offered paired devices as selectable under session-level blockers (runtime unsupported);
- showed only the first inventory disqualifier when several applied;
- had no shared projection path for workspace-symlink / prepared-auth session blockers.

ClawSweeper then found three false-disable P1s on the first preflight wire-up: derived/Git-ignored escaping symlinks, default-agent auth lookup, and empty-workspace local-folder scans.

## Fix

Keep one shared placement projection as the eligibility authority for New Session and Move Session. Stack connected-host inventory reasons and hard-disable every device row when session blockers apply.

Align preflight with transfer + runtime-auth owners (head `5886b8766b`):

1. **Transfer eligibility before symlink rejection** — skip derived paths (`node_modules`, caches) and Git-ignored paths only when transfer uses Git mode (`probeWorkspaceGitMode`; unborn repos stay plain).
2. **Selected-session auth** — `environments.list` accepts `agentId` / `authProfileId`; prepared-auth eligibility uses that agent store + profile. Empty profile snapshots still accept prepared `models.providers` API-key routes (auth-bridge `authRequirement: api-key` + `resolvedApiKey`). Move Session sends stored `authProfileOverride`, not a reconstructed model suffix.
3. **Empty / remote New Session sources** — omit local folder from symlink preflight when `worktreeSource: "empty"` or a remote repository is selected (no local copy).

Dispatch remains authoritative for include-list edge cases and final startup auth.

## User impact

Ineligible hosts are no longer offered as selectable. Disabled rows surface stacked accurate reasons. Valid destinations are no longer hard-disabled by unrelated `node_modules` / ignored symlinks, wrong-agent auth, empty-workspace local folders, missing profile snapshots with configured API keys, or unborn-repo Git exclusions.

## Evidence

- Tip FAIL (Claw 2/6): three false-disable P1s — derived/ignored symlink walk, default-agent auth, empty-workspace local scan; unit-only proof.
- Hermes re-score FAIL on `a86cc75a00` (overall 2/6 · proof 2/6 · patch 3/6): prepared API-key without profile; Move Session profile from model text; Git exclusions on unborn repos.
- Exact head PASS (`5886b8766b1681d420c03bba8cb76eb4339dae99`):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-core.config.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/session-placement-preflight.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **10 passed** (escaping; skip `node_modules`; skip Git-ignored; still flag eligible; unborn plain-mode; selected-agent/profile auth; prepared API-key without profile; pinned missing profile still blocks; stacking).
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts src/gateway/server-methods/environments.session-placement.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **1 passed**.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-client.config.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/environments.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **16 passed** (incl. agentId/authProfileId params).
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts ui/src/pages/new-session/device-placement.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **20 passed** (incl. empty/remote preflight omit).
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts ui/src/pages/new-session/where-chip.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **65 passed**.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-placement.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **20 passed** (incl. Move Session `authProfileOverride` → `environments.list`).
- **Gap (Kevin-owned screenshots):** sanitized Gateway/browser before/after screenshots of New Session + Move Session (blocked + valid destinations) still needed — not attached / not claimed PASS in this raise.

Closes #135378

prs.title: fix: deliver ask_user prompts after yielded continuations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `ask_user` prompts can appear only in Control UI and leave the originating channel turn blocked when a post-`sessions_yield` requester-settle continuation asks a question.

## User Impact

User impact: channel users receive the question in the originating conversation instead of having to discover and answer it in Control UI.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded progress controller converted an absent `onToolResult` callback into a truthy no-op callback. The tool lifecycle then reserved the question prompt for that callback even though it could not deliver anything. Embedded tool construction also omitted the direct channel sender needed after preserving callback absence.

This change preserves callback absence and supplies the originating-channel sender only for runs without a lifecycle delivery callback. Normal runs continue using their existing callback, avoiding duplicate delivery.

Requested by [Ian via WebChat](https://jarvis.tail1050ea.ts.net/chat/main/dashboard/e9d23dff-549b-45b5-9c7a-f6148816c98c).

## Evidence

- Added an exact-path callback-less requester-settle Slack loopback test. The same `notifyToolResult` produced by `createEmbeddedRunProgressController` is passed into the real `prepareEmbeddedAttemptToolBase` composition, which constructs the real `ask_user` tool through `createOpenClawCodingTools` and selects `createChannelQuestionPromptDelivery` only because that callback is absent.
- The proof uses the real Slack plugin/Web API adapter against a credential-free local HTTP server. It verifies the originating account token, channel, and thread; canonical single-select Block Kit buttons; exactly one `chat.postMessage`; one answered-state `chat.update`; a single persisted answer claim; rejection of a duplicate claim; answered status; and successful tool resumption containing `Staging`.
- Regression sensitivity was verified by temporarily restoring the broken progress-controller wrapper: the Slack test failed because no prompt reached the callback-less embedded fallback, then passed again after restoring the branch implementation.
- Added production-composition coverage for a Slack-thread requester-settle run with `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"` and deliberately conflicting explicit/fallback route fields.
- Retained the independent Telegram loopback transport proof as cross-channel coverage. It captures the Bot API prompt, answers through the question gateway, persists the reply, and verifies successful resumption without duplicate prompt delivery.
- Ordinary channel runs remain on the embedded lifecycle callback and do not construct a competing fallback.
- Final focused validation on the rebased head: 65 tests passed (63 embedded-attempt composition tests plus the Slack and Telegram loopback proofs).
- `pnpm check:changed` passed formatting, core/core-test/test-root typechecks, lint, dead-export scans, boundary checks, and static guards; `git diff --check` passed.
- No production channel, external credential, or model call is used. The Slack proof deterministically executes the real prepared tool rather than relying on a model stream; the exact changed embedded composition and the real question bridge, Slack plugin, and transport remain in the exercised path.

---
[View the OpenClaw team session](https://jarvis.tail1050ea.ts.net/chat/main/dashboard/e9d23dff-549b-45b5-9c7a-f6148816c98c)

prs.body:
Related: #171470. Backports #170779 to `release/2026.10.5`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor can finish successfully and then fail command cleanup when a loaded host needs more than 300 ms to confirm a force-killed process group has exited.

## User Impact

Doctor and updater-owned commands wait for confirmed cleanup instead of reporting a false failure. Truly surviving or identity-replaced groups still report uncertain settlement; command success is not forced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing main repair: retain the 300 ms cooperative termination grace and give post-SIGKILL extinction confirmation a separate, bounded 10-second allowance. All three production owners match upstream exactly, with Peter Steinberger's authorship preserved. The main-only extension cleanup test remains absent because it never existed on this release branch.

## Evidence

The initial CI failure was the release base's unrelated `worker-heap-flag.mjs` duplicate-scan coverage omission. Dallin merged [separate prerequisite #171504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171504) as `ade497cac39fe3b01604e867c47f5de2120d3630`. This PR is reconciled onto that base: range-diff is patch-identical and the native coverage guard passes. Existing focused proof and independent review are reused for the unchanged fix, not presented as a fresh review of the mechanical rebase.

- Release settlement regressions: 85 passed across six files, 61.37s wall. These include delayed extinction, genuine survivors, and process-identity replacement.
- Targeted formatting, lint, core/services test typegraphs, and mock-export validation passed.
- Fresh independent AutoReview through P2: no findings.
- The [original failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38362668271/job/115180822250) finished before #170779 landed. Its logs do not identify the retained PID, so attribution to the repaired window is source-backed inference. Full packaged Doctor and native Linux/Windows compositions remain for hosted CI.
- Current head `d306c54b210f1375feb398a6d96fbfc520a7d876` has [one failing UI-e2e leaf and the aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38495103289). This is an inherited dashboard-cold-load first-paint race: [earlier main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38033338182/job/114158789170) failed the same case with the same test blob before this Doctor change. The separate test-only [prerequisite #171543](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171543) adapts the maintained upstream persisted-transcript wait to the release cache layout; its CI/security and ClawSweeper review pass. This Doctor PR awaits prerequisite landing and base reconciliation. No CI rerun or unrelated UI patch is folded into the Doctor feature. [Explicitly requested ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171497#issuecomment-6158846198) completed on this exact head with 0 findings.

prs.title: fix(ui): thin Vietnamese Noto webfont fallback (#133930)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Issue:** #133930 — bundled Control UI fonts omit Vietnamese precomposed range (U+1EA0–U+1EF1, e.g. U+1EBF), so diacritics fall through to OS fonts.
- **Prior closed PR:** #134996 — closed for verify/proof stall; large surface (System unload/reload, e2e mega-suite). **This PR deliberately does not mega-redo that.**
- **Thin fix:** one self-hosted Noto Sans Vietnamese subset + typography loader stylesheet + `"Noto Sans"` immediately after each bundled face in stacks. No System ownership machinery, no e2e suite.

## Tip FAIL

- U+1EBF absent from every non-Noto bundled WOFF2.
- Instrument Sans `unicode-range` jumps U+1E9F → U+1EF2 (gap includes U+1EBF).

## Evidence (fail → pass)

- `scripts/check-vietnamese-font-coverage.py`: tip without subset assets → FAIL missing stylesheet; with assets → PASS cmap + unicode-range (U+1EA0–U+1EF1, U+031B, NFD marks). Re-run 2026-09-16 (venv fonttools): **exit 0** (unicode-range + both woff2 cmaps + Instrument Sans gap still present).
- `ui/src/app/theme-fonts.test.ts`: coverage + stack assertions (Noto on proportional faces only; `jetbrains-mono` / System stay Noto-free). Full file **25/25** passed after mono + test fixes (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts ui/src/app/theme-fonts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → exit 0).
- Loader asserts shared `/fonts/noto-sans-vietnamese.css` loads with every theme sync; System stacks stay Noto-free; **mono stacks keep proportional Noto out** (`--mono` in `base.css`, CRT/Phosphor theme overrides, and generated `jetbrains-mono` typeface stack).
- Browser suite `ui/src/e2e/theme-typography.e2e.test.ts` (updated counts: initial CSS 3→4 incl. Noto link; specimens 9→10; eleven theme stylesheet lists include `noto-sans-vietnamese`):
  - Full file first pass: **27/29** (2 flaky timeouts: `tide` `page.goto`, ligature composer wait — not assertion mismatches).
  - Retry `-t 'paints tide chrome|scopes the ligature'`: **2/2 exit 0**. Combined: **all 29 green**.
- **Kevin screenshots still needed** (NFC/NFD horn text + code alignment) from served candidate UI on this branch — box cannot attach current-branch UI screenshots here. Prior #134996 shots do not prove this loader.

## ClawSweeper raise (2026-09-16)

Addressed review findings on head `36045bf3c0`:
1. **P2 Preserve monospace metrics** — removed `"Noto Sans"` from mono stacks.
2. **P2 Update browser tests** — appearance-picker + theme stylesheet expectations updated for the Noto fallback link.

`@clawsweeper re-review` after this push (`e5feb98498`).


## Notes

Vendor: OFL Noto Sans subset; same provenance pin as #134996. Maintainer vendor-approval may still be required for merge.

Closes #133930

prs.title: fix(release): qualify extended-stable candidates from the previous extended-stable release
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Full Release Validation for an extended-stable `.33` candidate never upgrades from the extended-stable release its users run (2026.8.35 for 2026.9.33); it only qualifies the same-month stable predecessor (2026.9.9), and the upgrade survivor harness would pass shipped 8.35 an explicit `--tag`, which its extended-stable policy refuses.

## User Impact

No product change. Release operators now get cross-OS and upgrade survivor proof for the real extended-stable upgrade path (previous extended-stable release to candidate, through the old updater's `extended-stable` selector) before publishing a `.33+` release.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Qualification baselines: for an extended-stable candidate (an `extended-stable/YYYY.M.33` context or a `.33+` version), the primary `upgradeBaseline` becomes the newest published extended-stable release below the candidate, resolved from npm versions with the same helper regular stable candidates already use for their extended-stable survivor. The frozen month's stable predecessor stays in `upgradeSurvivorBaselines`. `validateQualificationBaselines` now owns the train-aware primary rule (newest extended-stable survivor for extended-stable candidates, newest survivor otherwise) and accepts the extended-stable predecessor on frozen contexts. The duplicate "newest selected predecessor" check in admission is removed. The SHA-pinned dispatcher already resolves through `resolveQualificationBaselines`, so it needs no separate change; `qualification_baselines_json` stays reserved there.
- Cross-OS: with an extended-stable baseline and candidate, `usesExtendedStableRegistryRoute` already drops `--tag` and sets `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_PACKAGE_SPEC=openclaw`/`NPM_CONFIG_TAG=extended-stable` against the loopback registry that publishes `extended-stable=<candidate>`. Shipped 8.35 resolves that selector through its loopback test seam (`resolveExtendedStableRegistryTarget`), so the lane now runs the old updater's real dist-tag path.
- Upgrade survivor: updates between extended-stable releases serve the candidate under `extended-stable` on the loopback registry (adding it to the scenario registry or starting a candidate-only one) and run `openclaw update` with `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_PACKAGE_SPEC=openclaw` and no `--tag`. Extended-stable to regular and regular to anything keep their existing explicit-target paths. The legacy-operator no-op step uses the same selector route, forward-ported from the 2026.9.33 branch.
- `pnpm update:compat:check` also requires the `extended-stable` dist-tag version when that tag exists.

Note: on current `main`, `pnpm update:compat:check` already fails on `beta` 2026.10.5-beta.3, and with this change it also reports 2026.8.35. The inventory is regenerated with verified tarballs through `pnpm update:compat:gen` in a separate step. This PR does not hand-edit it. The check is a manual maintainer report and does not run in CI.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/release-upgrade-baseline.test.ts`: 21 passed. Covers 2026.9.33 resolving `openclaw@2026.8.35` with survivors `[2026.8.35, 2026.9.9]`, the tag-context variant, 2026.9.34 to 2026.9.33, and validator rejection of a same-month or older extended-stable primary. Cost is about 1s of test time.
- New `test/scripts/upgrade-survivor-extended-stable-selector.test.ts`: 4 passed. It runs the real `configure_plugin_registry`/`update_candidate` shell for 8.35 to 9.33 (selector, `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_PACKAGE_SPEC=openclaw`, `extended-stable=2026.9.33` registry tag, with and without a scenario registry), 9.9 to 9.33 (`--tag`), and 8.35 to 10.1 (`--tag` plus `--channel stable`). Cost is 1.7s of test time (`--maxWorkers=1` wall 4.9s).
- `test/scripts/runtime-postbuild.test.ts`: 151 passed, including the new extended-stable refresh and invalid-tag cases (two added table rows, sub-second).
- Existing survivor and docker-build-helper suites: 146 + 112 passed. Release admission, publication, cross-OS, and summary suites passed, except three `full-release-publication-admission` workflow-body cases. Those fail locally only because macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2 treats `admission_args[@]` as unbound, and the workflows are untouched. Five Android projection cases also hit 30s timeouts under host load.
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, oxfmt, oxlint, `bash -n`, and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Live `pnpm update:compat:check` reports `2026.10.5-beta.3, 2026.8.35` missing, as described above.

prs.title: fix(agents): report allowlist provenance when no callable tools remain
prs.body:
## Summary

When a scheduled run resolves to zero callable tools, `buildEmptyExplicitToolAllowlistError` always closes with:

> Fix the allowlist or enable the plugin that registers the requested tool.

For a cron job created through the model-callable `automations` tool, that hint is wrong twice over, and it sends the operator after a cause that is not theirs. This PR makes the diagnostic tell the truth about **where the allowlist came from**.

It does **not** change which tools any run may call.

## Reproduction (reproduced live on installed OpenClaw 2026.9.4, 2026-09-15)

1. Call `automations(action:"add")` with an `agentTurn` payload and **no** `toolsAllow`. Returns ok. The persisted job contains:
   - `payload.toolsAllowIsDefault: true` and `payload.toolsAllow` = the full default list of 68 built-in tools (`ls`, `read`, `edit`, `write`, `apply_patch`, `exec`, `process`, `message`, `sessions_*`, `graphiti__*`, …)
   - `scheduledToolPolicy: { version: 1, mode: "account", ownerSessionKey: "agent:lucy:main", ownerAccountId: "lucy" }`
2. Force a run. It fails in 544 ms with `completionStatus: failed`:

   ```
   No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist
   (runtime toolsAllow: ls, read, edit, write, ... graphiti__summarize_saga);
   no registered tools matched. Fix the allowlist or enable the plugin that
   registers the requested tool.
   ```
3. Control: ~20 CLI-created cron jobs on the same gateway, same agent, same tool registry run successfully every night. The CLI stamps `mode: "trusted"`.

The tools named in that message are registered built-ins, and no plugin is missing. The operator is told to edit an allowlist they never wrote and to enable a plugin that is not the problem.

## Root cause of the misdiagnosis

The guard has no access to the two facts that explain the emptiness:

- **The allowlist was not operator-authored.** `capCronJobToolsAllow` (`src/agents/tools/cron-tool-creator-cap.ts:298-312`) copies the creating turn's effective tool surface into `payload.toolsAllow` and stamps `toolsAllowIsDefault: true` when the caller requested no allowlist. That is the origin of the 68-name list. Nothing downstream carried `toolsAllowIsDefault` into the run, so the guard could not distinguish it from a hand-written `tools.allow`.
- **A scheduled authority capped the run.** The job carries a server-stamped `scheduledToolPolicy` in `account` mode, which deliberately reduces the run to its authoring session's authority (`src/agents/conversation-capability-profile.ts:148-161`). `attempt.scheduledToolPolicy` was already present at the guard call site but was never passed in.

So `buildEmptyExplicitToolAllowlistError` (`src/agents/tool-allowlist-guard.ts`) fell through to its only non-workshop branch: reason `"no registered tools matched"` whenever `toolsEnabled && !toolsIntentionallyDisabled`, plus the unconditional "Fix the allowlist or enable the plugin" tail.

## What this PR does

- Adds `runtimeSupplied` to `ExplicitToolAllowlistSource` and to `collectExplicitToolAllowlistSources`, emitted only when true so existing shapes are unchanged.
- Threads `toolsAllowIsDefault` from the cron payload (`run-executor.ts`) through `RunEmbeddedAgentParams` and `run-attempt-dispatch.ts` to `collectAttemptExplicitToolAllowlistSources`, which marks the `runtime toolsAllow` source as runtime-supplied.
- Passes the already-available `attempt.scheduledToolPolicy?.mode` into the guard.
- When **every** enforced allowlist source is runtime-supplied, the guard now says the list was captured automatically from the creating session and, in `account` mode, that a scheduled `"account"` policy capped the run to that session's authority — and drops the misleading plugin hint.

Operator-authored allowlists keep the previous wording and the plugin hint, including when a scheduled policy is present. There is a regression test for that.

## Why this does not widen privilege

`toolsAllowIsDefault` is carried as a diagnostics-only fact and is read **only** inside the error-message builder. It is never consulted when constructing, filtering or projecting tools, and the field is documented as such in `params.ts`. Account mode remains exactly as restrictive as before — no code path was changed to force `mode: "trusted"`, and the privilege-reduction intent of account mode is preserved deliberately. The diff adds no tool to any surface.

## Scope: what this PR does not fix

**I did not reproduce or fix the zero-callable-tools collapse itself.** I want to be explicit about that rather than imply a root-cause fix.

What I ruled out in source, empirically, with a throwaway probe over `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` + `projectConversationToolNames` (probe deleted before committing):

- **Account mode does not empty the policy pipeline.** With a resolvable account, `account` mode projected the full runtime allowlist identically to `trusted` mode and to no scheduled policy at all (all three returned every requested name; `explicitToolAllowlist` was complete in each case).
- Account mode with a **named, non-default** account whose channel account cannot be confirmed **throws** a distinct error — `Scheduled account "lucy" is unavailable. Re-add it to the channel configuration, or recreate this automation from the intended account.` — not the empty-allowlist error. So `resolveGroupToolPolicyOutcome` fails loudly rather than silently emptying the set.
- `resolveCodingToolConstructionPlanForAllowlist` (`attempt-tool-construction-plan.ts`) selects the `base-coding`, `shell` and `openclaw` families for a concrete allowlist containing `ls`/`read`/`write`/`exec`, so construction does run.

Separately, and **not addressed here**: `scheduledRuntimeAuthority` and `scheduledRuntimeAuthorityRecoveryRequired` are forwarded from `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.ts:854-856` into `RunEmbeddedAgentParams` and on through `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/run-attempt-dispatch.ts:633-634` into the attempt, but an exhaustive grep finds no consumer anywhere — only the type declaration, those two assignments, and two cron tests. A cleared or drifted runtime-authority envelope therefore has no effect on the constructed tool surface. That looks like dead authority plumbing and may deserve its own issue; I did not change it.

## Verification

All commands run from the repo root on the branch, with real results:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/tool-allowlist-guard.test.ts` (before the fix) | **exit 1** — `Tests 3 failed \| 15 passed (18)`; the 3 new tests fail as intended |
| `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/tool-allowlist-guard.test.ts src/agents/scheduled-tool-policy.test.ts src/cron/scheduled-tool-policy.test.ts src/commands/doctor/cron/scheduled-tool-policy-migration.test.ts` | **exit 0** — `40 passed (40)` + `3 passed (3)` |
| `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/tool-allowlist-guard.test.ts src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.availability.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.payload-fallbacks.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.account-policy.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run-delivery-trace.tools-allow.test.ts` | **exit 0** — `18 passed`, `138 passed`, `22 passed`, `3 passed` (181 total) |
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | **exit 0**, no output |
| `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json --report-unused-disable-directives-severity error` on the 7 changed files | **exit 0** — `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors. Finished in 486ms on 7 files with 230 rules` |
| `pnpm lint` (full) | **could not complete on my machine.** The `--type-aware` shard's `tsgolint` child was OOM-killed twice (`signal: 'SIGKILL'`; kernel log: `Killed process … (tsgolint) … anon-rss:13482640kB`) on a 14 GB box. Shards 1 and 3 reported `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`. This is an environment memory limit, not a lint finding — hence the scoped oxlint run above (230 of the full run's 263 rules; the type-aware rules are the ones not covered). |

Reproduced on **2026.9.4**. Branch is based on `upstream/main` at `c20bd61ce`.

prs.title: fix(msteams): reactions on a channel thread reply fail with NotFound
prs.body:
Fixes #166178

## What Problem This Solves

Teams reactions to the current channel-thread reply discard its root and fail with Graph NotFound by treating the reply as a top-level message.

## User Impact

Users can react to the current channel reply without manually specifying its thread root.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the current Teams channel message's thread root when resolving message actions, and use the nested Graph reply resource for reactions and reads. Explicit IDs for unrelated messages do not inherit the current thread; chat and top-level channel resources retain their existing addressing.

The message resolver stays private in its existing action owner rather than introducing a new exported helper. Thanks to @ericcurtin for the fix and reproduction.

## Evidence

Built Gateway with the real msteams plugin, a scripted model invoking the shipped `message` tool with `action: react` and no message ID, and loopback Bot Framework/Graph boundaries. Inbound activities were posted to `/api/messages`; no session/database state was hand-written. OAuth and external transport were synthetic; this is not a live Teams tenant test.

### Independent API contract and proof boundary

[Microsoft's setReaction documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/chatmessage-setreaction?view=graph-rest-beta) explicitly specifies both channel resources:
```text
POST /teams/{teamId}/channels/{channelId}/messages/{messageId}/setReaction
POST /teams/{teamId}/channels/{channelId}/messages/{rootId}/replies/{replyId}/setReaction
```
It specifies `204 No Content` for success. The recorded head request below matches the second shape; the base request incorrectly uses the first shape with a reply ID. The isolated Gateway proof tests the shipped ingress, tool dispatch, authorization, and resulting HTTP request against this independently documented boundary contract.

The reporter's exact [issue #166178](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/166178) error is `Resource not found [code=NotFound]`. Its provenance matters: the issue explicitly says this was a loopback response, **not** an authenticated live Microsoft response. Neither the issue nor this PR claims a live-service failure or success was observed.

No Teams tenant or delegated `ChannelMessage.Send` consent is available in this environment. Live tenant proof will run after merge when a tenant is available; the present acceptance evidence is the isolated built-Gateway boundary proof, not authenticated API acceptance.

Base `5dd456acfa35575c342b43b944a9d0dbb911b68e`:
```text
channel-thread reply:
POST /beta/teams/<team>/channels/<channel>/messages/1759600123456/setReaction -> 404
message tool: Graph ... failed (404): Resource not found [code=NotFound]
top-level control:
POST /beta/teams/<team>/channels/<channel>/messages/1759600000000/setReaction -> 204
message tool: {"channel":"msteams","action":"react","reactionType":"like","ok":true}
```

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

Candidate, using the identical inbound activities and tool call:
```text
channel-thread reply:
POST /beta/teams/<team>/channels/<channel>/messages/1759600000000/replies/1759600123456/setReaction -> 204
message tool: {"channel":"msteams","action":"react","reactionType":"like","ok":true}
top-level control:
POST /beta/teams/<team>/channels/<channel>/messages/1759600000000/setReaction -> 204
message tool: {"channel":"msteams","action":"react","reactionType":"like","ok":true}
```

Focused checks: both changed test files passed (71 tests); targeted formatting and the candidate build passed.
The simplification removes the extra exported resolver and returns it to the existing private action owner. Against the merge base: production +49/-15 lines; tests +86/-8 lines. The remaining growth carries trusted thread identity and protects reply, root, and chat boundaries.

## Risk

Two-way door: a revert restores previous URL construction; no persisted schema or configuration changes. Blast radius is Microsoft Teams message actions on the current channel reply. Other channels are unchanged.

prs.title: refactor(ui): use native chat tool detail tabs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes the remaining Web Awesome tab group from chat tool details as part of the native Control UI migration.

## User Impact

Tool details still switch between Diff and Raw, preserve a manually selected Raw view across refreshes, and open errors or skipped results in Raw. Keyboard activation, message-scoped IDs, and the mounted inactive panel are preserved. The native panels remove the old control’s extra vertical padding.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses the existing Solid `Tabs` and `TabPanel` primitives, with the shared Tabs controller as the only keyboard owner. No dependencies, startup registrations, or lazy boundaries change. This follows the merged chat-pane migration (#169835).

Production LOC: `chat-tool-content.solid.tsx` **560 → 548** and `tool-cards.css` **1325 → 1315**; **22 fewer production lines**. Tests retain the prior identity, selection, output, and visibility assertions and independently exercise the skipped-result default.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed | 49.00 s |
| `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 39 passed | 67.04 s Vitest / 77.99 s command |
| `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-card-identity.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 2 passed | 4.25 s Vitest / 21.03 s command |
| Changed skipped case, `-t 'shows skipped edit output'` | 1 passed after setting `isError` false for the skipped fixture | 81.52 s Vitest / 96.97 s command |
| `pnpm ui:build` | Passed | 33.23 s Vite / 53.80 s command |
| Strict performance, same-host base/head | Passed, no violations | 0.74 s |
| Synthetic desktop/mobile captures | Diff → Raw → Home; no page errors | 4.68 s base / 11.14 s head browser flow |
| Codemod dry run | 0 templates, 0 diagnostics | — |
| Targeted lint/styles/format, keyless i18n baseline + verify | Passed | — |
| Independent review | No actionable P0–P2 findings; follow-up test negative control reviewed | — |

Same-host comparison uses base `5dd456acfa35575c342b43b944a9d0dbb911b68e` and head `5b50079068d7be`:

| Measured surface | Base | Head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS gzip | 349,028 B / 8 requests | 348,621 B / 8 requests |
| Startup CSS gzip | 49,703 B / 1 request | 49,703 B / 1 request |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,765,961 B / 32 requests | 1,757,443 B / 32 requests |

prs.title: fix(config): keep deep config loading stack-safe past include resolution
prs.body:
Closes #153430

Related: #152847 (include resolution itself, already stack-safe in #152889) — this PR extends the same stack-safe contract to the loading stages that run after the resolver.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: loading a config whose deeply nested value passes `$include` resolution still crashes with an opaque `RangeError` when the resolved value reaches value merging, env substitution, or the legacy migration probes. The first iteration of this PR also reversed object key order on every substituted config (leaves were resolved in a reverse loop, and object slots record first-write order); that regression is fixed here, with a unit test pinning document key order.

## User Impact

User impact: a machine-generated config that nests deeply now fails with the normal actionable schema error instead of a stack-overflow crash from a stage after the one that already promises stack safety; nothing that was previously accepted is rejected, and persisted config key order matches the authored document.

## Why This Change Was Made

The include resolver walks documents on an explicit work stack, but every later stage still recursed. Each remaining walk now runs on an explicit work stack so document depth costs heap instead of call frames:

- `src/infra/deep-merge.ts`: `mergeDeep` and its plain-object sanitizer clone walk iteratively; prototype-key filtering is preserved.
- `src/config/env-substitution.ts`: `substituteAny` allocates object slots in source order (key order follows the document) and schedules child tasks depth-first, so `onMissing` warnings keep their original order.
- Legacy migration probes: the load-time `structuredClone(root)` calls (Node's built-in clone recurses too) are replaced by a shared iterative `deepCloneForMigrationProbe` in `legacy-config-record-shared.ts` across the models/providers/retired/config-tranche probes.

Net production growth is the shared clone helper plus the iterative walkers; no new configuration surface is added.

Competition/fix-surface note: #129403 overlaps on the env-substitution walk but does not touch the deep-merge or migration-probe clone crash points; this PR covers all three stages with tests.

## Evidence

All commands run from the PR checkout (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` over the real CLI sources — the installed CLI runs dist and predates any local change).

**1. Full CLI chain, normal config through `$include` to merge, env substitution, migration probes, and schema (fresh config behavior).** `settings.json` is a minimal gateway block; `main.json` includes it and defines a provider whose `baseUrl` is `${PROOF_BASE_URL}/v1`:

```
$ PROOF_BASE_URL=https://proof.example.local OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/main.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config get models.providers.proof-provider.baseUrl
https://proof.example.local/v1
(exit 0)
```

**2. Full CLI chain, 600-level nested value.** `nested600.json` nests a scalar 600 levels deep under a top-level key. The chain runs to completion and the value is rejected by schema validation with the actionable error, not by a RangeError:

```
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/nested600.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config get agents.defaults.timeout
OpenClaw config is invalid: /tmp/proof-153431/nested600.json
- nested600.json:1 — agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: "timeout"
- <root>: Unrecognized key: "deep"
(exit 0; the CLI reports the schema error and the next step instead of crashing)
```

**3. Depth matrix over the changed walkers** (module-level probe: build an n-level nested object, call `mergeDeep(v, v)` and `resolveConfigEnvVars(v, {})`):

| depth | recursive implementation (base 8ebc8cd021e) | this PR (iterative) |
|---|---|---|
| 4000 | mergeDeep RangeError; envSub RangeError | both OK |
| 8000 | both RangeError | both OK |
| 20000 | both RangeError | both OK |

The same matrix over the legacy migration probe clone (`findLegacyConfigIssues` -> `LEGACY_CONFIG_MIGRATION_RULES[].match` -> `deepCloneForMigrationProbe`, the load-time doctor detection path): recursive baseline RangeError at 5,000 levels; this PR completes the probe at 100,000 levels.

**4. Boundary note on depth.** At 4,000+ levels the still-recursive include resolver aborts the load before the stages this PR owns (Include resolution failed: RangeError); stack-safe include resolution is #152847's contract, delivered by #152889. See items 6-7 for the full real-loader crash-point chain and the 2,000-level end-to-end window measured after the include-resolver fix.

**5. Tests.** `src/config/env-substitution.test.ts` (19 cases: the 4,000-level no-overflow case, plus a key-order case that fails on the reversed-write implementation) and `src/infra/deep-merge.test.ts` (6 cases incl. the 4,000-level merge) are green on this head.

**6. Real-loader crash-point chain (post-Rev3 update).** Walking the real CLI load chain depth-by-depth with an isolated config (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, synthetic values) maps every recursive crash point between the loader and the stages this PR owns, observed through a load-path probe on the real sources:

| Load stage | Observed crash depth | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `$include` resolution (`resolveConfigIncludes`) | ~600 (2,000+ RangeError) | #152889 (stack-safe) |
| Read-path `$include` pre-scan (`containsConfigIncludeDirective`, `io.read-helpers.ts`) | 2,000 OK / 2,300+ RangeError | newly located; fixed by #153711 |
| Deep merge / env substitution / legacy migration probes | >2,300 — masked upstream on recursive baselines; isolated matrix in item 3 | **this PR** |
| `stableConfigStringify` (`runtime-snapshot.ts`) | 2,200 OK / 2,400+ RangeError | not yet fixed (family follow-up) |

**7. Full-chain proof at the new window.** On a checkout combining #152889 (include resolution) with this PR's three stages, a 2,000-level document under `agents.defaults.params` loads **end-to-end through the real CLI**:

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/proof-153431/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/config/openclaw.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/index.ts config get agents.defaults.model
test-model
(exit 0)
```

With this PR's three-stage fix removed from the same tree (recursive merge/env restored), the identical document also loads — because on a real load the recursive merge crash point sits deeper than the two masked stages above, the merge stages can only be observed through the isolated matrix in item 3. The depth-4,000 end-to-end claim therefore remains blocked by `stableConfigStringify` (item 6, last row), a recursive walker outside this PR's surface; recording it here so the family follow-up (#153708's chain) has the measured map.

**8. Doctor CLI chain over a legal deep config (real `openclaw doctor` on both baselines).** A config with an 800-level value under the schema-legal `tts.providers` catchall, run through the real CLI sources against the recursive base (origin/main `e63393bddc3a`) and this PR head, with isolated state dirs (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`): both runs complete the full doctor flow (health checks, legacy-state detection, migration preview) with no RangeError, and the probe/merge/env stages this PR changes process the same config. At 1,300+ levels both runs abort with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the doctor flow completes. On the recursive baseline that abort is consistent with the merge/env/probe crash points this PR owns (item 3 matrix); on this PR head those stages are iterative, so the remaining abort sits in the still-recursive post-probe clones (the candidate `structuredClone` in `doctor-config-flow.ts`, `cloneConfigWithResolutionFacts` in `resolution-facts.ts`). The full-chain before/after delta is therefore masked by those family stages; the measured window is recorded here for the follow-up.

`tsgo` core (`tsconfig.core.json`) and the core-test shards exit 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean on the touched files; the line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets report no violations for the touched files.
