prs.title: fix: Windows Defender flags the scheduled-task health check during OpenClaw Node startup
prs.body:
Closes #138224

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows users running OpenClaw Node would see Windows Defender (and other AV) alerts on OpenClaw's own scheduled-task health check when the node service starts or reports status. The alerted process is OpenClaw's own status probe, but its command line embeds a base64 payload (`powershell.exe -EncodedCommand ...`), a pattern AV heuristics treat as malware obfuscation. Users may block the detection and break node-mode startup, and repeated alerts erode trust in the tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduled-task state probe (`src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.ts`) keeps its PowerShell body as a fixed literal `-Command` string and passes the task name to the child as base64 data on stdin, so no base64-encoded script appears in the command line and no new global `OPENCLAW_*` environment identifier is introduced (the shrink-only env-name ratchet stays untouched). Empty stdin selects the inventory path used by `listScheduledTasks`, so a single literal body covers both query shapes and the spawned command line never varies. This mirrors the fixed `-Command` pattern the same Windows subsystem already uses for process inspection (`schtasks-process-snapshot.ts`), without adding a persistent .ps1 artifact.

Because Scheduler fixtures identify the state probe by its command shape, the fixture family follows the new transport: routing predicates in `schtasks.settlement`, `schtasks.stop`, `schtasks-runtime.deadline`, `schtasks.redirect-stop`, `schtasks.startup-fallback` and the `schtasks.stop` test support accept the literal body in addition to the legacy encoded form (unrelated calls keep their existing routing), `inspect.windows.registered` reads the queried task name from stdin instead of decoding the command line, and `service-command-read` asserts the new argv shape.

### Rebased onto current `main`

This revision is rebased onto `main` at `8c22de3f`. The command transport is the **only** behavioural delta. Everything current main added to this file is preserved:

- `resolvePositiveTimerTimeoutMs()` budgets, the `Math.min(...)` allowance clamp and the expired-deadline guard (#155051, #154565);
- `resolveServiceManagerEnv()` (#139333) and the caller-supplied `env`;
- `windowsHide: false` and the console-creation behaviour from #148671;
- the nested `actions` / `enabled` snapshot fields read from `IRegisteredTask` (#151608);
- `diagnostic` / timeout / failure-detail reporting (#148671, #157719);
- the update-access probe from #166695 — `probeScheduledTaskUpdateAccess` and the `checkUpdateAccess` third parameter.

That last one is why this revision exists: #166695 introduced a **second** command body (the update-access variant that reports the caller's principal and token instead of the task snapshot). Both bodies are now fixed literals and only the lookup tail differs, so neither branch ever interpolates caller data into the command line. The non-elevated body is byte-for-byte the same as the previous revision of this branch (`2636f9bf…`, unchanged); the update-access body is carried over verbatim from main and re-expressed as a module-level literal.

Main keeps rewriting these fixtures, so this revision tracks its current shape rather than a previous one. Earlier rounds already absorbed main's fixture churn (it deleted `schtasks.shutdown.test.ts` outright, expanded `schtasks.settlement.test.ts` from four probe call sites to twelve, and collapsed the parametrized `taskTest.for` case in `schtasks.stop.test.ts`). This round's only conflict was the probe body above; its hunks in any file main has since removed stay dropped, and the transport predicate is re-applied only on call sites main still has, so no upstream change is reintroduced or reverted.

### Fixture family completed: the Windows update-CLI interceptors

Changing this shared spawn also moves two Windows update-CLI fixtures that intercept the probe **by command shape**. They are not new work, but they are exactly what this transport change breaks if left alone, so they are updated here:

- `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-windows-preflight.test-support.ts` — its `spawnSync` interceptor only recognised `-EncodedCommand` and otherwise delegated to the **real** native spawn. All seven `registerWindowsTaskAdmissionTests` scenarios install the actual `probeScheduledTaskUpdateAccess`, so under the literal transport they would have launched host PowerShell (or failed to find it) instead of reading the supplied principal / denial / timeout facts, and the final encoded-call assertions could not be satisfied. It now recognises the literal body, reads the task name from stdin, and asserts the new transport — including that the task name never reaches the command line. Its closing assertion also stopped counting **every** literal `-Command` spawn: `readWindowsProcessSnapshot` legitimately spawns one during a successful update, so the test now counts spawns whose body contains `Schedule.Service`, i.e. actual probe-shaped spawns, and still requires exactly one.

- `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-windows-probe.test.ts` — its interceptor threw `Unexpected native inspection` for anything that was neither the process probe nor an encoded one. It now accepts the literal body as the task probe, so the six strict-inspection scenarios keep exercising the real failure ladder.

Those two are the **complete** set: a repository code search for `args?.includes("-EncodedCommand")` returns exactly six files, and all six are in this PR's changed set. `audit/audit-138344-fixtures.json` records that check, so a future upstream fixture of the same shape cannot be silently missed. The branch against `main` is a clean 12-file diff (`mergeable: true`, +207/−76).

## User Impact

- Windows Defender no longer has an encoded-command heuristic to flag during node-mode startup or status checks; the spawned command line is a fixed, human-readable literal.
- Users no longer need antivirus exclusions to run OpenClaw Node cleanly.
- The spawned command line is fully auditable: a fixed literal body with the task name riding only as stdin data, so non-ASCII task names keep working.

## Evidence

Native Windows behaviour trace (Windows 11, Windows PowerShell 5.1). Both script bodies were **extracted programmatically from the rebased source** — not hand-copied — and spawned with the production argv shape, stdin transport, timeout and `windowsHide` setting. Re-runnable harness: `tools/verify-138344.mjs` (**16/16 checks PASS**).

Script body SHA-256 (non-elevated, the shipping path): `2636f9bfd8706e7c9af4478bd4063bf3cf7cd04a9d0778d4cb20acb062e32293`
Script body SHA-256 (update-access variant): `cfc8b52e461d2cc144abe4f3b525990e56cb759e09b9487d0474b12349c7a5e1`

1. Real registered task on this host — `\Clawdbot Gateway`, i.e. the OpenClaw gateway task itself:

```
exitCode=0  stdout={"status":"found","state":3,"enabled":true,"lastRunResult":"1","lastRunTime":"2026-10-09T11:08:14.0000000Z"}
```

   The nested `actions` / `enabled` fields introduced by current main survive the transport change, and `state` / `lastRunResult` / `lastRunTime` are unchanged.

2. Empty stdin (the `listScheduledTasks` inventory path):

```
exitCode=0  174 tasks parsed, 174 with taskPath
```

3. Absent task (locale-independent absence contract preserved):

```
exitCode=1  stdout=-2147024894   ->  status "missing"
```

4. Command-line assertions captured in the same run: `-EncodedCommand` absent; argv is exactly `["-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", <fixed body>]`, body length 1868 (the update-access body is 2534); the task name is absent from the command line as both plaintext and base64; the command body is byte-identical across two different task names (`[Console]::In.ReadLine()` is the only task-name-dependent path).

5. A task name containing shell metacharacters (`OpenClaw Gateway & calc.exe`) never reaches the command line and still resolves through the stdin transport.

6. Upgrade-path safety on this host's pre-existing install: `Get-ScheduledTask` reads the real service (`Date: 2026-02-17`, registered seven months before this branch), the candidate probe resolves it five consecutive times with **byte-identical** verdicts, and a static scan of the probe body finds no task-mutating verb — the upgrade path can only read. Full upgrade-chain evidence (a published updater crossing over a candidate install) is out of scope for any external contributor and is not claimed here.

7. The preserved update-access variant is exercised for real too, not just structurally: against the same registered task it exits 0 and returns

```
{"taskUserSid":"S-1-5-21-…-1001","callerSid":"S-1-5-21-…-1001","callerElevated":false,"taskRunLevel":0}
```

   i.e. valid facts that `probeScheduledTaskUpdateAccess` classifies as `allowed` (the same non-elevated user owns the task). A static scan of that body finds no task-mutating verb either.

8. Fixture coverage: a repository code search for `args?.includes("-EncodedCommand")` returns exactly **6** files, and all 6 are in this PR's changed set (`audit/audit-138344-fixtures.json` → `coverage.uncovered: []`). The static audit also asserts that every remaining recognition site carries a `Schedule.Service` body arm.

Local gates on the rebased head: `oxfmt 0.71.0 --check` clean and `oxlint 1.85.0` (CI's pinned version) reports 0 warnings and 0 errors across all 12 changed files. CI additionally lints with `oxlint-tsgolint`, and type-aware rules cannot be reproduced against a partial checkout, so the build also rejects the `prefer-includes` idiom syntactically rather than trusting the local lint pass alone. `src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.test.ts` keeps every existing case (including main's timeout-budget, expired-deadline and update-access matrices) and adds 2 cases locking the argv/stdin contract. No `node_modules` are available on this host and the local clone is a sparse partial checkout, so the vitest suite itself is exercised by CI rather than locally; the two update-CLI fixtures above are therefore type-checked and formatted here but executed by CI.

### Changed-test cost

`src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.test.ts` keeps every existing case and adds 2 cases; the other eleven changed files are existing fixtures whose probe-recognition predicates now also accept the literal body (one of them, `update-command-windows-preflight.test-support.ts`, was added to main by #166695). The rebase drops this branch's edits to test files main no longer has rather than reviving them. No test file is added, and no project or CI shard configuration changes, so this does not add a lane.

| Test file | Measured cost | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `src/daemon/schtasks.startup-fallback.test.ts` | 8.3 s whole-file segment (Windows lane) | `scripts/lib/ci-windows-test-plan.mts` → `fileSeconds`, maintained from a Windows CI run |
| the other 11 changed files | not published in the repo's timing tables (`fileSeconds`, `config/ci-test-timings.json`) | — |

`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall is not measurable on this host: the working copy is a sparse partial checkout without `node_modules` and the package-manager store is unusable, so vitest runs in CI only. This revision is a mock-routing/predicate change, so the fixture files execute the same number of cases as main (plus the 2 added probe cases).

---

prs.title: fix(discord): message edits cannot update Components V2 cards
prs.body:
Closes #165615

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the message tool cannot update an existing Discord Components V2 card, rejecting component-only edits and dropping card data when text is supplied.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can replace an existing card in place after a decision, including edits without a plain-text message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The public edit adapter now forwards the component specification and callback context. The runtime uses the existing component-edit writer, which builds the V2 PATCH without `content` and refreshes callback registrations. Component payloads are also exposed for enabled edit actions. Ordinary text edits and retained progress edits keep their existing path; account, action, target, and request-authority gates remain in place.

This is scoped to the documented component-spec object format and existing V2 cards. It does not establish conversion of classic text messages or native component-array edits.

## Evidence

- Source trace against upstream `553841e490220a6c723da84a4fdd3caf0dcb2a11` confirms the two failing boundaries: the public edit adapter omitted components, and the runtime required content and used the content-only writer.
- Added regressions in existing suites for public forwarding with optional text, edit discovery, disabled/blocked targets, and retained progress rendering with an irrelevant malformed component payload.
- Added a loopback REST regression through the public action and real component-edit writer that asserts V2 flags and components, without PATCH content or create-message nonce. This test is authored but **not executed**.
- Fresh independent source review of the final seven-file patch found no actionable P0–P2 defects. `git diff --check` passes.
- **Unrun:** focused tests, extension/contracts checks, formatting/types/build checks, live Discord card editing, and callback interaction proof. Required secretless execution isolation is unavailable on this host; repository code was not executed outside that boundary. AutoReview could not run because neither the Codex nor Claude CLI is installed; independent source review is not a completed AutoReview result.
- Test wall time and added CI seconds are unavailable because no test run was made. Keep this PR draft until the checks and relevant Discord flow are verified.

prs.title: fix(update): stabilize stalled recovery cleanup validation
prs.body:
Refs #170803 (stalled-recovery descendant race only).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed-service recovery cleanup validation can expire before a loaded runner starts and records the fixture's descendant process. Fixture teardown can also delete its temporary state directory before asynchronous database retirement finishes.

## User Impact

No production behavior, deadlines or configuration changes. Validation retains real descendant termination, failed-recovery checks and resource drainage before fixture-file removal.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture's one-second expiry could precede descendant startup. Its helper-only preload captures the actual recovery timeout callback and invokes it after an explicit readiness marker and a verified live, persisted descendant PID. A separate 30-second readiness watchdog still invokes native cleanup if readiness fails. Timeout → command close → helper completion ordering, dead-descendant and durable failure assertions remain.

The preload is ordinary lintable ESM in `test/fixtures/managed-service-recovery-clock.mjs`, loaded with `--import` and per-case JSON configuration. The added preload contains no generated JavaScript string or function serialization; descendants retain native clocks and spawns.

After the observed Linux teardown `ENOTEMPTY`, the shared fixture now awaits the maintained `closeStateDatabaseForTest()` before removing its directories. No filesystem retry, timing seam or triage rewrite is added. Natural local replay did not reproduce that Linux error; the async owner contract and existing controlled reader-retirement case support the repair.

The unrelated main SDK-budget failure is already repaired by Peter's [57547cb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/57547cb53547113a20efd7e019cc3e999410145b). All three feature commits are reconciled onto that concrete gate fix with equal range-diffs, patch IDs and final feature blobs. This PR changes no SDK or production files. Installer DNS and Kova observations remain outside scope.

## Evidence

- The original controlled descendant-startup delay reproduces the `undefined`-PID failure before the repair. The [original hosted failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38350592860/job/115142130324) remains separate evidence.
- Current head `5931272a3434d64ef68c570827c84c660bc39225`, base `57547cb53547113a20efd7e019cc3e999410145b`: canonical SDK surface guard passes (12.57s). Six selected current-base checks pass (156.90s wall): stalled recovery with the unchanged startup-delay diagnostic, slow guarded recovery, refused systemd restart, hung triage, retained updater notification, and the real SQLite-reader retirement owner. Changed transitive SQLite inputs are recorded; these checks do not claim full current-base breadth.
- Current-head core lint, infra type graph, formatting, line-cap, max-lines/environment ratchets and diff checks pass. The prior Doctor suppression gap is absent on the maintained new base; no waiver or baseline change was introduced by this feature.
- Current-head [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501112616) passes: native lifecycle [31/31](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501112616/job/115648509578), including the stalled-recovery case at 1.108s, and triage [14/14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38501112616/job/115648509585), including retained notification/exit 1 at 1.481s. Both jobs verify tested checkout `6258ba077bc4ff1e40c8e0357e647cc2dad1c2a2`, merging head `5931272a3434d64ef68c570827c84c660bc39225` into actual CI base `976cc974fab1912c696d1101bd17a1abf05eb77e`. This is 45 passing hosted cases, not the prior local owner proof or a fresh Linux teardown failure reproduction.
- Current-head [post-CI security review and aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38502221491) pass; all seven CodeQL categories pass. The requested [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171507#issuecomment-6158963708) now explicitly reviews `5931272a3434d64ef68c570827c84c660bc39225`, with 0 findings and no before-merge code blockers. Its human opt-in hold remains a maintainer landing decision, not a failing code finding.
- Prior-base complete lifecycle/triage plus controlled owner proof: 45+1 cases passed. Original, preload-refactor and async-cleanup canonical P2 reviews were scoped-clean. They remain patch-bound reviews reused after the mechanical rebase, not a freshly run new-base review.

prs.title: fix(sessions): preserve requester identity at execution admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #150705.

Fixes delegated work losing its original requester and steering attaching a new request to an active turn with different authority.

## User Impact

Authenticated requester facts survive execution, replies, nested/native delegation, workers, and recovery. Each new execution resolves the requester's current applicable policy at its destination and freezes it for that execution. Already admitted followups retain their policy while queued; human input waiting for admission sees current policy when admitted.

Human inbound configured for steering queues a different requester's message as a new turn in the same conversation. The runtime acknowledgment reports whether it remains queued and says it has not changed active work. A queued natural-language stop has not stopped that work. Same-requester compatible steering still requires a current execution owner; explicit incompatible `sessions_send(mode="steer")` refuses with followup guidance.

Accepted asynchronous work survives normal source completion. Intentional delegation to a more capable agent remains supported under destination authorization: there is no universal source-capability ceiling. Existing child ceilings and applicable requester restrictions remain effective. Shared history stays shared; configured interrupt mode and authorized stop commands keep their separate cancellation contracts.

**Upgrade consequence:** queued collectors created by v2026.10.3 or another version without requester recovery capture cannot safely reconstruct their original requester. After restart, such a launch records an explicit failure and asks the user to submit it again; it does not resume as system authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing owners carry requester facts separately from calculated policy. Native spawn captures those facts before collector callbacks clear ambient caller context, and the worker boundary carries them privately. Fresh followups to existing children apply current requester policy alongside the retained child envelope. Cross-session steering projects the incoming requester under current destination configuration through the recipient's existing tool-authority owner; incompatible policy refuses without refreshing the incumbent.

Telegram DM and X guest configuration resolve through channel owners. The shipped SDK prepared-policy adapter retains its original request/queued-turn lifetime for external integrations. History display removes private requester metadata without changing transcript custody. Pending-input custody reuses its decoded immutable requester facts; recovery combines an avoidable repeated keyed read. Cancellation, revocation, superseded-owner, integrity, and final-write checks remain authoritative. Diagnostic audit remains opt-in and is not an authorization source; this change adds no diagnostic-audit authority.

Native queued recovery records original requester/operator recovery facts in the existing launch descriptor and revalidates live authority before dispatch. Malformed capture is refused. Current records distinguish an owner-captured absence from an unclassified legacy record. Collector scheduler acceptance precedes execution admission, so a waiting collector resolves current applicable policy when its execution actually starts.

Settings, transcript bytes, and consumed receipts retain their existing storage owners; there is no requester backfill or schema-version change. The new recovery capture uses the existing persisted registry. A bounded nine-file alternative moved facts into a new prepared/admitted-run access path but retired no carrier or owner and established no ordinary-path capture reduction. We retained the existing carriers and owners. There is no new core manager, configuration option, or request-hash format.

## Evidence

### Source and line churn

The integrated candidate is commit `2d641296dbc1798a61eaa4ba89d92fc26588abab`, tree `d24bf7317bef0be99cfde611cdd6681c200ddb55`, on main `46053391a1ad842d290563c38ca17b6aeb1d1a46`; the checkout was clean when counted. These exact counts cover the **whole PR against that new base**, including the channel-reference and recovery-source codecs and extracted provider fixture:

| Area | Files | Added | Removed | Net | Churn |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 146 | 3,318 | 1,231 | +2,087 | 4,549 |
| Tests and support | 127 | 6,962 | 2,167 | +4,795 | 9,129 |
| Docs | 6 | 77 | 37 | +40 | 114 |
| Tooling and guard inventories | 4 | 3 | 3 | 0 | 6 |
| **Total** | **283** | **10,360** | **3,438** | **+6,922** | **13,798** |

These are raw added/removed lines, including moves and formatting. Production excludes executable tests, test support, docs, scripts, and guard inventories. Tests/support comprise **96 changed executable test files and 31 support files**. The pending-Stop test is now byte-identical to main and drops out; the existing `sessions-send-followup.test.ts` enters the inventory. The release-only registered Gateway fixture totals 1,641 lines across its test and two support files and runs all eight scenario helpers in one Gateway lifetime. Churn and command wall time are not product runtime overhead.

The integration from pre-rebase `fa697d8356` into prior head `50efea5c0f` was mechanical: both later commits retained identical patches; the first retained independent compatibility records/inventory from main and dropped the superseded pending-Stop fixture change. The current amendment then adds the codec and CI-fixture repairs described below. Main's worker, registry, shutdown and warmed-reader changes remain intact.

### Revision evidence and remaining gates

Tests ran serially against recorded frozen working-tree snapshots. The final pre-rebase passing source is bound by `revision-staged-sourceidentity.json` to index tree `1ee8ea256abe9d6c20cfc6e79fb56607f01e7a72`; staging changed no source byte. Those earlier results retain their original source scope. Integrated frozen dependency installation passes (5.8 s), whole-PR formatting passes (0.587 s), and `git diff --check` passes (0.067 s). Retry02 subsequently exercises the exact integrated candidate; its results and limits appear below:

| Boundary | Observed evidence | Remaining qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native spawn and workers | Original registered ordinary/collector steering lost requester identity; the private worker boundary also reproduced loss. Revised native adapter and worker suites each pass 6/6; spawn passes 35/35 and worker placement 21/21. | Both native variants and their source-completion controls pass in the complete registered flow on exact `2d641296db` in retry02. |
| Fresh followup to an existing child | Two original policy regressions fail on missing current Alice `deny: [exec]`; revised owner suite passes 27/27. Registered completed-child followup passes in the complete pre-rebase run. | Completed-child followup passes in the complete registered flow on exact `2d641296db` in retry02. |
| Same-person cross-session steering | Isolated registered group→DM reproduction establishes source `exec` denial followed by incorrect `accepted` steer. Revised requester projection passes 9/9; harness authority 44/44. | Early- and late-policy cases, compatible controls, and cross-human queued input pass on exact `2d641296db` in retry02. |
| Private requester custody and display | Both history methods fail before repair and pass afterward (3/3 including control); pending custody 30/30, transcript 28/28, persisted transcript 27/27. | These are owner and registered-method checks, not a new live transport campaign. |
| Restart and queued launch | Missing legacy capture and two malformed capture cases demonstrably accepted before repair; revised queued-recovery suite passes 15/15. Operator recovery 28/28, runtime recovery 16/16, outbound-recovery sibling 44/44 pass. | Published v2026.10.3 general stored-data and native-queue seeds pass candidate Doctor and both recovery verifiers on exact `2d641296db`; limits below. |

The complete pre-rebase registered Gateway flow **passes** (`revision-clean-registered.log`), taking **89.58146 s command wall**. One shared Gateway test covers all eight scenario helpers with no filtered or skipped scenario. The earlier 50.62 s command (23.620 s test body) failed because cleanup supplied a parent config replacement path instead of the exact `.tools.deny` array path; its late-policy assertion could have been masked and its cross-human helper was not reached. That failure remains recorded. The corrected run preserves all assertions and closes those pre-rebase coverage gaps. It remains historical evidence; retry02 separately proves the integrated candidate.

Fixture failures were separated from product defects: unsupported table context, silent synthetic child completion, skipped channel configuration, a revoked shared plugin owner, runtime-context text misrouting, and mutation of an immutable-config cache key. The fixture now uses one Gateway test lifetime and strips internal context only when selecting scripted provider responses; actual provider payloads remain unchanged. No timeout, guard, expected behavior, or baseline was weakened.

On the same pre-rebase source, touched-file lint passes (60.072 s), core types pass (90.950 s), and supported executable runtime preparation passes (119.573 s); formatting/diff checks, target-input controls (20.138 s), spawn JSON storage (23.272 s), and operator JSON storage (25.221 s) also pass. The broader test-type command stopped at its first failing graph after 372.155 s: `operator-run-recovery.test.ts:88` passes deserialized `unknown` to the typed recovery API. Agents-root and agents-tools type graphs passed. The fixture now decodes with the existing `decodeQueuedOperatorRecoverySource` before invoking that API, without casts, weakened assertions, or a broader production API. The corrected selected recovery case passes **1/1, with 27 unrelated cases skipped**, in **18.115 s**; its `core-test-gateway-root` graph passes in **13.698 s**, lint in **16.740 s**, and formatting in **0.264 s** (`revision-fixture-decoder-results.json`). These correction results precede the mechanical rebase and are not a full owner-suite rerun. The subsequent amended source passes the focused checks and reviews below. Retry02 subsequently passes its full registered flow, both Doctor/recovery cells and MCP ABBA comparison. The remaining matched performance matrix is **INCOMPLETE**; subsequent CI disposition appears below. Original failing proofs and all command costs remain in the revision evidence; they are not latency benchmarks.

A four-size custody baseline measured ten reads at median/p95 0.573/0.717 ms (1 KiB), 5.108/5.979 ms (1 MiB), 46.244/73.635 ms (10 MiB), and 119.592/191.478 ms (25 MiB minus 4096 bytes), with seven samples per size. This identified repeated payload parsing. **Matched integrated-candidate custody/admission/steering performance against pinned main `46053391` remains PENDING**; no speedup, throughput guarantee, or absence of regression is claimed. Most config preparation and capability fingerprint work predates this PR.

### Integrated CI repairs and current checks

[CI for prior head `50efea5c0f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38493119460) executed merge `989587c4e55d7d0e09e47269e3acd31d34edefdd` against main `5d62810e3cb1403739f2b49b53e4cac4f4f3a3bb`. That workflow settled with **124 successful, 22 skipped, and seven failed jobs**, including its aggregate gate. Builds and all production/test type checks passed. The broader multi-workflow PR check rollup is a different denominator.

Five underlying PR failures have concrete local repairs. The recovery schema/decoder moved unchanged into its single codec owner, breaking the static type-import cycle; the canonical import-cycle guard passes (30.542 s). The source-owner inventory now includes its actual recovery-test consumer. Active-run fixtures now use the same real destination configuration at both admissions, and injection assertions match their respective private preparation/backend boundaries. No runtime policy guard, assertion outcome, timeout, or baseline was weakened.

The frozen repair source passes **150 tests across seven focused files**: sessions 34/34 (50.842 s), steering 7/7 (29.017 s), child coordination 23/23 (58.720 s), queue authority 8/8 (33.223 s), operator recovery 28/28 (77.296 s), queued recovery 15/15 (41.071 s), and source-owner inventory 35/35 (70.489 s). An initial repair replay failed one backend-options assertion because it expected private requester preparation at the wrong boundary; correcting it to the actual prepared fingerprint yields the complete 34/34 run. Original failure evidence remains retained.

Touched source/root-test lint passes (27.119/18.629 s), core types pass (101.351 s), and the three affected test graphs pass (342.456 s combined). Formatting and diff checks pass. The normal commit hook preserved the validated tree exactly. Fresh whole-PR review of `50efea5c0f` and the subsequent complete repair-diff review are scoped-clean; the final backend assertion correction also received independent review. These combined reviews cover the amended source, rather than representing the older whole-PR review as a review run on the new SHA.

The sixth underlying failure was independently red on main: its new worker-publication fixture lacked the documented mock-isolation annotation. Main now owns the [one-line correction in `4a8b9b5b1d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4a8b9b5b1d3de05cab119565873fd9129c738204). Its patch preserves the executable test and every assertion. A separately prepared equivalent annotation passed the exact failing guard and fresh review, with the original 13/13 behavior proof reused; that duplicate repair was not published. An export-preserving experiment added 10.174 s to the affected case without preserving an exercised export. The subsequent CI merge included that correction and its guard passed.

[CI for `1c4d341525`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38496653489) settled with **130 successful, 22 skipped, and two failed jobs** (154 total), on merge `38f74109169d9f05c05b2373c3cd5e836b021253` against main `fd1eeeb685b11c47dc5417d423ccc19b21d42570`. All five branch-origin failures now pass, together with builds, production/test types, architecture and mock guards. The sole underlying failure was the SDK surface guard; the second failure was its aggregate gate.

The SDK guard was independently red on that exact main revision: 3,759 public exports exceeded 3,758, and 2,194 callable exports exceeded 2,193. The exact counter correction passes the registered guard (7.108 s), owner suite (5 passed, one Linux-only skip; 10.056 s), lint/format and fresh review. Main now owns [the correction in `57547cb535`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/57547cb53547113a20efd7e019cc3e999410145b). Its executable bytes match the separately tested candidate; two explanatory comments differ. The owner attributes the missing count to async model-auth preparation; no predecessor-count experiment established which earlier change first exceeded the budget. Our duplicate was not published.

Current head `2d641296db` is a **metadata-only amendment** after that main correction, with exactly the same tree, parent and source bytes as `1c4d341525`. [Fresh merge-ref CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38497948329) completes **SUCCESS: 136 successful jobs, 22 skipped, zero failures**, executing merge `7604dfef83a92009d1f44c3170336b17c0dd66a4`. The actual Linux SDK suite passes all six cases, including the previously failing guard and compiler-lifetime case (20.839 s file time; 10.637 s lifetime case). This refresh follows the verified owning main fix; whole-PR churn and source-review applicability are unchanged.

Two selected passing CI logs provide 85 passing case rows across three of the 96 changed executable files: child coordination 23/23 (36.754 summed case-seconds), transcript persistence 27/27 (11.673), and source-owner inventory 35/35 (74.940). All 890 rows across their three shards reconcile to reported totals. These are whole-case durations, not file wall time or incremental PR cost. Other current-run costs remain unobserved in this bounded sample.

### Current-source Gateway, stored-state and MCP proof

[Retry02 Testbox workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38500305189), lease `tbx_01m4w37m1znm50mrm6ft6yfm58`, verified clean candidate `2d641296db` and the tree above before execution. Linux reported CPU affinity **2**, Node **24.19.0**, and pnpm **12.9.0**. Base `46053391`, pre-repair parent `18cdb607`, and candidate runtime builds all passed in separate detached worktrees. Missing original requester recovery capture refuses before agent dispatch and records a durable failed collector outcome with resubmission guidance. | Doctor 11.697 s; verifier 34.101 s |

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent turn on a node-hosted (file-transfer) workspace fails with `WorkspaceAccessUnavailableError: Remote workspace skill discovery failed` when the node's pairing changes while Skill discovery is in flight, for example when a node reconnects and its capability surface is auto-approved.

## User Impact

User impact: the first turn after a node (re)connect no longer dies on a transient pairing change. Read-only Skill discovery and Skill resource reads retry against the new pairing; revoked nodes, non-retryable errors and mutating Skill operations still fail closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`node.invoke` already answers an invoke whose pairing generation moved with `UNAVAILABLE`, `retryable: true`, `details.code: "PAIRING_CHANGED"`. The file-transfer adapter that owns the `workspace.skills` invocation passed that through, and the core `loadSkills` wrapper turns any failure into a fatal error. The adapter now re-runs its read-only operations on that exact error, with a bound of two re-runs; nothing under `src/` changes.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and design</summary>

Main's daily scheduled run "OpenClaw Scheduled Live And E2E Checks" ([run 38347856255](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347856255), [job "Repo E2E (Gateway 1/4)"](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347856255/job/115141602656), 2026-10-13) failed `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/required-native-same-session.e2e.test.ts`:

```
agent.wait: {"runId":"REQUIRED-NATIVE-0-A","status":"error","error":"WorkspaceAccessUnavailableError: Remote workspace skill discovery failed"}
```

It reproduced locally under load (3 parallel instances of that e2e on one Mac, 2 of 6 runs). In the failing runs the Gateway log shows the remote Skills watcher stopping with `GatewayClientRequestError: node pairing changed while invocation was active`. About 2 s later comes `security audit: node capability surface silent auto-approve node=... commands=dir.list,file.fetch,file.stat,workspace.memory,workspace.skills`, and about 1 s after that the first turn's `message dispatch completed ... outcome=error error="WorkspaceAccessUnavailableError: Remote workspace skill discovery failed"`. In passing runs the auto-approve line lands 20 to 50 s before the first turn.

The node pairing generation key covers the node token and the surface approval time. A reconnect can therefore advance it twice in quick succession: token rotation, then the capability-surface auto-approve in `connect-node-session.ts`. `node.invoke` re-checks the generation around the node work (`continuePairingWork`) and rejects the in-flight invoke via `respondPairingChanged`. That `GatewayClientRequestError` reaches the plugin unchanged through the service-owned `openNodeDuplex`. `createNodeWorkspaceSkills` is the only `loadSkills` provider. The core wrapper in `src/agents/workspace-access.ts` converts every `loadSkills` failure into a fatal `WorkspaceAccessUnavailableError`, so the turn died on a read-only discovery whose error said it was retryable.

`createNodeWorkspaceSkills` (`extensions/file-transfer/src/workspace-skills.ts`) now routes discovery, `readInstructions`, `resolveResource` and `readResources` through a small `read` helper. When the rejection is a retryable `PAIRING_CHANGED`, the helper re-runs the invoke at most twice, and `node.invoke` captures the fresh generation on each run. Two re-runs rather than one cover the token-then-approval pair seen in the failing log. Everything else is rethrown unchanged:

- **Non-retryable errors and aborts** fail immediately.
- **A revoked node** keeps answering `PAIRING_CHANGED` and fails once the bound is reached.
- **Mutating and long-lived operations** are not retried: dependency installs, Skill lifecycle (apply/remove/ClawHub), the watch subscription, and Memory.

The classifier reads `retryable` and `details.code` structurally via `asOptionalRecord`, keeping the heavy `gateway-runtime` SDK barrel out of this lazily loaded module.

Not changed here:

- **Placement code:** synchronous placement replica reads during pending ACK writes are handled in a separate PR.
- **Remote Skills watcher:** it is owned by `src/skills/runtime/refresh-remote.ts`. On failure it deregisters and bumps the Skills snapshot version, and the next Skills refresh re-creates it.

</details>

## Evidence

The regression is in the plugin's owner test, `extensions/file-transfer/src/workspace-service.test.ts`. It drives the real registered `file-transfer-workspaces` service and the same core-bound `getAgentWorkspaceAccess(...).loadSkills` entry a turn uses, with the real file-transfer policy and the real node-host Skills worker. Only the paired connection is emulated: the transport mimics `node.invoke`'s pairing-generation check, advancing the generation while the node streams the discovery reply and rejecting with the `respondPairingChanged` shape.

On the current `origin/main` implementation (same test):

```
× retries Skill discovery after an in-flight pairing change
  → Remote workspace skill discovery failed
  Caused by: GatewayClientRequestError: node pairing changed while invocation was active
× fails Skill discovery closed for a pairing that keeps changing
  → expected 1 to be 3
✓ fails Skill discovery closed for a non-retryable Gateway error
```

With the fix, all three pass (2, 3 and 1 node invocations respectively). `pnpm test extensions/file-transfer/src/workspace-service.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "Skill discovery (after an in-flight pairing change|closed for)"`: 99 s wall locally including runtime preparation; Vitest 15.2 s, about 3.7 s of test time for the three cases.

Also run locally: the full `workspace-service.test.ts` plus `workspace-skills.windows.test.ts` and `workspace-skill-lifecycle.test.ts` (41 passed); oxfmt and oxlint on the touched files (clean); `git diff --check` (clean). Gaps left to PR CI:

- **Memory tests:** 5 tests in `workspace-service.test.ts` that spawn the Memory worker child fail identically on unmodified `origin/main` in this local worktree ("Workspace worker exited with 1"). The Skills tests in the same file pass.
- **Typecheck:** the extensions test-project typecheck reports no errors in touched files. Its errors elsewhere come from local dependency drift (`@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.26.0 installed against 0.26.3 locked).
- **E2E:** the intermittent e2e was not re-run under load for this PR.

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs.   • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203

Updates `openai/codex-action` from 1.12 to 1.13
Changelog

Sourced from openai/codex-action's changelog.

codex-action Changelog

v1.13 (2026-10-05)

  • #183 preserve system service access when restricting runner sockets under Linux drop-sudo.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a native worktree chat losing its workspace binding and effective working directory after `/new`, `/reset`, or idle rollover, even though its checkout remains registered.

## User Impact

Conversation resets keep the chat in its native worktree, including its selected project, nested working directory, and unfinished files. Plain **New Chat** still deliberately leaves the old worktree. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worktree belongs to the logical session; resetting the conversation changes the conversation identity. The rollover owner now retains the four native workspace fields together. Repository-workspace carry remains implicit-rollover-only, and stale generic spawn lineage is still cleared.

This is the owner-approved reset-versus-New-Chat policy, now documented in the managed-worktrees guide. Follow-up to [#159506](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159506).

## Evidence

- Exact candidate `3fa373f849775f30a4a82f99926291342aa8ddc8`: all three regression cases passed with one worker; **27.64 seconds wall time**, including native worker preparation and cleanup.
- The fixture exercises real session creation, worktree preparation, committed session state, the ingress working-directory consumer, and disposable worker placement. It verifies the original checkout and unfinished file survive. This is owner-boundary and placement proof; it does not claim a live worker execution.
- Normal formatting/privacy hooks and fresh scoped review passed. Required broad checks, refreshed unchanged-sibling coverage, and actual hosted CI timings are pending the published head; no inherited-CI waiver is requested.
- Production: **+11 / -4 lines (net +7)**. Regression test: **127 lines**; test routing: 1 line; documentation: 2 lines.

prs.title: fix(database): account, approval, and usage writes hold the SQLite writer during host admission
prs.body:
Related: #169260, #169283

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: personal model-account connect/link/unlink, operator-approval decisions, and auth-profile usage writes hold the shared-state SQLite writer while waiting for the host's first live-authority grant, so a busy Gateway main thread makes concurrent writes time out with `database is locked`.

## User Impact

User impact: when the Gateway main thread is slow, account connect/link/unlink, approval resolve/consume, and credential usage writes no longer hold the shared writer while they wait for their first authority check, so Gateway cron and cleanup writes keep their normal 5 s budget.

Trigger requires the same coincidence as #169260: a low-frequency interactive write overlapping a main-thread stall longer than the 5 s busy timeout. No deadlock. This is the same defect class #169283 repaired for update-history writers; its follow-up list named four producer groups but not the writers fixed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

These writers requested their first `transaction`-stage grant after `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. The host answers admission on its event loop, so any main-thread delay became writer hold time. `docs/reference/database-schemas.md` already requires the initial host grant before `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. Mirroring #169283, these writers now take the first grant before entering the write transaction; rows are still reread inside the transaction and the commit-stage grant still revalidates authority immediately before COMMIT. The host treats the transaction stage purely as an authority check, so a grant followed by a failed BEGIN leaks nothing.

Scope: `src/state/user-model-accounts.ts` (update/connect/link/unlink), the shared `transact()` helper in `src/gateway/operator-approval-store.operations.ts` (all `operatorApprovals.*` operations, both worker and native variants), and `authProfiles.personalAccept`/`authProfiles.usage` in `src/agents/auth-profiles/store.worker.ts`. Remaining producers (#169283's listed follow-ups such as `writeAdmitted`, plus `sqlite-wal`/upload-store/session-accessor sites) are unchanged and stay as follow-up; a shared move of the initial grant into one owner would cover them.

No config, schema, timeout, retention, protocol, or update-behavior changes.

## Evidence

Contention probes copied from `src/infra/update-run-contention.test.ts` (a competing connection attempts `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` while the host decides each admission stage; free means the writer lock was not held).

### Before fix

With the touched source files reverted to `origin/main`, the five new probes all fail:

```text
× leaves the writer free while the host decides credential update admission
× leaves the writer free while the host decides account connect admission
× leaves the writer free while the host decides link selection admission
× leaves the writer free while the host decides unlink selection admission
AssertionError: expected [ 'transaction:held', 'commit:held' ] to deeply equal [ 'transaction:free', 'commit:held' ]

FAIL leaves the writer free while the host decides approval admission
AssertionError: expected [ 'transaction:held', 'commit:held' ] to deeply equal [ 'transaction:free', 'commit:held' ]
```

### After fix

- New probes pass: `src/state/user-model-accounts-contention.test.ts` 4/4 (native path, one per edited writer), `src/gateway/operator-approval-store.worker.test.ts` 8/8 including the worker probe.
- Regression suites: `src/state/user-model-accounts.test.ts` 26/26, `src/gateway/model-account-connect.worker.test.ts` 13/13 (including the `["compare","transaction","commit"]` stage-order assertion), `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-personal.worker.test.ts` 12/12.
- Targeted typecheck: `tsconfig.core.json` incremental plus the `state-logging` and `gateway-root` core-test shards; the error set is byte-identical to the untouched baseline (31 pre-existing host-environment errors, 0 new).
- `oxlint` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean, `git diff --check` clean.
- Test cost: `pnpm test src/state/user-model-accounts-contention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 75.65 s wall (4 cases at 200-380 ms each); `pnpm test src/gateway/operator-approval-store.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` ~45 s wall.

Not covered: `authProfiles.personalAccept`/`usage` have no dedicated held/free probe (worker-only path; the existing oauth-personal behavior suite covers them), and the remaining first-grant-inside-BEGIN producers listed above are intentionally out of scope.

prs.body:
Closes #158816

## What Problem This Solves

Malformed installed SKILL.md files disappear from inventories without an explanation. Operators need the rejected file path and loading error, including when querying the running Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bounded diagnostic facts follow main's canonical source reader, worker-owned discovery snapshots, local/remote preparation and skills.status response. Diagnostic changes participate in the worker fingerprint: warning changes or removal publish a new inventory revision even when valid entries stay unchanged. Source precedence, host authority, Library preparation, file limits and CLI sanitization remain intact.

Current head `7ac5d439e8227183c885fabd9e4f5637c9110fee` integrates official main `3d385d4f74237055952758d1c83d9f1f49542b94` to resolve actual conflicts and follow its new discovery owner. Main's obsolete verified root cache, watcher-reuse test and startup skill prewarm stay removed. Bundle diagnostics live in the canonical private reader; the superseded exported helper is removed. The synchronous SDK inventory retains its established contract; async preparation keeps main's prepared facts and does not rediscover synchronously on the Gateway thread. Retired Curator interfaces are not restored.

## User Impact

`skills list`, `info` and `check` show load warnings in text and JSON. Bad files remain excluded, valid siblings remain available, and warnings update/clear when main's normal refresh publishes new facts. Passive on-disk refresh follows main's roughly one-minute policy; explicit owner actions retain their immediate refresh behavior. Responses retain at most 64 diagnostics plus an omitted count, with bounded paths/messages. No configuration, persisted-data migration, dependency or permission change is added.

## Evidence

- Current source integration: fresh canonical shared AutoReview of the final committed branch found no actionable P0-P2 findings (confidence 0.86), with source consistency verified; pinned-main `git diff --check` passed. The first review found an outdated status-repair fixture; it now awaits the actual `refreshSkillsDiscovery` operation and settles fixture discovery before path cleanup. Fresh new-head runtime/type/lint/build acceptance remains pending in secretless CI. No local fork execution, CI rerun, empty commit, assertion relaxation, timeout increase or paid test allocation was used.
- Formatting-only follow-up: prior `60c64838d340e51749dd92c70365bd55d1a79beb` [CI 38499612314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38499612314) failed its `check-docs` job on two TypeScript formatting differences; documentation content/config/link checks passed. The two files were formatted and checked with the exact official pinned oxfmt 0.71.0 and unchanged official configuration (scoped checks 62 ms / 56 ms). The diff only wraps arrays and orders pure imports; diagnostic logic and assertions are unchanged, so the final source review at 60c648 is reused for this mechanical change. Fresh CI remains pending.
- One real-worker regression through existing `prepareLocalSkillSources` fixtures checks missing-description → unterminated-frontmatter warning → removal with the valid sibling unchanged, cached facts before the fake minute boundary, refreshed facts and real watch notifications/revisions afterward. Older tests bound to the retired root-cache implementation are removed in favor of this canonical boundary. Fresh single-worker wall time, baseline execution and CI seconds have not yet been measured.
- **Actual prior-head CI failures:** [CI 38111419145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38111419145) on `83be4d015376cf87e92f869ae4cb4d4f231c6aa2` ended with 42 successful jobs, 27 skipped and 3 failed. The lint failure was our leftover unused `writeWorkspaceSkills` import after test pruning. Current main's legitimate passive-cache test uses that helper; this integration retains it and retires old mocks/tests. The source-contract failure was duplicate exported `intro`/`outro` in Configure and Doctor; official `3f08ea94a3373110e46b8f18cc4790344af4ecb3` renames Doctor exports and migrates callers, and is included here. The CI gate was dependent. Informational alias listings were not the root cause. The actual tested merge `035685675b93276f75d1168015052f4c6508ac0d` was verified to have parents `310bce6a751791a9f61ce7a3bfcb3fd79653642b` and this prior head. No current fix is called passing until new CI completes.
- **Prior passing evidence retains its head:** `fbe503562f6a18e0affca252effe1a92d789706f` [CI 38012019091](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38012019091) passed 45 jobs/27 skipped, CodeQL and gate; earlier `2ee6c6e` CI37899979807 passed 44/27 skipped. Reviews 17–19 found no actionable introduced defect and accepted source-supported reuse of the earlier real-path proof; they do not verify today's changed worker integration.
- `fc30172d141771446fa2c4f98a757188528e03c8` passed 77 relevant cases, production types, scoped lint/format and all 27 selected test-type groups. Its real authenticated Gateway/CLI probe passed in 98.75 s for exact file paths/errors, valid siblings, repair/removal, 64 records plus omitted: 1 and explicit-target disconnect refusal. It included the since-retired Curator command; list/info/check are the current surfaces. This is historical evidence, not a new-head runtime run.

Known limits: the CLI's existing 1.5 s deadline and inventory latency are outside this change. Current worker-source/runtime proof, build/type/lint acceptance and test cost remain pending; older synchronous-owner proof is not relabeled as today's acceptance.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves
A Slack agent serving several private customer channels needs to recall sibling threads without opening every conversation belonging to the agent.

## User Impact
Operators can opt into `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` to allow verified same-agent, same-channel session access while excluding other channels. Defaults and existing visibility modes are unchanged; thread sessions stay separate and recall is on demand, not automatic prompt injection.

This is **not a complete multi-tenant sandbox**: shared memory files, filesystem access, message-plugin history tools, external integrations and already-mixed transcripts need their own boundaries. Missing route facts deny cross-session access. Archived memory transcript hits are conservatively excluded. No production deployment or live Slack test was performed.

## Why This Change Was Made
The existing visibility decision owner already serves history, list, search, send and status. This extends that owner rather than introducing a second memory system or provider-specific policy in core.

- Compare trusted stored provider, explicit account, opaque destination, chat kind and workspace/space. Thread IDs are not part of the channel comparison; arbitrary peer IDs are not split to infer authority.
- Require the same agent; main aliases, spawned ownership, A2A permission and scoped grants cannot widen the new boundary. DM/main callers remain self-only.
- Prepare requester metadata once for list/search and filter candidates before returning metadata or reading snippets. Direct access uses exact owner-qualified descriptions and propagates the described session incarnation into the existing lifecycle fence.
- Apply the same policy to memory transcript hits, reject conflicting transcript aliases, and keep the default sandbox spawned clamp from widening `channel` to `tree`.
- No new storage, migrations, background jobs or model calls. Channel-only overhead is one requester metadata read for inventory/search, or two exact metadata reads for a direct cross-session access; unchanged modes do not incur these reads.

## Evidence
- Focused shared-policy, history, list, search, access and memory suites: **233 tests passed** (initial 6-file run, 4 shards, 46.09 seconds wall with `--maxWorkers=1`). The list regression was subsequently moved into its own small file to satisfy the repository line-cap guard.
- Final targeted recheck: **58 tests passed** across the policy suite and the extracted list regression (16.23 seconds wall). `pnpm check:changed` passed, including core/extension/test typechecks, SDK exports/surface/boundary checks, changed-file lint, config docs, dead exports and import cycles. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent native Codex review: no actionable P1/P2 findings. The repository `autoreview` helper was also invoked, but its separate CLI account could not access its configured review models; it did not produce a review, so the independent native review was used instead.
- Mock-Gateway tests exercise actual session tool entry points; they verify that another channel's history is never read and its metadata/snippets are not returned. SDK cases cover account/workspace/provider/agent mismatches, main/DM, malformed or missing facts, opaque peer IDs, incognito, scoped grants and sandbox clamps. Memory proof includes conflicting aliases and archived-hit denial.
- No live customer or Slack traffic, production config change, broad benchmark, or production deployment. CI timing is not available at submission; no workflow dispatch or rerun requested.


## 2026-10-10 refresh and after-fix proof

- Refreshed with current `main` by a normal merge at exact head `9b99db182f547aba65f3edfef8e9fd2d376ae932`; no force push. The search path now re-authorizes each channel-scoped candidate immediately before `sessions.search` and uses the exact session incarnation fence when available.
- Focused session visibility/search/history/memory suites: **141 tests passed**. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed all changed-file typechecks, SDK/boundary/config checks, lint, dead-code and cycle checks. Full `pnpm build` passed; its advisory Control UI startup gzip budget message was unchanged outside this backend patch.
- Isolated after-fix behavior proof used the built package at this exact head, an actual child Gateway process, canonical SQLite session storage, the model-facing `sessions_search` tool, and synthetic Slack-shaped routes/transcripts. No production Gateway/config, customer data, live Slack, or model call was used.
- Result: the requester and a same-agent/same-provider/same-account/same-channel/same-workspace sibling were searched and returned. Other-channel, other-account, and other-workspace markers were excluded, and no `sessions.search` call was issued for those targets.
- Fresh-authority result: after inventory, the sibling route projected by the host was changed while preserving its session ID; the new pre-I/O authorization rejected it, no sibling `sessions.search` call was issued, and only the requester result returned. This reassignment step was a controlled host-projection injection around the real Gateway call; the surrounding inventory, persistence, tool execution, and transcript search were real isolated runtime paths.

The remaining question is the maintainer-owned product/SDK contract: retrieval-only versus also permitting sibling send/status through the shared visibility owner.




<!-- shannon-followup-2026-10-11 -->
## 2026-10-11 exact-head security follow-up

- Integrated current main with a normal merge and published exact head ba0fe780e129dc2a4b3bf4ccc09f07f1a0b37306; no force push.
- Restored memory privacy ordering so archived-session inventory completes before the channel visibility catalog is read. The existing direct-to-group reset-recall regression now passes again.
- Channel-scoped search, history, send, status, and patch effects now re-read requester/target route facts and re-authorize at the final writer-ordered admission boundary. A preserved session ID no longer preserves stale channel authority after route reassignment.
- Added two explicit regressions: same-ID target reassignment after description is denied before transcript I/O, and a route change between initial and final scoped admission is denied before the effect callback.
- Focused result: 60 existing/new search, history, memory, and visibility tests passed; the final scoped-admission suite then passed 2/2 after its added regression.
- Changed-file checks passed conflict, line/max-line, SQLite, format, config/docs, SDK/boundary, core/extension/test typechecks, deprecation, and import guards. The only check:changed failure was the full-tree dead-export scan for GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2 and reconnectGateway, both in files untouched by this PR.
- Proof boundary: these are isolated exact-head source/SQLite/tool tests. No production Gateway/config, customer data, live Slack, or model call was used in this follow-up. The prior isolated Gateway proof remains scoped to its recorded old head and is not relabeled as current-head runtime proof.

The product/SDK choice remains maintainer-owned: retrieval-only, or permitting sibling send/status through this shared visibility owner.

<!-- shannon-followup-2026-10-14 -->
## 2026-10-14 exact-head review repair

- Merged current upstream main normally and published exact head `aa71886b6d05b535299459843c83001e0f845bd0`; no force push.
- Final `sessions_list` serialization now runs inside the current owner-held authorization read after asynchronous channel preparation, preserving reader, lifecycle, store, and physical-session checks at emission.
- Channel visibility is now retrieval-only: same-channel sibling `send` and `status` are denied, including `session_status` model mutations, while self-session behavior remains available.
- Focused policy/list/search/access tests passed (96 tests); core and extension typechecks, config-doc baseline, plugin assets, formatting, lint, boundaries, and other changed-file lanes passed. The sole `check:changed` failure was the Plugin SDK surface budget (3759 exports / 2194 callables), reproduced identically on upstream main `d1f7bc91f81f1099c461e842c8e2f7078af7e737` and not introduced by this PR.
- The canonical autoreview helper was attempted, but its configured review models were unavailable before producing a report; no clean-review claim is made.
- Proof boundary: exact-head local source/tool/typecheck evidence with synthetic routes. No production Gateway/config, customer data, live Slack, or model call was used. A fresh inspectable actual-Gateway/stable-upgrade proof and the maintainer product/SDK acceptance remain separate before-merge items.

prs.title: fix: native-app sessions fail to resume after restart
prs.body:
## Current maintainer contribution

Reviewed candidate: **`88e776d1286de82b8052ab39b31e26dcfbdc8d47`**, tree `d69623250560981f17bc50258b0064abbc669fd3`, with unchanged production from reviewed parent `bb34a01a7cc312068ddaec9ca257bc450db55b3f`; original contribution tested against main `46053391a1ad842d290563c38ca17b6aeb1d1a46`.

Jacqueline Henriksen's original commits remain in the ancestry through `8581ef5701c1ad70990a4ad5ab352312ef0a64eb`. The contribution integrates that fix with the tested main and strengthens its real permission/effect-boundary regressions. The prepared-requester-policy production repair is already upstream in `3b01cee14cfeb14080d5927340355206e5990936`; the remaining production delta is eleven lines in the native restart-recovery classifier.

An interrupted, authenticated native-app task with a surviving host-captured source must reach the existing authority restorer even when its historical transcript lacks human provenance. The retained source must exactly match the original run, agent, session key, incarnation, and lifecycle. Current device, authentication, role, grants, revocation, and original permission ceilings remain enforced by the existing restoration and commit owners. Source-less delegated input and detached cron input gain no authority. No schema, configuration, credential, or intentional permission change is introduced.

### Retained production evidence from reviewed parent `bb34a01a`

- **RED on main's production classifier:** native original input and native steering both skip recovery; both deferred initialization-pending replay controls pass.
- **Completed focused run: 56/56 pass**, exit 0, 159.42 seconds: nine native cold-state recovery cases, seventeen real creator-transport cases, twenty startup-admission cases, and ten search preparation cases.
- The native tests release the original capability, close private SQLite handles, replace the lifecycle generation and Gateway context, restore the persisted source, and invoke the production automation tool through the real Gateway/Cron commit owner. Allowed continuations persist one job; unowned/detached/mismatched sources and revoked device/role controls persist none.
- A held native Cron write also rejects device-token rotation, role downgrade, access-grant revocation, and claim retirement without adding a second job. All 26 existing restoration-owner cases passed.
- All 161 store-file cases emitted PASS, including seven exact-binding controls, but their larger batch hit its 360-second executor budget. **That aggregate is partial evidence, not a completed whole-suite pass.** The remaining focused files completed in the 56-test run. No test timeout/retry was increased.
- Seven selected type graphs passed, including commands; the final affected gateway-server graph was rechecked. Scoped lint, formatting, whitespace, and outgoing-content checks passed. All six touched test/helper files received whole-file audits.
- Independent API-key review of this exact head found **no actionable P0–P2 findings**.

The earlier `8581ef57` commands export error and deferred-startup timeout remain unclassified, not asserted to be inherited failures or CPU flakes. Current local commands/admission checks pass without an unrelated production patch; remote checks must evaluate the newly published head before landing.

### Exact-head CI follow-through: `88e776d1`

The published parent's CI exposed a terminal-redelivery fixture calling synchronous authorization without prepared session facts; it failed with `UNAVAILABLE` before reaching terminal-replay behavior. The same failure reproduced with the original main recovery classifier restored through an isolated loader (a classifier control, not a complete fresh-main runtime run). This one-file follow-up uses the existing asynchronous authorization preparation and releases retained authority in `finally`. Production code and all terminal-replay assertions are unchanged; current-authority checks remain real.

- Final complete affected `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`: **232/232 passed**, exit 0, 115.87 seconds. Scoped lint, formatting and diff checks passed.
- The entire 643-line touched admission helper and all eleven distinct cases were audited, including imports, fixture/setup/cleanup, real authority lifetime and failure paths. No warranted pruning, weaker assertions, added skips, or timeout/retry increases.
- Affected messaging type graph exit 0 is producer-recorded; its log is empty and is not independently rerun proof. The prior seven type graphs remain separately attributed above.
- Required independent manual/security and API-key-only delta review verified exact head/tree versus `bb34a01a`, found no actionable P0–P2 findings, and inspected the actual complete E2E/lint logs and full helper. The prior production review is reused only for unchanged production bytes.
- Parent security review passed on attempt 2 after correcting stale comparison metadata (8,219 claimed files versus the actual eight-file comparison); that prior-head success is not new-head CI. Fresh exact-head CI run `38499237380` and Security Review `38499231509` both completed successfully on attempt 1. The automatic post-CI refresh `38500247475` also succeeded and set `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review and security-sensitive review to **success** at 02:18 UTC on October 14, 2026. No old run was blindly rerun.
- ClawSweeper completed review of exact head `88e776d1286de82b8052ab39b31e26dcfbdc8d47` at 02:15:57 UTC on October 14, 2026: **zero findings, ready for maintainer review**, proof sufficient, 5/6. Its remaining `needs-human` / `not_opted_in` marker is a maintainer-review boundary, not a code defect or permission to merge. The review comment predates the final green CI gate.
- All runtime proof retained task-private SQLite, including children. Temporary compiler compatibility artifacts/caches were removed and canonical dependency links restored. No live-service, auth/config, database, merge or deployment action.

### Scope and evidence limits

These new observations are **in-process cold-state reconstruction**, not an OS-process kill, real-provider execution, signed wire-handshake, or live-service test. Provider/preflight collaborators are isolated; authority restoration and the durable Cron effect owner are real. All runtime proof used task-private SQLite, including spawned Node processes. The author's prior-head real Gateway kill/write proof below is separately attributed and was not repeated by this contribution.

Fresh main `4a8b9b5b1d3de05cab119565873fd9129c738204` was checked on October 13 at 19:21 MDT: the native classifier, source-capture and authority-restoration owners are unchanged from the tested base. The full later-main runtime was not locally rerun. This PR is a narrow native cold-restart fix, **not proof of every broader requester/session continuation contract**. No merge or live deployment is requested here.

---

## Original author's prior-head implementation and production proof

The following original evidence refers to its explicitly named historical heads, not the new candidate:

## What Problem This Solves

Authenticated native-app conversations could be marked failed after a Gateway restart despite retaining their original operator source. After fixing that admission, production recovery exposed a second failure: the missing-web-search guidance callback re-read session capability metadata after its worker preparation scope had ended, aborting tool construction before the resumed turn could execute.

Eligible native turns now resume in the same session under the original operator's current authority. The callback reuses the requester policy the turn already prepared. Already-terminal sessions still require explicit recovery. No schema, credential, role, configuration, or intentional permission change is included.

## Implementation

Recovery admits only the exact saved source run, agent, session key, session ID, and lifecycle revision, then delegates identity, device, authentication, role, grants, and revocation to the existing restoration owner. Unowned and mismatched internal input remains refused.

The merge with main `2bd6ca195418` retains #170252's browser/channel steering predicate unchanged. Follow-up `8581ef5701c1` passes `runtimeCapabilityProfile.policy` through the existing `preparedRequesterPolicy` argument in the embedded attempt's web-search callback. It adds no new policy owner, asynchronous execution replay, main-thread SQL, or guard bypass. The same omission remains in pinned main `33a438a7624d`.

## Evidence

- Unchanged `5804c062c649` reproduced the production preparation failure. A separate unchanged-build Inspector diagnostic captured the exact escape: `onWebSearchConfiguration` → native web-search routing → requester-policy resolution → unprepared lookup of the recovering session. Inspector was absent from the final proof.
- The persisted-dashboard regression fails before the fix at that exact callback: two intended failures, seven controls passing. With the repair, all nine cases pass, including native search, configured/disabled search, inherited dashboard denial, attribution cancellation, and permission rebuild/reset. Full file wrapper wall time: 41.42 seconds; approximately 2.9 seconds of test execution, with compiler/import preparation dominating. The fixture uses real SQLite metadata and worker preparation; only the existing coding-tool factory is mocked to invoke the real callback.
- All 18 native-search sibling cases pass (59.24 seconds wrapper wall time). Production types, the affected test typecheck shard, targeted typed lint, formatting, whitespace, line-growth and maximum-line checks pass.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P0–P2. The prior 17 combined native/browser/channel/refusal/composition cases passed at `5804c062c649`; their recovery guard is unchanged by this follow-up. These remain prior-head evidence, distinct from the exact-head production run below.
- The supported `sourcePerformance` runtime build passes in 75.18 seconds. Build identity: `2026.10.2-8581ef5701c1-2026-10-13T04-12-22.351Z`. Separate type checks cover affected production/test sources; public package declaration publication is not claimed. Exact-head CI seconds/results are pending.

## Exact-head production recovery and authority proof

Commit `8581ef5701c1ad70990a4ad5ab352312ef0a64eb`, isolated real Gateway, signed `MACOS_APP`/`UI` protocol client and its exact issued device token. Production `chat.send` captured custody for three synthetic sessions. Original Gateway PID 14537 was cold-killed (exit -9); successor PID 14668 automatically recovered eligible turns without another user turn or Resume action.

| Control | Same session | Actual production effect | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exact retained native source | Yes | Exactly one real `write`; sentinel exists | done; no active run |
| Device revoked after recovery admission | Yes | No write result or sentinel | killed; no active run |
| Delegated input without source custody | Yes | No recovery provider request or sentinel | refused with `delegated_authority_unavailable`; failed/inactive |

The allowed continuation completed before public `device.token.revoke` revoked the original native device. The revoked sibling had already entered its recovery model request. Releasing an offered write after revocation caused production owner cancellation before the offered tool call was consumed. Strict checks observed zero production fallback attempts, zero fallback HTTP requests, zero provider errors, and six total provider requests: three originals, two allowed recovery requests (write and final text), and one revoked recovery request.

Selected redacted runtime observations, October 12, 2026, Pacific:

```text
21:14:32.495 marked 3 startup-orphaned main session(s) for restart recovery
allowed: decision=started reason=dispatch_started
revoked: decision=started reason=dispatch_started
unowned: decision=blocked reason=delegated_authority_unavailable
21:14:35.258 device token revoked device=<synthetic-native-device> role=operator
21:14:35.267 [model-fetch] aborted name=AbortError code=OPENCLAW_DIRECT_ABORT
21:14:35.287 lane task error: Restart recovery operator authority changed; start a new user turn.
```

Artifact identities:

- Callback source SHA-256: `6e7b69133aa3fbf9f2f46fce6c23998de8d99d2dbfe4df465179d1c8a7696fd3`; compiled callback `dist/builtin-openclaw-Bgs0gAjQ.mjs`: `3f68e3913525f93c36ecae91c6f5731a3a696c1a861f475e7cf01c0859068674`.
- Recovery-store source: `8f4048720a346b97759943c964580986f75b752732cf558ec50607f744f8eaae`; compiled recovery chunk: `306759f468082ba43d83a7fc93e7cbf13e06b3adbe9bff8f0eeb54e3bc0e4150`.

## Proof scope and limits

Authentication, source capture/restoration, SQLite persistence, startup recovery, embedded OpenClaw execution, provider transport, and the filesystem write tool are production code. The HTTP provider is synthetic; the signed native protocol client is not the Mac UI app. Current `chat.send` supplies external-user provenance, so stopped isolated transcripts reconstruct historical native missing-provenance data. The unowned control has delegated provenance and custody removed. Recorded before/after comparisons show all 30 capability projection facts unchanged and the allowed/revoked native source records retained exactly. No authorization or agent-service mock is involved.

Revocation cancels the admitted turn while its provider response is held; this proves cancellation prevents the offered write, not an independently paused write-specific boundary. An ordinary public profile refresh and single session-create retry was needed during fixture startup, after confirming no partial session existed; no independent profile bug is claimed. No exact-head subprocess red/green baseline is claimed beyond the separately recorded pre-fix failure and regression.

All proof-owned Gateway/client processes and temporary sleep-prevention helpers were joined and independently confirmed absent. Workboard was disabled; its build-generated asset-digest manifest is preserved locally and excluded from the PR. The operator Gateway, existing patches, UI source, config/state and external accounts were untouched by these checks. Earlier backport proof and recovery evidence remain preserved separately.
