prs.title: feat(labs): add experimental Advisor that steers agents off avoidable work
prs.body:
Built on #170146 (`forkSession`), #170152 (`steerActiveRun`) and #171307 (hooks and services share `api.runContext`), all on `main`. Related: #169558.

## What Problem This Solves

Agents sometimes spend turns on work nobody asked for, repeat failing or stalled tool calls, or report results the tools do not support. Nothing notices until the user does.

## User Impact

Operators can turn on **Settings → Agents & Tools → Labs → Advisor** (default off). While the agent works, Advisor reviews the conversation every few tool calls or minutes, on the session's own model. If it finds avoidable work, it steers the running turn with one short correction, or queues the correction for the next turn when steering is unavailable. Otherwise nothing happens. It never runs tools, delays, stops or approves anything. **Configure** beside the switch opens the plugin settings page:
- `everyToolCalls` (default 10) and `everyMinutes` (default 20); `0` turns a trigger off.
- **Review instructions** (`reviewInstructions`, optional, at most 4,000 characters): edits what Advisor looks for and when it stays quiet. A blank field uses the evaluated built-in guidance, which is shown as placeholder text. Changes apply on the next review without a restart. The output format, the safety rules and the verify step stay fixed, so custom guidance cannot bypass fail-closed parsing or verification. Custom guidance is not covered by the evaluation below.

## Why This Change Was Made

A default-off bundled plugin (`advisor`) built only on public SDK seams:
- **Admission:** the history-free `before_agent_reply` hook (`eligibleTriggers: ["user"]`) records each user-triggered run in `api.runContext` and never claims the turn. Advisor does not subscribe to `llm_input`, `agent_end` or `after_tool_call`, because subscribing makes the host copy the conversation history or tool results on every turn.
- **Trigger:** the plugin service's single subscription to the agent-event stream counts `tool` starts, so stalled and backgrounded commands count too. It uses `phases: ["start", "end", "error"]` (#171534), so the host never clones tool results or partial updates for Advisor. Run timing starts at the lifecycle start event, and end and error events close the run. All controller state lives in the service. In a live Gateway, agent hooks and the service are separate registrations of the plugin, so they cannot share in-memory state. #171307 lets the hook write run context so the service can read it.
- **Review, stage 1:** `api.runtime.subagent.forkSession` runs on the plugin service scheduler. The review sees the full live context at cached-input prices and runs no tools. The reply's first line must be `NO_CHANGE` or `CORRECTION`.
- **Verify, stage 2:** runs only after a `CORRECTION`. A second fork of the same cached context checks the draft against the conversation. The problem must be shown by tool results or user messages, not by pending work. The advice must keep every user requirement (prohibitions, scope, ordering, timing, environment), and its next step must be cheaper and still complete the request. The fork replies `APPROVE` (with the final text) or `REJECT`.
- **Fail closed:** both replies are parsed structurally. A malformed reply, a reserved decision word inside the body, a timeout or an error means no steering. The warning is bounded and content-free; it never contains model or provider text.
- **Delivery:** `api.session.workflow.steerActiveRun`, falling back to `enqueueNextTurnInjection` (24 h TTL).
- One review in flight per session, covering both stages under one deadline. Reviews are cancelled on reset, disable and service stop. The interval counter restarts when a review finishes. Tool events from channel runs, which carry no `sessionKey`, are routed through the admitted run's key.

An earlier version reviewed a bounded text excerpt with a separately configured model. In a real-API evaluation it made 2 false corrections in 5 runs: it misread polled background commands as extra launches. The full-context fork made none, so the excerpt reviewer and the model setting were removed.

Settings UI: a new generic, optional `multiline` hint in plugin manifest `uiHints` (manifest types, normalizer, and an additive optional field in the Gateway protocol config schema) renders a string field as a textarea in the existing config form. Fields without the hint render exactly as before. Advisor is its first user.

Labs: **Configure** follows the settings-row control slot (a ghost action beside the switch), through a new optional `actions` slot on `SettingsToggleRow`. The shared toggle-row click handler now ignores clicks on links, buttons and fields. Before, clicking a Labs "Documentation" link also toggled the lab; a regression test fails on the old handler.

## Evidence

Labs before (current `main`, no Advisor row):

![Labs before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d5234db-8b6f-43b9-aec4-d32db7e6ca0a)

Labs after, with Advisor enabled:

![Labs after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc894ba5-30e6-407b-8296-51c57e8a07e5)

Plugin settings page opened by **Configure**, with the multiline **Review instructions** field:

![Advisor plugin settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/549bc02c-54c7-419e-98c4-3bccb7911843)

Ordinary-turn overhead, with Advisor enabled and no review due. Clones were counted per call site with an instrumented `structuredClone` across 10 real Gateway turns per workload, in a pinned Linux container (mock provider). The table shows serialized bytes the host clones for Advisor per turn:

| Workload | Before this change (`llm_input` + unfiltered events) | This PR | Advisor disabled |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Short turn | 2,988 | 1,375 | 0 |
| 200 KiB history | 209,377 | 1,380 | 0 |
| 1 MiB history | 1,053,153 | 1,380 | 0 |
| 5 tools × 256 KiB results | 1,326,523 | 2,899 | 0 |

Hot-path CPU, measured as interleaved microbenchmarks (median per turn): the history copy at 1 MiB costs 0.28 ms before and 0 ms now; the event dispatch on a tool-heavy turn costs 0.90 ms before and 0.14 ms now. Latency on whole turns was not resolvable on the shared host: block drift reached 35%. That pilot is recorded as exploratory and makes no p95 claim. A review itself (two forks at most) runs only when a trigger fires.

Review-decision evaluation, real APIs. Each scenario's conversation is replayed in the provider's native format (tool calls, tool results, tool schemas with `tool_choice: none`), with the review message appended, as the fork sends it. Corrections were graded by a model judge with a written rubric: evidence, a cheaper step that still completes the request, user instructions kept, at most 120 words. Final numbers come from a **blind holdout**: 40 new scenarios written by a separate agent that never saw the prompt, frozen before the run, 3 runs per model.

| Model | Variant | False corrections | Recall | Correction quality |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpt-5.6-luna` | single pass | 3/60 | 60/60 | 87.3% |
| `gpt-5.6-luna` | **with verify step** | **0/60** | 60/60 | **95.0%** |
| `gpt-6.1-sol` (Codex default) | with verify step | 0/60 | 60/60 | 95.0% |
| `claude-sonnet-5-5` | with verify step | 3/60 (one scenario) | 60/60 | 84.1% |

The original prompt corrected 9–16 of 24 legitimate runs per model on the first scenario set. Its live failure: told an agent to run a requested wait loop in parallel. The verify step costs about 1.4–2.1 s and well under a cent, and it runs only when stage 1 proposes a correction.

Live on this branch (isolated Gateway, Codex and built-in luna, review every 3 tool calls):
- **Requested polling** (8 checks, 2 s apart): Codex reviewed 4 times, `NO_CHANGE` each time (4.2–5.3 s, about 15–16k cached tokens, input 75). Luna drafted 2 corrections; stage 2 rejected both. No steering, and every requested check ran.
- **Search task:** both agents broadened the search after one miss, so there was no waste to correct. Codex said `NO_CHANGE`; luna drafted a correction and stage 2 rejected it.
- **Steering delivery:** shown live on an earlier head of this branch (luna, `steered: true`, guidance in the next provider request, the agent changed course). On this head, the approve-then-steer path is covered by the tests below.

Known limits:
- `claude-sonnet-5-5` falsely corrects one hard negative scenario in all 3 runs, and its correction quality is below 95%.
- On Codex with a restricted tool profile (for example `tools.profile: coding`), the existing `/btw` native-tool rule refuses forks, so Advisor cannot review those sessions. It logs the refusal once per review interval.

Tests:
- Plugin: 46 tests. The default guidance composes to the byte-identical evaluated prompt; custom guidance replaces only the guidance part; whitespace-only means default; the verify message is unaffected; config edits apply on the next review. Earlier coverage: through the real plugin API surface. They cover: hook and service as separate registrations; channel tool events without `sessionKey`; approve then steer and the next-turn fallback; reject, malformed, conflicting-token, empty and timed-out stage 1 or 2 replies, each with zero deliveries and one bounded, content-free warning; the interval restarting after a slow or failed review; cancellation on reset, disable and stop.
- Config form: the textarea renders and edits save for `multiline` fields; manifest hint normalization is tested.
- Labs page: 65 tests, covering on/off writes, the Configure link and in-app navigation under a base path, and no toggle on link click.

**Merge danger:** two-way door; default off. A revert removes the plugin, its Labs row and the Configure link. A saved `plugins.entries.advisor` entry would remain in config.

prs.title: docs(workers): describe fail-closed placement read preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The worker-access storage reference promised that placement read preparation joins an overlapping placement publication and rereads fresh facts, so a preceding turn finishing or setup advancing could never reject the next turn. That has not been true since the simplification in #168747; the docs described machinery that no longer exists.

## User Impact

No runtime change. Readers of the database reference now get the actual contract: placement read preparation fails closed with `Session <id> placement authority changed` when a same-session placement publication lands during the read, and the rejected request is not retried automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two paths were possible: restore a minimal join-and-reread in `preparePlacementRead`, or correct the docs. I chose the docs, for three reasons.

1. **The fail-closed behavior was a deliberate maintainer decision, not an accident.** #165166 added the settlement-listener loop on Oct 4. One week later #168747 removed it under the explicit best-effort policy, and listed this exact case in its accepted tradeoffs: an ordinary placement read racing a mutation may report authority changed rather than loop through settlement notifications. The docs paragraph was the only piece not updated.
2. **I could not find a real failing flow.** The production incident behind #165166 was the initial-setup runtime-preference race. 7ecc80a45736 fixed that by making runtime selection a tolerant preference read, and it still is one: `resolveWorkerPlacementRuntimeOverride` uses plain `readProjection`. #165166's own evidence shows 0/10 focused failures and 0/3 shard failures without forcing the race; its regression only failed when a promise held the projection read open. Today the likeliest real candidate is a queued follow-up overlapping the preceding turn's settlement, and that overlap is narrow. A local turn awaits its claim release before its run returns, and the writer installs the publication before `releaseTurn` resolves. For a remote turn with an early final reply (`worker-turn-early-final.test.ts`), the follow-up does its one strict read up front, then waits for the pending result through non-strict `getAsync` reads. GitHub has no issue reports of `placement authority changed`.
3. **Restoring the loop would not close the window.** Most callers recheck the same observation while consuming it: `admitUserTurn` after `readEntry`, session file reads inside `withSessionTurnAuthority`, `prepareSandbox` after workspace resolution, and workspace reservations through `run`. A publication arriving a few milliseconds later still rejects. A reread of the preparation read alone would bring back the settlement-listener bookkeeping and only shrink one of several fail-closed windows. Under root `AGENTS.md` (no engineering for millisecond races without a real incident; name the accepted edge case instead), the right fix is to document the accepted edge case.

The failure is visible and recoverable: the turn fails before execution with "Interrupted before the agent started it. It will not run automatically; copy it and send again."

## Evidence

- Source trace: `preparePlacementRead` in `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-read-authority.ts` reads once, then calls `authority.assertCurrent()`. In `capturePlacementObservation` (`placement-turn-authority.ts`), that check rejects on any committed same-session non-`tools` publication (`revokedBy`) or a pending one (`hasPendingPublication`), and also on an indeterminate outcome, owner closure or replacement, or a stale admission. It checks the abort signal before and after the read.
- History: `git show 5f72ae5c98f52` (loop and tests added) and `git show b690de6fbb428` (loop, `settlementListeners`, and both regression tests removed; the docstring changed to "A concurrent placement mutation fails this read; the caller can retry it.").
- Docs checks: `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs` passed, markdownlint-cli2 reported 0 issues, `oxfmt --check` passed, and `git diff --check` was clean.
- Codex autoreview (P2 scope, with the read/authority/caller sources as evidence): `scoped-clean`, "overall: patch is correct (0.95)"; every claim in the paragraph checked against the supplied implementation.

prs.title: feat(tools): per-turn per-target send budget guard for message tools
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a per-turn, per-target outbound send guard shared by the `message` and `conversations_send` tools to curb within-turn duplicate-answer storms.

The existing loop detector hashes full tool params, so a model that re-sends the same answer with slightly reworded text produces a distinct hash every time and stays invisible to it — a single healthy `200` run can emit six reworded variants of one reply. This adds a lightweight ledger, independent of the loop detector and its default-off switch, that counts *successful* deliveries per (turn, target).

Closes #119992

## What Problem This Solves

A model can emit many reworded copies of the same reply within one turn. The existing tool-loop detector hashes the full stable tool-parameter object, so each reworded body is a distinct call and evades it entirely — a single healthy run can fan out six variants of one answer to the same recipient. Nothing in the ordinary send path accounts for repeated deliveries per turn.

This change adds a shared per-agent-turn, per-destination ledger observed by both the `message` tool and `conversations_send`, giving the model a default-on nudge to finalize after the first repeat and an opt-in hard cap that blocks further sends before dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The loop detector cannot catch reworded duplicates (it is content-hash based and default-off), so the guard must be independent of it and count *successful* deliveries, not param hashes.
- The two send tools reach the same recipients, so the ledger has to be shared and keyed on one canonical destination identity, or alternating the tools would evade it.
- The ledger must run on the ordinary Gateway execution path (not just embedded/subagent paths), which requires the active run ID to reach the tools that gate on it.

Seven runtime-path defects surfaced in review are fixed here so the guard actually protects the claimed workflow:

- **Gateway path dropped the run ID.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools` forwarded `runId` to the mediated coding tools but not to `createOpenClawTools`, so the `message` tool and `conversations_send` received `runId=undefined` and their ledger contexts declined to activate — the nudge and cap were silently inert for every Gateway-scoped turn. `params.runId` is now forwarded to `createOpenClawTools`; it stays `undefined` on the single-shot HTTP `tools.invoke` path, which correctly leaves the ledger off there.
- **Current-source key split.** `resolveOutboundActionRoute` keyed current-source sends on a literal `<current-source>` sentinel, while `conversations_send` keys on the resolved concrete target. The two never matched, so alternating a no-target source reply with `conversations_send` to the same peer split the count across two ledger slots and bypassed both the nudge and the cap. The current source is now resolved to its concrete target (`currentMessagingTarget ?? currentChannelId`), failing open when it cannot be resolved (mirroring the existing multi-target bail), so both tools share one slot for the same recipient.
- **Routable target not threaded through the Gateway/CLI-loopback chain.** The fallback above resolves to the routable delivery target only if the Gateway scope actually carries `currentMessagingTarget`, but that field was dropped across the whole loopback chain (`GatewayScopedToolParams`, `McpLoopbackRequestContext`, `RunCliAgentParams`, the CLI MCP grant context, the loopback tool cache key, and the `createOpenClawTools` call), so on a gateway turn the key always fell back to the native `currentChannelId`. On channels whose native channel id differs from the routable target, the native/routable identity split was therefore incomplete. The trusted routable target is now threaded end to end and emitted by the CLI reply producer alongside the native id. The direct HTTP path already treats the `x-openclaw-message-to` header as the routable target, so it keeps its `agentTo` fallback. Security: the routable target is trusted only from the server-minted bound grant context — the grant-authenticated header branch fails closed and a spoofed `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` header can never override the bound value.
- **Ledger key was not canonicalized before admission.** The key was built from the raw agent-typed target text, but the delivery path canonicalizes the recipient later, so equivalent spellings of one peer (case, provider prefix, phone formatting) produced different keys and separate ledger slots — alternating them evaded the guard, and the `message` tool and `conversations_send` did not truly share a slot. The target is now canonicalized through the same synchronous, idempotent, provider-bound normalizer the delivery path uses, inside the shared `buildTurnSendTargetKey`, so both tools converge on one slot. Async directory-alias resolution (`@username` -> id) stays out of scope by design and off the cap hot path.
- **Queued was counted as a delivery.** `conversations_send` recorded a ledger entry on a `queued` status, but `queued` is distinct from `sent` in the gateway protocol and means the intent was enqueued without confirmed delivery. With a cap of one, a queued acknowledgement suppressed the next real send and the nudge falsely reported the message had already been sent. It now counts only confirmed `sent` deliveries, matching the delivery owner and the `message` tool (which has no `queued` concept and already counted only confirmed deliveries).

- **Overlapping same-session runs evicted each other's counts.** The ledger stored one slot per session and reset it whenever a different run recorded on that session. Concurrent foreground turns can share one session key with distinct run ids (see `src/auto-reply/dispatch.freshness.test.ts`, which starts run A, completes run B on the same session, then resumes A), so an A -> B -> A interleave let run B evict run A's slot; when run A resumed, its per-target count read zero and both the nudge and the opt-in cap were silently bypassed — exactly under the concurrency the cap exists to protect. The ledger is now keyed by a composite `(sessionKey, runId)` so overlapping runs keep independent counts. Each slot stays authoritative for the whole run lifetime (no idle expiry) and is deleted by the run owner at its terminal boundary (`clearTurnSendLedgerForRun`, wired into the embedded runner's fallback-chain `finally`); terminal cleanup is the ledger's only delete path — there is deliberately no size-based eviction, because evicting a slot while its run is still live (an idle run while many turns execute concurrently) would silently zero that run's committed counts and release the opt-in cap mid-turn. Retained slots are bounded by the number of concurrently live runs.
- **An idempotent message replay was blocked by the cap.** The message tool evaluated the opt-in per-turn cap before deriving its stable idempotency key and recorded successes with the operation-blind counter, so a retried tool call with the same idempotency key (which the Gateway resolves to the already-completed send and returns the original receipt without re-delivering) was rejected with `turn_send_budget_exhausted` — the model was told a completed send had failed. The key is now derived before the cap, the cap is skipped when that key was already recorded this turn, and success is recorded via `recordTurnSendOnce` so a replay is counted at most once; a genuinely new or reworded send still counts and caps. This matches the `conversations_send` cap, which already admits idempotent replays.
## User Impact

- **Default-on, model-only nudge**: from the second same-target send within a turn, the tool result carries a one-line, model-visible reminder to finalize instead of re-sending. It never alters the outbound message and does not pollute a `message_tool_only` final reply. Opt out via `tools.message.turnSendNudge: false` (per-agent override inherits the global).
- **Opt-in hard cap (default off)**: `tools.message.maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget` blocks a send before dispatch once the cap is reached, returning `turn_send_budget_exhausted`. Media (`sendAttachment` / `upload-file`) and broadcast fan-out are exempt from the cap but still counted.
- No hash normalization: legitimate distinct messages, multi-part replies, media, and fan-out remain fully allowed. Existing operators who take no action get only the model-visible nudge; nothing blocks delivery unless the opt-in cap is enabled.

## Design notes

- A "turn" is one agent run (`runId`). A slot is authoritative for the entire run lifetime — including long tool waits and provider-fallback candidates that reuse the `runId` — so the opted-in cap holds for the whole turn; the run owner deletes the slot at the terminal run boundary (`clearTurnSendLedgerForRun` from the embedded runner fallback-chain `finally`), and that terminal cleanup is the ledger's only delete path — retained slots are bounded by concurrently live runs, and no size-based eviction ever removes a live run's counts. Module-level, keyed by agent session, mirroring the reviewed `recentPollVoteBySession` precedent.
- Counting always runs regardless of the nudge toggle; only the reminder text is gated.
- The hard cap reserves a slot before dispatch and settles after delivery (reserve-then-settle), so concurrent same-target sends are counted synchronously; documented inline.

## Evidence

Real behavior verified at the two boundaries the guard depends on (redacted local run):

- **Gateway boundary — ledger activates only when the run ID flows through.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools({ runId, surface: "loopback" })` produces a `message` tool whose per-turn cap engages; reverting the `runId` forward makes this fail. Verbatim:
  ```
  gateway-core  src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts (11 tests)
    ✓ forwards runId so the message tool per-turn cap engages on the loopback surface
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  11 passed (11)
  ```
- **Mixed-tool shared slot — no-target `message` reply + `conversations_send` to the same peer now share one ledger slot.** With `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1` the second tool is capped; reverting to the `<current-source>` sentinel makes it deliver (`status: "sent"`) instead of `suppressed`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/conversation-tools.test.ts (15 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  15 passed (15)
  ```
- **Routable-target threading boundary — native id != routable target still share one ledger slot.** `resolveGatewayScopedTools` with `currentChannelId: "D123"` (native) and `currentMessagingTarget: "user:U123"` (routable) differing: a pre-seeded routable slot and a no-target source send resolve to the same key and hit the cap. Reverting the routable-param forward makes this fail (verified). The header fail-closed invariant is covered: a spoofed `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` header leaves the bound routable target undefined. Verbatim:
  ```
  gateway-core  src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts / mcp-http.request.test.ts / mcp-grant-context.test.ts
  Tests  24 passed
  ```
- **Canonical shared-slot boundary — equivalent spellings collapse to one ledger slot.** `buildTurnSendTargetKey` now runs the target through the provider normalizer, so two spellings of one peer produce a byte-identical key (verified by a spelling-equivalence unit test). Because both tools flow through this one builder, `message` and `conversations_send` to the same peer share one slot.
- **Queued does not consume a slot.** A `queued` (unconfirmed) `conversations_send` result no longer records a delivery or emits the false nudge; a subsequent `sent` to the same conversation is admitted as the first counted delivery. Verified by a queued-then-sent regression under `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1` plus a table over `suppressed`/`queued`/`unknown`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts / conversation-tools.test.ts
  Tests  27 passed
  ```
- **Overlapping-run isolation boundary — interleaved runs on one session keep independent counts.** With the ledger keyed by `(sessionKey, runId)`, an A -> B -> A interleave keeps run A's count climbing (`record(A)=1`, `record(B)=1`, `record(A)=2`, `peek(A)=2`, `peek(B)=1`) and per-run operation-id isolation holds; the A -> B -> A regression fails on the pre-fix single-slot code (the resumed run A reads a reset count of 1 instead of 2). The new tests are anchored to the concurrent-same-session behavior proven in `src/auto-reply/dispatch.freshness.test.ts`. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (16 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  16 passed (16)
  ```
- **Idempotent-replay-past-cap boundary — a retried send at the cap reaches delivery dedup.** With `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`, a first send is admitted and counted, a replay of the same tool call (same idempotency key) is not cap-blocked and returns the completed receipt without double-counting or a false nudge, and a genuinely different send is still capped. The regression fails on the pre-fix code (the replay came back `suppressed`/`turn_send_budget_exhausted`). Delivery-layer dedup here applies to Gateway-routed sends (the `conversations.send` `operationId` store); direct-mode channels do not yet dedup on the idempotency key at the delivery layer — tracked in #125824.
- Both regressions were confirmed to have teeth by reverting each production change and observing the corresponding test fail.
- Full suite for the feature: `turn-send-ledger.test.ts` + `message-tool.test.ts` + `conversation-tools.test.ts` pass; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0; changed files pass `oxlint --type-aware`.
- Rebased onto latest `upstream/main`; clean.




- **Live-run budget retention boundary — the cap survives long idle waits and provider fallbacks.** The 10-minute idle TTL is deleted: a `(sessionKey, runId)` slot now lives for the whole run and is removed only at the run's terminal boundary. Regressions (fake timers): a capped run stays `exhausted` after an idle interval far past the old TTL (this fails on the pre-fix TTL code — verified by temporarily restoring the prune), a committed operation is still admitted as a `replay` across the same idle wait, and `clearTurnSendLedgerForRun` deletes only the exact `(session, run)` slot (siblings on the same session and same-runId slots on other sessions stay intact; missing scope/slot is a no-op). Run-entry tests prove the budget survives the fallback boundary and is cleared on both success and throw paths. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (28 tests)
  embedded-agent-runner  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-entry.test.ts (22 tests)
  Test Files  passed   Tests  50 passed
  ```
- **Direct-mode replay cap guard — a duplicate model-emitted tool-call id is disambiguated into a distinct cap-blocked send, not admitted as a replay.** The discriminating regression drives the real streaming normalization (`wrapStreamFnTrimToolCallNames` -> `normalizeToolCallIdsInMessage`): a model response emitting the same `message` tool-call id twice with byte-identical arguments is rewritten to two distinct ids, so the copies derive different idempotency keys and the second is cap-blocked with a schema-valid `turn_send_budget_exhausted` result while the runner is invoked exactly once. This guards the exact mechanism that keeps the replay-admission branch unreachable from a real model turn on direct channels (the delivery-layer dedup gap for an admitted replay is tracked separately in #125824). Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts (253 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  253 passed (253)
  ```

- **Route-aware replay admission boundary — a replay is only admitted past the cap when the selected delivery route dedups it.** The message tool resolves the actual gateway-vs-direct delivery route BEFORE reserving and hands the operationId to the ledger only when delivery relays through the Gateway backend (whose completed-result store dedups the repeated operationId). On direct in-process routes a repeated operation is treated as an ordinary new send: cap-blocked when a cap is set, honestly counted otherwise — closing the hole where an admitted replay on a direct channel would re-deliver because the delivery layer does not dedup idempotency keys there (tracked in #125824). Route detection fails conservative: when unsure it withholds the operationId, which cap-blocks a replay rather than re-delivering it. Regressions drive the REAL delivery path (actual outbound adapter call counts): a direct-route replay is suppressed and delivers exactly once, and a Gateway-routed replay is admitted without re-delivering or double-counting. Both fail on the pre-fix unconditional replay admission. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-tools  src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts (254 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  254 passed (254)
  ```
- **Run-terminal budget release boundary — a reused runId starts the next turn with a fresh budget, and fallback candidates never lose committed counts mid-chain.** `prepareCliRunContext` records the exact ledger slot (agent/session/run) the loopback grant mints; CLI settlement deletes only that slot, and only at the true terminal — success or the FINAL fallback attempt's failure. A non-final failure hands off to the next candidate, which must inherit the committed counts, so settlement defers; a dispatched CLI candidate (no `isFinalFallbackAttempt`) defers to the embedded runner's fallback-chain owner, keeping exactly one cleanup owner per terminal. The threw state is derived from real control flow (a `completedNormally` flag), not from `runError`, so a `settleCliAuthProfile` throw after a successful non-final candidate defers exactly like a non-final run failure instead of wiping the budget mid-chain (discriminating regression: the pre-fix `runError` proxy fails it). Cron's isolated-agent finally adds a bounded, idempotent safety net keyed identically to the loopback grant (same `canonicalizeMainSessionAlias` composition, durable session id as runId), so a chain that throws before any candidate settles still releases the slot. Verbatim:
  ```
  agents-support  src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.test.ts (18 tests)
  cron            src/cron/isolated-agent/run.turn-send-ledger.test.ts (1 test)
  agents-tools    src/agents/tools/turn-send-ledger.test.ts (28 tests)
  Test Files  3 passed (3)   Tests  47 passed (47)
  ```

### Real delivery-boundary proof (mock provider + mock channel, ephemeral Gateway, in a container)

Added `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts`: a real-behavior proof that boots an ephemeral Gateway child with the mock-openai provider and the `qa-channel` synthetic transport, then exercises the shared per-turn send ledger at the real delivery boundary (Gateway + qa-channel outbound bus), not by stubbing `callGateway`. It was run inside a clean `node:24-bookworm` container with container-local Linux dependencies (not just a host unit run). All scenarios pass and the run emits a machine-readable verdict:

```
test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts (8 tests)
  ✓ sanity: a plain qa-channel DM turn delivers one outbound reply
  ✓ scenario 1: second confirmed message send in one turn nudges and both deliveries land
  ✓ scenario 2: hard cap returns a schema-valid suppressed conversations_send result
  ✓ scenario 3: a suppressed message send does not charge the per-turn budget
  ✓ scenario 4: idempotent conversations_send replay does not re-deliver or double count
  ✓ scenario 5: two concurrent distinct-op sends to one target admit exactly one under the cap
  ✓ scenario 6: a model-repeated direct message send under the cap is disambiguated and cap-blocked (exactly-once delivery) — proves the cap-block path, NOT idempotent admission
  ✓ scenario 7: a spoofed attach-grant principal is refused before any delivery I/O (authority chain)
Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Verdict (`pass: true`), summarized per scenario:

- **Soft nudge counts confirmed deliveries** — two confirmed `message` sends to one target land on the qa-channel bus; the second tool result carries the model-visible "already sent 2 messages to this target this turn" nudge. `deliveriesRecorded: 2`, ledger `{ "qa-channel:qa-operator": 2 }`.
- **Hard cap returns a schema-valid suppressed result** — with `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`, only one delivery reaches the bus; the second `conversations_send` returns `status: "suppressed"` with details that pass `Value.Check(ConversationSendResultSchema, details)` (only `status`, `conversationRef`, `channel`; no `reason`/`message`) and the block explanation in the result text. `deliveriesRecorded: 1`.
- **Only visible deliveries charge the budget** — applying the production `deliveredNothing` predicate: `suppressed` and `failed` do not count (`0`), `partial_failed` counts (`1`, a visible partial reached the peer), plugin/gateway `undefined` counts (`1`), `sent` counts (`1`); no false "sent" nudge is emitted for a non-delivery.
- **Idempotent conversations_send replay** — replaying the same `operationId` returns the Gateway's completed `sent` receipt without a second bus delivery, is not cap-blocked, and does not double-count. `deliveriesRecorded: 1`, ledger stays at `1`.
- **Concurrent distinct-op sends under the cap (reserve-then-settle)** — two parallel `conversations_send` calls with distinct operationIds (NOT a replay) to the same conversation under `maxMessagesPerTurnPerTarget: 1`: the first in-flight reservation counts toward the cap synchronously, so the second call is exhausted before it reaches the Gateway — exactly one delivery lands on the bus and the ledger commits exactly one send. This is the core concurrency regression for #119992 (the old peek→await→record path let both peek 0 and both deliver).
- **Cap-blocked model-repeated direct send (cap-block proof, NOT idempotent admission)** — the mock provider emits the SAME direct `message` send twice in one model response (identical planned call id and byte-identical args). The runtime disambiguates the duplicate model-emitted ids into two distinct tool-call ids, so the copies derive different idempotency keys: the first delivers, and the second is cap-blocked before dispatch with a schema-valid `turn_send_budget_exhausted` result fed back to the model. Exactly-once delivery is asserted on the RECEIVE side — the qa-channel outbound bus carries exactly one copy of the marker, and a re-delivered copy would surface as a second. This proves end-to-end cap enforcement for the direct `message` tool at the real delivery boundary; it proves the cap-block path, not the idempotent-admission path (a duplicate model-emitted send is always disambiguated upstream and can never be presented as an idempotent replay).
- **Authority chain — an unauthorized principal is refused before any delivery I/O (scenario 7).** The harness's own `attach.grant` method mints a real non-owner grant; the test then drives the REAL MCP loopback HTTP entry with that grant plus spoofed delivery-authority headers (`x-session-key`, message channel, account id, current channel id, and `x-openclaw-current-messaging-target` pointed at a registered conversation) — every hop is the genuine defense, with no mocked resolver output: `validateMcpLoopbackRequest` → `resolveAttachGrant` → `resolveMcpRequestContext` (grant branch forces every spoofable header, including the routable target, to undefined) → owner-only tool deny. Asserted: `tools/list` does not advertise `conversations_send` for the grant principal; a `tools/call conversations_send` attempt is refused; and zero deliveries reach the qa-channel bus. Positive control on the same lane: the legitimate owner-bound path (real Gateway `conversations.send` → qa-channel bus, as scenarios 2/4/5) delivers exactly one — so the zero above is a real refusal, not a dead harness. Verdict entries carry no tokens.

Full unit suite for the feature (`turn-send-ledger.test.ts` + `message-tool.test.ts` + `conversation-tools.test.ts` + `cli-run-settlement.test.ts` + cron `run.turn-send-ledger.test.ts`) passes; `tsgo:core`/`tsgo:extensions`/`tsgo:test:root` exit 0; changed files pass `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`. Rebased onto latest `upstream/main`; clean.

### Final-head validation (HEAD `782540cd69f`)

Second upstream catch-up: the published branch was brought up to current `upstream/main` via an ordinary merge commit that merged main `36537b21828`. No published commit was rewritten, so the branch stays a descendant of its published head `97eb46dc643` and an ordinary fast-forward push applies. This second merge only resolved the generated config-documentation baseline conflicts (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` / `.sha256`, core option count settles at 2450) alongside the auto-merged code; the CHANGELOG Unreleased section is byte-identical to the merged upstream parent.

Re-verified on this final head `782540cd69f`:

- **Real qa-lab per-turn-send-budget E2E: 8/8 passing.** All eight stable scenario outcomes are pre-registered and fail-closed — the run asserts no missing, duplicate, unknown, or unsuccessful outcome; every registered scenario reports its expected result and the machine-readable verdict is `pass: true`.
- **Typecheck green:** `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, and `tsgo:test:root` all exit 0.
- **Focused tests: 759 passing** across the feature's unit and integration suites, plus proof 9/9.
- **Config docs / lint / format / diff check green:** config docs generation, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` are all clean.
- **Autoreview (honest scope note):** the final PR-tree fresh autoreview was scoped-clean with 0 P0–P2 findings on the predecessor head `97eb46dc643`, run over the PR tree against that merge commit's second parent `8e1f02805f66` (exact `upstream/main`). This second catch-up merge (`782540cd69f`) only resolved the generated config-baseline conflicts and did **not** receive a new fresh autoreview on `782540cd69f`.

Note: the Telegram (D5) live-channel proof from earlier revisions was not rerun on this final head; the validation above covers the qa-lab delivery-boundary E2E, typecheck, focused tests, config/lint/format/diff, and the prior scoped-clean autoreview.



### CI line-cap ratchet remediation (HEAD `4bcae80db14`)

CI job `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed at `782540cd69f`: the send-budget work pushed eight grandfathered files past their `check:line-cap-ratchet` baseline (deterministic against the merge base `36537b21828`). No cap was raised, no rule disabled, and no coverage trimmed — each file drops back to or below its base counted-line count by relocating cohesive helpers and the new send-budget test group into focused sibling modules:

- `message-tool-execution.ts` → `message-tool-turn-send-budget.ts` (turn-send-budget resolve/reserve/settle/nudge orchestration).
- `message-tool.test.ts` → `message-tool.turn-send-budget.test.ts` for the per-turn-send-budget group; `createChannelPlugin` and the runner-input type shared via `message-tool.test-support.ts`. The tool-assembly wiring assertion stays where its `createOpenClawTools` mocks live.
- `command/attempt-execution.ts` → `attempt-execution-auth-profile.ts` (harness auth-profile selection).
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` → `auth-profile-resolution.ts` (CLI auth-profile resolution).
- `config/schema.labels.ts` → `schema.labels.message-tool.ts` (the `tools.message.*` label block).
- `agent-runner-memory.test.ts` / `gateway/mcp-http.test.ts` → `*.test-support.ts` siblings (flush-plan fixtures / schema-builder helpers).
- qa-lab `mock-openai/server.ts` → `mock-openai-per-turn-send-budget.ts` (QA-PTSB fixtures) and `mock-openai-tool-call-input.ts` (tool-call input parsers).

Validation on this head (`4bcae80db14`):

- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base 36537b21828` and `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet --base 36537b21828` both green; `git diff --check` clean.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test` all exit 0.
- `oxlint` (core + extensions) and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files.
- Feature suites green: `message-tool.turn-send-budget.test.ts` + `turn-send-ledger.test.ts` (53), and the parent `message-tool.test.ts` + `agent-runner-memory.test.ts` + `mcp-http.test.ts` suites.
- Real qa-lab `per-turn-send-budget.e2e.test.ts`: **8/8** passing (re-run because the QA fixture organization changed).

The eight node-compact shard failures on the prior run were single integration tests timing out at exactly 120000ms; each reproduced green locally (`message-tool.scheduled-writes` 7/7, and feishu-mutations + channel/slack read-authority 124/124), so they were CI resource-contention flakes, not a regression — left for the fresh run to clear rather than triggering unrelated edits. This change is refactor-only; no product behavior or send-budget semantics changed. The Telegram (D5) live-channel proof was not rerun.

prs.title: fix(cloud): refresh environments after plugin activation and keep repository labels stable
prs.body:
## Problem

### What Problem This Solves

Cloud environments can retain an empty snapshot inventory and an empty Machines section when a browser connects before worker-plugin activation. Deferred startup updates the server's advertised-method catalog without notifying existing connections. The UI's capability owner can refresh that catalog, but the page does not reload when image methods become available, and loaded config/schema do not refresh when plugin activation changes validation.

Local snapshot labels also fall back to the managed session worktree's name, even though the saved project root and cache identity belong to the canonical repository. Successive sessions can therefore appear as different repositories.

## Solution

Publish the existing `plugins.changed` event after deferred startup attachment succeeds. Keep the existing capability refresh owner and reload Cloud environments when `crabbox.images.list` becomes callable. The config write coordinator refreshes previously loaded config/schema on a published plugin generation, using its existing draft and connection guards.

Record project labels from the canonical repository's normalized origin, falling back to its root basename. Worktree-specific remotes and session names no longer change the label; project keys and snapshot compatibility stay unchanged.

## Impact

Existing browser connections discover snapshots and saved machine profiles after activation, including the first suggested-profile flow, without reconnecting. Session worktrees remain grouped under the repository identity. No new UI copy, badges, config keys, SQLite schema changes, or plugin-state format changes.

Update behavior: a Gateway upgrade uses the new startup publication and the accompanying UI refresh paths. Existing image labels refresh when their normal allocation metadata is next written; this change does not rewrite stored records at startup.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/worktree-setup.mjs full`: dependencies prepared; full declaration build stopped after 21m 15.4s while compiling unrelated package declarations. Switched to the repository's supported runtime profile; full declaration proof remains with CI.
- `pnpm build:runtime`: **passed, 125.53s**; Gateway/runtime packaging, lazy import/bootstrap checks, plugin assets, UI build and performance gate passed. No baselines, budgets or caps changed.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-git-base.test.ts ui/src/lib/config/runtime-config-capability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **154.87s**, 94 passed / 1 failed in the Gateway shard; the dispatcher stopped before the UI config shard. Git snapshot tests and the new startup-publication test passed.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'waits for startup plugin attachment|adopts a winning plugin generation'`: **passed, 30.38s**, both publication/retirement contracts.
- `pnpm test ui/src/lib/config/runtime-config-activation.test.ts ui/src/lib/config/runtime-config-capability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **passed, 6.12s**, 31 tests; activation refreshes loaded config/schema without a connection replacement or timer polling.
- `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/cloud-workers-snapshots.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **passed, 29.12s**, 5 scenarios. The new browser scenario starts with no image methods and an empty config projection, publishes activation with an unchanged config revision, then verifies the repository and saved machine appear on the same connection. The fixture only supplies RPC responses; the real Gateway store, capability refresh, config owner and page render execute.
- Read-only Control UI-mode `GatewayClient` probe: the currently running test Gateway advertised all five image methods and returned the `cloud` profile in `sourceConfig`, `resolved` and `config`. Its fresh-connection state no longer reproduces the original report; the connected-before-activation path is covered by the regression above. No Gateway restart, reconfiguration, session dispatch, lease creation or destruction was performed.
- Original-source Git label probe: original code produced `session-a`; candidate produced `repository` with identical project key/root (**3.29s**). Tests also cover canonical remote identity when a worktree overrides its own remote.
- `pnpm tsgo`: **passed, 740.07s** including artifact-lock wait.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`: **passed, 753.13s** including artifact-lock wait.
- `pnpm ui:build`: **passed, 14.43s** after the final refresh-effect simplification. UI performance limits remain unchanged.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-other.json --incremental`: **passed, 14.00s**; typed the new config activation regression and existing UI consumers.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json --incremental`: **passed, 203.32s** including artifact-lock wait.
- Touched-file lint: **passed, 59.34s**, using the repository's `--files-json` selection shown below; includes i18n, line limits and styles.
- Touched-file formatting: **passed, 1.04s**, command shown below. `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2 on the final candidate. No accepted/actionable findings.

### Lead-requested main/head comparison

Baseline: freshly fetched `origin/main` at `9a9e7bd47280ce19f4c35ca7cbf16ec606911dea`, in a task-owned detached worktree with its own `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (**passed, 10.08s**). Candidate: `23f1e8c75d093e9e7544074e4c2460d9d4abae7e`. Each command below ran once per checkout for this comparison.

| Exact command | origin/main | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm test src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'retires startup gateway_start admission parked behind suspension'` | **Failed, 48.70s** | **Failed, 21.52s** |
| `pnpm test src/gateway/server-kernel.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'dispatches health and an agent turn without creating a transport'` | **Failed, 105.04s** | **Passed, 82.22s** |

The admission failures are identical: `startup admission retires without reopening suspension: expected false to be true` at `src/gateway/server-startup-admission.test-support.ts:190`. The kernel failure on main matches the exact CI signature at `src/gateway/server-kernel.test.ts:908`: `plugins.metadata.scan` and `plugins.metadata.freeze` occur after `config.snapshot.read.materialize` and `.observe`, instead of before them. The local head passage does not establish a repair. These comparisons establish both failure signatures on current main; the earlier attribution based only on unchanged test code was insufficient.

No source changes, expectation edits, skips, retries, empty commits, or CI reruns were made for this follow-up. The temporary main worktree was removed after the comparison. The PR body is finalized before the single push; the head remains unchanged.

Initial proof attempts also found two test-fixture mistakes (ambiguous Advanced selector and wrong mock event-control method), both corrected before the passing browser run. The first Git test attempt failed because source was edited during compiled-subprocess preparation; stable-input runs followed.

<details>
<summary>Exact lint and formatting commands</summary>

```sh
pnpm lint --files-json '["src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts","src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.ts","src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts","src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-git-base.ts","src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-git-base.test.ts","ui/src/lib/config/config-state-model.ts","ui/src/lib/config/config-test-harness.ts","ui/src/lib/config/config-write-coordinator.ts","ui/src/lib/config/runtime-config-activation.test.ts","ui/src/pages/cloud-workers/cloud-worker-environments.tsx","ui/src/e2e/cloud-workers-snapshots.e2e.test.ts"]'
pnpm format:check docs/gateway/cloud-workers.md src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.ts src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-git-base.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-git-base.test.ts ui/src/lib/config/config-state-model.ts ui/src/lib/config/config-test-harness.ts ui/src/lib/config/config-write-coordinator.ts ui/src/lib/config/runtime-config-activation.test.ts ui/src/pages/cloud-workers/cloud-worker-environments.tsx ui/src/e2e/cloud-workers-snapshots.e2e.test.ts
```

</details>

CI completed on the exact head in [run 38433421468](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38433421468). The sole failing test job was `checks-node-changed-compact-large-14` (292s), with the kernel trace-order signature reproduced on main above; the aggregate CI gate consequently failed. Production types, test types, lint, the other test jobs, and Security Review passed. The corrected PR context/evidence gate also passed. The CI failure classifier originally marked the kernel failure **unknown** because it had no matching job on main; the direct main test now supplies the missing evidence. No rerun was requested.

Inspected synthetic screenshots: before activation, empty inventory and Machines 0; after activation, one repository and Machines 1. Attached below. Integrated live AWS verification is reserved for the lead.

## Release-note context

Fix Cloud environments staying empty after worker-plugin activation, and keep snapshot repository labels stable across session worktrees.

![Cloud environments before plugin activation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44969ac8-9da4-43c2-bbf1-0dc5aa37cbe3)

![Cloud environments after activation on the same connection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/064e7a61-1d79-4ea7-b836-7bc2a233efa9)

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid doubled restart advice in ownership-loss reads
prs.body:
Related: #170790

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a Gateway read is the first check to notice its state owner lock was removed or replaced, the error repeats the restart advice, e.g. `OpenClaw state ownership at <db> was lost: Error: <lock>: no longer current; lock removed/replaced; restart the Gateway.; restart the Gateway.`

## User Impact

Operators see one clear ownership-loss message that names the lock and says to restart the Gateway once. Access and loss behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#170790 (d0554f4a2507) made the recorded loss Error carry the lock path and restart step, but the cached-read assertion still wrapped that Error in a template that appends `; restart the Gateway.` again. The read path now rethrows a recorded loss unwrapped (`owner.lost.signal.throwIfAborted()`), as the strict access path already does, and otherwise throws the plain `owner lock was removed or replaced; restart the Gateway.` message. This ports the same fix already applied on `release/2026.10.4` (226ffd8fff4).

## Evidence

- New regression in `src/infra/gateway-state-owner.test.ts` (`reports a read-detected owner loss with one restart instruction`): a gateway-role owner whose lock is replaced is first observed by `assertStateDatabaseReadAllowed`, and the message must end in a single `restart the Gateway.`. It fails on `origin/main` without the source change and passes with it.
- `pnpm test src/infra/gateway-state-owner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "read-detected owner loss"`: 1 passed, test 160ms, wall 31.6s (Vitest duration 21.2s, mostly transform). Added CI cost is about 0.2s of test time in an existing file.
- `pnpm test src/infra/gateway-state-owner.test.ts src/infra/gateway-state-owner.heartbeat.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 47 passed.
- `pnpm test src/state/openclaw-state-db-cache.{cleanup,idle,retention}.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (cached-read caller): 20 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: pass. `npx oxfmt --check` on touched files, `git diff --check`: clean.

prs.body:
Related: #163153

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: swiping a long iOS chat lags and jitters when scroll updates rebuild the entire transcript.

## User Impact

The transcript does less work during a swipe while preserving sent-question anchoring, following the latest reply, jump-to-latest behavior, and the reader’s position when earlier history loads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scroll position and follow state now live in an observable object read only by the scroll-position modifier, follow-anchor modifier, and jump-to-latest slot. Scroll ticks and swipe-phase changes update those views without rebuilding every transcript row. The existing scroll-policy handlers and modifier placement are preserved.

This builds on #163153.

## Evidence

- The simulator fling benchmark uses `testLongTranscriptFlingScrolling` to fling a 60-question transcript 16 times. Debug tracing measured 5.1 transcript-body evaluations per swipe before state isolation and 0.0 afterward; total evaluations fell from 113 to 12.
- `ChatScrollCommandTests` and `ChatReaderScrollStateTests`: 26 tests passed across two suites.
- `ChatNativePrependViewportTests`: both tests passed, covering native prepend correction and reply growth below the reading row.
- `testLoadingEarlierHistoryPreservesReadingPosition` and `testNewlySentTurnWithCompletedReplyKeepsQuestionAnchor`: both simulator UI tests passed.
- iOS test build passed. SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint passed on both changed files with no violations.

prs.title: fix(ai): native video handoff to chat-completions providers + preflight video cost
prs.body:
# PR 2 — fix(ai): native video handoff to chat-completions providers

Branch: `pr/native-video-handoff` (12 commits)

**Problem**
Video attachments to non-last user turns were silently dropped, or the request was rejected
pre-flight with a phantom ~480k-token "context overflow" — making video unusable on local
chat-completions models.

**Root causes (all fixed here)**
1. Preflight estimator charged video data-URIs as prompt text (`estimateOpenAICompletionsContentChars`
   had a fixed cost for image parts but none for video parts) → requests rejected before send.
2. Provider-context materialization didn't run for completions transports/boundary copies →
   canonicalized media facts never projected into provider payloads.
3. Freshly drained/queued runtime turns carry media only in non-enumerable symbols or top-level
   fields; frozen hydrated copies crash symbol writes; current-turn facts missing from provider
   transcript copies; model resolution dropped declared video input modality.

**Fixes (12 commits, net of debug-only work)**
- Fixed-cost estimate for `video_url`/`input_video` parts (96k chars ≈ 24k tokens).
- Materialize provider context at completions transports + boundary installs.
- Carry non-enumerable runtime media facts across LLM boundary copies; rehydrate
  non-canonical media at provider materialization; inject current-turn facts.
- Frozen-hydration guards for runtime symbol tags; preserve declared video modality;
  trust configured native video models in media-understanding.

**Validation**: 124/124 targeted tests pass on current upstream (`openai-completions-params/
transport/messages`, `images.replay`, `media-facts.persisted`) + end-to-end live verification:
previously-unseen MP4 reaches the inference server (HTTP 200, `prompt_tokens` consistent with
video part, `videoBlocks=2` in materialized context).

Notes for reviewers: two unconditional `log.warn` probes (`provider media facts`,
`unprojected user media facts`) were kept from live verification; fine to drop on request.

prs.title: fix: plugin update leaves a manual-recovery backup when held files block replacement
prs.body:
Related: #169842

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a plugin update on Windows whose current install is held by a running process fails twice and leaves a backup directory that needs manual recovery, when the Gateway still has the plugin's files open.

This is the Windows publication path from #169842, reproduced end to end on current main (842ad901b) with a held file. The pin-guidance half of that issue landed separately; this repairs the remaining publication failure.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw plugins update` against a held install now fails once with one actionable error naming the held file and the stop-the-Gateway step, leaves the current install complete (including after partial child removal), keeps the config valid so the retry is not blocked, and succeeds when rerun after the holder closes. Previously the same run errored twice (EBUSY unlink, then "install target changed during rollback" with a "backup retained / recovery path" tail), left a `.openclaw-install-backups` directory behind, and, for git-sourced plugins, removed the manifest so the config turned invalid and blocked the recovery rerun itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

Displacement publishes the backup copy first and removes the original tree second. Two defects followed from that order:

1. Rollback unconditionally restored the backup over the still-present original, erroring again and leaking the backup. The original tree is now compared against the identity captured before displacement: a match means the original never left the target.
2. Copy fallback unlinks source children sequentially, so a held LATER child can leave the original partially removed with an intact identity — and for git plugins the removed manifest invalidates the config, which blocks the recovery rerun. Rollback now backfills every removed entry from the complete backup (the held entry never left and is never written), discards the backup only after the tree verifies whole, and keeps the backup with a named manual recovery path if backfill cannot complete.

Held-file displacement failures surface one error naming the errno and the operator step. The fs-safe dependency is untouched; both repairs live in the staged publish transaction that owns displacement and rollback.

Backfill writes are authority-gated per entry: every mkdir, copy, and symlink runs only after a retained assertion re-checks rollback ownership and the backup, base, and target identities — the recovery contract established by #138870 (recovery stops when ownership closes; substituted backups are rejected before mutation), mirroring how displacement and removal already assert. A refused or expired owner therefore performs zero filesystem writes and the backup is retained.

Data-model compatibility: this change is a pure filesystem transaction. It reads and writes only the installed plugin directory, its staged copy, and its backup; no SQLite schema, config shape, or stored-data format is touched, and the backfilled bytes are copied verbatim from the displaced original tree, so existing settings and package data load unchanged.

## Evidence

Real Windows 11 flow, captured end to end against a local git-sourced plugin (`hold-test`, managed clone under `~/.openclaw/git/`) whose `zzz.txt` is held by a native PowerShell handle with no delete sharing, Gateway never started. Command output is verbatim; paths are local fixtures.

Held update (one actionable error, file named, next step named):

```
$ pnpm openclaw plugins update hold-test
Cloning D:/obj/github/hold-test-git...
Installing plugin dependencies with npm…
Failed to update hold-test: failed to replace managed git plugin repository: Error: EBUSY:
resource busy or locked, unlink 'C:\Users\24614\.openclaw\git\git-4382b968b401fd11\repo\zzz.txt'.
The current install's files are held by another process, usually a running Gateway; stop the
Gateway and retry this update.
```

Immediately after: the managed clone is complete again (sequential unlinks had removed `package.json` and the manifest; rollback backfilled them from the backup), no `.openclaw-install-backups` directory remains, and the config snapshot reports `valid: true`. Before this change the same run instead left the clone holding only the held file, an orphaned backup, and an invalid config that refused the retry.

Same command after the holder closes:

```
$ pnpm openclaw plugins update hold-test
Cloning D:/obj/github/hold-test-git...
Installing plugin dependencies with npm…
Updated hold-test: 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0.
Updates saved; they will load on the next Gateway start.
```

Command invocations ran the shipped `runPluginUpdateCommand` module from this checkout via tsx, because the dev-checkout CLI bootstrap's own dist-publication gate times out in Windows service inspection on this host and is unrelated to the plugin update flow. Real files, real state, real native lock; no mocks.

Red/green regression, `pnpm test src/infra/install-package-dir.test.ts` (~30s local, Windows): 15 passed, including the intact-original case and the partial-removal case (an unlocked earlier child plus a held later child), which asserts the backfilled tree, zero backup leftovers, and a successful rerun. Red at merge base with only the tests applied fails on the missing guidance message and the leaked backup.

`pnpm test src/plugins/update.test.ts` on this Windows host: 3 failures in afterEach temp-dir cleanup (EPERM removing oc-vt-* temp dirs); identical 3 failures reproduce with this change stashed, so they are host-environment cleanup flakes, not regressions.

Red/green regressions, `pnpm test src/infra/install-package-dir.test.ts` (~35s local, Windows): 16 passed, covering the intact-original case, the partial-removal backfill case (unlocked earlier child plus held later child; asserts the backfilled tree, zero backup leftovers, successful rerun), and the revoked-ownership case — ownership closes after partial removal, and the test asserts zero backfill writes via the still-missing entries, the held file untouched, the backup retained, and the refusal surfacing with `backup retained at`. The revocation test fails against the pre-authority-gate backfill (red proof at aaac6501c).

Data-model compatibility is argued above rather than replayed: no storage layer is involved, so there is no stored-data migration to exercise.

Production delta: +108 / -22 in install-package-dir.ts plus the extracted staging module; the growth is the identity-checked, authority-gated rollback branch and its comments, kept inside the existing transaction owner rather than a wrapper.

prs.title: fix(sessions): sessions_history reads transcripts for configured ACP owners
prs.body:
Addresses the `sessions_history` follow-up in #164847. The `sessions_search` half was fixed by the merged #164897; the ACP `sessions_spawn` dispatch mismatch tracked in the same place remains open and is not touched here. Taken up at @obviyus's suggestion after #164901 was closed as a duplicate of #164897.

## What Problem This Solves

The model-facing `sessions_history` tool fails with `Unknown agent id "<harness>"` for a visible ACP session when the harness id is configured in `acp.allowedAgents` but absent from `agents.entries`. The tool sends that harness id explicitly to the Gateway `sessions.resolve` visibility probe and to `chat.history`, and the shared session-request validation (`resolveRequestedSessionAgentId`) rejects any explicit id outside the native roster before key-based admission could accept the configured store owner. The same authenticated caller can already list the session and read its transcript through the Gateway without that redundant explicit id.

## Why This Change Was Made

An agent-qualified session key already selects its owner, so the tool now omits the explicit `agentId` from both requests when it duplicates the key's own agent (`agent:<harness>:acp:<uuid>` keys from ACP spawn, resolved like any agent-qualified key). Unqualified keys and genuine owner mismatches keep sending the id, so callers that need the roster/mismatch guards keep them. Transcript-sharing and visibility checks are unchanged: `resolveSessionToolAccess` runs the same decision checkers, the Gateway sharing layer still filters the read, and with `tools.sessions.visibility: "self"` the same ACP transcript stays forbidden. Search does not grant new transcript visibility through this change either.

## User Impact

Agents configured with ACP harnesses (for example `opencode` or `codex` in `acp.allowedAgents`) can read session transcript history again without adding harness ids to `agents.entries`; today the whole tool call errors out and operators fall back to the Gateway `chat.history` RPC or the CLI.

## Evidence

- Failing-first on the current main tip (`e785c56d8`): reverting the two source files on top of this branch (`git checkout origin/main -- src/agents/tools/sessions-resolution.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts`) while keeping the new regression reproduces the maintainer-reported rejection from the real tool flow:

  ```
  { status: "error", error: 'Unknown agent id "opencode"' }
  ```

- New embedded-gateway regression (`reads a configured ACP owner transcript without an explicit agent id` in `src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.history.test.ts`) runs the real `sessions_history` tool against real session-request validation: seeded ACP store entry, seeded ACP runtime meta (as real ACP spawn persists), and `agents.entries: { main }` + `acp.allowedAgents: ["opencode"]`. It fails on base as above and passes with the fix (17/17 in that file).
- New gateway-level control in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read.test.ts` (`sessions history reads a configured ACP owner without an explicit agent id`): `chat.history` without the id returns the seeded ACP transcript on base and head, while the explicit harness id stays rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`, pinning the contract the fix relies on.
- Five wire-contract assertions were updated where they pinned the now-omitted redundant id (explicit `agentId` equal to the key's own agent): four in `sessions-resolution.test.ts`, one in `sessions-history-tool.test.ts`. The latter ("resolves current history under the requester instead of the fixed-store owner") also removes a latent contradiction derived from the code: under a global fixed store, the old explicit-id path validated `agent:<agent>:main` against the fixed-store owner, so the id the tool sent would be rejected by a real Gateway; the key-based admission this change relies on resolves the same request to the requester.
- Scoped runs: `pnpm test src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.history.test.ts`, `pnpm test src/agents/tools/sessions-resolution.test.ts` (25/25), `pnpm test src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.test.ts` (26/26), `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read.test.ts` (no failures), plus the `sessions-send-tool.*` and `sessions-search-tool.*` suites.
- `oxlint` on the six touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors; `oxfmt --check` clean; `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` passes.
- `tsgo:core` reports only two pre-existing errors in `src/infra/state-migrations.state-dir.ts` that reproduce identically with the change reverted; CI is authoritative for typecheck. Also pre-existing and unrelated on this Windows checkout (verified by reverting the change): the `sessions-access.test.ts` EPERM temp-dir cleanup cascade and one timing-sensitive `sessions-search-tool.test.ts` incarnation-race test.

Prepared with AI assistance (same as #164901); I have reviewed and verified the changes.


## Real behavior proof

Below: after-fix proof from a **real ACP setup** — the actual `openclaw gateway` process (spawned subprocess from source, real config file, real SQLite session store in a real state dir, `agents.entries: {main}`, `acp.allowedAgents: ["opencode"]`) plus a self-visibility denial control and a before-fix control on the same rig. No embedded gateway, no vitest: the gateway executed its own production tool set through the Gateway's `tools.invoke` RPC (which resolves the real `sessions_history` tool via the gateway's tool resolution and runs it with the production in-process gateway-request binding), as an operator client over the real WebSocket protocol with token auth.

Setup (per scenario):

```
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway --port <port>          # real gateway process
config: { "agents": { "entries": { "main": {} } },
          "acp": { "allowedAgents": ["opencode"] },
          "gateway": { "mode": "local", "port": <port>,
                       "auth": { "mode": "token", "token": "<redacted>" } },
          "plugins": { "enabled": false } }
# session store seeded the way ACP spawn persists it:
#   entry + canonical ACP runtime meta + one transcript message
#   sessionKey: agent:opencode:acp:acp-proof-<runId>, sessionId: acp-proof-<runId>

$ tools.invoke { "name": "sessions_history",
                 "args": { "sessionKey": "agent:opencode:acp:acp-proof-<runId>", "limit": 10 },
                 "sessionKey": "agent:main:main" }        # requester = main
```

**1. After fix — successful tool retrieval through the real Gateway** (`ok: true`, transcript read via key-based admission without the redundant explicit id):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "toolName": "sessions_history",
  "output": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "{\n  \"sessionKey\": \"agent:opencode:acp:acp-proof-r10\",\n  \"messages\": [\n    {\n      \"role\": \"assistant\",\n      \"content\": \"acp history needle LIVE-PROOF\",\n      \"timestamp\": 1700000000000,\n      \"__openclaw\": { \"id\": \"acp-answer\", ... }\n    }\n  ],\n  \"truncated\": false,\n  ...\n}" }]
  },
  "source": "core"
}
```

Gateway-side trace: `⇄ res ✓ tools.invoke ... conn=…` — a completed RPC whose tool executed the same `sessions.resolve` → `chat.history` sequence the fix relies on.

**2. Self-visibility denial control — same ACP session, `tools.sessions.visibility: "self"`, requester `main`** — the denial is preserved (the fix does not open cross-agent visibility):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "toolName": "sessions_history",
  "output": {
    "details": {
      "status": "forbidden",
      "error": "Session history visibility is restricted. Set tools.sessions.visibility=all to allow cross-agent access; use tools.agentToAgent to restrict permitted agent pairs."
    }
  },
  "source": "core"
}
```

**3. Before-fix control — same rig, only the two production files reverted to current main** (`git checkout origin/main -- src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-resolution.ts`): the exact failure this PR fixes, reproduced through the real Gateway:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "toolName": "sessions_history",
  "output": {
    "details": {
      "status": "error",
      "error": "Unknown agent id \"opencode\""
    }
  },
  "source": "core"
}
```

The working tree was restored to the PR head immediately after the capture.

## CI findings for run 37214065475 (failed checks on the reviewed head)

- `check-test-types-core-3` — **ours, fixed in this head**: `src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.history.test.ts(408,7): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'agentId' does not exist in type ...` (the excess-property finding). Landed commit `test(agents): drop unsupported agentId option in embedded history regression` removes the property; the shard's typecheck (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-tools.json`) now reports only the two pre-existing `src/infra/state-migrations.state-dir.ts` errors that reproduce identically on main.
- `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` — **not ours**: failed in `ui/src/e2e/chat-composer-catalog.e2e.test.ts` ("keeps the selected model during startup, then tracks fallback and recovery at 1280px/390px", `AssertionError: expected 'false' to be 'true'`). The PR diff touches only `src/agents/tools/*` and `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read.test.ts`; the Control UI composer catalog is outside the change surface, and recent `ci.yml` runs on `main` (e.g. 37255313251, 37255065184) pass the same workflow.
- `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway (2/2)` — **not ours**: failed in `ui/src/e2e/worker-initial-setup.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` ("holds browser and sessions_send input during sync, then launches each exactly once", ~39 s — a timeout-shaped failure in the Control UI worker-initial-setup custody flow). Also outside this PR's surface for the same reason.
- `openclaw/ci-gate` — aggregate of the three above.

## Test-cost measurements

Single-worker local wall times on this Windows checkout (Node v26.10.0, cold tsx transform dominates; CI timings come from the exact-head jobs):

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.history.test.ts`: 17/17 passed — 280.7 s vitest (296 s wall), of which 178 s was first-run module transform.
- Typecheck of the CI shard that failed (`tsgo` `tsconfig.core.test.agents-tools.json`): no errors in touched files; only the two pre-existing `src/infra/state-migrations.state-dir.ts` errors remain (identical on main).
- `oxlint` on the touched test file: 0 warnings, 0 errors; `check:line-cap-ratchet`: OK ("6 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth").
- Real-gateway proof rig: 3 gateway subprocess scenarios (after / self-visibility / before), each a single spawned `openclaw gateway` process; tool invocation round-trip per scenario ≈ 16 s RPC (`tools.invoke` completed in 16.1 s server-side on the cold run).

Prepared with AI assistance (same as #164901); I have reviewed and verified the changes.
