prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse rows after unrelated plugin reloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin config hot reloads invalidate every cached session row. Concurrent sidebar and project reads then wait several seconds for unrelated rows to rebuild.

## User Impact

Hook and enable/disable edits preserve rows whose model, harness, CLI backend, and session-extension facts are unchanged. Real plugin-derived changes still refresh affected agents, including native harness ownership. No schema changes or new config settings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config classifier included the whole plugins block. Catalog renewal also compared runtime registry identities, proxy arrays, and private thinking-policy callbacks, so an equivalent replacement looked different. Completed catalog publications now own plugin-derived row invalidation and compare captured semantic inputs per agent. The existing catalog WeakMap stores these inputs; managed contribution identity follows its source digest while unowned contributions retain conservative identity checks.

The existing shared preparation remains the single-flight owner. Replacement settlement cannot clear a successor's gate, and an awaited catalog read cannot publish an incomplete replacement. Native ownership expires only after a completed semantic policy change, preserving accepted facts while replacement work is pending. Duplicate ownership invalidation mutations use the existing records owner.

Production LOC is +181 net (206 additions, 25 deletions). This growth preserves the existing contracts for model data and thinking policy, installed code/config, unloaded harness availability, normalization, CLI selection, session extensions, and native ownership while removing coarse identity fences. It adds no parallel cache or reload path.

## Evidence

### Measurement

Same synthetic production-shaped state in place on an isolated Linux sandbox: 8,400 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 disabled cron jobs, 12 real project worktrees, and a 4.33 GiB agent database. Forty real WebSocket clients requested sidebar rows with limit=200 after actual plugin reload acknowledgment.

| Cohort | RPC p50 / p99 | Dirty / reused / materialized rows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before: enabled=false | 8,323 / 8,396 ms | 8,129 / 2 / 198 |
| After: enabled=false | 153 / 253 ms | 0 / 200 / 0 |
| After: enabled=true | 173 / 284 ms | 0 / 200 / 0 |
| After: hooks.allowPromptInjection=false | 172 / 266 ms | 0 / 200 / 0 |

All 120 final reload requests succeeded. Disable-reload p50/p99 improved 54.5×/33.2×; materialization yield wait fell from 8,149–8,349 ms to 1–2 ms. Warm controls also showed full reuse. Ordinary warm timing varies; removal of global invalidation is the decisive result.

Each cohort has 40 requests, so p99 is its maximum. RPC timing excludes startup and reload acknowledgment wait. The measured row-reuse path is unchanged. Subsequent CI repairs replace three method-presence expressions for typed lint and restrict native-ownership invalidation to pinned harness sessions; the failing RPC regression and native-ownership sibling pass after that repair. Baseline hooks reload did not acknowledge within 120 seconds after rematerialization queue pressure, so hooks has no reliable before/after ratio. The fixture's raw model inventory is empty; nonempty prepared thinking policies are exercised by the owning regression.

### Proof and review

- Production-path regressions fail on the old code: unrelated hook edits dirty all rows, overlapping replacement loses its gate, an in-flight read adopts incomplete ownership, and native ownership remains stale. Equivalent managed replacements now reuse sequences across concurrent lists; source or policy changes still update visible row facts.
- Final four-file command: row catalog, invalidation, runtime ownership, and accepted-facts tests; 36 tests passed, 69.61 s wall including compiler preparation. Earlier focused catalog/RPC siblings passed (36 tests), and the config-owner sibling passed (57 tests).
- Changed-file oxfmt and git diff --check passed. Nine focused source/test files passed repo lint. The main projection owner retains the existing max-lines diagnostic: 731 code lines versus a 700 limit, reproduced identically on original base and final source; its code-line count is unchanged.
- Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), clean on the final patch. The helper refused provider/config preflight; operator configuration was preserved.
- CI found introduced issues: typed lint rejected three unbound method references, and the sessions-list-config RPC regression detected an unnecessary repeat of an ordinary session read during catalog renewal. The same overbroad invalidation also dirtied a cold archived row. These were repaired; changed-file typed lint passed, the failing RPC file plus native-ownership file passed (six tests), and the archived sibling passed (seven tests). Independent review of the repair was clean. Full gates run on the final head in PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox leases or local builds/typecheck/suites were used. Sandbox runtime builds were measurement preparation only.

Client audit found no config-event reconnect and existing per-connection request coalescing. Cross-client auth/catalog refresh remains: a failed owner replacement does not guarantee an authoritative metadata publication, so removing that fallback would risk stale auth state. The benchmark exercised sidebar RPCs directly; it does not claim reduced models.authStatus traffic.

Final CI: all 97 completed checks passed on `05ef50069b3d66e1addafaaeafaf3263a2d00393`; required Actions and commit-status `openclaw/ci-gate` checks are both SUCCESS. This includes production/test typechecks, changed lanes, architecture guards, build artifacts, and UI E2E. The three previously failing jobs passed after the scoped repair. No CI rerun or inherited-failure exception was used for this final head.

prs.title: fix(agents): record the final-call context fact on cumulative provider usage (#125333)
prs.body:
Refs #125333.

## What Problem This Solves

On providers that report attempt-cumulative usage on the assistant message, the persisted context snapshot overstates the real prompt size, which trips compaction early. #125333 measured `totalTokens` climbing 455,917 → 607,947 on one session, where 607,947 is exactly `usage.input` 82,123 + `usage.cacheRead` 525,824 summed across a tool loop rather than the prompt of the final model call.

The transcript side has a root cause that is separate from candidate ordering: in `preservePendingAssistantUsage`, when the message already carries provider totals, the function returns early and the message reaches the transcript **with no `contextUsage` at all**. `Usage.contextUsage` is documented as "Exact context snapshot for the final provider iteration", and the CLI path fills it in `resolveCliTranscriptUsage` — but nothing fills it for other APIs. So every later reader (the session context snapshot, the memory-flush prompt estimate) has to infer the prompt size from cumulative token buckets, and overstates it by roughly one multiple per tool-call round trip.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ctx.state.pendingAssistantUsage` is the stream-captured snapshot for the assistant message, and at the point `preservePendingAssistantUsage` runs it is still the **final-call** value: `handleMessageEnd` only replaces it with the message's own usage afterwards, via `recordAssistantUsage(assistantMessage.usage)` on the next line. That makes it the authoritative call-scoped fact, available exactly where the transcript record is being finalized.

So this stamps it as `contextUsage` and leaves the provider's own token buckets untouched:

- the prompt figure comes from the existing exported `derivePromptTokens`, not a new formula;
- the shape mirrors `resolveCliTranscriptUsage` so both paths produce the same contract;
- an existing `contextUsage` — `available` or the `unavailable` barrier — is never overwritten;
- a pending snapshot with no prompt tokens stamps nothing;
- the pre-existing "fill in missing/zero usage" path is unchanged.

Deliberately kept out of scope so this does not collide with #125479, which is already open on the same issue:

- No change to `deriveContextPromptTokens` or to `agent-runner-memory.ts`. #125479's context-window bound and this change are complementary: with a call-scoped fact present in the transcript, that bound becomes a backstop against impossible values rather than the primary defense — which matters because a window bound cannot reject inflation that stays under the window (e.g. a true 30k prompt reported as 150k against a 200k window).
- No treatment of sessions that **already** persisted an inflated `totalTokens`. Those stay authoritative through `resolveFreshSessionTotalTokens` until either `SESSION_TOTAL_TOKENS_VERSION` is bumped or the persisted read is bounded; both are separable decisions, noted in my review on #125479.

## User Impact

Sessions on non-CLI providers stop accumulating an inflated context snapshot from tool-loop turns, so compaction and memory flush fire against the real prompt size instead of a multiple of it. No user-visible surface changes; the provider's reported token counts and costs are byte-identical.

## Evidence

New test file `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.lifecycle.usage.test.ts` (6 cases) uses the shapes from the report. The first case is an A/B on the same cumulative message: with the fact recorded the derived snapshot is the true final-call prompt `31,300`; constructed without it, the same message still derives `607,947` — the figure from the issue.

Local validation on this branch:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| new test file | 6/6 passed |
| regression: `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages*` + usage suites (7 files) | 165/165 passed |
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:test:src` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:assertion-safety` | OK — 4312 files, no new uncommented assertions |
| `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet` | OK — 901 grandfathered suppressions, none added |
| `oxlint` (changed files) / `oxfmt --check` | exit 0 / correctly formatted |

Not run locally: the full `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` suite — leaving that to CI.

prs.title: fix(cron): retry preflight on timeout and use shorter cache TTL for timeout failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`preflightCronModelProvider` probes local provider endpoints with a single 2500ms GET and caches **any** failure — including a pure client-side `TimeoutError` — as `unavailable` for 5 minutes. A momentary gateway event-loop stall can fire the deadline even when the provider is healthy, silently skipping every cron run scheduled in the next 5 minutes.

## Fix

**1. Retry on TimeoutError**: `probeLocalProviderEndpoint` now retries up to `PREFLIGHT_RETRY_COUNT` (2) times with a 400ms delay, but **only for client-side timeouts**. Hard connect errors are not retried — they are not transient.

**2. Shorter cache TTL for timeout-caused failures**: Timeout failures use `PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_CACHE_TTL_MS` (30 s) instead of the full 5-minute TTL.

Non-timeout failures continue to use the full 5-minute TTL unchanged.

## Test fix (addressing ClawSweeper review)

Updated `reprobes after a client timeout` → `retries on client timeout then reprobes after short cache TTL`:
- All `PREFLIGHT_RETRY_COUNT+1` mock rejections supplied (3 total timeout failures for the first call)
- `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1000)` for the retry delays
- Assert `fetchWithSsrFGuardMock` called 4 times total (3 retry attempts + 1 second preflight call)
- Added separate `does not retry on hard connect errors` test confirming `ECONNREFUSED` = 1 call only
- Second preflight call at `nowMs: 31_001` (past the 30s timeout TTL) gets a fresh probe → available

## Evidence

```
[retry on timeout, all attempts fail]
  Attempt 1 → TimeoutError
  Retry delay 400ms
  Attempt 2 → TimeoutError  
  Retry delay 400ms
  Attempt 3 → TimeoutError
  → cached as unavailable with isTimeout=true, TTL=30s

[second preflight at nowMs=31001 — past 30s TTL]
  → fresh probe → available ✅
  fetchWithSsrFGuardMock called 4 times total ✅

[hard connect error — no retry]
  Attempt 1 → ECONNREFUSED
  → cached immediately, fetchWithSsrFGuardMock called 1 time ✅
```

Tests added: `retries on client timeout then reprobes after short cache TTL` (parametrized across nested/non-nested TimeoutError) and `does not retry on hard connect errors`.

Fixes #156163

prs.title: fix(memory): reconcile and re-arm after the memory watcher is lost
prs.body:
Fixes #119411
Refs #40088
Follow-up to #137200

## What Problem This Solves

`dirty` is only ever produced by watch events, so once the memory watcher is lost there is nothing left to set it and every later sync trusts a stale clean flag and skips the memory source. On #119411 this shows up as memory files staying unindexed for hours or days (`memory status` reporting `Dirty: no` or an indexed count below the on-disk count) until a manual `openclaw memory index` or a gateway restart:

- a Raspberry Pi gateway lost the Linux directory-tree watcher with zero warnings in the journal — 765 memory files went unindexed for 42 hours until a new session happened to reconcile;
- on 2026.9.3 with default settings, files written outside an active session stayed unindexed until a manual index.

Three gaps made that loss terminal:

1. the chokidar error handler only logged — unlike the native handlers it did not even mark dirty to cover the gap;
2. a native watcher error whose chokidar fallback attach failed left the directory with no coverage at all, also as a log line only;
3. nothing detected a watcher that died silently (a chokidar instance that has been closed, or a native pair still parked on its parent watch after the replaced root directory already exists again — the parent event that should reattach it was lost).

The kernel-capacity variant of this is already handled by #137105 (watching disabled, index refreshed on search). This PR covers the recoverable, non-capacity losses.

Scope claim, stated plainly: this is bounded recovery for the loss states the manager can detect (a watcher error, a silently closed chokidar instance, or a native pair whose main watcher is gone while its root exists again). It does not claim to resolve every installed-system symptom reported on the linked issues; a watcher whose handle is intact but which silently stops delivering events is not detectable from user space and stays out of scope.

## What This Changes

Repair at the watcher lifecycle owner in memory-core, mirroring the #137105 boundary:

- `MemoryManagerWatchResources` gains a `memoryWatchLost` flag and a cheap liveness probe (`isMemoryWatchLost`): the flag, chokidar's public `closed` marker on a watcher the manager still holds, or a native pair with no main watcher whose root directory exists again. The probe does no I/O unless a pair is parked without a main watcher.
- `reconcileLostMemoryWatch()` drops all watch handles, forces one memory reconcile, and re-arms the watcher. It runs at the search boundary (right next to the #137105 capacity block, before the dirty gate decides whether memory needs work) and at each interval-sync tick. Repair is deferred to those boundaries — never inside a watcher error callback — so a persistent path error cannot rebuild the watcher in a tight loop. Re-arming runs inside `runInMemoryBackgroundContext`, the same boundary startup uses, so replacement watchers and the debounce timers they arm do not retain the turn whose search noticed the loss.
- The chokidar error handler now marks dirty to cover the reported gap, the same way the native handlers already do; a failed chokidar fallback attach records the loss instead of leaving it terminal.

Explicitly out of scope, to stay clear of the #40088 product discussion: no change to `intervalMinutes` or any other default or configuration, no count-based heuristics, no speculative polling. The reconcile only runs when watch coverage is known to be gone. The `memory.search.sync.*` keys are retired on current builds, so the search/session-start boundary is the production-reachable path this fix hooks.

## Evidence

Failing-first, real manager + real SQLite index + real search in all cases (only the OS watch layer goes through the repo's designated `openclaw.test.memory*Factory` hooks where noted); the second and third cases drive a real chokidar end to end.

Red (unmodified main, `manager.watch-liveness.test.ts`):

```
× memory watch liveness > reconciles and re-arms after a native watcher error whose chokidar fallback fails 21032ms
  → expected [] to include 'Cobalt heron discovered.'
× memory watch liveness > reconciles and re-arms after the held chokidar watcher is closed silently 19432ms
  → expected [] to include 'Cobalt heron discovered.'
```

Green (this PR):

```
✓ memory watch liveness > reconciles and re-arms after a native watcher error whose chokidar fallback fails 6521ms
✓ memory watch liveness > reconciles and re-arms after the held chokidar watcher is closed silently 4949ms
✓ memory watch liveness > re-arms outside the requesting turn's async context and releases the replacement on close 2389ms
Tests  3 passed (3)
```

Case 1 (error-driven death): the native watcher emits a non-capacity error and the chokidar fallback attach throws. After the one mark-dirty sync settles, a new memory file is invisible — `dirty` stays false — and repeated searches never index it on main. With this PR the next search rebuilds the watcher (asserted: fresh native watcher attached, old chokidar closed) and the file is found.

Case 2 (silent death): a real chokidar instance covering the memory directory is closed without any event while the manager still holds it. The test first proves the live watcher marks dirty on its own; after the silent close a new file leaves `dirty` false and main never indexes it. With this PR the next search notices the closed watcher, reconciles, and re-arms — and the re-armed watcher is proven live again by a later file marking dirty on its own before any search.

Case 3 (re-arm context isolation, no factory hooks — real native pair and real chokidar): the held chokidar watcher is closed silently, then the search that notices the loss runs inside nested turn/pending-input `AsyncLocalStorage` scopes, with the same `fs.watch` and debounce/pressure-timer probes `manager.watcher-filesystem.test.ts` uses for startup. Red against the first revision of this PR (re-arm called directly from the search): `expected { turn: 'requesting turn', pendingInput: 'accepted input' } to deeply equal { turn: undefined, pendingInput: undefined }`. Green with the background boundary: every replacement watcher and every timer it arms observes no store, the replacement still marks dirty on a later write, and closing the manager drains every watcher it opened (FSEventWrap census back to baseline).

Full memory-core suite passes with no new failures versus the pre-change baseline (pre-existing Windows-environment failures unchanged). `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, the assertion-safety, line-cap and max-lines ratchets, and the extensions/extensions-test/test-root/core typecheck graphs are clean.

prs.title: fix(doctor): respect deliberate Skill Workshop opt-outs
prs.body:
Fixes #171274

## What Problem This Solves

`doctor --lint` warns for a restricted reader agent that deliberately denies Skill Workshop, and recommends an `alsoAllow` grant that cannot override the deny.

## User Impact

Agents that explicitly deny `skill_workshop`, including through `group:agents` or a matching wildcard, opt out without a Workshop warning. A minimal profile alone still receives the actionable `alsoAllow` hint. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostic recorded only the first filter that removed the tool, so a profile exclusion hid a later deny. The diagnostic now checks the capability owner's resolved deny list with the canonical tool-policy matcher before generating advice. Runtime tool filtering remains owned by the existing policy pipeline.

## Evidence

prs.title: feat(ui): stream reasoning live in WebChat for /reasoning stream
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/reasoning stream` does nothing in the Control UI. While a turn runs, no reasoning appears, and after the turn the saved thinking blocks stay hidden as well, because the transcript projection shows saved reasoning only for `/reasoning on` (#136008). Users of local reasoning models (Qwen on vLLM in our case) who want to watch the model think have no way to do so in WebChat, even though the TUI shows the same stream live.

Verified on 2026.9.4 with a gateway-protocol observer: the gateway emits a `thinking` agent event on every reasoning delta regardless of the reasoning level, and `server-chat.ts` forwards those events to Control UI clients through the same throttled path as assistant text. The browser receives the stream; nothing renders it. No release since 2026.7.1 has had a consumer for `stream === "thinking"` in `ui/src`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool-stream lane already turns gateway activity into transient thread items (tool cards, commentary preambles), retires them when durable rows arrive, and reconciles them on history reload. Live reasoning fits the same lane.

1. **Consume the stream.** `handleReasoningStream` (new `tool-stream-reasoning.ts`) accepts `thinking` events for the run the pane is driving. The gateway sends the cumulative text of the current block plus the delta; a cumulative text that no longer extends the open block means a new assistant message started, so the previous block settles and a new one opens. A turn with several tool calls therefore renders one block per assistant row, in order. Blocks settle on the run's lifecycle end; stale or coalesced shorter snapshots are ignored by sequence and prefix.
2. **Render through the existing bubble.** Blocks become a new `reasoning` thread item, inserted by timestamp among that run's tool cards and before the live answer, and rendered by the same saved-reasoning bubble used for persisted thinking blocks, so the live copy and the durable row look identical.
3. **Retire in place.** Mid-turn assistant rows are not admitted into the live transcript (their `session.message` carries no run id), so the live block is the only copy until history reloads. Once the transcript carries a thinking block for the same run whose normalized text matches the block's normalized prefix, the live block is dropped, both in the thread builder and in the pane state after history hydration. No duplicates during or after the turn.
4. **Gate presentation.** Live blocks reach the thread only when the session's reasoning level is `stream` and View → Reasoning is on. Saved reasoning now shows for `stream` as well as `on`, so the turn looks the same before and after it settles; `off` stays hidden, including after reload.

Two files were at the 700-line lint cap, so the pane props and the saved-reasoning gate go through small helpers in `reasoning-segments.ts` rather than adding lines there.

### Follow-up: the viewport follows the live reasoning

The post-render follow scroll in `ChatStateController` only ran when transcript rows or the text stream changed. Live reasoning blocks update `chatReasoningSegments`, so after a send the viewport stopped at the first screenful of reasoning while the block kept growing below it, and the reader had to scroll by hand to watch it. The second commit watches that state the same way `chatStreamSegments` is watched (#144703). The existing reader policy is unchanged: a scroll up releases the pin so streaming does not fight the reader, and returning to the end pins it again. `chat-reasoning-stream-follow.e2e.test.ts` streams reasoning past a 480 px viewport and asserts all three states; before the change it fails at the first assertion (viewport 677 px above the end).

## User Impact

With `/reasoning stream` and the Reasoning view enabled, reasoning appears in WebChat as the model produces it, block by block, next to the tool cards of that turn, and stays in place as the saved transcript replaces it. `/reasoning on` behaves as before (saved reasoning after the turn); `/reasoning off` still hides everything. Sessions and panes not using `stream` see no change.

## Evidence

- `tool-stream-reasoning.node.test.ts`: accumulation of cumulative frames, new-block detection on restart, delta-only growth, stale-snapshot rejection, run scoping, blank-frame handling, settling on lifecycle end, and reset with the tool stream.
- `chat-thread.reasoning.test.ts`: reasoning items ordered before the live answer with the open block marked streaming, no items when the pane passes none, retirement once the transcript carries the same thinking for the run, and no cross-run retirement.
- `chat-reasoning-stream.e2e.test.ts`: replays a captured real turn (thinking stream, mid-turn `session.message` without run id, tool events, durable final row, text-only chat final) in Chromium against the mock gateway; asserts the live block appears for `stream` only, the earlier block stays while the run continues, and exactly one copy of each block remains after the turn settles.
- `chat-reasoning-visibility.e2e.test.ts`: expectations updated so `stream` shows saved reasoning like `on`.

```
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.ui.json                                   # clean
node_modules/.bin/oxlint <changed files>                                        # clean
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts ui/src/pages/chat ui/src/lib/chat
  Test Files  295 passed   Tests  6730 passed | 3 skipped
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  ui/src/e2e/chat-reasoning-stream.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/chat-reasoning-visibility.e2e.test.ts
  Test Files  2 passed   Tests  8 passed
```

prs.title: fix: config set gives no reason when a new agent model ref cannot resolve
prs.body:
Fixes #144744.
Related: #132614

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a user adding a model reference to a specific agent with `openclaw config set` or `openclaw config patch` would see the write rejected with no reason why, when the reference cannot be resolved.

The affected paths are the per-agent model references a write can newly introduce: `agents.entries.<id>.model.*` and `agents.list.<i>.model.*`. The same reference at `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` already reports its value and the resolver's message, so the two paths disagreed about the same failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

A ref was marked as a dependency whenever no entry existed at that identity in the previous config, because the ownership check compared `previousRef?.agentId !== ref.agentId` against a missing previous ref. With no previous ref the optional chain yields `undefined`, which differs from a defined `agentId`, so every newly authored ref at an agent path was marked as a dependency. Dependency refs take the redaction path in `formatModelRefError`, which replaces the value with `<configured model reference>` and the resolver's text with `Unable to resolve authored model reference`.

An ownership change now requires a previous entry at that identity. `dependency` continues to mark refs whose value the operator did not author in this mutation: refs inherited from `agents.defaults`, bare fallbacks whose provider changed with the primary, and case-only ownership moves. Hiding the value for those cases is deliberate and unchanged.

Non-goal: this does not change when a write is accepted or rejected. An unresolvable ref is still refused.

## User Impact

A rejected write at an agent path now names the reference and repeats the resolver's message, which is where the fix is stated. For example, a provider that has no registered model in the running state now reports the missing catalog entry and how to add it, instead of leaving an unknown model, a provider that is not registered, a provider denied by policy, and a damaged install indistinguishable from each other.

## Evidence

Observed CLI output, same commands, same isolated config (`{ "agents": { "entries": { "main": { "name": "unchanged" } } } }`), run against a clean build of `main` at `112e8e30` and against this branch rebased onto it. Nothing else differs between the two runs.

```
# before: main @ 112e8e30
$ openclaw config set agents.entries.main.model.fallbacks[0] missing-provider/missing-model
Cannot set model reference "<configured model reference>" at agents.entries.main.model.fallbacks.0: Unable to resolve authored model reference. Run openclaw models list to list available models.

$ openclaw config set agents.entries.main.model deepseek/nonexistent-model
Cannot set model reference "<configured model reference>" at agents.entries.main.model: Unable to resolve authored model reference. Run openclaw models list to list available models.

# after: this branch
$ openclaw config set agents.entries.main.model.fallbacks[0] missing-provider/missing-model
Cannot set model reference "missing-provider/missing-model" at agents.entries.main.model.fallbacks.0: Unknown model: missing-provider/missing-model. Run openclaw models list to list available models.

$ openclaw config set agents.entries.main.model deepseek/nonexistent-model
Cannot set model reference "deepseek/nonexistent-model" at agents.entries.main.model: Unknown model: deepseek/nonexistent-model. Run openclaw models list to list available models.
```

In both runs the config file is unchanged afterwards, so the accept/reject decision is the same; only the report differs.

Tests: `config-model-validation.reporting.test.ts` is added, with the newly added agent ref case plus four controls. The controls keep the existing behaviour: an inherited dependency ref stays redacted in both value and reason, an env-substituted value still keeps the shorthand at the defaults path and at an agent path, since there the resolver saw a value the operator never typed, and a ref whose agent id changed only in case is still treated as an ownership move. The boundary matrix below maps each case.

`config-cli.roster.integration.test.ts` "validates model references before writing" pinned the redacted message for a ref the operator typed on the command line, which is the defect, so that assertion now expects the authored ref and a reason, and rejects both `<configured model reference>` and the generic `Unable to resolve authored model reference`. The exact reason is pinned in the reporting test rather than here: the two `it.each` cases share one process, and the second one resolves through a retired plugin inventory, which the old redaction hid entirely.

The new case fails on `main` for the intended reason:

```
× config model validation reporting > reports the resolver reason for a newly added agent fallback
  → expected 'Cannot set model reference "<configur…' to contain 'Unknown model: acme/nope'
```

All 18 `src/cli/config-*` suites pass on the rebased branch, 602 tests, and `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the changed files.

The earlier `checks-node-compact-small-27` failure was this roster assertion; `checks-node-changed-extensions-config-49` (`memory-core` temporal ranking, FTS availability) does not touch any file in this diff.



### Test cost

Measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on a 4 vCPU Linux host, per the Cost budget in `docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md`. The reporting file was measured at head 43fbabb5c9d; the other two files are unchanged since 108a6b90515, where they were measured:

| File | Change | Tests | Vitest duration | Wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src/cli/config-cli.roster.integration.test.ts` | existing, +9 / -5 | 56 passed | 114.06 s | 118.8 s |
| `src/cli/config-model-validation.reporting.test.ts` | new, +207 | 5 passed | 71.58 s | 78.4 s |
| `src/cli/config-model-validation.test.ts` | existing, +0 / -1 | 40 passed | 20.58 s | 24.8 s |

`config-cli.roster.integration.test.ts` is an existing integration file over the 30 s budget; this PR only edits expectations in it (+9 / -5) so the roster reports the authored ref and its reason, and adds no new cases there. The new reporting file holds the five cases that need the CLI's real output path. Its local figure was taken while the host was under other load; the file's own test time is 1.8 s, and the rest is transform, which is shared with its sibling suites in CI (see below).

### Redaction boundary coverage

The change sits on the line between text the operator entered, which now shows the resolver's reason, and text they did not, which stays redacted. Each side of that line has a case:

| Boundary case | Where | Base `aa9b92a12d8` | This branch | `ownerChanged` forced false |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Newly added agent ref shows its value and the resolver reason | reporting: "reports the resolver reason for a newly added agent fallback" | fail | pass | pass |
| Inherited default stays redacted, value and reason | reporting: "keeps an inherited dependency ref's value and reason redacted"; validation: "validates defaults newly inherited after removing an agent model override" | pass | pass | pass |
| Env-expanded ref at the defaults path keeps the shorthand | reporting: "keeps the detail suppressed when env resolution rewrote the authored ref" | pass | pass | pass |
| Env placeholder newly added at an agent path shows the placeholder, hides the expanded value and the resolver's words (new) | reporting: "keeps the expanded value hidden for a placeholder newly added at an agent path" | fail | pass | pass |
| Ref whose agent id changed only in case stays redacted (new) | reporting: "keeps a ref redacted when only its agent id's case changed" | pass | pass | fail |
| Valid ref is accepted | validation: "accepts a resolved default primary", "validates touched fallback and per-agent model refs", "uses list index paths for list-shaped agent model refs" | pass | pass | pass |

The env case at an agent path is the one this change moves: on the base the placeholder was replaced by `<configured model reference>` because the ref counted as a dependency, and on this branch env expansion alone keeps the expanded value out. The case-only rename guards the half of the ownership condition this change keeps; it passes on both sides and fails only when the ownership check is disabled.

Base failures, with this branch's test file against the base source:

```
× reports the resolver reason for a newly added agent fallback
  → expected 'Cannot set model reference "<configur…' to contain 'Unknown model: acme/nope'
× keeps the expanded value hidden for a placeholder newly added at an agent path
  → expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]
Tests  2 failed | 3 passed (5)
```

With `ownerChanged` forced to false:

```
× keeps a ref redacted when only its agent id's case changed
  → expected [] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]
Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)
```

### CI seconds

From CI run 35966207006 on head 43fbabb5c9d, summing the per-test durations Vitest reports for each file in its job log (test time only, excluding import and setup):

| File | Tests | CI test time | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/cli/config-cli.roster.integration.test.ts` | 56 | 25.67 s | checks-node-changed-compact-small-11 |
| `src/cli/config-model-validation.reporting.test.ts` | 5 | 0.83 s | checks-node-changed-compact-small-11 |
| `src/cli/config-model-validation.test.ts` | 40 | 4.75 s | checks-node-changed-compact-small-11 |

The one failing job in that run, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-43`, failed two cases in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.ownership.test.ts` ("does not coalesce or wait for foreign durable work", `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times` at the default one-second `vi.waitFor` poll). This diff does not touch `src/agents`, which is identical to the merge base, and the same file passes 10/10 in three single-worker runs on that source. Main fixed that fixture in 3b1f0372143 ("await foreign maintenance startup in ownership fixtures"), which landed after this branch's merge base.

prs.title: fix(memory-core): make dream diary narrative timeout configurable
prs.body:
Fixes #138403

## What Problem This Solves

Dream Diary narrative generation in `extensions/memory-core` has a hardcoded 60-second completion timeout (`NARRATIVE_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` in `src/dreaming-narrative.ts`). Slow local models (e.g. a 27B LLM on a consumer Mac) routinely exceed 60s to produce a single 80–180 word entry, so every diary run degrades and writes the boilerplate fallback:

> "A memory trace surfaced, but details were unavailable in this run."

With a local-model setup this happens on every sweep — one install accumulated **130+ consecutive fallback entries over several months**, filling DREAMS.md with the same placeholder and making the feature effectively unusable. There is no way to configure the timeout: the dreaming execution config already has a `timeoutMs` field (`MemoryDreamingExecutionConfig`, resolved by `resolveExecutionConfig`), but the plugin JSON schema sets `additionalProperties: false`, which rejects the key before it can reach the narrative call.

This makes the timeout configurable through the existing dreaming execution config, so local-model users can raise it per phase or globally without code changes.

## Rebase note

Rebased onto current `main`; upstream consolidated the light/REM narrative completions into `runDreamingSweepPhases`, so the two per-phase call sites this branch originally edited no longer exist. The forwarding now hangs off the single consolidated call site, and the earlier line-neutral commit became obsolete (dropped). Net diff: 11 files, +106/-13. Local re-verification after the rebase: line-cap + assertion-safety ratchets, `config:docs:check`, `plugins:inventory:check`, `format:check` (47467 files), `tsgo:core` + `tsgo:extensions`, `lint`, and the dreaming test suites listed below. The `max-lines` ratchet reports one stale baseline entry (`extensions/telegram/src/fetch.ts`) that also reproduces on pristine `main` and is unrelated to this diff.

## Changes

- `src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.ts`: `resolveExecutionConfig` now inherits `fallback.timeoutMs` when a phase-local record has no `timeoutMs` (same fallback semantics as `speed`/`thinking`/`budget`/`model`). Previously a default-only `execution.defaults.timeoutMs` was dropped while rebuilding every phase execution, so the resolved value never reached the narrative call.
- `dreaming-narrative.ts`: `DreamNarrativeRequest` accepts optional `timeoutMs`; used when it is a positive integer, otherwise the 60s default applies (existing behavior unchanged).
- `dreaming-phases.ts` + `dreaming.ts`: forward `execution.timeoutMs` (already resolved by `resolveMemoryDreamingConfig`) to every narrative completion — light and REM share the consolidated `runDreamingSweepPhases` call site, deep keeps its own call in `dreaming.ts`. The forwarding stays line-neutral in the over-cap phases file (single object spread, line-cap ratchet).
- `openclaw.plugin.json`: allow `timeoutMs` (integer >= 1) in all four `execution` blocks (defaults + light/deep/rem); `additionalProperties: false` previously rejected the key.
- Tests: timeout pass-through + invalid-value fallback in `dreaming-narrative.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/dreaming.md`, `docs/reference/memory-config.md`.

## Usage

```json5
{
  plugins: {
    entries: {
      "memory-core": {
        config: {
          dreaming: {
            execution: { defaults: { timeoutMs: 600000 } },
            // or per phase:
            // phases: { deep: { execution: { timeoutMs: 600000 } } }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Evidence

- **Unit tests** — `vitest run`: memory-host-sdk dreaming 15/15 (incl. `inherits execution.defaults.timeoutMs into every phase and lets a phase override win` — fails on the pre-fix resolver), memory-core dreaming suite 198/198 across 13 files (incl. dreaming-narrative 17/17 timeout pass-through + invalid-value fallback): all pass.
- **Schema generation** — `generate-base-config-schema --check`: ok (the four `execution` blocks now accept `timeoutMs`).
- **Typecheck / lint** — `tsgo` extensions typecheck clean; `oxfmt --check` + `oxlint` on changed files clean.
- **Live observation** — the motivating failure is from a real install: with a local 27B model and the old hardcoded 60s budget, every sweep produced the placeholder entry (130+ consecutive in DREAMS.md); no code path regenerates a usable narrative once the timeout fires, because `subagent.complete()` aborts the run.
- **Behavior unchanged when unset** — `timeoutMs` is only used when present and a positive integer; otherwise the existing 60s default applies (covered by the invalid-value fallback test).
- **Default inheritance (ClawSweeper P1, addressed)** — a config with only `execution.defaults.timeoutMs` now resolves that value into light/deep/rem phase executions (regression test above); a phase-level `timeoutMs` override stays authoritative.

- **Real-behavior trace (after fix, local run against this branch)** — a real `resolveMemoryDreamingConfig` + `runDreamNarrative` run with only `dreaming.execution.defaults.timeoutMs = 600000` (plus a deep-phase override of 900000) produced:

```
[1] real resolveMemoryDreamingConfig:
    execution.defaults.timeoutMs = 600000
    phases.light.execution.timeoutMs = 600000
    phases.deep.execution.timeoutMs  = 900000
    phases.rem.execution.timeoutMs   = 600000
[2] subagent.complete received timeoutMs = 600000
```

The default reaches every resolved phase (deep keeps its override), and the value arrives at the real subagent completion boundary (`subagent.complete({ timeoutMs })`). The same run attempted a live completion against the local model endpoint; that endpoint did not answer within 4 minutes on this machine (the shared local 27B model was busy) — which is exactly the slow-model scenario #138403 reports, and the reason the configurable ceiling exists.


- **Real-behavior proof — successful live run (2026-09-05 03:24 GMT+8, added per ClawSweeper "needs proof")** — full production path on this branch (`2fc5ab2a`): real config (defaults-only `execution.defaults.timeoutMs = 600000`) → real `resolveMemoryDreamingConfig` → real `runDreamNarrative` (deep phase, with the SDK-backed SQLite state store wired as in plugin registration) → `subagent.complete` backed by the real local LM Studio endpoint (Qwen3.8-27B, `localhost:1234`) honoring the passed `timeoutMs` as the HTTP abort deadline → real `DREAMS.md` publication to a throwaway workspace. Script: `proof/real-behavior-proof.mts` (author's worktree, not part of the diff).

```
[1] real resolveMemoryDreamingConfig (config: defaults-only timeoutMs=600000):
    execution.defaults.timeoutMs     = 600000
    phases.light.execution.timeoutMs = 600000
    phases.deep.execution.timeoutMs  = 600000
    phases.rem.execution.timeoutMs   = 600000
[2] subagent.complete received timeoutMs = 600000
[3] live completion started against http://localhost:1234/v1 (model=qwen/qwen3.8-27b)
[4] live completion SUCCEEDED in 73.7s (675 chars)
[log:info] memory-core: dream diary entry written for deep phase
[5] runDreamNarrative outcome = {"status":"completed"}
[6] DREAMS.md written — entry:
---
*September 5, 2026 at 3:24 AM GMT+8*

The old timeout had been a scarlet line etched in stone, hard-coded since the first frosty Tuesday, and I used to pat it like a stubborn cat. Today it became a dial, a little brass knob of mercy. I turned it just enough for the slow local engine to finish its short, breathless entry without me tapping my fingers into a silent drum. It reminded me of the gateway that endured a whole night of restart storms, blinking like a lighthouse through its own churn, until the plugins finally sat down in their proper chairs. Maybe resilience is just patience with a config file. The sunset was #ff9e6d, and the server hummed a lullaby in the back room, half asleep, half listening.
```

This closes the "attempted local-model run did not yield an observed successful post-fix diary entry" gap from the 2026-09-04 review: the real 27B completion finished in **73.7s — already beyond the old 60s hard cap, well inside the configured 600000ms ceiling** — and a real diary entry was published (`status: "completed"`). Input snippets were kept generic/technical; the entry contains no personal data.

prs.title: perf(sessions): bound transcript append writer residency
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large transcript append streams progressively slow the agent database writer and can exhaust its heap, delaying other session writes behind it.

## User Impact

Appends keep bounded writer residency while preserving exact persisted transcript bytes, commit receipts, retry identity, model-context navigation, and byte accounting. Slow transaction warnings now include `context.payloadBytes` for the primary prepared event/message (or summed turn messages; optional initialization/header excluded). No schema, stored format, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The append owner added full parsed events to both the actor payload map and navigation. Residency then serialized the entire retained state on every settlement to enforce its 8 MiB budget. Large bodies therefore caused increasing JavaScript work, eviction/re-hydration, and eventually worker heap exhaustion. `phases.sqlMs` includes JavaScript executed inside the transaction; it is not a sum of SQLite statement timings.

Reuse the existing memory actor navigation projector for durable appends. Build detached receipts first, retain exact context byte metadata, then discard settled payload bodies at the residency owner. Retry reads use the existing canonical SQLite fallback. Remove the obsolete resident-payload rewrite loop and move message identity lookup into its existing owner.

Production LOC: **+42** (153 added / 111 removed, excluding tests/support/docs). The required new payload-size diagnostic contract needs command-shape handling and forwarding through worker transaction contexts; the navigation projector and identity lookup are moves. This adds no second cache or residency mechanism.

## Evidence

Synthetic production-shaped fixture on an isolated 128-core Linux sandbox: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, approvals/cron/projects/worktrees; initial agent database **4,641,595,392 bytes**. All commands restricted to allocated CPUs 64–127, 64 GiB memory, nice/idle I/O, isolated state. No production databases or services accessed. Node 26.8.2. Actual durable actor transport and writer worker; 6 MiB cache-TTL events. Five initial append samples excluded for lazy startup/warmup.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Sequential append writer phase, p50 / p99 (35 samples, matched 11-event sessions) | 63.90 / 112.96 ms | 22.72 / 70.80 ms |
| Sequential append round trip, p50 / p99 | 77.04 / 133.90 ms | 32.57 / 83.58 ms |
| 20 simultaneous appends: queue-to-worker-start wait, p50 / p99 (matched 2-event sessions) | 443.40 / 887.82 ms | 435.57 / 702.10 ms |
| Same burst: writer phase, p50 / p99 | 36.44 / 86.44 ms | 25.22 / 67.38 ms |

Queue measurement includes actor dispatch/admission and worker serialization, rather than isolating only SQLite reservation wait. No individual SQLite statement exceeded 50 ms during these measured runs. In an 80-event session stress case the old worker exhausted its heap on append 56 (preceding writer-phase p99 189.80 ms); the changed worker completed all 80 appends on a matched 80-event session, p50 27.54 ms / p99 104.79 ms after warmup. The median improvement is clear; the stress p99 narrowly exceeds 100 ms. This does **not** reproduce or claim to eliminate every reported 0.94–1.44 s production hold, nor qualify a 43 GB cold database. Payload attribution will help distinguish remaining causes.

Regression fails on the old retention behavior: reading another session forces the large append actor to rehydrate. Changed behavior preserves residency, exact receipt/stored bytes, UTF-8 byte totals, ancestry, and warm/cold context equivalence. Existing rewrite, receipt, append-postimage, kernel, context-metadata, memory-history, and transcript-payload contracts passed focused checks.

Local proof: changed-file `oxfmt`, changed-file repo `oxlint`, `git diff --check`; focused `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1` only. Final residency/kernel: 7 passed; rewrite/receipt/append-postimage: 17 passed; earlier context-metadata/memory-history/payload contracts passed. No Testbox/Crabbox lease: operator policy assigns full typecheck, suites, and closure gates to PR CI.

Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**, scoped clean at P2+. Autoreview refused because its requested provider did not match operator config; config unchanged. Full PR CI passed on the corrected head.


CI follow-up: initial head `43dc994ee299e17ab0553f3be4a2a01b8a089438` passed every selected broad gate except assertion-safety. Its existing safety note was above the projection call rather than the nested assertion. Commit `c21b2437b187` places the note immediately beside the same assertion; no behavior/types/assertions changed. Targeted `check-assertion-safety-ratchet` now passes, changed-file formatting/lint pass, and the independent reviewer approved the exact correction. This failure was caused by this diff and was fixed; it is not being treated as inherited. Full CI run [38499135883](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38499135883) and the required repository review gate passed on corrected head `c21b2437b187eb153660457567330ad75e92b579`. Merged as `a15b5c7109401c35c8fad9edeb3e28de913f7e0f`.

prs.title: fix: reduce New Session typing lag after models load
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: typing in New Session stalls after the model catalog loads because each input update repeatedly prepares the composer and resolves the same model/runtime.

## User Impact

New Session typing does substantially less synchronous work with a loaded model catalog. Model changes, catalog refreshes, placement eligibility, and live draft/lock state still update normally. No configuration changes or migrations are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share one composer-options projection per published page revision across the draft presentations, and keep a bounded runtime-resolution memo owned by the draft model control. Its key includes the model, runtime, catalog, retirement/policy state, and scalar agent/default inputs; resetting the owner also resets the memo. Preserve the composer's live getters so retained attachment callbacks do not capture stale text or lock state.

This removes repeated work at its source rather than debouncing keystrokes or delaying input updates.

## Evidence

- **Landing integration:** preserved current main’s placement-options memo and stable draft props. The refreshed candidate passed **675 affected tests**, including the New Session suites and all eight sidebar catalog-event tests; UI types passed. A fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings. The performance table remains the original paired browser measurement, not a remeasurement of the merged baseline.

- Reproduced against the unchanged production UI with a mocked gateway containing **1,000 models and 1,000 sessions**, then repeated against an isolated build of this patch. Same Chrome instance and input sequence: median input-to-next-animation-frame **94 ms → 42 ms**. The same textarea remained connected throughout both runs. This reproduces the loaded-catalog slowdown, not the full reported 30-second backlog; timings are local synthetic-input measurements, not a cross-device guarantee.
- **Exact reported scenario reproduced and verified:** New Session on the actual Gateway, local `juni0r` checkout, explicit **GPT-6.1 Sol**, Medium effort, with the model picker fully loaded (212 option rows). In Aside, the unchanged UI took **378–411 ms per character**. A paired run in one fresh isolated Chrome process compared the unchanged served UI against this patch, using the same real Gateway data and the same warmed 35-character sequence:

  | Input → next animation frame | Before | After | Speedup |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | **Median** | **336.4 ms** | **26.5 ms** | **12.7× (~13×)** |
  | Mean | 416.4 ms | 26.2 ms | 15.9× |
  | p95 | 751.0 ms | 34.4 ms | 21.8× |
  | Maximum | 773.2 ms | 37.9 ms | 20.4× |
  | Total for the sequential 35-character probe | 14.573 s | 0.918 s | 15.9× |

  **Median latency reduced 92.1% (~12.7× faster).** Both runs retained the same textarea. The before CPU profile is dominated by runtime/hosted-environment resolution; this work drops out of the after profile's hot functions. The probe waits for populated model options and a resolved model label, then warms input before measuring. This reproduces severe loaded-picker per-keystroke latency; it does not directly measure the originally reported 30-second native-keyboard queue.

  Patched JavaScript was substituted only in the isolated browser context. No running Gateway restart or served-file replacement occurred.
- **Earlier default-selection comparison (secondary):** Agent workspace + default GPT-6 Astra measured 42.15 → 20.75 ms median on the live catalog (66 characters). That easier configuration materially understated the reported issue; it is not the primary verification above.
- Regression tests fail against the unchanged implementation: **137 composer preparations for one published typing revision**, and **50 runtime resolutions for 50 unchanged reads**. With the fix: **one composer preparation per revision** and **no additional runtime resolutions for those reads**.
- Added coverage for in-place agent/default changes, explicit selection, catalog replacement/reset, stable textarea identity, and retained attachment callbacks reading current draft/lock state. The retained-callback test also fails when live getters are accidentally spread into snapshots.
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/new-session --maxWorkers=2`: **666 tests passed** across 58 files, including 15 Chromium browser tests.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, targeted oxlint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and isolated Vite production build passed. Oxlint retains one pre-existing structured-class warning on the page wrapper.
- Independent review: no actionable P0–P2 findings after addressing live-getter preservation.

- **CI follow-up:** run [38498023268](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38498023268) passed baseline ratchets, lint/types, performance and other selected checks but timed out in one sidebar catalog test. Integrated current main’s existing native-timer cleanup and per-file catalog clock isolation from #169835; no timeout increase or test assertion removal. The eight-test catalog suite also passes on the pinned Bun revision. The refreshed head passed [CI run 38499429638](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38499429638) and the separate security gates before merging.

No running Gateway was restarted and its served UI bundle was not replaced. Selected hosted PR CI checks passed before merging.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fix `/usage full` context-window formatting: 1,000,000 and 2,000,000 tokens now display as `1.0m` and `2.0m`, rather than `1000k` and `2000k`.

Thanks @yetval for reporting the mismatch and providing the original fix and regression tests. This revision retains those commits, resolves the conflict with main's shared numeric coercion, and limits the formatter change to million-token values. Existing sub-million formatting stays intact, including signed rounding (`-10500` remains `-10k`) and the sub-million boundary. No accounting, provider/model behavior, configuration, or delivery behavior changes.

## Evidence

Built and ran an isolated Gateway with synthetic OpenAI-compatible streaming responses. Through the shipped Gateway client and `chat.send` RPC, sent `/usage full` and a chat turn for each model, with normal outbound delivery to a local scripted IRC server. This exercises the real reply pipeline and captures the delivered footer bytes, not a direct renderer invocation. No live provider or production state was used.

Baseline: `344b71032447521feaff383f619667801dff6d83`. Built candidate: `d73f3a12a3f2e0ac09da320a0e3499425da4eb2b`, including the signed-rounding correction. The subsequent main merge fixes GitHub's comparison scope and leaves the formatter, tests, and documentation unchanged.

Captured output (synthetic channel; reply IDs omitted):

```text
BASE
```

prs.title: fix(active-memory): recall sub-agent receives huge prompt envelopes; bound recall context to 25K chars
prs.body:
Fixes #88077
Related: #92013

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Active Memory users on channel sessions with large runtime envelopes would see the blocking recall sub-agent ingest the full assembled `event.prompt` — observed in production at 29K-30K chars on ordinary Telegram group-topic turns (#88077) and at **609K-693K chars** with 30-second pre-prompt hook timeouts on long direct sessions (#92013) — even though the separate `memory_search` query was already clamped to ~480 chars. Every affected turn wasted tokens and added timeout/circuit-breaker risk inside a blocking hook.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildQuery` forwarded `latestUserMessage` (the raw `event.prompt`) unbounded into the recall sub-agent's conversation context in every `queryMode`. Two earlier attempts didn't land: #88078 strips the envelope down to a ~2K latest message (recall loses all conversation context), and #92099 was closed with a P1 for sourcing the current request from historical `event.messages` (stale current turn) plus adding a new config surface.

This fix keeps `event.prompt` as the only current-turn source and instead bounds the complete model-facing recall context to **25,000 UTF-16 chars** inside `buildQuery`, structure-aware:

- A generated context-engine envelope (`<conversation_context>…</conversation_context>` + `Current user request:`, the shape emitted by `extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-projection.ts`) is split: the **actual current user request is always preserved** (verbatim unless itself over budget), and only a **sanitized newest tail** of the context block fills the remaining budget — tool-call/tool-result traces, omitted-part placeholders, truncation markers, and envelope boilerplate are dropped.
- A channel inbound envelope keeps the whole `Current message:` section (including `[Replying to: …]` quoted-reply context) and a sanitized tail of the preceding metadata.
- A native reply-target block (`Reply target of current user message (untrusted, for context):`, producer `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts`) ahead of the projection envelope is preserved as bounded current-turn quote context.
- Unstructured oversized text is head-truncated UTF-16-safely with an explicit marker.
- The envelope split anchors on the projection's exact joint `\n</conversation_context>\n\nCurrent user request:\n` emission, so a request that QUOTES either marker (pasted transcript, hostile channel content) can never redirect the split and drop the real request — regression-tested.
- `queryMode: "recent"`/`"full"` use the extracted request as the latest message (recent turns already carry conversation context under their existing explicit budgets — no duplicated envelope), and the assembled output gets a final cap that keeps `Latest user message:` intact and drops the oldest turns first.
- The `memory_search` query is now seeded from the bounded request instead of the raw envelope head, and its 480-char clamp stays as defense in depth.
- Ordinary short prompts are character-for-character unchanged (beyond the pre-existing `.trim()`); no new config key — the 25K default matches the requested production behavior.
- Recall start logs gain ` queryCharsRaw=<n> queryBounded=true` when bounding engages (existing key=value logging convention; unbounded turns keep the existing compact line).

Explicitly **not** claimed fixed: the separate `memory_search` backend timeout — this PR only bounds what reaches the recall model and the search-query seed.

## User Impact

Active Memory users on Telegram/long direct sessions stop paying 600K-char recall prompts and their timeout/cost/latency risk in a blocking pre-prompt hook; recall keeps useful bounded recent context instead of losing it (the #88078 approach) or going stale (the #92099 approach). Operators see raw-vs-effective query sizes in the existing start log line when bounding occurs.

## Evidence

Real production observations (redacted; from the live gateway that motivated #92013 — `queryMode: "message"`, Telegram direct session):

```
[plugins] active-memory: ... start timeoutMs=30000 queryChars=609847 searchQueryChars=480
[plugins] active-memory: ... done status=timeout elapsedMs=30004 summaryChars=0
[plugins] active-memory: ... start timeoutMs=30000 queryChars=693210 searchQueryChars=480
[plugins] active-memory: ... done status=timeout elapsedMs=30011 summaryChars=0
```

**After-fix run from a real Active Memory gateway** (source gateway built from this branch, `openclaw gateway run` with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, a replica of the reporting operator's auth/state, memory-core slot with `text-embedding-3-large`; the same 620,391-char projection-envelope shape submitted as a real turn through the gateway's `/v1/responses` endpoint, which routes as a `webchat` session — redacted log lines, timestamps preserved):

```
2026-07-18T16:48:42.639-04:00 [plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:openresponses:e1fde2cb-… activeProvider=openai activeModel=gpt-5.4-mini thinking=off fast=inherit start timeoutMs=30000 queryChars=24680 queryCharsRaw=620391 queryBounded=true searchQueryChars=66
2026-07-18T16:49:01.938-04:00 [plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:openresponses:e1fde2cb-… done status=ok elapsedMs=19298 summaryChars=211
```

The 620,391-char raw prompt reaches the recall sub-agent as a 24,680-char bounded context (cap 25,000), the memory-tool query is the 66-char actual user request instead of the head of the envelope, and the recall **completes with a real memory summary** (`status=ok`, `summaryChars=211`) inside the 30s hook budget that production turns previously exhausted (`status=timeout elapsedMs=3000x` in the before logs above). The HTTP turn itself completed in ~52s end-to-end with the main model answering from the recalled facts.

Setup notes for reviewers: the run used the operator's real auth/state replica; their production 9,648-chunk memory index could not be reused directly because its index schema predates current main and memory-core correctly fails closed pending reindex (`OpenClaw version/index mismatch`), so recall-content proof used a freshly indexed memory file in the isolated workspace. Nothing on the operator's running installation was modified; the dev gateway ran on a separate port/state dir and was stopped after the runs.

Hook-level regression test mirrors the same shape (builds a >600K projection envelope and asserts the embedded recall prompt is <30K, contains the request, has no tool traces, and the start log carries `queryCharsRaw=6xxxxx queryBounded=true`).

Commands run locally (Linux source checkout, deps via `pnpm install`; remote proof backend unavailable in this environment, so trusted-source local fallback per AGENTS.md):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/active-memory/   # 4 files, 215 tests passed
pnpm tsgo:extensions                                        # clean
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test                                   # clean
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/active-memory/*.ts   # clean
pnpm format extensions/active-memory/... docs/...           # applied
git diff --check                                            # clean
```

New focused tests (`extensions/active-memory/query.test.ts`, 13 tests + 1 hook-level in `index.test.ts`): >600K generated conversation block bounded to the cap with the request preserved verbatim at the end; newest-tail retention with oldest content omitted; tool-call/tool-result/boilerplate removal; long pasted-document request bounded head-first; quoted-reply channel envelope preservation; UTF-16 surrogate-pair safety on giant emoji envelopes (lone-surrogate regex, works pre-ES2024 lib); recent-mode staleness guard (request comes from `event.prompt`, envelope not duplicated next to recent turns); full-mode overflow keeping `Latest user message:` intact; short-prompt no-op; under-cap full-mode byte-compat; reply-target block preservation; marker-injection (envelope markers quoted inside the request).

prs.title: fix(codex): keep native account models available after cold startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex-supported models can be missing from the model picker after a cold or changing account observation, while an unused OpenAI profile can hide native readiness.

## User Impact

A single transient empty or stale discovery no longer leaves native models unavailable; explicitly selected profiles and authored host routes keep their existing precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex catalog retries the paired model and account reads once when the raw list is empty or the captured account/config revision changes. The bounded retry is awaited inside the existing cancellation handler, so an indeterminate retry request retires its client. Native readiness can bypass only the presence of an unselected OpenAI profile for a native-owned row. Auth order, preferred or pinned profiles, and authored routes remain hard constraints.

## Integration

- Merge commit `89ccd73ac6672aaef218b2464d8a97bc721c2ab3` has prior A head `50712513e7aa979a15151a0190c52458ee8c9a78` as its first parent and official main `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54` as its second; the original published A head remains an ancestor. Follow-up commit `ddb44efe9187a3fef80f16cc7f164bd815ff1956` adds retry cancellation cleanup and its regression; `822378117bfad9c727a1fceed6edf45f7ac1f3e1` corrects that regression’s typed cancellation reason.
- The conflict resolution preserves main’s startup `account/read` before revision capture on each attempt and its per-entry authored-route cache, while retaining A’s one paired retry. Auth order, preferred/pinned profiles, endpoints, keys, route overrides, request parameters, and host-auth evaluations remain blockers.

## Evidence

- On the follow-up head, `pnpm test -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/model-catalog.test.ts` passed 17/17, including retry account/read cancellation coverage. `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` passed.
- Targeted Oxfmt and Oxlint passed on the two changed files; scoped `git diff --check` passed. No full build or full aggregate check was run.
- No authenticated native-account proof was run on this merged head. The linked Sep 27 canary is historical evidence from an older head only; it does not establish explicit-account isolation or rejection after revocation/reassignment before native execution. [Canary report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156491#issuecomment-5856964118)

Related: #156491

prs.title: fix(ui): keep child-session load errors compact and recover on reconnect
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Control UI users see a large technical error callout pushing sidebar sessions downward when child-session loading fails. A hidden main session can surface “child session list returned no result” directly below the Sessions heading.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a compact red indicator in the Sessions heading (or the expanded parent row), with text-only hover/focus details and a click/keyboard/touch-accessible popover containing Retry. Reuse the existing tooltip and popover owners; keep details out of list layout and reserve the row indicator’s hit area beside existing actions.

Also align child-load lifetime with the connection owner. `sessions.list()` returns null for disconnected or retired connection scopes; the paginator previously interpreted that as a missing-result failure because child generations were not retired at the socket boundary. Fence those loads on connection changes and avoid starting them while disconnected. Preserve retained rows, parent-scoped genuine failures, and explicit Retry behavior.

This cancellation mismatch is reproduced independently. The specific triggering event behind the reported production screenshot remains unproven; nearby successful requests do not establish that its child request succeeded, and a separate connection’s database error is not attributed to this incident.

## User Impact

- Session groups no longer move downward to make room for a child-load diagnostic.
- Hover/focus reveals details; click, Enter, or Space opens a labeled interactive popover with Retry focused. Escape and outside interaction dismiss it.
- Ordinary row controls remain separately clickable, including touch.
- Reconnection or client replacement no longer turns an intentionally retired child load into a sticky missing-result error.

## Evidence

- Original-controller cancellation regression fails with a latched per-parent error; fixed disconnect/client-replacement coverage passes.
- 375 focused tests passed across the full sidebar suite, child-snapshot freshness, child pagination, and session-roster refresh.
- 4 Chromium E2E cases passed: desktop (1440px) and touch/mobile (390px), each for hidden-main header and ordinary-parent row errors. They verify mouse/tap access, hover and genuine keyboard focus, Enter/Space, Escape focus restoration, outside-tap dismissal, exact parent-scoped Retry request count, recovered rows, and unchanged list bounds while details are open.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed: core-test and UI typechecks, i18n verification, formatting, guards, dead exports, changed-file lint and UI styles.
- UI bundled builds passed as part of Chromium E2E; `git diff --check` is clean.

No Gateway deployment, restart, service/config changes, or merge is included. Before/after synthetic browser captures are retained locally, but pixel inspection is blocked by the media-tool path boundary; do not treat those images as visually reviewed. The native autoreview harness was attempted but refused this environment’s proxy configuration; no safeguard or proxy setting was changed. Independent read-only reviews were performed, and the identified row-action overlap was repaired and covered by pointer/touch tests.

prs.title: fix(feishu): recognize images sent as files
prs.body:
## Summary
A Feishu or Lark user who sends a photo as a file (for example dragging a PNG into the chat as an attachment, or attaching it to a rich-text post as a file) delivers a `file` message or a post with top-level `files[]`. OpenClaw downloads the bytes, but the inbound media fact is always `kind: "document"`, so a vision-capable model gets zero image parts and cannot see the picture. This is the same defect #141292 fixed for Telegram and #165774 fixes for WhatsApp; Feishu kept the native-type-only classification. Related: #165778 (LINE).

## Root cause
`resolveFeishuMediaList` in `extensions/feishu/src/bot-content.ts` stamps every downloaded resource with the kind derived from the Feishu message type (`resolveFeishuMediaKind` maps `file` to `"document"`, and top-level post files are `"document"` too) and ignores the content type the media store sniffed from the downloaded bytes. Downstream, the shared media facts treat an explicit kind as authoritative, so `detectAndLoadPromptImages` skips the attachment.

before:
```ts
out.push({ path: saved.path, contentType: saved.contentType, kind: resource.kind });
```

## Fix
after:
```ts
out.push({
  path: saved.path,
  contentType: saved.contentType,
  kind:
    resource.kind === "document" && saved.contentType?.startsWith("image/")
      ? "image"
      : resource.kind,
});
```

`saved.contentType` comes from the shared media store (`saveMediaStream` via `saveMessageResourceFeishu`), which sniffs the bytes, the same signal the Telegram fix uses. Real PDFs and other files stay documents, and PDF bytes served with an image content type also stay a document. Image, audio and video messages, inline post media, and the download-failure placeholder are unchanged.

## Why this is the right boundary
`resolveFeishuMediaList` is the single place Feishu turns message resources into media facts, for both standalone `file` messages and post attachments, so one check covers both. The shared explicit-kind precedence in core stays as is, matching #141292 and #165774, which also fixed this at the channel's media resolver.

## Verification
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/bot-content.file-media-kind.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot-content.media.test.ts`: 10 passed.
- New `bot-content.file-media-kind.test.ts` drives the real Lark SDK client, the real auth exchange and the real media store against a loopback Feishu API. With the production file reverted to origin/main, the PNG file case and the PNG post-file case fail and the PDF cases pass on both.
- `oxfmt --check` on the changed files: clean.
- tsgo, oxlint and a full build were not run locally (left to CI).

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a Feishu image sent as a file reaches the agent as a document, so a vision model receives no image part for it.
Real environment tested: real `resolveFeishuMediaList` with the real Lark SDK client (tenant token exchange plus `GET /open-apis/im/v1/messages/{id}/resources/{file_key}?type=file`) over real HTTP, streaming into the real media store in a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, the real `toInboundMediaFactsWithMetadata` projection used by Feishu inbound dispatch, and the real embedded-runner `detectAndLoadPromptImages` with an image-capable model. The only stand-in is a local HTTP server configured as the account `domain` in place of open.feishu.cn, serving the bytes as `application/octet-stream`. Run on pristine main 988345fb91a and on this patch (head a7fe977fe14).
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `WT=$PWD ./node_modules/.bin/tsx proof.mts`, which delivers a Feishu `file` message carrying PNG bytes (`IMG_2041.png`) and a PDF control (`invoice.pdf`), and prints the saved content type, the agent fact kind and the native image part count.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 988345fb91a)
Feishu file message IMG_2041.png (photo sent as file), 70 bytes via GET /open-apis/im/v1/messages/om_proof/resources/file_v3_photo?type=file
  saved contentType=image/png
  agent fact kind=document -> native image parts for vision model: 0
Feishu file message invoice.pdf (pdf control), 48 bytes via GET /open-apis/im/v1/messages/om_proof/resources/file_v3_pdf?type=file
  saved contentType=application/pdf
  agent fact kind=document -> native image parts for vision model: 0
# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
Feishu file message IMG_2041.png (photo sent as file), 70 bytes via GET /open-apis/im/v1/messages/om_proof/resources/file_v3_photo?type=file
  saved contentType=image/png
  agent fact kind=image -> native image parts for vision model: 1
Feishu file message invoice.pdf (pdf control), 48 bytes via GET /open-apis/im/v1/messages/om_proof/resources/file_v3_pdf?type=file
  saved contentType=application/pdf
  agent fact kind=document -> native image parts for vision model: 0
```
Observed result after fix: the image sent as a Feishu file now becomes one native image part for the vision model, while the PDF control stays a document with no image part.
What was not tested: no live Feishu or Lark tenant or live model request; JPEG and HEIC files were not exercised separately.

prs.title: fix(feishu): return complete Bitable metadata
prs.body:
Supersedes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/117455 while leaving that contributor PR open. Original repair and authorship are credited to @steipete; exact head `fd310f0d17bfe7cb8a7eedae70b969fbcc798917` retains Peter Steinberger as commit author.

## What This Solves

Feishu Bitable table discovery and field listing previously returned only the first provider page. This repair uses one bounded Feishu-local collector for both metadata operations, preserves opaque continuation tokens exactly, rejects blank or repeated cursors, caps pagination at 100 requests, and fails the whole operation on later-page provider or transport errors. The tool schemas were mechanically moved into a private `bitable-schema.ts` module; no public export was added.

## Reviewed State

- Reviewed base: `ea1233bb131fb8d93ae86871f51ddfb8b21e09f5`.
- Exact head: `fd310f0d17bfe7cb8a7eedae70b969fbcc798917`.
- At `2026-09-05T07:30:49Z`, exact main was `9a6a97f8b72ec17c330d281fb12160e29d5719f0`. Main had no changes to the three owned Feishu Bitable paths since the reviewed base, and the merge-tree had no conflict.
- Production diff: raw `+156/-114`, net `+42`. Of the additions, 83 lines are the mechanical move of existing private schemas/constants into `bitable-schema.ts`; the remaining change owns bounded, fail-closed pagination and registration wiring. Tests add `+204`.

## Dependency Contract

Direct inspection of installed `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.73.0` runtime source confirmed that `appTable.list()` and `appTableField.list()` pass caller parameters to `httpInstance.request()` and rethrow request errors. Their `listWithIterator()` variants catch and log request errors without rethrowing; the iterator can yield `null` and stop. The direct `list()` APIs are therefore required for complete-or-error behavior.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix red proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33947809514 — `8 failed / 13 passed`.
- Exact-head Testbox proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33949922768, lease `tbx_01m1r42r8nt8zvgh5mt9hzr8sw` — `47/47` focused tests, `5/5` changed-gate contract tests, and all 25 planned checks passed.
- Formal autoreview exited `0`: scoped-clean through P0-P2, confidence `0.97`.
- Exact-head native CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33950483310 — attempt 2 succeeded. Attempt 1 had two unrelated flakes in unchanged owner paths; both passed the single failed-jobs-only rerun.
- Codex source was inspected directly at `codex-rs/core/src/session/mcp.rs`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/mcp.rs`, and `codex-rs/protocol/src/capabilities.rs`. This repair does not depend on Codex runtime or protocol behavior.

## Mandatory Blocker

No disposable authenticated Feishu/Lark credential exists in the operator surfaces available for this work: operator config, ambient environment, or repository, organization, and environment secrets/variables. Authenticated runtime proof for pagination beyond 100 fields and for table-list denial therefore cannot be performed.

The deterministic regression tests are not live provider proof. This PR remains draft and must not merge until that evidence gap is resolved or explicitly accepted by a maintainer.
