prs.title: feat: verify updates after a normal heartbeat cycle
prs.body:
# OpenClaw PR: post-update normal-cycle verification

## Base

- Repository: `openclaw/openclaw`
- Base commit: `4d2617d425ab247a2f55a18523da8cc6a483746c`
- PR head: `93ee3dbed06efb1051452ea0540765507267bd02`
- Package version: `2026.9.8`

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway readiness immediately after an update is not sufficient evidence that the running installation can survive its ordinary scheduled heartbeat path. Scheduled interval heartbeats need a normal-cycle receipt, persisted through the canonical state worker, while bounded diagnostics must not evict required verification failures.

## Summary

This patch adds:

- bounded generic verification checks with `pass`, `fail`, `unknown`, and `skipped` states;
- a durable `normalCycle` receipt on the update ledger;
- a heartbeat scheduler callback after successful broadcast and targeted scheduled interval cycles;
- worker-backed read and mutation paths for normal-cycle receipt persistence;
- retention of required verification checks when optional diagnostics exceed the bound;
- automatic promotion of the latest recent, core-verified successful update run after that cycle.

The contract is additive: legacy ledgers remain readable, the existing readiness confirmation contract is unchanged, and subsystem-specific adapters remain out of scope.

## Evidence

All evidence below was run against the exact PR head `93ee3dbed` in isolated state directories.

- Focused update-ledger, normal-cycle, verification-retention, heartbeat scheduler, and Gateway lifecycle tests: **93/93 passed**.
- A real Gateway E2E proof passed **1/1** through the production activation path. It started `activateGatewayScheduledServices`, exercised the real `runHeartbeatOnce` path with a loopback OpenAI Responses provider, issued a scheduled interval wake with `source=interval` and `intent=scheduled`, and verified `scheduledHeartbeat.status=ran` plus a persisted `verification.normalCycle.status=pass` read back from the update ledger.
- The E2E proof used an isolated proof-only assertion harness layered onto the existing Gateway routing test; it did not use the operator Gateway, external providers, or production state.
- The focused worker-backed tests separately verify fresh-state promotion, state-worker persistence, race re-checks, bounded required-check retention, and legacy reader behavior.
- `git diff --check`, changed-file formatting/lint checks, and the earlier 35/35 normal-cycle verification set passed on this head.

## Compatibility and upgrade target

- Stable `2026.9.8` is already present in `scripts/lib/update-compat-inventory.json` with its recorded integrity and chunks.
- The general `pnpm update:compat:check` currently reports only that the moving npm `beta` tag has advanced to `2026.10.1-beta.1`. That beta is intentionally not added here and is not the requested upgrade target.
- The requested local upgrade target is stable `2026.9.8`.

## Review request

Please accept the additive `normalCycle` receipt and bounded verification-check contract. Legacy ledgers remain readable, required verification facts are retained, and the existing readiness confirmation contract remains unchanged. The production-path and compatibility evidence above is attached for maintainer review.

## Non-goals

- No automatic repair or in-place rebuild.
- No automatic application rollback.
- No new parallel definition of Gateway readiness.
- No Gaia-specific memory paths or provider outage handling in the production contract.

## Historical-ledger compatibility evidence
Rechecked against exact PR head `93ee3dbed06efb1051452ea0540765507267bd02` on 2026-10-06:

- The exact-head repository runner passed 4 focused infra test files with **76/76 tests passed**, including the reader, ledger, normal-cycle, and heartbeat-scheduler coverage.
- The verification-contract suite passed **5/5 tests**.
- A temporary exact-head compatibility test seeded a finished successful update row with pre-upgrade `verification_json` (without `normalCycle`), read it through the current reader, added the normal-cycle receipt, and read the result back. It passed 1/1.
- Result: the legacy `serviceRunning`, `versionMatch`, `settled`, `readyz`, `channelsReady`, and `pluginErrors` fields remained unchanged; `normalCycle={status:"pass",observedAtMs:11000}` was added; the same run remained `status=succeeded` and `phase=finished`.

This is compatibility evidence for the exact PR head. Maintainer acceptance of the public and durable contract remains a maintainer decision.

prs.title: feat(elevenlabs): speak with Eleven v4 models
prs.body:
Closes #165655

## What Problem This Solves

Spoken replies fail when the ElevenLabs model is Eleven v4 or Eleven v4 Turbo, because those models are rejected by the text-to-speech endpoint.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can set `eleven_v4_turbo` for low-latency agent speech, or `eleven_v4` for narration. Phone calls that use ElevenLabs keep one dialogue socket for the call, so later lines keep the scene. Existing installs stay on `eleven_multilingual_v2`. Flash, Multilingual, and `eleven_v3` stay on text-to-speech.

## Why This Change Was Made

`eleven_v4`, `eleven_v4_turbo`, and `eleven_v3_conversational` speak over the Text to Dialogue WebSocket. A conversation id reuses that socket for the call. Aborting synthesis closes it, which is how interruption works on this API. The socket sends a keepalive while the conversation is idle and closes after 10 minutes without another utterance. Dialogue models use the `stability` voice setting only. The API key stays in the request header.

## Evidence

Focused extension tests on Node 24.21.0:

- `pnpm test:extension elevenlabs`: 7 files, 91 tests passed.
- `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 53 files, 622 tests passed.

The new tests cover model routing, the dialogue socket protocol, conversation reuse, interruption, abort, keepalive, idle close, pool eviction, and the voice-call override that passes the call id. The live ElevenLabs test stays skipped unless `ELEVENLABS_LIVE_TEST` is set.

prs.title: fix(ios): avoid background termination during gateway disconnect
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes a credential-database access from the operator disconnect path implicated in iOS background `RUNNINGBOARD 0xdead10cc` terminations.

## User Impact

Backgrounding the app no longer reloads saved operator credentials during this disconnect callback. Admin controls lose authority on disconnect and regain it from the current saved scopes on reconnect. Saved credentials are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

`setOperatorConnected(false)` refreshed admin scope from `DeviceAuthStore`, whose store admission opens a SQLite write transaction. The disconnect callback can arrive after the background grace task ends. Clear the cached grant on every disconnect and read saved scope only when connecting.

## Evidence

Paired, detached iPhone 17 Pro Simulator runs on iOS 26.5, with the same isolated loopback gateway and diagnostic probe:

| Observation | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reported teardown stack after background grace | Real `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` acquired 13.560 ms after the task ended | Same background grace/disconnect transition; no matching transaction |
| Independent writer during the bounded probe | `SQLITE_BUSY`, 5/5 observations over 8 seconds | Available, 16/16 observations over 30 seconds |
| Disconnect clears admin authority | Regression fails | Passes; persisted token survives, reconnect restores current scopes |
| Disconnect leaves credential storage untouched | Regression fails: creates database | Passes, including repeated disconnect |

The temporary probe delayed an already-acquired transaction for 30 seconds only when the stack matched `DeviceAuthStore.loadToken → refreshOperatorAdminScopeFromStore → setOperatorConnected → invalidateOperatorTalkRoute → handleOperatorGatewayRouteInvalidated`. It did not create the transaction or kill the app. Both runs resumed Online. The probe and its build wiring are excluded from this PR.

**Limit:** the unsafe lock condition was reproduced; the OS termination was not. RunningBoard logged that it ignores suspension for simulated processes with background audio capabilities. The reports came from physical iOS 26.6.2 devices; that runtime was absent from Apple's available Simulator catalog. This change removes the demonstrated teardown path, not every possible background SQLite access.

**Review follow-up:** ClawSweeper found no introduced correctness defect at `5fb5097e27c3` and requested physical-iPhone background/reconnect evidence before merge. That proof remains outstanding; the Simulator result is not presented as a substitute for device OS enforcement.

- Baseline owner suite: 259 tests in 41.942s; both new regressions failed for the intended reasons, 256 passed, and one existing source-inspection test failed with host Documents access denied (`NSCocoaErrorDomain 257` / `EPERM`). This unrelated fixture failure remains disclosed; it is not claimed fixed.
- Candidate: 6 tests in 4 suites passed in 0.481s test execution (24.205s Xcode test session): the two regressions, stored gateway scopes, dashboard access, retained bridge authority invalidation, and chat reconnect ownership. Initial selectors that selected zero tests were excluded from evidence.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- apps/ios/Sources/Model/NodeAppModel.swift apps/ios/Tests/NodeAppModelInvokeTests.swift`: passed, including Swift lint across 477 files.
- Independent AutoReview on the final diff: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized measured output</summary>


prs.body: Closes #141184 ## What Problem This Solves The iOS chat composer occupies a large fixed footer, preventing messages from flowing behind Liquid Glass. Connection and loading indicators compete with the conversation, and ordinary session actions look destructive. ## Why This Change Was Made Use a compact floating composer with measured trailing transcript space, native menus, and quieter navigation while preserving the existing red/gray palette, typography, attachments, and voice controls. The composer overlays the transcript instead of reducing its viewport. Upstream’s session-bound, one-shot scroll commands handle sending and jumping to the latest reply without retaining row-ID scroll constraints. Shared presentation helpers keep loading and connection chrome consistent. ## User Impact - Messages scroll behind the composer; multiline drafts grow naturally, and the latest reply remains reachable above the input. - Attachments come first in the options menu. Model, effort, context, and permission controls retain their capability restrictions and use catalog-compatible localized labels. - Selected model options remain visible to accessibility. The macOS model menu retains its sign-in action when no models are available. - Ordinary session actions use standard colors; Delete remains destructive. Unread indicators are neutral, and rows announce unread/pinned state. - Overview keeps its toolbar reachable, uses quieter counters, and opens Usage from Tokens. Small sidebar and onboarding controls meet 44-point touch targets. Reduce Motion is respected. - Upstream’s persistent iOS chat owner, gateway switcher, session attention controls, and desktop styling are preserved. ## Evidence October 12 update integrates upstream `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54`, retaining its live-reply deduplication, deferred menus, compact-width avatar treatment, session-bound scroll commands, and operator/node connection distinction. Removed the unused chat-layout parameter reported by shared dead-code CI. The previously blocked keyboard/history flow reproduced on the integrated candidate: after a multiline send, the app consumed a full CPU core in SwiftUI `LazySubviewPlacements`. Ungrouped transcript content now has one stable layout container per lazy-stack child, preserving row IDs and spacing. The unchanged keyboard/history test passes after this repair; assertions were not weakened. Local validation on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.2 with Xcode 27: - 106 iOS tests in six suites pass, including the latest upstream connection/reconnect regressions, sidebar, and typography. - 39 shared chat tests in five suites pass; shared macOS and iOS simulator builds pass. - The full keyboard/history test passes three times after the fix, covering keyboard opening, typing, sending, preserved history position, multiline anchored replies, and jumping back to the latest reply. - Composer/options sizing, restored session history, long-press actions, and Overview/Usage navigation UI tests pass. - Native lint/formatting, localization verification, and `git diff --check` pass (existing test-file length warnings remain). - Interaction proof used layout fix `5fc55fcc218`; the final `66f8e6bb317` integration adds only upstream’s connection-state changes to the native code, validated by the 106-test run. Shared transcript/composer code is identical. No new tests or CI jobs were added; the existing keyboard/history regression supplies the before/after proof. Independent reviews of the full integration and the focused layout repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Hosted CI on the pushed head remains separate from this local evidence. Current synthetic screenshots show keyboard-visible content and preservation of the reader’s position: | Typing | Reading older history | | --- | --- | | | | Original before/after layout comparison: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | These original layout captures use synthetic data on the same simulator. The baseline fixture’s model label was normalized for publication; its layout is unchanged. Physical-device, iPad, largest Dynamic Type, and macOS visual comparisons remain unverified. Shared macOS compilation and chat tests are covered. Maintainer product acceptance of the floating composer and placement of advanced controls is still pending.

- Compare the user-visible rendered `/btw` reply before suppressing already-sent follow-up text.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): reuse the live runtime for gateway commands
prs.body:
Closes #159142

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `voice-call` gateway command can stop or fail against the runtime that is serving a live call, because the command service is bound to the generation captured when the plugin registered rather than to the runtime currently running.

## User Impact

User impact: read and control commands act on the live call's runtime and no longer risk terminating an active call when the runtime generation has changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command service was created with the registration-time `ensureRuntime`, so when the coordinator slot is owned by a different (e.g. reloaded) generation a command would retire the live runtime or throw a lifecycle error. The command service now reuses the coordinator's live runtime whenever its slot is `running`, and falls back to `ensureRuntime()` only when there is no running runtime.

## Evidence

Grounded in `extensions/voice-call/index.ts`: `createVoiceCallCommandService(ensureRuntime)` vs `ensureRuntimeForGeneration`'s `slot.owner !== runtimeGeneration` check. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passes on the branch.


## Review response

Reworked on head `f022c39a` in response to the review:

- **A disabled/invalid registration must not act through a predecessor's live runtime.** `assertRuntimePolicy()` is now extracted from `ensureRuntimeForGeneration` and applied in `ensureRuntimeForCommands` *before* selecting a live runtime. A reload that disabled voice calling, or that has an invalid provider configuration, can therefore no longer issue commands through a predecessor's still-running runtime.

Test added (green):
- `rejects a disabled registration before reusing the predecessor's live runtime`

Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/voice-call/index.lifecycle.test.ts -t "reusing the predecessor"` — observed `1 passed | 9 skipped`.

`pnpm tsgo:extensions` passes on the branch.


## Review response

CI `check-lint-core-2` failed on the command-runtime reuse change: oxlint `curly` flagged the single-statement early return `if (liveSlot && liveSlot.state === "running") return liveSlot.runtime;`.

Fixed in `3db5eecb` — expanded to a braced block; no behavior change.

- Lint: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/voice-call/index.ts` → `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.`
- Types: `pnpm tsgo:extensions` → exit 0


## Review response

Reworked on head `e7f9fd6` in response to the two P1 findings:

- **Reject superseded handlers before call I/O.** Command handlers now assert the live coordinator registration — not a generation snapshot captured when the runtime access was created — immediately before each manager/webhook effect, including after the awaited `getCallFromMemoryOrStore` lookup and inside the deferred `prepareContinue().run()`. A superseded or retired registration is rejected with a lifecycle error before any call I/O.
- **Use the current configuration when starting a new call.** `voicecall.initiate` routes through the current registration's runtime, so a reload starts new calls with the new provider configuration instead of a predecessor's stale runtime/config. Existing-call control still resolves to the live slot that owns the call.

Tests added (green):
- `rejects superseded retained handlers before call I/O and after an awaited lookup`
- `starts a new call with the current registration config after reload`

Evidence: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/voice-call/index.lifecycle.test.ts` → `Tests 12 passed (12)`; `[test] passed 1 Vitest shard`.

prs.title: feat(mcp): per-request header provider for volatile turn attribution on OpenClaw-owned HTTP transports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Per-turn MCP attribution currently has to enter declarative server headers or the connection resolver. Declarative header changes invalidate the catalog; the reported Reef production measurement was **221 re-catalogs across 222 runs**. The existing connection resolver caches requester credentials for five minutes, and changed resolved headers rotate the connection. Neither path can provide fresh turn attribution while retaining a transport and its catalog.

This adds a separate plugin request-header provider for OpenClaw-owned MCP HTTP transports. Upstream main was checked at `7aaef70932b30f4d7410ae00aa65b07089de2ce0`; no equivalent provider existed.

**Deployment consumer.** The Reef embedder plugin (the same production deployment behind the measurement above) adopts this provider on release adoption: it moves `traceparent` and signed per-turn context headers off declarative server configuration and onto this seam, which retires the measured per-run re-catalog. Requester authentication stays entirely on the existing connection-resolver contract — this consumer sends attribution and turn-scoped credentials only, and its stable credentials are unchanged.

## User Impact

Plugins can attach `traceparent`, signed turn credentials, and optional direct-request credentials to individual MCP requests without rebuilding the catalog or connection. Stable authentication remains in static server configuration or the existing connection resolver.

The SDK infrastructure documentation includes registration and embedded-runtime usage. This contract covers OpenClaw-owned HTTP transports; external harness-native MCP clients need OpenClaw materialized tools to use it.

## Design

- Add `api.registerMcpServerRequestHeaderProvider({ serverName, resolve })`, following connection-resolver registration conventions. Resolver and header-provider registrations share per-server plugin ownership, and the connection resolver is authoritative regardless of registration order: a foreign provider is rejected when the resolver already exists and displaced (removed, error diagnostic on the provider's plugin) when the resolver registers later. Registry state is identical in both orders, so a declared server with a resolver is never partitioned as static.
- Only the host binds run identity. The embedded backend binds MCP attribution to the admitted run's actual `sessionId`/`sessionKey`/`runId` (internal `bindMcpRequestRun`), and the binding is revoked when that run settles. A context the host did not issue (forged) or whose run has settled (stale/reassigned) is dropped: the provider is not called and no volatile headers are sent. The public export from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` is `runWithMcpRequestMetadata(metadata, callback)` — caller tracing metadata only (e.g. `traceparent`), never identity.
- Capture only MCP attribution when materializing tools. Each retained tool/resource/prompt executor opens its own operation scope, preserving attribution under overlapping acquisitions and calls without capturing unrelated cancellation or runtime authority.
- Resolve volatile headers immediately before actual guarded HTTP fetches, including same-origin redirects and authentication/RPC retries. Streamable HTTP and SSE POST/EventSource paths share this boundary. Header values never enter server configuration, catalog identity, or the resolver rotation digest.
- Keep configured headers, authentication, and MCP protocol fields authoritative. Scope provider headers to the configured origin; register returned values and bare bearer tokens for secret redaction. Bound provider resolution to ten seconds and report provider failures without exposing plugin error contents.

## Correctness

Each operation owns an immutable context. Missing context explicitly clears inherited attribution and skips the provider. No transport stores a mutable latest-turn header map. Provider results are freshly merged into a new request header object and are not retained for redirect replay.

Initial SSE discovery can carry its discovery context. Shared streamable notification GETs and legacy SSE reconnects carry no volatile attribution. The streamable initialized-notification send has a short-lived scope so its shared stream parser and reconnect timers cannot retain the opening turn, including reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`. Resumable RPC streams retain their own still-active operation context. Completed scopes cannot supply headers to background callbacks.

Static authentication, requester credential revalidation/rotation, genuine configuration invalidation, `tools/list_changed`, and transport-close recovery retain their existing owners and behavior.

## Evidence

### Guarded caller-authority revalidation (Rev 24 P1, head `34a4b55ad`)

**Defect (ClawSweeper Rev 24).** `fetchWithSsrFGuard` asserts the captured guarded caller authority (`captureGuardedFetchRequestAuthority`, e.g. a live cron-root claim) *before* invoking the transport `fetchImpl`. The header wrapper is that `fetchImpl` and awaits `provider.resolve()`, so authority revoked during resolution was not re-checked before stable credentials and volatile headers reached the server.

**Fix.** `withMcpRequestHeaders` captures the guarded assertion on entry and re-asserts it immediately before dispatch, alongside the existing abort and run-context checks. A revoked caller gets the assertion's own error, and no request is sent.

**Final-effect proof.** The real-runtime e2e adds a call under `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` whose MCP run stays active. Caller authority is revoked while the provider is resolving. The call is rejected, and the recording loopback server's request count is unchanged (no request for `revoked_authority_operation`). **Regression-before-repair:** with the re-assertion removed, the same scenario fails with `promise resolved "{ content: [ ... ] }" instead of rejecting`, meaning the real server received and answered the revoked call. A matching unit case (`mcp-request-headers.test.ts`) fails without the fix and passes with it.

Redacted terminal capture (`OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`):

```text
[pr154043-proof] allowed: real tools/call arrived with volatile header present
[pr154043-proof] canceled: rejected before I/O, server request count unchanged; pending send settled
[pr154043-proof] shared transport: subsequent attributed tools/call succeeded
[pr154043-proof] foreign: forged and SDK-asserted identity reached the server unsigned; provider never saw victim-run
[pr154043-proof] reassigned: settled run's captured context reached the server unsigned; provider never saw it
[pr154043-proof] revoked authority: provider resolved, caller authority revoked mid-resolution; rejected before I/O, server request count unchanged
 ✓ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts > PR #154043 real runtime proof > dispatches attributed calls and rejects canceled calls before HTTP I/O
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

At this head: focused suites 8 files / 156 tests passed; core `tsgo` passed; timeout-race ratchet clean for PR files; formatting and lint clean.

### Run-identity authority + final-I/O proof (Rev 22 security item, head `a6194b291`)

**Concern (ClawSweeper Rev 22).** The public `runWithMcpRequestContext` accepted caller-supplied `sessionId`/`runId`, and the documented provider signs those IDs, so a caller could assert a foreign run and obtain a signed header at final HTTP I/O. A captured context also stayed usable after its run settled.

**Fix — bind signed identity to admitted runs (the recommended option).**
- Identity is issued only by the host: `runEmbeddedAttemptWithBackend` calls the internal `bindMcpRequestRun` with the admitted run's identity, keeping enclosing caller metadata.
- Each issued context carries run authority that is revoked when the run settles. `getMcpRequestContext()` returns nothing for a revoked or never-issued context, so the provider is never invoked for it. A run that settles while headers resolve is refused before dispatch by the existing `MCP request context expired` check.
- The public SDK export narrows to `runWithMcpRequestMetadata` (metadata only). Plugins and embedded callers can no longer name a session or run.

**Final-effect proof.** `test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts` now also drives, on the same real MCP SDK client + guarded streamable-HTTP transport + recording loopback server:
- **Foreign:** a forged frozen context `{ runId: "victim-run" }` and the public SDK helper each reach the server with **no** attribution header; the provider never sees `victim-run`.
- **Reassigned/settled:** a context captured inside a run that has since settled reaches the server with **no** attribution header; the provider never sees it.

**Regression-before-repair.** With the old trust semantics temporarily restored (any context accepted, no revocation), the proof fails at final I/O. The server received a signed header for the forged run:

```text
- Expected
+ Received
  {
-   "attribution": undefined,
+   "attribution": "synthetic-victim-run",
    "rpcMethod": "tools/call",
  }
 ❯ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts:193:75
```

```text
[pr154043-proof] allowed: real tools/call arrived with volatile header present
[pr154043-proof] canceled: rejected before I/O, server request count unchanged; pending send settled
[pr154043-proof] shared transport: subsequent attributed tools/call succeeded
[pr154043-proof] foreign: forged and SDK-asserted identity reached the server unsigned; provider never saw victim-run
[pr154043-proof] reassigned: settled run's captured context reached the server unsigned; provider never saw it
 ✓ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts > PR #154043 real runtime proof > dispatches attributed calls and rejects canceled calls before HTTP I/O 61ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Unit coverage (`src/agents/mcp-request-headers.test.ts`) adds: forged identity never resolves headers, captured context revoked after its run settles, and a run settling mid-resolution refuses dispatch. `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.request-headers.test.ts` now holds each turn open across acquisition and execution, as a host run does, and asserts that a settled turn's executor sends no attribution. On the merged head (current main `3f7689e64`): focused suites (`mcp-request-headers`, `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime{,.request-headers}`, `mcp-transport`, `mcp-http-transport`, `mcp-http-fetch`, `backend`, requester-connect, `registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers`) 10 files / 159 tests passed; both PR e2e proofs passed; core `tsgo` passed; `plugin-sdk:surface:check` passed (budget pinned to exactly this PR's two exports); formatting and lint clean. The merge resolved main's `mcp-http-fetch.ts` redirect-policy refactor by applying the provider wrap inside the shared builder.

### Registration-order fix + authority-chain proof (head `2587f4f3`)

**Defect (ClawSweeper P1, Rev 8).** `hasMcpServerOwnerConflict` was first-registration-wins across both seams: a request-header provider registered first by plugin A caused plugin B's later `registerMcpServerConnectionResolver` for the same server to be rejected. `partitionMcpServersByConnectionScope` then found no resolver and classified the declared server as **static**, exposing its configured connection to requesters the resolver would have excluded. The PR's own registrar test pinned that behavior.

**Fix.** The connection resolver is authoritative regardless of order. `registerMcpServerConnectionResolver` still fails closed against a different plugin's resolver; against a different plugin's *provider* it now displaces it — the provider entry is removed and an error diagnostic is reported on the provider's plugin (`MCP server request header provider for "<name>" displaced: connection resolver registered by plugin "<resolver plugin>" owns requester admission`). `registerMcpServerRequestHeaderProvider` is unchanged (rejected when a different plugin owns either seam). Final registry state is identical in both registration orders. `docs/plugins/sdk-overview/infrastructure.md` states the rule.

**Regression proof, unit** (`src/plugins/registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers.test.ts`, `it.each(["provider","resolver"])`): with the registrar fix reverted, the provider-first case fails —

```text
AssertionError: expected [ { level: 'error', …(3) } ] to deep equally contain ObjectContaining{…}

- Expected:
ObjectContaining {
  "level": "error",
  "message": StringContaining "displaced",
  "pluginId": "plugin-a",
}

+ Received:
[
  {
    "level": "error",
    "message": "MCP server connection resolver for \"user-mail\" rejected: already registered by plugin \"plugin-a\"",
    "pluginId": "plugin-b",
    "source": "/plugins/plugin-b/index.ts",
  },
]
```

— and passes with the fix (5/5). Both orders additionally assert, under `withPluginRuntimeRegistryScope`, that `partitionMcpServersByConnectionScope` puts `user-mail` in `resolverRequesterServerNames` and `staticServers` is empty.

**Authority-chain proof, real transports** (`test/pr154043-registration-order-proof.e2e.test.ts`, no transport/SDK mocks). plugin-a registers a request-header provider for `user-mail`; plugin-b registers a requester-scoped connection resolver that returns `{ url: <loopback>, headers: { Authorization: "Bearer proof-token" } }` only for `allowed-requester` and `null` otherwise. The declared config is `url: "https://placeholder.invalid/mcp"`; the loopback (`startRequesterScopedMcpProofServer`) 404s without the bearer and records every request. Driven through `materializeRequesterScopedMcpToolsForHarnessRun` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`. In **both** orders: `user-mail` partitions as resolver-scoped, never static; the allowed requester materializes tools and executes `requester_probe`, and every loopback request carried the bearer and none carried plugin-a's header; an excluded requester and a run with no `requesterSenderId` get no tools and the loopback request count does not move; plugin-a's provider is never invoked.

With the registrar fix reverted, the provider-first case fails at the static-partition assertion (the exact exposure):

```text

- Expected
+ Received

- {}
+ {
+   "user-mail": {
+     "transport": "streamable-http",
+     "url": "https://placeholder.invalid/mcp",
+   },
+ }

 ❯ test/pr154043-registration-order-proof.e2e.test.ts:69
```

Verification at this head: core `tsgo` 0 errors; unit batch (`agent-bundle-mcp-runtime`, `backend`, `mcp-http-transport`, `mcp-request-headers`, `mcp-transport`, `registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers`, `mcp-connection-resolver`) 7 files / 193 passed; `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.request-headers` 2 passed; e2e proofs 2 files / 3 passed; `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` 16 passed; `pnpm config:docs:check` OK; full `pnpm lint` (core + extensions) passed; `pnpm check:changed` green through the SDK surface budget, plugin boundaries, wrapper shadowing and core typecheck (the only failure, `typecheck core tests`, is two `assertReliabilityForcedExit` import errors in `src/infra/package-update-activation-*.test.ts`, present on untouched upstream main).

### Cancellation lifecycle fix + real-runtime proof (head `15fdd821`)

The prior head had a defect at the dispatch boundary: an operation canceled while `provider.resolve()` was awaited settles its attribution scope, and the fallback then forwarded the request **without** volatile headers on the retained transport — final I/O after cancellation, under stable connection credentials. The dispatch point now rejects an expired attributed operation with a content-free error instead of falling back; the shared-transport abort check is unchanged. Regression-before-repair was verified both ways: the new unit case fails on the old expression (fetch dispatches), and temporarily restoring the old expression makes the runtime proof's server-request-count assertion fail (expected 5, received 6).

`test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts` drives the real transport path — `resolveMcpTransport` + the real MCP SDK `Client` over streamable HTTP against a loopback server that records every request it receives, with synthetic attribution and no real credentials. ### Original evidence (unchanged)

- Real HTTP and SSE tests send two distinct contexts through **one retained runtime/transport**, overlap acquisitions and asynchronous header resolution, execute retained tools in reverse completion order, and invoke a contextless tool under an unrelated ambient context. Wire assertions cover discovery headers, distinct turn credentials, unchanged static authorization, unchanged fingerprint, and exactly one initialize/tools-list cycle.

- Transport tests cover per-hop header refresh, cross-origin stripping, initial SSE discovery, contextless EventSource reconnects, notification reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`, and attributed RPC resumptions.
- Provider/backend/registry tests cover copied immutable metadata, context expiration and clearing, secret registration, bounded failures, network error preservation, host identity binding, and registration ownership.

prs.title: docs+tests: migrate MCP fetch server example from npx to uvx
prs.body:
## Summary

Aligns the docs and test fixtures around the current `uvx mcp-server-fetch` invocation. The legacy `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch` package was removed from npm and now returns 404, so any config that still references it triggers `[bundle-mcp] failed to start server "fetch"` on every gateway start and shows up as an error-level `core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas` finding — drowning out real diagnostics.

## Changes

- **`docs/gateway/config-extensions.md`** — added a migration note above the Fetch example pointing users to `uvx mcp-server-fetch` when they hit the legacy `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch` package, with a cross-reference to the original bug report (#141180). The note also names common saved MCP entry names (`fetch`, `docs`, `DocsServer`, `web-fetch`) and tells operators to run `openclaw mcp show <name>` after the swap and to restart the gateway so the new command is picked up on the next agent tool discovery.
- **`extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.models-and-mcp.test-utils.ts`** — updated the three test fixtures that hard-coded the deprecated package to use `uvx mcp-server-fetch` instead, so future test runs match the documented config and stop embedding a 404 package in our own tree.

## Real-behavior proof

Direct end-to-end run from a clean checkout, against `uvx mcp-server-fetch` as published on PyPI (`mcp_server_fetch-2026.8.18`):

```text
$ pip install --quiet mcp-server-fetch
$ stdbuf -i0 -o0 mcp-server-fetch   # MCP stdio server

# initialize
> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"pr148239-proof","version":"1.0"}}}

# initialize response (truncated)
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{"experimental":{},"prompts":{"listChanged":false},"tools":{"listChanged":false}},"serverInfo":{"name":"mcp-fetch","version":"1.30.0"}}}

# tools/list
> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}
> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}

# tools/list response (truncated)
< {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"tools":[{"name":"fetch","description":"Fetches a URL from the internet and optionally extracts its contents as markdown.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"url":{"description":"URL to fetch","type":"string","format":"uri"},"max_length":{"default":5000,"type":"integer","minimum":0},"start_index":{"default":0,"type":"integer","minimum":0},"raw":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":["url"],"type":"object"}}]}}
```

`serverInfo.name: "mcp-fetch"`, `serverInfo.version: "1.30.0"`, and a single `fetch` tool with the expected `inputSchema` (`url`, `max_length`, `start_index`, `raw`) were returned. This is the exact behavior the policy Doctor fixtures now expect, and what `openclaw mcp show <name>` would launch once the gateway restarts after a user migrates their saved entry.

The previously merged PR (#141189) shipped the same example in v2026.9.5 and v2026.9.6; this PR extends the migration guidance for saved entries under arbitrary names and brings the policy fixtures into line.

## Linked issue

Closes the documentation half of #141180.

## Test plan

- Reviewer can re-run the `initialize` + `tools/list` trace above after `pip install mcp-server-fetch` to confirm the same `mcp-fetch` 1.30.0 server.
- The fixture changes in `register.models-and-mcp.test-utils.ts` are pure string substitutions; the surrounding assertions check policy findings based on server names, not on Fetch launching, so test behavior is unchanged. CI on this PR remains green.

prs.title: fix(macos): dismiss approval panels resolved elsewhere
prs.body:
Closes #142553

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS users would keep seeing an obsolete command approval panel after another client had already resolved the request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway prompter consumes approval events without blocking on modal UI and cancels only the matching presentation task for the approval kind, request ID, and Gateway lease. It preserves display-time session eligibility, reconnect ownership, and successful self-echoed resolution RPCs.

The current-main rebuild also preserves the newer plugin approval kind and shared Gateway payload decoder introduced after the original patch.

## User Impact

Approval panels now dismiss when the same request is resolved elsewhere, while unrelated, replacement, and in-flight locally decided approvals retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Exact head: `1c042d26dcc125bd7f1bb6c8f3625319811cf521`
Current-main parent: `e205c9d6fced8f9201e5aa500a355ec93dbcff0b`

- Rebuilt as one commit on current `main`; GitHub tree `d6aa30e9db94582e88785f9e98dce9a434dcd844` exactly matches the reviewed local tree.
- The first refreshed macOS CI run exposed an actor-isolation compile error in the DEBUG subscription-readiness seam. The seam is now actor-awaited.
- The next run compiled successfully and both dead-code scans passed; its only failure was SwiftFormat wrapping in the DEBUG waiter type. That type is now expressed as a formatter-compliant named struct.
- Removed timed polling from the approval regressions. Subscription startup and pending-prompt transitions now use continuations resumed by the owning state mutations.
- Production subscription and approval behavior are unchanged by the DEBUG-only synchronization seams.
- Added regression coverage for exact kind/ID cancellation, connection retirement, same-ID replacement ownership, stop cleanup, queued eligibility revalidation, and preserving locally submitted decisions.
- `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD`: pass.
- This Linux VPS has no Swift/macOS toolchain. Exact-head Swift formatting, compilation, native tests, and Periphery are delegated to GitHub Actions.

## Remaining native proof request

The only irreducible proof gap is an after-fix macOS app run showing:

1. another client resolves an active approval and the matching panel disappears;
2. another client resolves a queued approval and it never presents; and
3. a local decision still completes successfully.

A redacted recording, native validation transcript, or diagnostic logs are sufficient. No paired macOS node is currently available to this contributor, so this cannot be produced honestly from the Linux host.

AI assistance: Codex reconstructed and reviewed the current-main patch.

prs.title: feat(cron): run provenance, job kinds, agentTurn token budget, typed completion causes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Run-log entries and the Control UI Automations page can't answer the questions an operator actually asks: where did this run come from, what kind of job is it, when does it next run, what did it cost, and why did it stop. Producers write freeform errors; the runs pane renders a generic failure label; `agentTurn` jobs can't cap their token spend; and trigger provenance is inferred downstream by string-matching instead of recorded at admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Every run-log entry gains a **typed trigger origin** (schedule / manual / system / ACP admission), populated uniformly across all 9 run-admission paths, typed at the protocol layer.
- The Automations UI gains a **job-kind column + detail badge** and an **upcoming/ETA panel** — the page reads as a schedule, not a graveyard.
- `agentTurn` jobs accept **`tokenBudget` end-to-end**: protocol → normalizer → **create and same-kind update patch merge** → live config patch → UI form/table round-trip.
- **Completion causes become a closed typed set** (`CronCompletionCause`) with an **exact legacy codec** — restart/interrupt rows written by older versions decode identically, no silent reclassification. Producers emit typed causes; the runs pane renders cause-aware failure labels (7 buckets; producer cause wins over derived).

## User Impact

Operators see provenance, cost caps, and truthful stop reasons on the surface they already use. Old run rows decode byte-identically (codec round-trip tested), so history is not reclassified. Clients that ignore the new fields are unaffected.

## Evidence

**Live Control-UI proof on the current head (2026-09-02, isolated dev gateway — own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, own port; the operator's running gateway was never touched):**

- Runs pane shows **typed origin labels** rendered from the new fields: "Scheduled — cron fire", "Manual run", "On-exit watcher" (screenshots 1–2), plus job-kind labels, the token-budget column, and the upcoming/ETA panel (screenshot 1).
- Job editor shows the **Token budget** field with its help text under ADVANCED (screenshot 3).
- **TokenBudget round-trip proven at the wire level**, not just visually: a Playwright session listening on the gateway WebSocket captured the `cron.update` request the UI sends (`"payload":{"kind":"agentTurn","message":"…","tokenBudget":120000}`), and after save `cron get` on the same state dir returns the payload with `"tokenBudget": 120000`; re-opening the editor shows 120000 in the field and the jobs table shows it in the TOKEN BUDGET column (screenshot 4).
- **That wire-level probe caught a real gateway bug, fixed in this PR:** the UI was sending `tokenBudget` on edit, but same-kind `cron.update` merges rebuilt the agentTurn payload without reading `patch.tokenBudget` — create persisted the budget while every same-kind edit silently dropped it, and the explicit-null clear was never honored. `a5d2978f1d1` mirrors the model/thinking override rules (number sets, null clears, omitted leaves untouched) with failing-first regression tests. This is exactly the class of drop the tokenBudget enforcement work would have hidden: the cap lever existed in the form but updates never stored it.

**Redacted live proof (post-rebase re-verification recorded in the test battery, `~/openclaw-test-battery/evidence/`):** trigger origin visible on live run-log entries through the production gateway; typed completion causes flow producer → run record → cause-aware UI label against the live gateway.

**Land-time suites (per commit, openspec §2.2):**

| Commit | Slice | What | Land-time |
|---|---|---|---|
| `577db2e79f6` | 0 | populate trigger field on run log entries | 113/113 (post-CR-6-rebase) |
| `95a95088bf2` | 0 | typed run trigger-source enum (protocol) | 113/113 |
| `062c9718e5f` | 1 | trigger origin on all 9 admission paths + Unknown (legacy) | 142/142 |
| `9f0bf4dbac5` | 2 | job-kind column, detail badge, upcoming/ETA panel | 78/78 |
| `7d77eb1b42c` | 3a | agentTurn tokenBudget protocol + normalizer | 87/87 |
| `5b98180783f` | 3b | tokenBudget UI form/table, Unlimited / N-a display | 181/181 + UI build green |
| `ab0240077be` | 4a | typed completionCause contracts + exact legacy restart codec | 85/85 |
| `ea166202cc2` | 4b-c2 | producers emit typed causes + budget-cause gap fix | 305/305 (8 files) + 301/301 (9 files) |
| `260cd8d8595` | 4b-c3 | cause-aware failure label in runs pane, 7 buckets | 161/161 + UI build green |
| `6b1782aba48` | 5 | direct runs of event jobs stay `trigger=manual`; on-exit watchers pass explicit `triggerSource` (review fix) | cron admission + active-jobs suites green |
| `12a429956d7` | 5 | render localized run origin + job-kind labels via locale catalog (review fix) | UI cron suites green |
| `a5d2978f1d1` | 6 | **fix:** same-kind `cron.update` merges apply `tokenBudget` (number sets, null clears) — found by live wire-level probing, see above | payload-merge 19/19 (3 failing-first), apply-patch + protocol conformance/schema 52/52 |

- **Rebase onto current `main` (2026-09-02, final head `fd168c05633`):** two upstream movements were ported — (1) embedded-agent usage accounting moved into `createEmbeddedModelState`, so the `onRunUsageTotals` checkpoint lives in its `recordModelUsage` (threading verified across all 5 call sites); (2) #136075 derived the run-log entry type from the gateway-protocol wire schema — our `trigger`/`completionCause` fields already live in `CronRunLogEntrySchema`, so `src/cron/run-log-types.ts` adopted the upstream `Omit`-derivation verbatim. `pnpm tsgo:core` green; payload-merge 19/19, protocol conformance + gateway-protocol validators 21/21. A follow-up CI-gate commit (`fd168c05633`) regenerates the Swift protocol models for the new schema fields and removes knip-flagged dead code (superseded `run-origin.ts` formatter, test-only cause predicate/exports, production-dead UI helpers).
- Full CR-7 sweep at the pre-rebase tip: unit-src 486/490 (4 waivers logged, environmental/umask classes, baseline logs under `/tmp/cr7-batch/`), runtime-config 280/280, gateway-client 1148/1148, gateway-server/methods/plugin-sdk green, tsgo green, cron subsets 54/54/95, ui 857/857.
- Tree: 54 files, +1840/−12 over merge-base (final head `fd168c05633`). pnpm-lock: clean. Author/trailer audit: Forge only, zero trailers. Private-path/secret-shape audit: clean (waivers logged; sole hit is the `file:///etc/passwd` canary in the URL-sanitization *negative* test).
- `git diff --stat` numbers are stale-proof: recompute with `git diff --shortstat origin/main...HEAD`.

**Run-admission provenance note (CR-6):** the premature `TimedCronRunOutcome` annotation removed in Slice-0 was introduced by that commit itself (pre-rebase `97a31f34ac0`); final form is unannotated literal + `trigger: "scheduled" as const`, squashed into `577db2e79f6`. Both merge sites fully type-checked; `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0.

**Risk:** legacy decode is exact, not approximate (round-trip codec tests). UI is additive — old clients ignore new fields. No schema migration.

**Screenshots (isolated dev gateway, current head; hosted as fork release assets, no repo-branch artifacts):**

![Automations jobs table — job-kind, token-budget columns, upcoming panel](https://github.com/TheArchitectit/openclaw/releases/download/pr-proof-2026-09-02/automations-jobs-table.png)

![Run history — typed origin labels: Scheduled — cron fire, Manual run, On-exit watcher; cause-aware failure labels](https://github.com/TheArchitectit/openclaw/releases/download/pr-proof-2026-09-02/run-history-origins.png)

![Token budget field filled before save (ADVANCED disclosure)](https://github.com/TheArchitectit/openclaw/releases/download/pr-proof-2026-09-02/token-budget-field.png)

**Round-6 update (2026-09-04, rebased onto upstream `8e23a5324f5`, head `7daa73aa1e8`):**

prs.title: fix(gateway): re-sync pending GitHub identity with bounded backoff
prs.body:
Closes #141615.

## What Problem This Solves

A gateway connection runs its GitHub identity sync exactly once, in detached connect work. When that single attempt fails transiently (secondary rate limit, network blink), the client stays profile-pending for its whole life: every profile-gated RPC answers `INVALID_REQUEST ... Authenticated profile verification is unavailable` until the client reconnects. On a Docker-sandboxed agent whose container cwd is involved, the wedge also surfaces as `sessions.create cwd is unavailable` style failures after identity resolution is retried by hand. The reporter's session never recovered without a restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two bounded mechanisms instead of one fragile attempt:

- Connect-time detached sync now retries with a small backoff (2s/8s/30s) inside the same detached work, so short blinks self-heal without any client action. The loop is bounded — a wedged identity still gives up rather than looping forever.
- A gated RPC that finds its client still pending gives it one more bounded re-sync (`refreshPendingGatewayClientProfile`) before answering the retryable unavailable shape. The sync dedupes concurrent callers and drops rejected attempts, so the extra path cannot stack duplicate runs.

## User Impact

Sandboxed and remote clients recover automatically from transient identity-sync failures instead of staying wedged until reconnect. No protocol, config, or schema changes.

## Evidence

- `gateway-client-identity.test.ts`: a pending client whose first re-sync fails answers the retryable pending shape, then a healthy re-sync clears the gate; a client whose backend is still down stays pending without throwing; non-pending clients never re-enter the sync.
- Changed paths: `gateway-client-identity.ts` (bounded re-sync helper), `connect-session.ts` (backoff loop around the detached sync), `system-agent.ts` (gated RPC uses the helper).
- `gateway-client-identity.test.ts` 5/5 green; tsgo/oxlint/oxfmt clean.


---


---

## Update (a491ee99fe7) — Rev 3 findings addressed

Two review findings, both acted on:

1. **Dropped the duplicate handler-level re-sync (P1).** The router already awaits identity sync for pending profile-gated methods and returns retryable UNAVAILABLE — `openclaw.chat` included — so the handler change was unreachable and duplicated that owner. Removed the helper, the handler edit, and its tests. Recovery stays with the shared router.
2. **Backoff now ends on gateway cancellation (P2).** The connect-time retry checks the connection-work signal before each attempt and passes it to `sleep`, so shutdown/drain never waits out the 2s/8s/30s schedule plus request time.

The connect-time bounded backoff is the change's remaining scope: the connection still gets one detached sync attempt plus a short bounded retry for transient failures, and the loop is cancellation-aware. Request-time recovery already existed at the shared router, so this is narrowly about the connect-time window, not a new recovery owner.

The P0 merge-risk item — showing a real HTTP 403 outage recover with this patch — still needs live-behavior evidence, which is being prepared separately.



---

## Update (85fd7ff5b88) — Rev 5 type-contract finding

The shared `GatewayConnectPhaseContext.runDetachedConnectWork` callback type now accepts the abort signal, matching the implementation. No other change; the remaining before-merge item is the real transport trace (background recovery on the same connection + cancellation ending backoff), which is being prepared.



---

## Update (a491ee99fe7..e4a7a82f90c) — Rev 5 type-contract finding

The shared `GatewayConnectPhaseContext.runDetachedConnectWork` callback type now accepts the connection-work abort signal, matching the implementation; the backoff loop checks the signal before each attempt and passes it to `sleep`, so gateway drain ends the retry schedule immediately. The identity sync tail (bounded backoff + avatar adoption) moved into `github-identity-sync.ts`, keeping `connect-session.ts` inside the max-lines budget.


## Update (e4a7a82f90c..c915c4a4d57) — Rev 8 extraction findings

Both defects in the extracted helper are fixed: `github-identity-sync.ts` now imports `formatForLog` from `../../ws-log.js` (the gateway logging module — the old `../../../ws-log.js` path resolved to a nonexistent `src/ws-log.js` and broke module loading), and `adoptTailscaleAvatarIfMissing` reads the declared `hasAvatar` param directly instead of the nonexistent `params.profile` (both call sites in `connect-session.ts` pass the flat shape). Verified the connect-session module chain loads cleanly, tsgo reports no errors in the touched files, and a gateway server suite (16 tests) passes. The real-transport proof for the 403 recovery path is still the remaining item on our side.

prs.title: fix(config-cli): say the running gateway self-restarts, and name the deadline
prs.body:
## Summary

`config set` on a restart-required path always prints `Restart the gateway to apply.`, regardless of `gateway.reload.mode`. With live reload at its default that hint is wrong about **who** restarts, and silent about the fact that the restart has a **deadline**.

What actually happens when live reload is on:

1. The CLI writes the config file and prints `Restart the gateway to apply.`
2. The running Gateway's config watcher independently detects the change.
3. It classifies the path as restart-required and defers, waiting for active work to drain.
4. After `resolveGatewayRestartDeferralTimeoutMs()` (5m) it **force-restarts anyway**, aborting whatever is still in flight.

So the operator is told to perform a restart that is not theirs to perform, and is not told that an automatic one is already scheduled with a hard cut-off. If the edit was made from inside a long-running agent turn, that turn is aborted by its own config write.

## Reproduction

On a running Gateway with default `gateway.reload` settings:

```console
$ openclaw config set plugins.load.paths '["/path/to/my-plugin"]' --strict-json
Updated plugins.load.paths. Restart the gateway to apply.
```

The operator does nothing, believing the change is inert until they act. Five minutes later, unprompted:

```
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (plugins.load.paths)
[reload] config change requires gateway restart (plugins.load.paths) — deferring until 1 operation(s), 1 reply(ies), 1 embedded run(s), 1 gateway request(s) complete
[reload] restart still deferred after 30330ms ...
[reload] restart timeout after 300053ms with 1 operation(s), ... still active; forcing restart
[gateway] forced restart requested; skipping active work drain
[shutdown] aborted 1 active run(s) during restart shutdown
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=<redacted> durationMs=1504983 error="agent run aborted for restart"
```

A ~25 minute agent run was aborted. Nothing in the CLI output suggested that was coming.

`plugins.load.paths` is not special here — it has no hot-reload rule, so it takes the default in `buildGatewayReloadPlan`:

```js
const kind = rule?.kind ?? "restart";
```

Any restart-required path reaches the same outcome.

## Fix

Split the hint by who owns the restart:

| `gateway.reload.mode` | hint |
| --- | --- |
| default / `hybrid` | `A running gateway restarts itself to apply this: it waits for active work to drain, then aborts in-flight runs after 5m. Restart manually if no gateway is running.` |
| `off` | `Restart the gateway to apply.` (unchanged) |

The deadline is read from `resolveGatewayRestartDeferralTimeoutMs()` rather than hardcoded, so the message tracks the value the Gateway actually enforces.

Hot-appliable paths under `reload.mode: "off"` keep the manual hint — live reload is disabled, so the Gateway will not pick them up on its own.

## Tests

`src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — 243 passed.

- Two new cases pin both branches: the self-restart wording including its deadline, and the unchanged manual wording under `reload.mode: "off"`.
- Five existing assertions updated; they asserted the manual hint for restart-required paths running with live reload on, which is the behaviour being corrected.
- `docs/cli/config.md` hint table updated.

## Scope

This changes the `config set` / `config patch` / `config unset` hint only. `plugins-cli.runtime.ts` and `plugins-uninstall-command.ts` print their own copies of the same string and have the same ambiguity — left for a follow-up to keep this diff reviewable.

This is a message-accuracy fix. It does not change restart behaviour: the 5m deferral is still hardcoded and its timeout intent is still `force: true`, so a restart-required config write can still abort an in-flight run. Making that window configurable (and non-forcing by default) is a separate discussion I'm happy to open if maintainers want it.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill/hook requirements have all-of `env` with no any-of equivalent: a skill accepting either of two credential env vars cannot declare it, so eligibility is either too strict (all-of) or credential-blind (bins-only). This PR adds a generic `requires.anyEnv` contract (eval, manifest, runtime eligibility + credential injection, doctor/CLI/UI rendering, snapshot carry) with optional injection for alternate keys.

Note: #147346 (sag readiness) is already CLOSED completed by canonical #147685 (binary-only). This PR no longer claims it — sag stays binary-only here (P1 fix below). Generic sponsorship decision remains with the maintainer.

## Changes

- Generic `requires.anyEnv` plumbing: `src/shared/requirements.ts` (any-of eval), `frontmatter.ts`, `config-eval.ts`, `doctor-skills-core.ts`, CLI/hook formatters, UI `skills-shared`, `workspace-skill-prompt.ts` snapshot + `SkillSnapshot`/`OpenClawSkillMetadata` types, `env-overrides.ts` propagation on both direct + snapshot paths.
- `skills/sag/SKILL.md`: readiness restored to binary-only `{ bins: ["sag"] }` (matches `upstream/main`), preserving file-key setups (`--api-key-file`, `*_API_KEY_FILE` per SKILL.md:34). `primaryEnv` + `SAG_API_KEY` docs kept for optional injection only — no env gate. P1 regression withdrawn.
- Docs: `creating-skills.md` + `skills.md` generic contract.

## Evidence

P1 fix proof from this head (`02cfc06e1`), branch source:
```
sag requires now: { "bins": ["sag"] }
eligible binary-only zero-env: true
missing: {"bins":[],"anyBins":[],"env":[],"anyEnv":[],"config":[],"os":[]}
```
`isEnvSatisfied` (`requirements.ts:31`) checks env only, never key files — so the removed gate was the failure path; binary-only restores canonical behavior. Verified `upstream/main` sag is also bins-only (fetch `43d413bd`).

Gates on this push:
- `requirements` + `frontmatter` + `env-overrides`: 39/39 pass
- `oxlint`: 0 errors; `git diff --check`: clean
- Author: `Navras98 <andrea.sforna@gmail.com>` (amended before push)

## Honest gaps (not claimed)

- Maintainer decision on generic sponsorship is OPEN — happy to split, defer, or close on guidance.
- Snapshot carry is proven at unit level, not via a fresh-session resume run.
- UI screenshots exist locally (before/after) but are not embedded — no image-upload path from CLI.
- Full CI: runs on push, not claimed green here.

Related #147346 (closed by #147685); supersedes #147381 (closed unmerged).

## Generic proof (non-sag) from this head (`02cfc06e1`), real CLI entrypoints

Workspace skill `proof-anyenv` (generic, not sag) with
`metadata.openclaw.requires.anyEnv: [PROOF_KEY_A, PROOF_KEY_B]`, isolated
`OPENCLAW_HOME`, branch source, run from source:

**Neither key set** — `skills check` lists it under missing with the alternates group:
```
proof-anyenv (anyEnv: PROOF_KEY_A, PROOF_KEY_B)
```
(Eligible 44, Missing 22.)

**Only the alternate `PROOF_KEY_B` set** — it moves to "Ready and visible to model";
`skills info proof-anyenv --json` returns `"eligible": true` with
`"anyEnv": ["PROOF_KEY_A","PROOF_KEY_B"]` and `"missing": {"anyEnv": [], ...}`.
(Eligible 44→45, Missing 22→21.)

Injection + snapshot-carry: `env-overrides.test.ts` covers the direct path, the
snapshot path (`applySkillEnvOverridesFromSnapshot`), and the always-blocked guard;
335/335 touched-area tests pass locally (see comments).

UI: `computeSkillMissing` renders `env:any of (A, B)`; covered by
`skills-shared.test.ts` + page `view.test.ts`. Before/after screenshots of the real
Skills page were captured in headless Chromium (missing-requirements box absent
before, `env:any of (PROOF_KEY_A, PROOF_KEY_B)` shown after) — held locally, can be
drag-dropped into the thread on request.


## CI shard-failure attribution (finished run 34825094814, head `02cfc06e1`)

- `checks-node-compact-small-12` — `test/scripts/docker-build-helper.test.ts` expects `clawhub:@openclaw/kitchen-sink` in the Docker plugin sweep; area this PR never touches (no docker files in scope). Upstream-broken candidate.
- `checks-node-compact-large-12` — `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-module-identity.test.ts` timed out at 45s; `src/state` ownership/reclamation, outside this PR's scope. Flake candidate, passes locally on clean main per comment.
- Touched-area gates green locally: 335/335 + `oxlint` 0 errors + `git diff --check` clean. These two shards need a maintainer re-run, not a code fix.


## Proof 2026-09-14 (head `02cfc06e1`, fork-only, log redacted `/tmp/proof-147455.log`)

Real proof from this head, worktree pinned detached `02cfc06e1` (fork `Navras98/openclaw`), no push to upstream:

**sag accepts `SAG_API_KEY` alternate** (`sag 0.3.0` binary):
- `strings /usr/local/bin/sag | grep -o`: `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY_FILE`, `SAG_API_KEY`, `SAG_API_KEY_FILE` all present.
- No keys => `Error: missing ElevenLabs API key (set --api-key, --api-key-file, or ELEVENLABS_API_KEY)`.
- `SAG_API_KEY=[REDACTED]` dummy only => `Error: list voices failed: 401 Unauthorized` (missing-key gate GONE => alternate accepted; dummy value never printed, log contains no secret).

**`requires.anyEnv` resolves** (`src/shared/requirements.ts`, this head):
```
neither eligible=false missing.anyEnv=["ELEVENLABS_API_KEY","SAG_API_KEY"]
alt-only eligible=true missing.anyEnv=[]
primary-only eligible=true missing.anyEnv=[]
```

**sag readiness binary-only** (`skills/sag/SKILL.md`, this head):
```
sag requires now: { "bins": ["sag"] }
eligible binary-only zero-env: true
missing: {"bins":[],"anyBins":[],"env":[],"anyEnv":[],"config":[],"os":[]}
```

**Local tests green** (canonical `scripts/test-projects.mts`):
- `requirements` + `frontmatter`: 20/20 pass (unit-fast)
- `env-overrides` anyEnv (direct + snapshot + always-blocked guard): 3/3 pass
- `skills-cli.formatting` + `hooks-cli.toggle`: 143/143 pass
- `doctor-skills`: 10/10 pass
- Total touched: **176 passed, 0 failed**
- `oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors · `git diff --check`: clean

Merge-risk/compatibility: sag stays `{ bins: ["sag"] }` (canonical, no env gate); generic `anyEnv` is opt-in per-skill, defaults to empty (no behavior change for existing skills). No upstream push — fork branch only.


## Runtime proof: fresh + cold-resumed delivery, old snapshots, guard (head `f942a4d`, fork-only, redacted)

Real entrypoint `applySkillEnvOverridesFromSnapshot` in **separate fresh OS processes** (no shared memory), snapshots reloaded from disk JSON after the same JSON round-trip the session store performs (`stripRuntimeOnlySessionSkillsFields` drops only `resolvedSkills`; `skills[].anyEnv` survives persistence — `store-entry-shape.ts:190`). Config values were synthetic dummies, never printed; output below is booleans only.

- **FRESH** — new-format snapshot (`skillKey/primaryEnv/requiredEnv/anyEnv`, as `buildSkillSnapshot` emits), only the alternate `PROOF_KEY_B` configured:
`{"expectKey":"PROOF_KEY_B","hadBefore":false,"delivered":true,"alwaysBlockedHeld":true,"reverted":true}`
- **COLD RESUME** — same persisted JSON reloaded by a *different* fresh process (simulates restart: disk → parse → apply), only alternate configured:
`{"expectKey":"PROOF_KEY_B","hadBefore":false,"delivered":true,"alwaysBlockedHeld":true,"reverted":true}`
- **OLD SNAPSHOT (pre-change format, no `anyEnv` field)** — `requiredEnv: ["LEGACY_KEY"]` still delivered, no crash:
`{"expectKey":"LEGACY_KEY","hadBefore":false,"delivered":true,"alwaysBlockedHeld":true,"reverted":true}`
- **GUARD** — with `anyEnv` declared, always-blocked host key (`OPENSSL_CONF`) configured alongside the alternate: alternate delivered, host key refused (`Blocked skill env overrides for proof-anyenv: OPENSSL_CONF` in log):
`{"expectKey":"PROOF_KEY_B","hadBefore":false,"delivered":true,"alwaysBlockedHeld":true,"reverted":true}`

So: alternate-key delivery works fresh and after cold resume through the real snapshot path; pre-change snapshots load unchanged; the sanitizer allow-list still refuses host-dangerous keys.

## Generic Skills UI screenshots (real rendering, headless Chromium 153)

Real Skills page (`renderSkills` from `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts` + app `styles.css`, served by vite from this head) with a generic non-sag skill `proof-anyenv` missing `anyEnv: [PROOF_KEY_A, PROOF_KEY_B]`, detail dialog open. Same harness, only `computeSkillMissing` differs:

Before (base `61fe467c`): the dialog shows **no** Missing-requirements box — the alternate-credential need is invisible.

![before: no missing-requirements box](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Navras98/openclaw/proof/147455-assets/proof-assets/skills-before.png)

After (this PR): `Missing requirements — env:any of (PROOF_KEY_A, PROOF_KEY_B)`.

![after: env any-of group shown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Navras98/openclaw/proof/147455-assets/proof-assets/skills-after.png)

## Why generic (maintainer decision on deferral)

- **Concrete any-of credential reality, in-repo:** the `sag` binary itself accepts `SAG_API_KEY` **or** `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` (plus `*_FILE` variants — verified via `strings`/runtime in this thread). All-of `env` cannot express that without marking single-key users ineligible; bins-only cannot name the credential at all. File-key setups stay bins-only (P1 lesson kept); `anyEnv` is opt-in metadata for key-based setups, never a gate.
- **Symmetry with `anyBins`:** the codebase already solved the identical any-of problem for binaries (`anyBins`, rendered as `bin:any of (...)` in CLI/hooks/UI). `anyEnv` is the missing half — same evaluator shape, same render pattern, same snapshot carry.
- **Additive and safe to land:** optional field, defaults to empty (zero behavior change for existing skills); old snapshots load (proven above); the P2 propagation bug this PR fixed (eligible-but-keyless) already demonstrated the trap is real — deferring leaves it for the next alternate-credential skill. Happy to add a first in-repo consumer annotation if the maintainer prefers.

## CI attribution (run `34877456462`, head `f942a4d`)

- `preflight` fails in **Build CI manifest**: `Error: split timing generation repeats files for core-runtime-infra-storage-state` (`scripts/lib/vitest-shard-metadata.mts:79` via `ci-node-test-plan.mts:2740`) — harness shard-planning bug on upstream `main`, unrelated to this PR (touches no CI/shard files).
- `openclaw/ci-gate` fails in 3s as the aggregation gate consequence.
- Touched-area gates stay green locally (unit + `oxlint` + `git diff --check`, see thread). Needs a maintainer re-run after the harness fix, not a code change here.

Claw packages that declare catalog categories cannot be inspected or added because the strict manifest parser rejects the field.

## User Impact

Claw authors can declare one to three portable category slugs in `CLAW.md`; older packages continue to work. The receiving registry still decides which names it accepts.

Accept and preserve the optional field at the parser boundary without adding catalog taxonomy to agent runtime behavior.

## Evidence

- **Before:** Category-bearing packages failed `invalid_manifest` in [awesome-claws proof](https://github.com/openclaw/awesome-claws/actions/runs/38491926953/job/115618887431).
- **After:** 30/30 `src/claws/schema.test.ts` tests pass, including `CLAW.md` frontmatter reading and malformed category rejection. Production and test typechecks, targeted lint, and docs formatting pass.
- The standalone parser counterpart is [claws PR #5](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/claws/pull/5).

This is an optional additive manifest field; no migration or runtime action is required.

prs.title: fix(msteams): pasted DM images always time out as unavailable
prs.body: Related #169917 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: images pasted inline into MS Teams DMs always arrive as `[msteams attachment unavailable]`, because the download shared a 10s enrichment budget and authenticated Bot Framework attachment downloads take 30–50s. ## User Impact User impact: pasted Teams images reach the agent again. Optional enrichment (team identity, quoted message, thread history) keeps its 10s cap and is no longer starved by a slow download. ## Why This Change Was Made The 10s budget (#90738) was sized for optional lookups, but it also wrapped inbound media resolution, and each request got only the remaining slice of it. Media is message content, so it now has its own 120s deadline (the reporter measured 31–50s; their workaround used 90s). The remaining media budget bounds each request, and the 10s enrichment deadline starts after media finishes. The change is plugin-local: no core change and no new config. ## Evidence **Slow authenticated download through the production path (scratch proof, not added to the suite).** The real `createMSTeamsMessageHandler` handles a pasted-image DM activity (`image/*` attachment on a `smba.trafficmanager.net/.../v3/attachments/.../views/original` URL). From there the real media resolver, `downloadMSTeamsAttachments`, `fetchWithAuthFallback`, and `safeFetchWithPolicy` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` all run. That covers the allowlist, HTTPS, auth-host policy, real DNS resolution plus the IP policy, and the deadlines. Real timers, with nothing faked. Only the socket target is swapped: a fetch stub forwards each guarded request to a local server. That server returns 401 without a bearer token. With one, it sends headers after 4s, then streams a 663 KB PNG over about 45s, the shape the reporter measured. Same script on both sides; "before" swaps in the parent commit's four source files. Before (`e4f463159d0`): ``` handler settled after 10.5s 0.0s GET /au/tenant-redacted/v3/attachments/0-sau-d4-redacted/views/original auth=none 0.1s GET /au/tenant-redacted/v3/attachments/0-sau-d4-redacted/views/original auth=bearer 10.0s client aborted transfer at chunk 5/40 10.0s warn msteams attachment download failed host=smba.trafficmanager.net error=Failed to fetch media from https://smba.trafficmanager.net/au/tenant-redacted/v3/attachments/0-sau-d4-redacted/views/original: request timed out dispatched body: "what is in this screenshot?\n\n[msteams attachment unavailable]" dispatched media: [{"kind":"image","contentType":"image","stored":"unavailable"}] ``` After (`4d6db058b83`): ``` handler settled after 45.5s 0.1s GET /au/tenant-redacted/v3/attachments/0-sau-d4-redacted/views/original auth=none 0.1s GET /au/tenant-redacted/v3/attachments/0-sau-d4-redacted/views/original auth=bearer 45.1s body complete (663333 bytes) dispatched body: "what is in this screenshot?" dispatched media: [{"kind":"image","contentType":"image/png","stored":"91181be4-39c5-431a-8193-89bc41398811.png (663333 bytes)"}] ``` - `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.media.test.ts`: two new tests drive the real message handler with fake timers and a 45s download. Pasted DM image: before, the agent body had `[msteams … unavailable]`; after, the image arrives. Channel message with a slow image: the team-ID lookup still runs and `NativeChannelId` resolves after the download (failed before). 8/8, 69s wall warm (tests run in ms; the rest is worker compile). - `monitor-handler`, `attachments`, `request-timeout` tests: 123/123 (332s). `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, oxfmt, oxlint, `git diff --check` clean. - `git merge-tree` against `release/2026.10.5`: no conflicts. - Not tested against a live Teams tenant. - `docs/channels/msteams/troubleshooting.md` (#webhook-timeouts) now describes the separate 120s media and 10s enrichment budgets. `pnpm docs:check-links`: 0 broken links. oxfmt and `git diff --check` clean. ## Follow-ups (not addressed here, so this PR doesn't close #169917) - After a successful download, the inline `` copy of the paste (`asyncgw.teams.microsoft.com`, 401 to the bot token) still appends `[msteams attachment unavailable]`. - When the authenticated retry in `fetchWithAuthFallback` times out, the first attempt's `HTTP 401` is reported, which hides the timeout.
