prs.title: feat(sandbox): add lightweight local SRT backend
prs.body:
Related: #163540

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw needs a local sandbox backend that confines commands and file tools without Docker. This adds the `srt-sandbox` plugin through `registerSandboxBackend()`, configured for independent distribution (npm / ClawHub) rather than bundled inclusion, and corrects permission and process-lifetime defects in the original draft.

## User Impact

macOS uses Seatbelt; Linux uses Bubblewrap and seccomp. Private writable paths remain usable while restricted host workspaces, managed skills and readonly resources stay protected. Command descendants are swept on completion, failure, cancellation, timeout and owner death. Host runtime authority stays live: once the host revokes runtime authority, new commands, deferred exec specs, pin-owner mutations and broker policy writes reject immediately with the host's original error, while terminate/finalize/dispose/release keep working so cleanup stays available.

Windows execution is disabled before native provisioning with SRT 0.0.76. Configuration compatibility and read-only dependency discovery remain available, but every Windows command, preparation and filesystem entry rejects before account, credential, WFP or ACL mutation. The pinned installer cannot establish exclusive ownership of its shared account or safely cancel and reverse partial grants. Native Windows execution must remain disabled until an owner-aware provisioning API and the documented VM qualification are available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commands, buffered execution and file tools share one authoritative filesystem policy, including canonical aliases and nonexistent descendants of protected roots. Linux mounts writable ancestors of readonly roots as anchors so an ancestor rename cannot move a protected child. Supplied mutation pins must match the complete destination and remain live; expired, consumed and mismatched pins reject instead of resolving replacement authority. Host custody stays outside guest signaling permissions. All command routes use this custody. Before launching macOS guests, the existing Seatbelt profile is tightened to reject `setsid`, `setpgid` and `posix_spawn`, preventing descendants from leaving the owned process group. Ordinary fork/exec remains supported; spawn-based launchers, daemonization and job-control group changes are unsupported and fail closed. The pinned wrapper is decoded as literal argv without executing command bytes on a host shell; an unexpected wrapper rejects before launch. Buffered commands now start a fresh SRT process with the current policy; this adds per-command startup overhead. Startup-hook and loader environment variables are rejected before host interpreters launch. Container-style readonly resource path projection is unsupported.

The eight previous review findings are addressed as follows:

1. Workspace permissions: preserve `none`, `ro` and `rw`; protect canonical managed skills and readonly resources in command and file paths, including broad extra writable roots and symlink aliases.
2. Windows scope reuse: coalesce concurrent resolutions and reuse the same authoritative scope/policy across turns; reject different scopes and retired generations.
3. Windows provisioning retirement: remove the unsafe native provisioning path entirely. Execution rejects before installation or grants, including after retirement; no partial cleanup or shared-account adoption is claimed.
4. Streaming custody: host-owned liveness channels and guardians sweep descendants when the launcher or Gateway dies, while preserving output and exit status. Native macOS kernel restrictions prevent session/group-changing descendants from escaping that sweep; delayed-write proof covers ordinary buffered, broker and streaming routes.
5. Broker completion: execute buffered commands under independent host custody and sweep background descendants on success, failure and timeout. The session control process accepts health/policy RPCs only.
6. Windows network settings: reject all execution modes before persistent effects; runtime behavior, configuration hints and platform documentation agree.
7. Live runtime authority: the host's `assertRuntimeCurrent` callback is retained for the handle's lifetime and re-checked after every await, immediately before each effect-bearing operation — command launch (ordinary and broker routes), deferred exec specs, pin-owner spawns, owner RPC writes, and broker startup/health/policy writes. The deferred exec spec composes the caller's own `assertCurrent` with the authority recheck instead of discarding it. Rejection rethrows the host's original error unchanged; `allowFailure` does not swallow it; a rejected pinned mutation releases its held pin; a rejected broker launch handshake cancels the lease and closes the socket. Output-overflow termination stays independent of authority. An already-running command is not killed by the plugin on revocation; the core's cancel path handles running processes, and the plugin blocks every new effect.
8. Factory admission authority: the POSIX factory rechecks the host's `assertRuntimeCurrent` after dependency discovery and again after backend initialization, before the backend is published to the live-scope set. The existing catch stays the single cleanup path (no double dispose); a failed cleanup cannot replace the host's original error; and a provisioning-time revocation leaves no published handle or lingering proxy infrastructure. The exec-spec builder also closes any custody lease it opened itself on every failure path, so an early rejection no longer leaves a lease alive until scope teardown.

Distribution: the plugin now declares independent-distribution metadata following the existing `openshell` and `mxc` sandbox-backend conventions — `openclaw.release.publishToNpm`/`publishToClawHub`, install specs (`clawhub:@openclaw/srt-sandbox` / `@openclaw/srt-sandbox`, host floor matching `compat.pluginApi`), the root `!dist/extensions/srt-sandbox/**` package exclusion, README and `.npmignore` — and the generated inventory/reference docs list it under Official external packages. This matches the reviewer-recommended external-first route and VISION.md's preference for independently maintained optional plugins, and it gives the extension package-boundary tooling a packaged surface for srt-sandbox: previously the only `bundledDist:false` plugin without release metadata, which failed the boundary check with "No packaged surface for extension boundary: srt-sandbox". Maintainer confirmation of the external-first route (versus bundled sponsorship) is still requested in the PR discussion.

Session settings JSON and control messages are ephemeral runtime state, not a stored-data schema migration. Temporary command settings are removed by their custody finalizer, session settings are removed on disposal, and the existing configuration-contract tests cover the accepted settings. No database or user-state migration is introduced.

## Evidence

- Upstream `main` fetched and incorporated at `e43a62c404d457a7da2528e9b3e0dcaa09f98585`.
- Exact tested/pushed head: `0ed9a3717a31eb2e6c263dd4cd23440289e756e4`.
- Full exact-head SRT suite on macOS: 165 passed / 11 Linux-only skipped across 20 passed and 2 skipped files, zero failures. The earlier native Linux full-suite run below (120 passed / 16 macOS-only skipped) covers the permission, network and custody paths at a prior revision; a native Linux rerun at this head will follow with the gateway-level proof.
- Real macOS and native Linux backend tests prove deny-all rejection, strict allowlist success and off-list rejection, open-mode success, and the platform-specific Seatbelt or Bubblewrap/proxy wiring. Six permission cases cover `none`/`ro`/`rw` with buffered broker routing enabled and disabled, command/file mutations, hidden reads, managed skills and readonly resources.
- Real process tests kill the launcher and Gateway and verify descendant termination; buffered tests cover background descendants after exit codes 0 and 7, timeout 124, and guest attempts to disable cleanup. Exit/signal reporting includes 143.
- Runtime-authority revocation coverage drives the real backend factory with a toggleable host authority: revocation before the final I/O rejects ordinary and broker commands and pin-owner mutations; revocation during awaited wrapping or pin-owner preparation still rejects the later spawn/RPC write; the broker route is covered with per-session network enabled and a deny policy; `allowFailure` does not swallow the rejection; terminate/finalize/dispose keep working after revocation; and valid-owner positive cases run the same operations successfully, so a reject-everything implementation cannot pass the suite. Unit tests pin the composed deferred check (both callbacks run), the handshake rejection (lease cancelled, socket closed), pin release on a rejected pinned mutation, the broker startup/health/policy guards including the post-await policy-write recheck, and overflow termination that stays independent of authority. Every rejection test was verified red against the pre-fix production files and green after the fix. Factory provisioning-time revocation is covered separately with deterministic deferred-promise fixtures (no sleeps): revocation during dependency discovery and during initialization both reject with the exact host error after cleanup, no second dispose occurs on later removal or shutdown, a failed cleanup keeps the host's original error and leaves the coordinator faulted, a valid owner is published and reset exactly once, and a rejected second owner is released while the first owner's runtime survives — each in ordinary and per-session broker configurations.
- Red-before/green-after regressions reproduce the permission, reuse, retirement-entry, custody, broker and network contract defects. Windows evidence is deterministic admission/rejection coverage; no native account, ACL or WFP proof is claimed.
- Extension production/test typechecks, type-aware SRT lint, format, inventory/config-doc and SDK boundary checks, frozen install and whitespace checks passed. Runtime import cycles: zero. The changed-surface gate and full production Knip scan fail on one inherited core export: `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-turn-authority.ts: observePlacementAuthority`. A clean detached worktree at the exact upstream base reproduces the same production and full-tree export findings; the core file and export scanners are byte-identical to upstream. No SRT dead-code finding was reported. The script export scan passes. Earlier broad typechecks passed; no claim of an all-green repository-wide gate is made.
- Independent review of the remediation scope completed with no actionable P0/P1 findings after correcting the verified findings. A fresh independent P0/P1 review of the runtime-authority change found one remaining post-await recheck gap in the broker policy-update path; after correcting it (and the matching ping path), the re-review completed scoped-clean with no accepted/actionable findings. A fresh independent P0/P1 review of the factory-admission change completed scoped-clean in a single pass with no accepted/actionable findings. A fresh independent P0/P1 review of the distribution-metadata switch also completed scoped-clean in a single pass.
- Distribution switch verification: with the release metadata in place, the extension-boundary tooling selects srt-sandbox as a packaged surface, and its compile step type-checked all 50 plugin source files against the prepared SDK declarations locally with exit 0. The release and inventory suites (plugin-npm-release, plugin-clawhub-release, plugin-npm-package-manifest, bundled-plugin-build-entries, package-dist-inventory) pass; the npm package-lock generation and plugin runtime-build checks pass for the plugin. Generated inventory/reference docs regenerate cleanly and their `--check` modes pass. Known follow-ups that do not gate this PR: `pnpm plugins:sync` version alignment with the root package (a pre-existing release-preflight check, not run in PR CI), the publish-time npm security-scan allowlist entries (needed at publish time only), and an optional official-external-plugin-catalog entry (no check requires it).
- Native Linux proof ran with Node 26.8.2, pnpm 12.5.1, Bubblewrap and vendored seccomp on Linux 6.19.13 ARM64 in an isolated runner with an init reaper and the mount/user namespace privileges required for nested sandbox execution. It covered all six workspace-access/broker-routing cases, readonly ancestor rename protection, hidden paths, network modes and process custody. Host process identities were matched through `/proc` rather than interpreting guest namespace PIDs as host PIDs. Native Windows VM access was not supplied; the platform support matrix and required fresh/existing/shared-SID qualification are documented in `docs/plugins/reference/srt-sandbox.md`.

No UI screenshots apply. The inherited core export failure, hosted checks, native Windows qualification and maintainer confirmation of the external-first distribution route remain explicit landing considerations. A fresh ClawSweeper review is requested for this exact head; no readiness or merge action is requested.


### Redacted real behavior output

The pin regressions were first run against the preceding production bridge: 11 failed / 15 passed. On the final bridge, all 26 bridge tests pass. Consumed-pin cases first execute and verify a successful live mutation, then replace the parent and verify replay rejection; expired and mismatched cases also verify replacement paths remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ui): rail pins use smaller icons and show no fill when hovered or open
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: pinned pages in the sidebar rail use a smaller, thinner icon than the rail view buttons, and hovering or opening one shows no fill (only an accent-colored glyph), so the current page is hard to spot in the rail.

## User Impact

User impact: rail pins now look and behave like the rail buttons above them: same 20px icon, and the same filled background on hover and when that page is open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rail pins reuse the list's `nav-item` links, which kept the list's 16px/1.5px icon and the rail's transparent background override. The rail now applies its button hover/selected fill and icon size to those links too.

## Evidence

Dark theme, mocked Control UI. Each image shows Plugins as the open page (left) and the pointer over Apps (right).

**Before**

![Before: 16px pins, no fill on selection or hover](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0d3962e-da97-4fbc-bd7f-b0235c479852)

**After**

![After: 20px pins with the rail button fill on selection and hover](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/035a008c-7a5f-4020-8efc-6e66a0d91d75)

- `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-customization.e2e.test.ts` (8/8 pass): a pinned rail page has the same icon width as the Pages view button and the same fill on hover and when its page is open. The new assertion fails on main before this change (`expected 16 to be 20`).

prs.body:
## Problem and solution

The retained chat page still used Lit page/pane implementations and transitional transcript, markdown, message and tool-card adapters. This cutover renders the landed Solid composer and chat components directly, deletes superseded implementations, and moves the two remaining test adapters out of the production surface.

Plain TypeScript owners retain session, request, presentation, route readiness, eviction and disposal authority. Host tags, CSS classes, routes, selectors, fixed slots, three retained panes and one startup RPC remain intact. Connected frame ranges preserve widget iframe ancestry through reordering and disposal. Chat and optional surfaces remain lazy. No dependency or version change is added.

The port preserves queued-panel recipients, Home/workbench custody, prefetch listeners, scroll ownership and sidebar context replacement. Provider notices retain their DOM node across unrelated pane publications. The MCP harness recognizes the current Gateway listener marker while retaining PID liveness and `/readyz` checks and durable client-error diagnostics. Current-main mobile details, hidden-conversation error notices and companion-focus ownership are carried into the Solid consumers.

The sidebar catalog suite runs in the existing isolated UI project: its shared Bun worker hit the 20-minute deadline without a failed assertion, while all 81 cases pass standalone in 6.8 seconds and in the isolated project in 9.1 seconds. Assertions, timeouts and runtime coverage remain intact.

## Proof

Final head: `d76a87bf997a7a03e930ef8398b41f4cff000941`. Full run: [38496136885](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38496136885). `ci:full` runs every UI unit, browser, extension and real-Gateway shard.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Final full UI CI | All 14 shards passed: 3 unit, 9 browser, 2 real-Gateway |
| Build / types / security | Passed in final CI; local `pnpm tsgo:ui` also passed |
| Docker / MCP | Passed in final CI |
| Performance | Final strict and differential checks passed |
| Independent review | Cutover, integrations, provider-notice repair and final catalog isolation reviewed; no unresolved actionable finding |
| Focused regressions | Provider notice 15/15, sidebar roster 11/11, approval integration 8/8, isolated Bun catalog 81/81 passed |
| Retention / WeakRef | 22 WeakRef cases passed in earlier full UI CI; final full UI run covers the integrated owners. Earlier focused proof includes WebKit focus, retention, scrolling and coupled pane/history/panel cases |
| Production Knip | Final head and exact main baseline both report the same single unused `apps/linux/scripts/test-stage-package.mjs`; no new ignores |
| Inherited CI exception | One core job fails in two Plugin SDK surface-budget cases, reproduced on exact main baseline as detailed below |

The only failed CI job is `checks-node-compact-small-16`. Both cases are in `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`: “joins the registered SDK command’s compiler before reporting success” and “does not let a lowered export budget authorize a shipped name removal.” The exact main baseline `f183f386` reproduces the latter test failure and the former’s executed command, `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: public exports **3759 > 3758**, callable exports **2194 > 2193**. The complete `src`, `packages`, `extensions`, checker and test inputs are identical in baseline and CI merge `7119fe3b`. Paired builds on the same Mac measured main `9f79` at 348,753 B startup JavaScript gzip / 8 requests and Solid `b6e5` at 348,713 B / 8 requests; both had 49,590 B startup CSS gzip / one request. Both builds and strict/differential checks passed.

**UI production LOC: 24,483 → 25,629 (+1,146; 4.7%), 87 paths**, against integrated main `f183f386`. The no-renames union includes deleted Lit duals and excludes tests/support. Growth comes from explicit JSX/bridge lifetimes, the owner/render-host split and connected custody of widget frames. The MCP diagnostic adds 22 net test/harness lines outside that count.

## Before / after

Synthetic normal chat, 1440×960, light and dark. Main `0122` is left; Solid `b245` is right. Both raw pairs are byte-identical: zero changed pixels across 2,764,800 compared pixels. All originals and complete sheets were inspected. Later changes preserve these rendering contracts.

prs.title: fix(ui): old interrupted requests appear below recent replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes old interrupted or cancelled requests appearing below recent replies, making conversation history look out of order.

## User Impact

Saved attempts appear in the **existing composer queue**, with aligned status badges and explicit **Send / Discard** actions. Expand a row to inspect and copy its text or view available attachments. There is no separate panel or automatic replay.

**Search is preserved:** an explicit, nonblank conversation search still finds matching loaded saved attempts, with their original source identity and status. Clearing or closing search restores queue-only presentation; it does not put saved attempts back into the normal conversation.

Saved rows do not execute or change queue order. Native held/failed messages keep their existing recovery controls. Send accepts complete user-authored text through normal admission and preserves the draft; system/forwarded inputs stay read-only. Discard hides this viewer’s queue row in this browser—it does not cancel work or delete retained content.

**Limit:** server-only media or structured/incomplete payloads cannot be resent safely and fail visibly rather than sending a partial prompt. No Gateway schema, retention, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Owner-selected design:** Queue-native placement is the default requested by @vyctorbrzezowski, who also requested landing. Explicit search remains available.

Separate inactive saved presentation from executable queue ownership. The existing custody owner retains active-custody discovery and receipt retirement, including accepted requests that are running rather than waiting in the queue. This fixes stale-page duplicate Send and hidden held-row controls without changing the scheduling/drain engine.

The previous review’s search-compatibility concern is addressed by retaining the existing search path, not by accepting a loss of search. Matching pending results keep the existing no-reply/no-rewind guards. Queue placement remains the requested default.

## Evidence

**Local correction — not yet published; this PR remains at `8218a2a0751`:** a failed or volatile browser send must not permanently hide the retained Gateway attempt. Local admission and native held/failed handoff now suppress only the current client’s duplicate row. Persistent retirement waits for a qualifying current Gateway acknowledgment; receipt-free `in_flight`, terminal errors and stale connections do not qualify. Explicit Discard remains browser-persistent. A later native Retry/reconnect can conservatively reoffer the original saved attempt in a fresh client rather than silently lose it.

- **Current integrated recovery proof:** 999/999 tests across 14 queue/send/custody/attachment/camera/handoff files pass (54.62 s wrapper). Three real admission/outbox cross-tab-loss regressions failed before correction. Current accepted ACK, terminal/transport failure, receipt-free preregistration, stale epochs, same-client duplicate prevention, FIFO barriers and draft preservation remain covered.
- The complete integrated PR source and added fixture delta have independent P0/P1 scoped-clean reviews. UI production and affected test types, scoped lint, formatting and unchanged performance limits pass. Existing visual evidence below remains applicable; this correction does not redesign the queue.
- **Browser fixture ownership:** adapted only the initial-document setup from @steipete’s [maintainer proposal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159549), not its broader refactor. The real sandbox receives the intended document on its initial navigation. The original **1,000 ms readiness poll**, source checks, opaque sandbox, auth/epoch checks and navigation/order assertions remain. Seven fixture cases and the complete **115-file / 1,465-test Chromium suite pass** (46.60 s). A wrong-document control fails at 1,000.9 ms with zero navigation. This does **not** establish the original concurrent timing cause of [#159679](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159679).
- Earlier roster, attachment, tooling-fixture and MCP lifecycle prerequisites reuse their canonical main fixes. Ordered MCP predecessor/consumer proof passed both targeted cases and all 134 sibling cases on verified isolated source; main integration retains that fix without PR-specific production MCP changes.

**Publication prerequisite remains unmet:** local candidate `de5577e956b4` is committed and reviewed; this PR still points to `8218a2a0751`. Native build and full static checks pass. The latest [verified-source Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449754111) failed the existing `agent-bundle-mcp-retention.test.ts` at its 180,000 ms deadline. Native publication then refused with `Missing required artifact: .local/gates.env`. No full-suite pass, new publication, or merge is claimed.

The same retention source passed in 136,112 ms in the preceding prepared-head run; that does not prove a fix. A bounded local original-entry probe hit the separate 120,000 ms no-output watchdog. Proof-only nested tracing preserved both deadlines and exposed a 60,000 ms inner optional-memory timeout before observed inference HTTP traffic. Explicit projection settlement completed but did not repair that wait. The underlying cause remains unresolved; no speculative production change, timeout increase, test skip, or unchanged full-run retry was used. Diagnostic source copies are removed, and task-owned validation allocations are stopped/completed.

A preceding run exposed stale lifecycle-error mocks in two state-lease test files. Reused the exact [canonical main repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fa63d9bb844b823ee07644ef6f0ab6d09accf3b4): eight redundant mock lines removed, both result blobs match upstream, and all 12 cases pass under the native configuration (5.58 s). Existing assertion, expiry, scope, cleanup and forbidden-storage guards remain intact; lint and independent P0/P1 review pass.

<details>
<summary>Earlier failed validation attempts and their disposition</summary>

The f1878 run passed 32,806 tests in five completed suites but recorded tooling-fixture failures before an outer two-hour interruption; it was not green. Missing fixture dependencies and packaged-worker setup were repaired from upstream and 588 owner tests passed. A later run exposed three MCP global-manager lifecycle failures; original order reproduced the defect, the canonical owner repair was adopted, and ordered isolated proof passed. The 57c2 run passed native build/check but failed the plugin-frame readiness helper before navigation assertions. Bounded unchanged replays did not prove a fix; the narrow initial-document fixture repair above preserves the original deadline. Each interrupted/failed task-owned Testbox was stopped and verified terminal. No retries, longer assertion deadlines, skipped tests, raised baselines, or fabricated gate receipts were used to conceal these failures.

</details>

- **1,956 tests passed across all 36 direct custody/thread/search consumers** on published head `8218a2a0751` (integrating main `8e57f5447ed`) (29.08 s wrapper wall, one worker per shard). Redundant mocked paths and implementation-only assertions were removed; added regressions protect reproduced failures rather than implementation details.
- Real outbox regressions cover FIFO, draft/attachment preservation, held barriers, native retry across reconnect, and rejection of internal/system provenance before I/O. Eight stale-page cases cover ID/run matching before/during reads, for waiting and running custody.
- Independent review exposed two further failures, both reproduced before repair: older-page browsing could hide a running input, and cancelled custody could conceal a late-restored held owner. The existing pagination regression now covers waiting/running display and interrupted/cancelled native recovery. A separate boundary check confirms stale same-input replies are reread while a fresh cancellation still retires live custody.
- Actual source UI in Chromium passes durable Discard, full-message inspection, explicit Send, offline reorder → reconnect → FIFO delivery, and saved-search matching/nonmatching/clearing. Searching sends or aborts nothing and keeps the draft and ordinary queue intact.
- The saved-search notice regression failed before the repair, then passed. Focused independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues in that delta. Existing system-notice identity and normal-transcript omission remain covered.
- Exact UI-chat test types, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets, scoped lint, formatting, style/i18n checks, production build and explicit performance check pass. Startup JS is **372,326 B**, within the current-main **372,347 B** limit, with no budget or baseline exception. The existing width validator was simplified without changing accepted values; **25 Chromium width cases pass** (1.63 s wrapper).

**CI investigation at `651e8e86b663`:** [the original CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36362074741/job/108741341989) reported `ECONNRESET` instead of `ECONNREFUSED` in the unchanged legacy-listener retirement test. The original 69-file Node partition passed **1,062/1,062 tests** in 97.37 s on an isolated Linux/Node 24.19.0 [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36375437027); the standalone file then passed **13/13** (22.29 s wrapper wall), with matching source hashes. The reset/refusal failure remains unexplained; passing replays are not claimed as a fix. The packed job’s separate Bun phase could not start because Bun was absent, so this is not a full packed-job pass. No retry, timeout, or assertion was weakened. Current-main conflicts are resolved; guarded exact-head landing gates remain required.

The local formal Vitest E2E runner remains blocked by the host’s loopback proxy preflight; the isolated attempt stopped during runtime build before admission. Source-browser proof is not presented as a formal E2E pass. Cancelled jobs from earlier hosted runs are not passing evidence; exact-head CI and review still govern landing.

Before — previous PR alignment

![Before: saved badges sit above the action centerline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ffadf29-0dbd-4096-9b02-219fd6ad17a4)

After — aligned rows with read-only disclosure

![After: badge, text block, disclosure and actions share a centerline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7749bd21-339c-4577-bb46-d935ae9fad2e)

Mixed queue — two runnable messages and one inactive saved attempt

![Mixed queue preserves ordinary queued messages and a separate explicit saved Send](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/201d5b89-9e44-4d18-b369-5158f5ac647c)

<details>
<summary>Narrow layout and read-only inspection</summary>

![Narrow layout retains aligned statuses and explicit controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84998842-fb4b-4d28-8e6e-076a1ff86925)

![Expanded saved message retains its source identity and read-only copy access](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/666e3992-bb39-48b3-a5bb-f58913b64794)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Explicit saved-attempt search — before and after</summary>

Before — matching saved content was omitted

![Before: an explicit search reports no matching messages despite the saved attempt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/429e4798-c89e-4359-bf3f-431412c88cb5)

After — the match is visible, with its inactive status and unchanged queue

![After: explicit search finds the saved attempt without sending it or changing the queue](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02f7c747-ba67-4853-b622-3a239fc5f873)

</details>

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski, including queue-native placement, centered controls, deep safety testing, and removal of redundant tests.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/9fd56994-d68d-4025-b2ef-f288603a3785)

prs.title: fix(auth): move bundled inference and logout SQLite into auth workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

CLI-backed/system-agent inference and Models logout still reached native auth-profile SQLite on the Gateway thread. An async outer logout method did not move its transaction, save, or compensation off that thread.

## User Impact

Bundled inference and logout now await the existing auth workers. Profile selection, deletion, exact compensation, and deny-after-commit credential authority retain their contracts. Released synchronous SDK APIs remain available. A reconnect that reuses a deleted profile ID while selection cleanup runs may require selecting that account again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inference uses the existing async auth-profile loader throughout its bundled callers. Logout uses the existing typed auth writer command and publishes committed credential facts through the existing authority owner. Compensation captures the transaction's already-read cells and restores each exact prior cell only while it still matches the removal's postimage, including an originally absent credential row. Unknown credential-write outcomes remain denied. The worker-only update kernel is named accordingly; no new worker, handshake, schema, or SDK surface is introduced.

Removed checks and accepted edges:

- The preliminary pre-transaction credential reread is deleted. A credential change during preparation is handled by the single comparison inside the owning deletion transaction.
- The post-removal reconnect scan before queued selection cleanup is deleted. Same-ID reconnect during cleanup can lose its selection and require reselection.
- The per-session reconnect reread is deleted. The same accepted reselection edge applies; unrelated current profile selections are still preserved by the session patch.

## Evidence

| Authlive main-thread exposure | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Bundled live-runtime sites in the two assigned flows | 6 | 0 |
| Shared native primitive sites retained for synchronous compatibility | 6 | 6 |

Base committed inventory: 286 conservative T1 call expressions across 115 files at `46053391a1ad842d290563c38ca17b6aeb1d1a46`. The six shared native primitives are not relabeled worker-only; source call-graph closure removes their bundled inference/logout callers. The integrated-head CI worker ratchet passes at **224 → 224 live calls** and **12 → 12 compatibility calls**; all three changed-file dialect groups remain **0 → 0**. The six-site closure is a bundled call-path result, not a claim that shared compatibility primitives were deleted.

| Shared census workload | Base | Candidate | Delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Warm all-thread statements, median [min–max] | N/A | N/A | Not measured |
| Warm requests, median [min–max] | N/A | N/A | Not measured |
| MAIN statements | N/A | N/A | Not measured |
| Authlive operation counts | Not exercised | Not exercised | N/A |

The shared harness selects mock OpenAI HTTP with environment auth and does not configure CLI forwarding, a persisted profile pin, or `models.authLogout`. The lane's conditional harness pair therefore does not apply. No warmed-turn SQL, request, or latency saving is claimed.

Regression coverage exercises profile resolution, actual worker deletion, revocation observed by retained authority and subsequent inference, exact absent-cell compensation, and preservation of a newer in-process credential write during compensation. Local formatting/basic lint and diff checks precede publication; PR CI supplies focused/broad tests, type-aware lint, types, Madge, and worker/dialect ratchets. Ordinary PR CI excludes Knip, so its export scan ran through the campaign CPU gate. The unnecessary compensation-type export is now private. On implementation head `8265baded0fbba3013be8af48d30c5b22e054d1d`, the script export scan passes; production and full-tree scans report only `apps/linux/scripts/stage-package.mjs: stageInstalledPackage`. Running the identical `pnpm deadcode:exports` command on pinned main `f183f3867156a7fadc36af5e56983378de14fc80` reproduces that exact single finding in both scans. This untouched file came from the desktop packaging change; the inherited exception is recorded for the red-main owner. No update-driver cell or SDK diff is required for this scope.

Codex autoreview: two scoped-clean rounds, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The second reviewed the CI registry and fixture corrections. Local basic lint has one inherited `max-lines` finding in `src/agents/isolated-completion.ts` (711 lines, also on the base); all other changed files pass.

The first CI run passed all behavioral and type jobs. It found stale credential-writer caller registration after the worker rename and a missing fixture mock isolation declaration; both were corrected. Current main was merged after a publication-anchor conflict; the resolution preserves main's `sqlPublicationAnchor(database)` and the reviewed compensation path. The next run exposed three stale worker filenames in the guard's synthetic fixture; updating those paths passes the focused failing test locally (one test, 89 skipped). The next run passed behavioral, type, lint, source-contract, architecture/Madge, worker, and dialect checks but found an inherited missing mock-isolation annotation in `worker-turn-launcher.lazy.test.ts`, matching scheduled main CI. Integrating main brought its fix (`4a8b9b5b1d3de0`) and removed the earlier inherited UI export finding. [Integrated-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38496209769) passed types, lint, architecture, source contracts, and worker/dialect ratchets. Its mock-factory check required deleting the exact stale CLI-auth mock entry introduced by the newly integrated baseline; the canonical `--prune` command removed that one entry (9641 → 9640), with no expanded allowances.

The same run's SDK tooling shard reports `public exports 3759 > 3758` and `public callable exports 2194 > 2193`. On current main `fd1eeeb685b11c47dc5417d423ccc19b21d42570`, the focused lowered-budget test reproduces the callable error, and the underlying `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` command reproduces both exact errors. The other failing test wraps that command and is Linux-only; it was skipped on macOS, not reported as locally passed. Authlive changes no SDK surface. [Final CI on `b6410840ca557b0f9c7fde724720ad336d9cda1c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38497135639) completed: all runtime test shards, types, lint, architecture/Madge, source contracts, and baseline/worker/dialect ratchets pass. prs.title: fix(update): reclaim runtimes under protected systemd user managers
prs.body:
Closes #171410

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: successful Linux updates leave disposable updater runtimes behind when the same-user systemd manager's protected working directory cannot be inspected.

## User Impact

User impact: ordinary systemd user sessions can reclaim abandoned updater runtimes through Update and Doctor without configuring a privileged metadata provider. Live runtime references and readable working-directory holders continue to prevent removal. No configuration, schema, dependency, or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The default and update-repair process censuses share one narrow rule for the same-account standard Linux systemd user manager and its parent-bound PAM child. The manager requires an absolute standard systemd path and exactly `--user`; the PAM child requires exactly `(sd-pam)` and the observed same-account manager parent. Artifact-reference checks run first in both paths. Unknown processes still refuse cleanup.

[systemd v257 main.c](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v257/src/core/main.c#L3254) changes to `/` unconditionally before manager initialization and serving; reexec follows the same entry point. An extremely early census may miss the inherited cwd before initialization, but the manager does not consume OpenClaw artifacts before changing directory. Its [PAM helper](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v255/src/core/exec-invoke.c#L1206) waits and settles that login session; native evidence confirms its protected cwd is also `/`. Same-account argv impersonation is outside the artifact-custody trust model: that account already controls the retained directories. All other unresolved same-user process evidence still refuses cleanup.

Update behavior: the fix runs in the installed updater/Doctor's census; older published drivers retain their existing conservative behavior until upgraded. It only changes advisory reclamation of disposable artifacts, and never activation, rollback, database, or service authority.

## Evidence

Current published head: `ba2298625832a36c26c8d4825c9b26bfa916931b`, rebased onto main `7dfb334aa67a34b9e0ec4cbd8c022e8ea1dffec7` to incorporate the verified fixes for inherited CI failures. Both retained commits are identical in `git range-diff`; the full three-file patch and production/test Git blobs match prior reviewed head `553fc0a83e132c35ec113be291b3504be6fc5701`.

- Original production fails both standard manager-path cases; the initial repair fails the same-account PAM-helper case. The completed repair's default and update-repair regressions pass, including readable artifact cwd preservation and refusal of an unrelated `(sd-pam)` process.
- After the base repair, the full census suite passes 102/102 in 36.69 seconds wall / 30.93 seconds Vitest; targeted format, lint, and core typecheck pass. Earlier full census suite: 102 passed; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/openclaw-process-census.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (the repository test wrapper) took 78.79 seconds wall / 58.11 seconds Vitest. New cases take milliseconds; exact-head CI passes102/102 in4.22 seconds wrapper /2.82 seconds Vitest ([changed test job115618967606](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38491817569/job/115618967606)). After a mechanical lint-only test variable rename, the affected case passed in 15.73 seconds wall.
- Targeted formatting, core typecheck, syntax lint, and whitespace checks pass. Fresh independent autoreview is clean through P2; its update-repair sibling finding is resolved through the same shared owner rule. Prior-head ClawSweeper review [38489489588](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/38489489588) found zero actionable defects and called the fix scope complete. Fresh exact-head ClawSweeper [38492267159](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/38492267159) completed successfully with zero findings and marks code ready for maintainer review; its proof assessment predates the completed native acceptance and published-driver evidence below.
- Exact-current-source native AWS acceptance [run_c13cd9fe46960d966a100ff3cc581887](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c13cd9fe46960d966a100ff3cc581887) passes on task-owned lease `cbx_cd2fbdd297ba` (configured standard `c7a.8xlarge`). The direct command was `crabbox run --provider aws --id cbx_cd2fbdd297ba --keep --no-sync --no-hydrate --timing-json --script <owned-native-proof-script>`; it reused the wrapper-verified source, asserted physical checkout and frozen tree `64d79814fbc6f379c36c5784bc557321953d5aa3`, and checked the production file SHA256 `338a87d59851a7f1b0153ac07c8c1e6b1a5ccf051a5559dce78f5d41bf1986c1`. Source-capsule carrier `a12fa86c3ab7bb1e52aef66ba0d2e460acf5d46d` represents source `ba2298625832a36c26c8d4825c9b26bfa916931b`; it is not a changed product head.
- Actual same-UID systemd manager PID17553 and parent-bound PAM child PID17555 had protected cwd; privileged inspection confirmed both `/`. Pre-fix census refused exactly PID17553. Candidate default and update-repair censuses both passed without configuring a privileged process-metadata provider, filtering processes, or weakening custody safeguards. A real Node process holding a runtime cwd kept all three abandoned runtime projections; after its exit, the production Update/Doctor cleanup owner removed all three, and an unrelated operator sentinel remained unchanged. This is native cleanup-owner boundary proof, not a full CLI update. Command time: 4.970 seconds. The owned AWS VM is released with cleanupStatus=complete and provisioningResourceMayExist=false. Source, QA account/services, temporary runtime projections, holder process, and original directory permissions were restored or removed and separately verified by [cleanup run_a789fcf721c69bc623f158312c2eaa05](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a789fcf721c69bc623f158312c2eaa05).
- Earlier attempts were fixture failures: raw HEAD differed from the source-capsule carrier, the dedicated account lacked traversal of the capsule-owned checkout, and invoking the current account through sudo introduced a protected monitor. None justified broadening the census. The final run uses a dedicated task account with temporary checkout traversal, restored after proof.
- Exact-head normal PR [CI38491817569](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38491817569) passed. The required published-driver × combined candidate update proof passed; the additional forward-update experiment has a recorded unresolved failure below. No merge or release-branch backport is requested.

Inherited CI failure: [package-boundary job 115611527640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38489471835/job/115611527640) evaluates merge `65cbb4a7` against newer main `653003a010987ad75393bdd0ff067283f41a1be7`. That main commit (#171481) introduced `publishParticipants?.(participants)` at `session-accessor.sqlite-node-artifacts.ts:490`, calling an object with no call signature (TS2349/TS2757). The failing file's Git blob `a1e20c9ae25b1119ed091db1f2ac672af63f52fa` is identical in the tested main parent and tested PR merge; the pinned base and this PR's source retain the earlier blob `654a71ed14fed0d5531321099ee12e7853903ded` without that call. This PR changes no session owner, SDK declaration, dependency, or compiler input there. That prior-head CI finished red only on the inherited participant-publication type failure and an inherited mock-export violation in `openclaw-test-process.test.ts`. Main fixes `4aa62334122ed29f605f9820c4604539b3ccee77` and `e7a07c5aee577be3a2425ec4d88cad17813b7505` repair them; the rebase incorporates both. Current-head CI and review are green.


## Shared Update Compatibility Proof

The required [published-driver × combined candidate cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38489583100) passed: published stable `2026.10.3` installed frozen combined source `0471f447eb687007ee3c39fb1c9fb7e21a9c3406`, tree `4a63eeed836cc07ded69b99d3a26b0c4a01c6354`, on base `7f7fc2eddc99b0f2a419c1c717473152667b068e`. Package SHA256: `176d43d7162defd2899fd29d03e78823ac7dbb8d4bdf766feaa68237a473aeb5`. Native build carrier `98fc5321` represents that frozen source tree. This PR's bug-fix delta is identical after its rebase; exact-current-head CI remains separate evidence.

The updater exited 0 in 202.913 seconds. Durable run `02efd6c3-4258-4692-8c3b-b513250cd6ab` finished successfully; readiness returned 200; installed build, service PID, session survival, and incognito erasure assertions passed. This uses a real Gateway with a service shim. The exact incident beta was unsupported for this harness, so the tested driver is published stable `2026.10.3`; the JSON observer was not exercised. Native Linux runtime cleanup is proven separately above.

An additional [installed-driver forward update with a missing load path](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38493728042) failed after 225 seconds with CLI exit 1: `Command cleanup could not confirm that owned work stopped`. Its original cause remains unresolved because the harness tore down before ledger/process capture. One [diagnostic replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38495316771), using proof-only tree `179c9f` and the same package, failed differently: debug logging polluted schema-inspection JSON, the package swap failed and rolled back to a finished outcome, and previous-Gateway verification exited 0. PID 1 timeout/zombies indicate a reaping risk, but do not establish the original failure's cause. No passing forward-update replay or fix is claimed. This additional gap is recorded separately from the required passing compatibility cell and this PR's native cleanup acceptance.

prs.title: fix(doctor): preserve env SecretRef facts through auth-profile migration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` reports a false `config.plaintext_secrets` warning for Telegram (and other channel) accounts whose `botToken` values are authored with the documented `${ENV_VAR}` SecretRef shorthand, while `openclaw secrets audit --json` reports the same config clean (`plaintextCount: 0`). Reported in #171022.

Root cause: Doctor's auth-profile migration step rebuilds config through `structuredClone`, which drops the loader's resolution facts — provenance is recorded in a `WeakMap` keyed by config object identity (`src/config/resolution-facts.ts:16`). The later Security step (`collectPlaintextConfigSecretWarnings` → `classifyConfigSecretTarget` → `resolveConfigSecretRef`) then falls back to parsing the substituted literal string as a plain value and flags it as plaintext.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repo already owns helpers for exactly this provenance-carrying problem, used by the other Doctor migration paths (`src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-core-normalizers.ts`):

- `cloneConfigWithResolutionFacts` — clone while keeping the loader facts on the clone;
- `copyConfigResolutionFactsThroughRewrite` — re-carry facts onto a rewritten config while **dropping facts for paths the rewrite actually changed** (moved/dropped/overwritten credential paths must not keep answering lookups — exactly the invalidation the issue asks for).

This fix applies those existing helpers at the two clone sites the issue names:

1. `src/commands/doctor/auth-profile-repair.ts` — `repairAuthProfileMigration` now copies the caller's facts onto the returned config after `maybeRepairOpenAICodexAuthConfig`, covering the no-repair default path end to end (loader → migration → security audit).
2. `src/commands/doctor-auth-flat-profiles.ts` — `maybeRepairOpenAICodexAuthConfig` clones via `cloneConfigWithResolutionFacts` instead of a bare `structuredClone`, and re-carries facts through the `repairRetiredConfigModelRefs` root replacement when it actually rewrites.

No classifier behavior changes: literal tokens still warn, explicit `{ source: "env" }` refs were never affected, and only paths that survive a rewrite unchanged keep their facts.

## User Impact

Before: users authoring `botToken: "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}"` (the documented shorthand) get told on every `openclaw doctor` run that their config "contains plaintext secret-bearing config fields", pointing them at `openclaw secrets configure`/`secrets apply` even though `openclaw secrets audit --check` passes — misleading security advice with no actual remediation.

After: the same config produces no plaintext-secrets finding from Doctor, matching the secrets audit; genuine literal tokens in the same config still produce the warning with the correct paths.

## Evidence

Regression test: `src/commands/doctor/auth-env-facts-preservation.test.ts` drives the real chain — `resolveConfigForRead` (loader, records resolved env-ref facts) → `setConfigResolutionFacts` → `repairAuthProfileMigration` → `collectSecurityWarnings` — with no classifier mocks.

Pre-fix (fix stashed, test run against unmodified main) — reproduces the issue exactly:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/commands/doctor/auth-env-facts-preservation.test.ts
 ×  commands > keeps resolved ${ENV} botToken shorthand off the plaintext-secrets warning after auth migration
   → expected [ { …(5) } ] to deeply equal []
AssertionError: expected [ { …(5) } ] to deeply equal []
+     "checkId": "config.plaintext_secrets",
+     "detail": "openclaw.json contains plaintext secret-bearing config fields.",
 ✓  commands > still warns for literal plaintext bot tokens after auth migration
      Tests  1 failed | 1 passed (2)
```

Post-fix (this branch):

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/commands/doctor/auth-env-facts-preservation.test.ts
 ✓  commands > keeps resolved ${ENV} botToken shorthand off the plaintext-secrets warning after auth migration 14753ms
 ✓  commands > still warns for literal plaintext bot tokens after auth migration 6725ms
      Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

Surrounding suites on this branch (all green, no regressions from the two clone-site changes):

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run \
    src/commands/doctor/auth-env-facts-preservation.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-auth-flat-profiles.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-security.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-maintenance.service-identity.test.ts \
    src/config/resolution-facts.test.ts
      Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  67 passed (67)
```

Same pattern as already-merged code — `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-core-normalizers.ts:44,246` calls the identical `cloneConfigWithResolutionFacts` + `copyConfigResolutionFactsThroughRewrite` pair for the legacy-config migration path.

Fixes #171022

prs.title: fix(doctor): prioritize unresolved findings and explain repairs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor mixes current failures, optional advice, and historical recovery concerns, and can show successfully repaired findings as unresolved. The final report now shows unresolved end state with concrete next steps and documentation. Plugin backup inventories and coverage guidance landed separately in #169295.

## User Impact

- **Fix now:** current failures remain visible; verified repairs disappear.
- **Recommended improvements:** optional changes explain their benefits. Healthy browser/manual setup advice stays informational in lint and quiet in normal Doctor.
- **Historical recovery notices:** old transcript concerns share one summary with at most five examples across stores. Every current transcript failure remains visible individually.

Identical credential findings appear once, retaining store attribution where only part of the fleet is affected. No acknowledgement command or acknowledgement persistence is added.

## Recovery and Performance

**No additional update-time backup is introduced.** Doctor verifies and reuses the installed updater's existing recovery copy. The proposed supplemental full-capture mechanism and its wrapper are removed: no second copy or new backup-inventory scan expands an older capture. Existing standalone Doctor capture and retirement behavior remain in their original owners.

Older captures do not retroactively gain newly declared plugin files. Documentation states that automatic rollback may not restore external resources omitted from the original inventory; existing migration destinations and archives may be needed for manual recovery. Invalid admitted originals still refuse repair. This change adds no schema, storage format, durability policy, or runtime polling.

The existing result publisher remains the sole writer. It consumes the shared warning collector, preserves startup receipts, filters deferred notices against current evidence, and clears stale outcome fields before publishing current facts. The narrow warm-reader repair closes an invalidated owned admission and returns unavailable to the existing fresh-admission fallback; identity, lifetime, and cleanup failures still propagate.

## Validation

- **Current removal regression: 2/2 owning capture tests passed**, 150.05s wall / 139.71s routed wrapper. The main capture case took 18.654s and the namespace refusal 2.153s. Actual capture preserves config/skill/Canvas/plugin-SQLite payloads and source bytes. Sealed update reuse with a later-declared workspace absent from the original creates no additional capture; original manifest and workspace bytes remain unchanged.
- **Negative control:** the same regression against removed production code `757be431183` failed at the intended filesystem assertion: two `doctor-…` capture directories existed instead of one. The revised production source was restored byte-for-byte afterward. No large workspace file, new test case, Gateway boot, or increased deadline was added.
- Configured production and Doctor types, touched typed lint, formatting, whitespace, and docs links passed (15,415 links; zero broken). Fresh native review of all five changed files found zero findings through P2.
- Earlier owning proof includes 82 UX cases and nine schema/reader/seal controls (171.68s wrapper). These remain scoped prior-input evidence. Display remains supported by the actual CLI evidence below.
- Previous head `757be431183` CI completed 89 jobs: credential guard, all five legacy Doctor cases (yes-mode 18.086s), types, and conformance passed. Its sole execution failure was an unrelated owner-only-mode package fixture's existing 20-second offline npm receipt timeout. Producer and test match main; a matching main failure was not observed, so native classification is UNKNOWN and no known-red-main claim is made. No speculative timeout increase or unrelated packaging edit is included.
- [Prior packaged-driver acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38483537089/job/115606813025) passed first attempt: published 2026.10.3 → packaged candidate f2a536b using trusted harness 9940ac5. Exact build, replaced service PID, readyz 200, durable-session/orphan-OAuth preservation, incognito removal, and joined cleanup passed. The lane took 605s, update 500.272s. This is prior-head functional evidence, not a benchmark or an exact-current-head installed-package claim. The standard fixture does not seed omitted external Canvas resources or pre-existing archives.

CI on removal head `a9fb231d033` finished 94 jobs. Two execution failures occurred: a stale fleet-preflight expectation for the removed backup error text, and a worker mock-export guard inherited from prepared main. The former is corrected by test-only head `94a7ec9b546`: structured refusal kind/reason and the current retained-capture notice are checked; all no-repair/config/manifest/payload byte guards remain. All five owning fleet-preflight cases passed locally (155.39s routed wrapper, 94.87s Vitest; the reuse/refusal case 25.004s), with types/lint/formatting and fresh P0–P2 review passing. Main fixed the worker guard independently in [4a8b9b5b1d3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4a8b9b5b1d3de05cab119565873fd9129c738204); the next CI prepared merge is expected to include it. The earlier npm receipt timeout did not recur. New-head CI is pending. The previous exact-head ClawSweeper review had zero code findings and diamond patch quality; the latest removal has fresh native P0–P2 review. The PR remains non-draft, conflict-free, and unmerged.

### Actual CLI before and after

Both runs used `pnpm openclaw --profile doctor-proof-169299 doctor --non-interactive` with separate synthetic homes, state/config/workspaces, the same initial physical files, and no Gateway started. Plugins were intentionally disabled; the resulting browser/model inspection failures and unreachable synthetic Gateway demonstrate failure presentation, not a healthy installation. Both actual commands exited **0**. Before: `2dec18ec8b85e6fa31c33294035dc96b8e696687`; after: `87806fcedfc00fda99678ee486363796ab6b6caf`.

The physical fixture generated **14 historical transcript header/filename mismatch notices**. Before, its session panel described them as 14 session issues. After, the final report separates current inspection/Gateway failures from one historical summary: **five examples, nine omitted**, with retained evidence and conditional no-action guidance. Current transcript preservation beyond five is covered separately by the owning test.

prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: when a chat starts a visible session with `sessions_spawn` (`visible: true`) and that session asks with `ask_user`, the parent chat shows nothing. The question docks only in the child session, so a person working in the parent waits for a completion that cannot come while the child waits for an answer. ## User Impact User impact: a pending question from a direct child session now also docks above the parent chat's composer, marked "Asked by session …". Answering it there resolves the child's question and the child continues. The child session still shows the same question, and the answered question stays in the child's transcript. Approvals from child sessions already reach the parent this way ("Approval requested by session …"). ## Why This Change Was Made Visible spawned sessions are ordinary sessions, so they pass the primary-session gate for `ask_user` (`isPrimaryBootstrapRun` only excludes `:subagent:` and ACP keys); hidden subagents never receive the tool. The Control UI already receives these question records (`question.requested` goes to every authorized operator client, and the sidebar uses them for attention), but the chat pane only docked prompts whose session equals the open conversation. The pane now also docks pending prompts whose session is a direct child in the child roster it already loads for the subagent rows, keyed by the same owner-qualified parent key. Membership follows lineage, not sidebar placement: a child promoted to a sidebar root still counts, while the implicit Home link of operator-created roots does not make every dashboard session a child of Home (`isImplicitHomeLinkedRoot`, extracted unchanged from the sidebar placement rule). prs.title: fix(macos): sign with any valid certificate when no Apple-class identity is installed
prs.body:
Related: #118989, #119019

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw documents a four-tier macOS signing selection order: Developer ID Application, Apple Distribution, Apple Development, then the first other valid codesigning identity. The fallback parser never selected the fourth tier, and `restart-mac.sh` independently used an Apple-class-only predicate.

The historical PR also accepted any quoted `security find-identity` row. That is unsafe because macOS can quote an identity while marking it unusable, for example `(CSSMERR_TP_NOT_TRUSTED)`.

## Current-Main Change

Rebuilt as one commit on current `main`.

- The existing shared owner, `scripts/lib/mac-signing-identity.sh`, now parses the complete `security find-identity -p codesigning -v` output once.
- It preserves the documented ranking:
  1. Developer ID Application
  2. Apple Distribution
  3. Apple Development
  4. first other valid identity
- Rows carrying a Keychain status suffix after the quoted identity are rejected.
- Usable output is retained even if `security` exits nonzero.
- `restart-mac.sh` now delegates signing-key detection to that same selector, eliminating policy drift.

## Evidence

Current exact-head focused checks:

- tooling tests: **45 passed**, **61 platform-skipped**
- signer regression rejects `CSSMERR_TP_NOT_TRUSTED` rows
- restart auto-detection rejects the same invalid row
- valid non-Apple fallback is accepted by both paths
- ranked Apple-class preference is preserved
- usable output with a nonzero `security` status is preserved
- direct exact-file `oxlint`: passed
- `oxfmt --check`: passed
- `bash -n`: passed for the shared owner and both entry points
- `git diff --check`: passed
- exact GitHub tree matched the tested local tree before publication

The repository's type-aware lint wrapper exceeded this 3.7 GiB host's compiled-boundary budget before producing a source diagnostic; GitHub Actions is the authoritative full integration/type-aware run.

## Remaining External Decision / Proof

This patch does not decide the product policy. Maintainers still need to choose whether auto-selection should accept every identity macOS reports as valid, or only Apple-class identities.

If the documented fourth tier is retained, final native proof requires a macOS machine with an already-trusted non-Apple codesigning identity. This Linux VPS cannot fabricate that Keychain trust result. The committed synthetic regressions cover the parser and both entry points without treating invalid rows as valid.

AI-assisted; implementation and evidence reviewed before publication.

prs.title: improve(ci): speed up release plugin compilation
prs.body:
Related: #171473. Backports the native-compiler portion of #168816 to `release/2026.10.5`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: release plugin compilation repeatedly scans the entire checkout and installed dependency tree, pushing a passing package-boundary job near its timeout.

## User Impact

Less repeated compiler work in release validation; no package diagnostics, SDK declarations, input-containment rules, or process-completion checks are weakened. The 40-minute job budget is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main already removed the redundant before/after snapshots inside each native compiler. Carry that scoped repair and its caller/test alignment, preserving Peter Steinberger's upstream authorship. Release batch/build cache seals, consumed-input hashes, negative resolution lookups, output inventories, and joined cleanup remain in place.

Native-helper source edits during one invocation follow main's best-effort contract: finish edits before compiling or rerun. This does not relax between-run cache validation.

The original job restores main fallback producer `5cf2615e65ec2e8344c836a5572c523783981e60`, not an exact release hit. Fifteen of its 31 generator inputs differ from beta candidate `1808b57b75f056fe4ae247d6cbc1ba68f1717858`, including compiler, snapshot and manifest inputs bound into every plugin's receipt signature. Source-signature misses are therefore expected; a restored archive is not warm compilation. Release gates also do not publish matching compiled caches. This is source-backed attribution, not inspection of the old receipts' exact rejection records.

SDK/package preparation uses the same native compiler helper, so the redundant inner sealing work also applies during `prep`. This change reduces cold compilation and preparation cost without widening cache trust or publication authority.

## Evidence

The initial CI failure was the release base's unrelated `worker-heap-flag.mjs` duplicate-scan coverage omission. Dallin merged [separate prerequisite #171504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171504) as `ade497cac39fe3b01604e867c47f5de2120d3630`. This PR is reconciled onto that base: range-diff is patch-identical and the native coverage guard passes. Existing focused proof and independent review are reused for the unchanged fix, not presented as a fresh review of the mechanical rebase.

- Same checkout, same actual normalization-package compiler request, `GOMAXPROCS=2`: initial 28.18s → 5.49s; warm control 16.14s → 2.57s. All 675 consumed inputs and resolution lookup facts are identical. These are local compiler measurements, not a claim about whole-job CI speedup.
- Native declarations, tsdown integration, and cache invalidation: 39 passed / 6 existing platform skips across three files, 96.25s Vitest / 102.51s wall. The cache test preserves warm reuse and invalidation for changed bytes, resolutions, compiler identity, and ancestor installs.
- Targeted script/test lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Fresh independent AutoReview through P2 with unchanged owner context: no findings.
- Both previous-head hosted build jobs passed. The [package-boundary lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38489515156/job/115611487485) also passed with SDK preparation and one canary, but PR selection compiled zero plugins; it does not prove the original 128-plugin workload's wall clock. No Full Release Validation run was dispatched.
- [Original beta job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38362668271/job/115180817737) and [main comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38342969155/job/115118104139) retain their distinct source/runner timings; no timeout increase is used as performance proof. The precise old fallback receipt's rejection category was not recovered; cache trust/publication rules are unchanged.
- Current head `5f7ef8f1a60004382a0ae158985c44f96c9fe9b6` has [green hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38495085265). [Explicitly requested ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171501#issuecomment-6158844688) completed on this exact head with 0 findings.

prs.title: fix(update): release the writer during delayed host admission
prs.body:
Closes #169260
Related: #171411

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: update-history writes hold SQLite's writer for seconds while a busy updater host delays commit admission, causing the serving Gateway's cron and cleanup writes to time out.

## User Impact

Update validation releases the writer after a one-second commit-admission timeout and retries the rolled-back write. Required update and recovery evidence is still recorded, with live authority checked again. No configuration, schema, retention, or durability changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier repair moved initial admission before BEGIN but retained an unbounded wait before COMMIT. Bound that remaining wait using the existing admission timeout. Retry only a confirmed rollback, inside the same worker command, so later commands cannot overtake it. Fresh initial admission waits outside BEGIN; each attempt rereads current rows. Authority refusals and rollback/cleanup failures escape rather than replaying uncertain effects. A successful commit grant remains terminal.

Update behavior: this takes effect in an installed updater containing the fix and its matching worker. Installing a newer candidate cannot retroactively repair a wait in an older driver. Existing recovery formats and old-driver update compatibility are unchanged.

## Evidence

- The production shared-state dispatcher regression failed on the original implementation: delayed commit admission kept the writer until its late grant, with no rollback/retry opportunity for the competing writer; revocation was never observed.
- Both regression cases pass after repair. They advance only the admission clock, use real SQLite transactions, and prove a competing write succeeds after rollback, its canonical row change survives the retry, and revocation prevents the update mutation from committing. No real timers/sleeps or test-only production hooks.
- Changed regression file: `pnpm test src/infra/update-run-admission-hold.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 2/2, 31.49 s wrapper / 21.44 s Vitest / 1.57 s test time. CI seconds pending.
- 26 sibling tests passed across update-run contention, actual off-thread mutation/publication, and admission timeout/late-grant/receipt settlement. Worker compilation and the actual worker-broker mutation path pass; this is boundary proof, not a replay of the reporter's Debian update or a measured wall-clock 20.5 s stall.
- Independent AutoReview clean through P2; an independent source challenge also checked timeout CAS, live grants, rollback, and stale-refusal handling.
- Targeted core and infrastructure-test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. PR CI supplies broad build/suite proof.

The one-second budget is below the Gateway writer's normal five-second lock budget; it bounds host-admission holding, not arbitrary SQL/disk stalls or the updater host's total latency.

Current candidate is `6fe8a89753f5845ce18176b9d65d20cc4868b372`, rebased onto pinned main `7dfb334aa67a34b9e0ec4cbd8c022e8ea1dffec7` to incorporate the unrelated mock-export guard fix `e7a07c5aee577be3a2425ec4d88cad17813b7505`. The five-file repair's added/deleted edit lines are identical to the previously reviewed `5671ad158d3d573c09977de682b097acea49b5ed` patch. Only untouched dispatcher import context changed, and no conflict resolution was needed. Existing boundary regression, sibling proof, and independent review are reused for that unchanged repair; formatting, type-aware lint, core typecheck, and diff checks pass after rebasing.

Historical [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171493#issuecomment-6157847852) of `5671ad158d3d573c09977de682b097acea49b5ed` found no code issues or before-merge items, with platinum patch quality and gold proof confidence. That review is prior-head evidence. Fresh review of current head `6fe8a89753f5845ce18176b9d65d20cc4868b372` is complete at the same durable review link: no code findings or before-merge items, diamond patch quality, and gold proof confidence.

Historical [CI run 38487563256](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38487563256) failed only the unrelated baseline mock-export guard in `test/helpers/openclaw-test-process.test.ts`; all other jobs passed. Direct complete-log and source inspection established the main-only origin, despite `pnpm test:ci-failed 171493` reporting `new` from a historical main comparison. Main's named defect is now repaired. Current-head [CI run 38491571342](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38491571342) passed, including the formerly failing baseline ratchet. Effective `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review, and security-sensitive review all succeeded, with no failed or pending checks. No failed CI jobs were rerun. No backport or merge was performed.

## Shared packaged update proof

The required published-driver × candidate cell passed on the configured Blacksmith Testbox: [run 38489583100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38489583100). Published stable `2026.10.3` installed the combined frozen fixes on base `7f7fc2eddc99`: source `0471f447eb687007ee3c39fb1c9fb7e21a9c3406`, tree `4a63eeed836cc07ded69b99d3a26b0c4a01c6354`, package SHA256 `176d43d7162defd2899fd29d03e78823ac7dbb8d4bdf766feaa68237a473aeb5`. Native build carrier `98fc5321fd78` represents that same source tree. Updater exit 0; command wall time 202,913 ms and recorded update duration 172,117 ms; durable run `02efd6c3-4258-4692-8c3b-b513250cd6ab` succeeded/finished, `/readyz` returned 200, and installed build, service PID replacement, durable session preservation, and incognito erasure assertions passed. Frozen patch behavior evidence and current rebased-head CI identities are separate.

The extra installed patched-driver `missing-load-path` forward cell [failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38493728042): CLI exit 1 after 225 seconds, `Command cleanup could not confirm that owned work stopped`. Its cause remains unproven; the original harness removed the container before ledger/process capture. A single [diagnostic replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38495316771), with proof-only instrumentation tree `179c9fc91526` and the unchanged production archive, failed differently: supported debug logging polluted schema-inspection JSON, package swap failed, and the durable run finished rolled back with previous-Gateway verification exit 0. Captured PID 1 was `timeout`, with orphan zombies; that supports a reaping risk but does not establish the original error's cause. Neither forward attempt is claimed passing or fixed.

They run a real Gateway with a service-manager shim; native Linux cleanup proof and observer admission-boundary regressions remain separate. No merges, backports, or release publication occurred.

prs.title: fix: identify update snapshot failures before activation

Closes #171408

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading update failure headlines and retry instructions when candidate state snapshot preparation fails before activation.

## User Impact

Operators see `candidate-snapshot-failed` instead of `runtime-verification-failed` and can address the failed snapshot check. The previous Gateway continues serving; snapshot capacity admission and recovery safety remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canary already records snapshot-specific failure facts, but its outcome fell through to the runtime failure reason.
