prs.title: fix(memory): recover after terminal database worker loss
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory could keep reusing a worker-backed database after its worker crashed, exited, or lost admission: the manager's open-state check only knew about local closure and an optional native reader.

## User Impact

The next memory-manager acquisition now re-admits a fresh worker after terminal loss. In-flight requests settle with their existing result or an explicit error, and acknowledged writes remain acknowledged. No schema, retention, configuration, or stored-data changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing execution owner notifies subscribed V2 stores of terminal loss after accepted work settles. Each V2 store exposes a sticky `terminalSignal` after its pending publications settle. The logical execution owner retains its established native cleanup and retry behavior; recoverable opening contention is not terminal. Memory incorporates that signal into its database-open fact, so the existing manager registry owns replacement. Ordinary idle retirement still respawns on demand; explicit close is not reported as terminal loss. This adds no parallel lifecycle owner or synchronous fallback.

Accepted edge cases: a request arriving while terminal work is still settling can reject against the retiring owner; subsequent acquisition uses normal admission. A terminal notification never authorizes replaying an acknowledged or unknown-outcome write. No authority checks were removed: this is the narrow liveness correctness repair.

Consumer audit: memory's initial and lazy publication-worker paths retain the signal. Standing intents, entry origins, and Forget use operation-scoped V2 stores and close them in `finally`. Session writers retain guarded execution handles; transcript/metadata wrappers are operation-scoped, and usage workers already join accepted effects on exit. No additional retained V2 consumer needed wiring. Admission exit receipts retain the existing owner: workers without a borrowed database are skipped, revisions advance only for outstanding references, and exit codes do not control invalidation. Broker failure settlement joins native exit before accepted work resolves; terminal notification then joins V2 publications. This change does not touch the admission-owner API.

## Evidence

- Added real-worker crash/exit regressions for failed and queued requests, sticky terminal errors, and fresh admission; extended authority revocation and committed-write settlement coverage.
- Added a worker-only memory registry regression proving replacement after revocation, preserved indexed content, and subsequent sync. Extended idle retirement and explicit-close checks to prove neither signals terminal loss.
- Local changed-file oxfmt, oxlint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent Codex review: both rounds scoped-clean at P0/P1. No baseline failing run was executed locally.
- Initial CI caught over-eager logical-owner retirement, an incorrectly timed revocation fixture, and test fixtures missing the new callback. Focused local reruns pass: cleanup/recovery 7 tests; V2 and legacy worker stores 28 tests. The corrected fixture revokes after native COMMIT but before enclosing publication settlement.
- The automated GitHub P1 review identified the same eager-retirement recovery problem; the correction preserves logical-owner admission and removes the proactive close.
- An intermediate CI run found two inherited main failures: a mock-export guard and an SDK declaration caller. Integrated the main repairs (`e7a07c5aee577b`, `4aa62334122ed2`); final-head CI is green without exceptions.
- [Prior-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38490635194): passed all tests/types, lint, Madge architecture guards, source contracts, T1 and dialect ratchets without exceptions. Integrated main again to include receipt-preserving worker exit (`15534c36e2da`); no lane production files changed. [Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38492776005) passed on `d564f4972f208a367768b10aa65bd3bcba544e30`, including all tests/types, lint, architecture and source guards, T1 and dialect ratchets.
- Integrated-head `pnpm deadcode:exports`: full-tree and script scans passed. Production scan has one inherited finding, `ui/src/components/web-awesome.ts: consumeDropdownKeyboardDismissal`; main sidebar commit `f3e38df873ad6e` removed its production callers. The UI subtree and Knip configs match integrated main `6d874e3a88d04c`; only tests retain the symbol. No changed file is flagged. Recorded for the main-repair owner. Run separately because ordinary PR CI omits the dependency task; the preceding head passed all three scans.
- [Published-driver × candidate update cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38492782731/job/115632609035): passed on `d564f4972f208a367768b10aa65bd3bcba544e30`; the selected `published-driver-update` job and its actual test step both completed successfully. Unfinished update attempts were canceled when CI-driven corrections and main integration superseded their heads.

prs.title: fix(talk): keep accepted agent work after client failures
prs.body:
Fixes #171310

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Control UI Talk failure cancels an already-accepted agent request and loses its answer from the conversation.

## User Impact

Talk still ends with its visible error, while the accepted request finishes and its answer remains in the conversation. Explicit Stop still cancels. On failure, the original answer may appear alongside recorded speech because speech does not identify which overlapping consult was delivered.

An older Gateway retains its legacy abort behavior: Control UI sends `disposition` only when the current connection advertises `talk-session-close-disposition`. This uses the existing capability list because older strict schemas reject unknown fields. The additive optional `"abort" | "detach"` field has no protocol version bump; omission means abort. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failure owner commits detachment before UI callbacks can invoke Stop, and relay cleanup no longer sends a competing `chat.abort`. Close forwards the disposition to the existing realtime owner. Closed transports suppress tool-result sends; a rejected detach request reconnects only its original connection through the existing reconnect owner.

Answer visibility is decided at the consult's existing transcript preparation hook. A final prepared after detachment is written visibly from the start. If it was already prepared hidden, the consult owner retains its visible form until close and uses the existing append-only transcript-turn writer to add one visible entry. The original hidden entry remains byte-for-byte unchanged. The appended copy has a stable event/idempotency key and `excludeFromContext`, preserving model history without duplicate context. The display copy omits usage metadata so token/cost accounting remains on the original answer. No transcript scan, anchor lookup, or close-time rewrite remains. The existing `withRelayTranscriptRetries` is shared by both append paths. Ordinary voice writes fail fast on unknown outcomes; detached answers reconcile their stable idempotency key through the transcript-turn owner before inserting. Reconciled entries are published with the same message ID so a lost commit reply does not lose the live notification. Close attempts every retained answer even if an earlier one fails, then reports collected append/close errors after releasing the writer.

Stale-fact audit: the admitted session ID and lifecycle revision are checked against the current row atomically by the transcript-turn owner; the retained source environment, agent/key/store binding and physical writer/source authority are checked at each append admission; retained operator/device authority is checked immediately before the write. These checks remain valid after transport retirement. Pending runs use the existing Chat admission and terminal persistence authority. Detachment is presentation state, not authority. Configuration/request limits remain the accepted run's snapshot; the append uses the current runtime configuration to revalidate routing. Answer content and its stable deduplication identity are intentionally retained unchanged. Retained answers are bounded by the existing per-session tool-call admission ledger.

## Evidence

PR CI is the execution gate per maintainer policy. It covers protocol and native generation, types, Gateway persistence, and Control UI regressions. Tests include `settles close disposition %s (after final: %s; spoken transcript: %s; second consult: %s; unknown append: %s)`: real RPC/admission/transcript persistence with held model execution, both completion orders, overlap, and speech. It asserts every prior transcript entry is unchanged, one visible answer is present, and the appended copy is excluded from model context. Additional cases inject unknown outcomes before and after commit and check the visible answer reaches live events without a duplicate transcript entry. `settles detached answer recovery (%s)` covers transient/persistent append failure and voice-record close failure. Existing regressions cover schema enum validation, default abort/Stop, capability reset, append timeout, playback/output-cancellation failure, failed tool-result submission, and reconnect fencing.

Local unit tests, negative controls, typechecks, and live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof were intentionally skipped under the maintainer's lint-only policy. No leases or Gateways were started. Protocol JSON and Swift/Kotlin artifacts were regenerated through their generators; this revision does not change the schema. Changed-file oxlint/oxfmt passed. The 24 changed TypeScript files pass type-aware oxlint with the core config and oxfmt; the changed documentation is formatted. Final committed-branch Codex autoreview is clean at P0-P2. One earlier review finding corrected the regression oracle to expect existing speech before appended answers. Exact-head [CI run 38492106986](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38492106986) passed for `95e801a6b9977949d2b5dd72c1d68891cbfbc15b`: 73 jobs succeeded, 20 were skipped, and none failed. The earlier callback-typing and retained-source failures were fixed. Both automated P2 recovery findings were fixed and their review threads resolved. Upstream ratchet and participant-publication compiler failures were resolved by merging their main fixes (`e7a07c5aee577` and `4aa62334122ed`). The final committed-branch review is clean at P0-P2. All PR checks are green: 101 successful, 41 skipped, and one neutral, including the aggregate CI gate and both shared-kit scans.

| Scope | Added | Removed | Net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 270 | 103 | +167 |
| Tests | 810 | 275 | +535 |
| Docs | 11 | 1 | +10 |

The positive production delta supplies compatibility gating, cancellation ownership and guarded append-only recovery. The close-time transcript scan/rewrite and its watermark bookkeeping are gone. The previous implementation was +298/-103 (+195 net).

prs.title: fix(ui): keep reply strips and work attached through chat updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: live tools can lose their reply strip, and completing, steering, or reloading chat can detach work, absorb another run's failed attempt, or replace an answer's controls.

## User Impact

Known responses keep their tools, answer, and reply controls together. Confirmed steers affect only subsequent output without closing an already-open tool while the same execution is still active. Explicit replies to an older message remain visible while its original is loading or unavailable. Loading earlier history preserves a confirmed post-steer answer's focused controls.

Automatic resumes without a known human binding remain separate and unattributed instead of guessing from the last person who spoke. The strip design is unchanged. No Gateway protocol, storage, configuration, permission, or native-app changes.

**Remaining limits:** an unconfirmed peer input without a target-run receipt can still change a later answer's row key when earlier same-run history loads. The stable prepend guarantee applies to confirmed steers. The independent-run stress case still has measurable projection overhead; this is not a zero-slowdown claim. This PR remains a draft and has not been merged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Establish execution/display ownership before visual rollups can erase it. Keep execution liveness separate from display segments, and keep chronological reply context separate from automatic recipient attribution. Remove the superseded cross-turn reply-ownership path. Skip empty and singleton rollup work and temporary singleton frame arrays rather than pooling unrelated executions for speed.

## Evidence

- Both audit regressions failed through the mounted production transcript on the preceding PR head: a confirmed steer disconnected the focused open tool; an unbound run lost its explicit pending/missing reply strip. Both now pass. Starting a different execution does not keep the old run expanded.
- Final node scripts/check-changed.mjs passed (276.6 s): production and affected test types, lint, styles, i18n, ratchets and dead-export checks. Independent final AutoReview at P0–P2 is scoped-clean. The earlier review's two index-only findings were the reproduced bugs; the staged final repair was re-reviewed.
- Ownership, attribution, failure/recovery, navigation and cache siblings pass. Existing scale tests retain zero rereads of 3,000 historical messages for unchanged/text-only updates. Final changed-owner recheck: 68 grouping/index/cache cases plus 8 mounted control cases; the separate reply suite passes all 29 cases. Counts across repeated checks overlap.
- Final production bundle: **7/7 browser cases passed**, including native tool start/result output opened/closed/reopened with the actual keyboard toggle, and real paginated history loading that preserves the exact focused post-steer Reply button and viewport anchor (≤2 px). The two old browser gaps now have passing proof; the original failed selectors are not claimed conclusively diagnosed. Desktop, mobile and tablet participant controls also pass.
- Browser evidence is the actual bundled Control UI with a synthetic Gateway, not a live provider. Final bounded browser performance is measured below.

### Performance

A fresh balanced B–PR–optimized–optimized–PR–B comparison executes the real builder → chain → index path. Three warmups and 12 observations per process give 24 observations per revision/operation. Immutable props, cache reuse, effective tool/text/final transitions and prior-chain immutability are asserted. Node projection timings exclude rendering.

For 3,000 independent tool-only runs, optimized cold/tool/final medians are **29.905 / 32.203 / 30.235 ms**, versus previous PR **33.962 / 38.217 / 32.739 ms** and base **24.951 / 25.701 / 23.769 ms**. The redundant chain work is reduced, but **+4.955–6.502 ms** remains over base. At 300 mixed runs the residual is **+0.327–0.398 ms**. The corrected projection retains 3,001 execution frames rather than the base's pooled 1–2 rows; not all remaining cost is proven unavoidable. Ordinary 3,000-message structural medians are within −1.055 to −0.033 ms of base; single-active-run medians are +0.125 to +1.241 ms, with overlapping ranges. These bounded measurements do not prove universal equivalence, browser speed, or absence of leaks.

Final actual-browser comparison (B–F–F–B, six fresh-context observations/version): ordinary 3,000-message finalization **100.10 → 100.60 ms**; mixed 300-message text **48.025 → 48.125 ms**. Neither showed a consistent slowdown across balanced pairs. Mixed cold loading remains **516.65 → 556.85 ms (+40.20 ms / 7.78%)**, with positive deltas in both pairs and noisy magnitude. Mixed mounted rows/elements increase **3/62 → 15/326**; ordinary final remains **14/472**. These are render-to-frame opportunity proxies, not hardware paint, backend latency or CPU. Fixtures are newly frozen and identical between versions, not a numeric replay of the earlier audit. **The zero-slowdown objective is not met for mixed cold loads; keep this tradeoff visible during draft review.**

### Before

![Before: live tool activity has no reply strip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/618de6d2-7fb4-4bbe-b757-f3aebf1e9085)

### After

![After: the reply strip appears above live tools before the answer arrives](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/481a79a6-e12d-4f44-a100-01c056da10c4)

Existing representative captures: same synthetic conversation, 1440×900 dark viewport, actual Control UI. They show the original strip change; this follow-up repairs lifecycle/attribution behavior without redesigning that strip.

<details>
<summary>Measured local test cost</summary>

One-worker mounted-controls invocation: **4.40 s** total, 8 cases. Reply suite: **5.98 s** total, 29 cases. Grouping/index/cache recheck: **4.33 s** total, 68 cases across three files.

Final canonical browser file: **9.675 s** test time, **34.60 s** invocation, including a **21.43 s** production build. New pagination/native-tool cases take **1.066 / 1.128 s** and guard Gateway admission, native scrolling, focus and disclosure lifetime that projection assertions cannot prove. CI seconds for this revision are not yet available.

</details>

Requested by and co-authored with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3f3644ab-9b41-4fc1-a48a-b90a0eaa3fe2)

prs.title: fix(database): make agent projections and publication receipts portable
prs.body:
Related: #171350, #170055, #171434.

## What Problem This Solves

Agent database reads still build SQLite-only JSON aggregates, while several session publications and worker commit receipts use a different connection identity from PostgreSQL transaction settlement.

## User Impact

SQLite behavior and JSON-text boundaries remain unchanged. Standing-intent expiry keeps exact epoch-millisecond precision on PostgreSQL. Agent PostgreSQL remains disabled; this PR does not claim a working durable PostgreSQL actor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generic engine helpers now own selected-row arrays, selected-row objects, JSON tuples, and ordered aggregation. Session actor hydration and entry/member facts keep their projections in SQL. PostgreSQL aggregates preserve SQLite's ascending NULL ordering and return text, including `[]` for empty arrays. The actor retains its existing payload/navigation owner.

Session publication callers use `sqlPublicationAnchor`. The central worker receipt owner uses the same anchor for staging, pending-receipt checks, commit, and rollback. Connection-local read caches retain their existing identity. Ordinary memory relational persistence and snapshot/event mutations already use portable conflict targets and owned mutation results.

No schema, retention, durability, physical-open, FTS/vector, or payload-decoding change.

## Evidence

The capture harness invokes the actual owners with a PostgreSQL-branded capture connection, then PREPAREs and EXPLAINs their unmodified emitted SQL/bindings on PostgreSQL 17 against freshly generated agent DDL (`pnpm db:postgres:gen`). The separate generic-helper statement tests the actor's new row array/object primitive. The disposable external-SSD cluster used port 55447 and was stopped and removed.

| Statement | Owner / contract | PREPARE + EXPLAIN |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Exact entry facts: participant/member tuples | PASS |
| 2 | Selected entries: membership IDs | PASS |
| 3 | Full actor hydration | BLOCKED: unchanged PR5 model-navigation SQL calls SQLite `json_extract` |
| 4 | Standing-intent fired selection | PASS |
| 5 | Standing-intent expiration update | PASS |
| 6 | Standing-intent next-expiry projection | PASS |
| 7 | Engine selected-row arrays/objects used by actor hydration | PASS |

PostgreSQL execution additionally proves row-object arrays, SQL NULL for a missing object, empty `[]`, null-first order, and the text result boundary. **The whole-actor PREPARE requirement remains open until PR5 supplies its portable navigation expression.** No SQL replacement in the harness hides that failure.

SQLite owner proof: **20 files / 213 cases pass**, all run with `--maxWorkers=1`: 71 infrastructure cases, 107 runtime/config cases, 29 standing-intent cases, four session-notification cases, and two generic JSON cases. The infrastructure/runtime/standing batch completed in 636.95s wrapper wall time (147.60s / 368.15s / 71.88s Vitest config durations). The fixed JSON file passed in its 8.63s Vitest config; the wrapper inventory passed in 27.51s (the combined focused rerun took 50.43s wrapper wall time).

Core and extension typechecks/lint, final formatting, madge (zero cycles), and `git diff --check` pass. Two completed independent Codex reviews found no actionable P0–P2 defects. A subsequent mechanical guardrail correction uses Kysely-typed ordering references; recapturing all seven statements confirms byte-identical SQL and bindings. Production: +189/-72, **net +117**; tests and the wrapper manifest are separate.

The shrink-only dialect ratchet reports mechanical **0 → 0**, design **0 → 0**, maintenance **0 → 0** in changed files. It does not lexically count the Kysely JSON helper calls removed at the owners: the direct SQLite helper import and all three owner `json_group_array` builders are gone. No baseline or inventory exception was expanded. The full local worker census was stopped after ten minutes without a result. Current-head CI supplies the broad worker proof: live calls **302 → 302**, deprecated compatibility calls **13 → 13**, and the worker ratchet passes. Source audit found no new database access lane.

Initial validation exposed two fixture/tooling issues: edits during the first cold worker compile invalidated that run, and the new JSON fixture used `selectAll()`, which Kysely's SQLite JSON helper intentionally rejects. That fixture now selects explicit columns and passes. The first wrapper check identified the newly reachable JSON engine helper; its one-line manifest entry was added and the same check passes. No retry masks a production failure.

The branch was rebased over #171448, preserving the new context metadata fields; only the actor import block conflicted. Rebased core typechecking passes, and both affected actor suites pass 7/7 cases (79.48s Vitest duration). PostgreSQL statements were recaptured and reproven on this rebased source with the same 6-pass / 1-blocked result. A second mechanical rebase preserved the shared-state native-binding receipt changes on main; its only conflict was the import block. The native-binding settlement suite passes 5/5 cases (68.16s Vitest duration), and core typechecking and formatting pass again. The reviewed production patch is unchanged apart from dropping the now-shared import.

The first [CI run 38487006092](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38487006092) found a new Kysely identifier guardrail violation in the ordering helper. That is corrected with typed Kysely column references; the complete guardrail and core typecheck pass, and emitted SQL/bindings are byte-identical. The current head’s [architecture job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38488361142/job/115607959608) passes, including the Kysely guardrail. It also found an oversized actor-transfer assertion failure in `session-actor.test.ts` (missing immediate actor snapshot after commit). The CI classifier marks that failure **unknown** because there is no matching main job. A focused local replay passes both transfer cases (33.41s Vitest / 39.25s wrapper); this is replay evidence, not a proven repair. SQLite anchor identity and generated SQL are unchanged. The snapshot invalidation, commit-install, and eviction paths are owned by the untouched `session-actor-replica.ts`; no cause has been established there.

**PostgreSQL conformance passed** on `f191d4a65837b081f079bccf31dc63cbc33b620e`: [job 115607959313](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38488361142/job/115607959313). All three selected shards pass: **47 files / 463 tests passed**, with four files / 38 tests skipped by the existing suite selection (1047.08s wrapper duration). Generated agent DDL conformance verifies 45 tables, 378 columns, 66 CHECKs, 105 indexes, 28 FKs, and trigger parity with zero unexplained differences. The test-only maintainer CI dispatch preserves the draft state; ordinary draft PR CI skips preflight. The previous run was canceled after being superseded by the guardrail fix; no rerun was used to chase a passing result. Current-head `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` passes worker/dialect/assertion/timeout checks but fails mock-export validation in `test/helpers/openclaw-test-process.test.ts:5`. That file exists on CI base `af73fe4e28713def66b2457202d0d48b88e57786` (blob `55139480ed9a1a1d4b8f9790a23089b85e5d9e0e`) and is absent from this branch: the failure is inherited through the merge tree. The actor test shard passes on the current head. `check-dependencies` separately reports unused `scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts`; the script is unchanged from the branch base (blob `18bc16e755c1ae6cbe560166fa0532e9adcb910a`) and is documented as a standalone performance command. `checks-node-changed-compact-large-44` reports `ECONNRESET` in `server-agent-database-startup.test.ts`; the single failing case passes in a focused local replay (155.02s Vitest / 173.80s wrapper). That replay does not establish a repair or the cause of the CI connection reset. The broader CI run remains red from these recorded failures; PostgreSQL conformance is green. The gateway failure is not attributed to this patch without evidence.

## Skipped sites and coordinated follow-ups

- PR5: `transcript-payload.ts`, all `session-transcript-hydration*`, and the dependent `session-model-context-projection.ts` API cutover. Its callers need an engine argument together; no fallback or competing projection owner was added. The unchanged actor navigation expression is the statement-3 blocker.
- Dependent bounded projections: `session-accessor.sqlite-history-input-visibility.ts` and `session-accessor.sqlite-active-events.ts` need PR5's navigation/run-ID contract. `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-query.ts`, `session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-candidates.ts`, and `session-accessor.sqlite-reference-projection.ts` retain duplicate-key, malformed/overdepth, NUL/surrogate, and byte-order contracts requiring their complete projection cutover. PostgreSQL `json_each` decodes all strings and rejects escaped NUL/unpaired-surrogate JSON that the existing SQLite path can project. Faithful bounded support needs generic text-preserving traversal/validation (or a separately accepted migration contract); this PR does not add whole-payload JavaScript fallbacks.
- Async publication lane: actor/resident/rewrite sites in `session-actor.worker.ts`, `session-participant-contribution.worker.ts`, `session-transcript-authority.ts`, and `session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-{suffix-write,turn,write-snapshot}.ts`; credential authority, GitHub lifecycle, memory schema extension, and entry-cache-state remain with that lane. Its existing entry-cache-state ternary already resolves the PostgreSQL anchor.
- PR2: outbox FIFO reads still depend on implicit rowid and must move with the pending enqueue-sequence schema/migration.
- Memory embedding-cache eviction: equal-time FIFO rowid behavior is explicitly tested; replacing it needs an owned persisted ordering contract, not a new key-order tie-breaker.
- FTS/vec and their identity/publication paths remain P3-5. Historical transcript payload migration stays with the native/payload migration owner.
- ATTACH-based memory shadow publication remains a follow-up. Physical agent open/admission/lifecycle remains PR3.
- No edits to concurrent heartbeat/first-turn/context work, `sqlite-worker-store.ts`, #169580's files, or the shared inventory files.

Worker inventory delta: no new database access site or execution lane; existing worker-owned queries and publication receipt calls are retained. Only generic JSON construction and anchor normalization changed; shared inventory sources were not edited.

## Landing validation

Rebased onto merged #171449 with no conflicts, preserving its session-window projections, transcript facts, and cron listing semantics. The mechanical helper/anchor delta is retained. The one landing push is `700258b51e493740deb481d50c2cbc865f5b85be`. Post-rebase owner and wrapper closure proof passes: five files / 62 tests with `--maxWorkers=1`; the worker ratchet passes (T1 224 → 224, deprecated-only 12 → 12). No generated outputs conflicted.

[Exact-head CI run 38494536105](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38494536105) completed. [PostgreSQL conformance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38494536105/job/115627888621), security-fast, and every other selected job passed except the mock-export ratchet and its downstream gate.

The native inherited-failure admin exception is limited to [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38494536105/job/115627888337): `worker-turn-launcher.lazy.test.ts:212` mocks `./worker-turn-execution.js` without pass-through. This reproduces identically on main `92317bc41a6897`. The test, target, checker, and baseline have identical blobs in that main checkout, CI base `61ed7497922beb`, and tested merge `70696430ce1de3c012fcc68053f4fb1b07228157`. No inventory, closure, or ratchet exception is added by this PR. The original `openclaw-test-process.test.ts:5` ratchet failure also reproduced at its old CI base and was fixed on main in `e7a07c5aee577b`.

The original gateway `ECONNRESET` case passes in [current CI job 115627889196](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38494536105/job/115627889196). The original unused-file report does not reproduce with a frozen install at its original CI main base or current main. Neither earlier failure is claimed to have a proven root-cause repair; neither remains in current CI.

prs.title: fix(subagents): attribute crash-orphaned runs and notify requesters
prs.body:
Recreates https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/135490 after the repository author-PR ceiling was corrected and portfolio slots were deliberately reprioritized.

## What Problem This Solves

Subagents orphaned by a Gateway crash are later reaped with generic or misleading text, and no-output runs can be deleted without notifying the requester. A real 5m36s run reaped after a 34-minute VM outage appeared to have run for 40m35s, leading incident response toward a false timeout diagnosis.

## Why This Change Was Made

The orphan reconciler correlates runs with persisted Gateway and host boot lifecycle evidence, reports bounded elapsed time from the best available death signal, and declines attribution when evidence is insufficient or later run activity disproves the inferred death window.

Before crash attribution, the sweeper resolves any fresh persisted terminal child state. Attributed crash completions are explicitly recovery outcomes, so even a delayed restart beyond the original run deadline preserves the crash diagnosis and bounded death timestamp instead of converting it to a timeout. Startup restoration preserves eligible active orphans for requester-visible completion while still pruning queued orphans.

Host boot identity is resolved before each immediate SQLite write transaction. Its nullable column is owned by the canonical startup-additive registry, allowing same-version databases missing the column to be classified and repaired safely.

Crash recovery carries real authority — it can persist a terminal result, notify a requester, and clean up a session — so every completion request the orphan reconciler issues is now bound to the exact registry row it inspected, and that binding survives the retry and restart-drain paths. A same-id successor that takes the slot while the completion waits on the terminal lock is left untouched.

The recorded diagnostic no longer states facts the registry cannot back. Captured `resultText` and `fallbackResultText` are alternative result snapshots, not message records, so the text reports recorded-output presence rather than an invented assistant-message count. The interval between the run's last recorded activity and the restart is described as exactly that, not as an asserted Gateway outage duration — last activity can precede the crash, so that interval is an upper bound on downtime.

## User Impact

Requesters learn that a child was orphaned and why, while diagnostics avoid inventing lifetimes from a late reap timestamp. Legacy rows, clean shutdowns, runs active after a successor boot, uptime-derived identities, and already-terminal child sessions are not over-attributed. A requester whose run was replaced or released mid-recovery is not told the successor failed.

## Evidence

### Authority-chain proof

**Withdrawn claim (round 24).** An earlier revision of this section reported "three scenarios, 46 assertions, `All runtime assertions passed.`" plus an 8-assertion differential. Those numbers were measured on an older head. At head `b099c4fa5c3` the harness **did not execute at all** — it died on its first persistence call with `TypeError: persistSubagentRunsToDisk is not a function`, because the `persistSubagentRunsToDisk` / `…OrThrow` / `…AsyncOrThrow` family and `loadSubagentRegistryFromSqlite`'s old module home were removed from `origin/main` (the lifecycle controller persists through `mutateSubagentRuns` now and no longer accepts `persist*` options at all). Those numbers are withdrawn, not restated. Everything below was produced by running the repaired harness on the current head.

`scripts/proof-136476-orphan-owner-binding.ts` exercises resumption, requeue, release and replacement **during queued completion** and reads the final effects back out of a real SQLite state database.

Real, not mocked and not vitest: `reconcileStaleActiveSubagentRun`, `createSubagentRegistryCompletionRuntime`, `SubagentLifecycleController` (its actual terminal completion lock, `expectedEntry` guard and terminal-effect chain), the real `mutateSubagentRuns` publication path inside that controller, `persistRegistryFixture` / `loadSubagentRegistryFromSqlite` against a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `recordGatewayBootStart` / `readGatewayBootLifecycleSegments`. Stubs exist only at the transport edge (announce flow, completion-reply capture, gateway call, requester settle wake, browser cleanup) and are recorders, so "was the requester notified" is an observed fact. One row is written directly — the crashed predecessor boot, because the production writer can only ever record the current pid; it is inserted through the same schema with a foreign pid, no completion time and no outcome.

Six scenarios, 96 assertions, `All runtime assertions passed.`:

1. **current** (control) — the run goes durably terminal in SQLite with the attributed crash error, the published row is still the inspected run's own owner, the requester is notified exactly once, cleanup dispatches.
2. **replaced** — a successor row takes the runId while the completion is queued. Its in-memory record and its **durable SQLite row** are byte-identical to their pre-recovery snapshots; announce, completion-reply capture, gateway call, browser cleanup, requester settle wake and context-engine end notification are all zero.
3. **released** — the row is deleted while the completion is queued. The durable row is byte-identical to its pre-recovery snapshot and nothing is delivered.
4. **resumed** (new) — the **same** row acquires a live execution context while the completion is queued. `expectedEntry` still identifies its owner, so only the execution-authority fence can stop the terminal write, the notification and the cleanup.
5. **queued** (new) — the **same** run is republished as queued while the completion is queued. The republished row satisfies `isSameSubagentRunOwner`, so the controller would still admit it; the durable row must stay queued and byte-identical.
6. **history-read race** (repaired, round 25) — a successor takes the runId during the real read-worker round trip for boot history, after the helper has consumed its session observation and before it has decided anything.

   **Corrected claim (round 25).** As shipped at head `093609122f5` this scenario did not reach the boundary it advertised, and the review was right: the helper awaits session reconciliation first, so a replacement installed synchronously after the call landed in that earlier read and `assertReadCurrent` retired the helper before `loadGatewayBootSegmentsForAttribution` ever ran. The window is now entered deterministically rather than by timing. The run's recorded child session key is blank — the `missing-session-entry` orphan, whose classification resolves without a session worker read — so the history read is the only read the helper suspends on; the harness starts that read itself with the cache seeded stale and awaits it first, and the helper's own call finds the same load in flight and queues behind it. The successor is therefore installed while the helper is inside the real round trip. Two assertions count the selection checks (two before the read, exactly one after it) so the scenario cannot pass vacuously again.

   **Verified by deletion, as the review asked.** With the post-history `isCurrent()` check removed from `subagent-registry-sweeper-orphan.ts` and nothing else changed, the repaired scenario fails — and *only* the counting assertion fails:

   ```
   96 assertions, 1 failed.
     - race: the helper re-checked its selection after the history read :: {"selectionChecks":2}
   ```

   Every other race assertion still passed in that condition, because the downstream `expectedEntry` identity guard and the `recoveryCurrent` fence catch the replacement on their own. That is exactly why the previous assertion set could not isolate this guard — and with the guard still deleted, the *previous* scenario reported `94 assertions, 0 failed. All runtime assertions passed.` It certified a guard that was not in the tree.

The harness is discriminating, not green-by-construction. **Re-measured at the round-25 head with the 96-assertion harness** (the previous text's "94 assertions, 12 failed" was measured on the round-24 harness and is superseded, not restated). Reverting only `subagent-registry-sweeper-orphan.ts` and `subagent-registry-sweeper.ts` to `b099c4fa5c3` and changing nothing else fails **13** assertions. Twelve are the reported P1: the resumed and requeued rows are written durably terminal with the dead run's crash error and `endedReason: subagent-error`, and announce, browser cleanup, requester settle wake and the context-engine end notification all fire against live work. The thirteenth is the new pre-read selection count, which reads `0` on the reverted helper — it does not re-assert the selection before the history read at all:

```
96 assertions, 13 failed.
 - resumed: requester was NOT notified :: {"announce":1,"browserCleanup":1,"settleWake":1,"contextEngineEnded":1}
 - resumed: no browser cleanup dispatched / no requester settle wake /
   no context-engine end notification :: (same recorder)
 - resumed: durable row was never written to a terminal state ::
     {"status":"terminal","endedReason":"subagent-error",
      "outcome":{"status":"error","error":"gateway restarted at … ended without a clean stop …",
                 "startedAt":…,"endedAt":…,"elapsedMs":120000}}
 - resumed: durable row is byte-identical to its pre-recovery snapshot
 - queued: requester was NOT notified :: {"announce":1,"browserCleanup":1,"settleWake":1,"contextEngineEnded":1}
 - queued: no browser cleanup dispatched / no requester settle wake /
   no context-engine end notification :: (same recorder)
 - queued: durable row stayed queued and was never written to a terminal state ::
     {"status":"terminal","endedReason":"subagent-error", …}
 - queued: durable row is byte-identical to its pre-recovery snapshot
 - race: the helper consumed its session observation before the history read :: {"selectionChecks":0}
```

The control scenario also prints the real recorded error, which is where the two diagnostic corrections are visible in production output rather than in a test string:

```
gateway restarted at 2026-10-12T22:56:12.944Z (previous boot f0767e87-… ended without a clean stop
at an unrecorded earlier time); the host rebooted under it; run orphaned after at least 2m from the
run's last recorded activity, no output recorded in the run registry; the restart came 56m after the
run's last recorded activity
```

### Regression coverage

Nine cases in `subagent-registry-lifecycle-orphan-settlement.test-support.ts` drive the same boundary through the real caller → retry runtime → terminal lock path: three originating helper paths (persisted terminal, attributed orphan, lost context) × current/replaced/released ownership.

Three further cases in `subagent-registry-sweeper-orphan-contracts.test.ts` run the sweeper against the **real** session-reconciliation module rather than a mock of it — which is why the two reconciliation defects below were invisible to the existing orphan suite, whose `vi.mock` returns a reason string where production returns a deferred observation. Reverting only the two source files to `b099c4fa5c3` fails all three:

```
× reconciles a raw child session key through its recorded owner
  → promise rejected "Error: Session key does not contain an agent id…" instead of resolving
× resolves the deferred orphan observation instead of formatting the observation itself
  → "subagent run orphaned: [object Object]"  (expected "…: missing-session-entry")
× carries execution authority that refuses a run which comes back to life
  → { admitted: undefined, … }                (no fence on the completion request at all)
```

Eight further cases in `subagent-restore-resume-ownership.test.ts` (round 25) pin the restore path's resume/handoff predicate against the real reconciliation module; see [Restored-run resumption](#restored-run-resumption-round-25) for its differential.

A tenth lifecycle case (`does not reopen successor cleanup after orphan persistence fails twice`) was removed, not repaired: its premise was a `persistOrThrow` option on `SubagentLifecycleController` that no longer exists on `origin/main` — terminal writes go through `mutateSubagentRuns` now — so the seam it injected a failure at cannot be reached and the case had never compiled since the base merge. A duplicate copy of `does not apply a queued interrupted completion to a same-id successor`, resurrected by that same base merge in its older pre-`createDeferredCore` form, was also removed; `origin/main`'s current copy (which additionally asserts the rejection outcome) is retained.

### Restored-run resumption (round 25)

The restore path's resume/handoff predicate had the same defect as the proof scenario above, in the opposite direction: `resolveSubagentRunOrphanReason` returns a deferred `{ read }` object for the ordinary case — an unended, nonqueued run with a child session key and no retained obligation — so `Boolean(...)` over its result was true for **every** such run, without ever inspecting `sessionEntry` or `orphanReason`. Restoration handed the sweeper every active restored run, including recent children whose sessions had already finished cleanly, leaving their requesters unsettled until a later sweep. That inverts the distinction the predicate's own provenance names (`333e43cd52e`: recover interrupted owners while allowing completed sessions to resume normal settlement), which is the before-merge provenance item this round closes.

The three session-entry conditions now live in one exported pure classifier, `classifySubagentRunOrphanFromSessionEntry`. The deferred reader delegates to it, so the deferred and immediate forms agree by construction, and the restore predicate finishes the classification against the child session entry the restorer already read for that exact owner — no second worker round trip, and the recorded `childAgentId` scoping of that read is untouched.

**An existing test was red on the previous head and is green now.** `keeps restored recovery dormant until the Gateway lifecycle activates it` (`subagent-registry.persistence.resume.test.ts:568`) seeds a restored running child with a written child session, activates the Gateway, and waits for `recoveryRuntime.waitForAgent`. On head `093609122f5` it **timed out at 120s** — the row was never resumed, so the wait never happened. That file is byte-identical to `origin/main` on this branch, and `origin/main` does not contain the sweeper-ownership clause at all, so both the clause and the red were this branch's:

```
# head 093609122f5
 × subagent registry persistence resume > keeps restored recovery dormant until the
   Gateway lifecycle activates it  120027ms
   → Test timed out in 120000ms.
 Tests  1 failed | 70 passed (71)       # |agents-support| shard

# head cbce78e043a
 Tests  71 passed (71)
```

Eight new cases in `subagent-restore-resume-ownership.test.ts` pin the predicate directly against the real reconciliation module (the existing restore suite `vi.mock`s `resolveSubagentRunOrphanReason` to `() => null`, which is why neither it nor the type checker could see this). Reverting only the predicate, with the classifier extraction kept, fails exactly the two cases that assert resumption and none of the six that assert the orphan handoff:

```
 × resumes a recent child whose session already finished
 × resumes a recent child whose session is still running
 ✓ hands a run with no child session entry to orphan recovery
 ✓ hands a child session with no session id to orphan recovery
 ✓ hands a stale unended run to orphan recovery
 ✓ hands an aborted child session to orphan recovery
 ✓ resumes a run whose retained obligation already names its owner
 ✓ resumes a queued or already-ended row without consulting the session
 Tests  2 failed | 6 passed (8)
```

### Preserved positive trace

The parent-head isolated production proof used two real Gateway processes and one persisted state directory:

1. Gateway 1 accepted a real parent agent turn, spawned a real child, and confirmed both the registry row and task row were still `running` while the child command was alive.
2. Gateway 1 was killed abruptly.
3. Gateway 2 started against the same state database and ran the production sweeper.
4. The requester received the attributed terminal event in real session history; the registry row retired and the child session was deleted exactly once.

```json
{"beforeCrash":{"registryStatus":"running","taskStatus":"running","childCommandAlive":true},"restart":{"priorBootAbrupt":true,"bootRows":2,"sameHostBootId":true},"recovered":{"attributedRequesterEvent":true,"requesterHistoryVisible":true,"registryStatus":"retired","taskStatus":"failed","sessionDeleteCount":1}}
```

That trace was recorded on an earlier head and is **not** claimed as a fresh run on this one; it is preserved because it covers ordinary crash recovery, which the new harness does not replace. A real SQLite regression also retains 70 boot rows, proving the attribution reader overrides the ordinary 64-row diagnostic cap and preserves the oldest owning boot.

### Data-model compatibility (round 21)

`gateway_boot_lifecycle.host_boot_id` is a bare nullable `TEXT` column registered as a lazy additive column. The upgrade and rollback contracts were measured against real SQLite (ad-hoc script, not a committed harness — a committed `scripts/proof-*.ts` would have to be registered in `config/knip.config.ts`):

```
A  fresh start (empty state dir, real assertOpenClawDatabasesReady + open + recordGatewayBootStart)
   -> gateway_boot_lifecycle has host_boot_id; the boot row carries kernel:<uuid>
B1 preflight of a POPULATED pre-column database (previous schema SQL, same schema version, 2 real boot rows)
   -> status=startup-repairable requiresWrite=true foundVersion=17
      issues=["missing-column:gateway_boot_lifecycle.host_boot_id"]
B2 current-binary startup against that database
   -> both populated legacy rows preserved field-for-field; host_boot_id NULL on both;
      the new boot row carries a populated host boot id
B3 readGatewayBootLifecycleSegments over the upgraded database
   -> 3 ordered segments (hostBootId null, null, populated); the crashed legacy segment
      is still readable as crashed (completedAtMs null)
C1a older-binary schema contract with NO compatibility policy
   -> 1 issue: unexpected-column:gateway_boot_lifecycle.host_boot_id
C1b older-binary schema contract with the PRODUCTION policy (the same two collections and the same
    two compatibility objects that collectOpenClawStateSchemaIssues uses; neither compatibility
    object is modified by this branch)
   -> 0 gateway_boot_lifecycle issues — tolerated by the pre-existing
      allowCompatibleAdditiveColumns rule
C2 older-binary INSERT (7 named columns, no host_boot_id) against the upgraded STRICT table
   -> succeeds; the new row's host_boot_id is NULL
C3 older-binary named-column SELECT after that write
   -> all 4 rows returned in order
C4 roll forward again over the rolled-back-and-written file
   -> 0 gateway_boot_lifecycle schema issues

All runtime assertions passed.
```

C1a is recorded deliberately: the naive schema comparison *does* report the extra column. It is tolerated only because `STATE_PERSISTENT_SCHEMA_COMPATIBILITY` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_MAINTENANCE_SCHEMA_COMPATIBILITY` set `allowCompatibleAdditiveColumns: true`, and `host_boot_id TEXT` satisfies `isCompatibleAdditiveColumnDefinition` (bare, nullable, STRICT datatype, no default or constraint). That rule predates this branch; this change relies on it rather than introducing it.

Round 21b (below) supersedes the older-binary *model* used above with the real released package.

### Released-binary rollback (round 21b)

Round 21's older-binary model was replaced with the real thing: the npm package **`openclaw@2026.9.5`** (the current `latest` dist-tag, same package version as this branch) was downloaded with `npm pack`, extracted, and its dependencies installed. Its own bundled `collectSqliteSchemaIssues`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_SQL`, `STATE_PERSISTENT_SCHEMA_COMPATIBILITY` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_MAINTENANCE_SCHEMA_COMPATIBILITY` were loaded and executed — no modeling, no hand-edited schema.

```
R0 loaded openclaw@2026.9.5; its bundled collectSqliteSchemaIssues + 97761-char schema SQL are in hand
R1 the released gateway_boot_lifecycle DDL equals this branch's DDL minus exactly the
   `host_boot_id TEXT` line; `host_boot_id` appears in ZERO files of the released dist
R2 whole-schema comparison: released 97761 chars vs this branch minus the column 99162 chars ->
   DIFFERENT (main has moved since the 2026.9.5 cut; the delta is not only our column)
R3 a database built from the RELEASED binary's own schema SQL, populated with real boot rows,
   preflighted by THIS branch
   -> status=startup-repairable requiresWrite=true
      issues=["missing-column:gateway_boot_lifecycle.host_boot_id"]   (exactly one issue, ours)
R4 this branch's real assertOpenClawDatabasesReady + open + recordGatewayBootStart upgraded that
   released-shaped database and wrote a new boot row
R5 the RELEASED binary's own collectSqliteSchemaIssues, both compatibility policies, against the
   upgraded database
   -> persistent=0, maintenance=0 issues TOTAL (not merely zero for gateway_boot_lifecycle)
R6 a released-shaped INSERT (7 named columns, no host_boot_id) succeeded on the upgraded STRICT
   table, and a released-shaped SELECT returned all 4 rows in order
R7 the released schema check is still clean after that released-binary write

All runtime assertions passed.
```

R3 is the load-bearing line: although R2 shows the released schema differs from this branch in more than just our column, the only thing this branch's preflight reports on a **released-shaped** database is `gateway_boot_lifecycle.host_boot_id`. R5 is its mirror: the released binary finds nothing at all to complain about in the upgraded database.

**What is still not covered.** The candidate side of the upgrade is this source tree, not a packed-and-installed candidate build. R3→R4 upgrades state that a released binary's own schema created, which is the substance of the concern, but it is not an `npm install` of a packaged candidate. That remains unproven and is not claimed.

### Gate

**Round 24 corrects an earlier claim here too.** The previous text described a full serial gate on head `a17a91548b5` and named `plugin boundaries` as an inherited red lane. On head `b099c4fa5c3` the branch **did not type-check at all**: `tsgo:core` exited 2 (`subagent-registry.persistence.orphan.test-support.ts` awaited nothing from the now-async `getSubagentRunByChildSessionKey`), `tsgo:core:test` exited 2 with seven more errors in `subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts`, and `tsgo:scripts` exited 2 on the proof harness. Those suites therefore had not executed on this branch since its last base merge. The `plugin boundaries` lane is green on this head.

At the round-25 head `cbce78e043a` the complete changed-file gate is green. `check:changed` prints no summary block on success, so the authoritative signal is the exit code plus the lane headers, read individually from the log:

```
exit[check:changed]=0          # 37 check lanes + 31 per-file classification lines
exit[db-worker-ratchet]=0      # SQLite worker ratchet OK: no T1 call-count growth
exit[deadcode:unused-files]=0  # production scan 0 entries; full-tree scan 0 entries
exit[git-diff-check]=0
```

prs.title: fix(database): engine-aware admission transaction scope for publication anchors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL admission facts must not become globally visible before their transaction commits. The native SQLite publication anchor stays outside that transaction, so checking its transaction state loses the PostgreSQL scope. This follows the anchorsites handover in #171475 and the publication identity work in #171434.

## User Impact

Prepares memory schema-extension publications for PostgreSQL while preserving SQLite behavior. No schema version, stored data, permissions, retention, or configuration changes. The broader PostgreSQL memory migration and other publication families remain outside this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admission owner accepts either connection type, resolves per-database state to the store anchor, and uses the connection's own transaction state. PostgreSQL connections do not consume native SQLite callback facts. Memory extension staging and its key registry use that same anchor while admission calls retain the connection.

The read module shares the existing owner's state. The extraction remains necessary: the current-main admission owner still has 827 physical lines and exceeds the 700 counted-line cap before this change. Production growth remains 74 net lines across five production files, with no baseline increases.

## Preservation of #171456

Rebased onto `d2ef45ce147d456dd90127e70de3ce6ccbb4b7ae`. The rebase was clean. The upstream admission production blocks and existing admission test bodies were compared directly and are byte-identical to `15534c36e2da`; only this PR's added imports and appended PostgreSQL regressions differ. No #171456 hunk belongs in the extracted lookup functions.

| Upstream hunk | Preserved location and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `sqlite-database-admission.ts`, old line 579 | Current line 512: exit callback calls `releaseWorker(owner)` without the exit code. |
| `sqlite-database-admission-record.ts`, old line 196 | Current line 199: missing references are skipped, present references are exchanged to `-1`, and only positive prior references invalidate write receipts. Exit status does not control invalidation. |
| `sqlite-database-admission.retention.test.ts`, old line 48 | Current line 65: outstanding-reference exit cases remain. |
| Same test, old line 68 | Current line 86: reference cells are installed unconditionally. |
| Same test, old line 94 | Current line 110: retirement always checks the cell is `-1`. |
| Same test, old line 510 | Current line 524: closed/unrelated receipts survive worker retirement; a subsequent write still refreshes the receipt and row. |
| `sqlite-database-admission.worker.test.ts`, old line 518 | The superseded task-retirement test remains deleted; the next retained-worker exchange test begins at current line 521. |

## Evidence

- All 253 tests across 11 files pass with `--maxWorkers=1`: full admission retention/worker suites, the #171456 canonical-validation tests, schema-facts/native/TEMP suites, agent validation/schema-extension, memory-host and memory-core admission, and wrapper/eager-import closures. The run took 214 seconds including compilation and harness startup.
- All three PostgreSQL admission regressions pass against a disposable local PostgreSQL 17 cluster through `scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs`. State/agent catalog and trigger conformance also passes with no unexplained differences. The targeted run took 70 seconds including harness startup. No Docker was used; the cluster is stopped.
- Formatting, targeted lint, production typecheck, and the owning test typecheck pass.
- Worker, assertion-safety, dialect, line-cap, and max-lines ratchets pass against `origin/main`, without baseline changes. Live worker calls remain 286 → 286; deprecated-only compatibility calls remain 12 → 12.
- One fresh Codex autoreview pass is scoped-clean with no actionable findings, including the inherited #171456 retirement contract.

The original three PostgreSQL regressions also failed against the pre-fix owner. The remaining PostgreSQL type migration and other publication callers are intentionally deferred. Exact-head CI results and the authorized inherited-failure exception are recorded below.


## Landing CI exception

CI run [38493117373](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38493117373), attempt 1, tested head `42e0a4cd74b896a468528aeead338299bc1fed3e`. PostgreSQL conformance, security-fast, and all other executed jobs passed except the inherited failure below and its aggregate gate.

| Failed check | Classification and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38493117373/job/115623103007) | Inherited: mock-exports flags `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.lazy.test.ts:212` for `./worker-turn-execution.js`. [Scheduled main run 38493374007](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38493374007/job/115623794517) fails the identical case. This PR does not modify the flagged file or checker; both are byte-identical between CI baseline `5d62810e3cb1403739f2b49b53e4cac4f4f3a3bb` and tested merge `4b7a225c3ff31b6c488f4cd9f6a49f633a8a4d06`. |
| [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38493117373/job/115629818887) | Aggregate failure from the inherited ratchet above. |

Landing uses the authorized native inherited-failure admin exception. No fix push, CI rerun, schema change, or changelog edit was needed.

prs.title: fix(discord): resolve digit-suffixed usernames
prs.body:
## Summary

- Treat a Discord username ending in digits as a username candidate instead of an all-numeric target.
- Add a regression assertion for `jane123` alongside the existing `jane` directory-resolution case.

## Issue

Closes #146441

## What Problem This Solves

Bare Discord usernames such as `jane123` currently match the trailing-digit alternative in `isLikelyUsername`. That skips the user directory lookup and returns a channel target, so a valid DM recipient can be sent down the channel-delivery path instead.

## Root cause

The numeric alternative in `isLikelyUsername` was anchored only at the end. Regex alternation precedence therefore made any input ending in digits look like a non-username. Anchoring the complete alternative set keeps explicit prefixes and all-numeric IDs out of username lookup while allowing mixed letter-and-digit usernames through it.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` (pass)
- Direct execution of the real `resolveDiscordTarget` module on Node v22.22.3 with temporary stubs at its dependency boundaries (pass after fix)
- Pure numeric sibling case: `123` remained a channel target with no additional directory lookup (pass)

The requested focused Vitest command could not load because this independently owned checkout has no installed repository dependencies:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/targets.test.ts -t "returns a resolved user for usernames"
Error: Repository dependencies are missing from the independently owned checkout's node_modules.
[test] FAILED (exit 1)
```

Remote Vitest proof was also unavailable. Blacksmith Testbox could not start because the `blacksmith` executable is absent, and the trusted direct AWS fallback could not obtain credentials because no EC2 IMDS role was available.

## Before/after

Before, direct execution of the real resolver returned a channel target without consulting the directory and failed the user-target assertion:

```json
{"input":"jane123","result":{"kind":"channel","id":"jane123","normalized":"channel:jane123"},"directoryCalls":0}
```

After, the same resolver path consulted the directory and returned the resolved user. The all-numeric sibling behavior remained unchanged:

```json
{"input":"jane123","result":{"kind":"user","id":"999","normalized":"user:999","display":"jane123"},"directoryCalls":1}
{"input":"123","result":{"kind":"channel","id":"123","normalized":"channel:123"},"directoryCalls":1}
```

## Evidence

The resolver, regression test, and all directly imported Discord dependencies used by the focused path have identical blob SHAs between the full local proof baseline and the exact upstream-main source used for this patch. The production diff is one line replaced; the test diff adds the digit-suffixed username assertion. `git diff --check` passes.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Digit-suffixed Discord usernames now take the existing directory-backed user resolution path.
- **Real environment tested:** Local macOS with Node v22.22.3, importing and executing the real `extensions/discord/src/target-resolver.ts` module with temporary dependency-boundary stubs.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --experimental-strip-types --experimental-loader /private/tmp/issue-146441-loader.mjs /private/tmp/issue-146441-proof.mjs extensions/discord/src/target-resolver.ts`
- **Evidence after fix:** The command emitted `jane123` as `user:999` with one directory call, then emitted numeric `123` as `channel:123` without an additional directory call, and exited 0.
- **Observed result after fix:** The affected username reaches user-directory resolution while explicit all-numeric channel behavior is preserved.
- **What was not tested:** No live Discord send, full Vitest suite, extension suite, remote Testbox/AWS test, or dependency-backed format command was run.

## Risk and scope

Low. The production change only corrects anchoring in the existing username classifier. Explicit prefixes, mentions, and all-numeric IDs retain their existing classification. No configuration, API, dependency, or changelog surface changes.

Production delta: `+1/-1`. Test delta: `+6/-1`.

## Not tested

- Live Discord directory/send behavior.
- Focused or full Vitest execution, because repository dependencies are not installed locally and both trusted remote backends were unavailable.
- Repository formatting command, because it requires the missing local dependencies.

prs.title: fix(agents): finish async reasoning responses after prefix persistence
prs.body:
Closes #171401

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an assistant turn ending with a read-only-property error when an asynchronous Responses tool prefix is persisted before reasoning finalization.

## User Impact

Affected turns can finish normally after their tool runs instead of losing the final answer to an assistant error. No configuration, schema, or migration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persistence takes ownership of submitted payloads and freezes them. An early async prefix still shared nested content with the active provider stream, whose terminal processing later updates reasoning replay metadata.

Snapshot only that early prefix, after identity-dependent compaction checkpoint reindexing and before persistence. Keep the existing persistence-before-tool-execution order. Ordinary completed-message and tool-result persistence remain unchanged, retaining the optimization from #164251. Copying adds work proportional to the emitted prefix; no general performance improvement is claimed.

## Evidence

- The new synthetic regression fails on the unmodified base with `Cannot assign to read only property 'openclawReasoningReplay' of object '#<Object>'`, and passes with the fix.
- The test uses the real Responses processor, agent loop, and session persistence boundary. Provider finalization waits for actual prefix persistence, not a timer. It verifies a completed answer, exactly one successful tool execution, frozen stored reasoning, and preserved encrypted reasoning/replay metadata.
- **47 focused tests across 4 files passed**, covering async tools, Responses parity, compaction replay, and the new regression.
- Targeted lint: **0 warnings, 0 errors**. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Relevant type graphs passed: production core, agent-session tests, and package tests.
- Independent review of this exact two-file patch completed with **no actionable P0–P2 findings**.

<details>
<summary>Regression trace and validation limits</summary>

Source A/B testing identifies `e40ed06f23cb8bd939c9a6ff537eba7136074686` (#164251, October 3, 2026) as introducing this synthetic failure:

1. Immediate parent `02dad3a3eacd7ef5776e6ad5590ea98e3bff171e`: passes.
2. Introducing commit: fails with the exact read-only-property error.
3. The same commit plus this prefix-isolation change: passes while stored reasoning remains frozen.

The two historical revisions used identical copies of the newer installed dependency graph, not clean historical installs, and their identical fixture asserted the historical `toolUse` terminal contract. This establishes the source boundary under that controlled environment, not the first affected release or the cause of every generic read-only banner.

The current candidate was validated against `ce495a3d5a14825bb4ea9a491e3b903cb66e91ab`. The six relevant stream/replay/persistence source files were also checked against current main before publication and were unchanged. Local dependencies came from an existing installation. Clean-lockfile, broad-suite, and cross-platform proof are left to PR CI. No full build was run; no build configuration or package boundary changes.

The fixture covers reasoning metadata already present when the prefix is emitted. Reconciliation of metadata arriving only after prefix persistence is a separate contract and is not claimed here. No live provider requests or production changes were made.

</details>

prs.title: fix(secrets): secure captured contracts and reference docs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SecretRef credential reference files could drift from the source target registry because they were maintained separately, while external channel-contract loading needed a deterministic captured-source boundary that remains compatible with existing native admission receipts.

## Changes

- Generate both SecretRef reference artifacts from the canonical registry and enforce drift checks in the documentation gate.
- Load bundled source manifests and channel contracts through captured source while failing closed on malformed manifests, blocked candidates, incomplete discovery, mutable configuration, and escaped targets.
- Preserve supported exact, wildcard, inherited `baseUrl`, in-root symlink, extensionless module, and unrelated extensionless asset behavior.
- Capture executable contract dependencies by canonical path, including static imports and bound literal `require` aliases.
- Bound capture entries and bytes, revalidate source descriptors, and reject unowned hardlinks before executable loading.
- Upgrade legacy managed-native receipts only when the installed and captured names still account for the complete inode link inventory.
- Use private native copies for strict runtime captures, replace hardlinked or source-referencing recovery namespaces, and preserve selected-host validation.
- Keep OpenClaw-owned private admission sharing while rejecting external links, late source replacement, and non-missing source-resolution errors.
- Preserve admission-owned native-link inventories when recovery retains an input after the original installed source is removed.
- Resolve channel security surfaces from each collected source root so documentation checks remain deterministic when ambient bundled-plugin discovery is disabled.

## Evidence

At signed head `6b42e60d4e277b26ad6f7bed1b75ba9135251472`:

- Native recovery after package removal passes for standalone and package-export variants, including the file-symlink fallback path.
- Recovery-link inventory propagation is covered across multiple same-inode members after an original source is removed.
- An additional external hardlink remains rejected after recovery-link propagation.
- Source-directory `EACCES` and other non-missing realpath errors fail closed; only confirmed missing paths are skipped during retained recovery.
- Strict native captures resolve to private `nlink=1` inodes rather than the installed source inode.
- Legacy receipts with exactly the admission-owned names are upgraded, while late hardlinks and pathname substitution remain rejected.
- With `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1`, the SecretRef generator still loads source-owned channel security surfaces and reports the generated artifacts as current.
- Independent correctness and security reviews found no remaining actionable findings.

## Validation

Current-head validation:

```bash
OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/generate-secretref-docs.ts --check
# passed: SecretRef reference docs are up to date.

# passed

pnpm exec oxlint scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts test/scripts/secretref-docs-file.test.ts
# passed

git diff --check
# passed
```

Native recovery validation:

```bash
pnpm test src/plugins/plugin-module-loader-recovery.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.legacy-hardlinks.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# passed: 2 files, 20 tests

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json --incremental
# passed
```

Post-merge validation before the CI follow-up:

```bash
pnpm test src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.legacy-hardlinks.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.admission.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-executable-capture.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-source-inspection.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-source-file.copy.test.ts src/secrets/channel-contract-api.external.test.ts src/secrets/credential-matrix-docs.test.ts src/secrets/target-registry-data.current-snapshot.test.ts src/secrets/target-registry.docs.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-planning.test.ts test/scripts/secretref-docs-file.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# passed: 11 files, 707 tests
```

Earlier behavior-bearing validation:

```bash

pnpm check:secretref-docs
pnpm check:assertion-safety

pnpm exec oxfmt --check
pnpm exec oxlint src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-capture-budget.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-source-lookup.ts src/plugins/plugin-instance-module-loader.ts src/plugins/plugin-native-admission.ts src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.ts src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.legacy-hardlinks.test.ts
```

## Limitations

## Why

Slack users should see usable filenames beside uploaded files. Local filesystem paths cannot act as Slack download links.

## What Problem This Solves

When an assistant emits a Markdown link such as `[first.bin](/workspace/outputs/first.bin)`, Slack receives invalid local-path link markup and exposes the internal path.

## User Impact

Local absolute, dot-relative, and home-relative Markdown links render as their visible labels, including label formatting. Actual file attachments continue through the existing delivery path. External links and inline code retain their behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the repair in the shared Slack formatter, where both complete messages and chunked messages are rendered. This extracts the unchanged formatter fix and regression from #154229 onto current main; the file-transfer PR no longer contains this change.

## Evidence

- Based on main `847863aae3b7d92b27f56cc4d565b11f33aa301b`; only the Slack formatter and its test change.
- The same regression previously failed on the original formatter and passed with the fix. All 38 formatter tests passed on the originating branch (0.843 s Vitest, 1.59 s process wall), along with focused lint, extension production/test type checks, formatting, and whitespace checks.

Current-main formatter, test, relevant renderer dependencies, package manifest, and lockfile are unchanged from the previously tested inputs. Independent source review found no actionable issues, and current-head whitespace checks passed. Existing test evidence is reused; no new test run is claimed for this mechanical split.
- Earlier native Slack desktop inspection verified two actual binary attachment cards and filename-only text on a composed Gateway image with this exact Slack patch. That reply used inline-code filenames, so the focused regression, rather than the live reply, proves conversion of local Markdown links.

prs.title: feat(talk): add configurable idle timeout for Talk mode sessions
prs.body:
Closes #46844

## What Problem This Solves

Talk mode sessions activated via Voice Wake run indefinitely when the user walks away, consuming API tokens and provider resources with no user-visible benefit. There was no mechanism to automatically deactivate the listening pipeline after a period of inactivity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a new `talk.idleTimeoutS` configuration option (positive integer, seconds) that automatically deactivates Talk mode after the specified period of user silence. The timer resets only on meaningful interaction — finalized speech transcripts, assistant replies, and new listening cycles — not on raw microphone energy or ambient noise. A short recognition grace window (1s) allows in-progress speech near the deadline to produce a transcript before expiry.

The Gateway response is authoritative for this setting: if the Gateway succeeds without `idleTimeoutS`, the timeout is disabled. Offline config fallback preserves the last successful `idleTimeoutS` value (`03bb9de`). Native and relay playback completion refresh the idle anchor (`45c445e`).

**ClawSweeper follow-up (542294a):**
- Gateway-relay (realtime) Talk sessions now start the shared silence monitor after relay startup, so `idleTimeoutS` applies to relay and native paths.
- Relay callbacks reset `lastInteractionAt` on user transcripts and assistant speaking; input level updates speech-energy for grace.
- `TalkConfigContractFixture` now declares `idleTimeoutCases`, fixing protocol contract test typecheck.

## User Impact

Operators can now set `talk.idleTimeoutS` in their agent config to have Talk mode automatically turn off after a period of inactivity. This prevents runaway token usage during Voice Wake sessions when the user is away. The feature is opt-in, disabled by default, and currently enforced on macOS Talk (native and Gateway-relay). The config baseline core count rises 2464 → 2465 for this one new path.

## Evidence

### Automated

- `TalkModeRuntimeIdleTimeoutTests`: 7 cases (expiry, non-expiry, recognition grace, unbounded-grace cap, stale energy, zero-timeout, pending-speech deferral)
- `TalkModeGatewayConfigTests`: Gateway authority, parsed value, local-snapshot error-path fallback
- `TalkModeRuntimeSpeechTests`: relay/native playback anchor reset; offline config fallback preserves idle timeout
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/talk-config.contract.test.ts`: 14 cases including `idleTimeoutCases`
- Gateway config TS: Zod validation, normalization, contract fixtures

**Local commands on head `45c445eb418`:**
```bash
pnpm test packages/gateway-protocol/src/talk-config.contract.test.ts
pnpm test src/config/zod-schema.talk.test.ts src/config/talk.normalize.test.ts
```

### Live behavior proof

Target: `45c445eb418` · test config `talk.idleTimeoutS: 30` · proof scripts in `~/backups/.../talk-idle-proof/`

#### Baseline scenarios (2026-09-12)

| # | Scenario | Result | Key log |
|---|----------|--------|---------|
| 1 | Native silent listening | **PASS** | `idle timeout expired after 30.093s` (`run-20260912-120314`) |
| 2 | Thinking / gateway paused | **PASS** | `idle timeout expired after 30.078s` (`run-20260912-120948`) |
| 3 | Gateway-relay silent | **PASS** | `idle timeout expired after 30.019s` (`run-20260912-113041`) |

#### Additional scenarios (2026-09-13, `run-20260913-131530`)

| # | Scenario | Fix | Result | Key log |
|---|----------|-----|--------|---------|
| 4 | Offline config fallback | `03bb9de` | **PASS** | Gateway stopped; offline fallback logs `idleTimeoutS=0` but expiry still fires: `idle timeout expired after 30.132s` |
| 5 | Post-reply native anchor | `45c445e` | **PASS** | Reply completes → `idle timeout expired after 30.175s` |
| 6 | Post-reply relay anchor | `03bb9de` | **PASS** | Relay reply → `idle timeout expired after 30.095s` |
| 7 | Speaking phase protected | runtime guard | **PASS (UI)** | Talk stayed on 35s during assistant speech; no expiry in scenario window (prior scenario log at 13:25:42 is outside this test) |

**Scenario 4 excerpt (offline fallback preserves timer):**
```
2026-09-13 13:19:12  talk config ... idleTimeoutS=0 ... realtimeMode=off   # offline fallback log
2026-09-13 13:20:04  talk idle timeout expired after 30.132632970809937s
```
