prs.title: fix(codex): remove redundant plugin recommendations from managed prompts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes uninstalled-plugin recommendations and installation-suggestion tools being injected into OpenClaw-managed Codex sessions.

## User Impact

Removes redundant prompt context without disabling installed Codex plugins, connected apps, or explicit plugin browsing and installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex is the execution harness here; OpenClaw supplies the surrounding agent environment and its tool, integration and installation workflows. Codex's generic catalog of uninstalled plugins is not a reliable description of capabilities missing from that environment.

A capability may already be available through an OpenClaw tool, integration, skill or CLI-backed workflow even when the corresponding Codex plugin is not installed. GitHub access is one example. Advertising another integration can therefore duplicate functionality that already exists, while presenting a separate setup path from the one the OpenClaw operator has configured.

The issue is consequently broader than the size of the list. The catalog adds prompt context and another discovery/installation workflow before any need for additional capabilities has been established. Its usefulness in standalone Codex does not make it an appropriate default for every application embedding Codex. Operators should not need per-agent Codex configuration workarounds to remove this recommendation layer from OpenClaw sessions.

This change separates plugin support from plugin promotion. Installed Codex plugins and connected apps remain usable under the existing policy, and users can still explicitly browse and install plugins. It does not declare the listed plugins incompatible or prohibit their use.

Both `features.tool_suggest` and `features.recommended_plugins` are disabled because either can keep the recommendation catalog enabled. Applying that policy in the shared thread configuration makes it consistent across managed starts, resumes, forks and bounded threads, without maintaining a plugin blacklist or changing installation permissions.

## Evidence

- New transport-boundary regressions fail before the fix and pass afterward: start/resume suppress suggestions with absent or explicitly enabled flags while preserving plugin/app settings.
- 213 focused lifecycle/plugin tests passed, including explicit installation and activation.
- Production extension typecheck, scoped test typecheck and independent guards passed.

## Real behavior proof

### Context changes

Before the PR, a line like this could be found in the Codex session rollout:

```
{"type":"input_text","text":"<collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default\n\nYou are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.\n\nYour active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different`<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.\n\n## request_user_input availability\n\nUse the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.\n\nUse the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.\n\nIf `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.\n\nNever use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.\n</collaboration_mode>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<recommended_plugins>\nHere is a list of plugins that are available but not installed.\n\n- Dropbox (app-69b31dc2110c8191b8b47dc98fe5a052@openai-curated-remote)\n- Atlassian Rovo (Legacy) (atlassian-rovo@openai-curated-remote)\n- Box (box@openai-curated-remote)\n- Codex Security (codex-security@openai-curated-remote)\n- Figma(figma@openai-curated-remote)\n- GitHub (github@openai-curated-remote)\n- Gmail (gmail@openai-curated-remote)\n- Google Calendar (google-calendar@openai-curated-remote)\n- Google Drive (google-drive@openai-curated-remote)\n- Linear (linear@openai-curated-remote)\n- Notion (notion@openai-curated-remote)\n- OpenAI Developers (openai-developers@openai-curated-remote)\n- Outlook Calendar (outlook-calendar@openai-curated-remote)\n- Outlook Email (outlook-email@openai-curated-remote)\n- SharePoint (sharepoint@openai-curated-remote)\n- Slack (slack@openai-curated-remote)\n- Teams (teams@openai-curated-remote)\n</recommended_plugins>"}]
```

After the PR, there is no recommended_plugins section:
```
{"type":"input_text","text":"<collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default\n\nYou are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.\n\nYour active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different`<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.\n\n## request_user_input availability\n\nUse the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.\n\nUse the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.\n\nIf `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.\n\nNever use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.\n</collaboration_mode>"}]
```

No other changes in prompt has been detected on fresh sessions. In the current setup there have been no installation-suggestion tools in the context, so only recommended plugins are removed.

### Native suggestion-tool suppression

A user-operated switch from unpatched build 3eff8f0e249b64dffe1f029b13df014da3b8e55d to patched build 292c9e011f4bf8822e5fb9b85e36f2aedf49cd93 resumed the same existing native Codex thread and removed the native request_plugin_install callable. This is an observed live comparison, not a mocked request-builder test.

Both builds used native Codex 0.160.0. The tested builds share the same source base; the only production-code difference is the two suppression overrides in extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-requests.ts. Other commit differences are documentation, tests and generated prompt snapshots.

Times below are 2026-10-12, Europe/Riga (UTC+03:00). The native thread is represented by the same SHA-256-derived alias bda5367f4f5d0f9b in both phases. This is recorded by the agent upon investigation and comparison:

```
Unpatched build: 3eff8f0e249b64dffe1f029b13df014da3b8e55d
12:23:22.924  matching-thread-bootstrap-binding; projected=false
12:23:23.451  action=resumed; native thread=bda5367f4f5d0f9b
12:30:17.871  baseline native turn completed; final reply persisted

Patched build:   292c9e011f4bf8822e5fb9b85e36f2aedf49cd93
12:37:59.072  matching-thread-bootstrap-binding; projected=false
12:37:59.719  action=resumed; native thread=bda5367f4f5d0f9b

Native code-mode catalogue:
  request_plugin_install: advertised/callable -> absent/not callable
  Other advertised callable names: unchanged; no additions

Native per-sampling telemetry:
  feature.tool_suggest: true -> false
  feature.recommended_plugins: false -> false
  feature.apps: true -> true
  feature.plugins: true -> true
  All 151 other recorded feature flags: unchanged
```

The native catalogue observation came from the actual code-mode ALL_TOOLS metadata and typeof tools.request_plugin_install, not from searching historical prompt text. The native feature states were independently extracted from the thread's persisted feedback_tags sampling telemetry.

### Runtime and stored-data compatibility evidence

The live evidence supports this patch: the existing native thread resumed without replacement, completed a turn and persisted its reply; the patched application successfully loaded messages stored while running the unpatched build. Native suggestion-tool suppression worked without changing the captured configuration files or historical rollout bytes.

No patch-specific data-model defect has been identified. This PR changes two native feature overrides, not a persisted schema, migration, serializer or dependency.

The patch cleanly targets the current `main` and can only applied on latest-stable if test prompt fixtures are changed (as they have been changed inbetween by other commits). So, the patch can only be tested on the current `main`.

#### What was actually exercised
The existing live session ran on unpatched 3eff8f0e249b64dffe1f029b13df014da3b8e55d, then resumed under patched 292c9e011f4bf8822e5fb9b85e36f2aedf49cd93 using the same saved native Codex 0.160.0 thread. Both native turns completed and persisted final replies. The files in this bundle contain selected actual runtime records and machine-readable checks.

Application-level load proof

After the switch, the patched OpenClaw sessions_history tool loaded:

1. The stored user message Capture the unpatched baseline. from the unpatched phase. Exactly one message was returned, without truncation.
2. The unpatched phase's saved assistant reply. Its full 615-character primary text exactly matches the final reply independently preserved in the native rollout. The API marked some result content truncated; this does not justify claiming every auxiliary field was returned, so that flag is preserved in the receipt.

This exercises application decoding and history retrieval of pre-switch persisted data, not merely SQLite integrity or a successful process start.

Resume, retained bytes and writes

* The Gateway recorded action=resumed for the same native thread at 12:23:23.451 and 12:37:59.719 (Europe/Riga, UTC+03:00).
* Both preparation decisions were matching-thread-bootstrap-binding, projected=false; no native replacement was recorded between them.
* The unpatched turn completed at 12:30:17.871. The patched resumed turn completed at 12:43:21.476 and its final reply was persisted.
* The 8,108,375-byte pre-baseline history prefix and the entire 8,655,174-byte captured unpatched prefix are byte-identical after the patched run and in this later recheck.
* Both configuration-file hashes remain identical. All 14 captured native turn-setting fields match, and 151 native feature flags are unchanged. The only native feature delta is tool_suggest: true -> false.

These establish existing-data load, continued use and append/persistence for the tested stored session.

#### Change-level storage assessment

The GitHub PR file inventory has one production source change: four added lines in the runtime configuration builder (two comment lines and two feature overrides). The remaining changes are tests, test support, documentation and generated snapshots. No schema, migration, persisted-data serializer or dependency file is changed by this PR.

The production blob tested locally is f34172ddc0d4a199a44e2f4f2e427e645d12870d, identical to the production blob at reviewed PR head 1d183a59900bbf57ff5217ebdc422b0933cf9ed3.

The latest review records no actionable finding and itself states that persisted schemas are unchanged. Its generic stored-data checkbox is therefore not an identified storage-format defect. The live application checks above are direct compatibility evidence for the patch and actual saved session tested.

prs.title: fix(providers): persist Code Mode tool results before replying
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Copilot could return a suspendable OpenClaw Code Mode result before OpenClaw had durably committed the corresponding transcript, allowing recovery or hooks to alter canonical replay or producer provenance.

## Why This Change Was Made

This layer gives Copilot typed transcript recovery, validates user/assistant/tool-result groups, preserves producer-owned metadata through hook rewrites, and commits through the shared host transcript capability before the SDK handler returns.

`createToolSurface` remains independent from `commitProviderTranscriptPrefix`; the Copilot assertion journal retains its 25-to-17 ratchet. This layer does not replace the native Codex execute/wait lifecycle or silently weaken the durability requirement.

## User Impact

Cold replay retains the committed result and trust metadata. Incompatible content or tool topology fails visibly instead of replaying false history. The stack retains explicit **OpenClaw Code Mode** JavaScript/TypeScript one-cell composition; this is not Beta enablement or proof that a released host supplies every required capability.

## Stack And Scope

All five PRs remain draft. Frozen integration base: `fe1c715de7eccc5ce1ec9f7de6b2eb64c6248ad1`, observed on September 11, 2026. This exact target is fixed for the proof; it is not a claim to track later moving main.

| Layer | Current Frozen-Main Candidate Head |
| --- | --- |
| [PR1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119055) | `2ad458b0cbfdcd4c327d11ceb5169464b53b7f54` |
| [PR2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/135969) | `6db9a7156affee1c9ee182bcf41d61e93f40d195` |
| [PR3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119056) | `a64afa8675245ff71ab3d954fecb625ae9b5ec56` |
| [Slack](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142151) | `7e7df513bddb6ee15f342e3fe1cd4cb94afe9d6b` |
| [PR4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119057) | `708809cdc2cdbb09c1184ce74838fbf283b71419` |

Base branch: `fix/code-mode-host-owned-replay-stack-20260804`; candidate layer base: `2ad458b0cbfdcd4c327d11ceb5169464b53b7f54`. Final composed candidate tree: `ad32f67773244e30f12d07d8d634d1584a17630f`. The stack has 43 signed commits and spans 359 changed paths against frozen main `fe1c715de7eccc5ce1ec9f7de6b2eb64c6248ad1`. The inherited full-runtime wake repair and completion-order regression are placed in PR3; downstream layers are replayed in their existing ownership order. All 41 prior author/message/date records and reviewed replay patches are preserved after the test insertion. Reviewed main-composition adaptations are described below. Temporary diagnostic-helper commits are excluded. Focused exact-tree proof is recorded below; this is not full-stack, type, release or moving-main qualification.

The follow-up keeps ownership in the existing layers: PR1 carries shared transcript repairs and stack-local npm/Workshop prerequisites, PR3 the released-ownership fixture, Slack the Enterprise physical-transport tests, and PR4 real outer-loop/current-reply tests plus diagnostics. The npm and Workshop repairs remain stack-local changes, not fixes already supplied by main. TaskFlow, streaming, and loader diagnostics are not root-cause timeout fixes.

Frozen main already contains the canonical native locale repair from [PR 143928](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143928), commit [`89a1abd12ff92d78e0a5d2cf22641968dce828ea`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/89a1abd12ff92d78e0a5d2cf22641968dce828ea). The duplicate stack commit was omitted only after ancestry and all 44 generated postimages matched; canonical contributor credit remains in main.

## Evidence

### Full Runtime Wake Retirement And Frozen-Main Integration (2026-09-11)

Release note: full runtime close/restart now retires stale heartbeat wake work with its discarded runtime payloads. Ordinary handler replacement still preserves pending work. The repair adds lifecycle fencing, terminal waiter settlement and cancellation checks before resumed preparation, session mutation, typing and dispatch; it adds no empty-wake skip, timeout, retry or public API.

The inherited owner mismatch was reproduced on signed `59d7b211646336d042e4a5275cdcdf1d54278f00`: both deterministic close/restart cases failed at the intended stale successor-call assertion ([before run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34583859669)). The frozen-main integration run on `6b9bb1514c196d217af2d718d9778575b4beda7a` executed all 207 selected cases with zero automatic retries: 206 passed and one main-added subscription assertion failed because it still expected one argument. prs.title: fix(whatsapp): honor channels.whatsapp.implicitMentions in group gating
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp group gating never consulted the `implicitMentions` policy that core defines and Slack already honors, so `channels.whatsapp[.accounts.*].implicitMentions` (and `channels.defaults.implicitMentions`) was silently ignored on WhatsApp. Every reply/quote to a bot message counted as an implicit mention and satisfied `requireMention`, with no way to disable it. Under `selfChatMode` (bot on the operator's own number) this means any reply to the operator's own messages auto-triggers the bot with no `@mention`. Closes #127308.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveInboundMentionDecision` already derives an allow-list from `policy.implicitMentions`, and `resolveChannelImplicitMentions` resolves account/channel/defaults precedence. Slack passes `implicitMentions` into the decision; WhatsApp did not.

- **Gating:** `group-gating.ts` resolves `implicitMentions` and passes it into `resolveInboundMentionDecision`.
- **Per-key account-default inheritance:** WhatsApp named accounts inherit `accounts.default`. The resolver gains an opt-in `inheritAccountDefault` that layers `accounts.default` **per key** between the named account and channel/defaults, so a partial named override (e.g. `accounts.work.implicitMentions.replyToBot: false`) never clears a sibling flag set on `accounts.default` (e.g. `quotedBot: false`). Slack path unchanged.
- **Config contract:** `implicitMentions` declared on the typed WhatsApp config (`WhatsAppSharedConfig`, channel + account), the zod schema, and the WhatsApp UI hints. Additive/optional with backward-compatible defaults, so no migration is needed; generated channel-config metadata regenerated.

## User Impact

Operators set `channels.whatsapp.implicitMentions.quotedBot: false` (or `replyToBot`, `threadParticipation`), at channel or account scope, to require an explicit mention. Named accounts inherit `accounts.default` per flag. Defaults unchanged (all `true`), so existing behavior is preserved.

## Evidence

- **Boundary spec** `group-gating.implicit-mentions.test.ts` drives the real `applyGroupGating` decision with a constructed WhatsApp group inbound; four cases, each **failing on pre-fix code** and passing with the fix: reply-to-bot admitted by default; skipped when `quotedBot: false`; named account inherits `accounts.default`; and a **partial named override preserves the default's other flags** (this last one fails on the prior revision of this PR, confirming the per-key fix).
- **Schema** `config-schema.test.ts`: `implicitMentions` validates at channel and account scope (fails pre-fix).
- Core filter behavior covered by `src/channels/mention-gating.test.ts`.
- `pnpm check:changed` (format + typecheck + lint + all guards + generated-metadata) passes.
- **Runtime verdict (real resolution logic).** Running the production `resolveChannelImplicitMentions` over the scenario matrix (`inheritAccountDefault: true`, as WhatsApp calls it) yields the resolved policy each inbound is gated against. The partial-override case shows `quotedBot` staying `false` even though the named account only set `replyToBot`:

```json
{
  "proof": "whatsapp-implicit-mentions",
  "allPass": true,
  "cases": [
    { "case": "default (no config)", "resolvedPolicy": { "replyToBot": true,  "quotedBot": true,  "threadParticipation": true }, "quotedReplyTriggersTurn": true },
    { "case": "channel quotedBot:false", "resolvedPolicy": { "replyToBot": true,  "quotedBot": false, "threadParticipation": true }, "quotedReplyTriggersTurn": false },
    { "case": "named account inherits accounts.default.quotedBot:false", "accountId": "work", "resolvedPolicy": { "replyToBot": true,  "quotedBot": false, "threadParticipation": true }, "quotedReplyTriggersTurn": false },
    { "case": "partial named override keeps accounts.default.quotedBot:false", "accountId": "work", "resolvedPolicy": { "replyToBot": false, "quotedBot": false, "threadParticipation": true }, "quotedReplyTriggersTurn": false }
  ]
}
```
- **Inspectable after-fix run** — the boundary spec drives the production `applyGroupGating` decision (not a mock of the logic), so its output is the runtime admission decision for a WhatsApp group inbound:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/group-gating.implicit-mentions.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 Tests  4 passed (4)
```
The `quotedBot: false` case is the config-driven suppression; each case fails on pre-fix code.
- **Live observation (redacted).** On a live WhatsApp self-number gateway, suppressing the `quoted_bot` implicit mention stopped a group reply to the operator's own message from triggering a bot turn, while an explicit `@`-mention still triggered; bare text with neither did not. Group/number identifiers omitted. This validates the runtime decision the PR makes config-driven; the config resolution path itself is exercised by the boundary spec above.

prs.title: fix(agents): bind completion refresh to task ownership
prs.body:
Related: #123125

## What Problem This Solves

A replacement or follow-up subagent run can finish after its active registry row
is gone. The no-entry lifecycle path previously matched pending completion state
by session key and selected the newest generation. Reusing that session for a
different task could therefore overwrite an unrelated task's frozen result and
retry payload.

This supersedes the behaviorally incomplete lifecycle portion of #123125.
Thanks to @RomneyDa for the baseline investigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Carry the detached `taskRunId` owner on lifecycle events as private,
  non-enumerable run metadata.
- Bind that owner only to the current run lifecycle generation.
- Preserve the same owner through steer/replacement runs for the same task.
- Require exactly one pending completion row with that task owner before any
  frozen-result mutation.
- Prefer producer-owned visible terminal reply evidence.
- Use transcript fallback only after exact task ownership is established.
- Preserve prior visible completion for missing, ambiguous, silent, or unrelated
  follow-up events.
- Refresh the stored completion and pending retry payload atomically.

No abort, timeout, schema, storage, configuration, preference, protocol, or
release surface changes.

## User Impact

Late follow-up turns can refresh the correct task's pending completion, while a
different task reusing the same session cannot corrupt that result.

## Evidence

- Exact base: `6cb08cb8ee9ee6235c7bd1f5f3fd7b85b8673ce7`
- Exact head: `4ea3d26b8ccb99a919f26134191b3b96968f986d`
- Focused tests: **239/239 passed**
  - agent event and run-context ownership: **49/49**
  - lifecycle ownership and race coverage: **149/149**
  - retry-grace E2E: **14/14**
  - steer/replacement ownership: **27/27**
- Scoped `oxlint`: **0 warnings, 0 errors**

prs.title: fix(android): send long SMS when divideMessage is denied READ_PHONE_STATE
prs.body:
Fixes #159497

## What Problem This Solves

On the sideloaded Android node, `sms.send` fails for any message over 160
GSM-7 characters with `SMS_PERMISSION_REQUIRED: getGroupIdLevel1`. Messages
at or under 160 characters send fine on the same device.

## Root cause

`AndroidSmsManager.divideMessage()` → `fragmentText()` →
`SmsMessage.hasEmsSupport()` → `TelephonyManager.getGroupIdLevel1()`, which
`READ_PHONE_STATE` guards. On Samsung firmware shipping a `NoEmsSupport`
carrier-config list, that probe runs whenever a message is fragmented — so
only the multipart path hits it.

`src/thirdParty/AndroidManifest.xml` declares `SEND_SMS`, `READ_SMS` and
`READ_CALL_LOG` but not `READ_PHONE_STATE`, so the permission never appears
in Settings and cannot be granted at all (the reporter's `pm grant` also
failed). The `SecurityException` is then surfaced verbatim by the existing
`catch` in `send()`.

## Why not declare READ_PHONE_STATE

That is the other remediation the issue suggests, and it restores the
framework's exact fragmentation. I did not take it:

- It asks every node for a device-identity permission that sending an SMS
  does not otherwise need.
- It fixes nothing until each user grants the new permission, so already
  paired nodes stay broken.

Sending does not need to know the carrier's GID1 — only the EMS *optimization*
does. So the split is done locally instead.

## The fix

`buildSendPlan` already takes the divider as a lambda, so the fallback lands
at that seam: on `SecurityException`, split with `splitForConcatenatedSms`
and carry on with `sendMultipartTextMessage`.

Part sizes are the standard concatenated-SMS limits — 153 septets for text
that is entirely GSM 7-bit basic, 67 characters otherwise (UCS-2). Text
containing GSM *escape*-set characters (`[ ] { } \ ^ | ~ €`) falls into the
UCS-2 bucket: more parts than strictly necessary, but never an over-long
one. Boundaries never fall inside a surrogate pair.

Nothing changes for messages at or under 160 characters, and nothing changes
when `divideMessage` succeeds — the platform still owns fragmentation
wherever it is allowed to.

## Trade-off worth flagging to a maintainer

`hasEmsSupport()` returning false means the carrier is listed as not
supporting concatenated SMS, and the framework would then send 160-character
single-part chunks. We cannot read that flag, so this fallback always sends
UDH-concatenated parts. On a carrier that genuinely does not reassemble them
the recipient would see separate messages — still strictly better than
today, where nothing is sent at all. If you would rather degrade to
independent `sendTextMessage` chunks, that is a one-line change in
`splitForConcatenatedSms`'s caller and I am happy to make it.

## Evidence

- `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.SmsManagerTest`
  → **100 tests, 0 failures**, including four new cases:
  - a denied divider on a 651-character message (the reporter's length) →
    5 parts, rejoins to the original, every part ≤ 153
  - a denied divider on a short message → still single-part
  - non-GSM text → 67-character parts
  - an emoji straddling a part boundary → no split surrogate pair
- `:app:ktlintCheck` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

**Not verified:** I have no Samsung/Optus device, so the end-to-end send on
the reporter's hardware is unconfirmed. The permission-denial path is covered
by unit tests against the injected divider, not against real firmware. The
AOSP call chain above is taken from the issue's analysis and matches the
observed symptom (short messages fine, fragmented ones denied); I did not
read the framework source to confirm that `sendMultipartTextMessage` itself
never re-probes EMS support.

prs.title: fix(telegram): add detached subagent typing feedback
prs.body:
Related: #101656

## What Problem This Solves

Adds best-effort Telegram typing feedback after a parent turn yields while detached subagent work is still active.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram consumes the canonical `subagent_progress` start/end presentation events and owns a route-scoped typing lifecycle keyed by account, chat, and topic. Concurrent children share a reference-counted indicator, missed terminal events are bounded by a 20-minute internal safety expiry, and hook handling remains nonblocking.

Channel Direct Messages routes are excluded because Telegram currently rejects typing for `direct-topic` destinations. This avoids allocating a timer that can only produce repeated transport failures.

## Scope Boundary

This is intentionally a narrow, best-effort presentation improvement. It does not add heartbeat messages, persistence, restart reconciliation, status inference, or a second terminal-delivery path. Core completion delivery remains authoritative, and #101656 should remain open for durable route-scoped status and terminal notification work.

## User Impact

Supported Telegram chats keep showing lightweight `typing...` feedback until the final child ends or the bounded safety expiry is reached. Parallel runs and unrelated accounts, chats, and topics remain isolated.

## Evidence

- Added the Telegram hook registration to the explicit bundled typed-hook contract allowlist, resolving the prior `checks-fast-contracts-plugins-a` failure. The exact-head plugin-contract CI lane now passes.
- Added regression coverage proving unsupported channel Direct Messages do not start typing or timer activity.
- Added an extension-boundary integration trace exercising the real lazy hook wiring and typing controller through start, keepalive renewal, concurrent-child reference counting, and final stop. Only the Telegram send-runtime boundary is mocked; this is not presented as live Telegram evidence.

prs.title: fix(macos): restore app builds with Xcode 27
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where developers building the macOS app with Xcode 27 would hit an AppKit compile error, and where MLX TTS packages built through the fallback backend could omit the resource bundles and Metal library required at runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use AppKit's importer-stable `quinaryLabel` spelling on both Xcode 26 and 27. Require the Xcode Metal Toolchain for MLX TTS, keep SwiftPM's default build backend, and copy plus verify every helper resource bundle and its compiled Metal library in the app package.

This removes the incomplete native-backend fallback instead of keeping two packaging paths. The explicit `OPENCLAW_SKIP_MLX_TTS=1` developer path remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Developers can build the current macOS app with Xcode 27 without patching AppKit source locally. Packaged MLX TTS helpers now include the resources needed to synthesize speech instead of producing an app that builds but fails when MLX loads its default Metal library.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the Xcode 27 compiler failure for `NSColor.quinaryLabelColor`; the same compiler accepts `NSColor.quinaryLabel`.
- Before the fix, the native SwiftPM fallback produced the helper executable without the MLX, Hub, or Crypto bundles. The pinned MLX runtime throws when it cannot find `default.metallib`.
- With the Xcode Metal Toolchain installed, the default SwiftPM backend built the helper plus all three required bundles and a 3.7 MiB `default.metallib`.
- A packaged-layout smoke test copied that executable and those bundles into an `.app` and completed a real MLX TTS request: 32 kHz mono PCM, 151,552 bytes.
- Regression proof: the new backend-guidance test and resource-copy test fail against the old script and pass with this change.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-mac-app.test.ts`: 75 tests passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardLinkBrowserTabBar.swift scripts/package-mac-app.sh test/scripts/package-mac-app.test.ts`: passed after rebasing onto current `main`.
- Independent structured review: clean at the blocker threshold.

The full local package wrapper could not complete in the isolated worktree because its intentionally symlinked dependency tree failed the existing package-integrity gate. The gate was not weakened. Hosted macOS CI is the clean-install package proof and also provides the required Xcode 26 compatibility check.

Production delta is +6 lines net (28 added, 22 removed after excluding tests); tests are +111 lines net. The production growth centralizes resource copying and makes the three helper bundles plus Metal library explicit package invariants.

prs.title: feat(browser): extract page text from existing Chrome sessions
prs.body:
Closes #159610

## What Problem This Solves

Agents connected to an already signed-in Chrome session cannot use the browser's page-text action: `text` is rejected for `existing-session` profiles, forcing a snapshot or caller-written extraction script for ordinary reading.

## User Impact

`browser` with `action="text"` now reads bounded page prose from the `user` profile and other Chrome MCP existing-session profiles, including when caller-provided JavaScript evaluation is disabled. It accepts an optional native CSS selector, otherwise selects the first `article`, `main`, or `body`, and reports truncation with the resolved target and URL.

The existing-session selector uses native CSS only; Playwright selector extensions and shadow-root traversal are not supported. This reads the current document and does not add scrolling, feed parsing, or automatic expansion of collapsed content. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing text route now dispatches through the selected browser owner: Playwright for managed profiles, and the document-bound Chrome MCP adapter for existing sessions. The fixed internal reader checks the current document URL against the browser navigation policy, then checks the bound document and admitted URL again before reading text. Missing selectors wait under a shared, cancellable deadline and release the profile operation lock between attempts.

Results retain the existing 40,000-character ceiling and external-content wrapping. Unicode-safe truncation avoids splitting a surrogate pair in the new adapter. The capability flag, host-bound plugin schema test, shared tool fixture, and browser guidance now advertise text support. Existing tool text cases were moved into a focused sibling test file to preserve coverage without growing the oversized general browser-tool suite.

## Evidence

- **Before/after:** the new real-browser route test returns HTTP 501 when run with the baseline route and existing-session limit restored; the candidate returns bounded page text.
- **Real Chromium + packaged Chrome MCP:** all four tests in the existing opt-in Chromium suite passed. The added case exercises the registered `/text` route with `evaluateEnabled=false`, article/main/body fallback, first CSS match, hidden descendants, Chinese/emoji text, invalid selectors, and continued use of a snapshot button reference after reading.
- **Focused tests:** 284 cases passed across the route, tool, and real Chromium suites. After extracting the tool text cases into their own file, all 262 tool cases passed again. The final fixture-typing corrections were revalidated with all 17 affected route/tool cases passing.
- **Local static checks:** the implementation passed the complete changed-file lane, including production and test types, formatting, lint, unused exports, dependency guards, and runtime import cycles. The final capability-expectation and fixture updates also passed focused formatting and lint.
- **Plugin capability regression:** the host-bound existing-session schema must now expose `text` while still omitting unsupported actions. All 292 plugin/schema/tool cases and both dashboard cases passed with the aligned shared fixture.
- **Boundary tests:** the fixed extraction script is executed against a small document fixture to prove literal selector handling, length limits, delayed content, blocked URLs, document/URL changes during admission, and cancellation without reading prose.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and local validation commands</summary>

Against base `7f43b351149930f7db5b4545ad4df4693fe168fc`, preserve the new Chromium test and temporarily restore `routes/agent.debug.ts` plus `routes/existing-session-limits.ts` to their base versions. Run the new case with:

```sh
OPENCLAW_BROWSER_MCP_E2E=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.chromium.test.ts -t 'reads bounded page text' --maxWorkers=1
```

Observed baseline: `501`, with the existing-session text unsupported message. The candidate's new real-browser case passed in 2.4 seconds on this host.

Candidate validation (the changed-file checks also passed with `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 7f43b351149930f7db5b4545ad4df4693fe168fc --` followed by the implementation's 15 changed paths):

```sh
OPENCLAW_BROWSER_MCP_E2E=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.text.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.text.existing-session.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.chromium.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.text.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.text.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.text.existing-session.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/index.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.text.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.dashboard.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The new document fixture tests took about 0.13 seconds combined; the real Chromium test remains in the existing opt-in browser-MCP lane. Shared compiler startup is excluded from those case timings.

</details>

Independent pre-commit review completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings in the selected change and supplied document-owner context.

**Verification boundary:** the real-browser proof uses isolated Chromium and an explicit local CDP endpoint with the packaged Chrome MCP server. It does not exercise Chrome's interactive auto-connect permission prompt, a private signed-in website, or deployment to an operator's installed Gateway. prs.title: fix(progress): preserve words at Unicode truncation boundaries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where progress narration, reasoning drafts, and custom draft labels dropped a complete final word even when it fit the configured limit. Text containing astral Unicode characters could be shortened much more than necessary: a 120-code-point draft became only 41 code points.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three truncation paths mixed code-point limits with UTF-16 whitespace offsets and searched only the already-cut prefix. One shared word-boundary helper now includes the first omitted code point when deciding whether the last word fits. Narration requests, summaries, draft lines, and reasoning all use that owner; the duplicate implementations and slicing wrapper are removed.

Production is **+27/−55, net −28**. Tests are +518/−22; documentation is net neutral. The existing 500/280/120 budgets, reasoning-marker allowance, and middle truncation for paths and commands are unchanged. This counts Unicode code points, not grapheme clusters, and adds no configuration or dependency.

## User Impact

Progress text retains useful filenames and uses the available character budget consistently. For example, a 120-code-point label now retains `important.json` instead of dropping the entire filename. Documentation names the existing code-point unit explicitly.

## Evidence

The original source produced nine failures across the owner suites, two failures through real loopback Discord REST requests, and two failures through the maintained Gateway/Discord fixture. The repaired source passes **158 owner/REST tests plus both Gateway cases**. The Gateway command also completed its normal runtime build and prerequisites. Three unrelated short-label cases were filtered, not counted as passing.

```sh
pnpm test:e2e:gateway test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/channel-progress-presentation.e2e.test.ts -t "label='(complete-word|astral)'"
```

Both Gateway scenarios use the real isolated Gateway and Discord plugin with a mock provider and channel API. Accepted progress payloads changed from 105→120 and 41→120 code points; each flow delivered exactly one final reply and deleted the progress draft. This is mock-Gateway evidence, not a live Discord account test.

```json
{"kind":"mock-gateway","channel":"discord","cases":2,"status":"pass","progressPostsPerCase":1,"finalRepliesPerCase":1,"draftDeletedPerCase":true}
```

Focused coverage includes narration request context, reasoning, shared draft composition, complete-word boundaries, astral text, CJK, combining marks, and unchanged short text. Formatting, scoped diff checks, and independent Codex review passed. An initial Gateway filter selected zero cases; that attempt is excluded from the proof above, which uses the corrected command and actual executed cases.

CI exposed the compositor test file’s size limit. The two new reasoning cases now live in a focused companion file, preserving their inputs, assertions, canonical constructor defaults, and cancellation cleanup. The original compositor test file is restored to its baseline; all 49 cases across both files pass, as do core lint, formatting, and independent Codex review. Production code is unchanged. [The preceding CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33522251628) also failed a compact test group whose cause remains unproved; no timeout or assertion was relaxed, and the updated head must pass the required CI gate.

## Telegram regression coverage

Two isolated Telegram Test Server scenarios exercise complete-word and astral progress labels through a tool-backed agent turn. Each requires the exact progress label to reply to the current inbound message before the unique final response, then verifies the completed transcript and settled session. These scenarios observe native messages and edits; they do not claim draft-deletion coverage or default reply-routing behavior. The two files add 278 test lines and no production code.

Independent Codex review completed two passes with no actionable findings. Native review verification confirmed unchanged source and staged entries. The additional local wrapper check rejected a changed raw Git index checksum; that wrapper result is retained separately from the completed source review.

Local catalog/profile validation is **not green**: seven assertions passed (56 filtered), but the normal command did not finish before its 300-second deadline. A separate diagnostic through the canonical child runner passed five profile assertions before the normal 120-second watchdog fired; it produced no complete report. Neither attempt is counted as successful validation, and no timeout, assertion, or runtime policy was relaxed.

The new Telegram scenarios have not run yet. Landing still requires completed exact-head CI, successful catalog-owner validation, and both native Telegram scenarios.

### Exact-head CI and native Telegram result

[CI run 33577213062](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33577213062) passed for head `c655af0758109c5ed1ce8db49fd33d2f310e5544`. Its normal PR merge checkout `f52b528babffc96dc550b3a12dcfb9110e0de0bd` combines that head with `3699b5006e91fbbed2900f7524f97aad8579eaad`. [QA shard 3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33577213062/job/100083900523) explicitly passed the two targeted catalog cases and all five profile-selection cases; the complete shard finished with 77 files and 733 tests passing. All six QA smoke profiles also passed. This completes catalog-owner validation; the earlier incomplete local attempts remain recorded above.

The [native Telegram run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33577357161/job/100084952074) selected the same `c655af0758109c5ed1ce8db49fd33d2f310e5544` candidate, as recorded in both scenario evidence entries. Both scenarios stopped at the first real-user send with `sendMessage failed (400): Have no write access to the chat`. Their native timelines contain no inbound message and no events, so this is not label-rendering or finalization proof. The shared adapter sends to the leased native group; logical scenario IDs do not choose a different Telegram chat. No retry, altered assertion, or configuration fallback has been used to hide the failure.

The remaining landing gate is successful native Telegram ingress, progress-label, reply-binding, and finalization evidence. The failed artifact is retained while the QA-user group-access prerequisite is investigated. No changes to the shared credential pool or its membership have been made.

prs.title: fix(telegram): defer transcript echo until message admission
prs.body:
Closes #146311

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users running multiple bot accounts in a mention-gated group would see transcript echoes from every bot after sending one voice note, even though only the addressed bot admitted the message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram now uses the shared deferred preflight-audio behavior: transcription remains available before mention detection, but the user-visible transcript echo is held until the message passes the existing command and mention admission gates. Direct messages and admitted group messages retain the configured echo behavior and account/topic routing.

## User Impact

Only the Telegram bot that admits a voice message echoes its transcript. Unaddressed bots can still inspect the transcript for mention detection without leaking a duplicate reply into the group.

prs.title: fix(system-agent): verify declared fallback execution runtimes
prs.body:
## Problem

System-agent startup can reject a successful verification probe when an explicitly configured Codex route has a legitimate OpenClaw fallback. A numeric provider `timeoutSeconds` is one reproducer: it is treated as authored transport customization, and the Codex harness explicitly declares an OpenClaw fallback for that customization.

There is also a cold-start trap: the configured plugin is registered inside the probe's scoped generation, but may be absent before and after that scope. Resolving availability outside that scope keeps returning the authored Codex route, so merely separating configured and execution routes is insufficient.

## Change

- Keep the authored configured-route identity intact.
- Resolve the permitted effective execution runtime before staging its owner artifacts and running the probe.
- Load a cold configured runtime through the existing owned plugin-generation mechanism; reuse an already prepared runtime when appropriate.
- Revalidate the effective route and exact execution owner inside a fresh configured-runtime generation.
- Retain the existing exact harness, credential/owner, configured-route, and plugin-artifact checks. Reported proof never grants permission to select an arbitrary runtime.

No provider-timeout removal or global runtime change is required.

## Validation

- Targeted real-provider qualification of the cold fallback path, with the timeout unchanged.
- Unchanged-proof control and explicit rejection controls for an unannounced runtime, incorrect execution-owner proof, changed configured route, and mismatched owner plugin artifacts.
- Added focused source regression tests and ran lint on all eight changed source/test files with zero errors and warnings.
- The normal Vitest runner could not start in the available reused dependency tree (`defineCacheKeyGenerator is not a function`). That suite is not claimed as passed; targeted standalone source and real-provider checks were used separately.

Related to #134471. Complements the diagnostic improvement in #144165; this change addresses permitted fallback resolution rather than suppressing the ownership error.

prs.title: fix(macos): forward MCP app sandbox over remote SSH
prs.body:
Closes #145522

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS app's remote-over-SSH mode only forwards the Gateway control port. MCP App and Board widgets are served from the separate sandbox listener on the next port, so the dashboard can connect to the remote Gateway but widget iframes fail to load unless the user manually opens a second SSH forward.

## Why This Change Was Made

`RemotePortTunnel` adds a second `-L` mapping for the default sandbox listener, derived from the remote Gateway port as `remotePort + 1`. The mapping uses the same local port number that the remote Gateway advertises in `sandboxPort`, so existing dashboard URL resolution can reach the sandbox through the SSH tunnel without additional configuration.

The sandbox mapping is optional. Before adding it, the native tunnel owner now verifies that the local sandbox port is available and that it does not collide with the selected local control port. If either condition fails, only the existing control forward is emitted. This preserves Gateway connectivity when a local service or an existing manual sandbox forward already owns the sandbox port. The boundary case where the Gateway itself is on port 65535 also skips the derived mapping rather than overflowing the port range.

## User Impact

Remote SSH users on the default port layout can load MCP App and Board widget content without manually running a separate `ssh -L 18790:127.0.0.1:18790 ...` tunnel. Existing Gateway forwarding remains available if the optional sandbox port is unavailable instead of failing the whole SSH process through `ExitOnForwardFailure=yes`.

## Evidence

- `RemotePortTunnelTests` covers the normal two-forward case.
- Added targeted regression coverage showing an unavailable sandbox port leaves the control forward intact.
- Added targeted regression coverage showing a remapped control port equal to the derived sandbox port does not emit two conflicting `-L` mappings.
- The implementation reuses `RemotePortTunnel.portIsFree`, the same native bind-availability owner used for control-port selection.
- Local macOS Swift tests were not run in this automation environment because it does not provide the repository checkout/dependency runtime required by the native test lane. No local test result is claimed.
- GitHub's primary CI workflow for the latest revision was skipped rather than executed, so it is not counted as validation. Passive macOS and shared OpenClawKit Periphery checks completed successfully; other checks may still be running.

## Remaining Proof Gap

This revision addresses the actionable sandbox-bind compatibility finding in code and regression coverage, but it does not provide the requested after-fix macOS runtime capture. Native widget recovery and occupied-port behavior still need real macOS transport proof before this should be considered merge-ready.

prs.title: perf(sessions): avoid repeated transcript backfills and cron scans
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-list backfill re-read transcript events, snapshots, and visible-message metadata after every Gateway restart, even when the same rows had already been projected. Cron retention also rediscovered every agent's candidates at each sweep interval, including stores with no expiring runs.

This change persists the small preview/terminal-model projection on the existing session window. Current append writers update it in their existing window statement and publish it in their existing receipt. Startup consumes it in the existing batched row-facts query. Missing projections use one bounded writer operation, including successful empty results; the old read-only backfill RPC is removed. The cache is valid against the transcript timestamp and existing indexed sequence because supported older importers can preserve mtime while appending. No new generation or cross-thread handshake is introduced.

Cron retention derives the next expiry from metadata already read by its worker, retains that deadline per logical agent/store, and invalidates it on committed cron-row receipts. Empty stores stay idle. The existing minimum retry interval and final deletion guards remain.

### Measurement

Post-merge measurements use exact merge `3d385d4f74237055952758d1c83d9f1f49542b94`, compared with baseline `40fabad6db1608700507c2dccfd95271af1ec3c3`. One small/scaled pair before and one after, using the same retained harness; scaled means 200 sessions across five agents. Each run includes ten warmed turns, a 65-second settle, and 300 seconds of connected idle. Ranges below describe turns within one run, not independent-run confidence intervals. Both candidate workloads pass with complete causal/timer coverage and no failed SQL. Counts only: host load was approximately 18–24 on 32 cores during final runs; latency is unmeasured.

**The repeated backfill growth is removed.** Scaled boot/connect backfill falls from 850 statements / 170 requests to zero, matching the small fixture. Each targeted event, snapshot, and visible-message metadata read class falls from 170 to zero. Whole-workload backfill falls from 1,052 / 212 to 60 / 17 on scaled, versus 60 / 15 to 56 / 15 on small.

| Owner / phase, statements / requests | Small before → after | Scaled before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Backfill, boot | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 400 / 80 → 0 / 0 |
| Backfill, connect | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 450 / 90 → 0 / 0 |
| Backfill, whole workload | 60 / 15 → 56 / 15 | 1,052 / 212 → 60 / 17 |
| Cron reaper, whole workload | 4 / 1 → 4 / 1 | 24 / 9 → 24 / 9 |
| Backfill and cron reaper, connected idle | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 |
| Usage projection, boot/connect | 1 / 1 → 1 / 1 | 449 / 7 → 450 / 7 |
| Usage projection, first-warm background | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 440 / 69 → 162 / 25 |
| Transcript index, first-warm background | 0 / 0 → 0 / 0 | 211 / 1 → 0 / 0 |
| Backfill, first-warm background | 4 / 1 → 4 / 1 | 4 / 1 → 4 / 1 |

Cron reaper and transcript-index work are zero during boot/connect, and all four named owners are zero during connected idle. Cron reaper is also zero during first-warm background. Both target owners remain MAIN 0 throughout.

**The harness does not demonstrate cron deadline savings.** Reaper activity occurs entirely in the cron phase; baseline idle already contains no repeated reaper work. Deadline skip/invalidation behavior is regression-tested, but measured reaper counts remain unchanged, including their fixture-size growth.

| Warmed all-thread metric, median [min–max] | Small before → after | Scaled before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Causal statements | 118 [118–123] → 102 [102–107] | 131 [131–214] → 115 [115–127] |
| Causal requests | 34 [34–36] → 34 [34–36] | 37 [37–46] → 37 [37–40] |
| Raw statements | 122.5 [122–133] → 109 [108–113] | 137 [135–1,444] → 121.5 [121–296] |
| Raw requests | 36 [36–42] → 36.5 [36–38] | 39.5 [39–119] → 39 [39–67] |

Warm MAIN median is zero in every run; candidate raw MAIN maximum is also zero. The 16-statement causal reduction is **not attributed to this PR**: other main changes landed between baseline and merge, affecting post-commit envelopes, projection snapshots, active-context/reset-window reads, and participant reads. Small raw requests rise by 0.5 at the median from background scheduling; causal requests are unchanged and whole-workload requests fall 1,009 → 1,007. No target-owner regression is shown.

Shared warmed reads after the change: exactly two exact-entry fact reads per turn in both fixtures; zero hydration, watermark, and row-facts reads. Scaled entry-cache snapshots retain five background reads across all ten turns, with zero causal reads.

| Whole-phase counts, statements / requests / MAIN | Small before → after | Scaled before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Boot/connect | 1,318 / 108 / 448 → 1,175 / 96 / 448 | 2,493 / 640 / 119 → 2,045 / 463 / 124 |
| Connected idle | 44 / 19 / 0 → 44 / 19 / 0 | 84 / 30 / 0 → 72 / 27 / 0 |
| First-warm background | 10 / 6 / 0 → 6 / 2 / 0 | 671 / 75 / 9 → 169 / 27 / 0 |
| Whole workload | 5,030 / 1,009 / 505 → 4,583 / 1,007 / 470 | 15,980 / 3,377 / 178 → 14,227 / 3,161 / 146 |

Scaled boot/connect saves 850 backfill statements, offset by 402 additional statements in other owners, for a net saving of 448. Offsets include canonical-index repair, memory-schema admission, pinned-read transactions, and strict-schema checks. The additional five boot MAIN statements belong to canonical-validation receipt admission, not the target owners.

The first-warm background reduction is mostly a **phase shift**, not removed work. Scaled transcript-index whole-workload counts remain exactly 1,230 statements / 67 requests; 1,039 background statements moved from warm turns into first-turn. Usage work similarly moves earlier: whole-workload counts fall only 1,968 / 240 → 1,896 / 238. Startup usage full refresh and durable transcript-index completion remain follow-ups outside this PR; the earlier usage batching change already existed on baseline.

All phase totals reconcile exactly against the canonical SQL/request/MAIN aggregates. The baseline scaled run contains one shutdown `database is locked` SQL failure despite passing workload/coverage checks; both candidate runs contain none.

### Checks and accepted edges

- Target backfill and cron-reaper entry paths: Gateway-main SQL and direct T1 calls remain 0 → 0; all added persistence runs through the existing writer worker. Shared transcript kernels retain their existing mixed-use T1 annotations outside these target paths; this PR does not claim to retire those unrelated callers.
- Removed post-await materialization and duplicate generation/revision/readiness checks in backfill: optional display metadata may lag a concurrent rewrite until the queued refresh. The publication-time session/private-source identity check stays because text must not cross a replaced or revoked session.
- Removed duplicate admission/currentness checks around cron discovery and preparatory context checks: discovery may finish from an earlier snapshot; committed receipts advance retry, and the deletion owner still refuses changed or active rows at the real effect.
- Retained final cron deletion guards protect user data, unsettled descendants, and generated-media work.
- Bare nullable cache columns use the documented same-version additive migration contract. Older readers ignore them; older writes invalidate the derived cache through existing timestamp/index facts.

## Evidence

Final-head CI has completed: all selected behavioral/compact/UI tests and PostgreSQL conformance pass; remaining failures are the exact inherited static signatures documented below. The [published-driver × candidate update cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38487603607/job/115621624167) passes at production head `8392caee832de08685af59ff149b4c134c2be127`; the later `220c45de` commit changes tests only. Full package build, package integrity, and installer acceptance also pass. Changed-file basic lint, formatting, and diff sanity pass. Two independent Codex review rounds found no actionable P0/P1 findings. No SDK surface change. Diff against integrated main: 65 files, +971/−456 lines. Final post-merge counts and their attribution limits are recorded above.

CI repair preserves the actor's existing narrow window projection, removes a broad type import that formed a dependency cycle, and teaches migration identity/witness comparison that the two preview-cache columns are derived. Full custody fingerprints and retained-history checks remain. Historical migration assertions expect exactly two new nullable fields; original backup equality is unchanged. Legacy-preview fixtures now explicitly represent pre-cache writers, while reopen tests consume already-persisted previews immediately.

Focused reruns pass for the wrapper inventory (2 cases), canonical schema preservation (2), equivalent-history handoff, shared-store ownership, read-cache reconciliation, foreground preview, and recovery preview. Exact-head CI also passes Doctor partial-retry and canonical migration preservation, with no timeout increase. Focused health and bulk session-list cases pass. The remaining legacy-backfill failure was traced to its thread-pool test placement: writer-backed admission requires the host process, so the test moves to the existing forked database-worker group. Abort-aware test waiting ensures timeout cleanup completes. Both the legacy-backfill case and terminal-fallback sibling pass after that test-host correction. No broad local suite was rerun.

The required Knip scan found the now-unused synchronous terminal-model reader, which is deleted with its storage import. Four unrelated Muse exports fail identically on main at `9690a6d7fa9cdb0df6aaec32008a04b55e527499`; the three affected Muse files are unchanged ([main evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38478278963/job/115574544966)). The final Knip scan confirms there are no PR-caused unused exports; only those exact inherited Muse findings remain. Script export scan is clean. Final-head CI includes the deletion.

The forked test host also exposed a brittle process-wide timer count. The two cancellation cases now assert cancellation of the exact transcript refresh timer and zero later fact publications, independently of the writer broker's idle timer. Replacement preview is asserted from its committed receipt. Both cases pass locally; this last push changes tests only. Final-head CI confirms T1 302→302 and all dialect groups unchanged; source contracts, architecture/Madge, lint, and docs pass.

The merge-ref baseline job also reports an inherited mock-export violation at `test/helpers/openclaw-test-process.test.ts:5`, introduced on main by `65cbe2376353cbd895071e2da1cb012bc461d51d`. The file is absent from this branch; main contains the exact closed mock factory rejected by the unchanged checker, with no baseline exemption. The T1 and dialect checks in that same job pass.

Final-head merge-ref build, package-boundary, production-types, and test-types checks report the same inherited `TS2349`/`TS2757` error at `session-accessor.sqlite-node-artifacts.ts:490`. Main commit `653003a010987ad75393bdd0ff067283f41a1be7` (#171481) calls the participant publication object as a function after `5e9608dec7c575107b629de725528d7b7f841451` changed that API to `{ version, publish }`. The caller is absent from this PR head. Main has since repaired that call in `4aa62334122ed29f605f9820c4604539b3ccee77`, which is included in the verified merge. The package-boundary receipt error follows the same declaration-compilation failure. [Build evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38488972999/job/115610057817), [boundary evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38488972999/job/115610058010), [test-types evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38488972999/job/115610408206).

## What Problem This Solves

The two config-home resolution layers read overlapping environment variables at different precedence. Different subsystems call different resolvers, so when the layers disagree the result is **two openclaw.json files with no error on either side** — e.g. a CLI process whose `config set` lands in one home while the running gateway reads another, so the edit silently never applies. That failure mode was hit in practice this week: a config edit reported success while the gateway's live config never changed.

Adds `src/config/config-home-consistency.test.ts` — 4 tests pinning that `resolveStateDir` and `resolveConfigPath` agree on the same state directory across the env combinations that matter:

- `OPENCLAW_HOME` moves both resolvers
- `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` pins both
- a relative `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` resolves absolutely for both
- an existing config under the state dir is found by both

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): retry inbound DMs with transiently unresolvable LID identity
prs.body:
Part of #119475

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: inbound WhatsApp direct messages (DMs) whose LID→phone mapping is not resolvable at admission time are treated as non-messages and permanently dropped, silently.

This is the retryable half of openclaw/openclaw#119475 (P1, `impact:message-loss`). When a DM arrives from a `@lid`/`@hosted.lid` chat, the normalizer calls `resolveInboundJid(remoteJid)`; if it returns `null` (LID mapping lookup not yet hydrated, or the lookup fails transiently), the normalizer returns `null`, the durable ingress drain completes the claim, and the message is gone — with only a verbose-gated log line.

Production reports confirm a large share of these losses is a **race, not a permanent absence**: the mapping files (`lid-mapping-<lid>_reverse.json`) are written within the same second as the drop, so a short retry/re-resolve delivers the message (see the 2026-09-02 production analysis in #119475: "the mapping is not missing, it is late … a meaningful share of CTWA losses can be fixed without promoting unmapped LIDs to peers").

## User Impact

User impact: operators running WhatsApp no longer silently lose first-contact DMs (CTWA ad leads, @username senders) when the LID mapping is briefly unavailable; the message now waits in the durable drain and is delivered as soon as the mapping resolves, exactly like any other transiently deferred inbound.

No breaking change, no config change, no security-sensitive identity promotion: this fix only changes *when* an already-retryable message is re-normalized. The separate permanent-`sender_pn`-absent case (which requires admitting an opaque LID as a peer, pending the maintainer product/security decision in #119475) is intentionally out of scope here.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveJidToE164` intentionally returns `null` on a LID lookup miss or failure — that contract is locked by `text-runtime.test.ts` (`returns null when lidLookup throws`). The drop happens one layer up, in the direct-message normalizer, which converted that `null` into "this is not a message" (`return null`). The drain then treats a `null` preparation as terminal (`prepared === null → return "completed"`), permanently discarding the claim.

The fix routes the unresolvable-identity case into the existing "durable drain will normalize again" retry path instead of the terminal path:

- `message-normalization.ts`: for a direct DM, an unresolvable sender identity now throws `WhatsAppIngressIdentityUnavailableError` instead of returning `null`. The error is raised *before* `checkInboundAccessControl`, so it has no pairing-reply side effects and can be retried freely. Groups are unaffected (they don't resolve the peer).
- `message-delivery.ts`: the completed-drain read-receipt branch guards normalization with try/catch so an unresolvable identity only skips the read receipt and cannot abort the rest of the batch. The already-existing `accepted` branch already catches normalize errors and calls `finishPreparation(undefined)`, which is what lets the drain re-normalize.

The durable ingress monitor releases the claim on dispatch failure and retries with backoff (base 1s, cap 3m, 8 attempts, 24h dead-letter floor), which is ample time for the same-second mapping write to land. `resolveJidToE164` keeps its contract unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused regression test added in `monitor-inbox.reply-context.test.ts` — `retries a direct DM whose LID identity is transiently unresolvable instead of dropping it`:

- Drives the real `messages.upsert` → admission → durable drain flow through `startInboxMonitor`.
- Mocks `getPNForLID` to fail once (transient lookup failure), then succeed.
- Asserts the lookup is retried (`toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)`), the message is delivered with the correct conversation id (`+999`), and the body round-trips.

Test + related suites all green (WhatsApp extension shard):
- `monitor-inbox.reply-context.test.ts`: 10 passed
- `monitor-inbox.delivery-and-dedupe.test.ts`, `monitor-inbox.access-and-echo.test.ts`, `inbound.test.ts`, `text-runtime.test.ts`: 128 passed
- `approval-reactions.test.ts`, `monitor-inbox.policy.test.ts`: 29 passed

Verification commands run:
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-whatsapp.config.ts <files>` — all passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/whatsapp/tsconfig.json` — clean (production source typecheck)
- Direct `oxlint` on all three changed files — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

Notes on scope of evidence: this is a behavior fix on the channel boundary proven through the real mocked-Gateway ingress flow (the standard for this extension's inbound tests). Live WhatsApp proof for this exact race is documented by production reporters in #119475; a live account was not available in this environment.

### Focused one-worker run (measured)

The regression test was also run alone with `--maxWorkers=1` (real `startInboxMonitor` → `messages.upsert` → durable admission → drain retry → delivery flow, mocked socket + LID lookup):

```
✓ ... monitor inbox reply context > retries a direct DM whose LID identity is transiently unresolvable instead of dropping it 60063ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed | 9 skipped (10)
```

Measured one-worker wall time for the focused run: **380s** (dominated by first-run vitest worker compile + transform on this cold Windows host; the test itself reports 60s and 335ms when run warm alongside the rest of the file).

**AI assistance disclosure:** This PR was authored with AI assistance (CoMind), including the reproduction analysis, the fix, and the regression test. The human maintainer should review the identity-contract reasoning against the #119475 maintainer decision before extending this beyond the retryable share.

prs.title: fix(channels): stale-claim recovery no longer consumes ingress retry budget
prs.body:
Closes #158082

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a channel ingress event whose claim owner is lost (lease expired or process died) has its retry budget consumed and its real prior failure erased, so healthy events can be dead-lettered prematurely with no real handler failure behind them.

## User Impact

User impact: an inbound event interrupted by a crash, restart, or lease expiry is re-dispatched without burning an attempt, and its previous real handler failure is preserved for diagnostics. Premature dead-lettering from recovery churn is eliminated. No schema, configuration, public API, or data migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The release contract already records owner-loss as non-failure: every other owner-lost path in the ingress drain (`GatewayDrainingError`, unadopted, superseded) passes `recordAttempt: false` to `release`, which keeps `attempts`/`last_attempt_at`/`last_error` intact. `releaseClaimIfStillStale` was the only owner-lost path that instead incremented `attempts`, overwrote `last_attempt_at`, and never wrote `last_error`, violating that contract. Because `recoverStaleClaims` runs on every `drainOnce` with `staleMs: 0` (and `claimNext` routes stale claims through it too), a repeatedly re-claimed event could climb toward the dead-letter limit (default 8) purely from recovery, with backoff skewed and diagnostics misleading.

The fix stops the attempts increment and `last_attempt_at` overwrite in `releaseClaimIfStillStale` (the row's `status`/`claim_*` reset and `updated_at` remain). No new API surface; the behavior now matches the existing `recordAttempt: false` contract. The production change is the SET clause in one statement.

## Evidence

### Regression test (TDD: red before fix, green after)

Added to `src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts`: enqueue an event, fail it once via `release({ lastError: "real failure", releasedAt: 20 })`, re-claim with a replacement worker, then `recoverStaleClaims({ staleMs: 5, now: 30 })`.

- Before the fix: `AssertionError` — row returns `attempts: 2`, `lastAttemptAt: 30` (budget consumed, real failure erased).
- After the fix: `attempts: 1`, `lastAttemptAt: 20`, `lastError: "real failure"` (budget preserved, real failure intact).

```text
$ pnpm test src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts -t "recoverStaleClaims does not consume retry budget"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed | 32 skipped (33)
```

### Full related suite

```text
$ pnpm test src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts src/channels/message/ingress-drain.test.ts src/channels/message/ingress-drain.tombstone-lane.test.ts src/channels/message/ingress-claim-owner.test.ts
76 passed
```

Also ran the ingress subset of the state-migrations suite (passed).

### Typecheck

This change is a small, self-contained statement edit in `ingress-queue.ts` plus one test file. Full-repo `tsgo` on this Windows host cannot complete (the `run-tsgo` wrapper hangs in its job-object spawn layer; the underlying compiler binary completes), so I ran an A/B typecheck with the repo's native compiler (`tsc.exe` from the bundled tsgo distribution) on clean `main` vs. this branch: identical pre-existing error set (532 "cannot be named" declaration-emit errors in unrelated test-support files on both), zero errors in the changed files, zero diff between the two runs. This change introduces no new type errors.

### Scope boundary

Only `src/channels/message/ingress-queue.ts` (one SET clause) and its test file changed. No behavior change to `release()` (the `recordAttempt: false` path was already correct), no change to `recoverStaleClaims` selection logic, and no change to retry/dead-letter policy values.

prs.title: fix(agents): honor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR in claude-cli transcript resolution
prs.body:
<!--
Closes #145309
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the `claude-cli` backend with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set (e.g. a second Claude login on the same host) would lose session continuity on every cold turn and silently fall back to the next model with no history after any config hot-reload. The bundled `claude-cli` transcript resolver looked for project JSONL files under `$HOME/.claude/projects/…` and ignored `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so every transcript check missed — even though the session catalog scanner, provider-auth resolver, and Claude Code itself all honor `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` as the projects tree root.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two resolvers were hardcoding `~/.claude/projects` instead of honoring `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`:

1. **`resolveClaudeCliProjectDirForWorkspace`** (`src/agents/command/claude-cli-project-dir.ts`) — used by the transcript probe (`claudeCliSessionTranscriptHasContent`) and the doctor health check. A miss here triggers `reason=missing-transcript` session resets on every cold turn.

2. **`resolveClaudeProjectsDir`** (`src/gateway/cli-session-history.claude.ts`) — used by `resolveClaudeCliSessionFilePath` and `readClaudeCliFallbackSeed`. A miss here means the fallback prelude has no harvested context, so a fallback-model re-run starts with zero conversation history.

Both now follow the same pattern as the existing `resolveClaudeCliConfigDir` in `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-claude-compat.ts` and `configuredClaudeConfigDir` in `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-scan.ts`: when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set and non-blank, resolve project transcripts under `<resolved config dir>/projects`; otherwise fall back to `<homeDir>/.claude/projects` as before.

## User Impact

Users who set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (for a second Claude login, a dedicated profile, or a Docker-mounted config directory) will no longer experience:
- Cold-turn session resets (`reason=missing-transcript`) that discard the stored Claude session id.
- Warm-turn silent fallback to a different model with no conversation history after a config hot-reload.
- The cascading failure where the fallback process occupies the same live-session owner key, blocking the primary model from reusing the slot.

The existing workaround (symlinking `$HOME/.claude/projects/<key>` → `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/<key>`) is no longer needed.

## Evidence

### Production-path behavior proof

Exercises the **production exported functions the Gateway actually runs** — `claudeCliSessionTranscriptHasContent` (the session-continuity probe used on cold turns) and `readClaudeCliFallbackSeed` (the fallback-history recovery reader) — against a real `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` tree containing a Claude Code session JSONL (one user/assistant exchange):

```
[setup] CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = /tmp/oc-proof-prod-swqXxG/claude-config
[setup] transcript written to /tmp/oc-proof-prod-swqXxG/claude-config/projects/-tmp-oc-proof-prod-swqXxG-workspace-demo/prod-proof-session.jsonl

[1] production transcript probe (transcript under $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR):
    claudeCliSessionTranscriptHasContent() = true
    -> session stays LIVE, no missing-transcript reset: true

[2] production fallback history reader (readClaudeCliFallbackSeed):
    recentTurns = 2
    turn[0].role = user
    turn[1].role = assistant
    -> fallback re-run recovers the conversation from $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects

[3] negative control (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unset):
    probe = false (expected, no reset-triggering miss leak)
    seed = undefined (expected)

Result: production probe + production history reader both honor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.
```

What this demonstrates:
- The **production transcript probe** finds the existing Claude session under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/…` and returns `true` — the stored session id stays live across a cold turn instead of being reset with `reason=missing-transcript`.
- The **production fallback history reader** recovers the full recent-turn history (user + assistant roles) from `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/…` — a fallback-model re-run starts with the actual conversation instead of no context.
- The **negative control** (env var unset) shows the same session id resolves to `false`/`undefined` under the default `<homeDir>/.claude/projects` tree — the fix is selective, not a lookup leak.

(The one `v4 miss` warn line in the trace is the negative-control run emitting its expected structured miss for the default-tree path — the same warn Gateway operators would see before this fix on every turn.)

### CI

All 169 jobs green on head `d3d5304a5c` (run 34682440091, `openclaw/ci-gate` SUCCESS). Earlier runs hit two unrelated infra flakes — a `resolve-auth.test.ts` 1000ms timeout and a runner-preempted `checks-fast-bundled-protocol` job (0 steps executed) — both cleared on rerun; no test failure was ever traced to this patch.

### Resolver unit tests (4/4 passed)

```
✓ resolves under <homeDir>/.claude/projects by default
✓ resolves under $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects when configured
✓ falls back to <homeDir>/.claude/projects for a blank CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
✓ resolves a relative CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR against the process working directory
```

### Test-suite coverage (189/189 passed locally)

- **Transcript probe test** (`attempt-execution.test.ts`, 21 tests in the probe suite): writes a transcript under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/…`, verifies `claudeCliSessionTranscriptHasContent` returns `true` inside the env override and the file is absent from the default tree outside it (direct path check, no probe side-effects).
- **Fallback seed test** (`cli-session-history.test.ts`, 168 tests): writes a session JSONL under `configDir/projects/demo-workspace/`, verifies `readClaudeCliFallbackSeed` finds it with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set (2 turns, correct roles) and returns `undefined` without it.

### Patch history

- `6d11eda` — initial fix + tests
- `7c3d4f` — switch 6 synchronous `withEnvAsync` callbacks to `withEnv` (typecheck)
- `9205926` — avoid probe grace-period side-effects in the new test's negative assertion
- `4ee3802` / `5fce660` / `d3d5304` — empty CI-rerun commits for unrelated infra flakes
