prs.title: ci(linux): validate the Linux companion build on native aarch64
prs.body:
Related: #138279

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's Linux companion CI only ever validates the amd64 build. The aarch64 packaging path (added in #139729 — an architecture-portable tool manifest and dynamic AppImage runtime-path lookup) has never actually run in CI on real arm64 hardware; the only validation so far has been one contributor's own Raspberry Pi 5, entirely outside this project's CI, as reported in #138279.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an `aarch64` leg to the `linux-app.yml` build matrix using GitHub's free native `ubuntu-22.04-arm` hosted runner — no cross-compilation or QEMU. This is scoped to **CI validation only**, matching #138279's own stated non-goal for a first PR ("official arm64 packages build and start," not full release publication); extending the signed release pipeline (`linux-app-release.yml`) to actually publish aarch64 release assets is a separate, larger, secrets-touching change that should follow once this validation exists.

Three things beyond the runner label needed to change for the matrix to work correctly:
- **Cache key collision**: `runner.os` is `"Linux"` for both amd64 and arm64 hosted runners, so the arch was added to the cache key to stop the two legs from poisoning each other's `target/` directories.
- **Artifact name collisions**: the four `upload-artifact` steps used fixed names; both legs would otherwise overwrite each other's uploads. Names are now arch-suffixed.
- **No official aarch64 Arch Linux container image**: the packaged-runtime smoke test's optional cross-distro check pins an Arch Linux container by digest that only publishes an `amd64` platform (confirmed via `docker manifest inspect`; Arch Linux ARM is a separate project). That one optional check now only runs on the amd64 leg — the FUSE-based extraction/launch check it supplements still runs on both architectures.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Contributors and maintainers get real CI coverage of the aarch64 Linux build path, closing a gap where that path could silently break with no CI signal.

## Evidence

Dispatched this exact workflow on a fork and let it run to completion: https://github.com/kip-claw/openclaw/actions/runs/34689108136

All jobs passed, including `Build Linux companion (aarch64)` running natively on `ubuntu-22.04-arm` end to end: Rust compile, test suite, Tauri bundle build (deb + AppImage), AppImage finalization, and the packaged-runtime smoke test (with the Arch container check correctly skipped for aarch64).

Test plan:
- [x] Live dispatch on a fork, both architectures, full pipeline — see run linked above.
- [ ] Confirm the same on `openclaw/openclaw` once merged (a maintainer would need to dispatch it, or it runs automatically on the next relevant PR).

prs.title: perf(sqlite): skip absent TEMP transcript trigger drops
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh transcript-index connections issue `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS` for triggers that the required TEMP catalog read has already shown are absent. Reuse that catalog snapshot to omit the no-op drops. Reinstallation still drops existing triggers before creating their replacements; transaction rollback and write tracking retain the same owner.

This PR originally also removed canonical-schema comparison databases and their cross-worker handoff. That work independently landed in #171456 (`15534c36e2daaf1dae77c5422c44099dff4a4c49`). The final integration preserves main's implementation and regression coverage byte-for-byte. The remaining diff is only the TEMP-trigger optimization, its regression, and documentation: **+65 / −10, net +55 lines**.

The historical pair below measured both optimizations. **Do not credit this narrowed PR with the combined −122 statements / −10 requests.** Its directly attributable saving in that capture is **12 no-op trigger-drop statements on two fresh handles, with no additional or removed worker requests**. The other 13 statements in the historical generation-setup delta reflect one inventory installation moving outside the sampled work, not an additional saving.

## Historical measurement and attribution

Shared SQL harness v2.1.0, one completed baseline/candidate pair. Counts are all-thread; host load precludes latency claims. Measured candidate head: `1a24a4b6cbfe259388ddbf0f0731cd5f5e59d206`. Final scoped head: `01ef74bdb35789e8b9ae150a54cf4d4ea5f6c94a`. Both captures passed workload assertions with zero SQL execution errors. The candidate build passed; the optional macOS idle sampler initially divided by zero before workload execution, so the private harness copy handles zero ticks and reuses that build.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First-turn window SQL / requests / MAIN | 1,105 / 163 / 36 | 835 / 150 / 44 |
| First-turn causal SQL / requests / MAIN | 367 / 70 / 27 | 350 / 72 / 27 |
| Warm causal SQL median [min–max] | 124 [124–129] | 124 [124–129] |
| Warm causal requests median [min–max] | 34 [34–36] | 34 [34–36] |
| Warm causal MAIN | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Warm all-window SQL median [min–max] | 128.5 [128–152] | 128.5 [128–135] |
| Warm all-window requests median [min–max] | 36 [36–39] | 36 [36–40] |
| Warm all-window MAIN median [min–max] | 0 [0–4] | 0 [0–0] |

Whole capture: **4,953 → 4,831 statements (−122, −2.46%), 947 → 937 requests (−10), MAIN 504 → 504**. Warm all-window medians are unchanged at 128.5 statements / 36 requests; warm causal counts are exactly unchanged at 124 / 34 / 0 MAIN. The raw first-window saving includes background work moving into connect, particularly 134 memory-schema statements. It is not all eliminated work.

| First-window substep | Base SQL / requests / MAIN | Candidate SQL / requests / MAIN |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh-session creation/admission | 98 / 10 / 0 | 51 / 8 / 0 |
| Turn admission/runtime/context/catalog | 148 / 36 / 0 | 138 / 38 / 0 |
| Turn actor/session persistence | 132 / 24 / 0 | 125 / 24 / 0 |
| Turn postwork/activity/memory flush | 60 / 10 / 0 | 60 / 10 / 0 |
| Background memory setup | 445 / 30 / 0 | 275 / 26 / 0 |
| Other background work | 195 / 53 / 9 | 158 / 44 / 17 |
| Participant-triggered cold admission | 27 / 0 / 27 | 27 / 0 / 27 |
| Unassociated clean-close maintenance | 0 / 0 / 0 | 1 / 0 / 0 |

SQL follows execution time; requests follow dispatch time. Target-operation rows overlap: canonical comparison construction/read is **66 → 0** in the first window and **84 → 0** across the capture; model watermark and model catalog requests each fall **14 → 8 SQL**; first creation mutation falls **33 → 27 SQL**. TEMP generation setup is **65 → 40 SQL** across the capture: twelve no-op drops disappear on two fresh handles, two existing-trigger installations retain their drops, and one thirteen-statement inventory installation is absent because of startup ordering. Nonoverlapping totals are canonical helper 84 → 0, generation setup 65 → 40, and all remaining SQL 4,804 → 4,791. Do not add the nested watermark/catalog/creation savings to those totals.

Shared first-window read families (base → candidate, SQL/request membership): exact-entry facts 6/6 → 7/7; actor hydration 3/3 → 2/2; entry-cache snapshots 11/7 → 6/4; row facts 5/2 → 5/2; watermark leaf reads 4/4 → 4/4. Warm families do not rise. First causal requests rise by two (one zero-SQL inventory and one exact-entry read); retention gains two cold quarantine reads. These disclosed startup-order differences are outweighed by the measured net reduction. No new worker request is introduced by this patch.

The first-window MAIN increase of eight is background timing: four plugin-source capture statements move from connect, and four lease reads move from warm window 1. Whole-capture MAIN is unchanged, and every candidate warm window has MAIN zero.

Touched-area T1 inventory calls: **0 → 0**. The measured 27 causal MAIN statements are cold-handle admission triggered by participant publication, assigned to the separate t1tail2 lane; the actual participant write is already in a worker. This PR does not change that path. Warm causal MAIN is zero.

Main was merged to resolve the overlap with #171407, which retired generation triggers. That retirement remains intact; this PR retains the transcript-index snapshot optimization and its reinstall/rollback regression. The table above is the completed pre-integration pair, not a new measurement of the integrated head.

## Removed checks and accepted edges

- Skip no-op drops for absent TEMP triggers using the catalog snapshot already required for installation. The connection-local owner installs synchronously; no intervening writer or extra freshness check is introduced.
- Existing-trigger replacement, unexpected-object detection, rollback, and transcript write tracking remain unchanged.
- The format/PID/source-hash checks and canonical contract handoff removed in the historical pair are already retired on main by #171456; they are no longer part of this diff.

## Evidence

- Two clean Codex autoreview rounds completed for the original implementation and import cleanup. The remaining implementation and test are unchanged; conflict resolution preserves main's canonical owner and tests.
- Prior scoped head `0bd84f461f97729a10ca1ab67f464d213d99862f`: [CI run 38490678539](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38490678539) passed 74 jobs, including changed-owner tests, types, lint, source contracts, Madge, PostgreSQL conformance, and database ratchets. Its native same-session E2E passed all eight turns and four same-session pairs in 65.1 seconds.
- That prior run had one test failure: `codex-auth-product-proof.e2e.test.ts`, “returns bounded recovery after the explicitly selected profile is removed.” Credential removal succeeded, but config reload reported offline maintenance and the logout response included a reload-unconfirmed warning. The same case reproduces on main ancestor `48d4520c2ea53abc9086a4bd865b92f69bacc7d3` (verified source tree `dc50e125683f68e45ab0dbb7a9bfc4821db8b298`) in [focused baseline run 38488158969](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38488158969): one failed, one skipped, with the same reload warning at line 527. The source assertion and outcome are recorded in #171456 and its baseline transcript. Our duplicate baseline build was stopped before tests once that reusable evidence was found. An earlier native placement cancellation remains an investigated intermittent failure, not a proven fix.
- Final-head [CI run 38492997438](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38492997438) is complete: 46 checks passed; the only non-gate failure is the inherited mock-export ratchet below. All behavioral jobs, type checks, lint, source contracts, Madge, PostgreSQL conformance, and T1/dialect ratchets passed. The aggregate CI gate remains red for that inherited failure; it is not reported as green. Separate Knip scans on this head and exact main parent `a1ac97bcbe7b4e4b2985f4deccbb4856b2131581` produce the same sole production finding: `ui/src/components/web-awesome.ts: consumeDropdownKeyboardDismissal`. Full-tree and script export scans pass with zero entries on both. Ordinary PR CI does not run this scan. Earlier topology/Claw timeout and sidebar/Muse Knip failures are historical; they are not failures of the prior scoped head above.
- The current fast-ratchet failure is also reproduced on exact main parent `a1ac97bcbe7b4e4b2985f4deccbb4856b2131581`: `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base a1ac97bcbe7b4e4b2985f4deccbb4856b2131581` rejects the unannotated `./worker-turn-execution.js` mock at `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.lazy.test.ts:212`. This PR changes neither that test nor the UI export. The T1 and dialect ratchets pass. Landing uses the authorized inherited-only exception; neither failure is labeled green.
- Regression: first installation emits no absent-trigger drops; committed writes after reinstall update pending rows, and rolled-back writes do not leak pending rows.
- Published-driver × candidate update cell passed: published 2026.10.3 → candidate, 251,713 ms, phase `finished`, readiness HTTP 200, running version and durable/incognito after-update checks verified. This was required for the original broader scope. The remaining TEMP-only change adds no update/admission/lifecycle behavior.
- No schema/version change, new owner, cache, dependency, public SDK change, or ratchet-baseline edit. Touched-area T1 remains **0 → 0**.

Release-note context: reduce first-connection transcript-index setup SQL by omitting trigger drops already known to be unnecessary.

prs.title: feat(sdk): complete awaited SQLite compatibility migration paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin authors cannot complete the migration away from synchronous SQLite-backed SDK APIs while exact historical transcript-key lookup and TTS hint preparation lack public awaited replacements, and several legacy paths lack actionable migration diagnostics.

## User Impact

Adds `resolveTranscriptSessionKeyBySessionIdAsync`, `buildTtsSystemPromptHintAsync`, and public `prepareTtsPreferences` / `PreparedTtsPreferences`. Existing exports, synchronous results, prepared TTS overloads, and older-host adapters remain supported. No API is removed, no removal date is set, and no schema, retention, or update behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The historical resolver reuses the existing worker owner and retains exact historical session-window lookup after the current session changes. Current-entry lookup is not equivalent. Regression coverage exercises embedded-history ownership rejection and refreshed QA session metadata. Main independently landed their awaited readers during this PR; integration retains those current implementations, including the QA cross-process latest-read contract. TTS preparation retains explicit configuration/environment precedence and observes in-process path changes on the next preparation.

The remaining changes complete deprecation annotations, once-per-plugin-and-capability-family process warnings, migration examples, and qualified compatibility records. Affected families use an undated ordinary-stable deprecation gate. The shipped-surface evaluator is unchanged; a regression confirms an undated gate never authorizes removal. Stable publication, an announced window, reader/upgrade evidence, and explicit removal approval are still required.

### Deliberately retained consumers and decisions

- ClickClack binding/revocation checks, Codex binding lookup, Discord voice tool authority, and Discord/Telegram final command authorization still require current owner authority. An awaited snapshot is not a replacement until the owner publishes all required facts.
- Session-share's final synchronous listing protects against disclosure after sharing revocation; its existing async reader only asserts database identity, not current sharing rows.
- Reef legacy stores/cursor fallback, FaceTime's atomic fallback, Discord/Telegram synchronous persistence, and Matrix synchronous adapters preserve released older-host contracts. Removing them requires an explicit supported-host cutoff.
- Doctor/CLI one-shots remain exceptions. Hermes migration preview uses `database-path#profileId`, including new profiles: [`buildAuthItems`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f38650adbfaabe4237b3f88b87a6013dfa1b60da/extensions/migrate-hermes/auth.ts#L313-L337) selects the source profile ID when no existing profile matches and passes it to `authProfileTarget`. Keep auth display-path capability: profile/account metadata does not provide equivalent output. Public awaited parity or an approved locator redesign is a follow-up; this PR does not change it.
- Prepared reply-authority projections and final authority assertions also serve supported paths, so they remain silent. Actual legacy preparation/injection branches emit warnings. No authority checks were removed.

### SQL and size

| Metric | Before → after |
| --- | --- |
| Physical T1 sites retired | 0 (native compatibility implementations retained) |
| Final-head T1 inventory (`0426727d`) | 286 → 286 live calls; 12 → 12 deprecated compatibility calls (delta 0) |
| Warmed statements, requests, MAIN | Not measured; this is compatibility preparation, with no performance claim |
| SQL dialect changed-file groups | Mechanical 0 → 0; design 0 → 0; engine-maintenance 4 → 4 |
| Removal dates added | 0 |

The lane explicitly excludes the SQL harness. Source size: 130 files, +1,507 / −428 lines (net +1,079); most breadth is annotations and migration diagnostics.

## Evidence

Changed-file formatting, basic lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings; the second and final review covered the initial CI repairs and found no P0/P1 issues. Main integration retained newer owner APIs; conflicting edits were deprecation text, equivalent awaited-reader naming, and QA read consistency. Changed-file lint and formatting passed after resolution. A second main integration reconciled only compatibility-policy documentation; both sides now retain the undated stable-release gate and legacy-gate migration guidance. PR CI owns runtime tests, compatibility gates, docs checks, types, Knip, Madge, and database/dialect ratchets. The SDK declaration diff was generated separately because PR CI skips that report: 155 typed entrypoints, zero removed entrypoints or exports, one directly added typed export, four compatible signature changes, and 192 reachable-declaration changes. The two tool-factory signatures replace an inline `Omit` with an identical named alias; the transcript resolver derives the identical historical parameter type; the TTS path resolver retains the old optional overload and adds a prepared overload. TTS hint declarations retain the old call form and add prepared/async forms. `tts-runtime` is a runtime-only package entrypoint outside the typed report; its public preparation/type/async exports were checked directly. Report pins: `e80558a4da0f` → `c7008f770a4f`, digest `43fb0ea8`. Subsequent lane edits are test-only; integrations retain these public signatures and the new awaited implementations.

New or extended regressions cover historical lookup after reset without host SQL, TTS preference preparation and write visibility, retained synchronous signatures and warnings, embedded-history ownership rejection, refreshed QA metadata, legacy channel/approval/provider diagnostics, and rejection of undated removal authorization. No local broad suite was run. The published-driver update cell is not applicable.

CI repair notes: the first run exposed a redundant required-provider callback check, an overly narrow test callback signature, a missing wrapper inventory entry, and an outdated empty-stderr expectation. The SDK deprecation tally now accounts for the ten explicitly requested annotations; export/callable limits, shipped-name protection, and removal authorization remain unchanged. Focused provisioning, inventory, proxy-lifecycle, and surface-budget regressions pass.

Remaining P2 review findings are recorded in the [follow-up comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171443#issuecomment-6158470550), including Doctor, bundled approval/speech/realtime factories, current-authority warning routing, incognito freshness, and observer retries. They remain deferred under the requested two-round review cap; no P0/P1 finding remains.

The repair also updates two stale queue fixtures: Telegram now pauses the V2 store actually used by persistence, and the SQLite writer test waits for its first-start receipt under cleanup. A redundant intermediate assertion that assumed Promise-consumer microtask ordering is removed; final FIFO, durable-write, and timing assertions remain. Production queue code is unchanged. These are source-attributed test defects, not a claimed baseline failure or a request to bypass CI. Both focused Telegram cases and the SQLite case pass. Explicit test-only clock-phase signals keep the original numeric timing assertions deterministic across asynchronous admission.

The Codex side-question closure fixture now awaits its existing explicit startup callback and then joins the rejected run through cleanup. This removes fixed 1-second startup and 200-ms completion polls without changing the closure, AggregateError, or cause assertions. The exact case passes (1.54 seconds).

The integration of `ce651df5e7d7` retained main’s independently landed SQLite timing-fixture repair. The deprecation count combines the ten annotations here with one independently added on main. Conflict-file formatting, lint, and diff checks pass. prs.body:
## Architecture review — blocked

Current head `2d2e0d8d70299cef60dcd5da7449f2198596551d` is not ready to merge. Follow-up investigation found a blocking regression: the new admitted-envelope branch lacks the previous helper's user-role guard. When an admitted prepared user remains pending and the next append is an assistant message, the assistant is replaced by the existing user and its answer is not persisted. A real guarded-manager/SQLite probe reproduces the dropped assistant at this exact head.

The existing stale-view test establishes a defensive lower-boundary defect, not the reported Telegram release regression. An additional probe through `prepareEmbeddedAttemptSessionManager`, `prepareEmbeddedAttemptSessionBoundary`, and `submitEmbeddedAttemptPrompt` passes the ordinary fresh-photo vision case on unpatched base `50414196f1912053abee1ddcab595fca3c7e7889`. A controlled source rewrite by `before_message_write` does expose an upstream source-versus-admitted-message mismatch. The exact introducing change and differing fields in the reporter's 2026.10.1 path are not yet established.

The restoration should select canonical admitted input at replay preparation and retain the original role-safe runtime projection, rather than papering over that selection failure by copying an envelope in the persistence guard. The implementation and regression coverage below require rework; the earlier focused tests and green CI do not cover the newly demonstrated assistant-write failure.

---

Investigates #170091

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes vision replies failing for freshly received channel photos when ingress has persisted the user message before the runtime snapshot catches up.

## User Impact

Photo turns can reach the selected vision model without runtime image preparation conflicting with the accepted user message. No configuration changes, migrations, or user action are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session persistence guard now reuses the recorder-owned accepted envelope for a keyed replay and preserves its original write-hook decision. Inline images and their alignment metadata remain on the live runtime message for provider input; they do not replace the already-admitted transcript bytes. Strict transcript replay comparison is unchanged.

## Evidence

- On base `50414196f191`, the real guarded-session regression fails before provider dispatch with vision input while its text-only control passes. The fix passes all three cases, including a non-idempotent admission hook: one provider user, the live image, one durable user with unchanged bytes, and one hook invocation.
- **51 focused tests passed** across the new media-admission test, guard/transcript-event tests, and durable prompt-projection tests (157.38s combined wall time).
- New regression file: **3 tests passed**, 55.97s standalone wall time / 8.78s test execution. Hosted CI timing is pending.
- Production core typecheck, the agents-root test typecheck, touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, and the completed changed-file ratchets passed.
- Independent Codex AutoReview through P2: scoped-clean, no findings.

**Inherited validation failure:** `check:changed` stops at TS2322 in [`main-session-restart-recovery-admission.test.ts:705`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/50414196f1912053abee1ddcab595fca3c7e7889/src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-admission.test.ts#L705): `{ title: string }` is not a valid `Partial<InternalSessionEntry>`. Restoring all three changed paths to the exact base reproduces the same failure with the native agents-sessions typecheck. Subsequent aggregate check stages were not run; touched-file lint and the new test's type graph were checked separately. No test was skipped or weakened.

The regression exercises the shared channel-admission/guarded-runtime boundary with isolated SQLite state and synthetic photo data. It is not a live Telegram API test.

prs.title: chore(cron): cover destination-owned delivery boundaries
prs.body:
Related: #166746. Aligns with merged #168996.

## What Problem This Solves

The earlier version of this PR added a creator-side result copy that conflicts with native destination-owned cron results.

## User Impact

No production behavior or public contract change relative to the existing base `76edfee2d220`. Confirmed delivery belongs to the destination; creator-generation authorization remains separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current candidate removes all eight PR-only production modifications, including creator mirroring/wake events and the routing override. It keeps two regression test files covering destination-only results, destination media policy, and durable route revocation. The queue case now withdraws the route after observing persisted admission and verifies permanent rejection, released custody, and no recovery resend.

## Evidence

Current source head: `c1714fef494254ac0afa927eb1ee0a3718cb0f82`. Final diff against `76edfee2d220`: two test files, +461/-46; no production diff.

**Completion-signal review repair:** The Gateway listener is registered before the cron requests and buffers finished events by exact job/run identity, including events arriving before the cron.run response. Each cron wait uses the existing test abort signal, then reads settled cron.runs, traces and transcripts directly. This removes the new independent 15-second cron deadlines without extending the test budget or weakening result assertions.

This preserves #162945's produced-state synchronization intent: native finalization persists history and awaits delivery/result commit and continuation cleanup before emitting the matching finished event. Configured monitor completion also awaits heartbeat settlement. The inherited explicit-wake polling is unchanged because its heartbeat event has no run identity and precedes final queue cleanup; it is not a substitute completion signal for those assertions.

Exact-head [CI 38491899478](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38491899478) is successful: 21 jobs passed, 30 skipped, zero failures, including selected static checks and the aggregate gate. The [changed-test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38491899478/job/115619175687) completed all four planned invocations with 41 passing tests: config 18, SQLite queue 12, plugin loader 10, Gateway 1. The Gateway scenario took 53.986s (71.82s wrapper); queue suite 52.75s Vitest (54.39s wrapper).

Formatting and git diff --check pass. Independent source review of the final incremental diff found no P0-P2 findings. The local Gateway attempt hit its external 360-second limit (360.07s, exit 124) without a scenario result after expensive compiler/Gateway startup; this is not a runtime pass or a demonstrated assertion failure. Native type-aware lint refused linked TypeScript declarations outside the checkout; no guard was bypassed. The prepared local dependency view still uses fs-safe 0.26.3 instead of locked 0.26.2 and skips the unavailable A2UI build. These local limits are not frozen-install qualification.

**Historical evidence, not transferred to this head:** Prior `90655d415213` passed [CI 38487000557](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38487000557), with 21 successful jobs, 30 skips and 41 passing selected tests across four invocations (including 12 SQLite queue tests and the Gateway scenario). That pass did not resolve the subsequently reviewed polling reliability defect. The earlier `2393c750b151` CI failure exposed the removed live run alias; the retained-history helper correction uses native cron.history and remains in this revision. Earlier local timeout/dependency failures and the separate CLI-review authentication failure remain historical limitations.

The scenario retains one canonical destination result, no extra creator copy/event, allowed/denied destination media, retained execution transcripts and configured monitor routing. The separate real SQLite queue case retains post-admission route withdrawal, permanent rejection, released custody and no send/recovery replay. Mock channel/source-harness coverage is not live-provider/channel or original downstream-consumer proof. No merge, release adoption or carry retirement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Historical PR description and earlier readiness correction (superseded)</summary>

## Current Readiness

Update, October 13: the proposal and proof preserved below are historical, not current readiness.

At `2ca657dde20553339cb5b4e6915cfadede435431`, [CI 38350073218](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38350073218) fails the Gateway routing scenario and aggregate gate. [Revision 17](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165802#issuecomment-6003005071) identifies the competing creator-side mirror and the test's destination-exclusion expectation. The hosted log confirms the assertion fails because the resolved destination contains its canonical automation result.

Merged [#168996](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168996) deliberately assigns confirmed results to the destination and removes creator-awareness copies. The [pinned native contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4e26988b09017745426eeef313154237f8492020/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md) and dispatch source retain that ownership. Source-generation custody for authorization/recovery and destination media policy remain important; they do not require a second creator result.

This needs reconciliation with the existing owner, not acceptance on the old green head or an unchanged CI retry. The revised Gateway scenario should prove one destination result, no additional creator-awareness copy, and preserved media/queued-route protections. [#166746](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/166746) remains the canonical route. This source/log review does not establish complete original-consumer equivalence or new runtime proof; no source or merge action was taken here.

<details>
<summary>Historical October 7 proposal and proof, not current readiness</summary>

## What Problem This Solves

An implicit `last` cron delivery can recover its route from one exact canonical session, then independently choose another session when recording post-send conversation state. The transport send succeeds, but delivery awareness and the mirror can be attributed to the wrong conversation.

## How This Solves It

- attach provenance only for an unchanged implicit `last` route owned by the same canonical agent session
- use that proven source for transcript and delivery-awareness attribution
- independently retain the resolved destination as outbound policy context, including group media-read restrictions
- preserve explicit overrides, reroutes, custom-session priority, malformed or foreign-agent fallback, and ordinary native jobs

## Evidence

- prior secretless Testbox workflow: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37400241251

prs.title: feat(notifications): add opt-in answer and question previews
prs.body:
Closes #170854
Related: #162120, #144862, #143946.

## What Problem This Solves

People following background OpenClaw conversations must open the Control UI to see the content behind every generic completion or question notification.

## User Impact

Users can separately opt into final-answer excerpts and simple-question previews under **Detailed** notification settings. Both controls default to off. Existing Detailed account and browser preferences stay labels-only until explicit consent. Eligible questions display the exact prompt and choices; selecting the notification opens the authenticated question route.

Preview text can contain sensitive information and remain visible on lock screens or in browser/OS notification centers. Turning previews off affects future sends and cannot recall delivered notifications. Credential redaction is best effort.

**Owner decision remains open:** this proposes both answer and simple-question disclosure with independent consent. Notification owners must accept each privacy tradeoff, and the security-sensitive-change guard requires maintainer approval for the latest head before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consent belongs to the account or device layer selecting Detailed. Explicit device overrides cannot silently acquire account consent, and lowering detail clears consent at that layer.

Previews use the exact completed answer or canonical pending question. Original source identity and current recipient authority are checked before the encrypted send. Missing, retired, incognito or uncertified sources stay generic. Complex or secret questions, redaction-changing choices, and oversized envelopes also fall back to generic text. The payload-size check includes the displayed choices and preserves complete routing and metadata.

The live answer producer retains the completed projected text through transcript persistence using private publication metadata, so retiring the display tail does not remove the notification excerpt. That text is not added to the WebSocket payload.

The optional versioned question snapshot is display context, not permission to answer. The service worker retains authenticated click-through without reply actions. This feature adds no service, schema migration or protocol-version bump.

## Evidence

**Candidate:** `20a5e0a6932d24b776e796e93ff244e6b39e2b4e`, rebased onto upstream `main` at `46053391a1ad842d290563c38ca17b6aeb1d1a46`. Both independent preview opt-ins remain. Rebase conflicts preserve upstream question-access tests and use upstream's canonical session-sharing type; the redundant type file is removed. The content-test fixture now supplies the session-read preparation method added upstream. Browser proof remains pinned to its original tested revisions; current-base automated validation is listed below.

### Real-browser delivery and native click-through

An actual built Gateway and Control UI ran with synthetic isolated state. Chromium 153.0.8010.12 used a fresh temporary profile, normal dashboard/device pairing, and the shipped settings/subscription UI. Detailed initially left both preview consents off; each control was enabled separately and the preference response confirmed version 1 for each. The served UI bundle matched the tested build byte-for-byte.

A deterministic local OpenAI Responses fixture supplied the answer. Gateway HTTP/WebSocket ingress, browser push delivery, service-worker handling and notification creation were real, without transport interception or synthetic click events. The question was created through authenticated `question.request` and its production owner.

Both notification types were delivered on `fdebc827916`; answer delivery and native click-through were repeated on rebuilt `b31bb273b9e`. The subsequent review cleanups were test-only. This rebase incorporates newer upstream code; native-browser captures were not repeated, while both encrypted-delivery paths and notification UI tests passed on the rebased candidate. Browser notification readback:

Native desktop screenshots were inspected locally; only sanitized browser viewport captures are published. - **Rebase validation on `20a5e0a6932d24b776e796e93ff244e6b39e2b4e`:** 154 distinct focused cases pass across ten files: content projection and consent, answer authority, real encrypted delivery, question-session access, preference worker/upgrade compatibility, settings, and service-worker routing. prs.title: fix(gateway): keep local access when tailnet denies Serve
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway configured for Tailscale Serve exits when the tailnet reports that Serve is not enabled, preventing authenticated local access too.

## User Impact

The authenticated Gateway remains available on loopback after the confirmed Serve denial, with a warning that remote access is unavailable. Configuration and authentication stay unchanged. Restore the intended tailnet Serve policy and restart the Gateway to restore remote access. Funnel, cancellation, unknown errors, and failed cleanup remain fatal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify the complete known denial at the Tailscale command owner, including commands that exit successfully without publishing a route and commands that wait for enablement until the existing startup deadline. Local continuation requires successful worker retirement and a fresh cancellation check. Preserve both original and cleanup failures when retirement fails.

The supported dependency prints the feature text and enablement URL independently, and can wait for feature enablement: [Tailscale feature admission](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/blob/v1.102.3/cmd/tailscale/cli/serve_legacy.go#L746). Additional diagnostics do not qualify for recovery.

## Evidence

- Real route-claim/exposure boundary regressions reproduced the fatal denial before the fix; final focused owner suites pass: 48 tests, 54.34 seconds with `--maxWorkers=1` (31 command-owner tests and 17 exposure tests). Existing cold worker compilation dominates wall time; added cases use the existing process fixture and fake deadline clock.
- Numeric success/failure, waiting denial after retirement, independently printed enablement URL, and local warning pass. Funnel, arbitrary null exit, cancellation, additional diagnostics, and failed retirement retain fatal behavior and causes.
- Reused unchanged admission/startup proof separately: 30 loopback/authentication admission cases and one actual startup-cancellation case passed in the earlier 71-case batch (80.84 seconds).
- Changed-file lint, core and infra-test types, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and fresh full-owner independent review pass. `pnpm build` passes (47m10.2s, including cold declaration generation) on exact commit `0e8cb1d2ce27a1607d4cb267937f10fe12f09fdc`. Exact-head [CI run38491653256](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38491653256) and `openclaw/ci-gate` pass (836 seconds overall CI wall time; focused test timing above is separate). Requested ClawSweeper review of the same commit reports zero findings and no before-merge requirements.
- No live tailnet configuration or Gateway was modified; command outcomes are synthetic external-worker responses through the production owner. Local broad checks also identified an unchanged, inherited max-lines suppression in `doctor-database-port.ts`; the independent baseline repair is tracked in #171461.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep async metadata database opens off main thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first agent turn opened a native agent database on the Gateway thread solely to provide identity and publication hooks to async session metadata. The metadata SQL already ran in a worker, but that extra open caused 27 main-thread admission, lease, and connection-setup statements in the prior measured workload.

## User Impact

Async model/thinking/custom metadata and compaction persistence use the existing database worker executor. Transcript publication, durable appends, and released synchronous SessionManager APIs keep their contracts. No schema, configuration, or SDK surface change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The executor already publishes physical database identity. Retain that executor through each queued operation and use its identity to key the existing transcript commit-receipt hooks; do not acquire an additional native handle. Async compaction uses the same boundary. Memory sessions keep their existing owner.

Removed checks and superseded paths:

- Native `isTransaction` rejection: async callers no longer receive a native connection, and each worker command owns its transaction; no borrowed native transaction is supported on this path.
- Incognito native fallbacks: memory sessions already route through their memory owner; a missing or retired owner remains an error rather than reopening SQLite.
- Host identity read and optional publication branch: the worker's admitted identity supplies publication keying; publication remains mandatory for the durable worker path.

## Evidence

Local changed-file oxfmt, oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed. Both Codex autoreview rounds passed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Initial CI exposed a retained-rewrite lifetime regression: a prepared rewrite retained an assertion tied to an already-released database borrow. The correction preserves transcript authority while the commit acquires its own worker borrow. The five initially failing publication/compaction cases pass in focused local reruns; all affected test shards, lint, source contracts, production types, and database ratchets passed on the corrected implementation, and refreshed-head behavioral tests, all production/test types, lint, source contracts, and architecture checks are green after a clean main merge. The new public-API regression checks persisted metadata, commit-receipt publication, zero host SQL/native handle, actual worker termination, and successful reopen/append. Registered in the forked database-worker-core lane. Existing metadata admission, maintenance, memory, transcript authority, and compaction tests cover sibling paths.

Static direct-call T1 count in the touched async files is 0 → 0: the old native open was transitive and its individual admission/lock primitives were exempt. Runtime counts below are the relevant boundary proof. Shared inventory files are unchanged. Final-head CI reports global T1 302 → 302, deprecated-only T1 13 → 13, and all three changed-file dialect categories 0 → 0.

Knip initially found the retired sidebar exports on the older base; merging the existing main-branch cleanup fixed them. All three final-head Knip export scans pass with zero findings. The baseline-ratchet aggregate has one inherited mock-export error at `test/helpers/openclaw-test-process.test.ts:5` for `../../src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.js`; the exact same rule/file/message fails on [main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38487855087/job/115606191159), and this PR changes neither file. T1, dialect, and the other ratchets pass. This uses the campaign-approved inherited-failure exception, recorded in the red-main inbox. Main has since fixed the mock with the one-line isolation comment in `e7a07c5aee577be3a2425ec4d88cad17813b7505`; that fix changes no runtime behavior. The [published-driver × candidate update cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38488312419/job/115619488010) passed on reviewed head `a90c843da5fc9d40493360b81f15f8637c977390`. Package integrity, npm install acceptance, and the final Package Acceptance verifier also passed. The single shared-harness pair ran after merge through the local CPU gate: baseline `dffed430c51e903567a81e381bd0341ba95a47df`, candidate/merge `7dfb334aa67a34b9e0ec4cbd8c022e8ea1dffec7`. Both used identical harness v2.1.0 hashes; the private copy changed only the fixture-output prefix to external storage. All 13 turns, cron, compaction, and shutdown completed; all ten warmed turns have causal coverage. No latency claim: pre-run load was 22.3 and 31.5 on 32 cores.

| Metric | Merge parent | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First-turn causal MAIN statements | 27 | 0 |
| First-turn causal statements / requests | 308 / 69 | 247 / 67 |
| Warmed causal statements, median [min–max] | 102 [102–108] | 102 [102–142] |
| Warmed causal requests, median [min–max] | 34 [34–37] | 34 [34–41] |
| Warmed MAIN statements | 0 | 0 |
| Warmed causal statements / requests, mean | 102.6 / 34.3 | 106.0 / 34.7 |
| Legacy warmed-window statements, median [min–max] | 106.5 [106–113] | 107 [106–146] |
| Background statements per minute in warm windows | 202.7 | 208.3 |
| Whole-workload statements / requests | 4,547 / 942 | 4,531 / 951 |

### Measurement attribution

The first-turn native open disappears entirely: quarantine schema/decision 2, lease acquisition 9, connection/WAL setup 9, native lease record 6, and auto-checkpoint setup 1. Causal MAIN is zero on every candidate turn. The first-turn window still contains 13 unrelated background lease-expiry reads on MAIN on both sides; boot admission and shutdown are separate from the turn claim.

Metadata/append requests have identical complete SQL costs on both sides: first turn 42 statements / 4 requests; each warm turn 18 / 2; compaction 18 / 1; whole workload 466 / 47. Counts include every statement in those requests, not only statements whose stack names metadata.

The warm increase is entirely in turn 1. An identical 31-statement / 1-request session-actor schema admission moves from the first turn to the first warmed turn (matched SQL and worker-stack multisets). An actor hydration moves into an explicit request, without increasing aggregate hydration SQL. The candidate also performs two extra exact-entry reads in the shared retained-facts owner; the baseline instead has two extra first-turn read-only quarantine statements. First plus ten warmed turns therefore totals 1,334 → 1,307 statements (exactly −27 MAIN) and 412 → 414 requests. Warm turns 2–10 are identical at 102 statements / 34 requests. The second-session workload adds one ACP metadata SELECT, with unchanged request count.

Source tracing found both extra entry reads missed retained facts; cache identity and invalidation come from worker admission and write receipts, without a native-host-handle condition. One read serves ordinary session-sharing admission; the other higher-level caller is truncated in the trace. The extra shared reads remain counted: this one pair cannot establish whether their cache/scheduling difference is caused indirectly by the removed open. Whole-workload requests rise by 9 (+0.96%), comprising +2 foreground and +7 background requests; metadata requests do not rise. Warm medians and MAIN remain unchanged. The candidate has three failed background audit-pruning `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` attempts during shutdown, reported separately from successful-statement totals; the workload exits successfully. This result supports removing the first-turn host open, not a warmed-throughput or latency claim.

Production LOC: +82 / −118 (net −36); regression +109; documentation +7; test-lane registration +1.

prs.title: refactor(sessions): engine-owned transcript payload compression for PostgreSQL
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL cannot execute SQLite's `openclaw_transcript_payload_decode` function. The first version of this PR removed that decoder and rewrote 51 callers to expand payloads in JavaScript and feed their text back into SQL projections. That version is superseded: it added six main-thread database calls (T1 302 → 308), unnecessary re-projection, and hydration statements (84 → 116).

## Design and impact

Compression is owned by the storage engine. SQLite retains its existing zstd storage, decoder registration, and SQL payload projection. PostgreSQL writes canonical plain text to `event_json`, always leaves `event_zstd` NULL, and relies on native TOAST compression. Reusable payloads prepared on SQLite cannot copy compressed bytes into a PostgreSQL writer. Navigation/predicate fields retain the existing preparation rules.

Hydration uses one engine-owned read snapshot and one keyset loop: 256 rows per SQLite page, 16 per PostgreSQL page. Byte slicing stays in SQL and uses each engine's byte operations. Frames, ACKs, cancellation, and exact transcript bytes remain unchanged. The 51 payload callers keep their existing projections. The storage documentation records that a future SQLite-to-PostgreSQL agent port must decompress into `event_json`.

The participant-publication prerequisite is already on main as `4aa62334122e`; the landing rebase dropped its duplicate commit. The six-file payload patch is unchanged (`git range-diff` confirms equivalence). The rebase includes #170280, and `pnpm db:postgres:gen` followed by `pnpm db:postgres:check` passed without generated-file changes.

## Evidence

Measured against main `e7a07c5aee577be3a2425ec4d88cad17813b7505` using the real hydration worker and observed native database handles:

| SQLite operation | Main | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000-event hydration | 84 statements | 87 statements |
| Warm full-transcript read | 4 statements | 4 statements |
| Warm compressed-event read | 1 statement | 1 statement |

The three extra hydration statements replace one iterator with four keyset pages. Both versions produced identical bytes, 1,080 frames, and 10 ACKs. The owner regression covers page-boundary snapshot consistency, compressed and multibyte payloads, empty frames, cancellation, host errors, and negative sequence fences.

PostgreSQL 17.11 proof uses the real production bridge: direct preparation, PostgreSQL-prepared reuse, and SQLite-compressed prepared reuse each store the exact 200,075 UTF-8 bytes as text with `event_zstd = NULL`. Reading through `transcriptEventJsonSql` matches exactly. Hydration page and continuation-slice queries pass PREPARE/EXPLAIN and return exact slices under the engine read snapshot.

The source audit covers all 51 direct payload references plus the QA member-call reference. Current-source sampling covers 89 cases (84 distinct SQL statements): 65 pass PREPARE/EXPLAIN; 24 fail on surrounding dialect features listed below. None fails on the payload expression, decoder registration, zstd storage, or byte slicing. The disposable cluster was stopped and removed.

- Payload, hydration, and transcript-store owner tests: 45 passed, `--maxWorkers=1`.
- Gateway `chat.message.get`: all 4 selected tests passed, `--maxWorkers=1`.
- Managed-image branch retention: 3 passed, `--maxWorkers=1`.
- Wrapper inventory/eager-import closure: 17 passed, `--maxWorkers=1`.
- Participant canonical-repair regression: 2 passed, `--maxWorkers=1`.
- Hydration regression test bodies total 0.955s; the three-file owner wrapper takes 178.26s including preparation. CI timing is pending.
- Core and touched-test typechecks, touched-file formatting/lint, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Database-worker ratchet: T1 302 → 302; dialect ratchet: mechanical 1 → 1, design 13 → 13. Assertion-safety, max-lines, Kysely, and wrapper-shadowing guards pass against `origin/main`; no baseline increases or new non-null assertions.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Net production growth: 78 lines; hydration regression: 205 lines; documentation: 5 lines.

Two test wrappers first completed their assertions but rejected the run because the prerequisite source correction was made during compilation; both were rerun successfully on frozen source. The PostgreSQL fixture first needed its required foreign-key parents; its final run passed.

## Remaining PostgreSQL dialect work (not this PR)

The payload/storage contract is portable; whole caller statements can still depend on other SQLite features. These are deliberately left to PR4 (JSON functions) or follow-up dialect work. prs.title: fix(talk): voice consults loop on confirmations, start duplicate runs and block read-only commands
prs.body:
Related: #163122, #130094

AI-assisted (Claude Code and Codex).

Status: the confirmation, classifier and held-confirm changes are voice-tested on a phone, and the confirmed-retry changes on a desktop call. The changes that answer review (join, browser cancel of shared runs, busy refusal, the 20 s hold bound and its recovery, the newest read-only rules) are shown on a running Gateway in a real Talk relay session; see Live transport proof.

Busy refusal (review): this closes a defect, it is not a product choice. On `main` a voice consult sent to a busy chat is queued, and the queued follow-up starts under a new run id that has no voice binding, so the spoken-confirmation gate does not apply to it. A consult that cannot keep its voice binding must not start; the guard that already refuses goal operations on a busy session now refuses it too, and the caller asks again. The caller-visible effect (refused, not queued) is listed under User Impact for a maintainer to confirm.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a voice question that needs the agent can take about a minute, end in a tool error, or end the call, when the agent runs an ordinary read-only shell command, when the realtime model repeats its tool call or calls confirm before the user has answered, or when a CLI-backed chat loses the pending spoken confirmation.

## User Impact

User impact: voice consults that only read files answer without a confirmation prompt, a repeated tool call no longer starts a second run, a confirmation prompt is asked once and then waits for the user's answer, and a spoken "yes" resumes the pending action in CLI-backed chats.

- Read-only pipelines such as `find … -size 0`, `find … -empty`, `sort | uniq -c`, `cut`, `tr`, `file` and a single `sed` substitution to stdout no longer ask for a spoken yes. Options that write a file or run a program still do.
- **Behavior change:** a consult call that repeats the request of the consult already in flight for the same voice session (up to 120 s) joins that run. Only an exact repeat matches (question, context and spoken style, byte for byte); a different question is never answered by the running consult.
- **Fix with a visible effect:** a voice consult sent while the chat still has active or queued work is refused with a speakable "still working" message. Before, it was queued and later ran under a new run id with no voice binding, outside the spoken-confirmation gate. This includes a different question asked while a consult runs. The caller has to ask again when the earlier work is done.
- **Behavior change:** an app-routed confirm call sent before the user has answered is held for at most 20 s, then answered with a retryable error. The confirmation stays pending, so a later "yes" authorizes the next call.
- After a spoken "yes" the agent re-runs the exact command that was blocked, and it no longer asks for permission a second time in its own words.
- The spoken confirmation question now names the blocked action ("About to run: … Say yes to go ahead or no to cancel") when the call carries a title or a command. Other tools keep the generic question.

No configuration or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

One blocked command used to start a chain: the gate replaced the consult answer with a yes/no prompt, the realtime model called the consult tool again before the user had spoken, the Gateway rejected that call at once, and the model retried. The first five changes each remove one link; the next three answer review of the join; the last seven came from later live calls and the second review.

- **Confirmations survive the run.** The veto reply reaches the voice model even when a CLI-backed run publishes its final text after its execution binding is gone. A retry that omits the confirmation id is authorized only from that call's own saved affirmative speech.
- **Repeat calls join.** A consult call that repeats the running request joins the run in flight instead of sending another chat message into the busy session. A confirmed retry always starts its own run.
- **Read-only classifier.** The shell classifier recognizes `sort`, `uniq`, `file`, `cut`, `tr`, `basename`, `dirname`, a single `sed` substitution to stdout, and a backslash inside single quotes. Interpreters, heredocs, redirection, `sort -o`, `uniq` with an output file, `file -C`/`-z`/`-Z`/`-S` and `sed` `w`/`e` stay unclassified.
- **`find` metadata tests.** `find` with tests that only read metadata (`-size`, `-empty`, `-mtime`, `-newer`, `-perm` and similar, with `-o`/`-a`/`-not`) is read-only. `-exec`, `-delete`, `-fprint`, `-fls` and any unknown primary stay unclassified.
- **Early confirm calls wait.** An app-routed consult call sent through the Gateway relay now waits on the relay's existing confirmation readiness, the same owner the native relay path uses, instead of being rejected before the user has answered. The veto text tells the model to ask the question once and stop.

- **Only a matching request joins.** The first version joined every call in the voice session, so a different question received the earlier answer. Now the request (question, context, spoken style) must match. A different question gets its own start.
- **Busy chat (gate bypass closed).** That own start would be queued behind the running consult, and a queued follow-up gets a new run id with no voice binding, so the confirmation gate would not apply to it. Queueing is therefore not a safe option for a voice consult. The existing exclusive-admission guard now covers voice consults and refuses them while the session has active or queued work.
- **Shared-run cancellation.** A joined repeat now attaches its provider call to the relay run. Cancelling one of the calls aborts the run only when no other call is attached, and a repeat that was cancelled before it joined is refused without touching the run.

- **Confirmed retries carry the blocked arguments.** The confirmed retry used to hand the agent only an id, so it rebuilt the command from memory and could build a different one, which the gate then blocked again. The retry now carries the exact blocked arguments (JSON, up to 16 KB, kept only when their fingerprint matches the pending action).
- **The agent leaves confirmation to the gate.** A consult message now tells the agent to run the command and not ask for permission itself, because the system asks by voice. Before, the caller could be asked twice: once by the agent, once by the gate.
- **Delimited spoken question.** The veto text puts the instructions first and the question last, as one quoted string, so the voice model does not read instructions aloud.
- **The question names the action.** The spoken question used to say only "one pending action has not run", so the user could not tell what a "yes" would approve. It now reads the call's own `title`, or else its `command`, with quotes, backslashes and control characters removed and at most 120 characters. A label that the shared redactor would change (a token, password or API key in the command) is never spoken; the generic question is used instead. The label is for speech only: the grant stays bound to the fingerprint of the exact blocked arguments.
- **Held confirm calls are bounded (review).** The hold now ends after 20 s, inside the iOS client's 30 s start deadline, with a retryable error. The challenge stays pending.
- **Exact-match join (review).** Matching no longer folds spacing or letter case: `README` and `readme` can name different files.
- **Browser cancel (review).** The Control UI relay client sends `chat.abort` for a cancelled call only when no other call is waiting on the same run id. A cancelled call now leaves the waiter count in the same tick, so two joined calls cancelled together abort the shared run once instead of each seeing the other and aborting nothing (second review; test seen red, then green).

The authorization check itself is unchanged: neither a confirmation id nor model-written text grants execution; only later affirmative user speech for the exact pending action does, once.

## Evidence

### Live voice tests (iOS app, xAI realtime voice, author's Gateway, October 3 and 4)

Times are from the Gateway log, measured from the recognized question.

| Build | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Confirmation change only | Directory count blocked by the gate, then a spoken "yes" | The count ran and was answered (reported by the tester on a physical iPhone). Not established: whether the model supplied the confirmation id or the Gateway recovered it. |
| Confirmation change only | File-count question (the count itself takes 0.3 s) | About 71 s, ended in a tool error. Log: two read-only commands blocked by the gate, two confirm calls rejected with no spoken yes, duplicate consult dispatches, queued recounts. |
| All three changes | Count question, Codex-backed chat | Consult 11.6 s, spoken, 18 s end to end. No block, no duplicate. |
| All three changes | File-type question, Codex-backed chat | Consult 25.1 s (about a dozen separate `find` counts, none blocked), spoken, 47 s end to end. |
| All three changes | Four consults, Claude CLI-backed chat | All spoken. Result at 6.6–15.0 s, playback finished at 21–26 s. One question produced two tool calls and one run. |

| All three changes (October 3) | "Which of the text files are empty?" | The agent ran `find … -size 0`, which was blocked. Ten confirm calls were rejected in 35 s with no speech in between, then the session ended in an error. The two changes below address this. |
| All five changes (October 4, first session) | "Which text files are empty?", asked twice | `find … -empty` ran with no gate block both times; results at 7.2 s and 3.8 s. The second was spoken. After the first, the session ended in an error 1.8 s after the result and nothing was spoken; see Not claimed. |
| All five changes (October 4, first session) | Delete a file | The gate blocked the delete once. One spoken prompt (audio finished about 10 s after the block), the user's "yes" 2 s later, one confirmed run, file deleted, result spoken. No rejected confirm call, no loop. |
| All five changes (October 4, second session) | Create a file, then delete it | Create ran without a prompt (file-write tool). Delete: one block, one spoken prompt, "yes", one confirmed run, file deleted, result spoken. No rejected confirm call. Seven consults in this session, all spoken, no session error. |
| All five changes (October 4, second session) | A second question asked while a consult was running (twice) | The voice model held the second question until the first result, then sent one combined consult. One duplicate call joined the running consult (two results 2 ms apart, one run). |

| Confirmed-retry changes (October 5, desktop Control UI call) | Create a file with `touch` | One block, one spoken prompt, "yes", one confirmed run, file created. This build had the three confirmed-retry changes (exact arguments, agent note, delimited question) and other local changes that are not in this PR. |

**Not spoken by a person:** exact-match join, shared-run cancellation, the 20 s hold bound and the cancel race. A person cannot force these on a voice call: in the second October 4 session the voice model held the second question until the first result and then sent one combined consult (observed twice). They are forced by script on a running Gateway instead; see Live transport proof (October 6).

The October 3 rows that say "all three changes" ran a build with the confirmation, join and classifier-filter changes. All spoken rows used the earlier join, which accepted any call in the session. The live builds did not include the two review hardenings (`file -z`/`-Z`/`-S` kept gated, join map pruned). They have automated coverage only.

### Confirmation without an id: final effect (isolated runtime, this head)

A standalone harness, not part of the diff, drives the real `talk.client.transcript` and `talk.client.toolCall` handlers, consult start, trusted chat admission and dispatch, and the production tool wrapper. Only the model step and the final tool body are replaced: the tool appends one line to a task-local file. Each case first shows the blocked action doing no I/O, then saves the user speech "yes" through the transcript RPC and calls the consult tool with no confirmation id.

| Case | Times the tool body ran | File effect |
|---|---:|---|
| Exact pending action, saved "yes", no id | 1 | The original action's line, once |
| Same speech, another voice session | 0 | No file |
| Changed action arguments | 0 | No file |
| Replay in the same run and in a fresh run | 1 in total | The single original line |
| Speech invalidated after grant validation, before the grant is bound | 0 | No file |

5 of 5 passed on this head. With the source reverted to `main` the first case fails (the approved action performs no I/O: expected 1, got 0); the harness then aborts, so the other four are not meaningful there.

```
{"scenario":"exact-once","recordedSpeech":"yes","transcriptRpcAck":true,"consultRpcAck":true,"omittedId":true,"enteredFinalIO":1,"finalFileRows":1}
{"scenario":"wrong-scope","recordedSpeech":"yes","transcriptRpcAck":true,"consultRpcAck":true,"omittedId":true,"enteredFinalIO":0,"finalFileRows":0}
{"scenario":"changed-action","recordedSpeech":"yes","transcriptRpcAck":true,"consultRpcAck":true,"omittedId":true,"enteredFinalIO":0,"finalFileRows":0}
{"scenario":"replay","recordedSpeech":"yes","transcriptRpcAck":true,"consultRpcAck":true,"omittedId":true,"enteredFinalIO":1,"finalFileRows":1}
{"scenario":"pre-binding-invalidation","recordedSpeech":"yes","transcriptRpcAck":true,"consultRpcAck":true,"omittedId":true,"enteredFinalIO":0,"finalFileRows":0}
```

Limits: no provider, audio or network; request authority is a test fixture. It shows the guard and the one-shot final-I/O contract on this route, not live voice.

Denial without saved approval is also covered by handler tests in the diff: with no utterance, with "no", and with an unrelated question, the retried action stays blocked and no grant is bound; after a valid "yes" a different action stays blocked.

### Automated (this branch)

- **This head.** `4089a225dfe` answers the third review: the sed chain rule no longer accepts an escaped delimiter or a delimiter inside a bracket expression (see "sed chain rule" below). `tool-mutation.test.ts`: 144 of 144.
- **Previous head.** `bf339e2bef5` answers the second review: the browser abort held for a repeat awaiting its acknowledgement is now keyed on the same parsed question, context and spoken style the Gateway joins on (a question alias or another field order no longer looks like a different request; new case seen red without the change), and the race tests wait on a signal from the request mock instead of polling. Earlier in this PR: `51ce5abbef1` is a one-line lint fix (RegExp#test). `3655432d0fe` fixes CI on the previous head: the rebase left floating promises in one test and the new cancellation tests had two type errors; test-only changes. Earlier in this PR: `b655cbe3feb` also accepts several `sed` substitutions joined by `;` (a live call asked for a spoken yes on a per-extension file count, verdict 0.65); each step must still be a plain substitution, so a trailing `w`, an `e` flag, an empty step or another command asks. Earlier in this PR: `a4f6f32a8dc` widens the read-only list after a live call asked for a spoken yes on `cd DIR && timeout 20 find . \( -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.md' \) | wc -l` and on `sleep 7; echo waited` (the Decision model scored them 0.69 and 0.07): `cd`, `sleep`, `echo`, `true`, `false`, a `;` separator, `timeout DURATION command` (the command decides) and find's escaped `\( \)` grouping. Every segment must still be read-only, so `cd DIR && rm f`, `sleep 5; touch f`, `timeout 5 rm f`, a redirect and `find \( … \) -delete` or `-exec` still ask; 124 tests in `tool-mutation.test.ts` pass. Earlier in this PR: `f939b63b8d0` holds a browser abort while a repeat of the same request is still awaiting its acknowledgement (review): the abort is dropped if the repeat joins the run, and sent if it starts another run or fails; three new cases, each seen red without the fix. Earlier in this PR: `39f2b4727ac` updates the existing Browser Talk test that sent a second consult during a running one: it now expects the busy refusal (and that the running consult is not cancelled). That file is not in the PR's changed-test lane, so CI had not run it. `5e7169f4065` keeps credentials out of the spoken label and removes real-timer waits from the cancellation tests; `2f8cb337627` fixed the assertion-safety ratchet; `a208d2d670a` adds the named-action question: `src/talk/client-voice-confirmation.test.ts` 52 passed (three new cases), `oxfmt --check` clean, core type check with no semantic errors. The figures that follow were measured one commit earlier. Rebased on `main` at `5f23299a3b3`. The eleven test files this PR touches (ten Gateway/Talk files and `ui/src/pages/chat/talk/consult.test.ts`): 537 passed. Test type checks (`gateway-other`, `ui-pages`), `check:assertion-safety` and `check:max-lines-ratchet` pass. `oxfmt --check` clean, core type check with no semantic errors.
- **Red, then green (measured on the first review head, before the six later changes).** Eight test files: 511 passed. With only the source files reverted to `main` and the tests kept, 27 of those tests failed and 484 passed; the failures were spread over all eight files. The join test named "whatever its spacing or letter case" has since become "matches only an exact repeat".

  <details><summary>The 27 tests that failed without the source changes</summary>

  - `tool-mutation`: treats read-only shell command as non-mutating: bash find . -maxdepth 1 -type f | sed 's/.*\.//' | sort | uniq -c
  - `tool-mutation`: treats read-only shell command as non-mutating: bash find . -maxdepth 1 -type f | sed -E 's|.*/||' | sort -rn | head -5
  - `tool-mutation`: treats read-only shell command as non-mutating: bash ls -1 | tr A-Z a-z | cut -d. -f2 | sort -u | wc -l
  - `tool-mutation`: treats read-only shell command as non-mutating: exec file --mime-type notes.md
  - `tool-mutation`: treats read-only shell command as non-mutating: exec find . -type f -mtime -1 -o -name '*.md' | wc -l
  - `tool-mutation`: treats read-only shell command as non-mutating: exec find /tmp/ws -maxdepth 1 -type f -empty
  - `tool-mutation`: treats read-only shell command as non-mutating: exec find /tmp/ws -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.txt' -size 0
  - `server-chat.agent-events`: projects the current voice challenge into Claude CLI's final chat result
  - `chat-send-work-admission`: allows an idle consult through admission
  - `chat-send-work-admission`: refuses a consult before it can queue behind existing admission work
  - `chat-send-work-admission`: refuses a consult before it can queue behind existing queue work
  - `chat-send-work-admission`: refuses a consult before it can queue behind existing run work
  - `agent-consult.join`: does not cache a failed start, and waiters share one retry
  - `agent-consult.join`: joins repeat calls to the in-flight consult instead of starting more
  - `agent-consult.join`: keeps a started different request joinable when the earlier run ended meanwhile
  - `agent-consult.join`: matches a repeat whatever its spacing or letter case, and nothing else
  - `agent-consult.join`: starts a different request on its own and keeps the live run for its repeats
  - `talk handlers index`: joins an identical repeat to the running relay consult and starts a different question on its own
  - `talk handlers index`: records a chat-backed CLI veto for the server-owned voice result
  - `talk handlers index`: resumes one exact CLI action after persisted spoken confirmation without a model-supplied id
  - `relay confirmation`: does not admit an early app confirmation after close
  - `relay confirmation`: does not admit an early app confirmation after no
  - `relay confirmation`: holds an early app-routed explicit confirmation consult until a durable spoken yes
  - `relay confirmation`: holds an early app-routed observed confirmation consult until a durable spoken yes
  - `relay index`: keeps a shared consult running until every attached provider call is cancelled
  - `relay index`: refuses a repeat call cancelled before it joined without aborting the shared run
  - `client-voice-confirmation`: returns one exact spoken question and forbids consulting again before the user answers

- **Still gated.** The classifier tests assert the refusals as well as the new allowances: `sort -o`/`--output`/`--compress-program`, `uniq` with an output operand, `file -C`/`--compile`/`-z`/`-Z`/`-S`, `sed` `w`, `e` and `-i`, `awk`, and `find -delete`/`-exec`/`-fls`/`-fprint` all stay classified as mutating.

// Live-proof helper: one admin operator connection to the running Gateway, with raw events.
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { GatewayClient } from "../src/gateway/client.js";

export type Frame = { event: string; payload?: unknown };
export const t0 = Date.now();
export const stamp = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(11, 23) + "Z";
export const log = (line: string) => console.log(`${stamp()} ${line}`);

export async function connect() {
  const listeners = new Set<(evt: Frame) => void>();
  let hello!: () => void;
  const ready = new Promise<void>((resolve) => (hello = resolve));
  const client = new GatewayClient({
    url: "ws://127.0.0.1:18789",
    clientName: "openclaw-tui",
    clientDisplayName: "pr-164749-live-proof",
    mode: "ui",
    scopes: ["operator.admin", "operator.read", "operator.write"],
    instanceId: randomUUID(),
    onHelloOk: (h) => {
      log(`connected: gateway ${h.server.version} protocol ${h.protocol}`);
      hello();
    },
    onConnectError: (e) => log(`connect error: ${e.message}`),
    onEvent: (evt) => listeners.forEach((l) => l(evt as Frame)),
  });
  client.start();
  await ready;
  return {
    // Every frame this client sends is printed: the proof is what went over the socket.
    async request<T = unknown>(method: string, params?: unknown): Promise<T> {
      const p = params as { callId?: string; runId?: string } | undefined;
      const tag = [p?.callId && `callId=${p.callId}`, p?.runId && `runId=${p.runId}`].filter(Boolean).join(" ");
      log(`→ ${method} ${tag}`);
      try {
        const res = await client.request<T>(method, params);
        const r = res as { runId?: string; aborted?: boolean; runIds?: string[] } | undefined;
        log(`← ${method} ${tag} ok${r?.runId ? ` runId=${r.runId}` : ""}${r?.aborted !== undefined ? ` aborted=${r.aborted}` : ""}`);
        return res;
      } catch (err) {
        log(`← ${method} ${tag} ERROR ${(err as Error).message}`);
        throw err;
      }
    },
    quiet: <T = unknown>(method: string, params?: unknown) => client.request<T>(method, params).catch(() => undefined as T),
    addEventListener(listener: (evt: Frame) => void) {
      listeners.add(listener);
      return () => listeners.delete(listener);
    },
    stop: () => client.stopAndWait().catch(() => {}),
  };
}
