```ts
await Promise.all([c1.done, c2.done]);
await sleep(3000);

scene("D. First call cancelled while the repeat still waits for its acknowledgement: abort is held, repeat joins, run survives");
const cmdD = "cd /tmp; sleep 12; echo scene-D-finished";
const d1 = call(ask(cmdD));
await sleep(3000);
const d2 = call(ask(cmdD)); // request is on the socket, acknowledgement not back yet
await sleep(0);
log(`  cancel ${d1.callId} (the ${d2.callId} acknowledgement is outstanding)`);
d1.abort.abort();
await Promise.all([d1.done, d2.done]);
await sleep(1500);

scene("E. Control: a command that writes still asks for a spoken yes");
const marker = `/tmp/proof-749-gate-${Date.now()}`;
const e1 = call(ask(`touch ${marker}`));
await e1.done;
log(`  marker file exists: ${existsSync(marker)}`);
await sleep(1500);

scene("H. The same call is repeated before the user answers: held, then answered with a retryable error inside 20 s");
const held = Date.now();
const h1 = call(ask(`touch ${marker}`));
await h1.done;
log(`  held for ${((Date.now() - held) / 1000).toFixed(1)} s; marker file exists: ${existsSync(marker)}`);

scene("F. The user says yes; the next repeat runs the approved command");
log(`  heard: ${JSON.stringify(await speak("/tmp/p749/audio/yes.pcm"))}`);
const f1 = call(ask(`touch ${marker}`));
await f1.done;
log(`  marker file exists: ${existsSync(marker)}`);
await client.request("talk.session.close", { sessionId: relaySessionId });
log(`\nsession ${sessionKey}`);
await client.stop();
process.exit(0);
```

</details>

### sed chain rule: bypass found in review, closed (head `4089a225dfe`)

The third review found that the chained-substitution rule (added in `b655cbe3feb`) treated an escaped delimiter as the end of a part. GNU sed reads it as text, so `echo x | sed 's/x/printf … #\/;s/e;#/ignored/p'` was classified read-only while sed saw an `e` flag and ran the replacement in a shell. Fixing it showed a second case of the same kind: BSD sed (macOS) keeps a delimiter inside a bracket expression as text, so `sed 's/[/]/;s|/w|b|'` was classified read-only while sed saw a `w` flag and wrote a file.

The rule now matches only where the two implementations agree on where each part ends: no escaped delimiter, no delimiter inside a bracket expression (a leading `^` and a leading `]` are handled; `[.x.]` and `[=x=]` are not matched), and a delimiter from `/ | , # @ ! %`. Anything else stays gated.

**Final effect, production gate with a real shell.** A standalone harness (not part of the diff) wraps a tool whose body runs the command in a real shell with the production before-tool-call hook, classifier and confirmation gate. The voice-session lookup is a fixture. `sed` is GNU sed 4.10 or the macOS sed, by `PATH`.

This head:

```
{"scenario":"escaped-delimiter-exec","sed":"GNU 4.10","command":"echo x | sed 's/x/touch PWNED #\\/;s/e;#/ignored/p'","askedForSpokenYes":true,"shellRan":0,"filesCreated":[]}
{"scenario":"bracket-delimiter-write","sed":"BSD (macOS)","command":"echo a/b | sed 's/[/]/;s|/w|PWNED|'","askedForSpokenYes":true,"shellRan":0,"filesCreated":[]}
{"scenario":"read-only-chain","sed":"GNU 4.10","command":"echo src/notes.txt | sed -E 's|.*/||; s|.*\\.||'","askedForSpokenYes":false,"shellRan":1,"filesCreated":[],"stdout":"txt\n"}
{"scenario":"read-only-chain","sed":"BSD (macOS)","command":"echo src/notes.txt | sed -E 's|.*/||; s|.*\\.||'","askedForSpokenYes":false,"shellRan":1,"filesCreated":[],"stdout":"txt\n"}
```

Same harness with `src/agents/tool-mutation.ts` from the previous head `bf339e2bef5`: no question was asked, the shell ran, and the file was created in both cases.

```
{"scenario":"escaped-delimiter-exec","sed":"GNU 4.10","command":"echo x | sed 's/x/touch PWNED #\\/;s/e;#/ignored/p'","askedForSpokenYes":false,"shellRan":1,"filesCreated":["PWNED"],"stdout":"\n"}
{"scenario":"bracket-delimiter-write","sed":"BSD (macOS)","command":"echo a/b | sed 's/[/]/;s|/w|PWNED|'","askedForSpokenYes":false,"shellRan":1,"filesCreated":["|PWNED|"],"stdout":"a;s|b\n"}
```

**Differential fuzz against real sed.** A script (not part of the diff) generates sed programs from an alphabet of the characters that matter (`s / | [ ] \ ^ ; w e g p . : # ,` and a few more) and from mutations of the known bad scripts. Each program the classifier calls read-only is run by a real sed in an empty directory. For BSD sed a leak is a file that appears. For GNU sed the run uses `--sandbox`, where sed refuses any program that contains an `e`, `r` or `w`, so a leak is that refusal.

| sed | Rule | Unique programs | Classified read-only and run | Leaks |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GNU 4.10 `--sandbox` | previous head (control) | not recorded | not recorded | found, count not recorded |
| GNU 4.10 `--sandbox` | this head | 1,254,713 | 20,000 | 0 |
| BSD (macOS) | previous head (control) | 332,094 | 20,000 | 2,111 |
| BSD (macOS) | this head | 1,254,713 | 20,000 | 0 |

The BSD control row is from the run before the GNU mode was added; the later control runs printed leaks for both seds but their summary line was cut from the capture, so the GNU control count is not recorded. The first version of this fix was caught by this fuzz (`s/[^]/]/;s,/gw,x,` wrote a file on BSD sed); the bracket rule was corrected and the table is from the corrected rule.

**Unit tests, red first.** `tool mutation helpers` gained 11 gated cases and 3 read-only cases. Seven of the first eight gated cases were run on the previous head and failed; the other three are scripts the fuzz showed leaking there. 144 of 144 pass on this head.

Limits: the harness is not a voice call, and the running Gateway does not have this commit, so there is no live voice trace for the sed rule. The fuzz is random, not a proof; it covers GNU sed 4.10 and the macOS sed only (not BusyBox).

prs.title: fix(media-understanding): treat silent audio as an empty transcript in shared STT parsing
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/171512

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: audio without speech is reported as a failed transcription ("transcription response missing text") when the STT provider is OpenRouter, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, ElevenLabs or Deepgram. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/134377 fixed the same symptom for xAI only.

## User Impact

User impact: callers of file transcription get "no transcript" for silent audio instead of a provider failure, as they already do on xAI. `openclaw infer audio transcribe` reports "No transcript returned" instead of the provider error, a silent Talk transcription turn no longer fails the transcription session, and a silent Discord voice segment is treated as empty instead of "processing failed". For channel voice notes, the `audio: failed` warning is no longer logged and the attempt is recorded as skipped; the attachment still carries the existing "[Audio attachment could not be analyzed]" marker. A response without a transcript field, malformed JSON and HTTP errors are still failures.

For plugin authors: `requireTranscriptionText` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http` can now return an empty string, which the media runner already skips as empty output. It still throws when the value is not a string.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `requireTranscriptionText` helper threw on an empty string, while the media runner already treats empty output as a nonfatal skip. It now throws only for a non-string value, the contract xAI adopted in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/134377, and xAI uses the shared helper again instead of its own copy. Deepgram REST and Flux follow the same contract; a Flux stream that closes normally after the flush without any turn now counts as silence.

## Evidence

Tested at `c19862eac7d` (base `upstream/main` `e80558a4da0`).

A harness that builds both sides ran the built CLI on each, in an isolated home, against the real OpenRouter STT endpoint. The CLI's audio path uses OpenClaw's OpenRouter default model, `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`. Inputs: 3 seconds of 16 kHz silence, and a short spoken clip as a control. The proof ran on an earlier revision of this commit; since then a test helper's declaration changed and the helper's missing-value check was widened from `undefined` to any non-string, which does not change the string path exercised here.

Before (base `e80558a4da0`):

```text
$ openclaw infer audio transcribe --file silence-3s.wav --model openrouter/openai/whisper-1 --json
[media-understanding] audio: failed (0/1) reason=OpenRouter transcription response missing text
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "OpenRouter transcription response missing text"
  }
}
exit 1
```

After (this PR):

```text
$ openclaw infer audio transcribe --file silence-3s.wav --model openrouter/openai/whisper-1 --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "No transcript returned for audio: <input>/silence-3s.wav"
  }
}
exit 1
```

Observed result: on main the silent clip is a provider failure. With this change the provider returns an empty transcript, the runner records a skip (no `audio: failed` warning), and the CLI reports that no transcript was returned, the result xAI gives today. The spoken control transcribed on both sides ("Hello. Please remember that my favorite color is green. Thank you.", exit 0).

Checks: the touched tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time per file below; the existing xAI, ElevenLabs and media runtime tests also pass), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, and `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files; the broad suites run in this PR's CI. The new silence case in each file fails on the base and passes on this head.

| Test file | `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall time |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/deepgram/audio-flux.test.ts` | 6.6 s |
| `extensions/deepgram/audio.test.ts` | 6.5 s |
| `extensions/openai/media-understanding-provider.test.ts` | 10.8 s |
| `extensions/openrouter/media-understanding-provider.test.ts` | 4.5 s |

Each new case runs in about 0.1 s; most of each file's time is transform and existing cases.

Not covered: only OpenRouter was exercised live. Deepgram (REST and Flux) and the shared OpenAI-compatible path (OpenAI, Groq, Mistral, DeepInfra, SenseAudio, tested through the OpenAI provider) are covered by the provider tests above, not by live calls. ElevenLabs goes through the same shared helper but has no empty-transcript test. OpenAI `gpt-4o-transcribe` returned hallucinated text for silence in a live check, so it does not reach this path. Google Gemini audio is prompted LLM transcription and keeps empty output as an error, because an empty response can also mean a blocked or empty candidate. Talk transcription sessions and Discord voice consume the same runtime result but were not driven live.

prs.title: fix(ai): clamp OpenAI Responses max_output_tokens to model capacity
prs.body:
Closes #127560

## What Problem This Solves

An explicitly configured output budget larger than the selected model's catalog capacity reaches strict Responses endpoints unchanged. They reject an otherwise valid agent turn with HTTP 400.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both Responses request owners now reuse `clampMaxTokensToModel` after applying the existing 16-token minimum. This preserves explicit limits when custom-model capacity is unknown, fixes the previous simple-path NaN regression, and retains managed zero/undefined fallback behavior. No caller-side workaround or new configuration is introduced.

Ported @Parker-Fawcett's contributor commits onto current request construction; thanks to the contributor and the reporter of #127560. Consolidated coverage around the two actual request owners instead of duplicating provider cases. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## User Impact

Oversized budgets are capped at the model's declared output capacity. In-range budgets and unknown-capacity explicit budgets are unchanged. OpenAI and Azure Responses share these owners. Existing Codex unsupported-field stripping is unchanged.

## Evidence

Built current main (`653003a010987ad75393bdd0ff067283f41a1be7`) and candidate in a secretless Node 24 Docker container. Drove the shipped `openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> agent --local --agent main --message ... --thinking off --json` entry point with an `openai-responses` provider and an actual local HTTP recording endpoint. The endpoint rejects output budgets above the model's configured catalog capacity of 128 and otherwise returns a normal Responses SSE completion.

Captured results:

```text
base: configured=256; POST /v1/responses max_output_tokens=256
      HTTP 400 invalid_request_error: max_output_tokens exceeds model cap 128
      CLI exit=1; no completed answer
head: configured=256; POST /v1/responses max_output_tokens=128
      HTTP 200; CLI exit=0; finalAssistantVisibleText=CAP_OK
control base/head: configured=64; max_output_tokens=64; CLI exit=0; CAP_OK
```

Focused regression: pre-fix oversized case fails (`expected 256 to be 128`); candidate's three selected suites pass (76 tests). Cases protect the upper cap, unchanged in-range budget, 16-token floor, unknown capacity, and managed zero/undefined fallback. Changed-file oxfmt and oxlint pass.

Production +4/-2 (net +2: imports for the existing helper); tests +47/-0 against the merge base. No docs/configuration contract changes; changelog remains release-owned. Final revision only corrects the unknown-capacity test fixture typing; the six regression cases pass again and production/runtime proof inputs are unchanged.
Authenticated live gate on the same candidate: `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, requested `max_output_tokens=128`, CLI exit 0, final answer `LIVE_OK`. Credentials stayed in a temporary host-only 0600 file behind a request-forwarding proxy and were deleted afterward; none entered the container. The first proxy setup was blocked by the private-network guard; explicitly allowing this operator-controlled test endpoint fixed the setup, without product changes.


Two-way door: a revert fully restores prior request shaping; no persisted-state or schema changes. Blast radius is output-budget shaping for OpenAI-compatible and Azure Responses requests.

prs.title: perf(usage): bound session reports and retain visible results
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `sessions.usage` spending minutes scanning a large installation, then discarding the entire report because one session's access changed during the load. Team's observed calls failed after 103 and 757 seconds. Fractional model costs forced transcript replay even when durable usage partitions already contained the required totals; serial population-wide access reads added more work.

## User Impact

Aligned calendar ranges read the existing quarter-hour/month usage partitions. Token counts stay exact; regrouping buckets can change the last bit of floating cost addition and the existing latency sketch. Exact partial boundaries retain bounded replay and return visibly `computing` rows when the allowance is exhausted. Revocation drops affected rows from the page, totals, facets and creator options while preserving still-visible rows. Context from a replaced instance is stripped, and page hydration backfills once; continued churn can leave a short page after two passes.

Each request has a 15-second deadline and a 20,000-instance ceiling after creator filtering. Disconnecting cancels that request while another client's identical report continues independently. Report publication waits at most 100 ms for queued refresh work. Exact keyed readers still await their selected sessions; main's priority and idle-period refresh policies remain intact. The RPC documentation describes these limits and partial results.

## Why This Change Was Made

Durable usage summaries own data; present-time session capabilities own access. The handler uses resident capability facts, with the existing exact fallback only when those facts are unavailable. One rows builder owns both summary and overview results, and shared page selection owns filtering/sorting. The obsolete overview cache, worker operation and duplicate builder are deleted. Request-local source maps avoid repeated key encoding, and prepared visible rows are reused only when no await intervenes before publication.

Per-agent replay shares a 5-second/16 MiB allowance. Retained cache payloads and decoded JSON share a 32 MiB allowance, including compact numeric freshness facts reserved at 256 bytes per selected key. Existing SQLite streaming reads omit individual bodies above 1 MiB and headers above 64 KiB before materialization. The actor-backed private-store snapshot applies equivalent admission before `structuredClone`, then spends the remaining allowance on decoding. Both paths carry actual stored lengths and compact numeric freshness facts; current valid deferrals do not trigger refresh, while missing/truncated bodies and oversized headers retain canonical repair. Cheap producer encoding/length invariants are checked before decoded-budget deferral. Missing bodies and oversized partition metadata are invalid rather than permanently `computing`; invalid metadata overrides an earlier deferred monthly body.

Main's synchronous snapshot owner captures raw metadata, bodies and eligible partitions together, closes the database, and then permits awaited inventory, pricing and replay. Unaligned requests skip unused partition reads. Bodies and partitions spend their decoding allowance per row. Completed snapshots share the existing bounded eight-entry revision-owned cache; authorization/cancellation-bearing cold loads stay request-owned. Overlapping cold requests may duplicate bounded reads, and an earlier successful flight displaced by a later canceled flight can require a subsequent reread. No schema, index, stored shape, configuration option or public request shape changes.

## Evidence

### Measurement

| Integrated exact-read source measurement (3 samples) | Baseline | Measured lane source | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Median RPC wall time | 2,057.6 ms | 863.2 ms | 2.38× faster (-58.0%) |
| Median JavaScript worker CPU | 1,940 ms | 670 ms | -65.5% |
| Median main-thread CPU | 240 ms | 180 ms | -25.0% median; aggregate increases |

Individual wall/main/worker samples in milliseconds: baseline `2491.6/260/2380`, `2057.6/240/1940`, `1812.9/120/1700`; integrated source `2239.6/430/1190`, `863.2/180/670`, `842.3/150/660`. Main CPU totals 620→760 ms (+22.6%), while combined main/worker CPU totals 6,640→3,280 ms (-50.6%). No uniform main-thread improvement or blanket no-regression claim is made. Current-row authority checks and overview aggregation run on main; three samples do not isolate their cost from warming/GC variation. The tradeoff is bounded, successful reporting with substantially lower wall and total CPU. Final quiet windows were 30/60 ms. The first request uses 430 ms of main CPU versus 260 ms on baseline; that increase remains part of the result.

The real loopback WebSocket RPC uses an isolated synthetic Team-shaped fixture: 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, approvals, cron, 12 real project worktrees, 512 MiB logical transcript text and an approximately 1.6 GiB agent database. Fractional costs previously forced about 462 MiB of replay across 1,030 rollups. August 25/24/23 start dates produce distinct cold outer-cache keys over the same corpus. Startup maintenance and a full warmup are excluded; both sides require two consecutive five-second CPU windows below 200 ms. CPU sampling separates main from actual JavaScript WorkerThread threads at 10 ms resolution. All samples are retained.

Baseline `3d9e3fb92051d8e5dc248b226599432aad8ccc26` and that same source plus the frozen lane production files provide the controlled comparison. All 22 production paths and the unchanged snapshot-helper dependency are hash-verified. This is not an exact latest-main build claim; PR CI builds the exact published head. The source includes the partition guard and the rebased exact-read contract; its preparation build passed in 69.2 seconds. This source-pinned comparison measures `45f83824b33f5fcd93cf498859ac026ea5bc8a54`. The later private memory-store budget change affects only the actor path, which this durable fixture does not execute; it has focused functional proof, not an incognito performance claim.

Every complete sample succeeds with 5,000 fresh rows, no pending/stale/computing rows, 50 page rows and identical 1,201,500-token/$24.03000000000062 totals. The baseline also reproduced the access-changed `UNAVAILABLE` error through the real RPC. An earlier unaligned UTC+00:01 sample returned a partial view in 835 ms (172 cached, 4,828 pending), not a complete-export benchmark. The fixture is synthetic and quiescent, not production's multi-client load near full event-loop utilization.

Production diff: 1033 additions / 569 deletions, net +464 lines, excluding tests/docs. Deletions remove the competing overview route, result/operation variants and fractional-cost replay machinery. Growth implements the explicitly requested cancellation lifetime, time/size bounds, present-time access publication and bounded freshness/repair behavior. No speculative cache owner or compatibility shim is added.

### Proof and Review

Local validation is changed-file formatting/lint and focused tests only. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated. Measurements use only the owned Team sandbox, synthetic state, separate loopback ports, CPU/memory limits and low scheduling priority. Production state and the production Gateway are untouched; the synthetic Gateway stops after sampling, and sandbox cleanup follows CI/landing.

Focused handler/context proof passes 23/23, including access changes during loading/hydration, reset/incognito, bounded backfill, creator filtering before the ceiling, deadline and cancellation. Physical-owner attribution passes 11/11; shared overview passes 20/20; transport/lifetime caller cutover passes 7/7; refresh scheduling passes 21/21, including exact concurrent-append reads held beyond the report timeout. Worker/SQLite/projection/codec proof covers native omission, encoded/decoded deferral, stale checkpoint repair, batching, cancellation, receipt replacement and synchronous snapshot consistency.

The final cancellation/cache/SQLite run passes 61/61. The identical-client disconnect regression fails on the preceding shared-flight code; both oversized-first and oversized-last partition cases fail on the preceding reader and pass through canonical repair after the fix. Nine worker I/O and six selected SQLite corruption cases pass 15/15. The final codec/SQLite run passes 11/11 selected cases: impossible identity/zstd sizes remain invalid even with zero budget, valid bodies still defer, and the real-worker identity-size regression produces stale/invalid repair receipts and restores full/filtered totals. That real-worker case fails on the old decoder. Raw snapshot/per-row decoding proof passes 2/2 and fails against the prior eager-decoding helper.

Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**. Autoreview refused a route/operator-configuration mismatch; no configuration was changed. Fresh independent reviews found and verified the producer-budget, present-time visibility, cancellation-isolation and canonical-repair fixes. Final production changes, test-type corrections, conflict-driven refresh integration and the actor snapshot budget are independently reviewed clean, and addressed hosted conversations are resolved. A real exact-read regression caught the blanket report timeout after rebase; the 100 ms limit is now explicit only for partial reports. Exact readers retain session-specific completion and cancellation. The rebase integration three-file focused run passes 46/46 (19 handler, 21 refresh, 6 memory). Final actor proof passes 16/16: current/stale deferral, missing/truncated/corrupt bodies, oversized header repair, shared encoded/decode bytes, compressed expansion, metadata exhaustion, cancellation and detached snapshots. Three budget cases fail on the previous producer/decoder: it copies 36,941,280 bytes against the 33,554,432-byte cap and incorrectly decodes oversized/expanded bodies. Final formatting, focused lint and diff checks pass.

The preceding head `ba7ffb5274c1981b27f7cac981ffe8f7142a0cf7` passed full [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38484890444). The subsequent [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38486680312) found two missing test-fixture narrowing contracts and one unrelated tooltip timing failure. The fixtures now check the actual SQLite key type and generated partition presence; seven codec cases plus the real-worker repair case pass (8/8 selected), with fresh independent review clean. The actual merge conflict with main's selected-session refresh owner required a rebase onto `11d75e447e4452e7a88bf92ac5d684c1abad8c07` and the exact-read correction above. Final-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38490981082) passed for `1122dba5f2e047f05bb66c4d553841c79e227a50`, including builds, changed runtime lanes, UI/e2e, lint, production/test types and the CI gate; the controlled benchmark above measures the preceding durable-path source, as pinned in Measurement. Hosted review identified and verified the private memory-store clone/decode budget repair before final publication. The rebased CI found an inherited participant publisher call error in unchanged main inputs at `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-node-artifacts.ts:490`, affecting declarations, extension package boundary and test types. The tested merge `c8567197c68c638c814d8d0707f27a9cb27283cb` has ordered parents `e7a07c5aee577be3a2425ec4d88cad17813b7505` and the then-published lane head `45f83824b33f5fcd93cf498859ac026ea5bc8a54`. Main fixed that call independently in `4aa62334122ed29f605f9820c4604539b3ccee77`; no fix was copied into this branch and no CI rerun was requested. CI-owned failures were repaired rather than rerun: retired caller contracts, ES2023-compatible source-map construction, timer isolation, strict null-body expectations, and required fixture fields/real union narrowing. Conflict-driven rebases retained main's owner changes; no upstream fix was copied or cherry-picked. A superseded UI attachment timeout was classified under the five-run rule on identical production inputs and exact CI base/tested merge; later full CI passed it. This does not claim that contention-sensitive flake was fixed. No CI rerun was requested to chase green.

Earlier tooltip attribution: `ui/src/components/markdown-file-tooltip.browser.test.ts`, case `cancels delayed clipboard fallback after reopen dismissal`, failed with `false` instead of `true` at line 130. The whole single file passed 13/13 in five processes on each exact CI main parent (`2d9b602a74ee482171c5f80ac8a775c3a2d26a2a`), direct PR head (`1e55b64b846d1195a9e0c63799bfb3c441160930`) and tested merge (`31f0da7c276c1cc4af31963fda7d56cd52017dd9`). The tested merge has those exact ordered parents. Relevant tooltip/test/markdown/toast/style/config/dependency/runtime blobs are identical between the CI base and tested merge. The direct PR head has older upstream UI inputs, which are why the tested merge was also verified. This meets the standing unrelated-flake rule; it is not a claimed tooltip repair. The subsequent test-only head `09c1ac2b6ba0d7b3bad483b7874172fff9549ead` also passed 13/13 in five processes: 20 independent processes in total. After rebase, all 6,131 UI/Vitest/mermaid/runtime/lock blobs match the already-tested merge, and the pinned new main matches the tested CI base. These unchanged-input comparisons reuse that file-level attribution without claiming a fresh assertion run on the rebased head. No CI rerun or branch update was requested to chase green.

prs.title: fix(plugins): supply the admitted request to before_prompt_build on embedded and CLI runs
prs.body:
Related: #160232

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a plugin registered on `before_prompt_build` cannot tell which admitted request a turn belongs to when that turn runs on the embedded runner or the CLI backend. The event carried only `prompt` and `messages`, although `currentUserMessage` and `currentUserMessageId` are part of the documented event contract and are already supplied by the Codex, Copilot, and ACPX harness runtimes.

## User Impact

Plugins that scope their work to the current request now receive the request text and its stable admission identity on the default runtimes, exactly as they already did on the harness runtimes. The bundled `active-memory` plugin is the concrete consumer: without the fields it fell back to the assembled prompt for intent detection and to the query text for its deterministic-recall reuse key, so two independent turns with identical text could share one recall result.

**Compatibility:** the two fields are added only for turns whose admitted request is owned by a transcript recorder. A run with no recorder keeps the previous identity-free event, so a plugin that branches on field omission — including `active-memory`'s legacy path — sees no change for those runs. No config, schema, storage, migration, or default changes.

**Maintainer decision requested.** This makes `currentUserMessage` / `currentUserMessageId` informational on recorder-backed embedded and CLI turns, matching the contract the harness runtimes already implement. Requesting the plugin API owner's acceptance of that additive, omission-preserving event contract (the previous review's `Decision needed`); nothing else is pending on the contributor side.

## Why This Change Was Made

`currentUserMessage` / `currentUserMessageId` were introduced for the harness prompt path in #149180. The embedded runner assembles its prompt through a different function and never passed them, and the CLI backend reuses that same helper, so both producers were affected. Both now read the fields from the recorder-owned admitted request — the representation Codex uses — and share one event builder with the harness path instead of copying the text/identity derivation.

`currentUserMessageId` is the recorder's `idempotencyKey`: stable across retries and rebuilds of one admission and different between admissions. An admitted request without text (for example image-only input) is reported as an explicit empty string rather than falling back to the assembled prompt, which may contain reconstructed history.

🤖 AI-assisted: This PR was developed with AI assistance.

## Evidence

### 1. Real end-to-end turns on both changed runtimes

`extensions/qa-lab/src/embedded-prompt-build-current-input.e2e.test.ts` boots the repo Gateway from source, registers a probe plugin on `before_prompt_build`, sends a real qa-channel message, and asserts the event the plugin actually received — no injected assembly input:

- **embedded runtime** (mock OpenAI provider), and
- **CLI backend process** (bundled `claude-cli` backend with a fake `claude` on `PATH` implementing the stdio protocol), so a real CLI child process runs the turn.

```bash
$ pnpm test extensions/qa-lab/src/embedded-prompt-build-current-input.e2e.test.ts
CLI_PROCESS_TRACE {"turnStarted":true,"turnFinished":true,"reply":"fake-claude reply bb4caa70-f5cc-42e7-bc39-5a36a540fc1c"}
 ✓ binds the admitted request onto the embedded prompt boundary event 150470ms
 ✓ binds the admitted request onto the CLI backend prompt boundary event 147520ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
E2E_EXIT=0
WALL_SECONDS=1922
# leftover fake-CLI temp directories after teardown:
0
```

**CLI process observation (redacted).** The CLI case asserts that the child process actually ran the turn — `turn-started.json` and `turn-finished.json` written by the fake CLI, and its reply delivered to the channel — as well as the hook event:

```json
{ "turnStarted": true, "turnFinished": true, "reply": "fake-claude reply <uuid>" }
```

Raw hook event captured by the probe on the embedded harness (synthetic text, synthetic session, id truncated):

```json
[
  {
    "keys": ["currentUserMessage", "currentUserMessageId", "messages", "prompt"],
    "hasCurrentUserMessage": true,
    "currentUserMessage": "PROBE_TRACE_MARKER",
    "hasCurrentUserMessageId": true,
    "currentUserMessageId": "channel-user:v1:ec6ff72264a1a0e1…",
    "promptHead": "PROBE_TRACE_MARKER",
    "messageCount": 0,
    "trigger": "user",
    "inputProvenanceKind": null
  }
]
```

Before this change the same producers emitted only `{ prompt, messages }` — the shape reported in #160232.

### 2. Before / after on the embedded prompt-assembly entry point

```bash
# AFTER
$ pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-build.provenance.test.ts
 ✓ binds the recorder-owned admitted request to the hook event
 ✓ keeps an admitted request without text instead of reusing the projected prompt
 ✓ keeps the legacy identity-free event when no request was admitted
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
PROVENANCE_EXIT=0
```

```bash
# BEFORE: production change removed, test kept in place
$ pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-build.provenance.test.ts
AssertionError: expected { prompt: 'Handoff payload', …(1) } to match object { …(2) }
  {
-   "currentUserMessage": "Handoff payload",
-   "currentUserMessageId": "run-admitted:user",
+   "messages": [],
+   "prompt": "Handoff payload",
  }
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  3 failed | 4 passed (7)
TEST_EXIT=1
```

### 3. CLI backend producer — recorder-backed hook event at its preparation entry

`src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` resolves the recorder message and passes it to both the ordinary and the authorized prompt-build dispatch. `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` prepares a real `claude-cli` turn whose admitted request is owned by a transcript recorder and asserts the event the hook runner received:

```bash
$ pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts
 ✓ prepareCliRunContext > binds the recorder-owned admitted request to the CLI prompt-build event 1516ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  118 passed (118)
CLI_PREPARE_EXIT=0
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
OXLINT_EXIT=0
```

Observed dispatch (asserted in the test):

```
runBeforePromptBuild(expect.objectContaining({
  currentUserMessage: "latest ask",
  currentUserMessageId: "cli-admitted-request",
}), ctx)
```

The recorder-less fixture already in that file keeps its previous assertion with no fields, which is the compatibility case above.

### 4. Harness runtimes unchanged by the shared-builder extraction

```bash
$ pnpm test src/agents/harness/prompt-compaction-hook-helpers.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  25 passed (25)
```

### 5. Static gates

```bash
$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 <changed files>   # FMT_EXIT=0
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>           # Found 0 warnings and 0 errors. OXLINT_EXIT=0
$ NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm tsgo:core  # EXIT=0
$ NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs \
    -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental \
    --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo   # EXIT=0
```

The extensions test typecheck is the lane that caught the earlier synchronous cleanup callback; it is green with the async callback.

### Cost of the tests added

- `extensions/qa-lab/src/embedded-prompt-build-current-input.e2e.test.ts`: 298.0 s of test time (1922 s wall including the E2E runtime preparation build) for two Gateway boots on the QA-lab product-proof tier; one file, 300 s per-test timeout, no sleeps.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts`: +1 case, 1.5 s.

### What was not tested

- `active-memory` recall behaviour itself was not re-measured end to end; only the event contract it consumes is covered.
- macOS/Windows were not exercised.
- `pnpm check:changed` did not complete on this host: it aborted with `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit - JavaScript heap out of memory`, and a retry with `--max-old-space-size=12288` produced no output after ~25 minutes. The gates in section 5 cover the same changed-scope lanes for these files.

prs.title: refactor(ui): use native menus in the sidebar
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes the remaining Web Awesome menus and popups from the Solid sidebar.

## User Impact

The sidebar keeps agent search and pinning, gateway choices, account actions, catalog filters, reorder actions, and keyboard navigation while using the owned Menu and Popover primitives. Host tags, routes, and sidebar classes stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared overlay owner handles visibility, dismissal, nested navigation, and return focus. Sidebar Web Awesome event adapters and duplicate arrow navigation are removed. Small shared menu additions preserve grouped scrolling, compound pin rows, and existing build/theme controls. Lazy loading and deferred roster actions remain intact; legacy styles still needed by the separate chat/session-menu lane are retained.

CI exposed focus and adapter gaps during the cutover. Deferred roster rows now exist before menu admission; hover opening leaves focus in place; fixed headings and separators retain their DOM so refreshes do not displace the focused group. Tab reaches pin controls, search remains outside the menu-item sequence, and pinning restores focus after reordering. The autotype exemption is limited to sidebar menus, preserving the new-session picker contract. Submenu highlight state follows the same logical value as keyboard focus. Palette tests measure each menu/select while its own overlay is open. The existing selected-agent scroll now runs for both click and hover openings, with hover-only focus restoration preserved. A short-viewport regression proves the last selected agent stays visible in Chromium and WebKit.

Related: #168852, #171269.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI and UI-component test typechecks | Passed |
| Focused unit repairs | All seven cases from the first CI run pass, across three files |
| Focused browser proof | Sidebar layout, chip/roster focus, pin/unpin and focus retention, shared search/compound controls, LTR/RTL submenu navigation, and palette inheritance passed |
| Other focused components | Sidebar action/Tab and session-filter initial-focus tests passed |
| `pnpm ui:build` + strict performance, same machine | Passed. Startup JS **349,052 → 348,998 B gzip** (−54 B); CSS **49,719 → 49,703 B gzip**, **1 request**. No violations. |
| Visual proof | Three synthetic desktop states: identity menu, agent menu, session filters; before/after inspected |
| Independent review / targeted lint / styles | Reviewed at P0–P2; targeted checks passed |
| Broad proof | Final `ci:full` run 38490099544: all UI unit/browser, all nine Control UI E2E shards and both real-Gateway shards passed; inherited static/type failures documented below |

Three local WebKit native Tab assertions also fail identically on merge base `9fb1c91d38a983`: `opens at the last enabled item with ArrowUp and exits with native Tab`, `skips ineligible controls while preserving editing and native Tab exit`, and `keeps Tab in the current menu when a descendant menu has visible controls`. Each expects the following button and receives the document body on both base and candidate. These are recorded as baseline failures, not passing proof.

The max-lines ratchet reports an existing suppression in untouched `src/commands/doctor-database-port.ts`; the file is byte-identical to the merge base and the command fails identically on the clean base checkout.

The second full CI run exposed and drove fixes to submenu highlighting, visible-overlay palette proof, and a SAFETY comment placement. Its unrelated `terminal-panel-upload` retry-recovery case passed on both candidate and clean merge base when run alone; that replay is recorded as an unresolved CI flake, not a repair.

The third full CI run passed all three UI unit/browser shards, both real-Gateway shards, and eight of nine Control UI E2E shards. The remaining crowded-agent E2E exposed the click-open scroll regression fixed in the replacement head. Its unrelated process-mock ratchet fails identically on its exact main baseline (`af73fe4e28713d`), with byte-identical test/checker/child-module inputs.

The eight assigned sidebar modules shrink from **2,437 to 2,258 lines** (−179). No local E2E suite or remote lease was used.

![Identity menu after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e74c8f39-9b0f-4887-a6d2-f847ecb3bd55)

![Agent menu after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e66bb83-fd20-4f3b-9e72-931832bbc707)

![Session filters before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4258f12c-231a-4d62-91ee-a9afb4b35e3c)

![Session filters after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da2995ab-4ab6-424f-a4b4-11c7eacd283f)

Final-head CI (`8b6a9781eeed20`, run 38490099544) passed every UI unit/browser and E2E job. Eight static/type jobs fail on the same `session-accessor.sqlite-node-artifacts.ts:490` publisher-object call: package boundary, production types, test types, and core test types 1–5. The exact CI base `4466c0db930625` reproduces TS2349/TS2757 after an isolated frozen install; caller and producer blobs are identical in tested merge `155f4b78a4a7a9`. prs.title: fix(sqlite): avoid extra reads when idle workers retire
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes occasional extra SQLite work during warmed chat turns when unrelated workers retire or a history reader starts cold.

## User Impact

Session and auth caches keep valid write receipts when idle workers stop. Cold history readers avoid six unnecessary schema-comparison statements. Data validation, real write invalidation, and open-handle crash recovery remain intact; no schema, storage-format, retention, or update change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The database admission registry invalidated every database on any worker exit, including databases that worker never borrowed. It also invalidated handles that had already closed when intentional worker termination returned a nonzero exit code. Native close already settles receipts before releasing its final reference. Exit now invalidates only databases with an outstanding reference from that worker.

Canonical writer validation no longer uses triggers, but a fresh worker still constructed a temporary database to discover the expected pending-table definition. Derive that definition from normalized canonical DDL and delete the temporary database, expected-definition cache, environment transfer, and retention-request handoff. Actual catalog drift checks remain.

Removed checks and accepted edges:

- Unrelated-worker exit invalidation: a worker cannot leave an unpublished write in a database it never borrowed; foreign writers remain outside Gateway ownership.
- Exit-code revalidation after native close: closed handles have settled receipts even if their worker later fails; a genuinely still-open handle continues to invalidate on any exit.
- Expected-schema cache identity and handoff checks: expected definitions come directly from the current code's DDL, with no transferred cache to validate. Missing/drifted actual tables and unexpected triggers are still rejected.

## Evidence

A private copy of shared SQL harness v2.1.0 ran 30 warmed turns on baseline `d3bb490bbd81617be299877270a52e116fa75ba6`. Attribution follows turn causes across workers, rather than time-window overlap.

| Warmed metric | Baseline median [min–max] | Baseline p90 | Merged median [min–max] | Merged p90 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| All-thread statements | 112 [112–153] | 120 | 102 [102–107] | 102 |
| Worker requests | 34 [34–44] | 36 | 34 [34–36] | 34 |
| MAIN statements | 0 [0–0] | 0 | 0 [0–0] | 0 |

Turns 6, 13, 14, 21, and 29 exceeded median + 5. Turns 6/13/14 added sharing-cohort, exact-entry, actor hydration, cold-cohort, and auth reads. Turns 6 and 13 align with 30-second surplus-worker deadlines (596ms and 759ms before their start); turn 14 has no separately substantiated retirement trigger. Turn 21 added six temporary comparison statements plus two legitimate quarantine admission reads: a background identity read occupied the first history worker, so turn accounting opened the pool's second worker. Turn 29 added 41 statements across the same cache families and pending-input/transcript refresh. Two session-read workers reach their configured 60-second idle deadlines about 400ms before that turn, and another deadline falls between its two actor hydrations. These are deadline correlations, not proven exit timestamps: the baseline records SQL/requests but not worker exits or task completion.

The post-merge run on `15534c36e2daaf1dae77c5422c44099dff4a4c49` passed the full isolated workload under the shared CPU gate. Twenty-nine of 30 warmed turns used exactly 102 statements and 34 requests. The first warmed turn used 107/36: a retained-cohort cache miss in `createAdmittedSessionEntryCohortReader.withRead` runs `readSessionEntryCohort`, adding two entry SELECTs, one cold-archive metadata SELECT, and BEGIN/COMMIT. It does not recur. This misses the max ≤ median+3 aim by two statements; there were no turns above median+5. The private observer recorded three actual worker exits during warmed turns 17 and 19; both turns and all subsequent warmed turns stayed at 102/34.

Main was integrated after the baseline. The ten-statement median decrease is from other session changes: entry/participant projection, transcript projection/reset-window, and bounded active-context reads; it is not claimed as this patch’s saving. Baseline load was 53.5→42.5 and candidate load 35.2→25.7 on 32 CPUs; warmed windows were 56.8s and 43.5s. This is one 30-turn run per version, not a latency benchmark or a guarantee over every retirement cadence.

Shared read-family totals across the 30 warmed turns (each family is measured across all workers):

| Read family | Baseline | Merged | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exact entry facts | 65 | 60 | −5 |
| Actor hydration | 5 | 0 | −5 |
| Entry-cache snapshots | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Row facts | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Transcript watermark | 3 | 0 | −3 |
| Auth-profile reads | 34 | 30 | −4 |
| Canonical comparison SQL | 6 | 0 | −6 |

No measured shared read family increased. The removed comparison SQL contributes no request-count saving by itself. Total warmed requests fell from 1,045 to 1,022; the ordinary-turn request count remains 34.

T1 in the changed owners: **0 → 0**. No new SQL or synchronous Gateway path is introduced. The six removed cold-worker comparison statements do not change request count. Legitimate cold-worker quarantine reads remain.

Regression coverage extends the real direct/retained worker termination test: open handles invalidate, closed/unrelated handles preserve receipts, and a subsequent in-process update changes the scoped token and returns fresh data. Fresh-worker canonical admission must execute zero comparison bootstraps, while same-worker DDL drift remains rejected. The obsolete cache-transfer test and unrelated-worker retirement invalidation assertion are removed. The latter was caught by PR CI: its fixture never opened the database, so it pinned exactly the invalidation this fix removes; retained real-worker coverage protects open-handle recovery and closed/unrelated-handle stability.

Changed-file formatting and diff checks pass. Local lint reports only the existing admission-owner max-lines finding (827 total lines both before and after; 750 counted against 700). The repository CI wrapper treats this existing size limit as advisory. Focused owner tests, types, Madge, and database worker/dialect ratchets run in PR CI. Ordinary PR CI skips Knip, so its production, scripts, and full-tree export scans ran separately through the shared CPU gate and passed with zero entries on the integrated head. The initial scan found inherited Muse/sidebar exports; integrating their main fixes resolved them without conflicts. Types, lint, Madge, PostgreSQL conformance, and the database worker/dialect ratchets passed in PR CI. Both Codex review rounds completed scoped-clean at P0–P2; the final round included the close, receipt, and schema-normalization owners. No SDK surface or published-driver update cell applies.

Diff against integrated main: 43 insertions, 314 deletions across 11 files (net −271 lines).

CI diagnosis: the obsolete unrelated-worker assertion was deleted after the first run. The session-row topology recursion also reproduces on main head `2597a1aaa98f7d20755a7d65d5d97c770b40c1b3`, [scheduled job 115595038906](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38484533627/job/115595038906), with the identical test title, `RangeError`, and recursive `findSessionRowById` stack. The focused test alone passes on this branch; the existing main repair owner has the failure. The integrated CI run passes the native-workspace skill-discovery proof. Its auth-logout recovery case returned a warning after config reload encountered an offline-maintenance admission refusal. The exact selected-profile-removal case and assertion reproduce on baseline `48d4520c2ea53abc9086a4bd865b92f69bacc7d3` (verified source tree `dc50e125683f68e45ab0dbb7a9bfc4821db8b298`) in [focused baseline run 38488158969](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38488158969): one failed, one skipped, with the identical config-reload error and logout warning at line 527. All remaining behavioral CI failures are inherited; landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception. All static gates passed.

The final CI shard hit the existing Claw-removal stale-quiescence timeout family. Main head `2597a1aaa98f7d20755a7d65d5d97c770b40c1b3`, [scheduled job 115595038832](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38484533627/job/115595038832), has the identical first three cases and 120-second test / 180-second hook timeouts, then terminates before the remaining cases. The central main-repair owner is already tracking it.

prs.body:
Closes #145075

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI file actions are inconsistent between attachment cards, workspace/session files, and the preview dialog. Large text previews render the entire file even when only a small part is visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one contextual file-action menu with validated file identities and native keyboard controls. Window large text previews by default, with an explicit full-content mode for native Find, complete selection, and assistive reading.

## User Impact

Users can open file actions with a menu button, right-click, or the keyboard. Large-file scrolling keeps a bounded set of visible rows, while full-content mode preserves access to the complete text. Existing download-pending, loading, workspace filtering, and directory navigation behavior is preserved.

## Evidence

- 68 focused unit/browser tests passed, plus all 6 production-bundle file-link E2E tests. Chromium coverage includes native keyboard menu activation, focus return, pending downloads, Windows drive-relative path rejection, bounded scrolling, full-content Find/Selection, reconnection, and 320/390px layouts.
- Regression tests failed before their corresponding fixes, including missing full-content access, invalid drive-relative references, missing native menu activation, and a removed pending-download guard.
- UI typechecking, i18n verification, and targeted Oxlint/Stylelint passed. Core-test typechecking and the core graph boundary also passed.
- Production build passed; all 8 changed runtime sources matched their source maps, and all 872 gzip/Brotli assets matched after decompression.
- `check:changed` is not fully green on Windows: its script/full-tree Knip passes report two unchanged baseline exports (`canonicalProviderName` and `listPackagedStaticExtensionAssetOutputs`). Their production consumers exist; the pinned main configuration generates backslash glob entries that fail to match them. The production Knip pass reported zero entries. This PR does not change that configuration.
- Independent review of the complete final diff found no actionable P0-P2 findings.
- These are isolated test-fixture results. No global Gateway deployment or manual screen-reader acceptance is claimed.

prs.title: fix(node-cli): treat an empty --tls-fingerprint as unset, not as no pinning
prs.body:
## Summary

fix(node-cli): treat an explicit-but-empty `--tls-fingerprint` as unset so it falls back to the configured baseline fingerprint, instead of silently disabling certificate pinning

## What Problem This Solves

The recent TLS pin normalization (`11ebdfc9c32`, #125276) rewrote fingerprint selection in `resolveNodeGatewayOptions` to take any explicitly passed value verbatim:

```ts
const selectedTlsFingerprint =
  options.tls === false
    ? undefined
    : options.tlsFingerprint !== undefined
      ? options.tlsFingerprint
      : endpointChanged ? undefined : baselineTlsFingerprint;
const tlsFingerprint = selectedTlsFingerprint
  ? requireTlsFingerprint(selectedTlsFingerprint)
  : undefined;
```

Two regressions versus the previous behavior (which ran the value through `normalizeOptionalString` first):

1. **`--tls-fingerprint ""` silently disables pinning.** `""` is not `undefined`, so it is selected; being falsy, `tlsFingerprint` becomes `undefined` and the node connects with **no certificate pinning at all** — even though a baseline fingerprint is configured. Previously, the empty string normalized to "unset" and the baseline fingerprint stayed active.
2. **Whitespace-only values hard-fail.** `"   "` is truthy, so it goes to `requireTlsFingerprint`, which throws `Invalid TLS fingerprint` — the node command fails outright instead of falling back.

**代码证据**: `src/cli/node-cli/gateway-options.ts:78-89` — the selection no longer normalizes the option before deciding whether a baseline fallback applies.

Trigger condition: `openclaw node --tls-fingerprint ""` (or a whitespace-only value), or any tooling that forwards an empty value for the flag.

## Root Cause

- Introduced by commit `11ebdfc9c32` (2026-08-17, #125276, "normalize TLS certificate pins"), which made validation strict but dropped the empty-input normalization from the selection path.
- Violated invariant: "explicitly provided" must mean "provided with a non-empty value". An empty override should behave like no override — especially for a security control, where the wrong direction is a silent downgrade.

## Why This Fix

- Option A (chosen): run the option through `normalizeOptionalString` before selection, restoring the pre-strictness semantics for empty/blank input while keeping `requireTlsFingerprint` strict validation for real values. One line; matches the old behavior exactly for this case.
- Option B: special-case `""` only. Leaves whitespace-only input as a crash; normalizing covers both with the same established helper.
- Not chosen: making `requireTlsFingerprint` lenient — strict validation of actual fingerprints is the point of the referenced change and stays untouched.

## User Impact

- Affected scenarios: node startup with an empty or whitespace `--tls-fingerprint` value (scripts that always pass the flag, config templates with an empty field).
- Before: empty value → connection without certificate pinning (silent security downgrade); whitespace value → startup crash.
- After: both fall back to the configured baseline fingerprint; genuine fingerprints still validated strictly.
- Behavior change: restores the pre-#125276 fallback semantics for empty input only.

## Evidence

Runs the real `resolveNodeGatewayOptions` with a baseline fingerprint configured (Node v24, tsx) — no mocks.

### Before (on main)

```bash
$ node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs proof-tls-fingerprint-empty.mjs
FAIL tlsFingerprint: "" -> tls=undefined tlsFingerprint=<none> (expected pinned abababababab...)
Error: Invalid TLS fingerprint; expected a SHA-256 certificate fingerprint.
    at requireTlsFingerprint (packages/gateway-client/src/client-address-utils.ts:29:11)
    at resolveNodeGatewayOptions (src/cli/node-cli/gateway-options.ts:88:7)
```

(`--tls-fingerprint ""` connects unpinned; `"   "` crashes startup.)

### After (with fix)

```bash
$ node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs proof-tls-fingerprint-empty.mjs
PASS tlsFingerprint: "" -> tls=true tlsFingerprint=abab… (expected pinned)
PASS tlsFingerprint: "   " -> tls=true tlsFingerprint=abab… (expected pinned)
PASS control: no override -> tls=true tlsFingerprint=abab… (expected pinned)
RESULT: ALL PASS
```

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run src/cli/node-cli/gateway-options.test.ts` — 5/5 passed, including the new regression test `treats an empty --tls-fingerprint as unset instead of disabling pinning` (both `""` and whitespace-only fall back to the baseline fingerprint; strict rejection of invalid real values unchanged).
- `npx oxlint --deny=warn` on both changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Before/after real-behavior proof logs are embedded above.

prs.title: perf(process): attribute previously unscoped git launches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Git launches outside the registered Git worker boundary were grouped as `unknown`, hiding recurring callers behind subprocess churn.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish direct Git identity, project checkout, update inspection, worktree config and maintenance, workspace synchronization, and workspace-result work. Remaining unscoped Git launches receive bounded command labels. Execution, authorization, live-state reads, and storage are unchanged; arguments, config values, refs, and repository paths never become labels.

## Why This Change Was Made

Registered Git workers already carry their admitted operation. Add labels at direct runner owners and classify remaining unscoped launches at the existing spawn-accounting boundary. Unknown aliases and option layouts become `unscoped.other`; invalid explicit labels retain `unknown`. Native, brokered, and lower-priority launches share the same accounting. The streaming workspace inventory/pack writer now records previously omitted raw launches under `workspace.inventory` by default, preserving an admitted surrounding owner; its series can increase because these launches were formerly uncounted. Shared runners provide defaults without replacing an admitted owner.

This is the requested attribution step. There are no new caches, single-flight policies, or schema changes. Production LOC is +98 net (132 added, 34 removed), required for bounded telemetry and owner labels; no duplicate execution implementation is retained. A production deployment followed by a read-only metrics window is needed to identify the dominant real caller before removing work. The synthetic workload proves an actual recurring identity path, not its share of production traffic.

## Evidence

Changed-file oxfmt and repository oxlint passed. Focused tests ran with `--maxWorkers=1`: spawn-utils, github-read-identity, checkout-git-config.windows, workspace-sync-tunnel.git, placement-dispatch-recovery-admission, and workspace-sync-inventory. The final spawn-utils run passed all 19 tests, including real native/broker execution, explicit-owner retention, unscoped argv classification, failed launches, disabled diagnostics, and private-value exclusion. Attribution assertions fail on the original diagnostics implementation.

CI caught a real regression on the first head: the workspace-result runner replaced `workspace.result-cleanup`. The repair preserves admitted owners; the failing admission file passed all 13 tests locally. Review also caught an unlabeled config write loop, omitted raw inventory launches, and missing production command/global-option spellings; each is fixed. The final local run passed spawn-utils (19 tests) and the workspace-sync-inventory file in 39.73 seconds. The repaired predecessor passed full CI in run [38486694171](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38486694171). Final-head CI [38489297821](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38489297821) completed: 54 jobs passed, 27 skipped, nine inherited failures plus their aggregate gate. All selected test shards, lint/format, independent security checks, and review passed. See the inherited-failure evidence below; failed CI is not being reported as green.

independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): the initial change, ownership repair, classifier amendment, and streaming coverage amendment each received a fresh-context independent review, clean at P2 and above. Autoreview refused a provider selector that differed from the operator configuration; no configuration changed.

Measurements ran in an isolated Linux sandbox with 64 CPU affinity slots, a 64 GiB memory limit, low CPU/I/O priority, task-owned home/state/temp paths, and loopback port 41035. Synthetic state contained 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approval recovery rows, 100 disabled cron jobs, and 12 projects with real worktrees; the agent database was 4,639,805,440 bytes. Four Gateway protocol clients subscribed to sessions. After warmup, each run issued 84 `tools.github.status` and 84 `sessions.list` requests over 120.1 seconds. Counts use exact cumulative snapshots including unpublished diagnostics counters.

| Measurement | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Git launches per measured run | 84 | 84 |
| Git launches/min | 42.0 | 42.0 |
| Unattributed Git launches/min | 42.0 (`unknown`) | 0 |
| Attributed identity launches/min | 0 | 42.0 (`github.identity`) |
| Main-thread CPU, warmed run 1 | 22.92 s | 25.48 s |
| Main-thread CPU, warmed run 2 | 28.73 s | 30.16 s |

The CPU ranges overlap and unchanged-base runs vary by 25%. These samples establish no speedup or regression beyond observed run-to-run variation. This attribution-only change is neutral: it does not eliminate launches. An earlier exploratory pair was 25.62 s base versus 22.65 s head and likewise does not establish a speedup. Gateway measurements compare base `9940ac5fca34` with `585688dd01d3`; the later command-classification and streaming-coverage amendments leave the measured identity RPC path unchanged.

A seven-trial, 100,000-observation accounting microbenchmark on `2130359115b7` measured median CPU of 6.001 ms versus 6 ms base with diagnostics disabled, and 47.968 ms versus 33 ms enabled: about 0.15 microseconds extra per observation, approximately 6 microseconds/min at 42 launches/min. It measures the accounting callback, not subprocess execution.

No Testbox/Crabbox leases were allocated. PR CI supplies full typecheck, suites, and other broad gates. The measurement sandbox was removed after its processes exited. Production was not load-tested or restarted. Remaining gap: deploy these labels through the authorized lifecycle owner, then inspect a representative production metrics window before choosing a redundant-work optimization.

## Inherited CI Failures

Final PR head: `c060dd8e3021033a608dc79038d22cf6db9c5902`. CI tested merge: `62719940ed3654314038a8d4bcab0c32fd23f5d3`, with ordered parents main `221cb55583d54d416f44fe0624ad6bdf8b7d238d` and this PR head. Every failed job log was inspected once. All failures have two unchanged main-parent causes:

| Failed jobs | Cause and baseline evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (115611186027) | `test/helpers/openclaw-test-process.test.ts:5` has an unannotated closed first-party mock. A focused invocation of the owning mock-factory scanner reports the same finding and exit 1 on both the main parent and tested merge. File blob is `55139480ed9a1a1d4b8f9790a23089b85e5d9e0e` on both. Main has independently fixed the annotation in `e7a07c5aee577be3a2425ec4d88cad17813b7505`; this lane did not copy that fix. |
| `check-additional-extension-package-boundary` (115611186372), `check-prod-types` (115611876632), `check-test-types` (115611876636), `check-test-types-core-1` (115611876573), `core-2` (115611876651), `core-3` (115611876769), `core-4` (115611876660), `core-5` (115611876753) | All report TS2349 at `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-node-artifacts.ts:490` (the declaration emitter also reports TS2757): the object returned by `prepareSessionActorParticipantUpdate` is called as a function. Introduced on main by `653003a010987ad75393bdd0ff067283f41a1be7`. File blob is `a1e20c9ae25b1119ed091db1f2ac672af63f52fa` on both. The existing `session-actor-participant-repair.test.ts` fails both same-store and cross-store cases with `publishParticipants is not a function`, exit 1, on both revisions. |
| `openclaw/ci-gate` (115615125452) | Aggregate failure caused by those nine jobs; no additional independent defect. |

Baseline replay ran only the existing two-case file with `pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-actor-participant-repair.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` in the isolated Linux sandbox, using the exact main-parent archive followed by only this PR's patch to reconstruct the tested merge. Base: 2 failures, 54.80 seconds; tested merge: the identical 2 failures, 40.08 seconds. The single-file mock scan used the repository's native parser, `scanClosedMockFactories`, and current ledger; it was not a whole-repository ratchet replay. No full test or typecheck suite was replayed.

The automatic failure table compares against an older scheduled main run that predates these main changes; its “new” rows are superseded by this exact-parent source and runtime evidence. Landing uses the standing operator-authorized inherited-failure exception. The native wrapper selects the canonical checkout prohibited for this lane, so the already-authorized exact-head API fallback is used; no native-wrapper completion is claimed.

prs.title: feat: publish linux/riscv64 Docker images
prs.body:
Related: #11977
Prior art: #12033 (my earlier attempt, which the stale bot closed for inactivity)

> AI-assisted: I drafted and built this with Claude Code, then verified it by hand on real riscv64 hardware (see Evidence). I understand what the code does.

## Decisions I need from a maintainer

1. **Publishing an unattested tag.** The riscv64 image is pushed directly, not promoted from a sealed OCI payload, so it carries no provenance attestation. ClawSweeper flagged this as a release-owner call rather than a code question. Nothing here touches the attested `:latest`/`:<version>` aliases.
2. **One deliberate divergence from the canonical image**, in the health probe. Reasoning and measurements below.

## What Problem This Solves

There is no riscv64 OpenClaw image, so anyone on a RISC-V board cannot `docker pull` OpenClaw. `node:24-bookworm` has no riscv64 variant, so the platform cannot simply be added to the existing matrix.

## Why This Change Was Made

A separate `Dockerfile.riscv64` handles what differs: the runtime is `debian:trixie-slim` plus Node from unofficial-builds, and rolldown has no riscv64 binary, so the JS bundle is cross-built on the host.

Since the earlier review, upstream replaced the release pipeline: building moved to `docker-release-prepare.yml`, emitting sealed OCI payloads promoted only after attestation. The `build-riscv64` job this PR added depended on three jobs that no longer exist. The build now lives in a standalone `.github/workflows/docker-riscv64.yml` instead of the prepare matrix, because `docker-release-artifacts.mjs` pins `ARCHITECTURES` to amd64/arm64 and asserts both are present — a riscv64 leg there would become *required* and fold into the multi-arch aliases, letting a slow emulated build block a stable release. Separation is what makes it non-blocking, which is also why it drops `continue-on-error`: swallowing failures would only hide them. It reuses `environment: docker-release`, so the same required-reviewer gate applies.

**pnpm 12 (#131043) publishes binaries only for x86_64/arm64**, and `get-pnpm`'s `platformPackageName` throws for anything else, so the original design — install production deps natively on riscv64 — cannot work at all. Production dependencies are now resolved on the build host with `supportedArchitectures.cpu=riscv64` and copied in. Because cross-resolution can silently ship a wrong-architecture addon, the runtime stage walks the linked module graph and fails the build on any native addon that is not RISC-V.

Six regressions had also accumulated while this branch sat open, each aborting the build: a renamed `npm-runner.mjs`, and four modules (`root-package-bundled-plugin-excludes`, `node-version`, `package-lifecycle-marker`, `guard-inventory-utils`) that scripts import but the Dockerfile never copied. **The branch could not produce an image before this.**

## User Impact

```
docker pull ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:<version>-riscv64
```

Best-effort and manually dispatched, so a release may ship without it. Defaults stay amd64+arm64.

## Evidence

Built via QEMU on x86 (424s), then run natively on a Banana Pi F3 (Armbian 26.8.3, 8 cores):

- `OpenClaw 2026.8.1`; `process.arch` `riscv64`, Node `v24.18.0`
- `[gateway] ready`, 13 plugins; `/healthz` `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`, `/readyz` `{"ready":true}`
- `libgomp1` 14.2.0-19 and `openssh-client` present as riscv64 builds
- Container reports **healthy** on a non-default port
- `src/dockerfile.test.ts` 34 passed; the added coverage was checked by confirming it fails when the directive is reintroduced
- `docker-riscv64.yml` clean under `actionlint` and `yamllint`

**Health probe divergence.** The canonical `dist/docker-healthcheck.js` measured 14078/14466/14281ms here, so it cannot finish inside the 10s timeout — Docker logged `ExitCode: -1, exceeded timeout` and the container never left `starting`. Given 45s it completes but still exits 1 while both endpoints serve correctly. This image uses a probe that reads `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` and returns in ~2s. That exit-1 is characterised but not root-caused: not port resolution, not a replaced global `fetch`, not a cold-start effect. Worth its own upstream report.

## Limits

- No slim or browser variant; no browser automation (no riscv64 Chromium).
- The probe reads `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` and does not see a bare `--port`; documented in `docs/install/docker.md`.
- I have no Docker Hub secrets or `docker-release` environment on my fork, so the publish path itself is unexercised.

prs.title: fix: keep Gateway startup alive with V8 contradiction exit mode
prs.body:
Related: #166581

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway startup silently exiting with status 0 when Node combines an explicit heap budget with `--exit-on-contradictory-flags`.

## User Impact

Startup continues and emits the existing warning. This diagnostic mode retains the configured heap ceiling and prevents enforcing per-worker limits, matching the existing freeze/abort modes.

## Why This Change Was Made

V8's exit mode also enables contradiction checking. The shared worker heap guard now recognizes it before resetting V8 flags. The ordinary heap-limit path stays covered by the existing native worker cases. The docs already describe contradictory-flag modes and their warning behavior.

## Evidence

- **Failing original:** on main `0aae6c7725816feed5922112b4cb4e6c2e0b091e`, adding only the process-survival table row and running `pnpm test src/infra/worker-heap-flag.test.ts -t exit-on-contradictory-flags --maxWorkers=1` fails. The production worker-factory import exits before producing the expected main/worker heap results (status 0, empty output).
- **Passing repair:** `pnpm test src/infra/worker-heap-flag.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all eight cases pass; **42.22 seconds wall time**, 5.10 seconds total Vitest time. The added native case takes **194 ms**. Each startup flag requires a fresh process because V8's flag behavior is process-wide; no Gateway boots, sleeps, polling, new seams, or new timer behavior were added.
- **Reported service budget:** a native worker-factory probe using `--max-old-space-size=8192 --exit-on-contradictory-flags` completes, warns, and preserves the main and worker ceilings at 8,791,261,184 bytes under Node 24.16.0. Before the guard repair, import exited before its completion marker. This proves process survival and budget preservation, not the original Discord report's disconnect cause.
- The `core-test-infra` type graph passes (11.1 seconds). Focused repository lint, formatting, `node --check worker-heap-flag.mjs`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38487332355) passes, with a 644-second workflow wall time. The security review and combined `openclaw/ci-gate` also pass. **CI seconds:** the eight-case file takes **5.08 seconds wall time**, 3.23 seconds Vitest time, and the added native case takes **205 ms** ([job proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38487332355/job/115604461093)).

[Exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171490#issuecomment-6157794922): ready for maintainer review, no code findings, platinum hermit patch quality. Overall/proof rating is gold shrimp because this is factory-boundary proof rather than shipped-Gateway startup proof; the maintainer explicitly permits the lower overall rating when there are no code findings.

This is a main-branch follow-up only. Do not merge or backport automatically; the maintainer requested review first.
