prs.title: fix: keep Codex commands on the selected GitHub identity
prs.body:
Related: #157500
Depends on: #171168 (stacked base; local credential fixes remain in their own PR).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex native shell execution can bypass the managed GitHub profile selected for the OpenClaw run instead of using the same credential and authority owner as native/Pi execution.

## User Impact

Selecting a managed GitHub identity now routes Codex commands through OpenClaw's existing host-owned tools, preserving selected-profile launch binding, command approvals, caller lifetime, cancellation, and actionable authentication errors. An unavailable profile does not fall back to an ambient account; restoring or changing the identity through Settings allows recovery. Without a managed selection, native Codex defaults remain unchanged.

Ordinary node execution still uses node-local authentication. Selecting a Gateway GitHub identity or approving a command does not export its reusable bearer token to a paired node. Repository-bound workers keep their separate existing contract, and Gateway-side github_publish remains available. There is no new delegation capability or configuration migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one host-owned credential selection and execution lifecycle rather than introducing a Codex-only token grant. The harness advertises a non-secret host-execution requirement, binds the prepared selection into its tool surface, and disables competing native shell features for that run. Borrowing another agent's tool policy does not change the executing agent's credential identity. This avoids relying on Codex's serialized environment overlay as a credential-authority boundary.

Split from #157500 by @galiniliev, preserving contributor credit. Personally inspected the pinned upstream Codex 0.160.0 source at a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc, including child environment overlay ordering and native shell feature defaults.

## Evidence

- Actual Codex dynamic-tool to host-exec child proof covers selected identity, missing-profile refusal and restoration, denied/closed/revoked/reassigned callers, and revocation during an awaited hook.
- Native executing-agent identity, harness environment/authority, and ordinary node isolation are checked independently.
- Combined focused run: 70 passed across Codex host execution, native identity, private exec credential launch, and harness environment/authority (85.72s wall). The added profile-restoration assertion then passed in all eight Codex boundary cases (109.80s command wall, 104.42s Vitest including 77% compiler transformation; test bodies about 20 seconds). These actual-process tests exercise the owning launch/authority boundary rather than mocked credential decisions; no per-test Gateway boots are added.
- Core, extension, and extension-test typechecks passed. Full independent P0–P2 review and the restoration-test delta review were both scoped-clean.
- Ordinary-node credential-isolation cases: 3 passed (86.81s command wall); existing Codex paired-device relay: 44 passed (48.83s).
- The broader unchanged native-node suite had 37 passed and five failures (242.82s). Each failure reproduces on baseline 0fbc1a66690a without this PR: four prepared-policy cases return user-denied, and the prepared-policy revocation case times out at 120s. Baseline attempts took 67.34s and 155.14s. These are recorded unresolved baseline defects, not fixed or passing proof.
- Core typed lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and independent review of the final one-use alias cleanup passed. Full pnpm build passed on exact head 100907b3c04c516f8fea1539cedee3a59a8a95dc (1,908.39 seconds wall). Scoped typed extension lint passed on all four changed extension TypeScript files with zero warnings/errors (158.79 seconds including declaration preparation; 36.7 seconds linter time). The earlier stopped attempts were not counted as passes.
- Linux boundary proof does not claim a live provider turn, Settings UI automation, or Windows execution. Production-head CI [38448026973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38448026973) passed all 81 jobs, including openclaw/ci-gate, on 100907b3c04c516f8fea1539cedee3a59a8a95dc. The subsequent documentation-only commit cfe36a5b76202155f10948ab1dd693074a7c30e4 removes the obsolete Codex-native bypass description; formatting and whitespace checks passed. Production code and its build/test inputs are unchanged. Final documentation-head [CI 38450345456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38450345456) completed successfully on cfe36a5b76202155f10948ab1dd693074a7c30e4. Its separate [OpenGrep check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38450344317/job/115479321432) still reports the same two inherited findings described below; the complete check rollup is not green. The separate [OpenGrep check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38448026773/job/115471433688) reported two GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS findings in bash-tools.exec-request-preparation.ts:567–568. Both expressions and surrounding logic are unchanged from the stacked base and main ancestor e43a62c404d4. Source review confirms that this write composes operator-inherited Git settings with the fixed internal maintenance.auto=false/gc.auto=0 policy; host-env-security rejects request-supplied GIT_CONFIG_* overrides before this point. No suppression or security-policy change was added. These inherited scanner findings remain unresolved; the full check rollup is not claimed green. Per-file CI seconds are not available.

### Follow-up review and inherited credential-family repair

- A fresh full independent P0–P2 review of the shared contract found no actionable defect. A separate review of its local-credential base found that exporting a public-host token into both gh credential families could expose it to an explicitly selected unrelated Enterprise host. Base commit 359890d2047585a25e87dbbcaa09f5eec90f84ea fixes this by exporting only the selected host credential family and clearing the opposite and fallback variables.
- Intermediate shared head 35d9cb6066d25e87352c82ba733ff6c1c73b2a7e merges that independently reviewed base correction without changing the shared production delta. The canonical documentation retains the host-owned Codex execution description and now describes matching-token-family behavior.
- Combined candidate: all eight Codex host-execution boundary cases passed (66.66 seconds command wall); documentation MDX and whitespace checks passed. The base correction separately passed 41 launcher/sandbox cases (six native PowerShell cases skipped), core typechecking, typed lint, formatting, and a fresh independent delta review.
- Build and CI results above remain evidence for their explicitly named prior heads, not a claim about the new merge. Results for this intermediate head and the final repaired head are recorded below; the prior inherited OpenGrep and native-node failures remain unresolved until separately evidenced otherwise. No merge or auto-merge was requested or performed.

### Latest CI correction

- CI 38488202250 on 35d9cb6066d25e87352c82ba733ff6c1c73b2a7e found the same three stale local credential-test expectations. Current shared head 34df23eaa81124a7753cadbe7e84028c1f069aa4 inherits local repair 4c76ca768132e493dbf6cd93600cc0700b384d60. This changes only the test probe: all 20 actual-exec cases pass in the base (48.24 seconds wrapper wall), typed lint and formatting pass, and an independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Shared production code is unchanged by this merge.
- The prior separate [OpenGrep run 38488201829](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38488201829/job/115606867943) again reports the two inherited GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS reads described above; these remain unresolved scanner findings, not infrastructure. CodeQL, Critical Quality, and Security Review passed. Final exact-head [CI 38490657662](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38490657662) passed on 34df23eaa81124a7753cadbe7e84028c1f069aa4: 57 jobs passed, 24 skipped, and the three stale assertions no longer fail. The separate [OpenGrep 38490657794](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38490657794/job/115614792937) still reports those same two inherited findings; all checks completed but the full rollup remains red. Standalone Opengrep OSS success does not negate the precise workflow failure.
- No submitted reviews or inline comments were present. No PR merge or auto-merge was performed.

## Worked on by

- @galiniliev

prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).
- Contrast on the same day: same-repo PRs #140038 / #140040 (blacksmith profile, ~453KB) pass preflight; fork PRs #139979, #140008, #140045 fail with the same annotation. A retrigger of this same branch passed preflight once (run 34025126956) and failed twice — the payload sits at the cap edge, so fork-PR preflight is now a coin flip.
- All substantive checks on this PR's head are green (`check-test-types-*`, lint, node test shards that ran in earlier attempts); only `preflight` + the `ci-gate` aggregate are red.

prs.title: fix: keep cloud-worker GitHub credentials usable across long turns
prs.body:
Related: #157500

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: repository-bound cloud workers can lose GitHub authentication during long turns, or retain credential authority after their original session writer changes.

## User Impact

Long-running worker turns can renew the same selected GitHub identity without waiting for credential discovery at turn startup. Cancellation, writer replacement, profile removal, and terminal completion stop renewal and settle credential writes before cleanup. Older workers without renewal support are rejected through the existing rebuild/retry path.

This keeps the existing credential-carrying contract for repository-bound worker turns. It does not export Gateway credentials to ordinary paired-node exec, add repository-free delegation, or claim that deleting a local profile revokes a token already copied from it. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The background identity owner prepares the launch snapshot; an admitted turn retains its original caller, session writer, workspace, and account. Heartbeats can refresh that account only while those owners remain current. The worker writes the refreshed token privately for subsequent command launches, acknowledges installation, and joins in-flight writes before removing its per-turn profile.

Split from the worker credential investigation and implementation in #157500 by @galiniliev; preserves that contributor's credit while excluding the proposed broader node delegation.

## Evidence

- Background preparation, retained session/writer invalidation, renewal, terminal fencing, cancellation, private profile rotation, and old-worker rejection have focused regression coverage.
- Focused final-source runs: binding/old-worker admission 25 passed (77.54s wall, cold compiler preparation); retained session/writer and heartbeat RPC authority 22 passed (30.73s); lifecycle, private worker profile, and connection shutdown 37 passed (21.23s). Commands use pnpm test with --maxWorkers=1.

- Adjacent discovery/build-recovery suites: 32 passed and one existing reconnect test timed out at 120s (215.47s command wall). The exact same test also timed out at 120s on 0fbc1a66690a, which contains none of this lifecycle delta. Recorded as an inherited unresolved reconnect failure, not a passing test or a demonstrated regression fix. New old-worker admission coverage separately proves rejection before credential disclosure; the sibling suite covers existing redispatch/cancellation paths.
- Final core typecheck, typed lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting and whitespace checks passed. Full pnpm build passed on exact head 09b52d8cfcabddd4445a2a00c7a8edcf049d31e7: all 16 phases, including package declarations, 155 public SDK export checks, and UI build (1,698 seconds wall). The earlier stopped build was not counted as a pass. Exact-head CI run [38442993689](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38442993689) completed with one failed test: the existing session-portal boundary test exceeded 30 seconds. CI classified it unknown (no matching main job). The unchanged candidate passed a standalone replay (20.47-second test; 116.68-second command) and the portal case passed in a ten-file context replay (10.68-second test). The latter run had 27 passes and one unrelated local public-worker-ingress fixture failure because the secret-egress proxy returned 502 instead of 404. This does not establish a fix or prove the CI timeout inherited; it remains an unresolved CI-only timing failure. No CI rerun or timeout increase was used.
- No live GitHub bearer rotation or Settings UI automation is claimed. Tests use synthetic credentials and real local process/transport boundaries. Hosted per-file CI seconds are pending.
- Native/Pi and Codex shared policy are handled separately; local host/profile corrections are in #171168.

An actual merge conflict was reconciled with main 7e4c0f7378ea285e405bdb9cfca3207d2529d30f in d8fab149dcb22153a863068059acf8b6448f666a, preserving both parents rather than rebasing. prs.title: fix: keep local GitHub commands on the selected credential host
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local commands using a prepared Enterprise GitHub profile could read the github.com entry instead, and inherited Enterprise fallback tokens could survive the private launcher.

Related: #157500. This is the independently useful local-credential slice; it does not include cloud-worker lifecycle changes or paired-node credential delegation.

## User Impact

Local Pi exec, Codex gateway_exec, and opted-in Docker/Podman exec use the selected profile host and clear both public and Enterprise fallback variables. Public managed profiles stay pinned to github.com; only the matching public or Enterprise token family is exported. Ordinary paired-node execution is unchanged: it keeps node-local authentication and receives no Gateway-selected bearer token.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the admitted host into the existing private launcher, look up only that host in the private profile, and forward the existing token variables to opted-in containers by name. Missing, insecure, or wrong-host profiles fail before the requested command runs. No new credential store, delegation permission, or configuration setting is introduced.

This extraction preserves the contribution in the original PR by @galiniliev, with continuation and regression work requested by @vincentkoc.

## Evidence

- Baseline at e43a62c404d4: three new actual-child regressions failed as intended (public fallback clearing and two Enterprise hosts); the existing 17 cases passed.

Combined pnpm test command with --maxWorkers=1: 63.26s wall, 62.59s wrapper time. The first cold baseline command took 92.13s including compilation. Tests prove actual child environment and synthetic engine transport, not live Enterprise network access or native Windows behavior. Hosted node-test jobs consumed 4,289 aggregate job-seconds (including setup and broader affected suites); this is not per-file execution time.

A reproduced inherited Git-author override in the maintenance fixture was repaired by isolating and restoring its four author/committer environment variables; its delta received a fresh independent P0–P2 scoped-clean review. Production behavior did not change in this follow-up.
- Production typecheck passed; scoped typed lint passed with zero warnings/errors; formatting and git diff --check passed.

prs.title: feat(telegram): embed local files in rich messages
prs.body:
## What this solves Closes #128992. With `channels.telegram.richMessages: true`, permitted local photos, videos, audio, and voice files can appear inside rich replies. Explicit document, voice-note, and video-note sends retain their selected native routes; unsupported attachments remain ordinary attachments. Existing accounts that enabled rich messages receive eligible local media inline under that same opt-in. When Telegram rejects a rich page, plain-text fallback preserves the original payload attachment order and every repeated occurrence. For example, `[document, photo]` remains `[document, photo]` instead of becoming `[photo, document]`. Files already delivered in accepted rich pages are not sent again. ## Implementation - Resolve files through the existing host media-access contract and grammY multipart transport. Code examples and unsupported markup do not read files; caller media roots still apply. - Track each payload occurrence by its original index, independently of the per-path read cache. Keep ordinary batching, cancellation, reply ownership, inline controls, and partial-delivery receipts. - Discover HTML media with the existing quote-aware tokenizer and canonical attribute parser. Apostrophes, quoted `>` characters, source-like text inside other attributes, and encoded ampersands no longer hide or corrupt the actual local source. - Expose the canonical Markdown image-span parser through the existing text-chunking SDK subpath. Adjust the handwritten surface budgets by exactly two exports (function + result type) and one callable; add no wildcard exports or new subpath. - Integrate main `0513aeae6a87b5c9d9b16b5f623d23d5d830940f`, preserving its Telegram button-style normalization, send context, and delivery/activity reporting. The existing `richMessages` opt-in remains the product choice for maintainer review. This update does not add another configuration switch. ## Validation Candidate: `5db4df605eef7cb3517f9a497824af6e34fd1bca`. - Local-media HTTP boundary suite: **37/37 passed**, 24.49 s command wall, 21.13 s Vitest. The four new ordering cases take 77–114 ms each on this host. Restoring only the old fallback concatenation makes all four fail, including the partial-success case. The HTML discovery defect was also reproduced before the parser repair. - Related Telegram adapter, button, HTML, delivery, Markdown, and SDK suites: **138/138 passed** across eight files. Doctor contract checks: **6/6 passed**. - Canonical SDK surface check passed: **3,643 public exports, 2,112 callables, zero wildcard re-exports**, with no unauthorized shipped-surface removals. SDK package-export synchronization passed. - Formatting, whitespace/conflict checks, line-cap/max-lines ratchets, assertion-safety, SQLite-worker, timeout-race, mock-export, dependency-pin, config-doc, and plugin-boundary checks passed before the final parser repair where applicable. Final formatting and whitespace checks also passed. - Type-aware lint passed for all 22 changed TypeScript files, including SDK boundary declaration preparation. The focused Telegram production type graph passed with the original strict options, ambient declarations, and transitive imports. The all-extension typecheck exceeded its 300 s local limit. Full build completed package and runtime bundles but exceeded its 600 s local limit during common declaration generation; a complete build still needs CI confirmation. - Full `check:changed` did not complete: its first non-staged run exceeded Git's output buffer while comparing the in-progress merge to its old merge base. The corrected staged run passed the checks above and was stopped at the core TypeScript graph-boundary check to apply the review finding. Initial resource-constrained HTTP attempts stalled during module preparation; later isolated runs completed successfully. Hosted CI timing is pending. - Independent full-diff review found the quoted-attribute defect; it was repaired and separately reviewed with no further actionable findings. The ordering and SDK-budget corrections had no reported P0–P2 defects. The previous gateway shutdown and activity-summary failures are addressed by upstream commits [22d7946296bf](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/22d7946296bfae995db08e02fce0694bf8f92b45) and [5bfb545bfc34](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5bfb545bfc34fe6a956b22205de667b6a9122792), both included in the integrated main revision. An exploratory filename-with-spaces assertion also exposed existing grammY multipart metadata truncation: its current writer emits an unquoted `filename=...` header. The file bytes and selected local path were correct. The final apostrophe fixture uses `Bob's-chart.png` to isolate HTML discovery; multipart header formatting is unchanged. Fresh live Telegram proof was not run: this environment lacks the Convex-leased Test Server credentials/tooling. Historical recipient screenshots below remain evidence only for their recorded older heads, not for this candidate. The installed Gateway was not modified or restarted.
Historical validation and live screenshots from the previous PR head Candidate: `6da8d970ea79a322da38be05a3a1bbfee406c8c4`. **Review finding: repeated attachments.** A new adapter case sends one payload with the same permitted local photo twice and simulates a `RICH_MESSAGE_MEDIA_INVALID` rejection. It asserts that the rejected rich message carried two photo blocks, that the fallback sends one plain `sendMessage` and one `sendMediaGroup` whose two uploads both match the fixture bytes, and that the receipt keeps all three message IDs. Negative control on this head: with only the resolver reverted to its pre-fix version, exactly this case fails (1 of 29; the fallback sends a single `sendPhoto`); with the fix, 29 of 29 pass. Cost: the rich-local-media test file with `--maxWorkers=1` takes 23.8 s command wall (19.9 s Vitest); the new case runs in 56 ms. **Live proof at this head, with recipient screenshots.** The candidate's own outbound adapter sent three cases through the server's bot and local Bot API to a private owner chat in 30.3 s. A relay recorded only Bot API methods, statuses, errors, and message IDs: | Case | Payload | Bot API trace | Delivered | |---|---|---|---| | A | Markdown inline local photo, plus local video and audio attachments | `sendRichMessage` 200 | one rich message (73488) | | B | The same local photo attached twice | `sendRichMessage` 200 | one rich message showing both occurrences (73489) | | C | 20 nested `details` (a real depth rejection), plus the same photo twice | `sendRichMessage` 400 `RICH_MESSAGE_DEPTH_INVALID` → `sendMessage` 200 → `sendMediaGroup` 200 | plain text and both photos; receipt keeps 73490, 73491, 73492 | Recipient view in the author's Telegram Desktop client, cropped to the bot messages (files: [`proof/133406-live`](https://github.com/aspalagin/openclaw/tree/0571d51171c0a869c8040e19fbce53d6a58a10e9)): | A | B | C: fallback text | C: fallback album | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | | | | | In the fallback text, `repeat.png` marks each place an embedded file appeared; the files follow as ordinary attachments. **Other validation at this head** (host, memory-capped): - Tests: 32 Telegram test files that import changed modules, including the six Telegram test files in this PR: 719 passed. prs.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): preserve GPT-6 deployment capabilities
prs.body:
Related: #157995

## What Problem This Solves

Foundry login gives GPT-6 Astra, Sol, and Luna deployments generic 128k/16k limits and disables reasoning, even when Azure discovery returns the canonical model name.

## User Impact

Newly discovered GPT-6 deployments, including custom deployment names, receive 1,050,000 context and 128,000 output tokens, reasoning support, and model-specific thinking maps. Setup warns when a chat model still needs manually verified limits.

Existing configured token limits, thinking maps, and supported effort lists are preserved. Rerun discovery or edit affected model entries to correct previously saved defaults. Astra `off` omits effort and uses the provider default; it does not promise to disable reasoning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep Azure capability decisions in the Foundry plugin using [Microsoft's documented limits and API support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/reasoning#api-and-feature-support). Importing OpenAI's private catalog would cross plugin boundaries and assume identical provider contracts. Unknown future models retain conservative defaults with an explicit setup warning rather than guessed capabilities. This PR adds onboarding diagnostics, not a Doctor migration or shared catalog API.

GPT-6 `minimal` maps to `low`; `xhigh` is supported, and `max` is exposed only for Responses. Astra omits `none` in response to the reported rejection; Sol/Luna retain it. Microsoft's current table lists `none` for Astra, which conflicts with the reporter's observation. Live tenant validation remains needed to resolve that discrepancy.

The model metadata and its focused tests move into sibling files because the original files already exceed the repository's size limits.

## Evidence

Local macOS reproduction through the registered Entra ID auth method, with synthetic Azure CLI resource/deployment responses and aliases `production-astra`, `production-sol`, and `production-luna`. Azure credentials and HTTP inference are not used; the optional connection probe is unavailable in this fixture. No live tenant test was run (Azure CLI is unavailable on this host).

| Generated metadata | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context window | 128,000 | 1,050,000 |
| Output limit | 16,384 | 128,000 |
| Reasoning | false | true |
| Thinking map | absent | minimal→low, xhigh→xhigh, max→max on Responses |
| Off | no model-specific map | Astra: omitted; Sol/Luna: none |
| Chat Completions token field | max_tokens | max_completion_tokens |
| Unverified limits | silent fallback | provider note with deployment and repair guidance |
| Existing custom reasoning settings | overwritten during model selection and runtime normalization | saved thinking map and effort list retained |

Before the production fix, the regression failed against base `177cfe8022c15605dfcf5a2c58dcf50c2cf82576`:

```text
FAIL discovers GPT-6 deployment aliases with their Foundry limits and reasoning efforts
contextWindow: expected 1050000, received 128000
reasoning: expected true, received false
thinkingLevelMap: expected model-specific map, received absent
Test Files 1 failed
Tests 1 failed | 97 skipped
```

After the fix:

```text
pnpm test extensions/microsoft-foundry --maxWorkers=1
Test Files 4 passed (4)
Tests 125 passed (125)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 39.62s
```

- The same discovery regression passes for Astra, Sol, and Luna aliases. Coverage also checks Responses-only `max`, normalized input names, older model limits, and fallback warnings.
- ClawSweeper compatibility regression: on the prior PR head, selecting an existing Astra deployment changed its saved `{ off: "none", minimal: null, high: "high" }` map to `{ off: null, minimal: "low", ... }` (1 failed, 86 skipped). On the new head, both model selection and runtime normalization retain that saved map and its `["none", "high"]` supported effort list. The focused regression passes (16ms test execution; 41.22s wrapper wall time including worker setup).
- Checked the separate fallback-warning finding through `buildFoundryAuthResult` on the updated head. Known `claude-fable-5` (1,000,000/128,000), `claude-opus-4.5` (200,000/64,000), and `MAI-DS-R1` (163,840/163,840) emit no unverified-limit warning; unknown `gpt-6-future` (128,000/16,384 fallback) does. The warning filter calls the complete `resolveFoundryModelTokenLimits`, which handles all these families; the review appears to have mistaken it for the OpenAI-only helper.
- After restoring stale locked dependencies, `pnpm test extensions/microsoft-foundry/auth-discovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14/14 passed, 158.35s wrapper wall time. Shared worker compilation took 85.89s; the earlier plugin-wide run measured 32ms total for these 14 tests (no added timers/process boots). The existing `index.test.ts` measured 1.908s test execution after moving its metadata cases; its earlier standalone pre-split run was 49.80s wrapper wall time. These timings include substantial shared setup and host contention, not slow per-test work.
- Fresh independent isolated Codex review of the updated PR: no actionable P0–P2 findings (confidence 0.79; diff-scoped).
- `git diff --check`: passed. Plugin reference documentation regenerated.
- All selected `check-changed` gates passed across the initial run and resumed checks: production and test types, lint, formatting, size/suppression ratchets, Doctor contracts, plugin boundaries, dependency guards, dead-code scans, and database/media/runtime/import-cycle guards. The initial test-type check caught a wrong SDK type import in the new fixture; it is corrected and the test-type check now passes.
- GitHub CI for updated head `c144aba855e` is pending; the previous run covered an earlier head. CI test timing is not yet available.

The initial broad typecheck found stale local dependencies outside Foundry (`jose` missing and Teams API 2.0.16 installed where 2.1.0 is declared). `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` restored the declared dependencies without changing tracked manifests or the lockfile; validation was restarted.

Lint initially timed out while preparing SDK declarations alongside other scans. Running it in isolation completed preparation; the final lint run passed after adding required fixture braces and removing the now-unused file-size suppression. The corresponding baseline shrank by exactly one Foundry entry. No timeout or check was weakened.

prs.title: feat(plugin-runtime): support declarative tools and single-attempt completions
prs.body:
Related: #111889

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin authors can use `api.runtime.llm.complete`, but the helper cannot currently expose declarative tool schemas, return structured tool calls, or request zero SDK retries. Plugins that need a deterministic single-attempt decision must therefore bypass the supported runtime helper or weaken that execution contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing host-owned simple-completion path with optional `tools` and `maxRetries` inputs and a normalized `toolCalls` result. Tool schemas are passed to the model but never executed by the helper; omitted options preserve current provider defaults and behavior.

Invalid retry counts fail before model preparation or provider dispatch. The implementation retains the existing authority, model-selection, reasoning, authentication, usage-normalization, and audit paths.

## User Impact

Plugin developers can implement caller-controlled tool loops while keeping model preparation and credentials inside OpenClaw. Setting `maxRetries: 0` requests one provider/SDK attempt on transports that honor the option.

There is no change for existing callers that omit the new options.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.runtime.test.ts`: 24/24 tests passed.
- `oxfmt --check` on all five changed files: passed.
- `oxlint` on the changed TypeScript files: passed.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`: passed.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: passed; no forbidden package-exported subpaths.
- `pnpm docs:check-mdx`: 748 files passed.
- `pnpm test:contracts:plugins`: 926/961 tests passed. The remaining 35 are blocked before their assertions by OpenClaw's SQLite safety guard because this host runs Node 22.22.2 / SQLite 3.51.2; the repository requires Node 22.22.3+, 24.15.0+, or 25.9.0+.

After rebasing onto current `main`, the all-workspace run was stopped after 12 minutes because the constrained host reached 83% process memory and a full disk; it emitted no type errors before interruption. prs.title: fix(agents): keep the skills catalog when toolsAllow is not a narrow grant
prs.body:
## Severity: high — silent, fleet-wide, and invisible in telemetry

Every cron `agentTurn` job that carries a `toolsAllow` runs **without `<available_skills>` in its system prompt**. The model is never told which skills exist or where their `SKILL.md` files are, so it cannot deliberately use one — it can only rediscover a skill by searching the filesystem, or answer from priors. There is no error, no warning, and no log line.

Three things make this worth prioritising:

1. **On the 2026.7.2 line it hits every box.** Since #112483, `applyDefaultCronToolsAllow` stamps `toolsAllow = ["*"]` on **every** tool-using cron job, to record "unrestricted" as an explicit fact. `["*"].length` is truthy, so on that line *every cron job everywhere* loses its skills catalog.
2. **The failure is silent and plausible.** In our measurements an affected run did not say "I could not check" — one fabricated a confident, well-formatted answer for a capability it never queried.
3. **Telemetry reports the opposite.** `buildSystemPromptReport` is handed the **un-gated** `skillsPrompt` while the prompt is built from the gated one, so `systemPromptReport` shows the catalog as present in exactly the runs where the model never received it — identical hash and char count in a failing cron run and a passing chat run. Anyone diagnosing this from telemetry gets a confident false negative. (Not fixed here; flagged so it does not mislead the next person.)

## The bug

`prepareEmbeddedAttemptSystemPrompt`:

```ts
const effectiveSkillsPrompt = attempt.toolsAllow?.length ? undefined : params.skillsPrompt;
```

A non-empty `toolsAllow` is treated as proof of a narrow run. It is not.

`toolsAllow` is three-valued in this codebase — `undefined` unrestricted, a short array restricted, `["*"]` **explicitly** unrestricted — and the rest of the code honours that:

- `hasWildcardToolAllowlist` in `attempt-tool-construction-plan.ts` (sibling file, same directory);
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` normalising a wildcard back to `undefined`, covered by `does not restrict CLI-backed announce runs when toolsAllow contains a wildcard`.

Only this gate uses a bare `.length` check. It also cannot consult `toolsAllowIsDefault`, because `EmbeddedRunAttemptParams` does not carry it.

**Timeline** — the gate is not wrong for the callers it was written for. It predates cron's stamping by about a day, when every non-empty `toolsAllow` came from a genuinely narrow helper turn (realtime-voice consult, system-agent `["openclaw"]` / `[]`). Those still behave exactly as before after this change. Cron later walked into a gate built for something else.

## Evidence

Controlled harness, 20 runs per cell. Same agent, same five-section prompt, same model, same tool set, same skill; the **only** difference is whether the cron job carried an explicit tool list:

| cell | correct | skill body read | attempts at the capability |
|---|---|---|---|
| cron, tool list set | 8/20 | 5/20 | `{0:12, 1:2, 2:6}` |
| cron, no tool list | 20/20 | 20/20 | `{1:20}` |

Fisher exact: **p = 4.5e-05** on outcome, **p = 7.7e-07** on whether the skill body was read. Twelve of twenty affected runs made **zero** attempts at the capability.

## The fix

Rather than special-casing the wildcard, the predicate asks what the gate was approximating: *can this run open a skill body?* A skill is loaded by calling the read tool on the catalog's `<location>`, so the catalog is kept when `toolsAllow` grants `read` or is explicitly unrestricted, and still dropped otherwise.

A wildcard-only check would **not** be sufficient: agent-created jobs persist a mirror of the creating turn's own tools, which is a long, fully-privileged list with no wildcard in it. That is the shape that hit us in production.

`promptMode` is deliberately left untouched — this change is scoped to the skills catalog.

## Tests

`attempt-system-prompt-prepare.skills-catalog.test.ts` covers seven cases: unset, empty, explicit wildcard, wildcard needing normalization, a creator-cap list carrying `read`, and two genuinely narrow lists that must still skip the catalog.

Negative-controlled: with the predicate reverted to the current behaviour, exactly the three cases this PR fixes go red and the four that must not change stay green.

I could not find any existing test asserting the current coupling, nor a doc or CHANGELOG entry describing it — `docs/concepts/system-prompt.md` says Skills "stay available" under `minimal` mode, which is what this restores.

prs.title: fix(gateway): persist durable terminal receipts
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Terminal `agent.wait` outcomes previously lived only in Gateway process memory. A process restart could therefore turn a completed run into an unknown timeout, and exact `sessions.abort` could not reliably distinguish active, completed, and unknown opaque run IDs.

## Summary

- Persist a bounded, owner-scoped terminal control-plane receipt before publishing terminal completion. Receipts exclude transcript messages, assistant replies, and raw model output.
- Preserve execution settlement separately from delivery settlement, including a late chat delivery failure observed by public waits after controller cleanup.
- Recover `agent.wait` and exact `sessions.abort` only after authorization resolves to the exact retained session incarnation (`agentId`, `sessionKey`, and `sessionId`). Revalidate authorization after pending waits before releasing a terminal response.
- Preserve externally supplied and receipt-internal run/turn IDs as opaque, non-empty identifiers, including padded IDs; canonicalize session aliases through the retained owner's agent scope.
- Keep incognito outcomes process-local, retire completed incognito approval/fence bookkeeping, and preserve a fence only when stale-receipt invalidation fails.
- Bound retention and payload size, redact control-plane text, preserve first-owner/first-settled-write semantics, and fail closed on owner or validation conflicts.
- Merge state updates for retained approval IDs even after the 20-item admission cap.
- Resolve the sealed managed-handoff helper from the owning installation rather than the caller working directory, and restore the 64-byte Control UI build-variance guard.

## Storage and compatibility

- Keep the shared state schema contract at v17; this PR does not bump the schema version or rebuild an existing table.
- Add `agent_run_terminal_receipts` to the canonical fresh-database schema and lazily install the additive table/index for existing databases on first receipt mutation with `CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS` inside the repository-owned state transaction.
- Older v17 readers ignore the additive objects. No new schema/content marker or rollback migration is introduced.
- Retention is seven days, capped at 5,000 newest receipts and 64 KiB of terminal JSON per row.
- Explicit maintainer acceptance of this default retention, persistence-before-publication, and sustained-write-failure contract remains required.

## Evidence

Current feature head: `5f3992d9ff`.

- **Red/green review regressions:** approval-cap regression failed before the fix (retained `approval-0` stayed `waiting` and lost `toolCallId`) and passed after it. The added public post-controller-cleanup delivery-failure, source-runtime helper provenance, and incognito bookkeeping tests pass with the production fixes.
- **Focused review-fix suite:** 76/76 passed across receipt normalization (15), Gateway terminal/restart bookkeeping (48), and managed handoff provenance/native staging (13).
- **Final-response authorization:** 5/5 passed. Allowed retained callers succeed; unrelated and replaced callers fail closed; pending waits are denied when visibility is revoked or the retained session is reassigned before the final response.
- **Production completion + restart:** isolated live-Gateway E2E passed 1/1. A production lifecycle start/end wrote the receipt, `agent.wait` observed it before shutdown, a restarted Gateway recovered it, and unrelated/replaced/revoked abort targets were denied.
- **Write failure:** durable receipt suite passed 30/30, including 5 seconds / 20 retry intervals of sustained write failure with exactly one pending terminal, withheld success, and successful recovery after writes resumed.
- **Upgrade/downgrade/reopen:** additive schema suite passed 2/2. A published-v16-shaped database remained readable at v16 with the additive receipt table; the current candidate upgraded it to v17 without losing the receipt and reopened it again at v17. Existing-v17 lazy installation/reopen also passed.
- **Telegram boundary:** `extensions/telegram/src/send.test.ts` passed 277/277, including native `AbortSignal` forwarding and owner-cancellation propagation through `sendChatAction`. The required real Telegram lane was attempted with `pnpm openclaw qa telegram --list-scenarios --provider-mode mock-openai`, but this checkout's taxonomy reports no QA run profiles, so no live Telegram claim is made.
- **Static checks:** targeted `oxfmt --check` passed for all 14 review-fix files; targeted type-aware `oxlint` passed with 0 warnings/errors; `pnpm tsgo:core` passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- **Build:** the restart E2E rebuilt the complete TypeScript/plugin runtime successfully before executing.
- GitHub CI is authoritative for the integrated current head.

## Architecture rationale

SQLite is the repository-owned shared-state substrate and is needed because process memory cannot survive a Gateway restart. The persisted object is a bounded control-plane receipt, not a transcript or reply cache. Authorization remains tied to current session ownership and exact session incarnation before any retained result is returned, including a fresh check after awaited work.

## Known limits / maintainer decisions

- Maintainers must explicitly accept the seven-day/5,000-row/64-KiB retention contract and the choice to withhold completion while durable writes continue retrying.
- The published-runtime compatibility proof uses a database shaped to the published v16 contract plus the current candidate; it does not publish a package or perform a production deployment.
- Real Telegram Test Server proof remains blocked because the checkout's QA taxonomy has no run profiles. The scoped unit transport suite passes, but it does not replace required live Telegram proof.
- No production deployment, live user Gateway restart, schema version bump, dependency change, release, or package publication was performed.

## Worked on by

No attributed contributors were supplied; no agent coauthor trailers are included.

prs.title: fix(memory-core): add memory_get recall tracking with correct workspace and range
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory dreaming promotion never receives recall signals from `memory_get` reads (#94769). Without this, deep-dreaming considers the wrong content for promotion, so important `memory_get` interactions never reach long-term memory.

The original submission also had three issues flagged by ClawSweeper, all addressed here:

- **P1:** Used `cfg.workspace` instead of the resolved agent workspace → multi-agent recall tracking could write to the wrong store
- **P2:** Reconstructed the read range from request params → `endLine` was off by one, and default reads recorded `0` lines instead of the actual returned range
- **P1:** Had lowered the deep dreaming threshold from `0.75 → 0.55` without calibration evidence

## Changes

- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts`: Add optional `workspaceDir` param to `executeMemoryReadResult`; queue recall tracking after successful reads using the **actual** returned range (`MemoryReadResult.from` / `MemoryReadResult.lines`)
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/runtime-files.ts`: Export `resolveMemoryHostAgentWorkspaceDir`
- `src/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-runtime-files.ts`: Re-export through the SDK barrel
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.runtime.ts`: Re-export through tools runtime
- Keep the `0.75` deep dreaming threshold (current main has explicit calibration evidence supporting it) — no threshold change

## Evidence

- Rebased on current `main`: no merge conflicts (`mergeStateStatus` clean at time of submission)
- Recall tracking is **best-effort and non-blocking**: it only queues a read event after `executeMemoryReadResult` succeeds, so it cannot degrade existing `memory_get` behavior
- Range fix verified in code: reads now use the returned `from`/`lines` from `MemoryReadResult` (the authoritative value) instead of reconstructing from request params
- Workspace fix verified in code: uses `resolveMemoryHostAgentWorkspaceDir(cfg, agentId)` so multi-agent sessions write to the correct per-agent store
- Note: focused unit tests for `memory-core` recall tracking were not included in this PR scope; the change is an additive, guarded extension of the existing read path

## Verification

Builds on current `main` with no conflicts. Recall tracking is best-effort and non-blocking.

prs.title: fix(gateway): fence transport admission for a closing generation
prs.body:
Refs #127256 (partial fix: transport-admission slice; the canonical issue stays open for the worker pre-auth and operator-continuation gaps)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway that is directly closed (or is failing post-bind startup cleanup) keeps admitting new work into the generation it is already tearing down — it reports `draining` while it still serves new HTTP user requests, completes new WebSocket upgrades, and answers pre-auth connects.

Measured on a real public Gateway with `configReloader.stop()` gated, while `/readyz` already answered `gateway-draining` and `closePreludeStarted`/`connectionWork.isClosing` were both true:

| Real entry point | Before |
| --- | --- |
| Authenticated `POST /v1/chat/completions` | **HTTP 200 + a full chat completion** — new model work ran inside the retiring generation |
| Fresh WebSocket upgrade | **accepted**, socket then terminated; no 503 |
| Pre-auth `connect` on a socket upgraded before close | **no response, no close** (frame dropped) |
| New `status` RPC from a connected operator | **no response** until transport teardown |

Affected owners: direct/embedded Gateways (including the onboarding session Gateway) and managed post-bind startup-failure cleanup.

## User Impact

Starting a close now synchronously stops that Gateway generation from accepting new HTTP, upgrade, pre-auth connect, and worker connect work, using the contracts clients already understand: HTTP 503 `gateway_unavailable`, WebSocket upgrade 503 `websocket admission closed`, and retryable `UNAVAILABLE` for connect/RPC frames. Callers get a retry signal instead of an outcome-less wait or a socket that dies mid-request.

No user-visible change for managed stop/restart or suspension; already-admitted work still drains under the existing generation owners; readiness/startup probes stay reachable so operators can still observe `draining`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Process-global root work admission is the obvious fence, but closing it from a generic close would poison same-process successors and internal teardown — the issue calls this out. The generation already owns this exact decision: `GatewayConnectionWork.isClosing` is flipped synchronously by `markClosePreludeStarted()`, already terminates new sockets, and already routes close-time frames. This change makes that single generation-scoped fence authoritative at the remaining transport boundaries (HTTP stages/hooks/plugin routes, Gateway and Worker upgrades, desktop/node attach, pre-auth connect, worker connect, and new operator RPC frames) instead of adding a competing owner. Process-global admission is untouched.

`gateway-closing` is added to the protocol reason set with a detector and Control UI availability classification so the refusal is treated as transient rather than a hard error.

## Evidence

New regression test `src/gateway/server-close.transport-admission.test.ts` drives the real public server, gates `configReloader.stop()`, asserts each refusal contract while close waits, then releases the owner and joins the close.

- **Red on clean `main`:** fails at the first boundary — `expected 'upgraded' to deeply equal { status: 503, … }`; with that assertion temporarily removed, the next boundary fails — `expected 200 to be 503`.
- **Green with the change:** 1 passed, test wall **~14–33 s** (one real Gateway fixture; sibling `server.*` close/pre-auth cases cost 4–23 s each).
- `src/gateway/server-kernel.test.ts` 11/11 (direct + public close ordering), `server.request-lifetime.test.ts` 6/6, `server.preauth-hardening.test.ts` 10/10.
- `server-request-entry`, `server-methods.suspension-admission`, `message-handler.suspension-admission`, `plugins-http`, `server-http.probe`, `server-close`: passing.
- One expectation update in `src/gateway/server.node-shutdown.test.ts`: the direct-shutdown mode relied on the new connection being upgraded and then dying with 1006; it now asserts the same 503 upgrade rejection as restart drain (2/2 green).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/restart-unavailable.test.ts` 3/3; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, oxlint, and oxfmt clean on changed files.

<details>
<summary>Pre-fix probe output (real server, close held on `configReloader.stop()`)</summary>

```json
{
  "closePreludeStarted": true,
  "connectionWorkClosing": true,
  "freshUpgradeHttp": "UPGRADED",
  "preauthConnectFrames": [],
  "preauthClosed": [],
  "existingRpcReply": null,
  "existingClosed": [],
  "httpChatAdmitted": "HTTP 200 {\"object\":\"chat.completion\",\"model\":\"openclaw\",…}",
  "httpHealthz": "HTTP 200 {\"ok\":true,\"status\":\"live\"}",
  "readyz": "HTTP 503 {\"ready\":false,\"failing\":[\"gateway-draining\"],…}"
}
```

</details>

Known gaps: operator continuation frames (`question.resolve`, `exec.approval.resolve`) are still not settled during close; worker frames on an already-connected worker keep the existing drain path; the post-bind startup-failure sibling shares the same `beginClosePrelude` fence but has no dedicated test yet.

prs.title: feat(media): polish voice transcript echo for review UX
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When tools.media.audio.echoTranscript is enabled, the echoed transcript is a bare line: no visual marker and no link back to the voice note that produced it. In a busy channel it is ambiguous which inbound message the transcript belongs to, and it reads as a stray bot message rather than a transcription receipt.

## What This Changes

- Keep default echo format as note-quoted transcript (no upgrade behavior change).
- Opt-in tools.media.audio.echoReply (default false) threads the echo as a reply when a native inbound message id is available; graceful fallback to a normal send when it is not.
- Shared preflight SDK (createChannelPreflightAudio.send) now accepts messageId + optional chatType (+ optional prepared replyToMode), populates MessageSid / ChatType fields, and honors echoReply.
- Slack + Matrix bundled callers pass native inbound ids and chat type; Slack prefers root threadContext.replyToId over child message.ts, and forwards prepare-resolved room replyToMode.
- WhatsApp preflight producers forward inbound event.id as MessageSid/First/Full so enabled echoes can quote the source message.
- Reply-id resolver strips only a matching channel: prefix (Telegram-safe); preserves colon-bearing native ids (e.g. Matrix).
- Regenerated docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.jsonl so the public preflight messageId/chatType/replyToMode contract matches the export.
- Matrix QA owned audio restore list includes echoReply so baseline opt-in survives config reset (preservation regression added).
- Precedence: echoReply resolves mode through canonical resolveReplyToMode (channel threading adapter), so Telegram unset defaults to off; respects channel replyToMode off and Slack replyToModeByChatType / room overrides when present.
- First-slot: echo threading only when resolved mode is all or batched. replyToMode first keeps a normal-send echo so the agent response retains the single-use first reply slot.
- check-changed: diffRefsReady stays tri-state — only exact false forces remote hydration for release-metadata lanes.

## Evidence

Targeted suites cover media echo + preflight Slack chat-type/room precedence + Matrix colon-id under replyToMode all + Matrix QA echoReply restore + WhatsApp MessageSid boundary + check-changed undefined/false/true.

## Latest head (2026-08-16 ~16:15Z)

- Head: f588527bad3d9a1201234be34f557c097970928a (f588527bad3d).
- ClawSweeper P2: WhatsApp preflight producers now forward inbound event.id as MessageSid/First/Full (on-message + process-message) with boundary tests.
- ClawSweeper P2: restored tri-state diffRefsReady (exact false only) in shouldDelegateChangedCheckToCrabbox + undefined/false/true regressions.
- Still open: owner approval for permanent default-off echoReply + public preflight messageId/chatType/replyToMode; exact-head Mantis Telegram Desktop proof (prior artifacts on efd8fda42758).

prs.title: fix: settle database publications on their store anchors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Credential authority, session actor settlement, and GitHub lifecycle receipts used raw database handles for publication state. PostgreSQL transactions publish against a separate store anchor, so these keys could miss committed facts, fail receipt deferral, or fail rollback settlement.

## User Impact

These owners now capture, stage, and defer receipts through `sqlPublicationAnchor(db)`. SQLite receives the same object as before; SQL, worker calls, authority checks, and public APIs are unchanged. No migration or operator action is needed.

## Design and scope

Use the existing helper directly at the affected staging, capture, receipt, and custody-registry sites. The old raw-key paths are replaced. The machine-state credential worker and both GitHub mutation/request receipt callers use the same key as their publication owners.

Integration with the newly landed participant API also updates its canonical-repair caller from a function invocation to `.publish(participants)`, fixing the same type/runtime failure observed in CI. No checks are removed or added; credential and GitHub security checks remain intact. There are no newly accepted race conditions.

**Memory escape hatch:** memory schema-extension admission is deliberately excluded. `publishSqliteDatabaseAdmission` checks the anchor's native `isTransaction` state, which remains false during a PostgreSQL transaction. A key swap alone can therefore publish admission before a PostgreSQL commit and retain facts after rollback. The PostgreSQL admission owner must support managed publication scopes consistently across admission lookup, the extension-key registry, and publication before that family can be converted. All three memory files are unchanged from the base. This is the requested owner-redesign escape hatch, not a claim that the fourth family is fixed.

## Evidence

Distinct PostgreSQL-shaped connection fixtures backed by tracked SQLite anchors cover credential and GitHub lifecycle commit/rollback publication. A regression invokes the actual `machineState.write` worker handler and checks committed credential receipts and rollback discard; its SQL adapter delegates to the real SQLite writer. Existing session actor residency/rewrite tests cover settlement. These fixtures prove publication identity, not PostgreSQL SQL execution.

| Metric | Base → candidate |
| --- | --- |
| Warmed all-thread statements | Unmeasured; SQL unchanged |
| Warmed requests | Unmeasured; worker calls unchanged |
| Main-thread statements | Unmeasured; SQL unchanged |
| T1 sites in touched modules | 0 → 0; classification unchanged |
| Production LOC | +70 / -44 |
| Test LOC | +178 / -1 |

The lane explicitly excludes the harness for this SQL-neutral conversion. No statement-reduction or latency claim is made. The published-driver update cell is inapplicable: schema, migration, Doctor, plugin-loading, and service-lifecycle behavior are unchanged. There is no SDK API change.

Formatting, diff sanity, and type-aware oxlint passed. Two isolated Codex autoreview rounds completed; subsequent P1 inline findings prompted the caller corrections and memory exclusion described above. On final head `7da1417b132b7e42e293d194d51b72f6220e4fd2`, CI passed the touched-owner tests, type checks, lint, source/export contracts, Knip, Madge, and database-worker/dialect ratchets. The only failed required test is covered by the operator-authorized flaky-test exception documented below; its result remains recorded as failed.

Integration CI identified the stale canonical-repair call in `session-accessor.sqlite-node-artifacts.ts`: both declaration builds and two participant-repair cases failed at that call. The caller-only correction preserves the new `{ version, publish }` API. Both failing participant-repair cases pass in the focused rerun. The new credential worker fixture also supplies the worker-state admission identity required by the real handler; both commit/rollback cases pass in the targeted rerun. Final-head CI validated these combined corrections.


## Authorized flaky-test landing exception

Final-head [CI run 38489961039, job 115613272936](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38489961039/job/115613272936) failed only `src/gateway/server-close.agent-databases.test.ts`, “releases restart-aborted run leases before sidecar settlement and joins managed SIGTERM cleanup”, at line 774 (`readSqliteDatabaseCleanClose(agent.path)` was false). The existing log records `agent database clean-close receipt: checkpoint-incomplete` for both closing handles before that assertion. All earlier assertions passed: the agent handle was closed, shared state stayed open, and no agent leases remained.

The exact test **passed on latest scheduled main**, head `2597a1aaa98f7d20755a7d65d5d97c770b40c1b3`, [run 38484533627, job 115595039000](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38484533627/job/115595039000), in 4408 ms. Inventory drift puts it in `agentic-gateway-server-isolated-hosted-11` / `checks-node-compact-large-3` on main versus `hosted-12` / `checks-node-changed-compact-small-19` here. This is a flaky-test exception, **not an inherited-main-failure claim**.

Causal review: `sqlPublicationAnchor` returns the identical native SQLite object in this test. No changed publication or receipt key differs on SQLite. `createAgentDatabaseHandleCloser` prepares its seal from database admission, checks for an empty WAL after native close, and releases its lease with either a seal publisher or `uncheckpointed`; it does not inspect the publication-state maps. The lease owner logs `checkpoint-incomplete` for that conservative, unsealed outcome. The close, lease, WAL, seal implementations and failing test are byte-identical to the passing main revision. The participant `.publish` integration correction runs only while copying participant rows during canonical repair; this test creates a fresh session and does not invoke that repair branch. There is no anchor-dependent shutdown defect to fix.

Accepted test edge: the timing-sensitive assertion can observe the supported unsealed outcome after a nonblocking final WAL checkpoint; native close and lease release still succeed, and the next open performs validation instead of trusting a seal. The exact outstanding reader/checkpoint interleaving was not reproduced. Keep the conservative seal checks unchanged; follow up with the shutdown owner on deterministic checkpoint/reader settlement in this test.

The single Linux Testbox request queued and was cancelled; native status confirmed it stopped and its capacity token was released. No Linux reproduction ran, and the skipped macOS case is not passing evidence. The operator explicitly authorized landing a documented flaky failure after this source review when immediate Linux capacity is unavailable. No blind CI rerun was used. All exact-head static and security gates, touched-owner tests, and two Codex review rounds are complete.

prs.title: fix(talk): transcript events lose provider item and response ids on OpenAI realtime sessions
prs.body:
Related: #164456

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Talk `transcript.*` and `output.text.*` events carry no `itemId` or response id on OpenAI realtime sessions, so a client cannot tell which provider item or assistant response a piece of text belongs to.

## User Impact

User impact: `talk.event` subscribers now get the provider's `item_id` as `itemId` on user and assistant transcript events, and the assistant's `response_id` as `parentId` on output text events. Clients can group streamed text by response instead of inferring boundaries from delta order. This PR covers only the metadata half of #164456. The missing `turn.ended` on WebRTC sessions is left alone, because ClawSweeper's review says that half is provider-specific and needs live validation, so the issue stays open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI realtime event handler read `item_id` and `response_id` off the provider events but called `onTranscript` with only role, text, and the final flag. `onTranscript` already takes an optional metadata argument (used for `textMode: "snapshot"`), so the ids now travel in that argument as `itemId` and `responseId`, typed as `RealtimeVoiceTranscriptMetadata` in `src/talk/provider-types.ts`. Gateway Talk control copies them to the event's existing `itemId` and `parentId` fields. The relay used to spread the whole metadata object into its transcript message, so it now forwards only `textMode` and keeps its wire shape unchanged. The provider plugin docs name the two new fields.

## Evidence

- Red first. Test commit 59961bedd32 adds one case to `extensions/openai/realtime-voice-bridge-events.test.ts` (provider events carry ids into `onTranscript`) and one to `src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.test.ts` (ids reach `transcript.done` and `output.text.done`). On the test commit (upstream/main fe6414a2339 plus the tests) each file fails its new case: 1 failed, 33 passed and 1 failed, 25 passed. With the fix on top, 34/34 and 26/26 pass.
- After a rebase onto upstream/main fe6414a2339, the touched area passes: 12 test files, 288 passed, 0 failed (the two files above plus `realtime-session-harness`, `realtime-voice-response-control`, the quicksilver delegation tests, and `src/gateway/talk/relay/*`).
- `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` exit 0 on the 6 changed `.ts` files, `oxfmt --check` clean on all 7 changed files, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` exit 0.
- Not verified: a live OpenAI WebRTC call. The tests drive the bridge with recorded-shape provider events, not a real session.

## Real behavior proof

An AI agent (Claude Code) ran this on one machine, against the base fe6414a2339 (before) and this branch cec0001b17c (after), with the same script.

What was real:
- A real Gateway child process from source, started by the repo's QA fixture `createQaGatewayChild` with the bundled `openai` plugin.
- A real Gateway WebSocket client as the `talk.event` subscriber. It called `talk.client.create` with `provider: "openai"`, `transport: "webrtc"`, and `capabilities: ["gateway-control-v1"]`, then POSTed an audio-only SDP offer to the returned `/plugins/openai/realtime/calls` offer URL.
- The production path from there: the offer handler, the HTTPS call creation at `https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls`, the Location call id, `OpenAIRealtimeBridge` attaching the sideband at `wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?call_id=...`, `OpenAIRealtimeEvents`, Gateway Talk control, and the `talk.event` broadcast.

What was faked:
- Only the OpenAI endpoint. A local HTTPS and WSS server on 127.0.0.1 has a throwaway CA and a certificate for `api.openai.com`, which the Gateway trusts through `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. A `--import` preload sends `tls.connect` for `api.openai.com` to that local port. No Gateway or plugin code was changed or mocked.
- The fake answers call creation with 201, a `rtc_...` Location, and an SDP answer. It answers `session.update` with `session.updated`. It then sends OpenAI GA realtime events in the documented shapes: `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta` and `.completed` with `item_id`, `response.created`, `response.output_audio_transcript.delta` and `.done` with `item_id` and `response_id`, and `response.done`.

After, on cec0001b17c (session ids trimmed):

    talk.event {"type":"transcript.delta","turnId":"turn-1","itemId":"item_user683bf09075","payload":{"role":"user","text":"What time is it"},"final":false}
    talk.event {"type":"transcript.done","turnId":"turn-1","itemId":"item_user683bf09075","payload":{"role":"user","text":"What time is it in Tokyo?"},"final":true}
    talk.event {"type":"output.text.delta","turnId":"turn-1","itemId":"item_asst69c0b6ae6d","parentId":"resp_proofca403bd70a","payload":{"text":"It is about nine"},"final":false}
    talk.event {"type":"output.text.done","turnId":"turn-1","itemId":"item_asst69c0b6ae6d","parentId":"resp_proofca403bd70a","payload":{"text":"It is about nine in the evening in Tokyo."},"final":true}

The fake emitted user `item_id` `item_user683bf09075`, assistant `item_id` `item_asst69c0b6ae6d`, and `response_id` `resp_proofca403bd70a`. Every transcript and output text event matches them.

Before, on fe6414a2339, the same flow delivers the same four events with no `itemId` and no `parentId`:

    talk.event {"type":"transcript.done","turnId":"turn-1","payload":{"role":"user","text":"What time is it in Tokyo?"},"final":true}
    talk.event {"type":"output.text.done","turnId":"turn-1","payload":{"text":"It is about nine in the evening in Tokyo."},"final":true}

`session.ready`, `turn.started`, and `turn.ended` are identical on both commits.

Not verified: a real OpenAI account or model, and real WebRTC media. No browser peer connection, ICE, DTLS, or audio ran. The SDP offer and answer are hand-written, and the provider events come from the local fake, not from a live session. The `turn.ended` seen here comes from the fake's `response.done`. It says nothing about the WebRTC `turn.ended` gap in #164456, which this PR does not address.

## Test cost

`pnpm test extensions/openai/realtime-voice-bridge-events.test.ts src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on cec0001b17c: 34/34 and 26/26 pass. Wall time is 42.0 s cold (mostly transform) and 15.5 s warm. The two new cases take 88 ms and 2 ms.

AI disclosure: an AI agent (Claude Code) traced the dropped ids, wrote the tests and the fix, and ran the gates above: `pnpm test` on the two new test files and the Talk relay suite, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `oxfmt --check`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, and `pnpm tsgo:extensions`.

prs.title: fix(update): name the custody state when the executor binding refuses
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The candidate executor binding check compares about forty conditions across the six leases in the update custody chain (original, spawner, parent, child, plus the occupied slot pair and the retained pair), and it refused with one sentence that names none of them:

```
Failing check openclaw doctor (command-failed): Candidate executor binding does not match its parent.
```

Observed on a Windows install after three failed update attempts. Validation had passed completely — every candidate step green — and then `activating` failed in 2.91s on this assertion, with the run reporting `UpdateCommandRecoveryPendingError`, which reads as "recovery is pending" rather than "this condition did not hold". There was no way to tell a missing lease row from a version, owner, or process mismatch, and the run report carried no lease state at all.

Investigating it required reading the guard, deriving which store it reads (the handoff lease database), finding that database, and discovering that its lease table had no rows — work that the refusal itself should have made unnecessary.

## User Impact

A refusal now reports the custody state that produced it:

```
Candidate executor binding does not match its parent: slot:absent retained:absent legacy:no
parent=absent originalChild=absent child=absent slotChild=absent retainedLease=absent retainedChild=absent.
```

Each custody read reports `absent`, its non-current kind (`unreadable`), or `v<version>/<action kind>/owner:<set|none>`, so the common cases are self-diagnosing: an empty store, a version or action-kind mismatch, and a missing owner are all visible without reading the guard.

No behavior change on the accepting path: the production condition is untouched, and the diagnostic runs only when the binding has already refused. It reads nothing and mutates nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guard refuses correctly; it just does not say why. Since every one of the ~40 conditions compares the same handful of fields across the same six leases, reporting the observed state is both smaller and more useful than numbering the conjuncts, and it keeps a single source of truth for the condition rather than duplicating a 40-condition expression into a second, label-carrying copy that could drift.

The diagnostic reads only values the caller has already loaded, so it adds no store access and cannot itself change the outcome.

### Scope

This does not fix the underlying condition, and it does not make the failure recoverable — it makes the failure legible. The guard is an invariant check on a custody chain that a recreated or emptied handoff database cannot satisfy, and the store lives in the preferred temp directory, which is worth its own discussion; this change is what makes that discussion possible from a run report alone.

## Evidence

Before this change, and after, for the same input (a readable store with no lease rows):

```
before: Candidate executor binding does not match its parent.
after:  Candidate executor binding does not match its parent: slot:absent retained:absent legacy:no
        parent=absent originalChild=absent child=absent slotChild=absent retainedLease=absent retainedChild=absent.
```

The added assertion reproduces exactly the observed production state — the lease table exists but has no rows — and fails before this change for the intended reason:

```
AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw error matching
/binding does not match its parent:.*parent=absent.*child=absent/s but got
'Candidate executor binding does not match its parent.'
```

Checks on this branch (`main` at `4ee88721f04`):

- `pnpm vitest run src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-database-publication.test.ts` — 23 passed, 1 skipped.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` — clean on both files.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — clean.
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base origin/main` — OK.

The guard had no test coverage before this change: no existing case in the suite provokes this refusal, which is part of why the message went unremarked.
