releases.name: openclaw 2026.10.5-beta.3
releases.body:
## 2026.10.5-beta.3

### Highlights

- **Updates leave the Gateway running:** pnpm 12 installs keep their Gateway service and `openclaw` launcher on the durable install path, Windows updates accept qualified Scheduled Task accounts and their own verified driver, macOS accepts protected Bun service commands, and clean service-install refusals no longer leave the Gateway stopped. (#170003, #169059, #170131, #169244, #169481, #169563, #170006, #169662, #169658, #169915) Thanks @xilopaint, @k-sekula, @RomneyDa, @jokerman1302-eng, and @vincentkoc.
- **Stuck updates recover:** updates settle package-activation journals after filesystem remounts or device-number drift, ride out a briefly locked state database, stop reporting false post-install failures after migration, and reclaim retained updater runtimes that blocked npm recovery. (#169410, #170046, #169050, #169352, #168210, #170130, #169422, #170170, #169463) Thanks @patrickschiller, @RomneyDa, @SergeiAug, @angeliti999, and @Warhangel.
- **Doctor keeps credentials and data:** Doctor no longer deletes an OAuth profile when the legacy auth store is unreadable, refuses retired state before migrating the database, imports retained ACP metadata, and restores a stopped Gateway when cleanup fails. (#170256, #168959, #170051, #169918, #169759, #169783) Thanks @Yolo521-bot, @bautrey, and @RomneyDa.
- **Turns survive restarts:** interrupted turns, subagent work, automation turns, steered sessions, and node-hosted turns resume after a Gateway restart, and streamed replies from a killed worker stay in history. (#168650, #169144, #170162, #170252, #170161, #170223)
- **Telegram never replays old updates:** the first start after updating no longer re-dispatches months-old Telegram updates from the legacy spool as new owner instructions. (#170068, #169784) Thanks @angeliti999.
- **Codex and provider replies complete:** Codex replies keep their last tokens and accept follow-ups after a failed thread preparation, ChatGPT turns retry a mid-stream WebSocket close, and DeepSeek tool markup no longer leaks into messages. (#168400, #169431, #167512, #167345, #169728, #159665) Thanks @RomneyDa, @jjjhenriksen, @ericcurtin, @obviyus, @mightyx, and @TOMUIV.
- **Meta Muse Wonder:** Meta users can select `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` with tools, image input, streaming, reasoning controls, and a 1M-token context window. (#170232) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Plugin SDK compatibility:** plugins built against 2026.10.1 and 2026.10.2 can import `createSessionHeaderLink` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/control-ui` again. (#169746) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Changes

- **Meta Muse Wonder:** adds `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` with text and image input, tools, streaming, encrypted reasoning replay, and a 1,048,576-token context window; Spark remains the onboarding default. (#170232) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Device joins:** the CLI and Control UI join command now installs a background node service that can host agent sessions (`--service --session-host`), with a command-only service alternative, and already-paired devices get a working command to enable session hosting. (#168623) Thanks @obviyus.

### Fixes

- **Telegram:** legacy spool updates older than 24 hours are imported as stale and never dispatched, so already-handled messages are not executed again after an update. (#170068, #169784) Thanks @angeliti999.
- **Plugin SDK compatibility:** `createSessionHeaderLink` is restored in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/control-ui` as a deprecated export for plugins built against 2026.10.1 and 2026.10.2. (#169746) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- **Reply delivery:** streamed text from a killed native worker stays in history with its real failure, steered messages behind subagent announcements are no longer dropped as interrupted, blocking questions from routed agent turns reach their conversation, live sends survive delivery recovery, WebChat no longer shows false attachment errors or duplicate file cards, Talk consultations no longer abort right after connecting, and deleting a session records its cancellation before draining retained replies. (#170223, #168077, #170039, #169010, #169093, #170083) Thanks @RomneyDa and @brokemac79.
- **Restart recovery:** turns interrupted while a session was still preparing resume after a restart, interrupted subagents return to their parent with their history, automation turns, steered sessions, and node-hosted turns resume instead of failing with an active turn claim, a Gateway restarts cleanly when a stored cloud worker's machine is gone, and symlinked state directories keep working after a restart. (#168650, #169144, #170162, #170252, #170161, #168907, #168361) Thanks @obviyus.
- **Nodes and channels:** node requests and events no longer fail with "pairing changed" during another device's pairing activity, and channel tools keep working after a config write restarts the account. (#169486, #169575, #159396) Thanks @ceckert and @RomneyDa.
- **macOS app:** fresh app installs authenticate to their app-hosted Gateway and finish setup faster, and the Gateway reconnects automatically after a trusted TLS certificate renewal. (#169403, #168151)
- **Codex and OpenAI:** Codex replies keep their final tokens when a stream drops the last delta, Codex follow-ups work after a failed thread preparation, ChatGPT turns retry a mid-stream WebSocket close with code 1000, and personal-account quota rechecks no longer abort replies. (#168400, #169431, #167512, #167345, #170065) Thanks @RomneyDa, @jjjhenriksen, @ericcurtin, @obviyus, and @mightyx.
- **Models and providers:** DeepSeek tool-call markup is recovered instead of leaking into messages, Claude CLI sessions call registered OpenClaw tools by their MCP names, providers that never send response headers time out, agent runs honor the provider's live thinking levels without reloading catalogs, LM Studio refresh discovers new models, llama.cpp setup keeps aliased models and fails when credentials cannot be saved, and guarded model requests fall back to IPv6. (#169728, #159665, #153032, #168282, #168566, #168039, #150262, #168232, #168973, #87763) Thanks @TOMUIV, @kiranvk-2011, @RomneyDa, @obviyus, @jb-lopez, @an2in, and @georgenaz.
- **MiniMax:** M3.1 models honor their thinking effort levels, and MiniMax OAuth sign-ins refresh expired tokens instead of failing about two hours after login. (#160089, #160037, #160459, #77467) Thanks @NianJiuZst, @Takhoffman, @php737, @masatohoshino, and @rongtianhua.
- **ACP and compaction:** ACP agents keep plugin and OpenClaw tools when acpx is installed as a separate package, and the next turn after native compaction no longer fails while the transcript projection rebuilds. (#164272, #164211, #169583) Thanks @jayzhou2309, @obviyus, and @ajmtrz.
- **Automations:** manual runs keep tool access after the starting turn ends, cron no longer holds the state writer while waiting on the host so updates do not fail with a locked database, and a one-shot automation that fails terminally now sends a failure notice instead of disabling silently. (#168037, #168291) Thanks @obviyus.
- **pnpm and platform updates:** pnpm 12 Gateway services and `openclaw` launchers stay on the durable install link after updates, Windows updates accept qualified Scheduled Task account names and no longer roll back when Doctor re-checks ancestry, macOS updates accept protected Bun service commands, and clean service-install refusals stay recoverable. (#170003, #169059, #170131, #169244, #169481, #169563, #170006, #169662, #169658) Thanks @xilopaint, @k-sekula, @RomneyDa, and @jokerman1302-eng.
- **Update recovery:** package-activation journals settle after filesystem remounts and device-number drift, retained updater runtimes outside `node_modules` are reclaimed and never hard-link recovery files, upgrades keep state ownership across the heartbeat transition, and update-time Doctor keeps its child identities after a failed custody binding. (#169410, #170046, #169050, #169352, #170170, #169463, #169915, #169665) Thanks @patrickschiller, @RomneyDa, @SergeiAug, @Warhangel, and @vincentkoc.
- **Update outcomes:** updates with a running Gateway no longer record false post-install failures after migration, unsafe Doctor recovery guidance is kept until settled, candidate bookkeeping no longer makes older updaters refuse their config repair, and Doctor cleanup during updates no longer fails with nested-effect errors. (#170130, #169422, #170207, #170195, #170070, #168750) Thanks @angeliti999, @hannesrudolph, and @ezimerman.
- **Update database contention:** updates ride out a briefly locked state database, update history writes no longer stall Gateway cron and cleanup, and Doctor recovery captures stay stable while shared-state workers remain open. (#168210, #169283, #170022) Thanks @DonnieFi.
- **Doctor data safety:** Doctor keeps OAuth profiles when the legacy auth store is unreadable, refuses retired state before migrating the database, imports retained ACP metadata after archiving legacy session stores, restores a stopped Gateway when cleanup fails, and removes the `(multiple)` store sentinel registered as an agent database. (#170256, #168959, #170051, #169918, #169759, #169783, #170043, #169764) Thanks @Yolo521-bot, @bautrey, @RomneyDa, and @ourcoms2018.
- **oc-path:** `openclaw path set` refuses malformed UTF-8 before writing, preserving the file's bytes. (#168491) Thanks @wangmiao0668000666 and @Takhoffman.

### Complete contribution record

This audited record covers the complete v2026.10.5-beta.2..463017d7dfa5fcbcb6fff97f32c17e09267c2b5a history: 71 in-range PRs + 0 retained seed-only PRs = 71 unique PRs. The generation manifest also supplies direct commits as editorial input; the grouped notes above prioritize user impact.

issues.title: AutoCompact.check_expired does a full session scan on every 1s idle tick
issues.body:
nanobot-ai 0.3.0. `AgentLoop.run` calls `auto_compact.check_expired(...)` after every `bus.consume_inbound()` timeout of 1.0 s (`nanobot/agent/loop.py`, around line 1032). `AutoCompact.check_expired` calls `SessionManager.list_sessions()` on every call. That method opens every `sessions/*.jsonl` file and parses its metadata and preview. It then calls `_has_compactable_idle_tail` for each expired session, which fully loads the session.

Impact: in a workspace with thousands of session files, the idle loop reads the whole directory about once per second. Session LRU caches smaller than the file count are evicted on every pass. Observed in a downstream deployment with 2,183 files (124 MB): the process was CPU-throttled and idle with no turns. Local measurement: 2,000 session files, 10 idle ticks, about 0.14 s per tick at steady state.

Expected: an idle scan should be bounded, or should use an index or cached metadata, so its cost does not scale with total file count every second.

Environment: nanobot-ai 0.3.0, Python, Linux container. Downstream workaround: an override of `check_expired` that scans at most once per 60 s and caches sessions with nothing to compact.

issues.title: Google Sheets tool for reading and updating shared spreadsheets
issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

Spreadsheets are where a lot of small tracking data lives: expenses, task lists, inventories. nanobot can't read or update them, so the agent can only talk about a sheet if someone pastes the contents in.

### Proposed Solution

A `google_sheets` tool next to the Drive one. It lists the configured spreadsheets, reads a range, updates a range and appends rows. Only spreadsheet IDs added in Settings > Apps are reachable.

Ranges have to be bounded A1 ranges like `Sheet1!A1:C20`. Reads are capped at 200 rows and writes at 2000 cells by default. Values are sent as typed JSON, so numbers stay numbers, and formulas work because writes use `USER_ENTERED`.

It uses the same service account as the Drive tool when that key is already saved, so there is one key to paste and one email to share sheets with. It can also take its own key. Same hot-reload behavior as Drive, and it ships as a `sheets` extra that installs the same Google client libraries.

This builds on the Google Drive issue (#6187).

### Alternatives Considered

Letting the agent download a sheet as CSV through the Drive tool covers reading, but not writing back.

### Related Component

Other (agent tool and WebUI settings).

issues.title: Google Drive tool for reading files from shared folders
issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

A lot of working files live in Google Drive, and nanobot can't see them. Right now you download the file yourself and put it in the workspace before the agent can read it.

### Proposed Solution

A `google_drive` tool that authenticates with a service account. You share a folder with the account's email, paste the key and the folder ID into Settings > Apps, and the agent can list, search, read metadata for and download files under that folder. Nothing outside the listed folders is reachable.

It's read-only (`drive.readonly`), so it can't change anything in Drive. Google Docs, Sheets and Slides are exported as text, CSV and PDF. Downloads go to a subfolder of the workspace and are capped at 50 MB by default.

The key is stored in the config directory with owner-only permissions. Saving the settings turns the tool on in the running gateway; a restart is only needed if the Google libraries were installed in the same step. The libraries come from a new `drive` extra.

### Alternatives Considered

OAuth with a user account would reach everything the user can see, but it needs a consent screen and token refresh, and it's too much access for a bot that only needs a few folders. A Drive MCP server would also work. The tool keeps the folder allowlist and the download path under the existing workspace rules, which is why I'd rather have it in nanobot.

### Related Component

Other (agent tool and WebUI settings).

I have a working draft and will open a draft PR for it.

### Bug Description

```
git clone https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot
cd nanobot
docker compose up
```

The above does not result in a Nanobot that works. It should, that's the whole point of Docker, it's so that the developer can provide users with an image that Just Works without us having to read doc. I should be able to access a web UI at this point. This should be treated as a major usability bug. The current state expects the user to wade through a mix of overwritten doc that applies to multiple esoteric scenarios such as Cloudflare instead of just focusing on getting a working Docker example.

- The resulting container not reachable on any port. `curl http://localhost:8765` and curl http://localhost:18789` both return "Connection reset by peer"
- nanobot-api container constantly exiting and restarting (probably normal)

User has no clue what to next.

P.S. your default Docker images should include curl to help people troubleshoot issues. It's very common for web images to include curl even if the app doesn't need it, it saves the user the hassle of figuring out what your distro is, and the package manager command to install curl. It's only 300KB, no one's gonna care when your image is 1.22GB. Just add 'apt install curl' to the Dockerfile.


**What to actually do next, for people who found this issue via Google**

0- You ran `docker compose up` earlier, so the container is ready

prs.title: refactor(session): centralize state ownership in SQLite
prs.body:
Session persistence currently shares mutable cached sessions across turn execution, metadata updates, and shutdown. This replaces JSONL as the authoritative store with SQLite transactions and routes runtime state operations through a bounded worker pool, keeping storage I/O off the event loop.

A title or goal update can commit while a turn is running without being overwritten by that turn. Reset and deletion revoke old drafts so late results cannot restore replaced state. Accepted writes settle before cancellation or shutdown returns.

## Changes

- Store messages, metadata, provider continuation state, checkpoints, and pending inputs in SQLite with WAL, foreign keys, and `synchronous=FULL`. Metadata and checkpoint updates do not rewrite message history.
- Return detached session views and use explicit operations for turn commits, recovery, imports, forks, delivery, and Dream cleanup. Query sidebar metadata directly instead of scanning JSONL files.
- Check revisions before reusing owner-held history; submit changed message suffixes and keep metadata, checkpoint, and follow-up updates off the message table. Queue mutations through one FIFO writer; readers retain their own connections. Drain accepted operations and stop workers before closing their connections.
- Read detached headers for controls and task lists, and project a committed sidebar snapshot without waiting for every active turn. Discover display files once per query and reuse the metadata snapshot for visibility and workspace scope.
- Bound prompt filesystem work, history snapshots, and local token estimation in background jobs. Reuse skill discovery within one prompt, preserve next-prompt updates, and skip unused run-hook history snapshots. User hooks and runtime state changes remain on the owner loop.
- Drain the session worker on Windows Ctrl+Break and verify normal gateway exit before reopening its database in restart tests.
- Make SDK session operations asynchronous and remove deferred-save/flush behavior. Public interfaces intentionally change without compatibility wrappers; update SDK and CLI documentation accordingly.
- Import legacy JSONL once in a single transaction, leave source files unchanged, reject malformed/conflicting sources, and persist a completion marker to prevent reimport or resurrection of deleted conversations.
- Add ordered, transactional schema upgrades and explicit INSERT column lists. Preserve the v1 schema and reject newer databases before changing persistent settings.
- Keep JSONL support at the one-time import boundary and use SQLite backups for recovery. Remove the former `nanobot sessions restore-workspace` command; session-file export is deferred to a separate UI feature.

## Migration window

JSONL migration is introduced in **0.3.6**, supported through **0.4.x**, and removed in **0.5.0**. A version test requires removing the importer and startup hook at that boundary. Older installations must upgrade through the migration window.

This supersedes the persistence approach in #5580 and includes its event-loop fixes.

## Validation

Current head (`1d80fdc45`) is based on `4497f7ef2`. The latest commit removes the internal session-storage article and its references, keeps user upgrade/backup instructions in the CLI reference, and removes manual prose wrapping. Existing CI tests enforce storage compatibility, transactional upgrades, bounded admission, ordering, and shutdown drain. Focused storage/state/documentation-build selection: 69 passed; local links and diff checks passed. Production code and tests are unchanged from `34e72793e`, whose nine checks passed: [CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38505935250).

Earlier code verification (`414f707df`, based on `328e933d3`): Local regression selection: 4,651 passed, 21 skipped under the CI environment without external Langfuse tracing; Ruff, BasedPyright (0 errors/0 warnings), import boundaries, and diff checks passed. All nine current-head checks passed: [CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38393563059). Built gateway + Chromium verified `/help` delivery, refresh replay, stable sidebar handles, authenticated thread/task reads, and invalid-token rejection. The isolated gateway/browser were cleaned up.

Concurrency comparison against the previous PR head `f782b5485`: three alternating paired runs at 32 active conversations with 1,000 initial messages and 500 sidebar sessions. Keep real warmed token counting, provider retry/stream handling, SQLite usage recording, and 200 ms deterministic model waiting. Median complete-turn p95: 10,981.57 → 2,877.71 ms; throughput: 3.28 → 13.55 turns/s. Median event-loop p99: 3,724.95 → 32.50 ms; independent TCP command p99: 3,378.98 → 8.20 ms. Every measured turn and usage record was checked.

Three subsequent 30-turn-per-conversation runs (2,880 turns total) passed the predefined responsiveness limits: event-loop and command p95 ≤50 ms, p99 ≤100 ms, max ≤250 ms; sidebar/task-panel p95 ≤50 ms and p99 ≤100 ms. Command p99 ranged 7.26–7.98 ms, event-loop p99 43.56–48.41 ms, and sidebar p99 54.98–99.83 ms. The sidebar/task-panel p99 populations are sparse, and one short paired run had sidebar p95 80.88 ms; do not interpret this as a guarantee against every transient.

Stress boundary: 32 conversations retaining all 10,000 messages, with automatic compaction excluded, did **not** meet the same limits. Event-loop p99 was 166.51 ms; sidebar p99 391.79 ms and max 678.64 ms. This is a moderate remaining risk for large histories under continuous heavy concurrency. The verified envelope is 32 ×1,000 on this Windows / NTFS / 16 logical CPU host. Real model/network/tool load and concurrent browser frame rate are outside this controlled test. Earlier benchmark entries below retain their original identities.

Previous rebase (`f782b5485`): rebased onto `328e933d3`, migrated the asynchronous recovery coordinator to `nanobot/webui/recovery.py`, and kept main's generic session recovery and import boundaries. Removed `.agent/session-state-refactor.md`. The measured storage/cache/core execution files remain byte-for-byte identical to `1350196da`; performance evidence retains that original commit identity and excludes startup/import costs. Local verification: 390 focused architecture/config/session/SDK/agent/WebUI tests passed (2 skipped); 161 serial CLI and real gateway restart tests passed (1 skipped). Python import boundaries, Ruff, BasedPyright, and diff checks passed. All nine current-head CI checks passed: [CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38357212464).

Previous CI (`1350196da`): all nine checks passed on that head: [CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38344200639). Limit the Windows full suite to two pytest workers to bound concurrent storage work; preserve Linux auto concurrency and the existing serial CLI/native-process test routing. Windows full suite: 9,221 passed, 115 skipped in 434.90 seconds; serial CLI tests: 160 passed, 1 skipped. Workflow parsing/routing and diff checks passed.

Scope update (`7c8b83bbd`): removed JSONL file export and its CLI/API/documentation surface. Legacy child-session migration now uses independent JSONL input records. Local verification: 221 session, SDK, collision, and subagent tests passed (2 skipped); 160 serial CLI tests passed (1 skipped). Ruff, BasedPyright, and diff checks passed. These local results remain applicable because the subsequent change only adjusts CI concurrency. Earlier validation entries retain their original commit identities.

Previous CI repair (`789c36aea`): wait for lifecycle progress while surfacing producer failures, and run real WSL/PowerShell browser handoff tests in the existing serial Windows process job. Local verification: 92 lifecycle/activity tests passed serially and with four xdist workers, and 57 Windows process/handoff tests passed; the two readiness regressions passed again after cleanup changes. Ruff, diff checks, and workflow parsing/routing checks passed. All nine CI checks passed on `789c36aea`: [CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38340766425). Linux Python 3.11 and 3.14 each passed 9,341 tests (55 skipped) plus 161 serial CLI tests; the Windows process job passed 57 tests.

Workspace-context CI repair (`bd1cd91e4`): updated workspace-context regressions to commit scope through `SessionState` and prepare accepted input before runner checkpoints. Local verification: 42 runtime-control tests and 22 related workspace, injection, and generation tests passed. Ruff and diff checks passed. This commit changes tests only; production code matches the previous schema fix.

Previous schema fix (`bbf570501`) follows a rebase onto `cd2a86371`. Local session tests: 142 passed, 2 skipped; the four new schema compatibility tests also passed on a final rerun. Ruff, BasedPyright, and diff checks passed. The earlier full-suite, browser, lifecycle, and benchmark results below are historical evidence, not fresh validation of this head.

Earlier CI repair (`f34308616`): preserved legacy positional `RequestContext` arguments and updated tests to use owner-backed session state. Local verification: 117 focused tests passed; full Python run: 8,058 passed, 91 skipped; separate serial selection: 212 passed, 1 skipped. Ruff, BasedPyright, and diff checks passed. These results do not establish full NAN-52 acceptance; final-SHA lifecycle, benchmark, symlink, documentation, and browser verification remain outstanding. Validation entries below describe earlier runs, not final-SHA acceptance.

- Local Python suite: 8,030 passed, 47 skipped; serial CLI and real gateway tests: 161 passed. Focused session tests: 117 passed. Slow worker-close and burst-input regressions also passed.
- Native Windows Python 3.11 verified real gateway startup, messaging, restart recovery, normal shutdown, and committed checkpoint recovery after forced process exit. The final gateway/recovery selection passed on both Linux and Windows.
- [Performance comparison](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/5943#issuecomment-5858096332): 12 runs across four conditions; 10,000-message runtime turn p50 improved from 772.91 ms to 54.88 ms, versus 79.25 ms for JSONL with fsync. The report includes weaker-durability JSONL results, full-save regressions, disk usage, and reproduction commands.
- BasedPyright: 0 errors or warnings. Ruff and diff whitespace checks passed.
- WebUI: 93 focused tests and production build passed. Built gateway + Chromium verified command/reply persistence after refresh and authenticated HTTP thread replay.
- Public SDK/CLI smoke verified one-time migration, 50 concurrent imports without loss, invalid-import rollback, restart persistence, snapshot restore, deleted-session non-resurrection.
- Browser verification used deterministic built-in commands; no real model/provider calls. Isolated gateway and browser were cleaned up.

prs.title: feat(update): integrate managed installs and recoverable in-app updates
prs.body:
## Summary

Connect managed installation, exact-version updates, recovery and the WebUI into one flow. This PR continues chengyongru's updater work in #5817 and includes the prepare-only candidate pipeline from #6154. Their commits and attribution remain intact. Coordinate these overlapping PRs before merge.

- Fresh official installs use a dedicated environment and an explicit package-selection receipt, regardless of uv or pipx on PATH. A failed first install retains that owner for retry. Existing installations retain their owner, extras and constraints.
- Installer-managed WebUI starts a persistent gateway. Other installations retain their previous lifetime; `webui --detach` is explicit.
- The WebUI reviews one exact target, prepares a durable job, requests confirmation, installs staged files, reconnects and verifies the running version. Duplicate or lost requests do not repeat installation.
- Frozen workers and a standard-library recovery launcher remain usable if application dependencies break. Explicit repair reuses the saved files and original backup. A restart-only repair does not reinstall the package.
- Unsupported installation owners receive owner-specific instructions. The browser does not choose executable URLs or commands.
- Linux and Windows CI build native platform wheels, use the public installer and verify installed WebUI assets, bundled TUI and a real gateway. Routine checks retain only small reports.

## Latest fixes and review

The branch now includes `main` at `30e43aec8` (#6179). About and version information retain the new shared presentation views. The adapters keep the shared version-check state, exact update consent, readable checking feedback and saved-job re-entry. Both parents' tests remain, with an additional callback/re-entry regression. No installation or persisted-state contract changes in this merge.

The preceding refresh included `main` at `db804ef94`. Conflict resolution retains the runtime import boundaries, image-tool composition, session controls and bundled documentation, together with the updater's runtime admission checks and persistent installation owner. The later PPTX empty-column fix merged without conflict; all 37 document-parsing tests passed.

- WebSocket configuration uses the new pure config contract and retains maintenance admission. Shared text writes use the new file-I/O module; record writes retain the updater's standard-library atomic replacement, Windows snapshot readers and durability options.
- Python and client import-boundary checks remain in CI alongside Windows update coordination and native installation checks. The merge adds no data migration or new update behavior.

- Manual version checks show a readable checking state even when a cached response returns immediately. They hide stale results, prevent duplicate clicks and announce completion or failure.
- Status retries also show progress when the result is unchanged. They only read the original update job; they do not repeat installation.
- Gateway restart waits for authenticated reconnection before reading the saved job. A real access error remains visible instead of being hidden by an earlier reconnect timeout.
- **Settings → About → View details** can reopen a hidden update even when the installed package is already current.
- Recovery commands use absolute launcher and base-Python paths. The launcher retains the original gateway's job and lock scope when invoked from a terminal with a different HOME.
- The real-gateway stop test uses a separate startup deadline and reports startup logs on failure. Normal exit, stop deadlines and installation/data lease checks remain unchanged.
- Candidate verification binds bundled help documents and their source copies to the reviewed checkout. Stale or altered documents still fail verification.
- Atomic-write and session durability tests inject failures at the new file-I/O owners. The refactor removed the old incidental `helpers.os` attribute; assertions for fsync, error propagation and saved data remain unchanged.

## Compatibility and authority

Intentional, documented new-install default: fresh official installs are installer-managed and persistent. Existing venv, uv, pipx, source, Docker, service and Desktop installations are not adopted, moved or wiped. Unknown optional extras are not guessed. The verified uv native transaction is limited to POSIX uv 0.11.16 registry installations; other uv installations use their manager.

The gateway retains control of permission, exact consent, leases, data reservations, verified backups and runtime identity. Browser refresh does not restore installation consent. Repair does not automatically downgrade packages or restore live data. A package-manager success is not treated as proof that the running gateway was updated.

This follow-up adds no persisted schema or data migration. The operator update guide documents restart, reconnection, reopening a saved update and standalone recovery.

## Verification

- Local merge-boundary checks: 141 Python tests passed for maintenance, image hot reload, command queue, settings, update routes and WebSocket restart control.
- Local worker, restart and profile checks: 77 tests passed. Recovery from a different terminal HOME preserves lock exclusion and the original backup.
- Frontend: 36 focused update/About tests passed. The 95-test application-layout suite also passed on the merged base. Touched lint, strict Python type checks and the production TypeScript/Vite build passed.
- Browser review used the production dialog with isolated response fixtures. Immediate repeated failure, checking feedback, stable layout, close and reopen were verified. This is not another packaged installation E2E test.
- Earlier macOS arm64 acceptance used the public installer and performed a real private `0.3.5 → 0.3.6` update, backup, restart and reconnect. A separate forced restart failure was repaired offline without reinstalling or changing the original backup. These version labels were not public releases.
- Prior Windows/Linux CI verified native package installation, assets, TUI and gateway startup, plus platform-specific worker and installer regressions. These checks are not identical to the interactive macOS upgrade journey, and cross-built targets are not claimed as native E2E.

The Windows follow-up passed 81 focused local tests, with one Windows-only check left to native CI. A real source distribution passed application and bundled-document correspondence checks (58 documents); this check reused existing WebUI assets and is not final release acceptance.

After the latest base refresh, 296 focused Python tests passed for import/config boundaries, atomic storage, recovery, maintenance, durable update jobs, real gateway restart and WebSocket ingress/delivery. All 139 focused WebUI tests passed, as did the client import checker (37 passed, one Windows-only skip), WebUI lint/build, Python lint and focused strict type checks. The candidate packaging suite passed after committing the merged source, as required by its checkout-bound source comparison.

The first refreshed CI run exposed eight fault-injection tests that still referenced the old module owner. The same eight failures were reproduced locally; after correcting the test targets, all 112 focused durability tests passed. The packaging/CLI selection also passed all 203 tests on committed source.

Previous-head CI for **81eaceaf5** [passed all nine checks](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38373494122). That historical head included `main` at `db804ef94`. Both Linux Python versions passed 9,818 tests plus 163 serial CLI tests; Windows Python 3.14 passed 9,613 tests plus 162 serial CLI tests (platform skips remain separate). Windows process/installer compatibility, both native installation checks, WebUI and Docker also passed. Maintainer review is still required. Final release packages still require verification from the exact reviewed release source.

After integrating #6179, **154 focused WebUI tests** pass, including About, update notice/dialog/flow, application layout and component gallery. WebUI lint, import checks (37 passed, one Windows-only skip) and production TypeScript/Vite build pass. Browser smoke checks of the shared About view cover update, checking and error states with no console errors; these use gallery data, not a new installed-update E2E.

Current-head CI for **086cbcb57** [passed all nine checks](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38433115585). This head contains `main` at `30e43aec8`; GitHub reports no conflicts and still requires maintainer review. WebUI passed 2,731 tests across 160 files. Windows process checks passed 57 tests, and installer checks passed 74 tests. Platform skips remain separate. Linux/Windows native installation checks, Docker and change classification also passed. The actual native-package test merge has the exact current main/head parents. No approval, merge or release was performed.

## Release gates — not performed by this PR

- [ ] Review and merge the integration, coordinating #5817 and #6154.
- [ ] Select the actual version and stable/preview channel. Existing users install the first updater-enabled version with their original installation method.
- [ ] Confirm the distributor can honor the three-year corresponding-source and relinking offer in `tui/SOURCE_OFFER.md`. Review the pinned runtime notices and source materials.
- [ ] Build the final versioned candidate: five checked platform wheels, one sdist, matching native archives, checksums and provenance. Verify packaged upgrade and recovery; record native and cross-built coverage separately.
- [ ] Approve GitHub/PyPI/channel publication and release documentation. Verify public downloads, fresh installation and upgrade from the previous public version before announcing availability.

No release, tag, PyPI upload, channel publication or automatic daily release is enabled by this PR. The manual candidate workflow can retain approximately 400 MB for one day only with explicit opt-in; routine PR checks retain small reports. No paid macOS runner is added.

prs.title: fix(web): handle case-insensitive image media types
prs.body:
When a server returns `Content-Type: Image/PNG`, `web_fetch` misses its image checks and returns decoded image bytes as raw text. HTTP media type names are case-insensitive ([RFC 9110 §8.3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-8.3.1)).

Normalize the type/subtype for image handling in both the streaming and local extraction paths, while retaining parameter values. One parameterized regression checks native image blocks and the original bytes for lowercase and mixed-case headers, including opaque parameter preservation. It covers direct streaming and the supported connection-error-to-GET fallback using HTTPX MockTransport.

Validation:

- Before the fix: 4 regression cases failed; the 2 lowercase controls passed.
- After the fix: all 6 regression cases passed.
- WebFetch security, Jina privacy, and URL sanitization tests: 64 passed.
- Ruff on both changed files and `git diff --check`: passed.

prs.title: feat(tools): add Google Sheets tool
prs.body:
Closes #6188

Stacked on #6195. This branch comes from my fork, so it can't target that PR's branch; it targets `main` and includes the Drive commit until #6195 merges. The Sheets change is only the last commit (`feat(tools): add Google Sheets tool`).

This adds a `google_sheets` tool for spreadsheets shared with a service account. It can list the configured spreadsheets with their tab names, read a range, update a range and append rows. Only spreadsheet IDs under `tools.sheets.spreadsheetIds` are reachable.

Ranges must be bounded A1 ranges like `Sheet1!A1:C20` (append also takes `Sheet1!A:C`). Reads are capped at 200 rows and writes at 2000 cells by default. Values come in as a JSON array of rows and keep their types. Writes use `USER_ENTERED`, which means formulas work. That also means a value starting with `=` is evaluated as a formula, which is worth a look in review.

Setup is config only, like Drive:

```json
"tools": {
  "sheets": {
    "enabled": true,
    "spreadsheetIds": ["<spreadsheet id>"]
  }
}
```

When `credentialsPath` is empty it uses the Drive key, so one service account can serve both tools. It reuses `_google.py` from #6195, the config model is in `sheets_config.py`, and the `sheets` extra installs the same Google libraries as `drive`. Docs are in `configuration.md`.

To try it: enable the Google Sheets API for the service account, share a spreadsheet with its `client_email`, add the config above, restart, then ask the agent to read or append a row.

Same local checks as #6195, run on this branch.

prs.title: feat(tools): add read-only Google Drive tool
prs.body:
Closes #6187

This adds a `google_drive` tool that reads files from Drive folders shared with a service account. The agent can list a folder, search, read file metadata and download a file into the workspace. Google Docs, Sheets and Slides are exported as text, CSV and PDF on download.

Access is limited in three ways: the scope is `drive.readonly`, only files under the configured folder IDs are reachable (the client walks each file's parents to check), and downloads go through the workspace path resolver into a subfolder with a size cap (50 MB by default).

Setup is config only for now:

```json
"tools": {
  "drive": {
    "enabled": true,
    "credentialsPath": "secrets/drive-service-account.json",
    "rootFolderIds": ["<folder id>"]
  }
}
```

The tool stays off until it has a readable service-account key and at least one folder ID. The Google libraries come from a new `drive` extra. I have a WebUI settings screen for this as well, but left it out to keep the PR small. It can follow separately if it's wanted.

Key loading and API client setup live in `_google.py`, which the Sheets PR reuses. The config models are in `drive_config.py` and `google_config.py` per the config boundary rules, and both are on the import-boundary allowlist. Docs are in `configuration.md`.

To try it: create a service account with the Drive API enabled, share a folder with its `client_email`, add the config above, restart, then ask the agent to list or download something from that folder.

Checks run locally: ruff, basedpyright on the new files, the import-boundary script, and pytest on `tests/tools tests/agent tests/webui tests/config tests/architecture`.

prs.title: fix(api): release idle session locks
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #4883.

Completed API requests with distinct `session_id` values currently leave their locks in the application's registry indefinitely. Store these locks in a `WeakValueDictionary` so idle entries can be collected, while the existing request handlers and streaming tasks keep strong references to locks that are held or awaited.

The production change updates the registry's typed `AppKey`, local annotation, and initialization. It does not introduce expiration tasks or a new lock helper.

## Tests

- Exercise completed requests with 20 distinct session IDs through the real HTTP endpoint, for both streaming and non-streaming responses.
- Extend the existing serialization test to cover default and custom sessions in both response modes, including garbage collection while one request holds the lock and another waits.
- Synchronize request arrival with an event instead of relying on a scheduler yield.

## Related work

PR #4890 uses the same weak-reference approach and is currently open with merge conflicts. This proposal is based on current main, preserves its typed application keys, and adds streaming coverage to the API regression tests.

## Validation

- The new cleanup tests fail on unmodified main (`30e43aec822bdd1d6d770db43a3b27a08667ed53`) because both response modes retain 20 idle locks. After the repair, the API and AgentLoop lock-lifecycle suites pass: **34 passed**.
- Repository Ruff checks, Python import boundaries, and strict BasedPyright pass (**0 errors, 0 warnings**).
- Serial CLI tests: **159 passed, 1 skipped**. Windows process compatibility tests: **55 passed**.
- Initial broader Windows/Python 3.13.6 run: **9,256 passed, 120 skipped, 9 failed**. All nine failing test identities and causes reproduce on an unmodified checkout of the base commit. Six pass on both base and this branch with UTF-8 mode and uv on PATH; three cannot create symlinks on this host (`WinError 1314`). No test exclusions or workflow changes are committed.
- Broader rerun with the corrected local environment, excluding only those three symlink-privilege cases: **9,262 passed, 120 skipped**. Including the separate CLI and Windows process suites, **9,476 tests passed and 121 were skipped**.

prs.title: refactor(webui): separate presentation views and expand component gallery
prs.body:
Add `bun run gallery` as a gateway-free WebUI component reference: source, exports, direct consumers, and 120 live example families covering 159 of 202 current source modules. All foundation modules and all 18 channel registrations have examples. Preview-first navigation, search, related view links, and reloadable bookmarks make the rendered components easier to find.

Separate reusable presentation views from the adapters that own client subscriptions, requests, and service actions. Production screens and the gallery share the same host, pairing, file/web preview, session/subagent, automation, appearance, and version interfaces. Runtime lifecycle, persistence, browser restrictions, and gateway security policy remain with their existing owners. Provider management mounts the actual `ProvidersSettings` dialog and its add/configure flow; remove the unused `SettingsAddButton` and show preset deletion in the `RemoveActionButton` example.

Include `.ts` channel registration entries in the inventory. Shared channel forms use setup snapshots generated from Python channel contracts, preserving field types, defaults, and requirements. Linear, Feishu, Weixin, and WhatsApp share their actual presentation views with the gallery, including authorization, verification, member access, assistant management, and reset dialogs. Adapters retain polling, cancellation, permission checks, autosave, and connection lifecycle.

Move `ToggleButton` into `components/ui` and extract `StreamingLabelSheen` to remove the message/activity import cycle, preserving their implementations. The gallery uses the existing Vite setup, adds no dependencies, and excludes its entry, inventory payloads, and dedicated styles from production bundles. Include channel-owned sources in the Docker frontend builder for type-checking and production channel registration. Refresh the Browserslist datasets in both lockfiles. `webui/COMPONENTS.md` documents component ownership and gallery maintenance.

Validation:

- Focused gallery, provider, settings, host, pairing, preview, subagent, and automation tests pass; the channel follow-up covers 160 focused tests. ESLint, fixture snapshot verification, Ruff for the fixture generator, and the TypeScript/Vite production build pass.
- Headless Chromium renders all 120 examples and checks 317 state switches without gateway requests or runtime exceptions. All 18 channel entries resolve to actual previews; 72 channel layout checks cover light/dark themes at 320px/390px.
- Real provider dialog: add/configure/save, cancel drafts, keyboard/focus return, Chinese desktop, and mobile sheet checks.
- Isolated gateway: host menu, invalid pairing receipt with draft retention, About/Appearance, theme persistence after refresh, persisted chat replay through the UI and authenticated session API, and session details open/close.
- Channel gateway smoke: Email primary and advanced settings survive immediate close and reload without enabling the channel; Linear and Feishu production panels render their actual controls. The isolated runtime is cleaned up.
- Production assets contain no gallery entry or source-inventory payloads.

Model generation was not tested; the isolated verifier used an unavailable loopback provider.

prs.title: fix(webui): make browser notification failures actionable
prs.body:
## Problem

The notification switch can fail without an explanation when the browser lacks support, denies permission, or closes the permission prompt. Task notifications also use the `Notification` constructor, which can throw on mobile browsers.

## Changes

- Rename the setting to **Browser notifications**. Keep it off by default. Show the reason when it cannot be enabled and give the user a next step.
- Send notifications through the service worker. Bound permission and delivery waits. Keep notification errors separate from task completion.
- Add **Test notification**. Report submission to the browser, not confirmed display by the operating system.
- Subscribe to live task events outside the chat view. Suppress repeated events across tabs with a bounded receipt cache.
- Use generic notification text. Do not expose chat content or model errors. Do not report cancelled or interrupted tasks as completed.
- Handle notification clicks on the owning gateway without credentials in the URL. A remote view can reveal only its existing, online connection.
- Reuse the settings components and styles. Update all 10 languages and the WebUI guide.

## Compatibility and limits

The browser preference key and default are unchanged. There is no backend, session format, model prompt, tool schema, or completion-sound change.

Notification delivery now requires an active service worker. A blocked or stale worker has an explicit retry or reload message; there is no constructor fallback. This prerequisite and old-page/new-worker transitions still need real-browser acceptance before this draft is ready.

This does **not** add Web Push. The page must stay open and connected. A closed or suspended page cannot receive new task events. Temporary chats require their original page connection.

## Verification

- Full WebUI suite: 155 files and 2,688 tests passed before the final narrow corrections.
- After those corrections, 72 notification, service-worker, and localization tests passed. Production TypeScript/Vite build and ESLint passed on `3cc84ae73`.
- Checked the real settings components in English and Chinese, light and dark themes, and a 390 px viewport. The unavailable-browser state used a test fixture.
- The separate all-test-source TypeScript check still reports repository test-fixture/configuration diagnostics. The new notification files have no diagnostics.

## Draft acceptance still required

- Actual browser permission, system notification display, and click navigation, including multiple tabs and remote views.
- Android Chrome, iOS browser/Home Screen, and the reported embedded browser.
- Old-page/new-worker and new-page/old-worker transitions.

Mock tests and responsive screenshots do not establish device support or notification delivery. No user gateway was restarted or user notification permission changed.

prs.title: fix(session): preserve completed iterations in runtime checkpoints
prs.body:
## Summary

Preserve earlier completed tool iterations when recovering an interrupted turn.

Previously, restarting after two successful tool iterations restored only the latest iteration. The resumed model request therefore lost evidence of work that had already completed.

## Root cause

Runtime checkpoints contained only the current iteration's assistant message and tool results. Each checkpoint replaced its predecessor, while the complete turn transcript was persisted only after the run finished.

Recovery could consequently reconstruct only the last checkpointed iteration.

## Changes

- **Preserve earlier iterations in each checkpoint.** `AgentRunner.run()` records `turn_start` and wraps the checkpoint callback to include `turn_messages`, a cumulative snapshot of messages generated during the run.
- **Apply existing persistence rules without changing live history.** `AgentLoop._run_agent_loop()` passes checkpoint messages through `_save_turn()` using a temporary `Session`, applying the same filtering used for normal completion.
- **Prevent restored follow-ups from being queued again.** `_save_turn()` returns the IDs of persisted follow-ups, which the checkpoint stores as `acknowledged_followup_ids`. `restore_runtime_checkpoint()` acknowledges them after restoring their messages.
- **Reject incomplete recovery context.** `_checkpoint_turn_messages()` validates message ordering, tool-call/result pairing, and consistency with the latest iteration. `_runtime_checkpoint_is_well_formed()` uses this validation before allowing continuation.
- **Restore cumulative history without duplicates.** `restore_runtime_checkpoint()` materializes `turn_messages` and reuses overlap detection, while retaining legacy checkpoint support and the existing confirmation requirement for interrupted tools.

## Result

Completed tool calls and their results remain available in recovered history and subsequent model requests.

Injected follow-ups retain their position in the conversation. Normal completion does not duplicate messages, and pending tools are recorded as interrupted rather than automatically executed.

## Test

- Added integration coverage using real file writes, fresh session loading, recovery, and inspection of the resumed provider request.
- Covered interruption after completed tools, before the next tool executes, and after the final response checkpoint.
- Covered normal completion, follow-up ordering, repeated recovery, overlapping history, and rejection of an incomplete checkpoint prefix.
- Against the unchanged upstream code, the integration test file produced 3 failures and 2 passes.
- After the fix:
  - Session and runner suite: 277 passed.
  - Persistence, compaction, replay, and recovery suite: 229 passed.
  - These suites partially overlap.
- Ruff: passed.
- Targeted BasedPyright: 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- git diff --check: passed.

prs.title: feat(recovery): persist completed tool results at execution-batch bou…
prs.body:
## Problem

When a model response contains multiple tool calls, the runtime checkpoint is
only written twice: before execution (`awaiting_tools`, all pending) and after
(`tools_completed`, all completed). If the gateway crashes in the middle of a
tool-execution batch, the durable checkpoint still records every call as
pending. On recovery, completed tools — including side-effecting ones — cannot
be distinguished from work that never ran, so they are marked "interrupted"
and the model may re-run them, repeating external side effects.

## Root cause

`execute_tool_calls` (nanobot/agent/tools/execution.py) runs tool batches
internally with no checkpoint emission between batches, so the only persisted
shapes are "all pending" / "all completed". `_runtime_checkpoint_is_well_formed`
(nanobot/session/recovery.py) mirrors that by accepting only those two shapes,
rejecting legitimate partial state.

## Solution

- **execution.py**: `execute_tool_calls` gains an optional `checkpoint_callback`.
  After each batch (concurrent gather or serial tool) it invokes the callback
  with the cumulative `completed_pairs` in stable result order. The serial
  branch now unpacks the `(result, event)` pair explicitly (behaviour
  unchanged).
- **runner.py**: a closure `_on_tool_batch_completed` normalizes each completed
  tool call into a tool-result row, keeps the remaining calls as pending,
  reuses the existing `_emit_checkpoint` path and writes an intermediate
  checkpoint at the batch boundary (phase stays `awaiting_tools`).
- **recovery.py**: the `awaiting_tools` well-formed check is relaxed from the
  all-or-nothing shape to the partition invariant `completed ∪ pending == all
  calls` and `completed ∩ pending == ∅`. Legacy all-pending checkpoints remain
  valid (`completed = ∅`).

## Tests

- `test_partial_checkpoint_partition_is_well_formed` — intermediate state
  (A completed, B/C pending) and the legacy all-pending shape both pass.
- `test_partial_checkpoint_bad_partition_rejected` (parametrized) — overlapping,
  missing, and duplicated partitions are rejected.
- `test_execute_tool_calls_emits_batch_checkpoint_callback` — one callback per
  batch, `completed_pairs` accumulated in call order.
- `test_execute_tool_calls_serial_mode_emits_callback_per_tool` — serial mode
  emits a callback after each tool.
- `test_execute_tool_calls_without_callback_keeps_previous_behavior` — no
  callback ⇒ identical results/events as before.
- `test_partial_checkpoint_restore_keeps_completed_and_marks_pending_interrupted`
  — integration: completed results are materialized as-is, pending ones become
  explicit interrupted tool results.

Full suite locally: 5973 passed, 19 failed. The 19 failures are pre-existing
baseline failures (verified by a revert-control experiment: reverting the two
source files to HEAD leaves them failing; they also fail on the upstream CI
checkout, e.g. `test_runner_reuses_edit_diff_for_summary_and_progress`), and
are unrelated to this change.

prs.title: fix(recovery): persist partial tool progress at batch boundaries
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes #5747.

Runtime checkpoints previously persisted tool progress only before execution and after the entire tool-call set completed. A process exit between those boundaries could make already completed results, including evidence of external side effects, indistinguishable from unfinished calls.

This PR:

- exposes an awaited tool batch-completion callback;
- advances the existing `awaiting_tools` checkpoint after every completed execution batch;
- normalizes each tool result once and reuses the same message for checkpoints and the transcript;
- accepts strict, disjoint completed/pending partitions during recovery;
- preserves completed results while materializing pending calls as interrupted results;
- keeps restart recovery fail-closed and requires explicit user confirmation.

## Non-goals

- No automatic tool replay after restart.
- No exactly-once guarantee for external side effects.
- No new task ledger, recovery subsystem, scheduler, or public configuration.
- No session format or provider-state synchronization change.

## Tests

- `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/agent/test_runner_tool_execution.py tests/agent/test_runner_core.py tests/session/test_recovery.py -q` — 77 passed
- `uv run --no-sync ruff check` on all changed Python files — passed

prs.title: fix(docker): make first-run Compose services usable
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #6165.

The issue reports that a fresh `git clone && docker compose up` produces a nanobot that is unreachable on every published port, with `nanobot-api` crash-looping. Confirmed at the code level and reproduced end-to-end against the committed compose file:

- `entrypoint.sh` only bootstraps `config.json` when `RENDER=true`, so a local `docker compose up` starts with no config at all.
- The resulting default binds are container-local: `GatewayConfig.host` and the WebSocket channel's `host` both default to `127.0.0.1` (`nanobot/config/schema.py`, `nanobot/channels/websocket/runtime.py`), so the ports the compose file publishes (`8765`, `127.0.0.1:18790`) can never reach them — `curl` gets `Connection reset by peer`, matching the issue.
- `nanobot-api` is started with `serve --host 0.0.0.0` but no `api_key`, so the non-loopback auth guard rejects the host and the process exits (1) into the compose `restart: unless-stopped` loop — the "constantly exiting and restarting" container from the issue.

Reproduction log (before this change): gateway healthy but `WebSocket server listening on ws://127.0.0.1:8765/`; `curl` 8765/18790 → exit 56 (reset); api restart loop with `Error: host 0.0.0.0 is available beyond this device but api_key is not set.`

### Change

- Default Compose startup keeps both the gateway and OpenAI-compatible API running. `serve` reuses the existing unconfigured-provider runtime when provider/model setup is incomplete. Authenticated chat-completion requests return HTTP 503 with `configuration_error` before executing a turn, for both regular and streaming requests. Health and model-discovery endpoints remain available; API authentication requirements are preserved. Restart the API after configuring a model to load those settings, as with other configuration changes.
- First-boot Docker configuration uses Python models, JSON serialization, secure random credentials, and atomic `save_config`. A shared file lock serializes initialization when both services start. The entrypoint drops to UID 1000 before initialization, matching bind-mount ownership and the Compose capability boundary. Existing configurations and credentials are preserved.
- Only gateway/API startup triggers Docker initialization. CLI commands, including first-time non-interactive `onboard`, retain their original behavior without an extra overwrite prompt.
- `NANOBOT_WEB_TOKEN` and `NANOBOT_API_KEY` can supply first-boot credentials; generated credentials are printed by whichever service initializes the config. Deployment documentation uses combined Compose logs, leads with startup and WebUI model setup, and documents API setup errors. The image includes `curl`; Render retains its template/environment-reference flow.
- Docker CI checks the actual service lifecycle, credentials, API setup errors, container recreation, read-only mounts, and the legacy onboarding command. Test fixture writes use the container runtime UID so the smoke test also works for non-root CI runners.

### Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix

### Related Issue

- Fixes #6165

### Testing

- Windows: CLI, onboarding, OpenAI API, streaming, attachments, and Docker initializer regressions — 859 passed, 28 platform-dependent tests skipped.
- Ruff, touched-file strict BasedPyright with the test interpreter, Python import boundaries, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Ubuntu 22.04 under WSL: complete Dockerfile build, including compiled WebUI and default WhatsApp dependencies. The Docker smoke test also passed as a non-root host user (UID 1001).
- Generated and special-character credentials: both default services start; WebUI login accepts the persisted credential and rejects incorrect passwords; API health remains available before model setup; authenticated regular and streaming model requests return HTTP 503 with a setup error. Exactly one service initializes the shared config.
- First-time `docker compose run --rm --no-deps -T nanobot-cli onboard` succeeds without an overwrite prompt. Container recreation preserves provider settings and credentials despite changed environment values. Restarting the configured API enables authenticated model discovery.
- A read-only config mount exits with code 1, writes no config, and prints no successful login message. Test containers and networks are cleaned up.
- Authentication and API behavior were verified through real HTTP endpoints. No real model requests or browser interaction were exercised. 

- Windows config checks explicitly read and write UTF-8. The native handoff test keeps its ACL/readability/cleanup assertions with a 45-second PowerShell/C# cold-start budget.
- Remote CI: all 9 checks passed for `dfe3199d0`, including Windows Python 3.14: [Test Suite](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38373244018).

prs.title: fix(documents): preserve empty PPTX table columns
prs.body:
PPTX table extraction drops empty cells before joining a row, shifting values into the wrong columns. For example, a `Name / Q1 / Q2` table with `Alice / (blank) / 100` becomes `Alice\t100`. Preserve every cell position when joining rows, while continuing to skip wholly empty rows.

Adds real PPTX regression cases for leading, middle and trailing blank cells, plus a wholly empty row.

Validation on macOS / Python 3.14:
- Document parsing, read enhancements and search tests: 161 passed; serial CLI tests: 160 passed.
- Ruff, strict BasedPyright and dependency consistency checks passed. Real `read_file` and `grep` checks also preserved blank and merged cell positions.
- Python sdist/wheel build passed with WebUI building skipped.
- Full pytest: 9,359 passed, 14 skipped, 6 failed. The identical command on the original base SHA reproduced the same six failures (five configuration diagnostic tests and one OAuth test).

prs.title: refactor: isolate runtime contracts and enforce import boundaries
prs.body:
Configuration currently reaches concrete tools through package initializers and a runtime Pydantic rebuild, while session recovery and core turn delivery reach WebUI/channel adapters. Client components also contain two initialization cycles. Split those owners and enforce their dependency boundaries without changing configuration fields, wire keys, or gateway delivery behavior. Changes: - Keep tool-owned pure configuration DTOs in adjacent `agent/tools/*_config.py` modules so tools remain self-describing. Remove the runtime import/rebuild fallback and make public config, agent, tool, provider, and usage exports load their owners on demand. Preserve existing public class imports and `config_cls()`. - Keep generic recovery checkpoints/admission in `session/recovery.py`; move the WebUI coordinator into `webui/recovery.py`. Gateway startup supplies WebUI turn policy. Default turn delivery consumes the pure channel address contract for Slack thread replies and durable notifications, preserving public `AgentLoop` and `TurnDeliveryFactory` behavior. Session notification snapshots use the final route metadata. - Separate file I/O, generation/usage values, skill metadata, OAuth catalog caching, automation specs, and SSH process helpers from implementations and dispatchers. Usage persistence retains one store owner. - Extract the shared streaming label and remote context to break the MessageBubble/activity and RemoteInstances/page cycles. Separate localized time formatting from pure format utilities. Retain the earlier mention-type and channel-catalog ownership fixes. - Declare directly consumed yarl, botocore, platform-specific magic packages, and four frontend type dependencies; synchronize both frontend lockfiles. - Expand Python checks to ten ownership rules covering 158 production modules. Permit the pure channel address contract at the execution boundary and prohibit its dependencies on other nanobot modules. Permit the six tool-owned config modules at the configuration boundary and reject runtime or aggregate-config dependencies from them. Inspect literal dynamic imports in `if` conditions as well as their branches. Add client initialization-cycle detection through emitted imports, re-exports, top-level literal require, and eager Vite globs. The scans cover 312 WebUI/channel/shared files and 43 TUI/shared files. - Keep the checks in Python/WebUI/TUI CI and the client package commands, including both checker entrypoints in the TUI source archive. ## Dependency constraints Arrows point from importer to import target. Crossed arrows mark forbidden dependencies; solid arrows mark allowed contract imports. These diagrams show the checked ownership boundaries. Python labels omit the `nanobot.` prefix. ### Python runtime and shared primitives ```mermaid flowchart LR Core["Execution core
agent.loop / runner / turn_delivery"] Address["Pure address contract
channels.notification_routes"] Adapters["Adapters
api / channels / cli / gateway / webui"] Storage["Session storage and checkpoints
session.manager / history / summary / recovery"] Security["security/*"] Agent["agent/*"] Sessions["session/*"] Shared["Shared primitives
file_io / skill_metadata / generation
usage types / automation_spec"] State["apps/* / session/* / config/*"] Nanobot["Any nanobot module"] Core -->|allow| Address Core -- "deny except address contract" --x Adapters Address -- "deny" --x Nanobot Storage -- "deny" --x Adapters Storage -- "deny" --x Agent Security -- "deny" --x Adapters Security -- "deny" --x Agent Security -- "deny" --x Sessions Shared -- "deny" --x Adapters Shared -- "deny" --x Agent Shared -- "deny" --x State ``` Shared primitives are `utils.file_io`, `agent.skill_metadata`, `providers.generation`, `llm_usage.types`, and `session.automation_spec`. The address contract contains only standard-library imports; its guard rejects imports of any other nanobot module. ### Python configuration, transport, and provider contracts ```mermaid flowchart LR Config["Configuration contracts
config/* + config_base"] ToolConfigs["Exact six tool config modules
cli_apps / filesystem / image_generation
self / shell / web (_config.py)
Peer imports allowed within this set"] Base["config_base.Base"] Runtime["Adapters + agent/* + apps/* + session/*"] Aggregate["config/*"] Owners["Tool and channel modules
agent/tools/* + channels/*"] OldBase["config.schema.Base"] Websocket["channels.websocket.runtime"] WebsocketDeps["bus.outbound_events / command / runtime_context
security.workspace_access / session.goal_state
webui.cli_apps_api / forking / mcp_presets_api
webui.sidebar_state / transcription_ws"] Progress["bus.outbound_events.ProgressEvent"] Cache["providers.oauth_catalog_cache"] Providers["OAuth model catalog and providers
oauth_model_catalog / openai_codex_provider
github_copilot_provider / xai_grok_provider"] Config -->|allow| ToolConfigs ToolConfigs -->|allow| Base Config -- "deny except tool config modules" --x Runtime ToolConfigs -- "deny except peer config modules" --x Runtime ToolConfigs -- "deny" --x Aggregate Owners -- "deny" --x OldBase Websocket -- "deny except type-only ProgressEvent" --x WebsocketDeps Websocket -->|TYPE_CHECKING only| Progress Cache -- "deny" --x Providers ``` The six allowed tool config modules are exactly `agent/tools/{cli_apps,filesystem,image_generation,self,shell,web}_config.py`. Peer imports stay within that set. `TYPE_CHECKING` imports are checked too; only the WebSocket transport's `bus.outbound_events.ProgressEvent` dependency has a type-only exception. The exact source/target prefixes are defined in [the Python checker](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/4ecc5edc8b0d0a3cc5df3c54eab14bb871329f77/scripts/check_import_boundaries.py). Run `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` from the repository root. ### Client contracts and initialization ```mermaid flowchart LR SH["packages/client-events/**"] OTHER["Local source outside packages/client-events"] UI["react / react-dom / react-i18next
@radix-ui/* / lucide-react / @opentui/*"] I18N["i18next / react-i18next"] LIB["webui/src/lib/**"] FORMAT["webui/src/lib/format.ts"] VIEWS["webui/src/components/**
hooks/** / providers/**"] BOOT["webui/src/i18n initializer"] CONTRACT["webui/src/channel-plugins
types.ts / catalog.ts"] CLIENT["tui/src/client/**"] TVIEWS["tui/src/app/** / views/**
rendering/** / composer/** / menus/**"] SH --x OTHER SH --x UI LIB --x VIEWS LIB --x BOOT CONTRACT --x VIEWS FORMAT --x I18N CLIENT --x TVIEWS CLIENT --x UI ``` Application isolation also checks both directions: ```mermaid flowchart LR WebSource["webui/src/** +
nanobot/channels/*/webui/**"] TuiTarget["tui/**"] TuiSource["tui/src/**"] WebTarget["webui/** +
nanobot/channels/*/webui/**"] WebSource --x TuiTarget TuiSource --x WebTarget ``` Local imports from shared event contracts stay within `packages/client-events/`. Boundary checks include type imports. Each production scan includes shared event contracts; the WebUI scan also includes channel-owned frontend modules. Both clients reject initialization cycles through emitted static imports/re-exports, top-level literal `require`, and eager literal Vite globs. Erased type imports, declaration files, deferred dynamic imports, function-local `require`, and lazy globs do not create initialization edges. The exact rules are defined in [the client checker](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/4ecc5edc8b0d0a3cc5df3c54eab14bb871329f77/scripts/check_client_import_boundaries.mjs). Run `bun run check:imports` and `bun run test:imports` from `webui/` or `tui/`. Validation recorded for head `4ecc5edc8`: - Turn delivery, session persistence, subagent, notification, CLI, and architecture regressions: 391 passed / 1 skipped. The public default `AgentLoop.from_config` path preserves Slack thread routing for a late subagent result, and default turn delivery retains durable channel addresses. - Ruff, strict BasedPyright on the touched runtime files (0 errors), and `git diff --check` pass. The Python import checker passes ten rules across 158 production files. Independent clean-process probes confirm that the address contract loads without nanobot runtime modules and that custom route policies persist and deliver idle notifications to the final channel address. - [Current-head CI for `4ecc5edc8`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38351543609) is tracked separately from the local results above. Earlier linked CI runs apply only to their named historical heads. Documentation-only head `740218ddb` simplifies `.agent/design.md`, retaining ownership guidance, checker entrypoints, and coverage limits. On that head, runtime code, dependencies, checker rules, and tests are unchanged from `21219a25b`; the code-validation evidence below is reused for those unchanged files. [GitHub CI for head `740218ddb`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38342786335) is tracked separately. Validation recorded for code head `21219a25b`: - Configuration, tool discovery, plugin entry points, image hot reload, and import-boundary regressions: 217 passed / 1 skipped, including 45 architecture tests. - Fresh-process configuration validation and schema generation keep tool execution modules unloaded; existing class imports and `config_cls()` return the tool-owned models. - The Python import checker passes nine rules across 158 production files. Ruff, strict BasedPyright on the touched Python files (0 errors), and `git diff --check` pass. - [GitHub CI for head `21219a25b`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38339593163) is tracked separately from the historical results below. Validation recorded for original head `2780c1777`: - All nine [GitHub CI checks](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38224208065) pass on head `2780c1777`: Python 3.11, Linux/Windows Python 3.14, Windows process compatibility, WebUI, Linux/Windows TUI, Docker, and change classification. - Python regression run: 9,130 passed / 120 skipped, with 84.01% coverage. Separate CLI/channel checks: 291 passed / 1 skipped; serial Windows process checks: 55 passed. Final exec/config contract checks: 75 passed / 2 skipped. - All 2,660 WebUI tests and all 258 TUI tests pass. On this Windows machine, the WebUI run uses two workers and a verification-only 5-second Testing Library wait for cold lazy-module transforms; no repository timeout or assertion is weakened. - Strict BasedPyright, Ruff, ESLint, both client guards, WebUI production build, TUI type check, and native Windows TUI build pass. Checker tests: 38 WebUI passes; 37 TUI passes with the WebUI-only glob case skipped. - Grimp/NetworkX and dependency-cruiser confirm the removed reverse paths and component cycles; eager Vite edges are expanded separately. Nine clean-process Python import/config probes pass: importing Config loads 20 nanobot modules instead of 136, and importing Tool loads 4 instead of 136. - Manifest-aware deptry reports no missing/transitive/dev dependency violations; Knip reports no dependency issues. The all-extras/channel environment passes pipdeptree and uv dependency consistency checks. Data packages, SDK extras, and compatibility constraints flagged as unused are retained with their existing purpose. - The extracted TUI source archive installs from the frozen lockfile and runs both import-check commands. The WebUI frozen install and npm lock metadata are consistent. - Built WebUI through an isolated real gateway: a local deterministic model streams a reply, refresh replays it, authenticated thread API returns a completed turn, usage settings work, language changes render, and remote connection management opens. Browser application console is clean; no real channel credentials or external model calls are used. Three existing file-preview symlink cases cannot run on this Windows account because creating symlinks requires an unavailable OS privilege. The first full run reached that error before exercising their assertions; those cases are excluded from the successful local rerun and remain covered by CI. Validation recorded for head `fa0371d4d`: - All 39 Python import-boundary tests pass, including the conditional-import CLI regressions and the production repository scan. Ruff and `git diff --check` pass. - Rebase verification on `main@cd2a86371` passes the configuration suite (120 passed / 1 skipped), image tool/hot-reload/provider tests (106 passed), and recovery/routing/restart tests (124 passed). The extracted image configuration preserves `extra_headers` and `extra_body` from main. - Both client import checkers and checker tests, the WebUI production build, and the TUI type check pass. App layout and ThreadComposer tests: 244 passed. - [GitHub CI for head `fa0371d4d`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38335411756) is tracked separately from the original-head results above. These are responsibility checks and a client initialization graph, not a complete execution DAG. The remaining Python late-import pairs are within shell/process execution, CLI startup, desktop startup, and the Responses transport factory. Deferred channel UI composition is retained.
