prs.title: fix(pm): anchor mcp/homeassistant/sms/uvloop extras so legacy venv migration carries them
prs.body:
Fixes #123770

## Problem

`pm/extras.py::legacy_selection()` only carries extras listed in `ANCHORS` when migrating a main-era venv to the PM-managed environment. The `mcp` extra (and `homeassistant`, `sms`, `uvloop`) were missing from `ANCHORS`, so an install with MCP servers configured lost the mcp SDK on migration. Every HTTP MCP server then failed with:

```
MCP server 'X' requires HTTP transport but mcp.client.streamable_http is not available
```

and `hermes pm status` reported `"already in sync"` because the recorded selection never included `mcp` — the SDK was never reinstalled and the failure persisted across restarts.

## Fix

Add anchors for the real feature extras missing from the table:

- `"mcp": "mcp"` — the MCP client SDK (the reported bug)
- `"homeassistant": "aiohttp"`, `"sms": "aiohttp"` — same bug class (aiohttp is not a core dependency)
- `"uvloop": "uvloop"` — same bug class

Aggregate/alias extras (`all`, `termux`, `termux-all`) and empty aliases (`cron`, `pty`, `nemo-relay`) are intentionally left out.

## Validation

- Extended `tests/pm/test_extras.py::test_legacy_selection_carries_extras_the_main_era_venv_lazily_installed` to assert `mcp` is carried over.
- `tests/pm/test_extras.py` + `tests/pm/test_feature_inventory.py`: 20 passed.
- Production observation: after `hermes pm install --extra mcp` on the affected install, 6/6 non-OAuth MCP servers reconnected (105 tools registered); the two OAuth servers only needed interactive re-auth of expired tokens.

prs.title: fix(checkpoints): skip an untraversable working dir instead of logging a git traceback
prs.body:
## Problem

`tools/checkpoint_manager.py::_run_git()` guarded a **missing** working directory
and a **non-directory** working directory, but not one that exists and is a
directory yet **cannot be traversed by this process**. In that case
`subprocess.run(..., cwd=normalized_working_dir)` raises `PermissionError`
**before git is even exec'd**. It fell through to the generic
`except Exception as exc:` handler and was logged as an `Unexpected git error`
with `exc_info=True` on **every** snapshot, while the checkpoint was silently
dropped.

Because `_run_git()` is the single chokepoint for every checkpoint git call
(`add -A`, `rev-parse`, `read-tree`, `diff-index`, `ls-files`, `commit`, `gc`),
the noisy failure repeated for each call in a snapshot.

## Reproduction

Gateway running as a non-root user with a session whose working dir is a
root-owned `0700` path such as `/root`:

```
ERROR tools.checkpoint_manager: Unexpected git error running /usr/bin/git add -A: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root'
```

Minimal demonstration of the failing call path:

```python
import os, subprocess
p = "/root"
assert os.path.exists(p) and os.path.isdir(p)    # both guards in _run_git() pass
assert os.access(p, os.R_OK | os.X_OK) is False  # ...yet it is not traversable
subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=p)
# -> PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root'
```

## Fix

Treat an inaccessible working directory like a missing one:

1. Pre-flight `os.access(dir, os.R_OK | os.X_OK)` in `_run_git()`, mirroring the
   existing `exists()` / `is_dir()` guards, and skip quietly (debug level).
2. Catch `PermissionError` from the subprocess launch explicitly as
   defence-in-depth (covers a TOCTOU race or an ACL that `os.access` cannot
   see), instead of letting it surface as an `Unexpected git error` traceback.

This is a whole-bug-class fix: it covers every git call routed through
`_run_git()`.

## Validation

- **Regression tests** `test_run_git_skips_inaccessible_workdir_quietly` and
  `test_run_git_handles_permission_error_from_launch`. Both **fail on unpatched
  code** with the exact production signature
  (`Unexpected git error running /usr/bin/git add -A: [Errno 13] Permission denied`)
  and **pass with the fix**.
- `tests/tools/test_checkpoint_manager.py`: **58 passed**.
- **Live E2E** as the `hermes` user against `/root`:
  `_run_git(["add", "-A"], store, "/root")` →
  `(False, "", "working directory is not accessible: /root")` with a single
  `DEBUG` line and no `ERROR`.

Fixes #133096

prs.title: fix(migration): resolve SecretRef channel tokens instead of dropping them (#131863)
prs.body:
Addresses part of #131863 (the SecretRef half; the cron-archive half is untouched).

## Problem

The OpenClaw→Hermes migration accepts channel credentials as either a plain
string or a `SecretRef` (`{"source": "env", "id": "TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN"}`) — the
*normal* shape for any install using OpenClaw's secret store. Three channel
migration steps only kept a value when `isinstance(value, str)`:

- `migrate_secret_settings` (telegram `botToken`)
- `migrate_discord_settings` (`token`)
- `migrate_slack_settings` (`botToken`, `appToken`)

A `SecretRef` therefore failed the `isinstance(..., str)` check and was silently
dropped. With `--migrate-secrets` the run still records the `secret-settings`
step as `skipped: "No allowlisted Hermes-compatible secrets found"` and the
`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` / `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` / `SLACK_*_TOKEN` keys never reach the
target `.env` — a non-crashing migration that quietly loses the bot tokens.

## Fix

The resolver for exactly this case already existed — `_resolve_channel_secret`
(it calls `resolve_secret_input`, the same helper the provider-key path uses at
`openclaw_to_hermes.py:1678`) — but it had **no caller** anywhere in the script.
Wire it into the three channel-secret migrations so an env-backed `SecretRef`
(or a `"${VAR}"` template) is resolved to its plain value before the string
check. `resolve_secret_input` only resolves `source: "env"` (and templates);
`file`/`exec`-backed refs still return `None`, so those remain un-auto-migratable
exactly as documented — the change does not invent a value for them and is
otherwise behaviour-preserving (a plain string token still migrates verbatim).

## Validation

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_openclaw_migration.py` → **22 passed**.

Two tests added to `tests/skills/test_openclaw_migration.py`:

- `test_secretref_channel_tokens_are_resolved_not_silently_dropped` drives the
  real migration (`execute=True`, real `.env` write, no mocks) with env-backed
  `SecretRef`s for telegram/discord/slack and asserts each token lands in the
  target `.env`. It **fails on `main`** (the `SecretRef` is dropped, so no `.env`
  is written: `FileNotFoundError: .../.hermes/.env`) and passes with the fix.
- `test_unresolvable_secretref_stays_skipped_and_plain_tokens_still_migrate`
  pins the invariant: a `file`-backed ref is not invented, and a plain string
  token still migrates verbatim.

Sibling migration suites unchanged: `scripts/run_tests.sh
tests/skills/test_openclaw_migration_hardening.py
tests/hermes_cli/test_setup_openclaw_migration.py` → **20 passed**.

prs.title: fix(agent): re-fold the active /goal and its contract at the compaction boundary
prs.body:
## Problem

`/goal` state lives in `state_meta`, not in the transcript. The model sees it only as a user message — the kickoff, and the `[Continuing toward your standing goal]` prompt queued between turns. The todo list, by contrast, is re-folded into the transcript at **every** compaction boundary (`_fold_todo_snapshot`).

So whether the goal and its completion contract survive a compaction depends on where the goal text happens to sit when the cut lands:

- **Active turn opened by a goal prompt:** survives (the active request is kept in the tail).
- **Active turn opened by something else** (a real user interjection, a busy-steer, a `/heartbeat` tick, a `/loop` tick while the goal is parked): after a mid-turn compaction the goal and contract exist only inside the summary's **lossy free-text `## Goal` section**. `agent/context_compressor.py` writes that slot as model-authored prose ("What the user is trying to accomplish overall"), so **Verification, Constraints and Stop condition are routinely paraphrased or dropped** for the rest of the turn — exactly the fields the judge later enforces. Losing them lets the agent drift from the contract that decides continuation.
- **Gateway hygiene compaction** (in place, between turns, before the next message is appended): if that next message is not a goal continuation, the turn starts from a summary where the goal is free text only.
- **Third-party context engines:** any engine that does not reproduce the built-in active-request anchor drops the goal.

Reported as #133643.

## Fix

Give `/goal` the todo list's own machinery.

- `hermes_cli/goals.py`: factor the goal+contract body out of `GoalManager.next_continuation_prompt` into a shared `_goal_body_block()`, so the continuation prompt and the preserved block render the same contract fields from one place. Add `render_preserved_goal_block()` (active + not parked only) under a distinct, non-imperative header `[Your standing /goal was preserved across context compression]`, and `goal_is_parked()`.
- `agent/conversation_compression_goal_fold.py` (new topical sibling, kept out of the `conversation_compression` facade to respect its line cap): `fold_goal_snapshot()` mirrors `_fold_todo_snapshot` — strips any earlier preserved goal block (refresh, never stack), folds the live active-goal block into the trailing user row the todo fold already produced (so two synthetic user rows never sit adjacent), and appends a flagged row only when the tail is not a user row.
- `agent/conversation_compression.py`: the compaction commit boundary now calls `fold_state_snapshots()` (todo fold + goal fold) instead of the bare todo fold; the goal row is registered as synthetic (`_goal_snapshot_synthetic` flag + header prefix) so provenance/scaffolding classification (#69292) is unchanged and the row is never treated as human intent.
- Folds **nothing** for a goal the judge marked done, a paused/cleared goal, or a parked (waiting) goal — no resurrection (#34197). Skipped on a continuation-opened turn, where the goal is already verbatim in the request.

Carve-out respected: `next_continuation_prompt` output is byte-for-byte unchanged (only refactored through `_goal_body_block`).

## Why not a whole new mechanism

The todo list already solves exactly this ("state that lives outside the transcript but must survive compaction"); the goal is the one remaining such state. Reusing the fold keeps one code path and one set of provenance flags.

## Validation

- `tests/agent/test_goal_snapshot_fold.py` (new, 11 tests): contract carried verbatim; refresh-not-stack across two boundaries; merge into a trailing real user row (provenance stays real); done/paused/cleared/parked fold nothing; no duplicate on a continuation turn; an unavailable store preserves the pending snapshot; header literal stays in sync; and an **end-to-end** run through `compress_context` asserting the active goal + contract survives a compaction exactly once.
- Regression: `tests/hermes_cli/test_goals.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_goal_command.py`, `tests/gateway/test_goal_status_notice.py`, `tests/gateway/test_goal_resume_restart.py`, `tests/agent/test_context_compressor_zero_user_provenance.py`, `tests/agent/test_compression_rotation_state.py`, `tests/agent/test_skill_todo_retention_parity.py`, `tests/agent/test_in_place_compaction.py`, `tests/agent/test_compression_boundary.py`, `tests/agent/test_salvage_grown_transcript.py` — **all pass** (≈230 tests).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` (per-file isolation, CI parity); `python scripts/check` → 11 checks, ok (ruff + code-health ratchet clean; the new module keeps `conversation_compression.py` at its line cap).

fixes #133643

prs.title: docs(cli): list the five missing top-level commands and document `hermes verify`
prs.body:
## Problem

The CLI reference's **Top-level commands** table is the index readers use to discover
commands, but five commands that `hermes --help` lists are missing from it:
`worktree`, `browser`, `verify`, `monitoring` and `vault`. Of those, `hermes verify`
had **no documentation anywhere** in `website/docs`, so its phases, flags and exit
codes were undiscoverable.

Reproduction:

```bash
$ hermes --help | grep -E 'browser|monitoring|vault|verify|worktree'
    browser             Real-profile browsing helpers (close a browser locking ...
    monitoring          Inspect gateway monitoring (health & diagnostics export)
    vault               Manage the local encrypted autofill vault (add/list/rm ...
    verify              Detect a project's run recipe and smoke-test it
    worktree            Audit and reclaim accumulated git worktrees and merged branches

$ grep -n 'hermes verify' website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md
(no match)
```

The same table also carried one garbled row: the `pause` / `resume` entry read
"no new cron fires (…), kanban dispatch or gateway turns start until resumed",
which says the opposite of what the command does.

## The fix

- Add the five missing rows to the Top-level commands table. Four have topical pages
  (`cli.md#worktree-cleanup`, `features/browser.md`, `developer-guide/gateway-monitoring.md`,
  `features/credential-vault.md`), so the rows link to them rather than duplicating them.
- Add a full `## hermes verify` section: what it detects, the phase order
  (bootstrap → build → test → start → readiness → teardown), every flag, the exit
  codes, and examples.
- Repair the `pause` / `resume` row (`neither kanban dispatch nor new gateway turns
  start until resumed`) and note `hermes pause --reason <text>`.

## Why not another approach

No new page was needed: the four non-`verify` commands already have authoritative
topical pages, and the reference page's job is the command index. `verify` is the
only one with no page anywhere, so it gets the section.

## Validation

```bash
$ hermes verify --help        # every flag row matches the parser
$ hermes verify /tmp/verifydemo --detect-only   # -> {"source":"detected","recipe":{...}}, exit 0
$ hermes verify /tmp/emptyproj                  # -> "No recognizable project found", exit 1
$ hermes verify /tmp/does-not-exist-xyz         # -> "error: not a directory", exit 2
$ python3 website/scripts/check_doc_links.py    # -> OK: no route-style links ... (CI docs-site check)
```

Exit codes `0` / `1` / `2` documented in the new section were reproduced with the
three commands above. `check_doc_links.py` is the same script the `Docs Site Checks`
workflow runs.

prs.title: Stable publish advances feeds and Docker instead of failing on the existing head
prs.body:
Publishing a stable release now advances its desktop feeds and Docker aliases instead of failing after the GitHub release goes public.

## Symptom
`Stable Release Publication` for v0.22.0 (run 38505669816) made the release public, then failed at `[2/2] Advance channels`:

```
R2 PUT /hermes-agent-artifacts/releases/stable/release-candidates.json -> 412 PreconditionFailed
ChannelConflict: Channel write conflict: releases/stable/release-candidates.json
```

Result: `v0.22.0` is public on GitHub, while the R2 stable head (`releases/stable/release-candidates.json`, last modified Oct 12), the macOS stable feed and Docker `stable`/`latest`/`stable-desktop`/`latest-desktop` all still point at v0.21.7.

## Root cause
`advance_stable` wrote the stable head with no ETag, which `R2ChannelStore.put` sends as `If-None-Match: *` (create-only). The head exists after the first bundled release (v0.21.7 created it), so every later bundled publish is refused. The existing test only ever wrote the head into an empty store, or re-wrote identical bytes (which the store treats as success).

## Change
- `scripts/releases/channel_releases.py`: read the current head and write under its ETag (`If-Match`); create-only stays for a store with no head.
- `tests/scripts/test_release_channels.py`: the receipts test seeds a previous release's head and asserts the head ends up as the accepted release.

## Validation
| Check | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_accepted_release_receipts_feed_the_protected_head_without_rebuilding` with a pre-existing head | fails (ChannelConflict instead of the fixture error) | passes |
| `tests/scripts/test_release_{channels,sequencer,artifacts}.py`, `test_stable_release.py` | | 94 passed |

## After merge
Publication checks out the default branch, so once this merges, one owner-run `Stable Release Publication` dispatch for 0.22.0 should advance the head, feeds and Docker aliases. No re-cut is needed.

## Infographic
![Release channels advance](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aae4bcf/Qo9TrjYcaZgk6vYSOoSId_vEk6eM6V.png)

prs.title: fix(plugins): disk-cleanup never deletes protected or out-of-scope tracked paths
prs.body:
Fixes #135891.

## Problem

`plugins/disk-cleanup/disk_cleanup.py` `quick()` re-validates the stored category only for the `test` and `cron-output` cases, then falls through to `_delete_item`. Two gaps let a stored `tracked.json` entry delete something it must not:

- `_is_protected_dir()` guards **directories** only. A durable top-level HERMES_HOME **file** — `config.yaml`, `.env`, `auth.json`, `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `SOUL.md` — is not covered by it, and `_is_protected_cron_path()` covers only the cron control plane. `track()` accepts such a file (`is_safe_path()` allows anything under HERMES_HOME), so a `track ~/.hermes/config.yaml temp` (or any pre-fix entry) is unlinked by `quick()` after the 7-day temp window.
- `quick()` never re-checks scope. An entry whose path is now a symlink, or no longer resolves inside HERMES_HOME / `/tmp/hermes-*`, is deleted regardless.

Reproduction (failing on `main`, `dce1e9b`): `track(config.yaml, "temp")` returns `True`, and a stored `{"path": "…/.hermes/config.yaml", "category": "temp"}` entry made 30 days ago is unlinked by `quick()`. Same for symlinked and out-of-scope entries.

## Fix

Add one predicate, `_is_protected_scope(p)`, used consistently at every point that reads stored metadata:

- `quick()` / `dry_run()` — an entry that is now a symlink, resolves outside scope, or is a durable top-level HERMES_HOME file is **dropped from tracking, not deleted** (same disposition as the existing stale-entry/protected-dir paths).
- `track()` — refuses the same set up front, so a protected file never enters `tracked.json`.

The protected-file check reuses `_NEVER_TRACK_TOP_LEVEL` (which `guess_category()` already honours) matched at `len(rel.parts) == 1`, i.e. HERMES_HOME-root files only. It deliberately does **not** widen to files nested under durable trees, because `test_stale_cache_dir_entry_is_skipped_but_its_old_files_still_age_out` establishes that only a protected **directory** survives while ordinary `temp` files under it still age out — that behaviour is preserved (see the control test).

Why not refuse via `guess_category() != category` in `quick()`: that would drop every manually tracked `temp` entry outside `cache/` (`guess_category` returns `None` for them), breaking the manual `track` API. The explicit scope predicate targets only the unsafe class.

## Validation

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/test_disk_cleanup_plugin.py` — **51 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped** (was 36; +15 new cases in `TestProtectedPathsNeverDeleted`).
- New tests fail on unmodified `main` (14 failures: protected-file `track` refusal, protected-file stale entry, symlink entry, out-of-scope entry) and pass after the fix; the control (`temp` file under `cache/` still pruned) passes in both.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/test_multiplex_plugin_cache_scope.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd_list.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd_category_discovery.py` — 22 passed, 0 failed.

prs.title: fix(mcp): a shutdown-race scheduling error is teardown, not a server failure
prs.body:
## Problem

A gateway restart parks every managed MCP server:

```
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'virlo' failed after 5 reconnection attempts, parking; will self-probe
every 300s until it recovers (state: degraded → parked): RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after shutdown
```

Production observation (long-lived gateway, 7 remote MCP servers, 48h window of `errors.log`):

- 77 identical park WARNINGs, one per server per restart, all clustered inside gateway restarts (e.g. a restart at 13:06 produced the seven `virlo`/`cloudflare`/`x-docs`/`aixbt`/`blockscout`/`crypto-com`/`vfat` parks between 13:07 and 13:11).
- Each park cost 5 reconnect attempts plus backoff for a process that is already going away.
- The WARNING text says `degraded → parked`, so the error log reads as a real MCP outage on a machine whose servers were healthy.

## Reproduction

The error is a scheduling failure, so it needs no network: the code under test reaches the park on its own.

```python
from tools.mcp_tool import MCPServerTask
from tools.mcp_tool_server_run import _RetryBudget

task = MCPServerTask("t")
task._ever_connected = True
task._reconnect_retries = 0
await task._on_transport_error(
    RuntimeError("cannot schedule new futures after shutdown"), _RetryBudget())
```

Before this change: retries are charged and, with the budget exhausted, the server parks with the WARNING above (the first two tests in the new file fail on `main`, the third — the park with an exhausted budget — reproduces the exact production line).

## Fix

`tools/mcp_tool_server_run.py`:

- New `_is_shutdown_scheduling_error()` delegating to `tools.interpreter_shutdown.interpreter_shutting_down` — the shared predicate for this class (both CPython message variants: `cannot schedule new futures after shutdown` / `... after interpreter shutdown`, plus `sys.is_finalizing()`), already used by cron delivery, tool submission and the conversation retry (#55924/#58720).
- `_on_transport_error` checks it right after unwrapping the exception group, before classification: log DEBUG and `return False` (end the run loop), mirroring the existing `self._shutdown_event.is_set()` branch two lines below. Guarding the single entry point covers both the initial-connect and reconnect ladders and the park path.

Whole-bug-class, not one site: the MCP ladder is the sibling call path of the sites that already had this guard; the initial-connect ladder, the reinstated-stdio branch and both park sites all sit behind the same check.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_shutdown_scheduling_error.py` — 4 passed (2 parametrized shutdown variants, the exhausted-budget park case, plus a control asserting a genuine `ConnectionError` still charges the ladder).
- Regression: `pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_reconnect_log_hygiene.py tests/tools/test_mcp_rapid_drop_budget.py tests/tools/test_mcp_parked_self_probe.py tests/tools/test_mcp_park_log_dedupe.py tests/tools/test_mcp_cancelled_error_propagation.py tests/tools/test_mcp_shutdown_scheduling_error.py` — 18 passed.

fixes #136957

prs.title: fix(deps): bump dompurify 3.4.13 -> 3.4.16 (GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2, GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p)
prs.body:
## Problem

`dompurify` is pinned at `3.4.13` in **three** places, and that version is
vulnerable to two published advisories:

- [GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2)
  (2026-10-05) — `IN_PLACE` returns a force-removed rawtext root whose text can
  be re-parsed (XSS).
- [GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p)
  (2026-09-30) — `IN_PLACE`: a node-removing `afterSanitize` hook leaves a
  detached subtree that is still returned.

Both are fixed in `3.4.16`.

`dompurify` is a **production** dependency of the desktop app
(`apps/desktop/package.json` → `src/` sanitizes assistant-rendered HTML), so
this is a runtime XSS surface, not just a build-time one.

Reproduction (root lockfile):

```
$ npm audit --json | jq '.vulnerabilities.dompurify'
{ "severity": "low", "range": "<3.4.16", ... }
```

The pin is duplicated so a single-location bump silently leaves the other
sites vulnerable:

| Site | File |
| --- | --- |
| direct dependency | `apps/desktop/package.json` |
| root override | `package.json` (`overrides.dompurify`) |
| website override | `website/package.json` (`overrides.dompurify`) |

The three copies are also why `npm audit fix --force` aborts with `EOVERRIDE`
today (npm refuses an override that does not textually match the direct
dependency it replaces — see #136475).

## Fix

Bump all three sites to `3.4.16` and refresh the resolved entries in the two
committed lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `website/package-lock.json`). The
override and the direct dependency stay identical, so the `EOVERRIDE`
condition cannot be reintroduced.

Only the `dompurify` entries move; `3.4.16` has the same dependency metadata as
`3.4.13` (no `dependencies`, `optionalDependencies: {"@types/trusted-types": "^2.0.7"}`),
so no other node in either tree changes.

## Why not just bump the desktop dependency

Because the root/website overrides would keep resolving the vulnerable version
for the `^3.3.3` range (mermaid and friends pull it in transitively) — the same
bug class this repo has hit before with `js-yaml`/`aiohttp` (a fix that covers
one site only is rejected or lands half-applied).

## Validation

- Tarball integrity matches the registry:
  `sha512-sqo+pNp3qRhCIpbgRi1y8Tgk27Bo2Ry7w0dC1NBeNTdZChWjz9Xb/KOoZbRP/R6pQZ80Qw8YhXw13hWWBbMRnQ==`.
- Root tree: `npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts` → exit 0 (`added 1422 packages`).
- Website tree: `npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts` with the repo's required
  npm (`>=11.17.0`) → exit 0 (`added 1390 packages`).
- `npm audit --json` at the root no longer reports a `dompurify` entry.
- `grep -rn '3\.4\.13' package.json apps/desktop/package.json website/package.json package-lock.json website/package-lock.json` → no matches.

prs.body:
## Problem

The root lockfile resolves `shell-quote@1.9.0` (via the desktop dev toolchain),
which is vulnerable to a **critical** advisory:

- [GHSA-pqg4-j6r4-53mv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pqg4-j6r4-53mv) —
  `quote()` command injection via a line terminator (fixed in `1.11.0`).

`npm audit` also flags the carrier itself as critical, because `concurrently`
pins `shell-quote` **exactly** (`"shell-quote": "1.9.0"`), so no consumer range
can float it forward:

```
$ npm audit --json | jq '.vulnerabilities["shell-quote"]'
{ "severity": "critical",
  "range": "1.8.4 - 1.10.0",
  "fixAvailable": { "name": "concurrently", "version": "10.0.6", "isSemVerMajor": false },
  "effects": ["concurrently"] }
```

Adding an override would paper over a pin that upstream `concurrently` has
already fixed; the correct fix is to move the carrier.

## Fix

Bump the direct dev dependency `concurrently` `10.0.4` → `10.0.6` in
`apps/desktop/package.json` and refresh the two resolved lock entries. `10.0.6`
depends on `shell-quote@1.12.0`, so the vulnerable `1.9.0` node disappears from
the tree entirely (nothing else in the root lock requires `shell-quote`).

No other dependency of `concurrently` moves (`chalk 5.6.2`, `rxjs 7.8.2`,
`supports-color 10.2.2`, `tree-kill 1.2.2`, `yargs 18.0.0` are all unchanged).

## Validation

- Tarball integrity verified against the registry for both new versions:
  - `concurrently@10.0.6` → `sha512-qgICXXFp2/3nAebRLmxcINKEXM1mLK3ij/y31P02VTs/KIkddIeC05n73DxOXsXMB9LFSqNU1/na3lDlOhcbIw==`
  - `shell-quote@1.12.0` → `sha512-PcByqNyT/38F2kDNi006HAMRJaULuBzq/FOsw3qdZvX/GA9W/jamDaRskgHjubHiftXK5sIFxLNkvrXUwcof6Q==`
- `npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts` → exit 0 (`added 1422 packages`).
- `npm audit --json` → `vulnerabilities["concurrently"]` and
  `vulnerabilities["shell-quote"]` are both `null`; the reported `critical`

prs.title: fix(tui): recognize CRLF fused in one read as Enter (Android mobile TUI input)
prs.body:
Fixes Android/mobile TUI input: on Android terminals, Enter arrives as CRLF fused in a single read. The tokenizer deliberately does NOT split CR/LF (they are paste/newline content inside larger text tokens), so the fused CRLF falls through all branches of parseKeypress and returned name:'' instead of 'return'.

This adds '\r\n' to the lone-Enter branch so a CRLF token that IS the entire read is recognized as Enter, consistent with how lone \r and \n already work. CR/LF embedded in a larger text token remains whole (composer not prematurely submitted).

Includes 2 regression tests (lone CRLF -> return; embedded CRLF in larger token stays paste/newline content). All 209 tests in hermes-ink pass, tsc clean.

prs.title: kanban: never read an unreadable worker identity as death (boot-relative start time + tri-state liveness)
prs.body:
Fixes #123811.

### What goes wrong

A live worker is declared dead, killed, and de-owned. In one dispatch tick the reclaim path
declared six live workers dead; each recovery then spawned a duplicate beside the worker it had
just abandoned. A worker that has been "reclaimed" while still running cannot close its card:
`kanban_complete` is refused, its run is `crashed` in `task_runs`, `tasks.current_run_id` is NULL
and the card is `blocked` — bricked until a human clears it.

Liveness asked one question — "is this worker alive?" — and accepted only yes/no, so every failure
to *read* a process identity was answered "no". Three independent branches, each sufficient on its
own:

1. **The start-time reference steps.** The recorded fingerprint is an absolute start instant derived
   from the boot reference (plus psutil's `|INIT_BOOT_TIME - boot_time()|` shift on macOS), so the
   same live process reports a different value minutes apart:

   ```
   recorded at spawn   179030725877270          (ticks; Δ vs a re-read 9.27 s later: 927 cs)
   re-read later       179030725868000
   ```

2. **A failed probe is read as death.** `ps` exit status 1, or a `subprocess` failure, means "gone".
3. **An unreadable fingerprint is read as death.** A row whose fingerprint has an older shape (bare
   ticks, no boot component) cannot be compared at all — but it was compared, and the mismatch was
   read as "the PID was recycled".

### The change

* **`gateway/status.py`** — `host_boot_witness()` names the boot itself (`kern.bootsessionuuid` on
  macOS: fresh per boot, unaffected by clock or boottime adjustments; `boottime:<epoch>` as the
  fallback; never `''`). `get_process_uptime_start_time()` subtracts a boot reference read in the
  same call, so both halves of a comparison move together when the reference steps, and returns
  `None` — "cannot certify identity" — when it cannot read one. `start_time_fingerprints_match()` is
  the single comparator for the pair. `get_process_start_time()` keeps its absolute semantics.

* **`hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py`** — liveness is now a witness with three answers:
  `WORKER_ALIVE` / `WORKER_DEAD` / `WORKER_UNKNOWN`. `WORKER_UNKNOWN` is what an unreadable identity
  yields, never `WORKER_DEAD`; only `WORKER_DEAD` may release a claim, requeue a card or authorize a
  signal. Held rows are re-read next tick, bounded by the heartbeat/TTL backstops.

* **`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`** — the run-ownership guard separates the two cases it used to
  conflate: SUPERSEDED (a newer run owns the card — still refused on every transition, because the
  write would land on the successor) and UN-OWNED (`current_run_id` is NULL and the caller's run is
  the card's newest — the write lands):

  ```sql
  AND (current_run_id = ? OR (current_run_id IS NULL
       AND ? = (SELECT MAX(id) FROM task_runs WHERE task_id = tasks.id)))
  ```

  A recovery through that branch is recorded honestly rather than written into the crashed row: the
  completion lands on a synthesized run carrying `recovered_from_run_id` + `infra_reclaimed: true`,
  the crashed row stands as history, and the failure counter the reclaim booked is cleared.

* **`tools/kanban_tools.py`** — a refusal is built from the live row (`kanban_db.live_row_refusal()`:
  the card's status, which run owns it, whether the caller's run is superseded or was closed by the
  infrastructure and how to record that recovery) instead of `tasks.last_failure_error`, which is
  durable and describes a run that is over. The crash text is still shown — labelled as history.

### Two deliberate consequences

* A legacy-shaped fingerprint is uncomparable, so such rows are **held**, not reclaimed — the safe
  direction, and observable in the test suite. It costs nothing for rows this code wrote; for older
  rows the heartbeat/TTL backstops still bound the wait.
* A witness that comes back in a **different form** (the boot-session probe failing, leaving the
  `boottime:` fallback) reads as *unknown*, not as *a different boot*. A probe changing the shape of
  its answer is not proof that the host rebooted, and reading it as one would declare every live row
  dead in a single tick — the failure being fixed here. Same-form witnesses are compared exactly.

### Tests

New: `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_liveness_witness.py` (witness/liveness),
`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_run_fence_recovery.py` (run fence, recovery, refusal text),
`tests/tools/test_kanban_complete_refusal_live_row.py` (the refusal at the tool surface).
Updated for the new contract: `test_kanban_worker_pid_fingerprint.py`,
`test_kanban_terminal_worker_reaper.py`.

A/B, each test in its own process so a test the base code kills is still recorded:

```
base   d0288be5    PASS 11   RED 19   SIGTERM 1
branch 06b83d22    PASS 31   RED  0   SIGTERM 0
```

The `SIGTERM rc=143` row is the point of the change:
`test_a_failed_secondary_probe_holds_the_claim`, on the base tree, is killed by the base reclaim
path signalling the live PID it wrongly believes is a stale worker — the test process itself. On
this branch it passes.

```
python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_liveness_witness.py \
                 tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_run_fence_recovery.py \
                 tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_worker_pid_fingerprint.py \
                 tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_terminal_worker_reaper.py \
                 tests/tools/test_kanban_complete_refusal_live_row.py
```

### Related

#117505 — the same class of defect in cron's `_owner_is_live()` (an exact start-time compare
rejecting a live process).

prs.title: feat(desktop): zh localization for bundled skill display and slash rows
prs.body:
## What

zh users see English skill names, descriptions and slash-completion blurbs
everywhere in the desktop app — the Skills page, skill detail panes, the
official skill hub preview, and `/`-completion rows — even with the UI locale
set to zh. The backend owns those strings (SKILL.md frontmatter,
`commands.catalog`), so they arrive in English regardless of locale.

This adds a display-layer zh pass that is:

- **Locale-gated** — only active for `zh`; `en` and every other locale render
  byte-identical to today.
- **Source-gated** — every catalog entry carries the `sourceDescription` it
  was translated from. When upstream edits a skill's description, the entry
  is ignored and the fresh English text renders unchanged: a stale
  translation can never mask a meaning change.
- **Identifier-preserving** — `/name` command tokens, `(usage: …)` fragments
  and mutation identifiers stay raw; only prose is translated.

## How

- `src/lib/skill-localization.ts` — pure helpers: display name
  (`中文名 · <id>`), description (source-gated), category label, slash-row
  blurb, and search text that keeps Chinese, English and the identifier
  searchable, so existing English searches keep working.
- `src/i18n/skill-catalog.zh.json` — zh catalog covering all 58 bundled
  skills across 12 categories. Pure data; a JSON import keeps it out of the
  TS surface.
- Wiring: `skills-tab`, `skill-detail`, `official-skill-detail`,
  `skills-data` (search/filter), `use-slash-completions` (skill-kind rows).
  `zh.ts` gains one `commandDescs` entry (`/skills`, the desktop-owned
  command from `DESKTOP_COMMAND_SPECS`).
- Tests: catalog integrity (every entry carries Han + the identifier suffix,
  categories reachable from their entries), display behavior for zh/en,
  raw-token preservation through the real completion hook.

## Testing

- `vitest run` on the 11 affected files: **91 passed**, including the
  pre-existing suites for `use-slash-completions`, `desktop-slash-commands`,
  i18n `catalog-completeness` / `overlay-completeness` / `languages` /
  `registry`, and the skills component tests.
- New tests are red on base (`skill-localization` and the catalog do not
  exist there).
- eslint + prettier clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- This is the skills-display slice of the general zh desktop UI coverage in
  #38692; it follows the same locale-gated, `zhOverrides`-style approach and
  can merge independently.
- Catalog upkeep: when a bundled skill's description changes, its entry
  self-retires via the source gate — no wrong-language display, and
  refreshing the row is a data-only edit to the JSON.

prs.title: fix(compaction): never re-add the delivered reply after a surviving follower
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

After a compaction, `_ensure_compressed_keeps_last_assistant_reply` re-adds the just-delivered reply when the engine dropped it. `_reply_insertion_index` returns at the first follower that matches anything, and a text follower matches its **last** twin in the compacted list.

When the reply's first follower was dropped and a later row repeats its text (a second "continue" during a tool loop), the reply landed **after tool rows that originally followed it**. The in-place commit then persisted that order. A context engine that tracks rows in transcript order sees a stored row reappear after rows stored later than it.

This PR clamps a text-matched slot to the earliest surviving follower that can be located without ambiguity: by an unreused tool-call id, a tool-result id, or a preserved `_row_id`. The existing neighbour checks then run unchanged:
- **Slot next to an assistant row:** the reinsertion is skipped, as the function already does ("strict alternation beats recovery").
- **Legal slot:** the reply goes before every surviving original follower.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138173

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/conversation_compression_reply_anchor.py`: `_reply_insertion_index` clamps a text match to the earliest surviving unambiguous follower. Reused ids stay excluded, as before. The twin check, the reused-id `None` path, the no-shrink guard and the trailing-real-user fallback are unchanged.
- `tests/agent/test_compression_last_assistant_anchor.py`: three tests, one per clamp path:
  - tool call: the slot is clamped next to an assistant row, so the reinsertion is skipped and logged;
  - tool result: legal slot, so the reply is inserted before every surviving follower;
  - preserved `_row_id` of a follower the engine re-rendered.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/agent/test_compression_last_assistant_anchor.py -q`
   - On main (d97007c32d): the 3 new tests fail (`3 failed, 8 passed`).
   - On this branch: `11 passed`.
2. `pytest tests/agent/test_compression_rotation_state.py tests/agent/test_skill_todo_retention_parity.py -q`: 40 and 11 passed. These are the other files on the reply-anchor path.
3. The pure-host repro from #138173 no longer inserts the reply after `call_1`/`result_1`; it skips.

prs.title: fix(kanban): cap concurrent workers per board with kanban.max_spawn_by_board
prs.body:
## Problem

`kanban.max_spawn` is a single ceiling applied to every board's tick, and the host budget `kanban.max_in_progress` is shared first-come. A board with a deep queue spends the whole host budget, so every board ticked after it spawns nothing — one busy board starves the rest. The only per-board lever today is `set-dispatch on|off`, which is all-or-nothing and also stops that board's reclaim/promotion.

## Fix

Add opt-in `kanban.max_spawn_by_board` — a mapping of board slug to a positive-int ceiling (config.yaml only; no new env var). It is read into the dispatcher settings and resolved to **one board's ceiling per tick** at the `tick_once_for_board` call site, where it is passed as that board's `max_spawn`.

- The ceilings **allocate** the existing host budget; they never raise it. `_tick_spawn_budget` still applies `max_in_progress` across every board, so a board capped below the host budget can never hold more than its ceiling and leaves the remainder to the other boards, whatever order they are ticked in.
- A board not named keeps `kanban.max_spawn`, so an **absent or empty map is today's behaviour exactly** (opt-in, backward compatible).
- Defensive parsing: a non-mapping value, a ceiling below 1, and a slug not in the board inventory are each **ignored with a warning naming the entry** — never fatal, and never able to disable the global cap. A read failure of the board inventory fails open (keeps the map), so it cannot drop a real ceiling.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_per_board_spawn_ceiling.py` covers: absent/empty map unchanged; a named board's ceiling applies while others keep the global one; a ceiling limits its board while other boards still spawn; caps summing above the host budget never exceed it; a busy board cannot starve a quiet board; uncapped boards keep today's behaviour; invalid values and unknown slugs are ignored with a warning; an unreadable inventory fails open.

```
$ python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_per_board_spawn_ceiling.py -q
11 passed
```

Diff: 3 files, +337/-2 — one settings field + resolver, one small parse helper, a one-line change at the tick call site, a commented config default, and the tests.

prs.title: security: guard .hermes.md as project-context instruction file; add protected_instruction_allowlist_dirs
prs.body:
## What

`.hermes.md` / `HERMES.md` is loaded as project context at **priority 1** and has **no write guard**, while every other project-context instruction file does.

The prompt builder enumerates project-context types first-match-wins:

```
# agent/prompt_builder.py (upstream main)
# Project-context types in priority order: the first type with any non-empty file wins, later types are
# shadowed. ...
_CONTEXT_FILE_CANDIDATES = {
    "hermes_md": _hermes_md_candidates,   # .hermes.md / HERMES.md — nearest match walking parents to the git root
    "agents_md": _agents_md_candidates,   # AGENTS.md chain, git root -> cwd
    "claude_md": _claude_md_candidates,   # CLAUDE.md, cwd
    "cursorrules": _cursorrules_candidates,
}
```

So `.hermes.md` **shadows every `AGENTS.md` in the tree** — and `_find_hermes_md` walks parents up to the git root, so a match planted high in the tree wins from anywhere below it.

The write gate protects this set:

```python
# tools/file_tools_write_guards.py (upstream main, line 189)
_PROTECTED_INSTRUCTION_BASENAMES = frozenset({
    "agents.md", "claude.md", "soul.md", ".cursorrules"})
```

`.hermes.md` is in neither that set nor the config globs, nor the immediate-parent `.hermes` rule (which matches a file whose *parent directory* is named `.hermes`, not a file named `.hermes.md`).

## Why it matters

The gate's own rationale is that instruction files are a prompt-injection **persistence** vector, and that basenames match in ANY directory "because project-context instruction files are loaded from cwd trees — an AGENTS.md anywhere the agent might later run from is a live target". `.hermes.md` is exactly such a file, and a *higher*-priority one: it is the single instruction file an injected agent can rewrite with **no approval dialog at all**, from the position that outranks the guarded one.

## Repro

In a project directory:

```
cp AGENTS.md .hermes.md      # no approval prompt
# a subsequent targeted patch on .hermes.md -> no approval prompt
# the same writes against AGENTS.md prompt every time
```

Measured 2026-10-12 against a fork checkout of upstream main.

## The change

1. **Add `.hermes.md` and `hermes.md` to `_PROTECTED_INSTRUCTION_BASENAMES`.** Both spellings, because `_find_hermes_md` probes both; matching is case-insensitive, so this covers the loader exactly.

2. **Implement `security.protected_instruction_allowlist_dirs`** — an operator-declared list of absolute directory prefixes whose whole subtree is exempt from the gate, checked BEFORE the basename match.

Part 2 rides with part 1 because closing the guard also closes the only dialog-free path operators have for project instruction files. The exemption is the supported way to keep one: it is config-only (`config.yaml` is hard-blocked from agent writes, so an exemption is always a human declaration, never a self-grant), it is `realpath`'d on **both** sides so a symlinked directory or a symlinked target cannot evade it, it matches on a path boundary (`/work` does not exempt `/workshop`), and the gate stays ON everywhere else.

```yaml
security:
  protected_instruction_files: true
  protected_instruction_extra_patterns: []
  protected_instruction_allowlist_dirs: []   # e.g. ["/opt/sandbox"]
```

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_file_write_safety.py` + `tests/tools/test_protected_instruction_cli_channel.py`.

Two-arm run on the pushed tip, same invocation both arms:

```
BASE (unmodified):  1 failed, 73 passed, 6 skipped
GREEN (this branch): 1 failed, 85 passed, 6 skipped
```

The one failure is identical in both arms and is an artifact of running the suite inside a git worktree of a live install (the test resolves a real hermes-home path); it is unrelated to this change.

The added tests cover: `.hermes.md`/`HERMES.md` now prompt on every protected-name path shape (deny / once / yolo / case-variant / traversal / multi-file patch); the allowlist exempts each protected basename inside the declared tree; the gate stays on outside it; a symlinked allowlist entry still matches; a sibling prefix (`/work` vs `/workshop`) is not exempt; and the real config reader surfaces the key end-to-end.

releases.name: Hermes Agent v0.22.0 — The Threshold Release
releases.body:
# Hermes Agent v0.22.0

**Release Date:** October 13, 2026
**Since v0.21.0:** ~24,200 commits · ~6,080 merged PRs · ~15,600 files changed · ~2,045,000 insertions · ~1,140,000 deletions · **~7,180 issues closed** · ~2,520 contributors

> **The Threshold Release.** Hermes was the god of thresholds: the doorway, the crossing, the boundary stone. v0.21.0 assembled the pantheon; v0.22.0 is about getting through the door. A fresh desktop install now opens on a guided setup chat that runs on a free trial model, so a newcomer is talking to Hermes before they own an API key. Connectors carry the agent across into the apps you already use, with no account needed to start. Local models bring it home to your own hardware with a one-click llama.cpp runtime. And the threshold itself got sturdier: tested SemVer stable releases that installs follow by default, signed desktop packages (including the Microsoft Store), and one package manager underneath everything. Around that spine: a 600-plugin catalog, the Claude 5.5 / GPT-6 model wave, password-manager sign-in for the browser, a bot screen you can take over, one backend and one gateway for every profile, and a codebase a third smaller. This is the largest window Hermes has shipped, about 2.5x the v0.21.0 cycle, and it rolls up and fully documents the v0.21.1–v0.21.7 patch releases.

## ✨ Highlights

- **A first launch that sets itself up** — Open the desktop app on a computer where you have never used Hermes and it starts a short setup chat instead of a settings screen. One card at a time it asks your name, an accent color and a layout, which apps to connect, which plugins to install, then gives a quick tour and offers up to four first tasks picked for you. It installs and maintains llama.cpp with the right engine for your hardware (CPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan or ROCm), rates every catalog model against your GPU and RAM, and picks the highest-quality build that fits. Downloads pause and resume, the server starts and stops with Hermes, and engine updates are one click. ## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Python 3.14 is the runtime** for managed installs (the package manager installs it for you). KittenTTS is unavailable on 3.14. ([#102765](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/102765))
- **Windows desktop is MSIX-only** and needs Windows 11 22H2 or newer; the NSIS/MSI installers are gone. The macOS app is Apple Silicon only in default builds. ([#102765](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/102765), [#136603](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/136603))
- **One gateway per machine is the default.** `hermes update` folds per-profile gateways into the multiplexed default when nothing conflicts. ([#112854](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112854))
- **Chats no longer reset on an idle/daily timer.** `session_reset` idle/daily modes are retired (configs that still set them log a warning); `/new` or `/reset` starts fresh. ([#105021](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/105021), [#126244](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126244))
- **Old sessions are pruned automatically.** `sessions.auto_prune` now defaults to on: ended sessions inactive for 90 days are deleted at startup. Pinned and open sessions are never touched; set `sessions.auto_prune: false` to keep everything.
- **Memory providers moved to catalog plugins** (Honcho, Supermemory, Hindsight, Mem0, OpenViking, Holographic), as did Home Assistant, Spotify and Langfuse. Existing users are migrated on update or first start, with data intact. ByteRover and RetainDB remain bundled.
- **Plugin authors:** the old plugin compatibility import layer is gone ([#126164](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126164)), `hermes sync` (Skill Sync) was removed ([#132465](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/132465)), and the bundled tirith scanner was removed ([#133832](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/133832)). Several tools were renamed (`todo` → `todo_list`, `cronjob` → `cronjob_manage`, `process` → `process_manage`); the old names still work. ([#97979](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/97979))

## 📦 Stable Releases, Desktop Packages & Package Manager

### Stable releases & update channels
- **Tested SemVer stable releases and the channel switch** *(see Highlights)*. v0.21.6 and v0.21.7 were the first through the new gate; forks stay on `main`, and an install ahead of the newest release waits for the next.
- **Lighter update checks** — one GitHub API call a day replaces `git fetch` every 30 minutes. ([#107648](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/107648))

### Desktop bundles & the Microsoft Store
- **Sealed, signed desktop packages** *(see Highlights)*. In a package, `hermes update` points to the right updater (App Installer, Store or macOS). ([#134911](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/134911))
- **Packaged installs work end to end** — the agent's terminal runs `hermes`, Uninstall explains OS removal, and Python-dependency plugins install inside MSIX. ([#134051](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/134051), [#135333](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/135333) — @alt-glitch)

### Unified package manager
- **`hermes pm`** *(see Highlights)*: pinned, hash-checked Python 3.14, uv, Node, ripgrep, FFmpeg, Chromium and Git/Bash on Windows, with `hermes pm doctor|status|repair|gc`. Contributors use `source ./activate` (or `.ps1`/`.fish`).
- **Dependency environments are generations** — new ones are checked before use, so a failed install keeps the working one; updates and `hermes pm gc` reclaim old ones (92 GB to 18 GB on one host). ([#124968](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124968), [#133808](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/133808) — @JoaoMarcos44)
- **Optional features install on first use** — opt-in SDKs (Anthropic, Bedrock) load mid-session without a restart; `security.allow_lazy_installs: false` turns this off. ([#122221](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/122221) — @ethernet8023)
- **Plugins declare Python dependencies** — resolved with core across profiles; conflicts are refused, and updates disable a plugin that no longer fits. Hindsight, Honcho, Supermemory, Mem0 and Home Assistant moved to the catalog and auto-install where used. ([#113851](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/113851), [#122103](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/122103), [#114569](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/114569), [#132469](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/132469) — @ethernet8023)

### Install & update
- **Updates can't half-apply** *(see Highlights)*. A killed update repairs itself on the next launch. ([#132361](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/132361), [#120339](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120339))
- **Faster updates, smaller checkouts** — updates rebuild only what changed (16.5 s vs 32.5 s on macOS), clones are blobless, and partial-clone `.git` growth is fixed. ([#135092](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/135092), [#133016](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/133016), [#131679](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/131679) — @kshitijk4poor, @ethernet8023, @liuhao1024, @whyyagswhy)
- **Small, hash-checked installers** — `install.sh`/`install.ps1` verify pinned uv and Git, hand off to PM, log to `logs/install.log`, and now work on musl Linux (Alpine, Void), Windows 10 and Unicode Windows paths. ([#124964](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124964), [#125598](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125598), [#132430](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/132430) — @JoaoMarcos44, @kshitijk4poor, @Finn763, @OutThisLife)
- **Failures say why** — with opt-in telemetry, install, update, skill and plugin failures record a reason. ([#133809](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/133809))

### Docker / Nix / Termux / Windows
- **Docker** — pinned Debian 13 base with full Chromium; `stable`/`latest` move only on a published release; baked-in extras return after a restart. ([#135726](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/135726), [#135084](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/135084) — @unsupportedpastels)

## 🏗️ Core Agent, Sessions & Memory

### Agent loop & reliability
- **Stalled turns recover** — a watchdog (`agent.turn_liveness.timeout_s`, default 600 s) interrupts a no-progress turn and frees its session; repeated transcript repairs now raise one error and notice. ([#99758](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/99758), [#99687](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/99687) — @kshitijk4poor, @Finn763, @HexLab98)
- **Streams fail less and report honestly** — text-less dead streams retry, repetition loops are cut, and interrupted turns aren't reported as done. ([#113135](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/113135), [#130551](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/130551), [#112272](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112272) — @kshitijk4poor)

### Compression & context
- **Compaction triggers on real token counts** — provider-reported usage, not bytes/4; the protected tail is capped at 20% so small-window models compact. ([#104555](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/104555), [#117957](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/117957) — @686f6c61)
- **Bad summaries can't wipe context** — refusals and overloaded summary providers leave the transcript alone, and an uncommitted compaction changes nothing. ([#118920](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/118920), [#115906](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/115906), [#136083](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/136083) — @kshitijk4poor, @fangliquanflq, @mnajafian-nv)
- **New knobs** — provider-scoped `compression.model_thresholds` keys and `auxiliary.<task>.no_progress_timeout`. ([#108061](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/108061), [#115804](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/115804) — @chelsealong)

### Sessions & state.db
- **state.db reliability** — lock timeouts name the holding process, a busy database no longer kills a turn, and sibling PID namespaces can't steal leases. ([#116967](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/116967), [#134577](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/134577), [#132161](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/132161) — @kshitijk4poor, @686f6c61)
- **state.db stops growing** — auto-prune is on by default (ended sessions over 90 days) and closes stale cron/kanban/subagent sessions; VACUUM runs only when 25% is reclaimable. ([#101316](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/101316), [#100903](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/100903) — @stepanov1975)
- **Repair commands** — `hermes sessions set-journal-mode delete|wal`, `repair-profiles` (crossed profiles) and `repair-prompts`. ([#117684](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/117684), [#115689](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/115689), [#124200](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124200) — @kshitijk4poor, @JoaoMarcos44)
- **Cleaner session lists** — one-shot runs stay out of pickers, `sessions.show_subagents` lists titled subagent chats, messages get stable ids for context engines. ([#113826](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/113826), [#122304](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/122304), [#126687](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126687) — @OutThisLife, @kshitijk4poor, @100yenadmin)

### Memory
- **Memory providers leave core safely** — OpenViking and Holographic move to the plugin catalog on update or first start, data intact, or say why not. ([#134350](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/134350), [#136436](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/136436), [#131269](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/131269))
- **Built-in memory writes land** — hand-formatted MEMORY.md/USER.md accepted, refusals say what to fix, secrets scrubbed before providers see them. ([#133038](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/133038), [#134429](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/134429) — @aniruddhaadak80)

### Profiles & config
- **config.yaml survives bad moments** — a broken file falls back to the last good copy; read errors can't wipe it. ([#109463](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109463), [#120343](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120343) — @Shenrui-Ma, @huklaa)
- **Safer `hermes config`** — `get` masks secrets (`--raw` opts out); `set` refuses typo paths and stores env-style names in `.env`. ([#111341](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/111341), [#112250](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112250) — @webtecnica)
- **Profiles stay separate** — REST routes act on the profile they name, exports skip `.ssh`/`.aws`/`.gnupg`, and `import-agent --sync` keeps imports current. ([#118275](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/118275), [#132201](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/132201), [#88855](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/88855) — @kshitijk4poor, @JerryLiu369)

### Languages (i18n)

## ⏰ Cron, Kanban & Delegation

### Cron
- **Jobs follow your main model** — Unpinned jobs use the model configured at fire time; `pinned` locks one. ([#113679](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/113679))
- **Self-healing schedules** — A fire that never reached the model (e.g. after wake) re-runs after 5, 15 and 30 minutes, a provider "retry after" window parks the job quietly, and a slot missed during a restart fires once. ([#108731](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/108731), [#115843](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/115843))
- **Quieter alerts** — One alert per incident plus a reminder every `cron.failure_repeat_alert_hours`; `failure_deliver` reroutes or mutes failure notices; an agent can fail its run with `[CRON_FAILURE]`. ([#114807](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/114807), [#101373](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/101373), [#113155](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/113155)) — @victor-kyriazakos
- **New job options** — `--paused` creates a job unarmed; `--interpreter` runs scripts on your own venv. ([#104984](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/104984), [#125392](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125392)) — @M1racleShih
- **Profiles and delivery** — A multiplexed gateway runs each profile's jobs with that profile's env and secrets; delivery needs positive evidence, output is secret-redacted everywhere, and late or satellite runs are labelled. ([#118027](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/118027), [#100908](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/100908), [#112830](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112830)) — @yoniebans

### Kanban
- **Workers ride out provider trouble** — Failed turns retry in place with context; rate limits or 5xx requeue instead of burning retries. ([#112318](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112318), [#112500](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112500)) — @EvgenyMettsler, @dmelkk-secondbrain
- **A board that explains itself** — Cards show the worker's last output on failure; dispatch says why a card is held. ([#112618](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112618)) — @chelsealong
- **Workflow and tooling** — One workflow definition drives columns; workers get `kanban_schedule`; `kanban create --body-file`; Desktop follows gateway switches. ([#134340](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/134340), [#130455](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/130455), [#116791](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/116791), [#119054](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/119054)) — @benbarclay, @unsupportedpastels, @fangliquanflq

### Delegation & multi-agent
- **Live subagents, images and /stop** *(see Highlights)*. ([#105593](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/105593))
- **Fan-outs lose less** — Failed children surface at once, an owner crash keeps finished work, children can hand processes to the parent, and per-task completions are opt-in. ([#103549](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/103549), [#116707](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/116707), [#105125](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/105125))
- **Child routing** — `delegation.fallback_providers` gives children their own chain; `child_timeout_seconds` measures inactivity. ([#105347](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/105347), [#117606](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/117606)) — @ayushnangia
- **/goal** — Consistent on CLI, Desktop and messaging; the judge waits on subagents; `/goal pause for now` no longer overwrites the goal; gates run in the session workspace. ([#104833](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/104833), [#132251](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/132251), [#125453](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125453)) — @jayzhou2309

## 🔒 Security, Privacy & Codebase

### Security & privacy
- **v0.21.6 security fixes** — dashboard sign-in hardening (spoofed `X-Forwarded-For`, size caps, loopback-only login codes); automatic git skips repo filter programs; the email allowlist resists display-name spoofing. ([#133367](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/133367), [#130685](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/130685), [#130661](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/130661), [#125212](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125212)) — @unsupportedpastels, @kshitijk4poor, @Froraut, @jonpol01, @keeltrace
- **Secrets stay put** — child processes don't inherit adapter/dashboard secrets; remote `execute_code` keeps its token out of argv; profile exports skip credential stores; keys never reach foreign hosts on refresh/fallback. ([#125755](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125755), [#124262](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124262), [#130525](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/130525), [#120299](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120299)) — @kshitijk4poor, @jonpol01, @beardthelion, @leemove
- **Sharper redaction** — debug share redacts before truncating; file reads and terminal output mask `.env`/config secrets; `hermes config get` masks unless `--raw`; memory hand-offs are scrubbed; plain `token=` lines stay visible. ([#132270](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/132270), [#111422](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/111422), [#111341](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/111341), [#134429](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/134429), [#100564](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/100564)) — @kshitijk4poor, @Froraut, @shehjaddev, @webtecnica, @aniruddhaadak80, @fangliquanflq
- **Owner-only files at rest** — credentials, `state.db`, snapshots, browser profiles, media caches, any umask. ([#109509](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109509), [#127229](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/127229)) — @JoaoMarcos44, @rohitsabu, @OutThisLife
- **Wider guards** — more fetches pass the SSRF guard (`security.fake_ip_ranges` for fake-ip proxies); cloud-metadata fetches, zsh/dash pipe-to-shell and `deno eval` need approval; `approvals.deny` works in sandboxes; built-in rules replace bundled tirith. ([#114887](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/114887), [#113156](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/113156), [#116726](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/116726), [#103649](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/103649), [#133832](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/133832)) — @beardthelion, @AYin-Z, @fangliquanflq
- **Holes closed** — the MCP OAuth callback stops reflecting HTML; webhook, SMS and WhatsApp Cloud inbound reject blank signing secrets. ([#92612](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/92612), [#133257](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/133257)) — @memosr, @ahadvice
- **Opt-in shared metrics** — daily usage stats reach Nous only with consent; both `telemetry.shared_metrics` switches default off, each profile asks once, Enter = "No thanks". ([#95278](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/95278)) — @benbarclay
### Codebase & performance
- **Leaner prompts and tools** — ~2.1k fewer prompt tokens a request, on-demand vault tools, one-round-trip file probes, `hermes -w` no longer repacks each launch. ([#137084](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/137084), [#101599](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/101599)) — @yaojiejia
### Other
- **Safer backups** — `hermes backup` keeps the newest 3, flags incomplete archives; `hermes import` refuses damaged ones. ([#106455](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106455), [#121498](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/121498)) — @buihongduc132, @kshitijk4poor
- **Also** — `KEY_2`… env vars join credential pools; one-screen `hermes status`; opt-in `display.suppress_warning_notifications`; Desktop Bots roster sections; only Hermes' own node/npm/uv are used; Xiaomi MiMo v2.6. ([#112390](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112390), [#131034](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/131034), [#114370](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/114370), [#101290](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/101290), [#125589](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125589), [#118502](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/118502)) — @PhoeniXAbhisheK, @victor-kyriazakos, @fortun8te, @rob-maron
- **For contributors** — CODEOWNERS replaces the label gate; E2E (incl. native Windows) runs only on release builds; stable releases skip macOS Intel/Termux by default. ([#131726](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/131726), [#136603](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/136603)) — @ethernet8023

## 🐛 Notable Bug Fixes

**Onboarding, connectors & local models**
- Managed llama-server no longer crashes on Windows with 0xC0000374 and no longer inherits your credentials ([#116923](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/116923))
- Windows local-model servers are contained and orphans recovered safely; two backends booting together start one router ([#111038](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/111038), [#117600](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/117600) — @jquesnelle, @chelsealong)

**Install, update & packaging**
- Docker agents no longer lose their built-in API server, messaging and MCP dependencies after a restart. ([#135726](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/135726) — @unsupportedpastels)
- A `hermes update` killed mid-pull no longer breaks every entry point. ([#120339](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120339))

**Providers & models**
- A rate-limited Claude model no longer benches the whole credential for every other Claude model. ([#113171](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/113171) — @KoNit-K)
- Codex app-server sessions now get SOUL.md and the Hermes system prompt. ([#115759](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/115759) — @JonthanaHanh, @ooiuuii, @Momentum96)

**Agent loop, sessions & memory**
- A chat whose session row was deleted recreates it instead of silently dropping every later turn ([#124117](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124117) — @kshitijk4poor, @strzhao)
- Messages flushed at gateway shutdown are recovered into their session ([#114225](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/114225) — @kshitijk4poor, @spfcraze, @yoyodine-industries, @briandevans)

**Gateway & platforms**
- Telegram no longer stalls under flood control or stays connected but deaf on a wedged dispatcher. ([#116987](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/116987), [#132162](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/132162) — @kshitijk4poor)
- Slack native streaming stops posting answers twice. ([#121762](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/121762) — @kshitijk4poor, @ms-elbdev)

**Desktop**
- Replies no longer show twice, garble or vanish after resume, steer, a chat switch or reconnect ([#118890](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/118890), [#120290](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120290), [#121061](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/121061) — @BearHuddleston)
- Pressing Enter answers the clarify card on screen, not a background chat's ([#76472](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/76472) — @briandevans)
- Duplicate or vanishing replies after refresh, session switch or reused tool-call ids ([#131758](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/131758), [#128003](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/128003), [#130553](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/130553) — @OutThisLife, @alt-glitch, @kshitijk4poor)
- "This device" backends no longer idle-killed after an hour; new chats run on the gateway you picked ([#134942](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/134942), [#132538](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/132538) — @unsupportedpastels)

**CLI, TUI & dashboard**
- Dashboard saves no longer overwrite secrets with their masked preview ([#121250](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/121250) — @kshitijk4poor)
- Resizing the CLI no longer re-appends the conversation to scrollback ([#120321](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120321) — @Jackal991)

**Tools, MCP & browser**
- A parked OAuth MCP server no longer replays its dead refresh token on every new session, a storm that could trip a rate-limit ban ([#137502](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/137502)).
- `computer_use` element clicks work again on cua-driver 0.21+; only pixel clicks worked before ([#111313](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/111313) — @jeffjhunter).

**Plugins & skills**
- `hermes plugins list` and the dashboard Plugins page make at most one live catalog request instead of waiting through one timeout per installed plugin. ([#114811](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/114811))
- On treeless source checkouts the plugin inventory no longer takes 40–80 seconds, which was longer than the Desktop request timeout. ([#125716](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125716) — @liuhao1024)
- Enabling a plugin from Desktop, the TUI or the dashboard no longer strips the core tools. ([#135048](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/135048))
- A platform whose plugin failed to load at startup is flagged in `hermes status` and comes back without a restart. ([#130613](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/130613), [#133289](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/133289)) — @kshitijk4poor

**Cron, Kanban & delegation**
- Gateway `/goal` gate add no longer lets a non-admin reach the host shell ([#101499](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/101499))
- Automatic git in Kanban, worktree cleanup and subagents no longer runs a cloned repo's hooks or filters ([#130661](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/130661))

**Security & misc**
- Qwen models behind Alibaba's content guardrail end the turn with the safety notice instead of retrying for four minutes. ([#136425](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/136425))
- Detected password managers can be switched on from Settings again; the toggle was a no-op. ([#109558](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109558)) — @kokhlo
