issues.title: [BUG] Web UI: a session can disappear from the list while the model is still thinking (ghost session)
issues.body:
## Quick Summary

In the Web UI, a freshly created session can **silently disappear from the session list while the model is still thinking**, leaving what looks like a "ghost session": the chat you are looking at is no longer present in the history dropdown, and there is no way to get back to it. This report documents how sessions are currently listed/created and points at the two code paths that can produce the ghost.

## Environment & Tools
- **PicoClaw Version:** v0.3.1 (git `2cf030d2`)
- **Go Version:** go1.25.11
- **AI Model & Provider:** any (the issue is in session listing/creation, not the model)
- **Operating System:** Linux amd64
- **Channels:** Web UI (`pico` channel)

## 📸 Steps to Reproduce

Intermittent, but the pattern is:

1. Open the Web UI and start a **new chat** (or send the first message of a new session).
2. The turn starts — the "thinking" indicator shows and the model is working.
3. Open the **session history dropdown** (`SessionHistoryMenu`) while the turn is still running, and/or let the turn finish/error.
4. The session you are currently in is **missing from the list** (or never appears), even though you are looking at its transcript. It looks like a ghost session.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

The active session is not present in `GET /api/sessions`, so the history dropdown does not show it. The user is stuck in a session that "does not exist" according to the list.

## ✅ Expected Behavior

Any session that is currently open in the UI must be listed in the history — including one whose first turn is still in progress or that ended in an error. A session should never be invisible while the user is actively reading/writing it.

## 🔎 Root-cause analysis (current session handling)

Verified against `main` (`web/frontend` + `web/backend` + `pkg/session`). Two independent mechanisms can hide a session:

**1. Empty sessions are filtered out of the list.**
`web/backend/api/session.go` → `handleListSessions` skips any session for which `isEmptySession(sess)` is true:

```go
func isEmptySession(sess sessionFile) bool {
	return len(sess.Messages) == 0 && strings.TrimSpace(sess.Summary) == ""
}
```

A brand-new session whose first turn has not yet produced a persisted message (still thinking, or the turn failed before the assistant message was written) has **zero messages on disk** → it is dropped from the list. The frontend then shows the empty state (`chat.noHistory`) even though the user is inside that session. This is the most likely cause of the "ghost".

**2. The list is only refreshed when the dropdown opens, and it races with in-progress writes.**
`web/frontend/src/components/chat/chat-page.tsx` calls `loadSessions(true)` only on `SessionHistoryMenu` `onOpenChange` (i.e. when the user opens the dropdown). There is no refresh on `message.send`, on `typing.stop`, or when a turn completes. So if the list is fetched *before* the first message is flushed to disk (or while a write is in flight), the session is absent — and it stays absent until the user reopens the dropdown. Combined with (1), a session that is still empty at fetch time simply never shows.

**Why the active session is not special-cased:** the frontend generates the session id client-side (`features/chat/state.ts` → `generateSessionId()`, stored in `localStorage` as `picoclaw:last-session-id`) and opens the WebSocket with `?session_id=<uuid>`. The backend has no notion of "the currently open session", so it cannot guarantee the active session is always listed.

**Note on message counts:** `buildSessionListItem` counts only *visible* messages (`visibleSessionMessages`, thoughts excluded). A session whose only content so far is a reasoning/thought block can therefore report `message_count: 0` even though it is not technically empty — worth confirming whether that contributes to the perception of a ghost.

## 🛠 Proposed fix / diagnostics

- **Backend:** in `handleListSessions`, do not drop the session that is currently active. Simplest robust option: stop filtering empty sessions out of the list entirely (or only hide them when they are also not the active session), and/or expose an `is_empty` flag so the client can decide. Include sessions that only have a thought/tool-call message in the count.
- **Frontend:** refresh the session list after `message.send` and on `typing.stop`/turn completion, not only on dropdown open, so a just-created session appears as soon as it has content. Optionally optimistically insert the active session into the list.
- **Diagnostics wanted from maintainers:** confirm the intended semantics of `isEmptySession` and whether a session with an in-flight first turn is expected to be listed. If the ghost is instead caused by the JSONL write not being visible to the list reader (a read/write race in `pkg/session/jsonl_backend.go`), that is a second, separate fix.

## 💬 Additional Context

- Related prior issues (all auto-closed as `stale`): #2972 (Web UI "message chaos", new session attached old history) and #2621 (session context lost, duplicate default session). Neither covers the "active session disappears from the list while thinking" case.
- This is the same area as the session-list improvements requested in #3406; the ghost is a correctness bug that should be fixed before/alongside that UX work.

issues.title: [Feature] Web UI: clearer working indicator, separate manual/channel sessions, richer session list with archiving
issues.body:
## 🎯 The Goal / Use Case

The built-in Web UI (launcher dashboard, `web/frontend`) is now the main day-to-day way to chat with PicoClaw, but three UX rough edges make it frustrating for real use:

1. **"Is it still thinking?" is unclear.** While a turn runs, the chat shows a generic spinner (`components/chat/typing-indicator.tsx`: bouncing dots + a shimmer bar + 4 rotating canned phrases from `chat.thinking.step1..4`). It never reflects what is actually happening — connecting, waiting on the model, running a tool call, or stalled. During a long reasoning turn (or a hung provider) the user cannot tell the difference between "working" and "dead", so they wait, reload, or resend.

2. **Manual sessions and channel sessions are mixed together.** The session history dropdown is populated by `GET /api/sessions`, whose backend (`web/backend/api/session.go`, `handleListSessions`) only discovers the `pico` channel store (`findPicoJSONLSessions` → `extractPicoSessionIDFromScope` requires `scope.Channel == "pico"`). So every session is shown as one flat list with no source: manually created Web-UI chats, the Web UI's own `pico` session, and *external* integrations that also use the `pico` channel with a custom `session_id` (e.g. a webhook bridge using `session_id=trello-webhook`) all look identical. There is no way to filter "only my manual chats" vs. "only the Telegram/channel traffic".

3. **Session management is cramped and destructive.** The list is a tight dropdown (`components/chat/session-history-menu.tsx`, `w-72` / `max-h-[300px]`, infinite scroll). There is no search, no sorting, no rename, no pinning, and no **archive** — the only action is a hard delete (`DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` → `handleDeleteSession`), which permanently removes the transcript. Users who just want to declutter have to destroy history.

## 💡 Proposed Solution

### 1. Honest, state-driven "working" indicator
Replace the canned rotating text with a real phase indicator driven by the events the client **already receives** over the `pico` WebSocket (`features/chat/protocol.ts`):
- `typing.start` / `typing.stop` → idle vs. running
- `message.create` with `placeholder: true` → model is generating
- assistant message with `kind === "thought"` → a reasoning block is being produced (already parsed)
- assistant message with `kind === "tool_calls"` → a tool call is in flight (already parsed)
- `message.update` → streaming progress

Show the concrete phase (e.g. *Connecting… → Thinking… → Running tool `X`… → Writing…*), a live elapsed timer, and after N seconds escalate to a clearly different "still working — the model is taking longer than usual" state (with a hint that the turn can be interrupted). No fake progress; only what the stream actually reports.

### 2. Separate manual sessions from channel sessions
- Backend: expose the session **source** in the list item. `sessionListItem` (`web/backend/api/session.go`) already has access to `memory.SessionMeta` / `session.SessionScope`; add a `channel` (or `source`) field so the API returns where the session came from (`web`/manual, `telegram`, `pico`, `cron`, …).
- Frontend: add a source selector/filter to the history UI, defaulting to the **current** source, so "my manual chats" and "Telegram (or other channels)" never get mixed. This is the Web-UI counterpart of the closed #3307 (`/session list` for chat channels).

### 3. Comfortable session list + archiving
- Promote the history from a cramped dropdown to a proper list (dedicated panel/page or roomier drawer) with: search, sort (recent / created / message count), filters by source, rename, and pin/favorite.
- Add a **soft archive** action distinct from delete: archived sessions leave the default list but remain recoverable. Concretely, add an `archived` flag (or an archive endpoint) instead of forcing users to choose between "keep everything" and "hard delete". Keep permanent delete as a separate, confirmed action.

## 🛠 Potential Implementation (Optional)

- `web/frontend/src/components/chat/typing-indicator.tsx` — replace the canned steps with a phase machine fed from `store/chat.ts` state set in `features/chat/protocol.ts`.
- `web/frontend/src/features/chat/protocol.ts` — derive an explicit `turnPhase` (idle / thinking / tool / writing / stalled) from the events already handled.
- `web/backend/api/session.go` — extend `sessionListItem` + `buildSessionListItem` with a `channel`/`source` field; add an archive action and an `archived` filter to `handleListSessions`.
- `web/frontend/src/api/sessions.ts` — extend `SessionSummary` with the new fields; add `archiveSession`.
- `web/frontend/src/components/chat/session-history-menu.tsx` (+ a new sessions view) — source filter, search/sort, pin, archive.
- Persist the archive flag in the session store metadata (`pkg/session`, `memory.SessionMeta`) so it survives restarts, and consider excluding archived sessions from the default `GET /api/sessions` response (or gating them behind a query param).

## 🚦 Impact & Roadmap Alignment
- [ ] This is a Core Feature
- [x] This is a Nice-to-Have / Enhancement
- [ ] This aligns with the current Roadmap

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Only fix the indicator text**: rejected — the flat session list and the destructive-only delete are independent problems the user hits constantly.
- **Only add a client-side source filter without backend changes**: rejected — the source is not currently exposed by the API, so the client cannot distinguish sources reliably.
- **Reuse hard delete as "archive"**: rejected — it destroys history; archiving should be reversible.

Related prior issues (both auto-closed as `stale` without being resolved): #2216 (show thinking content in WebUI) and #3307 (session list/switch for chat channels). This issue covers the remaining Web-UI UX gaps.

## 💬 Additional Context

- Verified against `main` (`web/frontend` + `web/backend`). The Web UI lives in the main repo (`web/`), while `sipeed/picoclaw_fui` is the separate Flutter client — so these changes belong here.
- Real-world motivation for item 2: a `pico`-channel bridge with a custom `session_id` (e.g. `trello-webhook`) currently shows up in the same history list as the user's manual chats, with no way to tell them apart.

issues.title: Please enable private vulnerability reporting
issues.body:
Hi maintainers,

I'd like to report a few security issues in PicoClaw privately, but GitHub private vulnerability reporting is disabled for this repository and I couldn't find a security contact (there is no `SECURITY.md`).

Could you please enable private vulnerability reporting (Settings → Code security → Private vulnerability reporting), or tell me which private channel you prefer? If email works better, please confirm whether support@sipeed.com is the right address.

A `SECURITY.md` with the preferred contact would also help future reporters.

Thanks!

issues.title: Reliability fixes with reproducers (wave 1)
issues.body:
Hi maintainers 👋

I went through PicoClaw's core (agent loop, channels manager, config, updater) and found several bugs
that are reproducible on current `main` (bbf6893) and v0.3.1. Some of them were reported or even fixed
before, but those issues/PRs were closed by the stale bot before anyone could review them, so I am
collecting them here in one place. Every PR below contains a regression test that fails on `main` and
passes with the fix, plus an end-to-end check with a real gateway build.

| PR | Bug | Impact | Prior reports |
|---|---|---|---|
| #3399 `fix(updater): select the matching 32-bit ARM release asset` | `picoclaw update` on GOARCH=arm installs the arm64 archive | 32-bit Raspberry Pi / ARM boards get a binary that cannot run | — |
| #3400 `fix(config): persist all api_keys and enabled flag of multi-key models` | any config save keeps only the first of several `api_keys`, leaves dangling `__key_N` fallbacks; multi-key models are hidden from `picoclaw model` | silent loss of credentials | #3373 |
| #3401 `fix(channels): make Reload synchronous and nil-safe` | hot reload with an enabled-but-not-ready channel (e.g. Telegram without token) panics the gateway; a changed channel keeps receiving but never replies until restart | gateway crash / silent outage | — |
| #3402 `fix(agent): resolve the owning agent in context managers` | chats routed to a non-default agent lose their history; summarization/compression never run for them | broken multi-agent setups | #3301, #3316 (carried, original authors kept) |
| #3403 `fix(agent): deliver async tool results to the originating session` | results of `spawn` from all chats are appended to the default agent's main session; one user's result becomes context for another user's reply | cross-chat data leak | #2041, #2794 |

Each PR is small and independent, so they can be reviewed and merged in any order.
Could you please add `keep-open` to these PRs so the stale bot doesn't close them while they wait
for review? I'll keep them rebased and respond to feedback quickly.

Next wave (not yet submitted):
- `send on closed channel` panic when a channel worker is stopped while the dispatcher enqueues (StopAll / UnregisterChannel)
- async summarization drops messages appended during the LLM call
- web UI: multi-key models lose keys on edit via `PUT /api/models/{i}` and `PATCH /api/config`
- tests that write outside temp dirs when run as root (`TestSetDefaultModel_SaveConfigError` creates `/nonexistent/...`)

Suggested reviewers per CONTRIBUTING: @lxowalle @yinwm @alexhoshina @Zhaoyikaiii

Thanks for PicoClaw!

issues.title: [Feature] Add Tsubasa to the existing OpenAI-compatible provider catalog
issues.body:
# [Feature] Add Tsubasa to the existing OpenAI-compatible provider catalog

## 🎯 The Goal / Use Case

Users can already select Tsubasa through an explicit `openai` model entry with a custom API base, but the provider picker does not offer its endpoint or public model aliases. A small catalog entry would make that setup discoverable without adding a new transport.

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Add a named `tsubasa` provider using the existing HTTP/OpenAI-compatible path, the base URL `https://api.tsubasa.sh/v1`, and common models `tsubasa-fast` and `tsubasa-pro`. Preserve the existing API-base override and credential handling. Both aliases have a 32,768-token input-plus-output budget; a setup example should use `agents.defaults.context_window = 32768` and a bounded output setting such as `max_tokens = 4096`.

Do not add an unapproved icon or claim tool, vision, reasoning, or model-listing qualification. Keep model fetching disabled until that endpoint is verified.

## 🛠 Potential Implementation (Optional)

- Add the entry to `pkg/providers/provider_metadata.go`; keep `provider_catalog.go` deriving UI options from that source.
- Extend the existing compatible-provider case in `pkg/providers/factory_provider.go` and its routing/default-base tests.
- Exercise both aliases through `CreateProviderFromConfig`, `Chat`, and `ChatStream`, including explicit API-base override and rejected credentials.
- Add one setup example in the existing provider documentation and run `make check` before a PR.

## 🚦 Impact & Roadmap Alignment

- [ ] This is a Core Feature
- [x] This is a Nice-to-Have / Enhancement
- [ ] This aligns with the current Roadmap

Roadmap fit is for maintainers to determine. This issue comes before feature implementation, as requested by CONTRIBUTING.md.

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Keep the existing manual `provider: "openai"` route with a custom endpoint. It already works at the client boundary and remains a valid alternative if the project prefers fewer branded entries. No proxy, LiteLLM dependency, or additional SDK is needed.

## 💬 Additional Context

Inspected commit `bbf6893ca7afad27f1d00a0f5a45982a549c6ed6`. An isolated native-factory fixture passed eight requests: both public aliases, JSON and SSE responses, and 401 handling. Each serialized request passed Tsubasa's actual request schema and admission-budget helper. The fixture used synthetic credentials and a loopback server. This does not establish live inference, a complete agent run, or model-native tool quality.

Recent relevant precedent: [NEAR AI Cloud provider #2917](https://github.com/sipeed/picoclaw/pull/2917) and [MiMo common models #2915](https://github.com/sipeed/picoclaw/pull/2915), both merged. A search for Tsubasa issues/PRs found no existing contribution at the time of this investigation. This proposal and its controlled checks were prepared with AI assistance.

issues.title: Replace hard iteration limit with context-window bounding and loop detection

labels.name: type: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

The current `max_tool_iterations: 20` hard limit is too restrictive for complex tasks. It causes legitimate workflows to fail with "I've completed processing but have no response to give" before reaching their deliverable.

## Current Behavior

```json
// ~/.picoclaw/config.json
"agents": {
  "defaults": {
    "max_tool_iterations": 20
  }
}
```

After 20 tool calls, the agent stops regardless of task completion state.

## Problem

A typical literature review task requires:
- 1-2 iterations: project setup
- 2-4 iterations: pubmed search
- 3-6 iterations: pubmed fetch (multiple batches)
- 2-4 iterations: data processing/analysis
- 2-4 iterations: document creation (docx-review)
- 1-2 iterations: verification

**Total: 11-22 iterations minimum**

The agent consistently exhausts 20 iterations on data gathering and never reaches the document creation step.

## Evidence from Logs

```
iteration=19: pubmed fetch 41635784 41625329... --json > pubmed_fetch_more.json
iteration=20: python - <<'PY' ... (processing)
Response: I've completed processing but have no response to give.
```

The agent was still gathering data at iteration 20 - never got to `docx-review create`.

## Proposed Solution: OpenClaw's Approach

OpenClaw has no hard iteration limit. Instead it uses:

### 1. Context Window Bounding
```yaml
context_window: 150000  # tokens
```
The agent runs until it hits token limits, then compacts. This naturally limits iterations based on actual resource usage.

### 2. Loop Detection (Optional)
```yaml
loop_detection:
  enabled: true
  repeat_threshold: 3      # warn after 3 identical calls
  critical_threshold: 6    # hard stop after 6 identical calls
```
This catches infinite loops without penalizing legitimate complex workflows.

### 3. Compaction on Overflow
```yaml
compaction_mode: safeguard
```
When context fills, compact the conversation rather than failing.

## Why This Is Better

| Approach | Hard Iteration Limit | Context + Loop Detection |
|----------|---------------------|--------------------------|
| Complex tasks | ❌ Fails at 20 | ✅ Runs to completion |
| Infinite loops | ❌ Wastes 20 iterations | ✅ Caught at 3-6 repeats |
| Resource efficiency | ❌ Arbitrary cutoff | ✅ Based on actual usage |
| User experience | ❌ "No response to give" | ✅ Completes or explains why |

## Suggested Implementation

1. **Deprecate `max_tool_iterations`** or set default to 200+
2. **Add `loop_detection` config** with repeat/critical thresholds
3. **Add context window tracking** with compaction support
4. **Environment variable:** `PICOCLAW_LOOP_DETECTION_ENABLED=true`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Agent can complete a 30+ iteration task (literature review → Word doc)
- [ ] Infinite loops are detected and stopped within 6 iterations
- [ ] Context overflow triggers compaction, not failure
- [ ] Existing `max_tool_iterations` config still works (for users who want hard limits)

prs.title: feat(channels): add Sendblue iMessage and SMS transport
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

Adds a native Sendblue channel so users can text a PicoClaw agent over iMessage/SMS and get its answer on the same phone. The guide covers fresh free-account setup, human phone/contact verification, model prerequisites, secrets, and receive-webhook registration.

This draft proposes a self-contained channel through the existing factory and shared webhook server. It validates the secret, receiving line and sender; normalizes direct-message context; deduplicates the last 4096 accepted handles in memory; and uses the existing outbound workers. Configuration supports named instances, redacted secrets, environment overrides, persistence, and credential-triggered reloads.

Scope is direct-message text. Groups/status callbacks are ignored; incoming attachments produce an explicit unsupported-attachment notice. There is no durable inbox or exactly-once guarantee. Ambiguous sends are not automatically retried, because the provider endpoint has no idempotency key.

## 🗣️ Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 📖 Documentation update

## 🤖 AI Code Generation

- [x] 🤖 Fully AI-generated (100% AI, 0% Human)

Independent human review is still pending.

## 🔗 Related Issue

No existing issue. Draft integration proposal; upstream design acceptance is pending.

- **References:** [Send API](https://docs.sendblue.com/api/resources/messages/methods/send), [receiving/free-plan contact verification](https://docs.sendblue.com/getting-started/receiving-messages), [webhook registration](https://docs.sendblue.com/api/resources/webhooks).

issues.title: fix: Add maxTurns limit to prevent agent loop runaway
issues.body:
## Summary

The Claude Agent SDK's `query()` function is invoked without the `maxTurns` parameter, allowing unlimited loop iterations. This caused a production incident where the agent sent 21 duplicate messages within 32 seconds.

## Incident Details

- **Symptom**: User asked for a reminder in Finnish, received ~20 identical "I'll remind you" messages
- **Root cause**: Agent SDK looped 21 times without limit, calling `send_message` each iteration
- **Secondary issue**: Agent lost Finnish language context mid-execution due to degraded context over iterations
- **Duration**: 32 seconds, single container execution, exit code 0

## Technical Analysis

### Current State

**`container/agent-runner/src/index.ts:237`** - No `maxTurns` in query options:
```typescript
const result = await query({
  prompt: userMessage,
  options: {
    // maxTurns: NOT SET → UNLIMITED LOOP
  }
});
```

**`container/agent-runner/src/ipc-mcp.ts:60-65`** - Ambiguous tool response:
```typescript
// Returns "Message queued for delivery (filename)"
// SDK interprets this as "task not complete, keep going"
```

### Why This Happens

1. Agent receives message requiring action
2. Agent calls `send_message` tool
3. Tool returns generic "queued" response
4. SDK sees: task not complete, continue loop
5. Agent calls `send_message` again
6. **No `maxTurns` limit** → repeat indefinitely
7. Container eventually exits, but damage done

## Required Fixes

### Fix 1: Add `maxTurns` Parameter (Critical)

**File**: `container/agent-runner/src/index.ts`

```typescript
const result = await query({
  prompt: userMessage,
  options: {
    maxTurns: 10,  // ← ADD THIS - prevents runaway loops
    // ... other options
  }
});
```

**Rationale**: 10 turns is sufficient for complex tasks while preventing runaway behavior. Can be tuned based on usage patterns.

### Fix 2: Improve Tool Response Format (Secondary)

**File**: `container/agent-runner/src/ipc-mcp.ts`

Current response is ambiguous:
```typescript
return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `Message queued for delivery (${filename})` }] };
```

Improve to signal completion more clearly:
```typescript
return { 
  content: [{ 
    type: "text", 
    text: `✓ Message sent successfully. The user will receive: "${truncate(message, 100)}"`
  }] 
};
```

### Fix 3: Review Agent Instructions (Secondary)

**File**: `groups/main/CLAUDE.md` (lines 14-22)

Review for patterns that could trigger repeated sends:
- "make sure the user receives"
- "confirm delivery"
- "ensure the message is sent"

These patterns can cause the agent to retry `send_message` even after success.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `maxTurns: 10` added to query options in `container/agent-runner/src/index.ts`
- [ ] Tool response format reviewed/improved in `ipc-mcp.ts`
- [ ] Agent instructions reviewed for loop-inducing patterns
- [ ] Test with reminder request to verify no duplicate sends
- [ ] Rebuild container: `./container/build.sh`

## Environment

- **SDK Version**: `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` v0.2.29
- **Known SDK Issues**: 
  - Issue #16752: Warmup infinite loop
  - SDK v0.2.19 duplicate tool_use IDs

## References

- Claude Agent SDK has no built-in retry limit by default
- TypeScript SDK `query()` does not enforce `maxTurns` unless explicitly set
- Tool responses with ambiguous completion signals can trigger retry behavior

prs.title: fix(discord): strip newline suffix from custom_id before parsing Gateway interactions
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes every Discord DM approval-card button tap routing to **reject**, regardless of which button was pressed.

## Root cause

`@chat-adapter/discord` encodes button `custom_id` as `<actionId>
<value>` (newline delimiter). The Gateway interaction handler in `handleForwardedEvent` parsed `custom_id` directly without stripping the `
<value>` suffix, so `tail` ended up as `"0
0"` instead of `"0"`. This failed the `/^\d+$/` check in `resolveSelectedOption`, returned the raw string, and the approval handler's `if (selectedOption !== 'approve')` fast-path rejected everything — including taps on the Approve button. The "0 0" display visible in the edited embed was the raw `"0
0"` fallback label rendered by Discord.

## Fix

Extract the `actionId` by slicing at the first `'
'` before parsing the colon-delimited segments. This mirrors what `decodeDiscordCustomId` already does on the webhook path.

## Changes

- `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts` — one-line fix in `handleForwardedEvent`
- `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge-gateway.test.ts` — regression test: fires a real `GATEWAY_INTERACTION_CREATE` event at the bridge's local HTTP server with a `
`-encoded `custom_id` and asserts `onAction` receives a clean index string (`"0"`) with no newline

prs.title: feat(add-apple-container): run v2 agent sessions on Apple container instead of Docker (macOS)
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-apple-container`, a session-driver skill that runs each agent session on Apple's `container` runtime instead of Docker, on macOS. We have run v2 agent sessions on Apple container since June 2026: on a personal install first, and since August on a multi-user install.

- **Why**: by design, Apple container runs each agent session in its own lightweight VM with its own kernel; Docker Desktop and similar tools run every container inside one shared Linux VM. Apple container is Apache-2.0, whereas Docker Desktop is free only for small businesses, personal use, education and non-commercial open source ([license](https://docs.docker.com/subscription/desktop-license/)). With Apple container, memory also follows sessions: each session's VM has its own limit (1 GB by default) and returns its memory to macOS when that session ends. Docker Desktop runs one VM for all containers, allowed up to half the Mac's memory by default, and frees it only when the VM shuts down after five minutes with no containers running ([Resource Saver](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/use-desktop/resource-saver/)).
- **Skill**: the driver, its registration module and its tests ship in `.claude/skills/add-apple-container/payload/` (the `/add-onecli` shape). Apply copies them into `src/drivers/`, appends one import to `src/drivers/installed.ts`, and sets `NANOCLAW_RUNTIME_DRIVER=container`. `REMOVE.md` reverses all of it. Docker stays the default.
- **Driver**: no `--security-opt`/`--pids-limit` (the CLI rejects them; the pids cap becomes `--ulimit nproc`); `host.docker.internal` in env values rewritten to the bridge gateway IP, looked up from `container network inspect default` on every spawn (the subnet can move on a runtime restart); a failed lookup fails the spawn; nested file mounts never passed to the runtime (they replace the parent share, apple/container#2148): dropped when identical, otherwise copied into the parent share without following symlinks; JSON listing filtered by label client-side; `container system start` when the runtime is down; no sidecar containers.
- **Trunk, update drain** (`scripts/update/service.ts`): Apple container has no `ps` and no `--filter`, so cutover could not list containers and every update refused. Containers are now listed through one helper; Docker keeps its exact `ps --filter --format` call. On Apple container anything not yet `stopped`, including `stopping`, counts as alive.
- **Trunk, image build** (`container/build.sh`, only when `CONTAINER_RUNTIME=container`): passes `-m 8G` (the default builder VM runs out of memory), and prunes dangling images after a build (replaced images leak their snapshot, apple/container#2164).
- **Limitations**: Apple silicon and macOS 26; `container` 1.5.0 or newer. Container egress can stop after a macOS update or reboot; `container system stop && container system start` restores it. A nested file mount replaces its parent share, hence the driver's handling. There is no `container ps`. `build.sh` and the update controller read `CONTAINER_RUNTIME` from the environment, not `.env`, so the skill asks the operator to export it.
- **Rollback gap (not fixed here)**: a rollback does not restart gateway-role containers on Apple container. `restartGatewayContainers` calls `restart -t`, which `container` 1.5.0 does not have, and the printed manual hint uses Docker syntax (`ps -aq --filter`). A gateway running in Docker, such as iron-proxy's, is not seen by the Apple drain or restart.
- **Out of scope**: remote OneCLI gateways, a startup wait for the runtime's XPC service, and the agent-runner config-read retry (see Related work).

## Related work

No issue. It is safe to review directly because the driver only loads when an install applies the skill and sets `NANOCLAW_RUNTIME_DRIVER=container`, and the two trunk edits are gated on `CONTAINER_RUNTIME=container`, leaving Docker installs on the same commands. Overlapping Apple container PRs, all written against the pre-driver-seam `container-runner.ts`/`container-runtime.ts`:

- #2609 (file mounts, `host.docker.internal`, user mapping): covers nested file mounts and the `host.docker.internal` rewrite (resolved from `container network inspect default`, not a hardcoded `/etc/hosts` line). Does not cover its root-start plus `setpriv` user mapping; this driver uses the Docker driver's `--user`.
- #2649 (skip nested file mounts): covered inside the driver, without a trunk change.
- #2650 (retry the `container.json` read on a mount race): not covered.
- #2809 (Apple container runtime plus remote OneCLI gateway): covers the runtime switch, host-gateway rewrite, label-scoped orphan cleanup and `system start`. Does not cover the remote gateway, the host-side forwarder, or the `$HOME`/`TMPDIR` check.
- #1107 (remove the `.env` `/dev/null` shadow mount): that mount no longer exists in trunk; nothing to cover.
- #1128 (wait for the XPC service before startup): partly. `ensureReady` starts a stopped runtime; it does not wait for the service after a reboot.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm run format:check`, `pnpm run build`, container `tsc --noEmit` -> clean.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` (full) -> 281 files passed, 2 skipped; 3561 tests passed, 15 skipped.
- `scripts/update/service.test.ts` -> 46 passed. Red-proof: with upstream's `service.ts`, the 4 new Apple tests fail; treating only `running` as alive fails the `stopping` test. The existing Docker tests assert the unchanged `docker ps --filter ... --format ...` argv and pass before and after.
- Skill applied twice with `applySkill` on a clean `upstream/main` worktree -> first run wrote 6 files, appended 1 line, set 1 env key, built; second run changed nothing. `grep -c apple-container-registration src/drivers/installed.ts` -> 1.
- Installed tests, `pnpm exec vitest run src/drivers/` with `container` 1.5.0 on `PATH` -> 178 passed, 1 skipped, including the real-binary contract test (4 passed; it skips itself where the binary is absent).
- Gateway lookup red-proofs: adding a host-interface fallback on an inspect failure fails the inspect-fails test; returning a hardcoded address when `ipv4Gateway` is missing fails the no-ipv4Gateway test; caching the gateway per driver instance fails the moved-subnet test.
- Registration red-proof: deleting the `installed.ts` line turns both cases in `apple-container-registration.test.ts` red.
- Trunk driver conformance suite (`src/drivers/conformance.test.ts`) with an Apple container harness added locally -> 60/60 passed; removing the driver's `--label` args turns 3 red. Not shipped: the suite has no factory for out-of-tree drivers, and copying the trunk file into a payload is against the skill rules. A `defineSessionDriverConformance`-style factory would be a separate PR.
- `REMOVE.md` followed on the same worktree -> `git status` clean, `git diff upstream/main` empty (apply left an empty, git-ignored `.env`).
- `scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts` lints and stub-applies the skill -> passes.
- Live: v2 agent sessions have run on Apple container since 2026-06-18, about four months: a personal install from June, and a multi-user install (11 agent groups on one Mac, macOS 26.7) since 2026-08-07, through `container` 1.5.0 (upgrading through 1.0.0, 1.2.2 and 1.4.1). The workarounds in Limitations come from that use.
- **Not run in upstream CI**: the payload tests. `vitest.config.ts` excludes `payload/`, and `scripts/test-registry-skills.ts` only picks up registry-branch skills and provider payloads, so nothing in CI applies this skill or runs its tests. `apple-container-cli-contract.test.ts` needs a reachable `container` runtime and skips without one.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-apple-container skill: run agent sessions on Apple's container runtime (macOS 26, Apple silicon) instead of Docker. Updates now drain Apple container sessions correctly.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Containers: each session is a separate VM. `no-new-privileges` has no equivalent on this runtime; `--cap-drop=ALL` and `--init` are kept.
- Mounts: a nested file mount loses its read-only protection, because it reaches the guest through its writable parent share. When the content differs, the host copies the file into the root of a writable, non-install parent share via a temp file and rename; it never writes through a symlink, never blocks on a FIFO, and refuses read-only shares, install surfaces and deeper paths.
- Credentials: unchanged. The gateway proxy URL is rewritten from `host.docker.internal` to the bridge gateway IP; nothing new enters the container environment.
- Update drain: Docker installs keep the same command. On Apple container a list or parse failure refuses cutover rather than reporting drained.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): never lose or repeat a reply around send_message
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops agents losing or repeating a reply around `send_message`, for streaming providers (each message goes out as it is written) and end-of-turn providers (messages go out from the final answer).

- **Problem**: the runner guessed whether a turn had replied. An "On it" sent with `send_message` counted as the reply, so an answer then left unwrapped was dropped with no nudge (reported live below). The reverse case sent a reply twice.
- **Fix**: a `send_message` send or a reaction no longer settles the turn. If the final text is left unwrapped after one, the nudge shows the agent what it already sent, and where, and asks for `<internal>done</internal>` or only what is missing. In the retry, a block that exactly repeats a message the nudged turn already sent is not sent again.
- **Agents and blocks**: a block to another agent is not the reply, unless it goes back to the agent that woke the turn. A block that never went out (missed by the stream, or unknown destination) always gets the nudge.

Still not covered: one nudge per turn (if the agent ignores it, the answer is lost, as on `main`); a *wrapped* "On it" block followed by an unwrapped answer counts as replied; a retry that repeats a send through the tool instead of a block is not deduplicated.

## Related work

Related to #3026. Reported live on `main` in the comment below (ack by tool, long bare answer, nothing delivered).

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test` → 571 pass, 0 fail. Every rule is tested for both kinds of provider; removing any rule fails at least one test. New: the reported shape, retry repeats, a follow-up queued ahead of the retry, reaction-only turns, reply to a calling agent, emoji-safe quote clipping.
- Host `pnpm test` → 3344 pass, 0 fail. Typechecks, `skill-pins:check` and `prettier --check` on changed files → clean.
- Live on Claude at 3eaa5c66 (isolated Mac install): an ack by `send_message`, five tool calls, then a ~2,000-character bare report was nudged and delivered once, 3 of 3 runs. A reaction-only turn was nudged and answered done, with no extra message. A worker agent's block to its caller plus a bare closing note sent one message with no nudge, 3 of 3. After a nudge, a re-wrapped repeat of a tool send was skipped, 2 of 2.

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
**Agents no longer lose or repeat a reply around the send_message tool.** When an agent sends something with send_message and then leaves its answer unwrapped, it is shown what it already sent and asked to finish, and an exact repeat is not sent twice. Applies to every agent provider. On streaming providers, a reply sent with send_message and followed by plain closing text now costs one extra model turn.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. Reads the agent's own outbound rows; the nudge quotes only what the agent itself sent, escaped. No new inputs or permissions.

prs.title: feat(experts): add configurable expert plaza and first-run deliverables
prs.body:
## Summary

Add a configurable Expert Plaza where users discover task-specific Agents and summon them into a new conversation with an editable, unsent starter question. Move Kits into the shared Kits / Skills / Connectors directory. Expert content is maintained separately and delivered through Overmind plus a versioned CDN catalog.

The latest acceptance work makes popular default questions immediately usable: for example, the PowerPoint expert receives a complete coffee-shop business-review brief and produces a six-slide editable deck after one user message, without asking for a topic, audience or template.

## Changes

- Add featured scenarios, search, category filters, expert details and three starter questions. The content repository contains 70 bilingual experts, 15 categories and 14 scenarios, with office work, content creation and everyday computer tasks first.
- Keep Summon visible at the top right of each card; the remaining card surface opens details. Add category portraits, a compact robot fallback, a distinct navigation icon and an accessible featured rail without a visible native scrollbar.
- Add an installed-expert picker to the composer. Preserve the draft when switching Agents, reuse an installed preset when summoning, wait for OpenClaw configuration sync, and reveal the relevant sidebar group. Summoning never sends the draft automatically.
- Validate catalog schema, version, SHA-256 and download limits; deduplicate concurrent loads and retain an environment-isolated last-valid cache.
- Preserve existing Agent instructions, model, skills, identity and other user settings during catalog updates. Track avatar ownership with the nullable `agents.icon_customized` column: update recognized managed defaults while preserving user-selected avatars and main/custom Agents. Only send an icon update from settings when the icon actually changes.
- Update the bundled XLSX skill to 1.0.1. On Windows, recalculate `.xlsx` files with an isolated LibreOffice profile, bounded execution, output validation and an atomic replacement guarded against concurrent source changes. Timeout cleanup targets only the subprocess tree; existing Linux/macOS behavior is retained.
- Preserve the development profile and loopback renderer URL in protocol launches so login callbacks return to the same validation instance. Packaged registration and the authentication exchange are unchanged.
- Consolidate the feature design, compatibility rules, supporting fixes and acceptance findings in one Expert Plaza specification under `specs/features/expert-plaza/`. Temporary end-to-end drivers, browser profiles, session transcripts and output artifacts are excluded from Git.

## Content and first-run acceptance

The private [content feature branch](https://gitlab.corp.youdao.com/yangwn/lobsterai-expert-store/-/tree/feat/expert-plaza) contains the candidate catalog `2026-10-13.7` at commit `d5995d8`. It improves the first question for 24 popular experts, retains questions two and three, and adds first-delivery guidance for newly installed Agents. Existing installed Agent instructions are not rewritten.

Real Windows Electron / OpenClaw v2026.8.1 acceptance used the signed-in account's plan model, with only the catalog transport pointed at the local candidate. All model requests, tools and deliverables were real. The final runs covered the first 12 experts plus lesson planning and e-commerce: **14 final scenarios passed, each with one user message and no clarification call**. This is the result after fixes and reruns, not a 100% first-attempt success claim.

Deliverables included a six-slide PPTX with 223 editable shapes, a three-page DOCX, a three-sheet XLSX with 14 cached formulas, an actual poster and nine-second MP4, a working offline app, and checked reports/automation outputs. Six previously installed Agents were reused and their business settings compared before and after.

## Validation

The latest commit consolidates documentation only; no tests were rerun for that change. The results below are from the preceding implementation and acceptance work.

- All 13 GitHub checks passed on `5edfb8d83`, including CI, Electron Verify and security checks.
- 123 targeted Vitest tests across eight files passed (Agent/store compatibility, avatars, onboarding and catalog loading/validation).
- Seven content-repository tests and five XLSX Python unit tests passed.
- Changed-file ESLint, renderer TypeScript checks and Electron compilation passed; the merged local release preview was also checked and compiled.
- CDP-driven Electron acceptance and screenshots used no native keyboard/mouse automation. Actual files were inspected, Office documents rendered/opened, numeric results independently checked, and app interactions exercised.
- Earlier verification also covered the development login callback, sidebar behavior, narrow layouts, light/dark themes, English/Chinese and catalog loading in test/prod.

Known bounds: this covers selected examples on one model, not all 70 experts or arbitrary inputs. The default PPT demo uses editable shapes because native Chart/SmartArt previews are incomplete. Excel chart colors remain pale in the built-in preview, while values, cached formulas and conditional formatting were verified.

The [internal illustrated acceptance report](https://confluence.inner.youdao.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=442406715) contains the 14 scenario results, actual screenshots, downloadable deliverables, fixes and compatibility evidence.

## Screenshots

Expert Plaza card layout:

![Expert Plaza](https://ydhardwarecommon.nosdn.127.net/5c907428206013399463d936134c3abc.png)

Installed expert picker:

![Installed expert picker](https://ydhardwarecommon.nosdn.127.net/479752b7015d6f66de2d8444057c5ee0.png)

## Electron and release notes

- Main/preload: remote catalog service, `agents:expertCatalog` IPC and cache under `userData/expert-store`.
- Persistence: additive nullable `agents.icon_customized` migration; existing Agent records and preset IDs remain compatible.
- Runtime: existing Agent creation/config-sync path; no OpenClaw runtime patch.
- Development windowing: restore profile and renderer context before acquiring the single-instance lock.
- This PR targets `release/2026.10.13`. The local merged preview remains separate and is not pushed.
- Git publication does **not** deploy catalog `2026-10-13.7` to Overmind/CDN. The last verified test/prod catalog is `2026-10-13.5`; the candidate still requires the separate content-release flow. No production request samples are included.

## Design references

- [Expert Plaza design, compatibility and acceptance](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/blob/feat/expert-plaza/specs/features/expert-plaza/2026-10-13-expert-plaza-design.md)

prs.title: fix(openclaw): stop re-injecting AGENTS.md instructions into the first message
prs.body:
## Summary
The first message of every desktop session carries a `[LobsterAI system instructions]` block. That block repeats two sections that OpenClaw already puts into the system prompt through the agent's `AGENTS.md`:
- the default system prompt (`resources/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`, main agent only);
- the scheduled-task policy (every agent).

The same ~4.5K chars are also re-injected whenever the session prompt changes: when selected skills change, when Plan Mode is toggled, and on the first turn after an app restart.

With this change, the block leaves out a section only when both of these hold:
- the agent's `AGENTS.md` contains that section verbatim;
- the file fits OpenClaw's 20,000-char bootstrap budget.

Above that budget OpenClaw truncates `AGENTS.md`, so the injected copy may be the only complete one. In that case the prompt is kept as is.

## Related Issue
Refs #2440

## Changes Made
- **`src/main/libs/agentEngine/workspaceDeliveredInstructions.ts`** (new):
  - `removeWorkspaceDeliveredSections()` is pure. It removes the sections that appear verbatim in `AGENTS.md`, and only when the file exists and `trimEnd().length <= 20,000`. That limit is OpenClaw's `DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_MAX_CHARS`; LobsterAI does not set `agents.defaults.bootstrapMaxChars`.
  - `removeWorkspaceDeliveredInstructions()` reads `workspace-main/AGENTS.md` or `workspace-<agentId>/AGENTS.md`. It checks the default system prompt and `buildScheduledTaskEnginePrompt()`, the same sources that `syncAgentsMd()` writes.
- **`openclawRuntimeAdapter.ts`:**
  - `buildOutboundPrompt()` passes the injected body through the helper. Any failure logs a warning and keeps the full prompt.
  - When nothing is left, the block still has its header and the "replace earlier instructions" line, plus one line pointing at `AGENTS.md`. Earlier session-level instructions (for example Plan Mode) are therefore still replaced.
- **Unchanged:**
  - when the block is injected (still decided on the full prompt);
  - renderer, IPC and persisted session prompts;
  - `AGENTS.md` content.
  - Persisted prompts of existing sessions are deduplicated at injection time as well.
- **Spec:** `specs/bugfixes/system-prompt-duplicate-injection/2026-10-07-system-prompt-duplicate-injection-design.md`.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [ ] Manual testing performed

- **`workspaceDeliveredInstructions.test.ts`:** 9 passed. Covers:
  - delivered sections are removed;
  - the body is empty when everything is delivered;
  - a non-main agent keeps the default prompt;
  - a missing or over-budget `AGENTS.md` keeps everything;
  - real temp workspaces for main and for a non-main agent.
- **`openclawRuntimeAdapter.test.ts`:** 299 passed.
  - 3 new tests check the actual `chat.send` message.
  - The two dedup tests fail with the fix reverted.
  - The `createRunTurnAdapter` helper gained a `defaultSystemPrompt` option.
- **`src/main/libs/agentEngine` and `src/scheduledTask`:** 687 passed.
- **Lint and types:** ESLint (`--max-warnings 0`) on the touched files and `tsc --project electron-tsconfig.json --noEmit` are clean.
- **Real local state:** I ran the helper against my own OpenClaw state.
  - 10 of 12 active agents have an `AGENTS.md` under 20K.
  - For non-main agents, the first-turn block drops from 4,522 to 2,149 chars: the scheduled-task policy is removed, and the default prompt stays because their `AGENTS.md` does not contain it.
  - Not exercised through the `electron:dev` UI.

## Screenshots (if applicable)
N/A (no UI changes).

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [ ] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [ ] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management
- [ ] None

## Additional Notes
- **Workspaces whose `AGENTS.md` is over 20K keep the full injection.** My main workspace is about 20.2K, and the gateway logs `workspace bootstrap file AGENTS.md is 21655 chars (limit 20000); truncating`. Most of the excess is stale template content:
  - Old workspaces still have the template's `## 💓 Heartbeats - Be Proactive!` section (2.7K), which contradicts the managed Heartbeat Policy. `stripProactiveHeartbeatSection` only runs when a new workspace is seeded. OpenClaw 2026.8.1 renamed that heading to `## Automations - Be Proactive`, which the strip no longer matches.
  - OpenClaw doctor migrated the default TOOLS.md placeholder (about 0.9K) into `AGENTS.md`.
  - Trimming these comes in a follow-up PR.
- **Scope:** this only changes the runtime prompt. There are no IPC, storage, or OpenClaw config/restart changes.

Release notes

Sourced from @​univerjs/find-replace's releases.

🕶️ Release v1.0.3

New features

  • Pivot tables (Pro): Copy pivot tables together with worksheets.
  • Shape hyperlinks (Pro): Show hyperlink popups when hovering over shape text in Sheets, Docs, Slides, and Boards.
  • Notifications: Support custom CSS classes per notification.
  • Extensions: Expose the destination worksheet name to copy-sheet interceptors.

Improvements and fixes

  • Formulas: Improve conditional aggregate performance with array criteria.
  • Cell editing: Double-click a cell to select its editable content.

prs.title: fix(im): safely destroy background accumulators
prs.body:
## Summary

Prevent `IMCoworkHandler.destroy()` from throwing when it cleans up a background-delivery accumulator, which intentionally has no promise rejection callback.

## Related Issue

Fixes #926

## Changes Made

- Use optional invocation for the accumulator rejection callback during handler destruction.
- Add a regression test that creates a real background accumulator through a runtime message and verifies destruction does not throw.


prs.title: Preset spawn.allow: allowlist for spawn_agent targets
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds optional `agents.presets.<id>.spawn.allow` so a caller can only `spawn_agent` into listed presets (org-chart / coordinator graphs). Enforcement is in `resolve_preset` before provider work; the tool schema / description lists only allowed targets for the calling agent.

**Depends on:** [#1301](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/pull/1301) (chat ↔ sub-agent parity / patch `0002`) — **required**. This branch is stacked on that PR. Also [#1280](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/pull/1280) if that is still unmerged on the target base.

**Base pin:** `1f6d28ea750d6654d52d5899b8be67727ebf7a19` **with #1301 already applied**. Do not review against bare pin without parity — the hunks expect parity helpers and related `spawn_agent` / chat context changes.

**Compatibility (important):**

| `spawn.allow` value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Absent / `None`** | **Unrestricted** (legacy default — existing configs unchanged) |
| `Some([])` / empty list | Deny all spawn targets |
| Non-empty `Some([…])` | Allowlist only those preset ids |

RPC: `agents.preset.update` accepts `spawn_allow` (`null` clears to unrestricted); `preset.get` exposes `fields.spawn_allow`. Markdown agent defs: YAML frontmatter `spawn_allow` (CSV; empty string = deny all). Docs: `docs/src/session-tools.md`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-tools` — `test_resolve_preset_rejects_target_outside_spawn_allow`, `test_resolve_preset_empty_spawn_allow_rejects_all`, `test_resolve_preset_absent_spawn_allow_unrestricted`, `test_spawn_allow_bound_schema_*`, `test_execute_rejects_disallowed_preset_before_provider`
- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-config` — schema / agent_defs round-trip for `spawn_allow` (incl. empty list vs absent)
- [ ] Manual: caller with `spawn.allow = ["writer"]` → spawn `writer` ok, other preset → visible `spawn_agent denied`
- [ ] Manual: field absent → any known preset still spawnable (unrestricted)

prs.title: Chat ↔ sub-agent parity: persona, system_prompt_suffix, delegate_only, preset model
prs.body:
## Summary

Today several preset fields only affect `spawn_agent` sub-runs, not direct chat with the same agent. This makes coordinator/worker setups and “talk to the agent as itself” diverge.

This PR aligns the two paths:

1. **Sub-agent persona** — `build_sub_agent_prompt` loads the target workspace `IDENTITY.md` / `SOUL.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GUIDELINES.md` so a spawned agent gets the same written persona as direct chat.
2. **`system_prompt_suffix`** — appended in live chat turns, `raw_prompt`, and `full_context` (same Role / composite suffix content as spawn).
3. **`delegate_only`** — direct chat uses the same shared delegate toolset as spawn (`DELEGATE_ONLY_TOOLS`).
4. **Model resolve** — chat model order becomes explicit → session → **preset** → default / history, so a preset `model` is a real default when the session has none.

Docs comments on the preset schema note that suffix / `delegate_only` apply to chat and sub-agents.

**Base pin:** `1f6d28ea750d6654d52d5899b8be67727ebf7a19` (rebase onto latest `main` before merge). May also need [#1280](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/pull/1280) if that change is not already in the base (touches `spawn_agent` tool wiring). Independent of the follow-up `spawn.allow` PR.

**Compatibility:** additive for existing configs. No new required fields. Presets without suffix / `delegate_only` / `model` behave as before.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-tools` — workspace persona injection in spawn (`test_workspace_persona_injected_*`)
- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-chat` — `append_preset_system_prompt_suffix_*`, `resolve_chat_model_id_*`, `delegate_only_keeps_shared_delegate_toolset`
- [ ] Manual: agent with non-empty `system_prompt_suffix` → `chat.raw_prompt` / reply reflects it
- [ ] Manual: `delegate_only = true` → tool list matches spawn delegate set
- [ ] Manual: session without model, preset with model → chat uses preset model

issues.title: [Feature] Add built-in provider presets for CommandCode and Hugging Face
issues.body:
### Summary

Two OpenAI-compatible gateways are missing from the built-in provider catalog:
**CommandCode** and **Hugging Face Inference Providers**. Users can add them as
custom providers, but they get no preset entry and no official icon.

### Why these two

The built-in catalog already covers comparable aggregator / coding gateways such
as `opencode` and `kilo`. These two belong to the same category:

| Provider | Base URL | Compatibility |
|---|---|---|
| CommandCode | `https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1` | OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages |
| Hugging Face Inference Providers | `https://router.huggingface.co/v1` | OpenAI-compatible |

- **CommandCode** — a multi-model gateway (Claude / GPT / Gemini / top open
  models) with subscription plans (Go / GOAT / Pro / Max) plus a pay-as-you-go
  Provider API tier. The same API key authenticates both the CLI and the
  endpoints. Docs: https://commandcode.ai/docs/provider
- **Hugging Face** — Inference Providers, an OpenAI-compatible router that
  aggregates multiple inference backends under one token.
  Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers

### Request

1. Add both to the built-in provider catalog so they can be configured without a
   custom provider entry.
2. Add their icons to the frontend `providerIcon` map (providers without a mapped
   icon fall back to the letter icon today). Both have publicly-available icon
   assets (verified reachable on 2026-10-14):

   | Provider | Icon source |
   |---|---|
   | CommandCode | `https://commandcode.ai/apple-touch-icon.png` (180×180 PNG) or `https://commandcode.ai/favicon.ico` |
   | Hugging Face | `https://huggingface.co/front/assets/huggingface_logo-noborder.svg` (SVG) or `https://huggingface.co/favicon.ico` |

   (This follows the existing `kilo` pattern, which references
   `https://kilo.ai/favicon/android-chrome-192x192.png` directly.)

### Current workaround

Custom providers work fine; the only gap is the missing preset entry and icon
(they render the default placeholder / letter icon).

Thanks!

issues.title: [Bug]: Chat history bloat — file & screenshot tool outputs stored as base64 inside tool_result make long chats 10 MB+ and reliably hit the 30 s console timeout
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2-beta.3 (Docker)

## Description

Chat history responses become enormous — past 10 MB — because **tool outputs are persisted as base64 inside `tool_result` blocks** in the session JSON. Files sent via `send_file_to_user` store the **entire file base64-encoded** (e.g. a ~2 MB `.pptx` becomes a 2.2 MB text blob); screenshots / `view_image` outputs do the same (0.3–0.4 MB each). Combined with the console's fixed 30 s fetch timeout (see #6635), any chat where the agent sent a file or took screenshots becomes **unreliable to open on slow networks** (5 Mbps = ≥21 s ideal transfer for 13.3 MB, and lossy links push it past 30 s almost every time). Backend pagination (#7361) reduces download size but does not remove the base64 storage/transfer multiplier. **Update (2026-10-13):** response compression already landed in upstream main via #7917 (`ResponseCompressionMiddleware`, gzip for `application/json` full bodies, streams excluded); the measurements below were taken on v2.2.2-beta.3 which predates #7917, hence the missing `Content-Encoding`. The remaining gaps are the tool_result base64 bloat fixed by the companion fix PR #8229 and the frontend's still-fixed 30 s / `retries = 0` timeout.

**Related PR(s):** #7361 (chat history pagination + virtualization, open); #7917 (response compression, merged in main); companion fix PR #8229

**Security considerations:** None — no credentials or private data involved; this is about response size / timing behavior only.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2-beta.3
- **OS:** Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) inside Docker
- **Install method:** Docker image `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.2.2-beta.3` (pip venv at `/app/venv` inside the container)
- **Python version:** 3.11.15

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In the console, run a task that sends a file via `send_file_to_user` (e.g. a ~2 MB `.pptx`) and/or takes several screenshots / `view_image` calls.
2. Let the task finish, then open the same chat from the history list on a slow link (e.g. 5 Mbps).
3. Observe `GET /api/chats/{chat_id}?include_app_owned=false` transferring for ~30 s and then aborting; the transcript never renders and no error toast is shown.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `GET /api/chats/{chat_id}` returns the **entire** history as one uncompressed JSON. Measured on v2.2.2-beta.3: a 6-message chat (3 user + 3 assistant turns, 132 tool calls) produced a **13.3 MB** response (**96 % = 12.6 MB base64**; largest `tool_result`s are `send_file_to_user` at 2.19 MB and 2.12 MB plus several `view_image` outputs of 0.3–0.4 MB). No `Content-Encoding` is returned despite `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate` (no GZip middleware). Under a rate-limited (~50 KB/s) reproduction the fetch is **aborted at exactly 30.3 s** (`BrokenPipeError` server-side after ~40 % of the body sent, no retry — console request helper default `retries = 0`).
- **Expected:** oversized tool outputs should not be shipped inline as base64 in history; the transcript should load incrementally; and/or the frontend timeout should be adaptive with retry + an explicit error state.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
# persisted session JSON for the test chat
13,084,957 bytes  (default_*.json)

# GET /api/chats/{chat_id}?include_app_owned=false response
HTTP/1.1 200
content-type: application/json
(no content-encoding)            body: 13,298,482 bytes, ~0.8 s locally

# rate-limited proxy (50 KB/s) reproduction
[14:17:30] SLOW route ... len=3857591 start
[14:18:00] >> CLIENT DISCONNECT after 30.3s (sent 1540096/3857591) err=BrokenPipeError
```

## Additional Notes

- Backend root cause: `qwenpaw/app/chats/api.py` `get_chat()` converts and returns the **full** `agent.state.context` — no pagination, truncation or compression (`app/_app.py` has no `GZipMiddleware`).
- Frontend root cause: the shared request helper (`p()` in the console build, `Lc = 3e4`) applies a **fixed 30 000 ms `AbortController` timeout** with **0 retries** to every API call, including chat history.
- The storage bloat driver: `send_file_to_user` / screenshot / image tool outputs are persisted **as base64 inside `tool_result`** in the session JSON; a single file-transfer task can grow a 6-message chat to 13 MB.
- Suggested fixes: (1) persist file/screenshot outputs as workspace file references or content URLs instead of inline base64 (request-time stripping already exists for PDF blocks in #7621); (2) when serving history, truncate or omit oversized `tool_result` bodies (e.g. >64 KB) and show a "see attachment" placeholder; (3) response compression is already provided by #7917 on main (not yet in the 2.2.2-beta.3 release); the frontend timeout remains fixed at 30 000 ms with `retries = 0` even after #7917 (it only added retries for network-level errors), so an adaptive timeout / retry with a visible error state is still worth doing; (4) land #7361 pagination + frontend windowed loading for very long transcripts.

---

---

## QwenPaw 版本

2.2.2-beta.3（Docker 部署）

## 问题描述

历史会话响应体可膨胀到 10MB 以上，根因是**工具输出以 base64 形式内联持久化在 `tool_result` 中**。`send_file_to_user` 发送的文件会把**整个文件以 base64 编码**存入会话（例如约 2MB 的 `.pptx` 变成 2.2MB 的文本块）；截图 / `view_image` 的输出同理（每张 0.3–0.4MB）。叠加控制台固定的 30 秒请求超时（见 #6635），任何让 agent 发送过文件或截过图的会话，在弱网下都**难以打开**（5Mbps 下 13.3MB 理想传输就要 ≥21 秒，有丢包时几乎必然超过 30 秒）。后端分页 PR #7361 能减小下载量，但不会消除 base64 带来的存储/传输放大。**更新（2026-10-13）：** 响应压缩中间件已由 #7917 合入上游 main（`ResponseCompressionMiddleware`，仅对 `application/json` 完整响应 gzip，流式除外）；本文实测基于不含该中间件的 v2.2.2-beta.3，所以响应无 `Content-Encoding`。剩余缺口 = 由配套修复 PR #8229 修复的 tool_result base64 膨胀，以及前端仍然固定的 30 秒超时 / `retries = 0`。

**相关 PR：** #7361（历史会话分页 + 虚拟化，open）；#7917（响应压缩，已合入 main）；配套修复 PR #8229

**安全考量：** 无 —— 不涉及任何凭据或隐私数据，仅关于响应体大小与超时行为。

## 影响组件

- [x] 核心/后端（app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models）
- [x] 前端控制台（Console frontend web UI）

## 运行环境

- **QwenPaw 版本：** 2.2.2-beta.3
- **操作系统：** Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)，Docker 容器内
- **安装方式：** Docker 镜像 `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.2.2-beta.3`（容器内 `/app/venv` pip 虚拟环境）
- **Python 版本：** 3.11.15

## 复现步骤

1. 在控制台运行一个任务，让 agent 通过 `send_file_to_user` 发送文件（如约 2MB 的 `.pptx`），或多次调用截图 / `view_image`。
2. 任务结束后，在弱网（如 5Mbps）下从历史列表重新打开该会话。
3. 浏览器 DevTools 可见 `GET /api/chats/{chat_id}?include_app_owned=false` 传输约 30 秒后被中止；消息永远不会渲染，也无错误提示。

## 实际 vs 预期

- **实际：** `GET /api/chats/{chat_id}` 一次性返回**全部**历史记录，且为未压缩 JSON。v2.2.2-beta.3 实测：一个仅 6 条消息的会话（3 轮用户 + 3 轮助手，132 次工具调用）产生 **13.3MB** 响应（**96% = 12.6MB 是 base64**；最大的 `tool_result` 为 `send_file_to_user` 2.19MB / 2.12MB，另有多个 `view_image` 0.3–0.4MB）。请求头声明 `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate`，但响应**无 `Content-Encoding`**（后端没有 GZip 中间件）。在限速（约 50KB/s）复现中，请求在 **30.3 秒整被中止**（服务端发出约 40% 后收到 `BrokenPipeError`，无重试——控制台请求封装默认 `retries = 0`）。
- **预期：** 历史记录不应把超大工具输出以内联 base64 形式发送给前端；消息应增量加载；和/或前端超时应可自适应，并带重试与明确的错误提示。

## 日志 / 截图

```
# 测试会话的持久化 session JSON
13,084,957 字节  (default_*.json)

# GET /api/chats/{chat_id}?include_app_owned=false 响应
HTTP/1.1 200
content-type: application/json
（无 content-encoding）           body: 13,298,482 字节，本地约 0.8 秒

# 限速（约 50KB/s）复现
[14:17:30] SLOW route ... len=3857591 start
[14:18:00] >> CLIENT DISCONNECT after 30.3s (sent 1540096/3857591) err=BrokenPipeError
```

## 补充说明

- **后端根因：** `qwenpaw/app/chats/api.py` 的 `get_chat()` 将 `agent.state.context` **全量**转换并返回——无分页、无截断、无压缩（`app/_app.py` 未挂 `GZipMiddleware`）。
- **前端根因：** 共用的请求封装函数（console 构建中的 `p()`，`Lc = 3e4`）对包括历史会话在内的**所有** API 调用施加**固定 30 秒 `AbortController` 超时**，且**重试次数为 0**。
- **存储膨胀源头：** `send_file_to_user` / 截图 / 图片等工具输出以 **base64 形式持久化在会话 JSON 的 `tool_result`** 中；单次发送文件的任务就能让一个 6 条消息的会话膨胀到 13MB。
- **建议修复：** (1) 文件/截图工具输出改为持久化工作区文件引用或内容 URL，而不是内联 base64（请求阶段对 PDF 块的剥离已有类似实现，见 #7621）；(2) 提供历史记录时对超大 `tool_result` 体做截断或省略（如 >64KB），并显示"查看附件"占位；(3) 响应压缩已由 #7917 提供（main 上）；即使合入 #7917，前端超时仍固定为 30 000 ms 且 `retries = 0`（#7917 只增加了网络层错误的重试），因此自适应超时/可重试/可见错误状态仍值得做；(4) 合入 #7361 的分页 + 前端窗口化加载，以应对超长会话。
