prs.title: fix(console): echo the user's own message as the first frame of a new run stream
prs.body:
# fix(console): echo the user's own message as the first frame of a new run stream

## What Problem This Solves

A user message is only persisted at run end. While a run is in flight, neither `GET /api/chats` history nor the run's SSE stream contains the user's own message:

- the web console papers over this with a local optimistic echo;
- any client **without** a local echo — a mobile app, the console opened on a second device, an API consumer — cannot see this turn at all until the run finishes and it refetches history.

For multi-device setups the failure mode is "I sent a message and it is invisible on the other screen" for the whole duration of the turn.

## Change

Server-only, one file (`src/qwenpaw/app/routers/console.py`):

1. **`_user_message_echo_sse(content_parts)`** — best-effort serializes the request's content parts into an SSE frame:
   ```json
   {"type": "user_message", "id": "<uuid>", "content": [ ...parts... ]}
   ```
   Pydantic parts go through `model_dump(mode="json")`; `dict`/`str` pass through. If nothing is serializable the helper returns `None` and the stream is byte-identical to today.

2. **`_stream_with_user_echo`** — wraps `console_channel.stream_one`: yields the echo frame first, then delegates. The wrapper is passed to `tracker.attach_or_start` in place of the bare stream function.

### Frame-shape compatibility

The frame has **no `object` field** — the same shape as the existing out-of-band frames `turn_usage` and `replay_end`. The console chat SDK and the React Native client dispatch on frame type and ignore frames they do not recognize (those two frames have been emitted in production with no client changes required, which is the compatibility proof). No client is affected by this change.

### Reconnect semantics (verified in `task_tracker.attach_or_start`)

- the echo is produced **exactly once per run** — by the run producer, which is the only caller of the wrapped stream function;
- it flows into `run.buffer` like every other frame, so **reconnect replay includes it** — a reconnecting client sees the user's turn without waiting for the run to finish;
- attaching to a live run replays the buffer and never re-invokes the stream function, so there is **no duplicate echo** and the frame `id` is stable for the lifetime of the run (clients may use it for idempotency).

Reconnect requests (`reconnect: true`) are unchanged: they attach to the existing run and receive the already-buffered echo from the buffer.

## Evidence

New case `test_new_run_stream_leads_with_user_message_echo` (in `tests/unit/app/routers/test_console_chat_reconnect.py`): a fresh run's stream must lead with a `user_message` frame whose content equals the request input. All commands below run from the PR head (`693cbd49`).

(pre-commit, all 14 hooks over the two changed files)

```
$ pre-commit run --files src/qwenpaw/app/routers/console.py tests/unit/app/routers/test_console_chat_reconnect.py
check python ast.........................................................Passed
check docstring is first.................................................Passed
fix python encoding pragma...............................................Passed
detect private key.......................................................Passed
trim trailing whitespace.................................................Passed
Add trailing commas......................................................Passed
mypy.....................................................................Passed
black....................................................................Passed
flake8...................................................................Passed
pylint...................................................................Passed
```

(unit tests: new first-frame echo case + reconnect regression + tracker)

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/routers/test_console_chat_reconnect.py -q
5 passed in 1.88s

$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker.py -q

```

(adjacent regression: full routers suite + tracker)

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker.py tests/unit/app/routers/ -q

```

```

 .../app/routers/test_console_chat_reconnect.py     | 75 ++++++++++++++++++++++

```

## Out of scope

- No API schema change; no console front-end change; no React Native client change.
- The persisted message id is only known after the run ends; the echo frame's `id` is a per-run identifier (stable across reconnect replay of the same run). Clients that reconcile echo against history should key on content/position, as they already do for other frames.
- Web console handler for a second-device observer (optional hardening; the sending device's own local optimistic echo is unaffected) — follow-up if needed.

prs.body:
## Description

Add a clean plugin unload path and rollback-safe hot reload so plugin install / update / uninstall no longer rebuilds every live workspace, and a failed update does not leave users on a half-applied new version.

This PR introduces a two-layer teardown ledger (`PluginInstance`) and a `PluginLifecycle` facade (`load` / `unload` / `reload` / `update_config`):

- Official `register_*` entries record real teardowns (HTTP, provider, control command, middleware, prompt section, channel, tools, hooks). Workspace contributions are projected and revoked by name via `WorkspaceProjector` (`start_one` / `stop_one` for channels). Uninstall no longer calls `_schedule_all_agents_reload`.
- Unload modes (`shutdown` / `unload` / `uninstall`) share one ledger. Author shutdown / uninstall hooks run before table rows are dropped. `shutdown` only stops hosted resources (`custody` / `effect`) and does not clear tables or disk.
- Reload probes new code into `plugin_<id>__probe` first; import failure does not tear down the old instance. Hosted resources that do not go quiescent abort the swap. Rollback restores the previous directory / modules and does not run legacy uninstall hooks. Boot recovers interrupted “updating” / “migrating” markers.
- `update_config` rebuilds contributions without reimporting; a half-successful `register()` is torn down before the old config is restored. Disable is `config.plugins[<id>].enabled = false` (reserved framework key).
- Boot dependency policy is local-only: missing deps mark the plugin `FAILED` without installing. Explicit install / update / `POST /plugins/{id}/repair-dependencies` still go through `DependencyGate` (imported host-package blacklist → require restart). Console repair / status UI is intentionally not wired.
- CloudPaw no longer monkeypatches `PluginLoader.unload_plugin`; agent cleanup is an `api.provision` teardown (uninstall only).
- `LifecycleDelegate` is the single predicate at the reserved branch points (`owns_commit` / `owns_dependency_env` / `notify_unload`). Name collisions fail loudly and name the occupant.

Out of scope (documented as deferred): `SourceWatcher`, dry-run / interval-intersection gate enhancements, and Console repair / last-unload UI.

prs.title: fix(observability): Langfuse tool observation never records tool output
prs.body: ## Description Fixes Langfuse `tool.*` observations never recording `output`: tool spans were exported with `input` and `metadata` only, on 100% of normal (non-interrupted) tool calls. Root cause is an interaction between two components: 1. `ToolCoordinatorMiddleware._drain` returns as soon as it receives the final `ToolResponse` (and on ERROR/INTERRUPTED chunks), so it never resumes the `on_acting` generator chain afterwards. 2. `LangfuseToolSpanMiddleware.on_acting` wrote the observation output *after* its `async for event in next_handler()` loop. Since the generator is left suspended at `yield event` and later closed with `GeneratorExit`, that code never ran — while `tool_span`'s `finally: observation.end()` still ran during cleanup, which is why the span showed up with input but no output. The fix records the output at the moment the `ToolResponse` is captured, i.e. *before* yielding it, with a `try/finally` fallback for early generator close. The `finally` stays inside the `async with tool_span(...)` block so `observation.update()` always happens before `observation.end()`. More generally, any `on_acting` middleware code placed after its final `yield` is not guaranteed to execute because consumers may stop iterating once the terminal event is seen. This may be worth documenting in `MiddlewareBase.on_acting`; happy to follow up if desired. **Related Issue:** Fixes (#7963) **Security Considerations:** None. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Refactoring ## Component(s) Affected - [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [ ] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [ ] Documentation (website) - [x] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy ## Checklist - [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes - [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks - [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass - [ ] Documentation updated (if needed) - [x] Ready for review ## Testing 1. Unit: `pytest tests/unit/observability/test_langfuse_integration.py -v` — 14 passed, including two new regression tests: - `test_records_output_on_normal_drain`: output recorded exactly once on a fully drained consumer, and `update` strictly before `end`. - `test_records_output_when_consumer_stops_at_tool_response`: simulates `_drain` short-circuiting after the final `ToolResponse` (consumer breaks out of the loop, generator closed via `aclose()`) — the exact production path that lost the output. 2. Mutation check: with the fix reverted, the new regression test fails (`assert 0 == 1`), confirming it guards this bug. 3. End-to-end: ran a real agent tool call against a self-hosted Langfuse (langfuse SDK 4.15.4); the `tool.*` observation now contains the full `output` payload. ## Logs / Screenshots ## Evidence ```bash prs.title: fix: finish tool streams without yielding during GeneratorExit
prs.body:
## Description

Tool errors and interruptions can leave AgentScope's `Toolkit.call_tool()` suspended before its final `ToolResponse`. When QwenPaw stops consuming that generator, finalization enters AgentScope's yielding `finally` block and logs `RuntimeError: async generator ignored GeneratorExit` as an unhandled task exception. Returning immediately after a successful `ToolResponse` also skips middleware work after the stream.

Drain tool streams to exhaustion while retaining the first terminal result. The batch-tool path likewise preserves an interrupted result while consuming the remaining toolkit output. Handle `GeneratorExit` separately in `Runtime.run()` so closing a response stream saves partial state and runs cleanup without trying to emit an error envelope. Mark that closure as cancellation for persisted turn status. Ordinary cleanup exceptions after a terminal result are logged without overwriting the result; external task cancellation still follows the cancellation path.

Reproduced against upstream main `753cb6dc4`; this is not specific to research mode.

**Security Considerations:** No permission or authentication changes.

- [x] Bug fix

Existing tests cover tool lifecycle, offloading, cancellation, batching, and cancellation persistence. Fourteen additional local-only regression cases exercise the real AgentScope Toolkit for success/error/interruption, preserve a terminal error against later output, drain interrupted batch calls, explicitly close a Runtime stream, and distinguish ordinary cleanup failures from cancellation after terminal results. No test files are included in this minimal patch.

On unmodified upstream main, the local regression cases fail because tool streams are not exhausted; error/interruption paths log `async generator ignored GeneratorExit`. Explicitly awaiting `Runtime.run(...).aclose()` also raises that exact exception.

prs.title: fix(skills): sanitize skill_name before building staging paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`staged_skill_dir()` and `import_skill_dir()` interpolated a caller-supplied
`skill_name` straight into filesystem paths — both into the `mkdtemp` prefix and
into `<root> / skill_name`. A name such as `../escape` therefore escaped the
intended root.

CodeQL flagged one of these path expressions as *Uncontrolled data used in path
expression* (five tainted sources) during the review of #8055.

## Fix

- Drop `skill_name` from the temp-dir prefixes; use fixed module-level constants
  (`_SKILL_STAGE_PREFIX`, `_SKILL_IMPORT_STAGE_PREFIX`).
- Route the remaining sinks through the existing `safe_skill_dir()` guard
  (`normalize` + `resolve()` + `is_relative_to`) for defense in depth.
- `staged_skill_dir` builds its stage dir via `safe_skill_dir(temp_root,
  skill_name)` and still sweeps `temp_root` in `finally`, so a rejected name
  leaves no temp dir behind.
- `import_skill_dir` resolves both `target_dir` and `stage_dir` via
  `safe_skill_dir`, keeping the existing `bool` return semantics.

## Evidence

Local, on this branch:

- `pre-commit run --files <changed>` → all 17 hooks passed (`check-ast`, `mypy`,
  `black`, `flake8`, `pylint`, …).
- `pytest tests/unit/agents/skill_system/` → **777 passed**.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After `send_file_to_user` delivers an audio file, the tool-result keeps an audio `DataBlock` in session history. On later turns, `OpenAIChatFormatter` serializes it as `input_audio`. LM Studio (OpenAI-compatible, audio input limit = 0) rejects with:

```
Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'At most 0 audio(s) may be provided in one prompt. (parameter=audio)', 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': 'audio', 'code': 400}}
```

Neither `_is_audio_fallback_error()` nor `_EXPLICIT_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_PATTERNS` matched this wording on `main`, so strip → retry → learn never ran and the session stayed permanently wedged.

This is a third rejection shape in the family of #7015 / #7024. Open PR #7654 covers DashScope URL-shape and llama-server `audio input is not supported`, but **not** this LM Studio `At most 0 audio(s)` body — verified against #7654's diff before opening this PR.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8171

- Keep image/video `at most N` limits off the audio-strip path (they stay request-scoped media signals and do not teach `rejects_media` for a pure audio cap).
- Regression tests: classifier True/False cases + strip-and-retry / learn for the LM Studio body.

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, deleting a Creator project fails with `503 STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR` / `WinError 5` once that project's `creator.log` has been opened. `delete_project` renamed the project directory via `atomic_replace_path` / `os.replace` **before** releasing the per-project log handler (`close_creator_project_logging`) and the poller. prs.title: fix(task_tracker): register run only after the producer task exists
prs.body:
## Description

Two changes around `TaskTracker` bookkeeping.

**1. Register the run only after the producer task exists** (`task_tracker.py`)

`attach_or_start` registered the run with a placeholder `asyncio.Future` *before* creating the producer task, so a failure to create the task would leave an entry whose Future is never `done()` — and the status counters read `not state.task.done()`, so it would count as running forever. The producer task is now created first, and the run is registered only once it exists.

This is **defensive hardening, not a reachable bug fix**: the register/create window is synchronous (no `await`) and a running event loop cannot be closed, so the failure cannot occur in practice. It is kept because the ordering is strictly better and costs nothing.

**2. Stop a chat's live run when the chat is deleted** (`chats/api.py`)

`delete_chat` and `batch_delete_chats` did not call `request_stop`, so deleting a running chat left its run in `_runs` with a live task. The aggregate `get_global_status()["running_task_count"]` then stayed inflated while the chat could no longer appear in the chat list.

**Related Issue:** Refs #7991 — this does **not** close the issue. #7991's primary hypothesis is a counting-scope mismatch between the aggregate (all `_runs`) and the per-chat list (filtered by `archived` / app-owned / channel), which needs a product decision on whether the aggregate should count only visible chats. That part is left open for triage.

**Security Considerations:** N/A — no auth, config or data-handling surface changed.

issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up from #10601 for bounded sub-delegation approval enforcement.

Bounded child loops currently inherit tools without an approval manager. `gate_tool_approval` treats `approval: None` as `NotRequired`, so prompt-required inherited tools can execute in a child loop even though that loop has no operator approval route.

This issue tracks fail-closed approval enforcement for bounded child-loop tools other than the nested `delegate` special case already handled in #10601.

## Current Context

- #10188 closed the independent-delegate half by giving independent runs a fresh non-interactive approval manager from the target profile.
- #10601 closes the nested-`delegate` bounded-mode gap with a tool-level fail-closed refusal keyed on `approval_requirement("delegate")`.
- Bounded child loops still pass `approval: None` for other inherited tools, so the normal approval gate treats those calls as not requiring approval.
- #10610 is changing the shell V1 permission policy in nearby code and should be considered before choosing the bounded-mode behavior.

## Decision Needed

Threading a fail-closed approval manager into bounded child loops changes default supervised behavior: prompt-required inherited tools, including default supervised `shell`, would be denied instead of running without an approval decision.

Pick the bounded-mode policy before implementation:

- Follow #10188 and attach `ApprovalManager::for_non_interactive` from the target profile.
- Strip prompt-required tools from the bounded child registry instead.
- Add a new opt-in knob for this behavior.

## Acceptance

- Add an end-to-end regression with a non-`delegate` `always_ask` tool proving the tool implementation is never reached when no approval route exists.
- Cover supervised-denial, explicit `always_ask` denial, and explicit auto-approval cases.
- Document the bounded child-loop approval behavior and its relationship to #10188, #10601, and #10610.

issues.body:
### Affected component

zerocode/tui

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

Entering the SOP pane synchronously waits for `sops/list` before completing the global mode switch. While that RPC is pending, ZeroCode stops processing keyboard input and rendering updates.

This is especially visible when cycling through the top-level panes toward Quickstart: navigation reaches SOPs, pauses while the SOP list request is pending, and ignores further pane-navigation keys until the request completes or reaches the five-second client timeout.

On one current-master ZeroCode client reproduction against a same-version daemon, the SOP pane remained empty and displayed:

```text
RPC sops/list: timed out after 5s
SOP run status is stale. Retrying…
```

The timeout is intermittent: a later direct `sops/list` probe against the same daemon returned in about 1 ms, and a matched master TUI/daemon probe also opened the pane immediately. The responsiveness bug does not depend on the underlying reason for a slow response; any pending `sops/list` request blocks the main pane-switch path.

The blocking path is on current `master`: `switch_mode()` awaits `sop_pane.refresh()`, and `SopPane::refresh()` awaits `rpc.sops_list()` on the main event loop. This behavior was introduced when the SOP pane became a top-level ZeroCode mode in #9694.

### Expected behavior

Switching to or past the SOP pane should remain responsive regardless of daemon or filesystem latency. ZeroCode should enter the pane immediately, render a loading or stale-data state, and continue handling global navigation while `sops/list` runs asynchronously.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
1. Start ZeroCode from current master with a compatible daemon.
2. Use keyboard pane navigation to enter the SOP pane repeatedly until `sops/list` is slow or reaches its five-second timeout.
3. While the SOP list request is pending, press the pane-navigation key again.
4. Observe that ZeroCode does not navigate or respond until `sops/list` returns or times out.
```

### Impact

Affected users: ZeroCode users with a slow SOP directory, daemon, or RPC response.

Frequency: every entry into the SOP pane while `sops/list` is slow.

Consequence: global navigation and other keyboard input appear frozen for the duration of the request. A degraded SOP data source can therefore stall unrelated ZeroCode workflows.

### Logs / stack traces

```text
RPC sops/list: timed out after 5s
SOP run status is stale. Retrying…
```

### ZeroClaw version

v0.8.4 / master `d82b6f9cf6f20e02011cf514eeb29de2d2472cad`

### Rust version

rustc 1.97.0 (2d8144b78 2026-07-07)

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2

### Regression?

Yes, it worked before

### Pre-flight checks

- [X] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [X] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

milestone.description:
Phase 3: The Gateway. Separate the web surface from the agent core so the gateway is optional and can restart independently.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.9.0 gateway](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v090-gateway), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: agree the full core IPC contract first; finish the supported local IPC server; ship standalone zeroclaw-gw; migrate vendor webhook behavior into channel plugins; and have Tauri package and manage both processes.

Completion requires a core artifact without web assets or HTTP server code, a working IPC-connected gateway, core/channel operation when the gateway is absent, and demonstrated two-process desktop lifecycle. Existing OIDC, principal-isolation, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with this boundary. WATI is already retired. Feature acceptance and normal review/CI/release holds still apply.

issues.body:
## Purpose

This tracker is the source of truth for completing the remaining **Phase 2 runtime work in v0.8.6** and **Phase 3 gateway separation in v0.9.0** from [RFC #5574](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/5574).

It owns the deliverable map, remaining gaps, sequencing, and release-completion evidence. The [v0.8.6 milestone](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/milestone/31) and [v0.9.0 milestone](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/milestone/11) provide release assignment views. Existing implementation trackers, especially #8850, retain their detailed work lists; link them here instead of opening duplicate program trackers.

This revises the earlier fixes-only description of v0.8.6 to include the remaining Phase 2 work alongside compatible fixes. v0.9.0 is centered on separating the web surface from the agent core. Existing authentication, principal-isolation, security, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with that boundary.

## Evidence and scope

Audit date: 2026-09-18. Source baseline: [core master ecc0c30c6b](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/tree/ecc0c30c6b58c61914b665d51887870e008f34b0), live issue/PR states, and the official plugin repository.

“Landed” below means the named implementation was merged and/or is present in the inspected source. It does not certify the complete release acceptance scenario. No release-artifact or live-service acceptance test was run for this planning audit. All delivery checkboxes remain open until their acceptance evidence is attached.

Delivery-issue pass: 2026-09-20, checked against [core master a7dad4ae5c](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/tree/a7dad4ae5c0fa1b24996f6d94e07251edf11880b) and the live open-issue inventory. The uncovered work now has 12 focused sub-issues: seven assigned to v0.8.6 and five to v0.9.0. Each has acceptance criteria and links to the relevant existing work. `status:accepted` records the agreed delivery scope; it does not ratify an unresolved design or approve an implementation. Native blocking relationships record the explicit dependencies between these new issues.

The maintained [FND-001](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md), [ADR-006](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/decisions/ADR-006-runtime-channel-plugins.md), [ADR-007](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/decisions/ADR-007-gateway-extraction.md), and [ADR-009](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/decisions/ADR-009-wit-wasmtime-plugin-execution.md) qualify the older RFC excerpts:

- The accepted plugin execution backend is direct Wasmtime with WIT components. Extism was superseded by ADR-009.
- WATI was retired by #9571 and removed from FND-001's migration target. It is not a remaining channel deliverable.
- A `zeroclaw-gateway` crate and local daemon RPC already exist. A standalone `zeroclaw-gw` process and its complete supported IPC boundary do not.
- The current IPC endpoint is `<data_dir>/daemon.sock` on Unix and a data-directory-derived named pipe on Windows. The future `zeroclaw-kernel`, `ipc` feature, and `kernel.sock` names in the old text need an explicit mapping to the current implementation; they are not existing components.
- This plan does not require deleting all of `zeroclaw-runtime` before the gateway can be separated.

## v0.8.6 runtime

Theme: formalize a clean agent runtime and let users install optional capabilities without rebuilding ZeroClaw.

| Deliverable | Existing work and verified state | Remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1: Clean runtime composition boundary** | #5559 landed the workspace split; #7430 landed `DaemonRegistry`. Current `daemon/registry.rs` registers subsystem starters. The old #5618 issue is closed as not planned, so its state alone is not delivery evidence. | Define and finish the public runtime/registry composition contract, or record the reviewed equivalent of the RFC sketch. Move concrete provider/tool/channel construction to the owning composition layer. Runtime still depends on `zeroclaw-tools` and constructs concrete tools. Prove independent runtime use and a thin executable entry point. **Delivery: #10993**, with existing channel dependency work in #6864. |
| **D2: WASM execution bridge** | #8368 landed the Wasmtime component host; #10146 activates logical channel instances; #9582 governs tool HTTP egress; #10750 governs channel HTTP egress. ADR-009 owns the accepted backend design. | Complete the supported release-artifact backend/permission/configuration path and its end-to-end proof. #8863 supplies the still-open WebSocket capability needed by Discord and declares #8923 as its prerequisite. The existence of a host adapter does not prove every channel's networking or lifecycle is supported. **Delivery: #10994** (supported artifact) and **#10999** (Discord acceptance). |
| **D3: Registry client and package lifecycle** | #8264 landed registry search and install-by-name. Current `src/plugin_registry.rs` reads the official JSON registry, resolves versions, downloads archives, and checks provided hashes. `PluginHost` applies the configured manifest signature policy. CLI list/search/install/remove/info/migrate exist. #7333 was closed unmerged; #8264 is the landed implementation. | `plugin update` is absent from the current command enum. Define update/rollback and trust/compatibility behavior. Existing open work: #9584 grant ceremony, #10746 install load-verification, #10752 info/list load verdicts (depends on #10746), #10162 incomplete install/config seeding, and #9624 host/registry WIT compatibility. **New delivery issues: #10995** (update/rollback) and **#10996** (channel-instance configuration/grants). |
| **D4: Plugin installation during onboarding** | #9009 owns the broader operator onboarding program. Current Quickstart configures agents and channels. | Add an explicit onboarding-to-registry install/configure/activate flow that works from a downloaded binary without Cargo. **Delivery: #10997**; no implementation PR for the complete flow was found in the audit. Reconcile the original `zeroclaw onboard` command wording with the maintained CLI/Quickstart interface. |
| **D5: Core tools only in the default runtime** | #8850 is the existing optional-channel/tool migration tracker. Historical #5617 was closed with a “requirements have shifted” comment; its associated #5566 PR was closed unmerged. | Reconfirm the core tool set and move optional capability construction out of the default runtime. Current `all_tools_with_runtime` still builds cron, scheduling, Pushover, calculator, weather, canvas, and other tools beyond the RFC list. **Delivery: #10998**, including the focused composition slice and binary-size proof under #8850. |

### Runtime implementation PRs

PR states below were checked on 2026-09-18. Each link identifies the slice it supplies; the phase acceptance criteria still require the complete user-facing outcome.

| Deliverable | PRs to follow | Coverage and missing PRs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1: Runtime composition** | Merged: [PR #5559: workspace split](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/5559); [PR #7430: daemon registry](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/7430). Open supporting extraction: [PR #10557: extract cron into its own crate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10557). | Cron extraction reduces the holding crate, but does not complete the generic runtime composition contract. **No open PR completing the full D1 boundary was found.** |
| **D2: WASM execution and channel support** | Merged: [PR #8368: Wasmtime component host](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8368); [PR #10146: activate channel instances](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10146); [PR #9582: govern tool HTTP egress](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9582); [PR #10750: govern channel HTTP egress](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10750). Open drafts for the Discord transport path: [PR #9142: named TLS profiles](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9142); [PR #8923: TCP and STARTTLS](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8923); [PR #8863: channel WebSocket capability](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8863). | The execution foundations are present. The transport drafts, release backend/configuration choices, compatible Discord package publication, and end-to-end artifact proof remain. |
| **D3: Registry and package lifecycle** | Merged: [PR #8264: registry search and install by name](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8264). Open: [PR #9584: install/list egress-grant ceremony](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9584); [PR #10746: load-verify installation](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10746); [PR #10752: report info/list load verdicts](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10752). Merged supporting fix: [PR #11107: escape apostrophes in egress remedy commands](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11107), preserving the complete grant list as one shell argument. | These cover install usability and verification. **No open PR implementing the missing plugin-update/rollback command was found.** Channel-only grant seeding is explicitly outside #9584's scope. |
| **D4: Install plugins during onboarding** | **No dedicated open implementation PR found.** Existing coordination: #9009 and #8850. | Link the eventual install/configure/activate onboarding PR here; general onboarding changes alone do not meet D4. |
| **D5: Minimal core tools** | **No open PR delivering the complete core-only runtime tool set was found.** Existing coordination: #8850; historical #5617. | A focused tool-composition/packaging PR and binary-size evidence are still required. |

**Declared prerequisite order:**

- [PR #10746: install verification](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10746) precedes [PR #10752: load verdicts](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10752).
- [PR #9142: named TLS profiles](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9142) precedes [PR #8923: TCP/STARTTLS](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8923), which precedes [PR #8863: WebSocket capability](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8863).
- #9142 still cites [PR #8857: scoped secrets and encrypted state](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8857), which is **closed unmerged**. Its [closure record](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8857#issuecomment-5681552958) identifies merged [PR #9128: scoped tool secret service](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9128) and [PR #9129: channel config services](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9129) as the scoped-secrets replacement; the encrypted-state portion was deferred. Its other declared foundation, [PR #9137: shared egress policy](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9137), is merged. Reconcile that stale prerequisite before treating the transport chain as ready.

These dependency links come from the current PR descriptions and the verified predecessor dispositions. They do not certify that each branch has already incorporated the latest predecessor revision.

### Runtime gaps to close

- [ ] **R1: Runtime API and ownership.** #10993; supporting channel dependency cleanup remains in #6864. Finish D1 with explicit injection boundaries, dependency checks, and an independently usable runtime; incorporate the landed `DaemonRegistry` instead of treating it as missing.
- [ ] **R2: Supported plugin distribution.** #10994. Select and verify the execution backend for each shipped target and record the loading, grants, signature, and compatibility decisions. The current Cargo default feature set omits the plugin host. #8135 is still an unaccepted RFC with older Extism assumptions; citing it does not approve a default-on policy change.
- [ ] **R3: Registry update and install completeness.** #10995 (update/rollback) and #10996 (channel-instance configuration/grants), alongside existing #10162 (install recovery) and #9624 (compatibility). Finish the relevant #8850 install/verification work and define the missing update/rollback command. Include channel-instance grant/config seeding; #9584 explicitly excludes channel-only grant seeding.
- [ ] **R4: Install-from-onboarding experience.** #10997, coordinated with #9009/#8850. Provide a focused implementation under the existing onboarding/plugin programs and prove the complete user flow without a Rust toolchain.
- [ ] **R5: Minimal core and size evidence.** #10998. Agree the retained core tools, implement the optional-tool boundary, and record binary size for named release targets/profiles in release notes. Reuse #8850; historical issue closure is not proof of this criterion.
- [ ] **R6: Discord acceptance.** #10999. The official plugin repository contains [Discord source](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins/tree/main/plugins/discord), but its README requires host WebSocket capability. #8863 is open, that host feature is absent from the inspected master, and the [official registry index](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins/blob/main/registry.json) has no Discord entry. Publish and verify the compatible package and demonstrate install, configuration, inbound delivery, and replies from the supported release binary. Reconcile the original `channel-discord` example with the actual package name `discord`.

The RFC core-tool baseline is `shell`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `file_edit`, `git_operations`, `glob_search`, `content_search`, `memory_recall`, `memory_store`, `memory_forget`, and `web_fetch`. Any revised set needs a recorded rationale before D5 is marked complete.

**Runtime acceptance:** an independently usable runtime with the agreed dependency boundary; a real Rust/WIT tool plugin executing under the shipped host; Discord plugin installation and operation without recompilation; onboarding that installs plugins without Cargo; and published size measurements for the supported runtime artifact. A component unit test or a source directory alone does not establish these product outcomes.

## v0.9.0 gateway

Theme: make the web surface a separate, optional process that can be omitted or restarted without interrupting healthy agent execution.

| Deliverable | Existing work and verified state | Remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1: Agreed kernel IPC contract** | [RPC socket documentation](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/rpc-socket.md), `zeroclaw-api/src/jsonrpc.rs`, and the runtime RPC code define an existing NDJSON/JSON-RPC transport. The gateway also generates a partial OpenAPI 3.1 document in `openapi.rs`. #9133 recorded ADR-007; #8691 remains its decision-record home. | Agree the complete core-to-gateway contract for messages/streams, sessions, installed plugins, status, memory, and cron, including identity, permissions, version negotiation, cancellation, errors, reconnect, and lifecycle. Explicitly resolve how the requested OpenAPI 3.1 specification relates to existing non-HTTP JSON-RPC and the no-HTTP-server-in-core success criterion. **Design delivery: #11000**, with the review and decision linked through #8691/ADR-007 before dependent implementation. |
| **D2: Supported local IPC server** | `rpc/local.rs` already implements Unix sockets and Windows named pipes. Existing session/turn methods and protocol initialization are useful foundations. #8289/#7141 and open #10259 supply related principal/authentication work. | Complete the D1 method and lifecycle coverage for an external gateway; record the core owner/feature/endpoint mapping; prove isolation, authentication, version mismatch, cancellation, and reconnection on supported platforms. Existing local transport is partial delivery, not a reason to write a second server. **Delivery: #11001**, after #11000's contract review. |
| **D3: Standalone zeroclaw-gw** | `zeroclaw-gateway` already exists. ADR-007 describes the intended process boundary. Its current manifest still directly depends on `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zeroclaw-channels`; the daemon starts it through an in-process registry callback. PR #11041 supplies the dashboard/OpenAPI Nix package and NixOS module wiring as a packaging slice; it does not provide the standalone gateway process or IPC boundary. | Build and ship the standalone executable as an IPC client, move web assets and the HTTP server into its release artifact, replace process-local runtime access, and prove operation/restart/removal independently of the core. **Delivery: #11002**; no existing PR completing this extraction was found in the audit. |
| **D4: Channel-owned webhook behavior** | #8862 and #8949 are merged; generic plugin ingress and typed challenge replies are in current source. #8850 owns plugin migration. #8586 owns a narrower webhook-dispatch cleanup and explicitly does not implement the plugin migration. | Finish WhatsApp Cloud, Linq, Nextcloud Talk, and Gmail migrations with vendor-owned parsing/authentication, challenge replies, media, and delivery parity. Carry plugin route registration and dispatch across IPC: today's gateway receives an in-process `Arc<PluginWebhookRegistry>`. WATI is excluded because it was removed. **Cross-process delivery: #11003**; #8850 retains vendor migration ownership. |
| **D5: Tauri starts both processes** | #8708 and #9032 are merged, providing earlier sidecar packaging and dashboard embedding work. Current desktop code supervises the existing daemon/gateway product. | Package and supervise the separate core and `zeroclaw-gw` executables: startup ordering, readiness, authentication, compatible versions, gateway restart, coordinated shutdown, and upgrades. **Delivery: #11004**, after #11002; no implementation PR for the final two-process arrangement was found in the audit. |

### Gateway implementation PRs

| Deliverable | PRs to follow | Coverage and missing PRs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1: IPC contract** | Merged design record: [PR #9133: record gateway process and channel-plugin targets](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9133). | **No open PR completing the full gateway IPC contract was found.** The remaining design belongs with #8691 and ADR-007. |
| **D2: Local IPC parity and authority** | Open: [PR #10259: authenticated RPC principals](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10259). Open draft: [PR #10274: gateway route-layer principal consumption](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10274). | These are supporting authentication slices. **No single PR completing gateway IPC method/lifecycle parity was found.** The existing socket/pipe server is already present. |
| **D3: Standalone gateway** | **No standalone `zeroclaw-gw` extraction PR found.** Supporting viewer-lifetime work: [PR #10538: preserve a turn after WebSocket disconnect](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10538) and [PR #9002: gateway session lifecycle and reconnect](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9002), both open. | The two viewer-lifetime PRs overlap and need scope reconciliation. Neither implements the separate executable, removes direct runtime dependencies, or proves gateway-process fault isolation. |
| **D4: Channel webhooks across IPC** | Merged: [PR #8862: generic plugin webhook ingress](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8862); [PR #8949: typed plugin challenge replies](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8949). | **No verified open PR completing the required vendor migrations and cross-process webhook registration/dispatch was found.** Continue through #8850; #8586 remains a narrower dispatch-cleanup issue. |
| **D5: Two-process desktop** | Merged predecessors: [PR #8708: desktop sidecar packaging](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8708); [PR #9032: embed dashboard in the release sidecar](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9032). | **No open PR implementing final core-plus-gateway packaging and supervision was found.** Link that implementation after D1-D3 establish the supported process boundary. |

### Gateway gaps to close

- [ ] **G1: D1 design record.** #11000. Review the full IPC contract and its relationship to existing JSON-RPC before the process extraction is implemented. Link the decision through #8691 and ADR-007.
- [ ] **G2: IPC parity and authority.** #11001, blocked by #11000. Complete D2 for every supported gateway operation; keep domain state and authorization in the core and make the gateway a client.
- [ ] **G3: Binary and dependency separation.** #11002, blocked by #11000/#11001. Deliver D3, including release packaging and evidence that the core artifact contains no web assets or HTTP server implementation. Resolve any IPC transport conflict with that criterion in G1.
- [ ] **G4: Vendor webhook migration.** #11003 owns IPC registration/dispatch; #8850 retains the four vendor migrations. Finish D4 under #8850 with per-channel parity evidence and the cross-process registration/dispatch contract.
- [ ] **G5: Desktop integration.** #11004, blocked by #11002. Finish D5 and attach installer/startup/restart/upgrade evidence for the supported desktop platforms.

**Gateway acceptance:** `zeroclaw-gw` starts and serves the dashboard through the agreed local IPC contract; the core release artifact has no web assets or HTTP server code; stopping, restarting, or removing the gateway leaves healthy agent execution and supported channel plugins working; vendor webhook behavior lives in the channel plugins; and Tauri starts and manages both binaries.

#7759, #9002, and #10538 address viewer-disconnect/turn-lifetime behavior and are supporting work. They do not establish separate-process fault isolation. OIDC/principal work (#8289, #8290, #10259, #10274) and ZeroRelay (#8358) must be reconciled with G1/G2 rather than treated as proof of gateway extraction.

## Delivery order and routing

1. Close the runtime gaps through #10993–#10999 and the existing plugin/onboarding programs. #10998 depends on #10993; #10997 depends on #10996; #10999 depends on #10994/#10996 and the existing host WebSocket PR chain. The gateway IPC design (#11000) can proceed alongside this work.
2. Agree G1 in #11000, complete local IPC coverage in #11001, and deliver the standalone gateway in #11002. #11003 carries plugin webhooks over the reviewed IPC boundary. D4's channel migrations remain under #8850 and can proceed where their host and ingress contracts are ready.
3. Finish desktop integration in #11004 after #11002 supplies the separate executable and supported IPC boundary.
4. Attach release-artifact and end-to-end evidence before closing either phase.

Feature scope must be accepted before new milestone scheduling. Native reviews and checks remain the merge authority; normal compatible changes can merge once those requirements pass. Breaking changes keep `breaking-change` and the recorded `do-not-merge` release hold until the appropriate window and current validation permit it. This tracker does not ratify an open RFC or approve an implementation.

The target phase is recorded above. Linked work may currently be assigned to an earlier fix release, a later compatibility window, or no milestone; reconcile those assignments with scope and compatibility before claiming a complete release queue. In particular, #9584 and #10162 currently sit in v0.9.0 even though they contribute to the Phase 2 closeout, while #10746/#10752/#8863 are unassigned. This audit does not silently convert their PR review states into approval.

### September 28 supporting merges

- **v0.8.6 release reliability:** #11091, #11095, and #11105 are merged. Package preflight runs before the GitHub Release and gates stable version bumps; recovery can use verified master tooling against unchanged tagged source. Detailed implementation and validation evidence is recorded under R6/R7 in #10814. Required merge-queue CI passed; no live release or registry publication was performed.
- **v0.9.0 plugin egress coverage:** #11168 is merged as fe45268842 and closes #10008. The pinned-address regression test no longer depends on live DNS. Required merge-queue CI passed. This targeted test repair does not complete the broader plugin distribution or channel acceptance criteria above.

### September 30 authorization follow-ups

- Supporting v0.9.0 authorization work: #11234 (queued session ownership) and #11268 (shared gateway/RPC policy-publication documentation). CLI publication under #10876 and the nested-execution review concerns on #11220 remain open. These slices do not complete gateway extraction or release acceptance.

### October 3 supporting review routing

- **v0.8.6 compatible runtime and interface repairs:** #11424 (macOS daemon fail-fast behavior), #11447 (immutable process-test fixtures), #11445 (ACP recovery notices), and #11459 (transcript layout ownership). These are supporting repairs, not completion evidence for the phase deliverables.
- **v0.8.6 bounded placement exceptions:** #11436 names the manual-compaction runtime placement for #10905; #11476 names the worker-recovery placement for #11450. Placement approval does not approve either implementation. #11476 still has failing required Security/aggregate CI from the existing Wasmtime advisories; #11475 is the separate dependency repair.
- **v0.9.0 supporting boundary work:** #11455 confines dashboard filesystem reads, #11461 clarifies the deprecated legacy session-history append, and #10911 supplies the config-publication foundation. #10911 does not complete #10892; policy-publication ordering, nonparticipating writers, typed Web/TUI partial-success outcomes, and the applied-state ledger remain separate work. None of these PRs establishes the standalone gateway or full release acceptance.

### October 4 supporting review routing

- **v0.8.6 compatible test and guidance repairs:** #11495 (installed-executable budget fixture), #11483 (interpreter-launched MCP fixtures), and #11496 (localized iMessage/generic Chat guidance) received exact-head approval from @Aarlington. This is review evidence, not a merge or release-completion claim; #9965 and #9972 remain open.
- **v0.8.6 SQLite hygiene hardening:** #11458 has a focused change request for tests and Windows execution of its new non-Unix admission behavior. Its current required gate is green; the older Wasmtime-failure description has been superseded. The Unix missing-store permission finding is resolved.
- **v0.8.6 bounded placement records:** #11500, #11477, and #11476 have green required gates but conflict with master and need refreshed exception tables. The earlier required-CI hold on #11476 is cleared; placement sign-off remains pending. None of these records approves the associated implementation.

### October 7 supporting review routing

- **v0.8.6 compatible chat recovery:** #11431 received approval at `a74217e64ec1d4638013701c79de65812d045153`. Required CI passes, and the author verified a real daemon reload followed by automatic dashboard reconnect and a completed second answer in the same session. The change closes retired chat sockets through the existing gateway lifecycle; it does not implement gateway process separation.

### October 10 supporting review routing

- **v0.8.6 JPEG accounting correction:** #11637 received changes requested at `67e62d7301abe04c636391627c1813b89791e422`. Both encoded-input copies are now charged, but the reduced baseline projection still omits retained ICC and transient extended-XMP metadata. issues.title: feat(zerocode): make the per-pane session cap configurable
issues.body:
## Problem

A ZeroCode pane can track at most 8 sessions (the focused one plus background ones). The limit is a hardcoded constant:

- `apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs:487`: `const MAX_TRACKED_SESSIONS_PER_PANE: usize = 8;`, with the comment "Two panes keep the TUI comfortably under the daemon's 64-session cap."

When the pane is full, the sidebar "+", Change directory, resume and Ctrl+N all stop at the `zc-chat-session-cap` notice ("Session limit for this pane reached (8). Close a session from the sidebar first."). Startup resume also keeps any background entries past the cap in `resume_backgrounds` and doesn't reattach them (chat.rs ~2424).

Running several agents in parallel, one session per worktree, fills 8 slots quickly. The only fix is closing a session you still want. Meanwhile the daemon has room: its RPC `SessionStore` is built with 64 slots (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/daemon/mod.rs:967`, `SessionStore::new(64, ...)`), and two panes at 8 use 16 of them.

## Proposal

Add a ZeroCode config key for the per-pane cap, with the default kept at 8:

```toml
[sidebar]            # or wherever the maintainers prefer; see note
max_sessions_per_pane = 8
```

- Clamp to `1..=32` at load, so two panes stay within the daemon's 64 slots, matching the reasoning in the existing comment.
- Replace the constant at its call sites (chat.rs ~1851, ~1996, ~2424, ~4789) and use the configured value in the cap notice.
- The three `mpsc::channel(MAX_TRACKED_SESSIONS_PER_PANE)` buffers in `Chat::new` (~865-868) size reattach, resync and prompt-completion channels. They need to follow the configured value or get a fixed capacity of their own, so a larger cap can't block senders.
- If the daemon refuses a new session anyway (`session limit reached` from `SessionStore::insert`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/session.rs:552`; for example, other clients hold slots), the pane should show that error and keep the focused session as it is.

Note on placement: `SidebarSection` (`apps/zerocode/src/config/mod.rs` ~357) holds dock layout preferences, and this isn't one. A small `[chat]` section may fit better. Open to either.

## Out of scope

- Making the daemon's 64-slot `SessionStore` configurable (daemon side, separate change).
- Idle eviction of background sessions.

## Alternative

Raising the constant to 16 is a one-line change and keeps two panes at 32 of 64. That moves the limit without letting operators set it, which is why I'm proposing the config key.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** adds five rows to the holding-crate exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, and widens one existing row, so these changes to `zeroclaw-runtime` can merge under ADR-016:
  - **Operator override of an exceeded shared cost limit** (#11589, for #11585): the budget gate, the approval-adapter timeout plumbing and its localized text, plus releasing a waiting prompt when another session approves (`approval_withdrawn`). The override itself is persisted by `CostTracker` in `zeroclaw-config` so a restart keeps it until rollover; the row's review trigger no longer lists persistence, and adds an override that applies while `cost.allow_override` is off.
  - **Cost warning-threshold notice** (#11692, for #10950): one non-blocking `BudgetWarning` turn event per turn and its RPC `session/update` forwarding.
  - **Stored message times on `session/messages`** (#11622): an optional `created_at` on `MessageEntry`, read from the times the ACP session store already records.
  - **Per-session personality-file snapshot** (#11698, for #11696): the `Agent` renders its personality files once per session and reuses that text, so editing `AGENTS.md`/`SOUL.md`/... no longer invalidates the provider prompt cache for every live session; plus the owner-checked `session/reload_context` RPC method that re-reads them on request. First proposed separately in #11702, now folded here.
  - **Delegate child activity forwarding** (for #10531): a foreground agentic delegate's tool calls reach the parent turn as one live `DelegateActivity` event and `session/update` notification (tool name, secret-redacted argument summary, bounded result preview), so ZeroCode can show what a running child is doing. The event type lives in `zeroclaw-api`; the runtime part is the wiring. Not persisted, not forwarded for background delegates, and no new config key.
  - **#11456's existing row** named only `locales/en/cli.ftl`. That PR also adds its key to the es, fr, ja and zh-CN files, so the row now lists `locales/{en,es,fr,ja,zh-CN}/cli.ftl`.

  Greptile raised the missing exception on #11692. #11589 changes the same files, and #11622 adds an RPC field, so both need the same record, and so does #11698, and so does the #10531 forwarding work. The five new rows are marked **pending Core Team review**, like the other unapproved rows in the table. This PR changes no code.
- **Scope boundary:** this does not approve the code of #11589, #11692, #11622, #11698 or the #10531 forwarding change, and it does not generalise to other cost, budget, history, prompt or delegation work. The #11456 edit adds only the four locale paths. Each row lists the files, behavior and exclusions it covers.
- **Blast radius:** documentation only. Five added table rows and one widened path list.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11589, #11692, #11622, #11698, #11456, #11585, #10950, #11696, #10531. Replaces my own draft #11702 (same row, now closed).

### What this does, simply

New features in `zeroclaw-runtime` need a written exception from the Core Team before they merge. Five pieces of pending work add small features there: a prompt to continue past a spending limit, a warning when you get close to one, the time each stored message was recorded, and keeping each session's copy of its agent's notes files stable so editing them doesn't wipe the prompt cache, and showing a helper agent's tool calls live while it works. This PR writes down what each may touch, where the code is meant to end up, and when to look at it again, so the Core Team can approve or refuse them in one place. It also fixes one existing row that missed four translation files.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: documentation-only change to one table.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** none specific. The docs gates select files under `docs/book/src`, and the changed file is outside it.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** nothing validates the content of a row; that is what the Core Team's review is for.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`: `No docs files detected; skipping docs quality gate.` `git diff --check`: clean. Each new row has 4 cells, the same as the table.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The file lists against each PR's diff: #11589 at 225c52bb636f changes exactly the seven `zeroclaw-runtime` paths its row names, #11692 at 0bd22cf74fc4 changes exactly its four, and #11622 at 0435a94ce65b changes exactly `rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs` in runtime, its `dispatch.rs` changes all in `handle_session_messages` and the entry builder. #11698 at baea2ded64ad changes exactly `src/agent/{agent,prompt}.rs`, `src/tools/delegate.rs` and `src/rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs` in runtime. #11456 adds its key to all five locale files. The #10531 row names the files the forwarding change is planned to touch; its feature PR is not open yet, and I'll check the row against its diff before asking for review. The behavior claims were checked against the code: `try_send` and the turn-local latch in #11692; the period-bound grant on `CostTracker`, the per-agent exclusion and fail-closed handling in #11589.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New external network calls? **No**

## Compatibility (required)

prs.title: feat(zerocode): drag session rows and switch sessions by number
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Let users drag session rows to arrange Chat and Code sessions together in the Sessions panel.
  - Preserve click-to-focus and per-session close controls. Dragging above or below the list reveals additional rows.
  - Keep the selected order through daemon reconnects. Append new sessions and remove closed sessions without changing the panes' authoritative session state.
  - Mark the row being dragged with an accent underline and a ↕ in place of its close control. Many rows share an agent name and colour, so without the mark it was hard to see where the row would land.
  - Add direct session shortcuts: Ctrl+Cmd+1..8 on macOS, Ctrl+1..8 elsewhere. They focus the Nth session in the order the sidebar shows, so after a drag the number follows the row's new position. Composers in Chat and Code keep working with typed text; panes and modals that bind the chord keep it. Help lists the shortcuts. (These two shortcut commits come from Dan's dogfood stack, where the shortcuts counted pane order and went to the wrong row after a drag.)
- **Scope boundary:** Display order lasts only until ZeroCode exits. No daemon, protocol, config, disk persistence, or dependency changes. New keymap actions `FocusSession1`..`FocusSession8` only; existing locale strings reused.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode Sessions drawing and mouse routing, including release outside the panel and cancellation during keyboard input, resizing, hiding, or picker opening. Global key dispatch for the new shortcut chords.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's Sessions panel lists the Chat and Code conversations you can switch between. Until now, you could select or close a session, but you could not choose where it appeared in that list.

This PR lets you hold a session row and drag it up or down, including past sessions of the other type. The row you are dragging is underlined, so you can see where it will land. Ctrl+Cmd+1 through 8 (Ctrl+1 through 8 off macOS) jumps straight to the session in that position. A click still selects the session, and its close control still closes it. The order stays as you arranged it while ZeroCode runs, including when the daemon reconnects. Exiting ZeroCode resets the order; dragging does not change the sessions themselves.

## Testing

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Real terminal mouse delivery remains to be checked.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Sessions panel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Run ZeroCode connected to an existing daemon with several Chat and Code sessions. No configuration change is needed. Use a terminal that forwards mouse events.
- **Steps to run:** Drag a session row up and down across both session types. Click a row and then use its close control. In a short Sessions panel, drag above and below the visible list. Release over the conversation area, then move the mouse again. Start a drag and press a keyboard shortcut or resize the terminal. Reconnect the daemon and inspect the order, then exit and relaunch ZeroCode.
- **Expected on this branch:** Rows follow the drag, and list-edge dragging scrolls. The dragged row is underlined with ↕ at its right edge until release. After a drag, Ctrl+Cmd+N focuses the session now in position N. Clicking selects the right session; closing does not start a drag. Outside release and cancellation end the gesture. Reconnect retains the order; relaunch resets it.
- **Prior behavior on master:** The same row drag does not reorder sessions, and there are no number shortcuts. Clicking and closing already work.

### How I tested

Focused automated tests cover mixed Chat/Code ordering, redraws, stable duplicate-agent ordinals, row removal and insertion, close-control exclusion, edge scrolling, outside release, and reconstruction through the real pane constructors used for reconnect.

```text
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode sidebar -- --test-threads=1
test result: ok. 37 passed; 0 failed

rustfmt --edition 2024 --check apps/zerocode/src/agent_sidebar.rs apps/zerocode/src/app.rs
Passed.

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
Passed.
```

- **CI checks relied on:** No CI result is used as evidence yet. CI results for this head appear in GitHub checks.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Automated tests do not establish mouse-event delivery from an actual terminal or the complete reconnect interaction in a running process.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected display-order ownership, input routing, and cancellation paths. A running-terminal smoke has not been performed.

prs.title: fix(tools): expose scenario routing requirements
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Advertise `hint`, `model_provider`, and `model` as required nonblank strings when `model_routing_config` selects `upsert_scenario`. Put the guarded `if` and `then` directly on the object schema, without a top-level composition wrapper. Require an explicit action in the condition so an omitted action still defaults to `get`.
  - Share that field list with validation and report all missing, non-string, or blank required fields in one localized error, before reading or changing configuration.
  - Preserve whole-object argument recovery for schemas with `if`, `then`, or `else`. Decode one JSON-stringified value matching an explicit object/array type, then stop before conditional child traversal. Keep the existing reference, composition, tuple-array, ambiguous-type, malformed-input, shape and depth safeguards.
- **Scope boundary:** Other action contracts, optional-field parsing, persistence, permissions, provider implementations, and repetitive-tool recovery are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Consumers of this tool's parameter schema and scenario-validation feedback, plus native and text-fallback argument recovery for explicitly typed conditional schemas. The flat argument object and tool registration remain unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11708.
- **Runtime placement:** This PR includes the bounded #11371/#11479 scope amendment in the runtime's `AGENTS.md` and updates ADR-016 to allow a directly related amendment in the implementation PR. The proposed scope covers only explicit outer object/array decoding for conditional schemas and its focused regressions. It remains pending explicit Core Team approval before merge; the existing approval covers only the original scope.

### What this does, simply

Agents use this tool to choose which model handles a kind of request. Previously, its published instructions did not say which fields a scenario update required. If a model left several fields out, the tool reported only the first problem, leaving the model to discover the others over successive retries.

This change publishes the complete required set for scenario updates and returns every invalid required field together. The model receives enough information to correct the call in one retry. This does not guarantee that a model follows the instructions or chooses the right tool, and it does not turn model routing into a network-permission control.

Some models return the entire argument object as a JSON string. The new conditional schema initially prevented ZeroClaw from decoding it, so a requested scenario update could become a successful read without saving anything. The response parser now restores the declared outer object before dispatch. It leaves conditional child values to the tool's normal validation.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The focused suite exercises the actual tool dispatch, configuration bytes, schema cleaner, and prompt serializer deterministically; interactive model tool choice is nondeterministic.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# Passed.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib model_routing_config
# test result: ok. 16 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured;
# 2071 filtered out; finished in 0.27s

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib argument_preservation_tests
# test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured;
# 5718 filtered out; finished in 0.08s

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
# Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
# Passed.

bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
# Same-PR ADR amendment: markdownlint reports 0 errors.

bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
# 6 collector tests pass; no added links detected.
```

- **Coverage:** Tests check complete correction feedback for missing, wrong-type, and blank strings, byte-identical configuration after invalid calls, argument errors before config-read errors, preserved read-only admission, implicit `get`, partial `set_default`, valid scenario persistence, and dotted-provider agent calls without `model`. They also check that raw, OpenAI-cleaned, and Anthropic-cleaned schemas preserve the guarded requirements without root composition keywords, and that the complete schema reaches the text-tool prompt.
- **Recovery coverage:** The real routing tool's schema enters `interpret_chat_response` through native and extra-encoded text-fallback calls. Both retain `upsert_scenario` and save the expected route to a temporary configuration file. A separate control proves that conditional object/array schemas decode only their outer type and leave child strings untouched. Existing controls cover free text, references, composition, ambiguous types, tuple arrays, invalid input, type mismatches and depth limits.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The workspace Test job covers the tool and runtime library tests; Lint and Format cover the changed Rust code. [Required CI passes](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38505495932) at recovery commit `b92d5f20957b15c85264aa7fde3c41e1f016a79f`, including Test, Lint, Format and CI Required Gate. The later same-PR exception proposal at `a206e30553c3b7d69d221e4730b063448c0aecb4` changes two Markdown files only; local docs and link checks pass, and its fresh CI is pending.
- **Known coverage gap:** A live local-model conversation and vendor endpoint acceptance have not been tested. The tests establish contract visibility and validation behavior, not universal backend acceptance or a measured reduction in model retries.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The generated English catalogue matches the canonical catalogue plus the renderer's provenance header. No provider server or agent configuration was changed for testing.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No layout, styling, or rendering behavior changes; the changed error is a tool result returned to the model.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Tool tests ran at `48253684a5cb589a3ff158a9c4747011f06ec6f9`. The runtime argument-preservation suite ran on the patch committed as `b92d5f20957b15c85264aa7fde3c41e1f016a79f`, with source identity checked afterward. Evidence is in the owning module tests and the output above. The macOS linker warned that the test harness's unwind section exceeds the compact-unwind table limit; compilation and all selected tests completed successfully.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** An incomplete `upsert_scenario` call returns one error naming all invalid required strings and leaves saved configuration unchanged. JSON-stringified valid calls preserve their selected action and save the route rather than silently reading configuration.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace tests and Clippy were not repeated; the focused suite covers this bounded repair, with broader coverage left to hosted CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. The tool's schema descriptions and validation feedback change. The new error contains fixed field names, never argument values, and existing write admission remains in place.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing valid calls retain their behavior. Invalid scenario calls receive complete feedback instead of the first-field error.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Tool argument metadata, invalid-call feedback and conditional-schema argument recovery change; there are no new operator settings.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. Omitted-action reads, partial default updates, and dotted-provider agent updates keep their existing contracts.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits and rebuild or reinstall the previous binary. No configuration migration is needed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Valid routing calls unexpectedly fail or become reads without saving a route, omitted-action reads require scenario fields, or invalid calls return a missing-localization-key error instead of the complete correction.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. This PR does not supersede another contribution.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add optional `reasoning_tokens`, `provider_total_tokens`, and
    `provider_cost_usd` to the shared `TokenUsage` carrier and the cost ledger row.
  - Compatible OpenAI usage can put hidden reasoning only in `total_tokens`
    (Gemini-via-gateway) or `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`; those
    values were dropped before the ledger, so `costs.jsonl` under-counted.
  - Carry them through `price_usage` without touching rate-sheet `total_tokens`
    or `cost_usd`; providers that do not report them leave the fields `None`.
- **Scope boundary:** Accounting/plumbing only. Rate-sheet pricing and the
  recomputed `total_tokens = input + output` contract are unchanged; OpenRouter
  `usage.cost` construction stays at defaults (tracked in #11204).
- **Blast radius:** Provider usage parsing, the reliable/aggregate usage paths,
  and cost-ledger rows. Read-only consumers of `costs.jsonl` see new optional
  fields.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11613

### What this does, simply

Some providers hide "thinking" tokens outside the normal prompt/completion
counts, reporting them only inside `total_tokens` or a reasoning sub-count. Those
numbers never reached the cost ledger, so recorded usage was lower than what the
provider actually billed. This change adds them as optional fields on the usage
record and the saved ledger row, without changing the priced totals.

  usage` and `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- cost` → pass.

  real compatible provider and `settle_provider_attempts` lands

- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface.
- **Tested revision:** `c689f97117e7dcd61f870c39d06a2cd92bb00c57`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New external network calls? No

prs.title: fix(tool-call-parser): normalize DeepSeek DSML marker before parsing
prs.body:
> Maintainer note: I narrowed the description to the behavior supported by this patch and changed the closing reference to `Refs #11130`, keeping the remaining runtime classification and streaming work open.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** the tool-call parser extracts complete DeepSeek DSML blocks and parses their normalized inner tags through the existing parser. This recovers the reported simple text-only shell call. Malformed-output classification and streaming suppression are unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** only `crates/zeroclaw-tool-call-parser/src/lib.rs`. No changes to provider configs, `TOOL_CALL_OPEN_TAGS`/`TOOL_CALL_CLOSE_TAGS`, `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`, or any other crate.
- **Blast radius:** extraction runs at the entry point of `parse_tool_calls`, before the existing text-protocol fallbacks. Input without a DSML marker follows the existing parser behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** Refs #11130
- **Labels:** `bug`, `domain:security`, `size:M`, `risk:medium`, `needs-author-action`

### What this does, simply

Some models (DeepSeek family and derivatives) do not put tool calls in the API's native `tool_calls` field. They write them into the message text, wrapped in a marker made of `U+FF5C FULLWIDTH VERTICAL LINE` plus `DSML`, and they wrap **both** the opening and the closing tags:

```text
<｜DSML｜ calls>
<｜DSML｜ invoke name="shell">
<｜DSML｜ parameter name="command" string="true">ls -la ~/ 2>/dev/null</｜DSML｜ parameter>
</｜DSML｜ invoke>
</｜DSML｜ calls>
```

ZeroClaw already understands the XML/Hermes shape inside (`<invoke name="..."><parameter name="...">...</parameter></invoke>`), but nothing matched the wrapped version, so the markup was delivered to the user as ordinary assistant text and no tool ran. This PR extracts complete DSML blocks, removes their marker prefixes, and parses the inner tags through the existing parser. It does not add DSML recognition to runtime error classification or the streaming guard.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (tool-call parsing), `channel` output (the raw markup must no longer reach the user)
- **Setup / preconditions:** an agent configured against a DSML-emitting model (for the original report: an OpenAI-compatible provider serving a DeepSeek model)
- **Steps to run:** ask the agent for anything that needs a tool, e.g. `zeroclaw agent -a <agent> -m 'Run the shell command: echo ZCTEST'`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** for the complete sample on the non-streaming text-fallback path, the tool call is recovered and follows the normal approval flow. Malformed DSML and live streaming output are not covered by the parser-only change.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the raw DSML block is returned as assistant text, no tool is dispatched, and the turn ends. The runtime trace even records the turn as successful (`provider:receive=success` -> `agent:complete=success` -> `channel:outbound=success`), which is why the failure was silent.

### How I tested

```sh
# focused gate on the changed crate
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

New unit tests cover the real captured payload: the `shell` call is parsed with `command = "ls -la ~/ 2>/dev/null"`, the returned text contains no `DSML` marker, and the ASCII-pipe variant (`|DSML|`) is normalized too.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required Rust CI builds and tests the workspace, which covers the touched crate and its consumers.
