prs.title: fix(providers): recognize snake_case context-window overflow codes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** `is_context_window_exceeded` matches a list of phrases
  against the provider's error text. A local OpenAI-compatible server reports
  overflow as a snake_case `code` — `{"code":"context_length_exceeded", ...}` —
  instead of prose, and the existing entry `"context length exceeded"` only
  matches with a space, so the predicate returned `false`. That skipped the
  trim-and-retry recovery and left the user with the generic "the selected model
  provider rejected the request" text. This adds the one missing spelling, plus a
  regression test built from the real 400 body.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to trimming, token budgets, retries, refusal
  timing, or user-facing strings. `zeroclaw-channels` now delegates to this
  predicate, so no second list is touched.
- **Blast radius:** Narrow. The predicate only turns `true` for error text
  containing `context_length_exceeded`, which no other path in the workspace
  produces.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10329 (closed by #10416, which made the detector
  walk the error cause chain; this completes it for snake_case codes).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw decides "the conversation no longer fits the model's memory" by matching
phrases in the provider's error text. When it recognises overflow it drops the
oldest whole turns and retries, and it tells the user to shorten rather than
blaming the provider configuration. One local server words the same condition as
a JSON field name — `context_length_exceeded` — which the list did not contain,
so a conversation a few dozen tokens over the window failed outright. This PR
adds that spelling.

## Testing (required)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the trigger is a provider-specific error
  body that no public endpoint returns; the boundary is unit-tested.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers is_context_window_exceeded
# cargo test: 3 passed, 2024 filtered out (3 suites, 0.00s)
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings
# cargo clippy: No issues found
```

A/B against a local mock provider replaying the captured 400 body: on `master`
the second turn ends with `Error: The selected model provider rejected the
request…` and nothing is trimmed; on this branch the runtime drops the oldest
whole turn (`messages=4` → `messages=2` in the mock's request log) and the retry
answers.

Not verified: a live overflow against the real server (needs a multi-minute
prefill on a memory-tight machine), and a live channel turn; the channel path
inherits this predicate.

- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no rendered interface change.
- **Tested revision, interface:** `d3510d0`, surface `cli`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace suite, and
  the local `pre-push` hook that chains it (workspace tests, firmware protocol
  gate, parallel runtime gate), skipped with `git push --no-verify`; CI covers
  them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

All `No`: no new permissions or file system scope, no new network calls, no
secrets handling change, no PII, no model-visible text change.

## Compatibility (required)

Backward compatible `Yes`. No config/env/CLI surface change. No MSRV change.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert d3510d0`

prs.title: feat(runtime): let the operator override an exceeded cost limit
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `cost.allow_override` was documented but read by nothing, so an exceeded shared limit always failed the turn and the only way on was a daemon restart. With it on, the main tool loop now pauses before a provider call that would exceed the shared daily or monthly limit and asks through the turn's approval channel (`tool_name = cost_limit_override`, exported as `COST_LIMIT_OVERRIDE_APPROVAL`). Deny, no answer within 10 minutes, or a channel that cannot ask stops the turn exactly as before.
  - Approval calls `CostTracker::grant_override`, which records the override for the current UTC day or month on state shared by every derived tracker, so one answer covers every session and delegation of the daemon. `check_budget` skips that limit (and its warning) while the stored period matches, so it expires on its own at rollover. Per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, and `grant_override` refuses when `allow_override` is off.
  - The grant is written to `state/cost-overrides.json` beside the ledger (temp file plus rename, best effort) and loaded when the tracker starts, so a daemon restart keeps it until rollover. An unreadable file means no override, and a stored grant is ignored while `allow_override` is off.
  - A turn waiting on its own prompt also watches for a grant from another session (a `watch` channel on the tracker). When one arrives it drops its request and continues. `RpcApprovalChannel` sends a new `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn` (`request_id`), for any approval that ends without an answer from its client, and ZeroCode takes that prompt down. Before this, approving in one session left the same prompt up in the other, and that turn stopped at the 10-minute timeout although the limit was already lifted.
  - `RpcApprovalChannel` and `AskUserApprovalBridge` now implement `request_approval_attributed_with_timeout`. The trait default wrapped `request_approval_attributed`, whose own 120 s deadline fired first, so the 10-minute wait would have been cut short.
  - ZeroCode renders a `cost_limit_override` approval as a centred, bold red notice with Override and Stop buttons instead of the tool card. Only Override or Stop (key or click) closes it.
- **Scope boundary:** no warning at `warn_at_percent` (#10950) and no notice for a turn that stops with no override possible; both need a daemon-to-client budget event this PR does not add. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. Applying `config/set` limit changes to the live tracker is #11587.
- **Blast radius:** turns that hit a shared limit with `allow_override = true` now wait for an answer instead of failing, on any channel that answers approvals (ZeroCode, ACP, Telegram inline buttons). The approval bridge's timeout plumbing is used only by callers that pass a budget; tool approvals are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11585
- **Labels:** (set after open)

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can stop the agent when spending passes a daily or monthly limit. There was a setting meant to let you go past the limit, but nothing used it: once the limit tripped, every message failed, and the only way to continue was to raise the limit and restart, which closes every open session.

Now, with that setting on, the agent pauses when it reaches the limit and ZeroCode shows a red box asking whether to keep going. Say yes and the same task carries on, and the limit stays lifted until the day (or month) ends, even if the app or daemon restarts. If several sessions were waiting at the limit, one yes lets all of them continue. Say no, or leave it for ten minutes, and the task stops as it does today. Chat apps that cannot show the question, and scheduled jobs, still stop at the limit.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` `tui` (ZeroCode Code tab over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[cost] enabled = true`, `allow_override = true`, `daily_limit_usd` just above today's recorded spend.
- **Steps to run:** in ZeroCode, run a prompt that makes a few model calls until spend passes the limit. When the red notice appears, click Override. Then open a second session and send a prompt. Separately: get two sessions waiting on the notice at once and Override in one; and restart the daemon after an Override and send a prompt.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first turn pauses on the red notice and continues after Override; the second session is not asked again; with two waiting, the other notice closes and its turn continues; after a restart nobody is asked again that day. With Stop instead, the turn ends with the budget error.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the turn fails with `Budget exceeded: ... Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets.`, there is no prompt, and every later turn fails until a restart.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check   # rustfmt --edition 2024 on the changed files
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib cost::tracker
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib budget_override
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib approval_
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel
cargo test -p zerocode --bins -- approval parse_approval cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode approval
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust test and clippy jobs for the four crates; Docs Style for `docs/book/src/ops/cost-tracking.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no end-to-end test drives a real provider turn into the gate; the gate tests call it under a scoped tracker with a scripted channel.
- **Commands run and tail output:** on `225c52bb636f` (rebased on master `f12da7462a0f`): clippy `-D warnings` clean on the four crates; `cost::tracker` 50 passed; runtime `budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel` 17 passed; zerocode `approval parse_approval cost_limit` 13 passed; comment hygiene gate passed. With each fix disabled, `override_survives_a_restart_and_stops_counting_when_disallowed` and `approval_in_another_session_releases_a_waiting_prompt` fail. Earlier run at `58a7050d`: clippy `Finished`, no warnings. `cost::tracker` 47 passed, `budget_override` 3 passed, `approval_` 106 passed, zerocode `cost_limit` 2 passed, zerocode `approval` 9 passed, docs gate 0 errors.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Coverage: tracker override (day lifts, rollover expiry, derived trackers share it, per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, day does not lift month, refused when not allowed); gate (approve continues and does not ask twice, deny and runtime timeout stop, no prompt without `allow_override` or a channel); RPC channel honours a 600 s budget through `dyn Channel`; ZeroCode notice render and button clicks; restart persistence, unreadable file, cross-session release, `approval_withdrawn` sent only for unanswered prompts and cleared only for the matching id. I ran the override live in the experiment build; the two follow-up bugs above came from that run.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output pending; the render test asserts the title, summary, both buttons and the red button fill through `render_with_plan_placement` at 100x30.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `225c52bb636f` on master `f12da7462a0f`; tests on a remote macOS arm64 builder. Live: experiment build https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T015950Z-b89c9e407c42 (commit https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/b89c9e407c4279bbfb05f9d0e0cdec7e34b6e561).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** to be added from the dogfood smoke before Ready.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full crate suites not run locally; CI runs them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (one new file, `state/cost-overrides.json`, in the existing cost state directory)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The override is off by default and only an operator answer grants it; a runtime timeout or unreachable client does not.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. With `allow_override = false` (the default) behaviour is unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys; one new RPC `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn`, which older clients ignore; `allow_override` now does what its docs say, and the docs are corrected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 225c52bb636f 0c7a8844d260 312ffc65d3ae` (newest first).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `cost.allow_override = false` restores the hard stop without a revert.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** turns stuck waiting at the limit; grep the runtime trace for `cost limit overridden by the operator` and `cost limit override prompt failed`.

prs.title: feat(config): report per-target application results
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Record the latest application result for each changed config path and actual target instance. Saving a revision cannot establish that a running consumer adopted it.
  - Reuse the existing RPC model-provider refresh acknowledgement. Keep attempts pending until that captured session instance accepts or refuses the update, and reject superseded completions.
  - Add conservative schema-owned application capability metadata and authenticated HTTP/RPC status projections from the existing live config authority.
- **Scope boundary:** No new live consumers, security overlays, channel handovers, watcher, persistent result history or restart framework. The parent follow-ups for policy-publication ordering, independent tool writers and Web/TUI committed-outcome reporting remain separate.
- **Blast radius:** Config semantic comparison and schema derivation, runtime publication and existing model-provider refresh, gateway reload status, RPC config status and downstream Rust response/metadata constructors.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10892 and accepted RFC #7897. Builds on #10911 (merged). Keep #10892 open for its remaining follow-ups.
- **Runtime placement:** Depends on #11436. The covering scope needs a recorded Core Team decision in the exception table before this implementation merges.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `core`, `agent`, `channel`, `config`, `cron`, `daemon`, `gateway`, `provider`, `runtime`, `skills`, `tool`, `tests`, `channel:core`, `channel:telegram`, `channel:matrix`, `tool:delegate`, `channel:whatsapp`, `security:pairing`, `domain:security`, `domain:architecture`, `priority:p2`, `stacked`, `quickstart`, `risk:high`, `channel:line`, `size:XL`, `channel:acp`, `channel:wechat`, `cli`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets an operator save configuration while the daemon is running. A successful save means the new settings are stored and published, but it does not mean every running component is already using them. The existing reload flag cannot say which setting or session still needs attention.

This PR adds that distinction to the status APIs. A daemon-owned setting reports that reload is required. An existing session model-provider update reports pending until the actual session accepts the update, then reports the result for that session and revision. An old result cannot claim that a newer edit or replacement session was updated.

The status contains paths and result codes, not configuration values or provider error messages. It reports only changes and attempts observed during the current daemon authority's lifetime. Missing or evicted records do not mean success. This does not make more settings live-updatable, and `/admin/reload` remains the fallback.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The change is 17 files, +1279/-25. The new result module is 324 lines including its tests; other changes are schema/macro propagation, the existing authority and status adapters, focused regressions and two architecture documents.

There is one result store in `LiveConfigAuthority`, not separate HTTP and RPC stores. Schema metadata describes possible refresh capability; only an existing consumer's acknowledgement establishes adoption. Full replacement uses an unmasked semantic comparison, preserving dotted map keys and treating arrays as single properties. If comparison cannot establish the changed paths, publication still succeeds and status explicitly requires whole-config reload.

The latest results are bounded to 512 records. The response exposes `record_limit` and `truncated`; it is not an audit log or a complete subsystem inventory. Full reload creates a new epoch without synthetic success records. Runtime placement also needs the separately recorded Core Team exception required by [ADR-016](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/decisions/ADR-016-holding-crate-exceptions.md) before merge. This PR does not add its own exception.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The focused tests exercise the real authenticated HTTP write/status router and RPC refresh/status boundary, including the delayed acknowledgement state. No visual presentation changes are included.

### How I tested

The focused command ran against child `7c15d2396cc83aefb707d056d88cf8948be38987`'s unchanged source tree on frozen parent `21124975e538cf143d1053a8cea1e72a5bfd3ec7`:

```bash
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-macros --lib config_application -- --test-threads=2
```

```text
zeroclaw-config: 8 passed; 0 failed
zeroclaw-runtime: 4 passed; 0 failed
zeroclaw-gateway: 1 passed; 0 failed
zeroclaw-macros: 1 passed; 0 failed
Exit status: 0
```

The default schema-export feature was included. The tests cover unmasked secret changes and full replacements, opaque dotted keys, conservative capability classification, distinct path/target outcomes, stale revision and epoch completion refusal, bounded retention and unknown-scope fallback. The HTTP test proves unauthorized denial and daemon-only reporting, and shows that clearing the reload flag does not acknowledge application. The RPC test observes pending then acknowledged results through the existing refresh, checks principal/session visibility and removes retired instances.

- **Refresh onto master (2026-10-10):** rebased the single owned commit from frozen parent `21124975` onto `3465758fb70e`; it applied cleanly. Re-verified at `9ad6e7e632`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, and `cargo clippy --no-deps -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-macros -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass; `cargo test` on those four crates passed 8,311 tests. Five local failures are not from this change: three also fail on `master` on the same macOS host (two loopback-backlog relay tests and a `/var` tmp-workspace RPC grant test), the peer-turn cost test failed only under full-suite load and passed three isolated runs, and the `nul`/`NUL` policy fixture collides on the case-insensitive test filesystem. The CI link below is from the pre-refresh head.
- **Review follow-up (2026-10-10):** `1b86935af1` builds each snapshot's application metadata once per live-session refresh instead of once per changed path, and skips the diff when no session is live (greptile P2). fmt, clippy `--no-deps -D warnings` on config/gateway/runtime, and their tests (8,299 passed, same three master-failing host tests skipped) pass.
- **Refresh onto master (2026-10-14):** rebased onto `2fd19b1c4a98`. The two owned commits are now `74d08104cf0f` and `2c44755a7984`. Master's #11419 added a secret-map container row to the `Configurable` derive, so `feb7f313406c` gives that row an `application` value (`ReloadRequired`, the same as its entries). `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes, and so do the `zeroclaw-macros` and `zeroclaw-config` lib tests (1,784 passed), runtime `config_application` (4), gateway `api_config` (78) and config `secret_map` (8). One `zeroclaw-config` test, `policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception`, also fails on `master` on this macOS host: `nul` and `NUL` collide on a case-insensitive filesystem.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37048104535) passed at `7c15d2396cc83aefb707d056d88cf8948be38987`. Format, strict lint, default/no-default features, schema-enabled compilation, MSRV, platform builds and the parallel runtime test cover the cumulative stack. The Test job passed 19,093 workspace tests, its following 189-test run and seven informational golden-frame replays. One targeted Test-job retry cleared the unchanged Keenable socket-close assertion; no source change was needed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Other platforms receive the applicable CI compile/targeted checks, not a full execution of every new test. The changed result behavior runs in Linux CI and the focused local tests. Existing consumer coverage remains limited to the current RPC model-provider refresh, not new live-apply behavior.
- **Commands run and tail output:** The focused command above passed 14/14. Formatting, `git diff --check` and `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` passed. `DOCS_FILES` limited `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` to the two changed architecture documents; markdown lint reported `Summary: 0 error(s)`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected publication/result lock ordering, session incarnation fencing, fresh grants and principal ownership, daemon-only HTTP projection, bounded retention and the parent-to-child scope. No interactive interface smoke was performed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This changes structured status responses, not a rendered interface.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Child source tree above; authenticated HTTP config write/reload-status and RPC config/status/model-provider refresh tests in the owning modules.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Test results above; no visual claim.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Publish while a selected refresh is paused, observe pending, release it and observe that instance's result. An unrelated save preserves the actual earlier result revision; retired instances disappear and cannot be recreated by an old completion.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local whole-workspace and platform builds were not duplicated because exact-head CI supplies that coverage. No new settings apply live, so a wider live-consumer matrix would test behavior outside this slice. The local linker emitted the oversized macOS unwind-section warning also recorded in the parent's validation; linking and all selected tests completed successfully.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. Existing config/session grants and ownership rules constrain the additional status records.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. Semantic comparison must detect credential changes without masked display values. Its temporary materialized values are not retained in the result store or returned by status.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test credentials and principals are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- **Risk and mitigation:** Application status could reveal another principal's session or falsely claim adoption. RPC projection checks fresh authorization, principal and TUI ownership plus the live incarnation. HTTP exposes daemon targets only. Records carry paths, target identities, revisions and fixed outcome/reason codes, never config values, transcripts or raw errors. Status reads have no write or invocation authority.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for downstream Rust struct literals constructing `PropFieldInfo`, `ConfigStatusResult` or `ReloadStatusResponse`. Existing saved config and prior HTTP/RPC fields remain unchanged; new status fields are additive and the RPC application field is optional for decoding.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes for schema application metadata and structured status responses. No new config keys, environment variables or CLI options.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Exact upgrade steps for existing users:** No config migration. Rust callers constructing the affected metadata/response structs must initialize `application` with the conservative default, `None`, or the runtime-provided status as appropriate. Wire clients should continue ignoring unknown response fields and must not infer success from a missing record. The public-status additions need the normal compatibility assessment before release.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert feb7f313406c 2c44755a7984 74d08104cf0f` removes this change. It restores #10911's publication/status behavior and leaves saved config intact.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Existing `/admin/reload` remains available.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing or incorrect `application.records`, a pending result that never settles, another principal's visible session record, or an acknowledgement with the wrong revision/incarnation. Compare status against the existing refresh result rather than treating save or reload-flag success as adoption.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.9.0 gateway](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v090-gateway), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: agree the full core IPC contract first; finish the supported local IPC server; ship standalone zeroclaw-gw; migrate vendor webhook behavior into channel plugins; and have Tauri package and manage both processes.

Completion requires a core artifact without web assets or HTTP server code, a working IPC-connected gateway, core/channel operation when the gateway is absent, and demonstrated two-process desktop lifecycle. Existing OIDC, principal-isolation, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with this boundary. WATI is already retired. Feature acceptance and normal review/CI/release holds still apply.

prs.title: feat(cli): add zeroclaw plugin update with verified replacement
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Stacked on #11261, which is stacked on #11236. #11581 has landed on `master` as `ea4a54bb5b`: this branch merged its head first (`0ba2b77343`) and now carries the landed commit through `277aeabb0e`'s merge of `master`. `2f3409e9ba`, `bd2d4e5eea`, `f94508dc69` and `2ec36c26dc` merge #11261's head, now `369fb21334`, which carries #11236's `7a3ad81ed5`. Until they merge, this PR's diff also contains their commits. Please review the eight commits after `0ba2b77343`, up to `bab70cc225`, the follow-ups from `75116ac28a` to `a1d212eca1`, and `f3d0a59844`. `6354484051`, `2f3409e9ba`, `bd2d4e5eea` and `f94508dc69` only merge the base, `2ec36c26dc` with the adaptation described below; `277aeabb0e` and `2b3c93631d` merge `master`, with the resolutions described below.
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The command.** Adds `zeroclaw plugin update`, the missing lifecycle operation from #10995 (#7432 R3, Phase 2 D3). It implements the contract posted on the issue for review: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10995#issuecomment-5894198515.
    - Syntax: `plugin update <name>[@<version>]...`, `plugin update --all`, and `plugin update <name> --from <dir>`, with `--registry <url>` as for install. Update never installs a package that is not installed.
    - Version selection is install's rule: the last entry the registry lists for a bare name, the exact entry for `name@version`, compared only for equality. An equal version is "up to date" and nothing is downloaded. A different version, even an older one, is installed, so pinning the previous version is the way back. When both are semantic versions and the selected one is older by SemVer precedence, the result line says so (`Replaced 'x' 2.0.0 with 1.2.5, an older version than the one installed.`) instead of reporting an update. A `--from` package always replaces, so a rebuilt plugin can be reinstalled at the same version.
    - Verification is the existing path, reused: the registry download, with its digest when the registry entry lists one, then `PluginHost::admit_update` from the stacked host PR, then the install-time load check with the operator's `plugins.limits`. There is no `--no-verify` for update.
  - **Authority gate.** The runtime grants every permission a manifest requests. So an update is refused, before its component is compiled, when its manifest adds a permission, a capability, or a new `provides` id, or names a different publisher key than the installed version (or none where the installed version named one).
    - The refusal prints the exact command that accepts the difference, with one `--allow-token <item>` per added item, such as `--allow-token permission:<name>`; `--allow` still takes the same items as a comma-separated list. It is pinned to the reviewed version and quoted for the host shell by the egress ceremony's `ShellDialect`, because versions, `provides` ids and keys are publisher-controlled text. Every output line that carries manifest text escapes control, format, line separator and paragraph separator characters (Unicode Cc, Cf, Zl, Zp), line breaks and invisible characters included, so manifest text cannot rewrite, rearrange or disguise the prompt, including an approval block a batch printed earlier, or print a line of its own.
    - `--allow` and `--allow-token` apply to one plugin, and a registry update that uses either must be pinned as `name@version`.
    - The publisher key is a verified identity only under `signature_mode = "strict"`; the docs say so.
  - **Preserved state.** Config rows, secrets, `egress_hosts`, `egress_allow_private`, TLS profiles, durable state, and instance keys are never modified.
    - Missing rows are created without a grant and saved before the package changes, so nothing after the replacement can fail.
    - Egress keeps the never-extend rule: update seeds nothing, even into a row it creates, and prints the same declared-versus-granted difference install prints for an existing row.
    - When preserved config fails the new version's schema, the update still completes and names the instance and the schema location. A missing required property is named, since the name is the schema's own. A configured value, or a configured key the schema does not declare, is never printed, because either could hold a secret.
    - A package whose config row still uses the pre-1.0 package-name key is refused with the same guidance `plugin install` prints (its rename steps, or a deployment-wide egress refusal in their place), one line each under the result; the docs say so.
  - **Results and recovery.** Each plugin gets one result: updated, reinstalled, up to date, skipped (with `--all`, not listed in the registry), needs approval, or not updated with the version kept.
    - A failure does not stop the others, and the command exits 1 when any plugin was not updated.
    - A command that updated anything ends with one restart-the-daemon note, and a batch ends with a summary line.
    - A package an interrupted update displaced is put back by the next `plugin update <name>`, before the registry is consulted, so recovery works offline. Names that are not installed are answered before the registry too, with the install command for the source the update named. `plugin list` and `plugin update --all` point at the recovery with two complete commands (a plugins directory this process cannot lock, such as a read-only one, simply gets no such note in `plugin list`), one from the registry and one from a package directory, rendered for the selected configuration as the approval, install and not-installed commands are, and `--all` never restores a displaced package unasked. An update interrupted mid-swap points back at its own source, so a `--from` run is retried from the same directory; authority the update adds is asked for again.
    - A restored copy the host does not admit is reported with where it now is, and with `plugin list --verbose`, which prints discovery's reason.
  - **Pointers keep the source.** `plugin install` on an installed package now fails with the update command for the same source: `--from <dir>` after a local install, `name@version` after a pinned one. Likewise, `plugin update <name> --from <dir>` for a name that is not installed points at installing that directory. Neither ever offers the registry for a local build, and exit statuses are unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No new registry, installer, config key, or on-disk format.
  - No version ordering for selection. Semantic versions are compared only to report an older one.
  - No daemon signalling: channel instances keep their component until restart, and tool sets built afterwards load the new version.
  - Channel-instance config and grant seeding stays with #10996. Install's own `<already-installed>` semantics stay with #10162; this PR only adds the pointer.
  - Registry-side compatibility metadata (#9624) does not exist yet; the load check is the compatibility gate.
  - Known limits, documented where operators read them:
    - no `fsync` around the renames, as for install
    - a tool set built at the instant of the swap can be inconsistent once
  - A process killed between publishing the replacement and marking the replaced version for deletion leaves that version claimed in its hidden transaction. Recovery deletes it while the plugin is installed; after a later `plugin remove`, `plugin list` shows it as displaced until a named `plugin update` restores it, and `--all` never does. `plugin remove` leaving such a claim alone is a follow-up.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw plugin install`/`list`/`update`, the root plugin CLI, and five runtime Fluent catalogues.
  - `seed_plugin_config_entries` is split. Its row-finding first half becomes `ensure_plugin_config_entries`, shared with update, and install's behavior and output are unchanged.
  - A batch fetches the registry index once and compares versions before downloading, through `download_registry_entry` from #11581, which this branch merges. This PR no longer defines that function itself.
  - In `zeroclaw-plugins`, `validate_config_instance` names a missing required property in its `InvalidConfig` message, so every surface that reports that error, such as a daemon load failure, names it too. The existing test that config errors expose no secret values or undeclared keys still passes unchanged.
  - `ci.yml` adds the new component test to the root CLI plugin step, and the plugin backend change filter now selects the plugin CLI component tests.
  - The host PR builds update and its recovery on #11236's package lock and leased transactions, so updates, installs, removals and recoveries are serialized across processes, and a claim a running update holds is never touched. #11236 now carries #11232 merged in, and the stack is restacked onto it, so it holds one revision of each. Merge order: #11236, #11261 and #11581, then this PR. #11232 has landed.
  - `semver` becomes a direct dependency of the binary, behind `plugins-wasm`. It was already in the lock file through wasmtime.
  - #11302, which landed as `2286ef36c5`, and this PR refactored `seed_plugin_config_entries` in different directions (`stage_plugin_config_entries` there, `ensure_plugin_config_entries` here). `2b3c93631d` merges it: `stage_plugin_config_entries` now creates its rows through `ensure_plugin_config_entries`, and update takes its rows and declaration from #11302's helpers (`instance_rows`, `tool_binding_entries`, `declared_hosts_for_row`), as install does. Update creates only the default tool binding's row, without a grant, and a channel instance's row stays `plugin bind`'s to create.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10995. Depends on #11261, #11236 and #11715; #11581 has landed. Related #7432, #10162, #10996, #9624, #11232, #11302.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `ci`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `core`, `runtime`, `tests`, `scripts`, `distinguished contributor`, `release-gate`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `cli`, `ci:windows`, `topic:plugins`, `release:v0.8.6`.

### Since the last reviews

tidux requested changes at `796c418343`, which JordanTheJet and Audacity88 had approved. The approvals do not cover this head. Each item:

- **Superseded #11236.** Restacked onto #11236 `c5fbbe2313` and #11261 `420969ea90`. These commits applied without conflicts. The branch is still behind `master`, and it will be rebased onto `master` once the PRs below it merge.
- **`download_registry_entry` in two PRs** (raised on #11309). #11581, which bounds registry requests, now owns that function and lands first. This branch merges it (`0ba2b77343`), and the update commit no longer defines its own copy. The call sites are unchanged.
- **An older version reported as "Updated".** Reported with its own line, as above (`fdb12439ce`). It never blocks, so #10995's no-ordering rule stands.
- **"Verified" claims a digest check.** The docs and this description now say the archive digest is checked when the registry entry lists one (`bab70cc225`). Refusing a digest-less registry update is left for a separate change, because install has the same gap.
- **Prompt injection.** Answered Yes below, with the mitigation: an update can change skill content under an existing `skill` capability without asking.
- **`plugin update --help` in English.** `cli-plugin-update-about`, and `cli-plugin-about` for `zeroclaw plugin`, are in all five catalogues and in the parity test (`12aceb5a6b`).
- **Merge order with #11302.** Recorded under Blast radius.
- **`printable`.** It escapes every Cc, Cf, Zl and Zp character, from a fixed table of the format ranges, and the displaced-package note goes through it (`ed68ce6ad2`).
- **Local builds under `--all`.** Not changed. Skipping a package whose installed version the registry does not list would also skip every package whose registry has dropped an old version.
- **CLI text.** The es and fr approval lines are reworded as suggested, and `--all` no longer prints "No plugins installed." after only displaced-package notes (`bab70cc225`). The restart line is unchanged.

### What this does, simply

Until now the only way to move a plugin to a new version was to remove it and install the new one, with nothing checking the new version first or keeping the old one working if something went wrong. `zeroclaw plugin update` does it in one step.

It fetches the new version and runs every check a fresh install runs, including that the component actually loads on this host. Only then does it swap the package in. If anything fails before the swap, the old version is untouched; if the swap itself fails, the old version is put back. If the process dies mid-swap, the next update puts the old version back, even without network access.

A plugin's settings, secrets, network grants and stored data are keyed by its name, not its version, so they carry over. If a new version asks for more than the old one had (a new permission, a new capability, or a different publisher key), update stops and prints the exact command that accepts that difference. So an update can never quietly give a plugin more power. Update also never widens a plugin's network allowlist; it prints the command instead.

### Persistence and complete-token follow-up

The signed follow-up 75116ac28a0523f5e8be1304c38e070d36b3a55e repairs two update failures. New instance rows are prepared on an owned Config clone, persisted through the existing writer, and promoted to the live batch state only after a successful save. A failed save cannot leave phantom rows for a repeated target to use; earlier successful targets and unrelated pending metadata remain intact. This adds no on-disk or cross-process transaction guarantee.

Repeatable `--allow-token TOKEN` preserves complete authority values containing commas. Existing `--allow` comma lists remain supported. Printed update commands use one quoted full-token argument per item; both forms use the same pinned-version, single-target, known-kind and exact authority matching checks.

The follow-up includes real parser/shell/config-save controls and real-binary component tests for duplicate-target save failure and both approval forms. Source and independent review plus patch/whitespace checks passed; fresh official compiler, format, lint and runtime CI for this head are pending. No local Rust tests were run.

Before chain acceptance, reconcile the actual qualified #11261/#11236 parents and retain the landed #11581 registry foundation, including its mid-body stall test. The plain-rename, host-authority, single-generation discovery and other existing plugin holds remain separate. Older approvals and CI do not validate this new follow-up.

The current signed head 277aeabb0eb12673bf8b274168f50035a2f14ad2 is a normal merge of public master ea4a54bb5bd77dd56fb76e919754bc5d63a099c3 with the repair head 75116ac28a0523f5e8be1304c38e070d36b3a55e. The sole hand resolution removes registry conflict markers and retains the landed mid-body timeout regression. The reviewed save/parser/emitter helpers and new CLI tests are preserved; both parents’ feature dependencies and test selection are retained. Fresh official CI qualifies this combined tree. Separate unmerged #11261/#11236 parent reconciliation and broader plugin holds remain.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No new scope. `plugin update` writes only through the host's staged replacement inside the plugins directory, config rows through the existing dirty-path save, and the registry index cache under `data_dir`, as `plugin install` and `plugin search` already do.
- New external network calls? No new destinations: update fetches the registry index and archive the operator selects, exactly as install does.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Config rows and secrets are preserved untouched. The config-rejection report prints instance keys, schema locations, and a missing required property's name from the schema. It never prints configured values or undeclared configured keys: unit tests assert a configured value does not appear, and the existing secret-exposure test is unchanged and passes.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. An update replaces a plugin's bundled skill files, which the model reads.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Adding the `skill` capability is added authority, so it needs `--allow`. Changing skill content under an existing `skill` capability does not, as when the plugin is removed and installed again: the content comes from the package the operator chose, passes the configured signature policy, and passes the staged skill-bundle check discovery applies. The trust-relevant risks of an update, and how each is handled:
  - **Widening a plugin's authority without consent.** Every added permission, capability or `provides` id, and every change of the declared publisher key, is refused unless named in `--allow` for that one pinned plugin. This is decided before the component is compiled. The publisher key is a verified identity only under `strict` signature policy, and the docs state that.
  - **Widening network reach.** Update never seeds or extends `egress_hosts`, even in a row it creates.
  - **A local build replaced by a registry package of the same name.** Update does not record where a package came from, so `plugin update <name>` without `--from`, and `--all`, look the name up in the registry. Under a non-strict signature policy, a registry package of that name that requests no added authority replaces an unsigned local build without approval, because gaining a publisher key is not an increase, and it inherits the instance's config rows, secrets and grants. Strict policy admits no unsigned build in the first place. The docs tell operators with local builds to name plugins explicitly and to add `--from` when recovering one. Pointers printed during a run with a local source keep that source: the install pointer, the approval command and the interrupted-update pointer use `--from <dir>`, and the not-installed pointer installs the directory. The displaced-package note from `plugin list` and `--all` cannot know the source, so it prints two complete commands: one that updates from the registry, and one with `--from <dir>` that updates from a package directory instead. The two never share a command line, because `plugin update` refuses `--from` together with `--registry`.
  - **Losing a working plugin.** Every check precedes the swap, a failed swap restores the previous package, and an interrupted swap is recovered by the next update, offline included.
  - **Shell injection through the printed command.** Versions, `provides` ids and keys come from the manifest, so every value is quoted with the egress ceremony's `ShellDialect`, and a line that no Windows form can pass literally is the marked PowerShell form.
  - **Terminal control sequences at the prompt.** Every output line that carries manifest text escapes control, format, line separator and paragraph separator characters, line breaks and invisible characters included, so manifest text cannot rewrite or rearrange what the operator reads before accepting, or print a line of its own. A value that needed escaping cannot be accepted by pasting the printed command, so it fails closed; removing and reinstalling remains the way to accept it.

prs.title: feat(plugins): replace an installed package through staged admission
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Depends on #11236; current signed `f33c9cd81d` normally merges its exact qualified `df6978c9ed` head. Earlier parent merges and update follow-ups are preserved in history. The reviewable update slice remains the host update/cache/admission implementation and its original corrections; the normal merge adds the tested recovery/dependency parent.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #10995 asks for `zeroclaw plugin update` with verified replacement and rollback. This PR is the host half; the stacked CLI PR, #11262, builds on it. The contract was posted on the issue for review: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10995#issuecomment-5894198515. It is built on the package protocol #11236 introduces, so every step that changes the plugins directory runs under the persistent hidden package lock, holds each moved directory generation in a leased hidden transaction, uses no-replace renames where supported, and deletes only through the transaction's own handle. The existing plain-rename fallback remains under the separate source-race hold noted below.
  - `PluginHost::admit_update(name, source)` is `admit_source` with the identity decided the other way round. `name` must be loaded, which is checked before the source is opened. The source's manifest must name it, which `admit_open_directory` checks after the shape check and before the signature check and the component read. Everything else is #11236's admission, unchanged.
  - `PluginHost::update_admitted(admitted)`, under the package lock:
    - stages the replacement in a leased `installing` transaction exactly as `install_admitted` does, then checks the staged skill bundle of a skill-capable package as discovery will: staging copies no symbolic links while admission follows links inside the package, so a bundle admission accepted can stage incomplete. It is refused, with the reason, before the installed package is touched;
    - claims the installed directory into a leased `replacing` transaction and checks that the claimed generation has the manifest text, which carries all the authority the caller compared, and the admitted component this host loaded. A package replaced since with a different manifest or component is published back untouched and the update refused with `NamespaceChanged`. Skill content is not compared; it was never admitted bytes;
    - publishes the replacement into the directory the package was discovered in, by #11236's publication helper. Its no-replace path refuses an existing destination; the plain-rename fallback remains under a separate hold. If that fails, the claimed generation is published back; if even that fails, the new `PluginError::ReplacementInterrupted` names where it is preserved, and its lease is released on return. On every other error the installed package is exactly as it was;
    - gives the replaced generation the delete mark #11236's remove sets once it commits to a delete, then deletes it through its handle, so recovery only ever finishes that delete. One that cannot be deleted stays there, marked, and `ReplacedPackage::leftover` names it.
  - `update_admitted` does not compare authority. Its rustdoc now states the precondition: the caller compares what the replacement requests (permissions, capabilities, `provides` ids and publisher) with the loaded generation and has the operator accept any increase, as #11262's CLI does. What the method guarantees is that the generation it replaces is the one that comparison was made against. An `# Errors` section lists what it returns and what state each leaves. Moving the comparison into the host is #11561.
  - `PluginHost::recover_interrupted_update(name)` covers a process stopped mid-update. Under the lock it judges only `replacing` transactions of `name` whose lease it can take; a held lease is reported as `RecoveryRetained`, and a lookup error inside a claim refuses rather than counting as absence. Whether the package is installed is judged by discovering the plugins directory again under the lock, never from the host's earlier view, which can predate the update that left the claims, and an installed package of the name takes precedence over any claimed generation. When it is installed, every claimed generation is marked for deletion and deleted, and one that cannot be is reported in `UpdateRecovery::Swept.kept`. When it is not, the one restorable claim is published back to `<plugins_dir>/<name>`, so the restored package is admitted only if the configured policy accepts it. Several claims, or anything already at the name, are reported and left as found; a generation marked for deletion is never put back; a claim that holds neither is finished; an empty transaction a stopped process left without a lease is removed, and a non-empty one is reported. Abandoned stages of `name` are swept with #11236's `remove_stale_staging`, and a namespace change refuses. `displaced_packages()`, also under the lock and judging installation the same way, lists the names with an abandoned claim that holds a package.
  - Also: `write_package` writes the admitted component after the `skills/` copy, so a component under `skills/` holds the admitted bytes even if the source changed after admission. One fix of #11236's own scope is carried here because the update work found it: install now runs the same staged skill check, so it refuses a staged bundle discovery would reject instead of publishing a package discovery then skips. Configuration and durable state are untouched: `PluginInstanceId` excludes the version, so the package's `[[plugins.entries]]` rows and state carry over.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No CLI, config, WIT, or on-disk format change beyond one more hidden transaction kind, `replacing`. The one operator-visible change is install's refusal above. The CLI, its Fluent strings, and the operator docs are in #11262.
  - `remove` and discovery behave as in #11236; install does too, except for the `write_package` order and the staged skill check above. `remove` leaves `replacing` transactions alone: the displaced generation of a removed package is put back only by a named update.
  - Renames are not followed by `fsync`, as #11236's install does not fsync either, and the replaced generation is deleted right after the replacement is published. A power loss right after an update may leave the new package partly unflushed with the previous one already gone; #11262's docs give the remedy.
  - Discovery still reads a package's manifest and its component by path at different moments, so a daemon that discovers during a swap can pair the previous manifest with the new component when no `wasm_sha256` binds them, until its next discovery. Admitting discovered packages through one directory handle, as admission already does, is #11562.
  - Staging never follows symbolic links, so a bundle with real skills beside linked ones still installs and updates without the linked ones.
  - A process killed between publishing the replacement and marking the replaced generation for deletion leaves that generation claimed. Recovery deletes it while the package is installed; after a later `plugin remove`, a named update would put it back.
- **Blast radius:** The published `zeroclaw-plugins` API gains `admit_update`, `update_admitted`, `recover_interrupted_update`, `displaced_packages`, `ReplacedPackage`, `UpdateRecovery`, and `PluginError::ReplacementInterrupted`. #11236's exhaustive `is_structural_admission_failure` classifies the variant as non-structural here, since admission never returns it. `host/recovery.rs` gains `transaction_package`, and #11236's delete mark is now shared by remove and update; `LoadedPlugin` keeps its admitted manifest text. Update opens the plugins root on first use, as install and remove do.
  - #11232 has landed on `master`, and #11236 merges `master` after it, so the stack holds one revision of each. `claimed_is_loaded` relies on `admit_component_in`, which #11232 and #11236 moved onto the no-follow walk; the replacement and recovery tests pass on this head. Merge order: #11236, this PR, #11262.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10995 (closed by the stacked CLI PR, #11262). Depends on #11236 and #11715. Related #7432, #11232. Follow-ups: #11561, #11562.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `core`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `release-gate`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `cli`, `ci:windows`, `topic:plugins`, `release:v0.8.6`.

### Since the last reviews

tidux requested changes at `f817e5386e`, which JordanTheJet had approved. Each item:

- **Restack.** The commit is rebased onto #11236's fixes, `c5fbbe2313`, as `420969ea90`, and `89cd78102d` merges #11236's later merge of `master`. The rebase conflicted only in `host/recovery.rs` and `host/recovery_tests.rs`, as your simulated restack showed. The approvals at `f817e5386e` do not cover this head.
- **One delete mark.** `SUPERSEDED` and `Transaction::retire` are gone. Update gives the replaced generation the mark remove sets (`mark_deleting`) and deletes it with `finish_delete`, and recovery classifies a marked claim as one it only ever deletes. The mark's doc comment says what it means for both.
- **Bounded barrier.** #11236's version, which gives up after 30 seconds, is kept, and this commit no longer changes it.
- **One empty-entry rule.** `abandoned_claims` uses `Root::remove_empty_entry`.
- **Tests on the new walk.** The replacement and recovery tests pass on `369fb21334`; see the commands below. Since #11236 now opens the plugins root on first use, update, recovery and `displaced_packages` do too.
- **Authority in the host API.** Documented as a precondition, with an `# Errors` section, on `update_admitted`. Moving the check into the host is tracked in #11561.
- **Mixed manifest and component in discovery.** Tracked in #11562, linked from the scope boundary.
- **`plugin remove` retiring abandoned `replacing` claims.** Not done here. `remove` still leaves `replacing` transactions alone, as the scope boundary says. The window it would close, a stop between publishing and marking, is narrow, and it would make remove act on update's transactions, which I'd rather review on its own.

### What this does, simply

To update a plugin, ZeroClaw has to swap one package directory for another without leaving the operator with no working plugin when the swap fails or the process stops part-way. This PR adds that swap to the plugin host; the command that uses it is the next PR.

The new version is first checked exactly as a fresh install is checked, then written, complete, into a hidden folder. Only then does the host move the installed folder into a hidden folder of its own, check that it is still the version the update was prepared against, and move the new folder into its place. If that move fails, the old folder is moved back.

Every step that changes the plugins folder happens under the same lock install and remove use, so those steps never interleave across processes, and whatever ran before the lock is checked again under it. If the process dies part-way, the hidden folders say how far it got, and the lock on each ends with the process: the next update puts the old version back, or finishes cleaning up. An update and its recovery never delete a package by name.

### Completed-update cache correction

The signed follow-up 284d2820482d3b818e386ad5320654c3b3d49edd fixes a host that loaded a package before another host completed an update and could retain the old generation after all update claims were removed. Recovery now refreshes the installed view under the existing package lock even when no abandoned claims remain. This also removes stale cached packages that another host deleted, while preserving current and missing-package no-op behavior.

The one-file follow-up adds three deterministic host regressions for completed replacement followed by another replacement, external removal while preserving another package, and current/missing-package no-ops. Source and patch/whitespace checks pass. The follow-up was separately qualified on its earlier named heads; current combined execution is supplied by the f33 current-head run above. No duplicate local execution is claimed.

The f33 normal parent integration now adopts the corrected #11236 copy and atomic-only move implementation. The current combined run qualifies the named mutex/cache/recovery controls. #11561/#11562 and downstream CLI/configuration acceptance remain separately scoped; no broader closure is claimed.

### Since the cache correction

`9014776427` answers the review thread on `displaced_packages`: two calls on one host shared one open lock file, and `flock` does not make a second taker of the same open file wait. `recovery::Root` now also holds an in-process mutex for as long as its lock guard lives, under the same bounded wait. `a_second_thread_sharing_the_root_waits_for_the_package_lock` covers it and fails with the mutex removed.

`ade89c66c5` merges #11236's current head, `9f2af02f72`, which streams skill assets through a bounded buffer and keeps executable helpers' execute bits. The merge was clean and leaves the update commits unchanged.

`ef150ebef3` answers the review thread on batch updates: recovery judged the whole plugins directory again, so `plugin update --all`, which recovers each of its names, admitted every installed package once per name. Recovery now judges again only the package it was asked about. The refresh keeps discovery's loop, because discovery keys a package by its manifest's name and admits neither of two directories that claim one name, and skips each entry whose manifest names another package before anything else about it is checked. `recovery_without_claims_refreshes_only_the_named_package` fails if the no-claims branch rediscovers everything, and `recovery_refresh_admits_neither_package_of_a_name_two_directories_claim` fails if the refresh matches by directory name instead.

`93f1337146` merges #11236's `7a3ad81ed5`, which brings in the 36 `master` commits since `ee79b1f483`, among them #11302. #11302 gives `publish_and_seed_plugin` a channel binding argument, so the stranded-directory install test passes none. The update commits are unchanged.

`c21e06242d` answers the review thread on `--all` putting back a package it never named. A batch takes its names from the host's discovery, so a package an interrupted update displaced after that was still listed, and recovery restored it. `sweep_interrupted_update` is the recovery a batch runs: it deletes what finished updates left, but leaves a claimed package where it is and reports `UpdateRecovery::Displaced`, which it decides under the package lock. `a_sweep_leaves_a_package_displaced_after_discovery_where_it_is` fails if the sweep puts the package back.

`369fb21334` answers the review thread on recovery dropping its cleanup warnings. Recovery deletes the generations finished updates left before it puts a displaced package back, and only a `Swept` outcome reported one it could not delete. `Restored`, `Ambiguous`, `Occupied` and `Displaced` now carry `kept` too, and `UpdateRecovery::kept` returns it for any outcome. `recovery_that_restores_a_package_reports_a_generation_it_cannot_delete` fails if a restoring recovery drops it. The commands below ran on `369fb21334`.

### Current public parent integration

Signed `f33c9cd81d0a72ad1ccf1d10f2ca2e161fb9eae5` normally merges the exact qualified #11236 head `df6978c9ed70d953438c2413e8234384161955a6`. This retains the host update/cache/admission implementation, mutex lifetime and explicit lease unlock, while adopting the parent's atomic-only helper and seven regression bodies. Existing author workspace dependencies are retained in the composed lock; the genuine shared registry resolution contains 1,293 identities, `probe-rs 0.32`, and no `ruzstd` or `espflash`.

[Current Quality Gate 38418042404](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38418042404) completed SUCCESS: 39 jobs passed and five were conditionally skipped; gate 115374348573 passed. Current Security policy/locked fetch/audit, Format, lint and Rust 1.96 checks pass on a CI tree equal to the public source. All 16 focused methods have actual named PASS records in both workspace and no-default Cranelift plugin-library lanes: seven atomic controls, three cache controls, mutex/lease handling and four refresh/retention controls. These are 32 observations of 16 distinct methods, without borrowing older execution.

Depends on #11236 and #11715. Protected merge still requires their actual acceptance/landing and this head's qualifying Core/CODEOWNERS reviews. Earlier evidence below applies only to its named earlier revisions. Current advisory Windows, full platform and release acceptance remain separate.

The current f33c9cd [Windows advisory job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38418043599/job/115368451089) completed with FAILURE: nine workspace and two hardware tests failed, while the existing advisory `continue-on-error` policy makes the workflow conclusion SUCCESS. The Cranelift plugin library passed 348 tests; four receiving Windows recovery methods have eight named passes across workspace and Cranelift. Unix-only atomic-error injection/substitution tests are not credited on Windows. This is scoped plugin evidence, not full Windows success, a baseline comparison or a causal finding for the eleven failures.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: library-only. An operator exercises this through the stacked CLI PR, whose body carries reviewer steps and an exact-output walkthrough.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - The workspace `Test` job runs the `host.rs` and `host/recovery_tests.rs` unit tests, which have no feature gate. The cross-process tests spawn the test binary itself and pause it at named steps, as #11236's do.
  - The `Check (plugins …)` legs compile the crate with each backend and run its lib tests with Cranelift.
  - `Lint` and the rustdoc gate cover the new public items.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows.
  - No required job compiles the plugin crate for Windows. The advisory Windows nextest was cancelled on `89cd78102d` ([job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37707727510/job/113086251012)). The completed log sections passed 322 of 322 plugin library tests, 204 of 204 plugin tests in the full workspace run, and 33 component end-to-end tests. Later root-binary coverage did not complete. Those include the replacement and cross-process update-recovery tests. The recorded workspace and hardware sections contain nine and two failures respectively, matching #11236's run on `b17f915a60`; the advisory check itself is CANCELLED. The run on `ef150ebef3` was cancelled too, but #11262's run on `bd2d4e5eea`, whose host files matched `ef150ebef3`, completed ([job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38204522312/job/114665160734)): 347 of 347 plugin library tests, 214 of 214 plugin tests in the full workspace run, and 42 of 42 plugin component end-to-end tests passed, and its 11 failures are the same tests outside `zeroclaw-plugins`. The run on `369fb21334`, this head, completed ([job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38330825759/job/115080246836)): 348 of 348 plugin library tests, 215 of 215 plugin tests in the full workspace run, and 42 of 42 plugin component end-to-end tests passed, the sweep and refresh tests among them. It failed 12 tests outside `zeroclaw-plugins`: the same 11, and the gateway's `webhook_sse_abort_cancels_backpressured_unread_client`, which timed out waiting for its provider fixture in the workspace run and passed in the job's gateway group.
    - Source inspection maps eight of the eleven failures to existing follow-ups: #11361 covers directory attachments and the chunked-upload path fixture, #11362 the SOP partial-save reader, #11363 the filesystem adapter, #11365 the agent-bundle path check, #11366 multimodal path probing, and #11364 the two Arduino tests. Passing Windows evidence remains a separate requirement.
    - Three fixture failures remain outside those six patches: the legacy image-marker JSON assertion, `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, and the MCP image-path text assertion. No current-master runtime comparison has been verified. These are passing completed plugin groups; the cancelled advisory does not establish full Windows coverage.
  - Five tests are `#[cfg(unix)]`. Three create symbolic links: `update_refuses_a_staged_bundle_that_lost_a_linked_skill_md`, `install_refuses_a_staged_bundle_that_lost_a_linked_skill_md`, and `admit_update_refuses_a_bundle_whose_only_skill_is_a_linked_directory`. Two use file permissions to make a delete fail: `a_replaced_generation_that_cannot_be_deleted_is_kept_marked` and `recovery_reports_a_claimed_generation_it_cannot_delete`. So the refusals of an incomplete staged bundle and the undeletable-generation paths are untested off Unix.
- **Commands run and tail output** (macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0, head `369fb21334`):

  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --lib` → `245 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib` → `378 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the same with `--features plugins-wasm-cranelift` → no diagnostics
  - `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` → no diagnostics
  - `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features` → no warnings
  - `cargo doc --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-plugins` (rustdoc warnings are errors in `.cargo/config.toml`) → no diagnostics
  - `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.py` over the files the gate lists → `Comment hygiene gate passed.` (the gate's own ripgrep listing could not run on this machine); `./scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` → no prose em-dashes, markdownlint `0 error(s)`
  - The `recovery_tests` module (28 tests, almost all across real processes), run 60 times from the built test binary → 0 failures.
  - The root binary's lints, tests and component tests ran on #11262's head, which contains this commit.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **Mutations.** Each guard was broken on purpose, one at a time, and the named test failed. Most ran at `f817e5386e`; the two that involve the delete mark ran again after the restack, on the same commit before its final rebase onto #11236's last fixes:
    - recovery without the package lock, and update without it → `recovery_waits_for_an_update_another_process_is_running`
    - installation judged from the host's earlier view instead of under the lock → `recovery_judges_installation_from_the_directory_not_a_stale_view` and, across processes, `recovery_by_a_host_built_before_the_claim_puts_the_package_back`
    - an empty claim kept instead of finished → `recovery_finishes_a_claim_the_ambiguous_remedy_emptied` and `an_update_stopped_before_its_claim_leaves_nothing_to_recover`
    - an empty transaction without a lease never removed → `recovery_removes_an_empty_transaction_and_reports_one_that_is_not`
    - install without the staged skill check → `install_refuses_a_staged_bundle_that_lost_a_linked_skill_md`
    - recovery's discovery taken before the lock instead of under it → `recovery_judges_installation_after_taking_the_lock`
    - the listing of displaced packages without the lock → `listing_displaced_packages_waits_for_a_running_update`
    - no refreshed view when there is nothing to judge → `recovery_waits_for_an_update_another_process_is_running`
    - a held lease treated as abandoned → `recovery_leaves_a_claim_whose_lease_is_held`
    - no check that the claimed generation is the loaded one → `an_update_refuses_a_package_that_changed_since_this_host_loaded_it`
    - no put-back after a failed publication → `a_failed_publication_puts_the_claimed_generation_back`
    - no delete mark before a delete → `recovery_reports_a_claimed_generation_it_cannot_delete` and `a_replaced_generation_that_cannot_be_deleted_is_kept_marked` (re-run)
    - a generation marked for deletion treated as restorable → `recovery_never_puts_back_a_generation_marked_for_deletion` (re-run)
    - no validation of the staged skill bundle → `update_refuses_a_staged_bundle_that_lost_a_linked_skill_md`
    - the component written before the `skills/` copy → `a_component_under_skills_keeps_the_admitted_bytes_after_a_source_swap`
  - **Across processes**, with #11236's harness:
    - an update killed after its claim is put back by recovery in another process, byte for byte, and its stage is swept;
    - one killed after publishing is finished by another process's recovery, which deletes the claimed generation and keeps the replacement;
    - a recovery started while another process's update holds its claim waits for the package lock instead of touching the claim, then finds nothing to do;
    - a host built before another process's update claimed the package, which that process then left when it was killed, puts the claim back rather than deleting the only copy;
    - an update killed between creating its claim and making it leaves nothing for recovery to do, and its stage is swept;
    - a recovery that already discovered the package, paused before the lock while an update claims the package and dies, puts the claim back;
    - listing displaced packages waits for a running update's lock.
  - **In process**, the tests also pin: admission refusals (not installed; a source for another package, refused before its oversized component is read; strict policy for unsigned and untrusted replacements; a digest mismatch); the admitted bytes being installed after a source swap; a failed put-back reporting the preserved generation, which recovery then restores; the several-claims and occupied-name refusals; near-miss transaction names left alone; a skill bundle replaced as a whole; replacement in a misnamed discovery directory; and a failed staging write leaving the installed package untouched.
  - **Not verified:** Windows beyond the advisory job above, and the Unix-only tests listed there.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no interface changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `369fb21334`, library tests only.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The workspace-wide gates run on the stacked CLI PR, whose head contains this commit.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. Every move and delete stays inside the plugins directory the host already owns, through #11236's retained root: claims and publications are renames that never overwrite, and a generation is deleted only through the handle of the transaction that claimed it. Recovery judges only transactions whose lease it can take; the one directory it removes by name is an empty transaction without a lease, by a removal that refuses a non-empty directory.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The replacement passes the existing admission, signature policy included, before anything is written, and the claimed generation must be the one whose authority the caller compared. Nothing here changes what a plugin may do once loaded; the stacked PR gates added authority.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for operators and on-disk state. Rust callers of `zeroclaw-plugins` that match `PluginError` exhaustively need an arm for `ReplacementInterrupted`; the one in this workspace has it.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` of the top commit. If #11262 has landed, revert it first; nothing else calls this API.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - A plugin missing from `zeroclaw plugin list` while a hidden `.<name>.replacing-v1-<id>` directory holds its package: an update was interrupted, and `recover_interrupted_update`, through `zeroclaw plugin update <name>`, puts it back.
  - A hidden `.<name>.replacing-v1-<id>` directory holding a `deleting` mark next to an installed package is inert, and the next update deletes it.
