prs.title: feat(whatsapp-web): implement add_reaction and remove_reaction (rebase of #7535)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Preserves the WhatsApp Web reaction implementation carried from #7535 by @chengzhichao-xydt and refreshed in this PR by @s7dhansh.
  - Threads the native WhatsApp message ID into inbound `ChannelMessage` values so acknowledgement reactions can address the original message instead of a generated UUID.
  - Records canonical WhatsApp `MessageKey` values only for inbound 1:1 messages with non-empty native IDs, then uses those keys for `add_reaction` and `remove_reaction`.
  - Keeps empty message IDs as safe no-ops, while non-empty group, own-message, unknown, expired, or evicted targets return an error instead of reporting a reaction that was not sent.
  - Clears account-scoped reaction targets after an explicit logout and before a newly paired client can be installed, while preserving eligible targets across ordinary reconnects.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR does not add group-chat reactions, reactions to messages sent by the linked account, or new reaction metadata to the shared channel trait.
- **Blast radius:** WhatsApp Web acknowledgement reactions, inbound WhatsApp `ChannelMessage.id` values changing from generated UUIDs to native message IDs, and a bounded in-memory registry of up to 1,024 targets. Entries are eligible for at most one hour, may be evicted earlier at capacity, and are cleared when the linked account is explicitly revoked. Other channels and WhatsApp message content delivery are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #7518
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `channel`, `channel:whatsapp`, `needs-author-action`, `risk:medium`, `size:S`

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can show that it received and finished handling a message by adding acknowledgement reactions. WhatsApp Web previously lacked the channel methods needed to send those reactions, and the first implementation attempt could build a reaction key from only a chat and message ID. That was not enough to know whether a target was an inbound direct message, a group message, or a message sent by the linked account. This repair keeps the original reaction implementation but records the complete native key when an eligible inbound 1:1 message arrives. Later calls with a non-empty ID must find that recorded key or return an error, so a tool cannot claim an unknown, expired, or evicted reaction succeeded. Explicit logout clears the old account's keys before re-pairing; ordinary reconnects preserve still-eligible keys. Group and own-message reactions remain unsupported until the shared channel boundary carries their additional metadata.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. A linked-device smoke would add vendor-side evidence beyond the protocol-shaped unit test.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** channel: WhatsApp Web
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build with `whatsapp-web`, connect a test WhatsApp account, and enable `[channels].ack_reactions` in a disposable configuration.
- **Steps to run:** Send the bot an inbound 1:1 message from another account and let one normal agent turn complete. Separately send a group message and a message from the linked account.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The inbound 1:1 message receives the configured processing reaction and then the completion reaction. The group and linked-account messages do not receive an acknowledgement reaction.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** WhatsApp Web has no `add_reaction` or `remove_reaction` implementation, so the same inbound 1:1 turn sends no WhatsApp reaction.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Exact-head CI is green for commit `1c8029e42616a74b3f2cd7d258eecb23a2c78619`: 34 checks passed, 4 conditional checks were skipped, and no checks failed or remained pending. The formatting, lint, build, platform, feature-matrix, security, MSRV, and test lanes cover the changed Rust channel surface alongside the focused local tests below.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI and the local protocol-shaped hook do not prove acceptance by a live WhatsApp linked-device session.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```sh
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  # passed with no output

  git diff --cached --check
  # passed with no output before commit

  bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  # passed

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --features whatsapp-web -- -D warnings
  # finished successfully on the current head

  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features whatsapp-web reaction_
  # test result: ok. 14 passed; 0 failed

  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features whatsapp-web reactions_use_only_inbound_one_to_one_native_targets
  # current head: test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed

  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features whatsapp-web whatsapp_web
  # preceding behavior-equivalent head: test result: ok. 113 passed; 0 failed
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected the inbound registration, explicit-logout teardown, reconnect, and outbound send paths. The focused hook tests capture the outgoing protocol message and verify the native ID, remote JID, `from_me: false`, `participant: None`, emoji text, empty-text removal payload, caller-visible non-empty misses with no send, explicit-logout invalidation, and ordinary-reconnect preservation. No live WhatsApp account smoke was run.
- **Visual interface changed?** N/A; this changes channel protocol behavior, not rendered presentation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** A live linked-device smoke was not run because no disposable WhatsApp test session or credentials were used. The local build emitted the existing macOS compact-unwind `__eh_frame section too large` linker warning and the existing future-incompatibility notice for `proc-macro-error2 v2.0.1`; neither affected the passing test results.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **Yes.** Eligible acknowledgement reactions are sent through the already configured WhatsApp Web connection. The bounded registry admits only canonical inbound 1:1 native message keys; non-empty unsupported or synthetic targets return an error without sending, and explicit logout clears the old account's entries before re-pairing.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** The existing channel turn-context preamble now carries the native WhatsApp message ID instead of a generated UUID so the acknowledgement-reaction lifecycle can target the inbound message. This does not change user-message content or add a new parser. The ID remains structured channel metadata, and outbound reactions require an exact canonical key recorded from an eligible inbound event.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes at the API and configuration surfaces.** Inbound WhatsApp `ChannelMessage.id` values intentionally change from generated UUIDs to native message IDs, which also changes the existing autosave-key input and turn-context metadata for those messages.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the eventual squash commit for #9894 with `git revert <merged-squash-sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Disable `[channels].ack_reactions` to stop acknowledgement reactions without disabling WhatsApp Web message delivery.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Acknowledgement reactions are absent from eligible inbound 1:1 messages, a reaction appears on a message other than the triggering inbound message, a caller reports success for an unavailable target, an old-account target is attempted after re-pairing, or a processing reaction remains after a turn exceeds the one-hour registry eligibility window.

prs.title: feat(runtime): preserve per-message steering provenance
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Gateway WebSocket and RPC steering attach conservative source facts to each injected message through the existing `SteeringInput`. The runtime evaluates those facts before auto-save or transcript insertion instead of borrowing the enclosing turn's context.
- **What changed and why:** Unstamped `SteeringInput` values retain explicitly unknown provenance. The ToolLoop handoff admits the original user message without reclassifying an accepted injection as agent-direct input.
- **Scope boundary:** No configurable policy, JSON-RPC payload change, invented gateway identity, or derived SOP/delegate/skill-review provenance. Existing consume-time authorization, tool narrowing, cancellation and session-generation checks remain in place.
- **Blast radius:** Streamed agent turns, gateway WebSocket steering and RPC session steering. The default ingress policy remains `Loop`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10891. This PR implements its steering slice; derived-turn provenance remains separate.
- **Runtime placement:** Depends on #11436. The covering scope needs a recorded Core Team decision in the exception table before this implementation merges.

### What this does, simply

During an active agent turn, a person can send a correction without starting a separate turn. The runtime already checks whether the sender is still allowed to steer and limits the tools available to that sender. But the correction did not carry its own source information into the ingress policy. That policy could judge it using the original turn's facts.

This PR keeps source information with each correction. RPC records the person operating that connection, including an administrator steering someone else's session. Gateway corrections remain external and untrusted without inventing an identity. Unstamped in-process messages remain unknown. These facts do not grant permission or replace the live authorization checks, and the default policy still accepts steering as before.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The change extends the existing steering carrier instead of introducing a second receiver or message hierarchy. One policy evaluator handles known and unknown ingress facts. The Agent wrapper keeps authorization callbacks attached across memory writes and rechecks them before model use. This six-file slice is mostly regression coverage; it does not add persisted state, configuration or another identity registry.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; policy-input and controlled-Drop tests expose the source-context distinction, while the default `Loop` policy produces no distinct manual UI result.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** At `f5a4b624d7881e7c8be4b9679a8486fd11303c9a`, [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37558822676/job/112591201195), Parallel Runtime Test, Lint, Format and the default-features all-targets check succeeded. Test runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`, covering the provenance/Drop tests and existing delayed-revocation, tool-ceiling and replaced-incarnation regressions. The workspace checks also compile the gateway integration.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live gateway or RPC client smoke was run. The source facts and controlled-Drop behavior are exercised at the runtime policy and RPC handler boundaries.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check` and `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I traced edge-stamped facts through the canonical `SteeringInput`, policy admission and model handoff, and checked that the live authorization callback remains attached through awaited memory writes and final readmission.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no visual presentation changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** [Hosted validation](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37558822676) ran on `f5a4b624d7881e7c8be4b9679a8486fd11303c9a`, which includes merged #11132 at `2125a1301ed4da056eb211f2a83190b63383a211`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The passing regressions cover distinct source contexts at policy admission, Drop before tool narrowing/auto-save/history, no extra model request for a late dropped correction, and RPC attribution to the acting administrator rather than the session owner.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local test execution was skipped in favor of the hosted `Test` job. Broad local checks would duplicate required CI coverage.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; test identities are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Steering already reached the model; this change carries its own conservative source facts to policy admission. The default policy remains `Loop`.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Future policy must not mistake steering for trusted agent-direct input. Authorized gateway/RPC producers stamp the source facts; no client-supplied provenance is accepted. Unknown facts stay unknown, and live sender authorization remains separate.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes; existing `SteeringInput` constructors and `From<String>`/`From<&str>` conversions remain, as does the JSON-RPC request shape.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's provenance changes without reverting the already-merged #11132 authorization and generation checks.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A steering message disappears, persists after a policy Drop, carries the wrong RPC actor or triggers an extra model round. Use the focused provenance and steering regressions to isolate the failure.

prs.title: feat(providers): support multiple models per provider profile
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds a `[providers.models.<family>.<alias>.models.<model_alias>]` subtable so one provider profile (a single credential + endpoint) can host multiple models, each with its own model id and tuning. Previously each model required a duplicate profile that re-declared the same connection.
  - Introduces three-segment model refs `<family>.<alias>.<model_alias>` resolved via `Config::resolve_model_selection`; two-part profile refs select `models.default`, otherwise the sole nested entry, otherwise the legacy profile-level model. The selected entry's overrides (`id`, `temperature`, `context_window`, `max_tokens`, `think`, `vision`, `native_tools`, `replay_assistant_reasoning`, `provider_extra`, `chat_template_kwargs`) are intended to apply on top of the profile options across the assembly paths below; the covered assembly paths are: CLI session (incl. `--model-provider type.alias.model`), agent loop (initial construction, in-turn switch, hot reload), orchestrator/channels (classifier route, route selection, channel `/model`), delegate, model_switch, SOP `llm.generate`, gateway boot, doctor, and `model_routes` (a route with no explicit `model` resolves its `model_provider` through the same selection contract).
  - **Migration chain is sequenced, not stamped:** `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 5. V3→V4 removes inert agent tunables, `summary_model`, old top-level Twitter/Reddit spellings, and unsupported `[channels.notion.*]` maps with their references. It preserves supported SaaS/CLI settings, Twitter/Reddit aliased channels and their references, top-level Notion settings, and `skills.prompt_injection_mode`. V4→V5 mints `models.default.id` from a legacy profile-level `model` while keeping `model` readable. A V3 or V4 config migrates on load; **a V3-era binary rejects a V5 config** — the schema_version gate is the compatibility boundary, no cross-version read is claimed. Integration with the separate V4 cut in #8754 still requires reconciliation; independent landing in either order is not claimed.
  - **Cost fix (folded in; now also on master through #9938):** the channels path built its pricing view with a type-level map that merged every alias of one provider family into a single price slot, so two profiles of the same type (e.g. `custom.cheap` + `custom.premium`) collided and could not be priced independently. Every path now uses the alias-keyed `build_model_provider_pricing`; cost resolves by the exact `<type>.<alias>` profile key (carried by `Agent` construction and the accepted-route report) and then per model id. Removes the now-unused type-level builder, its merge helper, and the type-keyed fallback branch in `provider_pricing`.
- **Scope boundary:** Fallback and pricing stay profile-level (profile `pricing` is already keyed by model id, so per-model pricing needs no new field). No entry-level `fallback_models` / `pricing`.
- **Blast radius:** Config schema (+migration), provider factory/assembly, runtime agent + loop + cost tracking, channels orchestrator, gateway, doctor, quickstart, CLI.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8310, Related #8754 (V4 cut prior art), Related #9573 (alias-qualified pricing), Related #9938
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `core`, `agent`, `channel`, `config`, `doctor`, `gateway`, `provider`, `runtime`, `tool`, `tests`, `principal contributor`, `channel:core`, `tool:delegate`, `observability:log`, `domain:architecture`, `needs-author-action`, `risk:high`, `risk:manual`, `web`, `quickstart`, `zerocode`, `size:XL`, `channel:acp`, `cli`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** cli. Web/ZeroCode interaction remains unverified.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A provider profile with a `models` subtable, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.gw]` (uri + api_key) plus `[providers.models.openai.gw.models.fast] id = "gpt-4o-mini"` and `[providers.models.openai.gw.models.big] id = "gpt-4o"`. Point an agent at `openai.gw.fast`. For the cost fix: configure two same-type profiles (`[providers.models.custom.cheap]` + `[providers.models.custom.premium]`) with different `[...pricing]`.
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw config migrate --json` on a `schema_version = 3` file; `zeroclaw models list`; `zeroclaw agent -a <alias> --message hi` (default nested selection); `zeroclaw agent -a <alias> --model-provider openai.gw.big --message hi` (non-default switch); `config/set providers.models.openai.gw.models.big.temperature = 0.5` while a session is live. For cost: drive a turn against each `custom.*` alias and read `/api/cost`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Migration reports `migrated: true, schema_version: 5` and mints `models.default.id`; `models list` shows both nested entries; the default and switched turns each dispatch with their own model id; the live session keeps serving `gpt-4o` after the hot reload instead of falling back to `models.default`; each `custom.*` alias bills its own rate.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** No `models` subtable; a three-segment ref is rejected and each model requires a duplicate profile. At the original base, same-type aliases shared one merged price slot (last-alias-wins). Current master includes the profile-attribution repair from #9938.

### How I tested

Historical local validation on `be2fbc55f9c75b0b0069575f1ebbba003081acde`:

```sh
env -u RUSTC_WRAPPER CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/test/ref/llm/agent/claws/zeroclaw/target cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime  # passed
cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-runtime -- --check  # passed
git diff --check                          # clean
```

Parent head `3a1a45cc736bf66e074150d300f217b61f458523` local validation:

```sh
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh  # passed
bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh    # passed
env -u RUSTC_WRAPPER CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/test/ref/llm/agent/claws/zeroclaw/target cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --features channel-telegram  # passed
cargo fmt --all -- --check  # passed
git diff --check            # clean
```

The focused late-revocation runtime regression build was started but stopped after a prolonged local runtime link step; it did not produce a test result. Fresh hosted CI is the current-head runtime verification.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI passes on `3c021b1689de1a15605d2cdfb9f1bc5fad98f7af` in [Quality Gate run 35732263344](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/35732263344). The local command results and CLI smoke below are historical evidence, not new runs on this head. Hosted CI does not establish the missing Web/ZeroCode interaction result or clear the remaining review findings.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Web/ZeroCode interaction and visual evidence remain missing. Historical CLI smoke and config map-key tests cover their respective paths; they do not establish the rendered editor or picker interactions.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```sh
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-config            # ok. 1509 passed; 0 failed (lib) — incl. 7 new v3_to_v4_* migration cases
                                           # ok. 90 passed; 0 failed (migration integration)
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools             # ok. 1716 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers         # ok. 1470 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway           # ok. 469 passed; 0 failed (lib) + 9 (doc)
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::agent::tests              # ok. 121 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::config_set # ok. 27 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::model_switch               # ok. 16 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib orchestrator::tests::load_runtime_config # ok. 5 passed; 0 failed
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-runtime \
               -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-tools \
               --all-targets -- -D warnings                                # exit 0
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                               # exit 0
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Behavior regressions added for the review blockers:
  - `config_set_provider_refresh_preserves_session_nested_model_ref` — a live session bound to `openai.<alias>.fast` survives a provider-scoped `config/set` of that entry's `temperature`: the rebuild keeps the three-segment selection (model stays the `fast` entry's id, not `models.default`'s) and picks up the new temperature.
  - `turn_bills_selected_same_family_alias_rate` — a real `Agent::turn` against a mock endpoint with `custom.cheap` + `custom.premium` at distinct rates bills exactly the selected alias's rate ($12.50 for premium, not the sibling's $0.75 and not zero).
  - `set_preserves_three_segment_ref_and_derives_model_id` / `set_rejects_unknown_nested_model_alias` — model_switch keeps (or refuses) the full ref.
  - `load_runtime_config_preserves_nested_model_ref` — channel hot-reload keeps the nested ref and its per-entry temperature.
  - `model_route_effective_model_resolves_nested_refs` — a `model_routes` entry with no explicit `model` dispatches to the nested entry's id; an explicit `model` still wins.
  - `from_config_preserves_alias_for_cost_recording` — Agent construction carries `<type>.<alias>` into cost recording.

  CLI user-boundary run on revision `36557c5dd62bcb64b6140c416c60302f0593476f` against a local OpenAI-compatible mock:
  - `zeroclaw config migrate --json` on a V3 file → `{"migrated": true, "schema_version": 5}` with a backup; the file gains `[providers.models.custom.gw.models.default] id = "old-legacy-model"`.
  - `zeroclaw models list` on the migrated file → `[custom.gw.default] model: old-legacy-model`; on a two-entry profile → both `[custom.gw.fast] model: proof-fast-model` and `[custom.gw.big] model: proof-big-model` listed.
  - `zeroclaw agent -a default --message hi` → mock received `model=proof-fast-model auth=Bearer proof-key`, replied `mock-reply-for:proof-fast-model`.

prs.body:
Reason: MiniMax-M3 image and video inputs were serialized as plain text despite the model supporting multimodal content parts.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Advertise vision for aliases configured with MiniMax-M3, using the configured model as the source of truth.
  - Keep M3 system messages separate so user images reach the existing image-normalization path while literal system media examples stay text.
  - Convert explicit user video markers into video content parts across all eight chat entry points, including streaming and native tool requests.
  - Document accepted HTTPS and MiniMax file references and preserve text for unsupported video references and non-user roles.
- **Scope boundary:** Local video loading, video uploads, embedded video data, pricing, endpoints, and model defaults are unchanged; MiniMax-M2.7 retains its text-only behavior.
- **Blast radius:** MiniMax adapter request shaping, its factory capability reporting, and provider documentation.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

A MiniMax-M3 alias can send normalized user images and explicit `[VIDEO:https://example.com/clip.mp4]` or `[VIDEO:mm_file://file_id]` references as multimodal input. System prompt examples remain text. Local videos must be uploaded separately before supplying a MiniMax file reference.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; the regression test captures the emitted HTTP payload for all eight adapter entry points.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Provider adapter HTTP boundary used by chat surfaces; no visual interface changed.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Rust development dependencies; no live API credentials needed.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers minimax --lib`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Separate system text, an image part, and two video parts reach each captured request.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The M3 factory reports no vision, merges system messages, and sends media markers as text.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** No pending CI is treated as evidence; local checks below cover the adapter, factory, workspace lint, and documentation.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live MiniMax inference call was performed.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fetch --locked`: passed.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers minimax --lib`: `8 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib`: `1916 passed; 3 failed; 4 ignored`. The failures involved shared proxy state and a temporary executable reporting `Text file busy`.
  - `target/debug/deps/zeroclaw_providers-bf43e3aef7aace24 --test-threads=1`: the same newly built test binary passed with `1919 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored`.
  - `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh`: passed workspace formatting, correctness lint, and the provider dispatch gate without warnings.
  - `BASE_SHA=origin/master DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/providers/catalog.md ./scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`: `0 error(s)`.
  - `BASE_SHA=origin/master DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/providers/catalog.md ./scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`: passed; optional HTTP validation was skipped because lychee is unavailable.
  - `cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`: passed with rustdoc warnings denied.
  - `git diff --check`: passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Checked the request contract against the [MiniMax API documentation](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-openai-api); inspected the earlier merged system-message fix to preserve literal examples, and checked related PRs for overlap.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no rendered interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `20db222`, HTTP capture in `minimax_multimodal_reaches_every_chat_entry_point` plus factory and marker-policy regressions.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Captured request assertions require one image part and two video parts in each of eight requests, with unchanged system text; the test binary result is recorded above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** M3 user media is structured; non-user video markers, malformed references, and text-only model requests remain text; existing cache metadata stays on the final text part.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Live inference was not run; deterministic tests use a local mock endpoint. HTTP link validation is optional in the documented gate.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: configured M3 aliases advertise image capability. Existing image loading and normalization policies continue to apply.

prs.title: feat(dashboard): show OpenRouter credit balance
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds an optional, encrypted OpenRouter management API key, separate from the inference API key.
  - Adds an authenticated gateway endpoint that retrieves OpenRouter credit totals without exposing the management credential or upstream response to the browser.
  - Shows an OpenRouter balance card in the web dashboard only when an enabled agent uses OpenRouter and the integration is configured and reachable.
  - Adds English and Portuguese UI strings and documents the optional configuration.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not change inference routing, model selection, billing, or other providers. It does not expose the management key to the dashboard.
- **Blast radius:** OpenRouter provider configuration, the authenticated web API, and the dashboard overview. Existing installations without `management_api_key` retain their current behavior and do not show the card.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.
- **Labels:** To be assigned by maintainers/path labeler.

### What this does, simply

OpenRouter users could configure inference but could not see their remaining credits in ZeroClaw. This change introduces a distinct management credential for the OpenRouter credits API, keeps that credential encrypted and server-side, and conditionally displays the returned credit balance on the dashboard. If OpenRouter is not actively configured, the management key is absent, or the request fails, the endpoint returns no content and the dashboard card stays hidden.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Configure an enabled agent with an OpenRouter provider, an inference API key, and a valid `management_api_key`; start the gateway and pair/authenticate the dashboard.
- **Steps to run:** Open the dashboard overview and inspect the OpenRouter balance card. Then remove or invalidate `management_api_key`, restart the gateway, and reload the dashboard.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** A valid active integration shows credit totals. A missing, inactive, or unavailable integration does not render the card. Unauthenticated access to `/api/openrouter/credits` returns `401`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** No OpenRouter credit endpoint or dashboard balance card exists.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None yet; the PR CI will provide the canonical cross-platform result.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Visual evidence was manually verified on Windows; no screenshot is attached because it contains account billing information.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0

cargo check -p zeroclaw-gateway
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway openrouter_credits --lib
test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed

cargo test -p zeroclaw-config openrouter_management_key_encrypts_and_decrypts --lib
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed

cargo web check
# exit 0

npm run build
# production dashboard bundle generated successfully

cargo build --release --bin zeroclaw
Finished `release` profile [optimized] target(s)
```

The repository pre-push gate began `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D clippy::correctness`, but it was intentionally interrupted while compiling the full workspace after the focused checks above had passed. PR CI is expected to run the complete canonical gate.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Installed the release binary and static dashboard on Windows, imported a valid OpenRouter management credential through ZeroClaw's config encryption path, and verified: the Windows service remained automatic/running; `/health` returned `200`; the dashboard returned `200`; unauthenticated `/api/openrouter/credits` returned `401`; and the authenticated dashboard displayed the actual OpenRouter credit balance. Also verified the upstream credits API returned `200` with the expected schema. Secret values and upstream response bodies were not logged or committed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface observation; screenshot omitted because the card contains private billing/account data.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Commit `0f965eee`; Windows web dashboard served by the ZeroClaw gateway at the local loopback endpoint.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Manual final dashboard observation: the OpenRouter balance card rendered with live totals only after authenticated pairing and valid management API connectivity.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Removing authentication produced `401`; inactive/missing/unavailable integration paths return no content and keep the card hidden.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full-workspace pre-push clippy was interrupted during its initial dependency compilation; focused Rust tests/checks, dashboard build, and release build completed, and canonical CI will cover the workspace gate.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **Yes**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The gateway makes a fixed-host HTTPS request to OpenRouter's credits API with a short timeout. The distinct management key uses the existing encrypted configuration path, is never returned to the browser, and upstream bodies are not logged. The endpoint is protected by the gateway bearer authentication and returns only normalized numeric totals.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Existing users need no action. To enable the optional card, add `management_api_key` to the relevant OpenRouter provider entry; omitting it preserves existing behavior.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk. Roll back with `git revert 0f965eee`.

prs.title: fix(providers): rotate live credentials after rate limits
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Rotate only credentials that the selected provider actually sends, and cool the exact credential that returned a retryable rate limit.
  - Resolve route, alias, fallback, and model-switch credentials from canonical live configuration so removal, replacement, and endpoint isolation remain authoritative.
  - Build a live daemon-backed Agent's provider from the same configuration generation the rest of that Agent is built from, so a reload landing during construction cannot leave an Agent whose endpoint, credential pool, and failover graph disagree with its model, route metadata, and policy state.
  - Preserve streaming safety: credentials may rotate only before the first stream item is exposed; visible partial output is never replayed across a credential, provider, or model.
  - Keep the established public `ReliableModelProvider::with_api_keys` and one-field `ProviderSwitchConfig` APIs source-compatible while retaining the live-config handle privately on `Agent`.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not add credential storage, new provider permissions, a new configuration field, or replay after exposed streaming output. It does not attempt a live multi-key third-party smoke test. It does not change the documented live seam where a rotated credential attempt is rebuilt from the canonical configuration at dispatch time.
- **Blast radius:** Reliable provider retry/fallback dispatch, provider auth-mode selection, route validation, live model switching, and daemon-backed agent construction.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #9190.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `docs`, `agent`, `config`, `provider`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `provider:reliable`, `provider:openai`, `provider:anthropic`, `provider:router`, `domain:security`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `do-not-merge`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Canonical live config"] --> B["Typed provider factory"]
    B --> C["Eligible credential attempts"]
    C --> D["Reliable provider entry"]
    D --> E["Exact credential cooldown"]
    A --> F["Model-switch target snapshot"]
    F --> B
    A --> G["Agent construction generation"]
    G --> B
```

The live config is the source of truth. Credential digests identify cooldown ownership without logging or storing raw keys in a second policy table; provider reconstruction remains in the typed factory so auth mode, endpoint, TLS, and wrapper rules stay centralized. A caller that has already captured a configuration generation hands that generation to the factory instead of letting it take a second, later read.

Current head `b48d4937a555b8aeef2aacb72a5c982c10109a6b` is the previously reviewed head `62724a5c3fae0dea8548c6048e811253bcfc9472` plus one conflict-free merge of `master` (11 commits, up to `46479bdca7`) and two fixes for the 2026-09-09 review:

- **Live Agent construction generation.** `create_routed_model_provider_with_live_config_options` took a second read of the canonical handle after the asynchronous Agent setup had already run against a snapshot. It now reads once for callers that have not captured a generation and delegates to `create_routed_model_provider_for_live_generation`, which takes the caller's generation (`crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs:2298-2362`). `Agent::from_config_with_session_cwd_and_mcp_approval_mode` passes its construction snapshot to that entry point (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/agent.rs:1782-1816`). The canonical handle still travels with the provider for per-request credential resolution.
- **Bare Codex `api_url`.** A gateway supplied through the separate `api_url` parameter was neither used by the legacy Codex construction branch nor seen by the rotation-eligibility predicate, which reads the endpoint from the runtime options. `options_with_supplied_api_url` folds a supplied `api_url` into the effective options before both, leaving an alias-resolved endpoint untouched (`crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs:1388-1401`, `:1590-1609`, `:1611-1626`).

None of the 11 merged `master` commits touch any of this PR's eleven files, so no reviewed line moved in the merge.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; deterministic local HTTP fixtures and focused factory/runtime regressions exercise the security boundary without requiring real provider credentials.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The Test job runs the configured Codex gateway HTTP regression (a 429 on the primary bearer key followed by an alternate-key request to the same `/v1/responses` endpoint), the default-OAuth negative regressions, and both new configuration-generation regressions; the same tests run in the local suites below.
  - Hosted CI on this head (`b48d4937a555b8aeef2aacb72a5c982c10109a6b`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34555349111.
  - Historical, for the previous head `62724a5c3fae0dea8548c6048e811253bcfc9472`: the [required `CI Required Gate`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34181976836) passed. `gh pr checks 9419 --repo zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw --json name,state,link` on that head reported 35 successful checks, four skipped (Nix Module Eval, Nix Hash Drift, Relay Container Fresh-Volume Smoke, targeted Windows Clippy), and one failed non-required [`Advisory Windows nextest (scoped, plugin-host=true)`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34181976836/job/101922930805) job.

The earlier blank `--package` failure did not recur after the included #10675 scoping fix.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live multi-key provider account smoke. Local fixtures verify exact outbound authorization headers, endpoint isolation, and failover-graph provenance without real secrets. prs.title: feat(runtime): re-sample and flag replies claiming unreceipted actions
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `tool_receipts` can prove a *cited* tool result is genuine, but is silent on the opposite failure: the model narrates an action in prose, emits no tool call, and there is nothing to cite. The per-turn receipt collector is empty, which is proof the action never ran — and nothing reads it. This wires that signal up.
  - Adds an opt-in check in `run_tool_call_loop` where a final answer is produced. If the answer matches one of `claim_patterns` and the turn holds no qualifying receipt, the loop **re-samples the answer once**, then appends a warning if the claim survives.
  - Placed in the shared loop rather than at each reply seam, so one site covers channel agents, the gateway, ACP, and direct CLI turns. Nested SOP step loops and delegate sub-loops pass `claim_check: None`: their text becomes a tool result for the parent turn, whose own final answer is what gets checked.
  - `claim_patterns` ships **empty**, so enabling `verify_claims` alone changes nothing. The vocabulary that means "I did it" is agent-specific, and matching is unanchored substring, so a generic default (`"sent"` inside *present*, *absent*, *consent*) would flag ordinary prose.
  - Collapses the channel orchestrator's `show_receipts_in_response` bool — a hand-copied mirror of `tool_receipts.show_in_response` — into the `ToolReceiptsConfig` snapshot it came from, since the loop now borrows that config anyway. Net one field where there were two.

### Why the runtime, and why a re-sample

Measured on a self-hosted 27B tool-calling agent that writes structured records through an MCP server. One real failing turn was replayed 60 times with full fidelity (real system prompt, real 39-tool schema set, real 120-message history including genuine `tool_calls` and `tool` messages):

| condition | final answer asserted a write with no tool call |
|---|---|
| as deployed | **13 / 60 (22%)** |
| a second, unambiguous turn | 0 / 20 |

In every failing sample the chain of thought was correct and ended with explicit intent — "Let me log it." — and the model then emitted prose instead of the call. Four sampling configurations, two reasoning-effort settings, streamed and non-streamed, and three chat-template variants were measured; none reduced the rate and several raised it. That is what makes this a runtime concern rather than a prompt or provider one.

Failures are independent draws, so one re-sample takes 22% to roughly 5%. A re-sample also costs the operator nothing on a false positive: one extra generation, no human in the loop.

### Why the re-sample is safe

It is gated on two conditions that are safety properties, not tuning knobs:

- **No tool executed this turn** (empty collector) — there is no side effect to duplicate.
- **The text was not streamed live** — there is nothing already delivered to retract.

Conversation history is not yet updated at that point, so `continue` re-draws the same prompt rather than showing the model its own discarded answer. If either condition fails — a read tool ran, or the text was streamed — the loop skips the retry and appends the warning instead. One re-sample per turn.

The warning is appended to the delivered text only. The assistant message stored in history keeps the model's own words, so the next turn is not primed with a runtime notice it did not write.

- **Scope boundary:** Does not block, error, or retry more than once. Does not force tool use, and cannot: it re-rolls once and then tells the truth about the outcome. Does not touch receipt generation, HMAC verification, `show_in_response` rendering, the system-prompt addendum, or approval gates. Does not add persistence. No change to any existing default: `verify_claims` is `false` and `claim_patterns` is empty, so an untouched config produces byte-identical replies.
- **Blast radius:** `ToolLoop` gains one field, so every construction site is updated (mechanical; all nested/embedder sites pass `None`). The channel orchestrator's runtime context swaps one bool for the config struct it mirrored. With the feature off, the added cost per turn is one `Option::is_some` check on the final-answer path.
- **Linked issue(s):** None
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `agent`, `channel`, `config`, `runtime`, `skills`, `channel:core`, `tool:delegate`, `agent:prompt`, `domain:security`, `risk:medium`, `size:L`, `topic:agent-loop`, `needs-author-action`

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — the behavior is only observable with a model that actually exhibits the failure, but the re-sample itself is reproducible with any provider that returns a claiming answer with no tool call.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: cli` (direct `Agent::turn`) and `channel` (any messaging channel; the check is in the shared loop).
- **Setup / preconditions:**
  ```toml
  [agents.<alias>.tool_receipts]
  enabled = true
  verify_claims = true
  claim_patterns = ["logged", "recorded"]
  ```
- **Steps to run:** Send a turn that invites an action the agent can only perform with a tool, using a model prone to narrating instead of calling.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The runtime re-samples once. If the second answer still claims the action with no receipt, the reply arrives with `⚠️ Unverified: this reply claims an action, but no tool performed it.` appended, and a WARN `unverified_claim` record is emitted.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The fabricated confirmation is delivered verbatim with nothing to contradict it. `RUST_LOG=zeroclaw_runtime::agent=debug` shows no receipt for the claimed call, but nothing surfaces that to the user.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust build/lint/test jobs cover all three changed crates; `Docs Style` covers the changed Markdown.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None. The measured 22% failure rate comes from a local model and is evidence for *why* the feature exists, not a CI assertion; the re-sample logic itself is covered by deterministic tests.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```console
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo test --workspace --locked --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
81 suites, 13122 passed, 1 failed
# The single failure is environmental, not related to this change:
#   component::daemon_startup_feedback::daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions
#   panicked: "expect must be installed for the PTY regression test" (the `expect`
#   binary is absent on this host). `zeroclaw-desktop` was excluded because its
#   GTK/webkit build dependencies (webkit2gtk-4.1.pc) are absent on this host.

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib claim
test agent::claim_guard::tests::a_claim_is_recognised_case_insensitively ... ok
test agent::claim_guard::tests::a_read_only_receipt_does_not_satisfy_a_write_tool_list ... ok
test agent::claim_guard::tests::an_empty_pattern_list_disables_the_check ... ok
test agent::claim_guard::tests::blank_patterns_are_ignored_rather_than_matching_everything ... ok
test agent::agent::tests::unverified_claim_is_resampled_once ... ok
test agent::agent::tests::a_surviving_claim_ships_with_the_warning ... ok
test agent::agent::tests::verify_claims_off_leaves_the_reply_untouched ... ok
test agent::agent::tests::no_claim_patterns_means_no_check ... ok
test result: ok. 51 passed; 0 failed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That the check is reachable from the channel path and not only the direct-turn path — the first draft of this change lived at the `agent.rs` reply seam and would never have fired for a channel-served agent, which is why it moved into the shared loop. Also verified that the warning does not enter conversation history, and that with `verify_claims = false` the reply is byte-identical to `master`.
- **What I did NOT verify:** behavior under a live streaming channel where `response_streamed_live` is true — that path is designed to skip the re-sample and warn instead, and is covered by reasoning about the flag rather than an end-to-end streaming test.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none skipped. `zeroclaw-desktop` is excluded from the workspace test run because its GTK/webkit build dependencies are not present on this host; CI covers that target.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No** — a re-sample is an additional call to the already-configured provider on the same turn, bounded at one.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No** — the receipt key is untouched and still never reaches the model.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No** — the warning is appended to delivered text only and is never written into conversation history, so it cannot be echoed back to the model as instruction.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — `verify_claims` defaults to `false` and `claim_patterns` to empty; an unchanged config produces identical replies.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes** — three additive optional fields on `[agents.<alias>.tool_receipts]`: `verify_claims`, `claim_patterns`, `write_tools`. No upgrade steps; existing configs parse unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** set `verify_claims = false` (no restart-order constraints beyond the usual config reload), or `git revert <sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[agents.<alias>.tool_receipts] verify_claims`, plus `claim_patterns` as a second gate — emptying it disables the check without touching the flag.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** grep logs for `unverified_claim`. A `Retry` record is a re-sample; a `Note` record is a claim that survived one. A sudden run of `Note` records with no `Retry` records means the re-sample is being skipped, i.e. a read tool is running on claiming turns (name the write tools in `write_tools`) or replies are streaming live. Unexpected warnings on ordinary prose mean `claim_patterns` is too broad.

prs.title: feat(security): implement the accepted shell V1 permission policy (RFC #7155 Phase 0+1)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Implements the accepted Phase 0 + Phase 1 scope of RFC #7155 (the unified tool permission policy & tiered approval), delivered as five single-concern commits (the RFC's own PR slicing, kept as commits in this one PR):
  1. `fix(runtime): stop advertising self-approval in tool schemas` — removes the model-facing `approved` parameter from the shell/schedule/cron tool schemas (§5.1: an approval result never comes from model-supplied tool arguments).
  2. `feat(api): freeze the trusted confirmation contract types` — `zeroclaw-api::permission`: `ActionFingerprint` (domain-separated SHA-256 over canonical action facts), `TrustedConfirmation` (`#[non_exhaustive]`), the frozen §5.2 `ConsumeOutcome` terminal-state table, `TimeWindow`, `ApproverKind`, `RouteId`.
  3. `feat(config): add the three-tier tool policy rule engine` — `zeroclaw-config::tool_policy`: `Decision`/`PolicyRule`/`RuleMatcher`, the shell extractor reusing the exact `policy.rs` parsing primitives, `CompiledRuleSet` compiling every legacy field into rules, the strict `resolve_decision` precedence `Deny > Ask > Allow` with unmatched → `Ask` (per the approving Core ballot: a matching `Ask` prompts even when a more specific `Allow` also matches — no `Allow` source, explicit or session, downgrades a matched `Ask`, and only a legacy non-wildcard `allowed_commands` entry exempts from the High-risk block), the `tool_policy` config schema with load-time validation and shadowing warnings, and golden equivalence tests against the legacy validator.
  4. `feat(runtime): wire the rule table and confirmation ledger into the approval gate` — the gate resolves the actual shell command (Deny → no prompt, Allow → no prompt, Ask → prompt), an approval mints + consumes a fingerprint-bound single-use confirmation, "Always" grants become narrow session rules (exact executable + approved argument prefix), and the shell tool validates through the confirmed entry.
  5. `feat(runtime): intent display aid, confirmation audit, and semantic no-escalation` — optional untrusted `intent` shown beside the real command in the CLI prompt (new Fluent key in all five locales), audit entries record fingerprint/route/terminal-state, and `ensure_no_escalation_beyond` compares child/parent `tool_policy` rules on resolved semantics.
- **Scope boundary:** Shell V1 only, as ratified. No all-tool extractors, no regex (rejected at pattern-parse time with a Phase 3 pointer), no multi-scope merge, no sandbox-escape or automated approval. Desktop/node capabilities (`node_tool.rs`) keep their model-facing arg — explicitly Phase 2 (#6909). Independent delegate managers now attach the effective target policy and execution context. Configless test paths retain legacy tool-name gating.
- **Blast radius:** Every supervised shell approval flow (CLI prompt, channel inline approval), the cron/schedule/skill command validation surfaces, config schema (additive `tool_policy` section), and the audit log shape (additive serde-defaulted fields). Earlier branch validation reported api 214, config 1556, and runtime 4100 tests (one unrelated pre-existing flake in `process_stats` passed in isolation); these are historical counts, not current-head totals.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #7155 (the accepted RFC), Related #10339 (the implementation tracker — this completes its first close criterion and most of the rest for shell; not marked `Closes` because the tracker also covers resolver-authority unification of remaining tool-name surfaces and follow-ups). Supersedes #10539 (the first commit was that PR).

## Testing (required)

Current-head CI at `e6232ba6bc7f8962cf9abdddf24128f1c8c82a0a`: 40 successful checks, four skipped checks, and one advisory Windows failure. Required CI passes. The [advisory Windows job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/35456595493/job/105932958169) fails two untouched Arduino-upload tests (`failed_preflight_does_not_compile_or_upload` and `fake_cli_success_runs_all_stages_and_cleans_workspace`); these failures are separate from the changed shell-policy code. Local validation below is historical unless its revision is explicitly current.

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the approval UX deltas are easiest to feel live.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (interactive approval prompt), `channel` (inline approval on a connected channel).
- **Setup / preconditions:** A supervised agent profile (default), CLI session.
- **Steps to run:** (A) run an allowlisted low-risk command (`ls -la`) — before this PR every shell call prompted; now it runs without a prompt (Allow tier). (B) run a non-allowlisted command (`ffmpeg -version`) — before: hard "not allowed" reject; now: an approval prompt, and approving it executes once (the unmatched→Ask delta). (C) answer `always` to a `git push` approval, then issue `git push --force` — before: also pre-approved (tool-name Always); now: it prompts again (the narrow session rule covers only the approved argument prefix). (D) run a high-risk non-allowlisted command (`sudo rm /tmp/x`) — no prompt, straight denial that states no approval can change it.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** as described per step.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** as described per step.

### How I tested

Historical local validation at `22f95dfcbf`:

```sh

The ledger's terminal states are unit-tested row by row against the RFC §5.2 table. No-escalation pattern containment is table-tested (narrower child ok; wider child, dropped deny, extended window, unprovable glob → escalation). I did NOT verify against a live channel session end-to-end.
- **Visual interface changed?** `Yes` — the CLI approval prompt now prints an optional intent line (labeled "Stated intent (agent-claimed, untrusted)") beneath the real command. Evidence: the rendering code path in `prompt_cli_interactive` plus the `cli-approval-intent` Fluent key added to en/es/fr/ja/zh-CN. Terminal-width screenshots can be attached on request; the change is a single eprintln line using the existing prompt layout.

- **Screenshot evidence:** on request.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No` — this PR narrows them (see below).
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `Yes` — two changes, both defensive: (1) REMOVED the schema text that invited model self-approval; (2) ADDED the untrusted `intent` display aid, whose security contract is enforced structurally: it is clamped to 200 chars, never enters the fingerprint facts, never appears in any authorization comparison, and is rendered with an explicit untrusted label next to the real command. Risk note: a misleading intent cannot authorize anything — approvals bind the fingerprint.
- Behavior deltas (all RFC-sanctioned, each asserted in tests): unmatched shell commands now prompt instead of hard-rejecting; allowlisted low-risk commands stop prompting; `auto_approve`/Full autonomy no longer bypass command-level Ask tiers (RFC §1.3 acceptance criterion — configs relying on `auto_approve = ["shell"]` to run risk-tier commands unattended must move to explicit `tool_policy` rules or relax the risk flags); the skill tool no longer self-approves its substituted commands (risk-tier skill commands now fail closed — approving the skill invocation never approved the model-supplied arguments); approval messages say "operator approval" instead of the self-approval-teaching "(approved=true)".

- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

prs.title: feat(zerocode): show message times in the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The ZeroCode transcript never showed when anything happened. When an automated prompt, a refused queued message and a long tool call overlap in one session, there was no way to tell the order or the durations from the screen. A time on every message proved to be too much (an earlier revision of this PR did that). The transcript now shows time context in two places only:
    - a dim, centered divider (`── Today 01:00 ──`, `── Yesterday 22:20 ──`, or a date) before a prompt that starts the transcript, comes 15 minutes or more after the previous activity, or starts a new day. A quick back-and-forth gets no dividers.
    - a dim footer (`─── 01:00 → 01:31 · 31m 40s`) under a turn that ran for a minute or more. Short turns get none.
  - `session/messages` entries gain an optional `created_at` (RFC 3339) wherever the store has one: ACP full loads, ACP cursor pages, and the Chat backend via `load_with_timestamps`. It is skipped when absent and `#[serde(default)]` on the client, so either side can be older.
  - **Store fix underneath.** Checkpointed ACP turns write all their visible rows at finalization with one timestamp, so a turn's prompt read as the time the turn **ended**. A divider or footer built on that would be wrong by the whole length of the turn. The checkpoint row now records `started_at` (a nullable column, added on upgrade), and finalization and crash recovery stamp the turn's prompt row with it. The other rows of the turn keep the finalization time, which is the turn's end: exactly what the footer needs.
  - Live turns: entries are stamped on receipt, and the footer is placed when the turn settles. A later terminal frame for the same turn does not move it. A history load taken mid-turn hands the footer to the live settle.
  - A reloaded turn that ends in a recovery marker gets no footer, because recovery stamps its rows when it runs, which can be hours after the turn stopped.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Individual tool calls and replies in ACP history still share the turn's finish time. Giving each its own time would need a time on every checkpoint journal event; it isn't needed for dividers and footers.
  - No toggle. The only existing display toggle is thoughts; a timestamp toggle would need a new action, keybinding and help text.
  - The Chat-backend path (gateway SQLite) is affected by #11420, which rewrites every row's `created_at` on each turn. This PR passes through what that store holds.
- **Blast radius:** the ACP store's write path for checkpointed turns (only the prompt row's `created_at`) and one additive column on `acp_turn_checkpoints`; the `session/messages` wire shape (additive, optional); ZeroCode transcript layout (divider and footer rows drawn outside each entry's line range, with the tail re-render accounting for them).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11620. Related #11420.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode now shows a small grey date-and-time line when you come back to a conversation after a break or on a new day, and a small grey line under any turn that took more than a minute, saying when it started, when it finished and how long it took. Quick exchanges look exactly as before. Under the hood, the daemon's database used to record every message of a turn as happening when the turn finished; this PR records when the prompt was sent, so those lines are right after a reload too.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode over the daemon socket)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a daemon and ZeroCode built from this branch; any agent.
- **Steps to run:** send a prompt that runs a tool and takes over a minute. Then send a quick follow-up. Wait 15 minutes (or reload a session from yesterday) and send another. Switch away from the session and back to force a `session/messages` reload.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** a `── Today HH:MM ──` divider above the first prompt; a `─── start → end · duration` footer under the long turn; nothing around the quick follow-up; a new divider after the gap. The same marks after the reload. A session from an older daemon shows no marks rather than wrong ones.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no times anywhere.

### How I tested

All builds and tests ran through `scripts/zc-cargo` on the remote build host.

- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the touched files: clean.
- `zc-cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `zc-cargo test -p zerocode`: `test result: FAILED. 1433 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, fails the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --lib`: `test result: ok. 314 passed; 0 failed`.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`: `5627 passed; 4 failed` at the earlier head. The 4 (`relay::local_dial_tests` x2, `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, `peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`) fail the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host. The runtime diff is unchanged since.

Each new test fails with its fix reverted and passes with it restored:

- Store: `finalized_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time_and_reply_keeps_finalization_time`, `recovered_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time` (fail when the prompt keeps the finalization time); `turn_checkpoint_start_column_is_added_to_an_existing_database` (fails without the migration).
- RPC: `conversation_message_entries_carry_each_source_message_time` (fails when the projection drops times).
- Rules (`chat::entry_time`): `dividers_mark_the_first_prompt_gaps_and_day_changes_only` (fails when every prompt divides), `a_day_change_divides_even_after_a_short_gap` (fails without the day check), `footers_follow_finished_turns_of_a_minute_or_more` (fails without the one-minute floor), plus label and parsing tests.
- Transcript: `transcript_shows_gap_dividers_and_long_turn_footers_not_message_times` and `a_live_turn_gets_its_footer_when_it_settles` (fail when the layout drops the footer row, when a settle doesn't invalidate the tail, or when a later frame may move the end); `a_history_load_taken_mid_turn_hands_the_footer_to_the_live_settle` (fails when a moved footer doesn't force a full rebuild); `a_footer_on_a_divided_entry_keeps_one_divider` (fails when the tail re-render ignores the divider row); `a_recovered_turn_gets_no_footer_from_its_recovery_time`.

`rpc::dispatch::tests::cursor_pages_equal_legacy_projection_for_valid_tool_groups` was updated: cursor pages now carry times, so its full-load reference uses the timed projection.

- **CI checks relied on:** the Rust lanes for the three crates.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** no end-to-end daemon+TUI run in CI for this.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The divider and footer rows were checked in a live ZeroCode pane against a scratch daemon (seeded history plus a live turn), by reading the terminal's text.
- **Visual interface evidence:** I'm verifying this in the experiment build.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Times are display-only and never reach the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The new wire field is optional both ways. The new column is nullable and added on open; an older binary ignores it (its inserts name their columns). A checkpoint begun by an older binary has no start time, and its prompt keeps the finalization time as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the PR's commits. The added `acp_turn_checkpoints.started_at` column is harmless to the reverted code and needs no down-migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** no dividers or footers (old daemon or missing `created_at`), or a footer whose start is later than expected (start time not recorded).

prs.title: fix(zerocode): render live session updates promptly under load
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The app event loop drained the notification broadcast only once per frame and otherwise blocked in `event::poll` for up to the 200 ms idle `TICK`, so streamed `session/update`s rendered late. The input wait is now split into 16 ms slices (`poll_input_or_transport`). It returns early when either chat pane reports pending transport events (`has_pending_transport_events`: notification broadcast, prompt completions, resync and reattach results). Input is always polled for one slice first, so redraws stay at about 60 fps or less while streaming.
  - Every `ToolResult` called `mark_dirty_full()`, which re-renders up to 1000 entries (markdown parse and wrap) per result. With large transcripts and tool-heavy turns, those slow frames are what let the broadcast overflow. A result on the tail entry now uses `mark_dirty_tail`. `rebuild_lines` already falls back to a full rebuild when the mutated entry is not the cached tail (parallel tool calls), so the cache never goes stale.
  - `NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_CAPACITY` goes from 1024 to 4096 as headroom for draw stalls (resize storms, full rebuilds, descheduling).
  - Why it matters: after #10801, a `Lagged` broadcast no longer cancels turns. It still reloads every tracked session's durable transcript with the live stream gated, and with large transcripts that shows up as multi-second stalls in live updates whenever several sessions or tool calls are active. This PR makes that lag much rarer.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change the `Lagged` recovery path (`begin_notification_resync` / `Reattach` from #10801), the daemon, or the wire protocol. Does not move broadcast draining onto a dedicated task. #10785 also suggests that, but it needs the synchronous `push_notification_for_test` → `drain_notifications` tests reworked, so it is left for a follow-up.
- **Blast radius:** zerocode TUI only. Affects the app event loop's input wait (redraw cadence for every pane), chat/ACP transcript caching for tool results, and the per-connection notification buffer size, which also backs the Logs pane subscriber.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10785 (follow-up to #10801; addresses its "drain more promptly / raise the capacity" item but not the off-draw-loop drain).
- **Labels:** (path and size labelers to apply; maintainer to set `risk:*`)

### What this does, simply

When several agent sessions are streaming in zerocode, or a turn makes many tool calls, the screen can stop updating for seconds and then jump ahead. Three things caused this. Zerocode only checked for new updates about five times a second. Each tool result made it re-render the whole visible transcript. If too many updates piled up between checks, the buffer overflowed and zerocode reloaded every session from scratch, showing nothing new until the reload finished. With this change, zerocode wakes up as soon as updates arrive (at most about 60 redraws a second), re-renders only the tool card that changed, and has a four-times-larger buffer. Overflows are much rarer, so live output keeps flowing. If an overflow still happens, the recovery behaves exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `tui` (zerocode Code/Chat panes, agent sidebar)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A daemon with an agent on a chatty model that runs tool loops. Open 3 or more Code (ACP) sessions in one zerocode instance.
- **Steps to run:** Start a long tool-heavy turn in each session. Watch the focused transcript and the sidebar status dots. Optionally stress the draw loop by resizing the terminal repeatedly, or by `kill -STOP <zerocode pid>` for about 1 s then `kill -CONT`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Streamed text and tool cards appear smoothly with no visible 200 ms batching. The "Live updates were missed, so the durable transcript was reloaded" notice is rare and only shows up after long stalls.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Output arrives in visible 200 ms batches. With several busy sessions, the reload notice appears repeatedly and the live stream freezes for each reload.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required Rust lint and test jobs cover `apps/zerocode` (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test` for the zerocode bin target, where the chat and app tests live). Pending on this head; not yet used as evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not exercise a live daemon with concurrent streaming sessions, so the latency improvement is not proven end-to-end by CI (see the manual verification note below).
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode
# test result: ok. 1396 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 5.75s

cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- tool_result_rerenders input_wait_returns_early notifications_route_to_background
# test chat::tests::notifications_route_to_background_sessions ... ok
# test chat::tests::tool_result_rerenders_only_the_tail_card_and_matches_full_rebuild ... ok
# test app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events ... ok
# test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1395 filtered out

cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 45.68s   (no warnings)

cargo fmt -p zerocode -- --check
# (clean)
```

  New and extended tests:
  - `input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events`: pending transport ends the wait after exactly one slice; input wins in the same slice; when idle, the wait slices up to the full timeout and never polls past a slice.
  - `tool_result_rerenders_only_the_tail_card_and_matches_full_rebuild`: a tail `ToolResult` sets `TailChanged`, and the incremental output equals a forced full rebuild; a non-tail result (parallel calls) also equals a full rebuild.
  - `notifications_route_to_background_sessions`: now also asserts `has_pending_transport_events()` is true with a queued notification and false after draining.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Code-path review: `has_pending_transport_events` uses only non-consuming `is_empty()` checks; every pane `tick()` reached by the extra early-wake iterations (dashboard, logs, quickstart, SOP, chrome status) is already rate-limited, so faster wakes do not add RPC traffic. **Not verified:** a live multi-session run against a daemon. The reviewer A/B steps above are the intended end-to-end check.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No layout, styling, or wrapping change: transcript output is unchanged (the tail re-render produces lines identical to a full rebuild), and only redraw timing changes. The equality assertion is helper-level, not final-interface evidence.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `265465ddc`, zerocode bin unit tests, Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.1.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A (see above)
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See the test descriptions above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full-workspace `cargo test` and `clippy` were not run locally: the change is confined to `apps/zerocode` and the required CI covers the workspace.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 265465ddc` (single commit, zerocode only)
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Higher zerocode CPU while sessions stream (expected up to about 60 redraws/s; sustained CPU when idle would be a regression). A tool card not showing its result until the next full redraw would indicate the tail-path fallback misbehaving. The "Live updates were missed…" notice (`zc-chat-resync-*`) appearing as often as before would mean the lag is not reduced.
