prs.title: fix(runtime): cancel a turn's parallel and agentic delegate children with the turn
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Aborting a turn did not reach the delegate children it had started. `DelegateTool` derived every child token from its own private `CancellationToken`, which nothing outside tests ever cancels (`with_cancellation_token` and `cancel_all_background_tasks` have no production caller). Parallel fan-out and nested agentic runs are spawned tasks, so when the turn was cancelled and its tool future dropped, the `JoinHandle`s were dropped and the children kept running as full agent loops with their own trace ids. In production that looked like `POST /api/sessions/{id}/abort` answering `no_active_response` while three delegate children went on emitting `llm_request`.
  - The tool loop now scopes the running turn's token as a task-local around each tool's `execute` (`tool_execution::scope_turn_cancellation`, read through `current_turn_cancellation`). `DelegateTool::turn_bound_child_token` hangs parallel children and the agentic child loop off that token, so an abort of the turn cancels what the turn started. A delegate instance built inside a spawned task is handed the turn lineage separately, as `turn_token`, for its foreground children (a parallel worker's own tool runs with no turn scope, so this is how the turn reaches what it delegates; the bounded child's own tool is dispatched inside its sub-loop's scope and keeps it as a fallback); its own `cancellation_token`, which its background tasks derive from, stays a child of the parent tool's token exactly as on `master`, so stopping the turn never stops work launched to outlive it, at any depth.
  - Background tasks (`background: true`) keep the tool's own token on purpose, at every depth: they outlive the turn by design and are cancelled through `cancel_task`. A parallel child that makes a plain model call without a tool loop is not interrupted mid-call and ends with that call's own timeout (pre-existing, left for follow-up work). Documented in a `delegate` cancellation section of `delegation.md` and in the persistence table.
- **Scope boundary:** no change to the abort route, to which turns register a cancel token (WS and webhook SSE only), to `spawn_subagent` (already cancelled by its parent future), to `agentic_timeout_secs`, or to background-task lifecycle.
- **Blast radius:** any turn that fans out through `delegate` now stops its in-turn children when the turn is cancelled from any surface that carries a token (gateway abort, channel interruption, RPC cancel). Children that were previously orphaned and ran to completion will now end as cancelled.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #7759 (the abort path is named there as the one way to cancel a turn), Related #10531.

### What this does, simply

When you stop a turn, the sub-agents that turn launched now stop too. Before, only the parent stopped; children started in parallel or as nested agent loops carried on unseen, still calling the model, with no handle left to stop them.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; cheap A/B on the gateway.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web` surface (`POST /api/sessions/{id}/abort`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** two agents where the caller may delegate; a prompt that makes the caller fan out (`delegate` with `parallel: [...]`) to a slow task.
- **Steps to run:** send the prompt over the chat WebSocket, wait for the children's `llm_request` events, then call the abort route.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the children's loops end (`ToolLoopCancelled` in the log; no further `llm_request` under their trace ids).
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the parent ends; the children keep running to completion.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust lint/test jobs cover `zeroclaw-runtime`; Docs Style covers the two Markdown lines.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none identified.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `9cf33971cf`; the same gates pass on the merge result with current `master`, `35dad4a6f3`)

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                 # exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings          # exit 0
bash scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh                              # 3 runs, 16 threads
#   zeroclaw-runtime:  test result: ok. 5444 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored   (x3)
#   zeroclaw-channels: test result: ok. 1967 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored  (x3)
#   (new: tools_see_the_running_turn_token_only_while_the_turn_runs_with_one,
#         in_turn_child_tokens_follow_the_running_turn,
#         handed_turn_lineage_binds_foreground_children_without_touching_background_lineage,
#         cancelling_the_root_turn_stops_the_foreground_child_and_spares_its_background_grandchild,
#         cancelling_the_root_turn_stops_every_parallel_worker)
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-runtime          # exit 0
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                    # Comment hygiene gate passed.
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh                                      # no prose em-dashes (docs_links_gate needs lychee, not installed locally)
```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Provenance of the token: `execute_one_tool` receives the turn token → scoped around `tool.execute` → read at the in-turn derivation sites in `delegate.rs`; the background site is unchanged, and the two instance construction sites inside spawned tasks (bounded child, parallel worker) keep `cancellation_token` on the parent tool's lineage and take the turn lineage as `turn_token`. `tools_see_the_running_turn_token_only_while_the_turn_runs_with_one` proves the scope through the real dispatch boundary and that it does not leak past it; `in_turn_child_tokens_follow_the_running_turn` proves the derivation in both situations; `cancelling_the_root_turn_stops_the_foreground_child_and_spares_its_background_grandchild` starts a foreground child and its background grandchild, cancels the root turn, and observes the former stop and the latter complete; `cancelling_the_root_turn_stops_every_parallel_worker` fans out to two agentic workers held in their first model call, cancels the turn, and observes that neither makes a second request. Not verified: a live multi-agent abort against a real provider.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (behavioural: cancelled turns now cancel their in-turn children)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <sha>`; no persisted-data change.

prs.title: feat(release): ship the WASM plugin host in supported release artifacts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `test/10994-plugin-artifact-smoke` (stacked on #11311; retarget to `master` once it merges)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Root `Cargo.toml`: `plugins-wasm-cranelift` joins `dist_extra_features`, so the standard distribution artifacts carry the WASM plugin host with the compiler that loads `.wasm` components, the only form the plugin registry publishes. `dist_target_exclusions` removes it for `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` and `arm-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` (Cranelift has no native ARM32 backend, and no native ARM32 runner can prove wasmtime's Pulley fallback) and for `aarch64-linux-android` (experimental, not a required asset). The Pulley feature comment now describes what the feature does.
  - Generated surfaces regenerated with `cargo generate installers` (source container builds, AUR package, Nix flake, `setup.bat`, container tag registry); the base-image digest refresh the generator also performs is left out on purpose.
  - `release-stable-manual.yml`: `plugin-smoke-packages` builds the fixture plugin packages once on Linux; `plugin-smoke` downloads each of the seven 64-bit desktop and server archives on a runner of its own platform and runs `scripts/ci/plugin_artifact_smoke.sh` against the packaged binary; the legs set up no toolchain and compile nothing. `publish` and `docker` need it. Both jobs run with `permissions: contents: read` and a checkout that persists no credentials. `BINARY_SIZE_HARD_LIMIT` rises from 64 MiB to 80 MiB.
  - `cross-platform-build-manual.yml`: the same two jobs against the binaries it builds, so one dispatch both measures sizes and proves plugin execution for a distribution change.
  - Tests and docs: an xtask test ties "this target carries a plugin backend" to "the release has a smoke leg for it" in both directions; the architecture suite pins the wiring (needs, artifact names, least privilege, the whole smoke invocation, no `continue-on-error`, no condition on the smoke step); generator tests match feature names as whole tokens; the dist parity test reads the build job's matrix. Every page that said prebuilt binaries lack the host now says which artifacts carry it, which do not, and where the proof is recorded; the protocol page gains a per-artifact table and the limits that hold for all of them; the operator page gains the release-binary walkthrough and rollback; the Nix module and README explain `MemoryDenyWriteExecute` against plugin loads.
- **Scope boundary:** Cargo `default`, every runtime default (`plugins.enabled`, `plugins.auto_discover`, `signature_mode`), the plugin host, the WIT contract, the CLI code, and the desktop bundles are unchanged. Existing external actions remain pinned; the Stable build step now uses the local shared release recipe. No release asset is added, renamed, or removed. The `v*` tag trigger of docker-publish.yml is unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** the seven 64-bit desktop and server CLI archives; the GHCR `latest`, versioned and `debian` images, repackaged from two of them; source builds from the generated distribution list (the GHCR `dist` variant, the AUR package, the Nix flake package, `setup.bat`); the stable release and manual cross-platform workflows; the plugin documentation; consumers of `/api/plugins`, the dashboard Plugins page, and `zeroclaw status` output, which change what they report; the cron database, where any plugin-host binary that opens or creates it adds an empty `plugin_outbox` table; and, with `skills.install_suggestions.enabled = true` (default off) and a registry index cached by `plugin search` or `plugin install <name>`, a release binary now answers a matching turn with a `zeroclaw plugin install` suggestion instead of calling the model, whatever `plugins.enabled` says. Not affected: the ARM32 and Android archives, the desktop bundles, `cargo install`, and `install.sh` source builds.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10994; the issue closes after the v0.8.6 run posts downloaded-artifact evidence on #10994, #7432 and #10999. Depends on #11311 and #11310.
- **Labels:** `ci`, `dependencies`, `dev`, `docs`, `tests` (path labeler). The size and risk labelers run only for PRs based on `master`, so `size:*` arrives at the retarget and `risk:high` needs a maintainer.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can load WebAssembly plugins, but until now the prebuilt release binaries were built without that plugin host: `zeroclaw plugin ...` was not even a command, and outside the amd64 `all-features` container image a plugin needed a source build. This PR puts the plugin host, with the compiler that loads ordinary `.wasm` plugins, into the release binaries for the seven 64-bit desktop and server targets. For an operator who does not use plugins, what is off stays off: the plugin system is disabled by default, a plugin is instantiated only by the operator's own `plugin install`, `plugin info` or `plugin list --verify` commands, and it is offered to the model only after the operator enables the plugin system and turns discovery on. What such an operator does see change on a release binary: `zeroclaw plugin` exists as a command, `zeroclaw status` lists a `Plugin` channel row, `/api/plugins` reports `wasm_plugins_available: true`, and the dashboard's Plugins page says the plugin system is disabled instead of unavailable in this build.

What was missing was proof. A binary can carry the host and still fail to run a plugin, so the release now checks itself: one job builds a small test plugin, and one job per archive downloads the archive that is about to be published, installs the plugin through the normal commands, and makes an agent call it. On a dispatched release, the GitHub Release and the container images are created only if every one of those checks passes. The manual cross-platform build runs the same checks, so a change to what ships can be rehearsed before a release.

Limits: the two 32-bit ARM archives and the experimental Android archive still have no plugin host. The binary size cap grows because the host adds about 4.7 MiB. Plugins are experimental: a plugin must be built against the WIT contract shipped with the release that runs it.

Decisions taken here and flagged for maintainers (from the plan on #10994):

| # | Decision | What this PR does | Needs sign-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Size cap | 64 MiB to 80 MiB. The v0.8.5 x86_64 Linux binary was 61,537,880 B against 67,108,864; the host adds 4,909,008 B measured on aarch64-apple-darwin with this machine's stable toolchain, rustc 1.97.1 (36,802,864 to 41,711,872 at master 4f93bf5399). | Yes. An estimate until a Cross-Platform Build dispatch on this branch reports the x86_64 Linux sizes. |
| D2 | Backend per target | Cranelift on the seven 64-bit desktop and server targets; none on ARM32 and Android. | Yes |
| D3 | Package formats | `.wasm` only; no artifact ships a deserialize-only backend. | Follows from D2 |
| D4 | Smoke plugin | The in-tree `tool-fixture` packages (eight variants) for the blocking gate. `redact-text@0.3.0` from the registry was verified by hand on a release-profile build while planning. | No |
| D5 | Gate strength | `publish` and `docker` both need `plugin-smoke`; the images repackage two smoke-gated archives. | Yes, for `docker` |
| D6 | Nix hardening | `MemoryDenyWriteExecute` stays on; comments and README say plugin loads fail under it and how an instance overrides it on its own unit. | No |
| D7 | Authority | FND-001 section 4.4.2 plus `status:accepted` on #10994 cover artifact-only inclusion with defaults unchanged. FND-001 says every binary carries the plugin host; after this PR the ARM32 and Android archives do not, and the desktop bundle sidecars never did. Both are recorded gaps, not edits to the protected document. | Yes |

### Current bounded GNU ARM64 diagnostic follow-through

Signed `5dc49764031c73b25492946930357d87d692ef92`, tree `022cee7cfa5d592907d5aec81d9c172c57d6c916`, is a normal successor of `75993ac`. The original topic, draft and #11311 base remain. Root and independent source review accepted the corrected two-file diagnostic slice; the first source review's header, upload-order mutation and buffered-read defects were corrected before publication.

Two ARM64-only steps capture and upload whitelisted initial runner metadata before Build release: at most 16 KiB JSON, unbuffered reads of at most 4,096 bytes, bounded fixed metadata commands, source/run/attempt/target/input binding, private owned files and an exact pinned upload with one-day retention. These consume the existing GNU job budget. Removing the two steps restores the prior workflow; build recipes, Ubuntu 22 producer ABI, resources, parallelism, features, profiles, cache policy, 80 MiB cap, permissions and gates are unchanged.

[Current Quality Gate 38501736562](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38501736562) is still qualifying this head. [Format](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38501736562/job/115650030944) failed with eight official Rustfmt layout hunks in the new test tuples/macros. A formatting-only follow-up is being prepared; no local formatter, diagnostic or Rust test was run. The four new controls and their internal 20 wiring, 14 Python and one CLI mutant obligations remain uncredited until their actual named results are qualified.

No new GNU trial has been selected or executed on this diagnostic head. Earlier shutdown/communication-loss results and partial archives remain on their own sources/attempts. Initial metadata would establish neither effective limits, peak/failure-time usage, process exit nor cause; no repair is claimed. Current Full Quality Gate, real GNU archives, two native suites, completeness, Stable/full-platform and human/Core/release acceptance remain separate requirements.

### Prior public integration and finite Stable qualification

Prior signed `75993ac6bdd13bf2f79ac63654903810662d4d41`, tree `cabbaa5df320bc806b98b5731bdb7e5642ca16d0`, continues the original topic, draft and #11311 base. Its parent is `6fcbbc7`. The normal public-parent integration carries exact #11311 `6b05d5c`, including the genuine dependency lock: 1,293 dependencies, Quinn-proto0.11.19, probe-rs0.32, no ruzstd/espflash.

Stable's `Build release` step calls the shared local action with the original target/linker/cross bindings and no FEATURES emission. The exact old 2,360-byte Bash recipe, all ten target rows, compiler/setup/cache, release/locked flags, features, inclusive83,886,080-byte cap, 90-minute ceiling and packaging/publish dependencies are preserved. Normal manual distribution/tool-only routes keep their behavior, including their existing Mac180 and ARM resource envelopes. The qualifier omits a workflow/job incremental declaration; the pinned cache exports effective `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, which receipts capture and require. Python3.8-compatible prefix slicing is retained.

[Prior-head Quality Gate38462337922](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38462337922) is SUCCESS:42 successful jobs, three conditional skips; Required Gate115526471859 passed all35 needs. Security, Format, Lint, Docs, generator-sync, declared-floor and selected compiler lanes passed. Workspace19530 tests passed with39 selected skips. All24spec and17requested architecture methods have individual current PASS rows, plus one actual Unix Scoop method. The complete wiring method now exercises its caught structural mutants, empty-FEATURES refusal/removed-guard boundary and later15 producer-admission cases; inventory refusal/type/hash controls pass. Internal fixture/mutation assertions are source-derived execution scope under named methods, not individually printed test rows. Synthetic archive carriers are not release-binary or ABI proof. Actual CI/public trees match exactly; no predecessor test execution is substituted.

The observed formatter, whole-job matrix-selection and incomplete clean-fixture failures were repaired without changing workflow logic or weakening assertions. The target reader now selects the actual matrix, with non-target/valid-duplicate caller-contamination controls. The test-only source/run/attempt seeds reach the existing controlled status91 boundary; refusal status1 and markers remain. Current ordinary execution qualifies those receiving corrections. The older `8b04361` archive/native results remain historical and provide no current artifact credit.

Two finite nonpublishing GNU Ubuntu22 runs on this exact head have now failed: [38465773281](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38465773281), then one separately reviewed fresh full run [38476464670](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38476464670), both attempt 1. Each selected `distribution=dist`, `qualification_profile=stable-gnu-ubuntu22`, `release_tools_only=false`. The ARM64 build received an official runner shutdown signal and exited 143 after 31m9.573s and 27m13.845s, respectively, below the unchanged 90-minute ceiling. Neither log emits a compiler, SIGKILL or linker error. The underlying shutdown cause remains unknown; a diagnostic follow-up is being prepared, with no third unchanged dispatch or repair claim.

Fresh run 38476464670 attempt 1 finished with seven successful jobs, two failures and five skips. The three other GNU builds and their real archives passed: nine input/ABI pairs, 216 payload hashes and seven official ZIP digests were verified. All six reached caches reported MISS. These are partial build/package results. Both native suites were NOTRUN, and the completeness guard correctly rejected `BUILD=failure` and `NATIVE=skipped`; no provider/artifact runtime control is credited.

The separately reviewed full [debug run 38476464670 attempt 2](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38476464670/attempts/2) is terminal FAILURE: seven successful jobs, two failures and five skips. It reran all producers on this frozen head and original inputs. Three new archives and nine input/ABI pairs are verified; both native suites were NOTRUN and completeness correctly refused with exit 2. Eight Runner/Worker diagnostic pairs were delivered for other jobs. The failing ARM64 job is annotated as hosted-runner communication loss, but its raw job log returns 404 and no ARM64 Runner/Worker carrier was delivered. Its process exit, build duration and underlying cause remain unknown; this is not classified as another exit-143 shutdown, compiler error or OOM. No source, repository-setting, recipe, budget, resource, feature, cache-policy, cap or gate changed. A bounded source-only next disposition is being prepared; no further retry or repair is selected.

The normal profile remains the default. The finite selection still requires both release-tool legs, canonical web/fixture producers, four Stable GNU Ubuntu22 rows, two archive-only native consumers and always-selected completeness. It retains the 90-minute build/30-minute native ceilings, inclusive 83,886,080-byte main cap, canonical FEATURES resolution, pinned restore-only cache roles and all gates. No raw-binary fallback or resource/profile/feature/cap/gate change has been made.

Complete qualification requires every selected role to succeed, twelve input/ABI observations, four real archives and both full 13-provider/18-artifact native suites, with exact source/tree/run/attempt/profile/web/fixture/binary/manifest/archive bindings. That requirement remains unmet. Carrier hashes alone are not runtime proof, and Ubuntu24 execution does not prove Ubuntu22 runtime. ARM32 and companion runtime, remaining Stable platforms/90-minute builds, human/Core, #11715→#11310→#11311 acceptance/landing and full release acceptance remain separate.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional: an A/B run of the smoke against a release-profile build takes about twenty minutes of compile time on a laptop plus a minute for the checks.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Rust 1.98.0 with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, Python 3.8 or newer, bash. Nothing under `~/.zeroclaw` is used; the smoke runs in a throwaway configuration directory.
- **Steps to run:**
  ```sh
  FEATURES="$(cargo run -q -p xtask --bin generate -- features --selection dist --target "$(rustc -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')")"
  echo "$FEATURES"
  cargo build --release --locked --no-default-features --features "$FEATURES" --bin zeroclaw
  bash scripts/ci/build_plugin_smoke_packages.sh /tmp/plugin-smoke-packages
  bash scripts/ci/plugin_artifact_smoke.sh --binary target/release/zeroclaw --expect host --packages /tmp/plugin-smoke-packages
  ```
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `$FEATURES` contains `plugins-wasm-cranelift`; the smoke prints eighteen `PASS` rows and a report headed `... passed`, exit 0.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** on the base branch `test/10994-plugin-artifact-smoke` (which carries the two scripts; `master` has neither) `$FEATURES` has no plugin feature, and every smoke check fails, starting with the first, because the binary has no `plugin` command; exit 1.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Current `5dc4976` is being qualified by Quality Gate 38501736562; Format reports eight official layout hunks in the new architecture tests, and the remaining job results must be read from this run. The earlier 759 Quality Gate is prior-head evidence only. Real package/runtime qualification remains the separately reported nonpublishing GNU workflow; its partial results and failed completeness do not qualify the full release. Contributor-local commands below are historical reports, not current-head execution credit.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the seven release legs, the musl archives built through `cross` with wasmtime, and the Windows leg run only in Release Stable or the manual Cross-Platform Build; a dispatch of the manual workflow on this branch is the planned proof before this PR leaves draft.
- **Commands run and tail output:** aarch64-apple-darwin, this machine's stable toolchain (rustc 1.97.1; the release workflow pins 1.98.0, so the Cross-Platform Build dispatch is the size measurement that counts for D1), head of this branch:
  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                  (clean)
  $ cargo clippy -p xtask -p zeroclaw-dist --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings   (clean)
  $ cargo clippy --test architecture --no-deps -- -D warnings                      (clean)
  $ cargo nextest run -p xtask
       Summary [   0.890s] 241 tests run: 241 passed, 0 skipped
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-dist
  test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo test --test architecture
  test result: ok. 56 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo generate installers --check
  ok: ... in sync   (21 surfaces)
  $ cargo run -q -p xtask --bin generate -- features --selection dist --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
  acp-bridge,...,observability-prometheus,plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,whatsapp-web
  $ cargo run -q -p xtask --bin generate -- features --selection dist --target armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf
  (no plugins-wasm feature; the same for aarch64-linux-android)
  $ BASE_SHA=<merge-base> bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.
  $ BASE_SHA=<merge-base> bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  Errors...........0
  $ BASE_SHA=<merge-base> bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
  $ python3 scripts/ci/release_attestation_contract_test.py
  Ran 11 tests ... OK
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** (1) A release-profile build of the exact resolved dist list for aarch64-apple-darwin at this head (`cargo build --release --locked --no-default-features --features "$FEATURES" --bin zeroclaw`; 1096 s cold at an earlier head of this branch, 586 s on a warm dependency cache at this one) passes all 18 smoke checks: binary 41,995,504 bytes, tool call turn 579 ms, report in the collapsed section at the end of this body. The same list without the plugin host measured 36,802,864 bytes at master 4f93bf5399. (2) The `run:` bodies of both new smoke steps, extracted from the workflow YAML with the matrix target substituted, executed locally against that binary: the release step against an archive packaged like the build job's output (binary plus `web/dist`), the manual step against the raw binary with its executable bit cleared; both exit 0 with 18 PASS rows and write the evidence file and the step summary. (3) Mutation checks on the two new gate tests: dropping a smoke leg, excluding the backend for a target that keeps its leg, giving armv7 a backend, removing `plugin-smoke` from `publish` or `docker`, adding an `if:` to `docker`, adding a permission to a smoke job, and appending `|| true` to the smoke call each fail the intended test; the real files pass. Not verified: the Windows leg, the musl archives built through `cross`, the source container images building with Cranelift for linux/arm64 and Alpine, and plugin-load behavior under `MemoryDenyWriteExecute` on Linux.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output` for the `zeroclaw --help` command list, the `zeroclaw status` channel list, and the `/api/plugins` JSON, below. The dashboard Plugins page is a rendered interface whose change is not semantic-only (its build-limitation notice stops rendering and its status badge text changes), so it needs a browser screenshot of the page served by a release-profile binary. The page was rendered in a browser against the evidence binary (dashboard built from this branch with `cargo web build`, daemon on loopback with `require_pairing = false`) in two states: plugin system off with nothing installed (badge "Plugin execution disabled", filter buttons, empty catalog, no build-limitation notice) and plugin system off with the fixture package installed (one `tool-fixture` card: Installed, 0.0.0, capability `tool`, permission `config read`, same badge). The screenshot files are still to be attached to this PR and are, with the Cross-Platform Build dispatch, a precondition for leaving draft.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the release-profile binary was built at 84d58f016c, this PR's head, with rustc 1.97.1 (`zeroclaw 0.8.5 (v0.8.5-419-g84d58f016c)`, SHA-256 `525df2be867a29cfbda148d7adb3e81e229ed69293ca5ed91b0daa19082cccbb`); `cli` and the gateway API over loopback; smoke report in the collapsed section at the end of this body; locale pinned to `en` by the configuration.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** release-profile binary `zeroclaw 0.8.5 (v0.8.5-419-g84d58f016c)` (this PR's head) on aarch64-apple-darwin, a fresh configuration directory holding only `schema_version = 3` and `locale = "en"`, noninteractive output:
  ```text
  $ zeroclaw --help | grep -E '^\s+plugin\s'
    plugin        Manage WASM plugins
  $ zeroclaw status                      (Channels section, excerpt)
    Filesystem ❌ not configured
    Webhook   ❌ not configured
    Plugin    ❌ not configured
  $ curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/plugins      (daemon at default config: pairing required; headers abridged)
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  content-length: 0
  $ curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/plugins      (same, with [gateway] require_pairing = false for the loopback probe; headers abridged)
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  content-type: application/json
  {"plugins_enabled":false,"wasm_plugins_available":true,"plugins_dir":"<config-dir>/plugins","plugins":[],"issues":[]}
  ```
  On a binary without the plugin host (a `master` release binary, or a debug build without the feature, which is where the `--help` and `status` comparison was taken) `--help` lists no `plugin` command, `zeroclaw status` has no `Plugin` row (its Channels list ends at `Webhook`), and the same JSON answers `"wasm_plugins_available":false` (`crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_plugins.rs`); by code (`web/src/pages/Plugins.tsx`) the dashboard Plugins page renders that flag as "WASM plugins unavailable" with the build-limitation notice, and `true` as the disabled state; rendered evidence for that page is pending as noted above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** state: a fresh configuration directory with the plugin system at its defaults (off); observed: the outputs above. The `master` side of the comparison (no `plugin` command, no `Plugin` row, `wasm_plugins_available: false`) is by code and from a debug build without the feature, not from a `master` release binary.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** workspace-wide clippy and tests were left to CI, since no Rust source outside tests changed; `cross` builds and the Windows leg need their runners.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `Yes`. The 64-bit desktop and server release binaries now contain a code-loading runtime (wasmtime with Cranelift). Compiled-in effects that do not depend on config: the `plugin` CLI, the gateway plugin webhook routes, `/api/plugins`, a status row, and the empty `plugin_outbox` table added when the cron database is opened or created. Instantiating a component calls no export but does run any start function its core modules carry (for example a reactor's `_initialize`). `plugin install` (unless `--no-verify`), `plugin info` and `plugin list --verify` instantiate the component whether or not the plugin system is enabled, in a store with no preopened files, no network or egress authority, and the per-call fuel, memory and time limits. Exports run only after the operator opts in. With `plugins.enabled` and `plugins.auto_discover` set, every build of the tool registry compiles, instantiates and queries each admitted tool component for its metadata under the package's declared permissions and egress policy, and the tool is offered to the model; each `execute` then needs approval unless pre-approved (`auto_approve` by name or `*`, `level = "full"`, or an Always grant). A skill package needs `enabled` and `auto_discover`. A channel package needs `enabled`, a `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` declaration, and an enabled agent that lists `plugin.<alias>`. The smoke proves the closed defaults per archive: install leaves the plugin system off, discovery without enabling offers nothing, enabling without discovery offers nothing, a discovered tool waits for approval, and payload digests, the WIT world and the signature policy are enforced at install.
- New external network calls? `Yes`. `plugin search` and `plugin install <name>` fetch the registry index, operator-initiated. A plugin granted `http_client` or socket permissions can make policed egress from a release binary once enabled, including during the metadata probe; egress is deny-by-default through the per-instance allowlist. The release smoke itself talks only to a local stub provider.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`. The new jobs receive no secrets, hold `contents: read`, and check out with `persist-credentials: false`. The added diagnostic reads only whitelisted public identity/resource/package fields and writes two private runner-temp files. It adds a bounded upload to the existing GitHub artifact service, with no new permission or destination; no environment, argv, process, kernel, network or credential dump is collected.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `Yes`, in reach rather than mechanism: once a plugin is enabled, its tool name, description, parameter schema and results are model-visible text supplied by the plugin. Source builds have this today; this PR makes it reachable from release binaries once the operator enables the plugin system and discovery: the name, description and schema reach the model at registration without any approval, and results only after an approved call. A plugin skill package injects package-supplied skill text once the plugin system is enabled and discovery is on, and a channel plugin feeds inbound text to the model.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: covered in the answers above. wasmtime advisories become release-relevant; `cargo deny` and the daily audit already gate them.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes`: the 64-bit desktop and server release binaries gain the `zeroclaw plugin` subcommand and the gateway's plugin webhook route. `/api/plugins`, present in every gateway build, now answers `wasm_plugins_available: true` and lists installed packages; the dashboard's Plugins page shows the plugin system as disabled rather than unavailable; `zeroclaw status` gains a `Plugin` channel row; any plugin-host binary that opens or creates the cron database adds an empty `plugin_outbox` table. No config or environment surface changes. Exact upgrade steps for existing users: none; the plugin system stays off until enabled.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the four commits together (`git revert` of the merge commit, or of the four SHAs in reverse order); they restore the policy, the generated surfaces, the workflows, the tests and the docs as one unit. A partial rollback has to go further than the policy line: remove `plugins-wasm-cranelift` from `dist_extra_features` and from the three `dist_target_exclusions` entries (the resolver rejects an exclusion that names a feature outside the selection), remove the two `plugin-smoke` jobs from both workflows and `plugin-smoke` from the `publish` and `docker` needs, update the xtask and architecture tests and the docs, then run `cargo generate installers`. Rolling back one target is smaller: add it to `dist_target_exclusions` and drop its leg from both workflows; the xtask test holds the two in step.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** runtime `plugins.enabled` (default `false`) and `plugins.auto_discover` (default `false`); operators pin an older release with `zeroclaw update --version <previous> --force` (musl and package-manager installs reinstall the previous archive or package instead).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a `Check binary size` failure on a build leg (`Binary exceeds 80MB safeguard`); a `Plugin Smoke <target>` leg failing, with its step summary naming the failed check, which skips `publish` and `docker`; `zeroclaw --help` listing no `plugin` command on a 64-bit desktop or server archive, which is the smoke's first check.

## Known risks

- The Windows smoke leg is the first blocking Windows plugin check. The harness handles MSYS paths and `.exe` but has run only on macOS and Linux so far.
- The musl archives build through `cross`; wasmtime's C helpers in that container are unproven until the manual workflow runs.
- `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners execute the aarch64 archives; the glibc one links glibc 2.35 (built on 22.04) and runs on 24.04. The manual rehearsal cross-builds on `ubuntu-latest`; once that label moves past 24.04 the binary may need a newer glibc than the runner has.
- The 80 MiB cap is an estimate until the manual workflow reports x86_64 Linux sizes.
- A release started by a tag push also triggers Docker Publish on its own `v*` trigger, which does not wait for the smoke; the dispatch path is the gated one.

## Follow-ups, not in this PR

- ARM32 with the Cranelift feature and wasmtime's automatic Pulley target: a compile check in CI, then an emulated smoke.
- A `plugin sign` command (proposed in RFC #8135, which is deferred and not accepted).
- A way to ask a binary which backend it carries; `--version` lists no features.
- Registry CI that instantiates published artifacts (#9624), and registry signing.
- Size figures in generated release notes; a smoke inside the published container image.
- The plugin crate setup snippet clones the WIT from `master`; now that release binaries are the documented host it should pin the release tag (`--branch vX.Y.Z`).
- #11335 and #11336, found while building the harness.

prs.title: fix(plugins): recover incomplete installs through plugin remove
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11098 already builds every new package in a hidden `.<name>.installing-<pid>` staging directory and renames it into place, so the current installer never leaves a half-written package under the real name, and discovery ignores a staging directory a crash stranded. Its test covers a failed `skills/` copy. Still open from the issue: deterministic faults at the manifest and payload writes, a recovery path for a final directory an older installer stranded (install answered `AlreadyLoaded`, `plugin remove` answered `NotFound`, so only a manual delete worked), and documentation of the observable behavior.
  - `install_admitted` now reports anything occupying an unloaded package name as a new `PluginError::UnadmittedPackage { name, reason }` instead of `AlreadyLoaded`. It checks with `symlink_metadata`, so a file, a symlink, or a dangling link counts. The CLI adds `cli-plugin-install-unadmitted-package` (all five catalogues) naming `zeroclaw plugin remove <name>`.
  - `PluginHost::remove` gains recovery for a canonical package name the host did not load. Install and remove share an OS lock under a retained plugins-root directory handle. Recovery moves the selected directory into a fresh, unique leased transaction, then checks that the claimed directory has the selected identity. Admission and recursive deletion use that claimed directory handle, so a replacement at the original name is not deleted. A retry that finishes a delete recovery had begun deletes what is left of that claim without a second verdict or identity check; the Security section states the trust assumption.
    - A manifest-less directory is recoverable only when empty. A non-regular or uninspectable manifest is refused. Otherwise, the shared admission checks must reject the package for its contents rather than its signature or another operational failure, and the claim must hold only what an install writes: a `manifest.toml` naming that package, the component at the manifest's `wasm_path` as a regular file with the directories on its way, and, for a skill plugin, a `skills/` tree of directories and regular files; only `manifest.toml` when the manifest does not parse. Anything else, such as a plugin's source checkout whose component is not built yet, skill drafts next to a tool manifest, or a symlink or FIFO where the component goes, is refused, and the reason says why.
    - A refused claim is restored without replacing another occupant that holds files. If restoration is blocked, both are preserved and `RecoveryRetained` reports the retained path. A retry restores abandoned recovery claims before applying normal admission, except one recovery had begun deleting, which it finishes.
    - Staging cleanup removes only recognized abandoned leased transactions after a final package has been claimed and judged recoverable. Active transactions and legacy PID-only staging directories are retained and reported. Calls with no final package do not sweep stages, unless they finish a delete an earlier remove had begun.
  - Merged with #11232, which has since landed on `master` as `05f9fe95d4`. Install and recovery admission read the component through the same no-follow, non-blocking handle walk #11232 gives discovery, from the source directory install opened or the generation recovery claimed. Before, they opened the payload with a blocking open, so a FIFO in its place hung `plugin install`, and hung `plugin remove` while it held the package lock. The payload read reports a namespace that changed after confinement as `NamespaceChanged` rather than `InvalidManifest`, which recovery reads as defective contents: a package root that no longer names the confined directory on every platform, the substitutions the pathname checks catch elsewhere, and on Unix a symlink or non-directory the walk meets.
  - Package moves now require an atomic rename that refuses every existing destination. Linux/Android/Apple retain the existing atomic primitive, and Windows retains its existing nonreplacement move. When that primitive is unavailable, including older kernels or affected filesystems and other Unix platforms, installation and recovery refuse the move instead of using a plain replacing rename. Failed claims leave the selected entry unmoved; failed publication/restoration retains the package and reports its transaction path.
  - Recovery prints its own refusal reasons as written, without the `invalid plugin config:` prefix they had picked up. It removes a transaction entry a stopped process left empty instead of refusing every later remove, and a retry finishes a delete that a stopped remover had begun instead of putting back what it left for another verdict.
  - Install and remove give up waiting for the package lock after 60 seconds and name the lock file. An existing lock file is reopened for writing, which an exclusive lock over NFS needs, or for reading only when this user cannot write it.
  - A host opens the plugins root, and its lock, the first time it takes the package lock. A host that only discovers plugins, including each one the daemon keeps, holds nothing in the plugins directory: on Windows it no longer pins that directory and its ancestors against rename, and an ancestor it cannot open no longer fails discovery (#11359).
  - A transaction's lease is unlocked before its file is closed. Closing alone releases the lock only once nothing else refers to the open file, and a child process that another thread is spawning briefly does, so a recovery right after could take a released transaction for a live one and keep its claim.
  - The recovery messages the CLI prints (`cli-plugin-recovery-retained`, `cli-plugin-staging-retained`, `cli-plugin-namespace-changed`, and the new `cli-plugin-install-retained`) are in all five catalogues, next to the other plugin keys, and the parity test covers them. An install that could not publish keeps its staged copy and says to run the install again, instead of pointing at `plugin remove`, which may sweep that copy. A remove or retry that did its work but could not clear the claim's transaction entry reports `RecoveryRetained` naming that entry instead of a bare I/O error, and an install that published its package but could not clear its stage succeeds, leaving the stage's entry to the stage sweep.
  - On Windows, install and recovery admission refuse a payload that is not a regular file before opening it, as admission on Unix already did. Before, a directory there failed the open with an access error, which recovery read as an I/O failure.
  - Tests and docs: a `#[cfg(test)]` thread-local seam in `write_package` cuts the manifest or payload write off half-way, so the tests fail an install at exactly the steps the issue names. The plugin guide gains a "Recovering an incomplete installation" subsection, which states what an install writes, and "How plugins work" one sentence on hidden staging.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Staging and rename now use unique leased transactions and publication that never replaces an entry holding files. The shared admission rules, digest and signature policy, and exact admitted bytes remain the basis for acceptance. Active staging directories remain protected.
  - `plugin remove` does not sweep staging directories when no stranded package directory exists, because a live install may own them. The one exception is a remove that finishes a delete an earlier remove had begun after judging a final package.
  - Pre-existing and unchanged here: for a loaded package, `remove` deletes `plugins_dir/<name>` rather than that package's own directory. For a package discovered under a directory named differently from its manifest, it removes whatever sits at `<name>` and leaves the real files. Tracked in #11357. `plugin migrate` still moves packages without the package lock (#11358).
  - Accepted trade-off: an interrupted cross-filesystem `plugin migrate` copy that left a manifest-less partial directory now needs a manual delete. Its legacy source is intact.
  - No new config keys or flags. The repair adds `cap-std` 4.0.3, Unix `rustix` 1.1.4 filesystem support, Windows `winx` 0.36.4, and filesystem support through `windows` 0.61. `same-file` stays a dependency on every platform, where #11232 alone moves it to non-Unix targets, because the recovery identity checks use it on Unix too.
  - #11232's head `3dec521b79` was merged into this branch in `933c7dde21`, which resolved the conflict in `Cargo.toml` and the payload read (`git show --remerge-diff 933c7dde21`). #11232 has since landed on `master` as `05f9fe95d4`, with the same patch apart from one docs file. `b17f915a60` merges `master` after it, resolving the same conflicts the same way and keeping `master`'s Wasmtime 48.0.4 upgrade. This PR's own change is byte for byte what it was before that merge.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw plugin install` and `zeroclaw plugin remove`. The gateway and runtime never call `install` or `remove`, and only those two open the plugins root, so the daemon's discovery-only hosts hold no handle in the plugins directory. On Windows an opened root keeps the plugins directory and each of its ancestors from being renamed or deleted until its host drops, which for the CLI is the end of the command. `PluginError` gains recovery variants; outside this crate's own recovery classification, nothing in the workspace matches it exhaustively.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10770. Closes #11359. Follows #11232, which has landed (see Scope boundary). Depends on #11715.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `ci:windows`, `cli`, `core`, `dependencies`, `distinguished contributor`, `docs`, `domain:security`, `release-gate`, `release:v0.8.6`, `risk:high`, `runtime`, `size:XL`, `topic:plugins`.

### Since the last reviews

tidux requested changes at `d1d6115149`, which JordanTheJet had approved. Each item is addressed in the six commits since. After them, `b17f915a60` merges `master` (see the scope boundary), which leaves this PR's own diff unchanged:

- **Recovery could delete files no install writes** (`ceddf3e5d4`). Before it marks a delete, recovery now refuses a claim that holds anything an install never writes, and says why. Every installer writes a package under its manifest's name: the manifest, the component at `wasm_path` as a regular file, and, for a skill plugin only, a `skills/` tree it copies as directories and regular files. So a manifest naming another package, a component that is a directory, symlink or FIFO, `skills/` next to a manifest without the skill capability, or a link inside `skills/` is refused too. Next to a manifest that does not parse, only `manifest.toml` is allowed, and the reason says so. A filesystem that does not report entry types while listing is asked for each entry's metadata instead.
  - `remove_keeps_a_directory_holding_files_an_install_never_writes` keeps five such directories byte for byte: a broken manifest next to a note, a source checkout whose component is not built, a stray file beside the component, a directory where the component goes, and skill drafts next to a tool manifest. `remove_keeps_a_package_whose_manifest_names_another_package`, `remove_keeps_a_package_holding_a_symlink_an_install_never_writes` (a linked component, and a link in a skill bundle) and `remove_keeps_a_package_whose_payload_is_a_fifo_without_blocking` (which expected the delete before) cover the rest.
  - `remove_recovers_a_broken_package_whose_component_is_nested` still recovers what a skill plugin's install writes, and the shapes test passes unchanged.
  - On Windows a directory at the payload failed admission with an access error, not as a payload that is not a file, so recovery would have refused that case for the wrong reason. Admission there now checks for a regular file before it opens one, as on Unix.
  - The plugin guide's two recoverable cases now state the rule, and the walkthrough below adds the source-checkout refusal.
- **Every host pinned the plugins directory** (`f2a4c806be`, closes #11359). The root opens the first time a host takes the package lock. `only_a_package_operation_opens_the_plugins_root` checks that discovery opens nothing and that a remove does. The Windows test now checks that discovery alone pins nothing, and that an opened root pins until its host drops. One consequence: the root's identity is now taken at that first operation, not before discovery, so removing a loaded package no longer notices a plugins directory replaced in between. That path deletes by name, as on `master` (#11357).
- **English-only messages and the install retained message** (`cc3e404159`). The three recovery messages are translated into es, fr, ja and zh-CN, sit next to the other plugin keys, and are in the parity test. An install that could not publish now says to run the install again, and `a_retained_install_points_at_installing_again` checks that it never names `plugin remove`.
- **Partial success** (`3dfce36639`, `c5fbbe2313`). A remove that deleted the package but could not clear its transaction entry now reports `RecoveryRetained` naming that entry and saying that only the entry is left. So does a retry that finished an earlier remove's delete, and a refusal that put the package back, which also keeps its reason. It still exits as a failed remove and does not list the stages it kept; reporting it as a success with something left over needs a result type of its own, which I have left out of this PR. An install that published its package but could not clear its stage now succeeds. Not changed: when a retry finishes an earlier delete and then refuses the current occupant, it reports only the refusal. The finished delete is one that the earlier remove had already judged and committed to.
- **Following links when selecting and opening the claim.** Not changed. As your review says, it holds today by analysis: selection refuses a link before it takes the directory's identity, a link swapped in after that is moved itself, and the identity check or cap-std's confinement to the transaction refuses it. `open_dir_nofollow` is in `cap-fs-ext`, not cap-std 4.0.3, and I'd rather change the selection path with Windows coverage for it in a follow-up than in this PR.
- **Windows tests on the landing head.** The advisory nextest on `d1d6115149` was cancelled. On `b17f915a60` the [`ci:windows` job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37707724330/job/113086323251) ran: every plugin test passed, 292 of 292 in the plugin library group and 174 of 174 in the full workspace run. That includes `windows_parent_capabilities_pin_renames_once_the_root_is_open`, `only_a_package_operation_opens_the_plugins_root`, and the footprint test with a directory where the component goes, which the Windows payload-open change exists for. The job's 11 failures are all in other crates (see How I tested).

Also new: `eca169e979` unlocks a transaction's lease before closing it (see Summary). A 200-run soak of the recovery tests failed once on the previous local head: a remove right after another found the claim's lease still locked while a parallel test spawned a child. `a_dropped_transaction_releases_its_lease_while_its_file_is_shared` reproduces that through a duplicate descriptor and fails without the unlock.

### Earlier reviews

JordanTheJet requested changes at `5850deff90`, and Audacity88 approved `188de8507f`. The blocking finding was that recovery decided to delete before it fixed which directory it would delete. Each part of the suggested minimal fix:

- **Claim and validate one generation, delete only it through handles** (`43953d9f17`). `remove` takes a package lock shared with install across processes, on a retained plugins-root handle. It moves the selected directory into a fresh, private leased `.<name>.recovering-v1-<32 hex>` transaction, checks that the claimed directory has the identity it selected, judges that handle, and deletes through it. The final unlink is empty-only.
- **No staging sweep without proof the owner is gone.** Cleanup removes only protocol transactions whose lease it can take. PID-named stages from older installers are kept and reported.
- **Namespace changes refuse.** `NamespaceChanged` is a separate variant and never a structural verdict, including the payload walk's substitution and moved-root cases after the #11232 merge.
- **Regressions with real processes and deterministic pause points:**
  - `separate_remover_deletes_only_claimed_generation_after_final_replacement`: a package written at the name while the remover is paused before its delete survives byte for byte.
  - `a_second_remover_and_an_installer_wait_for_a_remover_paused_before_its_delete`: the reviewed sequence with cooperating processes. Both wait for the lock instead of finishing under the paused remover, and the installer's healthy package survives byte for byte.
  - `paused_stage_cleanup_does_not_delete_replacement_generation` and `real_active_stage_survives_and_abandoned_protocol_stage_is_cleaned`: the staging window.

Also since those reviews:

- `f0c0e03bce` makes a skill-bundle inspection error refuse recovery.
- `933c7dde21` merges #11232.
- `a62384ba5e` reads install and recovery payloads through #11232's no-follow walk.
- `e39b630fa4` makes the test barrier wait for an explicit continue. A killed child that saw stdin close had run past it: 2 of 100 soak runs failed before, 0 of 200 after.
- `d8a44c6e0b` adds the cooperating-process regression.
- `8e2de5910d` adds the plain-rename fallback, `6c5f7ed4c2` the plain refusal reasons, and `e376167ad1` the cleanup of empty transaction entries. That fallback is superseded by the atomic-only correction at `1743b13959`.

### What this does, simply

Installing a plugin copies it into the plugins folder. A recent change made new installs assemble the package in a hidden folder and move it into place in one step, so a crash halfway through no longer leaves a broken package behind. But folders that older versions left broken still blocked every later install of that plugin with a misleading "already loaded" error. Such a folder might be empty, or hold a manifest but no WebAssembly file. `zeroclaw plugin remove` said "not found", so the only fix was deleting the folder by hand.

Now install says the name is taken by something that is not an installed package, and tells you to run `zeroclaw plugin remove <name>`. That command claims the selected folder before deciding whether to delete it. It also cleans recognized abandoned staging transactions, while keeping active or legacy staging directories. The selected folder is recoverable in only two cases:

- The folder is empty.
- It has a manifest, it holds nothing an install would not have written, and the checks install and discovery use reject its own contents rather than its signature. That includes a package this host could never load, such as one whose component is over the size limit.

The command refuses files and symlinks at that name, folders with files but no manifest, folders holding files no install writes (such as a plugin's source checkout), folders it cannot inspect, loaded plugin folders, packages the checks accept, and packages rejected by signature policy. If another occupant prevents restoring a claimed package to its original name, the command preserves the claim and reports its retained location. The signature is checked first, so under `strict` that last case includes an interrupted install of an unsigned package.

```text
[exit 1]
$ ls -A plugins
.demo.installing-4242
.locked.installing-7
.notes.installing-5
.zeroclaw-package-lock-v1
demo
devtool
locked
notes
$ zeroclaw plugin remove filey
Error: `zeroclaw plugin remove` left 'filey' in place: it is not a directory. It deletes a directory the host has not loaded only when the directory is empty, or when it holds only what an install writes and admission rejects its own contents rather than its signature; delete 'filey' by hand if it should go.
[exit 1]
$ zeroclaw plugin remove unsigned
Error: `zeroclaw plugin remove` left 'unsigned' in place: plugin 'unsigned' is unsigned and signature verification is required. It deletes a directory the host has not loaded only when the directory is empty, or when it holds only what an install writes and admission rejects its own contents rather than its signature; delete 'unsigned' by hand if it should go.
[exit 1]
```

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** recorded in the transcript.
  - The refused install left `demo` and its staging directory as found. `plugin remove demo` deleted `demo`, kept the legacy `.demo.installing-4242` and said why, and the retry installed the package.
  - Each refused remove left its target and that name's staging directory in place, and printed its reason as written. The source checkout `devtool` was kept, naming `src`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Current project validation is supplied by the required hosted run; no duplicate local rerun is claimed. Five conditional jobs are skipped by the existing CI selectors. Earlier local transcripts apply only to their named revisions. Current advisory Windows/platform and full release acceptance remain separate.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: `plugin remove` can now delete a directory the host never loaded.
  - **What it can reach.**
    - Only a canonical package slug: one path component, with no `.` or `..`, no hidden names, and no separators.
    - Only the selected real directory, after a claim into a fresh transaction and an identity comparison. A file or symlink at the package name is refused. Recursive cleanup uses held directory handles; final directory unlink is empty-only. Windows also pins ancestors, from the first package operation until the host drops, and uses `MoveFileW` without replacement. A retry that finishes a delete recovery had begun does not compare identities again.
    - Never the directory a loaded package was loaded from, matched by file identity (device and inode on unix, `same_file::Handle` elsewhere), so a differently cased name on a case-insensitive file system still matches. A directory whose identity cannot be read is kept.
  - **What it deletes, and nothing else.**
    - An empty claimed directory, through empty-only removal, which fails if an entry appears meanwhile.
    - A directory whose `manifest.toml` is a regular file naming that package and that holds only what an install writes (`manifest.toml`, the `wasm_path` component as a regular file with the directories on its way, and, for a skill plugin, a `skills/` tree of directories and regular files; only `manifest.toml` when the manifest does not parse), when admission rejects the directory for its own contents. That covers a truncated or unparsable manifest, a missing or digest-mismatched component, and a package this host cannot accept as written, for example a component over the 64 MiB admission limit or a `config_schema` the `regex` dialect cannot compile. Discovery never loads those, and the operator named the directory.
    - What is left of a claim recovery had judged incomplete and begun deleting, which its transaction marks with a `deleting` file. A retry finishes that delete without judging it again, even when the remainder would pass admission, as a skill bundle stopped between its skills can. Only this protocol writes inside a leased transaction; changing what one holds takes write access to that transaction's directory. That includes a process whose working directory was inside the folder before the claim moved it: what it writes there after the verdict, or after a stop and before the retry, is deleted with the claim.
  - **What it keeps, with the reason printed.**
    - a directory holding files but no manifest
    - a directory holding anything an install never writes, named in the reason and checked before the delete is marked: a plugin's source checkout whose component is not built, `skills/` next to a manifest without the skill capability, a symlink or special file at the component or inside `skills/`, or a manifest naming another package
    - a `manifest.toml` that is not a regular file
    - anything whose identity cannot be read, whose manifest cannot be inspected, or whose directory cannot be listed; all are checked before any staging sweep
    - a package admission accepts, unless recovery had begun deleting it
    - a trust-policy rejection (`UnsignedPlugin`, `UntrustedPublisher`, `SignatureInvalid`, `PayloadDigestRequired`). Admission checks the signature before the component, so under `strict` this also keeps an unsigned interrupted install, which then needs a manual delete.
    - `AlreadyLoaded`
    - any other I/O error
  - **How new error variants are handled.** The classification is an exhaustive match with no wildcard arm, so a new `PluginError` variant does not compile until it is classified.
  - **The staging sweep.** Unique `.<name>.installing-v1-<32 hex>` transactions contain a `package` directory and held `lease`. Cleanup requires ownership of an abandoned transaction. Live leases and ambiguous legacy `.<name>.installing-<digits>` directories are retained and reported. `.<name>.recovering-v1-<32 hex>` transactions preserve claimed package data across recovery failures, unless recovery had begun deleting that package.
  - **Skill-bundle inspection.** An inspection failure inside the skill bundle, such as an unreadable nested skill directory, is an I/O error rather than defective contents, so recovery refuses and keeps every byte (`f0c0e03bce`, `remove_refuses_inaccessible_nested_skill_and_preserves_all_bytes`).
  - **Special files.** A FIFO in place of the component fails admission at once on install and recovery, as on discovery, and the regular-file check refuses any other special file, instead of an open that could block while `plugin remove` holds the package lock. Recovery then keeps the package, because no install writes a special file.
  - **Package lock.** Any local account that can read the lock file in the plugins directory can hold the lock. Install and remove then fail after 60 seconds, naming the lock file, rather than wait without end. Nothing is written or deleted while they wait. The file-permission policy is #11360.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? The existing supported atomic Linux/Android/Apple and Windows move paths are retained. This is an explicit compatibility change for kernels/filesystems or other Unix platforms without atomic nonreplacement: package install, recovery claim and restoration refuse instead of falling back to a replacing rename. Existing and staged data is preserved; retained publication/restoration reports its path. Unsupported file locking continues to refuse.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes (CLI behavior only)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none.
  - Installing over something at the package name now fails with the new message instead of `already loaded`.
  - `zeroclaw plugin remove <name>` now clears an empty directory, or one that holds only what an install writes and whose own contents fail admission, instead of answering `not found`.
  - For other unloaded names that exist on disk, it now says why it kept them instead of `not found`.
  - No flags or config keys change. The plugins root gains `.zeroclaw-package-lock-v1` and versioned leased install/recovery transactions. Existing package layout remains supported; legacy PID-only staging directories are retained rather than automatically deleted.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` reverts the code, but does not restore the previous transient disk layout. Preserve retained recovery transactions and their package data before rollback. Older code cannot automatically recover the new transactions; do not treat hidden recovery directories as disposable staging. No automatic downgrade recovery procedure has been validated.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - `zeroclaw plugin remove <name>` reports success for a name `zeroclaw plugin list` did not show, while an admissible package directory disappears. The refusal cases are covered by tests.
  - `plugin install` reports `was left untouched` for a name that has nothing at `<plugins dir>/<name>`.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): open local file paths from the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - ZeroCode only recognised `http(s)://` links, so clicking a file path in the transcript was left to the terminal's own link detection. That breaks two ways. ZeroCode wraps long lines itself, so the terminal sees each row as a separate line, and a click on the second row opens a wrong, relative path. A path with a space in it (`/Volumes/Work SSD/...`) is cut off at the space.
  - Transcript text that names an **existing** local path (absolute or `~/`, optionally with a `:line[:col]` suffix) is now a link. Because detection checks the filesystem, a match can extend across spaces while it still names a real path, and ordinary prose stays plain text. Lookups are cached for 5 s so streaming frames don't hit the disk each time.
  - Paths use the same hit map as URLs, which is built from the real wrapped layout. A click on any row of a wrapped path resolves to the whole path.
  - Plain click opens the path. Right-click gives **Open**, **Reveal in Finder** (labelled "Show in folder" off macOS), **Copy path** and **Add path to chat** (appends the path as a code span to the composer).
  - Files that could run code when opened (app bundles, files with the executable bit set, scripts, installers, `.command`, `.webloc`, and similar) are revealed instead of opened, with a notice. Transcript text can come from a model, so a click must never launch something.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Cmd-click is not handled. Terminal mouse reports don't carry the Command key, so ZeroCode can't see it. Making the terminal's own Cmd-click work on wrapped paths needs OSC 8 hyperlinks, which ratatui doesn't emit. That is a separate follow-up.
  - Relative paths (`src/main.rs`) are not linked. They would need the session's cwd, which the transcript renderer doesn't have.
  - The `:line` suffix is part of the highlighted text but is not passed to the opener.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode transcript rendering (link styling and the hit map) and the chat context menu. No daemon or wire changes.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

File paths in the ZeroCode chat are now clickable like web links, including long paths that wrap onto several lines and paths with spaces in them. Clicking one opens the file. Right-clicking gives a menu to open it, show it in Finder, copy it, or drop it into your next message. If a file is something that would run when opened, like an app or a script, ZeroCode shows it in Finder instead of running it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode over the daemon socket)
- **Setup / preconditions:** ZeroCode built from this branch, any agent, a pane narrow enough that a long path wraps. Create a folder with a space in its name and a file inside it.
- **Steps to run:** send a message containing the file's absolute path, then click the path's second row. Right-click it and try each menu item. Put the path of a `.command` or `.app` in a message and click it.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the whole path is underlined across every row it wraps onto. Clicking any row opens the file. The menu shows Open / Reveal in Finder / Copy path / Add path to chat / Copy. The `.command` or `.app` is revealed in Finder, not run. A path that doesn't exist stays plain.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** paths are plain text. Cmd-click (the terminal's detection) opens a wrong relative path from a wrapped row and stops at the first space.

### How I tested

All builds and tests ran through `scripts/zc-cargo` on the remote build host.

- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the touched Rust files: clean.
- `zc-cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: `Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 14.01s`, exit 0.
- `zc-cargo test -p zerocode`: lib `test result: ok. 52 passed; 0 failed`; bin `test result: FAILED. 1432 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The 1 is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`. It fails the same way on unmodified `master` (cbe753fbe3) on the same host, so it is environmental (signal handling) and unrelated.

New tests:

- `chat::tests::wrapped_path_with_space_is_one_link_on_every_row`: a real temp file under a directory with a space, wrapped over at least 3 rows. Every hit cell carries the full path with one occurrence id, a click on the last row opens the full path, and each menu item maps to its request. With path detection disabled, it fails at the first assertion.
- `chat::tests::missing_paths_stay_plain_text`, `chat::tests::add_path_to_chat_appends_a_code_span`.
- `path_open::tests::*` (9): spaces plus trailing punctuation, prose and missing paths rejected, several paths on one line, `~/` expansion with no-`HOME` rejection, `:line[:col]` stripping, URLs and truncated table cells never treated as paths, launch detection (extension, bundle `Contents/Info.plist`, executable bit), open falls back to reveal for those, macOS reveal is `open -R`, relative, missing and control-character paths rejected.

- **CI checks relied on:** the Rust lanes for `zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** none of the tests actually launches Finder or the default app. The spawned argv is asserted instead.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I ran this branch's daemon and ZeroCode (debug build via zc-cargo) against a scratch config with a dead provider URI, in a 110×32 tmux pane, with `HOME` set to a demo directory. I sent a message with one absolute path containing spaces and one `~/` path with `:12`, plus a missing path. Both real paths were underlined across their wrapped rows and the missing one stayed plain. A right-click (an SGR report) on the second row of the long path opened the path menu. Choosing "Add path to chat" put the full backticked path in the composer. Not verified live: Open and Reveal actually launching Finder (headless run).
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `b1c0571f9211`, ZeroCode Chat pane, 110×32, rendered from `tmux capture-pane -e`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

  ![Wrapped paths underlined across rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/b1c0571f9211e1d4093c8c7029a7209c9565cd35/.pr-evidence/pr-path-links-00-wrapped-path.png)

  ![Path context menu opened from the continuation row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/b1c0571f9211e1d4093c8c7029a7209c9565cd35/.pr-evidence/pr-path-links-01-wrapped-path-menu.png)
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** right-click on the wrapped second row opens the path menu for the full path.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** a full workspace test run was skipped: the change is confined to `apps/zerocode`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. ZeroCode now runs `stat` on path-shaped transcript text and can hand a user-clicked path to the platform opener. Mitigation: only existing absolute paths, one argument per process (no shell), control characters rejected, and anything that could execute is revealed, not opened.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Model output can now produce clickable paths. A click is still required, and the reveal-instead-of-open rule stops a crafted path from launching code.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert` of the two commits.
