prs.title: fix(zerocode): show temporary local file-write diffs
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Eligible local ZeroCode `file_write` calls now show red removed lines and green added lines from a bounded observation taken before the successful write. Overwrite cards put `Overwrote existing file` above the content, and six-row previews offer Show all whenever rows are omitted.
- Previous text travels through a separate local notification, outside ordinary tool results, model messages and saved history. A private client inbox and the rendered view share a five-minute deadline. Direct ACP clients stop constructing creation diffs from write input, including live events, restored history and approval requests.
- **Scope boundary:** Capture requires native read authority as well as write authority, a readable workspace path and supported text. Unsupported writes and restored history show the recorded summary with a clearly labelled supplied-content preview. The pre-write observation cannot guarantee the exact inode contents replaced if another process modifies the file concurrently.
- **Blast radius:** File-write observation, transient native RPC events, local ZeroCode Chat/Code cards and ACP write presentation. Existing file authorization and atomic replacement are preserved. No new dependency, configuration or durable schema is introduced.
- **Linked issue:** Related #10294. This covers bounded local native diffs; remote and direct ACP diffs remain unavailable.
- **Runtime placement:** Depends on #11436. The covering scope needs a recorded Core Team decision in the exception table before this implementation merges.
- **Labels:** `agent`, `bug`, `channel`, `channel:acp`, `channel:core`, `docs`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `runtime`, `size:XL`, `tool`, `tool:file`, `zerocode`

### What this does, simply

An agent can replace an existing file with `file_write`. Showing only the new text as green additions makes that replacement look like a creation. ZeroCode can now show what was removed and added when the agent already has permission to read that workspace file. The old text stays in the local client briefly and disappears from this view after five minutes. Reopening the conversation shows the saved write summary, because old text is not saved with it. Files that cannot be captured still have a visible overwrite heading and an explicit unavailable-diff label.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, with disposable synthetic files.
- **Interfaces to exercise:** Local native ZeroCode Chat and Code. Direct ACP write presentation has focused automated coverage.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build daemon and client from the same revision. Use an agent whose effective tools include native `file_write` and `file_read`, with no excluded read tool or pending read approval. Use a fresh conversation and an unused text file in its authorized workspace. A profile with only write authority intentionally receives the fallback preview.
- **Steps to run:** Use `file_write` to create a file with eight numbered lines, then overwrite it with three different lines. Expand the overwrite card and choose Show all. Wait five minutes or disconnect, then reopen the conversation. Repeat with read authority disabled to inspect the fallback. Use `file_edit` separately to check its existing diff behavior.
- **Expected on this branch:** The overwrite has a prominent heading, red removals, green additions, `Changes · temporary local view`, and Show all when more than six diff rows exist. An identical rewrite says `Content unchanged`. Expired, restored or unsupported overwrites show the recorded size summary and `Content preview · diff unavailable`. Pending and unknown calls do not acquire success claims. Direct ACP does not synthesize a creation diff from arbitrary write input.
- **Prior behavior on master:** Results report bytes written and path; write previews look like additions regardless of previous contents.

### How I tested

- `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode -E 'test(local_file_diff) | test(file_write::tests) | test(chat::tests::file_tool_preview) | test(chat::tests::recorded_file_write_results) | test(chat::tests::file_write_base64) | test(chat::tests::tool_entry_disclosure) | test(chat::tests::expanded_tool_display) | test(diff::tests::) | test(transcript_layout) | test(chat::tests::rebuild_lines)'`: 79 selected tests passed after integration with the current transcript-cache owner. The existing expiry test also passed with an added private-URL projection assertion.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, comment hygiene and authored Markdown checks passed. The English tools catalog matches the repository generator.
- `cargo build --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw -p zerocode --bin zerocode`: matched daemon/client build passed.

Focused checks exercise actual filesystem writes and the spawned native turn, including absence of old-text sentinels from serialized results and model history. Negative cases cover read exclusion or approval, foreign and write-only roots, binary/control text, credential filenames, hard links, bounds, failures, nonlocal transport and revoked grants. Client checks cover an idle generic subscriber, private-inbox limits and retirement, cache expiry, repeated IDs, restored history, original copy text, red/green rows and disclosure.

[Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37143875544) passes at `6d0f053e10352a9c38840fea48b2a26766fc2da1`, including Lint, Test, platform/feature checks and the aggregate required gate. An unchanged plugin tool test process crashed in the first attempt and passed on a targeted retry. No broad local workspace test run was performed.

### Visual evidence

> **Screenshot placeholder:** Attach two direct ZeroCode captures of the overwrite in Preview and Show all.

Use the updated revision in an English-locale terminal around 120 columns by 40 rows. Show the overwrite heading, red and green rows, temporary-view caption and disclosure controls with enough surrounding context to judge clipping and spacing. A direct capture of this revised layout is pending; renderer assertions do not establish visual acceptance.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes, a write can make a bounded previous-text observation for local display. It requires existing effective native read authority, readable-path policy and workspace containment. No permission is granted by the model's arguments.
- New external network calls? No. Private evidence is sent only to its trusted local native RPC connection. Remote RPC, direct ACP, gateway and channel adapters do not receive it.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes, previous text temporarily exists in memory. Each old and new snapshot is limited to 16 KiB and 1,024 lines. Capture skips unreadable, binary/control-containing text, listed credential filenames and key extensions, and Unix files with multiple hard links. The filename exclusions are not a detector for secrets in arbitrary readable files.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; test content is synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes, success text gains pre-write existence and byte counts. Captured previous text never enters ordinary tool output, model messages, hooks, observers, receipts, checkpoints or saved history. Rendering escapes terminal controls.

The private inbox and view each cap raw pairs at 64 KiB and 16 entries per session; the inbox tracks at most 16 sessions and each pane at most eight. The generic notification buffer holds only opaque tokens. Private delivery rechecks current read grants under an authority lease and drops evidence if the bounded writer queue is full. Expiry, disconnect, retirement and history replacement clear their owned payloads and derived render/selection/copy caches. Explicit copies, terminal scrollback, screen captures and operating-system memory are outside this automatic retention guarantee; memory is not cryptographically erased. Failed capture or delivery does not fail an otherwise authorized write.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for tool arguments and durable history. Successful human-readable result text changes. Native matched-version RPC gains an optional local-only notification. Direct ACP write input preserves `path`, `content` and optional `encoding` instead of synthesizing `newText`; clients must read those original arguments and respect their encoding.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps: Build daemon and ZeroCode together. No configuration migration. The compact summary recognizes saved English success results with a matching argument path; unknown or localized result formats retain their original display. Historical results without pre-write evidence remain unknown.

## Repository ownership

The new runtime admission and RPC adapters need a recorded Core Team exception under the runtime holding-crate policy before merge. The transient value, capture and view live in their API, tools and client owners; extracting the existing agent-loop/RPC owners would be a separate refactor. This PR does not grant itself an exception.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits and rebuild daemon and ZeroCode together.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No new toggle. Excluding native `file_read` or requiring read approval prevents capture for that agent and uses the fallback preview.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing temporary diff despite eligible read authority, old lines appearing after expiry or in restored history, incorrect overwrite heading, or failed write cards. The fallback remains usable when capture or delivery is unavailable.

Updates `highlight.js` from 11.11.1 to 11.12.0
Release notes

Sourced from highlight.js's releases.

v11.12.0 - Summer, hot and rainy.

Parser Engine:

  • fix(parser) count named capture groups when rewriting backreferences [spokodev][]

New Grammars:

  • add FreeDesktop config file (.desktop / systemd) grammar [gg582][]
  • added 3rd party Cedar grammar to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [Dhruv Maniya][]
  • added 3rd party DAX and M (Power Query) grammars to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [jiaopengzi][]
  • added 3rd party Djot grammar to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [Mark Scherer][]
  • added 3rd party Igor Pro grammar to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [Ryne Andal][]
  • added 3rd party Jaiva grammar to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [Lehlogonolo Poole][]
  • added 3rd party Liquidsoap grammar to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [Romain Beauxis][]
  • added 3rd party MoonBit grammar to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [Kaida-Amethyst][]
  • added 3rd party Pkl grammar to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [Dan Chao][]
  • added 3rd party RAScript grammar to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [Joshua Raphael][]
  • added 3rd party Veryl grammar to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [Naoya Hatta][]
  • added 3rd party Why3 grammar to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [JGalego][]
  • added 3rd party Xojo grammar to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [patricksalo][]
  • referenced existing 3rd party ES|QL grammar in SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES [Styx0x6][]

Core Grammars:

  • fix(c) only match real atomic_* type names, not C11 atomic functions, issue #3837 [Mark Xian][]
  • fix(c, cpp) bound the run of type tokens in front of a function name (ReDoS), issue #4362 [Jayesh Bhade][]
  • fix(c, cpp) scope angle-bracket header string to #include, issue #3505 [Pablo][]
  • fix(c, cpp) stop a raw string's closing delimiter from swallowing quotes, issue #3585 [David Pavlovschii][]
  • enh(cmake) add block and endblock keywords [Anonymous Maarten][]
  • fix(cmake) only highlight standalone numbers, not digits that begin an identifier (e.g. 3rdparty), issue #4170 [Mark Xian][]
  • fix(cpp) require a word boundary before numeric literals so digits inside identifiers aren't highlighted as numbers, issue #4231 [Mark Xian][]
  • fix(crystal) stop treating integer division // as a regex literal [Zain Asif][]
  • enh(csharp) support digit separators in binary literals and numeric type suffixes, and stop highlighting the leading _ of an identifier, issue #4258 [Sarath Francis][]
  • enh(css) add corner-shape properties [Hama Tanveer][]
  • enh(css) support six-digit unicode-range values [Konstantin Baltsat][]
  • enh(dart) add highlighting for class and function names [guuido][]
  • enh(dns) highlight registered CAA property tags, issue #4475 [Joey Huang][]
  • enh(dns) improve grammar: character strings, TXT, classes, escapes, addresses [Checconio][]
  • enh(dos) add batch as an alias, issue #4395 [Hashim Khan][]
  • enh(gherkin) update keyword list [Hirse][]
  • enh(gherkin) variables can't contain whitespace [Hirse][]
  • enh(gherkin) docstrings can use backticks [Hirse][]
  • enh(go) recognize binary integer literals [spokodev][]
  • enh(groovy) support underscores in numeric literals [greymoth][]
  • fix(haskell) highlight where in GADT and closed type-family declarations, issue #3753 [Konstantin Baltsat][]
  • enh(java) improve detection of types, including generic and array types [Hannes Wallnoefer][]
  • enh(javascript) add self to built-in variables [Dsaquel][]
  • enh(kotlin) add ktm and ktx aliases [DarkMatter-999][]
  • fix(leaf) fix bug in Leaf keyword highlighting [Francesco Paolo Severino][]
  • fix(lisp) preserve highlighting after quoted multiplication expressions [arturict][]

... (truncated)

Updates `react` from 19.2.4 to 19.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from react's releases.

19.3.0 (September 9, 2026)

Below is a list of all new features, APIs, and bug fixes.

Read the React 19.3 release post for more information.

New React Features

  • <ViewTransition />: Adds <ViewTransition /> and addTransitionType APIs to power View Transition animations in React (@​sebmarkbage, @​jackpope, @​gaearon: #31975, #31987, #31996, #31999, #32001, #32002, #32028, #32029, #32031, #32034, #32038, #32041, #32050, #32090, #32105, #32254, #32379, #32422, #32462, #32540, #32545, #32585, #32599, #32611, #32612, #32617, #32651, #32653, #32656, #32664, #32699, #32723, #32734, #32751, #32752, #32760, #32761, #32764, #32772, #32790, #32819, #32820, #32822, #32833, #32849, #33094, #33191, #33200, #33206, #33293, #33330, #33331, #33332, #33357, #33362, #33433, #33576, #34374, #34450, #34481, #34500, #34502, #34510, #34511, #34539, #35567, #35564, #35485, #35380, #35063, #35060, #34676, #36917, #35337, #35520)
  • Fragment Refs: Add Refs to <Fragment /> to support composable platform behavior (@​jackpope, @​sebmarkbage, @​eps1lon, @​Dhakshin2007, @​chirokas, @​teamleaderleo, @​fallintoplace: #32465, #32613, #32619, #32654, #32660, #32682, #32722, #32813, #32814, #33056, #33058, #33093, #34069, #34103, #34544, #34545, #37062, #37061, #37060, #36047, #36010, #35642, #35641, #35637, #35630, #34935, #37457, #37408, #37326, #37251, #37171, #37169, #37168, #37167, #37166, #37165, #37164, #37163, #37162, #37161, #37160, #37125, #37063)

New React DOM Features

  • browser(): a new react-dom API that returns a usable which errors during server rendering and resolves in the browser. use(browser()) inside a <Suspense> boundary marks a subtree as browser-only without reporting a recoverable error (@​gnoff: #37143, #37241)
    • Added an onBrowserBailout option to the react-dom/server APIs to observe when a subtree defers to the browser (@​gnoff #37193)

Notable changes

  • Enable Trusted Types API integration (@​rickhanlonii #35816)
  • Transitions now render independently instead of being entangled into a single render, so a slow transition no longer holds up unrelated ones (@​acdlite #37290)
  • Added a DEV-only warning when a component appears to have been unblocked by calling use() conditionally (@​hoxyq, @​eps1lon: #37104, #37203, #37491)

All Changes

React

  • Fast Refresh Fixes
    • Fix Fast Refresh to find and remount edits to components wrapped behind lazy() (@​sophiebits #36965)
    • Fix Fast Refresh so edits to a memo() comparison function take effect (@​sophiebits #36964)
    • Fix Fast Refresh crash when an edit changes the kind of a component's type (@​sophiebits #36963)
    • Unify hot reload type resolution for Fast Refresh (@​sophiebits #36962)
    • Fix Fast Refresh to remount correctly when an edit changes the component kind (@​sophiebits #36950)
    • Double invoke effects in StrictMode after Fast Refresh (@​eps1lon #35962)
  • Performance Track Fixes
    • Prevent crash when accessing $$typeof in Performance Tracks (@​eps1lon #35679)
    • Handle non-string function names in Performance Tracks (@​eps1lon #35659)
    • Use minus (-) instead of en dash for removed props in Performance Tracks (@​eps1lon #35649)
    • Handle arrays with bigints in deep objects in Performance Tracks (@​eps1lon #35648)
    • Don't enumerate typed array props in Performance Tracks in DEV (@​UditDewan #36913)
    • Bail out of diffing wide objects and arrays in Performance Tracks (@​eps1lon #34742)
    • Clear potentially large performance measures in DEV (@​hoxyq #34803)
    • Fix missing else branch for renders with no props change in Performance Tracks (@​hoxyq #34837)
  • Activity Fixes
    • Fix useSyncExternalStore missing store mutations that happened while an Activity tree was hidden (@​sophiebits #36947)
    • Hide portal contents when an Activity is hidden (@​acdlite #35091)
    • Prevent metadata hoisting in hidden <Activity> trees (@​ronnakamoto #34983)
    • Prevent errors thrown inside a hidden Activity from escaping to the visible UI (@​acdlite #35074)
    • Don't unhide a node if a direct parent Offscreen is still hidden (@​sebmarkbage #34821)
    • Don't show internal <Offscreen> component in error messages (@​rickhanlonii #35763)
  • Warn in DEV when a component appears to have been unblocked by a conditional use() (@​hoxyq, @​eps1lon: #37104, #37203, #37491)
  • Render transitions independently instead of entangling them into a single render (@​acdlite #37290)

prs.title: docs(plugins): document the Discord plugin and its acceptance run
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Issue 10999 asks for the official Discord plugin to be documented under its real package name and proven end to end from a published binary. This adds the operator page and the maintainer runbook for that. It is a draft until the pieces it documents have merged (listed below).
  - `channels/discord.md` gains "Running Discord as a plugin (experimental)": what the host needs, install and bind (`zeroclaw plugin install discord --channel-alias main --egress declared`, or `plugin bind` for an installed package), why the grant is `discord.com` plus `*.discord.gg`, the instance key for the alias `main`, the token through the masked `config set` prompt, turning plugins on, routing `plugin.main` to an agent, a peer group that admits numeric user IDs, what to check once it runs, and a comparison with the built-in channel. A callout warns against giving one bot token to both.
  - `plugins/distributing-plugins.md` gains "Package names and Cargo features": the registry package is `discord`; `channel-discord` is the Cargo feature that compiles the built-in channel; FND-001 and FND-004 say `channel-discord` and `channel-discord.wasm` for what is now the `discord` package. It also tells publishers to keep a package's name, because every instance key derives from it.
  - New `maintainers/plugin-release-acceptance.md`: the acceptance runbook. It covers recording the environment, installing by name, binding, and exercising the plugin. A 14-row evidence template (inbound, outbound, built-in channel idle, negative control, reconnect, shutdown, denied destination and recovery, denied sender, missing platform permission, invalid token, trust policy) is followed by redaction, posting, and cleanup. The page is registered in `SUMMARY.md` and the maintainers index.
- **Scope boundary:** Docs only, English source only; translations follow the normal sync. No edits to FND-001 or FND-004, which are ratified; the distribution guide records the mapping instead. No edits to pages that say release binaries ship without the plugin host, which the #10994 work owns, or to the binding docs #11302 adds.
- **Blast radius:** four existing pages gain a section or a line; one new page.
- **Current prerequisites and merge hold** (the PR remains draft):
  - #11302 is merged; its binding commands, readiness report and linked `binding-a-channel-instance` heading are now in this receiving source.
  - #11303 and #11348 are merged; the documented polling, shutdown and guest-health lifecycle is in public master.
  - #11304's WebSocket-denial record remains a prerequisite. Its current `95dcb66` CI is green, but current review and landing remain separate. #11228's selected host baseline likewise still needs its protected Runtime-owner review and landing.
  - The original [Discord port #161](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins/pull/161) is ready for review on `985702c`, with #160 merged. It intentionally remains `registry = false` against `wit/next`; source/CI does not establish package publication.
  - A compatible published host archive and a separately reviewed released-WIT/Discord registry promotion are required before install by name. Published v0.8.5 lacks the port's required WebSocket contract; current registry/release assets contain no Discord package.
  - Actual published-pair acceptance still needs all 14 redacted observations. Every evidence cell in this PR remains blank; no current host, guest or live Discord result is credited here.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10999. Related #7432 (R6).

### Current source reconciliation

Signed `26b216a43451d1860191a6aff4300a685c210c51` normally merges public master `996355b83c403e8e9b8080dff5f9b75cea188459` into the original docs topic. The merge was clean, with no manual source changes: four whole author pages, the original SUMMARY insertion, all master entries and all 14 blank acceptance rows are preserved. The binding anchor comes from already-merged #11302. No #11228 or #11304 feature parent was added.

Root and independent static review checked all 15 added links and their headings against this receiving source. These are source checks, not a built-book or live-command result. #11310 subsequently landed as `266ce2e`; its public signer changes are reconciled as current-master context for the actual tested CI merge. [Automatic Quality Gate 38499975529](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38499975529) is qualifying this new head. Its actual checkout, selectors, results and skipped work will be reported separately; older `25d38658` CI and author-local checks supply no successor execution credit. No local Rust, docs helper or live Discord command was run for this publication.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can talk to Discord in two ways: the Discord support built into the program, or a Discord plugin installed separately that runs in a sandbox and can reach only the servers you allow. This PR explains how to set up the plugin, how it differs from the built-in support, and how maintainers prove the published plugin installs and runs on a released copy of ZeroClaw before telling people it works.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional: read the new section in `channels/discord.md` and the new runbook. The commands can only be run once the dependencies above merge.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Documentation source review. The operator CLI and Discord workflow are instructions for a future qualified run, currently NOTRUN.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Read the five changed pages. Live testing needs the exact compatible published host/package pair, dedicated test bot and explicit grants described in the runbook.
- **Steps to review:** Check the binding link and the package/config/egress guidance, then confirm that the evidence template keeps all 14 outcomes and redaction requirements.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The Discord operator guide and maintainer acceptance runbook are linked from the book; the binding anchor resolves in receiving source.
- **Prior behavior (before):** These operator and acceptance instructions were absent; the earlier topic also lacked the merged binding anchor.


### Follow-up: invalid-token acceptance control

The invalid-token row now requires a syntactically valid invalid or revoked
token entered through the masked prompt. It distinguishes Discord's
authentication refusal from malformed-token rejection during local
configuration. The evidence cells remain blank; this change records no new
live acceptance result.

Validation for `25d38658`:

- Full-file `docs_quality_gate.sh` on the changed runbook: zero lint errors.
- `docs_links_gate.sh` against parent `7b4e389d`: all six collector controls
  passed; no added links.
- Only the runbook's invalid-token row changed. The PR remains draft with
  the same declared merge and publication prerequisites.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Docs Style` (markdown lint, prose em-dash check, added-link and all-internal-link gates).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the link gates strip `#fragments`, so anchors are unchecked in CI. I checked them separately (below).
- **Commands run and tail output:** Historical author-local report from before the `26b216a` receiving publication, on macOS 26 (aarch64). These commands were not repeated by Root and are not current receiving-head execution evidence.

```text
$ BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.
Linting: 4 file(s)
Summary: 0 error(s)
$ BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
Collected 9 added link(s) from 5 docs file(s).
Checked 9 local docs link target(s).
No added HTTP(S) links detected in changed docs lines.
$ python3 scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py
Checked authored Markdown links in 218 file(s); no broken local targets.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Historical author checks follow. Current static source/link preservation is recorded above; the older missing-anchor exception is resolved by the public-master import.
  - Every anchor link in the changed pages resolves against the source headings, except `plugins/index.md#binding-a-channel-instance`, which #11302 adds.
  - `git merge-tree` against the heads of #11302, #11262, #11310, #11311, #11284, #11303, #11304, and #11348: clean.
  - Each runtime claim was checked against `master` source:
    - plugin senders are matched exactly (`plugin_sender_allowed` in `plugin_runtime.rs`);
    - the `channel inbound message` and `reply delivered` records run inside a scope carrying `channel = plugin.<alias>`;
    - `/health` names the component `channel:plugin.<alias>`; on `master` it tracks only the listener, and with #11348 (head `de4f86dca6`) it reads `error` on a failed poll and otherwise follows the plugin's health check, which is what the page states;
    - conversation history is keyed by channel and alias, so `plugin.main` and `discord.main` do not share conversations;
    - the instance keys are `zpi1_` plus base64url of `["discord","channel","<alias>"]`;
    - only a Cranelift build compiles `.wasm`;
    - the sender refusal key is `plugin_channel_sender_denied`;
    - an unsigned package is skipped at discovery under `strict`.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** a full `cargo mdbook build` was not run; the change adds no preprocessor directives, and the book is built on `master` by `docs-deploy`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: All No. The docs tell operators to enter the bot token only at the masked prompt, and the runbook requires a dedicated test bot, a token reset afterwards, and redaction of user, server, and channel IDs and message text before evidence is posted. The example IDs are placeholders.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** N/A (docs only).


## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. The original PR, topic, author and review history are preserved.

prs.title: fix(runtime): estimate context usage when provider omits token counts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - ZeroCode's context meter stayed blank for agents on local OpenAI-compatible providers (llama.cpp) even though Anthropic/OpenAI/xAI showed correct usage. Those servers routinely omit `usage`, so the meter had a budget but no numerator.
  - The **previous revision of this PR** filled `TurnEvent::Usage.input_tokens` with a local history estimate. That field is the canonical *measured-usage* surface: the gateway sums it into billing totals, RPC emits it as `context_usage`, and the ACP session store persists it as a durable token count. Publishing a derived value there gave one provider call two contradictory token truths and durably stored estimates indistinguishable from measured usage.
  - **This revision keeps `input_tokens` strictly provider-reported** and carries the estimate on a new, display-only `TurnEvent::Usage.estimated_input_tokens`:
    - Accounting and persistence read `input_tokens`, which stays `None` exactly when the provider reported nothing. The gateway usage fold ignores the estimate explicitly; ACP persistence cannot see it.
    - The RPC `context_usage` surface uses the estimate as its display numerator and labels provenance via a new `input_tokens_source` (`provider` | `estimate`), reusing the existing `TokenCountSource` vocabulary.
  - For cached-only responses, the measured total remains unknown and the display estimate is `max(history_estimate, cached_input_tokens)`, so the meter cannot show less than the known cached subset.
- **Scope boundary:** Carries estimate provenance through ZeroCode and marks estimated counts and percentages with `~`. Does not change runtime-profile budget resolution or provider pricing/cost accounting. Does not add provider-side usage parsing for llama.cpp. Does not alter billing totals, the per-(provider, model) breakdown, or ACP persisted token counts.
- **Blast radius:** `TurnEvent::Usage` producers/consumers (runtime turn loop, gateway WS usage fold, RPC `context_usage`, ACP token persistence), plus the ZeroCode client, state, and status-bar renderer. Estimated values appear only on the labelled display path, only when the provider omits usage.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to prior context-meter work using runtime-profile budget (#8872); no dedicated issue closed by this PR.
- **Labels (live snapshot):** `bug`, `agent`, `channel`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `principal contributor`, `channel:core`, `risk:medium`, `zerocode`, `size:L`, `channel:acp`, `breaking-change` (milestone: `v0.9.0`)

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `rpc` (`session/update` → `context_usage`), `tui` (ZeroCode status bar meter)
- **Setup / preconditions:** Agent bound to a local llama.cpp (or other OpenAI-compatible) provider that omits `usage`; ZeroCode connected to the daemon
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Open ZeroCode with the local-model agent
  2. Send any prompt and wait for the turn to complete
  3. Observe the bottom status-bar context meter, and the `context_usage` notification on the RPC stream
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The meter shows a numerator sourced from the estimate, and the notification carries `"input_tokens_source":"estimate"`
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Same steps leave the meter without a numerator for llama.cpp; cloud providers are unaffected

### How I tested

- **Head tested:** `37d0b4481ed8a81a8dfdbfa021460f957d5dd5df`
- **Current-head CI update:** At `37d0b4481ed8a81a8dfdbfa021460f957d5dd5df`, `Test`, `Security`, and `CI Required Gate` pass, with no failed or pending checks. The advisory Windows jobs were skipped. The failed-gate discussion below describes the earlier tested head.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI compiles and tests `zeroclaw-runtime`, `zeroclaw-api`, `zeroclaw-gateway`, `zeroclaw-channels`, and `zerocode`. The workspace Test job includes ZeroCode and excludes the desktop app.
- **Historical required-gate result at `a9b73ae2d`:** `CI Required Gate` is **failed**, because `Security` is failed. The `Security` failure is `RUSTSEC-2026-0292` in `imbl-sized-chunks v0.1.3`, reached transitively through `matrix-sdk -> eyeball-im -> imbl` (a dev-dependency of `zeroclaw-channels`). This is **not** introduced by this PR and is not fixable inside it:
  - This diff changes no dependency manifest — `git diff upstream/master -- '*Cargo.toml' '*Cargo.lock' 'deny.toml' '.cargo/*'` is empty, and the string `imbl` does not appear in the diff.
  - The same advisory fails on `master` itself at `c1e79a774` (the exact commit this branch merges), in `Quality Gate` run `35585963039` and `Daily Advisory Scan` run `35581901209`.
  - `deny.toml` already carries a deliberate ignore for the sibling advisory `RUSTSEC-2026-0247` (`bitmaps`) on the *same* `matrix-sdk -> eyeball-im -> imbl` chain, with an upstream tracking link. Whether to ignore, or wait for a `matrix-sdk` release off the `imbl` stack, is a maintainer security decision and is deliberately not taken unilaterally in a context-meter PR.
  - Every other check at this head is green, including `Test`, `Lint`, `Format`, `Zerocode RPC Boundary`, `Semgrep`, `CodeQL`, and the channel test matrix.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** No live llama.cpp + ZeroCode session was run in this environment (no local model server available). See the interface-evidence note below for exactly what was and was not exercised.
- **Commands run and observed results:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                     # clean
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-gateway \
    -p zeroclaw-channels -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings   # no warnings
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets # clean

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime  --lib   # 4985 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api      --lib   #  270 passed, 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway  --lib   #  612 passed, 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib   # 1948 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored
$ cargo test --locked -p zerocode                  # 1308 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored
```

  New coverage in this revision:

```text
producer  cached_only_usage_floors_the_display_estimate_at_the_cached_minimum
producer  cached_floor_does_not_cap_a_larger_history_estimate
rpc       cached_only_usage_forwards_a_numerator_at_or_above_its_cached_subset
rpc       unknown_total_without_an_estimate_stays_absent
client    parse_context_usage_decodes_the_estimate_provenance_marker
client    parse_context_usage_decodes_the_provider_provenance_marker
state     context_usage_provenance_travels_with_the_count_it_describes
widget    estimated_count_renders_an_approximation_marker
widget    provider_reported_count_renders_without_an_approximation_marker
widget    unknown_provenance_is_not_marked_approximate
widget    estimated_count_without_a_denominator_is_still_marked
tui       status_bar_marks_estimated_context_and_not_measured_context
tui       approximation_marker_does_not_shift_status_bar_layout
```

- **Reconciliation with the previous review's validation:** That review observed `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` abort on a stack overflow in `tools::send_message_to_peer::tests::peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`, and could not complete `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` because `glib-sys` could not find `glib-2.0` via `pkg-config`. Neither reproduced in this environment at the head above: the full runtime lib suite completed with 4652 passed / 0 failed, and the workspace check completed successfully. Both are environment-sensitive (thread stack size; system library availability), so this is recorded as a difference in observation, not as a refutation.

- **Interface evidence — User-Boundary Proof (final interface, exact head):**

  *User action:* a turn completes on a provider that omits `usage`, so the runtime supplies a labelled estimate; ZeroCode renders the status-bar context meter.

  *Boundary:* the ZeroCode TUI status bar, rendered through the production `draw_status_bar` renderer into real terminal cells (not a component snapshot). Exercised by `app::tests::status_bar_marks_estimated_context_and_not_measured_context` and `app::tests::approximation_marker_does_not_shift_status_bar_layout`.

  *Environment:* `TestBackend` terminal, 100x1 for the capture below and 80/100/120 columns for the layout assertion; default locale.

  *Observed result* (final terminal cells, exact head `37d0b4481`):

```text
measured (provider) | ctx:  100,000 / 200,000  [████████░░░░░░│░]   50%                                 tui-1 ● Connected|
estimated           | ctx: ~100,000 / 200,000  [████████░░░░░░│░]  ~50%                                 tui-1 ● Connected|
```

  The estimated row is marked `~` on both the count and the percentage; the measured row is not. The tests compare those two states of the new renderer at 80, 100, and 120 columns. They establish visible estimate markers, but do not prove layout parity with the previous revision: the known-denominator label grows by two columns. With a production-length TUI ID and Browse active, source inspection identifies percentage-suffix clipping at 83 and 84 columns. No actual-terminal screenshot covers that state.

  *Upstream of the client*, the serialized `session/update` frames the TUI consumes:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"input_tokens":100,"input_tokens_source":"provider","max_context_tokens":180000,"model_context_window":200000,"session_id":"s1","type":"context_usage"}}

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"input_tokens":4200,"input_tokens_source":"estimate","max_context_tokens":180000,"model_context_window":200000,"session_id":"s1","type":"context_usage"}}
```

  *Not exercised:* a live llama.cpp session driving a real terminal. There is no local model server in this environment. The boundary above is the production renderer with a synthetic event, not a screenshot of a live session.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
  - Corrected from the previous revision, where this answer was `No` while the tests in fact carried an identity-shaped agent alias (`melfina`). Those fixtures now use the neutral `test_agent` placeholder per `docs/book/src/contributing/privacy.md`. Verified: `git diff upstream/master | grep melfina` returns nothing.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`No` — Rust API only; wire format is compatible)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- **Upgrade steps for existing users:**
  - `zeroclaw-api` is a published crate. `TurnEvent` is `#[non_exhaustive]` at the enum level, but the `Usage` **variant** is not, so adding `estimated_input_tokens` is a breaking change for out-of-workspace code that constructs `TurnEvent::Usage` with a struct literal or destructures it without `..`. Such code must add `estimated_input_tokens` (use `None` to preserve current behavior) or switch to `..`. All in-workspace sites are updated in this PR.
  - Wire compatibility is preserved: `input_tokens_source` is `Option` with `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`, so existing `context_usage` payloads are unchanged when no provenance is known, and older clients ignore the new field.
  - **Open question for reviewers:** marking the `Usage` variant `#[non_exhaustive]` would make future field additions non-breaking, at the cost of blocking external struct-literal construction. Deliberately not done here to keep this PR's contract change reviewable; happy to add it if preferred.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After squash merge, retrieve the landed commit with `gh pr view 9453 --repo zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw --json mergeCommit --jq '.mergeCommit.oid'`, then revert that SHA on a rollback branch and submit a revert PR.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `None`. The estimate is unconditional whenever an accepted response has no provider `input_tokens`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - *Wire:* `session/update` frames of `"type":"context_usage"` carrying `"input_tokens_source":"estimate"`. A revert removes the `input_tokens_source` field entirely and restores an absent numerator for usage-omitting providers.
  - *Meter:* context meter numerators that move without a corresponding provider usage report; the estimate can undercount tool-heavy requests because it excludes separately supplied native tool schemas, and the heuristic can err in either direction.
  - *Accounting:* billing totals, the gateway per-(provider, model) breakdown, and ACP `token_count` must **not** move as a result of this change. If any of them shift for a usage-omitting provider, the display/measured separation has been violated — that is the primary regression to watch for.
  - **Persistence note:** unlike the previous revision of this PR, a revert here has no durable-data cleanup problem. Estimates are never written to the ACP session store (`estimated_usage_is_never_persisted_as_a_session_token_count` covers this), so no derived values can be left behind misrecorded as measured usage.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A

prs.title: feat(config): make secret key/value maps editable in zerocode and dashboard
prs.body: ## Summary - **Base branch:** `master` - **What changed and why:** - MCP server `env` could not be added from zerocode or the dashboard. The backend stored, encrypted, and passed it to the stdio child, but the `Configurable` derive only emitted one `.` property per *existing* key, so an empty map produced no rows and no surface could add the first entry. The same applied to every `#[secret] HashMap`: MCP `headers`, provider `extra_headers`, `observability.otel_headers`, plugin `config`, file-transfer `headers`. - Add `PropKind::SecretMap`: the derive now always emits a container row per secret string map (display = sorted key names only, never values), followed by entry rows in stable sorted order. - Setting an entry to `""` now removes it, so a non-interactive empty-value `config set` or the dashboard `remove` op drops the key on disk instead of leaving `KEY = ""` (an empty env var exported to the MCP child). Writing the bare container path is rejected with guidance. - zerocode gains a `[+ Add entry]` two-step (name, then masked value) flow; the dashboard renders entries inside a container block with an inline add control. - Classify these maps `encrypted_secret`: the credential audit now reaches them because the container rows always exist. - **Scope boundary:** No change to how MCP servers are spawned or how secrets are encrypted. Does not migrate other `Vec` sections, does not touch the stale `docs/dashboard-mcp-per-field-todo.md`, and only adds English strings (other locales via `cargo fluent fill`). - **Blast radius:** Every config surface built on `prop_fields()` (RPC `config/list`, gateway `/api/config/list`, CLI `config list`, dashboard `FieldForm`, zerocode config editor). New container rows appear in listings for these 8 fields. zerocode mirrors `PropKind` by hand, so a zerocode built before this PR cannot deserialize `config/list` from an upgraded daemon. - **Linked issue(s):** None found. ### What this does, simply Some config settings are lists of named secrets — e.g. the environment variables handed to a local MCP server (`GITHUB_TOKEN=...`) or HTTP headers sent to a remote one. ZeroClaw already supported these in `config.toml` and the CLI, but the zerocode and dashboard config editors could only show variables that already existed. A server with no env vars showed nothing to click, so you could not add the first one, and "deleting" one actually left it behind with an empty value. This PR makes each such setting always show up in both editors with an "add entry" control (name + hidden value), lists existing entries by name (values stay hidden and encrypted), and makes delete really remove an entry. Runtime behavior of MCP servers is unchanged. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes - **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (zerocode), `web` (dashboard), `cli` - **Setup / preconditions:** A config with one stdio MCP server and no `env`, e.g. `[[mcp.servers]] name = "fs"`, `command = "npx"`. - **Steps to run:** 1. zerocode: `/config` → `mcp.servers` → `fs`. Select the `env` row, Enter, type `API_TOKEN`, Enter, type a value, Enter. Then select `env.API_TOKEN` and delete the row. 2. Dashboard: Config → MCP servers → `fs`. Under **Env**, enter a name and value, click **Add entry**. Trash the entry, Save. 3. CLI: `zeroclaw config set mcp.servers.fs.env.API_TOKEN` (masked), then `zeroclaw config set --no-interactive mcp.servers.fs.env.API_TOKEN ""`, inspecting `config.toml` after each. - **Expected on this branch (after):** An `env` row is shown even when empty; the entry is added, listed by name only, stored encrypted in `config.toml`; delete removes the key from `config.toml` entirely. - **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** No `env` row exists for a server with no env vars in either UI (nothing to add from); removing an entry through the property API leaves `API_TOKEN = ""` in the file. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Required CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36952286607) passes on `63150af34`. The Test job includes empty-map container emission, secret-safe add/list/remove, encrypted persistence and removal, and the zerocode two-step RPC flow. The local results below remain the author-reported validation. - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The [author walkthrough](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11419#issuecomment-6156575739) shows addition in zerocode, visibility in the dashboard, dashboard removal, and absence again in zerocode. It does not demonstrate dashboard addition or capture the masked input prompt. The zerocode two-step flow has automated coverage; dashboard helper tests cover grouping and validation. - **Commands run and tail output:** ```text $ cargo fmt --all -- --check # clean $ cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings exit=0 $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config test result: ok. 1761 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --features schema-export --lib -- schema_markdown test result: ok. 16 passed; 0 failed $ cargo test -p zerocode test result: ok. 1395 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-macros test result: ok. 12 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- config test result: ok. 305 passed; 0 failed (x2) $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway test result: FAILED. 637 passed; 1 failed tests::run_gateway_starts_with_mismatched_provider_api_key — fails identically on master in this environment: "config lifecycle is already owned at ~/.zeroclaw/data/config-lifecycle.lock" (collides with a locally running daemon); unrelated. $ cargo fluent check --catalog zerocode # ok for en/es/fr/ja/zh-CN $ (web) node --test …secretMap.logic.test.ts (in `npm test` main group) ℹ tests 32 ℹ pass 32 ℹ fail 0 $ (web) npx tsc -b 134 errors both with and without this change, none in touched files (pre-existing: missing `react-test-renderer` etc. in local node_modules) ``` One run of `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- config` failed `configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock`; it passes in isolation on both master and this branch and in two subsequent full filtered runs — timing flake under parallel load. - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests at the behavior boundary: empty map emits a `SecretMap` container row with `encrypted_secret` class; add/list/remove via `set_prop` never leaks values into any display; `set_prop_persistent` + `save_dirty` writes the added key encrypted and removing it drops the key from disk; container writes are rejected; zerocode two-step flow sends `config/set` for `mcp.servers.acme.env.API_TOKEN` against a scripted fake daemon and refuses invalid names / empty values without RPC; dashboard grouping/validation logic; generated docs show per-entry `config set .`. **Visually verified in zerocode** (`/config` → `mcp.servers` → `localrag`, see Visual Evidence): on `master` the server's field list has no `env` or `headers` row; on this branch both appear as `[+ Add entry]`. **Later real-editor evidence:** the [October 13 walkthrough](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11419#issuecomment-6156575739) shows a disposable `FOOBAR` entry added in zerocode, visible in the dashboard, removed there, and absent again in zerocode. Dashboard addition and the masked input prompt are not shown. - **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `63150af34`; automated tests and original zerocode before/after screenshots. The October 13 author walkthrough reports running the unchanged branch with an isolated copied config and a separate gateway port, using zerocode and the dashboard. - **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** see Visual Evidence section - **Action or changed state and observed result:** See test list above. - **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `npm run check:generated` / `cargo web check` not run: generated API files are gitignored build output and `PropKind` is not part of the exported schema (gateway emits `kind` as a string). `./dev/ci.sh all` not run; per-crate suites above cover the changed crates. ## Visual Evidence: old behavior new behavior ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No - New external network calls? No - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No - If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Secret maps gain a listing row and a removal path. The container row exposes only key names (already visible in entry row paths), is marked `is_secret` so the RPC/gateway omit its value, and tests assert no secret value appears in any display string. Values are still encrypted at rest via `SecretStore` (asserted on disk). Eight fields gain explicit `encrypted_secret` classification, matching their existing encryption. ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? No (client/daemon skew only) - Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No - Upgrade steps: Upgrade zerocode together with the daemon — an older zerocode fails to deserialize `config/list` once it contains the new `secret_map` kind. Behavior change: setting a secret-map entry to an empty value (including removal through the editors) now removes the entry instead of storing `""`; an intentionally empty env var / header is no longer expressible through the property API (hand-edit `config.toml`). `config.toml` format is unchanged. ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) - **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 63150af34` (single commit; no data migration — `config.toml` format unchanged). - **Feature flags or config toggles:** None - **Observable failure symptoms:** zerocode config pane failing to load (`config/list` deserialize error, unknown variant `secret_map`); dashboard env/headers block missing or add failing with a `ConfigApiError`; `config set …env.` errors.

Updates `libc` from 0.2.189 to 0.2.190
Release notes

Sourced from libc's releases.

0.2.190

There is now a single config for enabling 64-bit time_t: libc_unstable_time64. This can be set unconditionally; it opts in to 64-bit time_t on the following platforms that use 32-bit by default:

  • 32-bit Linux-GNU
  • 32-bit Linux-uClibc
  • 32-bit Linux-musl. Note that setting this flag also enables some other changes that happend in musl v1.2.
  • 32-bit Windows-GNU
  • ESP-IDF (all targets with this environment are 32-bit)

Most other 32-bit platforms are either already using 64-bit time_t, or are considered legacy and will not be gaining support from their upstream maintainers.

You can enable this using RUSTFLAGS:

RUSTFLAGS='--cfg=libc_unstable_time64' cargo ...

Note that there may still be some changes to features gated by this config option, hence "unstable" in its name. In the near future we will rename it to just libc_time64. Until then, please test it out and report any bugs you find!

Support

  • Add initial support for HelenOS (#4355)

Added

We are slowly filling out the Default implementations, to reduce the need for mem::zeroed() in user code:

  • Unix: Implement Default for a number of structs, especially on Apple platforms (#5576)
  • Linux, NetBSD: Give statvfs a Default impl (#5583)

prs.title: fix(security): apply configured firejail_args to the Firejail wrapper
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `FirejailSandbox` used to be a unit struct, and `wrap_invocation` built a fixed argument list. Configured `firejail_args` never reached the firejail command line, even though the risk-profile schema accepts them and `security status` feeds them into the sandbox config. The struct now holds validated extra arguments. `create_selected_sandbox` builds it through `FirejailSandbox::with_args(&sandbox.firejail_args)` on both the explicit-backend path and the auto-detect path. The arguments go after the wrapper's own flags and hardening flags, and before the wrapped invocation, so firejail reads them as its own options and not as arguments to the target command.
  - Validation follows the maintainer decision on #11594. An entry is rejected if it is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, is `--`, isn't a single `--option` / `--option=value` (for example `none` or `-q`), or names an option that would undo the wrapper. The rejected options are `--profile` (the wrapper sets `--noprofile`), `--include`, `--ignore` (it can drop the wrapper's flags), `--private` / `--private=…` (the wrapper sets `--private=home`; `--private-tmp`, `--private-etc=…` and similar are still allowed), `--allow-debuggers`, `--join`, `--join-or-start`, `--join-network`, `--join-filesystem`, `--chroot` / `--chroot=…` (chroot mode clears Firejail's `--noroot` and skips the private home setup, undoing the wrapper's `--noroot` and `--private=home`), `--seccomp-error-action=log` (logging executes the syscall instead of preserving seccomp denial), and every `--keep-dev-*` option (`--keep-dev-shm`, `--keep-dev-ntsync`, `--keep-dev-tpm`), which Firejail documents as re-exposing host devices or the host `/dev/shm` even with the `--private-dev` the wrapper requires. Option names may contain dots (`--seccomp.block-secondary`, `--caps.drop=…`): each dot-separated segment must start with a letter or digit, so `--seccomp.`, `--.x` and `--a..b` are still rejected. The name grammar and the conflict check are separate steps.
  - If Firejail is selected but its arguments are rejected, the sandbox becomes `RejectedFirejailArgsSandbox`. It refuses every command (`wrap_command` / `check_initialization` return `InvalidInput` with the reason), the same way `FailedSeatbeltSandbox` does. It does not fall back to running without the arguments or to `NoopSandbox`, since either would present the configured hardening as active when it isn't.
  - `sandbox_posture`, which feeds `security status`, now describes the active Firejail backend as "Firejail selected, but firejail_args were rejected; commands are blocked (…reason…)". Before, it described a configuration that wouldn't be applied.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR doesn't touch #11538 / #11539 (the hard-coded `--private=home` / `--nowheel` launch failures) or the docs change in #11591. It doesn't edit the schema doc comment or the generated `config.md`. `firejail_args` still has no effect when another backend is active (Landlock, Bubblewrap, and so on), which matches its documented meaning ("when sandbox_backend resolves to firejail").
- **Blast radius:** Linux, and only when Firejail is the selected sandbox backend. With empty `firejail_args` (the default and all presets) the firejail command line is byte-for-byte the same as before; a test covers this. A profile that has non-empty `firejail_args` gets them applied now. If they're invalid, its shell commands are refused with the reason and no longer run without them.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11594

### What this does, simply

A risk profile can list extra Firejail options in `firejail_args` (for example `--net=none`), but ZeroClaw silently ignored them while still reporting them back. Now they're actually passed to firejail. Options that would break or weaken ZeroClaw's own Firejail setup, or that aren't Firejail options at all, are rejected with a clear message. In that case commands are blocked, not run as if the hardening applied, and the sandbox status says so.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The new behavior is in command construction and backend selection, which the unit tests cover without needing firejail installed. A live Firejail smoke test would add signal, but I couldn't run one here (see below).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The Rust test and lint jobs run the `zeroclaw-runtime` unit tests, which include the new `security::firejail` and `security::detect` tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Nothing exercises a real firejail binary. The non-Linux `cfg` branches (where firejail isn't compiled) were only checked by reading them: I don't have a macOS/Windows target installed, so CI's cross-platform jobs are the check for those.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux x86_64):
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- security::firejail security::detect`
    ```
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_wrap_passes_configured_args_before_the_wrapped_command ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_wrap_without_configured_args_is_unchanged ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_accepts_single_options_with_and_without_values ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_rejects_args_that_are_not_options_or_undo_the_wrapper ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_with_args_reports_rejected_args_before_probing ... ok
    test security::detect::tests::selected_firejail_with_rejected_args_blocks_commands_instead_of_dropping_them ... ok
    test security::detect::tests::firejail_posture_reports_rejected_args ... ok
    test result: ok. 43 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5663 filtered out; finished in 0.03s
    ```
  - `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-runtime -- --check`: clean
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings`: no findings in `security/firejail.rs` or `security/detect.rs`. The crate still fails clippy on lints that already exist on master with this box's newer toolchain: deprecated `fetch_update` in `rpc/upload.rs` and `rpc/dispatch.rs`, and `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `agent/turn/stream_guard.rs`. This PR doesn't touch those files.
  - Follow-up commit 806fc4b (review fixes: option-name validation, Fluent text, comment hygiene): `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- security:: i18n::` → `test result: ok. 405 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → passed; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` → no findings in `security/`.
  - Follow-up commit aca1e8ad (review fixes: reject `--keep-dev-*`, accept dotted option names). With only the validator change reverted, the two new tests fail:
    ```
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_rejects_args_that_reexpose_host_devices_despite_private_dev ... FAILED
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_accepts_dotted_options_and_passes_them_before_the_wrapped_command ... FAILED
    test result: FAILED. 19 passed; 2 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5688 filtered out
    ```
    With it: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::firejail` → `test result: ok. 21 passed; 0 failed` (including `firejail_rejects_malformed_dotted_option_names`), and `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::` → `test result: ok. 365 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings`: no findings in `security/`; it still stops on the same pre-existing toolchain lints listed above.
  - Final-command output at aca1e8ad (`cargo build --bin zeroclaw`, Debian 13 x86_64, `firejail` 0.9.74 installed so Firejail is the selected backend, `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`, temporary `HOME` and `--config-dir`, an agent whose risk profile sets `sandbox_enabled = true`, `sandbox_backend = "firejail"`). Only the `Sandbox:` line differs between the two runs; the full output is in the PR comment.
    ```
    # firejail_args = ["--keep-dev-shm"]
    $ zeroclaw security status --agent local
    Sandbox:    requested firejail, active firejail (Firejail selected, but firejail_args were rejected; commands are blocked (firejail_args rejected: --keep-dev-shm conflicts with the options ZeroClaw's Firejail wrapper sets))

    # firejail_args = ["--seccomp.block-secondary", "--net=none"]
    $ zeroclaw security status --agent local
    Sandbox:    requested firejail, active firejail (Linux user-space sandbox (requires firejail to be installed))
    ```
  - Follow-up commit f4af67eb (review fix: reject `--chroot`). With `--chroot` removed from the conflict list, the new test fails:
    ```
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_rejects_chroot_because_it_disables_noroot_and_private_home ... FAILED
    --chroot: ["--net=none", "--chroot"]
    test result: FAILED. 21 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5688 filtered out

    Sandbox:    requested firejail, active firejail (Firejail selected, but firejail_args were rejected; commands are blocked (firejail_args rejected: --chroot conflicts with the options ZeroClaw's Firejail wrapper sets))

Current [Quality Gate run 38342067128](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38342067128) completed successfully. Current PR checks report 45 successes and 8 skipped checks, with no failed or pending checks. This update relies on CI for this head; it does not claim a fresh local test or new final-command capture.

prs.title: fix(channels): wait out Telegram retry_after instead of retrying sendMessage into a 429
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `send_text_chunks` used to answer an HTTP 429 on the HTML `sendMessage` with an immediate plain-text `sendMessage`. That is a second request into the same flood limit, and it cannot help because the formatting was never the problem. A 429 now goes through a new `send_message_honoring_rate_limit` helper. The helper reads `parameters.retry_after`, waits that long, and resends the *same* body. It does this at most `TELEGRAM_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES` (2) times, and only while the wait is ≤ `TELEGRAM_MAX_INLINE_RETRY_AFTER` (60 s).
  - A penalty longer than 60 s, or a 429 that keeps coming after the retries, fails the chunk right away with `Telegram sendMessage rate limited (429 …)`. There is no plain-text attempt and no further request inside the window. A WARN event with `retry_after_secs` is logged. `SendChunksError` now carries `rate_limited: true` for this case. `finalize_send_chunks` then skips its resume. It returns `FinalizePartialDelivery` when some chunks were accepted. When none were, it returns a new `zeroclaw_api::channel::FinalizeUndelivered` error, which the orchestrator handles by not resending and not firing `message_sent`. Neither the resume nor the orchestrator's "send as new message" fallback sends inside the penalty window. Other failures keep the existing resume and fallback behavior.
  - Multi-message `finalize_draft` (follow-up dead5bd3): if the pending-narration send hits a flood limit, the loop stops right there. It makes no further narration attempts and skips the final-answer send and attachments, then returns `FinalizeUndelivered`. Narration chunks Telegram already accepted stay posted and aren't resent. Before this change the loop retried the narration up to `MULTI_MESSAGE_FINALIZE_RETRIES` times and then sent the final answer, all inside the penalty.
  - Non-429 failures (for example an HTML parse error) keep the existing markdown → plain fallback. If the plain request itself gets a 429, it waits and retries the same way.
- **Scope boundary:** this covers the `sendMessage` path only, which serves `send`, `finalize_send_chunks` and the orchestrator's "send as new message" fallback, since they all go through `send_text_chunks`. This suppresses fallback resends. It does not guarantee the streamed draft stays visible when finalization has already deleted it (the existing attachment and long-answer branches delete the draft before `finalize_send_chunks`). It does **not** change the `editMessageText` steps in `finalize_draft` (HTML edit → plain edit → delete+send). It does not add a durable requeue for penalties over 60 s, and it does not add adaptive `draft_update_interval_ms` backpressure. The triage comment suggests keeping that last one as a separate follow-up.
- **Blast radius:** Telegram outbound text sends, plus one new orchestrator finalize arm that only matches the new `FinalizeUndelivered` error. A reply that hits a short 429 is now delayed by `retry_after` instead of failing at once.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11615. This is the immediate-retry part of the send path; the finalize-edit path and the long-penalty queueing remain.

### What this does, simply

When Telegram says "too many requests, retry after N seconds", ZeroClaw used to resend the message right away as plain text. When that also failed, it gave up. Every extra request inside the penalty window makes Telegram extend the penalty, which matches the escalating `retry_after` values in the issue (536 s → 1390 s). Now ZeroClaw waits the time Telegram asks for and sends the same message again. If the wait is too long to do inline (over a minute), it stops instead of hammering, and it logs why.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behavior is covered by wiremock tests that return real Telegram 429 bodies; reproducing a real flood limit needs a throttled bot token.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test/lint jobs run `zeroclaw-channels` unit tests, which include the new tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live Telegram flood-limit check.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux x86_64, rustc 1.99.0 stable):
  - New tests fail on `master`. I ran them with the source change reverted:
    ```
    test telegram::tests::send_text_chunks_waits_retry_after_then_resends_same_format ... FAILED
    test telegram::tests::send_text_chunks_does_not_retry_inside_long_flood_penalty ... FAILED
    ... panicked at crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/telegram.rs: the resend must wait for retry_after
    ... panicked at crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/telegram.rs: sent 0 chunk(s) then failed: Telegram sendMessage failed (markdown 429 Too Many Requests: {...,"parameters":{"retry_after":536}}; plain 429 Too Many Requests: {...,"parameters":{"retry_after":536}})
    ```
  - With the change (follow-up commit 20c2c139, rebuilt on the current branch): `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib telegram`
    ```
    test result: ok. 405 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 1572 filtered out; finished in 8.87s
    ```
  - `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: passed. The first CI run failed it on the `Issue #11615` references in two test comments, which are now removed.
  - `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-channels -- --check`: clean
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args`: clean for `zeroclaw-channels`. The only error is a pre-existing `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` at `orchestrator/mod.rs:4845` (`.map(&fmt_sel)`), which this PR does not touch; it's reported by the rustc 1.99 clippy on this box. Without `--no-deps`, the same lint also fires in `zeroclaw-providers`.
  - Follow-up dead5bd3 plus a merge of current `master` (4e18dcff, no conflicts). It adds two new tests that go through `finalize_draft` in multi-message mode with pending narration: `finalize_draft_multi_message_stops_on_narration_flood_limit` (zero accepted prefix) and `..._after_accepted_prefix` (one narration chunk accepted, then `retry_after: 536`). With only the narration-loop change disabled, both fail:
    ```
    test telegram::tests::finalize_draft_multi_message_stops_on_narration_flood_limit ... FAILED
    test telegram::tests::finalize_draft_multi_message_stops_on_narration_flood_limit_after_accepted_prefix ... FAILED
    assertion `left == right` failed: no request after the flood-limited one ... left: 5 right: 2   (the final answer was sent)
    ```
    With it, on the merged tree: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib telegram::` gives `test result: ok. 379 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored`. `cargo fmt --all` is clean. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args -A deprecated` is clean (the two allowed lints only fire in pre-existing code with this box's rustc 1.99 toolchain). `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The new tests cover: a 429 with `retry_after: 1` followed by a 200 sends exactly two requests, both `parse_mode: HTML`, and the second waits ≥ 1 s; a 429 with `retry_after: 536` sends exactly one request and returns `delivered == 0` with a "rate limited" error; a 429 that keeps coming sends exactly 1 + `TELEGRAM_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES` requests, all HTML; a 429 on the plain-text fallback waits and resends the identical plain body; a rate-limited `finalize_send_chunks` with nothing accepted returns `FinalizeUndelivered` (not `FinalizePartialDelivery`) after one request; a flood limit during multi-message pending narration stops finalization with no further request, never sends the final answer, posts an accepted narration chunk exactly once, and returns `FinalizeUndelivered`; and `telegram_retry_after` reads `parameters.retry_after`, defaults a bare 429 to 1 s, and ignores non-429 statuses. I did **not** check against a real throttled bot.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I didn't run the full workspace `cargo test` on this box. The first CI run's `Test` failure was `component::verifiable_intent_notice_visibility::enabling_the_section_through_config_patch_records_the_notice_once` (a `zeroclaw config patch` trace check), which doesn't touch Telegram code. I didn't reproduce it locally. I ran the crate's telegram tests. On 20c2c139 a local `cargo clippy --no-deps` stops on pre-existing lints from my newer local toolchain (e.g. `orchestrator/mod.rs:4845`, outside this diff), so I relied on CI clippy for that commit. The follow-up also touches `zeroclaw-api/src/channel.rs` (new `FinalizeUndelivered` type) and the orchestrator's finalize match (one new arm). There is no orchestrator-level test for that arm, and none existed for the `FinalizePartialDelivery` arm either.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No (the same `sendMessage` request is resent at most twice, after Telegram's requested delay)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After merge, revert the resulting merge commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** grep for `Telegram sendMessage rate limited; waiting retry_after before resending` / `...; not retrying inside the penalty window` (WARN). Telegram replies that are delayed by up to ~2×60 s under flood limiting are expected; replies that are delayed with no such log line are not.
