prs.title: fix(rpc/zerocode): scope-filter live-session refresh before locking; keep TUI alive on RPC timeout
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `prepare_live_sessions_refresh` (the live-session rebuild step of a route-affecting `config/set`) now checks whether a session is in scope for the edit *before* taking that session's `model_provider_update` guard. Previously it locked every live session first and filtered second. `handle_session_prompt` holds that guard for the whole turn, so editing an idle agent's `model_provider` parked behind an unrelated busy agent's turn, and the issuing TUI's next `config/list` hit its 5s client deadline.
  - zerocode's `call_with_timeout` returns a typed `DaemonRpcTimeout` instead of a bare string error, and the config manager's `handle_key` / `handle_mouse` absorb it into the loaded detail screen's existing status row (existing `zc-config-status-load-failed` key). Nothing is drawn differently: no new status, style or layout. Before, the error unwound through `app::run` and the whole TUI exited with `zerocode: RPC config/list: timed out after 5s`.
  - New regression test `config_set_for_other_agent_does_not_wait_on_busy_session`: two agents, one live session with its turn guard held; `config/set agents.<other>.model_provider` must complete within 1s and leave the busy session's provider untouched. Hangs on the old code, passes now.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change the rule that a session's guard is held across its whole turn, or that an *in-scope* edit (editing the provider of the agent that is mid-turn) waits for that turn. Does not change the 5s client deadline. Does not touch other panes' error handling. A timeout while only the section list is showing (no section loaded yet; `init` always loads the first one, so ordinary navigation barely reaches this) shows no message, but the pane stays up.
- **Blast radius:** Config transaction path in `zeroclaw-runtime` (`config/set`, `config/set-many`, `config/delete`, alias rename — all go through `prepare_live_sessions_refresh`); zerocode Config pane error handling. Any zerocode code matching on the timeout error *string* still works (Display text unchanged).
- **Linked issue(s):** None filed; observed live on a two-agent daemon.
- **Holding-crate exception:** The `zeroclaw-runtime` change is covered by the ADR-016 exception row recorded in #11640 (merged).

### What this does, simply

When you change a config value that affects which model provider a running agent uses, the daemon rebuilds the provider for every live session that the change applies to. To do that safely it takes a per-session lock, and a running turn holds that same lock until it finishes. The bug was that the daemon grabbed the lock for *every* session before asking whether the change applied to it, so changing agent B's provider could sit waiting for agent A to finish a long turn. Meanwhile the terminal UI that issued the change gave up after 5 seconds and quit entirely. This PR asks "does this edit apply to you?" before taking the lock, so unrelated busy sessions are skipped, and it makes the UI report a slow RPC as a status message instead of exiting.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — the daemon side is cheap to reproduce.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (zerocode Config pane) against a local daemon over the unix-socket RPC.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A config with two agents, say `a` and `b`, both with valid `model_provider`s. zerocode connected to the daemon with a session open for agent `a`.
- **Steps to run:** (1) In agent `a`'s session, send a prompt that will take ≥10s (e.g. a `shell` tool call that sleeps). (2) While it runs, open Config → agents → `b` → `model_provider` and set it to another valid provider ref, Enter.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The set completes immediately; status line shows "Set agents.b.model_provider"; agent `a`'s turn is unaffected.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The set hangs until `a`'s turn ends. If that is longer than 5s, zerocode exits with `zerocode: RPC config/list: timed out after 5s`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` for `zeroclaw-runtime` covers the new regression test and the existing provider-refresh ordering tests; `cargo test -p zerocode` covers the Config-pane handlers; `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` covers both crates.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Commands run and tail output** (remote build host; head `93d7862520e4`, which merges master `b6bad4d41e`):

```
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <changed .rs files>   # clean
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh              # Comment hygiene gate passed.

cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test rpc::dispatch::tests::config_set_for_other_agent_does_not_wait_on_busy_session ... ok
test rpc::dispatch::tests::model_provider_update_converges_on_latest_agent_config ... ok
test rpc::dispatch::tests::model_provider_update_queued_refresh_reads_newer_configure_override ... ok
test result: FAILED. 5712 passed; 4 failed; 8 ignored
  failed: relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener
          relay::local_dial_tests::a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget
          rpc::dispatch::tests::new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants
          tools::send_message_to_peer::tests::peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget

cargo test -p zerocode
test config_manager::tests::config_pane_handlers_still_propagate_non_timeout_rpc_errors ... ok
test config_manager::tests::config_pane_survives_rpc_timeout_on_real_key_and_mouse_input ... ok
test result: FAILED. 1446 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored
  failed: connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint
```

None of the five failures come from this PR. The three relay/dispatch tests and the zerocode SIGINT test fail the same way on untouched master `b6bad4d41e` on the same build host (a non-tty ssh session; the dispatch test trips the host's temp-dir workspace check). `peer_turn_cost_scope_…` passed on rerun. CI is green on `93d7862520e4`, including the Test job.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Daemon side: removing the scope pre-filter block makes `config_set_for_other_agent_does_not_wait_on_busy_session` fail with `Elapsed`; restored, it passes.
  - zerocode side: `config_pane_survives_rpc_timeout_on_real_key_and_mouse_input` wires the Config manager to an in-process fake daemon, loads the first section the way `init` does, then leaves `config/list` unanswered. That head also added a section-list hint-row status, which `3b4325fe8b` removed, so I've dropped that capture from this body.

prs.title: feat(plugins): sign a manifest document in one step
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `signature::sign_manifest_document` returns a signed manifest with the root `signature` and `publisher_key` entries already embedded. It places the entries first and signs the resulting layout, so the signed bytes are exactly what the host reconstructs when it removes them. Hand-embedding after `sign_manifest` verifies only while nothing that was signed ends up attached to an embedded entry; a test pins the working placements and both failing ones (decoration above the fields that was already signed, and anything added below them).
  - A `sign_manifest` cargo example gives publishers the "short Rust helper" the distribution guide has been telling them to write: `keygen` and `sign`, with the payload digest that strict mode requires, a self-check with the host's verifier, and a warning when the output has no digest.
  - The distribution guide documents the helper and states the embedding rule precisely.
  - The signing commands now have three tests in the example target, selected explicitly by component CI. Private-key buffers are zeroized after use, and the guide explains Windows inherited ACLs.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to verification, admission, signature policy, or its defaults. No `zeroclaw plugin sign` command. The `zeroclaw` CLI is unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-plugins` (a published crate) gains one public function and one example. The example is compiled by the `lint` job's `--all-targets` clippy pass and by the default-features `--all-targets` check leg; `cargo package` does not build examples.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10994. The follow-up smoke harness PR depends on this one.

### What this does, simply

Plugin publishers sign their manifest so that operators who run a strict policy can trust it. ZeroClaw's crate had the signing primitives but no complete "sign this file" step, and the manual step had a trap: the TOML editor the host uses attaches a blank line or comment to the entry below it, so signature fields pasted directly under a blank line that was part of the signed text take that line with them when the host strips them again, and the signature fails. This PR adds the complete step to the crate, a small command-line helper that publishers can run from a ZeroClaw checkout, and documentation of the rule.

### Current public security-parent and package-recipe follow-through

Signed `d0a8dbe10cdd1eb90c6ba0843a4a8313846b4954` normally merges the exact public #11715 head `9af44a08f918666c167a6b85d77a1c0f6b6bf08e`, retaining the original signer history. The genuine shared lock is byte-identical to that parent: 1,293 dependencies, Quinn-proto 0.11.19 and probe-rs 0.32, without ruzstd/espflash. Relative to that public parent, only the original five signer topic paths differ. Signing code, signature tests, example handler tests and their CI selection are unchanged from `0d9465d`.

The guide and example now assemble one fresh package containing the signed manifest, its exact referenced Wasm payload and required assets, and create a new archive from only that package. The unsigned source manifest is excluded. This fixes the misplaced-payload/multiple-manifest recipe; it changes no signing, admission, key-permission or overwrite behavior. Static syntax/hash/source checks passed. [Quality Gate 38433555120](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38433555120) now succeeds on this exact combined head: 41 jobs passed and three were conditionally skipped. The tested tree equals the entire public source. Current workspace and explicit no-default Cranelift lanes each pass the same 27 signature and three example methods: 30 distinct methods and 60 actual PASS observations. Current Security passes deny, locked fetch and audit over 1,293 dependencies, with three existing allowed unmaintained warnings; Format, Lint, Docs, generator sync and the declared-floor check pass. The skipped Windows advisory supplies no execution credit. The Linux signer argv/stdout/stderr/file-state boundary now passes the source-equivalent hosted process check below. Current #11311 also supplies valid-Wasm strict directory-package installation/load/tool proof against this same SDK. The newly documented ZIP assembly recipe, Windows ACL and broader platform/release acceptance remain separate.

Prerequisite #11715 merged as `b6bad4d41e3db803721fb9c274ce412e25a2a456` at 23:22:56 UTC on October 13. Its landed tree equals the public parent integrated here. [JordanTheJet](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11310#pullrequestreview-5508527342) and [tidux](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11310#pullrequestreview-5511258203) have approved this exact `d0a8dbe` head; Tidux explicitly clears his earlier change request. Current required checks pass, and protected-queue qualification against master remains required. ZIP assembly, Windows ACL, Stable archives and full platform/release acceptance remain separate.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional; about a minute.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (the example binary; the `zeroclaw` CLI is unchanged)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a ZeroClaw checkout with Rust 1.98.0.
- **Steps to run:**

  ```sh
  mkdir -p /tmp/sign-demo
  cat > /tmp/sign-demo/manifest.toml <<'EOF'
  name = "demo"
  version = "0.1.0"
  wasm_path = "demo.wasm"
  capabilities = ["tool"]
  permissions = []

  [config_schema]
  type = "object"
  additionalProperties = false
  EOF
  printf 'component bytes' > /tmp/sign-demo/demo.wasm
  cargo run -p zeroclaw-plugins --example sign_manifest -- keygen /tmp/sign-demo/publisher.pk8
  cargo run -p zeroclaw-plugins --example sign_manifest -- \
      sign /tmp/sign-demo/manifest.toml /tmp/sign-demo/signed/manifest.toml \
      --key /tmp/sign-demo/publisher.pk8 --payload /tmp/sign-demo/demo.wasm
  cargo run -p zeroclaw-plugins --example sign_manifest -- \
      sign /tmp/sign-demo/manifest.toml /tmp/sign-demo/signed/no-digest.toml \
      --key /tmp/sign-demo/publisher.pk8
  ```

- **Expected on this branch (after):** `keygen` prints a hex key and creates `/tmp/sign-demo/publisher.pk8` readable by you only. The first `sign` creates `/tmp/sign-demo/signed/manifest.toml` with `wasm_sha256`, `publisher_key`, and `signature` before `[config_schema]`, and prints the same hex key. The second prints a warning that strict mode refuses a manifest without `wasm_sha256`, then writes the file.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the example does not exist.

### How I tested

The review follow-up adds the three command tests, explicit CI selection, key-buffer zeroization, and Windows ACL guidance. TOML/YAML validation, documentation lint, and whitespace checks passed locally. Fresh required CI passes at d0a8dbe10cdd1eb90c6ba0843a4a8313846b4954, including all three example handler tests in each of two lanes; no new local Rust execution is claimed. The command results below remain historical author-reported evidence for 88f37b709f and are not current process/output observations.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI is green at d0a8dbe10cdd1eb90c6ba0843a4a8313846b4954. [Workspace Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38433555120/job/115421645291) and [Cranelift backend](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38433555120/job/115421644996) each execute 27 signature controls and all three sign_manifest example tests. The example is registered with `test = true`; the backend command explicitly selects `--example sign_manifest`. These validate the SDK and shared handler, including emitted file assertions. The separate source-equivalent hosted process run below supplies the real argv and captured stdout/stderr evidence. Format, Lint, Docs Style, generator sync and declared-floor checks pass.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the added component CI step executes the example test target. Three tests cover keygen/overwrite refusal and Unix permissions, payload hash plus strict-host signature verification, and refusal without `wasm_path` or output creation. These call the shared command dispatcher; they do not prove the complete argv/process boundary or valid-Wasm admission. The dependent smoke harness remains responsible for the full signed-package install path and platform acceptance. The three tests pass in both hosted lanes at current d0a8dbe10cdd1eb90c6ba0843a4a8313846b4954; Linux real argv/status/output/file-state now passes the process check below. Valid-Wasm strict directory-package proof is reused from current #11311; the ZIP assembly recipe, Windows ACL and full-platform smoke remain separate.
- **Commands run and tail output:** aarch64-apple-darwin, toolchain 1.98.0, revision 88f37b709f.

  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                              (clean)
  $ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets --features plugins-wasm-cranelift -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile
  $ RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --all-targets
      Finished `dev` profile
  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib signature
  test result: ok. 29 passed; 0 failed
  $ cargo doc --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-plugins                          (no warnings)
  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
  $ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh and scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh on the changed page
  Summary: 0 error(s) / Errors 0
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Historical author report for 88f37b709f: the documented commands with a fresh `HOME` and a fresh directory, key/output directory creation and the no-digest warning; strict-host installation and rejection after a manifest edit. Current real-process/stdout/stderr receipts now come from the source-equivalent hosted check below; strict valid-Wasm directory installation/load/tool proof comes from current #11311. The handler assertions remain separate. ZIP assembly, Windows ACL and full-platform acceptance remain unverified.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output from the current publisher-facing `keygen`/`sign` executable is supplied by the source-equivalent hosted process check below. The `zeroclaw` CLI remains unchanged. No presentation-sensitive layout claim is made.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Public SDK/example d0a8dbe10cdd1eb90c6ba0843a4a8313846b4954, exercised by auxiliary a581f2ad27bee1ac3b46241940bd564155a3cdb8. Only the temporary workflow differs; all 2,199 other objects, including the SDK, example, manifests and lock, match d0. Linux x86_64 / Ubuntu 22.04, Rust1.98, locked no-default Cranelift debug example, actual direct argv with space-bearing owned paths, captured noninteractive stdout/stderr. Current unit-handler results remain separate; old local reports remain historical.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Actual process run 38448210611](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38448210611/job/115472069698) retains all twelve stdout/stderr pairs, argv/status/state receipts and public manifests in its pinned artifact. Successful keygen/sign/no-payload stdout is the same exact 64-character lowercase public-key line followed by a newline; ordinary refusal stdout is empty. No private-key bytes or hashes are included. Exact warning and usage are shown below.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Twelve real processes execute: keygen creates the owned private key; overwriting it exits 1 and preserves its bytes; payload signing writes the expected digest/public fields; signing without a digest emits the captured warning; payload-without-wasm_path and seven invalid-argv cases exit 1 with no refused output creation. The actual mode, cleanup and unchanged-key checks pass through their source-bound assertions. No extra fault-injection or independent remote filesystem probe is claimed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** workspace-wide clippy and tests were left to CI; the change is confined to `zeroclaw-plugins`.

### Current Linux supported-command proof

[Nonpublishing run 38448210611](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38448210611) succeeded with both original tool-smoke jobs; only Linux executed the three signing-evidence steps. All twelve real processes have named expected exit records and captured public output/state. The source-equivalent auxiliary has only a one-workflow delta from this PR head. The actual non-test example binary is bound to the current build and source hashes, with complete markers, unchanged source/lock and the verified 32-member public evidence artifact. No current full QG, guest build or directory-package test was repeated.

Exact captured stderr from the missing-digest case (exit 0):

```text
warning: the manifest has no wasm_sha256; hosts in strict signature mode refuse it. Pass --payload to record the component's digest.
```

Exact captured stderr for empty/invalid argv (exit 1):

```text
Error: usage:
  sign_manifest keygen <private-key-out>
  sign_manifest sign <manifest-in> <manifest-out> --key <private-key> [--payload <component>]
```

This closes the Linux supported-command output hold. Runtime guard/fault mutations are unexecuted, the Windows tool leg gives no signer/ACL credit, and ZIP/Stable/full-platform and release acceptance remain separate.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. The example generates Ed25519 signing keys and writes the private key to the path the publisher names, with mode `0600` on Unix, refusing to overwrite an existing file. Its generated/read private-key buffers are wrapped in `Zeroizing`; Windows file access follows inherited ACLs as documented. It never prints or logs the private key. The documentation tells publishers to keep the key outside the plugin and ZeroClaw trees.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: see above.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: new publisher-facing Cargo example `keygen` and `sign` commands. Existing `zeroclaw` commands, config and environment contracts are unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: no config migration or existing-command change. Publishers may use the new Cargo example from a checkout; adoption is optional.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert this PR's merge commit through the normal PR workflow.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): make scrollbar seeking continuous across loaded history
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- Use the same absolute pointer mapping for scrollbar clicks and drags, so dragging no longer jumps back toward the pre-click position.
- Make the scrollbar cover the complete loaded transcript while retaining the 1,000-entry render window. Intermediate seeks skip entries that produce no visible rows.
- Paint the scrollbar inside the same track used for pointer hit testing. Reuse indexed viewport lookup for thumb position and preserve transcript selections until cached content changes.
- **Scope boundary:** Loaded transcript navigation. Keyboard bindings, clipboard transport and history pagination remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** Chat and Code transcript rendering, scrollbar pointer handling and selection during seeking.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10301.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `risk:medium`, `zerocode`, `topic:zerocode`.

### What this does, simply

The scrollbar currently moves on a click, then calculates the following drag from the position before that click. This makes the transcript jump. In long sessions, its range also describes only the current render window, so it cannot seek directly to older loaded messages.

This repair makes pointer position choose the transcript position consistently. The track can reach the oldest and newest loaded messages and positions between them without rendering the entire history. A character selection stays valid while the viewport moves within the same cached content and clears when seeking replaces that content.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, terminal mouse forwarding is useful additional evidence for the original SSH report.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui`, Chat and Code panes.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Run this branch's `zerocode` against your normal daemon and open an existing session with enough loaded history to scroll. Use the same session on `master` for comparison; no provider turn is needed.
- **Steps to run:** Click the middle of the right-edge scrollbar, hold the button and move one row. Drag to its top and bottom. For a long loaded transcript, seek between older and newer messages, resize the terminal, and repeat. Select transcript text and move the scrollbar within the same render window. Repeat over SSH in Windows Terminal or WezTerm when available.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The viewport stays at the clicked position before the pointer moves, then follows the drag. The track reaches the loaded-history endpoints. Selection survives movement within one cached geometry and clears when that geometry changes.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The first drag uses the old scroll anchor, and long-history seeking stays within the current render window.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** After publication, the required `Test` job runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`, including ZeroCode's mouse-dispatch and render tests. `Fmt` and `Lint` cover formatting and Rust linting. Current-branch CI is pending publication.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Real terminal/SSH mouse forwarding and a direct capture of scrollbar presentation.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0

git diff --check
exit 0

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

On `c9ce4f68288b` (rebased onto current master, ported to the `transcript_layout` cache from #11459), through the remote cargo wrapper:

```text
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode scrollbar
test chat::tests::scrollbar_stays_at_the_newest_entry_when_scrolled_inside_a_live_reply ... ok
test chat::tests::scrollbar_seeks_complete_history_with_a_bounded_render_window ... ok
test chat::tests::scrollbar_drag_works_outside_browse_mode ... ok

cargo test -p zerocode
test result: FAILED. 1446 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored

cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
exit 0
```

The single failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, also fails on the pre-fix head `541daebd1dc5` on the same build host, and master's CI Test job passes, so it is specific to the host, not this change.
- **Automated cases:** `scrollbar_stays_at_the_newest_entry_when_scrolled_inside_a_live_reply` covers the Greptile finding: with 2,200 entries and a streaming reply, scrolling up one row keeps the thumb at the newest entry. Without the fix it fails with `left: 1200, right: 2199`. The existing drag test checks unchanged pointer position, one-row movement and endpoint clamping. A production-dispatch/render test seeks through 2,200 loaded entries with browse mode, hidden thoughts, empty messages, repeated movement and resize. Existing selection tests cover preservation within one cache and invalidation when seeking changes its entries.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source review of the mouse path, loaded-history ownership, bounded renderer and current selection invalidation. On 2026-10-13, I used the scrollbar in a real terminal on the experiment build [experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123) (commit [4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/4989c40271232a882026c0149ab99a88726bcd3e)) (dogfood base [dogfood/zerocode-builds/20261008T194402Z-0341618f9d69](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/dogfood/zerocode-builds/20261008T194402Z-0341618f9d69) (commit [0341618f9d69](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d))) and it works. That build carries this PR's change through its dogfood base, adapted to the base's `transcript_layout` refactor. Its `seek_scrollbar`, `scrollbar_state` and `scrollbar_seeks_complete_history_with_a_bounded_render_window` test match this PR's head `541daebd1dc5` except for the `transcript_layout.view()` field paths. It is not a build of the exact PR head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** I verified this in the experiment build. No screenshot.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** ZeroCode TUI, experiment build [experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123) (commit [4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/4989c40271232a882026c0149ab99a88726bcd3e)), on macOS.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Production-boundary tests have been adapted to the current renderer. In the build, the scrollbar behaved as described under "Expected on this branch". SSH mouse forwarding (Windows Terminal or WezTerm) is still untested.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** None skipped. The tests above ran on the remote build host.

### Visual evidence

I verified this in the experiment build on 2026-10-13: [experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T013200Z-4989c4027123) (commit [4989c4027123](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/4989c40271232a882026c0149ab99a88726bcd3e)). No screenshot.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any Yes, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.

- Upgrade steps: None.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's merge commit with `git revert <merge-commit>` and rebuild ZeroCode.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A drag jumps unexpectedly, a loaded-history endpoint becomes unreachable, or selected text remains tied to replaced render content. These are visible TUI symptoms; no new log event is introduced.

N/A. This PR carries the local repair for #10301.

prs.title: fix(delegate): keep a bounded delegate's workspace, tool ceiling and command policy bound beyond the turn (#9872)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. The head under review is `1a328ea53`; `master@0f8fb9d37` was merged in by `ba665d125`, so that revision is an ancestor of the head. `master` has moved on since (`ea4a54bb5` when this text was written, 13 commits later); `git merge-tree` of the head against it is clean and it has not been merged here. The branch was reconciled with `master` repeatedly during review; each reconciliation is a merge commit in the history. Re-read the head before relying on this line: it names the revision the numbers below were taken on.
- **Problem:** the bounded-delegation contract says the caller bounds what a bounded target can do: its filesystem tools work in the target's own workspace, the caller's tool registry is a ceiling, and the caller's command policy stays authoritative. That bound was applied while the target's turn was assembled and then lost by anything that runs *after* that point, because such work rebuilt its tools or its policy without it. Each escape below is repaired where the bound has to survive, not at the reported symptom.
- **What changed:**
  - **Workspace (original scope, #9872).** A bounded delegate's filesystem tools are rebuilt against the target's own policy and workspace. Follow-ups in the same spirit: `git_operations` gets a real command boundary built from the target's sandbox (`DelegateTool::rebuild_target_git_operations_tool`), and `backup`/`data_management` keep the target's policy over `master`'s shared data directory.
  - **Tool ceiling carried into work that outlives the turn.** `SopStepReassembly` carries `caller_allowed`; `all_tools_with_runtime` forwards the ceiling to the scheduler tools and to `spawn_subagent`, which closes the replay of a stored job; `send_message_to_peer` takes a `caller_ceiling` and the entry point it relays through, `process_message_shared_with_live_config_and_admission_and_principal`, an `allowed_tools`, so a relayed peer's turn is capped by the sender's ceiling (including the SOP step that peer starts).
  - **Ceiling derivation.** The sealed ceiling is a set of names, so two stand-ins that report the name of a real capability are excluded at the one place it is sealed: `BoundedSopApproveDenied` (`sop_approve`) and `sub_delegate_tool` (`delegate`). It is sealed after the headless SOP step-scope exclusions.
  - **Deferred shell.** A shell job stores a command, not a tool list, and the scheduler runs it under the owning agent's policy. `require_shell_within_ceiling` refuses `cron_add`'s shell branch, `cron_update`, `schedule` and `cron_run` unless the caller held `shell`; `cron_run` now branches on `job_type`.
  - **Persistence windows.** `cron_update`/`schedule` resume check the ceiling as a `JobGuard` inside the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction that commits the write (`cron/store.rs::update_job_inner`), so a concurrent write from another turn of the owning agent cannot land in between. `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` cancel a run they would leave parked (`WaitApproval`, `CheckpointWait`, `Pending`), and so does the live SOP driver at a park it reaches after running a queued step (`QueuedSopAction::bounded_caller`); a cancellation that cannot be persisted is reported, never claimed. The bounded rebind of `sop_execute` records no initiating agent.
  - **Command policy across hops and deferred work (`fe804dd56`).** The maintainer's review of `5758af5b2` asked for this in the PR. The mechanism: *any command a bounded target runs, or leaves behind to run later, under a policy rebuilt one hop below the caller, was judged only by the target's command policy.* The callers' command fields (`autonomy`, `allowed_commands`, `block_high_risk_commands`, `require_approval_for_medium_risk`) now travel inside `SecurityPolicy` as `caller_command_bounds`, root first (`policy.rs:514`, anchor `pub caller_command_bounds: Vec<CallerCommandBound>`), and `validate_command_execution_for_shell` requires a command to clear the policy's own rules and each caller's (`policy.rs:3491`, anchor `for bound in &self.caller_command_bounds`). The chain is attached where the bounded branch of `policy_for_target` already binds budget and cost (`delegate.rs:890`, anchor `target_policy.caller_command_bounds = self.security.caller_command_bounds.clone();`) and inherits the parent's, so hop N is bound by the whole path from the root. Cloning a policy carries it; `ensure_no_escalation_beyond` rejects a child policy that drops one (`policy.rs:4852`, anchor `Err(EscalationViolation::CallerCommandBoundDroppedByChild)`). This replaces the `CallerCommandPolicyShell` wrapper, which gated only the target's direct `shell`.
    - Covered: `cron_add`, `schedule` (`expression`, `delay`, `run_at`), `cron_update` and `cron_run` when a command is written or launched; the STORED command when a job is reused without a command patch (`cron_update` of another field, `schedule` resume), re-judged inside the guarded write (`caller_ceiling.rs:297`, `require_job_within_ceiling`); a `spawn_subagent` child; a second delegation hop, whose "caller" used to be the first target's raw policy.
    - Deferred agent jobs: a bounded registration refuses a stored `allowed_tools` list that keeps `shell`, named or inherited from a ceiling that holds it, at write and at launch or re-arm (`caller_ceiling.rs`, `refuse_deferred_shell` at `:197`). A deferred agent has no command to judge when it is written, so the capability is not deferred.
  - **Review follow-ups after the merge with `master@9cd75ac34`.**
    - *Fail closed on reuse.* `sop_execute`, `sop_advance` and `sop_workshop` leave `SAFE_FOR_BOUNDED_REUSE` for a new `REBOUND_BY_DOWNCAST_TOOL_NAMES` (`tools/mod.rs:620`). A bounded target receives them only as an instance rebound to the sealed ceiling; an instance the downcast cannot resolve (wrapped, or `as_any` not forwarded) is omitted, whether or not a root config is attached, because the name check in `delegate.rs` sits before `reuse_is_earned`.
    - *`sop_workshop`.* Under a caller ceiling it keeps only `list` and `inspect`. `apply` writes a SOP definition and reloads the shared engine, and `propose`, `capture_run`, `reject` and `quarantine` save proposals that a later run consumes, so all five are refused. The ceiling reaches it through the bounded rebuild and through `all_tools_with_runtime`.
    - *`sop_execute`/`sop_advance` in every registry built with a ceiling.* Before, only the bounded delegate rebuild gave them the ceiling, so the park-cancellation described above did not apply to a restricted `agent::run` (and with it a `spawn_subagent` child or a cron-fired job) or a peer relay. A SOP step turn never held them (`SOP_CONTROL_TOOLS` excludes them by name). Under a ceiling `sop_execute` also records no initiating agent, as the bounded rebuild already did, so a run whose cancellation cannot be persisted cannot be resumed as the caller. `all_tools_with_runtime` now passes `caller_ceiling` to both, in the branch with an audit logger and the one without.
    - *`CallerCommandBound`.* `from_caller` destructures, and `overlay` builds, `SecurityPolicy` field by field with no `..policy.clone()`, so a field added later stops them compiling until it is decided which side owns it.
    - *Inventory.* The four `a2a_*` tools capture the caller's `SecurityPolicy`, so they are classified as denied for bounded targets, and the maximal-registry fixture now builds them. A new test walks the compiled inventory (`BUILTIN_TOOLS`), so a tool that fixture forgets cannot stay unclassified.
    - Comments that described the pre-inversion fallthrough were corrected, and `delegation.md` states where the `sop_workshop` and park-cancellation behavior applies and that an `independent` hop below a bounded target carries neither the ceiling nor the command chain.
  - **Review follow-ups after `b2795136a`** (from the automated review of the PR and a cold re-read of the delta).
    - *Nested bounded hop and MCP.* A hop hands its nested delegate only the MCP tools its own bundles grant (`bounded_base_tools` filters with `mcp_tool_is_granted`, `delegate.rs`), so a nested target cannot recover an MCP server its caller was not granted (`e8ebeb34a`).
    - *Audit of a refused SOP run.* When `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` cancel a run they would leave parked, the audit trail (`log_run_start`, `log_step_result`, `log_run_complete`) is written before the refusal is returned; the early return used to skip it (`e8ebeb34a`).
    - *The ceiling describes the turn, not the caller.* A turn given a per-run `allowed_tools` (`agent::run`, and `process_message_inner` for a relayed peer) used to seal that list as it came in. The turn's own policy then removes tools from it, so a job, child or relay created in the turn carried names the turn never received: a peer whose policy has no `shell` could store a shell job because `require_shell_within_ceiling` found `shell` in the raw list. The handle is now created before the tools are built (`pending_for_turn`) and sealed once the registry is assembled, to the intersection of the incoming names and that registry (`seal_to_registry`, `tools/caller_ceiling.rs`; calls in `agent/loop_.rs`), the way the bounded delegate assembly already sealed its set (`bddec0914`).
    - *Deferred MCP tools.* Sealing from the registry alone dropped the MCP tools that only become callable after `tool_search` activates them under `mcp.deferred_loading`, so a job, child or relay lost valid tools. That regression came from the previous bullet and was found by the automated review. `ScopedAssembled::deferred_mcp_tool_names` reports the policy-admitted stubs, only when `tool_search` survives assembly, and `seal_to_registry` adds them, still intersected with the caller's names (`1c679eed9`). The bounded delegate assembly has no such gap: its target never receives `tool_search`, and a deferred tool the caller already activated is an ordinary MCP wrapper in the target's registry, which the ceiling is sealed from. A test pins that.
    - *Bounded rebuild reads the admitted config.* The rebuild of workspace-, identity-, channel- and autonomy-bound tools (and the target's skills and workspace for the prompt) read `self.root_config`, the snapshot the `DelegateTool` was built with, while the rest of that function prefers the config the delegation was admitted against. It now uses the admitted config and falls back to the snapshot (`rebuild_config`, `delegate.rs`; `bddec0914`).
    - *Fluent.* The refusals this PR adds were bare English literals in seven tool sources. They now come from 15 `bounded-ceiling-*` keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl` with the exact wording they had, and a test pins each key's text. The other locales fall back to English until their catalogs are filled, and existing literals in `tools/*.rs` are untouched (`1a328ea53`).
- **Known boundary, not covered here:** the command chain travels by cloning the policy, so it does not reach a turn started for a different agent that rebuilds that agent's policy from config and receives only the caller's tool-name ceiling. Today that is a `send_message_to_peer` relay (`send_message_to_peer.rs:268`, anchor `let allowed_tools = match self.caller_ceiling.as_ref()`, passes tool names; `loop_.rs:3554`, anchor `let security = Arc::new(SecurityPolicy::for_agent(&config, agent_alias)?);`, builds the peer's policy fresh) and a live SOP step naming another agent (`assemble_owned_execution_with_admission` in `turn/mod.rs:3439`, anchor `SecurityPolicy::for_agent(config, alias)`, which receives only `caller_allowed`). There the recipient's `shell` is judged by the recipient's own command policy; the tool-name ceiling still applies. This is read from the code, not exercised end to end, and it is stated in `delegation.md`. Threading the chain through `process_message*` and the SOP reassembly is the same change as `allowed_tools` but widens an already large diff; the maintainers asked for it as a follow-up, which is now #11667 (opened as a feature: whether a turn started for another agent should inherit the caller's command policy). The scheduler also still validates a stored command with the owning agent's policy when a job fires: the callers' bounds are enforced when a command is written, re-armed or run through these tools.
- **Second declared gap (predates this PR):** an `Agent` session narrowed by an RPC principal's tool selector applies `principal_allowed_tools` by name after the tools are built (`agent/agent.rs:2979`, anchor `caller_allowed: principal_allowed_tools.as_deref()`, and `:3132`, anchor `.allowed_tools(principal_allowed_tools)`), but its scheduler tools and `send_message_to_peer` are built with no sealed ceiling (`agent/agent.rs:2937`, anchor `No ceiling is built here`), and a SOP step naming another agent is re-assembled without one (`agent/agent.rs:4097` and `:4694`, anchor `caller_allowed: None`). `principal_allowed_tools` was already in `agent.rs` on `master` before this branch's last merge (8 references at `e16fd898b`). This is read from the code, not exercised in a restricted-principal session. This PR corrects the comments that denied it; building a pre-sealed ceiling from `principal_allowed_tools`, the way `run()` does (`agent/loop_.rs:1706`, anchor `crate::tools::caller_ceiling::seal_to_registry(`), will be tracked as a separate issue (first described in https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10391#issuecomment-5924985449)
- **Scope boundary:** this does not change approval routing: the bounded child approval gate (#10937, the fix for #10643) is `master`'s, integrated here. It does not retro-cap jobs already stored under the old, wider ceiling (it closes the write path, not what is written). It adds no completeness check over registry-creating call sites, and no typed-context refactor distinguishing "capability offered" from "capability granted". The completeness test now also walks the compiled inventory (`BUILTIN_TOOLS`), and the four `a2a_*` tools are classified as denied for bounded targets. It does not close the loss of authority on an **unbounded** SOP run's own `drive_headless_run` path, which a human reviewer confirmed predates this branch against the merge-base; it will be tracked as a separate issue.
- **Blast radius:** the tool-registry factory (`all_tools_with_runtime*`, which every agent turn that builds a registry goes through, with a new trailing parameter), the cron store's guarded write (`cron/store.rs`), the scheduler tools, the SOP tools (`sop_execute`, `sop_advance`, `sop_workshop`), and `validate_command_execution_for_shell` through the new `caller_command_bounds` on `SecurityPolicy`. Agents with no ceiling are unchanged: the tests build the same registry with and without a ceiling. What operators can notice: a job or run restricted by `allowed_tools` that starts a SOP which would park for approval now has that run cancelled, and the same restriction removes `sop_workshop`'s write actions; both apply to operator-authored lists too (see Compatibility).
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #9872. Related #10937 (bounded child tool approvals, merged to `master`; it is the fix for #10643; integrated here). Filed from earlier work on this PR: #10721 (a pre-existing tilde-expansion defect in `knowledge.db_path`, not fixed in this PR; fixed separately by #10819, merged 2026-09-13). Follow-ups from this review: #11667 covers the command chain across a peer relay and a cross-agent SOP step (opened as a feature). The other two declared gaps are not open yet: RPC principal sessions that build a registry with no ceiling, and a parked SOP run that resumes through `drive_headless_run` with `allowed_tools: None`. A search of upstream issues for each mechanism did not turn up an existing one, and they will be opened as separate issues once their analysis is done. #11652 is the holding-crate exception row for this change.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets one agent hand a task to another. In the "bounded" mode the second agent is supposed to stay inside three limits set by the first: it works in its own workspace, it may only use tools the first agent had, and it may only run commands the first agent could run. Those limits held while the second agent's turn was running. They were lost by anything that kept going afterwards: a scheduled job it created, a procedure (SOP) run that was waiting for approval, a message relayed to a peer, a sub-agent it started, or a further hop of delegation. In those cases the work ran later with the full authority of whichever agent owned it.

This PR carries the limits along with that work. A job or run created under a limit is capped by it, a procedure run that would wait for an approval nobody in the turn can follow is cancelled instead, and a command has to satisfy the rules of every agent above it. It adds no capability; it only removes authority that leaked.

What stays the same: agents that are not under a limit behave as before, and jobs already stored are not retroactively capped. The limits listed under "Known boundary" and "Second declared gap" are not closed here and are tracked as follow-ups. What operators will notice: a job or run restricted by `allowed_tools` can no longer leave a SOP waiting for approval, and can no longer write SOP definitions through `sop_workshop`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: every escape needs a bounded delegation to line up, plus, depending on the case, a peer relay, a concurrent second writer, an externally triggered resume or a further hop. The regressions drive exactly that through real `agent::run` / `process_message`, provider, scheduler and SOP-engine boundaries.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (one-shot `agent::run`), the cron scheduler executing a stored job, an in-process peer turn via `process_message`, a real second SQLite connection racing a guarded write, and the live `SopEngine` through `sop_execute`/`sop_advance`.

### How I tested

Each refusal is paired with a positive control that runs the *same* chain and config with one difference, so a passing negative cannot be explained by an unrelated gate turning the job away first. Every new test was seen red against a prediction written before the run, and each code site was neutralized one at a time to confirm its test goes red.

| Route | Bound | Regression |
|---|---|---|
| Deferred shell ops need `shell` in the caller's ceiling | refused otherwise; `pause` and disable-only patches exempt | `a_bounded_delegate_cannot_store_a_shell_job_through_cron_add`, `a_bounded_delegate_cannot_create_a_shell_job_through_schedule` (+ controls); unit tests for `schedule` resume, `cron_update` (shell job) and `cron_run` (3, incl. that a shell job's stored list does not govern it) |
| Agent jobs stay within the ceiling | patch that never names `allowed_tools`; force-run | `a_patch_that_never_names_allowed_tools_cannot_re_arm_an_unbounded_job`, `a_bounded_caller_cannot_force_run_an_agent_job_reaching_beyond_the_ceiling` |
| `sop_approve` / `delegate` capability | never stored, offered or replayed | `a_cron_job_scheduled_without_explicit_tools_does_not_store_sop_approve`, `a_replayed_bounded_cron_job_is_never_offered_sop_approve`, `a_child_spawned_from_a_bounded_delegate_is_never_offered_sop_approve`, `a_job_scheduled_from_a_bounded_delegate_cannot_store_delegate` |
| Peer relayed via `send_message_to_peer` | peer's turn bound by the sender's ceiling | `a_peer_relayed_from_a_bounded_delegate_is_bound_by_the_callers_ceiling` (the SOP step that peer then starts has no dedicated regression, see limits) |
| Concurrent write between a guarded read and its write | rival's `UPDATE` cannot land | `a_concurrent_unbounded_widen_cannot_land_between_a_bounded_cron_updates_read_and_its_write`, `..._resumes_read_and_its_write`, plus 7 store-level unit tests |
| SOP run left parked by a bounded caller | cancelled, not resumable | `execute_supervised_sop_under_ceiling_is_refused_and_the_run_cannot_be_approved` and its `sop_advance`, checkpoint and `Pending` siblings (the `WaitApproval` and `CheckpointWait` ones each paired with a control that reaches a non-parking transition); `a_bounded_targets_sop_execute_refuses_a_parking_run_through_the_real_delegate_assembly` (real `caller → delegate(bounded) → target → sop_execute` chain); persistence-failure tests for both tools |
| Live SOP driver reaches a park after a queued step | cancelled at the park | `bounded_live_driver_cancels_a_run_that_reaches_approval_after_a_step`, `..._left_pending_on_a_dependency`, `..._a_deterministic_run_that_reaches_a_checkpoint`; control `unbounded_live_driver_still_parks_for_approval`; `run_tool_call_loop_bounded_sop_{execute,advance}_cannot_leave_a_run_parked_after_a_live_step`; `bounded_live_driver_reports_a_cancellation_it_could_not_persist`; `rebound_with_ceiling_does_not_carry_the_initiator` |
| Step scope denies `shell` | no deferred shell job stored | `bounded_delegate_under_a_sop_step_scope_cannot_store_a_shell_job_the_step_denied` (+ control) |
| `git_operations` writes in the target's workspace | real boundary attached | `bounded_delegate_git_operations_can_write_in_the_target_workspace`, negative control `..._write_still_blocked_under_docker_runtime` |
| `backup` / `data_management` over the shared data dir | run under the TARGET's policy | `bounded_delegate_backup_creates_archive_in_shared_data_dir_not_callers_workspace`, `..._backup_runs_under_the_targets_policy_not_the_callers`, `..._data_management_reads_under_the_targets_policy_not_the_callers` (+ control) |
| Bounded `shell` under the caller's command policy | a command runs only if both policies admit it | `bounded_shell_enforces_the_callers_command_policy`, `bounded_shell_keeps_the_targets_own_command_policy`; control `bounded_shell_runs_a_command_both_policies_admit` |
| Deferred shell op, command denied by the caller and allowed by the target | refused; each control changes only the caller's allowlist | `cron_add_refuses_a_shell_job_the_caller_command_policy_denies`, `schedule_{expression,delay,run_at}_refuses_a_command_the_caller_denies`, `cron_update_refuses_a_command_patch_the_caller_denies`, each with a control (`tests/bounded_delegate_caller_command_policy.rs`) |
| Job reused without a command patch | the STORED command is re-judged | `cron_update_without_a_command_patch_refuses_a_stored_command_the_caller_denies`, `schedule_resume_refuses_a_stored_command_the_caller_denies` (+ controls); `cron_update_may_still_disable_a_job_whose_command_the_caller_denies` |
| `cron_run` of a stored shell job; `schedule` resume with approval | refused before a run is recorded; resume takes `approved` | `a_bounded_run_refuses_a_stored_command_the_caller_command_policy_denies` and its control (which launches `echo`); `a_bounded_resume_re_judges_the_stored_command_and_takes_the_request_approval`, control `an_unbounded_resume_still_re_judges_nothing` |
| Deferred agent job that keeps `shell` | refused when named or inherited; a list without `shell` is stored | `a_bounded_agent_job_naming_shell_is_refused`, `..._inheriting_a_ceiling_with_shell_is_refused` and two controls; 5 unit tests in `caller_ceiling.rs` |
| Further hop and `spawn_subagent` child | the root caller's, and a middle hop's, restriction still bind | `cron_add_two_hops_down_still_honours_the_root_caller_command_policy`, `..._honours_a_restriction_set_by_the_middle_agent` (+ control); `a_spawned_child_of_a_bounded_target_honours_the_caller_command_policy` (+ control) |
| Chain semantics | AND in both directions, every link, approval, high-risk and read-only fields; a clone carries it; a child cannot drop one | 9 unit tests in `policy.rs` |
| SOP step agent assembled under a caller's ceiling | the ceiling survives into the step agent; an unbounded control proves the tool was there to lose | `assembling_a_step_agent_applies_the_callers_ceiling` (red when the test-only wrapper passes `None`); the existing `a_cross_agent_sop_step_under_a_bounded_chain_runs_within_the_caller_ceiling` is red when the production call passes `None` |
| `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` in a registry built with a ceiling (a restricted `agent::run`, hence a `spawn_subagent` child and a cron-fired job, and a peer relay through the same factory) | both carry the ceiling in both construction branches and `sop_execute` records no initiating agent under it; a restricted run refuses and cancels a parking run | `sop_execute_and_advance_built_under_a_caller_ceiling_carry_it`; `a_restricted_runs_sop_execute_refuses_a_parking_run` with control `an_unrestricted_runs_sop_execute_still_parks_the_run` (`tests/restricted_run_sop_execute_ceiling.rs`) |
| `sop_workshop` under a caller ceiling | every persisting action refused (sealed and unsealed ceiling), nothing stored or written, `list`/`inspect` work; the unrestricted `apply` is the control | `under_a_ceiling_every_persisting_action_is_refused_and_stores_nothing`; `sop_workshop_built_under_a_caller_ceiling_refuses_persisting_actions` (with a no-ceiling control); `a_bounded_targets_sop_workshop_refuses_persisting_actions_but_keeps_list` (`tests/bounded_delegate_sop_workshop_ceiling.rs`, a real `delegate(bounded)` chain) |
| A rebound-only SOP tool the downcast cannot resolve | omitted, with and without a root config | `bounded_target_omits_unrebindable_sop_tools_without_root_config` (guards the name check); `bounded_target_omits_sop_tools_the_downcast_cannot_rebind` (guards the list membership, so it stays green if only the name check is removed) |
| `CallerCommandBound` field sides | command fields from the caller, everything else from the target, compared as a whole value; a new `SecurityPolicy` field stops `from_caller` and `overlay` compiling | `overlay_takes_the_command_fields_from_the_caller_and_everything_else_from_the_target`; the compile errors `E0027` (`from_caller`) and `E0063` (`overlay`) when a field is added (mutation) |
| Command chain by delegation mode | attached for a bounded target, not for an independent one | `policy_for_target_attaches_the_command_chain_only_for_a_bounded_target` |
| Inventory classification | every `BUILTIN_TOOLS` row is in exactly one list, bar three that never reach the classifier (`delegate`, `execute_pipeline`, `tool_search`) | `every_inventoried_tool_is_classified_for_bounded_delegation` |
| Nested bounded hop and MCP servers | a nested target gets only the MCP tools its caller's bundles grant; a server granted at every hop still reaches it | `bounded_nested_hop_cannot_recover_an_mcp_server_its_caller_was_not_granted`, `bounded_nested_hop_keeps_an_mcp_server_its_caller_was_granted` |
| A refused SOP run is still audited | the run start, the step and the cancelled run reach the audit trail before the refusal | `execute_supervised_sop_under_ceiling_still_audits_the_run_start_and_its_cancellation`, `advance_into_a_park_under_ceiling_still_audits_the_step_and_the_cancelled_run` |
| Peer turn sealed to what it holds | a peer whose policy has no `shell` cannot store a shell job although the sender could; `seal_to_registry` keeps only names in both the registry and the incoming list | `relayed_peer_turn_cannot_store_a_shell_job_when_its_own_registry_has_no_shell` (`agent/loop_.rs`, a real `process_message` turn with a provider); unit tests `a_name_the_turn_never_received_is_not_sealed`, `a_tool_the_caller_did_not_name_is_not_sealed_in`, `a_turn_without_an_allowlist_has_no_handle` (`caller_ceiling.rs`) |

For the SOP park: read `SopEngine::gate_state` to confirm a cancelled run can never resolve as `Resumed`. - **Visual interface changed?** `N/A`

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**: this only removes capability from bounded targets and their relayed peers.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- **Risk and mitigation:** the refusal strings are model-visible. Most are static authored text; `send_message_to_peer: refused — a delegated caller ceiling was declared but never published, so the recipient's turn cannot be bounded` fires only on an internal wiring failure, the same fail-closed contract as `spawn_subagent`'s. The two SOP refusals interpolate values the caller supplied in the same tool call (`sop_execute`'s `name`, `sop_advance`'s `run_id`), each validated against a real SOP definition or run before being echoed, the same class as the existing `require_within_ceiling` echo of stored tool names. Their failure branch also echoes the backend `StoreError`, and the live SOP driver's error echoes an engine-generated run id and the same `StoreError`: backend-internal values, so no new injection surface, with the leak risk (a storage path or driver message in a tool result) of the class already accepted for `require_within_ceiling`. `fe804dd56` adds two strings in `caller_ceiling.rs`: the `refuse_deferred_shell` refusal (static text plus the tool's own name and the literal `shell`) and the stored-command refusal `{tool}: refused — {reason}`, where `reason` is the command policy's message and can echo the stored command text (`Command not allowed by security policy: <command>`). That command was supplied when the job was written and is echoed into a tool result, again the same class. `sop_workshop`'s refusal is static text plus the action's wire name, which comes from a fixed enum (`sop_workshop.rs`, anchor `is not available under a caller tool ceiling`). The 15 refusals this PR adds render from `bounded-ceiling-*` Fluent keys with their previous English wording, pinned by a test, so that change introduces no new model-visible text.
- **Declared gaps:** see the Known boundary and the Second declared gap in the Summary: the command chain does not reach a peer relay or a cross-agent SOP step, and a principal-narrowed `Agent` session's scheduler tools carry no sealed ceiling. They are limits of what this PR closes; the code before this branch had neither bound.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No**, deliberately.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- **Exact upgrade steps for existing users:** no migration is required for existing stored jobs or running deployments; nothing persisted changes shape (see Rollback). It **does** change public Rust signatures:
  1. `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::all_tools_with_runtime`, `all_tools_with_runtime_and_acp_sessions` and `all_tools_with_runtime_and_execution_capability` (`tools/mod.rs`) each gain a final `caller_ceiling: Option<CallerCeiling>`: source-breaking for a positional caller, though the type is `pub(crate)`, so an out-of-tree caller can only pass `None`. The cross-crate callers in this tree (`zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs`, twice, and `zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`) pass `None`. The `process_message*` entry points keep `master`'s public signatures.
  2. `zeroclaw_runtime::cron::update_job_for_agent` and `resume_job_for_agent` each gain a final `guard: JobGuard<'_>` (`cron::unguarded` for a caller with no bound to enforce). Only `zeroclaw-runtime` calls them today, but both are `pub`.
  3. `zeroclaw_config::policy::SecurityPolicy` gains a `pub` field `caller_command_bounds` (source-breaking for an out-of-tree struct literal that does not use `..Default`), a new `pub` type `CallerCommandBound` is added, and `EscalationViolation` gains a variant, `CallerCommandBoundDroppedByChild` (source-breaking for an exhaustive match). `CallerCommandPolicyShell` is removed.
  4. `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::REBOUND_BY_DOWNCAST_TOOL_NAMES` is a new `pub const` (`tools/mod.rs:620`), and `BOUNDED_DENIED_TOOL_NAMES` gains the four `a2a_*` names. `SopWorkshopTool`, `SopExecuteTool` and `SopAdvanceTool` gain `pub(crate)` methods only.
  5. `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::scoped::ScopedAssembled` gains a `pub` field `deferred_mcp_tool_names: Vec<String>`: source-breaking for an out-of-tree struct literal or an exhaustive destructure (the five destructures in this tree use `..`).
  The other registry-constructor changes (`send_message_to_peer_tool`, `sop_execute`/`sop_advance`'s `caller_ceiling`, and so on) are `pub(crate)`, so they carry no external burden.

  Behavior changes for bounded delegation:
  - shell-job creation, resume and force-run need `shell` in the ceiling; patches are capped; scheduled jobs store the intersection; `sop_approve` and `delegate` cannot be smuggled into a stored job by omitting `allowed_tools`; a bounded target's action budget is intersected with the caller's; a relayed peer's turn, and a cross-agent SOP step that peer starts, are bound by the intersection;
  - a concurrent write from another turn of the owning agent can no longer land between a bounded `cron_update`/`schedule` resume's check and its write;
  - a bounded caller's `sop_execute`/`sop_advance`, and the live SOP driver after a queued step, cancel a run that would park (approval, checkpoint, unmet dependency) instead of leaving it resumable with full authority; a bounded rebind of `sop_execute` records no initiating agent;
  - a bounded delegation made inside a headless SOP step seals a ceiling that excludes what the step's scope denies;
  - `backup`/`data_management` follow `master`'s shared data directory under the target's policy;
  - every command a bounded target runs, or stores to run later, must also clear the command policy of each caller above it, at every bounded hop and for a `spawn_subagent` child; a command the caller's policy refuses is refused even if the target's profile allows it;
  - a bounded registration cannot store, launch or re-arm an agent job whose `allowed_tools` keeps `shell`, and `schedule` resume reads the request's `approved` like the create routes. A job already stored with `shell` stays stored, but a bounded turn cannot launch or re-arm it;
  - a command denied by both the target's and a caller's policy reports the target's message;
  - any `agent::run` given a per-run `allowed_tools` (a stored cron agent job with its own list, for example) now builds its scheduler tools with a ceiling sealed to the tools that run actually holds (the list intersected with its assembled registry), so a job it stores or launches is capped by it and an agent job that keeps `shell` is refused (`agent/loop_.rs:1706`, anchor `crate::tools::caller_ceiling::seal_to_registry(`, and `cron/scheduler.rs:1180`, anchor `job.allowed_tools.clone()`). Read from the code.
  - `sop_workshop` keeps only `list` and `inspect` under a caller ceiling, and `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` cancel a run that would park in every registry built with one: a bounded target, a restricted `agent::run` (so a `spawn_subagent` child and a cron-fired job) and a peer relay; a SOP step turn never holds these two tools, because the step scope excludes them by name. Under a ceiling `sop_execute` also records no initiating agent. This includes a job whose `allowed_tools` an operator wrote: such a job can no longer leave a SOP waiting for approval or write SOP definitions, so a job that has to do either must not be restricted by `allowed_tools`. An RPC principal session restricted by tool names builds its registry with no ceiling and is not covered (see the Second declared gap).

  - a turn given a per-run `allowed_tools` seals its ceiling to the tools it actually holds (plus the deferred MCP tools it may activate), not to the names it was handed: a name its own policy removed no longer counts as held, for example `shell` for a peer whose profile has none;
  - a bounded delegate's rebuilt tools read the config the delegation was admitted against, so a feature switched on or off in that config is seen by the target;
  - a nested bounded hop is handed only the MCP tools its own bundles grant;
  - the 15 refusals added by this PR render from Fluent keys; in a locale without a translation they stay English.

  Jobs already stored under the old, wider ceiling are **not** retro-capped, and a SOP run already left parked before this is deployed is not retroactively cancelled.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the commits on this branch, or revert the PR merge commit. No migration or state cleanup: nothing persisted changed shape.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The bound is active whenever a ceiling is in force.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a legitimate scheduled job stops being created, re-armed or launched; a legitimate `sop_approve`/`delegate` capability stops surviving into a stored job; a legitimate peer relay stops receiving a tool the peer's own profile grants; a legitimate concurrent job update starts losing to a rival write; a SOP run started by a bounded caller is cancelled instead of resumable; a bounded target's command is refused that its own profile allows. Grep tool results for:
  - `refused — this stores or re-arms a shell job` (`cron_add`, `cron_update`, `schedule`, `cron_run`)
  - `refused — this job's stored allowed_tools reach beyond` and `refused — this job stores no allowed_tools`
  - `refused — this agent job would keep 'shell'`: a bounded registration tried to defer an agent with `shell`; the job has to list its tools without it
  - `<tool>: refused — ... Command not allowed by security policy` from `cron_update` or `schedule` resume: a caller's policy refuses the job's stored command; check the caller's `allowed_commands` before treating it as a regression
  - `refused — this tool was registered under bounded delegation but the caller's tool ceiling was never sealed`, and `send_message_to_peer: refused — a delegated caller ceiling was declared but never published`: fail-closed paths that indicate a sealing bug, not a policy decision
  - `refused — SOP` / `refused — run ... left outside this turn ... has been cancelled` (`sop_execute`, `sop_advance`): the parked-run cancellation path
  - ``sop_workshop `<action>` is not available under a caller tool ceiling``: the `sop_workshop` write refusal (`propose`, `capture_run`, `apply`, `reject`, `quarantine`); `list` and `inspect` are unaffected
  - `could NOT be cancelled ... may still be active - treat it as unresolved, not closed`: the cancellation failed to persist, the run is still parked and resumable; investigate the persistence backend
  - log line `bounded live SOP driver: cancelled a run that would have parked outside the turn`; its unpersisted counterpart `bounded live SOP driver: parked run could not be cancelled` comes with a turn error containing `reached a park that a bounded caller's tool ceiling cannot follow past this turn`
  - a cron job update or resume that fails with no obvious cause: check for a concurrent write from another turn of the same agent; it now surfaces as lock contention or a guard refusal instead of silently winning or losing
  - From `1a328ea53` the refusal strings above come from the `bounded-ceiling-*` keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`; in a locale without a translation they stay the English text quoted here.

prs.title: fix(mcp-builder): support mcp>=2 streamable_http_client import and custom headers
prs.body:
Fixes #1668

### Problem
In `mcp>=2.0.0`, `streamablehttp_client` was renamed to `streamable_http_client`, and custom HTTP headers are configured via `create_mcp_http_client` / `http_client` rather than as a direct kwarg to `streamable_http_client`.

Because `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/connections.py` unconditionally imported `streamablehttp_client` at module scope, importing `connections` or running `evaluation.py` fails on startup when installing `requirements.txt` (which specifies `mcp>=1.1.0` without an upper bound):

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../scripts/evaluation.py", line 19, in <module>
    from connections import create_connection
  File ".../scripts/connections.py", line 10, in <module>
    from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client
ImportError: cannot import name 'streamablehttp_client' from 'mcp.client.streamable_http'
```

### Solution
1. **Compatible import:** In `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/connections.py`, import `streamable_http_client` and `create_mcp_http_client` with fallback to `streamablehttp_client as streamable_http_client` for `mcp<2.0.0`.
2. **Context configuration:** In `MCPConnectionHTTP._create_context()`:
   - When `create_mcp_http_client` is available, create `http_client` with custom headers and pass to `streamable_http_client(url=self.url, http_client=http_client)`.
   - On `mcp<2.0.0`, pass `headers=self.headers` directly.
3. **Regression tests:** Added `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/test_connections.py` testing import resolution, stdio/sse/http transport factories, context manager creation, and validation error cases.

### Verification
- Ran `pytest skills/mcp-builder/scripts/test_connections.py -v`: all 5 tests passed.
- Verified `python skills/mcp-builder/scripts/evaluation.py --help` under `mcp 2.1.1` and Python 3.14: cleanly displays full usage and exits 0.
- Verified compilation with `python -m py_compile`.

prs.title: fix(skill-creator): isolate trigger evals and handle Windows and runtime failures
prs.body:
## Problem

Trigger evaluation can report false misses or invalid scores: per-worker command probes compete, select() on subprocess pipes fails on Windows, and unrelated tools stop the scan. Runtime failures also become non-triggers, incorrectly passing negative examples and misleading optimization.

Fixes #556.

## What changes

- Install one real candidate skill at `<temporary project>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, preserving its production name and candidate description. Parallel workers share it; concurrent runs use distinct UUID-based roots.
- Leave caller files untouched. The legacy `project_root` argument remains accepted but is no longer used.
- Reject same-name personal skill collisions, including those under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
- Resolve the Claude executable, including Windows npm shims. Read stdout/stderr with portable threads instead of select(). Close stdin and cap probes at eight turns.
- Keep scanning after Bash/Glob and other orientation tools. Match exact Skill names or skill-entrypoint Read paths, including Windows separators.
- Stop the probe process tree during cleanup: `taskkill /T /F` on Windows; a separate session/process group on POSIX.
- Treat error results, timeouts, truncated output and worker failures as invalid evaluations. Abort the batch instead of assigning zero trigger rates. Cancel pending work where possible; active workers finish their bounded cleanup.
- Preserve successful evaluation JSON. Initial optimization failures propagate; later failures preserve completed iterations. Empty and partial reports render correctly.
- Write candidate artifacts as UTF-8.

## Validation

Latest revision: Windows, Python 3.14.

```sh
# From skills/skill-creator
python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
uvx ruff check scripts/run_eval.py scripts/tests/test_eval_failures.py scripts/tests/test_stream_probe.py
git diff --check
```

- **21/21 tests pass.** Coverage includes artifact isolation, exact matching, late triggers, configuration collisions, invalid batch rejection, cleanup and partial-result recovery.
- A real Windows .cmd wrapper launches a Python child; the regression verifies that the child cannot continue after timeout. This test requires process-termination permissions and was run outside the restricted sandbox.
- Ruff passes for the files changed in the latest revision. Whitespace checks pass.
- Tests make no model calls and need no credentials. Instructions and limitations are in `scripts/tests/README.md`.

## Scope and limitations

The temporary project excludes caller-project files and configuration. Queries requiring local fixtures need those fixtures made available separately. Personal and managed Claude configuration is not fully isolated.

The original investigation included live routing experiments on Claude Code 2.1.149. Those historical observations are not a claim about every current version. This revision has not rerun live model evaluation or POSIX integration. The candidate uses the standard skill layout independently of legacy command behavior.

Related work: #794, #996, #1027, #1755 and #1757. This PR combines a real-skill artifact with portable stream handling, full-turn detection and explicit failure semantics.

prs.title: skill-creator: harden eval viewer (script breakout, DNS rebinding, cross-site POST, escaping)
prs.body:
## What

Hardens the `skill-creator` eval viewer (`generate_review.py` + `viewer.html`). The viewer is a local page that renders eval outputs (model-written, so untrusted) and saves feedback via a small HTTP server on localhost. Three gaps:

1. **Script breakout.** The page data is embedded as JSON in an inline `<script>`. A value containing `</script>` ended the block and the rest ran as HTML. Now `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028 and U+2029 are escaped as `\uXXXX` in the embedded JSON; it still parses to the identical object.
2. **No Host/Origin check on the local server.** Any web page open in the same browser could POST to `/api/feedback`, and a DNS-rebinding page could read the data back. Now `do_GET` and `do_POST` return 403 unless `Host` is `localhost:<port>` or `127.0.0.1:<port>` and `Origin`, if present, is one of those hosts. Requests without `Origin` (curl, same-origin GET) still work.
3. **Incomplete HTML escaping in `viewer.html`.** `escapeHtml` did not escape quotes and several fields (`metadata.timestamp`, `evals_run`, `runs_per_configuration`, the delta fields, `configLabel`, `run_number`, including a `title` attribute) went into `innerHTML` unescaped. `escapeHtml` now escapes `& < > " '` and returns `""` for null/undefined, and is applied to those fields.

## Testing

Ran the same script against the original and patched files (Python 3 + Node):

| Check | Original | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| `</script>` payload does not add a closing tag | fails | passes |
| Embedded JSON round-trips to identical object | passes | passes |
| `escapeHtml` escapes `"` and `'` | fails | passes |
| Same-origin POST `/api/feedback` | 200 | 200 |
| POST with no Origin | 200 | 200 |
| POST with foreign Origin | 200 | 403 |
| GET with foreign Host (rebinding) | 200 | 403 |
| GET `/` | 200 | 200 |

`py_compile` is clean. The browser page only calls relative `/api/feedback`, so the normal flow is unchanged. A separate read-only review of the diff found no blocking issues.

## Not covered (follow-up)

- A port-less `Host: localhost` is rejected; browsers always send the port here because it is non-default.
- Some other values still reach `innerHTML` unescaped: `r.passed`, `r.total`, `r.errors` in the benchmark table, and `summary.passed/failed/total` in `renderGrades`. They are normally numbers; I left them out to keep this change focused. Happy to extend the patch.
- The same files exist in `anthropics/claude-plugins-official` (`plugins/skill-creator`); I have not opened a PR there.

prs.title: fix(docx): report LibreOffice timeout as an error and verify the output
prs.body:
## What changed
`skills/docx/scripts/accept_changes.py` now returns an Error when `soffice` times out instead of reporting success, and only claims success after checking that the output DOCX no longer carries revision marks (`w:ins` / `w:del` / `w:moveFrom` / `w:moveTo`) in `word/*.xml` parts.

## Why
Defect 1 in #1770: `soffice` operates in place on a copy and the macro stores/closes the document itself, so a timeout leaves the output in an unknown state (possibly untouched, possibly partly processed) while the caller was told "Successfully accepted all tracked changes". `__main__` keys on `"Error" in message`, so the process also exited 0.

## How verified
LibreOffice is not installed in this environment, so the fix is verified with mocked `subprocess.run` plus real DOCX fixtures:
- Timeout (`subprocess.TimeoutExpired`): returns an Error mentioning the timeout, never "Successfully".
- `returncode == 0` but the output still contains `<w:ins>`: returns "tracked changes remain in output document".
- `returncode == 0` with a clean output DOCX: still reports success.
- `_docx_still_has_tracked_changes`: True for each revision marker (`w:ins`, `w:del`, `w:moveFrom`, `w:moveTo`) and for a non-zip file, False for a clean DOCX.
- `python -m py_compile` clean; no new third-party imports (`zipfile` is stdlib).

The macro-setup path (`_setup_libreoffice_macro`) is untouched.
